Ciel’s indignation was so prim it practically came with its own little huff.
She really was endlessly entertaining to watch.
“A brace—oh, the one around that tree in the courtyard. You’ve been at it again; you really do like that sort of thing. If you keep doing odd jobs, the teachers will start relying on you, so you’d better stop.”
“I don’t mind—I do it because I enjoy it. Besides, the teachers do care about the school, so it’s improper to talk about them that way.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No, fixing splints.
Please don't make me angry when I am eating."
Ciel-senpai gets angry.
She seems to be someone you can never tire of watching.
"Fixing splints…?
Ah, the splints in the courtyard!
You were at it again?
You sure enjoy that kind of thing, Senpai, but you'd be better off if you gave up.
If you keep doing things like that, the teachers will start expecting you to do them."
"That's all right, I do it because I enjoy it.
You shouldn't talk about the teachers like that though, you know.
They really care about the school."

entries.japanese:
……二人の会話の内容は、こっちにはどうにもわかりづらい。
「先輩、もしかして普段からああゆうコトやってるの？」
「おう。
なんだ遠野、知らないのか。
シエル先輩っていったら影の生徒会長って呼ばれてるぐらい便利な人なんだぞ」
「いや、俺は先輩に聞いたんだけどね。
まあいいけど……なに、その影の生徒会長って」
　強いの？
と目で聞いてみる。
　うむ、とおおげさに有彦は頷いた。
entries.maoEnglish:
Their conversation was difficult for an outsider to follow.
“Do you do things like that all the time?”
“Sure does. What, Tohno, you didn’t know? Ciel’s so useful they call her the shadow student-council president.”
“I was asking her, actually. But never mind—what’s a shadow student-council president?”
Is that powerful? I asked with my eyes.
Arihiko nodded grandly.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… I'm finding it difficult to follow their conversation.
"Senpai, don't tell me that you normally do that sort of thing?"
"Yeah.
Didn't you know, Tohno?
Ciel-senpai is so handy they call her the 'Shadow President' of the student council."
"No, I was asking Senpai.
Wait, never mind… what on earth is the 'Shadow President'?"
"Is she strong?" I ask with my eyes.
"Yeah," responds Arihiko with an exaggerated nod.

entries.japanese:
「強い。
肩書きだけの生徒会と違って、先輩に頼めばなんでも解決してくれるっていうぐらい、完璧な三年生だ。
　一年じゃファンクラブまであるし、教師連中もなにか厄介ごとが起こると『シエルに相談すれば大丈夫だ』なんて暖簾に腕押し状態だからな。
いまじゃ先輩が何をしたって、文句をいってくる教師もいないぐらいなのだ」
　有彦は我が事のように誇らしげに語る。
「へえ。
すごい人だったんだ、シエル先輩って。
うちの教師連中に頼りにされるなんて、よっぽどのことだよ、それ」
　感心して先輩を見る。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Powerful. Unlike the council, which only has the title, she’s the perfect third-year—ask her for anything and she’ll solve it.
The first-years even have a fan club for her, and whenever trouble starts, trying to get the teachers to do anything is hopeless; they just say, ‘Ask Ciel and she’ll handle it.’ At this point, she could do practically anything without a teacher daring to complain.”
Arihiko spoke as proudly as if these were his own accomplishments.
“Wow. I had no idea you were that remarkable. Getting our teachers to depend on you is no small feat.”
Impressed, I turned to her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"She's quite something, totally unlike the Student Council, which is the student council in name only.
She's a third-year who'll solve anything for you if you ask her.
Even got a fan club among the first years!
And if something happens, the teachers all rely on her.
There isn't a single teacher who complains about what Senpai does."
Arihiko speaks with pride as if he was actually talking about himself.
"Wow… Ciel-senpai sure is amazing.
Even the teachers rely on you."
I look at Senpai, impressed.

entries.japanese:
「あ、はい。
その、ありがとうございます」
　……何が恥ずかしいのか、先輩は顔を真っ赤にして照れている。
　先輩はかちゃかちゃとスプーンでカレーライスをかきまわす。
　照れ隠しらしいのだけど、それでこっちも当面の敵を思い出した。
　カレーライスだけならいざしらず、その後にはカレーうどんが控えているのだ。
　医者からあんまり食事を摂ってはいけないと忠告されてはいるが、この場合はしかたないのでとにかくカレーライスを食べ始めた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh. Well, thank you.”
For some reason, she turned scarlet with embarrassment.
She stirred her curry rice with a clatter of spoon against plate, apparently to hide her embarrassment.
The sound reminded me of the enemy still before me.
Even if I conquered the curry rice, the curry udon remained.
My doctor had warned me not to eat too much, but I had no choice, so I started on the curry rice.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah, yes.
Uh… thank you."
Senpai turns bright red, embarrassed.
Senpai churns her curry rice with her spoon.
I guess it's to hide her embarrassment, but it reminds me of the enemy I have to face.
Curry rice by itself is fine, but after that awaits curry udon.
My doctor warned me not to eat too much, but I don't think there's anything else in this situation that I can do.
So I start to dig in to the rice.

entries.japanese:
…………もぐもぐ。
　とりあえず一品食べ終わろうと、全精力をカレーライスにふりむける。
　その間、先輩と有彦はなにやら自分の家について話をしていた。
　有彦に親御さんがいないのは知っていたけど、先輩も一人暮しをしているらしい。
　先輩のアパートは、学校からわりかし近いそうだ。
ちょうど大通りと公園の間ぐらいか。
entries.maoEnglish:
Chew, chew.
I devoted every last resource to finishing at least one dish.
Meanwhile, she and Arihiko talked about their homes.
I knew Arihiko’s parents weren’t around, but apparently she lived alone as well.
Her apartment was fairly close to school. About halfway between the main avenue and the park.
entries.mirrorMoon:
*munch* *munch*
Having decided to try to finish one dish quickly, I direct all my concentration to the rice.
Meanwhile, Senpai and Arihiko began talking about their own homes for some reason.
I already know that Arihiko doesn't live with his parents, but it seems Senpai is also living by herself.
Apparently, Senpai's apartment is quite close to school.
It's roughly between the main street and the park.

entries.japanese:
「ふーん。
それじゃ遠野くんはどのあたりに住んでるんですか？」
「え？」
　無言でカレーライスを食べていたこっちの顔を覗き込んで、先輩はトウトツになんの関連性もない事を聞いてきた。
「どのあたりって……どうしてそんなこと聞くんですか、先輩は」
「遠野くん、わたしの家の場所聞いちゃいましたよね？
　なのにわたしだけ遠野くんのお家を知らないのは、不公平だと思います」
「不公平って───妙なことを気にするんだな、先輩は」
entries.maoEnglish:
“I see. What part of town do you live in, Tohno?”
“What?”
She peered into my face as I ate in silence and abruptly asked something completely unrelated.
“Why do you want to know where I live?”
“You heard where I live, didn’t you? It seems unfair if I’m the only one who doesn’t know where your home is.”
“Unfair—you worry about some peculiar things.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hmmm… So, Tohno-kun, where do you live?"
"Huh?"
I silently eat my food when Senpai, peering at me, asks a completely unrelated question.
"Where…?
Why do you ask, Senpai?"

"You already heard where I live, right, Tohno-kun?
I think it's unfair if I don't know where your house is."
"Unfair?
You worry about the strangest things, Senpai."

entries.japanese:
「妙なことじゃないです。
どこに住んでるかわからないんじゃ、なにかあった時お見舞いにもいけないじゃないですか」
　カレーライスを食べる口が止まる。
　何かいま、さらりと嬉しくなるような事を言われた気がした。
「……えっと。
お見舞いって、その、俺が風邪でもひいたら先輩が見舞いにきてくれるの？」
「いえ、行きませんよ。
今のところそんな予定はありませんから」
　笑顔で、きっぱりと、当たり前のように先輩は速答した。
entries.maoEnglish:
“It isn’t peculiar. If I don’t know where you live, I couldn’t visit if something happened to you.”
My spoon stopped halfway to my mouth.
She had just said something casually that made me strangely happy.
“Um. Do you mean you’d come visit if I caught a cold?”
“No, I wouldn’t. I have no plans to right now.”
She answered at once, smiling as though it were the most obvious thing in the world.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"It's not strange.
If I don't know where you live, I can't visit you if something happens, right?"
I stop eating the curry rice.
I have the feeling that something has been said that I should be jubilant about.
"Eh… Visit?
You mean you'd come and visit me if I catch a cold or something?"
"No, I wouldn't.
I don't have any plans to visit at the moment."
Smiling, Senpai replies instantly, as if stating the obvious.

entries.japanese:
「……………」
　さっきの嬉しくなるような感情はぬか喜びだったらしい。
先輩にはまったく悪意がない。
　そうか、天然なんだなこの人。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
Apparently that little rush of happiness had been premature. She hadn’t meant a word of it cruelly.
So she really was oblivious.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……"
It seems like the euphoria is premature.
Senpai doesn't seem to have any unusual intentions.
I see now… that's just the way she is.

entries.japanese:
「……仕方ないな。
　うん、俺の家もこの周辺だよ。
徒歩にして四十分弱。
ほら、郊外の坂の上に住宅地があるでしょ。
あそこの奥まで行ったところです」
「そっか。
今日から引っ越すんだっけ、おまえ」
　ポン、と手をうつ有彦。
　先輩はかすかに首をかしげている。
「引っ越したって───遠野くん、転校生だったんですか？」
「は？」
　先輩はおかしな事を言い出す。
　つい、有彦と無言で目があってしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…Fine.
I live around here too—just under forty minutes on foot. You know the residential neighborhood on the hill outside town? My house is all the way at the back.”
“Oh, right. You’re moving today.”
Arihiko smacked one fist into his palm.
She tilted her head slightly.
“You moved—Tohno, are you a transfer student?”
“What?”
She had suddenly said something bizarre.
Arihiko and I exchanged a silent look.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I guess I have to tell you.
Yeah, my house is nearby too, only a forty minute walk.
There's a residential district on top of the hill, right?
Just go a little further and you're there."
"Oh yeah.
You're moving today, right?"
Arihiko strikes his hand on the desk.
Senpai tilts her head slightly.
"Moving?
Tohno-kun, were you a transfer student?"
"Huh?"
Senpai asks a strange question.
Arihiko meets my gaze.

entries.japanese:
「……あのですね。
俺は一年からこの学校にいるし、先輩ともその頃から顔見知りだったじゃないですか。
なんだってそこで転校生だなんて単語が出てくるんです？」
「だって遠野くん、昨日引っ越したって───」
「引っ越したら誰だって転校生になるわけじゃありません。
ただ住所が変わっただけで、学校は変わってないんです。
今まで隣街の親戚の家にいたんですけど、もともとの自分の家に戻っただけなんですよ」
　わけのわからない驚き方をしている先輩は、なるほど、と納得したようだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…I’ve attended this school since first year, and we’ve known each other since then. How did the phrase ‘transfer student’ enter this conversation?”
“But you said you moved yesterday—”
“Moving house doesn’t automatically make someone a transfer student. My address changed, not my school. I was living with relatives in the next town, and now I’m simply returning to my original home.”
After her baffling surprise, she finally seemed to understand.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Uh, listen… I've been here since the first year.
We've known each other since then, right?
Why are you asking if I'm a transfer student now?"
"But Tohno-kun, you moved yesterday, so--"
"Moving doesn't automatically make you a transfer student.
I'm just changing my address, not my school.
Until now, I've been living with some relatives in the neighboring town.
I'm just going back to my real home, that's all."
Senpai, who wears a look of surprise, seems to understand.

entries.japanese:
「お家が変わっただけなんですね。
それで今は郊外の住宅地に引っ越した、と」
「そっ。
坂の上にある仰々しいところにね。
……正確にいうと、そこに行くのは今日からなんだけどさ」
「……はあ。
それってもしかして、遠野さんのお屋敷の事ですか？」
　先輩は恐る恐る、遠慮するように聞いてきた。
　街の人達からすれば、坂の上にある洋館はなにか特別なものとして映っているのだろう。
　こっちだってこの八年間戻っていないけど、記憶の中にある遠野の屋敷はばかみたいに大きかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Only your home has changed. And now you live in that residential district outside town.”
“Exactly. In that absurdly grand place on top of the hill. Though, strictly speaking, I won’t actually move in until today.”
“…Could that be the Tohno estate?”
Ciel asked timidly, as though afraid of prying.
To the people of this town, the Western-style house on the hill must have seemed like something apart.
I hadn’t returned for eight years myself, but in my memory the Tohno estate was absurdly large.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I see, you've only changed your residence.
So, now you live in the outskirts of town."
"Yeah.
It's that colorful place on top of the hill… I'm moving there today."
"Haah… could that possibly be the Tohno-san mansion?" Senpai asks with some hesitation.
The western-style house at the top of the hill is probably seen as something special by residents of this town.
I haven't been there for eight years, but even in my memories, the Tohno mansion was ridiculously large.

entries.japanese:
「まあそういうこと。
自分でも場違いだとは思ってるんだけどね、引っ越しちまったものはしょうがないから」
「───ふぅん。
その様子じゃあんまり乗り気じゃなかったのか、おまえ」
「さあ、良くも悪くもないっていうのが本当のところだよ。
自分でもよくわかってないんだ」
「ま、自分の家っていっても八年ぶりなんだろ？
　落ち着かないのもわかるぜ。
しばらくは他人の家みたいに感じるんだろうさ」
「……どうだろうね。
まだ帰ってないからよくはわからないよ。
まあ、俺にはおまえの家っていう避難場所があるから気は楽だけど」
entries.maoEnglish:
“That’s right. I know I’ll be out of place there, but the move is already settled, so there’s no use arguing.”
“───Huh. From the sound of it, you weren’t too excited about going back.”
“Honestly, I feel neither good nor bad about it. I’m not sure what I feel myself.”
“Well, even if it’s your home, you haven’t been there in eight years. No wonder you’re uneasy. It’ll probably feel like somebody else’s house for a while.”
“Maybe. I haven’t gone back yet, so I can’t really say. At least I know I can always escape to your place.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yeah, that's right.
I don't think it's the right place for me either, but it's too late now that I'm done moving."
"Hmm… You don't seem too happy about it."
"It's neither good nor bad.
I don't quite understand it either."
"Well, even if it is your house, it's been eight years, right?
I can understand if you're feeling strange.
It'll probably feel like someone else's house for a while."
"I wonder if that's so… I haven't gone back yet, so I don't know.
Well, I'm a bit relaxed, since I've always got a refuge at your place."

entries.japanese:
「……むっ。
ふざけんな、オレん家はおまえの避難場所じゃねえぞ。
休みになりゃあ泊まりにきやがって、おかげで姉貴はオレより友達の遠野くんびいきになっちまったじゃねえか」
「…………」
　それは有彦の素行が悪いからだと思うんだけど、口にするとますます話がこじれるので止めておこう。
 ───正直、自分の家が話題にあがるのは気持ちがいいものではない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hey. Don’t call my house your refuge. Every school holiday you come barging in to stay, and now my sister favors her dear friend Tohno over her own brother.”
“…”
That was probably because Arihiko behaved so badly, but saying so would only make things worse.
───Truthfully, I didn’t enjoy having my home discussed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yeah, right.
My house is no refuge of yours.
When you come over during the holidays, my sister treats you better than me!"
"……"
That's probably only because Arihiko has terrible behavior, but I refrain from telling him that in the interests of preventing the conversation from getting any worse.
---To be honest, it's not pleasant to have my home raised as a topic of conversation.

entries.japanese:
「へえ。
仲がいいんですね、二人とも」
　先輩は興味深そうに俺と有彦を眺めている。
「まさか。
俺と遠野は奪い合う事はあっても手を取り合う事がない、いわば敵同士なのですよマドモアゼル」
　有彦はうんざりした口調で言う。
　……こっちだってこいつのエセ外人くさいところにうんざりしそうだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh. You two really are close.”
She looked back and forth between us with interest.
“Hardly. Tohno and I may fight over the same spoils, but we would never join hands—we are enemies, mademoiselle.”
Arihiko sounded thoroughly weary.
I was getting thoroughly weary of his bargain-bin foreigner act.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Wow… You two certainly get along well." Senpai peers at Arihiko and me.
"No way!
Me and Tohno would never help each other, no matter how much trouble we were in.
In other words, we're enemies, mademoiselle."
Arihiko says in a fed-up tone.
I'm getting pretty fed-up myself with his pseudo-foreigner-isms, too.

entries.japanese:
「でも遠野くんは乾くんのところに泊まりにくるぐらいなんでしょう？
　仲、すごくいいじゃないですか」
「違いますよ先輩。
遠野のヤロウは両親に遠慮して、長い休みになると家に居づらいってんで逃げてくるだけです。
このヤロウ、預けられたってことで有間の家の人たちに遠慮してたんだ。
　で、ていよく部屋が空いてるオレのところに転がり込んでくるってワケ。
こいつは外見がいいから姉貴にも気に入られちまってさ、厚かましくも手ぶらで泊まりにくるんだぜ！」
　許せん、と有彦は握りこぶしを震わせる。
「……預けられたって、遠野くんがですか？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“But Tohno stays at your house, doesn’t he? That makes you sound very close indeed.”
“It’s not like that. Tohno feels so indebted to his foster parents that he can’t relax at home during long holidays, so he runs away; ever since the Arimas took him in, the bastard’s been walking on eggshells around them. Since I conveniently have a spare room, he comes rolling into my place instead.
Worse, he’s got a pretty face, so my sister adores him. He even has the nerve to show up empty-handed!” Outrageous, Arihiko proclaimed, shaking a clenched
fist.
“The Arimas took you in, Tohno?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"But your relationship is so good that Tohno-kun has stayed over at your house before, right?
Doesn't that mean you get along really well?"
"You're wrong, Senpai.
That damn Tohno is too reserved toward his parents, and he'd come over to my place every vacation.
He's reserved toward them 'cause they're taking care of him.
That's why he comes over to my place, where we conveniently have an empty room.
Since he looks pretty decent, my sister took a liking to him, and he shamelessly comes to stay with us without paying a cent!"
Arihiko's fist trembles, as if to say "unforgivable!"
"…… Taking care, Tohno-kun?"

entries.japanese:
「あっ――――」
　ハッとして自分の口を押さえる有彦。
「……わりい。
無闇に口にするコトじゃなかった」
「いいよ。
別に悪いことじゃないんだから」
　有彦の顔を見ずに、カレーライスを食べながらそう言った。
「そっか。
ま、そーだよな。
アレで文句を言ったらバチが当たるってもんか」
　うん、と納得する有彦。
　こいつのこういう、突き抜けたような楽観性は本当にうらやましい。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ah—”
Arihiko caught himself and covered his mouth.
“…Sorry—that wasn’t mine to blurt out.”
“It’s fine. It isn’t anything shameful.”
Without looking at him, I kept eating my curry rice.
“Right. Yeah, of course. After all they did for you, you’d be tempting fate if you complained.”
Arihiko nodded, satisfied.
I really envied that irrepressible optimism of his.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah…"
Arihiko clamps a hand over his mouth.
"…… Sorry.
I should've thought before I spoke."
"It's okay.
You didn't say anything bad."
I continue to eat my food without looking at Arihiko.

"Really?
Yeah, you're right.
If you complained about that, you'll be in for some punishment."
Arihiko nods to himself in agreement.
His overwhelming optimism is something I am truly envious of.

entries.japanese:
「……ごめんなさい遠野くん。
その、前のご家族とはうまくいってなかったんですか……？」
「いや、そんなコトはないっスよ。
こいつ、有間の親御さんとは何の問題もないもんな。
　あ、有間っていうのがこいつが預けられてた家の人達なんだけど、これがすっごくいい人達でさ、オレから見れば幸せな家庭だった。
　だっていうのにこいつは養子にならないかって話も断って、休みになればオレんところに逃げてきやがるんだ。
ったく、ホントに何が不満なんだオマエは」
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’m sorry, Tohno. Did you not get along with the family you lived with?” “No, not at all—he never had any
problems with the Arimas. That’s the family who took him in, by the way, and they’re wonderful people.
From where I stood, it was a happy home.
And yet he turned down their offer to adopt him, then ran to my place every holiday. Seriously, what are you so unhappy about?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I'm sorry, Tohno-kun.
Um… did you not get along with your previous family?"
"No, that's not it.
He has no problem with the Arimas.
Oh, the Arimas were the family who took care of him.
They're really nice people, and from what I could tell, they're a happy family.
Even so, he refused to be their adopted kid, and he escaped to my place every vacation.
Sheesh… just what were you not satisfied with, anyway?"

entries.japanese:
「不満なんかあるわけないだろ。
よくしてもらってるから、これ以上負担をかけたくないだけじゃないか」
　答えて、カレーライスを食べ終わった。
　さて、残るはカレーうどんだけなのたが―――
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’m not unhappy. They’ve done so much for me that I don’t want to burden them any further.”
With that answer, I finished my curry rice.
Now only the curry udon remained—but—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"There's nothing I wasn't satisfied about.
It's just that I've received so much from them already, I didn't want to be a further burden on them."
I finish my rice as I reply.
Now, only the curry udon is left…

entries.japanese:
「いいよ、先輩。
つまんない話をきかせて悪かった」
「え、そんなコトないですよ。
わたしのほうこそヘンなコトを聞いてしまって、すみません」
　先輩はむりやりに明るく振る舞おうとする。
　……中学校から友人だった有彦ならいざ知らず、先輩を相手にこんなこみいった話をしても迷惑なだけだろう。
　事実、先輩はとても居づらそうにそわそわしている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“It’s all right. Sorry we made you listen to such a dreary story.”
“No, not at all. I’m the one who asked something strange—I’m sorry.”
She tried to sound bright.
Arihiko had known me since middle school, but burdening her with such complicated family business could only be awkward.
In fact, she was fidgeting as though deeply uncomfortable.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"It's okay, Senpai.
Sorry for making you listen to something so boring."
"Eh, not at all.
I'm sorry for asking you something so strange."
Senpai forces herself to look cheerful.
The topic might be fine for a long-time friend like Arihiko, but a complex matter like this would only have been troublesome for Senpai.
And to prove my point, Senpai sits there uneasily.

entries.japanese:
「あー、ゴメン先輩。
オレ、ちょっと遠野と内緒話があるからさ、席外してもらえない？」
　無造作に、有彦はとんでもないことを言い出した。
　今のセリフは遠まわしに、いやストレートに『先輩は邪魔だから消えてくれ』、と言っているようなものじゃないか……！
「ばっ、なに言ってるんだおまえ！
　内緒話なんてどこでもできるし、先輩メシ食べ終わって――」
―――る。
　あんなに有彦と話をしていたのに、いつのまにかちゃっかりきっかり、先輩はカレーライスを平らげていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Uh, sorry, but I need to speak to Tohno in private. Would you mind giving us a minute?”
Arihiko tossed out the outrageous request as casually as anything.
Indirectly—no, directly—he had just told her, You’re in the way, so disappear……!
“Y-you idiot! What are you saying? We can talk privately anywhere, and she’s already fin――
―――ished.
Despite talking with Arihiko the whole time, she had somehow polished off every last grain of curry rice.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah, Senpai… sorry, but I've got something private to talk to Tohno about.
Would you mind leaving?"
Arihiko has no problems making such an offensive request.
Isn't that phrase an indirect… no, a direct way of saying 'We don't want you, Senpai, so get lost…'?
"You idio---What do you think you're saying!?
We can discuss those things anywhere!
And Senpai is still finishing her--"
---Lunch.
Despite all the talking with Arihiko, Senpai has finished her rice anyway.

entries.japanese:
「わかりました。
それじゃあ、お先に失礼しますね」
　先輩はペコリ、とおじぎをして席を立っていった。
　テーブルには自分と有彦の二人きりになる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“All right. Then I’ll leave you two to it.”
She gave us a small bow, rose, and left.
Arihiko and I were alone at the table.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No, I understand.
Well then, I'll be leaving."
Senpai lowers her head in a quick bow and leaves.
Only Arihiko and I remain at the table.

entries.japanese:
「……はあ。
先輩も居づらそうだったし、俺もこうしたほうがいいとは思ったけどさ。
おまえってわりと紙一重だよな、有彦」
「んー、まあ、さっきのは仕方ねえだろ。
口をすべらしたのはオレのほうなんだから、嫌われ役ぐらいは買ってでるよ」
　……ぞぞぞ、と力うどんをすする有彦。
　先輩と話をしていたせいですっかり冷めてしまっているようだ。
「……悪い。
おまえ、先輩のこと狙ってたんだろ？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“…I suppose she was uncomfortable, and I agree this is probably better. But you really do walk a very fine line, Arihiko.”
“Well, that couldn’t be helped. I’m the one who let it slip, so the least I could do was play the villain.”
Arihiko slurped his mochi udon.
It seemed to have gone completely cold while we talked to Ciel.
“Sorry. You were after her, weren’t you?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
I sigh.
"Well, it looks like Senpai was having a hard time too, so it was for the best, but you were really pushing it there, Arihiko."
"Hmm… Well, it's not like I had a choice.
Anyways, I guess I'll take the role of the guy she ends up disliking."
*slurp* *slurp* *slurp*
Arihiko slurps away at his chikara udon.
It seems it has gone cold while we were talking to Senpai.
"…… Sorry.
You were trying to hit on Senpai, weren't you?"

entries.japanese:
「そりゃあね。
うちの学校の中じゃピカイチだからさ。
でもまあ、アレぐらいで気にするような性格だったらどうでもいい。
　それ、と。
オレが遠野に内緒話があるっていうのもホントのことだし」
「………？」
　有彦の声はわりと深刻だった。
　ぱきん、と割り箸を割って、カレーうどんを食べ始める。
「……なんだよ。
気持ち悪いな、急に深刻になって。
いっとくけどお金ならないぞ。
今日から俺は金欠少年として生きるんだから」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Sure. She’s the best-looking girl in the whole school. But if something that minor is enough to put her off me, then to hell with it.
And another thing. I really did need to speak to you in private.”
“…?”
His voice had turned surprisingly grave.
I snapped apart my chopsticks and began on the curry udon.
“What is it? Don’t suddenly get serious; it’s creepy. And if you want money, I haven’t got any. As of today, I begin my new life as an impoverished youth.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Of course.
She's probably the number one girl at our school.
But if she's the type to care about something like that, then she's not worth it.
Oh, yeah, I really do have something to talk to you about in private."
"…?"
Arihiko's voice turns serious.
I split my chopsticks with a snap and begin to eat my udon.
"What's wrong?
Why so serious all of a sudden?
I'll let you know right now that I don't have any money.
From today onwards, I'm going to be living life as a penniless student."

entries.japanese:
「―――そんなんじゃねえって。
オレが聞きたいのはさ、遠野は実際どうなのかな、と」
「どうって、なにが」
「だから。
おまえ、小学校から有間の家に預けられてたんだろ？
　どんな理由でか知らないが、それから八年も経つんだ。
なんで今になって勘当してた息子を呼び戻すんだろうかな、キミの父親は」
　……そうか。
　こいつはこいつなりに、遠野志貴のことを心配していてくれたらしい。
entries.maoEnglish:
“—That’s not it. What I want to know is how you’re actually taking all this.”
“Taking what?”
“You’ve lived with the Arimas since elementary school, haven’t you? I don’t know why, but it’s been eight years. Why would your father suddenly summon the son he disowned after all this time?”
…I see.
Apparently, in his own way, Arihiko had been worried about Shiki Tohno.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"It's not that, damn it.
What I want to know is this; what's really going on with you, Tohno?"
"What do you mean?"
"You've been at the Arimas' since primary school, right?
I don't know why, but it's been eight years already.
Your dad has basically disinherited you.
Why is he calling you back all of a sudden?"
…… I see.
In his own strange way, Arihiko is worried about me.

entries.japanese:
「……いや、別に勘当されてたわけじゃないよ。
なんとなく屋敷から追い出されただけだから、有彦が気に病む程度のことじゃない」
「あのな、遠野くん。
なんとなくで子供を家から追い出すような家庭があったら、それはすでに悲劇ではなく笑い話だ。
オー、イッツパーティージョーク。
しかし寒すぎて笑え、ナイ」
　有彦は大げさに両手を広げて肩をすくめる。
「……まあ、そうかも。
たしかになんとなくで家から追い出されたら、そりゃあ笑うしかないだろうね」
entries.maoEnglish:
“No. I wasn’t disowned; I was just sort of thrown out of the estate, so this isn’t something you need to worry about.”
“Listen, Tohno. If a family throws a child out for no particular reason, that stops being a tragedy and becomes a joke. Oh, it is party joke. But is too cold, so laugh—NO.”
Arihiko spread his hands and shrugged theatrically.
“Maybe. If I were thrown out for no reason, I suppose all I could do is laugh.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"He didn't 'disinherit' me.
He just kicked me out of the house somehow."
"Tohno-kun, if there ever was a family that kicked their kid out of their house 'somehow', that's not a tragedy, it's a comedy. 'Oh, it's a party joke!' But it's so boring, it's not funny."
Arihiko spreads his arms and shrugs.
"…… Yeah, I guess you're right.
If you get kicked out of the house, all you can really do is laugh."

entries.japanese:
「だろう？
　おまけに二度と敷居は跨ぐなっていう決め台詞付きときた。
世間さまではそーゆーのは勘当というんだぞ。
　今まで聞かなかったけどな、おまえはどうして勘当されたんだ」
「……………」
　……………さあ。
　そんな事、こっちが聞きたいぐらいだ。
「ま、話したくないなら、いい」
　有彦はどんぶりを両手でもって、ぐびぐびと冷めた力うどんの汁を飲み干していく。
　休み時間は短い。
　有彦の早食いを見習って、こっちもぐびぐびとカレーうどんを平らげる事にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Exactly. And they even gave you the grand line about never darkening their doorstep again. The rest of society calls that disowning someone.
I’ve never asked before, but why did they disown you?”
“…”
I had no idea.
I would have liked an answer myself.
“Well, if you don’t want to talk about it, forget it.”
Arihiko raised his bowl in both hands and gulped down the cold mochi-udon broth.
Lunch break was short.
Following his example, I hurriedly finished my own curry udon.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"And then he said some cliche line like, 'Never step foot in this house again!' or something, right?
That's what people would call 'disinheritance.'
Come to think of it, I've never heard why you were disinherited."
"……"
…… Who knows?
That's something I'd like to know too.
"Well, if you don't want to talk about it, you don't have to."
Grabbing his bowl with both hands, Arihiko drains what is left of his chikara udon.
Lunchtime is short.
Following Arihiko, I decide to quickly finish my curry udon.

entries.japanese:
昼休みの廊下は何かと込み合っている。
　これから学食に行こうとする生徒や、お弁当を片手にお気に入りの場所に向かう生徒たち。
　そんな人の流れに混ざりながら、学食に行こうか購買に行こうかふらふらと迷ってみる。
「……………」
　なんか、すごく自分が暇人のような気がしてきた。
　こんなところで油をうっている暇があるなら、有彦のいる学食に向かったほうが幾分ましだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
The corridors were crowded at lunchtime.
Students were heading for the cafeteria or carrying boxed lunches to their favorite haunts.
I drifted with the flow, unable to decide between the cafeteria and the school store.
“…”
I was starting to feel like I had nothing better to do.
If I had time to loiter here, I might as well join Arihiko in the cafeteria.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The hall during lunchtime is packed.
Students head to the cafeteria or to their favorite places, lunches in hand.
Caught in the flow of people, I contemplate whether I should go to the cafeteria or the store.
"……"
I'm taken aback by my own leisure.
If I have time to waste here, it'd be better if I go to the cafeteria where Arihiko is.

entries.japanese:
食堂の席は、もうほとんどが埋まっていた。
　教室でぼんやりとしていたタイムロスのせいで、学食の席はほぼ全滅状態になっている。
「―――空いてる席なんてない、か」
　混雑した学食を見渡す。
　この時間で席なんて空いているはずがないけど、それでも一応テーブルの状態を確認する。
entries.maoEnglish:
Almost every seat in the cafeteria was already taken.
Thanks to the time I had wasted staring into space in the classroom, nearly every seat was gone.
“―――No seats left, then.”
I surveyed the packed cafeteria.
Nothing should have been free at this hour, but I checked the tables anyway.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Almost all the seats in the cafeteria are taken.
Because I spaced out in the hallway, empty seats are pretty much non-existent at this point.
"---Aren't there any empty seats?"
I cast my gaze over the crowded cafeteria.
There shouldn't be any spare seats this late, but I decide to check the tables out anyway.

entries.japanese:
「………あ」
　驚いた、というより呆れた。
　ものの見事に二つといわず三つも四つも席が空いているテーブルがある。
　そこに座っている生徒は二人。
　そのうちの一人が、席を探してきょろきょろしている俺に気がついたみたいだ。
「いょぉう、遠野！」
　なんて、ぶんぶんと手を振ってくる生徒は、髪をオレンジ色に染めたクラスメイトだ。
「………………」
　あたま、いたい。
　けど他にあいている席もなし、仕方なく手を振ってくる友人のテーブルへと歩いていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…Oh.”
I was less surprised than exasperated.
One table had not two but three or four empty seats,
even though two students were sitting there.
One of them seemed to notice me looking around.
“Heeey, Tohno!”
The student waving both arms was my orange-haired classmate.
“…”
My head hurt.
But there were no other empty seats, so I reluctantly headed for my waving friend’s table.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Ah."
I'm surprised…… no, I'm astounded.
There, plain as day, is a table with not two, not even three, but four unoccupied seats.
There are two students sitting at the table, and it seems like one of them noticed me during my efforts to locate a seat.
"Yo, Tohno!"
The student vigorously waving his hand is my dear classmate with the dyed orange hair.
"……"
My head hurts.
But there isn't anywhere else to sit, so I have no choice but to return the wave and walk towards the table where my friend is sitting.

entries.japanese:
テーブルには有彦と、意外な人が同席していた。
「あれ、シエル先輩」
「あれ、遠野くんですね」
　二人して、間の抜けた指差し確認なんかをしたりする。
entries.maoEnglish:
Arihiko was sharing the table with someone unexpected.
“Oh—Ciel.”
“Oh—it’s Tohno.”
We pointed stupidly at one another, each confirming the other’s identity.
entries.mirrorMoon:
An unexpected person is sitting at the table with him.
"Huh, Ciel-senpai?"
"Ah, if it isn't Tohno-kun."
We point at each other simultaneously.

entries.japanese:
「よう遠野っ―――て、なに？
　先輩、遠野のこと知ってるの？」
「はい、今日も一度会っています。
廊下でだーんとぶつかったんですよね、遠野くん」
「あ……はい、その節は、どうも」
　すみません、と頭をさげる。
「いえいえ、こちらこそぼーっとしていてごめんなさい。
遠野くん、真面目な人なんですね」
「真面目って……そんなことは、ないんですけど」
　先輩は笑顔のままで、満足げに頷く。
　……なんていうか、やっぱり独特の雰囲気をもった先輩だ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hey, Toh—wait, what? You know him?”
“Yes, we’ve already met once today. We went bang into each other in the corridor, didn’t we, Tohno?”
“Ah—yes, sorry about that.”
I bowed my head in apology.
“No, I’m sorry; I was daydreaming. You’re very conscientious, Tohno.”
“Conscientious—I wouldn’t say that—” Still smiling, she nodded with evident satisfaction.
There really was something singular about her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yo, Tohno---hey wait…… Senpai, do you know Tohno?"
"Yes, I've met him once today already.
We bumped into each other with a bang today, didn't we, Tohno-kun?"
"Ah…… yes, sorry about that."
I lower my head in apology.
"Not at all.
I'm also sorry for spacing out like that.
You're a serious person, aren't you, Tohno-kun?"
"Serious……?
No, not really."
Smiling, Senpai gives a satisfied nod.
How should I say this…… Senpai has a unique atmosphere around her.

entries.japanese:
「でも意外です。
遠野くん、乾くんとお知り合いだったんですね。
もしかしてクラスが一緒なんですか？」
「その通り！
　オレと遠野は知り合いも知り合い、一年からクラスは一緒で、かつ中学校時代からの腐れ縁っていう大親友ですよ、オレたちは！」
　だん、とテーブルを叩いて力説する大親友。
　……なんていうか、いつも以上にハッスルしているように見えるのは気のせいか。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Still, what a surprise. I didn’t know you and Inui were acquainted. Are you in the same class?”
“Exactly—acquainted doesn’t begin to cover it. Tohno and I have shared a class since first year, and we’ve been inseparable since middle school—we’re the best of friends!”
My best friend slammed the table to emphasize the point.
Was it my imagination, or was he even more worked up than usual?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"But it's sure surprising that Tohno-kun and Inui-kun know each other.
Could it be that you two are in the same class?"
"That's right!
Me and Tohno are more than casual acquaintances!
We've been in the same class since our first year, and we've been inseparable best friends since middle school!"
My best friend strikes the table with a bang for emphasis.
…… Is it just me, or is he more hyper than usual?

entries.japanese:
「ほら、座りたまえ大親友！
　いつまでもぼけーっとつっ立っているとせっかくの力うどんがのびてしまうじゃあないか。
さっさと座って、オレに断りもなくどうやって先輩と知り合ったのか洗いざらい聞かせてくれ」
　有彦はばんばん、と楽しそうに背中を叩いている。
「…………」
　有彦が想像しているような話なんてないけど、他に席は空いていない。
　騒々しくなる事を覚悟して、有彦の隣に座った。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Come on, sit down, my dearest friend! If you stand there gawping any longer, your precious mochi udon will get soggy. Now sit and tell me every last detail of how you met Ciel without my permission.”
Arihiko cheerfully thumped me on the back.
“…”
There was no story remotely like the one he was imagining, but no other seats were free.
Resigned to the coming uproar, I sat beside him.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Come on, best friend, sit down!
If you just keep standing there vacantly, your chikara udon is going to go stale.
Hurry up and sit down, and let me hear all about how you got to know Senpai."
Arihiko slaps my back cheerfully.
"……"
While I really have no story like Arihiko might be hoping for, there are no other seats available.
Reluctantly, I take a seat next to him.

entries.japanese:
有彦はシエル先輩と親しいみたいだ。
　まだ数回しか会ったコトのない俺に比べて、気軽に先輩と話をしている。
「ところで先輩、さっき遠野とぶつかったとか言ってたけど、なにがあったんスか？」
「はい、休み時間に遠野くんとぶつかってしまったんです。
わたしはケガがなかったんですけど、遠野くんは頭をぶつけてしまいまして」
「ふうん……遠野がそんなヘマやるとは思えないな。
コイツ、ぼけーっとしているように見えるけど、根はとんでもなくしっかりしてるヤツなんスよ。
甘えるのが下手っていうか、人様に迷惑をかけるのを嫌っているっていうか」
entries.maoEnglish:
Arihiko seemed close to Ciel.
Unlike me, who had met her only a handful of times, he spoke to her with easy familiarity.
“By the way, you said you collided with Tohno earlier—what happened?”
“We ran into each other during the break. I wasn’t hurt, but Tohno struck his head.”
“Huh. I can’t imagine Tohno making a blunder like that. He may look half asleep, but underneath he’s incredibly dependable; I guess he’s bad at leaning on people and hates causing anyone trouble.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
It seems Arihiko is close with Senpai.
In contrast with me, who's only met her a few times, he's able to talk to her quite casually.
"By the way, Senpai, you said you ran into Tohno, what happened?"
"Yes, I bumped into Tohno-kun between classes.
I wasn't hurt, but Tohno-kun bumped his head."
"Hmm…… I wouldn't have thought Tohno would do something as clumsy as that.
This guy may look spaced out, but he's actually an unbelievably sharp guy.
He doesn't like to depend on others, and he hates causing trouble for others……"

entries.japanese:
「あ、なんとなくわかります。
ぶつかった時もわたしの心配ばかりしていましたし、さっきも謝ってくれましたし」
「でしょ？
　コイツはそうゆうヤツだからそんなヘマはしないんスよ。
……あ、もしかしてまた貧血でも起こしたのか、おまえ」
　有彦の声は真剣にこっちの体を気遣っている。
「……いや、違うよ。
引っ越しの手続きでさ、事務室まで走ったんだ。
その時にどっかーん、と先輩にぶつかったワケ」
「―――そうか。
まあ、なんにせよおまえの不注意ってコトか。
さすがの遠野も引っ越しでまいってるってワケね」
　納得いった、とばかりに有彦は腕を組んでうなずく。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh, I can see that. When we collided, he only worried about me, and he apologized again just now.”
“Exactly. That’s the kind of guy he is, so he doesn’t make mistakes like that. Wait—did you have another one of your fainting spells?”
Arihiko’s voice was suddenly full of genuine concern.
“…No. I was running to the office with some moving paperwork, and I went crashing into her on the way.”
“―――I see. Either way, it was your fault. Even our Tohno’s feeling the strain of moving, then.”
Arihiko spoke with a smug nod.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah, I also got that impression.
He was only concerned about me when we ran into each other, and he apologized to me just now, too."
"See?
That's the kind of guy he is, so he doesn't make those kind of mistakes.
…… Ah, could it be that your anemia was acting up again?"
Arihiko's voice shows his serious concern for my physical health.
"…… No, it's not that.
I was running to the office to deal with some details for me moving.
That's when I ran into Senpai."
"Really?
Well, I thought you became careless because you're depressed over the move."
Arihiko folds his arms and nods to himself in agreement.

entries.japanese:
――――と。
「遠野くん、転校するんですか！？」
　なんて、先輩がすっとんきょうな発言をしてきた。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――Then.
“Tohno, are you transferring?!”
At that, Ciel blurted out the absurd question.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----And then,
"Tohno-kun, are you changing schools!?"
Senpai exclaims almost hysterically.

entries.japanese:
「先輩、俺は転校なんかしないよ。
ただ今日から住むところが変わるから、住所変更の書類を出してただけなんだって」
「え………っと、つまり、一人暮しをするんですか？」
「それも違う。
自分の家に戻るだけだから。
　坂の上にある仰々しいところでさ、いまいち実感がわかないんだけどね」
「……はあ。
それってもしかして、遠野さんのお屋敷の事ですか？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ciel, I’m not transferring. I’m only changing where I live today, so I had to submit a change-of-address form.”
“Then… are you going to live
alone?” “That’s not it either.
I’m merely returning to my own home. It’s that absurdly grand place on top of the hill,
so the whole thing still doesn’t feel real.” “Could that be the Tohno estate?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I'm not changing schools, Senpai.
I'm just changing my place of residence, so I filed the paperwork for a change-of-address."
"Eh…… So that means you're going to be living alone?"

"No, I'm just going back to my real home.
It's that fancy place on top of the hill.
I still can't quite believe it yet."
"Oh…… Could that possibly be the Tohno-san mansion?"

entries.japanese:
先輩は恐る恐る、遠慮するように聞いてきた。
　街の人達からすれば、坂の上にある遠野の洋館はなにか特別なものとして映っているのだろう。
　こっちだってこの八年間戻っていないけど、記憶の中にある遠野の屋敷はばかみたいに大きかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
Ciel asked timidly, as though afraid of prying.
To the people of this town, the Tohno family’s Western-style house on the hill must have seemed like something apart.
I hadn’t returned for eight years myself, but in my memory the Tohno estate was absurdly large.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Senpai asks with some hesitation.
The western-style house on top of the hill is probably seen as something special to the residents of this town.
I haven't been there for eight years, but even in my memories, the Tohno mansion was ridiculously large.

entries.japanese:
「まあそういうこと。
自分でも場違いだとは思ってるんだけどね、引っ越しちまったものはしょうがないから」
「───ふぅん。
その様子じゃあんまり乗り気じゃなかったのか、おまえ」
「さあ、良くも悪くもないっていうのが本当のところだよ。
自分でもよくわかってないんだ」
「ま、自分の家っていっても八年ぶりなんだろ？
　落ち着かないのもわかるぜ。
しばらくは他人の家みたいに感じるんだろうさ」
「……どうだろうね。
まだ帰ってないからよくはわからないよ。
まあ、俺にはおまえの家っていう避難場所があるから気は楽だけど」
entries.maoEnglish:
“That’s right. I know I’ll be out of place there, but the move is already settled, so there’s no use arguing.”
“───Huh. From the sound of it, you weren’t too excited about going back.”
“Honestly, I feel neither good nor bad about it. I’m not sure what I feel myself.”
“Well, even if it’s your home, you haven’t been there in eight years. No wonder you’re uneasy. It’ll probably feel like somebody else’s house for a while.”
“Maybe. I haven’t gone back yet, so I can’t really say. At least I know I can always escape to your place.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yeah, that's right.
I don't think it's the right place for me either, but it's too late now that I'm done moving."
"Hmm…… You don't seem too happy about it."
"It's not a particularly good or bad thing.
I don't really understand it myself."
"Well, even if it is your house, it's been eight years, right?
I can understand if you're feeling restless.
It'll probably feel like someone else's house for a while."
"I wonder if that's so…… I haven't gone back yet, so I don't know.
Well, I'm a bit relaxed, since I've always got a refuge at your place."

entries.japanese:
「むっ。
おまえね、何かイヤなコトがあるたびにオレん家に泊まりに来るのは感心しねーぞ。
遠野の昼行灯な性格は気に入ってるけどな、その遠慮しすぎる性根は気に食わねえんだ、昔っから！」
　だん、と机を叩く有彦。
「……………」
　なんていうか、実に有彦の言うとおりなんで、こっちとしては反論のしようがない。
「乾くん、遠野くんってそんなに頻繁に乾くんの家に泊まりにくるんですか？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hey. I don’t approve of you staying at my house whenever something unpleasant happens. I like that laid-back, unassuming nature of yours, but I’ve always hated the way you bend over backward not to impose!”
Arihiko struck the table.
“…”
He was entirely right, which left me nothing to say.
“Inui, does Tohno stay at your house that often?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hmph.
Listen, you, I'm not impressed with how you come to stay at my house every time something bad happens.
I like your personality trait of not standing out, but I've hated how you're always too reserved for a long time now!"
Arihiko strikes the table with a bang again.
"……"
Well, everything Arihiko said is true, so there's no way to fight back.
"Inui-kun, does Tohno-kun really stay at your house that often?"

entries.japanese:
「そうッスよ。
遠野のヤロウは両親に遠慮して、長い休みになると家に居づらいってんで逃げてくるんです。
このヤロウ、預けられたってことで有間の家の人たちに遠慮してたんだ。
　で、体よく部屋が空いてるオレのところに転がり込んでくるってワケ。
こいつは外見がいいから姉貴にも気に入られちまってさ、厚かましくも手ぶらで泊まりにくるんだぜ！」
　許せん、と有彦は握りこぶしを震わせる。
「……預けられたって、遠野くんがですか？」
「あっ――――」
　ハッとして自分の口を押さえる有彦。
entries.maoEnglish:
“He sure does. Tohno feels so indebted to his foster parents that he can’t relax at home during long holidays, so he runs away; ever since the Arimas took him in, the bastard’s been walking on eggshells around them. Since I conveniently have a spare room, he comes rolling into my place instead.
Worse, he’s got a pretty face, so my sister adores him. He even has the nerve to show up empty-handed!” Outrageous, Arihiko proclaimed, shaking a clenched
fist.
“The Arimas took you in, Tohno?”
“Ah—”
Arihiko caught himself and covered his mouth.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yeah, he does.
That damn Tohno is too reserved toward his parents and he would come to my place every long vacation.
He's reserved towards them cause they're taking care of him.
That's why he comes over to my place, where we conveniently have an empty room.
Since he looks pretty decent, my sister took a liking to him, and he shamelessly comes to stay with us without paying a cent!"
Arihiko's fist trembles, as if to say 'unforgivable!'
"…… Taking care of Tohno-kun?"
"Ah----"
Arihiko clamps a hand over his mouth.
"…… Sorry.
I should've thought before I spoke."
"It's okay.
You didn't say anything bad."
I continue to eat my chikara udon without looking at Arihiko.

entries.japanese:
「……わりい。
無闇に口にするコトじゃなかった」
「いや、いいよ。
別に悪いことじゃないんだから」
　有彦の顔を見ずに、力うどんを食べながらそう言った。
「そっか。
ま、そーだよな。
アレで文句を言ったらバチが当たるってもんか」
　うん、と納得する有彦。
　こいつのこういう、突き抜けたような楽観性は本当にうらやましい。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Sorry. That wasn’t mine to blurt out.” “It’s fine. It isn’t anything shameful.” Without looking at him, I kept eating my mochi udon.
“Right. Yeah, of course. After all they did for you, you’d be tempting fate if you complained.”
Arihiko nodded, satisfied.
I really envied that irrepressible optimism of his.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Really?
Yeah, you're right.
If you complain about that, you'll be in for some punishment."
Arihiko nods to himself in agreement.
His overwhelming optimism is something I am truly envious of.

entries.japanese:
「遠野くん。
その、前のご家族とはうまくいってなかったんですか……？」
「いや、そんなコトはないっスよ。
こいつ、有間の親御さんとは何の問題もないもんな。
　あ、有間っていうのがこいつが預けられてた家の人達なんだけど、これがすっごくいい人達でさ、オレから見れば幸せな家庭だった。
　だっていうのにこいつは養子にならないかって話も断って、休みになればオレんところに逃げてきやがるんだ。
ったく、ホントに何が不満なんだオマエは」
「不満なんかあるわけないだろ。
よくしてもらってるから、これ以上負担をかけたくないだけじゃないか」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Tohno… did you not get along with the family you lived with?”
“No, not at all—he never had any problems with the Arimas. That’s the family who took him in, by the way, and they’re wonderful people.
From where I stood, it was a happy home.
And yet he turned down their offer to adopt him, then ran to my place every holiday. Seriously, what are you so unhappy about?”
“I’m not unhappy. They’ve done so much for me that I don’t want to burden them any further.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Tohno-kun, um…… did you not get along with your previous family?"
"No, that's not it.
This guy had no problem with the Arimas.
Oh, the Arimas were the family who took care of him.
They're really nice people, and from what I could see, they're a happy family.
Even so, he refused to be their adopted child, and he escaped to my place every vacation.
Sheesh…… just what were you not satisfied with, anyway?"
"There's nothing I wasn't satisfied about.
It's just that I've received so much from them already, I didn't want to be a further burden on them."

entries.japanese:
……先輩はしゅん、と肩をすくめて黙ってしまった。
　どうも、オレの家の事情を聞いたことで申し訳なく思っているみたいだ。
「いいよ、先輩。
つまんない話をきかせて悪かった」
「え、そんなコトないですよ。
わたしのほうこそヘンなコトを聞いてしまって、すみません」
　先輩はむりやりに明るく振る舞おうとする。
　……中学校から友人だった有彦ならいざ知らず、先輩を相手にこんなこみいった話をしても迷惑なだけだろう。
　事実、先輩はとてもいづらそうにそわそわしている。
entries.maoEnglish:
Her shoulders drooped, and she fell silent.
Apparently she felt guilty for asking about my family.
“It’s all right. Sorry we made you listen to such a dreary story.”
“No, not at all. I’m the one who asked something strange—I’m sorry.”
She tried to sound bright.
Arihiko had known me since middle school, but burdening her with such complicated family business could only be awkward.
In fact, she was fidgeting as though deeply uncomfortable.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Senpai drops her shoulders and falls silent.
It looks like she's sorry for asking about my family situation.
"It's okay, Senpai.
Sorry for making you listen to something so boring."
"Eh, not at all.
I'm sorry for asking you something so strange, too."
Senpai forces herself to look cheerful.
The topic might be fine for a long-time friend like Arihiko, but a complex matter like this would only have been troublesome for Senpai.
And to prove my point, Senpai sits there uneasily.

entries.japanese:
「先輩、あのさ―――」
「えっと、ごはんを食べ終わったのでお先に失礼します。
どうも、ごめんなさいでした」
　先輩はペコリ、とおじぎをして席を立っていった。
　テーブルには自分と有彦の二人きりになる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Listen, I—”
“Um, I’ve finished my lunch, so I’ll be going now. I’m very sorry.”
She gave us a small bow, rose, and left.
Arihiko and I were alone at the table.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Listen, Senpai---"
"Um, I've finished eating, so I'll be leaving now.
I'm really sorry."
Senpai lowers her head in a quick bow and leaves her seat.
Only me and Arihiko remain at the table.

entries.japanese:
「……悪い。
せっかく二人で食べてたのに、邪魔しちまったな」
「気にするな。
今のはオレの不注意なんだから仕方がない。
むしろ先輩に悪かったなって思ってる」
　……ぞぞぞ、とうどんをすする有彦。
　先輩と話をしていたせいですっかり冷めてしまっているようだ。
「ま、頃合い的にもちょうどいいしな。
遠野に内緒話があったから、先輩が先に戻ってくれてラッキーだ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Sorry. You two were having lunch together, and I barged in.”
“Forget it. That was my fault, so it couldn’t be helped. I feel worse for her.” Arihiko slurped his udon.
It seemed to have gone completely cold while we talked to Ciel.
“The timing works out, anyway. I had something private to ask you, so I’m lucky she left first.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Sorry.
You were finally able to eat with just the two of you, but I got in the way."
"Don't worry about it.
That was my fault for not paying attention.
I thought it was bad for Senpai, actually." …… *slurp* *slurp* *slurp*
Arihiko slurps away at his udon.
It looks like it's gotten cold while we were talking.
"Well, that was convenient for us, anyway.
I've got something to talk to you about in private, so it was lucky that Senpai left first."

entries.japanese:
「なんだよ、急に深刻になって。
いっとくけどお金ならないぞ。
今日から俺は金欠少年としていきるんだから」
「―――そんなんじゃねえって。
オレが聞きたいのはさ、遠野は実際どうなのかな、と」
「どうって、なにが」
「だから。
おまえ、小学校から有間の家に預けられてたんだろ？
　どんな理由でか知らないが、それから八年も経つんだ。
なんで今になって勘当してた息子を呼び戻すんだろうかな、キミの父親は」
　……そうか。
　こいつはこいつなりに、遠野志貴のことを心配していてくれたらしい。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What is it—why so serious? And if you want money, I haven’t got any. As of today, I begin my new life as an impoverished youth.”
“―――That’s not it. What I want to know is how you’re actually taking all this.”
“Taking what?”
“You’ve lived with the Arimas since elementary school, haven’t you? I don’t know why, but it’s been eight years. Why would your father suddenly summon the son he disowned after all this time?”
…I see.
Apparently, in his own way, Arihiko had been worried about Shiki Tohno.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"What's wrong?
Getting all serious all of a sudden.
I'll tell you now, I don't have any money.
From today onwards, I'm going to be living life as a penniless youth."
"It's not that, damn it.
What I want to know is this; what's really going on with you, Tohno?"
"What do you mean?"
"You've been at the Arimas' since primary school, right?
I don't know why, but it's been eight years already.
Your dad has basically disinherited you.
Why is he calling you back all of a sudden?"
…… I see.
In his own way, he is worried about me.

entries.japanese:
「……いや、別に勘当されてたわけじゃないよ。
なんとなく屋敷から追い出されただけだから、有彦が気に病む程度のことじゃない」
「あのな、遠野くん。
なんとなくで子供を家から追い出すような家庭があったら、それはすでに悲劇ではなく笑い話だ。
オー、イッツパーティージョーク。
しかし寒すぎて笑え、ナイ」
　有彦は大げさに両手を広げて肩をすくめる。
「……まあ、そうかも。
たしかになんとなくで家から追い出されたら、そりゃあ笑うしかないだろうね」
entries.maoEnglish:
“No. I wasn’t disowned; I was just sort of thrown out of the estate, so this isn’t something you need to worry about.”
“Listen, Tohno. If a family throws a child out for no particular reason, that stops being a tragedy and becomes a joke. Oh, it is party joke. But is too cold, so laugh—NO.”
Arihiko spread his hands and shrugged theatrically.
“Maybe. If I were thrown out for no reason, I suppose all I could do is laugh.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"He didn't 'disinherit' me.
He just kicked me out of the house for some reason."
"Tohno-kun, if there ever is a house that kicks their child out of their house 'for some reason', that's not a tragedy, it's a comedy. 'Oh, it's a party joke!' But it's so boring, it's not funny."
Arihiko spreads his arms and shrugs.
"…… Yeah, I guess you're right.
If you get kicked out of the house, all you can really do is laugh."

entries.japanese:
「だろう？
　おまけに二度と敷居は跨ぐなっていう決め台詞付きときた。
世間さまではそーゆーのは勘当というんだぞ。
　今まで聞かなかったけどな、おまえはどうして勘当されたんだ」
「……………」
　……………さあ。
　そんな事、こっちが聞きたいぐらいだ。
「ま、話したくないなら、いい」
　有彦はどんぶりを両手でもって、ぐびぐびと冷めたうどんの汁を飲み干していく。
　休み時間は短い。
　有彦の早食いを見習って、こっちもぐびぐびと力うどんを平らげる事にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Exactly. And they even gave you the grand line about never darkening their doorstep again. The rest of society calls that disowning someone.
I’ve never asked before, but why did they disown you?”
“…”
I had no idea.
I would have liked an answer myself.
“Well, if you don’t want to talk about it, forget it.”
Arihiko raised his bowl in both hands and gulped down the cold udon broth.
Lunch break was short.
Following his example, I hurriedly finished my own mochi udon.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"And then he said some cliche line like, 'Never step foot in this house again!' or something, right?
That's what people would call 'disinheritance.'
Come to think of it, I've never heard why you were disinherited."
"……"
…………… Who knows?
That's something I'd like to know, too.
"Well, if you don't want to talk about it, you don't have to."
Grabbing his bowl with both hands, Arihiko drains his cold udon soup.
Lunchtime is short.
Following Arihiko, I decide to quickly eat my own chikara udon.

entries.japanese:
食堂の席は、もうほとんどが埋まっていた。
　教室でぼんやりとしていたタイムロスのせいで、学食の席はほぼ全滅状態になっている。
「―――空いてる席なんてない、か」
　混雑した学食を見渡す。
　この時間で席なんて空いているはずがないけど、それでも一応テーブルの状態を確認する。
「………あ」
　驚いた、というより呆れた。
　ものの見事に二つといわず三つも四つも席が空いているテーブルがある。
entries.maoEnglish:
Almost every seat in the cafeteria was already taken.
Thanks to the time I had wasted staring into space in the classroom, nearly every seat was gone.
“―――No seats left, then.”
I surveyed the packed cafeteria.
Nothing should have been free at this hour, but I checked the tables anyway.
“Oh.”
It was less surprise than disbelief.
One table had not one or two but three or four seats standing completely empty.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Almost all the seats in the cafeteria are taken.
Because I spaced out in the hallway, empty seats are pretty much non-existent at this point.
"---Aren't there any empty seats?"
I cast my gaze over the crowded cafeteria.
There shouldn't be any spare seats this late, but I decide to check the tables out anyway.

"…… Ah."
I'm surprised…… no, I'm astounded.
There, plain as day, is a table with not two, not even three, but four unoccupied seats.
There are two students sitting at the table, and it seems like one of them noticed me during my efforts to locate a seat.

entries.japanese:
そこに座っている生徒は二人。
　そのうちの一人が、席を探してきょろきょろしている俺に気がついたみたいだ。
「いょぉう、遠野！」
　なんて、ぶんぶんと手を振ってくる生徒は、髪をオレンジ色に染めたクラスメイトだ。
「………………」
　あたま、いたい。
　けど他にあいている席もなし、仕方なく手を振ってくる友人のテーブルへと歩いていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
Two students sat there.
One of them seemed to notice me looking around.
“Heeey, Tohno!”
The student waving both arms was my orange-haired classmate.
“…”
My head hurt.
But there were no other empty seats, so I reluctantly headed for my waving friend’s table.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yo, Tohno!"
The student vigorously waving his hand is my dear classmate with the dyed orange hair.
"……"
My head hurts.
But there isn't anywhere else to sit, so I have no choice but to return the wave and walk towards the table where my friend is sitting.

entries.japanese:
テーブルには有彦と、意外な人が同席していた。
「あれ、シエル先輩」
「あれ、遠野くんですね」
　二人して、間の抜けた指差し確認なんかをしたりする。
entries.maoEnglish:
Arihiko was sharing the table with someone unexpected.
“Oh—Ciel.”
“Oh—it’s Tohno.”
We pointed stupidly at one another, each confirming the other’s identity.
entries.mirrorMoon:
An unexpected person is sitting at the table with him.
"Huh, Ciel-senpai?"
"Ah, if it isn't Tohno-kun."
We point at each other simultaneously.

entries.japanese:
「よう遠野っ―――て、なに？
　先輩、遠野のこと知ってるの？」
「はい、今日も一度会っています。
廊下でだーんとぶつかったんですよね、遠野くん」
「あ……はい、その節は、どうも」
　すみません、と頭をさげる。
「いえいえ、こちらこそぼーっとしていてごめんなさい。
遠野くん、真面目な人なんですね」
「真面目って……そんなことは、ないんですけど」
　先輩は笑顔のままで、満足げに頷く。
　……なんていうか、やっぱり独特の雰囲気をもった先輩だ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hey, Toh—wait, what? You know him?”
“Yes, we’ve already met once today. We went bang into each other in the corridor, didn’t we, Tohno?”
“Ah—yes, sorry about that.”
I bowed my head in apology.
“No, I’m sorry; I was daydreaming. You’re very conscientious, Tohno.”
“Conscientious—I wouldn’t say that—” Still smiling, she nodded with evident satisfaction.
There really was something singular about her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yo, Tohno---hey wait…… Senpai, do you know Tohno?"
"Yes, I've met him once today already.
We bumped into each other with a bang today, didn't we, Tohno-kun?"
"Ah…… yes, sorry about that."
I lower my head in apology.
"Not at all.
I'm also sorry for spacing out like that.
You're a serious person, aren't you, Tohno-kun?"
"Serious……?
No, not really."
Smiling, Senpai gives a satisfied nod.
How should I say this…… Senpai has a unique atmosphere around her.

entries.japanese:
「でも意外です。
遠野くん、乾くんとお知り合いだったんですね。
もしかしてクラスが一緒なんですか？」
「その通り！
　オレと遠野は知り合いも知り合い、一年からクラスは一緒で、かつ中学校時代からの腐れ縁っていう大親友ですよ、オレたちは！」
　だん、とテーブルを叩いて力説する大親友。
　……なんていうか、いつも以上にハッスルしているように見えるのは気のせいか。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Still, what a surprise. I didn’t know you and Inui were acquainted. Are you in the same class?”
“Exactly—acquainted doesn’t begin to cover it. Tohno and I have shared a class since first year, and we’ve been inseparable since middle school—we’re the best of friends!”
My best friend slammed the table to emphasize the point.
Was it my imagination, or was he even more worked up than usual?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"But it's sure surprising that Tohno-kun and Inui-kun know each other.
Could it be that you two are in the same class?"
"That's right!
Me and Tohno are more than casual acquaintances!
We've been in the same class since our first year, and we've been inseparable best friends since middle school!"
My best friend strikes the table with a bang for emphasis.
…… Is it just me, or is he more hyper than usual?

entries.japanese:
「ほら、座りたまえ大親友！
　いつまでもぼけーっとつっ立っているとせっかくの力うどんがのびてしまうじゃあないか。
さっさと座って、オレに断りもなくどうやって先輩と知り合ったのか洗いざらい聞かせてくれ」
　有彦はばんばん、と楽しそうに背中を叩いている。
「…………」
　有彦が想像しているような話なんてないけど、他に席は空いていない。
　騒々しくなる事を覚悟して、有彦の隣に座った。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Come on, sit down, my dearest friend! If you stand there gawping any longer, your precious mochi udon will get soggy. Now sit and tell me every last detail of how you met Ciel without my permission.”
Arihiko cheerfully thumped me on the back.
“…”
There was no story remotely like the one he was imagining, but no other seats were free.
Resigned to the coming uproar, I sat beside him.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Come on, best friend, sit down!
If you just keep standing there vacantly, your chikara udon is going to go stale.
Hurry up and sit down, and let me hear all about how you got to know Senpai."
Arihiko slaps my back cheerfully.
"……"
While I really have no story like Arihiko might be hoping for, there are no other seats available.
Reluctantly, I take a seat next to him.

entries.japanese:
有彦はシエル先輩と親しいみたいだ。
　まだ数回しか会ったコトのない俺に比べて、気軽に先輩と話をしている。
「ところで先輩、さっき遠野とぶつかったとか言ってたけど、なにがあったんスか？」
「はい、休み時間に遠野くんとぶつかってしまったんです。
わたしはケガがなかったんですけど、遠野くんは頭をぶつけてしまいまして」
「ふうん……遠野がそんなヘマやるとは思えないな。
コイツ、ぼけーっとしているように見えるけど、根はとんでもなくしっかりしてるヤツなんスよ。
甘えるのが下手っていうか、人様に迷惑をかけるのを嫌っているっていうか」
entries.maoEnglish:
Arihiko seemed close to Ciel.
Unlike me, who had met her only a handful of times, he spoke to her with easy familiarity.
“By the way, you said you collided with Tohno earlier—what happened?”
“We ran into each other during the break. I wasn’t hurt, but Tohno struck his head.”
“Huh. I can’t imagine Tohno making a blunder like that. He may look half asleep, but underneath he’s incredibly dependable; I guess he’s bad at leaning on people and hates causing anyone trouble.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
It seems Arihiko is close with Senpai.
In contrast with me, who's only met her a few times, he's able to talk to her quite casually.
"By the way, Senpai, you said you ran into Tohno, what happened?"
"Yes, I bumped into Tohno-kun between classes.
I wasn't hurt, but Tohno-kun bumped his head."
"Hmm…… I wouldn't have thought Tohno would do something as clumsy as that.
This guy may look spaced out, but he's actually an unbelievably sharp guy.
He doesn't like to depend on others, and he hates causing trouble for others……"

entries.japanese:
「あ、なんとなくわかります。
ぶつかった時もわたしの心配ばかりしていましたし、さっきも謝ってくれましたし」
「でしょ？
　コイツはそうゆうヤツだからそんなヘマはしないんスよ。
……あ、もしかしてまた貧血でも起こしたのか、おまえ」
　有彦の声は真剣にこっちの体を気遣っている。
「……いや、違うよ。
引っ越しの手続きでさ、事務室まで走ったんだ。
その時にどっかーん、と先輩にぶつかったワケ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh, I can see that. When we collided, he only worried about me, and he apologized again just now.”
“Exactly. That’s the kind of guy he is, so he doesn’t make mistakes like that. Wait—did you have another one of your fainting spells?”
Arihiko’s voice was suddenly full of genuine concern.
“…No. I was running to the office with some moving paperwork, and I went crashing into her on the way.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah, I also got that impression.
He was only concerned about me when we ran into each other, and he apologized to me just now, too."
"See?
That's the kind of guy he is, so he doesn't make those kind of mistakes.
…… Ah, could it be that your anemia was acting up again?"
Arihiko's voice shows his serious concern for my physical health.
"…… No, it's not that.
I was running to the office to deal with some details for me moving.
That's when I ran into Senpai."
"Really?
Well, I thought you became careless because you're depressed over the move."
Arihiko folds his arms and nods to himself in agreement.

entries.japanese:
「―――そうか。
まあ、なんにせよおまえの不注意ってコトか。
さすがの遠野も引っ越しでまいってるってワケね」
　納得いった、とばかりに有彦は腕を組んでうなずく。
―――と。
「遠野くん、転校するんですか！？」
　なんて、先輩がすっとんきょうな発言をしてきた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――I see. Either way, it was your fault. Even our Tohno’s feeling the strain of moving, then.”
Satisfied with his conclusion, Arihiko folded his arms and nodded.
―――And then.
“Tohno, are you transferring?!”
At that, Ciel blurted out the absurd question.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----And then,
"Tohno-kun, are you changing schools!?"
Senpai exclaims almost hysterically.

"I'm not changing schools, Senpai.
I'm just changing my place of residence, so I filed the paperwork for a change-of-address."
"Eh…… So that means you're going to be living alone?"

entries.japanese:
「先輩、俺は転校なんかしないよ。
ただ今日から住むところが変わるから、住所変更の書類を出してただけなんだって」
「え………っと、つまり、一人暮しをするんですか？」
「それも違う。
自分の家に戻るだけだから。
　坂の上にある仰々しいところでさ、いまいち実感がわかないんだけどね」
「……はあ。
それってもしかして、遠野さんのお屋敷の事ですか？」

先輩は恐る恐る、遠慮するように聞いてきた。
　街の人達からすれば、坂の上にある遠野の洋館はなにか特別なものとして映っているのだろう。
　こっちだってこの八年間戻っていないけど、記憶の中にある遠野の屋敷はばかみたいに大きかった。

「まあそういうこと。
自分でも場違いだとは思ってるんだけどね、引っ越しちまったものはしょうがないから」
「───ふぅん。
その様子じゃあんまり乗り気じゃなかったのか、おまえ」
「さあ、良くも悪くもないっていうのが本当のところだよ。
自分でもよくわかってないんだ」
「ま、自分の家っていっても八年ぶりなんだろ？
　落ち着かないのもわかるぜ。
しばらくは他人の家みたいに感じるんだろうさ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ciel, I’m not transferring. I’m only changing where I live today, so I had to submit a change-of-address form.”
“Then… are you going to live
alone?” “That’s not it either.
I’m merely returning to my own home. It’s that absurdly grand place on top of the hill,
so the whole thing still doesn’t feel real.” “Could that be the Tohno estate?”
Ciel asked timidly, as though afraid of prying.
To the people of this town, the Tohno family’s Western-style house on the hill must have seemed like something apart.
I hadn’t returned for eight years myself, but in my memory the Tohno estate was absurdly large.
“That’s right. I know I’ll be out of place there, but the move is already settled, so there’s no use arguing.”
“───Huh. From the sound of it, you weren’t too excited about going back.”
“Honestly, I feel neither good nor bad about it. I’m not sure what I feel myself.”
“Well, even if it’s your home, you haven’t been there in eight years. No wonder you’re uneasy. It’ll probably feel like somebody else’s house for a while.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No, I'm just going back to my real home.
It's that fancy place on top of the hill.
I still can't quite believe it yet."
"Oh…… Could that possibly be the Tohno-san mansion?"

Senpai asks with some hesitation.
The western-style house on top of the hill is probably seen as something special to the residents of this town.
I haven't been there for eight years, but even in my memories, the Tohno mansion was ridiculously large.

"Yeah, that's right.
I don't think it's the right place for me either, but it's too late now that I'm done moving."
"Hmm…… You don't seem too happy about it."
"It's not a particularly good or bad thing.
I don't really understand it myself."
"Well, even if it is your house, it's been eight years, right?
I can understand if you're feeling restless.
It'll probably feel like someone else's house for a while."
"I wonder if that's so…… I haven't gone back yet, so I don't know.
Well, I'm a bit relaxed, since I've always got a refuge at your place."

entries.japanese:
「……どうだろうね。
まだ帰ってないからよくはわからないよ。
まあ、俺にはおまえの家っていう避難場所があるから気は楽だけど」
「むっ。
おまえね、何かイヤなコトがあるたびにオレん家に泊まりに来るのは感心しねーぞ。
遠野の昼行灯な性格は気に入ってるけどな、その遠慮しすぎる性根は気に食わねえんだ、昔っから！」
　だん、と机を叩く有彦。
「……………」
　なんていうか、実に有彦の言うとおりなんで、こっちとしては反論のしようがない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Maybe. I haven’t gone back yet, so I can’t really say. At least I know I can always escape to your place.”
“Hey. I don’t approve of you staying at my house whenever something unpleasant happens. I like that laid-back, unassuming nature of yours, but I’ve always hated the way you bend over backward not to impose!”
Arihiko struck the table.
“…”
He was entirely right, which left me nothing to say.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hmph.
Listen, you, I'm not impressed with how you come to stay at my house every time something bad happens.
I like your personality trait of not standing out, but I've hated how you're always too reserved for a long time now!"
Arihiko strikes the table with a bang again.
"……"
Well, everything Arihiko said is true, so there's no way to fight back.

"Inui-kun, does Tohno-kun really stay at your house that often?"

entries.japanese:
「乾くん、遠野くんってそんなに頻繁に乾くんの家に泊まりにくるんですか？」
「そうッスよ。
遠野のヤロウは両親に遠慮して、長い休みになると家に居づらいってんで逃げてくるんです。
このヤロウ、預けられたってことで有間の家の人たちに遠慮してたんだ。
　で、体よく部屋が空いてるオレのところに転がり込んでくるってワケ。
こいつは外見がいいから姉貴にも気に入られちまってさ、厚かましくも手ぶらで泊まりにくるんだぜ！」
　許せん、と有彦は握りこぶしを震わせる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Inui, does Tohno stay at your house that often?”
“He sure does. Tohno feels so indebted to his foster parents that he can’t relax at home during long holidays, so he runs away; ever since the Arimas took him in, the bastard’s been walking on eggshells around them. Since I conveniently have a spare room, he comes rolling into my place instead.
Worse, he’s got a pretty face, so my sister adores him. He even has the nerve to show up empty-handed!” Outrageous, Arihiko proclaimed, shaking a clenched
fist.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yeah, he does.
That damn Tohno is too reserved toward his parents and he would come to my place every long vacation.
He's reserved towards them cause they're taking care of him.
That's why he comes over to my place, where we conveniently have an empty room.
Since he looks pretty decent, my sister took a liking to him, and he shamelessly comes to stay with us without paying a cent!"
Arihiko's fist trembles, as if to say 'unforgivable!'

entries.japanese:
「……預けられたって、遠野くんがですか？」
「あっ――――」
　ハッとして自分の口を押さえる有彦。
「……わりい。
無闇に口にするコトじゃなかった」
「いや、いいよ。
別に悪いことじゃないんだから」
　有彦の顔を見ずに、力うどんを食べながらそう言った。
「そっか。
ま、そーだよな。
アレで文句を言ったらバチが当たるってもんか」
　うん、と納得する有彦。
　こいつのこういう、突き抜けたような楽観性は本当にうらやましい。
entries.maoEnglish:
“The Arimas took you in, Tohno?”
“Ah—”
Arihiko caught himself and covered his mouth.
“Sorry. That wasn’t mine to blurt out.” “It’s fine. It isn’t anything shameful.” Without looking at him, I kept eating my mochi udon.
“Right. Yeah, of course. After all they did for you, you’d be tempting fate if you complained.”
Arihiko nodded, satisfied.
I really envied that irrepressible optimism of his.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Taking care of Tohno-kun?"
"Ah----"
Arihiko clamps a hand over his mouth.
"…… Sorry.
I should've thought before I spoke."
"It's okay.
You didn't say anything bad."
I continue to eat my chikara udon without looking at Arihiko.

"Really?
Yeah, you're right.
If you complain about that, you'll be in for some punishment."
Arihiko nods to himself in agreement.
His overwhelming optimism is something I am truly envious of.

entries.japanese:
「遠野くん。
その、前のご家族とはうまくいってなかったんですか……？」
「いや、そんなコトはないっスよ。
こいつ、有間の親御さんとは何の問題もないもんな。
　あ、有間っていうのがこいつが預けられてた家の人達なんだけど、これがすっごくいい人達でさ、オレから見れば幸せな家庭だった。
　だっていうのにこいつは養子にならないかって話も断って、休みになればオレんところに逃げてきやがるんだ。
ったく、ホントに何が不満なんだオマエは」
「不満なんかあるわけないだろ。
よくしてもらってるから、これ以上負担をかけたくないだけじゃないか」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Tohno… did you not get along with the family you lived with?”
“No, not at all—he never had any problems with the Arimas. That’s the family who took him in, by the way, and they’re wonderful people.
From where I stood, it was a happy home.
And yet he turned down their offer to adopt him, then ran to my place every holiday. Seriously, what are you so unhappy about?”
“I’m not unhappy. They’ve done so much for me that I don’t want to burden them any further.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Tohno-kun, um…… did you not get along with your previous family?"
"No, that's not it.
This guy had no problem with the Arimas.
Oh, the Arimas were the family who took care of him.
They're really nice people, and from what I could see, they're a happy family.
Even so, he refused to be their adopted child, and he escaped to my place every vacation.
Sheesh…… just what were you not satisfied with, anyway?"
"There's nothing I wasn't satisfied with.
It's just that I've received so much from them already, I didn't want to be a further burden on them."

entries.japanese:
……先輩はしゅん、と肩をすくめて黙ってしまった。
　どうも、オレの家の事情を聞いたことで申し訳なく思っているみたいだ。
「いいよ、先輩。
つまんない話をきかせて悪かった」
「え、そんなコトないですよ。
わたしのほうこそヘンなコトを聞いてしまって、すみません」
　先輩はむりやりに明るく振る舞おうとする。
　……中学校から友人だった有彦ならいざ知らず、先輩を相手にこんなこみいった話をしても迷惑なだけだろう。
　事実、先輩はとても居づらそうにそわそわしている。
entries.maoEnglish:
Her shoulders drooped, and she fell silent.
Apparently she felt guilty for asking about my family.
“It’s all right. Sorry we made you listen to such a dreary story.”
“No, not at all. I’m the one who asked something strange—I’m sorry.”
She tried to sound bright.
Arihiko had known me since middle school, but burdening her with such complicated family business could only be awkward.
In fact, she was fidgeting as though deeply uncomfortable.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Senpai drops her shoulders and falls silent.
It looks like she's sorry for asking about my family situation.
"It's okay, Senpai.
Sorry for making you listen to something so boring."
"Eh, not at all.
I'm sorry for asking you something so strange, too."
Senpai forces herself to look cheerful.
The topic might be fine for a long-time friend like Arihiko, but a complex matter like this would only have been troublesome for Senpai.
And to prove my point, Senpai sits there uneasily.

entries.japanese:
「先輩、あのさ―――」
「えっと、ごはんを食べ終わったのでお先に失礼します。
どうも、ごめんなさいでした」
　先輩はペコリ、とおじぎをして席を立っていった。
　テーブルには自分と有彦の二人きりになる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Listen, I—”
“Um, I’ve finished my lunch, so I’ll be going now. I’m very sorry.”
She gave us a small bow, rose, and left.
Arihiko and I were alone at the table.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Listen, Senpai---"
"Um, I've finished eating, so I'll be leaving now.
I'm really sorry."
Senpai lowers her head in a quick bow and leaves her seat.
Only me and Arihiko remain at the table.

entries.japanese:
「……悪い。
せっかく二人で食べてたのに、邪魔しちまったな」
「気にするな。
いまのはオレの不注意なんだから仕方がない。
むしろ先輩に悪かったなって思ってる」
　……ぞぞぞ、とうどんをすする有彦。
　先輩と話をしていたせいですっかり冷めてしまっているようだ。
「ま、頃合い的にもちょうどいいしな。
遠野に内緒話があったから、先輩が先に戻ってくれてラッキーだ」
「なんだよ、急に深刻になって。
いっとくけどお金ならないぞ。
今日から俺は金欠少年としていきるんだから」
「―――そんなんじゃねえって。
オレが聞きたいのはさ、遠野は実際どうなのかな、と」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Sorry. You two were having lunch together, and I barged in.”
“Forget it. That was my fault, so it couldn’t be helped. I feel worse for her.” Arihiko slurped his udon.
It seemed to have gone completely cold while we talked to Ciel.
“The timing works out, anyway. I had something private to ask you, so I’m lucky she left first.”
“What is it—why so serious? And if you want money, I haven’t got any. As of today, I begin my new life as an impoverished youth.”
“―――That’s not it. What I want to know is how you’re actually taking all this.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Sorry.
You were finally able to eat with just the two of you, but I got in the way."
"Don't worry about it.
That was my fault for not paying attention.
I thought it was bad for Senpai, actually." …… *slurp* *slurp* *slurp*
Arihiko slurps away at his udon.
It looks like it's gotten cold while we were talking.
"Well, that was convenient for us, anyway.
I've got something to talk to you about in private, so it was lucky that Senpai left first."

"What's wrong?
Getting all serious all of a sudden.
I'll tell you now, I don't have any money.
From today onwards, I'm going to be living life as a penniless youth."
"It's not that, damn it.
What I want to know is this; what's really going on with you, Tohno?"
"What do you mean?"

entries.japanese:
「どうって、なにが」
「だから。
おまえ、小学校から有間の家に預けられてたんだろ？
　どんな理由でか知らないが、それから八年も経つんだ。
なんで今になって勘当してた息子を呼び戻すんだろうかな、キミの父親は」
　……そうか。
　こいつはこいつなりに、遠野志貴のことを心配していてくれたらしい。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Taking what?”
“You’ve lived with the Arimas since elementary school, haven’t you? I don’t know why, but it’s been eight years. Why would your father suddenly summon the son he disowned after all this time?”
…I see.
Apparently, in his own way, Arihiko had been worried about Shiki Tohno.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"You've been at the Arimas' since primary school, right?
I don't know why, but it's been eight years already.
Your dad has basically disinherited you.
Why is he calling you back all of a sudden?"
…… I see.
In his own way, he is worried about me.

entries.japanese:
「……いや、別に勘当されてたわけじゃないよ。
なんとなく屋敷から追い出されただけだから、有彦が気に病む程度のことじゃない」
「あのな、遠野くん。
なんとなくで子供を家から追い出すような家庭があったら、それはすでに悲劇ではなく笑い話だ。
オー、イッツパーティージョーク。
しかし寒すぎて笑え、ナイ」
　有彦は大げさに両手を広げて肩をすくめる。
「……まあ、そうかも。
たしかになんとなくで家から追い出されたら、そりゃあ笑うしかないだろうね」
entries.maoEnglish:
“No. I wasn’t disowned; I was just sort of thrown out of the estate, so this isn’t something you need to worry about.”
“Listen, Tohno. If a family throws a child out for no particular reason, that stops being a tragedy and becomes a joke. Oh, it is party joke. But is too cold, so laugh—NO.”
Arihiko spread his hands and shrugged theatrically.
“Maybe. If I were thrown out for no reason, I suppose all I could do is laugh.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"He didn't 'disinherit' me.
He just kicked me out of the house for some reason."
"Tohno-kun, if there ever is a house that kicks their child out of their house 'for some reason', that's not a tragedy, it's a comedy. 'Oh, it's a party joke!' But it's so boring, it's not funny."
Arihiko spreads his arms and shrugs.
"…… Yeah, I guess you're right.
If you get kicked out of the house, all you can really do is laugh."

entries.japanese:
「だろう？
　おまけに二度と敷居は跨ぐなっていう決め台詞付きときた。
世間さまではそーゆーのは勘当というんだぞ。
　今まで聞かなかったけどな、おまえはどうして勘当されたんだ」
「……………」
　……………さあ。
　そんな事、こっちが聞きたいぐらいだ。
「ま、話したくないなら、いい」
　有彦はどんぶりを両手でもって、ぐびぐびと冷めたうどんの汁を飲み干していく。
　休み時間は短い。
　有彦の早食いを見習って、こっちもぐびぐびと力うどんを平らげる事にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Exactly. And they even gave you the grand line about never darkening their doorstep again. The rest of society calls that disowning someone.
I’ve never asked before, but why did they disown you?”
“…”
I had no idea.
I would have liked an answer myself.
“Well, if you don’t want to talk about it, forget it.”
Arihiko raised his bowl in both hands and gulped down the cold udon broth.
Lunch break was short.
Following his example, I hurriedly finished my own mochi udon.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"And then he said some cliche line like, 'Never step foot in this house again!' or something, right?
That's what people would call 'disinheritance.'
Come to think of it, I've never heard why you were disinherited."
"……"
…………… Who knows?
That's something I'd like to know, too.
"Well, if you don't want to talk about it, you don't have to."
Grabbing his bowl with both hands, Arihiko drains his cold udon soup.
Lunchtime is short.
Following Arihiko, I decide to quickly eat my own chikara udon.

entries.japanese:
昼休みになって、教室は騒々と活性化する。
　食堂に向かって飛び出していく男子、机をくっつけてテーブルを作る女子のグループ、弁当を手にしてゆったりと教室を出ていく生徒。
　そんな光景を眺めながら、自分の机に購買で買ってきた三角パンと牛乳を置く。
「ったく、相変わらず小食だな遠野は」
　……目の前にこの男がいるのは、もはや日常なのでいまさら文句を言っても始まらない。
entries.maoEnglish:
At lunchtime, the classroom came noisily to life.
Boys raced for the cafeteria; groups of girls pushed their desks together into tables; students with boxed lunches drifted leisurely out of the room.
Watching it all, I set a triangular bun and a carton of milk from the school store on my desk.
“Honestly, Tohno, you still eat like a bird.”
Arihiko’s presence opposite me had become so routine that there was no point complaining anymore.
entries.mirrorMoon:
It's lunchtime and the classroom starts to liven up.
Some guys are dashing off towards the cafeteria, a group of girls are rearranging desks to form a table, and some students are calmly leaving the classroom, boxed lunches in hand.
I watch them while I set down the milk and bread I bought.
"Sheesh, not much of an appetite as usual, huh, Tohno?"
This guy in front of me being here is already a part of my daily routine, and I'm not about to start complaining now.

entries.japanese:
「しっかしさあ、大の男が二人きりで顔合わせて昼飯っていうのもナンだよな。
食事に華がないのはどうかと思うんよ、オレ」
「そう。
華がないならあっちのグループに入れてもらえば？
　別に止めないよ、俺は」
「ばかもの、華っていうのは可憐なのが一輪咲いているからいいんじゃねえか。
ああゆうふうに徒党をくんでるのは駄目だね。
美しくないどころかありふれて毒に見える」
　……女子のグループに聞かれていたら石でも投げられかねない発言をする有彦。
　幸い、今のところコイツの毒舌がクラスの女子に聞かれたコトはない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Still, there’s something bleak about two grown men sitting face-to-face over lunch. This table needs a little feminine grace.”
“Then ask that group to let you join them. I won’t stop you.” “Fool.
Grace means one delicate flower blooming alone. A whole huddle like that is no good. It’s not beautiful; it’s commonplace enough to look poisonous.”
Arihiko made a remark that might have gotten him stoned if the girls had heard.
Fortunately, none of the girls in class had heard his venomous remarks yet.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"But man, what's up with us, just the two of us eating lunch together?
What kind of meal goes unaccompanied by a beautiful blossom?"
"If you don't have any 'blossoms', why don't you join that group over there?
I'm not going to stop you."
"Idiot!
When I say 'blossom', I mean a single, beautiful blossom.
Those girls making a group aren't good.
They're poisonous, rather than being beautiful."
…… Arihiko's comment would've probably earned him some rocks thrown in his direction if the group of girls had heard him.
Luckily, the girls in our class didn't hear his poisonous words.

entries.japanese:
「……ひどい言いようだね、有彦。
おまえは前からひどいヤツだったけど、最近特にひどくなってないか？
　ひどいというより外道いって感じ」
「仕方ないだろ。
実際に美しい華が学校にいるんだから、鑑識眼も厳しくなるってもんだ」
「……はあ。
美しい華って、誰さ」
「それは秘密ということで。
あんまりライヴァルを増やしたくないんでね」
　ふふふ、と野心に満ちた笑みをこぼす有彦。
　こいつの剥き出しの感情表現は、自分にはないものでちょっと感心したりする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“That’s vicious, Arihiko. You’ve always been awful, but haven’t you gotten even worse lately? You’ve crossed from awful into godawful.”
“Can’t be helped. There’s a genuinely beautiful flower at this school, so naturally my standards have risen.”
“…Who is this beautiful flower?”
“That’s a secret. I’d rather not create more rivals.”
Arihiko chuckled, his smile nakedly ambitious.
I almost admired how openly he wore the emotions I could never express.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… That's pretty harsh, Arihiko.
I know you were a bad guy before, but haven't you been getting worse lately?
You're surpassing merely 'bad' and getting into 'deviant'."
"I can't help it, can I?
When there's a truly beautiful blossom at our school, my discerning eye grows more critical."
"Hah…… So, who is this beautiful 'blossom'?"
"That's a secret.
I don't want more competition, now do I?"
Arihiko laughs with an ambitious smile spilling over his face.
As it is something I don't have, I'm a little impressed by his ability to express himself so frankly.

entries.japanese:
――――と。
　教室のドアから、ついさっき出会った人がこっちに向かってやってきた。
「…………あ」
　お弁当片手にやってくるその姿は、見間違えるハズもなく―――
「こんにちは遠野くん。
お邪魔しにきちゃいましたけど、いいですか？」
「え―――あ、もちろんいいですけど―――」
　……シエル先輩は笑顔のまま、当たり前のように椅子を持ってきて座ってしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――And then.
Someone I had met only a little while ago came through the classroom door and headed toward us.
“Oh.”
Carrying a boxed lunch, the approaching figure was impossible to mistake—
“Hello, Tohno. I came to join you for lunch—is that all right?”
“Wh—oh, of course, but—”
Still smiling, Ciel fetched a chair and sat down as if it were the most natural thing in the world.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----And then.
The person I just met comes in from the classroom door.
"…… Ah."
With a boxed lunch in one hand, there is no way I could mistake her---
"Hello, Tohno-kun.
Mind if I interrupt?"
"Eh---Ah, it's fine, of course---"
Smiling, Ciel-senpai brings over a chair and sits down naturally.

entries.japanese:
「あの……先輩、やっぱりケガしてたんですか？」
「いいえ、ケガなんかしてませんけど？」
　笑顔でそんな返答されても、困る。
「わたし、遠野くんにお昼休みにおいでって言われましたから、こないとまずいかなって」
「う……確かにそうは言ったけど」
　……俺としては、もしケガでもしてたら責任をとるから来てくれって意味だった筈だ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ciel, were you hurt after all?”
“No, I wasn’t hurt at all?”
That answer, delivered with a smile, left me at a loss.
“You told me to come by at lunch, so I thought I ought to.”
“Well—I did say that.”
What I had meant was that she should come if she discovered an injury, so I could take responsibility.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Um…… Senpai, are you hurt?"
"No, I'm not hurt at all."
Even her smiling reply troubles me.
"You said to come here at lunchtime, so I thought it would be rude if I did not."
"Uh…… It's true that I said that, but……"
What I intended to say was that she could come and I would take responsibility if she ended up being hurt.

entries.japanese:
「せ、せ、先輩っっっっつ！」
　ダン！
　と音をたてて立ちあがる有彦。
「あ、乾くん。
あれ、もしかして遠野くんとお知り合いだったんですか？」
「ええ、知り合いも知り合いッスよ！
　遠野とはガキの頃からの友人ですから！
　な、遠野！
　オレたちゃあ、むしろマブと呼び合ってもおかしくない友情ぶりだよな！」
「―――――――」
　ぐぐっ、と握りこぶしをして力説する有彦。
　そこには同意の言葉も反論の言葉も差し入れる隙間がない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“C-C-Ciel!”
Bang! Arihiko shot to his feet.
“Oh, Inui. Are you and Tohno acquainted?”
“Acquainted? We’ve been friends since we were kids! Right, Tohno? Our bond is so deep we might as well call each other blood brothers!”
“―――――――”
Arihiko clenched his fist and proclaimed our friendship.
He left no opening for either agreement or protest.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"S-s-senpaiiii!"
Arihiko slams the table with a bang as he stands up.
"Ah, Inui-kun.
Could it be that you and Tohno-kun are acquainted?"
"Yeah, we're more than casual acquaintances!
Tohno and I have been friends since we were kids!
Right, Tohno?
You could even say we were best friends!"
"--------"
Arihiko makes a tight fist for emphasis.
There's no room for agreement or disagreement.

entries.japanese:
「へえ、そうだったんですか。
遠野くんと乾くんが友人同士なんて、偶然ってあるんですね」
「そうッスね！
　まったく、このヤロウは大人しい顔してやがって、いつのまに先輩と仲良くなってたんだろうなー、とか純粋に疑問に思いますよオレは！」
　ははは、と先輩に笑いかけながら、ぎろりと俺を睨みつけてくる有彦。
　こういうのも八面六臂の大活躍って言うのかな、とぼんやりと思ってみる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Really? What a coincidence that you and Inui are friends.”
