Somewhere in her voice was a hint of wistfulness.
Perhaps it's because of the red light from the sunset, but somehow, Yumizuka looks lonely.
"…… What do you mean?
You can talk to me anytime."
"No, I can't.
Inui-kun is always around you, and besides… I can't become someone like you, Tohno-kun."
With that reserved answer, Yumizuka draws away from me.

entries.japanese:
「それじゃあ、わたしの家はこっちだから。
また明日、学校で会おうね」
　ばいばい、と笑顔で手をふって弓塚は別の道へ歩いていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“My house is this way, so I’ll leave you here. I’ll see you at school tomorrow.”
Yumizuka waved goodbye with a smile and set off down another road.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Well, my house is this way, so I'll see you at school tomorrow."
"Bye-bye!" Smiling, Yumizuka waves her hand and begins walking down another street.

entries.japanese:
いつもとは違う帰り道を歩く。
　見知らぬ道を通り抜けて、段々と遠野の屋敷へ近付いていく。
　まわりの風景は、知らない風景ではなかった。
　少なくとも自分は八年前───九歳まで遠野の屋敷で暮らしていたから、屋敷へ帰る道は初めてというわけでもないのだ。
　……少しだけ気持ちは複雑だ。
　この帰り道は懐かしくて、新鮮でもある。
　さっきまで遠野の家に戻るのは気が進まなかったっていうのに、今はそれほどイヤでもなくなっている。
entries.maoEnglish:
I followed a different road home than usual.
Unknown streets carried me steadily closer to the Tohno estate.
Yet the scenery around them was not entirely unfamiliar.
I had lived at the estate until I was nine, eight years ago, so this was not truly my first journey home.
My feelings were complicated.
The road seemed nostalgic and new at once.
Only a little while ago, I had dreaded returning to the Tohno home, but now the prospect no longer seemed so unpleasant.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I walk along a different path than the one I usually take.
Passing through unfamiliar streets, I slowly approach the Tohno mansion.
The surroundings are not completely unfamiliar.
After all, I had lived here until I was nine years old---eight years ago.
This is not the first time I have taken this path back to the mansion.
…… My feelings are a little complex.
The path home is nostalgic, yet fresh.
Up until just now, I had not looked forward to returning to the Tohno household.
Now, it doesn't seem so bad.

entries.japanese:
……遠野志貴が九歳まで暮らしていた家。
　そこにあるのは日本じゃ場違いな洋館で、今は妹の秋葉が残っているという話だ。
　俺を嫌っていた父親───遠野家の当主である遠野槙久は、先日他界したという。
entries.maoEnglish:
The house where Shiki Tohno had lived until the age of nine.
An absurdly out-of-place Western house stood there, and I had been told my younger sister Akiha still lived there.
My father, who had hated me───the head of the Tohno family, Makihisa Tohno───was said to have died only recently.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… The house I lived in until I was nine years old.
Right now, my sister Akiha is in that utterly un-Japanese western-style mansion.
Tohno Makihisa--My old man who hated me, and the master of the Tohno household, died a few days ago.

entries.japanese:
母親は秋葉が生まれた時に病死してしまっていたから、遠野の人間は自分と、妹である秋葉の二人きりになってしまった。
　本来なら長男である自分───遠野志貴が遠野家の跡取りになるのだろうけれど、自分にはそんな権利はない。
entries.maoEnglish:
Our mother had died of illness when Akiha was born, so my sister and I were now the only Tohnos left.
Ordinarily, as the eldest son, I───Shiki Tohno───would have inherited the family, but I no longer had that right.
entries.mirrorMoon:
My mother died from illness after Akiha was born, so the Tohnos had dwindled down to me and my sister.
Being the eldest son, you would think I would stand to become the Tohno heir… but I have no such privilege.

entries.japanese:
遠野家の跡取りになる、という事はがんじがらめの教育を受けるという事だ。
　それがイヤで自由に暮らしていて、父親から何度小言を言われたかわからない。
　そんな折、俺は事故に巻き込まれて病弱な体になってしまい、父親はこれ幸いにと俺を切り捨てた。
　父親曰く『たとえ長男であろうと、いつ死ぬかわからない者を後継者にはできん』とかなんとか。
　あいにく父親の予想を裏切って回復してしまったけれど、その頃には遠野家の跡取りは妹の秋葉に決められていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
Becoming the Tohno heir meant submitting to an education that bound you hand and foot.
I hated that and lived as freely as I could, earning more lectures from my father than I could count.
Then I was caught in the accident and left sickly, and my father seized the opportunity to cast me aside. His explanation was something like, “Eldest son or not, I cannot make an heir of someone who might die at any moment.”
Unfortunately for him, I recovered, but by then my sister Akiha had been chosen to inherit the Tohno family.
entries.mirrorMoon:
To become the Tohno heir means being bound by a strict upbringing.
I have lost count of the number of times my father scolded me over my dislike of not being able to live freely.
That was when I got involved in that accident, and my body became weakened… My father saw it as a good opportunity to get rid of me.
His reasoning was something along the lines of "someone who could die any moment can't become the heir, even if he is the eldest son".
Sadly for my father, I betrayed his expectations by making a recovery, but my sister Akiha was already deemed to be the heir to the Tohno household.

entries.japanese:
それまで遠野の娘に相応しいように、と厳格に育てられていた秋葉は、それからよけい厳しく育てられたらしい。
　昔───事故に巻き込まれるまでは一緒に屋敷の庭で遊んだ秋葉とは、あれからまったく会っていない。
entries.maoEnglish:
Akiha had already been raised under strict discipline to make her a proper daughter of the Tohno family; after that, I heard, her upbringing became harsher still.
Long ago───before the accident───we had played together in the estate gardens, but I had not seen her once in the eight years since.
entries.mirrorMoon:
And so I've heard that Akiha, who was already being raised harshly in order to become a proper daughter of the Tohno household, received an even harsher upbringing since then.
That was a long time ago--I played together with Akiha in the mansion back before the accident.
After that, I never saw her again.

entries.japanese:
……まったく会っていないっていえば、それは秋葉だけの話じゃない。
　なにぶん八年前の事だからよく覚えていないけど、屋敷には同い年ぐらいの子供たちがいたはずだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
Akiha wasn’t the only person I had not seen at all.
My memory was vague after eight years, but there had been other children around my age living at the estate.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Akiha isn't the only person I haven't seen since then.
I can't remember all the details because it's been eight years, but there were other children at the mansion around the same age as me.

entries.japanese:
名前までは思い出せないけど、たしか双子の女の子だった。
　身寄りがなくて、使用人として働くことを前提に引き取った、と親父は話していた。
「……おかしいな。
子供のころは三人でよく遊んだのに、名前が思い出せないなんて」
　目を閉じて思い返す。
entries.maoEnglish:
I couldn’t remember their names, but I thought they were twin girls.
Father had said they had no family and had been taken in on the understanding that they would work as servants.
“How strange. We played together constantly, yet I can’t remember their names.”
I closed my eyes and searched my memory.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I don't remember their names, but there were two girls who were twins.
Father has once said that they didn't have any relatives, so he took them to work as servants.
"…… That's weird.
We played together so often when we were small, but I can't remember their names."
I close my eyes and cast my mind back.

entries.japanese:
たしかに思い出せる。
　いつも明るくて、見ているだけでこっちまで元気になってくるような女の子だった。
　屈託のない性格で、屋敷のみんなから可愛がられていた女の子。
　歳が近いっていう事もあって、俺とこの子はすごく気が合って、毎日のように庭を走りまわっていた。
『志貴ちゃん、いっしょにあそぼ』
　なんて言って、部屋に閉じこもっていた自分を外に連れ出してくれたのを、覚えている。
entries.maoEnglish:
Yes, I could remember one of them clearly.
She was always cheerful; simply looking at her filled me with energy.
Everyone at the estate adored her for her bright, untroubled nature.
We were close in age and got along wonderfully, racing through the gardens together almost every day.
‘Shiki, come play with me’
she would say, drawing me outside whenever I shut myself in my room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I should be able to remember.
She was a girl who was always cheerful… so cheerful that you would become cheerful just by looking at her.
A girl with a carefree personality who was loved by everyone at the mansion.
Because she was close to my age, I got along very well with her, and it seemed like every day we would run around the garden together.
"Let's play together, Shiki-chan."
She would say, and I could remember her taking me out of my room after I secluded myself inside.

entries.japanese:
彼女はよく笑って、内気だった秋葉の手をとって俺たちと遊ばせようとしていた。
　もしかしすると、実際は俺たちより年上だったのかもしれない。
　あの子は俺たちや秋葉が遊ぶように手を取らせる半面、いざ俺たちが遊びだすと少し離れて俺たちの様子を見守っていてくれた。
　秋葉の教育係だった厳しい執事も仕方なさそうに『―――が一緒ならかまいません』なんて言って、秋葉を外に出してくれたことがある。
entries.maoEnglish:
She laughed often and would take shy little Akiha by the hand to bring her into our games.
Perhaps she had actually been older than the rest of us.
She would gather us together and make sure Akiha joined in, but once we began playing, she stepped back a little and watched over us.
Even the stern steward responsible for Akiha’s education once relented and said, ‘As long as ――― is with you, I suppose it is all right,’ before allowing Akiha outside.
entries.mirrorMoon:
She would often laugh and take shy Akiha's hand, trying to make her play with us.
Maybe she was older than the both of us.
She would guide me and Akiha to play together, but once we started playing, she would just watch over us.
Even Akiha's tutor, the harsh butler, would say "I don't mind, as long as ****** is with you guys", and let Akiha out to play, as if there was no helping it.

entries.japanese: そんな彼女とは対照的だったのが、もう一人の女の子だった。
entries.maoEnglish: The other girl could not have been more different.
entries.mirrorMoon: In contrast to that girl was the other one.

entries.japanese:
屋敷の二階。
　俺たちが中庭で遊んでいる時、屋敷のほうに振り返るときまって俺たちを見下ろしている少女の姿があった。
entries.maoEnglish:
The second floor of the estate.
Whenever we played in the courtyard and I glanced back at the house, a girl was invariably standing there, looking down at us.
entries.mirrorMoon:
On the second floor.
While we played in the garden, there was always a girl looking down at us every time I turned to look at the mansion.

entries.japanese:
あの明るい女の子と双子である少女は、けれどいつも無表情で俺たちを眺めていた。
　少女は、決して屋敷から外に出ようとはしなかった。
　ただ冷たい目をして、ずっと俺たちのことを眺めているだけ。
entries.maoEnglish:
She was the cheerful girl’s twin, yet she always watched us without expression.
She never once tried to leave the estate.
She merely stood there, gazing down at us with cold eyes.
entries.mirrorMoon:
She was the twin of that cheerful girl, but she would always gaze at us expressionlessly.
That girl would never try to leave the house.
All she would do was watch us with those cold eyes.

entries.japanese:
―――結局。
　その少女とは、最後に少しだけ言葉を交わしただけだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――In the end.
I exchanged only a few words with that girl, just before I left.
entries.mirrorMoon: ---Well, in the end, I only ended up talking a little with her.

entries.japanese:
「あの子たち、今も屋敷にいるのかな……」
　そんな事を思いだしつつ、鞄から白いリボンを取り出す。
　古びた白いリボン。
　最後に、彼女たちから渡されたもの。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I wonder if those girls are still at the estate…”
As the memories returned, I took a white ribbon from my bag.
An old white ribbon.
Something the girls had given me at the very end.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I wonder if those girls are still at the mansion…"
While I think about that, I take a white ribbon out of my bag.
An old white ribbon that the girls gave me at the very end.

entries.japanese:
―――八年前。
　事故に巻きこまれた後、遠野の屋敷から有間の家に預けられる事になった日。
　屋敷を出ようとした直前、何を思ったのか女の子はこのリボンを渡してくれた。
　……貸してあげるから、返してね。
　たしかそんなふうな事を言って、女の子は走り去っていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Eight years ago.
The day after the accident when I was sent from the Tohno estate to the Arimas.
Just before I left, for some reason, one of the girls handed me this ribbon.
I’ll lend it to you, so make sure you give it back.
She had said something like that, then run away.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Eight years ago.
After I was involved in the accident.
The day I was entrusted to the Arima family.
Right before I was to leave the mansion, the girl gave me this for some reason.
…… I'm just lending it to you, so be sure to return it.
Saying something along those lines, she ran off.

entries.japanese:
その後、俺はすぐに使用人に見付かって、屋敷の玄関まで連れていかれた。
　あとは誰の見送りもなく、有間のおばさんに手を引かれて、あのだだっ広い屋敷の正門をくぐり抜けた。
　それが八年前、遠野の屋敷を後にする時の最後の記憶。
entries.maoEnglish:
A servant found me soon afterward and took me to the entrance hall, with no one else there to see me off.
My aunt from the Arima family took me by the hand, and together we passed through the gates of that immense estate.
That was my final memory of leaving the Tohno estate eight years ago.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Afterwards, I was quickly found by one of the servants and taken to the front entrance.
With no one to see me off, I walked out of the gates of that giant mansion while the Arima lady held my hand.
It was my last memory of when I left the Tohno mansion, eight years ago.

entries.japanese:
「……………はあ」
　ため息をついて、リボンを鞄の中にしまう。
「けど、八年も前の話だもんなあ……」
　あの女の子がまだ屋敷にいるのかどうかも分からなければ、名前さえ覚えていない。
　あまつさえ、どっちの子がリボンを渡してくれたのかさえ定かじゃない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Whew.”
I sighed and returned the ribbon to my bag.
“But that was eight years ago.”
I didn’t know whether the girl was still at the estate or even remember her name.
Worse, I was no longer certain which of the twins had given me the ribbon.
entries.mirrorMoon:
*sigh*
I put the ribbon back in my bag.
"But it's been eight years, after all…"
Not only do I not know if they are still at the mansion, I can't even remember their names.
To make things worse, I can't even remember which girl gave me the ribbon.

entries.japanese:
「……別に、そう大した約束じゃないからどうでもいいんだけど」
　けど、覚えているかぎりは守りたい。
　こうして屋敷に戻ることを承諾したのは秋葉が一人きりで屋敷にいるからだ。
　八年間もアイツを放っておいて、全ての責任をあいつに押しつけて勝手気侭に暮らしていた自分に負い目があるから屋敷に戻る。
　……そのついでというワケじゃないけど。
　まだ屋敷にあの子が残っているのなら、八年前の約束をキチンとはたしてあげたかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“It wasn’t an important promise, so I suppose it hardly matters.”
Still, as long as I remembered it, I wanted to keep it.
I had agreed to return because Akiha was alone at the estate.
I had abandoned her for eight years, leaving every responsibility on her shoulders while I lived however I pleased; the guilt of that was what called me back to the estate.
Returning the ribbon was not exactly an afterthought.
If that girl was still at the estate, I wanted to keep the promise I had made eight years ago.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Still, it's not like it was some important promise or anything."
But I want to keep the promise, as long as I still remember it.
I agreed to return to the mansion because Akiha is now there all by herself.
I left her there for eight years, pushing all responsibility onto her while I selfishly lived freely.
I am going back because I feel guilty for what I did to her.
…… I didn't exactly plan to use this as an opportunity to do so, but if that girl is still at the mansion, I want to properly fulfill the promise from eight years ago.

entries.japanese:
有間の家に預けられた当初、秋葉は何度か訪ねにきてくれたらしい。
　あいにくとこっちは病院通いの毎日で会う事もできず、秋葉が全寮制のお嬢様学校に進学してからはまったく連絡をとっていなかった。
　自分は秋葉とは違い、本家から外れた人間だ。
　だからこうして自由気ままな生活を送れている。
　高校もあくまで平均的な進学校で、ここ八年ばかり妹との接点は皆無といってよかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
When I first went to live with the Arimas, Akiha apparently came to see me several times.
Unfortunately, I spent nearly every day at the hospital and never managed to see her; after she entered an exclusive girls’ boarding school, we lost contact altogether.
Unlike Akiha, I had been cast out of the main Tohno family.
That was why I could live as I pleased. I attended an ordinary college-preparatory high school, and for the past eight years, my sister and I had shared virtually nothing.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Apparently, Akiha tried to visit me a few times when I first was entrusted to the Arimas.
Unfortunately, we were never able to meet because I had to go to the hospital every day.
We completely lost contact after Akiha went to a boarding school.
Unlike Akiha, I am isolated from the main family.
That's why I can live freely like this.
My high school is just an average high school and our chance of contact was pretty much zero.

entries.japanese:
父親が死んで、俺は屋敷に戻ってこいと連絡を受けた。
　はっきりいって、いまさら遠野の家に戻るつもりなんて全然なかったんだ。
　ただ、遠野の屋敷には秋葉がいる。
　子供の頃。
　秋葉は大人しくて、いつも何かを我慢しているように怯えていて、トコトコと足音をたてて俺の後についてきた。
　長い黒髪と豪華な洋服のせいか、秋葉は本当にフランス人形のように儚げな少女だったっけ。
entries.maoEnglish:
After Father died, word came that I was to return to the estate.
Frankly, I had no intention of going back to the Tohno family after all this time.
But Akiha was there.
When we were children.
Akiha was quiet and timid, forever as though she were holding something back; she would patter along behind me wherever I went.
Perhaps it was the long black hair and elaborate Western dresses, but she had seemed as fragile as a porcelain doll.
entries.mirrorMoon:
My old man died and I received word telling me to come back.
To be blunt, I had no intention whatsoever of returning to the Tohno house.
But Akiha is at that house.

When we were children…
Akiha was an obedient child, always looking frightened, as if she were constantly enduring something.
She would always follow close behind, her footsteps pattering behind me.
She was frail, and her long black hair and fancy western clothes made her resemble a French doll.

entries.japanese: あの広い館で父親をなくして一人きりの秋葉が心配だったし、なにより────全ての責任をあいつに押しつけて勝手気侭に暮らしていた自分に負い目もある。
entries.maoEnglish: I worried about Akiha, left alone in that vast estate after losing her father, and more than anything, I felt guilty for saddling her with every responsibility while I lived however I pleased.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I am worried about her living all alone in that big mansion, with the old man gone.
But more than anything----I feel guilty, after pushing all the Tohno family responsibilities on her and selfishly living a free life by myself.

entries.japanese:
今回の話を了承して屋敷に戻る事にしたのは、そんな秋葉に対する謝罪の意味もあったのかもしれない。
　遠野の屋敷は不必要なまでに大きい。
　鉄柵で囲まれた敷地の広さは異常とさえいっていい。
なにしろ小学校ぐらいならグラウンドごと中に入ってしまうぐらいなんだから。
entries.maoEnglish:
Perhaps agreeing to return was, in its own way, an apology to her.
The Tohno estate is absurdly large.
Even the grounds enclosed by its iron fence are beyond reason. An entire elementary school, playing field and all, could fit inside.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Perhaps my acceptance to return to the mansion is like my apology to Akiha.
The Tohno mansion is unnecessarily big.
Surrounded by iron railings, you could say the entire lot is abnormally expansive, being so large that a whole elementary school could fit inside.

entries.japanese:
木々に囲まれた庭は、すでに庭というより森に近い。
その森の中心に洋館があり、離れにはまだいくつかの屋敷がある。
　子供のころは何も感じなかったけれど、八年間ほど一般家庭で暮らしてきた自分にとって、この大きさはすでに犯罪じみている。
entries.maoEnglish:
The tree-choked garden is less a garden than a forest. The Western-style main house stands at its heart, with several smaller residences scattered beyond it.
I had thought nothing of the place as a child, but after eight years in an ordinary home, its sheer size now seemed almost criminal.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The garden, surrounded by trees, is more like a forest.
The mansion is at the heart of that forest, and there are a few other buildings separated from it.
I didn't think anything of it when I was a child, but now that I have lived in an ordinary household for eight years, the excessive size feels almost criminal.

entries.japanese:
門に鍵はかかっていない。
　力任せに押しあけて、屋敷の玄関へと向かっていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
The gate was unlocked.
I heaved it open and headed for the estate's front entrance.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The gates aren't locked.
I push them open, and head towards the mansion doors.

entries.japanese:
屋敷の玄関は重苦しくそびえ、訪れる者を威圧している。
　鉄でできた両開きの扉の横には、不釣り合いな呼び鈴があった。
entries.maoEnglish:
The entrance loomed above me, ponderous and forbidding.
Beside the iron double doors was a doorbell that looked almost comically out of place.
entries.mirrorMoon:
They tower oppressively, bearing down on any visitors.
Beside the iron double doors is an unmatching doorbell.

entries.japanese:
「…………よし」
　緊張を振り払って呼び鈴を押す。
　ぴんぽーん、なんていう親しみのある音はしない。
　重苦しい静寂が続くこと数秒。
　扉の奥でぱたぱた、という慌ただしい人の気配がした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“All right.”
Shaking off my nerves, I pressed the bell.
No friendly little chime answered me.
Several seconds passed in oppressive silence.
Then came the hurried patter of someone beyond the doors.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Alright."
Shaking off my nervousness, I press it.
There isn't any affectionate "Ding-dong" chime from the doorbell.
The oppressive silence continues for a few seconds.
Then, the sound of pattering footsteps behind the door indicates someone's presence.

entries.japanese:
「お待ちしておりました」
　がちゃり、と扉が開く。
　開いた先にあるのは見覚えのあるロビーと、割烹着を着た少女の姿だった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“We’ve been expecting you.”
The door opened with a heavy click.
Beyond it lay a familiar lobby and a girl in an old-fashioned house apron.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"We have been waiting for you."
The door opens with a creak.
Inside lay the lobby I remembered, and a young girl in an apron.

entries.japanese:
「よかった。
あんまりに遅いから迷っているのかなって心配しちゃってたんですよ。
日が落ちてもいらっしゃらなかったらお迎えに行こうかなって思ってたんですから」
　割烹着なんていうアナクロなものを着込んだ少女はにこにこと笑っている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Thank goodness. You were so late, I was afraid you’d lost your way. If you hadn’t arrived by sundown, I was going to come and find you.”
The girl beamed at me, dressed in that anachronistic house apron.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Thank goodness.
You're so late I was beginning to worry that you had gotten lost.
I was thinking about going out to meet you if you hadn't arrived by sunset."
The girl in the anachronistic apron smiles warmly.

entries.japanese:
「あ、いや───それは、その」
　こちらはというと、少女のあまりに時代錯誤なカッコウに面食らってしまって、まともな言葉が口にできない。
　おどおどとしたこっちの口調を不審に思ったのか、少女はかすかに首をかしげた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh—no, I mean…”
Her anachronistic outfit had taken me so completely aback that I could barely string two words together.
Perhaps puzzled by my stammering, she tipped her head slightly.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah, no--that's… uh…"
I am so taken aback by her outdated mode of dress that I can't even form a proper sentence.
Perhaps attributing my hesitance to distrust, the girl tilts her head a little.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま、ですよね？」
「え───ああ。
さまっていうのは、その、余計だけど」
「ですよね？
　もう、脅かさないでくださいっ。
わたし、また間違えちゃったかなって恐くなったじゃないですか」
　少女はめっ、と母親が子供をしかるような仕草をした。
　だっていうのに顔は微笑んでいて、少女はともかく暖かい雰囲気を崩さない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You’re Master Shiki, aren’t you?”
“Uh—yes. You can leave off the ‘Master,’ though.”
“I knew it! Oh, please don’t frighten me like that. I thought I’d gotten it wrong again.”
She wagged a finger as though scolding a naughty child, but her smile never faltered.
Nothing she did disturbed the warmth about her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"You're Shiki-sama, aren't you?"
"Eh--Yeah, but you don't have to call me '-sama'."
"You are, right?
Oh, please don't scare me like that!
I was beginning to think I had made another mistake back there."
The girl's mannerisms are like those of a mother scolding her child.
But in spite of that, there's a smile on her face, and it doesn't break the warm feeling about her.

entries.japanese:
……着物に割烹着。
　客を出迎えにきて、俺なんかのことを『さま』づけで呼ぶ。
　ということは、この子は────
entries.maoEnglish:
A kimono beneath a house apron.
She had come to greet me and called someone like me ‘Master.’
Then she had to be────

entries.japanese:
「えっと、その───君、もしかしてここのお手伝いさん？」
　こちらの質問に少女は微笑みだけで答えた。
「さ、お疲れでしょう？
　遠慮せずにあがってくださいな。
居間で秋葉さまもお待ちになってらっしゃいますから」
　少女はさっさとロビーを横切って居間へと歩いていく。
　と、思い出したようにくるりと振り返ると、満面の笑みをうかべてお辞儀をした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Um—are you one of the maids here?”
Her smile was her only answer.
“Come in. You must be tired. Miss Akiha is waiting for you in the sitting room.”
She set off briskly across the lobby.
Then, as though suddenly remembering something, she spun around, bowed, and gave me a radiant smile.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Um, uh… are you one of the maids here, by any chance?"
The girl answers my question with nothing but a smile.
"Come; you must be tired.
Please do come in.
Akiha-sama is waiting for you in the sitting room."
The girl quickly crosses the lobby and heads towards the sitting room.
Turning back as if she just remembered something, she makes a bow, a full smile on her face.

entries.japanese:
「お帰りなさい志貴さま。
どうぞ、今日からよろしくお願いしますね」
　少女の挨拶は、本当に華のような笑顔だった。
　それに何ひとつ気のきいた言葉も返せず、おずおずと彼女の後についていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Welcome home, Master Shiki. I look forward to serving you from now on.”
Her greeting came with a smile like a flower in bloom.
Unable to think of anything remotely clever to say, I followed her with faltering steps.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Welcome home, Shiki-sama."
Her greeting is accompanied by her flower-like smile.
I can't think of any reply, so I just follow her hesitatingly.

entries.japanese:
少女に案内されて居間へ移動する。
 ───居間は、初めて見るような気がした。
　八年前の事で覚えていないのか、それともあれから内装を変えでもしたのか。
　とにかく他人の家のようで落ち着かない。
　きょろきょろと居間の様子を見回していると、割烹着のお手伝いさんがペコリと頭をさげていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
The girl led me into the sitting room.
───I felt as if I had never seen the room before.
Perhaps eight years had erased it from my memory, or perhaps it had been redecorated.
Whatever the reason, I felt like a guest in a stranger’s house.
While I stood there looking around, the maid in the house apron bowed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Guided by the girl, I head to the sitting room.
---It's as if I'm seeing it for the first time.
I don't know if I've forgotten about it in the last eight years or they had it refurbished since then.
Either way, it feels like someone else's house now, and it's unsettling.
As I'm looking around the sitting room, the maid in the apron lowers her head in a quick bow.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さまをお連れしました」
「ごくろうさま。
厨房に戻っていいわよ、琥珀」
「はい」
　お手伝いさんはコハク、という名前らしい。
　琥珀さんはそれでは、とこっちにも小さくおじぎをして居間から出ていく。
　残されたのは自分と───見覚えのない、二人の少女だけだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’ve brought Master Shiki.”
“Thank you. You may return to the kitchen, Kohaku.”
“Yes.”
So her name was Kohaku.
With another small bow in my direction, she excused herself and left.
That left me alone with two girls I did not recognize.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I've brought Shiki-sama with me."
"Well done.
You may return to the kitchen, Kohaku."
"Thank you."
It seems that maid's name is Kohaku.
Kohaku-san gives a small bow, as if to say farewell, and leaves the sitting room.
This leaves me, and--two girls I don't recognize.

entries.japanese:
「お久しぶりですね、兄さん」
　長い黒髪の少女は凛とした眼差しのまま、そんな言葉を口にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“It has been a long time, Brother.”
The long-haired girl spoke without relaxing her proud, steady gaze.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"It has been a long time, Nii-san,"
says the girl with the long black hair and sharp eyes.

entries.japanese:
……はっきりいって、思考は完っ全に停止してしまっている。
　真っ白な頭はろくに挨拶もできず、ああ、とうなずく事しかできない。
　……だって、そりゃあ仕方ないと思う。
　八年ぶりに見た秋葉は、こちらの記憶にある秋葉ではなく、まるっきり良家のお嬢様と化していたんだから。
entries.maoEnglish:
To be perfectly honest, my mind had stopped dead.
My head was blank; I could not even manage a greeting, only nod and mumble, ‘Right.’
Who could blame me?
After eight years, the Akiha standing before me was nothing like the one I remembered; she had become, in every particular, a young woman of impeccable breeding.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… All my thought processes stop at once.
My mind goes blank, and I can't think of any words of greeting.
All I can do is nod with a "Yeah."
…… I don't think it can be helped.
This Akiha that I had not seen in eight years is not the Akiha I remember.
She's completely transformed into a proper young lady of a noble family.

entries.japanese:
「兄さん？」
　黒髪の少女はかすかに首をかしげる。
「あ────いや」
　情けないことに間の抜けた言葉しか言えない。
　こっちは目前の少女を秋葉と認識するために頭脳をフル回転させてるっていうのに、秋葉のほうはとっくに俺を兄と認識出来てしまっているようだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Brother?”
The black-haired girl tilted her head.
“Ah—no.”
Pathetically, that was the best I could manage.
I was working my brain to exhaustion trying to recognize the girl before me as Akiha, while she had apparently recognized her brother at once.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Nii-san?"
The black-haired girl tilts her head slightly.
"Ah… um."
Pathetically, all I can say are dumb-sounding things.
My mind is turning in somersaults as I try to recognize the girl before me as Akiha, but it seems like Akiha already recognizes me as her brother.

entries.japanese:
「なにか気分が悪そうですね。
お話の前にお休みになりますか？」
　秋葉はじろりとした視線を向けてくる。
　……なんだか、すごく不機嫌そうに見えるのは気のせいなんだろうか。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You don’t look well. Would you like to rest before we speak?”
Akiha fixed me with a hard stare.
Was I imagining it, or did she seem extremely displeased?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"You do not look well.
Would you like to rest before we talk?"
Akiha throws a sharp glance in my direction.
…… Is it just my imagination that she looks like she's in a bad mood?

entries.japanese:
「……いや、別に気分は悪くない。
ただその、秋葉があんまりにも変わってたんで、びっくりしただけなんだ」
「八年も経てば変わります。
ただでさえ私たちは成長期だったんですから。
　――――それともいつまでも以前のままだと思っていたんですか、兄さんは」
　……なんだろう。
秋葉の言葉は、なんとなく棘があるような気がする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“No, I feel fine. It’s just—you’ve changed so much that I was startled.”
“Eight years will change a person. We were both still growing, after all.
――――Or did you imagine I would remain exactly as you left me, Brother?”
What was this? There seemed to be a barb hidden in everything Akiha said.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… No, I'm alright.
I was just surprised at how much you've changed, Akiha."
"People do change over the course of eight years, Nii-san.
We are at an age of change--or did you think we would remain as we were forever?"
…… What is this?
…… I can feel the thorns in Akiha's words.

entries.japanese:
「いや、それにしたって秋葉は変わったよ。
昔より格段に美人になった」
　お世辞ではなく素直に感想をもらす。
 ────と。
「ええ。
ですが、兄さんは以前とあまり変わりませんね」
　なんて、瞳を閉じたまま秋葉は冷たく言い切った。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Even so, you really have changed. You’re much more beautiful than you used to be.”
It was no flattery; I simply said what I thought.
────And then.
“Yes. But you have hardly changed at all, Brother.”
Eyes closed, Akiha delivered the verdict with glacial finality.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No, you've definitely changed, Akiha.
You've become more beautiful than before."
That isn't flattery.
It's how I really feel.
---And.
"Indeed.
But you, on the other hand, have not changed much at all."
Akiha answers coldly, her eyes closed.

entries.japanese:
「………………」
　……まあ、それなりに覚悟はしていたけど。
　やはり秋葉は俺の事をよく思っていてはくれなかったみたいだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
Well, I had been braced for this.
It seemed Akiha had not forgiven me after all.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……"
…… Well, I came prepared for something like this.
It is as I had thought.
It seems Akiha does not think well of me.

entries.japanese:
「体調がいいなら話をすませましょうか。
兄さん、詳しい事情は聞いてないんでしょう？」
「詳しい事情もなにも、突然屋敷に帰ってこいって事だけしか聞いてない。
親父が亡くなったっていうのは新聞で知ったけど」
entries.maoEnglish:
“If you feel well enough, let us settle the matter at hand. Brother, you haven’t been told the details, have you?”
“What details, when all I heard was that I was suddenly supposed to come back? I learned Father had died from the newspaper.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"If you are feeling well, let us finish our conversation.
You have yet to hear the details about why you were called back here, Nii-san?"
"I've heard nothing more than a sudden 'Come back to the mansion', though I found out the old man passed away in the papers."

entries.japanese:
……一企業のトップに立っていた人物が亡くなれば、それぐらい経済新聞で取りあげられる。
　遠野槙久の訃報は、彼の葬式が終わった後に新聞づてで息子である遠野志貴に届けられた。
　親戚から報せなんてなくても、勘当された息子は一部百円のペーパーで親の死亡を知ることができた。
　皮肉な話だけれど、本当に便利な世の中になったもんだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
When the head of a company dies, it warrants at least a notice in the financial press.
The news of Makihisa Tohno’s death reached his son, Shiki Tohno, by newspaper—after the funeral was already over.
No message from the family was necessary; for a hundred yen, a disowned son could learn that his father had died.
Ironic, perhaps, but what a wonderfully convenient age we live in.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… If the head of a major company dies, it definitely makes it in the financial papers.
Word of Tohno Makihisa's death reached his son, Tohno Shiki, via the newspaper after the funeral.
Even though his relatives hadn't told him, this disinherited son could pick up news of his father's death merely by buying a one hundred yen newspaper.
It might be cynical of me to say so, but the world has certainly become a convenient place.

entries.japanese:
「……申し訳ありません。
お父さまの事を兄さんに報せなかったのはこちらの失策でした」
　秋葉は静かに頭をさげる。
「いいよ。
どのみち俺が行ったって死人が生き返るわけでもないし。
秋葉が気にする事じゃない」
「……ごめんなさい。
そういってもらえると少しは気が楽になるわ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’m sorry. Failing to inform you of Father’s death was an oversight on our part.”
Akiha bowed her head in silence.
“It’s all right. Even if I’d been there, the dead would not have come back to life. This is nothing you need to worry about.”
“I’m sorry… but hearing you say that does make me feel a little better.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I am sorry.
It was my fault that you did not get the news about Father."
Akiha quietly lowers her head.
"It's alright.
Either way, it's not like he would come back from the dead if I went.
It's not something you should be worried about."
"…… I am sorry.
It is somewhat comforting to hear you say that."

entries.japanese:
秋葉は深刻な顔をするけど、そんなのは本当にどうでもいい話だった。
　葬式というものは故人に対して感情を断ち切れない人達が、その感情を断ち切るために行う儀式だ。
とうの昔に感情を断ってきた自分とあの父親の場合、葬式の必要はないと思う。
entries.maoEnglish:
Akiha looked grave, but the whole matter truly meant nothing to me.
A funeral is a rite for those who cannot release their feelings for the dead, meant to help them finally let go. My father and I had severed those feelings long ago; in our case, there was no need for a funeral.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Akiha's face is serious, but this is not a topic I care much about.
A funeral is a ceremony for those who cannot let go of their feelings for the deceased to achieve such detachment.
For someone like me, who cut off such feelings a long time ago, there is no need.

entries.japanese:
「兄さんをこちらに呼び戻したのは私の意向です。
いつまでも遠野の長男が有間の家に預けられているのはおかしいでしょう？
　お父さまが亡くなられた以上、遠野の血筋は私と兄さんだけです。
お父さまがどのようなお考えで兄さんを有間の家に預けたかは分かりませんが、そのお父さまもすでに他界なさった身。
　ですからこれ以上兄さんが有間の家に預けられる必要はなくなったので、こちらに戻ってもらう事にしたんです」
entries.maoEnglish:
“It was my decision to bring you back. The eldest Tohno son cannot remain indefinitely in the care of the Arima family, can he?
With Father dead, you and I are the only Tohnos left by blood. I don’t know what he intended when he sent you to the Arimas, but he is no longer here.
There is no reason for you to remain in their care, so I decided that you would return home.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Calling you back here was my idea.
It would be odd for the eldest son of the Tohnos to be entrusted to the Arimas forever.
Now that Father has passed away, the only Tohnos by blood are you and I, Nii-san.
I don't know what Father was thinking when he entrusted you to the Arimas, but he's no longer with us, so there's no longer any need for you to live with them.
That is why I had you come back here."

entries.japanese:
「……まあいいけど、そんなんでよく親戚の連中が納得したな。
俺を有間の家に預けろって言い出したの、たしか親戚の人たちじゃなかったっけ？」
entries.maoEnglish: “Fine, but I’m surprised the relatives agreed. Weren’t they the ones who demanded I be sent to the Arimas in the first place?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… That's all well and good, but I'm quite surprised you were able to get our relatives to agree to this.
Wasn't it they who came up with the idea of leaving me with the Arimas in the first place?"

entries.japanese:
「そうですね。
けれど今の遠野の当主は私です。
親戚の方達の進言はすべて却下しました。
「兄さんにはこれからここで暮らしてもらいたいのですけど、ここにはここの規律があります。
今までのような無作法はさけていただきますから、そのつもりで」
entries.maoEnglish:
“They were. However, I am now head of the Tohno family. I rejected every one of their objections.
“I want you to live here from now on, but this household has rules of its own. I will not tolerate the discourtesies you have allowed yourself until now; remember that.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"That may be so, but now I am the head of the Tohno family.
I declined every one of the proposals from our relatives.
I would like you to continue living here, Nii-san, but this is a place with rules.
You will avoid living the overly casual lifestyle you've been leading up until now."

entries.japanese:
「はは、そりゃあ無理だよ秋葉。
いまさら俺がお行儀いい人間に戻れるわけないし、戻ろうって気もないんだから」
「できる範囲でけっこうですから努力してください。
それとも───私にできた事が兄さんにはできない、とおっしゃるんですか？」
　じろり、と秋葉は冷たい視線を向けてくる。
　なんだか無言で、八年間もここに置き去りにしてきた恨みをぶつけられている気がする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ha, that’s asking the impossible, Akiha. It’s far too late for me to become well behaved again—and I have no desire to try.”
“Then make whatever effort lies within your power. Or are you claiming that what I could do is beyond you?”
Akiha gave me another icy look.
Without saying a word, she seemed to be hurling eight years of resentment at me for leaving her here alone.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Haha.
I'm afraid that isn't going to happen, Akiha.
There's no way I can go back to being some well-mannered gentleman now.
Not that I want to."
"I will not ask more of you but do try to--or are you saying you are unable to do what I already have?"
Akiha shoots me a cold look.
It feels like she's hitting me with her grudge against me for leaving her here for the last eight years.

entries.japanese:
「……オーケー、わかった。
なんとか努力はしてみる」
　秋葉はじーっ、と信用できなさそうに睨んでくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“All right, all right. I’ll do my best.”
Akiha stared at me as though she believed none of it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Alright.
I get it.
I'll try my best."
Akiha just stares at me, as if she doesn't quite believe me.

entries.japanese:
「努力する必要はありません。
結果を出していただければそれで結構です」
　凛、とした姿勢のまま、秋葉は容赦のない言葉を繰り出してくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I have no interest in your efforts. Results will be sufficient.”
Without wavering, Akiha delivered the merciless retort.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"You do not need to try, as long as you get the results."
Her pose is dignified, her words merciless.

entries.japanese:
「話を戻しますね。
　現在、遠野の家には兄さんと私しか住んでいません。
わずらわしいのはイヤなので人払いをしたんです」
「え？
　ちょっと待てよ秋葉、人払いっておまえ───」
「兄さんだって親戚の人達と屋敷の中で会うのはイヤでしょう？
　使用人も大部分に暇をだしましたけど、私と兄さん付きの者は残してありますから問題はありません」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Let us return to the subject.
At present, only you and I live at the estate. I sent everyone else away because they had become tiresome.”
“Wait, Akiha—you sent everyone away?” “You would not want to meet the relatives in the halls either, would you?
I dismissed most of the servants as well, but kept those assigned to each of us. There is no problem.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Let's get back to the topic.
Right now, you and I are the only ones living here.
I do not care for having too many people around, so I cleared everyone out."
"Eh?
Hold on a second, Akiha.
You 'cleared everyone out'?"
"You wouldn't want to run into one of our relatives in the mansion, would you, Nii-san?
I have put off most of the servants, but there are enough for you and I, so there are no problems."

entries.japanese:
「いや、問題ないって秋葉。
そんな勝手な事しちゃ親戚会議でたたかれるじゃないか！」
「もう、つべこべ言わないでください。
兄さんだって屋敷の中に人が溢れかえっているより、私たちしかいないほうが気分は楽でしょう？」
　……う。
　まあ、それは本当に気が楽になるんだけど。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Of course there’s a problem! You can’t act that arbitrarily without getting torn apart at the next family council!”
“Oh, stop fussing. Surely you prefer having the estate to ourselves over finding it crammed with people?”
Urgh.
She was right; that did make me feel considerably better.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Wait, 'no problems'?
You're going to get attacked at our family meeting if you do something like that!"
"Oh, please be quiet.
Rather than have the mansion overflowing with people, wouldn't you feel more relaxed with just the two of us here?"
…… Urgh.
Well, it's true that I would feel relaxed, but…

entries.japanese:
「だけど当主になったばかりの秋葉が、その、そんな暴君みたいなワガママを通したら親戚の連中が黙っていないんじゃないか？
　親父だって親戚の意見には逆らわなかったじゃないか」
「そうですね。
だからお父さまは兄さんを有間の家に預けたんです。
けど私、子供の頃からあの人達が大っ嫌いでしたから。
これ以上あの方達の小言を聞くのは御免です」
「ゴメンですって、秋葉───」
entries.maoEnglish:
“But you’ve only just become head of the family; if you start forcing through whims like some petty tyrant, won’t the relatives revolt? Even Father never defied them.”
“Precisely. That is why Father sent you to the Arimas. But I have detested those people since I was a child, and I refuse to listen to another one of their lectures.”
“You refuse? Akiha—”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"But you've only just become head of the family, Akiha.
If you go around abusing your powers like some kind of dictator, our relatives are not going to keep quiet.
Even the old man didn't go against their opinions."
"Indeed.
That's why father entrusted you to the Arimas.
I, on the other hand, have despised them ever since I was a child.
I am not going to put up with their whining any longer."
"'Not going to put up with'… look, Akiha---"

entries.japanese:
「ああもう、いいから私の心配なんかしなくていいの！
　兄さんはこれからのご自分の生活を気に病んでください。
色々大変になるって目に見えてるんだから」
　秋葉は少しだけ俺から視線をそらして、不機嫌そうにそう言った。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh, enough—stop worrying about me! You should worry about your own life from now on. Anyone can see how difficult it is going to be.”
Akiha looked slightly away from me as she spoke, sounding cross.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ahh, enough!
Just listen!
You don't have to worry about me!
Please, just worry about your own life from now on, Nii-san.
I can see it's going to be difficult for you in many ways."
Akiha says sullenly, looking away a little.

entries.japanese:
「それじゃあ、これからは分からない事があったらこの子にいいつけて。
────翡翠」
　秋葉は傍らに立っていた少女にめくばせする。
　ひすい、と呼ばれた少女は無表情のままペコリとお辞儀をした。
「この子は翡翠。
これから兄さん付きの侍女にしますけど、よろしいですね？」
 ────────え？
「ちょっ、侍女って、つまり、その」
「分かりやすくいうと召使い、という事です」
　秋葉は当たり前のように、きっぱりと言い切った。
entries.maoEnglish:
“From now on, if there is anything you do not understand, tell her. ────Hisui.”
Akiha glanced toward the girl standing beside her.
The girl she had called Hisui bowed without a trace of expression.
“This is Hisui. She will be your personal maid—is that acceptable?”
────────What?
“W-wait, a maid—that means—”
“To put it plainly, a servant.”
Akiha pronounced it as though it were the most obvious thing in the world.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Now then, if there's anything you don't understand, ask her--Hisui."
She looks at the girl standing by her side.
The girl called Hisui bows expressionlessly.
"This is Hisui.
She will be your personal maid from now on.
Is that acceptable?"
--------Eh?
"Hold on… personal maid?
You mean…?"
"In other words, she's your servant."
Akiha declares, as if it were obvious.

entries.japanese:
……信じられない。
　洋館に相応しく、メイド服を着込んだ少女は秋葉同様、そうしているのが当然のように立っていた。
「───ちょっと待ってくれ。
子供じゃあるまいし侍女なんて必要ないよ。
自分のことぐらい自分で面倒みれるから」
「食事の支度や着物の洗濯も、ですか？」
　うっ。
　秋葉の指摘は、カナリ鋭い。
entries.maoEnglish:
I could not believe this.
Dressed in a maid’s uniform perfectly suited to the Western-style main house, the girl stood as though this arrangement were every bit as natural to her as it was to Akiha.
“Hold on. I’m not a child. I don’t need a personal maid; I can take care of myself.”
“Including preparing your meals and doing your laundry?”
Urgh.
Akiha had struck home.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… I can't believe it.
Fitting with the western style of the house, the girl in the maid outfit stands there, as if it is natural to do so.
"--Hold on.
I'm not a kid, you know.
I don't need a servant.
I can take care of myself."
"Would that include the cooking and the laundry?"
Urgh.
Akiha is pretty sharp at pointing these things out.

entries.japanese:
「ともかくこの屋敷に戻ってこられた以上は私の指示に従ってもらいます。
有間の家ではどう暮らしていたかは知りませんが、これから兄さんは遠野の家で暮らすんです。
それ相応の待遇は当然と受け入れてください」
「う………」
　言葉もなく、翡翠に視線を泳がす。
　翡翠はやはり無表情で、ただ人形のようにこちらを見つめ返してくるだけだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Now that you have returned to this estate, you will follow my instructions. I do not know how you lived with the Arimas, but from now on you will live as a Tohno. Accept the treatment that comes with your position.”
“Urgh…”
At a loss for words, I looked helplessly toward Hisui.
Still expressionless, she merely stared back at me like a doll.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"At any rate, now that you've returned to this house, you will obey my directions.
I don't know how you lived at the Arima house, but you're living at the Tohno house now.
Please accept everything given to you."
"Urgh…"
I can't say anything, and I my eyes drift towards Hisui.
As expected, she simply looks back at me expressionlessly like a doll.

entries.japanese:
「それじゃ翡翠、兄さんを部屋に案内してあげて」
「はい、お嬢さま」
　翡翠は影のような気配のなさでこっちへ歩いてくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hisui, show him to his room.” “Yes, Miss Akiha.”
Hisui approached so silently that she might have been a shadow.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Well then, Hisui.
Please show Nii-san to his room."
"Yes, my lady."
Hisui approaches me with a shadow-like lack of presence.

entries.japanese:
「それではお部屋にご案内します、志貴さま」
　翡翠はロビーへ向かう。
「……はあ」
　ため息をつきながら、こっちもロビーへ歩きだした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I will show you to your room, Master Shiki.”
Hisui headed for the lobby.
“Haaah…”
Sighing, I followed her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I will guide you to your room, Shiki-sama."
Hisui heads towards the lobby.
Sighing, I head off towards the lobby as well.

entries.japanese:
ロビーに出た。
　この洋館はロビーを中心にして東館と西館に分かれている。
　ロビーが鳥の胴体、東と西の館が鳥の翼のように斜めに伸びていて、片翼───つまり一方の館の大きさは小さな病院なみだ。
　作りは左右対称で、東館も西館も同じ間取りをしていたと記憶している。
entries.maoEnglish:
We entered the lobby.
The main house was divided into east and west wings, with the lobby at its center.
The lobby was the body of a bird, and the two wings slanted away on either side; each wing alone was as large as a small hospital.
The structure was symmetrical, and as I remembered it, both wings had identical floor plans.
entries.mirrorMoon:
We enter the lobby.
This mansion is split into east and west wings, with the lobby in the middle.
The lobby is like the body of a bird whose wings are the halls extending diagonally to the east and west.
Each wing is about the size of a small hospital.
I remember the house is constructed symmetrically, so both the east and west wings have the same floor plan.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さまのお部屋はこちらです」
　翡翠は階段をあがっていく。
　どうやら遠野志貴の部屋は二階にあるみたいだ。
　……そういえば、使用人の部屋は一階の西館にあったはずだから、翡翠と琥珀さんの部屋は一階にあるのだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Your room is this way, Master Shiki.”
Hisui started up the stairs.
Apparently Shiki Tohno’s room was on the second floor.
Come to think of it, the servants’ rooms had been on the ground floor of the west wing, so Hisui and Kohaku’s rooms were probably there.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Your room is this way, Shiki-sama."
Hisui climbs up a flight of stairs.
It seems like my room is on the second floor.
…… Come to think of it, the servants' rooms should be on the first floor of the west wing, so that's probably where Hisui and Kohaku-san's rooms are.

entries.japanese:
外はすでに日が落ちている。
　ぼんやりと電灯の点った長い廊下を、メイド服の女の子が無言で歩いている。
「……なんか、おとぎの国みたいだ」
　思わずそんな感想を洩らす。
「志貴さま、何かおっしゃられましたか？」
　立ち止まって振りかえる翡翠。
entries.maoEnglish:
The sun had already set.
A girl in a maid’s uniform walked wordlessly down a long corridor lit by dim electric lamps.
“It’s like something out of a fairy tale.”
The thought escaped my lips.
“Did you say something, Master Shiki?”
Hisui stopped and looked back.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Outside, the sun has already set.
The girl in the maid uniform walks down the long, dimly lit hallway without a word.
"…… It kind of feels like a wonderland."
Without thinking, I let my thoughts slip out.
"Did you say something, Shiki-sama?"
Hisui stops and looks back at me.

entries.japanese:
「いや、ただの独り言だから気にしないでくれ」
「……………」
　翡翠はじっとこちらを見つめたあと、それでは、と一礼して歩き出した。
entries.maoEnglish:
“No, it was only something I said to myself.”
“…”
Hisui studied me for a moment, bowed as if to say very well, and resumed walking.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No, I'm just talking to myself.
Don't worry about it."
"………"
After staring at me, Hisui bows and starts walking again.

entries.japanese:
「………………」
　言葉を失う、というのはこういうコトだろうか。
　翡翠に案内された部屋は、とても一介の高校生が住む部屋の作りをしていなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
So this was what it meant to be speechless.
The room Hisui showed me bore no resemblance to anything an ordinary high-school boy ought to inhabit.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……"
I guess this is what they call being 'at a loss for words'.
The room Hisui led me to is not one made for a mere high school student to live in.

entries.japanese:
「……俺の部屋って、ここ？」
「はい。
ご不満がおありでしたら違うお部屋をご用意させていただきますが」
「いや、不満なんてあるわけないけど、その――」
　ちょっと、いやかなり立派すぎるかなって。
「志貴さま？」
「―――いいんだ、なんでもない。
喜んでこの部屋を使わせてもらうよ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“This is my room?”
“Yes. If it is not to your liking, another room can be prepared.”
“No, there’s nothing to dislike; it’s just――”
It was a little—no, vastly—too grand for me.
“Master Shiki?”
“―――Never mind; it’s nothing. I’ll be delighted to use this room.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Is this my room?"
"Yes.
If you are displeased with it, I can arrange a different one for you."
"No, there's no way I could be displeased with it.
It's--"
It's just a little--no, really too fancy for me.
"Shiki-sama?"
"---It's fine.
I'll gladly use this room."

entries.japanese:
「はい。
お部屋は八年前から手を加えていませんので、不具合はないと思います」
「―――？」
　翡翠の言い方は、ちょっとヘンだ。
　それじゃあまるで、ここが俺の部屋だったみたいな言い方じゃないか。
「……ねえ。
ここって、もしかして俺の部屋だったの？」
「そう伺っておりますが、違うのですか？」
　翡翠はかすかに首をかしげる。
　……安心した。
　この娘にも、それなりに感情表現というものがあるみたいだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Very good. Nothing in the room has been changed in eight years, so I do not expect any inconvenience.”
“―――?”
There was something odd about the way Hisui had put that.
She made it sound as though this had always been my room.
“…Was this my room before I left?”
“That is what I was told, but was it not?”
Hisui tilted her head ever so slightly.
What a relief.
Apparently she did possess some means of expressing emotion.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yes.
This room has not been touched since eight years ago, so I do not believe you will find anything unsatisfactory with it."
"--?"
There's something a little odd about the way Hisui said that.
It's as if she was implying this was once my room.
"…… Hey.
Is this by any chance my old room?"
"That is what I have been told.
Am I mistaken?"
Hisui inclines her head to the side slightly.
…… I feel relieved.
It seems this girl can express emotion after all.

entries.japanese:
「……まあ、言われてみればそうかもしれない。
少しは覚えがあるし、きっとそうだったんだろう」
　親近感はまったく湧かないけど、八年間も離れていればそんなものなのかもしれない。
「けど、やっぱり落ち着かないな。
今朝まで六畳半の部屋で暮らしてたからさ、なんだか高級ホテルに泊まりに来たみたいだ」
「お気持ちはわかりますが、どうかお慣れください。
志貴さまは今日から遠野家のご長男なのですから」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Now that you mention it, perhaps it was. A few things do seem familiar, so I suppose that must be right.”
The room stirred no affection in me at all, but perhaps eight years away would do that.
“Still, I can’t relax here. Until this morning I lived in a cramped six-and-a-half-mat room; this feels like checking into a luxury hotel.”
“I understand, but please try to become accustomed to it. As of today, Master Shiki is once again the eldest son of the Tohno family.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Well, it might be, now that you mention it.
I do remember it faintly, so it must be so."
I can't feel any sense of familiarity about this place at all, but I guess that's what it's like after you leave a place for eight years.
"I can't get settled here, though.
I was living in a six-and-a-half-mat sized room until this morning.
It's like I'm staying in some high class hotel."
"I understand how you feel, but please try to get used to it.
From today onwards, you are the eldest son of the Tohno house, Shiki-sama."

entries.japanese:
「そうだね。
せめて外見ぐらいは笑われないように頑張ってみるよ」
　トン、と机に鞄を置いて背筋を伸ばす。
―――色々と神経がまいりそうだけど、たしかに今日から慣れていくしかないだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You’re right. I’ll at least try to look the part well enough not to be laughed at.”
I set my bag on the desk with a thump and straightened my back.
―――It was going to fray my nerves in all sorts of ways, but from today on, I simply had to get used to it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"You're right.
I've got to do my best so I at least look like it on the outside."
With a thump, I drop my bag on the table and stretch my back.
---I've been feeling a little stressed out with everything that's happened so far, but I guess I've got no choice but to adjust from today onwards.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さまのお荷物はすべて運び込みましたが、何か足りないものはありますか？」
「―――いや、別にないけど。
どうしてそんな事を聞くの？」
「……いえ、荷物が少なすぎるようですから。
必要なものがおありでしたら用意いたしますから、どうかお聞かせください」
entries.maoEnglish:
“All Master Shiki’s belongings have been brought in; is anything missing?”
“―――No, I don’t think so. Why do you ask?”
“Your luggage seemed unusually sparse. If you require anything, we will obtain it; you need only tell me.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama, all of your luggage has been brought here.
Is there anything more you require?"
"---No, not really.
Why do you ask?"
"…… There was very little delivered.
If there is anything you need, I can have it prepared, so please do not hesitate to ask."

entries.japanese:
「……そっか。
いや、とりあえず足りないものなんてないよ。
もともと荷物は少ないんだ。
自分の荷物っていったら、その鞄とこのメガネと……」
　鞄の中に入っている教科書とか、誰のものとも知らない白いリボンとか、それだけだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I see. No, I’m all right for now. I never owned much to begin with. Everything I have amounts to that bag, these glasses, and…”
The textbooks in my bag and a white ribbon whose owner I did not even know—that was all.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I see.
No, I don't need anything more for now.
I didn't have much luggage to begin with.
My luggage is just this bag, these glasses, and…"
The textbooks in my bag, and that white ribbon with an unidentified owner.
That's all----

entries.japanese:
「ともかく、荷物のことは気にしないでいい。
こんな立派な部屋だけで十分だよ、俺は」
「……かしこまりました。
では、一時間後にお呼びにまいります」
「一時間後って、もしかして夕食？」
「はい。
それまで、どうぞおくつろぎください」
　
　翡翠はやっぱり無表情で言ってくる。
……しかし。
おくつろぎくださいって言われても、ここでどうおくろつぎすればいいんだろう？
entries.maoEnglish:
“In any case, don’t worry about my luggage. A room this splendid is more than enough for me.”
“Understood. I will return for you in one hour.”
“One hour—is that dinner?”
“Yes. Until then, please make yourself comfortable.”
Hisui said it all without expression.
But. How was I supposed to make myself comforble—comfortable here?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Anyways, you don't have to worry about the luggage.
This fancy room is more than enough for me."
"…… I understand.
Well then, I shall come to call you in an hour's time."
"An hour?
For dinner, you mean?"
"Yes.
Please relax until then."
As expected, Hisui says everything with an expressionless face.
…… But even if she tells me to relax, just how am I supposed to do that here?

entries.japanese:
時計は夕方の六時をまわったあたり。
　いつもなら居間にいってテレビでも見てる時間だけど、この屋敷にそんなものがあるかどうか真剣に疑わしい。
entries.maoEnglish:
The time was a little past six in the evening.
Ordinarily I would be in the living room watching television, but I had serious doubts that the estate contained one.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The clock says it's six o'clock.
Usually, I'd be watching TV in the sitting room around this time, but I'm having serious doubts as to whether there's any such thing in this mansion.

entries.japanese:
「翡翠、つまらない事を聞くけどさ。
この屋敷にテレビってあるの？」
「テレビ……ですか？」
　翡翠はかすかに目を細める。
　……なんていうか、自分で言っておいてなんだけど、ひどく頭が痛くなる質問だ。
　これだけ贅沢な洋館において、テレビがあるかないかを訊ねるなんてどこか間違ってる気がする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hisui, this may be a silly question. Does the estate have a television?”
“A television…?”
Hisui narrowed her eyes slightly.
Even as the person asking, I could feel a headache coming on.
Something was deeply wrong with having to ask whether an estate this lavish owned a television.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hisui.
I know it's kind of a trivial thing to ask about, but is there a television in this mansion?"
"A television…?"
Hisui's eyes narrow slightly.
…… I know I'm the one who asked, but it really is a stupid question.
I feel there's something wrong with asking about the presence of a TV in a luxurious mansion like this.

entries.japanese:
翡翠はめずらしく困ったような顔をして、視線を宙に泳がした。
「……居間にはありません。
ご逗留の方々はご使用になってらっしゃいましたが、出立される時に荷物はすべてお持ち帰りいただきましたので残ってはいないと思います」
entries.maoEnglish:
For once, Hisui looked uncertain as her gaze drifted into the air.
“There is none in the sitting room. Some of the relatives staying here had televisions, but they took all their belongings when they departed, so I do not believe any remain.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
Hisui makes a rare troubled face, and stares off into space.
"…… There is no television in the sitting room.
Some of the visitors did make use of one, but when they departed, they packed it up with their luggage and took it back with them, so I do not believe there are any remaining."

entries.japanese:
「ちょっと待った。
逗留って、誰がどのくらいしてたんだ？」
「分家筋である久我峰さまのご長男のご家族、刀崎さまのご三女とその婚約者、軋間さまのご長男がご逗留なさっていました。
期間は三年ほどです」
「……三年、か。
翡翠、そういうのって逗留っていうんじゃなくて居候って言うんじゃない？」
　翡翠は答えない。
　居候していた連中がどんな人間であろうと、使用人である以上失礼な事は言えないみたいだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Wait. Which relatives were ‘staying’ here, and for how long?”
“The family of the eldest son of the Kugamine branch; the Tosaki family’s third daughter and her fiancé; and the Kishima family’s eldest son. They stayed for roughly three years.”
“Three years? Hisui, I think the word for that is freeloading, not staying.”
Hisui did not answer.
No matter what those freeloaders had been like, a servant could hardly speak ill of them.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hold on.
Visitors?
Like who?
For how long?"
"Relatives.
The eldest son of Kugamine-sama from a branch of the family, Touzaki-sama's third daughter and her fiance, and Kishima-sama's eldest son came to stay for close to three years."
"…… Three years, huh?
Hisui, that's what you'd call freeloaders, not visitors."
Hisui does not reply.
No matter what kind of people these freeloaders were, it seems that servants can't say anything bad about them.

entries.japanese:
まあ、ともかく逗留していた親戚筋の連中は自分たちの荷物を持ちかえらされたという事らしい。
　となると、あの現代的な文化ってモノを俗物的と毛嫌いしていた父親がテレビなんて観るはずもない。
　父親のもとで八年間も躾けられた秋葉も同じだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
At any rate, Akiha had evidently made the resident relatives take their possessions with them.
Father had despised modern culture as hopelessly vulgar, so he certainly would never have watched television.
After eight years under his discipline, Akiha was probably the same.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Well, at any rate, it seems like those relatives had brought, and taken back, their own luggage with them.
My old man hated the products of modern culture, thinking them all vulgar.
There was no way he would ever watch a TV.
Akiha, who had been educated by him for the last eight years, would probably be the same.

entries.japanese:
「───ま、ないからって別に死ぬわけでもないか」
　翡翠は黙っている。
　……使用人の鑑というか、翡翠は聞かれた事以外は何も喋らない。
　当然、こっちとしては気が滅入る。
　なんとかしてこの無表情な顔を笑わせてみたいと思うのだけど、どうも生半可な努力では不可能そうではある。
entries.maoEnglish:
“───Well, I’m not going to die without one.”
Hisui remained silent.
The perfect servant, perhaps: she never said anything she had not been asked.
Naturally, that left me feeling rather low.
I wanted to find some way of making that blank face smile, but no ordinary effort was likely to succeed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"--Well, it's not like I'll die without one."
Hisui is silent.
…… Like a perfect example for servants, Hisui says nothing unless she is being asked a direct question.
This is, of course, kind of depressing for me.
I want to make that expressionless face break into a smile somehow, but that seems impossible with just any old half-hearted effort.

entries.japanese:
「いいや、たしか一階の西館のほうに書庫があったよね。
暇なときはそこから何かみつくろう事にするよ」
　翡翠は答えない。
　ただ部屋の入り口に突っ立ったまま、どこを見ているんだかわからない眼差しをしている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Actually, there was a library on the ground floor of the west wing, wasn’t there? I’ll find something to read when I’m bored.”
Hisui gave no answer.
She simply stood in the doorway, staring at some point I could not identify.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Oh, there was a library on the first floor of the west wing, wasn't there?
Maybe I'll go find something to read when I have some free time."
Hisui does not reply.
She just stands there in the doorway.
I can't even tell where she's looking.

entries.japanese:
「───翡翠？」
　翡翠はうんとも言わない。
　と、突然まっすぐにこちらを見据えてきた。
「姉さんの部屋になら、あると思います」
「は？」
　いやもう、ワケがわからない。
「……えーっと。
あるって、何が」
「ですからテレビです。
以前、姉さんの部屋で見かけた記憶がありますから」
　翡翠はまるで数年前の出来事を思い出すように言った。
entries.maoEnglish:
“───Hisui?”
She did not so much as murmur.
Then, without warning, her gaze fixed directly on me.
“I believe there is one in my sister’s room.”
“What?”
Now I was completely lost.
“…There’s what in her room?”
“A television. I remember seeing one there before.”
Hisui spoke as though dredging up an incident from years ago.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Hisui?"
Hisui doesn't say a word.
Suddenly, she looks straight at me.
"I believe there is one in Nee-san's room."
"Huh?"
I have no idea what she's talking about.
"…… Uh… there's one of what?"
"A television.
I remember seeing one in Nee-san's room."
Hisui says, as if remembering something from many years ago.

entries.japanese:
「ちょっと待って。
姉さんって、もしかして琥珀さんのこと？」
「はい。
現在、このお屋敷で働かせていただいている者はわたしと姉さんの二人きりです」
　……言われてみればよく似てる。
琥珀さんがニコニコしていて、翡翠が無表情だからなんとなく姉妹だって結びつかなかった。
「そっか。
琥珀さんならたしかにバラエティー番組を観てそうなキャラクターだ」
　しかし、かといって『テレビ観せてくれい』と琥珀さんの部屋に遊びに行くのも気がひける。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Wait. By your sister, do you mean Kohaku?”
“Yes. My sister and I are currently the only two servants employed at this estate.”
Now that she mentioned it, they did look alike. Kohaku’s perpetual smile and Hisui’s blank face had kept me from thinking of them as sisters.
“I see. Kohaku certainly seems like the sort to watch variety shows.”
Even so, barging into Kohaku’s room and asking to watch her television felt rather presumptuous.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hold on.
Nee-san?
Don't tell me you're talking about Kohaku-san?"
"Yes.
Right now, the only people working at this mansion are Nee-san and I."
Now that she mentions it, they do look alike.
I just couldn't connect them as sisters because Kohaku-san is always smiling so warmly, and Hisui is always expressionless.
"I see.
Kohaku-san does look like the type of person who'd watch those variety shows."
But I balk at going to Kohaku-san's room to tell her, "Let me watch your TV."

entries.japanese:
「ごめん、この話はなかった事にしてくれ。
これからここで暮らすんだから、屋敷のルールには従わなくっちゃいけないしね」
　それにテレビなんてものを観ていたら、秋葉にどんな皮肉を言われるかわかったもんじゃない。
　ここは遠野家の人間に相応しい、勤勉な学生になりきろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Sorry—forget I asked. I’m going to live here now, so I ought to respect the rules of the estate.”
Besides, if Akiha caught me watching television, there was no telling what cutting remark she might make.
I would simply become the diligent student worthy of the Tohno family.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Sorry, just forget I ever asked.
After all, I'll be living here from now on, so I've got to follow the rules of the mansion."
God knows what sort of cynical comment I'd be in for from Akiha if I started watching television.
It seems I'll be leading a scholarly student life fit for a member of the Tohno family from now on.

entries.japanese:
「それじゃ夕食まで部屋にいるから、時間になったら呼びにきてくれ。
翡翠だって他にやる事あるだろ？」
　翡翠ははい、とうなずいて背中を向ける。
　きい、と静かにドアが開かれて、翡翠は部屋から退室していった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’ll stay here until dinner; come and get me when it’s time. You must have other work to do.”
Hisui nodded and turned away.
The door opened with a quiet creak, and Hisui slipped out of the room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Alright.
I'll be in my room until dinner, so just come and call me when it's time.
You've got other things to do, don't you, Hisui?"
Hisui nods in assent, and turns around.
Silently opening the door, she leaves the room.

entries.japanese:
「――――――――でかい」
　正門について、ついそんな言葉が口に出た。
　一般家庭に慣れしたんだ自分にとって、遠野の屋敷は大きく現実からかけ離れてしまっている。
「………早まったかな、俺」
　……いや、今さら後悔しても始まらない。
　門は開いている。
　力任せに押しあけて、屋敷の玄関へと向かっていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――――――It’s enormous.”
The words escaped me when I reached the main gate.
After growing accustomed to an ordinary household, the Tohno estate seemed impossibly vast, almost divorced from reality.
“Maybe coming back was a mistake.”
No—regret would accomplish nothing now.
The gate stood unlocked.
I heaved it open and headed for the estate’s front entrance.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----It's huge."
The words escape my mouth when I reach the gate.
For someone like me, used to living in a normal house, the Tohno mansion seems well out of reality.
"…… I wonder if I rushed into this?"
…… No, it's too late to start regretting things now.
The gates aren't locked.
I push them open, and head towards the mansion doors.

entries.japanese:
屋敷の玄関は重苦しくそびえ、訪れる者を威圧している。
　両開きの扉の横には、不釣り合いな呼び鈴があった。
「…………よし」
　緊張を振り払って呼び鈴を押す。
　ぴんぽーん、なんていう親しみのある音はしない。
　重苦しい静寂が続くこと数秒。
　扉の奥でぱたぱた、という慌ただしい人の気配がした。
entries.maoEnglish:
The estate’s front entrance loomed above me, ponderous and forbidding.
Beside the massive double doors was a doorbell that looked almost comically out of place.
“All right.”
Shaking off my nerves, I pressed it.
No friendly little chime answered me.
Several seconds passed in oppressive silence.
Then came the hurried patter of someone beyond the doors.
entries.mirrorMoon:
They tower oppressively, bearing down on any visitors.
Beside the iron double doors is an unmatching doorbell.
"…… Alright."
Shaking off my nervousness, I press it.
There isn't any affectionate "ding-dong" chime from the doorbell.
The oppressive silence continues for a few seconds.
Then, the sound of pattering footsteps behind the door indicates someone's presence.

entries.japanese:
「お待ちしておりました」
　がちゃり、と扉が開く。
　開いた先にあるのは見覚えのあるロビーと、割烹着を着た少女の姿だった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“We’ve been expecting you.”
The door opened with a heavy click.
Beyond it lay a familiar lobby and a girl in an old-fashioned house apron.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"We have been waiting for you."
The door opens with a creak.
Inside is the lobby I remembered and a young girl in an apron.

entries.japanese:
「よかった。
あんまりに遅いから迷っているのかなって心配しちゃってたんですよ。
日が落ちてもいらっしゃらなかったらお迎えに行こうかなって思ってたんですから」
　割烹着なんていうアナクロなものを着込んだ少女はにこにこと笑っている。
「あ、いや───それは、その」
　こちらはというと、少女のあまりに時代錯誤なカッコウに面食らってしまって、まともな言葉が口にできない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Thank goodness. You were so late, I was afraid you’d lost your way. If you hadn’t arrived by sundown, I was going to come and find you.”
The girl beamed at me, dressed in that anachronistic house apron.
“Oh—no, I mean…”
Her anachronistic outfit had taken me so completely aback that I could barely string two words together.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Thank goodness.
You're so late I was beginning to worry that you had gotten lost.
I was thinking about going out to meet you if you hadn't arrived by sunset."
The girl in the anachronistic apron smiles warmly.
"Ah, no--that's… uh…"
I am so taken aback by her outdated mode of dress that I can't even form a proper sentence.
Perhaps attributing my hesitance to distrust, the girl tilts her head a little.

entries.japanese:
おどおどとしたこっちの口調を不審に思ったのか、少女はかすかに首をかしげた。
「志貴さま、ですよね？」
「え───ああ。
さまっていうのは、その、余計だけど」
「ですよね？
　もう、脅かさないでくださいっ。
わたし、また間違えちゃったかなって恐くなったじゃないですか」
　あはは、と気さくな笑いをこぼす少女。
　確証なんかないけど、ぴたりと、イメージが合ってしまう。
entries.maoEnglish:
Perhaps puzzled by my stammering, she tipped her head slightly.
“You’re Master Shiki, aren’t you?”
“Uh—yes. You can leave off the ‘Master,’ though.”
“I knew it! Oh, please don’t frighten me like that. I thought I’d gotten it wrong again.”
She laughed with easy, unaffected warmth.
I had no proof, but she fit the picture in my memory perfectly.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"You're Shiki-sama, aren't you?"
"Eh--Yeah, but you don't have to call me '-sama'."
"You are, right?
Oh, please don't scare me like that!
I was beginning to think I had made another mistake back there."
She gives a good-natured laugh.
I have no basis for this, but she fits the image perfectly.

entries.japanese:
「えっと、その……君、もしかして子供のころ俺たちと一緒に遊んだ子？」
　恐る恐る聞いてみる。
　少女は、ほんとうに嬉しそうな、満面の笑みをうかべた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Um—you wouldn’t happen to be the girl who played with us when we were children?”
I ventured the question timidly.
The girl’s whole face lit with genuine delight.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Um… uh… could it be that you're the girl who played together with us when we were small?"
I inquire tentatively.
She gives a full smile, looking truly happy.

entries.japanese:
「さ、お疲れでしょう？
　遠慮せずにあがってくださいな。
居間で秋葉さまもお待ちになってらっしゃいますから」
　少女はさっさとロビーを横切って居間へと歩いていく。
　……と、少女は思い出したようにくるりと振り返ると、満面の笑みをうかべてお辞儀をした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Come in. You must be tired. Miss Akiha is waiting for you in the sitting room.”
She set off briskly across the lobby toward the sitting room.
Then, as though suddenly remembering something, she spun around, bowed, and gave me a radiant smile.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Come; you must be tired, right?
Please do come in.
Akiha-sama is waiting for you in the sitting room."
The girl quickly crosses the lobby and heads towards the sitting room.
Turning back as if she just remembered something, she makes a bow, a full smile on her face.

entries.japanese:
「お帰りなさい志貴さま。
どうぞ、今日からよろしくお願いします」
　少女の挨拶は、本当に華のような笑顔だった。
　それに何ひとつ気のきいた言葉も返せず、おずおずと彼女の後についていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Welcome home, Master Shiki. I look forward to serving you from now on.”
Her greeting came with a smile like a flower in bloom.
Unable to think of anything remotely clever to say, I followed her with faltering steps.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Welcome home, Shiki-sama."
Her greeting is accompanied by her flower-like smile.
I can't think of any reply, so I just follow her hesitantly.

entries.japanese:
少女に案内されて居間へ移動する。
 ───居間は、初めて見るような気がした。
　八年前の事で覚えていないのか、それともあれから内装を変えでもしたのか。
　とにかく他人の家のようで落ち着かない。
　きょろきょろと居間の様子を見回していると、割烹着のお手伝いさんがペコリと頭をさげていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
The girl led me into the sitting room.
───I felt as if I had never seen the room before.
Perhaps eight years had erased it from my memory, or perhaps it had been redecorated.
Whatever the reason, I felt like a guest in a stranger’s house.
While I stood there looking around, the maid in the house apron bowed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Guided by the girl, I head to the sitting room.
---It's as if I'm seeing it for the first time.
I don't know if I've forgotten about it in the last eight years or if they had it refurbished since then.
Either way, it feels like someone else's house now, and it's unsettling.
As I'm looking around the sitting room, the maid in the apron lowers her head in a quick bow.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さまをお連れしました」
「ごくろうさま。
厨房に戻っていいわよ、琥珀」
「はい」
　お手伝いさんはコハク、という名前らしい。
　琥珀さんはそれでは、とこっちにも小さくおじぎをして居間から出ていく。
　残されたのは自分と───見覚えのない、二人の少女だけだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’ve brought Master Shiki.”
“Thank you. You may return to the kitchen, Kohaku.”
“Yes.”
So her name was Kohaku.
With another small bow in my direction, she excused herself and left.
That left me alone with two girls I did not recognize.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I've brought Shiki-sama with me."
"Well done.
You may return to the kitchen, Kohaku."
"Thank you."
It seems that maid's name is Kohaku.
Kohaku-san gives a small bow, as if to say farewell, and leaves the sitting room.
This leaves me, and--two girls I don't recognize.

entries.japanese:
「お久しぶりですね、兄さん」
　長い黒髪の少女は凛とした眼差しのまま、そんな言葉を口にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“It has been a long time, Brother.”
The long-haired girl spoke without relaxing her proud, steady gaze.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"It has been a long time, Nii-san,"
says the girl with the long black hair and sharp eyes.

entries.japanese:
……はっきりいって、思考は完っ全に停止してしまっている。
　真っ白な頭はろくに挨拶もできず、ああ、とうなずく事しかできない。
　……だって、そりゃあ仕方ないと思う。
　八年ぶりに見た秋葉は、こちらの記憶にある秋葉ではなく、まるっきり良家のお嬢様と化していたんだから。
entries.maoEnglish:
To be perfectly honest, my mind had stopped dead.
My head was blank; I could not even manage a greeting, only nod and mumble, ‘Right.’
Who could blame me?
After eight years, the Akiha standing before me was nothing like the one I remembered; she had become, in every particular, a young woman of impeccable breeding.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… All my thought processes stop at once.
My mind goes blank, and I can't think of any words of greeting.
All I can do is nod with a "Yeah."
…… I don't think it can be helped.
This Akiha that I had not seen in eight years is not the Akiha I remember.
She's completely transformed into a proper young lady of a noble family.

entries.japanese:
「兄さん？」
　黒髪の少女はかすかに首をかしげる。
「あ────いや」
　情けないことに間の抜けた言葉しか言えない。
　こっちは目前の少女を秋葉と認識するために頭脳をフル回転させてるっていうのに、秋葉のほうはとっくに俺を兄と認識出来てしまっているようだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Brother?”
The black-haired girl tilted her head.
“Ah—no.”
Pathetically, that was the best I could manage.
I was working my brain to exhaustion trying to recognize the girl before me as Akiha, while she had apparently recognized her brother at once.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Nii-san?"
The black-haired girl tilts her head slightly.
"Ah… um."
Pathetically, all I can say are dumb-sounding things.
My mind is turning in somersaults as I try to recognize the girl before me as Akiha, but it seems like Akiha already recognizes me as her brother.

entries.japanese:
「なにか気分が悪そうですね。
お話の前にお休みになりますか？」
　秋葉はじろりとした視線を向けてくる。
　……なんだか、すごく不機嫌そうに見えるのは気のせいなんだろうか。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You don’t look well. Would you like to rest before we speak?”
Akiha fixed me with a hard stare.
Was I imagining it, or did she seem extremely displeased?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"You do not look well.
Would you like to rest before we talk?"
Akiha throws a sharp glance in my direction.
…… Is it just my imagination that she looks like she's in a bad mood?

entries.japanese:
「……いや、別に気分は悪くない。
ただその、秋葉があんまりにも変わってたんで、びっくりしただけなんだ」
「八年も経てば変わります。
ただでさえ私たちは成長期だったんですから。
　――――それともいつまでも以前のままだと思っていたんですか、兄さんは」
　……なんだろう。
秋葉の言葉は、なんとなく棘があるような気がする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“No, I feel fine. It’s just—you’ve changed so much that I was startled.”
“Eight years will change a person. We were both still growing, after all.
――――Or did you imagine I would remain exactly as you left me, Brother?”
What was this? There seemed to be a barb hidden in everything Akiha said.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… No, I'm alright.
I was just surprised at how much you've changed, Akiha."
"People do change over the course of eight years, Nii-san.
We are at an age of change--or did you think we'd remain like back then forever?"
…… What is this?
…… I can feel the thorns in Akiha's words.

entries.japanese:
「いや、それにしたって秋葉は変わったよ。
昔より格段に美人になった」
　お世辞ではなく素直に感想をもらす。
 ────と。
「ええ。
ですが、兄さんは以前とあまり変わりませんね」
　なんて、瞳を閉じたまま秋葉は冷たく言い切った。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Even so, you really have changed. You’re much more beautiful than you used to be.”
It was no flattery; I simply said what I thought.
────And then.
“Yes. But you have hardly changed at all, Brother.”
Eyes closed, Akiha delivered the verdict with glacial finality.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No, you've definitely changed, Akiha.
You've become more beautiful than before."
That isn't flattery.
It's how I really feel.
---And.
"Indeed.
But you, on the other hand, have not changed much at all."
Akiha answers coldly, her eyes closed.

entries.japanese:
「………………」
　……まあ、それなりに覚悟はしていたけど。
　やはり秋葉は俺の事をよく思っていてはくれなかったみたいだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
Well, I had been braced for this.
It seemed Akiha had not forgiven me after all.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……"
…… Well, I came prepared for something like this.
It is as I had thought.
It seems Akiha does not think well of me.

entries.japanese:
「体調がいいなら話をすませましょうか。
兄さん、詳しい事情は聞いてないんでしょう？」
「詳しい事情もなにも、突然屋敷に帰ってこいって事だけしか聞いてない。
親父が亡くなったっていうのは新聞で知ったけど」
entries.maoEnglish:
“If you feel well enough, let us settle the matter at hand. Brother, you haven’t been told the details, have you?”
“What details, when all I heard was that I was suddenly supposed to come back? I learned Father had died from the newspaper.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"If you are feeling well, let us finish our conversation.
You have yet to hear the details about why you were called back here, Nii-san?"
"I've heard nothing more than a sudden 'Come back to the mansion', though I found out in the papers the old man passed away."

entries.japanese:
……一企業のトップに立っていた人物が亡くなれば、それぐらい経済新聞で取りあげられる。
　遠野槙久の訃報は、彼の葬式が終わった後に新聞づてで息子である遠野志貴に届けられた。
　親戚から報せなんてなくても、勘当された息子は一部百円のペーパーで親の死亡を知ることができた。
　皮肉な話だけれど、本当に便利な世の中になったもんだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
When the head of a company dies, it warrants at least a notice in the financial press.
The news of Makihisa Tohno’s death reached his son, Shiki Tohno, by newspaper—after the funeral was already over.
No message from the family was necessary; for a hundred yen, a disowned son could learn that his father had died.
Ironic, perhaps, but what a wonderfully convenient age we live in.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… If the head of a major company dies, it definitely makes it in the financial papers.
Word of Tohno Makihisa's death reached his son, Tohno Shiki, via the newspaper after the funeral.
Even though his relatives hadn't told him, this disinherited son could pick up news of his father's death merely by buying a one hundred yen newspaper.
It might be cynical of me to say so, but the world has certainly become a convenient place.

entries.japanese:
「……申し訳ありません。
お父さまの事を兄さんに報せなかったのはこちらの失策でした」
　秋葉は静かに頭をさげる。
「いいよ。
どのみち俺が行ったって死人が生き返るわけでもないし。
秋葉が気にする事じゃない」
「……ごめんなさい。
そういってもらえると少しは気が楽になるわ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’m sorry. Failing to inform you of Father’s death was an oversight on our part.”
Akiha bowed her head in silence.
“It’s all right. Even if I’d been there, the dead would not have come back to life. This is nothing you need to worry about.”
“I’m sorry… but hearing you say that does make me feel a little better.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I am sorry.
It was my fault that you did not get the news about Father."
Akiha quietly lowers her head.
"It's alright.
Either way, it's not like he would come back from the dead if I went.
It's not something you should be worried about."
"…… I am sorry.
It is somewhat comforting to hear you say that."

entries.japanese:
秋葉は深刻な顔をするけど、そんなのは本当にどうでもいい話だった。
　葬式というものは故人に対して感情を断ち切れない人達が、その感情を断ち切るために行う儀式だ。
とうの昔に感情を断ってきた自分とあの父親の場合、葬式の必要はないと思う。
entries.maoEnglish:
Akiha looked grave, but the whole matter truly meant nothing to me.
A funeral is a rite for those who cannot release their feelings for the dead, meant to help them finally let go. My father and I had severed those feelings long ago; in our case, there was no need for a funeral.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Akiha's face is serious, but this is not a topic I care much about.
A funeral is a ceremony for those who cannot not detach their feelings for the deceased to achieve such detachment.
For someone like me, who cut off such feelings a long time ago, there is no need.

entries.japanese:
「兄さんをこちらに呼び戻したのは私の意向です。
いつまでも遠野の長男が有間の家に預けられているのはおかしいでしょう？
　お父さまが亡くなられた以上、遠野の血筋は私と兄さんだけです。
お父さまがどのようなお考えで兄さんを有間の家に預けたかは分かりませんが、そのお父さまもすでに他界なさった身。
　ですからこれ以上兄さんが有間の家に預けられる必要はなくなったので、こちらに戻ってもらう事にしたんです」
entries.maoEnglish:
“It was my decision to bring you back. The eldest Tohno son cannot remain indefinitely in the care of the Arima family, can he?
With Father dead, you and I are the only Tohnos left by blood. I don’t know what he intended when he sent you to the Arimas, but he is no longer here.
There is no reason for you to remain in their care, so I decided that you would return home.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Calling you back here was my idea.
It would be odd for the eldest son of the Tohnos to be entrusted to the Arimas forever.
Now that Father has passed away, the only Tohnos by blood are you and I, Nii-san.
I don't know what Father was thinking when he entrusted you to the Arimas, but he's no longer with us, so there's no longer any need for you to live with them.
That is why I had you come back here."

entries.japanese:
「……まあいいけど、そんなんでよく親戚の連中が納得したな。
俺を有間の家に預けろって言い出したの、たしか親戚の人たちじゃなかったっけ？」
entries.maoEnglish: “Fine, but I’m surprised the relatives agreed. Weren’t they the ones who demanded I be sent to the Arimas in the first place?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… That's all well and good, but I'm quite surprised you were able to get our relatives to agree to this.
Wasn't it they who came up with the idea of leaving me with the Arimas in the first place?"

entries.japanese:
「そうですね。
けれど今の遠野の当主は私です。
親戚の方達の進言はすべて却下しました。
「兄さんにはこれからここで暮らしてもらいたいのですけど、ここにはここの規律があります。
今までのような無作法はさけていただきますから、そのつもりで」
entries.maoEnglish:
“They were. However, I am now head of the Tohno family. I rejected every one of their objections.
“I want you to live here from now on, but this household has rules of its own. I will not tolerate the discourtesies you have allowed yourself until now; remember that.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"That may be so, but now I am the head of the Tohno family.
I declined every one of the proposals from our relatives.
I would like you to continue living here, Nii-san, but this is a place with rules.
You will avoid living the overly casual lifestyle you've been leading up until now."

entries.japanese:
「はは、そりゃあ無理だよ秋葉。
いまさら俺がお行儀いい人間に戻れるわけないし、戻ろうって気もないんだから」
「できる範囲でけっこうですから努力してください。
それとも───私にできた事が兄さんにはできない、とおっしゃるんですか？」
　じろり、と秋葉は冷たい視線を向けてくる。
　なんだか無言で、八年間もここに置き去りにしてきた恨みをぶつけられている気がする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ha, that’s asking the impossible, Akiha. It’s far too late for me to become well behaved again—and I have no desire to try.”
“Then make whatever effort lies within your power. Or are you claiming that what I could do is beyond you?”
Akiha gave me another icy look.
Without saying a word, she seemed to be hurling eight years of resentment at me for leaving her here alone.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Haha.
I'm afraid that isn't going to happen, Akiha.
There's no way I can go back to being some well-mannered gentleman now.
Not that I want to."
"I will not ask more of you, but do try to--or are you saying you are unable to do what I already have?"
Akiha shoots me a cold look.
It feels like she's hitting me with her grudge against me for leaving her here for the last eight years.

entries.japanese:
「……オーケー、わかった。
なんとか努力はしてみる」
　秋葉はじーっ、と信用できなさそうに睨んでくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“All right, all right. I’ll do my best.”
Akiha stared at me as though she believed none of it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Alright.
I get it.
I'll try my best."
Akiha just stares at me, as if she doesn't quite believe me.

entries.japanese:
「努力する必要はありません。
結果を出していただければそれで結構です」
　凛、とした姿勢のまま、秋葉は容赦のない言葉を繰り出してくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I have no interest in your efforts. Results will be sufficient.”
