“I shall take my leave, then. Please retire for the night.”
Hisui bowed and reached for the doorknob.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Anyhow, that's how it is.
Don't be so formal towards me.
I'll be grateful if you'd tell that to your sister Kohaku-san, too."
"Very well, as you say, Shiki-sama."
Expressionless, Hisui bows her head.
She completely failed to understand.
"I will be leaving now.
Please rest now for tonight."
Bowing, Hisui puts her hand on the doorknob.

entries.japanese:
────と、一つ聞き忘れていた。
「あ、ちょっと待った」
　ドアに走り寄って、立ち去ろうとする翡翠の肩に手を置いた。
　瞬間────翡翠の腕が、物凄い勢いで俺の腕を払った。
entries.maoEnglish:
────And then I remembered one last question.
“Oh, wait a second.”
I hurried to the door and put a hand on Hisui’s shoulder as she was leaving.
In that instant, Hisui knocked my arm away with astonishing force.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Oh, I forgot to ask something.
"Ah, hold on for a second."
Running towards the door, I put my hand on Hisui's shoulder before she leaves.
In an instant---Hisui's arm pushes away my arm with incredible momentum.

entries.japanese:
バシ、と音をたてて手がはたかれて、翡翠は逃げるように後退する。
「え────」
　あんまりに突然のことで、そんな言葉しかだせない。
　翡翠は無表情のまま、けれどたしかに、仇を見るような激しさでこちらを睨んでいる────
entries.maoEnglish:
The slap cracked through the room, and Hisui sprang back as though fleeing from me.
“What────”
It happened so suddenly that no other word would come.
Hisui’s face remained expressionless, but she was unmistakably glaring at me with the ferocity one reserves for a hated enemy────
entries.mirrorMoon:
With a 'whack!', she slaps my hand away and leaps back.
"Eh---?"
It's so sudden, that's the only thing I can say.
Hisui is expressionless, but she glares at me fiercely.

entries.japanese:
「えっと―――俺、なにかわるいことしちゃったかな」
「あ……」
「……申し訳、ございません……」
　緊張のまじった翡翠の声。
「……体を触れられるのには、慣れていないのです。
どうか、お許しください」
　翡翠の肩はかすかに震えている。
　なんだか、ものすごく悪いことをしてしまったような気がする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Um―――did I do something wrong?”
“Ah……”
“I am terribly sorry…”
Tension threaded Hisui’s voice.
“I am not accustomed to being touched. Please forgive me.”
Her shoulders trembled faintly.
Somehow, I felt as though I had done something truly awful.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Eh… Did I just do something wrong?"
"Ah…"
"…… I am very sorry…"
Hisui's voice sounds very nervous.
"…… I am not used to being touched.
Please forgive me."
Hisui's shoulders are faintly trembling.
I feel like I just did something really terrible.

entries.japanese:
「あ───うん、ごめん」
　思わず謝った。
　自分でもよくわからない。
ただ翡翠が可哀相に思えて、ペコリと頭をさげていた。
「──────」
　翡翠は何も言わない。
　ただ、心なし視線が穏やかなものになった気がする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh—yes, sorry.”
The apology came out before I knew it.
I could not have explained why. She simply looked so pitiful that I found myself bowing to her.
“──────”
Hisui said nothing.
Still, I thought her gaze softened a little.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah… Yeah, I'm sorry."
I apologize without thinking.
I don't understand why myself.
I just feel sorry for Hisui and I lower my head.
"------"
Hisui says nothing.
I get the feeling her stare is calm again.

entries.japanese:
「───志貴さまが謝られる事はありません。
非があるのはわたしのほうです」
「いや、まあそうみたいなんだけど、なんとなく」
　ぽりぽりと頭をかく。
　翡翠はじっと俺の顔を見つめてから、一瞬だけ目を伏せた。
「その……ご用件はなんでしょうか、志貴さま」
　そうだった。
　部屋を立ち去る翡翠を呼び止めたのは聞きたい事があったからだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“───You have no reason to apologize, Master Shiki. The fault was mine.”
“I suppose you’re right, but somehow—” I scratched my head.
Hisui studied my face, then lowered her eyes for a fleeting moment.
“What did you need, Master Shiki?”
Oh, right.
I had stopped her because there was something I wanted to ask.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---You have nothing to apologize for, Shiki-sama.
I am the one to blame."
"No, well, maybe, but I just…"
I scratch my head.
Hisui stares at me, pausing only to blink for a second.
"Um… What was it you wanted to ask me, Shiki-sama?"
That's right.
I stopped Hisui because I wanted to ask her something.

entries.japanese:
「いや、秋葉はどうしてるのか気になってさ。
あいつ、全寮制の学校に行ってたんじゃなかったっけ？」
「志貴さま、それは中学校までの話です。
秋葉さまは今年から特例として自宅からの登校を許可されていらっしゃいます」
「……えっと、つまりこの家から学校に行ってるってコト？」
「はい。
ですが、今日のように夕方に帰られる事は稀です。
秋葉さまは夕食の時間まで習い事がありますから、お帰りになられるのは決まって七時前です」
entries.maoEnglish:
“I was wondering about Akiha. Didn’t she attend a boarding school?”
“Master Shiki, that was only through middle school. Beginning this year, Miss Akiha has been granted special permission to commute from home.”
“So she commutes from this house?”
“Yes. However, it is rare for her to return as early as she did today. Miss Akiha has lessons until dinnertime, so she ordinarily arrives just before seven.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Oh, I wanted to ask about Akiha.
Doesn't she go to a boarding school?"
"That was only during middle school, Shiki-sama.
From this year onwards, Akiha-sama has special permission to attend school from home."
"Eh… You mean she goes to school from here?"
"Yes, but it is uncommon for her to come home before dusk like today.
Akiha-sama has practice up until dinner, so she is always home before seven.

entries.japanese:
「習い事って―――それ、なに？」
「今日は木曜日ですのでヴァイオリンの稽古でした」
「────え」
「平日は夕食前には戻られますから、秋葉さまにお話があるのでしたら夕食後に姉さんに申し付けてください」
　では、と翡翠は頭をさげてから部屋を出ていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Lessons―――what kind?”
“Today was Thursday, so she had violin practice.”
“────What—”
“She returns before dinner on weekdays, so if you wish to speak with Miss Akiha, please ask my sister after the meal.”
With that, Hisui bowed and left the room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Practice?---Practice what?"
"Today is Thursday, so she would have had violin practice."
"----Eh?"
"Usually, she is able to return before dinner on weekdays, so if you have anything to say to Akiha-sama, please let Nee-san know after dinner."
Hisui bows to say goodbye, and leaves the room.

entries.japanese:
「ヴァイオリンの、稽古」
　なんだろう、それは。
　どこかのお嬢様じゃあるまいし、なんだってそんな面倒なことを―――
「……って、どこかのお嬢様だったんだ、あいつ」
　そう、そういえば遠野志貴の妹は遠野秋葉という、生粋のお嬢様だったっけ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Violin lessons.”
What was that about?
It wasn’t as though she were some pampered young lady, so why bother with something so―――
“Oh—right; she is a pampered young lady.”
Right—come to think of it, Shiki Tohno’s little sister was Akiha Tohno, a young lady born and bred.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Violin practice…"
What on earth is that?
She's not some upper-class lady or anything, so why should she have to do something as bothersome as---
"…… Oh wait, she is an upper-class lady."
Yes.
Come to think of it, my sister, Tohno Akiha, is a natural born upper-class lady.

entries.japanese:
こっちの記憶の中じゃ秋葉は大人しくて、いつも不安げな瞳で俺のあとをついてくる一歳年下の妹だった。
　子供の頃の秋葉は無口で、自分のやりたい事も口にだせないほど弱気で、いつも父親である遠野槙久に叱られないかっておどおどしていた線の細い女の子だったのに。
「───そうだよな。
八年も経てば人間だってガラリと変わる」
　自分が八年間で今の遠野志貴になったように、
　秋葉もこの八年間で今の遠野秋葉になったんだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
In my memories, Akiha was my quiet little sister, one year younger, always trailing behind me with anxious eyes.
As a child she had been frail and timid, too shy even to say what she wanted, forever frightened that her father, Makihisa Tohno, might scold her.
“───Of course. Eight years is enough to change anyone completely.”
Just as those eight years had made me into Shiki Tohno,
they must have made Akiha into Akiha Tohno as well.
entries.mirrorMoon:
In my memories, she was always the obedient, ever-uneasy sister constantly following me around.
As a child, she was always quiet, never having even the courage to express her own desires.
She was a frail girl who would always live in fear of a scolding from our father.
"---Yeah, people really do change after eight years."
After eight years, I've become the me I am now.
Akiha has become the person she is right now, too.

entries.japanese:
―――八年間は、長い。
　今までの人生の半分。
　それも子供から大人になろうと成長しようとする一番大切な時期に、俺はこの屋敷にいなかった。
「……ごめんな、秋葉」
　その八年間を一緒にいてやれたらどんなに良かったろう、と思えて。
　知らず、そんな謝罪の言葉を呟いた。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Eight years is a long time.
Half my life so far.
I had been absent from this house during the years that mattered most—the years when a child struggled to become an adult.
“I’m sorry, Akiha.”
If only I could have been there beside her through those eight years.
The thought brought the apology unbidden to my lips.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Eight years is a long time.
It's half of our lives up until now.
I was absent from this mansion during that vital period where a child becomes an adult.
"…… I'm sorry, Akiha."
I think things would have been better if I had been with her during those eight years.
I unknowingly mumble an apology.

entries.japanese:
……えっと、琥珀さんの部屋は……ここかな？
　コンコン、と扉をノックする。
「琥珀さん、います？」
「はーい、ちょっと待ってくださいねー」
　部屋の中から陽気な声が聞こえてくる。
　待つ事三分弱。
　扉が開いて琥珀さんが顔を出してきた。
entries.maoEnglish:
Now, was this Kohaku’s room?
I knocked twice.
“Kohaku, are you in there?”
“Coming—just a minute!”
Her cheerful voice floated through the door.
I waited just under three minutes.
The door opened and Kohaku poked her head out.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Let's see… Kohaku-san's room is… here, isn't it?
Knock knock.
I knock on her door.
"Kohaku-san, are you there?"
"Yes, please hold on for a minute."
I can hear her cheerful voice from inside the room.
I wait for about three minutes.
Kohaku-san opens the door and pokes her head out.

entries.japanese:
「あれ、志貴さまじゃないですか。
どうしたんです、こんな時間に？」
「えっと、その―――テレビを見せてもらおうかなって」
「へ？」
　ぽかん、と目を白黒させる琥珀さん。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh, Master Shiki! What brings you here at this hour?”
“Um, well―――I thought maybe I could watch television with you.”
“What?”
Kohaku stared at me, blinking in astonishment.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Oh, it's you, Shiki-sama.
What are you doing here at this time?"
"Uh… well---I was wondering if you'd let me watch your TV…"
"Eh?"
Kohaku-san gives me a bewildered look.

entries.japanese:
「あ、そのですね、この家ってテレビがないでしょ？
　今まで普通の家で暮らしてきた俺にしてみると、夕食後のテレビを見るのは日課だったりするわけで、見ないと落ち着かないというか、その……」
　……口にすればするほど、自分がとんでもなくバカな真似をしているんだと気がついた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Well, there aren’t any televisions anywhere else in the house, and watching after-dinner television was part of my routine until yesterday. Without it I can’t quite settle down, so—”
The longer I talked, the more painfully aware I became of how idiotic I sounded.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah… well, there's no TV in this house, is there?
I've been living in a normal house up until now, so it's become a daily routine for me to watch TV after dinner.
I guess I can't calm down without watching it or something like that, so…"
…… The more I say it, the more I realize I'm doing something stupid.

entries.japanese:
テレビを見せてくれ、なんて言って女の人の部屋にあがりこもうなんて、本当にどうかしてる。
　見ろ、琥珀さんだって目を白黒させたまま呆れて―――ないや。
「あはは、そういえばそうですよね。
志貴さまは昨日まで有間のお屋敷で暮らしていたんですもの。
いきなりではこのお屋敷の空気は重かったでしょう？」
　琥珀さんは陽気に笑いかけてくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
Trying to invite myself into a woman’s room on the pretext of watching television—what on earth was wrong with me?
Just look at Kohaku: she was still staring, appalled by my behavior—or perhaps not.
“Ahaha, of course! Master Shiki was living at the Arima estate until yesterday. Being dropped into this estate all at once must have felt terribly oppressive.”
Kohaku beamed at me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
There is something not right about barging into a lady's room demanding to watch her TV.
Look, even Kohaku-san is just standing there, looking bewilder---wait, no she's not.
"Ahaha, I guess you're right.
You've been living at the Arima household up until yesterday, after all.
You must think this mansion to be kind of depressing after moving here all of a sudden."
Kohaku-san gives a cheerful laugh.

entries.japanese:
「えっとですね……このコト、秋葉さまと翡翠ちゃんに話しちゃいました？」
「このコトって、琥珀さんの部屋に行くってこと？」
　はい、と頷く琥珀さん。
「いや、誰にも話してないけど、それがどうしたんですか？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Did you happen to tell Miss Akiha or Hisui about this?”
“About coming to your room?”
Kohaku nodded.
“No, I told no one; why do you ask?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Eh, let's see… Have you talked to Akiha-sama and Hisui-chan about this yet?"
"You mean about coming to your room, Kohaku-san?"
Kohaku-san nods.
"No, I haven't talked to anyone about it yet.
What about it?"

entries.japanese:
「いえいえ、もしお話されていたら志貴さまを追い返さないといけないなって、そんな感じです」
　笑顔のまま言って、琥珀さんはきょろきょろと廊下を見渡す。
「さいわいあたりに人影なし。
ささ、見つかるとタイヘンですから早くあがってくださいな」
　ぐっ、と琥珀さんはこっちの腕を掴む。
「えっ、ちょ、ちょっと琥珀さん……！」
entries.maoEnglish:
“No, no—if you had, I would have had to send Master Shiki away.”
Still smiling, Kohaku peered up and down the corridor.
“Fortunately, there’s no one in sight. Quickly now—come in before we’re caught.”
Her hand closed firmly around my arm.
“W-wait, Kohaku…!”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No, no, it's nothing.
It's just that I would have to turn you away if you had already talked to them about it."
Smiling while she speaks, Kohaku-san looks up and down the hallway.
"Luckily for us, there isn't anyone else around.
Please hurry up and come in.
It'll be troublesome if we're caught."

entries.japanese:
「適当な所に座ってください。
わたし、お茶を淹れてきますから」
「…………」
　こほん、と咳払いをしてから座る。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Sit wherever you like. I’ll make us some tea.”
“……”
I cleared my throat and sat down.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Please, just sit anywhere.
I'll go make some tea."
"……"
Coughing to clear my throat, I take a seat.

entries.japanese:
琥珀さんの部屋はたくさんの小物がある。
　女の子の部屋にしては散らかっている方なのかもしれない。
可愛い、という小物はあんまりなくて、あるのはあまり役に立ちそうにない物ばかりだ。
　……どっちかっていうと、整理整頓が好きな学者さんの部屋みたいな雰囲気がする。
entries.maoEnglish:
Kohaku’s room was crowded with little objects.
Perhaps it was rather messy for a girl’s room. Almost none of them were what one might call cute; most looked as if they had no practical use whatsoever.
The place felt less like a girl’s bedroom than the study of an unusually tidy scholar.
entries.mirrorMoon:
There are all sorts of little things in Kohaku-san's room.
It might be thought of as a bit messy for a girl's room.
There aren't really many things you could call cute, and what she does have is a lot of things that don't look very useful.
…… Rather, it has an atmosphere of a room belonging to an orderly, scholarly person.

entries.japanese:
色々とある雑多な品物。
　その中にうずもれるようにテレビがあるのを発見した。
　テーブルの上にはリモコンがある。
……琥珀さんも、さっきまでテレビを見ていたのだろうか。
entries.maoEnglish:
There were miscellaneous objects everywhere.
Half buried among them, I found the television.
Its remote lay on the table. Had Kohaku been watching it before I arrived?
entries.mirrorMoon:
Buried in the miscellaneous objects, I find the TV.
On top of the table is the remote… maybe Kohaku-san has been watching the TV until just now.

entries.japanese:
「はい、お待たせしました。
お茶でいいですよね、志貴さま」
「あ、どうも。
その、おかまいなく」
「いえいえ、こちらこそ気の利いたおもてなしは出来そうになくてすみません」
　琥珀さんはニッコリとした笑顔で言う。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Here we are. Tea is all right, isn’t it, Master Shiki?”
“Oh, thanks. You really didn’t have to fuss.”
“Not at all—I should apologize for having nothing better to offer.”
Kohaku said it with a radiant smile.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Thanks for waiting.
Tea is fine for you, isn't it, Shiki-sama?"
"Ah, thank you.
Please don't mind me too much."
"Oh no, not at all.
I'm sorry I can't do much to treat you."
Kohaku-san says so, smiling warmly.

entries.japanese:
「テレビでしたね。
志貴さまはこの時間、なにを観ているんですか？」
「とくに決まってないけど、基本的にはニュースかな。
わりとミーハーでさ、スノッブな話が好きなんだ」
「そうなんですか。
志貴さまは落ち着いていますから食後は読書をなさるのかな、なんて思ってたんですけど」
「あはは、そんな優雅な趣味はしてないよ。
自分では落ち着いているって気もしないんだけど、メガネをかけてるとそういうイメージが先行するのかもしれないね」
entries.maoEnglish:
“You came for television, didn’t you? What does Master Shiki usually watch at this hour?”
“Nothing in particular; mostly the news, I suppose. I’m a sucker for whatever is current, especially fashionable nonsense.”
“Really? Master Shiki seems so composed that I imagined you spent your evenings reading.”
“Ahaha, I’m not nearly that refined, and I don’t think I’m particularly composed either. Maybe the glasses just give people that impression.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"So, the TV.
What do you watch at around this time, Shiki-sama?"
"I don't have any set programs in particular, but the news is a pretty basic one.
I like to hear new trends, and I like snob stories."
"Is that so?
You seem like a very laid-back person, so I thought you'd be reading after dinner or something."
"Ahaha, no, I don't have such refined interests.
I don't consider myself laid-back either, but maybe that's the impression I give with my glasses."

entries.japanese:
「――あっ、志貴さまメガネをかけてたんですよね。
秋葉さまは志貴さまがメガネをかけているなんて一言もおっしゃいませんでしたから、お迎えにあがった時はびっくりしました」
　……そうか。
このメガネをかけてから、秋葉には直接会ってはいないんだっけ。

「けど、このメガネは伊達メガネなんだ。
目が悪いっていえば悪いんだけどね、視力は人よりいい方だと思う。
別に勉強のしすぎで視力が落ちたわけじゃない……って、ああ、しまった。
知的なイメージがあったのに、幻滅させた？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“――Oh, that’s right—Master Shiki wears glasses now. Miss Akiha never mentioned that Master Shiki wore glasses, so I was quite surprised when I came to meet you.”
Of course. I had not seen Akiha in person since I began wearing them.
“They’re only plain glass. Something is wrong with my eyes, but not my eyesight; I can probably see better than most people. I didn’t ruin my vision by studying too hard, either. Ah—did I just shatter your image of me as an intellectual?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Ah!
You wear glasses, Shiki-sama.
Akiha-sama didn't say anything about that at all, so I was quite surprised when I saw you at the door."
…… I see.
I haven't met Akiha since I started wearing these glasses.
"These glasses are just for show.
I guess you could say my eyes are bad, but I think my vision is better than that of most people.
It's not because I studied too much and went near-sighted or anything… Ah, crap.
I had an intellectual image, but did I disappoint you?"

entries.japanese:
「そんなことはないですよ。
わたしだって本よりテレビのほうが楽しいですもの。
志貴さまが思ったとおりの元気な方で、嬉しいです」
「あ……うん、どうも」
　なんか、照れる。
　琥珀さんは真正面から屈託のない笑顔を向けてきて、ついドキマギしてしまう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Not at all. I enjoy television more than books myself. I’m glad Master Shiki turned out to be just as lively as I imagined.”
“Oh—well, thanks.”
That was embarrassing.
Kohaku’s open, unguarded smile struck me head-on and left me flustered.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Not at all.
I enjoy watching TV more than reading, too.
I'm glad that you're an energetic person, just like I thought you were."
"Ah… yeah, thanks."
I'm a little embarrassed.
Faced directly with Kohaku-san's carefree smile, I can't help but feel a little nervous.

entries.japanese:
「あ、ごめんなさい。
ニュースを観にこられたんですよね、志貴さまは」
　琥珀さんはテレビのスウィッチをオンにする。
　時刻はすでに夜の九時。
　ニュースはいつもどおりの、少し大げさな手振りで一日の事件を報道している。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh, I’m sorry. Master Shiki came to watch the news, didn’t he?”
Kohaku switched on the television.
It was already nine.
As usual, the news was presenting the day’s events with gestures just a little too dramatic.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah, I'm sorry.
You came to watch the news, didn't you?"
Kohaku-san switches the TV on.
It's already nine o'clock.
The news, as it usually does, reports the day's events with a little exaggeration.

entries.japanese:
「ありゃ。
また通り魔殺人ですか」
　琥珀さんはとなりに俺がいるのに、まったく気にした風もなく独り言を言う。
　ニュースは、ちょうど連続通り魔殺人を特集していた。
　となり街から始まった通り魔殺人は、現在この街で集中的に起こっている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh dear. Another random street killing?”
Though I was sitting beside her, Kohaku murmured to herself without the least self-consciousness.
The news was covering the string of random street killings.
The attacks had begun in the neighboring city, but lately they were concentrated here.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Oh dear.
Looks like there's been another one of those serial murders."
Kohaku-san says to herself while sitting next to me, sounding not the least bit concerned.
The news is running a special feature on the serial killings.
The serial murders, which began in the neighboring town, are now beginning to be concentrated within this town.

entries.japanese:
内容は単純なものだ。
　深夜、出歩いている若い女性を無差別に拉致して殺害、最後に血液を抜き取る、なんていう真似をしている。
　被害者は昨夜で九人目になってしまったらしい。
entries.maoEnglish:
The pattern was simple.
Young women out late at night were abducted at random, murdered, and finally drained of their blood.
Last night’s victim had apparently been the ninth.
entries.mirrorMoon:
It's a pretty simple story.
Late at night, he attacks young girls indiscriminately, and in the end, he drains their blood.
It seems like last night's victim is the ninth one so far.

entries.japanese:
「お巡りさんは何をしているんでしょうね」
「どうだろう。
深夜に通り魔が出てくるなら簡単に捕まえられそうなものだけど、犯人はものすごく周到なヤツで尻尾を出さないとか」
entries.maoEnglish:
“What are the police doing?”
“Who knows? You’d think someone who strikes after midnight would be easy to catch, unless the killer is incredibly careful and never leaves a trace.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I wonder what the police are doing about it?"
"Who knows?
It would seem pretty easy to catch a murderer who comes out at night, but maybe he's really careful so they can't trace him."

entries.japanese:
「そうかもしれませんね。
殺人は数を重ねれば重ねるほど証拠を残してしまいますから。
九人も殺されてしまっているのに犯人を捕まえられないなんて、よっぽど用意周到な犯人なんでしょう」
「用意周到な通り魔、か。
けど、通り魔って突発的な犯罪じゃない？
　それが用意周到っていうのもおかしな話だけど」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Perhaps. The more murders someone commits, the more evidence they should leave behind. If the police still cannot catch the culprit after nine victims, the killer must be exceptionally meticulous.”
“A meticulous random attacker. Isn’t that a contradiction? These attacks are supposed to be crimes of impulse.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"You could be right.
The clues about murderers build up as they kill more people, so if they haven't caught him even after nine murders, he must be really carefully prepared for the killings."
"A careful killer, huh?
But aren't these killings spontaneous crimes?
It's quite strange to think of them as being carefully prepared."

entries.japanese:
「ですねー。
一切の証拠が残らない時点で通り魔殺人ではないのかもしれません。
はじめから綿密な計画のもとで犯人は犯行を重ねているとしか思えません」
「ああ、なるほどね。
けどさ、それじゃあ殺された九人の女の子って何か意味があるのかな。
友人とか、知り合いとか」
entries.maoEnglish:
“You’re right. If no evidence is ever left behind, perhaps these are not random attacks at all. It seems more likely the culprit has followed a careful plan from the very beginning.”
“I see. Then do those nine girls mean something? Were they friends, or acquaintances?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"You're right.
If there's no evidence left at all, then maybe he's not a random killer at all.
I can only think that he's got it all planned out from the start for execution."
"Ah, I see.
But then what would be the point of killing those nine girls?
Are they friends of his?
Acquaintances?"

entries.japanese:
「うーん、ないんじゃないでしょうか。
そんな繋がりがあったらお巡りさんも気がつくと思います。
　結局のところ、これは目的や関連性のない、極めて理解不能の事件ですねー」
　……琥珀さんは物騒な話題を笑顔で言う。
　琥珀さんはこの事件にはあまり関心はないみたいだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hmm, probably not. If there were a connection, the police would have noticed.
In the end, it is an utterly incomprehensible case, with neither motive nor link between the victims.”
Kohaku discussed the grisly subject with a smile.
She did not seem particularly interested in the case.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hmm… probably not.
If there were connections like that, then I think the police would have realized it by now.
In the end, I suppose it's an incomprehensible case without motive or connections."
…… Kohaku-san says all of this disturbing stuff with a smile.
It seems like she's not really worried about this case.

entries.japanese:
「琥珀さん、これってこの街で起きてる事件なんだよ。
琥珀さんだって若い女の人なんだから、少しは恐いって思うでしょう？」
「大丈夫ですよ。
通り魔さんは深夜に出現するだけですから。
夜は外に出なければ会うこともありません」
　琥珀さんの考えは実にスッキリしている。
　……そう割り切るには少し生々しすぎる気もするのだけど、確かにニュースで知る事件なんてのはそんなものかもしれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Kohaku, this is happening in our city, and you’re a young woman too. Doesn’t it frighten you at least a little?”
“I’ll be perfectly safe. The attacker only appears after midnight. If I don’t go out at night, we’ll never meet.”
Her reasoning was beautifully simple.
The murders felt too immediate for such detachment, but perhaps that was what every tragedy on the news became to people watching from home.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"These murders are happening right here in this town, Kohaku-san.
You're a young girl and all, so aren't you even a little scared?"
"I'll be fine, since the killer only appears late at night.
If I don't go out at night, I won't run into him."
Kohaku-san really is a clear thinker.
…… It is perhaps a bit of a raw explanation, but I suppose that's how a mere news story should be treated.

entries.japanese:
「お邪魔しました。
また観たくなったらやってきますから、よろしく」
「はい、お待ちしております」
　琥珀さんはきょろきょろと廊下を見渡す。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Thanks for having me. I’ll come back whenever I feel like watching again, if that’s all right.”
“Of course—I’ll be waiting.”
Kohaku peered up and down the corridor.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Sorry for intruding on you.
I'll be counting on you again the next time I feel like watching TV."
"Sure, I'll be waiting."
Kohaku-san looks up and down the hallway.

entries.japanese:
「このままお部屋までお送りしたいんですけど、志貴さまのお部屋には翡翠ちゃんが待ってますから、ここで失礼しますね」
「はい。
それじゃ、おやすみなさい」
「……」
　……屋敷の就寝時間が夜の十時なんて、知らなかった。
　この屋敷では十時以降は部屋から出てはいけない、という暗黙のルールがあるらしい。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I would walk you back, but Hisui will be waiting in Master Shiki’s room, so I’ll say good night here.”
“All right. Good night, Kohaku.”
“……”
I had not known everyone in the estate retired at ten.
Apparently an unspoken rule forbade anyone from leaving their room after that hour.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I'd like to escort you back to your room, but Hisui-chan is waiting there, so I'll have to say goodbye here."
"Okay.
Good night."
"……"
…… I had no idea bedtime at the mansion was at ten.
Apparently, there's some kind of unwritten rule here that one is not to be out of their room after ten.

entries.japanese:
「親父がいなくなっても堅苦しいのは変わらないんだ」
　ま、それも当然か。
　こっちも慣れない屋敷の空気に疲れているし、大人しく部屋に戻ろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Even with Father gone, the estate was as rigid as ever.”
Well, I supposed that was only natural.
The unfamiliar atmosphere of the estate had worn me out anyway, so I might as well return quietly to my room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"It's still so formal here, even with the old man gone."
Well, I guess it's only natural.
I'm also getting tired from my unfamiliarity with this mansion, so I obediently return to my room.

entries.japanese:
「あ―――――」
　部屋に戻ってくると、ベッドメイクが済んでいた。
……俺が留守の間に翡翠が済ませてくれたのだろう。
「嬉しいんだけど、なんか身に余るよな、こういうのって」
　ぽりぽりと頬を掻く。
――――――――と。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ah―――――”
When I returned to my room, the bed had already been made. Hisui must have done it while I was out.
“I’m grateful, but this kind of treatment feels wasted on me.”
I scratched my cheek.
――――――――Just then.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah---"
When I return to my room, my bed has been made… Did Hisui do it while I was away?
"I'm glad she did, but it's really more than I deserve."
I scratch my cheek.
------Then.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま、いらっしゃいますか？」
　ノックと一緒に翡翠の声が聞こえてくる。
「いるよ。
どうぞ、中にはいって」
「はい、それでは失礼します」
「こんばんは。
ありがとう翡翠、ベッドメイクしておいてくれたんだろ」
　はい、と静かにうなずく翡翠。
「…………う」
　やっぱり、自分にはこういうのは似合わない。
「……えっと、何かな。
他に伝言でもある？」
「いいえ、わたしからは何も。
ですが秋葉さまから、もし志貴さまから何かあるようでしたらお答えするように、と」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki, are you there?”
Hisui’s voice came through the door with a knock.
“I’m here. Come on in.”
“Yes—excuse me.”
“Good evening. And thank you, Hisui—you made the bed for me, didn’t you?”
Hisui nodded quietly.
“Ngh.”
This sort of thing really did not suit me.
“So, um—what is it? Another message?”
“Not from me. Miss Akiha instructed me to answer any questions Master Shiki might have.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Are you there, Shiki-sama?"
I can hear Hisui's voice along with a knock at the door.
"Yeah, I'm here.
Come in."
"Excuse me."
"Good evening.
Thanks for making my bed, Hisui."
Hisui quietly nods in acceptance.
"…… Urgh."
Just as I thought, I'm not used to this.
"…… Uh… is there anything else you want to tell me?"
"No, nothing from me, but Akiha-sama has instructed me to answer any questions you may have."

entries.japanese:
「……そっか。
	確かに聞きたい事だらけだけど、そんなのは暮らしていくうちに覚えていくもんだしな……」
　うん。
今すぐ、寝る前に知っておきたい事っていったら、それは―――
「それじゃ聞くけど、ここの門限が七時っていうのは本当？」
「はい。
　正確には七時に正門を施錠して、八時に屋敷の出入り口をすべて施錠いたします。
　午後十時を過ぎたあとは屋敷内の移動も控えていただくのが規則です」
entries.maoEnglish:
“I see. There is plenty I want to ask, but I can learn most of it as I settle in.”
Right. If there was one thing I needed to know before bed, it was―――
“Then tell me this: is the curfew really seven?”
“Yes.
To be precise, the main gate is locked at seven and every entrance to the estate at eight.
After ten, the rules require everyone to refrain from moving about the estate.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I see.
There are many things I want to ask, but I'll probably get to know them as I continue to live here……"
Yeah.
What I want to know right now before I sleep is---
"Is it true that the curfew here is seven?"
"Yes.
The main gate is locked at seven, and all the entrances to the mansion are to be locked at eight.
It is also a rule that one must try not to go walking around in the mansion after ten."

entries.japanese:
「屋敷の中も出歩くなっていうのか？
　……まあ文句はないけど、それって厳しすぎないか？
　俺も秋葉も子供じゃないんだから、そこまでしなくてもいいと思うけど」
「……はい。
ですが志貴さま、規則ですからこればかりはお守りください。
近頃の夜は物騒だと志貴さまもご存知ではないのですか？」
　……ああ、有彦がいっていた例の吸血鬼騒ぎか。
　たしかにこの街で連続殺人が起きている以上、用心にこした事はないんだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“We’re not even allowed to walk around inside? I’m not complaining, but isn’t that a little extreme? Akiha and I aren’t children anymore.”
“Yes. But it is a rule, Master Shiki, and I must ask you to observe it. Surely Master Shiki knows how dangerous the nights have become?”
Oh—that vampire panic Arihiko had mentioned.
With a string of murders taking place in the city, I supposed there was no such thing as being too careful.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Not even walking around in the mansion?
…… Well, I've got no complaint with that, but isn't that kind of harsh?
Akiha and I aren't children, so I don't think you have to go that far."
"…… Indeed.
It is a rule, however, so please abide by it.
You are aware of the recent disturbances at night, are you not, Shiki-sama?"
…… Yeah, that vampire thing Arihiko was talking about.
Well, as long as something like that is happening, I guess it's better to be safe than sorry.

entries.japanese:
「あとは……そうだな、あまり関係ない話なんだけど、いいかい？」
「はい、なんでしょう」
「翡翠と琥珀さんがここでどんな仕事をしてるのか知りたいんだけど、どうかな」
「わたしが志貴さま付きで、姉の琥珀は秋葉お嬢さまのお世話をさせていただいています。
　お二人が留守の間は屋敷の管理を任されていますが、それがなにか？」
「……お世話って、やっぱりそういうコトか」
entries.maoEnglish:
“There is one more thing—it is not particularly relevant, but may I ask?”
“Of course.”
“What exactly do you and Kohaku do here?”
“I am assigned to you, Master Shiki, while my sister Kohaku attends Miss Akiha.
When neither of you is home, we are entrusted with managing the estate; is something wrong?”
“So attending her really does mean exactly that—”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"What else… Oh, do you mind if I ask an off-topic question?"
"Yes, what is it?"
"I'd like to know what kind of work you and Kohaku-san do around here."
"I am here to serve Shiki-sama's needs, and my sister Kohaku to serve Lady Akiha-sama.
In our spare time, we do the maintenance chores around the mansion.
Is there anything more you would like to know?"
"…… To serve… So that's what it is after all."

entries.japanese:
がっくりと肩が重くなる。
　秋葉は当然のように言っていたけど、こっちはあくまで普通の高校生だ。
　同い年ぐらいの女の子に世話をしてもらうなんて趣味は、今のところありはしない。
entries.maoEnglish:
My shoulders sagged.
Akiha had spoken as though this were perfectly natural, but I was still an ordinary high-school student.
I had no desire—at least not yet—to be waited on by a girl about my own age.
entries.mirrorMoon:
My shoulders suddenly feel heavier.
It seemed completely natural to Akiha when she said it, but I'm nothing more than a normal high school student.
I have no interest in having a girl around my age serving me, at least not for now.

entries.japanese:
「……志貴さま付きって事は、俺専用の使用人ってこと？」
「はい。
なんなりと申し付けてください」
「……まあ、それはわかったよ。
秋葉のあの言いぶりじゃ君を解雇させてくれそうにないし、大人しく世話してもらうけど───」
「何か、特別なご要望でもあるのですか？」
「特別ってわけじゃない。
ただ、その志貴さまっていうのを止めてくれないか。
正直いって、聞いてると背筋が寒くなる」
entries.maoEnglish:
“…If you’re assigned to Master Shiki, does that make you
my personal servant?” “Yes.
Ask anything of me.” “All right, I understand. From the way Akiha spoke, she would never let me dismiss you, so
I’ll accept your help, but───”
“Do you have some special request?” “Nothing special. Just stop calling me Master Shiki; honestly, it sends a chill down my spine.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… By serving me, you mean you're a personal servant?"
"Yes.
Please do not hesitate to ask anything of me."
"…… Well, I get it.
Going by how Akiha was talking about you, it doesn't seem like I can dismiss you, so I'll just obediently let you serve me…"
"Is there anything in particular you would like?"
"Nothing in particular, but could you stop calling me 'Shiki-sama'?
To be honest, I get chills down my back when I hear it."

entries.japanese:
「ですが、志貴さまはわたしの主人です」
「だからそれがイヤなんだって言ってるんだ。
俺は昨日まで普通に生きてた身なんだ。
いまさら同い年ぐらいの女の子に様づけで呼ばれる生活なんてまっぴらだよ」
　はあ、と翡翠は気のない返事をする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“But you are my master, Master Shiki.”
“That’s exactly what I don’t like. Until yesterday I was living a perfectly ordinary life. The last thing I want now is a girl my age treating me like some lord of the manor.”
Hisui gave a listless acknowledgment.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"But Shiki-sama, you are my master."
"That's what I'm saying I hate.
I've been living a normal life up until yesterday.
I have no desire to start living a life where a girl my age addresses me with '-sama'."
"I see." Hisui's response was less than enthusiastic.

entries.japanese:
「俺の事は志貴でいい。
そのかわりに俺も翡翠って呼び捨てにするからさ。
それと堅苦しいのもなしにしよう。
もっと気軽に、気楽に行こうよ」
　翡翠は無表情ながらも眉を下げて、なんだか困っているような素振りをする。
「ですが、あなたはわたしの雇い主ですから」
「俺が雇ってるわけじゃないだろ。
翡翠は俺にできない事をやってくれるんだから、そっちのほうが偉いんだぞ」
　はあ、と翡翠はまたも気のない返事をする。
　……どうも一朝一夕でこの子に言い含めるのは無理のようだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Just call me Shiki. I’ll call you Hisui in return. And let’s drop the stiff formalities. We can be more relaxed with each other.”
Hisui’s face remained blank, but her brows drooped slightly, as if I had put her in a difficult position.
“But you are my employer.”
“I’m not the one who hired you. Besides, you do all the things I can’t, so if anything, you’re the important one.”
Hisui again gave the same listless acknowledgment.
Apparently this was not something I could talk her out of overnight.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Just call me Shiki, and in exchange, I'll call you Hisui.
Let's do away with the formalities and be more casual with each other."
Still expressionless, Hisui lowers her eyebrows as if she's being troubled.
"But, you are my employer."
"It's not like I'm hiring you.
You're the one doing the things I can't, so you're the great one."
"I see." Hisui gives another unenthusiastic reply.
…… It looks like I won't be able to talk her into it in just one day.

entries.japanese:
「―――ともかくそういう事だから、俺に対してあんまりかたっくるしいのはナシにしてくれ。
お姉さんの琥珀さんにも伝えてくれるとありがたい」
「はい。
志貴さまがそうおっしゃるなら」
　翡翠は無表情で頭をさげる。
　ものの見事に、全然わかってない。
「それでは失礼します。
今夜はこのままお休みください」
　翡翠は一礼してドアのノブに手をかける。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――Anyway, that’s how I feel, so please don’t be so formal with me. I’d appreciate it if you told your sister the same thing.”
“Yes. If that is what Master Shiki wishes.”
Hisui bowed, her face utterly blank.
She had missed the point so completely it was almost impressive.
“I shall take my leave, then. Please retire for the night.”
Hisui bowed and reached for the doorknob.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Anyhow, that's how it is.
Don't be so formal towards me.
I'll be grateful if you'd tell that to your sister Kohaku-san, too."
"Very well, as you say, Shiki-sama."
Expressionless, Hisui bows her head.
She completely failed to understand.
"I will be leaving now.
Please rest now for tonight."
Bowing, Hisui puts her hand on the doorknob.

entries.japanese:
────と、一つ聞き忘れていた。
「あ、ちょっと待った」
　ドアに走り寄って、立ち去ろうとする翡翠の肩に手を置いた。
　瞬間────翡翠の腕が、物凄い勢いで俺の腕を払った。
entries.maoEnglish:
────And then I remembered one last question.
“Oh, wait a second.”
I hurried to the door and put a hand on Hisui’s shoulder as she was leaving.
In that instant, Hisui knocked my arm away with astonishing force.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Oh, I forgot to ask something.
"Ah, hold on for a second."
Running towards the door, I put my hand on Hisui's shoulder before she leaves.
In an instant---Hisui's arm pushes away my arm with incredible momentum.

entries.japanese:
バシ、と音をたてて手がはたかれて、翡翠は逃げるように後退する。
「え────」
　あんまりに突然のことで、そんな言葉しかだせない。
　翡翠は無表情のまま、けれどたしかに、仇を見るような激しさでこちらを睨んでいる────
entries.maoEnglish:
The slap cracked through the room, and Hisui sprang back as though fleeing from me.
“What────”
It happened so suddenly that no other word would come.
Hisui’s face remained expressionless, but she was unmistakably glaring at me with the ferocity one reserves for a hated enemy────
entries.mirrorMoon:
With a 'whack!', she slaps my hand away and leaps back.
"Eh---?"
It's so sudden, that's the only thing I can say.
Hisui is expressionless, but she glares at me fiercely.

entries.japanese:
「えっと―――俺、なにかわるいことしちゃったかな」
「あ……」
「……申し訳、ございません……」
　緊張のまじった翡翠の声。
「……体を触れられるのには、慣れていないのです。
どうか、お許しください」
　翡翠の肩はかすかに震えている。
　なんだか、ものすごく悪いことをしてしまったような気がする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Um―――did I do something wrong?”
“Ah……”
“I am terribly sorry…”
Tension threaded Hisui’s voice.
“I am not accustomed to being touched. Please forgive me.”
Her shoulders trembled faintly.
Somehow, I felt as though I had done something truly awful.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Eh… Did I just do something wrong?"
"Ah…"
"…… I am very sorry…"
She sounds very nervous.
"…… I am not used to being touched.
Please forgive me."
Hisui's shoulders are faintly trembling.
I feel like I just did something really terrible.

entries.japanese:
「あ───うん、ごめん」
　思わず謝った。
　自分でもよくわからない。
ただ翡翠が可哀相に思えて、ペコリと頭をさげていた。
「──────」
　翡翠は何も言わない。
　ただ、心なし視線が穏やかなものになった気がする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh—yes, sorry.”
The apology came out before I knew it.
I could not have explained why. She simply looked so pitiful that I found myself bowing to her.
“──────”
Hisui said nothing.
Still, I thought her gaze softened a little.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah… Yeah, I'm sorry."
I apologize without thinking.
I don't understand why myself.
I just feel sorry for Hisui and I lower my head.
"------"
Hisui says nothing.
I get the feeling her stare is calm again.

entries.japanese:
「───志貴さまが謝られる事はありません。
非があるのはわたしのほうです」
「いや、まあそうみたいなんだけど、なんとなく」
　ぽりぽりと頭をかく。
　翡翠はじっと俺の顔を見つめてから、一瞬だけ目を伏せた。
「その……ご用件はなんでしょうか、志貴さま」
　そうだった。
　部屋を立ち去る翡翠を呼び止めたのは聞きたい事があったからだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“───You have no reason to apologize, Master Shiki. The fault was mine.”
“I suppose you’re right, but somehow—” I scratched my head.
Hisui studied my face, then lowered her eyes for a fleeting moment.
“What did you need, Master Shiki?”
Oh, right.
I had stopped her because there was something I wanted to ask.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---You have nothing to apologize for, Shiki-sama.
I am the one to blame."
"No, well, maybe, but I just…"
I scratch my head.
Hisui stares at me, pausing only to blink for a second.
"Um… What was it you wanted to ask me, Shiki-sama?"
That's right.
I stopped her because I wanted to ask her something.

entries.japanese:
「いや、秋葉はどうしてるのか気になってさ。
あいつ、全寮制の学校に行ってたんじゃなかったっけ？」
「志貴さま、それは中学校までの話です。
秋葉さまは今年から特例として自宅からの登校を許可されていらっしゃいます」
「……えっと、つまりこの家から学校に行ってるってコト？」
「はい。
ですが、今日のように夕方に帰られる事は稀です。
秋葉さまは夕食の時間まで習い事がありますから、お帰りになられるのは決まって七時前です」
entries.maoEnglish:
“I was wondering about Akiha. Didn’t she attend a boarding school?”
“Master Shiki, that was only through middle school. Beginning this year, Miss Akiha has been granted special permission to commute from home.”
“So she commutes from this house?”
“Yes. However, it is rare for her to return as early as she did today. Miss Akiha has lessons until dinnertime, so she ordinarily arrives just before seven.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Oh, I wanted to ask about Akiha.
Doesn't she go to a boarding school?"
"That was only during middle school, Shiki-sama.
From this year onwards, Akiha-sama has special permission to attend school from home."
"Eh… You mean she goes to school from here?"
"Yes, but it is uncommon for her to come home before dusk like today.
Akiha-sama has practice up until dinner, so she is always home before seven.

entries.japanese:
「習い事って―――それ、なに？」
「今日は木曜日ですのでヴァイオリンの稽古でした」
「────え」
「平日は夕食前には戻られますから、秋葉さまにお話があるのでしたら夕食後に姉さんに申し付けてください」
　では、と翡翠は頭をさげてから部屋を出ていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Lessons―――what kind?”
“Today was Thursday, so she had violin practice.”
“────What—”
“She returns before dinner on weekdays, so if you wish to speak with Miss Akiha, please ask my sister after the meal.”
With that, Hisui bowed and left the room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Practice?---Practice what?"
"Today is Thursday, so she would have had violin practice."
"----Eh?"
"Usually, she is able to return before dinner on weekdays, so if you have anything to say to Akiha-sama, please let Nee-san know after dinner."
Hisui bows to say goodbye, and leaves the room.

entries.japanese:
「ヴァイオリンの、稽古」
　なんだろう、それは。
　どこかのお嬢様じゃあるまいし、なんだってそんな面倒なことを―――
「……って、どこかのお嬢様だったんだ、あいつ」
　そう、そういえば遠野志貴の妹は遠野秋葉という、生粋のお嬢様だったっけ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Violin lessons.”
What was that about?
It wasn’t as though she were some pampered young lady, so why bother with something so―――
“Oh—right; she is a pampered young lady.”
Right—come to think of it, Shiki Tohno’s little sister was Akiha Tohno, a young lady born and bred.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Violin practice…"
What on earth is that?
She's not some upper-class lady or anything, so why should she have to do something as bothersome as---
"…… Oh wait, she is an upper-class lady."
Yes.
Come to think of it, my sister, Tohno Akiha, is a natural born upper-class lady.

entries.japanese:
こっちの記憶の中じゃ秋葉は大人しくて、いつも不安げな瞳で俺のあとをついてくる一歳年下の妹だった。
　子供の頃の秋葉は無口で、自分のやりたい事も口にだせないほど弱気で、いつも父親である遠野槙久に叱られないかっておどおどしていた線の細い女の子だったのに。
「───そうだよな。
八年も経てば人間だってガラリと変わる」
　自分が八年間で今の遠野志貴になったように、
　秋葉もこの八年間で今の遠野秋葉になったんだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
In my memories, Akiha was my quiet little sister, one year younger, always trailing behind me with anxious eyes.
As a child she had been frail and timid, too shy even to say what she wanted, forever frightened that her father, Makihisa Tohno, might scold her.
“───Of course. Eight years is enough to change anyone completely.”
Just as those eight years had made me into Shiki Tohno,
they must have made Akiha into Akiha Tohno as well.
entries.mirrorMoon:
In my memories, she was always the obedient, ever-uneasy sister who'd always follow me around.
As a child, Akiha was always quiet, never having even the courage to express her own desires.
She was a frail girl who would always live in fear of a scolding from our father.
"---Yeah, people really do change after eight years."
After eight years, I've become the me I am now.
Akiha has become the Akiha of right now, too.

entries.japanese:
―――八年間は、長い。
　今までの人生の半分。
　それも子供から大人になろうと成長しようとする一番大切な時期に、俺はこの屋敷にいなかった。
「……ごめんな、秋葉」
　その八年間を一緒にいてやれたらどんなに良かったろう、と思えて。
　知らず、そんな謝罪の言葉を呟いた。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Eight years is a long time.
Half my life so far.
I had been absent from this house during the years that mattered most—the years when a child struggled to become an adult.
“I’m sorry, Akiha.”
If only I could have been there beside her through those eight years.
The thought brought the apology unbidden to my lips.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Eight years is a long time.
It's half of our lives up until now.
I was absent from this mansion during that vital period where a child becomes an adult.
"…… I'm sorry, Akiha."
I think things would have been better if I had been with her during those eight years.
I unconsciously mumble an apology.

entries.japanese:
ひとり残されて、ベッドに横になった。
　八年ぶりの家。
　八年ぶりの肉親。
　なんだか、他人の家のように感じる自分。
「……はあ。
これからどうなるんだろ、俺」
　誰に聞かせるわけでもなくぼやいて、そのまま眠りへと落ちていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
Left alone, I lay down on the bed.
Home for the first time in eight years.
With my own family for the first time in eight years.
Yet I felt as though I were in a stranger’s house.
“God… what is going to happen to me now?”
With no one there to hear me complain, I drifted into sleep.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Left by myself, I lie on my bed.
This house from eight years ago…
My blood relative from eight years ago…
It feels a little like they belong to someone else.
*sigh*
"…… I wonder what's going to happen to me now?"
Grumbling to no one in particular, I fall asleep.

entries.japanese:
オーーーーーーーーーン。
―――波の音のように、何かの声が聞こえてくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
Awooooooooooo.
―――A voice reaches me, rising and falling like the sea.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Awooooo.
---I hear the wave-like sound of something's voice.

entries.japanese:
オーーーーーーーーーン。
―――なにかの遠吠え。
野犬にしては細く高い。
entries.maoEnglish:
Awooooooooooo.
―――Something is howling. Too thin and high to be a stray dog.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Awooooo.
---Something is howling.
It's too sharp and high-pitched to be a stray dog.

entries.japanese:
オーーーーーーーーーン。
―――鼓膜に響く。
月にでも吠えているのか。
entries.maoEnglish:
Awooooooooooo.
―――It rings in my ears. Is it howling at the moon?
entries.mirrorMoon:
Awooooo.
---It echoes in my eardrums.
Is it howling at the moon?

entries.japanese:
オーーーーーーーーーン。
―――厭なにおい。
この獣の咆哮は、頭痛を招く。
entries.maoEnglish:
Awooooooooooo.
―――A foul smell. The beast’s cry brings on a headache.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Awooooo.
---This doesn't feel right.
The beastly howling is beginning to give me a headache.

entries.japanese:
オーーーーーーーーーン。
―――音はやまない。
entries.maoEnglish:
Awooooooooooo.
―――The sound will not stop.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Awooooo.
---It doesn't stop.

entries.japanese:
オーーーーーーーーーン。
　オーーーーーーーーーン。
　オーーーーーーーーーン――――――――
entries.maoEnglish:
Awooooooooooo.
Awooooooooooo.
Awooooooooooo—
entries.mirrorMoon:
Awooooo.
Awooooo.
Awooooooooooooooo---

entries.japanese:
「……ああ、やかましいっ！」
　目が覚めた。
　窓の外からはワンワンと犬の鳴き声が聞こえてくる。
　時計は夜の十一時になったばかり。
　近所迷惑どころの話じゃない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“God, shut up!”
I woke with a start.
A dog was barking outside the window.
The clock had only just struck eleven.
This was more than a nuisance to the neighbors.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Argh, just shut up already!"
I wake up.
I can hear the sound of a dog barking outside the window.
The clock indicates it is just past eleven.
This is more than just a neighborhood nuisance.

entries.japanese:
「くそ、こんなんじゃ眠れやしないじゃないか」
　犬の遠吠えは屋敷の塀の近くから聞こえてくる。
　……このままじゃ眠れそうにない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Damn it, how am I supposed to sleep through this?”
The howling came from somewhere near the estate wall.
There was no chance of sleeping like this.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Damn, I can't sleep like this!"
The dog's howling comes from somewhere near the mansion's fence.
…… It doesn't seem like I can go back to sleep at this rate.

entries.japanese:
こんなにうるさくては秋葉たちも眠れずに悩んでいるだろう。
　屋敷にいる男手は自分だけだし、ここは様子を見にいくしかないと思う。
entries.maoEnglish:
With this much noise, Akiha and the others must be lying awake too.
I was the only man in the house, so I supposed it fell to me to investigate.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Even Akiha and the others wouldn't be able to sleep with a racket like this.
Since I'm the only man in the house, I guess I've got no choice but to go investigate.

entries.japanese:
「……屋敷の右手のほう、かな」
　カーテンを開けて、外の様子を確かめる。
――――と。
　部屋の外の大きな木。
　その枝に、一羽の青い鴉が止まっていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“It’s coming from the right side of the estate, I think…”
I drew back the curtains and looked outside.
――――And there.
A large tree stood outside my window.
Perched on one of its branches was a blue crow.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I think it's coming from the right side of the mansion."
I open the curtains and check what's happening outside.
---And,
outside my room is a large tree.
On one of the branches is perched a blue crow.

entries.japanese:
闇夜の中。
　黒としか見えないのに、はっきりと鴉は蒼く見えた。
「………………」
　青い鴉なんて、見たことも聞いた事もない。
　ぎょろり。
　意志のない、機械のレンズのような鴉の目が、こっちを睨んだ気がした。
entries.maoEnglish:
In the darkness of night.
Though everything should have looked black, the crow was unmistakably deep blue.
“……”
I had never seen or even heard of a blue crow.
Its eye rolled.
The crow’s eye, empty of will and glassy as a machine lens, seemed to glare straight at me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
In the dark night,
I can see nothing but black, and yet it's quite clear to me that the crow is blue.
"…………"
I've never seen or even heard of a blue crow before.
It glares at me.
It feels like the eyes of the crow are staring at me, like soulless, mechanical lenses.

entries.japanese:
くあう。
　あくびのような鳴き声をあげたあと、鴉は羽音もたてずに飛び去っていった。
「……なんだ、今の」
　……かすかに背筋が寒い。
　犬の遠吠えはさらに大きくなっている。
entries.maoEnglish:
Kwaa.
After giving a cry like a yawn, the crow flew away without a whisper of wings.
“What was that?”
A faint chill crept down my spine.
The dogs were howling louder than ever.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Kwaaw!
After a yawn-like cry, it noiselessly flies off.
"…… What was that?"
…… I can feel a faint chill on my back.
The howling of the dogs grows louder.

entries.japanese:
オーーーーーーーン。
　　　　　　オーーーーーーーン。
　　　　　　　　　　　　　オーーーーーーーン。
「……………」
　なんだか、この音は癇に障る。
　うるさいという以前に、聞いているだけで心臓がどくどくと活性化するような、生理的な嫌悪感だ。
「うる―――さい」
　寝巻から制服に着替えて、部屋を後にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
Awooooooo.
        Awooooooo.
                Awooooooo.
“……”
The sound was getting under my skin.
It was more than noise: just hearing it made my heart pound into frantic life—a purely physical revulsion.
“Shut―――up.”
I changed out of my pajamas and into my uniform, then left the room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Awoooooooo.
Awoooooooo.
Awoooooooo.
"…………"
It's really starting to get on my nerves.
Not only is it noisy, but hearing it causes my heart to start pounding.
I have an almost instinctual distaste for it.
"Shut---up!"
I change out of my pajamas into my uniform, and leave the room.

entries.japanese:
オーーーーーーーーン。
　遠吠えは夜に響く。
　音は、間違いなく屋敷の右手側のほうから聞こえてくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
Awooooooooooo.
The howl rang through the night.
There could be no mistake: it was coming from the right side of the estate.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Awoooooooo.
The howling echoes through the night.
That sound is definitely coming from the right-hand side of the mansion.

entries.japanese:
「………………」
　なぜか喉が乾いている。
　屋敷の周り、高い壁が延々と続く夜道。
　喉をならしながら、犬たちが集まっている場所へ歩いていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“……”
For some reason my throat had gone dry.
Outside the estate, the high wall stretched endlessly along the night road.
Swallowing against the dryness, I followed it toward the place where the dogs had gathered.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…………"
For some reason, my throat feels dry.
The high walls stretch their way around the mansion.
Clearing my throat, I head towards where the dogs must be gathered.

entries.japanese:
鳴き声がしている場所にきた。
「……あれ？」
　オーーーーーーーーーン。
　鳴き声は依然としてやまない。
　なのに、そこに犬の姿なんてなかった。
　あるのは―――人影だけだ。
　ぽつん、と闇をきりとったような街灯の明かりの下、黒いコートの男が立っている。
　遠吠えは、男の側から聞こえている。
―――――だが、犬の姿などどこにもない。
entries.maoEnglish:
I reached the source of the noise.
“Huh…?”
Awooooooooooo.
The howling had not stopped.
Yet there was not a dog in sight.
There was only―――a human figure.
A man in a black coat stood alone beneath a streetlamp, its island of light cut from the darkness.
The howling came from beside the man.
―――――Yet there was no dog anywhere.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I arrive at where the howling originates.
"…… Huh?"
Awoooooooo.
The howling doesn't stop.
But there are no signs of any dogs.
All there is---is a person.
Under the light from the streetlight that carves apart the darkness stands a man in a dark coat.
The howling is coming from right beside him.
------But there are no dogs to be seen anywhere.

entries.japanese:
コートの男はかなりの長身だ。
　がっしりとした体格をした男は、こちらに背を向けて立ち尽くしている。

「――――――」
　喉が、乾く。
　オーーーーン、という犬の声が鼓膜に響く。
　夜の空気が、じっとりと肌に絡み付く。
　なにがどうというワケでもないのに。
　海の底にいるみたいに、呼吸も身動きもひどく重苦しく感じられる――――
entries.maoEnglish:
The man in the coat was extremely tall.
Broad and powerfully built, he stood motionless with his back to me.
“――――――”
My throat dries.
The dog’s drawn-out howl pounds against my eardrums.
The night air clings damply to my skin.
Nothing at all had happened.
Yet breathing and moving feel unbearably heavy, as though I were trapped at the bottom of the sea――――
entries.mirrorMoon:
The man in the coat is pretty tall.
He has a strongly built body, and his back is facing me.
"---------"
My throat… so dry.
Awoooooooo.
The voice of the dog resounds in my ears.
The night air coils itself around my skin.
For no apparent reason, I have difficulty breathing and moving, as if I'm at the bottom of the sea---

entries.japanese:
くわあ。
　頭上から声がした。
　ばさん、という羽音とともに、蒼い鴉が男の肩に降りてくる。
　―――と。
　鴉は、唐突にその姿を消してしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
Kwaa.
The sound came from above.
With a sudden flap of wings, the deep-blue crow descended onto the man’s shoulder.
―――And then.
The crow abruptly vanished.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Kwaah!
A cry overhead.
With a loud flapping of its wings, the blue crow lands onto the man's shoulder.
---Then,
suddenly, the crow vanishes.

entries.japanese:
「…………え？」
　目の錯覚だろうか。
　鴉は、黒いコートの中に消えたように見えた。
「―――――」
　黒いコートが振りかえる。
　白い街灯の下、人影はまさしく影そのものだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What…?”
Had my eyes deceived me?
It looked as though the crow had disappeared inside the black coat.
“―――――”
The black coat turns.
Under the white streetlamp, the figure was shadow itself.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Eh?"
Can it be an illusion?
It looked like the crow disappeared into his black coat.
"------"
The man in the black coat turns around.
Under the white streetlight, he is just like a shadow.

entries.japanese:
黒い塊。
　その中で、凶器みたいな理性をもった目だけが、爛々と輝いている―――――
「…………あ」
　呼吸ができない。
　けれど、幸いに。
　男の目は、こちらのことなどまるで見えていないようだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
A mass of black.
Within it, only the eyes shone—eyes filled with a cold intelligence as keen and lethal as a weapon―――――
“Ah…”
I cannot breathe.
Yet, thankfully.
The man’s eyes seem not to see me at all.
entries.mirrorMoon:
A black lump.
In the middle of that lump, only the weapon-like eyes shine out, burning with a fiery intelligence.
"…… Ah."
I can't breathe.
But fortunately, those eyes seem like they're not even looking at me.

entries.japanese: 「ここでは、なかったか」
entries.maoEnglish: “Not here, then.”
entries.mirrorMoon: "Not here after all."

entries.japanese: 黒いコートが立ち去っていく。
entries.maoEnglish: The black coat walks away.
entries.mirrorMoon: The man in the black coat leaves.

entries.japanese:
人影が完全に見えなくなって、ようやくまともに呼吸ができるようになった。
「は――――はあ、あ」
　ホッと息をつく。
　気が付けば、犬の遠吠えは止んでいた。
entries.maoEnglish:
Only after the figure had vanished completely could I breathe again.
“Hah――――haa, ah.”
I let out a breath of relief.
Only then did I realize that the dogs had stopped howling.
entries.mirrorMoon:
When I can no longer see him, I am finally able to breathe properly again.
"Hhahh---haah, ah."
I manage to take a few breaths.
I realize the dogs' howling has ceased.

entries.japanese:
部屋に戻ってきた。
　秋葉たちは起きている気配がなく、あの犬の遠吠えに我慢できなかったのは自分だけだったらしい。
「―――――ぐ」
　なんだろう。
　まだ、頭が痛い。
entries.maoEnglish:
I returned to my room.
There was no sign that Akiha or the others had awakened; apparently I was the only one who had found the howling unbearable.
“―――――Ngh.”
What was this?
My head still hurt.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I return to my room.
There is no sign of Akiha or the others being awake.
I guess I'm the only one who couldn't stand the dogs' howling.

"------Guh!"
What's happening?
My head still hurts.

entries.japanese:
「あれ……なんで震えてるんだろ、俺」
　見れば指が震えている。
　全身も小刻みにガタついていて、背筋がやけに冷たい。
　例えるなら、そう。
　脊髄をひきぬかれて、代わりに氷の柱を刺し込まれたみたい。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Why am I shaking…?”
My fingers were trembling.
My whole body shuddered in tiny spasms, and an unnatural cold ran down my back.
If I had to compare it to something—yes.
It felt as though someone had torn out my spinal cord and driven a pillar of ice into its place.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Huh… ?
Why am I trembling?"
Looking down, my fingers are trembling.
My entire body is shaking, and my back feels very cold.
It's almost like… yes.
It's like someone ripped out my spine and replaced it with ice.

entries.japanese:
「―――――」
　くらり、と眩暈がした。
　……いつもの貧血だろうか。
　意識が地面に落ちていく感覚。
　その途中で、イヤなものを、見てしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――――”
The room lurched.
Was it my usual anemia?
I felt my consciousness plummeting toward the floor.
And on the way down, I saw something horrible.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------"
I feel dizzy.
…… Is it just the usual anemia?
I get the feeling of falling towards the floor.
On the way, I see something unpleasant.

entries.japanese:
「なっ―――――」
　メガネをしてるのに、あの『線』が視える。
「うっ………」
　ここのところまったく視ていなかったせいか、反動が大きい。
　気持ち悪い。
　貧血の眩暈とあいまって、今にも胃の中のモノを吐き出してしまいそうだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Wh―――――”
Even through my glasses, I can see those “lines.”
“Ugh…”
Perhaps the backlash is so strong because I have not seen them at all lately.
I feel sick.
Together with the dizziness, it feels as though I might vomit at any moment.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Wha---!?"
Even though I'm wearing my glasses, I can still see the "lines".
"Uuh……!"
I hadn't seen them at all for a long time, so my reaction is magnified.
I feel sick.
With the dizziness from my anemia, I feel like I'm about to throw up the contents of my stomach.

entries.japanese:
「……どうなってんだよ、これ」
　よく、わからない。
　ただ、目を開けているかぎりあのラクガキが視界に飛び込んできてしまう。
　―――悪い、夢だ。
　なんとかベッドに倒れこむ。
　……そう、眠ってしまえばいい。
見えている物を否定するには、それが一番てっとり早い方法だ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What the hell is happening?”
I could not understand.
As long as my eyes remained open, those hideous scribbles forced themselves into my vision.
―――A bad dream.
Somehow I collapsed onto the bed.
…Yes—I only had to sleep; the quickest way to deny what I was seeing was to stop seeing anything at all.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… What's, going on?"
I don't understand.
Only that as long as my eyes are open, scribbles fly everywhere across my vision.

---It's a bad… dream.
Somehow, I manage to collapse into bed.
…… Yes.
I should sleep.
That's the easiest way to deny what I'm seeing.

entries.japanese:
体も思うように動かない。
　このまま、死体のように。
　ベッドの上に倒れこんで、泥のように眠ってしまえばいいだけだ――――
entries.maoEnglish:
My body would barely move.
Like a corpse.
All I had to do was collapse onto the bed and sink into sleep as deep and heavy as mud――――
entries.mirrorMoon:
My body doesn't move as I want it to.
All I should do is lie here and fall fast asleep, like a corpse---

entries.japanese:
犬の遠吠えはまだ続いている。
　このままじゃはっきりいって眠れない。
　……眠れないけど、まあ、それは常人の神経のレヴェルの話だ。
「………………眠いので、パス」
　シーツをかぶって、ベッドに横になる。
　犬の遠吠えなんて、道を走る自動車の音だと思えばいい。
entries.maoEnglish:
The dogs were still howling.
There was no way anyone could sleep through this.
That was true only for someone with normal nerves.
“I’m too sleepy, so I’ll pass.”
I pulled the sheet over my head and lay down.
I could pretend the howling was only traffic passing on the road.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The howling continues.
There's no way I can sleep like this.
…… I can't sleep, but that's just normal.
"…… I'm sleepy, so I'll pass."
Pulling the sheets over me, I stretch out on the bed.
I can just think of the howling as the sound of something mundane as cars driving by on the street.

entries.japanese:
「………はあ」
　今日はなんだか長い一日だった。
　慣れない屋敷での夕食や秋葉たちとの会話で精神も疲れきっている。
その前には犬の遠吠えなんて、ただの雑音に他ならない。
　目を閉じてしまえば、あとはゆるやかに眠りの中へと落ちていけた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Haa…”
It had been an awfully long day.
Dinner in the unfamiliar estate and all those conversations with Akiha and the others had exhausted me. Against that, the dogs were nothing but background noise.
Once I closed my eyes, I slipped gently into sleep.
entries.mirrorMoon:
*sigh*
Today's been a very long day.
I'm mentally tired from eating dinner in this unfamiliar mansion and my conversations with Akiha and everyone else.
After all that, the howling is just background noise.
I close my eyes and gently fall asleep.

entries.japanese:
「――――ん」
　なにか、物音が聞こえた気がした。
　ねぼけまなこで時計を見てみると、時刻は午前二時になったばかりだ。
　……さっきの野犬の騒ぎから、二時間ほど経っている。
　野犬の鳴き声はとっくにやんでいた。
　屋敷の夜は時計の秒針の音が響くぐらい、静かだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――Mm?”
I thought I heard something.
Peering blearily at the clock, I saw that it had just turned two in the morning.
About two hours had passed since the uproar with the stray dogs.
Their howling had long since stopped.
The estate was so quiet that the ticking clock carried through the night.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Nng."
I think I just heard something.
Half-awake, I look at the clock.
It's just past two.
…… It's been about two hours since I heard the dogs howling.
The dogs' howling has already stopped.
The mansion is so quiet, I can hear the clock ticking in the silence.

entries.japanese:
「――――――？」
　また物音が聞こえた。
　……屋敷の中……ロビーのほうだろうか。
「―――――まさか、泥棒？」
　ありえない話じゃない。
　この屋敷は金目のものでしか構成されていないとんでもない屋敷だ。
くわえて、今は俺と秋葉、琥珀さんと翡翠しかいないっていう無用心ぶりである。
「……………」
　ベッドから出て、足音を立てないように部屋を出る。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――――?”
There it was again.
Somewhere inside the estate—perhaps near the foyer.
“―――――A burglar?”
It was not impossible.
This enormous estate seemed to be made entirely of valuables. On top of that, only Akiha, Kohaku, Hisui, and I were living here.
“…”
I slipped out of bed and left the room without making a sound.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------?"
I hear it again.
…… Inside the mansion… from the lobby?
"-----Could it be a burglar?"
It's not impossible.
The mansion's contents are outrageously valuable.
On top of that, with no one here now except Kohaku-san, Hisui, Akiha and myself, it's very insecure.
"……"
Getting out of bed, I slip out of the room quietly.

entries.japanese:
……もし泥棒だったら秋葉たちが危ないし、こればっかりは見過ごしておけない。
　二階からロビーの様子を眺めるだけなら、こっちにも危険はないと思う。
entries.maoEnglish:
If it was a burglar, Akiha and the others might be in danger, and I could not ignore that.
Watching the foyer from the second floor should not put me at any risk.
entries.mirrorMoon:
If it's a burglar, Akiha and everyone will be in danger, so I can't let this one go.
I'll just look down from the second floor into the lobby; that should be safe enough.

entries.japanese:
……ロビーには異状はない。
「……………！」
　いや、誰かいる。
　玄関から入ってきて、ふらふらとおぼつかない足取りでロビーを横切っていく姿は―――
「あき……は？」
　秋葉は二階の自分の部屋にではなく、一階の西館へ歩いていく。
　その先にあるものは琥珀さんの部屋と、親父の部屋ぐらいのものだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
Nothing seemed amiss in the foyer.
“……!”
No—someone was there.
A figure had entered through the front door and was staggering unsteadily across the foyer—
“Aki—ha?”
Instead of going upstairs to her room, Akiha headed into the west wing on the ground floor.
The only rooms that way were Kohaku’s and Father’s.
entries.mirrorMoon:
There's nothing wrong there.
"…… !"
No, someone's there.
The figure that enters from the entrance and crosses the lobby with wobbling, uncertain steps, is---
"Aki… ha?"
She's not going to her own room on the second floor, but to the first floor of the west wing.
The only things there are Kohaku-san's room and my old man's room.

entries.japanese:
「……なにしてたんだ、アイツ。
こんな夜更けに……」
　呟いてみても答えはない。
　しばらくロビーの様子を眺めてから、大人しく自分の部屋に戻ることにした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“……What was she doing out this late?”
The empty foyer offered no answer.
After watching for a while longer, I returned quietly to my room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… What's she doing at this time of night?"
I can murmur all I want, but I won't be getting any answers.
After gazing at the lobby for a while, I decide to return to my room.

entries.japanese:
……まあ、何か用事があったのか、それとも琥珀さんに会いにいったのかもしれない。
　こっちもこっそり盗み見ていたという負い目もあるし、あれこれ詮索するのも気が引ける。
「……寝よ寝よ。
明日も学校だ」
　ベッドにもぐりこんで、目を閉じる。
―――眠りに落ちる途中。
　ロビーで見かけた、うつろな瞳をした秋葉の姿が、なにかよくない物のように、何度も何度も思い返されていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
Perhaps she had some errand, or had gone to see Kohaku.
I felt guilty enough for spying on her, so prying any further seemed wrong.
“Back to bed. I have school tomorrow.”
I crawled beneath the covers and closed my eyes.
―――As I drifted back to sleep.
The image of Akiha crossing the foyer with vacant eyes returned to me again and again, like the memory of something ominous.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Well, she probably had something to do, or went to see Kohaku-san.
I feel bad about sneaking around and watching her, and I don't want to just ask her about everything she does.
"…… Sleep, sleep.
There's school tomorrow."
I bury myself in bed and close my eyes.
---As I fall asleep,
my thoughts keep returning over and over to Akiha's hollow-eyed figure in the lobby… and how something seemed wrong.

entries.japanese:
犬の遠吠えはまだ続いている。
　このままじゃはっきりいって眠れない。
　……眠れないけど、まあ、それは常人の神経のレヴェルの話。
「………………眠いので、パス」
　シーツをかぶって、ベッドに横になる。
　犬の遠吠えなんて、道を走る自動車の音だと思えばいい。
entries.maoEnglish:
The dogs were still howling.
There was no way anyone could sleep through this.
That was true only for someone with normal nerves.
“I’m too sleepy, so I’ll pass.”
I pulled the sheet over my head and lay down.
I could pretend the howling was only traffic passing on the road.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The howling continues.
There's no way I can sleep like this.
…… I can't sleep, but that's just normal.
"…… I'm sleepy, so I'll pass."
Pulling the sheets over me, I stretch out on the bed.
I can just think of the howling as the sound of something mundane, like cars driving by on the street.

entries.japanese:
「………はあ」
　今日はなんだか長い一日だった。
　慣れない屋敷での夕食や秋葉たちとの会話で精神もつかれきってる。
　その前には犬の遠吠えなんて、ただの雑音に他ならない。
　目を閉じてしまえば、あとはゆるやかに眠りの中へと落ちていけた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Haa…”
It had been an awfully long day.
Dinner in the unfamiliar estate and all those conversations with Akiha and the others had exhausted me.
Against that, the dogs were nothing but background noise.
Once I closed my eyes, I slipped gently into sleep.
entries.mirrorMoon:
*sigh*
Today's been a very long day.
I'm mentally tired from eating dinner in this unfamiliar mansion and my conversations with Akiha and everyone else.
After all that, the howling is just background noise.
I close my eyes and gently fall asleep.

entries.japanese:
――――懐かしい、夢を見た。
　八年前の夏の終わり。
　大きなケガをして、誰も来ない病院にうつされて、先生に出会ったあと。
　屋敷に帰ってきた自分は、そこで、知らない家に預けられるという事を、父親の口から聞いた。
　ことは、すごくあっけなかった。
　退院した次の日、自分は有間の家に行くことになったから。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――I dreamed an old, familiar dream.
It was the end of summer, eight years ago.
After my terrible injury, after they transferred me to a hospital where no one came to visit, after I met Teach.
When I returned to the estate, Father told me I was being sent to live with a family I had never met.
It all happened with startling abruptness.
The day after I left the hospital, I was sent to the Arima estate.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---I have a nostalgic dream.
The end of summer eight years ago.
After I was injured, was taken to that hospital where no one ever visited, and met Sensei.
Upon returning to the mansion, I heard from my old man that I would be taken in by a family I had never heard of.
Everything happened so fast.
Right after the day I left the hospital, I ended up going to the Arima household.

entries.japanese:
それは、雲一つない青空だったのを、覚えている。
　秋の始まり。
　自分は手をひかれて遠野の屋敷を後にした。
　けど、そのほんの少し前。
　あの子が、大人たちの目を盗んで会いに来てくれた。
entries.maoEnglish:
I remember the sky was blue and utterly cloudless.
Autumn was just beginning.
Someone took my hand and led me away from the Tohno estate.
But shortly before I left.
That girl slipped past the adults and came to see me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
There was not a single cloud in the blue sky that day.
The start of autumn.
I was led away from the Tohno mansion.
But a little before that…
That girl had come to see me, sneaking past the eyes of the adults.

entries.japanese:
『ここを出る時、裏庭の木にきてください』
　そう言われて、父親の目を盗んで裏庭に行った。
entries.maoEnglish:
“When it’s time for you to leave, come to the tree in the back
garden.” She told me that, so I slipped past Father and went to the back garden
entries.mirrorMoon:
"When you are about to leave, please come to the tree in the rear courtyard."
After being told that, I snuck out from under my old man's eye and out to the rear courtyard.

entries.japanese:
青い空。
　どこまでも落ちていけそうな青い空の下、彼女は一人で待っていた。
　自分が知るかぎり、あの子が屋敷から外に出たのは、これが初めてだった気がする。
entries.maoEnglish:
The blue sky.
Beneath a blue sky that seemed deep enough to fall into forever, she waited alone.
As far as I knew, it was the first time she had ever ventured outside the mansion.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The sky was blue.
Below that deep blue sky that seemed to extend forever, she waited for me.
As far as I knew, this was the first time she had left the mansion to come outside.

entries.japanese:
『これ、持っていって』
　言って、少女は自分の髪を留めていたリボンをほどいて手渡してくれた。
　餞別だったのだろうけど、なにぶん子供だった自分は、嬉しいともかんじない。
　……だって、リボンをもらって喜ぶ九歳の男の子はいないと思う。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Take this with
you.” The girl untied the ribbon from her hair and placed it in my hand, a
farewell gift, though I was only a child and felt no particular pleasure in it.
After all, I doubt any nine-year-old boy would be delighted to receive a ribbon.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Take this."
Saying that, she undid the ribbon that bound her hair and handed it to me.
I guess it was her farewell gift to me, but as a child, I didn't even feel happy about it.
…… After all, what kind of a nine year old boy would feel happy about receiving a ribbon?

entries.japanese:
『そのリボンお気に入りなの。
だから、あとでちゃんと返してね』
　けど、その言葉で、救われた。
　返してね、と少女はいった。
　帰ってきてね、と自分には聞こえた。
――――それだけで、よかった。
　誰一人として見送りさえしてくれなかった最後の日。
　今まで一度も話したことがなくっても、彼女がそう言ってくれたのが、嬉しかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“That ribbon is my favorite, so make sure you return it to me later.”
Those words saved me.
Return it to me, the girl said.
Return to me, I heard.
――――That alone was enough.
It was the last day, and not one person came to see me off.
I was glad she had said it—even though we had never spoken before.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"That ribbon is my favorite, so give it back to me later, okay?"
But those were the words that saved me.
"Give it back," she said.
"Come back," is what I heard from those words.
---Just that was good enough for me.
That last day, with no one to even see me off.
For her, who I had never even spoken to, to say that to me… it made me happy.

entries.japanese:
―――けど、きっと返すよ、とは言えなかった。
　こんな時にかぎって利口な自分は、もうこの屋敷に帰ってこれることはないって理解してしまっていたんだろう。
　……交わした言葉は、ただそれだけ。
　少女の氷のような目は、けど、どこか哀しかった。
　時間だから、と玄関へと歩いていく。
　少女は、やっぱり人形みたいに立ち尽くして、去り行く自分の姿を見つめていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――But I could not tell her, “I’ll be sure to return it.”
At the one time I wished I could have been foolish, I must have understood that I would never be allowed to return to this house.
That was all we said.
The girl’s eyes were cold as ice, yet there was something sad in them.
When the time came, I walked back toward the entrance.
She remained where she was, standing like a doll and watching me go.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---But I could not say, "I'll definitely return it."
As clever as I was at the time, I realized I would never be able to return to this mansion ever again.
…… Those were the only words we exchanged.
Something about her icy eyes was very sorrowful.
It was time, so I began walking towards the doorway.
The girl just stood there like a doll, watching me leave.

entries.japanese:
あおいそら。
　くもひとつない、それは、ある晴れた日の、とおいゆめ。
entries.maoEnglish:
blue sky.
not one cloud—a faraway dream of one bright day.
entries.mirrorMoon:
A distant dream of what happened on one fine day.
Under the cloudless blue sky.

entries.japanese:
やる事もないし、早々に学校を後にする。
　……考えてみれば、こうやって正門から下校するのなんて入学式以来だ。
「これからはここから屋敷に帰る道が通学路になるワケか……」
entries.maoEnglish:
With nothing else to do, I left school early.
Come to think of it, I hadn’t gone home through the front gate since the entrance ceremony.
“So this is going to be my route back to the estate from now on…”
entries.mirrorMoon:
I don't have anything to do, so I hurry up and leave school.
…… Come to think of it, I hadn't left the school by the main entrance since the entrance ceremony.
"I guess this'll be the way to and from school from now on since I live in the mansion…"

entries.japanese:
正門から出て住宅地に通じる交差点に出る。
　ここから街に出るか、屋敷のある住宅地に出るかに別れるのだが――――
「あれ、遠野くんだ」
　ばったり、弓塚に出会ってしまった。
「あれ、弓塚さんだ」
　弓塚が目を白黒させて俺を見ているように、こっちも目を点にしてみたりする。
entries.maoEnglish:
Beyond the front gate, I reached the intersection leading into the residential district.
One road led downtown; the other toward the neighborhood where the estate stood――――
“Oh, it’s Tohno.”
I had run straight into Yumizuka.
“Oh, it’s Yumizuka.”
She stared at me wide-eyed, and I stared back in equal surprise.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Leaving from the main gate, I come to the intersection that leads to the residential district.
This is the point at which the paths to the city and the residential district, where the mansion is, part----
"Oh, it's Tohno-kun."
Suddenly, I run into Yumizuka.
"Hey, it's Yumizuka-san."
Yumizuka-san looked at me, bewildered.

entries.japanese:
「えーっと、弓塚さん？
　俺の顔に何かついてる？」
「だって、どうして遠野くんがここにいるのかなって。
遠野くんの家、反対方向だよ？」
「あ……まあ、昨日まではそうだったけど、今日からは別だよ。
これからはあっちの住宅地の奥にある、坂の上の家に住む事になったから」
「あ、朝に言ってたのはその事だったんだ」
　ぽん、と手を叩いて納得する弓塚。
　……まあ、お世辞抜きにして、そういう仕草は愛らしいと思う。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Um, Yumizuka? Is there something on my face?”
“I was wondering why you were here. Your house is in the opposite direction, isn’t it?”
“Ah—it was until yesterday. Starting today, I’ll be living over there—in the house on the hill beyond the residential district.”
“Oh, so that’s what you were talking about this morning.”
Understanding dawned, and Yumizuka clapped her hands together.
Flattery aside, little gestures like that really were charming.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Uh… Yumizuka-san?
Is there something on my face?"
"Um, I was wondering what you were doing here, Tohno-kun.
Isn't your house in the other direction?"
"Ah… Well, it was until yesterday, but I'm living somewhere else starting today.
From now on, I'll be living at the place at the end of that residential district, on top of the hill."
"Ah, so that's what you were talking about this morning."
Yumizuka claps her fist and hand together in understanding.
…… Well, all flattery aside, that gesture seems incredibly cute.

entries.japanese:
「……そういう事。
弓塚さんは知ってるから隠しても仕方ないよな。
俺さ、預けられていた有間の家から今日づけで実家に戻ることになったんだよ」
「実家って、その……遠野さんのお屋敷に？」
「ああ。
自分でも似合わないって思うんだけど」
「そっか、遠野くんってば本当は丘の上の王子さまなんだもんね。
わたしと乾くんぐらいしか知らない秘密だったのに、これじゃすぐみんなにバレちゃうかなあ」
　ふふ、と淡い笑顔をうかべて、弓塚は遠くに視線を投げた。
　空の向こう。
　遠くの坂の上にある、遠野の屋敷を見つめるように。
entries.maoEnglish:
“That’s right. You already know, so there’s no point hiding it from you. As of today, I’m leaving the Arimas, who took me in, and moving back to my birth family’s home.”
“Your family home… You mean the Tohno
estate?” “Yes—I know I hardly look as though I belong there.”
“Of course—you’re really the prince on the hill. It used to be a secret only Inui and I knew, but I suppose everyone will find out soon now.”
With a faint smile, Yumizuka let her gaze drift into the distance.
Beyond the sky.
She seemed to be looking toward the Tohno estate high on a faraway hill.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… That's right.
I guess there's no point hiding it from you, since you already know.
I'm leaving my guardians, the Arimas, and going back to my real house today."
"Your real house… You mean the Tohno-san mansion?"
"Yeah.
I don't think it really suits me, either."
"I see.
You're really a prince on top of a hill, after all.
It was a secret only Inui-kun and I knew, but now I guess everyone's going to find out."
With a faint smile, Yumizuka casts her gaze into the distance.
She looks out at the horizon, as if looking at the Tohno mansion, off in the distance on top of the hill.

entries.japanese:
「でも大丈夫？
　自分のお家だって言っても、もう八年も離れているんでしょう？
　その、恐いなー、とか不安だなー、とか思わない？」
「そうだね、実際不安ではあるよ。
もとから俺はあの屋敷が好きじゃなかったし、今じゃ他人の家みたいに感じるしね。
けど、それでも―――」
　……妹である秋葉を一人残したまま、自分だけのんびりと暮らしていくことなんてできない。
　どんなに不安でも、俺は屋敷に戻らないといけないんだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“But will you be all right? It may be your own home, but you’ve been away for eight years. Aren’t you scared or uneasy?”
“I am uneasy, to tell the truth. I never liked that estate to begin with, and now it feels like someone else’s house. Even so―――”
I couldn’t leave my little sister Akiha there alone while I went on living comfortably elsewhere.
However uneasy I might be, I had to return to the estate.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"But will you be alright?
Even if it is your house, you've been away for eight years, right?
Aren't you afraid, or worried?"
"Yeah.
I'm actually kind of uneasy.
I never liked that mansion to begin with, and now it's going to feel like someone else's house too.
But still---"
…… I can't lead a carefree life on my own and leave my sister Akiha there all by herself.
No matter how uneasy I am, I have to return to the mansion.

entries.japanese:
「―――やっぱり自分の家なわけだから。
そこに戻るのが一番自然な形だと思うんだ」
「……そっか。
あ、呼び止めちゃってゴメンなさい。
遠野くん、急ぐんでしょ？」
「いや、別に用事はないよ。
のんびり散歩がてらに帰ろうとしてただけだから」
「あ―――そう、なんだ」
　どうしてか、弓塚はうつむいたまま黙ってしまう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――After all, it is my home. Going back is the natural thing to do.”
“I see. Oh, I’m sorry I stopped you. You’re in a hurry, aren’t you?”
“No, I have nowhere else to be. I was just planning to take a leisurely walk home.”
“Oh—so you’re not.”
For some reason, Yumizuka lowered her head and fell silent.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---In the end, it's still my home.
I think it's only natural for me to go back."
"…… I see.
Ah, sorry for stopping you, Tohno-kun.
You must be in a hurry, right?"
"No, not really.
I was just having a stroll on the way home."
"Ah… I see."
For some reason, Yumizuka looks downcast and falls silent.

entries.japanese:
「……弓塚さん？
　どうしたの、気分でも悪いの？」
　声をかける。
　それでも彼女は中々顔を上げずに、じっと下を向いていた。
「………………」
　放っておくわけにもいかず、こっちもじっと彼女の様子をうかがう。
―――、と。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Yumizuka? What’s wrong—are you feeling sick?”
I called out to her.
Still, she would not raise her face and kept staring at the ground.
“…”
I couldn’t simply leave her there, so I waited and watched her closely.
―――And then.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… What's wrong, Yumizuka-san?
Are you feeling sick?" I ask her.
But she continues to stare downwards without raising her head.
"……"
I can't just leave her there, so I continue to stand there, looking at her.
---And then.

entries.japanese:
「あ、あのね！」
「うん、なに」
「あの、そのね、わたしの家と遠野くんの家って、坂に行くまで帰る道が一緒、なんだ、けど……」
「そうなんだ。
それじゃ途中まで一緒に行こっか」
「――――え？」
　目をきょとん、とさせる弓塚。
　そのまましばらく固まったあと、
「う、うん―――そうだよね、帰る道が一緒なんだから、途中まで一緒でもおかしくないよね！」
　と、やけに弾んだ声をあげてこっちの横にやってきた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“U-um!”
“Yes?”
“Well, my house and yours are in the same direction until the road reaches the hill…”
“Really. Then why don’t we walk together that far?”
“――――What?”
Yumizuka’s eyes went round.
She stood frozen for several moments, then—
“Y-yes—of course; if we’re going the same way, there’s nothing strange about walking together part of it!”
Her voice had become remarkably buoyant as she hurried to my side.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"U… um!"
"Yeah, what?"
"Um… uh… I'm going home along the same way as you, until we reach the hill…"
"Really?
Then let's go together for part of the way."
"…… Eh?"
Yumizuka's eyes widen and she stands there stiffly for a moment.
"Y… yeah!
You're right.
We're going back the same way, so it wouldn't be strange for us to go together for part of the way, right!?"
She says this all with an excessively cheerful voice and comes right beside me.

entries.japanese:
「丁度よかった。
俺、このあたりの道に不慣れだからさ、弓塚さん案内してくれないか」
「うん、それじゃあこっちの道に行こっ。
坂道までの裏道があるんだ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Perfect timing. I don’t know these streets very well, so would you show me the way?”
“Of course. Let’s go this way—there’s a back way to the hill.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Just at the right time, too.
I'm not too familiar with the streets around here, so would you mind guiding me?"
"Sure.
Then, let's go down this street.
It's a back street that leads all the way to the street on the hill."

entries.japanese:
―――弓塚と話をしながら帰り道を歩いていく。
　弓塚との会話は、これといって特徴こそないものの穏やかで楽しいものだった。
　弓塚さつきはとても柔らかな雰囲気をしていて、一緒にいると安心できるタイプだと思う。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――And so I walked home, talking with Yumizuka along the way.
There was nothing remarkable about our conversation, but it was easy and pleasant.
Satsuki Yumizuka had such a gentle air that being with her put me at ease.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---I walk home while chatting with Yumizuka.
Talking to Yumizuka isn't anything particularly special, but it is enjoyable in a peaceful kind of way.
…… Yumizuka Satsuki has a gentle air about her, and I feel safe when I'm with her.

entries.japanese:
「―――ふふ」
　と。
会話のおり、突然思い出したように弓塚は笑みをこぼした。
「なに、いきなり。
なにかおかしなこと言った、俺？」
「ううん。
単にね、わたしと遠野くんは明日から同じ通学路になるんだなあって」
　本当に嬉しそうに、彼女は笑った。
　その笑顔は飾ったところがなくて、見ているこっちまで嬉しくなる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――Hee hee.”
And then. In the middle of our conversation, Yumizuka suddenly laughed as though something had just occurred to her.
“What was that for? Did I say something funny?”
“No. I was only thinking that starting tomorrow, you and I will take the same route to school.”
She looked genuinely delighted.
Her smile was so artless that merely seeing it made me happy too.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Huhu."
While we are talking, Yumizuka suddenly laughs as if she had remembered something.
"What is it, all of a sudden?
Did I say something funny?"
"No, that's not it.
It's just that starting tomorrow, I'll be taking the same route to school as you."
She laughs, looking truly happy.
That honest, smiling face is enough to also make me happy as I watch her.

entries.japanese:
……その、今まで気がつかなかったけど。
　容姿や仕草がどうこう言う前に、弓塚さつきは可愛いと思う。
　前からクラスの男子たちが弓塚さつきにお熱だった理由が、ちょっとだけ理解できた。
entries.maoEnglish:
I had never noticed it before.
Before looks or gestures even entered into it, Satsuki Yumizuka was simply cute.
For the first time, I began to understand why the boys in our class had always been so taken with her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… I didn't realize it up until now.
Even putting her looks and mannerisms aside, Yumizuka Satsuki is kind of cute.
I am slowly beginning to understand why the boys in our class had been so worked up over her for so long now.

entries.japanese:
会話が途切れた。
　弓塚の笑顔に見惚れてしまった俺と、弓塚が黙ってしまったからだ。
　二人とも無言で、夕暮れの住宅地を歩いていく。
　不意に――――
entries.maoEnglish:
The conversation lapsed.
I had become absorbed in Yumizuka’s smile, and she had stopped talking.
We walked together in silence through the residential streets at dusk.
Then, without warning—
entries.mirrorMoon:
Our conversation ceases.
