I'm simply fascinated by Yumizuka's smile and the two of us fall silent.
Without saying anything, we walk towards the residential district in the sunset.
Suddenly---

entries.japanese:
「ね。
中学二年生の冬休みこと、覚えてる？」
　そう、弓塚は呟いた。
「――――？」
　首をかしげる。
　中学二年生の冬休みっていったら、有間の家に居づらいんでわざと補習をうけたり学校に残ったりしていたころだ。
　覚えているかと言われれば覚えているけど、どうしてそんなことを聞かれるのかてんで理由がわからない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hey. Do you remember winter break in our second year of middle school?”
Yumizuka murmured the question.
“――――?”
I tilted my head.
Winter break in our second year was when I felt so uncomfortable at the Arimas’ that I deliberately signed up for extra lessons and lingered at school.
I remembered the period well enough, but I had no idea why she was asking about it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hey, do you remember what happened during the winter vacation of our second year of middle school?"
Yumizuka murmurs.
"……?"
I tilt my head to one side.
The winter vacation of the second year of middle school was when I had applied to stay for extra lessons at school because I felt bad about staying at the Arimas'.
I remember it well enough, but I still don't understand why she had asked me about it.

entries.japanese:
「やっぱりなあ。
遠野くんの事だから、絶対に覚えてなんかないと思った」
　がっくりと肩をおとす弓塚。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I knew it. Knowing you, I was sure you wouldn’t remember.”
Yumizuka’s shoulders sagged.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Just as I thought.
Someone like Tohno-kun would never have remembered."
Disappointed, Yumizuka's shoulders droop.

entries.japanese:
「ほら、わたしたちの中学校って体育倉庫が二つあったでしょ？
　一つはおっきな運動部が使う新しい倉庫、もう一つはバドミントン部とか小さな運動部が使っていた古い倉庫。
　で、この古い倉庫っていうのが問題でね、いつも扉の建て付けが悪くて、開かなくなる事が何回もあったの」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Remember how our middle school had two equipment sheds? There was the new one for the big sports clubs, and the old one that smaller clubs like badminton used.
The old shed was the problem; the door never fitted properly and got stuck all the time.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"There were two sports sheds at our middle school, remember?
One was a new shed used by the big clubs, and the other one was an old one used by the smaller clubs like Badminton.
The old shed had a certain problem where the alignment of the door was bad, so there were often times when it wouldn't open."

entries.japanese: 古い倉庫……体育館裏にあったコンクリート製の小さな建物……？
entries.maoEnglish: The old shed—that little concrete building behind the gym…?
entries.mirrorMoon: Old shed… That little concrete building at the back of the gymnasium…?

entries.japanese:
「ああ、あの倉庫か。
一度生徒が中に閉じ込められてから使われなくなったっていう」
「そうそう。
その生徒っていうのが当時のバドミントン部の二年生」
「――――ああ」
　そう、確かにそんなコトがあった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh, that shed. They stopped using it after a student was locked inside once.”
“Exactly. That student was a second-year in the badminton club.”
“――――Oh.”
Yes—it had happened just as she said.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah, that shed.
The one which they stopped using after some students got trapped inside."
"Yeah, that's the one.
The students were second years from the Badminton club."
"----Ah!"
Yes, something like that did happen.

entries.japanese:
あれは新年になったばかりの、冬の寒い日だった。
　三が日があけて、有間の家に居づらくなった俺は自分から補習を受けたり、学校に残れるような手伝いを申し出ていた。
　けど、それも夕方の五時頃までだ。
　あたりも暗くなってしまい、学校にいた教師たちも帰るという事で俺は教室から追い出された。
entries.maoEnglish:
It was a bitterly cold day just after the New Year.
Once the first three days of the holiday were over, I had grown uncomfortable at the Arimas’ and volunteered for extra lessons and odd jobs that would keep me at school.
But even that only lasted until around five.
Darkness had fallen, and the remaining teachers were leaving, so they chased me out of the classroom.
entries.mirrorMoon:
It was early in the new year, on a cold winter's day.
The first three days of the new year having passed, I had applied for extra lessons and requested to stay behind at school and help out because I felt bad about staying at the Arimas'.
But even that was only until five in the evening.
It had become dark, and I was forced out of the classrooms as all the teachers were going home.

entries.japanese:
冬も最中。
　夕方の五時過ぎといえば、あたりは本当に暗くなっている。
　その日はたしか雪が降ると予報された日で、寒さも一段と厳しかった。
　そんなわけで今日ぐらいはまっすぐ家に帰ろうとした時、校舎裏の旧倉庫からガンガンという音が聞こえてきて、様子を見に行ったんだっけ。
entries.maoEnglish:
It was the dead of winter.
After five in the evening, the grounds were already dark.
Snow had been forecast that day, if I remember correctly, and the cold was especially fierce.
I had decided that, for once, I should go straight home when I heard a furious banging from the old shed behind the school and went to investigate.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The middle of winter.
Even if it was only five, the surroundings really had darkened.
The weather report had predicted snow for that day, and the cold was extra harsh.
And so, just when I had decided to head straight home for the day, I heard a banging sound from the old shed and I went to check things out.

entries.japanese:
―――中に誰かいるの？
　そう問いかけてみたら、倉庫の中から数人の女生徒の声が返ってきた。
　部活の片づけをしている最中、風が入ってきて寒いので扉を閉めたら開かなくなってしまって、もう二時間も閉じ込められている、という事だった。
　どうやっても扉は開かないらしく、できれば先生を呼んで助けてほしい、という。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Is somebody in there?
When I called out, several girls answered from inside.
They had been putting their club equipment away when a cold wind made them shut the door, and then it would not open again; they had already been trapped for two hours.
Nothing they tried would budge the door, so they begged me to find a teacher and get them out.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Is anyone in there?
I asked, and I heard the voices of several female students in reply from inside the shed.
They had been trapped in there for two hours.
While packing up the club equipment, they had closed the door because of the cold, and now it wouldn't open again.
They couldn't open the door no matter what, and wanted me to call one of the teachers for help.

entries.japanese:
……けど、教師たちは全員帰ってしまったし、今から電話で呼びつけても一時間はこのままだろう。
　この日の寒さは、本当にひどかった。
　雪が降ってこないのがおかしいぐらいの寒さの中、体操服のままで二時間も倉庫に閉じ込められていた中の子たちに、もう一時間も待たせるのは酷だと思った。
entries.maoEnglish:
But all the teachers had gone home, and even if I called one back, the girls would remain trapped for another hour.
The cold that day was vicious.
It was strange that snow had not begun to fall, and making girls who had already spent two hours shut in there in nothing but their gym clothes wait another hour seemed cruel.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… But the teachers had all gone home.
Even if I were to call them now on the phone, it'd at least take another hour.
The cold on that day was truly terrible.
In the kind of cold that should have prompted snow, I thought it would be cruel to leave those girls stuck in the shed wearing only their PE uniforms for another hour.

entries.japanese:
少し迷ったあと、周囲を見渡してあたりに誰もいない事を確認し、メガネを外して倉庫の扉に見える『線』を切った。
　そうして扉は開いて、中から五人ほどの、涙で目を真っ赤にした女生徒たちが飛び出してきたんだっけ――――
entries.maoEnglish:
After a moment’s hesitation, I looked around to make sure no one was watching, then removed my glasses and cut one of the ‘lines’ I could see across the door.
The door opened, and five or so girls burst out, their eyes scarlet from crying――――
entries.mirrorMoon:
After some hesitation, and confirming that no one else was around, I took off my glasses and cut the "line" on the shed door.
The door opened, and about five female students, eyes red from crying, poured out---

entries.japanese:
「……そういえば、そんな事もあったな。
　でもそんな話をよく知ってるね。
あれ、閉じ込められてたバドミントン部の主将が“部の存続にかかわるからこの事は秘密にしなさい”って、俺に脅しをかけてきたぐらいなんだけど」
「もうっ。
遠野くんってば中に誰が閉じ込められてたか、まったく興味がなかったんだね。
いい？
　わたしはそのころバドミントン部の部員だったんだよ」
　拗ねるような、弓塚の声。
　えっと―――つまり、それは。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…Now
that you mention it, I do remember. But how do you know so much about it? The badminton captain even threatened me afterward, saying I had to keep quiet or it could
cost them their club.” “Honestly! You really had no interest in who was trapped inside, did you? Listen, I was in the badminton club then.”
Yumizuka sounded almost sulky.
Um―――so that meant…
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Come to think of it, there was something like that.
But I'm surprised you know about it.
The captain of the badminton club who had been trapped had told me, 'This has to do with the club's survival, so don't tell anyone else.' It was almost like she was threatening me."
"Oh, Tohno-kun!
You had no interest in knowing who was trapped inside there, did you?
Listen.
I was one of those badminton club members."
Yumizuka sounds like she's pouting.
Eh… So in other words…

entries.japanese:
「――わたし、ちゃんと憶えてるよ。
　今にして思えばただ倉庫に閉じ込められただけだったんだけど、あの時は寒くて暗くて、すごく不安だった。
　このままここで凍死しちゃうんだーって、みんな本気で思ってたんだから。
おなかだってぐうぐうに減ってたし、ほんとーにダウン寸前だったんだ」
「はあ。
それは、タイヘンだったね」
　いまいち実感が湧かず、気の無い返答をしてしまう。
　弓塚は気にせず、昔の出来事を鮮明に思い出すように語り続けた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――I remember it perfectly Looking back, we were only locked in a shed, but at the time it was dark and freezing, and we were terrified.
We honestly thought we might freeze to death in there.
We were starving too—really, we were on the verge of collapsing.” “That sounds…
awful.” I still couldn’t quite imagine it, and my answer came out halfhearted.
Yumizuka paid no attention.
Unbothered, she went on as though the memory remained brilliantly vivid.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---I still remember it well.
When I think about it now, it was only being trapped inside a shed, but at the time, it was cold and dark, and I was really worried.
Everyone thought we were going to freeze to death like that.
My stomach was growling from hunger, too.
I was just about to collapse."
"Hmm… That must have been rough."
I can't really empathize with her, so I give a half-hearted response.
Unconcerned, Yumizuka continues her recollections, bringing up old events anew.

entries.japanese:
「そうしてみんなが震えてる時にね、遠野くんがやってきたの。
いつもの、自然で気負ったところのない口調で“中に誰かいるの？
”って。
見てわからないのかーっ、て主将がカンシャクをおこしたの、覚えてる？」
「ああ、それは覚えてる。
ドガンって扉にバットを投げつけた音だろ。
アレ、びっくりしたよ」
　そうそう、と弓塚は笑った。
entries.maoEnglish:
“While we were all shivering, you came along. In your usual calm, unruffled voice, you asked, ‘Is anyone in there?’ as though it were nothing. Remember how our captain lost her temper and shouted that it should have been obvious?”
“That I remember. She hurled a bat at the door with a huge bang. It scared the life out of me.”
Yumizuka laughed and agreed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"And just when everyone was trembling, you came along and asked, 'Is anyone in there?' in your usual unexcited voice… and then the captain got angry and shouted, 'Can't you tell just by looking!?'… Do you remember?"
"Yeah, I remember.
There was a loud bang when she threw a bat at the door.
I was really surprised."
"That's right!" Yumizuka says, laughing.

entries.japanese:
「でも、先生方はみんな帰ってるって聞いて、わたしたち本当に絶望したんだから。
あと一分だって耐えられないのに、もしかしたら明日までここに閉じ込められるかもしれないって思って。
　そうしてわたしたちが世をはかなんでいる時にね、コンコンって扉がノックされて、遠野くんはこう言ったんだ。
『内緒にするなら開けられないこともないよ』って」
「ああ。
そこでまたドガンって音がしたっけ。
“かんたんに開けられるなら苦労しないわーっ！
”って、すごい剣幕だった」
entries.maoEnglish:
“But when you told us all the teachers had left, we despaired. We couldn’t stand another minute, and suddenly we thought we might be trapped there until morning.
Just when we had abandoned all hope, someone tapped on the door. Then you said you might be able to open it if we promised to keep it secret.”
“Right. Then there was another tremendous bang.
Your captain was furious. She screamed that if it were that easy, we would not have been in that mess.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"But when we heard all the teachers had gone home, we really lost all hope.
We couldn't stand being there for even a minute longer, and we had to face the prospect of being trapped until the next day.
Just when we were thinking about how miserable the world was, you knocked on the door and said 'I might be able to open the door, if you can keep it a secret.'"
"Yeah.
And then I heard another bang, and someone said, 'If it opened that easily, we wouldn't be suffering in here!' She was really angry."

entries.japanese:
「あはは。
うん、主将はわたしたちが閉じ込められて責任を感じていたから、ちょっと余裕がなかったんだ。
でもね、そしたらすぐに扉が開いたんだよ。
　みんな主将のバットが効いたって喜んで外に飛び出したけど、わたしは扉の横でぼんやりと立ってた遠野くんをちゃんと見てたよ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ahaha. The captain felt responsible for getting us locked in and had no composure left, but then the door opened immediately. Everyone decided her bat must have done it and rushed outside cheering.
I saw you, though, standing beside the door with that absent look on your face.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ahaha.
Yeah, the captain felt responsible for us getting trapped, so she didn't have much patience to spare.
But soon after that, the door opened.
Everyone was happy that the captain's knocking with the bat must have worked and ran outside, but I was watching you, standing by the door."

entries.japanese:
弓塚は暖かい眼差しを向けてくる。
　……けど、そんな目を向けられても、困る。
　あんなこと、こっちにとってはなんでもない事なので、あまり感謝される実感がない。
entries.maoEnglish:
Yumizuka regarded me warmly.
But that kind of look only made me uncomfortable.
What I had done meant nothing to me, so I couldn’t feel that I deserved her gratitude.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Yumizuka looks at me warmly.
…… But that only troubles me.
To me, it meant nothing, so I can't really appreciate her gratitude.

entries.japanese:
「その時ね、わたし、すごく泣いてたの。
まぶたなんか腫れに腫れちゃって、もうクシャクシャ。
そんなわたしを見て、遠野くんはなんて言ったと思う？」
「わからないな。
なんて言ったの？」
　……本当に覚えていないので、他人事のように聞いてみる。
　だっていうのに、弓塚はやっぱり嬉しそうに笑って俺を見た。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I was crying so hard that day. My eyelids were swollen, and my whole face was a mess. What do you think you said when you saw me?”
“I have no idea. What did I say?”
I truly didn’t remember, so I asked with all the detachment of someone hearing about a stranger.
Even so, Yumizuka smiled at me as happily as ever.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I was crying really hard at that time.
My eyes just felt like they were swelling up, and they looked terrible.
What do you think you said when you saw me like that?"
"I don't know.
What did I say?"
…… I really don't remember, so I ask, as if it were something someone else had done.
Despite this, Yumizuka still looks at me happily.

entries.japanese:
「それがね、わたしの頭にぽんって手をのっけて、“早く家に帰って、お雑煮でも食べたら”って。
わたし、よっぽど寒そうに震えていたんだなって恥ずかしくなっちゃった」
「……………」
　むむ、と眉をよせる。
　自分の事ながら、言動の意味が解らない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You put your hand on my head and said, ‘Why don’t you hurry home and have some rice-cake soup?’ I got so embarrassed, thinking I must have looked absolutely frozen.”
“……”
I knitted my brows.
Though I was apparently the one who had said it, I couldn’t fathom what I had meant.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"You put your hand on my head, and said 'Hurry up and go home, and eat some Ozouni'.
I was a little embarrassed because I was trembling so much from the cold."
"……"
"Hmm." I knit my brows.
I don't know what I meant back then.

entries.japanese:
「きっとね、遠野くんはお雑煮を食べれば体が温まるよって言いたかったんだと思う」
「……そっか。
正月の後だったからね」
　……それは、たしかに俺の言いそうな間の抜けたセリフだ。
　こうして言われてみると、もうちょっとマシなセリフがあったんじゃないかって後悔してしまうぐらい。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I think you meant the soup would warm me up.”
“Oh. It was just after New Year’s.”
That did sound exactly like the sort of foolish thing I would say.
Hearing it now almost made me regret that I hadn’t managed something a little better.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I think you meant for me to warm up my body by having some Ozouni."
"…… I see.
It was right after New Year's, after all."
…… That does sound like the stupid kind of thing I would say.
Now that it's put to me like this, I regret not having picked something better to say.

entries.japanese:
「わたしね、あの時に思ったんだ。
　学校には頼れる人はいっぱいいるけど、いざという時に助けてくれる人っていうのは遠野くんみたいな人なんだって」
「まさか、それは買い被りすぎだよ。
ほら、ひよこが初めて見た人間を親と思うのと一緒。
たまたま俺が助けられただけっていう話じゃないか」
「そんな事ない……！
　わたし、あの時から遠野くんならどんな事だって当たり前みたいに助けてくれるって信じてるんだから」
　そうして、彼女は思い立ったように顔をあげた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“That was when I realized something.
There are plenty of people at school you can rely on, but when it truly matters, the person who will save you is someone like you.”
“That’s giving me far too much credit. It’s like a chick deciding the first person it sees must be its mother. I merely happened to be there and happened to be able to help.”
“That isn’t true…! Ever since that day, I’ve believed that no matter what happened, you would save me as though it were the most natural thing in the world.”
With sudden resolve, she raised her face.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Back then I thought, there are plenty of reliable people at school, but if I ever really need to be saved, it will be someone like Tohno-kun who saves me."
"You're exaggerating.
Look, it's like how a baby chick thinks the first human it meets is its mother.
I just happened to help you."
"That's not true…!
Ever since then, I really believed that you'd come and help me no matter what the problem was."
Her expression is quite resolute.

entries.japanese:
「弓塚さん、それ過大評価だよ。
俺はそんなに頼れるヤツじゃないんだけど」
「いいの。
わたしがそう信じてるんだから、そう信じさせて」
　まっすぐに見つめられて断言されると、こっちとしては気恥ずかしくて反論ができない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Yumizuka, you’re overestimating me. I’m really not that dependable.”
“That’s all right. I believe it, so please let me keep believing it.”
When she looked me straight in the eye and said it so firmly, I was too embarrassed to argue.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"You're giving me too much credit, Yumizuka-san.
I'm not that reliable of a person."
"It's alright.
That's what I believe, so let me keep believing it."
She pronounced while staring straight at me, and I am too embarrassed to offer a rebuttal.

entries.japanese:
「――まあ、それは弓塚さんのかってだけど」
「でしょ？
　だからまたわたしがピンチになっちゃったら、その時だって助けてくれるよね？」
　弓塚は笑顔で告げてくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――Well, I suppose you can believe whatever you like.”
“See? So if I ever find myself in trouble again, you’ll save me then too, won’t you?”
Yumizuka asked with a smile.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"--Well, I guess you can believe what you want."
"Isn't that right?
So If I'm ever in a pinch, you'll come and help me, right?"
Yumizuka asks me, smiling.

entries.japanese:
……それは、正直困る。
　俺は弓塚が思っているほどなんでも出来るヤツっていうワケじゃない。
　ワケじゃないけど……こんな笑顔を向けられているのに、その信頼を台無しにする事なんて、したくなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
Honestly, that put me in a difficult position.
I couldn’t do anything and everything the way Yumizuka imagined.
I couldn’t—but with her smiling at me like that, I didn’t want to betray her trust.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… To be honest, that would be kind of troubling.
Despite what she thinks, I'm not the sort of guy who can do everything.
I'm not… but when she faces me with that smile, I don't want to destroy that faith she has in me.

entries.japanese:
「そうだね。
俺に出来る範囲なら、手を貸すよ」
「うん。
ありがとう、遠野くん。
随分と遅れちゃったけど、あの時の遠野くんの言葉、嬉しかった」
　言って、弓塚の足がぴたりと止まった。
　つられてこっちの足も止まる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“All right. If it’s within my power, I’ll help.”
“Thank you, Tohno. I know it’s terribly late to say it. But what you said that day made me happy.”
With that, Yumizuka stopped dead.
I stopped beside her without thinking.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yeah.
If it's within my power, I'll help you."
"Yep!
Thank you, Tohno-kun.
I know it's a bit late to say this, but I was really happy because of what you said to me back then."
So saying, Yumizuka suddenly stops.
Naturally, I stop too.

entries.japanese:
「わたし、遠野くんとこうして話せたらいいなって、ずっと思ってた」
　それは、どこか思いつめたような声だった。
　夕焼けの赤色のせいか、弓塚はどことなく寂しそうに、見える。
「……なにいってるんだ。
話なんていつでもできるよ」
「だめだよ。
遠野くんには乾くんがいるから。
それに、わたしは遠野くんみたいになれないもの」
　遠慮がちに返答して、弓塚は俺から離れていく。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’ve always wished I could talk with you like this.”
There was an intensity in her voice, almost as though she had brooded over the words for a long time.
Perhaps it was only the red of sunset, but Yumizuka looked somehow lonely.
“What are you talking about? We can talk whenever you want.”
“No, we can’t. You have Inui. And I could never be like you.”
Her answer was diffident as Yumizuka stepped away from me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I've always wanted to talk with you like this, Tohno-kun."
Somewhere in her voice was a hint of wistfulness.
Perhaps it's because of the red light from the sunset, but somehow, Yumizuka looks lonely.
"…… What do you mean?
You can talk to me anytime."
"No, I can't.
Inui-kun is always around you, and besides… I can't become someone like you, Tohno-kun."
With that reserved answer, Yumizuka draws away from me.

entries.japanese:
「それじゃあ、わたしの家はこっちだから。
また明日、学校で会おうね」
　ばいばい、と笑顔で手をふって弓塚は別の道へ歩いていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“My house is this way, so I’ll leave you here. I’ll see you at school tomorrow.”
Yumizuka waved goodbye with a smile and set off down another road.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Well, my house is this way, so I'll see you at school tomorrow."
"Bye-bye!" Smiling, Yumizuka waves her hand and begins walking down another street.

entries.japanese:
「え？
　あ、その、なんだか遠野くんのほうが落ち着いてるなって、ちょっと驚いてました」
「そうですか？
　うちはもともと厳しい家だったから、こういうのに慣れてるだけだなんです。
それより先輩、話があるんじゃないんですか？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“What? Oh, I was just surprised that you seemed more at ease with all this than I am.”
“Do I? My family was always strict, so I’m simply used to it. More importantly, didn’t you have something you wanted to discuss?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Eh?
Ah, um… I was just a little surprised at how calm you were about all of this, Tohno-kun."
"Really?
Well, my family is a strict one, so I'm used to these kinds of things.
More importantly, Senpai, didn't you have something you wanted to talk to me about?"

entries.japanese:
「はい。
朝のお礼をまだ言っていなかったので、こうしてお世話をしてあげようかなって思ってたんです」
　先輩は柔らかな笑顔で、なんかとんでもない事を言ってきた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Yes. I still hadn’t thanked you for this morning, so I thought I might look after you like this in return.”
With a gentle smile, she said something rather outrageous.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yes.
I haven't thanked you for this morning yet, so I thought I'd take care of you for a bit like this."
Senpai makes her incredulous statement with a soft smile.

entries.japanese:
「お、お世話って、なんか日本語の使いかた間違ってるよ、先輩」
「あれ、そうですか？
　えっと、礼をつくしておもてなしをする事をお世話をするって言うんじゃないんですか？」
「―――言わない。
間違いではないと思うけど、ちょっと正しくないと思う」
「うーん。
やっぱりこういう作法は難しいんですね。
なれないコトはするものじゃないってコトなんでしょうか」
　あはは、と先輩は照れ笑いをする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“L-look after me?
I think you’re using that phrase wrong, Ciel.” “Am I? I thought giving someone every courtesy and making them welcome was called
looking after them.” “―――Not quite—it may not be completely wrong, but it still isn’t right.”
“Hmm. Etiquette really is difficult, isn’t it? Perhaps this means I shouldn’t attempt things I’m not used to.”
Ciel laughed, a little embarrassed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"T-take care of me?
That's not how you use the phrase 'take care' in Japanese, Senpai."
"Oh, really?
You mean people don't say 'taking care' when they're showing someone hospitality in order to thank them?"
"---No, they don't.
I don't think it's a mistake, exactly, but it's not quite right either."
"Hmm.
These manners-related phrases sure are difficult, aren't they?
I suppose I shouldn't try to use them if I'm not familiar with them."
Senpai laughs embarrassedly.

entries.japanese:
「そんなことないよ。
作法はまず心からって言うし、もてなしたいっていう先輩の気持ちがあるんだから、些細な間違いなんて問題ないでしょう」
　先輩は目をきょとん、とさせてこちらを見つめてくる。
　……なんだか自分が動物園の珍獣になったかって思えるぐらい、先輩は真剣な眼差しを向けてきた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“That’s not true. Good manners begin with the heart, and since you genuinely want to make me welcome, a tiny mistake hardly matters.”
Her eyes widened, and she stared at me.
Her gaze was so earnest that I began to feel like some rare beast on display at the zoo.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No, not at all.
They say manners come from the heart, after all.
As long as you have the right feelings, it's just a trivial error."
Senpai's eyes snap in my direction as she stares at me.
…… Her gaze is so serious I feel like I just became some kind of rare animal in a zoo.

entries.japanese:
「あの……先輩？
　俺、なんか生意気なこと言いましたか？」
「……………………」
　じーっ、と先輩は見つめてくる。
「あの………先輩？」
　なんだか、ひどく恥ずかしい。
「―――遠野くん、やっぱり似合いすぎてます。
わたしより年下なのに落ち着いていて、生意気です」
　むむっ、と先輩は睨んでくる。
　……なんというか、やっぱりこの人の行動心理はよくわからない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ciel? Did I say something impertinent?”
“……”
She continued staring.
“Um…?”
I was becoming acutely embarrassed.
“―――Tohno, this suits you far too well. You’re younger than I am yet far too composed; it’s cheeky.”
She glared at me with a little frown.
As usual, I couldn’t begin to understand what went on in her mind.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Um…… Senpai?
Did I just say something rude?"
"………………"
Senpai continues to stare at me.
"Um……… Senpai?"
For some reason, I feel incredibly embarrassed.
"------It really does suit you well, Tohno-kun.
Being younger yet calmer than me… you're impertinent."
Senpai glares at me.
…… I don't understand how her mind works at all.

entries.japanese:
「―――すみません。
なんだか偉そうな言い方をしちゃってましたよね、さっき」
「はい。
あんまりに生意気なんで、不覚にも感動しちゃいました」
　はあ、と両肩を落として先輩はお茶をすする。
「わたし、遠野くんのコトが知りたくなっちゃいました。
なんでもいいですから話してくれると嬉しいです」
　先輩は姿勢を正して、まるで教師を見る生徒のような態度をする。
「……………」
　とてもじゃないけど、断れる雰囲気じゃない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――Sorry. I sounded awfully pompous just then, didn’t I?”
“Yes. You were so cheeky that, in spite of myself, I was impressed.”
Her shoulders slumped as she sighed and drank her tea.
“I’ve decided I want to know more about you. Anything at all would make me happy, if you’re willing to tell me.”
She straightened her posture like a student waiting for her teacher to begin a lesson.
“……”
This was hardly an atmosphere in which I could refuse.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------I'm sorry.
It was kind of arrogant for me to speak like that."
"Yes, it was so impertinent I was moved."
She lowers her shoulders with a sigh and she sips her tea.
"I've become curious about you, Tohno-kun.
Please, talk to me.
It can be about anything."
Senpai straightens her posture, with an attitude like a teacher looking at her student.
"…………"
It doesn't seem like I can refuse.

entries.japanese:
「……ま、いいけど。
俺の話なんかしてもつまらないぞ、先輩」
　はい、と先輩は笑顔で応える。
　……仕方がない。
　性に合わないけれど、学校での出来事とかを話してみようか―――
entries.maoEnglish:
“All right, then. Nothing about me is very interesting, Ciel.”
Ciel answered with a smiling yes.
I had no choice.
It wasn’t in my nature, but perhaps I could tell her about things that had happened at school―――
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Well, okay, but it's not going to be very interesting if we're just going to talk about me, Senpai."
Senpai responds with a smile.
…… I've got no choice.
It's not like me, but I suppose I'll talk to her about school------

entries.japanese:
結局、先輩はどんな話でも喜んで聞いていた。
　中学時代の話が一番盛り上がったのが意外で、先輩は修学旅行には行かなかったらしい。
『いいですね、みんなで旅行に行くなんて』と目を輝かせていたのが印象的だった。
　ともあれ、一時間も一方的に話すと疲れる。
　先輩に許してもらって、そろそろ帰路につく事にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
In the end, she delighted in everything I told her.
To my surprise, stories from middle school excited her most; apparently she hadn’t gone on the school trip.
I still remembered how her eyes shone as she said, “It sounds wonderful, everyone traveling together.”
Still, talking by myself for an hour was exhausting.
With her permission, I finally set out for home.
entries.mirrorMoon:
In the end, Senpai was happy to listen no matter what I talked to her about.
It was surprising to see her get so worked up when we were talking about middle school.
Apparently, Senpai had never been on a school trip.
"That sounds nice, everyone going on a trip together," she said, her eyes twinkling.
It was quite an impressive sight.
At any rate, I held a one-sided conversation for an hour, but it made me rather tired.
With Senpai's permission, I decide to head home.

entries.japanese:
「おはよう琥珀さん。
今朝はいい天気ですね」
「はい、おはようございます志貴さん」
　ありきたりの朝の挨拶に、琥珀さんは満面の笑みを返してくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Good morning, Kohaku. Beautiful day, isn’t it?”
“Good morning, Shiki.”
Kohaku answers my commonplace greeting with a radiant smile.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Morning, Kohaku-san.
Today is a lovely day."
"Yes.
Good morning, Shiki-san."
Kohaku-san delivers her ordinary morning greeting with a smile on her face.

entries.japanese:
「昨夜はよくお眠りになられましたか？
　慣れないお屋敷の夜でしたから、色々と不具合がないかって心配していたんですけど」
「ああ、とりあえず困るようなコトはないよ。
これでも昔はここに住んでいたんだし、今はちゃんと気を配ってくれる琥珀さんがいるし」
「あら。
お上手ですね、志貴さん」
「えっ？
　いや、たんに思ったことを口にしただけど……お上手って、なにが上手なんですか？」
　琥珀さんは笑顔のままこっちを眺めているだけだ。
　……なんていうか、そうまっすぐに見られると照れくさくて、視線をよそに移す。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Did you sleep well? It was your first night in an unfamiliar estate, so I was worried something might not suit you.”
“Nothing’s given me any trouble so far. I did live here once, after all—and now I have you looking after me so thoughtfully.”
“My, how smooth of you, Shiki.”
“What? I only said what I was thinking… Smooth at what, exactly?”
Kohaku merely keeps smiling at me.
Having her look at me so directly is embarrassing somehow, and I turn my eyes away.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Did you sleep well last night?
I was worried that you might be inconvenienced, staying in an unfamiliar mansion and all."
"Ah, no, there were no problems.
I used to live here, after all, and now I've got you to watch over me, Kohaku-san."
"Oh, you're quite good at this, Shiki-san."
"Eh?
No, I'm just saying what I think… what is it I'm good at?"
Kohaku-san just looks at me, smiling.
…… Somehow, I feel embarrassed when she looks directly at me, so I shift my gaze to the side.

entries.japanese:
―――と。
　さっきから無言でこっちを見つめている、もう一つの視線に気がついた。
「あ……よお」
　軽く手をあげて挨拶をする。
　秋葉はじっとこっちを見つめてくる。
……っていうか、睨んできてる。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――That was when.
I notice another pair of eyes that has been silently fixed on me all this time.
“Oh—hey.”
I raise one hand in a casual greeting.
Akiha keeps staring at me. No, she is glaring.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---And then.
--I realize another stare, one which has been on me silently for a while now.
"Ah… hey there."
I give a light wave to greet her.
Akiha continues to stare at me… or perhaps, glare would be a better word.

entries.japanese:
「えっと、その……おはよう、秋葉」
「あら、無理に挨拶をしてくれなくてもいいのに。
どうぞ、私のことは無視して結構です。
兄さんは琥珀と楽しく朝を迎えたいみたいですから」
「うっ……」
　秋葉の言葉はちくちくする。
　……こっちだって別に秋葉のことを無視していたわけじゃなくて、ただ琥珀さんに挨拶をしただけなんだけど……。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Um—good morning, Akiha.”
“Oh, you needn’t force yourself to greet me. Please, feel free to ignore me. You clearly prefer beginning your morning with Kohaku.”
“Urgh…”
Akiha’s words prick like needles.
I had not meant to ignore Akiha; I simply greeted Kohaku first.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Well… um… good morning, Akiha."
"Oh?
You don't have to force yourself to greet me.
Please, go right ahead and ignore me.
After all, it seems you'd prefer to enjoy the morning with Kohaku."
"Uuh…"
Akiha's words sting.
…… It's not like I had intended to ignore her.
I just said hello to Kohaku-san…

entries.japanese:
「秋葉さま、あんまり志貴さんをいじめないであげてください。
お時間もありませんし、志貴さんはまだ朝食を済ませていないんですから」
「朝食が済んでいないのは兄さんの起床が遅いからでしょう。
朝があわただしくなるのは兄さんの自業自得です」
　ふん、と鼻をならす秋葉。
　……どうも、俺がこの時間にやってきた事に文句があるのにプラスして、秋葉に挨拶をしなかったのがダブルパンチで気に食わないみたいだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Miss Akiha, please don’t tease Shiki so. We’re short on time, and he hasn’t eaten breakfast yet.”
“He hasn’t eaten because he rose too late. If his morning is rushed, he has no one but himself to blame.”
Akiha gives a disdainful little sniff.
Apparently she resented both my arriving at this hour and my failure to greet her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Please don't tease Shiki-san too much, Akiha-sama.
We don't have much time, and Shiki-san hasn't finished his breakfast yet."
"Well, that's Nii-san's fault for waking up late, isn't it?
He's just getting what he deserves for leaving everything to do in a rush in the morning."
"Hmph!" Akiha sniffs.
…… It seems like my failure to greet her was another point she was unimpressed with, in addition to her objection to my late arrival.

entries.japanese:
「……あの、琥珀さん。
朝食って、俺の分はできてるんですか？」
「はい、食堂にご用意させていただきました。
どうぞ、ゆっくり召し上がってくださいな」
「だめよ琥珀、そんなの無理にきまってるでしょう。
もうこんな時間なんだから、兄さんに朝食を摂る時間なんてありません」
entries.maoEnglish:
“…Kohaku, did you make breakfast for me?”
“Yes, it’s waiting in the dining room. Please take your time and enjoy it.”
“Don’t be absurd, Kohaku; he can hardly take his time at this hour. Brother has no time left for breakfast.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Um… Kohaku-san.
Is my breakfast ready?"
"Yes, I've laid it out in the dining hall.
Please, eat up at your leisure."

entries.japanese:
「あのな秋葉、まだ七時を過ぎたばかりなんだから、それぐらいの時間はあるよ。
ここからうちの高校まで徒歩三十分ちょいなんだから、十分ぐらいゆっくりしてられるじゃないか」
「つまり朝食にかける時間は十分だけですか。
おなかをすかせた犬じゃないんですから、朝食はゆっくりとってほしいですね」
「─────」
　秋葉の言葉には、やっぱり棘がある。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Listen, Akiha, it’s only just past seven, and school is barely more than thirty minutes away, so I can spare ten minutes easily.” “Ten whole minutes for breakfast?
You’re not a starving dog. I would prefer you ate like a civilized human being.”
“─────”
There are thorns in every word she says.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"That won't do, Kohaku.
Nii-san has no time to eat breakfast at this time."
"Hey, listen, Akiha.
It's only seven, so I've got at least that much.
It's an easy thirty minute walk from here to school, so I can take it easy for at least ten minutes, can't I?"
"Are you saying you're going to finish breakfast in just ten minutes?
You're not some starving dog, so if you're going to eat breakfast, I'd like you to take your time."
"------"
Akiha's words really do have thorns in them.

entries.japanese:
「二人とも、おはよう」
「おはようございます、志貴さん」
　琥珀さんは白い割烹着に相応しい、これ以上ないっていうぐらいの笑顔で挨拶をかえしてくれた。
　一方秋葉はというと、ちらりとこちらを一瞥するなり、
「おはようございます。
朝はずいぶんとゆっくりなんですね、兄さん」
　なんて最高に気の利いた嫌味をこぼしてくれる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Morning, you two.”
“Good morning, Shiki.”
Kohaku answers with the warmest smile imaginable, perfectly at home above her snowy kitchen smock.
Akiha, on the other hand, gives me one sidelong glance and—
“Good morning. You certainly take your time getting started, Brother.”
A magnificently well-aimed piece of sarcasm.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Good morning, you two."
"Good morning, Shiki-san."
Wearing a white apron that suits her, Kohaku-san replies with a smile that could not possibly be any larger.
On the other hand, Akiha just casts a glance at me.
"Good morning.
You certainly took your time this morning, Nii-san."
She certainly knows how to put a damper on things.

entries.japanese:
「ゆっくりって、まだ七時を過ぎたばっかりじゃないか。
ここからうちの高校まで徒歩三十分ちょいなんだ、今日は早起きしたほうだよ」
「つまり朝食にかける時間は十分だけですか。
おなかをすかせた犬じゃないんですから、朝食はゆっくりとってください」
「─────」
　秋葉の言葉には、やっぱり棘がある。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Take my time—it’s only just past seven, and school is barely more than thirty minutes away. By my standards, I got up early today.”
“Which leaves you ten whole minutes for breakfast. You’re not a starving dog, so please eat like a civilized human being.”
“─────”
There are thorns in every word she says.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Took my time?
It's barely past seven!
It only takes thirty minutes to get to school from here, so I'm actually up early."
"So you're saying you're going to finish breakfast in just ten minutes?
You're not some starving dog, so if you're going to eat breakfast, I'd like you to take your time."
"------"
Akiha's words really do have thorns.

entries.japanese:
その頃、屋敷は大きな遊び場だった。
　深い森のような庭。
　高い城のような家。
　何日かかっても探険しきれない閉じた箱庭の世界で、ボクたちは遊びまわった。
entries.maoEnglish:
Back then, the estate was one enormous playground.
A garden as deep as a forest.
A house as tall as a castle.
We ran wild through that little walled-off world, too vast to explore even if we spent days trying.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Back then, the whole mansion was like a giant playground.
The garden, a deep forest.
The house, a tall castle.
We played in our own little world, which would take days to explore.

entries.japanese:
毎日は楽しかった。
　年をとるなんて事もしらなかったし、
　朝と夜はおんなじように繰り返されるんだって疑いもしなかった。
　それは、ただ、子犬のようにはしゃぎまわった幼年期。
　ボクらはとても気が合って、最高の遊び仲間だった。
entries.maoEnglish:
Every day was fun.
We did not know that people grew older,
and we never doubted that morning and night would go on repeating exactly the same way forever.
It was childhood, nothing more: the years when we tumbled about like puppies.
We understood each other perfectly and were the best playmates in the world.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Every day was fun.
No one thought about ever growing up,
and we believed that days and nights would always be the same.
It was just a childhood spent playing like puppies.
We got along wonderfully, and were the best of playmates.

entries.japanese:
振り向けばいつもあきはがいて、手を振ると恥ずかしがって隠れてしまう。
　うん、そんなのもいつもどおり。
entries.maoEnglish:
Whenever I looked back, akiha was there; whenever I waved, she blushed and hid.
Yes—that was how it always was.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Whenever I turned back, Akiha would be there, waving her hands and hiding shyly.
Yes, always the same.

entries.japanese:
その頃、屋敷は大きな遊び場だった。
　深い森のような庭。
　高い城のような家。
　何日かかっても探険しきれない箱庭の閉じた世界で、ボクたちは遊びまわった。
entries.maoEnglish:
Back then, the estate was one enormous playground.
A garden as deep as a forest.
A house as tall as a castle.
We ran wild through that little walled-off world, too vast to explore even if we spent days trying.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Back then, the whole mansion was like a giant playground.
The garden, a deep forest.
The house, a tall castle.
We played in our own little world, which would take days to explore.

entries.japanese:
「―――おはようございます」
　……聞き慣れない声がする。
　見ていた夢が急速に失われていった後に残るのは、目覚めようとするけだるい体の感覚だけだ。
「朝です。
お目覚めの時間です、志貴さま」
　聞き慣れない声がする。
　……だから、志貴さまはやめてくれないか。
　そう言われると背筋が寒くなるって、昨日ちゃんと言ったっていうのに────
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――Good morning.”
An unfamiliar voice.
The dream vanished with startling speed, leaving behind only the leaden sensation of a body struggling to wake.
“It is morning. Time to wake up, Master Shiki.”
That unfamiliar voice again.
Could she stop calling me Master Shiki already?
I had told her yesterday that it sent a chill down my spine────
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Good morning."
…… I hear an unfamiliar voice.
The dream disappears, and all that remains is the feeling of my languid, waking body.
"It is morning.
Time to wake up, Shiki-sama."
An unfamiliar voice greets me.
…… Stop calling me Shiki-sama already.
I told you yesterday, it sends chills down my back----

entries.japanese:
―――――目が覚めた。
　翡翠はベッドから離れたところで、なにかの彫像のように立ち尽くしている。
「…………」
　ここは、ドコだっけ。
「おはようございます、志貴さま」
　メイド服の少女がおじぎをする。
「……ああ、そうだ。
俺は、自分の家に戻ってきたんだっけ」
　体を起こして部屋の様子を流し見る。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――――My eyes opened.
Hisui stood well away from the bed, motionless as a statue.
“……”
Where was I?
“Good morning, Master Shiki.”
The girl in the maid uniform bowed.
“Oh… right—I came back home.”
I sat up and surveyed the room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---I wake up.
Hisui stands far from the bed, like a statue.
"……"
Where am I?
"Good morning, Shiki-sama."
A girl in a maid uniform bows.
"Ah… yeah, I came home, right…"
I push myself up, and look around the room.

entries.japanese:
「おはよう翡翠。
わざわざ起こしてくれて、ありがとう」
「そのようなお言葉は必要ありません。
志貴さまをお起こしするのはわたしの責務ですから」
　翡翠は淡々と、まったくの無表情で返答する。
「そ、そうか。
なら、いいんだけど」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Good morning, Hisui. Thanks for going to the trouble of waking me.”
“Your thanks are unnecessary. Waking Master Shiki is one of my duties.”
Hisui answered evenly, without the slightest change of expression.
“O-oh. Well, all right, then.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Good morning, Hisui.
Thanks for coming to wake me."
"There is no need to thank me.
It is my duty to come and wake you, Shiki-sama."
Hisui answers indifferently, completely expressionless.
"Ah, really…?
Okay then…"

entries.japanese:
……ひいき目に見なくても、翡翠はきれいな顔立ちをしていると思う。
　そういう子に起こされるのは喜ぶべきことなんだろうけど、翡翠にこうも感情がないとあまり嬉しい、という感じはしない。
　……もったいない。
　翡翠も琥珀さんの半分ぐらい明るければ、ものすごく可愛いと思うんだけど。
entries.maoEnglish:
Even without the benefit of bias, Hisui had a beautiful face.
Being awakened by a girl like her ought to have been a pleasure, but with so little emotion in her, it did not feel particularly delightful.
What a waste.
If Hisui were even half as cheerful as Kohaku, she would be incredibly cute.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Even in an unfavorable light, I think Hisui's features are beautiful.
It should be wonderful for such a girl to wake me every morning, but as Hisui never smiles, I don't feel that happy about it.
…… What a shame.
If Hisui only had half of Kohaku's brightness, she would be really cute.

entries.japanese:
「―――なにかご用ですか？」
　こっちの視線に気づいたのか、翡翠はまっすぐに見つめ返してくる。
「いや、なんでもない。
目が覚めてまっさきに翡翠の顔を見て、ここが遠野の屋敷なんだなって実感しただけだよ」
　さて、とベッドから起きて、うーんと大きく両手を伸ばす。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――Do you require something?”
Perhaps she had noticed me staring, for Hisui met my eyes directly.
“No, nothing. Seeing your face first thing when I woke up simply made it sink in that I’m back at the Tohno estate.”
I climbed out of bed and stretched both arms high above my head.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Do you need something?"
Realizing I am looking at her, Hisui stares straight back at me.
"No, nothing at all.
Waking up with you there makes me feel like I'm really at the Tohno mansion."
Now then.
Getting off the bed, I stretch out both arms.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま、お時間があまりございません。
お屋敷から志貴さまの学校まで三十分ほどかかりますから、あと二十分ほどで朝食を召し上がっていただかないと」
「え―――うわあ、もう七時をすぎてるじゃないか！」
　時計を見て愕然とした。
　……昨日の夜、何度も目を覚ましたせいで体内時計が狂ったみたいだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki, there is very little time. It takes approximately thirty minutes to walk from the estate to Master Shiki’s school, so you must finish breakfast within the next twenty.”
“What—oh no, it’s already past seven!”
I stared at the clock in horror.
Waking so many times during the night must have thrown off my internal clock.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama, there is no time.
From the mansion to your school is a thirty minute trip.
This leaves only twenty minutes for breakfast."
"Eh?
…… Ahh!
It's already seven o'clock!?"
I gasp in amazement after looking at the clock.
…… My repeated awakenings last night must have messed up my sleep pattern.

entries.japanese:
「学校の制服はそちらにたたんであります。
着替えが済みしだい居間においでください」
「くそ、どうせ起こしてくれるならもっと早く起こしてくれればいいのに……！」
　自分勝手な独り言をいいながら、たたまれた学生服に手を伸ばす。
　学校の制服はきちんとたたまれていて、シャツにはアイロンまでかけられている。
　袖に腕を通すと、なんだか新品みたいに気持ちがよかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Your school uniform is folded over there. Please come to the sitting room once you have dressed.”
“Damn it, if she was going to wake me, she could at least have done it earlier…!”
Muttering this thoroughly selfish complaint, I reached for my folded uniform.
It had been arranged perfectly, and even the shirt was freshly pressed.
Sliding my arms into the sleeves felt almost as good as putting on something new.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Your uniform is folded and awaits you over there.
Please come to the sitting room after you have changed."

"Damn it, if you're going to wake me, wake me up earlier…"
Muttering selfishly to myself, I reach for the uniform.
It's folded neatly, and the shirt has even been ironed.
Passing my wrists through the sleeves feels good.
It's that fresh, brand-new feeling.

entries.japanese:
居間には秋葉と琥珀さんがくつろいでいた。
　秋葉の制服は浅上女学院、という有名なお嬢様学園の物だろう。
　二人はとっくに朝食をすませたのか、優雅に紅茶なんぞを飲んでいた。
entries.maoEnglish:
Akiha and Kohaku were relaxing in the sitting room.
Akiha’s uniform must belong to Asagami Girls’ Academy, that famous school for well-bred young ladies.
They had evidently finished breakfast long ago and were now sipping tea with infuriating elegance.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Akiha and Kohaku-san are relaxing in the sitting room.
Akiha is wearing the uniform of the Asagami Ladies' Academy, a famous school for young girls.
They are drinking tea together gracefully, as if breakfast ended a long time ago.

entries.japanese:
「―――おはようございます」
　……聞き慣れない声がする。
　見ていた夢が急速に失われていって、現実に呼び起こそうとする声がする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――Good morning.”
An unfamiliar voice.
My dream drained rapidly away as the voice called me back to reality.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Good morning."
…… I hear an unfamiliar voice.

The dream quickly fades away as a voice calls me back to reality.

entries.japanese:
「朝です。
お目覚めの時間です、志貴さま」
　聞き慣れない声がする。
　……だから、志貴さまはやめてくれないか。
　そう言われると背筋が寒くなるって、昨日ちゃんと言ったっていうのに────
entries.maoEnglish:
“It is morning. Time to wake up, Master Shiki.”
That unfamiliar voice again.
Could she stop calling me Master Shiki already?
I had told her yesterday that it sent a chill down my spine────
entries.mirrorMoon:
"It is morning.
Time to wake up, Shiki-sama."
An unfamiliar voice greets me.
…… Stop calling me Shiki-sama already.
I told you yesterday, it sends chills down my back----

entries.japanese:
―――目が覚めた。
　翡翠はベッドから離れたところで、なにかの彫像のように立ち尽くしている。
「ん…………」
　寝ぼけ眼であたりを見渡す。
「おはようございます、志貴さま」
　メイド服の少女がおじぎをする。
　一瞬我が目を疑って、ようやく遠野志貴の現状を思い出した。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――My eyes opened.
Hisui stood well away from the bed, motionless as a statue.
“Mmm……”
I peered around through half-awake eyes.
“Good morning, Master Shiki.”
The girl in the maid uniform bowed.
For one moment I doubted my eyes, then at last remembered the situation Shiki Tohno was in.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---I wake up.
Hisui stands far from the bed, like a statue.
"Mm……"
I sleepily look around.
"Good morning, Shiki-sama."
A girl in a maid uniform bows.
For a moment, I doubt my eyes.
Finally, I recall my current condition.

entries.japanese:
「……そっか。
自分の家に戻ってきたんだっけ」
　体を起こして部屋の様子を流し見る。
　窓の外はいい天気だ。
　夢の中で見たような、ぬけるような青い空。
「おはよう翡翠。
わざわざ起こしてくれて、ありがとう」
「そのようなお言葉は必要ありません。
志貴さまをお起こしするのはわたしの責務ですから」
　翡翠は淡々と、まったくの無表情で返答する。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh… right—I came back home.”
I sat up and surveyed the room.
The weather outside was beautiful.
The sky was the same boundless blue I had seen in my dream.
“Good morning, Hisui. Thanks for going to the trouble of waking me.”
“Your thanks are unnecessary. Waking Master Shiki is one of my duties.”
Hisui answered evenly, without the slightest change of expression.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yeah, I came home, right…"
I push myself up, and look around the room.
Outside the window, the weather is great.
A blue sky like the one I saw in my dream.
"Good morning, Hisui.
Thanks for coming to wake me."
"There is no need to thank me.
It is my duty to come and wake you, Shiki-sama."
Hisui answers indifferently, completely expressionless.

entries.japanese:
「……はあ。
どうしてそうかたっくるしいのかなあ、翡翠は」
　本当にもったいない。
　翡翠も琥珀さんの半分ぐらい明るければ、ものすごく可愛いと思うんだけど。
「志貴さま。
なにかご用ですか？」
　こっちの視線に気づいたのか、翡翠はまっすぐに見つめ返してくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“……Honestly, Hisui, why do you have to be so stiff?”
It really was a waste.
If she were even half as cheerful as Kohaku, she would be incredibly cute.
“Master Shiki, do you require something?”
Perhaps she had noticed me staring. Hisui met my eyes directly.
entries.mirrorMoon:
*sigh*
"…… Why do you have to be so formal, Hisui?"
It's really a shame.
If Hisui only had half of Kohaku's brightness, she would be really cute.
"---Do you need something?"
Realizing I am looking at her, Hisui stares straight back at me.

entries.japanese:
「あ、いや、なんでもない。
目が覚めてまっさきに翡翠の顔を見て、ここが遠野の屋敷なんだなって実感しただけで――――」
　氷のような、翡翠の瞳。
　それはついさっきまで見ていた、ゆめのなかの光景に酷似している―――
「―――――そう、か」
　完全に思い出した。
　あの日、去り際にリボンを渡してくれたのは、いつも窓から俺たちを眺めていた少女のほうだ。
　それは、つまり―――
「翡翠……だったんだ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh, no, nothing. Seeing your face first thing when I woke up simply made it sink in that I’m back at the Tohno estate────”
Hisui’s eyes were cold as ice.
They were exactly like the eyes from the dream I had been having moments ago―――
“―――――I see.”
The memory returned in full.
The girl who gave me the ribbon as I left that day was the one who had always watched us from the window.
Which meant―――
“It was you—Hisui.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah, no, nothing at all.
Waking up and seeing your face, I just felt like I'm really at the Tohno mansion…"
Hisui's eyes are like cold ice.
Seeing that all of a sudden, something reminiscent of a dream flashes through my mind---
"-----I, see."
I remember it completely.
That day, that girl who gave me the ribbon right before I left was the one who always watched us from that window.
That is, in other words---
"It was…… Hisui."

entries.japanese:
「はい。
何かおっしゃられましたか、志貴さま？」
「ああ……翡翠、覚えているかな。
八年前、俺がここを出ていく時のことなんだけど」
「はい、それでしたら覚えております。
ですが、それが何か？」
「え―――何かって、翡翠」
「申し訳ありませんが、志貴さまがお屋敷を後にしてから八年が経ちました。
ですからあの頃の事をおっしゃられましても、わたしは克明にお答えできません」
「な―――――」
　それは、あの時の約束なんて覚えていないっていう事なのか。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Yes? Did you say something, Master Shiki?”
“Hisui, do you remember the day I left here eight years ago?” “Yes, I remember.
But why do you ask?” “Wh―――what do you mean, Hisui?”
“My apologies.
Eight years have passed since Master Shiki left the estate. I cannot answer every question about those days in precise detail.”
“Wh―――――”
Did that mean she had forgotten the promise we made?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yes?
Did you say something, Shiki-sama?"
"Ah…… Hisui, do you remember?
About when I left here eight years ago?"
"Yes, I remember it.
But, was there anything special that happened?"
"Eh---anything special?
Hisui?"
"Please forgive me.
Eight years has passed since you departed this mansion.
So even if you speak of those times, I cannot answer with any specific details."
"Wha-----"
Does she not remember the promise we made back then?

entries.japanese:
「翡翠―――リボンのこと、覚えてないのか」
「……リボン……ですか？」
　なにか言いにくそうに俯いて、翡翠ははい、と断言する。
「……そっか。
そうだよな、八年も前のことだもんな。
……ごめん、なんでもないんだ。
今のは忘れてくれ」
「………………………」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hisui―――don’t you remember the ribbon?”
“A ribbon…?”
Hisui lowered her head as though the answer were difficult to give, then answered with a firm yes.
“I see. Of course—it was eight years ago. Sorry, it’s nothing. Forget I asked.”
“……”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hisui---you don't remember about the ribbon?"
"…… Ribbon……?"
She looks downcast as she admits with difficulty that she does not remember.
"…… I see.
That's right, it was eight years ago…… Sorry, it's nothing.
Just forget about what I said."
"……………………"

entries.japanese:
……約束は忘れられていた。
　けど、それを恨むような気分でもない。
　なにぶん子供のころの話だし、あの頃、あの約束のおかげで前向きに生きていこうって思えたのは本当のことなんだし。
entries.maoEnglish:
The promise had been forgotten.
Yet I could not bring myself to resent her.
We had only been children, and it remained true that the promise had given me the strength to face my new life.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… She doesn't remember the promise.
But, it isn't anything I can hold against her.
Even though it was maybe just a childish promise, it really did help me to face forward into the future back then.

entries.japanese:
「さてと、それじゃあ起きるとしますか。
翡翠、いま何時だかわかる？」
「はい、朝の七時をすぎた頃です」
「オーケー、それなら少しは余裕があるかな」
　うーん、と背を伸ばしてベッドから立ちあがる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Well, time to get up. Hisui, do you know what time it is?”
“It’s shortly after seven.”
“Okay, then I have a little time to spare.”
I stretched and rose from the bed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Well, time to get up.
Hisui, do you know what time it is?"
"Yes, it is now past seven o'clock in the morning."
"Okay, that leaves me just a little time then."
Stretching my back, I get up out of bed.

entries.japanese:
「お言葉ですが、あまりお時間はございません。
このお屋敷から志貴さまの学校まで三十分ほどかかりますから、あと二十分ほどで朝食を召し上がっていただかないと」
「え―――そっか、ここ有間の家じゃないんだっけ！」
　愕然とした。
　慣れ親しんだ有間の家からだったら二十分ぐらいで学校に行けるんだけど、ここからだと近道さえ解らない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Forgive me, but there is very little time. It takes approximately thirty minutes to walk from the estate to Master Shiki’s school, so you must finish breakfast within the next twenty.”
“What—that’s right, this isn’t the Arima estate!”
I froze in horror.
From the familiar Arima estate I could reach school in twenty minutes, but from here I did not even know the shortcuts.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"You say that, but you do not have much time.
It takes about thirty minutes to go from the mansion to your school.
You only have twenty minutes to eat breakfast and get ready."
"Eh----that's right, this isn't Arimas' house!"
I'm filled with horror.
I was so used to the Arima house being only twenty minutes away from school, but from here, I don't even know a shortcut.

entries.japanese:
「学校の制服はそちらにたたんであります。
着替えが済みしだい居間においでください」
「くそ、どうせ起こしてくれるならもっと早く起こしてくれればいいのに……！」
　自分勝手な独り言をいいながら、たたまれた学生服に手を伸ばす。
　学校の制服はきちんとたたまれていて、シャツにはアイロンまでかけられている。
　袖に腕を通すと、なんだか新品みたいに気持ちがよかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Your school uniform is folded over there. Please come to the sitting room once you have dressed.”
“Damn it, if she was going to wake me, she could at least have done it earlier…!”
Muttering this thoroughly selfish complaint, I reached for my folded uniform.
It had been arranged perfectly, and even the shirt was freshly pressed.
Sliding my arms into the sleeves felt almost as good as putting on something new.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Your uniform is folded and awaits you over there.
Please come to the sitting room after you have changed."
"Damn it, if you're going to wake me, wake me up earlier…"
Muttering selfishly to myself, I reach for the uniform.
It's folded neatly, and the shirt has even been ironed.
Passing my wrists through the sleeves feels good.
It's that fresh, brand-new feeling.

entries.japanese:
居間には秋葉と琥珀さんがくつろいでいた。
　秋葉の制服は浅上女学院、という有名なお嬢様学園の物だろう。
　二人はとっくに朝食をすませたのか、優雅に紅茶なんぞを飲んでいた。
entries.maoEnglish:
Akiha and Kohaku were relaxing in the sitting room.
Akiha’s uniform must belong to Asagami Girls’ Academy, that famous school for well-bred young ladies.
They had evidently finished breakfast long ago and were now sipping tea with infuriating elegance.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Akiha and Kohaku-san are relaxing in the sitting room.
Akiha is wearing the uniform of the Asagami Ladies' Academy, a famous school for young girls.
They are drinking tea together gracefully, as if breakfast ended a long time ago.

entries.japanese:
「秋葉さま、そろそろお時間のほうも限界ですけど、よろしいんですか？」
「……わかってます。
もうっ、初日からこれじゃ先が思いやられるじゃない」
　ぶつぶつ、と文句らしきものを呟いて秋葉はソファーから立ちあがる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Miss Akiha, you’re nearly out of time—are you certain you shouldn’t leave?”
“…I know—honestly, if this is how things are on the very first morning, I dread what comes next.”
Still muttering complaints, Akiha rises from the sofa.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Akiha-sama?
It's almost time to leave; is this alright?"
"…… I know.
Sheesh, don't be so worried over stuff like this on the first day."
Muttering some complaints, Akiha stands up.

entries.japanese:
「それでは、私は時間ですのでお先に失礼します。
兄さんもお気をつけて勉学に励んでください」
　秋葉はそのまま居間を後にした。
　秋葉を玄関まで送るのか、琥珀さんも居間を後にする。
「勉学に励めって、秋葉」
　……やっぱり親父の下で八年間もしつけられたからだろうか、細かいところで古くさいというか、礼儀ただしいというか。
「……まあ、言われなくても学校には行くけどさ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“I must be going. Take care, Brother, and apply yourself diligently to your studies.”
With that, Akiha leaves the sitting room.
Kohaku follows, presumably to see her to the front door.
“Apply myself diligently, she says…”
Perhaps eight years under Father’s discipline made her sound old-fashioned—or simply very proper.
Well, I was going to school whether she told me to or not.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Well, I must say goodbye.
Nii-san, you should apply yourself to your studies today."
Akiha leaves the sitting room.
Kohaku-san follows, seeing her off.
"Apply myself to my studies…?"
She's quite ceremonious about trivial things in an old fashioned kind of way… I guess it's because she's been disciplined under our old man for the last eight years.
"…… Well, I'd have gone to school even if she hadn't said anything."

entries.japanese:
ぽりぽり、と頬をかく。
　去り際にみせた秋葉の顔はどうしてか胸をついて、朝から色々と注意されたことなんてどうでもよくなってしまった。
「そっか――――」
　ぽん、と手を叩く。
　さっきの秋葉の顔は、昔の秋葉にすごく似ていたから、俺はわけもなく目を奪われてしまったのだろう―――
entries.maoEnglish:
I scratch my cheek.
The expression Akiha wore as she left struck strangely deep, until all her scolding this morning ceased to matter.
“So that’s it――――”
I clap my hands together.
That expression looked so much like the Akiha I knew as a child that it must be why I could not take my eyes off her―――
entries.mirrorMoon:
I scratch my cheek.
There was something about Akiha's face as she left… because of it, I paid no attention at all to her various admonishings this morning.
"Of course---"
I clap my hands together.
For some reason, Akiha's face just then seemed to resemble her face from long ago---

entries.japanese:
琥珀さんが用意してくれた朝食を食べたあと、ロビーに出る。
　と、ロビーには翡翠が鞄を持って待っていた。
「志貴さま、お時間はよろしいのですか？」
「ああ、こっから学校まで走れば二十分ないからね。
いま七時半だろ、寄り道をしても間に合うよ」
　こっちの説明に満足したのか、こくん、と翡翠は頷く。
entries.maoEnglish:
After eating the breakfast Kohaku prepared, I step into the entrance hall.
Hisui is waiting there with my schoolbag.
“Master Shiki, are you certain you have enough time?”
“Sure. If I run, I can make school in under twenty minutes—even with a detour, I have plenty of time.”
Apparently satisfied, Hisui gives one small nod.
entries.mirrorMoon:
After eating the breakfast Kohaku-san prepared, I exit into the lobby.
Hisui was waiting there with my bag.
"Shiki-sama, have you enough time?"
"Yeah, it should only be twenty minutes to school if I run.
It's only seven-thirty, so I should be fine even if I take the long way."
Seeming satisfied with this answer, Hisui bows her head in assent.

entries.japanese:
「それでは、外までお見送りいたします」
「え―――あ、うん、どうも」
　……やっぱり、自分付きの使用人というのはひどく照れくさい。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Then I shall see you to the gate.”
“Oh—sure, thanks.”
Having a servant assigned especially to me is still painfully embarrassing.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Then, allow me to see you out."
"Eh?
Ah, yeah… thank you."
…… I still feel terribly awkward having my own servant.

entries.japanese:
「あ、志貴さん！
　ちょっと待ってください！」
　たたたっ、と琥珀さんが二階から降りてきた。
「……………………」
　翡翠は琥珀さんがやってくると、すい、と身を引いて黙ってしまう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Shiki! Please wait!”
Kohaku comes pattering down the stairs.
“…”
The moment Kohaku approaches, Hisui smoothly withdraws a step and falls silent.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Oh, Shiki-san!
Please wait just a moment!"
With pattering footsteps, Kohaku-san runs down from the second floor.
"……"
Hisui steps back and falls silent as Kohaku-san approaches.

entries.japanese:
「あれ、琥珀さんは秋葉と一緒じゃなかったの？」
「秋葉お嬢様はお車で学校に向かわれますから。
今朝は志貴さんにお届け物があるので屋敷に残らさせていただいたんです」
「お届け物って、俺に？」
「はい。
昨日、有間家のほうから荷物が届いたんですよ」
　ニッコリと琥珀さんは笑顔をうかべる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Weren’t you going with Akiha?”
“Miss Akiha travels to school by car. I stayed behind because I have something to give you this morning.”
“Something for me?”
“Yes. A parcel arrived from the Arima family yesterday.”
Kohaku smiles brightly.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Huh?
Weren't you with Akiha?"
"Lady Akiha goes to school by car.
Since I had something to give to you this morning, I stayed behind."
"Something to give me?"
"Yes.
This came from the Arima family yesterday."
Kohaku-san smiles.

entries.japanese:
「え───？
　いや、俺は自分の荷物は全部持ってきたよ。
もともとむこうで使ってたのは有間の家のものだったから、自分の物なんて着てる服ぐらいのものなんだけど……」
「そうなんですか？
　こちらが届けられたお荷物ですけど」
　琥珀さんは二十センチほどの、細い木箱を手渡してくる。
　重量はあまりない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What? But I brought everything of mine. Most of what I used over there belonged to the Arimas, so aside from the clothes on my back, I hardly owned anything…”
“Is that so? This is the parcel they delivered.”
Kohaku hands me a slender wooden box about twenty centimeters long.
It weighs very little.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Eh?
But, I have all my luggage already.
The things I used while I was at the Arimas' house all belonged to them, so all I've got are my own clothes…"
"Really?
But this was sent here, nonetheless…"
Kohaku-san hands me a thin wooden box, perhaps twenty centimeters long.
It's not heavy at all.

entries.japanese:
「───琥珀さん、俺はこんなの見た事もないんだけど」
「はあ。
なんでも志貴さまのお父さまの遺品だそうですけど。
志貴さんに譲られるようにって遺言があったとか」
「……あの親父が俺に？」
　……それこそ実感がわかない。
　八年前、俺をこの屋敷から追い出した親父がどうして俺に形見分けをするんだろう？
entries.maoEnglish:
“───Kohaku, I’ve never seen this before.”
“Yes. I’m told it was among Master Shiki’s father’s effects. Apparently his will instructed that it be left to you.”
“That man left something to me?”
It doesn’t feel real.
Why would the father who cast me out of this estate eight years ago leave me a keepsake?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Kohaku-san, I've never seen this before."
"Well… apparently it was left to you by your departed father.
It was to be given to you in the will."
"…… By my old man?"
…… I can't feel anything about that.
What's the old man who expelled me from this mansion eight years ago doing leaving me things?

entries.japanese:
「まあいいや。
琥珀さん、これ部屋に置いておいて」
「─────」
　琥珀さんはじーっ、と興味深そうに木箱を見つめている。
　なんだか玩具をほしがる子供みたいな仕草だ。
「じーーーーっ」
　いや、子供そのものだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Whatever. Kohaku, leave it in my room for me.”
“─────”
Kohaku stares avidly at the wooden box.
She looks like a child longing for a toy.
“Staaaaare.”
No—she really is a child.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Oh well.
Kohaku-san, please take it to my room for me."
"-----"
Kohaku-san is staring intently at the wooden box.
She seems almost like a child who wants a toy.
Staaaaaare.
No, she is a child.

entries.japanese:
「……わかりました。
中身が気になるんですね、琥珀さんは」
「いえ、そんなことないです。
ただちょっと気になるなって」
　………だから、十分気になってるじゃないか。
「なら開けてみましょう。
せーのっ、はい」
　スッ、と乾いた音をたてて木箱を開ける。
　中には────十センチほどの、細い鉄の棒が入っていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…I see—you want to know what’s inside, don’t you?”
“Not at all. I’m only a little curious.”
That still means she’s curious.
“Then let’s open it. Ready—and there.”
The wooden lid slides aside with a dry whisper.
Inside lies――――a slender iron rod about ten centimeters long.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I get it.
You want to know what's inside, right?"
"Oh, not at all.
I merely wondered for a moment."
…… Like I said, you do wonder what's inside.
"Alright, let's open it.
One, two… three!"
With a dry sound, the wooden box opens.
Inside, there is----a ten-centimeter bar of thin iron.

entries.japanese:
「………鉄の棒………だ」
　何の飾り気もない、使い込まれて手垢のついた鉄の棒。
　……こんなガラクタが俺に対する形見分けとは、親父はよっぽど俺が気に食わなかったとみえる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“An iron rod…”
Plain, well worn, and darkened by years of handling.
If this piece of junk is all Father left me, he must have disliked me even more than I thought.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… It's… an iron bar."
Undecorated and worn, it has finger marks all over it.
…… The old man must have really hated me to leave me a piece of junk like this.

entries.japanese:
「───違います志貴さん。
これ、果物ナイフですよ」
　琥珀さんは鉄の棒を箱から取り出す。
「ほら、飛び出しナイフってあるじゃないですか。
あれと同じみたいです。
せーの、はいっ」
　パチン、と音がして棒から十センチほどの刃が飛び出す。
　……なるほど、たしかにこれはナイフだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“───No, Shiki. This is a fruit knife.”
Kohaku lifts the iron rod from the box. “You know those spring-loaded
knives? This one seems to work the same way—ready, there!” A snap, and a blade about ten centimeters long leaps from the handle.
She’s right.
It is a knife.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No, Shiki-san.
It's a fruit knife."
Kohaku-san takes the iron bar out of the box.
"See, isn't it one of those folding knifes?
One, two… three!"
With the sound of sliding metal, a ten-centimeter blade pops out from the bar.
…… I see, it certainly is a knife.

entries.japanese:
「ずいぶんと古いものみたいですけど、作りはしっかりしてますよ。
裏に年号がかかれてます」
　琥珀さんは刃をしまってからナイフを手渡してくる。
　たしかに握りの下のほうに数字が刻まれていた。
　七という漢字と、その後には夜という漢字。
entries.maoEnglish:
“It seems very old, but it’s sturdily made. There’s a date engraved on the back.”
Kohaku retracts the blade and hands me the knife.
There are indeed characters carved near the bottom of the grip.
First the character for seven, then the character for night.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"It's old, but it seems pretty solid.
The year and the era it was made in is written on the back."
Kohaku-san replaces the blade, and hands over the knife.
Certainly, there's a number written on the grip.
The character "seven", and under it, the character "night".

entries.japanese:
「姉さん、これは年号じゃないわ。
七つ夜って書かれているだけよ」
「っ！」
　びっくりして振り返る。
　と、今まで黙っていた翡翠が後ろからナイフを覗きこんでいた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Sis, that isn’t a date. It only says Nanatsu-Yoru.”
“!”
I whirl around in surprise.
Hisui, silent until now, has been peering at the knife over my shoulder.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Nee-san, there is no era by that name.
It just says 'Nanatsu-yoru'."
"Ah!"
I turn around in surprise.
Hisui, who had been silent until now, was looking at the knife over my shoulders.

entries.japanese:
「び、びっくりしたあ……翡翠、人が悪いぞ。
そんな後ろから覗かなくても、見たければ見せてあげるのに」
「あ―――――」
　とたん、翡翠の頬がかすかに赤くなる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You startled me, Hisui… That was mean; you didn’t have to sneak up behind me when I would’ve shown it to you if you asked.”
“Ah—”
A faint blush instantly rises in Hisui’s cheeks.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Y, you surprised me… Hisui, you should say something.
You don't have to look over my shoulder like that, you know.
If you want to see it, I'll show it to you."
"Ah----"
Hisui's cheeks become faintly red.

entries.japanese:
「し、失礼しました。
あの―――その短刀があまりにキレイでしたから、つい」
「キレイ？
　これ、キレイっていうかなあ。
どっちかっていうとオンボロな感じだけど」
「――――そんな事はありません。
見事な刃文をした、由緒正しい古刀だと思います」
「……そうなの？
　俺にはガラクタにしか見えないけど……」
entries.maoEnglish:
“M-my apologies. I couldn’t help myself—the dagger was so beautiful.”
“Beautiful? I don’t know about that. It looks more battered than anything.”
“――――It is nothing of the kind. Its exquisite temper line marks it as an ancient blade with a distinguished history.”
“Really? It still looks like junk to me…”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"P-please excuse me.
Um---That knife was so beautiful that I could not help myself."
"Beautiful?
You really think it's beautiful?
It looks kind of beat up to me."
"---Not at all.
The tempering of the blade is masterful.
I think it is a knife with its own proper history."
"Really?
It looks to me like a piece of junk…"

entries.japanese:
翡翠があんまりにも強く断言するもんだから、こっちもその気になってきた。
　……うん。
これはこれで、形見としては悪くないのかもしれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
Hisui insists so firmly that I begin to believe her.
…Yes—perhaps it isn’t such a bad keepsake after all.
entries.mirrorMoon:
But since Hisui seems so convinced, I begin to feel the same thing.
…… Hmmm.
In its own way, I guess it's not such a bad inheritance.

entries.japanese:
「七つ夜……ですか。
その果物ナイフの名前でしょうかね？」
「そうかもね。
ナイフに名前を付けるなんてヤツはそういないと思うけど」
　なんにせよ年代物という事ははっきりしている。
「ま、もらえる物はもらっとくのが俺の信条だし」
　刃を収めて、ズボンのポケットにナイフを仕舞う。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Nanatsu-Yoru… Could that be the fruit knife’s name?”
“Maybe. Not many people bother naming their knives, though.”
Whatever else it may be, the thing is clearly an antique.
“Still, never turn down something free—that’s my creed.”
I fold the blade away and slip the knife into my trouser pocket.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"'Seven nights'…?
Maybe that's the name of this fruit knife?"
"Maybe… though, I can't imagine him naming a knife like that."
Whatever the case may be, it's obvious that it's an antique.
"Well, in any case, I believe in taking what's given to me."
I replace the blade, and put the knife in my trouser pocket.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま。
お時間はよろしいのですか……？」
「まずい、そろそろ行かないと間にあわないか。
それじゃ琥珀さん、届け物ありがとうね」
　いえいえ、と琥珀さんは笑顔で手をふった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki. Are you certain you have time…?”
“Damn, I’d better go or I really will be late. Kohaku, thanks for bringing me the parcel.”
Smiling, Kohaku waves away my thanks.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama, have you enough time…?"
"Ah!
I have to get going.
Well, Kohaku-san, thanks for the delivery."
Kohaku smiles and waves me off.

entries.japanese:
庭を抜けて門に出る。
　翡翠は無言でしずしずと付いてきた。
「……翡翠。
もしかして俺の見送り？」
　はい、と　翡翠は無表情でうなずく。
entries.maoEnglish:
I cross the garden and reach the gate.
Hisui follows in stately silence.
“…Hisui—are you seeing me off?”
She nods without a flicker of expression.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I come out to the gates.
Hisui follows in silence.
"…… Hisui.
You're seeing me off?"
Hisui nods wordlessly.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま。
お帰りはいつごろでしょうか」
　……翡翠はあくまで俺の名前にさまを付けたいらしい。
　ここで話し込んで学校に遅刻するわけにもいかない。
『さま』づけ論争に関しては時間がある時にするべきだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki, when should we expect you home?” …Hisui
seems determined to keep addressing me as Master Shiki.
I can’t stand here debating it and make myself late for school. The debate over the title will have to wait until we have time.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama?
What time shall we expect your return?"
It seems Hisui will continue to use "-sama" to the bitter end.
Well, if I take time to argue it now, I'll be late for school.
I'll complain about the honorific later.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま？」
「あ、えーと、そうだな。
四時あたりには帰ってこれると思うよ。
俺は部活やってないから」
　有彦と遊びにでかけなければ、まあ大体夕方には帰ってこれる。
　こっちのいい加減な目算に翡翠は深々と頭をさげた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki?”
“Oh—right. I should be back around four. I’m not in any clubs.”
Unless Arihiko talks me into going somewhere, I ought to be home by late afternoon.
Hisui bows deeply at my very rough estimate.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama?"
"Ah, yeah.
Uh… probably around four o'clock, I think.
I don't do any club activities."
When I don't hang out with Arihiko, I usually get back pretty early in the evening.
Hisui bows deeply at my random estimate.

entries.japanese:
「わかりました。
では、行ってらっしゃいませ。
どうか、道々お気をつけて」
　……何をお気をつけてなのかは不明だけど、おそらくはこっちの体を気遣ってくれてるんだろう。
「ああ、サンキュ。
翡翠も気をつけてな」
　好意には好意で返すのは当たり前。
　軽く手をあげて、翡翠に元気よく手をふってから屋敷の門を後にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Understood. Have a safe journey, and please take great care on the way.”
…I’m not sure what danger she expects, but she’s probably worried about my health.
“Thanks. You be careful too, Hisui.”
Kindness deserves kindness in return.
I raise one hand, give her a cheerful wave, and leave the estate gate behind.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I understand.
Please take care on the way."
…… I'm not sure what to take care about, but she's probably just worried about my health.
"Yeah, thanks.
You too, Hisui."
I return the goodwill with good intentions.
With an energetic wave of the hand at Hisui, I leave the gates of the mansion behind.

entries.japanese:
───坂道を下っていく。
　今まで有間の家から高校に通っていたから、この道順での登校は初めてだった。
「────あんまりいないな、うちの学生」
　この周辺の家庭にはうちの高校に通っている人間は少ないようだ。
　朝の七時半。
　道を小走りで進んでいく学生服姿は自分しか見あたらない。
entries.maoEnglish:
───I head down the hill.
Until now I always commuted from the Arima home, so this is my first journey to school by this route.
“────Not many students from our school around here.”
Apparently few families in this neighborhood send their children there.
It is seven-thirty in the morning.
I’m the only uniformed figure jogging down the road.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---I go down the hill.
Since I've attended school from the Arimas' house up until now, this is my first time taking this route.
"Not many from our school…"
Apparently, there are not many people from my school who live around here.
Half past seven in the morning.
I can't see anyone running along the streets in a school uniform except me.

entries.japanese:
ちらほらと学生服をきた人影がまざってくる。
　ここのあたりにくるとうちの学校の通学路になるのだろう。
「……弓塚さんは……ま、都合よくいないよな」
　昨日、ここで『家がこっちだから』と別れたクラスメイトの笑顔を思い出す。
　教室に行けば弓塚さつきがいると思ったとたん、心なしか足の進みが速くなった。
entries.maoEnglish:
A few other uniforms begin to appear.
This must be where the neighborhood roads join the main route to our school.
“Yumizuka—well, I couldn’t be that lucky.”
I remember the smile of the classmate who parted from me here yesterday, saying her house was this way.
The moment I think that Satsuki Yumizuka will be waiting in the classroom, my feet quicken almost of their own accord.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Slowly, I begin to see some people in school uniforms intermingled with the crowd.
This is around where the road to school begins.
"…… Where's Yumizuka-san…?
Well, I'm not going to be that lucky…"
I recall the smiling face of the classmate who departed here yesterday saying "my house is this way".
As I think of Yumizuka Satsuki in the classroom, my pace quickens a little, and I hurry towards the classroom.

entries.japanese:
住宅地を抜けて交差点につく。
　校門が閉まるまであと十分ほど。
　遅刻しないようにとアスファルトの路面を駆け出した。
――――――到着。
　屋敷から徒歩で三十分、というより二十分程度か。
途中で何度か走ったから、ゆっくりしたいのなら七時すぎに屋敷を出る必要があるだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
I leave the residential district and reach the intersection.
Ten minutes until the gates close.
I break into a run over the asphalt, determined not to be late.
――――――Made it.
They said it was thirty minutes from the estate, but it was closer to twenty. Since I ran part of the way, though, I’ll have to leave just after seven for a leisurely walk.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I leave the residential area and reach the crossroads.
The gates will be closed in about ten minutes.
I start to run across the asphalt.
------I made it.
It seems like it took twenty minutes rather than thirty from the mansion.
I'll need to leave around seven if I want to go slowly, since I ran several times on the way.

entries.japanese:
「――――？」
　教室に入るなり、空気がどこかあわだたしい事に気がついた。
　朝の教室はいつも騒がしいけど、今日の騒がしさはどこか毛色が違う気がする。
　窓際の自分の机まで歩いていく。
　そこには仏頂面をした有彦が待っていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――?”
The moment I enter the classroom, I notice something unsettled in the air.
Mornings are always noisy here, but today’s commotion has a different pitch.
I walk to my desk by the window.
Arihiko is waiting there with a sour expression.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----?"
When I get to the classroom, I notice the air is buzzing.
Although the classroom in the morning is always noisy, there's something different about the noise today.
I walk to my desk by the window.
Arihiko is waiting there sullenly.

entries.japanese:
「有彦、なにかあったのか？」
「……さあね。
別にたいした事じゃない。
たんにうちのクラスの誰かが家出したってだけの話だ」
「そっか、どうりで騒がしいはずだ」
　自分の机に座って、ふう、と一呼吸つく。
「―――って、そりゃ大事じゃないか！
　誰が家出したんだよ、誰が！」
「そんなの俺が知るか。
朝のホームルームが始まればイヤでもわかるだろ。
家出したヤツは学校には来ないだろうから、空いてる席が家出をしたヤツだ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Arihiko, did something happen?”
“…Who knows? Nothing important—somebody in our class ran away from home, that’s all.”
“Oh—no wonder everyone is making such a fuss.”
I sit down and breathe out.
“―――Wait, that is important! Who ran away—who?!”
“How should I know? We’ll find out when homeroom starts. Whoever ran away won’t be at school, so the empty desk will tell us.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Arihiko, did something happen?"
"…… Dunno.
It's nothing big.
There's a rumor that someone in class ran away from home."
"Ahh… that's what all the fuss is about, then."
I sit down at my desk with a sigh.
"---What do you mean, nothing big!?
Who ran away?
Who!"
"How should I know?
But we'll know when homeroom starts.
Whoever's seat is vacant, they must be the one who ran away from home."

entries.japanese:
「ああ、そりゃ納得」
　納得だけど、有彦の態度はいつになくドライだ。
　……クラスメイトが家出したっていうのに、まるで他人事みたいに無関心なのは問題があると思う。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Right—that makes sense.”
It does, but Arihiko is unusually cold about this.
A classmate has run away from home, and treating it like someone else’s problem seems wrong.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ahh, that's true."
It's true, but, Arihiko's attitude seems a little dry.
…… If one of our classmates really has run away from home, I think it's a bit much to just ignore it as someone else's problem.

entries.japanese:
「有彦。
おまえ、ひどく無関心じゃないか。
クラスメイトが家出したんだぞ。
心配にならないか？」
「あ？
　ばっか、そんなの本気で心配してんのはオマエぐらいなもんだよ。
クラスの連中が騒いでるのは、わりかし珍しい話題だからだ。
　オレやおまえが家出したわけじゃないんだし、関心なんてあるわけないだろ」
　……そういえば、こいつは身内以外にはひどく冷たいところがあるヤツだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Arihiko. Aren’t you being awfully indifferent? One of our classmates has run away. Aren’t you worried?”
“What? Idiot, you’re probably the only one honestly worried. Everyone else is excited because it’s unusual gossip.
It isn’t as though you or I ran away, so why would I care?”
Come to think of it, he has always been brutally cold toward anyone outside his own circle.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Arihiko?
Aren't you being insensitive?
One of our classmates ran away from home… aren't you worried?"
"Eh?
You're the only one who's seriously worried, dumbass.
Everyone's talking about it because it's an interesting thing to talk about.
It's not as if you or I had run away from home, so there's no need to worry, is there?"
…… Now I remember.
This guy's cold like that to everyone except his friends.

entries.japanese:
「……でもまあ、違った意味で心配はしてるけどな。
こんな時に家出をするなんて、よっぽど度胸があるのかよっぽどのアレかだし」
「……？
　こんな時って、どんな時？」
「昨日言っただろ、遠野。
いま街じゃ通り魔殺人が流行ってるんだって。
どこに家出したかしらないが、そこらへんで野宿してたらバッサリと通り魔に襲われても文句は言えないだろ」
「まさか――――いくらなんでも、そんなことはないだろ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“…I’m worried in another sense, I suppose. Running away at a time like this takes either remarkable courage or remarkable
stupidity.” “What do you mean, a time like this?”
“I told you yesterday, Tohno. Random street killings are spreading through the city. I don’t know where this person ran to, but if they sleep on the street and get carved up by a random attacker, they’ll have no one to blame but themselves.”
“No――――surely it won’t come to that.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Though, I guess I am a bit worried.
Running away from home at a time like this… they'd have to be really brave or really…"
"…?
A time like this?
What kind of time is that?"
"I told you yesterday, Tohno.
There's a serial killer going around on the streets right now.
I don't know who ran away from home, but they'd have no excuse if they got attacked by him while living on the streets."

entries.japanese:
「遠野、おまえはちゃんとテレビを見なさい。
今までで犠牲者が八人だぞ？
　それも全員無差別に殺されてるんだ。
自分だけは安心、なんていう考えは捨てちまえ。
　最近の夜の街はさ、それは静かなもんなんだぜ。
出歩いているのは危機感が麻痺してる酔っ払いと警官だけでね、おかげで退屈で退屈で仕方がない」
　有彦の声はいたって真面目だ。
　……それを聞かされると、こっちも不安になってしまう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Tohno, start watching the news. Eight people have died already—do you understand? Every victim was chosen at random. Stop imagining you’re somehow safe.
The city is dead quiet at night now. The only people outside are drunks with no sense of danger and police officers, and the boredom is unbearable.”
Arihiko’s voice is entirely serious.
Hearing it put that way makes me uneasy too.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Can't be----there's no way that'd happen."

"Tohno, you should watch TV more.
There's been eight victims already, and he doesn't discriminate.
You'd better think again if you think you're safe.
The town's empty at night nowadays.
The only people who go out are drunkards and policemen, which is why it's so boring."
Arihiko's voice is very serious.
Hearing it, I begin to feel uneasy.

entries.japanese:
「―――おっ、国藤が来たぜ。
お待ちかねのホームルームだ」
　有彦は自分の席に戻っていく。
　しばらくして、全員が席についた。
　生徒が座っていない席は一つしかない。
　その席は、間違いなく弓塚さつきの机だった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――Oh, here comes Kunifuji. Homeroom at last.”
Arihiko returns to his seat.
Soon everyone is seated.
Only one desk remains empty.
It is unmistakably Satsuki Yumizuka’s.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Oh, Kunifuji's here.
It's homeroom at last."
Arihiko returns to his seat.
After a while, everyone is seated.
Only one seat is empty.
There's no mistaking it.
The desk of Yumizuka Satsuki is empty.

entries.japanese:
「それじゃあわたしは家がこっちだから。
　ばいばい、また明日学校でね」
entries.maoEnglish:
“My house is this way, so I’ll leave you here.
Goodbye—see you at school tomorrow.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Well, my house is this way.
Bye-bye.
See you at school tomorrow."

entries.japanese:
「………」
　……昨日の別れ際、弓塚は確かにそう言っていた。
家で何があったか知らないけど、あの笑顔はとても家出する直前には見えなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
That is exactly what Yumizuka said when we parted yesterday. Whatever may have happened at home, that smile didn’t belong to someone about to run away.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……"
…… Yumizuka said that when we parted yesterday.
I don't know what happened at home, but I can't see her making that smiling face before running away.

entries.japanese:
「弓塚は欠席だな」
　教壇に立つ担任は、ただ弓塚さつきを欠席扱いにして出席をとっていく。
　……何事もなかったように、ホームルームは進んでいく。
　俺は――――
entries.maoEnglish:
“Yumizuka is absent, then.”
At the lectern, our homeroom teacher merely marks Satsuki Yumizuka absent and continues taking attendance.
Homeroom proceeds as though nothing has happened.
I――――
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yumizuka is absent."
Yumizuka Satsuki is merely treated as absent as attendance is taken.
…… As if nothing is amiss, homeroom proceeds.
I----

entries.japanese:
―――――昨日の弓塚の笑顔を知っている。
　あんな顔をしてばいばい、なんて言えるヤツが家出をするなんて、とても思えない。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――――I remember Yumizuka’s smile yesterday.
Someone who could smile like that and say goodbye could not possibly have been about to run away.
entries.mirrorMoon:
-----I know Yumizuka was smiling yesterday.
I didn't think that she could make such a face, say "bye bye", and then run away from home.

entries.japanese:
「―――先生」
「なんだ遠野。
質問か？」
「はい。
うちのクラスで家出をした生徒がいると聞きましたけど、それは本当なんですか？」
「む―――――」
　ぴたり、と教室中の空気が固まった。
　担任は難しい顔をしたあと、言いにくそうに顔をしかめてうなずいた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――Sir.”
“What is it, Tohno? A question?”
“Yes—I heard that someone in our class ran away from home. Is that true?”
“Hmm―――――”
Every breath in the classroom stops.
Our teacher frowns, plainly reluctant, then gives a grave nod.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Sensei."
"What is it, Tohno?
A question?"
"Yes.
Is it true that a student in our class has run away from home?"
"Hrm------"
Instantly, the air in the classroom solidifies.
He frowns, then, with a difficult expression, bows his head in assent.

entries.japanese:
「……たしかに弓塚さつきのご両親から、そういった報せは届いている。
弓塚は昨夜から家に帰ってきていないそうだが、捜索願いが出されているのだからすでに見付かっているだろう」
　そうして、担任は教室を後にした。
　教室はざわざわと騒がしくなる。
　なにか、イヤな予感がする。
　……重苦しい。
椅子に体が縛り付けられているみたいに重苦しい、イヤな予感だった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Satsuki Yumizuka’s parents did contact us with such a report. Yumizuka has not been home since last night, but a missing-person report has been filed, so I expect she has already been found.”
With that, our teacher leaves the room.
The classroom erupts into murmurs.
Something feels wrong.
…A heavy, sickening premonition, as though its weight has bound my body to the chair.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yes, that is what we've heard from Yumizuka Satsuki's parents.
Yumizuka didn't come home last night, but they've been searching, and I'm sure they've already found her."
Saying so, he departs.
The classroom becomes noisy again.
I have a bad feeling about this.
…… It's really heavy.
A terrible feeling as if my body is tied down to this chair.

entries.japanese:
―――聞いたところで、担任が教えてくれるとは思えなかった。
　有彦の言う通り家出だとしたら、それはプライベートな事だ。
　クラスメイトがなにげに『弓塚さん家出したんですか』なんて聞いても、答えてくれる教師はいないだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Even if I asked, I doubted our teacher would tell me anything.
If Arihiko is right and she ran away, it is a private family matter.
No teacher would answer some classmate casually asking whether Yumizuka had fled home.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---I was about to ask, but I didn't think the teacher would tell me.
If she did run away from home like Arihiko said, it's her business.
