Shiki-san, you do not seem to understand Lady Akiha.
If you did that, she would get angry for another reason, I think."
"…… I don't get it, but you're saying she'll get angry whatever happens?"

entries.japanese:
「あはは、そういえばそうですよね。
ええ、そうゆうわけですからやっぱり止めてください」
　笑顔で、きっぱりと琥珀さんは言いきる。
「…そっか。
そうだよな、どっちにしても琥珀さんが秋葉に怒られるんなら、俺が手伝っても迷惑な話か。
ごめんな、考えなしで余計な真似しようとして」
「いいえ、ぜんぜん余計なんかじゃありません。
わたしも手伝ってもらえるって分かった時、すごく嬉しかったですから」
　うう、そう屈託のない笑顔で言われると結局手伝ってあげられない自分が辛い。
　はあ、とため息をつく。
　琥珀さんは俺の顔を楽しそうに見上げている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ahaha, I suppose she will. Yes, so you really mustn’t help.”
Kohaku said it with smiling finality.
“Right. If helping means Akiha will take it out on you either way, I’d only be making trouble. Sorry—I should have thought before barging in.”
“It wouldn’t be trouble at all. I was so happy when I realized you wanted to help me.”
It hurt to see such an open smile when I could not help her after all.
I sighed.
Kohaku looked up at me, plainly enjoying herself.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ahaha, that's it.
So please do not worry about sweeping."
Still smiling, Kohaku-san says this directly.
"…… Oh.
No matter what happens, Akiha will get mad at you.
Then I don't want to make any trouble for you.
Sorry, forgive me for just being careless."
"No, you were not being careless.
I'm very happy you wanted to help me."
Even though she says that with her bright smile, I feel bad because I really did want to help her.
I sigh.
Kohaku-san looks up at my face cheerfully.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さん、ほんとに手伝ってくれます？」
「ああ、そりゃあ琥珀さんに迷惑がかからないならいくらでも手伝うけど───」
「それじゃあ場所を変えましょうか。
ここだと秋葉さまに見つかってしまいますから、裏のほうでこっそりお掃除すればいいんです」
「裏って───その、裏庭？」
「はい。
そこなら秋葉さまにも見つかりません。
二人で仲良くお掃除しましょう」
　はい、と琥珀さんは自分の持っていたホウキを手渡してくれる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Shiki, do you truly want to help?”
“Of course—as long as it won’t get you in trouble, I’ll help as much as you like───”
“Then let’s move elsewhere. Miss Akiha might see us here, but we can clean in secret around the back.”
“The back───you mean the back garden?”
“Yes. Miss Akiha won’t find us there. We can have a lovely time cleaning together.”
Cheerfully, Kohaku handed me her broom.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-san, did you really want to help me?"
"Yeah, if I won't get you in trouble…"
"Then, shall we go somewhere else?
Akiha-sama will find us here, so I think it is better if we sweep behind the mansion."
"Behind…… in the backyard?"
"Yes.
Akiha-sama will never find us there, so we can sweep all we want.
Here you go," Kohaku-san hands me the broom she had in her hands.

entries.japanese:
「それじゃあ倉庫からホウキを持ってきますから、志貴さまは先に行っていてください。
途中、くれぐれも翡翠ちゃんと秋葉さまに見つからないでくださいね」
　たたた、と軽い足取りで琥珀さんは走っていってしまった。
 ───いたずらっこみたいな人だな、ほんと。
　気がつけば口元がにやけていた。
　秋葉と翡翠が冗談の通じない性格な分、琥珀さんの明るさは本当に微笑ましい。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’ll fetch another broom from the storehouse, so you go on ahead, Master Shiki. And whatever you do, don’t let Hisui or Miss Akiha see you on the way.”
Kohaku scampered away on light feet.
───Honestly, she was like a child plotting mischief.
Before I knew it, I was grinning.
Akiha and Hisui had no sense of humor at all, which made Kohaku’s cheerfulness that much more endearing.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I will go to the shed to get another broom, so please go ahead, Shiki-sama.
Please don't let Hisui-chan or Akiha-sama spot you as you go, okay?"
Trot trot trot!
Kohaku-san dashes with quick, light steps.
---She really looks like a mischievous kid.
Before I realize it, a grin creases my lips.
Akiha and Hisui don't seem to be the joking type, so Kohaku-san's brightness is quite charming.

entries.japanese:
「よし、やるか─────！」
　さっきまで琥珀さんが使っていた竹ぼうきを力強く握り締めて、俺は人目につかないという屋敷の裏庭へと歩いていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“All right—let’s do this─────!”
I tightened my grip on the bamboo broom Kohaku had been using and set off for the secluded back garden.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Alright, let's do this----!"
Gripping the broom that Kohaku-san was using earlier, I covertly walk to the garden behind the mansion.

entries.japanese: ……そうだな、昨日から世話になっているんだから、こうしてぼんやりしている暇があったら翡翠の手伝いぐらいしないと罰があたる。
entries.maoEnglish: She had been looking after me since yesterday; if I sat here idling instead of at least helping Hisui, I deserved divine punishment.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… That's right.
She's been taking care of me since yesterday, so if I have time to fool around, I ought to go help Hisui.

entries.japanese:
―――さて。
　屋敷を掃除するって言ってたけど、翡翠はどこにいるんだろう。
　ロビーに下りてくる。
　二階の廊下には翡翠の姿は見当たらなかったから、いるとしたら居間のほうだろうか。
　……いない。
　…………いない。
　…………………いない。
　…………………………………いない。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Now, then.
Hisui had said she would be cleaning the estate, but where was she?
I went down to the lobby.
She had not been in the upstairs corridor, so perhaps she was in the sitting room.
…Not here
……Not here
………Not here
…………………Not here
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Well then.
Hisui said she'd be cleaning the mansion, but where could she be?
I go down to the lobby.
She wasn't in the hallway on the second floor, so maybe she's in the sitting room?
…… Not here.

………… Not here.
……………… Not here.
…………………… Not here.

entries.japanese:
一階に翡翠の姿はない。
　まだ見ていないのは鍵がかかっている遊戯室と客間、秋葉がいるっていうサロンぐらいなものだ。
「……すれ違って二階に行ったのかな」
　これだけ広い屋敷だから、入れ違いになる事ぐらいはあるだろう。
　気を取りなおして二階に向かった。
entries.maoEnglish:
Hisui was not anywhere on the ground floor.
The only rooms I had not checked were the locked game room and guest room, and the salon where Akiha was working.
“Maybe we passed each other and she went upstairs.”
In an estate this large, that was entirely possible.
I gathered my resolve and headed back up.
entries.mirrorMoon:
She's not anywhere on the first floor.
The only place I haven't been are the locked recreation rooms, the guest rooms, and the salon where Akiha is right now.
"…… I guess she's on the second floor then."
It is a big mansion, so there's probably a bunch of places I haven't looked.
Psyching myself up, I start up the stairs.

entries.japanese:
階段をあがって、廊下を見渡す。
　と。
　東館の奥、窓際に立ち尽くしている翡翠の姿を見つけた。
entries.maoEnglish:
At the top of the stairs, I looked along the corridor.
There.
At the far end of the east wing, I found Hisui standing beside a window.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I go up the stairs and glance down the hallway.
And then,
I see Hisui's silhouette standing by the window in the east hall of the mansion.

entries.japanese:
「ひす―――」
　声をかけようとした喉が止まる。
　廊下の奥。
　明かりも満足にない暗がりのなか、翡翠は一人でぴくりとも動かないで立っていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“His―――”
My voice died in my throat.
At the far end of the corridor.
Hisui stood alone and utterly still in the gloom, where barely any light reached.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hisu--"
My voice dies in my throat.
In the middle of the hallway.
In the twilight, between light and shadow, Hisui stands motionless.

entries.japanese:
「――――――」
　……声が、出ない。
　翡翠の姿は、どこか、危うい。
　暗い洋館の中で佇む翡翠。
　たしかに可憐だと思うのに、同時に幽霊を見るような肌寒さを思わせる静けさ。
　翡翠は指先さえ動かさず、ただ窓の外を眺めている。
「――――――」
　その窓は。
　子供のころ、あの少女がいつも見下ろしていた窓ではなかったか。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――――”
I could not speak.
There was something perilously fragile about the sight of her.
Hisui stood motionless in the dark mansion.
She was undeniably lovely, yet her stillness carried the chill of seeing a ghost.
Not even her fingertips moved as she gazed through the window.
“――――――”
That window.
Wasn’t it the same one where the girl from my childhood had always stood looking down?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------"
…… I can't… speak.
Something about her seems… dangerous.
Hisui lingering in the gloom of this western-style mansion.
She seems so incredibly beautiful; but at the same time, a chill runs through me, as if I were looking at a ghost.
She doesn't even move a finger.
She simply stares out the window.
"------"
That window.
Is that the same one she watched us from back then?

entries.japanese:
「ひす―――――い」
　こういうのも見惚れる、っていうんだろうか。
　声をかける事も、かといって目をそむける事もできず、ただ呆然と翡翠を見つめる。
――――と。
　人形のようだった翡翠の瞳が、つい、とこっちに向けられた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“His―――――ui.”
Was this what people meant by being spellbound?
Unable either to call out or look away, I could only stare at her.
――――Then.
The eyes of the doll-like figure shifted quietly toward me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hisu----i"
I can't do anything but stare in fascination.
I'm so dumbstruck I can't speak, or even blink.
I can only watch her.
----And then.
Her eyes, still like that of a doll's, suddenly turn towards me.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま、どうかなされましたか？」
「あ―――いや、別にどうしたっていうわけでもない、んだけど……」
「？」
　かすかに首をかしげる翡翠。
　そこに、さっきまでの不思議な緊張感はなくなっていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Is something wrong, Master Shiki?”
“Ah―――no, nothing’s wrong, exactly…”
“?”
Hisui tilted her head a fraction.
The strange tension that had surrounded her moments before was gone.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama, is something wrong?"
"Ah---no, nothing, I just, um……"
"?"
Hisui tilts her head in curiosity.
That seems to break the mysterious spell I was under.

entries.japanese:
「暇だから何か手伝いをしたくて捜してたんだけど、翡翠が中々見付からなくて。
いま、ようやく見つけたところ」
「……そうですか。
ですが志貴さまがそのようなことをなされる必要はありません。
どうかお部屋にお戻りください」
「む…………」
　なんとなく予想はしていたけど、やっぱり翡翠は俺に働かせるつもりはないらしい。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I had nothing to do, so I came looking for you to see if I could help. You were difficult to find, but I finally managed it.”
“I see. However, there is no need for Master Shiki to perform such work. Please return to your room.”
“Mm…”
I had expected as much; Hisui had no intention of letting me work.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I was looking for you because I had some free time and thought I'd give you a hand.
For some reason, I couldn't find you, but I made it."
" …… I see.
But Shiki-sama, there is no need for you to do that.
Please return to your room."
"Hmmm………"
I thought it would turn out like this, Hisui doesn't want me to do any work.

entries.japanese:
「けど翡翠、他にやる事がないんだからしょうがないだろ。
ぼーっとしているのも体に悪いんだから、なんでもいいから手伝わせてくれないか」
「お言葉ですが、志貴さまに手伝っていただけるような仕事はすべて終わりました。
残っているのは秋葉さまの寝室の整理だけです。
　たとえ志貴さまでも、男の方を秋葉さまの寝室にお入れするわけにはまいりません」
「む、むむむ…………」
　それは、たしかにその通りだ。
　……けど、なんか卑怯だ。
翡翠はわざと俺にできっこない事を口にしている気がする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“But I have nothing else to do. Sitting around all day is unhealthy, so can’t you let me help with anything?”
“Forgive me, but every task with which Master Shiki could assist has already been completed. Only Miss Akiha’s bedroom remains to be put in order.
Even for Master Shiki, I cannot permit a man to enter Miss Akiha’s bedroom.”
“Mm, mmmmmmmm.”
She was right.
Still, it felt unfair. I suspected Hisui had deliberately named the one task she knew I could never help with.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"But Hisui, I don't have anything else to do.
I don't like just doing nothing, so I thought I ought to pitch in."
"Shiki-sama, you may say that, but there is no longer any work that you might assist me with.
The only thing that remains is to arrange Akiha's bedroom.
No males are allowed to enter Akiha's bedroom.
Not even you, Shiki-sama."
"Hmmmm…………"
Well, that's definitely true.
…… But, it is a little cruel.
She didn't have to emphasize that last part.

entries.japanese:
「それではわたしは仕事が残っていますので失礼します」
　翡翠はツカツカと足音をたてて、そのまま秋葉の寝室に入っていってしまう。
「……………む」
　さすがに、暇だからって女の子の寝室に入っていくわけにはいかない。
「……仕方ない、部屋に戻るか」
　踵を返す。
　と、その前に翡翠が見ていた窓のことが気になった。
「あれ―――中庭にいるの、琥珀さんかな」
　窓からは中庭の様子が一望できる。
　翡翠は子供のころと同じように、この窓から中庭の様子を見つめていたんだろうか……？
entries.maoEnglish:
“I still have work to complete, so please excuse me.”
Her footsteps clicking briskly, Hisui entered Akiha’s bedroom.
“Mm.”
However bored I might be, I could hardly follow her into a girl’s room.
“No choice—I’ll go back.”
I turned away.
Before I did, I remembered the window where Hisui had been standing.
“Ah―――is that Kohaku in the courtyard?”
The window overlooked the entire courtyard.
Had Hisui been watching it from here, just as that girl had when we were children?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Please excuse me, I have to finish my duties."
Her footsteps echo in the air and she goes into Akiha's bedroom.
"…………… Sheesh."
I can't just go into a girl's bedroom because I have free time.
"…… Oh well, I guess I'll go back to my room."
I turn on my heels.
Before doing so, I get curious about the window Hisui was staring out of.
"Huh---isn't that Kohaku-san in the courtyard?"
You can see the whole courtyard from this window.
Was Hisui looking out into the courtyard from this window just as she did when she was a child……?

entries.japanese:
……いや、無理に動き回って翡翠や琥珀さんの仕事を邪魔するのも気が引ける。
　屋敷に帰ってきてまだ二日目。
　まだ馴染んでいないせいか、どことなく体も疲れているし、夕食までゆっくり休む事にしよう。
entries.maoEnglish:
No—I should not force myself to bustle around and get in Hisui and Kohaku’s way.
This was only my second day back at the estate.
Perhaps because I was not used to it yet, I felt tired all over, so I decided to rest until dinner.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… No, I would feel bad about moving around and interfering with Hisui and Kohaku-san's work.
It's still only been two days since I came back to the mansion.
Perhaps it's because I'm not used to it yet, but for some reason, I feel tired.
I should relax and rest until dinner.

entries.japanese:
夕食が済んで、居間で食後のお茶を飲む。
　目の前には秋葉がいて、壁際には翡翠が控えている。
　居間にはテレビなんてものはないし、秋葉も余分な事は話しかけてこない。
―――なんていうか、上品すぎる食後の時間だ。
entries.maoEnglish:
After dinner, I sat in the sitting room drinking tea.
Akiha was opposite me, while Hisui waited by the wall.
There was no television, and Akiha made no attempt at idle conversation.
―――It was an almost excessively refined way to spend the evening.
entries.mirrorMoon:
It's after dinner, and we drink tea in the sitting room.
Akiha sits across from me and Hisui stands by the wall.
There is no such thing as a TV in the room, and Akiha doesn't say much.
---Everything seems so… high-class.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さーん、ちょっといいですかー」
　と、ロビーのほうから琥珀さんの元気な声が聞こえてきた。
「兄さん？
　琥珀が呼んでいますけど、なにか呼ばれるような事をしたんですか？」
「いや、身に覚えはないけど―――ちょっと行ってくる」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Shiki, could you come here a moment?”
Kohaku’s lively voice rang from the foyer.
“Brother? Kohaku wants you—what did you do?”
“Nothing I can think of―――I’ll be back in a bit.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-saaan, can you come here for a moment?"
Kohaku-san's cheerful voice calls from the lobby.
"Nii-san?
Kohaku is calling you.
Did you do anything to make her call for you?"
"No, I don't remember anything---I'll be right back."

entries.japanese:
秋葉と翡翠を居間に残してロビーにやってくる。
　琥珀さんは玄関の前でなにやらぐるぐると歩いていたりする。
「……琥珀さん。
それ、なにやってるの」
「あ、志貴さん。
それがですね、ちょっと複雑な事情なんです。
……そこにいられるとまずいですから、ちょっと外に出てくれますか？」
「……？」
　訳が分からないまま、とりあえず琥珀さんの後についていく。
entries.maoEnglish:
I left Akiha and Hisui in the sitting room and went out to the foyer.
Kohaku was pacing in circles by the front door.
“…Kohaku, what are you doing?”
“Ah, Shiki. It’s rather complicated; since it would be awkward if you stayed there… could you come outside?”
“…?”
I had no idea what was happening, but I followed her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I leave Akiha and Hisui behind and go to the lobby.
Kohaku-san is pacing back and forth by the entrance.
"…… Kohaku-san.
What are you doing?"
"Ah, Shiki-san.
Well, it's a little complicated…… Can you please step outside with me?
Here is not a good place."
"……?"
I don't understand what's going on, but I follow her anyway.

entries.japanese:
「話ってなんですか？
　もしかしてみんなには秘密にしておきたい事？」
「はい。
とくに秋葉さまの耳に入ると、志貴さんが怒られそうなお話です」
　秋葉に怒られそうな話……？
「なんですかそれ。
俺、秋葉を怒らせるような真似はしてないけど」
「あ、志貴さんがどうこうしたワケじゃないんです。
その、実はですね。
志貴さんと秋葉さまのご夕食の最中、お客さまがおみえになられたんです」
entries.maoEnglish:
“What did you want to tell me? Is it something you need to keep secret from everyone else?”
“Yes. Especially if Miss Akiha hears, because you’ll likely get scolded.”
Something that might get me scolded by Akiha―――?
“What are you talking about? I haven’t done anything to upset her.”
“Oh, it isn’t anything you did. The truth is… a visitor came while you and Miss Akiha were having dinner.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"You have something to tell me?
Is it a secret or something?"
"Yes.
If Akiha-sama were to hear it, she would get mad at you, Shiki-san."
Something Akiha would get mad over……?
"What do you mean?
I haven't done anything to make her mad."
"Oh, it isn't anything you did.
But you know, while you were eating with Akiha-sama, a guest came to see you."

entries.japanese:
「え？
　お客さまって、俺に？」
「はい。
門の外でぐるぐると歩いていたので、気になって声をかけたんです。
着ているご洋服が志貴さんの高校の制服だったものですから、もしかしてと思いまして」
　そうして琥珀さんはそのお客さんの風貌を話してくれた。
　年のころは俺と一緒で、やや童顔。
長い髪を両おさげにした可愛い女の子……？
entries.maoEnglish:
“A visitor? For me?”
“Yes. She was pacing outside the gate, so I went to speak to her. She was wearing your school’s uniform, and that made me wonder.”
Kohaku described the visitor for me.
She was about my age and a little baby-faced. A pretty girl with long hair in twin braids…?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Huh?
A guest, for me?"
"Yes.
She was walking around the front gate, so I called out to her.
She was wearing the school uniform of your high school."
And then Kohaku-san began to describe the guest's appearance.
About my age, with a slightly childish face.
A cute girl, her long hair tied in pigtails……?

entries.japanese:
「……………」
　どくん、と視界が真っ暗になった気がした。
　その風貌。
　それは、家出しているっていう弓塚さつきそのものじゃないんだろうか―――
entries.maoEnglish:
“……”
My heart lurched, and for a moment my vision went black.
That description.
Could it really be Satsuki Yumizuka, the girl everyone said had run away from home―――
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…………"
Thump.
I feel as if my world is enveloped in darkness.
That description.
Isn't it Yumizuka Satsuki, who ran away from home---

entries.japanese:
「それでですね、その子、ここが遠野さんのお屋敷ですか？
って聞いてきたんです。
そうですよって答えたら、それなら遠野くんはいますか？
って」
「……うん。
それでどうしたの、琥珀さん」
「はい。
志貴さんと話がしたがっていたようなので、おあがりいただこうとしたんですが断られちゃいました。
なんでも今はまだ会えないからいいんだそうです」
　なんなんでしょうね、と琥珀さんは首をかしげる。
　けど、それを聞きたいのはこっちのほうだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Then she asked, ‘Is this the Tohno estate?’ I said yes. Then she asked, ‘Is Tohno here?’”
“I see. What happened next, Kohaku?”
“She seemed to want to speak with you. I invited her inside, but she refused. She said she couldn’t see you yet.”
Kohaku tilted her head and wondered aloud what that could mean.
But I was the one who wanted to know.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"She asked 'Is this Tohno-san's mansion?' And I answered 'Yes it is.' Then she asked 'Is Tohno-kun here now?'"
"…… Hmm.
And then what, Kohaku-san?"
"Yes, well she seemed to want to talk to you, but she refused when I asked if she wanted to come in.
She seemed okay that she would not get to meet you right now."
Kohaku-san wonders aloud what it was all about, and she tilts her head.
But, I'm the one who wants to know.

entries.japanese:
「なんで――――――弓塚さんが、俺のところに来るんだろう………」
　わからない。
　わからないけど、ただ、厭な予感だけがしている。
「……琥珀さん、それってどのくらい前のこと？」
「えっと、志貴さんのご夕食が終わる前でしたから、かれこれ十分ほど前です」
「――！
　それで、その子はどっちのほうに帰っていったかわかる？」
「坂を街に向かって下りていきましたから、駅前のほうだと思いますよ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Why would――――――Satsuki Yumizuka come looking for me………?”
I didn’t understand.
I didn’t understand, but all I had was a terrible feeling.
“How long ago was this?”
“Let me see; it was before you finished dinner, so about ten minutes ago.”
“――! Which way did she go?”
“She walked down the hill toward town, so I think she went toward the station.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Why------why did Yumizuka-san come to my place……"
I don't know.
I don't know, but, I have a bad feeling about this.
"…… Kohaku-san, how long ago was this?"
"Um, it was before the end of dinner, so about ten minutes ago."
"--!
And, which direction did she go?"
"She went down the hill, towards the station, I think."

entries.japanese:
―――十分前か。
　走れば―――運がよければ、見つけられるかもしれない。
「……わかった。
ちょっと出てくるから、この話は秋葉には黙っててくれ」
「存じております。
秋葉さまが知ったら、また志貴さんがいじめられちゃいますから」
　楽しそうに微笑む琥珀さんに礼を言って、夜の街へと走り出した。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Ten minutes.
If I ran—and got lucky—I might still find her.
“…All right; I’m going out, so don’t tell Akiha any of this.”
“I know. If Miss Akiha found out, you’d only be tormented again.”
I thanked Kohaku, who was smiling as if she enjoyed the whole thing, and ran out into the night.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Can I make it?
If I run---if I get lucky, I might make it.
"…… Got it.
I'll be gone for a little bit, so please keep this a secret from Akiha."
"I understand.
If Akiha-sama found out, she would not leave you alone, Shiki-san."
Giving a quick bow to the smiling and cheerful Kohaku-san, I run down the road and into the night.

entries.japanese:
「はあ――――はあ、はあ――――」
　坂道を全力で下って、駅前方面に走っていく。
「はあ、はあ、はあ、はあ――――！」
　駅前の人込みをかきわけて、弓塚らしき姿を捜す。
「はあ……はあ、はあ………」
　息があがる。
　苦しくなって、走りどおしだった足を止めた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hah――――hah, hah――――”
I sprinted down the hill toward the station.
“Hah, hah, hah, hah――――!”
I forced my way through the crowd outside the station, searching for anyone who looked like Yumizuka.
“Hah―――hah, hah―――”
I was gasping.
The strain finally made me stop after running without rest.
entries.mirrorMoon:
*pant*----*pant*, *pant*----
Dashing with all my strength, I run toward the station.
*pant*, *pant*, *pant*, *pant*----!
I look for someone like Yumizuka in the crowd in front of the station.
*pant*…… *pant*, *pant*………
I'm out of breath.
My legs are painfully aware of how fast I was running, and they stop.

entries.japanese:
「……やっぱ、り……そう、簡単には、見付からない、よな……」
　はあ、はあ。
　荒い呼吸を整えて、すぐに走り出す。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I—I knew she wouldn’t be that easy to find……”
Hah, hah.
I steadied my ragged breathing and immediately started running again.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I, knew…… it wouldn't, be this easy, to find, her……"
*pant*, *pant*.
Trying to control my breathing, I start to run again.

entries.japanese:
―――弓塚さつきの姿は見当たらない。
　当たり前といえば当たり前なのに、どうしてか簡単に諦められない。
　……自分は別段、弓塚さつきが心配なわけではないと思う。
　この胸にはほんの些細なわだかまりがあって、そのためにこうして走りまわってしまっている。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――There was no sign of Satsuki Yumizuka.
That should have been no surprise, yet I couldn’t bring myself to give up.
I didn’t think I was especially worried about Satsuki Yumizuka.
There was simply some tiny unease lodged in my chest, and it kept me running through the streets.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---I don't see Yumizuka Satsuki anywhere.
It's only natural, but I can't seem to give up that easily.
…… I don't think it is because I am so worried about her.
It's just that I have this terrible premonition, that's why I am running like this.

entries.japanese:
―――それじゃあね。
ばいばい、遠野くん。
　それは、どこにでもあるさよならのセリフ。
　……本当に幸せそうだった、柔らかな笑顔。
　あんな顔をするヤツが家出なんかするわけがない。
―――ピンチの時は助けてね、遠野くん。
　そう、こんな事をしている理由なんて単純だ。
　俺はただ、あの時の笑顔が裏切れないだけなんだから――――
entries.maoEnglish:
―――See you, then. Bye, Tohno.
It was an ordinary goodbye, the sort heard anywhere.
The soft smile she wore had looked so genuinely happy.
Someone who could smile like that wouldn’t run away from home.
―――Help me if I’m ever in trouble, Tohno.
Yes―――the reason I was doing this was simple.
I simply couldn’t betray the smile she’d given me then――――
entries.mirrorMoon:
---I'll be going.
Bye-bye, Tohno-kun.
That was a goodbye just like any other.
…… A truly happy, gentle smile.
That was not the face of someone who'd run away from home.
---Tohno-kun, help me when I'm in a pinch, okay?
Yes, it really is that simple.
I just… don't want to betray that smile----

entries.japanese:
「はあ―――はあ――――はあ―――」
　公園にも弓塚らしき人影はない。
　……初めから、何の手がかりもなしで人を捜し出せるはずはなかった。
　見つけられっこないんだから、いいかげん屋敷に戻ろう。
「……く……そ……」
　だっていうのに、まだ街のほうを見て回ろうと踵を返した。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hah―――hah――――hah―――”
There was no one resembling Yumizuka in the park either.
I could never have found someone without a single lead to begin with.
I wasn’t going to find her, so I ought to return to the estate.
“Damn―――it―――”
And yet I turned back toward town to search a little longer.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I pant with exertion.
I don't see her in the park, either.
…… There wasn't a way to find her from the beginning.
I should just give up and go back to the mansion.
"…… Damn…… it……"
Still, I try to look for her as I turn to go back through town.

entries.japanese:
もう一度駅前にやってくる。
　時刻は夜の九時をすぎてしまっている。
　連日の通り魔殺人のせいか、まだ九時だっていうのに人通りは極めて少ない。
――――と。
「弓――――塚」
　一瞬、自分の目を疑った。
　けど目の前で歩いている後ろ姿は、弓塚さつきに似すぎていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
I returned to the station once more.
It was already past nine.
Perhaps because of the recent random street killings, there were remarkably few people out even though it was only nine.
――――And then.
“Yumi――――zuka”
For an instant I doubted my eyes.
But the figure walking ahead of me looked too much like Satsuki Yumizuka.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I come to the front of the station once more.
It's already past nine o'clock.
It's probably because of all the recent serial killings that the area around the station is quite empty already.
----At that moment,
"Yumi----zuka."
For an instant, I doubt my eyes.
But the back of the figure in front of me, it resembles Yumizuka Satsuki too much.

entries.japanese:
弓塚はふらふらとした足取りで人込みの中を歩いていく。
　……遠くて、よくわからない。
　見間違いかもしれないけど、とにかく追いついて呼びとめよう、と走った。
「待って、弓塚さん―――！」
　追いかけながら声をかける。
entries.maoEnglish:
Yumizuka drifted unsteadily through the crowd.
She was too far away to see clearly.
I might have been mistaken, but I ran after her to catch up and call her back.
“Wait, Yumizuka―――!”
I called out as I chased her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Yumizuka walks quickly into the midst of the crowd.
…… I can't tell for sure.
I may have been wrong, but I decided I should catch up to her and call out to her.
"Wait, Yumizuka-san---!"
I shout while running.

entries.japanese:
「――――――」
　声が聞こえたのか、弓塚はちらりとこっちに振り向いた。
　その顔は、なんということはない。
　前を歩いている少女は間違いなく弓塚さつきだし、彼女の顔が恐ろしげな表情をつくっていたわけでもない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――――”
Perhaps she heard me, because Yumizuka glanced back over her shoulder.
There was nothing remarkable about her face.
The girl ahead of me was unmistakably Satsuki Yumizuka, and she wasn’t wearing any frightening expression.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------"
Did she hear me?
Yumizuka quickly turns around to face my direction.
That face… there's no confusing it.
The girl walking ahead of me is unmistakably Yumizuka Satsuki, and the expression on her face wasn't frightening.

entries.japanese:
「――――あ」
　なのに、ぞくりとした悪寒を感じてしまった。
―――どくん、と。
　心臓の鼓動が速くなる。
　あたまの後ろのほうがクラクラと重くなって、喉が少しだけ熱を帯びる。
「なんだろう……なんか、ヘンだ」
　体中が熱い。
　質の悪い熱病にうかされたみたいに、クラクラする。
　そうしている間に、弓塚はまた歩き出してしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――Ah”
Even so, a chill ran through me.
―――Thump.
My heart quickened.
The back of my head grew dizzy and heavy, and my throat grew faintly warm.
“Something―――something feels wrong.”
My whole body burned.
I reeled as though delirious with a vicious fever.
While I stood there, Yumizuka began walking again.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----Ah."
But I feel a chill run through my spine.

entries.japanese:
「ま―――待てって、弓塚さん……！」
　走りながら呼びかける。
　弓塚は振り向かずに、ふらふらと歩いていく。
「こ―――の、聞こえないのか弓塚……！」
　熱い体にムチを打って走る。
　けど、どうやっても弓塚の背中をつかまえられない。
　……いくら走っても、歩いている弓塚に追いつけない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Wai―――wait, Yumizuka……!”
I called as I ran.
Without looking back, she kept walking unsteadily.
“D―――damn it, can’t you hear me, Yumizuka……!”
I forced my feverish body to keep running.
But no matter what I did, I could not catch her.
However fast I ran, I could not catch up with Yumizuka even though she was only walking.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Thump.
My heart starts to pound quickly.
The back of my head throbs heavily, and my throat is burning.
"What is this… It's weird…"
The inside of my body is burning.
I feel dizzy as if I'm in the grip of a terrible fever.
In that moment, Yumizuka begins to walk again.

entries.japanese:
「――――――」
　なにか、おかしい。
　そうわかってはいるのに、何がおかしいのかわからなかった。
　今の自分に出来る事といえば、なんの解決策もないまま弓塚さつきを追いかける事だけだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――――”
Something was wrong.
I knew that much, but I could not tell what.
All I could do was chase Satsuki Yumizuka without the least idea how that would solve anything.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Wa---wait, Yumizuka-san…!"
I call out, running.
Yumizuka walks on unsteadily, not turning.
"Ca… can't you hear me, Yumizuka…!"
I urge my hot body onwards.
But, no matter how much I try, I cannot catch Yumizuka.
…… No matter how fast I run, I cannot catch up to her even as she walks.

entries.japanese:
――――と。
　不意に弓塚の背中が消えた。
　さっきまで、追いつかないまでもちゃんと見えていたあいつの背中が見当たらない。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――And then.
Yumizuka’s back suddenly vanished.
Until then, her back had remained in sight even though I could not catch up, but now it was nowhere to be seen.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------"
Something is… strange.
I know that, but I couldn't tell what it is.
Right now, all I can do is follow Yumizuka Satsuki.
--And then.
I lose sight of her.
Yumizuka Satsuki, whom I had been chasing without success, is nowhere to be seen.

entries.japanese:
「……くそ……なんだっていうんだ、一体……！」
　立ち止まって、呼吸を整える。
　はあはあ、と胸が大きく上下していた。
　……今まで気がつかなかったけど、随分と長い間走っていたみたいだ。
「……いま、何時、だろ……」
　両膝に手をついて、適当なショーウィンドウに視線をなげる。
　時刻は―――夜の十二時にさしかかっていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Damn it―――what is going on……!” I stopped and steadied my breathing.
My chest heaved as I panted.
I had not noticed until now, but I seemed to have been running for a very long time.
“What time is it―――?”
Bracing both hands on my knees, I looked toward a nearby shop window.
The time was―――almost midnight.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Shit… What the hell is going on…!"
I stop, catching my breath.
My chest heaves deeply.
…… Though I hadn't realized until now, I must have been running for a long time.
"What… time is it…?"
Resting my hands on my knees, I glance up at a nearby store window.
It is--already midnight.

entries.japanese:
「――――うそ。
そんなに走ってたのか、俺」
　……そんな実感はないけど、時計に間違いはない。
　見渡せば、繁華街の明かりも淋しくなりつつある。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――No way. Was I really running that long?”
It did not feel possible, but the clock could not be wrong.
Looking around, I saw that even the lights of the entertainment district were beginning to die.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----Can't be.
I couldn't have been running for that long."
…… It's hard to believe, but the clock is correct.
Looking around, most all the lights in the shopping district are off.

entries.japanese:
「―――帰、ろう」
　弓塚のことは気になるけど、これ以上捜しても見つけられない気がする。
　……だいたい三時間近く追いかけて、何度も呼びかけたのに振り向きもしないなんて、あいつは何を考えてるんだろう。
　はあ、と大きく深呼吸をして、屋敷に戻ることにした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――I should go home.”
Yumizuka still worried me, but I no longer believed I could find her.
I had chased her for nearly three hours and called to her again and again without so much as a glance back; what was she thinking?
I took one long, deep breath and started back toward the estate.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---I should… go back."
Even though I'm worried about Yumizuka, I feel like I won't be able to find her anymore.
…… I chased her for almost three hours, calling her name all this time, but she did not even respond.
What was she thinking?
With a big sigh, I decide to head back to the mansion.

entries.japanese:
――――自分の錯覚を、無視できない。
　もう何人も殺人を犯している通り魔が徘徊しているっていう夜の街で、怪しい物音がした路地裏に行こうだなんてどうかしてる。
　どうかしてるけど、俺は――――昨日の弓塚の笑顔が忘れられない。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――I couldn’t ignore it, even if it was only my imagination.
Going into a suspicious alley at night, while a random killer who had already murdered several people roamed the city, was insane.
Even so, I――――couldn’t forget Yumizuka’s smile from yesterday.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----I can't ignore my feelings.
With a killer skulking around town at night looking for victims, I shouldn't be investigating suspicious sounds in alleyways.
But… I still remember Yumizuka's smiling face from yesterday.

entries.japanese:
弓塚がいるはずなんてないけど。
もしそこに弓塚がいて、なにか取り返しのつかないコトになっていたのなら。
　……俺は、それを見逃したコトを絶対に後悔する。
entries.maoEnglish:
There was no reason for Yumizuka to be there. But if she was, and something irreversible had happened to her…
I would never forgive myself for walking away.
entries.mirrorMoon:
There's no reason for Yumizuka to be there.
But if she is, she might need my help.
…… I'll never forgive myself if I just ignore this.

entries.japanese:
「――――よし」
　ポケットの中に手をいれると、かつん、という冷たい感触があった。
　使うつもりはさらさらないが、とにかくこっちにも武器があると思うと気が楽になる。
　……それに、いざとなれば遠野志貴にはこの『眼』があるんだ。
　先生は無闇に使うなって言ってたけど、相手が殺人鬼なら許してくれるだろう。
「……音、こっちからだったな」
　覚悟をきめて、路地裏へ足を運んだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――All right”
I slipped a hand into my pocket and felt the cold, hard touch of metal.
I had no intention of using it, but knowing I had a weapon made me feel better.
And if the worst happened, Shiki Tohno had――――these eyes.
Teach had warned me never to use them carelessly, but surely a murderer would be an exception.
“The sound came from this way.”
Bracing myself, I entered the alley.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----Alright."
Putting my hand in my pocket, there is the cold touch of iron.
Even though I don't intend to use it, it's comforting to know that I'm not unarmed.
…… And if it comes to it, I have my "eyes" too.
Sensei said not to use them recklessly, but she'll find it acceptable if I use it against a killer.
"…… The sound… it came from here…"
Preparing myself, I step into the alley.

entries.japanese: ―――どくん。
entries.maoEnglish: ―――Thump.
entries.mirrorMoon: ---Thump.

entries.japanese:
心臓が、ひときわ大きく脈をうつ。
　路地裏は静かだ。
　……物音は、この奥の広場から聞こえてきた。
entries.maoEnglish:
My heart gave one enormous beat.
The alley was silent.
The sound had come from an open space farther in.
entries.mirrorMoon:
My heart pounds.
The back alley is quiet.
…… The noise came from the open area at the far end.

entries.japanese: ―――どくん。
entries.maoEnglish: ―――Thump.
entries.mirrorMoon: ---Thump.

entries.japanese:
首のうしろが、痛い。
　極度の緊張で痙攣でもしているのか、背骨が皮膚から飛び出しそうなぐらい、痛い。
entries.maoEnglish:
The back of my neck hurt.
Perhaps the tension had made it spasm; the pain felt as though my spine were trying to burst through my skin.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The back of my head, hurts.
As if convulsing under the utmost strain, my wracked spine hurts as if it's about to rip itself out of my body.

entries.japanese: ―――どくん。
entries.maoEnglish: ―――Thump.
entries.mirrorMoon: ---Thump.

entries.japanese:
どうしてだろう。
　俺は何も考えていないのに、本能がさっきから警告を鳴らしている。
entries.maoEnglish:
Why?
My mind was blank, yet every instinct I possessed had begun to sound an alarm.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Why is it?
I can't think, yet my instincts shout at me.

entries.maoEnglish: ―――Thump.
entries.mirrorMoon: ---Thu-mp.

entries.japanese:
行くな。
　その先には行くな。
　行けば、きっと戻れない。
entries.maoEnglish:
Don’t go.
Don’t go any farther.
If you do, you will never come back.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Don't go.
Don't go any further.
If you do, you won't be able to come back.

entries.maoEnglish: ―――Thump.
entries.mirrorMoon: ---Thu-mp.

entries.japanese:
けど、もう遅い。
　路地裏を抜けて、俺はその広場へと足を踏み入れてしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
But it was already too late.
I emerged from the alley and stepped into the open space beyond.
entries.mirrorMoon:
But it's already too late.
I step out of the back alley, and into the open space.

entries.japanese:
「――――え？」
　ただ、そんな声しか、出せなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――What?”
It was the only sound I could make.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----Eh?"
That weak voice is all that I can get out.

entries.japanese:
路地裏は、一面の赤い世界だった。
　ゴミやガレキにまじって手足が散乱している。
　手足は犬や猫のたぐいじゃない。
　その断面から赤い血と、骨と、生々しい肉を見せた、紛れもない人間の手足だった。
entries.maoEnglish:
The alley opened onto a world painted entirely red.
Arms and legs lay scattered among the rubbish and rubble.
They did not belong to dogs or cats.
Their severed ends exposed red blood, white bone, and wet flesh; they were unmistakably human.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The back alley is a single sheet of crimson.
Limbs are strewn amongst the garbage and rubble.
Not the limbs of dogs, or cats, or the like.
They are human limbs, blood dripping from fresh meat and bone.

entries.japanese:
地面や壁には赤い血が塗りたくられている。
　鼻孔をつく重い匂い。
　どろり、と。
　赤い霧になって体にまとわりついてきそうなほど、濃厚な血のにおい。
entries.maoEnglish:
Blood was smeared across the ground and walls.
A heavy smell struck my nostrils.
Thick and cloying.
The stench of blood was so dense it seemed ready to become red mist and cling to my body.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The ground and the walls are painted with red blood.
A heavy scent fills my nostrils.
Thick.
Like a red fog permeating my body, the choking smell of blood.

entries.japanese:
顔。
顔。
顔。
　首元から断ち切られ、苦悶の表情のまま転がった顔。
　木乃伊のように干からびて、真っ二つに割れてカラカラと転がっている顔。
　両目を刳り抜かれて、男とも女ともとれないぐらい正体不明のまま放置された顔。
entries.maoEnglish:
Faces. Faces. Faces.
A face severed at the neck, lying where it fell with its agony intact.
A face shriveled like a mummy, split in half and rattling dryly over the ground.
A face with both eyes gouged out, abandoned beyond all recognition of whether it had belonged to a man or woman.
entries.mirrorMoon:
A face.
A face.
A face.
A face on a severed head, rolling around with an expression of agony.
A face shriveled up like a mummy, split in halves.
A face with both eyes gouged out, so distorted I can't even tell if it used to be a man or a woman.

entries.japanese:
「―――――」
　声も出せず、ただ、ソレらの亡骸を傍観した。
　いや、人の死体というにはあまりにも遠すぎる。
　出来の悪いオブジェにしたって、もうすこしはマシだろう。
　死体は、四つあった。
　どれもこれも食い散らかされた残飯みたいに転がっている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――――”
Unable to speak, I could only stare at those remains.
No—they were too far removed from humanity to call corpses.
Even a shoddy art installation would have looked better than this.
There were four bodies.
Every one lay discarded like the scraps of some devoured meal.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-----"
Unable to make a sound, I merely gaze speechless at the corpses.
No, they can't even be called human bodies any more.
Even a badly made sculpture looks better than this.
There are four bodies.
They roll around like scraps of leftover food.

entries.japanese:
「は―――――は」
　愕然と死体の海を見つめる。
　首のうしろがズキズキと痛んで、喉が乾いて呼吸が火のように熱い。
　指先はガクガクと震えていて、口元がいびつな形にゆがんでしまう。
　これは―――何だ。
　いま目の前に広がっている世界は、なんだ。
「――――赤い」
　そう。
　目が醒めるぐらいに、攻撃的な一面の色―――
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ha―――――ha”
I stared at the sea of bodies.
The back of my neck throbbed, my throat was dry, and every breath burned like fire.
My fingers shook uncontrollably; my mouth twisted out of shape.
What―――was this?
What was the world spread before me?
“――――Red”
Yes.
A single, aggressive color vivid enough to shock me awake—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah----ah."
I gape in shock at the sea of bodies.
The back of my head throbs, my throat is parched, and my breath burns like fire.
My fingertips quiver, and my mouth distorts.
What---is this?
What is this world before my eyes?
"----Red."
Yes.
Before my eyes, everything is that terrible color---

entries.japanese:
ただ、ぼうと立ち尽くす。
　悲鳴も出ない。
恐怖もない。
　ただ、忘我して異状な光景を映画のワンシーンのように、路地裏を見つめている自分がいた。
　きっと。
　そうでもしていないと正気がなくなってしまうので、理性がそういった方法で俺をとどめてくれているのだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
I stood there, empty.
No scream came. There was no fear.
I merely watched the impossible alley as though it were a scene in a film and I had nothing to do with it.
Surely.
Reason was holding me at that distance because any closer contact would have cost me my sanity.
entries.mirrorMoon:
But I merely stand.
No screaming, no fear.
Like the scene of an accident in a movie, I only stare at the back alley.
Undoubtedly,
this is how my mind is protecting myself.
Otherwise I would have gone mad.

entries.japanese:
がさり、と壁際の死体が動いた。
　いや、違う。
　そこにいるのは死体じゃない。
　無造作に転がっている手足とは違う。
　ちゃんと手足がある、生きている人間のようだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
Something rustled among the bodies by the wall.
No—that was wrong.
It wasn’t a corpse.
It was different from the limbs strewn carelessly around it.
It appeared to be a living human being, with all four limbs intact.
entries.mirrorMoon:
A corpse against the wall moves.
No, that's wrong.
It's not a corpse.
It's not like the scrapped hands and feet.
It's a living human being, with limbs attached.

entries.japanese:
「あ…………」
　なにか、意外なものを見た。
　人が生きていたという事を喜ぶより、この光景の中で生きている人間がいる事が、なんだか不自然な気がして。
　けど、生きているのなら。
　生きているんなら、助けて、あげないと。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ah…”
I had seen something unexpected.
Instead of relief that someone had survived, I felt only that a living person was somehow unnatural in this place.
But if that person was alive.
If they were alive, I had to help them.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah………"
I see something out of place.
In this ghoulish spectacle, the response to seeing someone alive is more of astonishment than happiness.
But, if he's alive.
If he's alive, I have to help him.

entries.japanese:
「あの―――もしもし？」
　麻痺した感情のまま、まだ生きている人間のところに歩み寄っていく。
「――――ギ」
　ずるり、と地の海から這い上がって、ソレは俺にむかって顔をあげた。
　その、干からびた、シャレコウベのような顔を。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Um―――hello?”
With my emotions still numb, I approached the survivor.
“――――Gih”
It dragged itself out of the sea of blood and raised its face toward me.
That withered face, like a bare skull.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Uh---hello?"
With my mind still paralyzed, I step towards the living figure.
"---Gih."
Pulling itself up from the sea, it raises its face toward me.
A face like a dried out skull.

entries.japanese:
「ひ―――――！」
　反射的に後ろに逃げる。
　けど、そんな俺の動きなんかより、シャレコウベのほうが何倍も速い。
　ひゅうひゅうという声をあげて、ソイツは俺の上にのしかかってきた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ee―――――!”
I recoiled on instinct.
The skull-faced thing moved many times faster.
Wheezing, it threw itself on top of me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hii----!"
I leap back reflexively.
But, the skull moves faster than I do.
With a voice crying out "hyuuu!
hyuuu!" he jumps at me.

entries.japanese:
――――ひゅう、ひゅう。
　イヤな声が、目の前で聞こえた。
　見れば―――シャレコウベの喉は大きな穴が開いていて、満足に発音できないらしかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――Hhhee, hhhee.
The loathsome sound came from inches away.
When I looked―――a great hole gaped in the creature’s throat; apparently it could no longer form proper words.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----Hyuu!
Hyuu!
A hideous voice, right next to me.

Looking down---there is a large hole in the skull's throat, preventing him from speaking correctly.

entries.japanese:
「――――あ」
　干からびた顔、干からびた腕がのしかかってくる。
　骨と皮しか残っていない喉の声帯が、ぶるぶると不気味な声にあわせて振動している。
「うわあああああ！」
　ただ、必死になってソイツを引き剥がそうとした。
　だがソイツは不気味な声をあげて離れようとしない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――Ah”
Its shriveled face and arms bore down on me.
The vocal cords in its skin-and-bone throat trembled with each horrible sound.
“Aaaaaah!”
I fought desperately to tear it off.
But it only wheezed and refused to let go.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----Ah!"
The dried up face, the dried up arm reaching for me.
In the throat of this bag of bones, vocal chords vibrate in accord with the ghastly voice.
"Uwaaaahhhhh!"
Desperately, I try to tear him off me.
But he merely raises that ghastly voice, and will not get off.

entries.japanese:
ごり、と。
　ソイツの指が、肩口に突き刺さった。
entries.maoEnglish:
Crunch.
Its fingers drove into my shoulder.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Rip.
Its fingers pierce my shoulder.

entries.japanese:
「っっっっっ！」
　痛みで体が跳ねる。
　ソレの指は、鋭いキリのようだった。
　容赦なく俺の皮をさいて肉をえぐり、そのまま神経を引きずっていく激痛―――
「あ、ああ、あ――――！」
　ただ痛くて、そんな声しか出せない。
　悲鳴をあげながら懸命にソイツを引き剥がすが、ソイツの力は強すぎた。
俺が何をしようがびくともしない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――――!”
My body jerked with pain.
Its fingers were sharp as awls.
They sliced mercilessly through my skin, gouged into my flesh, and dragged raw pain through every nerve―――
“Ah, aaah――――!”
The pain left me capable of nothing but that cry.
Screaming, I fought to wrench it away, but it was monstrously strong. Nothing I did moved it an inch.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Chhh!"
My body arcs from pain.
The fingers were like a sharp needle.
It shreds my skin mercilessly, scooping out nerves and flesh as it goes---
"Ah, aahhh----!"
The pain is so great that I can say nothing else.
Though I try to tear him off me screaming, he is too strong.
Whatever I do, he does not move.

entries.japanese:
カカ、と音をたててシャレコウベの口が開く。
　肩を一口で噛み砕けるぐらいに開いた口が、死にたくない、と助けをこうように、俺の顔へと近寄ってくる。
「や――――」
　やめろ、という声も通じない。
　骨と皮だけのソイツは、そのまま俺の頭にかじりつこうとして――――そのまま、唐突に、崩れ落ちた。
entries.maoEnglish:
Its jaws clacked open, wide enough to crush my shoulder in one bite.
That mouth came toward my face as if pleading for help—as if begging not to die.
“St—”
It could not understand me telling it to stop.
The thing of bone and skin lunged to bite into my skull—and then, without warning, collapsed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
With a creak, the skull's jaw opens.
The mouth opens wide enough to rip off my shoulder with a single bite, and he approaches my face as if saying, "I don't want to die, somebody save me".
"St---"
I can't even say "stop".
The guy made only of skin and bones, tries to bite my head----and suddenly, he collapses.

entries.japanese:
「へ……？」
　あんなに強かった力が消えていく。
　かろうじて骨と皮だけが残っていた人の形をしたソイツは、残された骨と皮さえも無くして、跡形もなく消え去っていく。
　さらさらと。
　悪い夢みたいに、ソレは灰になって散っていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Huh…?”
Its terrible strength ebbed away.
The thing had barely retained a human shape in bone and skin; now even those remnants vanished, leaving nothing behind.
Softly, grain by grain.
It crumbled into ash and scattered like a nightmare breaking apart.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Eh…?"
The awesome power vanishes.
The bag of bones in a person's form crumples to the ground and disappears.
Softly,
like a bad dream, it turns to ash and blows away.

entries.japanese:
「………なんだよ、これ」
　ずきりと、肩から痛みが走る。
「あ………つ」
　背中に自分の血が流れていく。
　痛みは現実。
だからこれは、紛れもない現実。
　ひどい、悪夢だ。
　こんなコト―――悪い夢でしかないのに、夢ですら、ないなんて。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…What the hell was that?”
Pain stabbed through my shoulder.
“Ah…
ngh.”
My own blood ran down my back.
The pain was real, and therefore this was real.
A hideous nightmare—something that could only be a bad dream, yet wasn’t even a dream.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… What the hell is this?"
Pain runs through my shoulder.
"Ach…"
My own blood flows down my back.
The pain is real.
So this must be real.
A terrible nightmare.
But---it can't be a nightmare, because it's not a dream.

entries.japanese:
「遠野くん。
それ以上そこにいると危ないよ」
「――――！」
　背後からの声に振りかえる。
　入ってきた路地裏の入り口に、弓塚さつきが立っていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Tohno. It’s dangerous to stay there.”
“――――!”
I spun toward the voice behind me.
Satsuki Yumizuka stood at the entrance to the alley.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Tohno-kun.
It'll be dangerous if you stay there."
"----!"
I turn towards the voice behind me.
At the mouth of the alley where I came from, I see Yumizuka Satsuki.

entries.japanese:
「弓、塚―――？」
「こんばんは。
こんなところで会うなんて、奇遇だね」
　まるで、街中で偶然であったように、気軽に弓塚は語りかけてきた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Yumizuka―――?”
“Good evening. Fancy meeting you in a place like this.”
Yumizuka spoke as lightly as though we had bumped into each other on an ordinary street.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yumi… zuka---?"
"Good evening.
Fancy meeting you in a place like this, huh?"
As if we had merely bumped into each other in the mall, Yumizuka greets me lightheartedly.

entries.japanese:
「弓塚、おまえ……おまえこそ、こんな時間に何してるんだよ」
「わたしはただの散歩。
でも、遠野くんこそ何をしてるの？
　そんなにいっぱいの人を殺しちゃうなんて、いけないんじゃないかな」
　ふふ、と淡い笑顔で弓塚は言った。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Yumizuka, you―――what are you doing out at this hour?”
“I’m only taking a walk. What are you doing, Tohno? Killing so many people is rather naughty, don’t you think?”
Yumizuka gave a faint, soft laugh.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yumizuka, you… What are you doing, out at a time like this?"
"Oh, just going for a walk.
But what's Tohno-kun doing?
Killing so many people like this is bad, right?"
Yumizuka says, with a light smile.

entries.japanese:
「人を殺したって―――え？」
　周囲を見渡す。
　……それで、自分がどんな惨状の中で立ち尽くしているのかを思い出した。
　一面の血の海の中。
　遠野志貴は、まるで殺人犯のように、呆然と立ち尽くしている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Killing people―――what?”
I looked around.
Then I remembered the carnage in which I stood.
I stood in the middle of a sea of blood.
Shiki Tohno stood frozen there like the murderer himself.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Killing so many people… eh?"
I look around me.
…… And I remember the tragic scene I'm surrounded by.
In a sea of blood.
Tohno Shiki stands aghast like a murderer.

entries.japanese:
「ち、違う、これは俺じゃない……！」
「違うことはないでしょう。
みんな死んでいて、生きてるのは遠野くんだけなら誰だってやったのは遠野くんだって思うわ」
「そんなワケないだろう！
　俺だってコイツに襲われかけたんだぞ……！」
　さっきまで自分を襲っていた怪物を指差す。
　けど、そこにはもう何もない。
　アレは骨はおろか、灰さえものこさずに風に散って消えていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“N-no, I didn’t do this!”
“But how could it be anyone else? With everyone dead and you the only one alive, anyone would think you did it.”
“That’s ridiculous! That thing attacked me too!”
I pointed to the creature that had been on top of me.
Nothing was there.
Not even ash remained; it had scattered on the wind and disappeared.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"N… no!
This wasn't me!"
"Oh, of course it was.
Everyone's dead, and Tohno-kun's alive, so obviously Tohno-kun must have killed them."
"No way!
It just attacked me……!"
I point at the monster that attacked me moments ago.
But, nothing's there.
Even the ashes of the bones have been blown away by the wind.

entries.japanese:
「あ――――」
　息を飲む。
　弓塚はくすくすと笑っている。
「ち、ちがう―――俺じゃ、俺じゃない、んだ」
　あたまがマヒして、そんな言葉しか言えない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ah――――”
My breath caught.
Yumizuka giggled.
“N-no―――it wasn’t me, it wasn’t me”
My mind was numb; those were the only words I could produce.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah----"
I swallow my breath.
Yumizuka is chuckling.
"It's not… this wasn't… wasn't me…"
My head is paralyzed, and can only manage broken language.

entries.japanese:
……わかってる。
　ちゃんと何がおかしくて何がおかしくないのか解っているんだけど、思考が空回りして喋れない。
　例えば、家出しているっていう弓塚がどうしてこんなところにいるのか。
　例えば、こんな惨状を目の前にして、どうして弓塚はそんなふうに笑ってられるのか、とか。
entries.maoEnglish:
I understood.
I knew what made sense and what did not, but my thoughts spun uselessly and left me unable to speak.
For instance, why was Yumizuka—supposedly a runaway—here at all?
And how could she smile like that with this carnage before her?
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… I understand.
I can think clearly, but I can't put my thoughts into words.
For example, why is Yumizuka at a place like this after running away from home?
For example, why is Yumizuka laughing in the face of this tragic scene?

entries.japanese:
「弓塚さん、俺は―――」
「うん、ほんとは解ってるんだ。
遠野くんは食事中に出くわしただけなんでしょう？
　いじわるなこと言ってごめんね。
わたし、いつも自分の気持ちと反対のことをしちゃうから、遠野くんにはいつもこんなふうにしてばっかり」
　弓塚はまだ笑っている。
　……それがこの惨状にあまりに不釣り合いで、ぞくりとした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Yumizuka, I—” “I know the truth.
You only stumbled across me while I was eating, didn’t you? I’m sorry I teased you. I always do the opposite of what I really feel. Somehow, I’m always like that with you.”
Yumizuka was still smiling.
…The smile was so grotesquely out of place that a chill ran through me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yumizuka-san, I---"
"Yeah, I know.
You just interrupted someone's meal.
I'm sorry for sounding mean.
I always act against my feelings, so I'm always acting like this to you."
Yumizuka is still laughing.
…… It's so inappropriate for this scene, I feel a chill.

entries.japanese:
弓塚は路地裏の入り口から動かない。
　不自然に組まれた両腕。
まるで、何かを隠すように後ろに組んでいる。
―――注意して見れば。
　彼女の肘のあたりには赤々としたモノが、まだら模様をつくっていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
Yumizuka remained at the entrance.
Her arms were held in an unnatural pose behind her back. It was as if she were hiding something.
―――When I looked closely.
Vivid red stains mottled the skin around her elbows.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Yumizuka doesn't move from the entrance of the alley.
Her arms are positioned strangely, as if she's hiding something behind her back.
---And, looking closer,
there are spots of something red on her sleeve.

entries.japanese:
「弓塚、おまえ――――」
「どうしたの？
　恐い顔して、ヘンな遠野くん」
　また、クスリと笑う。
「――――――」
　……違う。
　彼女は、弓塚さつきなんかじゃ、ない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Yumizuka, you――――”
“What’s wrong? You look frightening, Tohno.”
She giggled again.
“――――――”
No.
This couldn’t be Satsuki Yumizuka.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yumizuka, you---"
"What is it?
Your face looks scary, Tohno-kun."
She laughs again.
"------"
…… No.
Somehow, this girl cannot be Yumizuka Satsuki.

entries.japanese:
「弓塚―――なんでおまえ、手を隠してるんだ」
「あ、やっぱりバレちゃった？
　遠野くんってば抜けているようで鋭いんだよね。
わたしね、あなたのそうゆう所が昔っからいいなあって思ってたんだ、志貴くん」
　そう、わざとらしく志貴くん、と強く発音して。
　弓塚は、両手を前にさし出した。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Yumizuka―――why are you hiding your hands?”
“Oh, you noticed? You act absentminded, but you’re surprisingly sharp. That’s something I’ve always liked about you, Shiki.”
She placed an almost theatrical emphasis on the name Shiki.
Then Yumizuka brought both hands out in front of her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yumizuka… why are you hiding your hands like that?"
"Ah, have I been found out?
I guess you're too observant to miss that, huh.
I've always liked that about you, Shiki-kun."
After emphasizing the "Shiki-kun",
she brings her hands out.

entries.japanese:
真っ赤に染まった両手。
　血は乾ききっておらず、ぴちゃぴちゃと音をたてて赤い雫をこぼしている。
　それを、誇るように。
　弓塚さつきは、口元に笑みをうかべていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
Both hands were stained scarlet.
The blood had not yet dried.
Red drops pattered wetly from her fingers.
As though displaying something to be proud of, Satsuki Yumizuka smiled.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Both hands are dyed crimson.
Not yet dry, the blood drips off them in red droplets.
And, proudly,
Yumizuka Satsuki is smiling.

entries.japanese:
「弓塚、その手―――」
「うん。
わたしが、その人たちを殺したの」
「な――――」
「あ、でもこれは悪いことじゃないんだよ。
わたしはこの人たちが憎くて殺したんじゃないもの。
生きていくためにはこの人たちの血が必要だから、仕方なく殺したんだから」
　……なん、だろう。
　弓塚は、なにか、よく解らないことを、言っている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Yumizuka, your hands―――”
“Yes. I killed those people.”
“Wha――――”
“But this wasn’t wrong. I didn’t kill them because I hated them. I need their blood to live, so I had no choice.”
What was she saying?
Yumizuka was saying something I couldn’t understand at all.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yumizuka, your hands---"
"Yeah.
I killed those people."
"Wha---"
"Oh, but, it's okay.
I didn't kill them because I hated them.
I just needed their blood to live, so I had to kill them."
…… What… is this?
I… don't really understand what Yumizuka is saying.

entries.japanese:
「殺したって―――ホントなのか、弓塚」
「嘘だって言っても信じてくれないでしょ？
　それともわたしみたいな女の子じゃこんなコトできないって思ってくれる？」
　クスクス、という笑い声。
―――信じられない。
　信じられないけど、間違いなく彼女は嘘なんてついていない。
　この惨状は。
　みんな、弓塚が起こしたものなんだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You killed them—really, Yumizuka?”
“You wouldn’t believe me if I said no, would you? Or do you think a girl like me couldn’t possibly do something like this?”
Her soft laughter answered me.
―――I couldn’t believe it.
I couldn’t believe it.
And yet there was no question that she was telling the truth.
All this carnage—Yumizuka had done it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"You… really killed them, Yumizuka?"
"You wouldn't believe me even if I told you it's a lie, right?
Or do you think it's impossible for a girl like me to do such a thing?"
Her voice laughs softly.
---I don't believe her.
I don't believe her, but she is definitely not telling a lie.
This tragic scene.
It's all Yumizuka's doing.

entries.japanese:
「どうして―――こんな、酷い事を」
「ひどくなんかないよ。
さっきも言ったでしょう、わたしはこの人たちが憎くて殺したんじゃないもの。
志貴くん、生きるために他の生き物を殺すことはね、悪いことじゃないんだよ」
「なにを―――！
　どんな理由があったって、人殺しは悪いことだろ！」
「そんなコトないけどね。
あ、でも悪いことも一つだけしちゃったみたい。
　わたし、今日が初めてだから加減ができなくて、血を吸う時に自分の血も送っちゃったの。
そのせいで逝き残ったのが出てきて、志貴くんが襲われる事になったわ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Why would you do something this horrible?”
“It isn’t horrible. I told you, I didn’t kill them because I hated them. Shiki, there’s nothing wrong with killing other creatures so you can live.” “What are you talking about?
Murder is wrong no matter what reason you have!” “I don’t think so.
Oh—but I suppose I did do one bad thing. It was my first time, so I couldn’t control myself.
When I drank their blood, some of mine went back into them. One of them lingered on without changing all the way, and that’s why it attacked you.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Why… such a terrible thing…?"
"It's not terrible.
Like I said, I didn't kill them because I hated them.
There's nothing wrong with killing others in order to live, is there, Shiki-kun?"
"What…!
That's absurd!
Killing is wrong!"
"No, it's not.
But, I did do one bad thing.
Since today was my first time drinking blood, I let a little of my blood get back into them.
Because of that, you got attacked, Shiki-kun.

entries.japanese:
「ごめんなさい。
わたし、あやうく志貴くんを巻き込むところだった。
ソイツが成りきれないで死んでくれて、本当によかった」
「なにを―――なにを言ってるんだ、弓塚」
「今は解らなくていいよ。
わたしもまだ自分自身のことを把握しきれてないから、うまく説明できないわ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’m sorry. I almost got you caught up in this. I’m so glad that thing died before it could finish changing.”
“What—what are you talking about, Yumizuka?”
“You don’t have to understand yet. I still don’t entirely understand what’s happened to me, so I can’t explain it very well.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I'm sorry for getting you involved.
But we're lucky; it died without being able to finish changing."
"What… what are you talking about, Yumizuka?"
"It's okay if you don't understand right now.
I don't really understand myself yet, so I can't explain it very well."

entries.japanese:
「けど、何日かすればきっと志貴くんみたいになれると思う。
　志貴くんみたいな、立派な――――」
　言いかけて、弓塚は顔を歪ませて苦しみだした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“But give me a few days and I’m sure I’ll become like you.
Someone like you—a proper—”
Before she could finish, Yumizuka’s face twisted in agony.
entries.mirrorMoon:
But, I think after a few days I can become like Shiki-kun.
Like Shiki-kun, become a great---"
As she says so, her face distorts in pain.

entries.japanese:
「はっ―――あ、う…………！！」
　苦しげに喉をかきむしって。
　弓塚は、ごぶりと、口から血を吐き出した。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hah—ah…
ngh…!”
She clawed desperately at her throat, then vomited a thick gush of blood.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ha---… aaau!!!"
Rasps of agony echo from her throat.
Yumizuka chokes up blood.

entries.japanese:
「いた――――い。
やっぱり、お腹が減ったからって無闇に吸ってもダメみたい。
質のいい、キレイな血じゃないと、体に合わないのかな―――」
　コホコホとせき込む。
　その咳は赤く、あきらかに血を吐いていた。
「ん――――く、んああ…………！！！」
　弓塚の体がガクガクと震えている。
　……よくわからない。
　もう、何もかもよくわからないけど、ただ、弓塚がひどく苦しんでいるという事だけは、はっきりとした事実だった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“It hurts. I guess I can’t just drink from anyone because I’m hungry.
Maybe my body will only accept good, clean blood—” She coughed and coughed, bringing up unmistakable blood each time.
“Nn—gh, aaah…!”
Her whole body convulsed.
I didn’t understand.
I understood nothing anymore.
But one fact was undeniable: Yumizuka was in terrible pain.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"It----hurts.
I guess, even if I'm hungry, I shouldn't just drink blood at random.
If it's not good quality, beautiful blood, it won't agree with me…"
She breaks out in a fit of coughing.
She chokes out blood with every cough.
"Nn---kuh, nnaaah…!!!"
Yumizuka's body convulses.
…… I don't really understand.
All I know is, Yumizuka's in terrible pain.
That's all I can clearly understand.

entries.japanese:
「おい……苦しいのか、弓塚……！？」
　弓塚に駆けよって、その手を取ろうとする。
「――――だめ！
　近寄らないで、志貴くん！」
　だが、それは弓塚の声で止められた。
「……ダメ、だよ、全然大丈夫じゃないよ、志貴くん」
　はあはあと。
　苦しげな呼吸が、赤い血を吐いて、届いてくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hey…
are you in pain, Yumizuka?”
I rushed toward her and reached for her hand.
“—No! Stay away from me, Shiki!”
Her cry stopped me. “No… don’t.
I’m not all right at all, Shiki.”
Her labored breaths reached me in wet, bloody gasps.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hey… are you okay, Yumizuka…!?"
I run towards her to take her hand.
"----No!
Don't come any closer, Shiki-kun!"
But, Yumizuka's voice stops me.
"…… You mustn't.
I'm not… entirely okay, Shiki-kun."
She speaks painfully, still vomiting red blood.

entries.japanese:
「弓……塚、おまえ―――」
　俺には、わからない。
　弓塚が苦しんでいる理由も、どうして、彼女がそんなふうになってしまっているのかも。
「どうしたんだよ、いったい。
人を殺したって言ってたけど、そんなの嘘だろ、弓塚……？
　そんなに苦しいんならすぐに病院に行かないとだめじゃないか」
　……なんて、偽善。
　弓塚が本当にこの惨状を作ったんだって分かっているのに、そんな、つまらない嘘を口にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Yumi…zuka, what—” I didn’t understand why she was suffering, or how she had become like this.
“What happened to you?
You said you killed those people, but that was a lie, wasn’t it?
If you’re hurting this badly, you need a hospital right now.”
What hypocrisy.
I knew perfectly well that she had created this slaughter, yet I offered her that paltry lie.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yumi… zuka, you…"
I don't understand.
Why Yumizuka's in pain, or why she's like this.
"What the hell is going on?
You said you killed those people, but it's a lie, right, Yumizuka…?
If you're in that much pain, shouldn't you be in a hospital?"
…… I'm fooling myself.
Even though I understand Yumizuka brought about this tragic scene, I still lie to myself.

entries.japanese:
「弓塚―――そっちに行くけど、いいな？」
　優しく話しかける。
　けど弓塚はブンブンと頭をふって、さっきより激しく俺を拒絶した。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Yumizuka—I’m coming over there, all right?”
I kept my voice gentle, but she shook her head wildly,
rejecting me even more fiercely than before.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yumizuka… I'm coming over there, okay?"
I speak gently.
But Yumizuka shakes her head in violent refusal.

entries.japanese:
「どうして―――苦しいんなら、すぐに病院に行かないとダメだろう……！」
「……ダメなのは志貴くんのほうだよ。
ほんとに、いつもいつも、わかってくれないん、だから」
「ばか―――それを言ったらさっきから何一つわからないよ、俺は―――！」
「あ……は、そっか、そうだよね……それでも、わたしに付きあってくれてるんだ―――」
　よろり、と。
　逃げるように、弓塚の体が後ろに引いていく。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Why? If you’re in pain, you need to get to a hospital!”
“You’re the hopeless one, Shiki. You never understand. You never, ever understand…”
“Idiot—if that’s what you mean, then I haven’t understood one thing you’ve said all night!”
“Ah… ha. That’s true, isn’t it?
And you’re still staying here with me…”
She staggered backward as though trying to escape.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Why!?---If you're in pain, we have to get you to a hospital right away…!"
"Shiki-kun, you're not getting it.
You really never understand anything…"
"Idiot!
I told you before, I don't understand…!"
"Ah… yeah, you did, didn't you.
But you're still here…"
Yumizuka begins to pull away.

entries.japanese:
「……痛いよ、志貴くん」
　ぜいぜいと、呼吸を乱して、赤い血が、吐き出される。
「……痛くて、寒くて、すごく不安なの。
　ほんとは、今すぐにでも志貴くんに助けてほしい」
―――けど、今夜はまだダメなんだ。
　そう言って。
　弓塚は、突然に体を持ちなおした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“It hurts, Shiki.”
Her breath came in ragged wheezes, spilling bright blood.
“It hurts, and I’m cold, and I’m so afraid.
The truth is, I want you to save me right now.”
―――But not tonight. Tonight is still too soon.
With those words,
Yumizuka abruptly mastered herself.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… It hurts, Shiki-kun."
She breathes raggedly, coughing up red blood.
"It hurts, it's cold, and I'm scared.
I really want your help right now, Shiki-kun."
---But it's too early.
Saying that,
Yumizuka straightens up again.

entries.japanese:
「―――待っててね、すぐに一人前の吸血鬼になって、志貴くんに会いに行くから！」
「あ―――待て、弓塚！」
entries.maoEnglish:
“—Wait for me. I’ll become a full-fledged vampire soon, and then I’ll come see you, Shiki!”
“Ah—wait, Yumizuka!”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Wait for me, okay?
I'll go become a great vampire, then I'll come back and see you!"
"Ah… wait, Yumizuka!"

entries.japanese:
「――――――」
　弓塚の姿はない。
　俺が一歩駆け出す間に、弓塚はとっくに路地裏から走り去ってしまった。
　……そのスピードは人間のものではなく、獰猛な獣のそれだ。
「―――弓塚、おまえ―――」
　なにが、あったっていうんだ、本当に………！
entries.maoEnglish:
“—” She was gone.
Before I had taken a single running step,
Yumizuka had already vanished from the alley.
That speed belonged not to a human being,
but to a savage beast.
“Yumizuka, what—” What in God’s name had happened to her…?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------"
Yumizuka is gone.
Even as I start to run, Yumizuka is long gone.
…… Her speed is inhuman, like that of a wild beast.
"---Yumizuka, you---"
What happened to you, really………!?

entries.japanese:
「ぐ―――――！」
　傷つけられた肩が痛む。
　振りかえれば。
　あれだけ人間の部品が散乱していた路地裏の広場には、赤い血しか残っていない。
　顔も。
臓物も。
手足も。
　さっきのシャレコウベのように、灰になって消えてしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ghh—!”
My wounded shoulder throbbed.
When I looked back, nothing remained in the little alley square but red blood.
The faces, the viscera,
the arms and legs—all had turned to ash and
vanished just as that skull had.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Gah---!"
My injured shoulder throbs.
When I look back, the open space where all the limbs were scattered only left red blood.
The faces, the organs, the hands and feet.
They all turned to ashes, like the skull did before.

entries.japanese:
「く―――そ」
　ただ悔しくて、壁を叩く。
「どうなってんだよ、一体―――！」
　怒鳴り声だけが、虚しく路地裏に反響した。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Damn it.”
Helpless fury drove my fist into the wall.
“What the hell is going on?”
Only my shout answered, echoing hollowly through the alley.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Sh… it…"
Angrily, I strike the wall.
"What the hell is going on!!!"
I bellow pointlessly, and the alley echoes my voice.

entries.japanese:
「――――――」
　気がつけば屋敷の玄関までやってきていた。
　ずきり、と肩の傷が痛む。
　屋敷の明かりはみな消えている。
　連絡もいれず、こんな夜遅くに帰ってくることになるなんて思いもしなかった。
　秋葉―――秋葉はきっと、俺のことを怒っているんだろうな、なんて思いながら、玄関の重いドアに手をかけた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“—” Somehow I found myself at the mansion’s front door.
Pain stabbed through my shoulder.
Every light in the house was out.
I had never expected to come home this late without so much as calling.
Akiha would be furious with me.
Thinking that, I put my hand on the heavy door.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----"
The next thing I know, I'm at the gates of the mansion.
The wound on my shoulder aches.
The lights of the mansion are dark.
Somehow, I hadn't realized I would be coming back so late.
Akiha--Akiha will surely be angry with me, I think as I put my hand on the heavy doors.

entries.japanese:
……ロビーには誰もいない。
　さて、どうしようか。
　傷の手当てをしたいんだけど、眠っているだろう琥珀さんたちを起こすわけにはいかないし―――
「……兄さん？」
「え――――秋葉？」
　声がした方に顔をあげる。
　……見上げれば、階段に秋葉の姿があった。
entries.maoEnglish:
The lobby was empty.
What now?
I wanted to tend the wound, but I couldn’t wake Kohaku and the others when they were probably asleep—
“Brother…?”
“Huh—Akiha?”
I looked toward the voice.
She stood above me on the stairs.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… The lobby is empty.
So, what should I do?
Even though my wound needs treating, Kohaku-san is probably asleep--
"…… Nii-san?"
"Eh?----Akiha?"
I look up in the direction of the voice.
…… Akiha is standing on the stairs.

entries.japanese:
「やっぱり兄さんですね。
もうっ、こんな夜遅くに帰ってくるなんて、いったい何を考えて――――」
　階段を下りてくるなり、秋葉はそんな小言を口にして立ち止まった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I thought so, Brother.
Honestly, coming home at this hour—what were you thinking—” Akiha started down the stairs, scolding me, then stopped short.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"It is you.
Coming back so late at night, just what do you think---"
Akiha reaches the bottom of the stairs, and her rebuke stops.

entries.japanese:
「兄さん、その肩―――どこで傷つけられたんです？」
「あ―――」
　しまった、と傷口を隠しても、いまさら遅い。
「いや、これは、その……」
「いいですから、じっとしていてください。
傷口は肩だけですね……？」
「あ――そうだけど、よく、わかるな」
「そんなに服を血に汚していれば判ります。
事情は後で聞きますから、今は治療を先にしましょう。
　兄さん、少し失礼します」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Brother, your shoulder—where did you get that wound?”
“Ah—” Too late.
Hiding it now would accomplish nothing.
“No, this is… I mean…”
“Never mind that. Hold still. Your shoulder is the only place you’re hurt, correct?”
“Yes—but how could you tell?”
“Your clothes are drenched in blood. We can discuss how it happened later; the wound comes first.
Brother, excuse me for a moment.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Nii-san… where did you hurt your shoulder?"
"Ah---"
Damn it.
I had wanted to hide the wound, but it's too late now.
"Ah, no, this is…"
"Never mind.
Hold still.
Is it only your shoulder…?"
"Ah--yes, but, how do you know…"
"I can tell with all that blood on your clothes.
I'll hear about it later, but right now, we'll treat it.
Please, forgive me, Nii-san."

entries.japanese:
有無を言わせぬ迫力で秋葉は俺の肩に手を触れた。
「――――っ！」
　秋葉の指が触れただけで、体がびくんと動く。
　……どうやら傷口は思っている以上に深いようだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
With an authority that allowed no argument, Akiha put a hand on my shoulder.
“—!”
The merest touch of her fingers made my whole body jerk.
Apparently the wound was deeper than I had realized.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Saying so, Akiha touches my shoulder.
"---Tch!"
My body jumps at only the slight touch of Akiha's finger.
…… It appears that the wound is deeper than I thought.

entries.japanese:
「あ―――すみません、痛みましたか、兄さん」
「……いや、大丈夫……って言いたいけど、ダメかな。
触れられるだけで、すごく痛い」
「そうですか……これだけ深いと琥珀では無理ですね。
私が手当てをしますから、居間のほうに行っていてください」
　秋葉は階段を昇っていく。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh—I’m sorry. Did that hurt, Brother?”
“I’d like to say I’m fine… but I don’t think I can. Even touching it hurts like hell.”
“I see… Kohaku can’t handle a wound this deep. I’ll treat it myself. Go and wait in the sitting room.”
Akiha went back upstairs.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah… I'm sorry, did it hurt, Nii-san?"
"…… No, I'm… I'd like to say I'm okay, but I guess I'm not.
Even a touch is really painful."
"I see… if it's this deep, I think it is too much for Kohaku.
I'll treat it, so please go into the sitting room."
Akiha walks upstairs.

entries.japanese:
「…………ふう」
　居間の電気をつけて、ソファーに座る。
　肩の傷はズキズキと痛んで、時間が経つごとに我慢できなくなりつつあった。
「お待たせしました。
傷口を看ますから、楽にしていてください」
　秋葉は手に何やら応急セットを持ってやってきた。
　……そんなものでこの傷がどうにかなるとは思えないけど、消毒ぐらいはしないとまずいとは思う。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Whew…”
I turned on the sitting-room light and sank onto the sofa.
My shoulder throbbed, growing harder to endure with every passing minute.
“Thank you for waiting. Make yourself comfortable while I examine it.”
Akiha returned carrying some sort of first-aid kit.
I doubted anything in there could fix this, but at the very least the wound needed disinfecting.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"………… Phew."
I turn on the sitting room lights, and sit on the sofa.
The wound on my shoulder hurts, and begins to become unbearable.
"Sorry for making you wait.
I'll treat the wound, so please relax."
Akiha comes in holding a first aid kit.
…… I don't think that would really help on this wound, but I guess I should at least get it disinfected.

entries.japanese:
秋葉は俺の背中に回って、傷口の手当てをする。
　血に濡れた服をハサミで切って、傷口を露出させて、消毒液で血を洗い流していく。
entries.maoEnglish:
Akiha moved behind me and began treating the wound.
She cut away the blood-soaked cloth, exposed the wound, and washed the blood off with antiseptic.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Akiha moves behind me, and begins to treat the wound.
The uniform, damp with blood, is cut away with scissors, and the wound is exposed and disinfected.

entries.japanese:
「――――ぐ！」
　つぷ、と体の中に指をつっこまれたような痛み。
　……けど、その後はさしたる痛みもなく、傷口の痛みも段々と薄れていった。
　秋葉の手当てが上手いのか、それとも大した傷ではなかったのか。
　数分経って、痛みは完全に消えてくれた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“—Ghh!”
Pain plunged into me as if she had driven a finger under my skin.
After that, however, there was little pain at all, and even the wound’s ache gradually receded.
Either Akiha was remarkably skilled or the injury had never been that serious.
Within minutes, the pain was completely gone.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Guuuh!"
I clench my fists as the pain flashes through my body.
…… But after that, the ache of the wound begins to fade.
Akiha must be skilled at medical care, or perhaps the wound wasn't so bad to begin with.
After a few minutes, the pain completely goes away.

entries.japanese:
「はい、これでおしまいです。
その程度の傷口でしたら、明日の朝には塞がっているでしょうね」
　テキパキと応急セットを片付ける秋葉。
　……なんていうか、意外だ。
　秋葉のことだからどこでケガをしたんだとか、いつまで遊び歩いているんだとか叱りつけてくると思ったのに。
entries.maoEnglish:
“There. All done. A wound like that should be closed by morning.”
Akiha briskly packed the first-aid supplies away.
It was unexpected.
I had been sure she would demand to know where I had been hurt and lecture me for staying out so late.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Alright, we're done.
I expect a wound like that should be healed by the morning."
Akiha packs away the first aid kit.
…… Somehow, I'm surprised.
I would have expected Akiha to ask where I got injured, and to rebuke me for playing outside so late.

entries.japanese:
「……聞かないんだな、秋葉」
「聞かないって、何をですか？」
「その、さ。
俺がこんな時間に帰ってきた理由とか、こんなケガをしてる理由とか」
　ぽつり、と。
　まるで弱音をはくように、そんな事を言ってしまった。
　弓塚との事があって、俺はすごく疲れている。
　疲れているから―――そんな弱音を口にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You’re… not going to ask, Akiha?”
“Ask what?”
“Why I came home this late.
Why I’m hurt.”
The words slipped out quietly, almost like an admission of weakness.
What had happened with Yumizuka had left me exhausted—and in that exhaustion,
I let myself sound weak.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… You haven't asked, Akiha."
"I haven't asked… about what?"
"Well… you know.
Why I'm back so late.
Why I'm hurt."
I blurt it out like a complaint.
After what happened with Yumizuka, I'm exhausted.
And because I'm tired, I said such a thing.

entries.japanese:
「―――兄さん。
私、物事の順序ぐらいはわきまえているつもりです。
今の兄さんにはまず傷の手当てが必要だったから、あくまでそちらを優先させただけでしょう」
「……そっか。
それは、そうだよな」
「もうっ。
人のことをどう思っていたのよ、兄さんは。
私、人が傷ついているのを放っておいてまで小言を口にしたりはしないわ」
「……そっか。
ごめん、色々と世話になって。
けど、手当てをしてもらってなんだけど―――」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Brother. I do know what comes first. You needed your wound treated, so of course I took care of that before anything else.”
“Right… of course.”
“Honestly, what sort of person did you take me for, Brother? I would never leave someone bleeding merely so I could lecture them.” “Right.
Sorry—and thanks for everything. Though after letting you patch me up, this is going to sound awful—”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Nii-san.
I… think I know the right order for things.
Right now, the priority is to tend to your injury."
"…… I see.
Of course, I see…"
"Ohh!
What kind of person did you think I was, Nii-san!
I'm not about to yell at someone who's hurt."
"…… You're right.
I'm sorry; thank you for everything.
But, even though you treated it--"

entries.japanese:
「事情は話せないって言うんでしょう？
　そんな言い訳は聞たくありませんけど、今日は特別です。
　兄さんが話したくないっていうんでしたら、私も深くは詮索しません」
「え―――その、いいのか。
俺、こんな夜遅くに帰ってきたのに」
「……たしかに兄さんが何をしていたかは気になりますけど、これでも信じてますから。
危ないことはしていないでしょうし、それに―――そんな顔をした人から無理やり話を聞くなんて、できないわ」
　ふい、と照れくさそうに秋葉は視線を逸らした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You’re about to say you can’t tell me what happened, aren’t you? I have no desire to indulge such excuses, but tonight will be an exception.
If you don’t want to speak, Brother, I won’t pry.” “Huh?
You’re really all right with that? Even after I came home this late?”
“Of course I’m curious what you were doing, Brother. But I do trust you. I’m sure you haven’t been doing anything dangerous, and besides—I can’t force answers from someone wearing a face like that.”
Embarrassed, Akiha abruptly looked away.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"You're going to say you can't explain the situation, right?
I don't want to listen to your excuses, but today is special.
If you do not wish to talk about it, I won't inquire either."
"Eh?
Is that, okay?
I came back so late at night…"
"…… Certainly, I am curious about what might have happened to you.
But, I trust you and I have enough trust to believe you weren't doing something too dangerous.
And… I can't force someone to talk when they look like that."
Akiha looks away shyly.

entries.japanese:
「…………」
　そんな顔って―――今の自分はそんなにひどい顔をしているんだろうか。
「事情は兄さんが元気になったら聞きますから。
一晩ぐっすり休めば顔色も良くなるでしょうし」
「――――――」
　気まずくなって、秋葉から視線を逸らす。
　……俺が元気になるまで話は聞かないっていうのは嬉しいんだけど、明日の朝になったって事情なんか話すことはできない。
　結局、秋葉には何も話せない。
　それが後ろめたくて、秋葉の顔をまっすぐに見る事ができなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
A face like what? Did I really look that terrible?
“I’ll ask when you’re feeling better, Brother. A full night’s sleep should put some color back in your face.”
“—” Awkwardly, I turned my eyes away from her.
I was grateful that she would wait until I recovered—but
morning wouldn’t make any of this easier to tell.
In the end, I could tell Akiha nothing.
The guilt kept me from meeting her eyes.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……"
Look like that---is my expression that bad right now?
"I'll listen when you have recovered, Nii-san.
If you rest overnight, your health should improve."
"------"
Feeling awkward, I look away from Akiha.
…… I'm glad she won't listen to me until I'm better, but I feel like I won't be able to talk about it even in the morning.
In the end, I can't tell Akiha anything.
I feel too guilty to even look at her face.

entries.japanese:
「……秋葉、俺は―――」
「ああもうっ、いつまでもそんな顔をしないでくださいっ！
　今日だけは特別に許してさしあげますから、部屋に戻って休んだらどうですか？
　どうせ私には話せない事情なんでしょうから！」
　話したがらないこっちの気持ちを読み取ったのか、不機嫌そうに秋葉はロビーへと歩いていく。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Akiha, I—”
“Oh, enough! Stop making that face. I’m granting you a special pardon for tonight, so why don’t you go to your room and rest? Whatever happened, you clearly can’t tell me!”
Perhaps she had read my reluctance. Looking displeased, Akiha strode toward the lobby.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Akiha, I---"
"Ohh, please don't keep making that face!
I told you, I'll make an exception today, so go back to your room and rest, alright?
I bet it's something you can't talk to me about anyway!"
Having read my expression perfectly, Akiha turns and goes out to the lobby.

entries.japanese:
俺はソファーに座ったまま、秋葉の後ろ姿を見送るしかできない。
　ふと、思った。
　秋葉がすぐロビーにやってきたのは、帰ってこない俺をずっと待っていたからなんだろうか、なんて都合のいいことを。
entries.maoEnglish:
I could only remain on the sofa and watch her go.
A thought occurred to me—an embarrassingly convenient one.
Had Akiha come to the lobby so quickly because she had been waiting all night for me to return?
entries.mirrorMoon:
I can only sit on the sofa and watch her leave.
Suddenly, I wonder.
Was Akiha waiting for my return?
Is that how she appeared in the lobby so quickly?

entries.japanese:
「―――秋葉」
「なんですか、兄さん」
「……手当て、ありがとうな。
心配かけさせて、すまない」
「え―――――」
　ぴたり、と秋葉の足が止まる。
―――と思ったら、秋葉はすぐにふい、と顔を背けてしまった。
「わ、私は兄さんの心配なんてしてませんっ。
そんなお世辞を言う余裕があるんでしたら、ご自分の体を大切にしてくださいっ」
　バタン、と乱暴にドアが閉められた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Akiha.”
“What is it, Brother?”
“Thank you for treating me. And I’m sorry I made you worry.”
“What—” Akiha
stopped dead.
―――Then, almost immediately, she looked away.
“I-I was not worried about you, Brother! If you have enough strength left for flattery, use it to take better care of yourself!”
The door slammed shut with unnecessary force.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Akiha."
"What is it, Nii-san?"
"…… Thank you for treating me.
I'm sorry for making you worry."
"Eh----"
Suddenly, Akiha stops walking.
---And then she turns away.
"I… I wasn't worried about you, Nii-san.
If you've that much energy for flattery, you should concentrate on taking care of yourself!"
With a crash, she slams the door behind her.

entries.japanese:
「―――よくわからないヤツだな、あいつも」
　それでも、秋葉なりに俺のことを心配してくれているのは分かる。
「……危ない事はしていない、か」
　秋葉は俺の事を信じているから、そんなことはしていないでしょう、と断言した。
　だっていうのに、俺はあんなに危険な場面にでくわしてしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“She’s impossible to understand too.”
Even so, I knew that in her own way Akiha had been worried about me.
“She said I wouldn’t do anything dangerous…”
Because she trusted me, she had declared that as a certainty.
Yet I had stumbled into danger all the same.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---I really don't understand her."
But, I do understand that she was worried about me.
"…… Seems like I wasn't doing something too dangerous, huh?"
Akiha seems to believe me since she said that.
But really, it was a frighteningly dangerous scene.

entries.japanese:
路地裏に散乱した死体。
　両手を血に染めた、弓塚の姿。
「――――――く」
　思い出すだけで寒気が走る。
　傷口を庇うように立ちあがって、部屋に戻ることにした。
entries.maoEnglish:
The bodies scattered through the alley.
Yumizuka standing there, both hands drenched in blood.
“—Ngh.”
The memory alone sent a chill through me.
Careful not to jar my injured shoulder, I got up and went to my room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The bodies scattered in the back alley.
The figure of Yumizuka, her hands stained red with blood.
"---Guh."
A chill runs through me just at the memory.
I stand up, taking care of my wound, and return to my room.

entries.japanese:
着替えて、ベッドに倒れこんだ。
　まぶたを閉じると路地裏での光景が浮かんでくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
I changed and collapsed onto the bed.
The moment I closed my eyes, the alley returned.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I change clothes, and fall onto the bed.
But if I close my eyes, I'll see the scene in the back alley.

entries.japanese: ―――わたしが、その人たちを殺したんだよ。
entries.maoEnglish: ―――I killed those people.
entries.mirrorMoon: ---I killed all those people.

entries.japanese: なんでもない事のように、弓塚はそう言った。
entries.maoEnglish: Yumizuka had said it as though it were nothing at all.
entries.mirrorMoon: Yumizuka said so, as if it was nothing.

entries.japanese: ―――その人たちの血が必要だったから。
entries.maoEnglish: ―――Because I needed their blood.
entries.mirrorMoon: ---I needed their blood.

entries.japanese:
だから殺したって。
　まるで吸血鬼みたいな、たちの悪い、冗談。
entries.maoEnglish:
That was why she killed them.
A vicious joke, as if she were some vampire.
entries.mirrorMoon:
So, she killed them.
Just like a vampire.
Like… a bad joke.

entries.japanese:
―――待ってて。
一人前の吸血鬼になって―――
entries.maoEnglish: ―――Wait for me. Once I’m a full-fledged vampire—
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Wait, okay?
I'll go become a great vampire---

entries.japanese:
……よく、思い出せない。
　弓塚は最後になんて言ったんだっけ。
「ふ…………ぁ」
　眠気が体に浸透してきた。
　弓塚の顔が脳裏から離れないまま、ゆっくりとまぶたを閉じた。
entries.maoEnglish:
I couldn’t remember clearly.
What had Yumizuka said at the very end?
“Haa…”
Drowsiness seeped through my body.
With Yumizuka’s face still fixed in my mind, I slowly closed my eyes.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… I don't remember.
What did Yumizuka say at the end.
"Huh…"
Sleepiness fills my body.
With Yumizuka's face still etched in my mind, I close my eyes slowly.

entries.japanese:
……確かな事は、ただ一つだけ。
　弓塚の言っていた事は全部本当で、路地裏の死体は彼女が殺してしまった人間たちということ。
　だっていうのに。
　俺はそんな寒気がする事実を恐怖するより、彼女がもらしたたった一言のほうに気を取られてしまっている。
entries.maoEnglish:
There was only one thing I knew for certain.
Everything Yumizuka had said was true, and the bodies in that alley belonged to people she had killed.
And yet, instead of recoiling from that chilling truth,
my thoughts kept fastening on a single thing she had said.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Only one thing is clear.
That Yumizuka told the truth, and she really did slaughter all those people.
But even then.
Instead of fearing everything that happened, I'm more concerned about the one thing she said.

entries.japanese: ―――痛い……すごく痛いよ、志貴くん―――
entries.maoEnglish: ―――It hurts… It hurts so much, Shiki—
entries.mirrorMoon:
---It hurts.
It really hurts, Tohno-kun---

entries.japanese:
……どうかしている。
　弓塚は人殺しなのに、彼女のその言葉が、どうしても頭から離れてくれないなんて―――
entries.maoEnglish:
Something was wrong with me.
Yumizuka was a murderer, yet I could not drive those words from my mind—
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… There's something wrong with me.
Yumizuka is really a murderer, but those words will not leave my mind---

entries.japanese:
――――自分の錯覚を、無視できない。
　もう何人も殺人を犯している通り魔が徘徊しているっていう夜の街で、怪しい物音がした路地裏に行こうだなんてどうかしてる。
　どうかしてるけど、俺は――――昨日の弓塚の笑顔が忘れられない。
　弓塚がいるはずなんてないけど。
　もしそこに弓塚がいて、なにか取り返しのつかないコトになっていたのなら。
　……俺は、それを見逃したコトを絶対に後悔する。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――I couldn’t ignore it, even if it was only my imagination.
Going into a suspicious alley at night, with a killer roaming the city after already claiming several victims, was insane.
Even so, I couldn’t forget Yumizuka’s smile from yesterday.
There was no reason for her to be there.
But if she was, and something irreversible had happened to her…
I would never forgive myself for walking away.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----I can't ignore my feelings.
With a killer skulking around town at night looking for victims, I shouldn't be investigating suspicious sounds in alleyways.
