But… I still remember Yumizuka's smiling face from yesterday.

There's no reason for Yumizuka to be there.
But if she is, she might need my help.
…… I'll never forgive myself if I just ignore this.

entries.japanese:
「――――よし」
　大きく息を吸って、気を引き締めた。
　なに、いざとなれば遠野志貴にはこの『眼』があるんだ。
　先生は無闇に使うなって言ってたけど、相手が殺人鬼なら許してくれるだろう。
「……音、こっちからだったな」
　覚悟をきめて、路地裏へ足を運んだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“All right.”
I drew a deep breath and gathered my nerve.
If the worst happened, Shiki Tohno still had these eyes.
My teacher had warned me never to use them carelessly, but surely a murderer would be an exception.
“…The sound came from this way.”
Bracing myself, I entered the alley.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----Alright."
Taking a deep breath, I steel my spirit.
Besides, if it comes to it, I have my "eyes" too.
Sensei said not to use them recklessly, but she'll find it acceptable if I use it against a killer.
"…… The sound… it came from here…"
Preparing myself, I step into the alley.

entries.japanese:
―――どくん。
　心臓が、ひときわ大きく脈をうつ。
　路地裏は静かだ。
　……物音は、この奥の広場から聞こえてきた。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Thump.
My heart gave one enormous beat.
The alley was silent.
The sound had come from an open space farther in.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Thump.
My heart pounds.
The back alley is quiet.
…… The noise came from the open area at the far end.

entries.japanese:
―――どくん。
　首のうしろが、痛い。
　極度の緊張で痙攣でもしているのか、背骨が皮膚から飛び出しそうなぐらい、痛い。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Thump.
The back of my neck hurt.
Perhaps the tension had made it spasm; the pain felt as though my spine were trying to burst through my skin.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Thump.
The back of my head, hurts.
As if convulsing under the utmost strain, my wracked spine hurts as if it's about to rip itself out of my body.

entries.japanese:
―――どくん。
　どうしてだろう。
　俺は何も考えていないのに、本能がさっきから警告を鳴らしている。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Thump.
Why?
My mind was blank, yet every instinct I possessed had begun to sound an alarm.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Thump.
Why is it?
I can't think, yet my instincts shout at me.

entries.japanese:
―――どく、ん。
　行くな。
　その先には行くな。
　行けば、きっと戻れない。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Thump.
Don’t go.
Don’t go any farther.
If you do, you will never come back.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Thu-mp.
Don't go.
Don't go any further.
If you do, you won't be able to come back.

entries.japanese:
―――どく、ん。
　けど、もう遅い。
　路地裏を抜けて、俺はその広場へと足を踏み入れてしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Thump.
But it was already too late.
I emerged from the alley and stepped into the open space beyond.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Thu-mp.
But it's already too late.
I step out of the back alley, and into the open space.

entries.japanese:
「――――え？」
　ただ、そんな声しか、出せなかった。
―――路地裏は、一面の赤い世界。
　そこかしろかに、ゴミやガレキにまじって手足が散乱している。
　手足は犬や猫のたぐいじゃない。
　その断面から赤い血と、骨と、生々しい肉を見せた、紛れもない人間の手足だった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What…?”
That was the only sound I could make.
―――A world of red spread across the alley.
Arms and legs lay scattered among the rubbish and rubble.
They did not belong to dogs or cats.
Their severed ends exposed red blood, white bone, and wet flesh. They were unmistakably human.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----Eh?"
That weak voice is all that I can get out.
---The back alley is a single sheet of crimson.
In it, limbs are strewn amongst the garbage and rubble.
Not the limbs of dogs, or cats, or the like.
They are human limbs, blood dripping from fresh meat and bone.

entries.japanese:
地面や壁には赤い血が塗りたくられている。
　鼻孔をつく重い匂い。
　どろり、と。
　赤い霧になって体にまとわりついてきそうなほど、濃厚な血のにおい。
entries.maoEnglish:
Blood had been slathered
across the walls and ground.
A heavy smell assaulted my nose—thick enough to
become a red mist and cling wetly to my body.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The ground and the walls are painted with red blood.
A heavy scent fills my nostrils.
Thick.
Like a red fog permeating my body, the choking smell of blood.

entries.japanese:
顔。
顔。
顔。
　首元から断ち切られ、苦悶の表情のまま転がった顔。
　木乃伊のように干からびて、真っ二つに割れてカラカラと転がっている顔。
　両目を刳り抜かれて、男とも女ともとれないぐらい正体不明のまま放置された顔。
「―――――」
　声も出せず、ただ、ソレらの亡骸を傍観した。
　いや、人の死体というにはあまりにも遠すぎる。
　出来の悪いオブジェにしたって、もうすこしはマシだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
Faces. Faces. Faces.
A face severed at the neck, lying where it fell with its agony intact.
A face shriveled like a mummy, split in half and rattling dryly over the ground.
A face with both eyes gouged out, abandoned beyond all recognition of whether it had belonged to a man or woman.
“……”
Unable to speak, I could only stare at those remains.
No—they were too far removed from humanity to call corpses. Even a shoddy art installation would have looked better than this.
entries.mirrorMoon:
A face.
A face.
A face.
A face on a severed head, rolling around with an expression of agony.
A face shriveled up like a mummy, split in halves.
A face with both eyes gouged out, so distorted I can't even tell if it used to be a man or a woman.
"-----"
Unable to make a sound, I merely gaze speechless at the corpses.
No, they can't even be called human bodies anymore.
Even a badly made sculpture looks better than this.

entries.japanese:
死体は、四つあった。
　どれもこれも食い散らかされた残飯みたいに転がっている。
「は―――――は」
　愕然と死体の海を見つめる。
　首のうしろがズキズキと痛んで、
　喉が乾いて呼吸が火のように熱い。
　指先はガクガクと震えていて、口元がいびつな形にゆがんでしまう。
entries.maoEnglish:
There were four bodies.
Every one lay discarded like the scraps of some devoured meal.
“Hah… hah…”
I stared, stunned, across the sea of corpses.
The back of my neck pulsed with pain.
My throat was dry, every breath hot as fire.
My fingertips trembled, and my mouth pulled itself into a crooked shape.
entries.mirrorMoon:
There are four bodies.
They roll around like scraps of leftover food.
"Ah----ah."
I gape in shock at the sea of bodies.
The back of my head throbs,
my throat is parched, and my breath burns like fire.
My fingertips quiver, and my mouth distorts.

entries.japanese:
これは―――何だ。
　いま目の前に広がっている世界は、なんだ。
「――――赤い」
　そう。
　目が醒めるぐらいに、攻撃的な一面の色――――
　ただ、呆と立ち尽くす。
　どうかしている、と思った。
　どくん。
どくん。
どくん。
　こんな、ワケのワカラナイ風景を前にして。
　俺の心臓は、どくどくと、何かを期待するように、高鳴ってしまっている、なんて。
entries.maoEnglish:
What was this?
What was this world spread before me?
“…Red.”
Yes.
A single, aggressive color vivid enough to shock me awake—
I stood there, vacant.
Something is wrong with me, I thought.
Thump. Thump. Thump.
Confronted with this incomprehensible scene,
my heart was pounding as if in anticipation.
entries.mirrorMoon:
What---is this?
What is this world before my eyes?
"----Red."
Yes.
Before my eyes, everything is that terrible color---
But I merely stand.
I think I may be going crazy.
Thump.
Thump.
Thump.
While being faced with a totally bizarre, alien landscape like this,
my heart screams shrilly in anticipation.

entries.japanese:
がさり、と壁際の死体が動いた。
　いや、違う。
　そこにいるのは死体じゃない。
　無造作に転がっている手足とは違う。
　きちんと手足がある、れっきとした生きている人間のようだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
Something rustled among the bodies by the wall.
No—that wasn’t a corpse.
Unlike the discarded limbs around it,
this figure still had arms and legs.
It seemed to be a complete, living human being.
entries.mirrorMoon:
A corpse against the wall moves.
No, that's wrong.
It's not a corpse.
It's not like the scrapped hands and feet.
It's a living human being, with limbs attached.

entries.japanese:
「あ……」
　なにか、意外なものを見た。
　人が生きていたという事を喜ぶより、この光景の中でまだ生きている人間がいる事が、なんだか不自然な気がして。
　けど、生きているのなら。
　生きているんなら、助けて、あげないと。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ah…”
I had found something unexpected.
Instead of relief that someone had survived, I felt only that a living person had no place in this scene.
But if they were alive—if they were alive,
I had to help.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah…"
I see something out of place.
In this ghoulish spectacle, the response to seeing someone alive is more of astonishment than happiness.
But, if he's alive.
If he's alive, I have to help him.

entries.japanese:
「あの―――もしもし？」
　どくどくと高鳴った感情のまま、まだ生きている人間のところに歩み寄っていく。
「――――ギ」
　ずるり、と血の海から這い上がって、ソレは俺にむかって顔をあげた。
　その、干からびた、シャレコウベのような顔を。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Um―――hello?”
With that feverish emotion still pounding through me, I approached the survivor.
“—Gih.”
It dragged itself up out of the sea of blood and raised
its face to me—a withered face like a bare skull.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Uh---hello?"
In my rush of emotion, I step towards the living figure.
"---Gih."
Pulling itself up from the sea, it raises its face toward me.
A face like a dried out skull.

entries.japanese:
「ひ―――――！」
　反射的に後ろに逃げる。
　けど、そんな俺の動きなんかより、シャレコウベのほうが何倍も速い。
　ひゅうひゅうという声をあげて、ソイツは俺の上にのしかかってきた。
――ひゅう、ひゅう。
　イヤな声が、目の前で聞こえた。
　見れば―――シャレコウベの喉は大きな穴が開いていて、満足に発音できないらしかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ee—!”
I recoiled on instinct.
It moved many times faster than I did.
Wheezing, it threw itself on top of me.
――Hhhee… hhhee…
The loathsome sound came from inches away.
A great hole gaped in the creature’s throat; apparently it could no longer form proper words.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hii----!"
I leap back reflexively.
But the skull moves faster than I do.
With a voice like "hyuuhyuu!", he jumps on me.
----Hyuu!
Hyuu!
A hideous voice, right next to me.
Looking down---there is a large hole in the skull's throat, preventing him from speaking right.

entries.japanese:
「――――あ」
　干からびた顔、干からびた腕がのしかかってくる。
　骨と皮しか残っていない喉の声帯が、ぶるぶると不気味な声にあわせて振動している。
「うわあああああ！」
　ただ、必死になってソイツを引き剥がそうとした。
だがソイツは不気味な声をあげて離れようとしない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ah—” Its shriveled face and arms bore down on me.
The vocal cords in its skin-and-bone
throat trembled with each horrible sound.
“Aaaaaah!”
I fought desperately to tear it off, but it only wheezed and clung tighter.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----Ah!"
The dried up face, the dried up arm reaching for me.
In the throat of this bag of bones, vocal chords vibrate in accord with the ghastly voice.
"Uwaaaahhhhh!"
Desperately, I try to tear him off me.
But he merely raises that ghastly voice, and will not get off.

entries.japanese:
カカ、と音をたててシャレコウベの口が開く。
　肩を一口で噛み砕けるぐらいに開いた口が、死にたくない、と助けを請うように、俺の顔へと近寄ってくる。
「や――――」
　やめろ、という声も通じない。
　骨と皮だけのソイツは、そのまま俺の頭にかじりつこうとして――――そのまま、唐突に、崩れ落ちた。
entries.maoEnglish:
Its jaws clacked open, wide enough to crush my shoulder in one bite.
That mouth came toward my face as if pleading for help—as if begging not to die.
“St—” My attempt to say stop meant nothing to it.
The thing of bone and skin lunged to bite into my skull—and then,
without warning, collapsed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
With a creak, the skull's jaw opens.
The mouth opens wide enough to rip off my shoulder with a single bite, and he approaches my face as if saying, "I don't want to die, somebody save me".
"St----"
I can't even say "stop".
The guy made only of skin and bones, tries to bite my head---and suddenly, he collapses.

entries.japanese:
「え……？」
　あんなに強かった力が消えていく。
　かろうじて骨と皮だけが残っていたソイツは、残された骨と皮さえも無くして、跡形もなく消え去っていく。
　さらさらと。
　悪い夢みたいに、ソレは灰になって散っていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Huh…?”
Its terrible strength ebbed away.
The thing had barely retained a human shape in bone and skin;
now even those remnants vanished, leaving nothing behind.
Softly, grain by grain, it crumbled into ash and scattered like a bad dream.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Eh……?"
The awesome power vanishes.
The bag of bones in a person's form crumples to the ground and disappears.
Softly,
like a bad dream, it turns to ash and blows away.

entries.japanese:
「………なんだよ、これ」
　ずきりと、肩から痛みが走る。
「あ………つ」
　掴まれていた両肩が、赤く腫れ上がっている。
　痛みは現実。
だからこれは、紛れもない現実。
　ひどい、悪夢だ。
　こんなコト―――悪い夢でしかないのに、夢ですら、ないなんて。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What the hell was that…?”
Pain stabbed through my shoulders.
“Ah…!”
Where it had gripped me, both shoulders were swollen red.
Pain was real. So this was unmistakably real too.
A hideous nightmare.
Something that could only be a bad dream—and yet was not even a dream.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… What the hell is this?"
A pain runs through my shoulder.
"Ach…"
My shoulders begin to turn red and swell where he has grasped me.
The pain is real.
So this must be real.
A terrible nightmare.
But---it can't be a nightmare, because it's not a dream.

entries.japanese:
「遠野くん。
それ以上そこにいると危ないよ」
「――――！」
　背後からの声に振りかえる。
　入ってきた路地裏の入り口に、弓塚さつきが立っていた。
「弓塚、さん―――？」
「こんばんは。
こんなところで会うなんて、奇遇だね」
　まるで、街中で偶然であったように、気軽に弓塚は語りかけてきた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Tohno. It’s dangerous to stay there.”
“—!”
I spun toward the voice behind me.
Satsuki Yumizuka stood at the mouth of the alley.
“Yumizuka…?”
“Good evening. Fancy meeting you somewhere like this.”
She spoke as casually as if we had bumped into each other downtown.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Tohno-kun.
It'll be dangerous if you stay there."
"----!"
I turn towards the voice behind me.
At the mouth of the alley where I came from, I see Yumizuka Satsuki.
"Yumizuka… san---?"
"Good evening.
Fancy meeting you in a place like this, huh?"
As if we had merely bumped into each other in the mall, Yumizuka greets me lightheartedly.

entries.japanese:
「弓塚さんこそ……こんな時間に、何してるんだよ」
「わたしはただの散歩。
でも、遠野くんこそ何をしてるの？
　そんなにいっぱいの人を殺しちゃうなんて、いけないんじゃないかな」
　ふふ、と淡い笑顔で弓塚は言った。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What are you doing out this late, Yumizuka?”
“Just taking a walk. But what are you doing, Tohno? Killing so many people is awfully naughty, don’t you think?”
She said it with a soft little smile.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yumizuka-san, what about you… what are you doing, out at a time like this?"
"Oh, just going for a walk.
But what's Tohno-kun doing?
Killing so many people like this is bad, right?"
Yumizuka says, with a light smile.

entries.japanese:
「人を殺したって―――え？」
　周囲を見渡す。
　……それで、自分がどんな惨状の中で立ち尽くしているのかを思い出した。
　一面の血の海の中。
　遠野志貴は、まるで殺人鬼のように、呆然と立ち尽くしている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Killing people—what?”
I looked around and remembered what
sort of horror I was standing in.
In the middle of that ocean of blood,
Shiki Tohno stood frozen like the murderer himself.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Killing so many people… eh?"
I look around me.
…… And I remember the tragic scene I'm surrounded by.
In a sea of blood.
Tohno Shiki stands aghast like a murderer.

entries.japanese:
「ち、違う、これは俺じゃない……！」
「違うことはないでしょう。
みんな死んでいて生きてるのは遠野くんだけなら、誰だってやったのは遠野くんだって思うわ」
「そ、そんなワケないだろう……！
　俺だってコイツに襲われかけたんだぞ……！」
　さっきまで自分を襲っていた怪物を指差す。
　けど、そこにはもう何もない。
　アレは骨はおろか、灰さえものこさずに風に散って消えていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“N-no, I didn’t do this!”
“But how could it be anyone else? Everyone is dead, and you’re the only one alive. Anyone would think you killed them.”
“Th-that’s ridiculous! That thing attacked me too!”
I pointed to the creature that had been on top of me.
Nothing was there.
Not even ash remained; it had scattered on the wind and disappeared.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"N… no!
This wasn't me!"
"Oh, of course it was.
Everyone's dead, and Tohno-kun's alive, so obviously Tohno-kun must have killed them."
"No way!
It just attacked me……!"
I point at the monster that attacked me moments ago.
But, nothing's there.
Even the ashes of the bones have been blown away by the wind.

entries.japanese:
「あ――――」
　息を飲む。
　弓塚はくすくすと笑っている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ah—” My
breath caught.
Yumizuka was giggling.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah----"
I swallow my breath.
Yumizuka is chuckling.

entries.japanese:
「ち、ちがう―――俺じゃ、俺じゃない、んだ」
　あたまがマヒして、そんな言葉しか言えない。
　……わかってる。
　ちゃんと何がおかしくて何がおかしくないのかわかっているんだけど、思考が空回りして喋れない。
　例えば、弓塚がどうしてこんなところにいるのか。
　例えば、こんな惨状を目の前にして、どうして弓塚はそんなふうに笑ってられるのか、とか。
entries.maoEnglish:
“N-no—I didn’t. It wasn’t me.”
My mind was numb; that was all I could say.
I knew.
I could tell perfectly well what made sense and what did not, but my thoughts spun uselessly and left me unable to speak.
For instance: why was Yumizuka here?
And how could she smile like that with this carnage before her?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"It's not… this wasn't… wasn't me…"
My head is paralyzed, and can only manage broken language.
…… I understand.
I can think clearly, but I can't put my thought into words.
For example, why is Yumizuka at a place like this?
For example, why is Yumizuka laughing in the face of this tragic scene?

entries.japanese:
「弓塚さん、俺は―――」
「うん、ほんとはわかってるんだ。
遠野くんは食事中に出くわしただけなんだって。
　いじわるなこと言ってごめんね。
わたし、いつも自分の気持ちと反対のことをしちゃうから、遠野くんにはこんなふうにしてばっかり」
　弓塚はまだ笑っている。
　……それがこの惨状にあまりに不釣り合いで、ぞくりとした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Yumizuka, I—” “I know the truth.
You only stumbled across me while I was eating, didn’t you?
I’m sorry I teased you. I always do the opposite of what I really feel. Somehow, I’m always like that with you.”
Yumizuka was still smiling.
…The smile was so grotesquely out of place that a chill ran through me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yumizuka-san, I---"
"Yeah, I know.
You just interrupted someone's meal.
I'm sorry for sounding mean.
I always act against my feelings, so I'm always acting like this to you."
Yumizuka is still laughing.
…… It's so inappropriate for this scene, I feel a chill.

entries.japanese:
弓塚は路地裏の入り口から動かない。
　不自然に組まれた両腕。
まるで、何かを隠すように後ろに組んでいる。
―――注意して見れば。
　彼女の肘のあたりには赤々としたモノが、まだら模様をつくっていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
Yumizuka remained at the entrance.
Her arms were held in an unnatural pose behind her back, as if she were hiding something.
―――When I looked closely,
vivid red stains mottled the skin around her elbows.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Yumizuka doesn't move from the entrance of the alley.
Her arms are positioned strangely, as if she's hiding something behind her back.
---And, looking closer,
there are spots of something red on her sleeve.

entries.japanese:
「弓塚、おまえ――――」
「どうしたの？
　恐い顔して、ヘンな遠野くん」
　また、クスリと笑う。
「――――――」
　……違う。
　彼女は、弓塚さつきなんかじゃ、ない。
「弓塚――なんでおまえ、手を隠してるんだ」
「あ、やっぱりバレちゃった？
　遠野くんってば抜けているようで鋭いんだよね。
　わたしね、あなたのそうゆう所が昔っからいいなあって思ってたんだ、志貴くん」
　強調するように、俺の名前を口にして。
　弓塚さつきは、その両手を前に出した。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Yumizuka, you—” “What’s wrong?
You look so frightening, Tohno.”
She giggled again.
“—” …No.
This couldn’t be Satsuki Yumizuka.
“Yumizuka—why are you hiding your hands?”
“Oh, you noticed?
You act absentminded, but you’re surprisingly sharp.
That’s something I’ve always liked about you, Shiki.”
She placed deliberate emphasis on my name,
then brought both hands out in front of her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yumizuka, you---"
"What is it?
Your face looks scary, Tohno-kun."
She laughs again.
"------"
…… No.
Somehow, this girl cannot be Yumizuka Satsuki.
"Yumizuka---why are you hiding your hands like that?"
"Ah, have I been found out?
I guess you're too observant to miss that, huh.
I've always liked that about you, Shiki-kun."
After emphasizing my name,
she brings her hands out.

entries.japanese:
真っ赤に染まった両手。
　血は乾ききっておらず、ぴちゃぴちゃと音をたてて赤い雫をこぼしている。
　それを、誇るように。
　弓塚さつきは、口元に笑みをうかべていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
They were stained scarlet.
The blood had not yet dried;
red drops pattered wetly from her fingers.
Satsuki Yumizuka smiled as though she were proud to display them.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Both hands are dyed crimson.
Not yet dry, the blood drips off them in red droplets.
And, proudly,
Yumizuka Satsuki is smiling.

entries.japanese:
「弓塚、その手―――」
「うん。
わたしが、その人たちを殺したの」
「な――――」
「あ、でもこれは悪いことじゃないんだよ。
わたしはこの人たちが憎くて殺したんじゃないもの。
生きていくためにはこの人たちの血が必要だから、仕方なく殺したんだから」
　当たり前のように、彼女は言った。
　そんな事、俺にはもちろん理解できない。
　わかるのは、ただ―――この全身に、ゾクゾクと血が溜まっていく事だけだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Yumizuka, your hands—”
“Yes. I killed those people.”
“Wha—” “But it wasn’t wrong.
I didn’t kill them because I hated them. I needed their blood to stay alive, so I had no choice.”
She said it as if it were self-evident.
Of course I could not understand.
All I knew was the tingling pressure of blood gathering throughout my body.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yumizuka, your hands---"
"Yeah.
I killed those people."
"Wha---"
"Oh, but, it's okay.
I didn't kill them because I hated them.
I just needed their blood to live, so I had to kill them."
She says it as if it was normal.
Of course I can't understand it.
All I do understand is---my blood is pulsing wildly throughout my whole body.

entries.japanese:
どくん。
どくん。
どくん。
　はあ。
はあ。
はあ。
　まるで、血に染まった弓塚に一目惚れでもしてしまったみたいに、興奮、してる―――
entries.maoEnglish:
Thump. Thump. Thump.
Hah. Hah. Hah.
I was aroused—as if I had fallen in love at first sight with Yumizuka drenched in blood—
entries.mirrorMoon:
Thump.
Thump.
Thump.
*pant*.
*pant*.
*pant*.
Like I've fallen in love at first sight with that bloody Yumizuka, I am excited---

entries.japanese:
「殺したって―――ホントなのか、弓塚」
「嘘だって言っても信じてくれないでしょ？
　それともわたしみたいな女の子じゃこんなコトできないって思ってくれる？」
　クスクス、という笑い声。
―――信じられない。
　信じられないけど、間違いなく彼女は嘘なんてついていない。
　この惨状は。
　みんな、弓塚が起こしたものだ。

「どうして―――こんな、酷い事を」
「ひどくなんかないよ。
さっきも言ったでしょう、わたしはこの人たちが憎くて殺したんじゃないもの。
志貴くん、生きるために他の生き物を殺すことはね、悪いことじゃないんだよ」
「なにを―――！
　どんな理由があったって、人殺しは悪いことだろ！」
「そんなコトないけどね。
あ、でも悪いことも一つだけしちゃったみたい。
　わたし、今日が初めてだから加減ができなくて、血を吸う時に自分の血も送っちゃったの。
そのせいで逝き残ったのが出てきて、志貴くんが襲われる事になったわ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You killed them—really, Yumizuka?”
“You wouldn’t believe me if I said no, would you? Or do you think a girl like me couldn’t possibly do something like this?”
Her soft laughter answered me.
―――I couldn’t believe it.
I couldn’t believe it,
and yet there was no question that she was telling the truth.
All this carnage—Yumizuka had done it.
“Why would you do something this horrible?”
“It isn’t horrible. I told you, I didn’t kill them because I hated them. Shiki, there’s nothing wrong with killing other creatures so you can live.” “What are you talking about?
Murder is wrong no matter what reason you have!” “I don’t think so.
Oh—but I suppose I did do one bad thing. It was my first time, so I couldn’t control myself.
When I drank their blood, some of mine went back into them. One of them lingered on without changing all the way, and that’s why it attacked you.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"You… really killed them, Yumizuka?"
"You wouldn't believe me even if I told you it's a lie, right?
Or do you think it's impossible for a girl like me to do such a thing?"
Her voice laughs softly.
---I don't believe her.
I don't believe her, but she is definitely not telling a lie.
This tragic scene.
It's all Yumizuka's doing.
"Why… such a terrible thing…?"
"It's not terrible.
Like I said, I didn't kill them because I hated them.
There's nothing wrong with killing others in order to live, is there, Shiki-kun?"
"What…!
That's absurd!
Killing is wrong!"
"No, it's not.
But, I did do one bad thing.
Since today was my first time drinking blood, I let a little of my blood get back into them.
Because of that, you got attacked, Shiki-kun.

entries.japanese:
「ごめんなさい。
わたし、あやうく志貴くんを巻き込むところだった。
ソイツが成りきれないで死んでくれて、本当によかった」
「なにを―――なにを言ってるんだ、弓塚」
「今はわからなくていいよ。
わたしもまだ自分自身のことを把握しきれてないから、うまく説明できないわ。
　けど、何日かすればきっと志貴くんみたいになれると思う。
　志貴くんみたいな、立派な殺人鬼に――――」
　言いかけて、弓塚は顔を歪ませて苦しみだした。
「はっ―――あ、う…………！！」
　苦しげに喉をかきむしって。
　弓塚は、ごぶりと、口から血を吐き出した。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’m sorry. I almost got you caught up in this. I’m so glad that thing died before it could finish changing.”
“What—what are you talking about, Yumizuka?”
“You don’t have to understand yet. I still don’t entirely understand what’s happened to me, so I can’t explain it very well.
But give me a few days and I’m sure I’ll become like you.
Someone like you—a proper murderer—”
Before she could finish, Yumizuka’s face twisted in agony.
“Hah—ah…
ngh…!”
She clawed desperately at her throat, then vomited a thick gush of blood.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I'm sorry for getting you involved.
But we're lucky; it died without being able to finish changing."
"What---what are you talking about, Yumizuka?"
"It's okay if you don't understand right now.
I don't really understand myself yet, so I can't explain it very well.
"But, I think after a few days I can become like Shiki-kun.
Like Shiki-kun, become a great---"
As she said so, her face distorts in pain.
"Ha---… aaau!!!"
Rasps of agony echo from her throat.
Yumizuka chokes up blood.

entries.japanese:
「いた――――い。
やっぱり、お腹が減ったからって無闇に吸ってもダメみたい。
　質のいい、キレイな血じゃないと、体に合わないのかな―――」
　コホコホとせき込む。
　その咳は赤く、あきらかに血を吐いていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“It hurts.
I guess I can’t just drink from anyone because I’m hungry.
Maybe my body will only accept good, clean blood—” She coughed and coughed,
bringing up unmistakable blood each time.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"It---hurts.
I guess, even if I'm hungry, I shouldn't just drink blood at random.
If it's not good quality, beautiful blood, it won't agree with me…"
She breaks out in a fit of coughing.
She chokes out blood with every cough.

entries.japanese:
「ん――――く、んああ…………！！！」
　弓塚の体がガクガクと震えている。
　……よくわからない。
　もう、何もかもよくわからないけど、ただ、弓塚がひどく苦しんでいるという事だけは、はっきりとした事実だった。
「苦しいのか、弓塚……！？」
　思わず弓塚に駆けよって、その手を取ろうとする。
「――――だめ！
　近寄らないで、志貴くん！」
　けど、それは弓塚の声で止められた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Nn—gh, aaah…!”
Her whole body convulsed.
I didn’t understand.
I understood nothing anymore. But one fact was undeniable: Yumizuka was in terrible pain.
“Are you hurting, Yumizuka?”
Without thinking, I rushed toward her and reached for her hand.
“—No! Stay away from me, Shiki!”
Her cry stopped me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Nn---kuh, nnaaah…!!!"
Yumizuka's body convulses.
…… I don't really understand.
All I know is, Yumizuka's in terrible pain.
That's all I can clearly understand.
"Are you okay, Yumizuka…!?"
Without thinking, I run towards her to take her hand.
"----No!
Don't come any closer, Shiki-kun!"
But, Yumizuka's voice stops me.

entries.japanese:
「……ダメ、だよ、全然大丈夫じゃないよ、志貴くん」
　はあはあと。
　苦しげな呼吸が、赤い血を吐いて、届いてくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“No… don’t.
I’m not all right at all, Shiki.”
Her labored breaths reached me in wet, bloody gasps.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… You mustn't.
I'm not… entirely okay, Shiki-kun."
She speaks painfully, still vomiting red blood.

entries.japanese:
「弓……塚、おまえ―――」
　俺には、わからない。
　弓塚が苦しんでいる理由も、どうして、彼女がそんなふうになってしまっているのかも。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Yumi…zuka,
what—” I didn’t understand why she was suffering,
or how she had become like this.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yumi… zuka, you---"
I don't understand.
Why Yumizuka's in pain, or why she's like this.

entries.japanese:
「……どうしたんだよいったい。
人を殺したって言ってたけど、そんなの嘘だろ……？
　弓塚、そんなに苦しいんならすぐに病院に行かないとだめじゃないか」
　……わかっている。
　弓塚が本当にこの惨状を作ったんだってわかっていたけど、そんな、つまらない嘘を口にした。
「ほら、弓塚―――そっちに行くけど、いいな？」
　優しく話しかける。
　けど弓塚はブンブンと頭をふって、さっきより激しく俺を拒絶した。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What happened to you? You said you killed those people, but that was a lie, wasn’t it?
Yumizuka, if you’re hurting this badly, you need a hospital right now.”
I knew.
I knew perfectly well that she had created this slaughter, yet I offered her that paltry lie.
“Come on, Yumizuka—I’m coming over there, all right?”
I kept my voice gentle, but she shook her head wildly, rejecting me even more fiercely than before.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"What the hell is going on?
You said you killed those people, but that's a lie, right, Yumizuka…?
If you're in that much pain, shouldn't you be in a hospital?"
…… I know.
Even though I understand Yumizuka brought about this tragic scene, I still lie to myself.
"Hey, Yumizuka---I'm coming over there, okay?"
I speak gently.
But Yumizuka shakes her head in violent refusal.

entries.japanese:
「どうして―――苦しいんなら、すぐに病院に行かないとダメだろう……！」
「……ダメなのは志貴くんのほうだよ。
ほんとに、いつもいつも、わかってくれないん、だから」
「ばか―――それを言ったら、さっきから何一つだってわからないよ、俺は！」
「あ……は、そっか、そうだよね……それでも、わたしに付き合ってくれてるんだ―――」
　よろり、と。
　逃げるように、弓塚の体が後ろに引いていく。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Why? If you’re in pain, you need to get to a hospital!”
“You’re the hopeless one, Shiki. You never understand. You never, ever understand…”
“Idiot—if that’s what you mean, then I haven’t understood one thing you’ve said all night!”
“Ah… ha. That’s true, isn’t it?
And you’re still staying here with me…”
She staggered backward as though trying to escape.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Why!?---If you're in pain, we have to get you to a hospital right away…!"
"Shiki-kun, you're not getting it.
You really never understand anything…"
"Idiot!
I told you before, I don't understand…!"
"Ah… yeah, you did, didn't you.
But you're still here…"
Yumizuka begins to pull away.

entries.japanese:
「……痛いよ、志貴くん」
　ぜいぜいと、呼吸を乱して、赤い血が、吐き出される。
「……痛くて、寒くて、すごく不安なの。
　ほんとは、今すぐにでも志貴くんに助けてほしい」
―――けど、今夜はまだダメなんだ。
　そう言って。
　弓塚は、突然に体を持ちなおした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“It hurts, Shiki.”
Her breath came in ragged wheezes, spilling bright blood.
“It hurts, and I’m cold, and I’m so afraid.
The truth is, I want you to save me right now.”
―――But not tonight. Tonight is still too soon.
With those words,
Yumizuka abruptly mastered herself.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… It hurts, Shiki-kun."
She breathes raggedly, coughing up red blood.
"…… It hurts, it's cold, and I'm scared.
I really want your help right now, Shiki-kun."
---But it's too early.
Saying that,
Yumizuka straightens up again.

entries.japanese:
「―――待っててね、すぐに一人前の吸血鬼になって、志貴くんに会いに行くから！」
「な―――待てよ、弓塚！」
「――――――」
　弓塚の姿はない。
　俺が一歩駆け出す間に、弓塚はとっくに路地裏から走り去ってしまった。
　……そのスピードは人間じみたものではなく、獰猛のケモノのソレだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“—Wait for me. I’ll become a full-fledged vampire soon, and then I’ll come see you, Shiki!”
“W-wait, Yumizuka!”
“—” She was gone.
Before I had taken a single running step,
Yumizuka had already vanished from the alley.
That speed belonged not to a human being, but to a savage beast.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Wait for me, okay?
I'll go become a great vampire, then I'll come back to see you again!"
"Wha---wait up, Yumizuka!"
"------"
Yumizuka is gone.
Even as I start to run, Yumizuka is long gone.
…… Her speed is not that of a human's, but of a wild beast.

entries.japanese:
「―――弓塚、おまえ―――」
　なにが、あったっていうんだ、本当に………！
「ぐ―――！」
　強く掴まれた肩が痛む。
　振りかえれば。
　あれだけ人間の部品が散乱していた路地裏の広場には、赤い血しか残っていない。
　顔も。
臓物も。
手足も。
　さっきのシャレコウベのように、灰になって消えてしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Yumizuka,
what—” What in God’s name had happened to her…?
“Ghh—!”
My bruised shoulders throbbed.
When I looked back, nothing remained in the little alley square but red blood.
The faces, the viscera,
the arms and legs—all had turned to ash and
vanished just as that skull had.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Yumizuka, you---"
What happened to you, really…?
"Gah---!"
My shoulders throb in pain where he grabbed earlier.
When I look back, the open space where all the limbs were scattered only left red blood.
The faces, the organs, the hands and feet.
They all turned to ash, like the skull did before.

entries.japanese:
「――――――あ」
　どくん、と。
　血液が逆流しているかのような、吐き気。
「うそ、だ――――」
　どくん、と。
　今にも射精してしまいそうなぐらいの、興奮。
「こんな、の―――」
　いつまでも。
　眼球に焼き付いて離れない、血の朱色。
「こんなのは、うそだ――――！」
　ぐらりと。
　目に映るものすべてが、歪んで見えた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“—Ah.”
Thump.
Nausea rose through me as if my blood had begun to flow backward.
“No… that’s not…”
Thump.
Arousal so fierce I felt on the verge of climax.
“This can’t…”
The scarlet of blood remained
seared forever across my eyes.
“This is a lie!”
The world lurched,
and everything before me warped out of shape.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------Ah."
Thump.
I feel sick as if I'm going to cough up blood.
"This can't, be----"
Thump.
This excitement, is so intense, I almost ejaculate.
"This---"
For a while,
the crimson color of blood burns in my eyes.
"This can't be real----!"
My world swims before me.
My eyes see nothing but a distorted world.

entries.japanese:
―――気がつくと、屋敷に帰ってきていた。
　動物の帰巣本能というヤツだろうか。
　今にも眩暈で倒れそうだって言うのに、ちゃんと自分の家に戻ってこれるなんて思わなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――When awareness returned, I was back at the mansion.
Animal homing instinct, perhaps.
I was dizzy enough to collapse, yet somehow my body had carried me all the way home.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Before I realize it, I'm back at the mansion.
Just like a pet somehow finding its way home, I guess.
I'm on the verge of collapsing from dizziness; I didn't think I would make it back this far.

entries.japanese:
「………く」
　吐き気。
吐き気がする。
「はっ―――は、あ―――」
　なのに心臓はどくどくと脈打っていて、呼吸さえ、難しかった。
「……早く……休まないと、と……」
　昔っから貧血で何度も倒れている分、自分がもうすぐ倒れるっていう気配がわかる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ngh…” Nausea.
I was going to be sick.
“Hah—hah…”
Yet my heart kept hammering, making even breathing difficult.
“I have to… lie down…”
After fainting from anemia so many times, I knew the signs. I was about to collapse.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……… Ggh."
Vomit.
I'm going to vomit.
"Ah---gha, ah---"
My heart is exploding, I can hardly breathe.
"…… I have to…… hurry and rest……"
Since I've collapsed so many times before from my anemia, I know I'm about to faint.

entries.japanese:
―――休めば。
　ベッドで体を休めてしばらくすれば、こんな吐き気も心臓もおさまって、みんな元通りになる。
　あんな―――あんな出来事も忘れて、何もなかったみたいに、いつも通りの朝が迎えられる。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――If I rested.
If I lay in bed for a while, the nausea and the pounding heart would subside and everything would return to normal.
I could forget that—forget all of it—and wake to an ordinary morning as though nothing had happened.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---If I rest.
If I just rest my body in bed, this nausea, my exploding heart, will all go back to normal.
I---I can forget all about that, as if nothing happened, and wake up to a normal day.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さん？
　お帰りになられたんですか？」
「あ……琥珀、さん」
　西館の廊下から、ひょっこりと琥珀さんが顔を出す。
　……そういえば、一階の西館に琥珀さんの部屋があるんだっけ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki? Is that you?” “Ah…
Kohaku.”
Kohaku peered out from the west-wing corridor.
Her room was on the west side of the first floor, now that I thought of it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-san?
You have returned?"
"Ah…… Kohaku--san."
Kohaku-san emerges from the west hallway.
…… That's right, Kohaku-san's room is in the west hallway on the first floor.

entries.japanese:
「お帰りなさい志貴さん。
それで、お知り合いの方にはお会いになれました？」
「あ―――ああ、一応は、会えた」
　答えて、思い出してしまった。
　散乱した手足。
　顔。
顔。
顔。
顔。
　血にまみれた路地裏。
　両手を真っ赤に染めて、クスクスと笑う弓塚の顔――――
entries.maoEnglish:
“Welcome home, Master Shiki. Did you manage to find your acquaintance?” “Yes… yes, I found her.”
The answer brought everything back.
Scattered limbs. Faces.
Faces.
Faces. Faces.
The blood-soaked alley.
Yumizuka’s giggling face above two scarlet hands—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Welcome back, Shiki-san.
Did you get to meet your friend?"
"Uh---ah, yes, I met her."
I remember as soon as I answer.
The scattered limbs.
Face.
Face.
Face.
Face.
The blood-stained alley.
Yumizuka's laughing face and her bloody hands----

entries.japanese:
「……ごめん。
部屋に戻るから、琥珀さんも、戻ってくれ」
　今は誰とも話したくない。
　琥珀さんを振り払って、階段を昇っていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Sorry. I’m going to my room, so please go back to yours.”
I wanted to speak to no one.
I brushed past Kohaku and climbed the stairs.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Sorry.
I'm going back to my room, so please go back as well, Kohaku-san."
I don't feel like talking with anyone right now.
I leave Kohaku-san behind and go up the stairs.

entries.japanese:
そのままベッドに倒れこんだ。
「は―――――あ」
　胸が大きく上下して、空気を吸いこむ。
「―――――――」
　遠くなっていく意識。
　眩暈がやってくる。
　このまま、たとえ気を失うっていう事でも、今はこのまま眠りたかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
I collapsed straight onto the bed.
“Haaah…”
My chest heaved, dragging in air.
“—” Consciousness receded.
Vertigo closed over me.
Even if it meant passing out,
all I wanted was to sleep.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I collapse on my bed.
"Ah----ah."
My chest rises and falls as I take deep breaths.
"-------"
My mind feels faint.
Dizziness overwhelms me.
Even if it means passing out, I just want to go to sleep right now.

entries.japanese:
―――なのに寝つけない。
　眩暈はしているっていうのに、いつもみたいに意識が薄れてくれない。
　まぶたを閉じると、さっきの路地裏の光景が蘇ってくる。
　どくん、と高鳴る心音。
　それは恐怖ではなく、むしろ―――性的な興奮に近かった。
「なん、で――――」
　それこそ理由はわからない。
　もしかすると恐怖と性欲っていうのは、とても近い位置付けなのか。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――And yet sleep would not come.
My head spun, but consciousness refused to fade as it usually did.
Whenever I closed my eyes, the alley returned. My heart thumped hard.
It was not fear.
If anything, it felt closer to sexual excitement.
“Why…?”
I had no answer to that either.
Perhaps terror and desire lived very near each other.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---So why can't I sleep?
I'm so dizzy right now, but why don't I pass out like always?
If I close my eyes, the vision of that scene in the alley shows up under my eyelids.
My heart throbs violently.
It isn't terror, rather---it's closer to sexual excitement.
"Why----"
I don't understand it at all.
Is there this thin of a line between terror and lust?

entries.japanese:
「え…………？」
　こんな夜更けに、誰だろう。
「志貴さま、起きていらっしゃいますか……？」
　囁くような声は、翡翠のものだった。
　とくん、と。
　翡翠の姿を想像しただけで、胸の高鳴りは少しだけ収まってくれた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Huh…?”
Who could it be at this hour?
“Master Shiki, are you awake?”
The whisper belonged to Hisui.
A gentler beat passed through my chest.
Merely picturing her quiet figure eased the pounding a little.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Eh…………?"
Who can it be at this hour?
"Shiki-sama, are you awake……?"
That whisper is Hisui.
Thump.
Just imagining her form, my heart calms down a bit.

entries.japanese:
「……ああ、起きてるよ。
なにか用があるんなら、中に入って」
「―――失礼します」
　……なんだろう。
　翡翠は盆にコップと薬らしい紙の包みをもって入ってきた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Yes, I’m awake. If you need something, come in.”
“Excuse me.”
What was this?
Hisui entered carrying a tray with a glass and a paper packet that appeared to contain medicine.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Yeah, I'm awake.
Please come in."
"---Please excuse me."
…… What's this?
Hisui enters carrying a tray and something that looks like medicine wrapped in paper.

entries.japanese:
「……翡翠。
どうしたんだよ、こんな時間に」
「はい。
志貴さまがお休みになられないようなのでお薬をお持ちしました」
「え………？
　いや、それはそうなんだけど……よくわかったね、翡翠」
「姉からの言付けです。
志貴さまはお疲れのようなので、気を使ってあげなさい、との事でした」
　……そうか、琥珀さんか。
　さっきロビーで出会った時に、俺の顔色が悪いのをちゃんと見てくれたんだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hisui? What are you doing here so late?”
“I brought you medicine because you did not appear able to sleep, Master Shiki.”
“What…? You’re right, but how did you know?” “My sister asked me to come.
She said Master Shiki seemed exhausted and that I should look after you.”
So it was Kohaku.
She had noticed how pale I was when we met in the lobby.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Hisui.
What are you doing at this hour?"
"Shiki-sama, you seemed to have trouble sleeping so I brought you some medicine."
"Eh………?
Uh, that's right.
…… But how did you know, Hisui?"
"I heard it from my sister.
She told me that you were very tired, so I should give extra care."
…… I see, it was Kohaku-san.
She must have seen how bad my face looked when we met in the lobby.

entries.japanese:
「……で、そのクスリってなに？」
「睡眠導入剤です。
志貴さまの主治医から、服用しても問題はないと許可をいただきました」
「許可って……こんな夜遅くに！？」
「いえ、志貴さまがこの屋敷においでになる聞いて、姉が志貴さまの主治医から許可を頂いたそうです」
「はあ―――さすがは琥珀さん。
気が利くなんてもんじゃないな」
　とにかく、今はありがたい。
　翡翠から水を受け取って、薬を飲む。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What kind of medicine is it?”
“A sleeping aid. Your physician has confirmed that it is safe for you, Master Shiki.”
“Confirmed—at this hour?”
“No; when my sister learned that Master Shiki would be returning to the mansion, she obtained permission from Master Shiki’s physician in advance.”
“Of course she did. Kohaku doesn’t miss a thing.”
Whatever the circumstances, I was grateful now.
I took the water from Hisui and swallowed the medicine.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… And, this medicine is?"
"It is a sleep-inducing medicine.
Your personal physician gave his approval that it could be used for you."
"Approval…… at this hour!?"
"No, my sister asked your personal physician as soon as she found out you were coming here to live in this mansion."
"Wow--Kohaku-san is pretty amazing.
She's pretty thoughtful."
Anyway, I'm very thankful right now.
Taking the water from Hisui, I drink the medicine.

entries.japanese:
「ん―――――あ」
　ほどなくして、とろんとした眠気がやってくる。
「……ありがと、翡翠。
琥珀さんにもお礼を言っておいてくれ」
「かしこまりました。
それではおやすみなさいませ、志貴さま」
　……翡翠の足音が聞こえる。
　体から力が抜けていくような感覚。
「ん―――気持ち、いい―――」
　ぼんやりと。
　気絶するように、眠りへと落ちていける―――
entries.maoEnglish:
“Nn… ah.”
Before long, a warm, liquid drowsiness came over me.
“Thank you, Hisui. Please thank Kohaku for me too.”
“Certainly. Good night, Master Shiki.”
I could hear Hisui’s footsteps.
It felt as though strength were draining from my body.
“Mm…
that feels good…”
Hazy, I sank into sleep as though losing consciousness—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Nn----ah."
I start to feel very sleepy after a while.
"…… Thanks, Hisui.
Please give Kohaku-san my thanks as well."
"As you wish.
Well then, please rest well, Shiki-sama."
…… I can hear Hisui's footsteps.
It feels like all the power is draining from my body.
"Mm---feels, good---"
I space out.
As if I was passing out, I quickly fall asleep---

entries.japanese: ―――それは夢か。
entries.maoEnglish: ―――Was it a dream?
entries.mirrorMoon: ---Is this a dream?

entries.japanese:
赤い路地裏。
　俺が足を踏み入れる前の、路地裏。
　そこで弓塚さつきは殺している。
　大通りで適当な通行人に声をかけて、路地裏につれこんで。
　容赦なく後ろから首をひねって、ぞうきんみたいに捻じ曲がった首筋に、歯をつきたてる。
　一人。
　二人。
　三人。
　四人。
entries.maoEnglish:
The red alley.
The alley before I entered it.
There, Satsuki Yumizuka is killing people.
She approaches random passersby on the main street and leads them into the alley.
Without hesitation, she twists each neck from behind, wringing it like a wet rag, then sinks her teeth into the twisted neck.
One.
Two.
Three.
Four.
entries.mirrorMoon:
A red alley.
The same back alley that I was in before.
Where Yumizuka Satsuki is killing.
Luring appropriate passers-by into that back alley.
Mercilessly killing them from behind by twisting their necks like a damp cloth, then plunging her teeth into them.
One person.
Two people.
Three people.
Four people.

entries.japanese:
#0000ff
　　オレをさしおいて　そんなコトを　よくも
entries.maoEnglish: How dare she do that without me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
#0000ff
How dare she--do those things without me!

entries.japanese:
#ffffff
　ただ夢中に、貪るように血を吸ったあと、弓塚は四つの死体をバラバラにして、まだ血を舐める。
　赤い世界。
　けど、不思議と忌まわしいという感覚はない。
entries.maoEnglish:
After drinking their blood in a mindless frenzy, Yumizuka tears all four bodies apart and keeps licking up the blood.
A red world.
Yet, strangely, I feel no revulsion.
entries.mirrorMoon:
#ffffff
As if in a dream, indulging herself in drinking the blood, Yumizuka tears apart the four dead bodies and continues licking the blood.
A crimson world.
But, I don't feel it is sick, or detest it at all.

#ffffff

　手にはナイフ。
　呼吸ははあはあと荒い。
　心臓はピストンのように、さっきからオレにそうしろとせかしている。
entries.maoEnglish:
Amateur. Amateur. Amateur.
There is a knife in my hand.
My breath comes hard and fast.
My heart pumps like a piston, urging me to do it.

#0000ff

Pathetic.
Pathetic, pathetic.
#ffffff

A knife in my hand.
*pant* *pant* My breathing is out of control.
My heart is pounding like a piston, urging me to do something.

#0000ff

　　　　　オレなら　もっとうまくやる
entries.maoEnglish: I would do it better.
entries.mirrorMoon:

If it were me, I'd do a much better job.

#ffffff

　はあ、はあ、はあ。
　あえぐ吐息。
　それは―――自分も弓塚さつきのようにしてみたい、という衝動を抑えているが為に、呼吸が乱れに乱れてしまっているのか。
　乱れている。
　こんなモノ―――俺は、見たくないから。
entries.maoEnglish:
Hah, hah, hah.
Panting.
Is my breathing this wild because I am fighting the urge to do what Satsuki Yumizuka did?
My breathing is ragged.
Because I don’t want to see a thing like this.
entries.mirrorMoon:
#ffffff

*pant*, *pant*, *pant*.
I breathe hard.
Is it because I'm holding back my impulse of wanting to do the same things Yumizuka Satsuki is doing?
I'm going out of control.
Because I don't---want to see such a thing.

entries.maoEnglish: I’m not holding anything back.

　　　　　　耐えることに価値なぞない
entries.maoEnglish: There is no virtue in restraint.

entries.maoEnglish: I want to exist exactly as I please.
entries.mirrorMoon:

I   I want to do   what I want to do.

　その声は、自分の、声だ。
　……弓塚は泣いている。
　うまく殺せなくて泣いているのか、それとも痛くて泣いているのか、よくわからない。
entries.maoEnglish:
That voice is my own.
Yumizuka is crying.
I cannot tell whether she is crying because she cannot kill properly, or simply because she is in pain.
entries.mirrorMoon:
#ffffff

That voice.
It is, my own.
…… Yumizuka is crying.
Is she crying because she's not good at killing?
Or is it because she's in pain?
I don't know.

entries.japanese:
「やっ。
おはよう秋葉」
「―――おはようございます、兄さん」
「おはようございます志貴さん。
朝食の支度でしたら食堂のほうにできていますから、どうぞ召し上がってください」
　冷たい秋葉とは対照的に、ニコニコとした笑顔で挨拶をしてくれる琥珀さん。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hey. Morning, Akiha.”
“―――Good morning, Brother.”
“Good morning, Shiki. Breakfast is ready in the dining room, so please help yourself.”
In stark contrast to chilly Akiha, Kohaku greets me with a beaming smile.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hey.
Good morning, Akiha."
"---Good morning, Nii-san."
"Good morning, Shiki-san.
Breakfast is ready in the dining hall.
Please eat up."
In contrast to Akiha, Kohaku-san greets me with a cheerful smile.

entries.japanese:
「あ、どうもありがとうございます。
……けど、秋葉はもう済ませたのか？
　見たところ食後のお茶みたいだけど」
「当然です。
兄さんがどんな時間に起床しようとかまいませんが、せめて朝食ぐらいは余裕をもってください。
七時をすぎて朝食をとるなんて、たるんでいる証拠です」
「……いや、七時ごろに朝食をとるのは普通だと思うけど。
そういう秋葉は何時に起きたんだよ」
「朝の五時には起床しますけど、なにか？」

「………………」
　……さすがだ。
そんな早くに起きて何をするかはわからないが、もう反論のしようもないほど完璧な起床時間である。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh, thank you. But have you already eaten, Akiha? That looks like after-breakfast tea.”
“Of course. You may rise whenever you please, Brother, but you could at least leave yourself time for breakfast. Eating after seven is proof that you’ve let yourself go.”
“Seven is a perfectly normal time for breakfast. What time did you get up, then?”
“Five in the morning; why?”
“………………”
Of course. I have no idea what she does at that hour, but five is such an unimpeachably perfect answer that I cannot argue with it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah, thank you very much… It looks like you're having your after-meal tea.
Have you already finished breakfast, Akiha?"
"Of course.
I don't care when you get up, Nii-san, but please at least make some time for breakfast.
Having breakfast after seven is a sign of sloppiness."
"…… I think having breakfast at seven is pretty normal.
What time do you get up, Akiha?"
"I get up at five in the morning.
What about it?"
"………"
…… Wow.
I don't know why she gets up so early, but it was so perfect a time to get up that I have no room to retort.

entries.japanese:
「だいたい、兄さんの学校はここから徒歩で三十分ほどなんでしょう？
　そんなに近いところに学校があるのに遅刻なんかしないでくださいね。
恥ずかしいですから」
「…………う」
　秋葉の言葉には、いちいち棘があってチクチクする。
　けどまったくの正論なので、反論をする余地がまるでない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Your school is only a thirty-minute walk from here, isn’t it? Please don’t be late when you live so close. It would be embarrassing.”
“Urgh…”
Every word out of Akiha’s mouth has a barb on it.
The worst part is that she’s entirely right, leaving me no room to fight back.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Besides, your school is thirty minutes from here on foot, isn't it?
Please don't be late to a school that's so close by.
It'd be an embarrassment."
"…… Urgh."
Akiha's words are filled with thorns that stab at me.
But as it's the truth, there's no opening for a counter-argument.

entries.japanese:
先生は言った。
　この目が見てしまうモノは、物の壊れやすい個所なのだと。
　それは人間でいうのなら急所、という事だろうか。
entries.maoEnglish:
Teach had told me.
What these eyes saw were the places where things were most easily broken.
In a human being, perhaps one would call them vital points?
entries.mirrorMoon:
Sensei told me.
My eyes could see the points where things could easily be broken.
And if that 'thing' were to be a person, then what I would see would be their vital spots.

entries.japanese:
そこを刃物で通せば、何の力も要らずにモノを切断できてしまう線。
　鉄みたいな硬いものでも、あの『線』は等しく切断できてしまう。
「つまりね、志貴。
　あらゆるモノは“壊れてしまう”という運命を内包しているのよ。
カタチがある以上、こればっかりは逃れようが無い条件だからね」
entries.maoEnglish:
They were lines along which a blade could sever anything without the slightest force.
Even something as hard as iron could be cut apart if the blade followed one of those “lines.”
“In other words, Shiki.
Everything carries within it the fate of one day breaking. As long as a thing has form, there is no escaping that condition.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
Lines which, if cut, could break something apart without any effort.
With those lines, even things as hard as steel could easily be cut.
"In other words, everything in existence has its destiny of 'breaking' internalized within it.
This is something inescapable for anything with a physical form, Shiki."

entries.japanese:
先生はそう言った。
　子供のころ。
　その意味がようやく理解できて、とても恐くなった記憶がある。
　それはつまり、セカイはツギハギだらけでいつ壊れてもおかしくないという事だ。

地面にもラクガキが走っているのなら。
　そこを歩いていたら、とうとつに地面が砕けてしまうという可能性があるというコト。
―――その意味に気がついた時、心底先生のくれたメガネに感謝した。
entries.maoEnglish:
That was what Teach told me.
I was still a child.
I remember how frightened I felt when I finally understood.
It meant the whole world was a patchwork, liable to fall apart at any moment.
Suppose those scribbles ran across the ground as well.
Then the earth might suddenly shatter beneath someone’s feet as they walked over them.
―――When I grasped what that meant, I thanked her from the bottom of my heart for the glasses she had given me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
That's what Sensei had said.
I was still a child back then.
I remember finally understanding what she meant and getting scared.
In other words, the world is full of cracks, and it could collapse at any instant.
If there are scribbles all over the ground, then there's a possibility that the earth would start breaking apart if I walk over it.
---When I realized what she meant, I thanked Sensei from the bottom of my heart for the glasses she gave me.

entries.japanese:
こんな線がいつも見えてしまっていたら、とてもじゃないけど生きていけない。
　モノの壊れやすい個所。
　そんなものが見えても、得になるコトなんて何ひとつないんだから―――――
entries.maoEnglish:
No one could live while seeing such lines every waking moment.
The places where things were fragile.
There was not a single advantage to seeing anything like that―――――
entries.mirrorMoon:
I couldn't have gone on living if I had continued to see the lines all the time.
The points where things could easily be broken.
There isn't a single advantage to being able to see them---

entries.japanese:
「―――おはようございます」
　……聞き慣れない声がする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――Good morning.”
An unfamiliar voice.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Good morning."
…… I hear an unfamiliar voice.

entries.japanese:
「朝です。
お目覚めの時間です、志貴さま」
　……だから、志貴さまはやめてくれないか。
　そう言われると背筋が寒くなるって、昨日ちゃんと言ったっていうのに────
entries.maoEnglish:
“It is morning. Time to wake up, Master Shiki.”
Could she stop calling me Master Shiki already?
I had told her yesterday that it sent a chill down my spine────
entries.mirrorMoon:
"It is morning.
It is time for you to awaken, Shiki-sama."
…… Stop calling me Shiki-sama already.
I told you yesterday, it sends chills down my back----

entries.japanese:
―――目が覚めた。
　
　翡翠はベッドから離れたところで、なにかの彫像のように立ち尽くしている。
「…………」
　ここは、ドコだっけ。
「おはようございます、志貴さま」
　メイド服の少女がおじぎをする。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――My eyes opened.
Hisui stood well away from the bed, motionless as a statue.
“……”
Where was I?
“Good morning, Master Shiki.”
The girl in the maid uniform bowed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---I wake up.
Hisui stands far from the bed, like a statue.
"……"
Where am I?
"Good morning, Shiki-sama."
The girl in a maid uniform bows.

entries.japanese:
「……ああ、そうだ。
俺は、自分の家に戻ってきたんだっけ」
　体を起こして部屋の様子を流し見る。
　とたん――――
―――ズキリと、こめかみに痛みがはしった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh… right—I came back home.”
I sat up and surveyed the room.
At once────
―――A sharp pain stabbed through my temple.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah… yeah, I came home, right…"
I push myself up, looking around the room.
In that instant---
---I feel sharp pain in my temples.

entries.japanese:
「あれ―――」
「眼鏡、でしょうか？」
　翡翠は丁寧な動作でメガネを渡してくれた。
「――――ふう」
　……一息つけた。
　昨日の夜―――眠る前に、メガネをかけていたのに『線』が見えた気がしたけど、どうやら気のせいであってくれたらしい。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What―――”
“Your glasses, perhaps?”
Hisui handed them to me with meticulous care.
“――――Whew.”
I could breathe again.
Last night, before I fell asleep, I thought I had seen the lines despite my glasses―――but apparently it had only been my imagination.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Huh---?"
"Are you looking for your glasses?"
Hisui gently hands me my glasses.
"---Phew."
…… I let out a breath.
Last night---Before I went to sleep, I had the feeling I was seeing the lines even with my glasses on.
Seems like it was just my imagination.

entries.japanese:
「つ……」
　慣れない部屋で眠ったせいだろうか、意識は靄がかかっているように空ろだ。
「志貴さま……？」
　翡翠が声をかけてくる。
　ブンブンと頭をふって、寝ぼけたままの頭を覚醒させた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ngh…”
Perhaps it was because I had slept in an unfamiliar room, but my mind felt hollow and veiled in mist.
“Master Shiki…?”
Hisui called to me.
I shook my head vigorously, trying to wake my sleep-fogged brain.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Sstt……"
Maybe it's because I slept in an unfamiliar room, but my mind is hazy.
"Shiki-sama…?"
Hisui calls out to me.
Shaking my head, I shake away my sleepiness.

entries.japanese:
「おはよう翡翠。
わざわざ起こしてくれて、ありがとう」
「そのようなお言葉は必要ありません。
志貴さまをお起こしするのはわたしの責務ですから」
　翡翠は淡々と、まったくの無表情で返答する。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Good morning, Hisui. Thanks for going to the trouble of waking me.”
“Your thanks are unnecessary. Waking Master Shiki is one of my duties.”
Hisui answered evenly, without the slightest change of expression.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Good morning, Hisui.
Thanks for coming to wake me."
"There is no need to thank me.
It is my duty to come and wake you, Shiki-sama."
Hisui gives a plain and completely expressionless response.

entries.japanese:
……ひいき目に見ても、翡翠はきれいな顔立ちをしていると思う。
　そういう子に起こされるのは喜ぶべきことなんだろうけど、翡翠にこうも感情がないとあまり嬉しい、という感じはしない。
　……もったいない。
　翡翠も琥珀さんの半分ぐらい明るければ、ものすごく可愛いと思うんだけど。
entries.maoEnglish:
Even making every allowance for bias, Hisui had a beautiful face.
Being awakened by a girl like her ought to have been a pleasure, but with so little emotion in her, it did not feel particularly delightful.
What a waste.
If Hisui were even half as cheerful as Kohaku, she would be incredibly cute.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Even in an unfavorable light, I think Hisui's features are beautiful.
It should be wonderful for such a girl to wake me every morning, but as Hisui never smiles, I don't feel that happy about it.
…… What a shame.
If Hisui only had half of Kohaku's brightness, she would be really cute.

entries.japanese:
「―――なにかご用ですか？」
　こっちの視線に気づいたのか、翡翠はまっすぐに見つめ返してくる。
「いや、なんでもない。
目が覚めてまっさきに翡翠の顔を見て、ここが遠野の屋敷なんだなって実感しただけだよ」
　さて、とベッドから起きて、うーんと大きく両手を伸ばす。
　と、そこで自分がキチンと寝巻に着替えている事に気がついた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――Do you require something?”
Perhaps she had noticed me staring, for Hisui met my eyes directly.
“No, nothing. Seeing your face first thing when I woke up simply made it sink in that I’m back at the Tohno estate.”
I climbed out of bed and stretched both arms high above my head.
That was when I noticed I had been properly changed into pajamas.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Do you need something?"
Realizing I am looking at her, Hisui stares straight back at me.
"No, nothing at all.
Waking up with you there makes me feel like I'm really at the Tohno mansion."
Now then.
Getting off the bed, I stretch out both arms.
Suddenly, I realize I'm wearing pajamas.

entries.japanese: ―――えーっと、たしか昨日は……
entries.maoEnglish: ―――Wait, yesterday I had—
entries.mirrorMoon: ---Eh, I'm sure that yesterday, I…

entries.japanese:
「ありゃ？
　俺、昨日制服のまま眠ったと思うんだけど」
「はい。
あのままではお体に悪いので、姉さんが志貴さまを着替えさせたあと、ベッドに寝かし付けたのです」
　翡翠は当然のように事情を説明してくれた。
　そっか、着替えさせてくれたのか。
たしかにあのまま眠っていたら風邪をひいていたかもしれない。
　さすがメイドさん、行き届いてるな―――って、ちょっと待った……！
entries.maoEnglish:
“Huh? I thought I fell asleep in my uniform.”
“Yes. As that would have been bad for your health, my sister changed Master Shiki’s clothes and put him to bed.”
Hisui explained this as though it were the most natural thing in the world.
So she had changed me. Fair enough—I might have caught a cold otherwise.
Just what you would expect from a maid―――wait a minute…!
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Huh?
I thought I slept in my uniform last night."
"Yes.
Since it is bad for your health to do so, Nee-san changed your clothes and put you to bed afterwards."
Hisui explains it as if it is something perfectly natural.
I see.
She changed my clothes.
It's true that I could have caught a cold if I had just slept like that.
Just the kind of attentive service you'd expect from a maid---Hey, wait a minute…!

entries.japanese:
「な─────っ」
　ばっ、とズボンとパンツを確認する。
　ズボンは真新しい寝巻で、パンツもまっさらな新品だった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Wh―――――!”
I yanked at my waistband and checked my trousers and underwear.
The pajama bottoms were brand-new, as were the briefs underneath.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Wh------!?"
I quickly check my pants and underwear.
My pants are brand new pajama pants.
Even my underwear is new.

entries.japanese:
「なっ、なっ、なっ」
　なんてコトをするんだ、と言いかけて、なんとか言葉を飲み込む。
　とりあえず落ち着いて考えよう。
　……えっと、まず悪いのは半分ぐらい自分自身だ。
　それに着替えさせたのは翡翠じゃなくてお姉さんの琥珀さん。
　なら翡翠に文句を言うのはお門違いじゃないか。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Wh-what, what—”
I nearly demanded what on earth they had done to me, but somehow swallowed the words.
Calm down and think.
First, at least half the blame was mine.
Second, Hisui had not changed me; her sister Kohaku had.
Complaining to Hisui would be completely unfair.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Wh-wh-wh-!?"
I want to say 'What the hell did you do!?', but somehow the words are stuck in my throat.
I've got to calm down and think things over for now.
…… Let's see.
First of all, half the blame belongs to me.
And the one who changed me wasn't Hisui, it was her sister, Kohaku-san.
It would be wrong to complain to Hisui.

entries.japanese:
「────翡翠」
「はい、なんでしょう」
「これからは、そういう余計な事はしなくていい。
どうしてもって時は起こしてくれないか。
着替えぐらい自分でできるから、自分でやりたいんだ」
　顔を真っ赤にしながら言うと、翡翠ははい、と素直にうなずいた。
「学校の制服はそちらにたたんであります。
着替えが済みしだい居間においでください」
entries.maoEnglish:
“────Hisui.”
“Yes, what is it?”
“From now on, you don’t need to do anything like that. If it’s absolutely necessary, wake me up first. I can change my own clothes, and I’d rather do it myself.”
My face burning, I forced the words out, and Hisui nodded obediently.
“Your school uniform is folded over there. Please come to the sitting room once you have dressed.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Hisui."
"Yes, what is it?"
"You don't have to do anything uncalled for like this from now on.
If you have to, please wake me up.
I can change myself, so I'd like to do so."
My face is a deep red as I say all of this.
Hisui obediently nods in affirmation.
"Your uniform is folded and awaits you over there.
Please come to the sitting room after you have changed."

entries.japanese:
「………………」
　くそ、なんて不覚。
　昨夜、あのままベッドで眠ってしまった事も不注意なら、着替えさせられてる時に目を覚まさなかったのも無神経すぎる。
「ふつう気がつくもんだけど……よっぽど疲れてたのかな、俺」
　自分自身にグチってみても、起きてしまった事は変わらない。
いつまでもバカな独り言をしてないで、さっさと着替えて朝食にしよう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“……”
Damn it—what a disgrace.
Falling asleep on the bed in my uniform had been careless enough, but failing to wake while someone changed me was beyond oblivious.
“Was I really so tired I failed to notice…?”
Complaining to myself would not undo what had happened. Enough idiotic muttering; I needed to dress and get to breakfast.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"………"
Damn it.
How careless could I be.
It was careless of me to begin with when I fell asleep on the bed like that, but to not have woken up while I was being changed is over the top.
"Usually I would have sensed it, but… maybe I was just really tired."
Complaining to myself isn't going to change anything.
I can't just keep standing here talking to myself like an idiot.
I'd better hurry up and change, then go have breakfast.

entries.japanese:
学校の制服はきちんとたたまれていて、シャツにはアイロンまでかけられている。
　袖に腕を通すと、なんだか新品みたいに気持ちがよかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
My uniform had been folded perfectly, and even the shirt was freshly pressed.
Sliding my arms into the sleeves felt almost as good as putting on something new.
entries.mirrorMoon:
My school uniform is neatly folded, and my shirt is even ironed.
Passing my wrists through the sleeves feels good.
It's that fresh, brand-new feeling.

entries.japanese:
「…………いや、別にハダカぐらいいいんだけどね、うん」
　いいんだけど、あのニコニコ笑顔の琥珀さんに着替えさせられた、という事実はどうしようもなく気恥ずかしい。
　おまけに鏡に映った自分の顔は赤くなっているくせに、何度か嬉しそうにニヤついたりする。
　……大丈夫なのか、遠野志貴。
　こんなんじゃここで暮らしていけるのか不安になってくるじゃないか、未熟者め。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I mean, being naked is no big deal, sure.”
It wasn’t—but the fact that smiling, cheerful Kohaku had undressed me was unbearably embarrassing.
Worse, although the face in the mirror was scarlet, it kept breaking into a pleased little grin.
Was Shiki Tohno going to be all right?
At this rate, how was I ever going to survive living here, hopeless amateur that I was?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… No, there's nothing wrong with being naked, is there?
Yep."
There was nothing wrong with it, but I couldn't help being embarrassed at the fact that I was being changed by the warmly smiling Kohaku-san.
To top things off, the face in the mirror keeps smiling from time to time despite being bright red.
…… Are you really okay, Tohno Shiki?
I thought you were supposed to be uneasy about staying here, you amateur.

entries.japanese:
居間には秋葉と琥珀さんがくつろいでいた。
　秋葉の制服は浅上女学院、という有名なお嬢様学園の物だろう。
　二人はとっくに朝食をすませたのか、優雅に紅茶なんぞを飲んでいた。
　俺は――――
entries.maoEnglish:
Akiha and Kohaku were relaxing in the sitting room.
Akiha’s uniform must belong to Asagami Girls’ Academy, that famous school for well-bred young ladies.
They had evidently finished breakfast long ago and were now sipping tea with infuriating elegance.
I――――
entries.mirrorMoon:
Akiha and Kohaku-san are relaxing in the sitting room.
Akiha is wearing the uniform of the Asagami Ladies' Academy, a famous school for young girls.
They are drinking tea together gracefully, as if breakfast ended a long time ago.
I----

entries.japanese:
「やっ。
おはよう秋葉」
「―――おはようございます、兄さん」
　あわただしく居間に入ってきた俺とは対照的に、秋葉はとても落ちついている。
「おはようございます志貴さん。
朝食の支度でしたら食堂のほうにできていますから、どうぞ召し上がってください」
　冷たい秋葉とは対照的に、ニコニコとした笑顔で挨拶をしてくれる琥珀さん。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hey. Morning, Akiha.”
“―――Good morning, Brother.”
Unlike me, bursting breathlessly into the sitting room, Akiha is perfectly composed.
“Good morning, Shiki. Breakfast is ready in the dining room, so please help yourself.”
In stark contrast to chilly Akiha, Kohaku greets me with a beaming smile.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hey.
Morning, Akiha."
"--Good morning, Nii-san."
In contrast to my hurried entrance, Akiha is perfectly calm.
"Good morning, Shiki-san.
If you're looking for breakfast, it's ready in the dining hall, so please eat up."
Kohaku-san greets me with a warm smile, in contrast to Akiha's coolness.

entries.japanese:
「あ、どうもありがとうございます。
……けど、秋葉はもう済ませたのか？
　見たところ食後のお茶みたいだけど」
「当然です。
兄さんがどんな時間に起床しようとかまいませんが、せめて朝食ぐらいは余裕をもってください。
七時をすぎて朝食をとるなんて、たるんでいる証拠です」
「……いや、七時ごろに朝食をとるのは普通だと思うけど。
そういう秋葉は何時に起きたんだよ」
「朝の五時には起床しますけど、なにか？」
「………………」
　……さすがだ。
そんな早くに起きて何をするかはわからないが、もう反論のしようもないほど完璧な起床時間である。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh, thank you. But have you already eaten, Akiha? That looks like after-breakfast tea.”
“Of course. You may rise whenever you please, Brother, but you could at least leave yourself time for breakfast. Eating after seven is proof that you’ve let yourself go.”
“Seven is a perfectly normal time for breakfast. What time did you get up, then?”
“Five in the morning; why?”
“………………”
Of course. I have no idea what she does at that hour, but five is such an unimpeachably perfect answer that I cannot argue with it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah, thank you very much.
…… It looks like you're having your after-meal tea.
Have you already finished breakfast, Akiha?"
"Of course.
I don't care to know when you get up, Nii-san, but please at least allow time for breakfast.
Having breakfast after seven is a sign of sloppiness."
"…… I think having breakfast at seven is pretty normal.
What time do you get up, Akiha?"
"I get up at five in the morning.
What about it?"
"………"
…… Wow.
I don't know why she gets up so early, but it was so perfect a time to get up that I have no room to retort.

entries.japanese:
「だいたい、兄さんの学校はここから徒歩で三十分ほどなんでしょう？
　そんなに近いところに学校があるのに遅刻なんかしないでくださいね。
恥ずかしいですから」
「…………う」
　秋葉の言葉には、いちいち棘があってチクチクする。
　けどまったくの正論なので、反論をする余地なんてまったくない。

「ああもう、仕方ないだろ。
昨日の夜はうるさくて中々寝つけなかったんだから」
「あ、そっか。
兄さんは帰ってきたばかりでまだ部屋に慣れていないんですね。
……まあ、それなら今日ぐらいは大目に見てさしあげます」
「いや、別に部屋に慣れてなかったってワケじゃなくて―――」
　昨日の夜は、とにかく野犬がうるさかった。
なかなか寝つけなかったのは部屋のせいというより犬のせいだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Your school is only a thirty-minute walk from here, isn’t it? Please don’t be late when you live so close. It would be embarrassing.”
“Urgh…”
Every word out of Akiha’s mouth has a barb on it.
The worst part is that she’s entirely right, leaving me no room to fight back.
“Oh, come on—I couldn’t help it. It was so noisy last night that I barely got to sleep.”
“Oh, of course. You only just came home, so you aren’t used to your room yet. Very well—I’ll overlook it today.”
“No, the room wasn’t the problem―――”
The wild dogs had made an incredible racket last night. My strange room had much less to do with my sleeplessness than they did.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Besides, your school is thirty minutes from here on foot, is it not?
Please don't be late to a school that's so close by.
It would be an embarrassment."
"…… Urgh."
Akiha's words are filled with thorns that stab at me.
But as it's the truth, I once again have no room to make any counter-argument.
"Argh, geez!
I couldn't help it.
It was so noisy last night that I couldn't get to sleep."
"Ah, I see.
You must not be used to your room yet, having just returned… Well, I'll let you off the hook this time."
"No, it's not because I'm not used to the room, but--"
At any rate, those stray dogs last night were really noisy.
It wasn't because of the room, it was because of them.

entries.japanese:
「おはよう琥珀さん。
今朝はいい天気ですね」
「はい、おはようございます志貴さん」
　ありきたりの朝の挨拶に、琥珀さんは満面の笑みを返してくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Good morning, Kohaku. Beautiful day, isn’t it?”
“Good morning, Shiki.”
Kohaku answers my commonplace greeting with a radiant smile.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Morning, Kohaku-san.
Today is a lovely day."
"Yes.
Good morning, Shiki-san."
Kohaku-san delivers her ordinary morning greeting with a smile on her face.

entries.japanese:
「昨夜はよくお眠りになられましたか？
　慣れないお屋敷の夜でしたから、色々と不具合がないかって心配していたんですけど」
「ああ、とりあえず困るようなコトはないよ。
これでも昔はここに住んでいたんだし、今はちゃんと気を配ってくれる琥珀さんがいるし」
「あら。
お上手ですね、志貴さん」
「えっ？
　いや、たんに思ったことを口にしただけど……お上手って、なにが上手なんですか？」
　琥珀さんは笑顔のままこっちを眺めているだけだ。
　……なんていうか、そうまっすぐに見られると照れくさくて、視線をよそに移す。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Did you sleep well? It was your first night in an unfamiliar estate, so I was worried something might not suit you.”
“Nothing’s given me any trouble so far. I did live here once, after all—and now I have you looking after me so thoughtfully.”
“My, how smooth of you, Shiki.”
“What? I only said what I was thinking… Smooth at what, exactly?”
Kohaku merely keeps smiling at me.
Having her look at me so directly is embarrassing somehow, and I turn my eyes away.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Did you sleep well last night?
I was worried that you might be inconvenienced, staying in an unfamiliar mansion and all."
"Ah, no, there were no problems.
I used to live here, after all, and now I've got you to watch over me, Kohaku-san."
"Oh, you're quite good at this, Shiki-san."
"Eh?
No, I'm just saying what I think… what is it I'm good at?"
Kohaku-san just looks at me, smiling.
…… Somehow, I feel embarrassed when she looks directly at me, so I shift my gaze to the side.

entries.japanese:
―――と。
　さっきから無言でこっちを見つめている、もう一つの視線に気がついた。
「あ……よお」
　軽く手をあげて挨拶をする。
　秋葉はじっとこっちを見つめてくる。
……っていうか、睨んできてる。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――That was when.
I notice another pair of eyes that has been silently fixed on me all this time.
“Oh—hey.”
I raise one hand in a casual greeting.
Akiha keeps staring at me. No, she is glaring.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---And then,
I realize another stare, one which has been on me silently for a while now.
"Ah… hey there."
I give a light wave to greet her.
Akiha continues to stare at me… or perhaps, glare would be a better word.

entries.japanese:
「えっと、その……おはよう、秋葉」
「あら、無理に挨拶をしてくれなくてもいいのに。
どうぞ、私のことは無視して結構です。
兄さんは琥珀と楽しく朝を迎えたいみたいですから」
「うっ……」
　秋葉の言葉はちくちくする。
　……こっちだって別に秋葉のことを無視していたわけじゃなくて、ただ琥珀さんに挨拶をしただけなんだけど……。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Um—good morning, Akiha.”
“Oh, you needn’t force yourself to greet me. Please, feel free to ignore me. You clearly prefer beginning your morning with Kohaku.”
“Urgh…”
Akiha’s words prick like needles.
I had not meant to ignore Akiha; I simply greeted Kohaku first.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Well… um… good morning, Akiha."
"Oh?
You don't have to force yourself to greet me.
Please, go right ahead and ignore me.
After all, it seems you'd prefer to enjoy the morning with Kohaku."
"Uuh…"
Akiha's words sting.
…… It's not like I had intended to ignore her.
I just said hello to Kohaku-san…

entries.japanese:
「秋葉さま、あんまり志貴さんをいじめないであげてください。
お時間もありませんし、志貴さんはまだ朝食を済ませていないんですから」
「朝食が済んでいないのは兄さんの起床が遅いからでしょう。
朝があわただしくなるのは兄さんの自業自得です」
　ふん、と鼻をならす秋葉。
　……どうも、俺がこの時間にやってきた事に文句があるのにプラスして、秋葉に挨拶をしなかったのがダブルパンチで気に食わないみたいだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Miss Akiha, please don’t tease Shiki so. We’re short on time, and he hasn’t eaten breakfast yet.”
“He hasn’t eaten because he rose too late. If his morning is rushed, he has no one but himself to blame.”
Akiha gives a disdainful little sniff.
Apparently she resented both my arriving at this hour and my failure to greet her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Please don't tease Shiki-san too much, Akiha-sama.
We don't have much time, and Shiki-san hasn't finished his breakfast yet."
"Well, that's Nii-san's fault for waking up late, isn't it?
He's just getting what he deserves for leaving everything to do in a rush in the morning."
"Hmph!" Akiha sniffs.
…… It seems like my failure to greet her was another point she was unimpressed with, in addition to her objection to my late arrival.

entries.japanese:
「……あの、琥珀さん。
朝食って、俺の分はできてるんですか？」
「はい、食堂にご用意させていただきました。
どうぞ、ゆっくり召し上がってくださいな」
「だめよ琥珀、そんなの無理にきまってるでしょう。
もうこんな時間なんだから、兄さんに朝食を摂る時間なんてありません」
entries.maoEnglish:
“…Kohaku, did you make breakfast for me?”
“Yes, it’s waiting in the dining room. Please take your time and enjoy it.”
“Don’t be absurd, Kohaku; he can hardly take his time at this hour. Brother has no time left for breakfast.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Um… Kohaku-san.
Is my breakfast ready?"
"Yes, I've laid it out in the dining hall.
Please, eat up at your leisure."

entries.japanese:
「あのな秋葉、まだ七時を過ぎたばかりなんだから、それぐらいの時間はあるよ。
ここからうちの高校まで徒歩三十分ちょいなんだから、十分ぐらいゆっくりしてられるじゃないか」
「つまり朝食にかける時間は十分だけですか。
おなかをすかせた犬じゃないんですから、朝食はゆっくりとってほしいですね」
「─────」
　秋葉の言葉には、やっぱり棘がある。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Listen, Akiha, it’s only just past seven, and school is barely more than thirty minutes away, so I can spare ten minutes easily.” “Ten whole minutes for breakfast?
You’re not a starving dog. I would prefer you ate like a civilized human being.”
“─────”
There are thorns in every word she says.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"That won't do, Kohaku.
Nii-san has no time to eat breakfast at this time."
"Hey, listen, Akiha.
It's only seven, so I've got at least that much.
It's an easy thirty minute walk from here to school, so I can take it easy for at least ten minutes, can't I?"
"Are you saying you're going to finish breakfast in just ten minutes?
You're not some starving dog, so if you're going to eat breakfast, I'd like you to take your time."
"------"
Akiha's words really do have thorns in them.

entries.japanese:
「犬じゃないんですからって、秋葉―――」
　と、思い出した。
　犬っていえば、昨日の夜のことがあったのだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“A dog, Akiha―――”
Then I remembered.
There had been the business with the dogs last night.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I'm not a dog, Akiha--"
Then I remember.
Speaking of dogs, there is what happened last night.

entries.japanese:
「二人とも、おはよう」
「おはようございます、志貴さん」
　琥珀さんは白い割烹着に相応しい、これ以上ないっていうぐらいの笑顔で挨拶をかえしてくれた。
　一方秋葉はというと、ちらりとこちらを一瞥するなり、
「おはようございます。
朝はずいぶんとゆっくりなんですね、兄さん」
　なんて最高に気の利いた嫌味をこぼしてくれる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Morning, you two.”
“Good morning, Shiki.”
Kohaku answers with the warmest smile imaginable, perfectly at home above her snowy kitchen smock.
Akiha, on the other hand, gives me one sidelong glance and—
“Good morning. You certainly take your time getting started, Brother.”
A magnificently well-aimed piece of sarcasm.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Good morning, you two."
"Good morning, Shiki-san."
Wearing a white apron that suits her, Kohaku-san replies with a smile that could not possibly be any larger.
On the other hand, Akiha just casts a glance at me.
"Good morning.
You certainly took your time this morning, Nii-san."
She certainly knows how to put a damper on things.

entries.japanese:
「ゆっくりって、まだ七時を過ぎたばっかりじゃないか。
ここからうちの高校まで徒歩三十分ちょいなんだ、今日は早起きしたほうだよ」
「つまり朝食にかける時間は十分だけですか。
おなかをすかせた犬じゃないんですから、朝食はゆっくりとってください」
「─────」
　秋葉の言葉には、やっぱり棘がある。
「犬じゃないんですからって、秋葉―――」
　と、思い出した。
　犬っていえば、昨日の夜のことがあったのだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Take my time—it’s only just past seven, and school is barely more than thirty minutes away. By my standards, I got up early today.”
“Which leaves you ten whole minutes for breakfast. You’re not a starving dog, so please eat like a civilized human being.”
“─────”
There are thorns in every word she says.
“A dog, Akiha―――”
Then I remembered.
There had been the business with the dogs last night.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Took my time?
It's barely past seven!
It only takes thirty minutes to get to school from here, so I'm actually up early."
"So you're saying you're going to finish breakfast in just ten minutes?
You're not some starving dog, so if you're going to eat breakfast, I'd like you to take your time."
"------"
Akiha's words really do have thorns.
"I'm not a dog, Akiha---"
Then I remember.
Speaking of dogs, there is what happened last night.

entries.japanese:
「なあ。
昨日の夜のコトだけど、ここって毎晩あんななのか？」
「―――はい？」
　こちらの質問に、秋葉は首をかしげて応える。
　……どうも、こちらの質問の意図がまったく伝わってくれてないみたいだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Listen. About last night—does it get like that every night around here?”
“―――Excuse me?”
Akiha tilts her head at my question.
Apparently she hasn’t understood what I mean at all.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hey, about what happened last night… does that happen every night?"
"---What?"
Akiha tilts her head slightly in response to my question.
…… It seems the point of my question has completely failed to reach her.

entries.japanese:
「だから、昨日の夜の話だよ。
ワンワンワンワンってうるさかったじゃないか。
アレじゃ秋葉たちだって眠れなかっただろ」
「―――兄さん？
　それ、なんの話です？」
「なんの話かって、昨日の夜の話に決まってるだろ。
夜の十一時ごろ、野犬が吠えっぱなしだったじゃないか」
　秋葉と琥珀さんは顔を見合わせたあと、そろり、と二人そろってこっちの顔をうかがう。
　……人をキチ〇イか何かだと思っているような態度、許すまじ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Last night. All that barking—it was deafening. You two couldn’t have slept through it either.”
“Brother… what are you talking about?”
“Last night, obviously. Around eleven, those wild dogs wouldn’t stop barking.”
Akiha and Kohaku exchange a glance, then slowly turn together to study my face.
I will not stand for being treated like some kind of lunatic.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I'm talking about what happened last night.
That noisy 'woof woof woof woof' racket.
Even you wouldn't have been able to sleep with that going on, right?"
"---Nii-san?
What are you talking about?"
"What?
I'm talking about last night, of course.
Around eleven at night.
Some stray dogs were barking their heads off."
Akiha and Kohaku-san exchange looks, and then together, they both look back at me.
…… It's like they think I'm some kind of nutcase.
I can't just let this slip by.

entries.japanese:
「いい、秋葉には聞かない。
琥珀さん、昨日の夜はうるさかったよね？」
「―――ええっと、どうなんでしょうか。
たしかに昨夜は風が強かったと思いますけど……深夜の見まわりで発見した異状は、志貴さんが制服のままベッドの上で眠っていらしたことぐらいですよ」
「……ああ、ソレですか。
これからは、その、気をつけます」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Fine, forget Akiha. Kohaku, you heard all that noise last night, didn’t you?”
“―――Well, I’m not sure. The wind was strong, but the only irregularity on my late-night rounds was you asleep on your bed in your school uniform.”
“Oh, that. I’ll be more careful from now on.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Fine, I'm not asking you anymore, Akiha.
Kohaku-san, it was really noisy last night, wasn't it?"
"---Eh… was it really?
I did think the wind was quite strong, but… the only unusual thing I found while looking around late at night was you, sleeping in your uniform on top of your bed."
"…… Ah, yes.
I'll be more careful from now on."

entries.japanese:
「なに？
　なにかあったの、琥珀？」
「いえ、別になにもありませんでしたよー。
ちょっと志貴さんの寝相が悪かった、というだけですから」
　琥珀さんは笑顔で、秋葉の質問をサラリと流す。
　……そう言えば、琥珀さんは志貴さん、と呼んでくれている。
　昨夜の伝言を翡翠はちゃんと伝えてくれたみたいだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What? Did something happen, Kohaku?”
“Nothing at all. Shiki was merely sleeping a little restlessly.”
Still smiling, Kohaku glides neatly past Akiha’s question.
Come to think of it, she calls me simply Shiki now.
Hisui must have passed along my request from last night.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"What?
What happened, Kohaku?"
"Oh, nothing in particular.
Shiki-san just has bad sleeping posture, that's all."
Kohaku-san dodges Akiha's question with a smile.
…… Come to think of it, Kohaku-san is calling me "Shiki-san" now.
It seems like Hisui passed on my message from last night.

entries.japanese:
「……ホントに二人とも気がつかなかったのか？
　昨日の夜、三十分ぐらい外で野犬が吠えてたのに。
ワンワンワンワンって、そりゃうるさいったらありゃしなかった」
「ははあ。
それはワンワンパニックですね」
　……琥珀さんは、なんだかどこかズレてる気がする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…You honestly didn’t notice? Wild dogs barked outside for half an hour last night—bark, bark, bark, without a moment’s peace.”
“Ah. A full-blown bow-wow panic.”
There is something ever so slightly off about Kohaku.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Are you sure neither of you noticed?
Those dogs were barking for about thirty minutes straight last night.
'Woof woof woof woof'.
If that isn't noisy, I don't know what is."
"Haha… It really was a woof-woof panic, wasn't it?"
…… Somehow, I get the feeling Kohaku-san has missed the point.

entries.japanese:
「……まあ、わかりやすく言うと、そういうコト」
「ふーん―――私はそんな覚えはないけど。
琥珀もないでしょう？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Well, in plain language, yes.”
“Hmm—I don’t remember anything like that. Neither do you, Kohaku?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Well, that's basically how it was."
"Hmmm---I don't remember anything like that.
You don't either, do you, Kohaku?"

entries.japanese:
「そうですねー。
志貴さんには申し訳ないんですが、昨夜はとくにそのような事はなかったと思います」
「決まりね。
あと考えられるケースっていったら、兄さんが犬に吠えられる夢でも見てたんじゃないかってコトですか」
「…………う」
　そりゃあたしかに、夢だったんじゃないか、と言われればそうだったかもしれないけど。
entries.maoEnglish:
“No, I’m afraid not. I don’t believe anything like that happened last night.”
“Then that settles it. The only remaining possibility is that Brother dreamed of dogs barking at him.”
“Urgh…”
Admittedly, once she suggests it was a dream, I can’t say it’s impossible.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No, I don't.
Sorry, Shiki-san.
There wasn't anything particularly like that last night that I can remember."
"Then it's decided.
The only possibility left I can think of is that Nii-san had a dream about it."
"…… Uuh."
Well, now that she mentions it, maybe it was a dream, but…

entries.japanese:
「―――兄さんはまだ屋敷に慣れていないから、そんな質の悪い夢を見たんでしょう。
　そうですね、今夜も野犬に吠えられるようでしたら、とびっきり獰猛な番犬でも飼う事にしましょうか」
　くすり、と底意地の悪い笑みをこぼす秋葉。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――You’re still unaccustomed to the estate, Brother, which must be why you had such an unpleasant dream.
If the wild dogs trouble you again tonight, perhaps we should buy an exceptionally vicious guard dog.”
Akiha lets out a small, malicious laugh.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---You must have had a nightmare because you aren't used to the mansion yet, Nii-san.
Oh, I know what.
If that stray dog barks again tonight, perhaps we shall start keeping an extra-vicious guard dog here."
A malicious giggle comes out from Akiha.

entries.japanese:
「私は時間ですのでお先に失礼します。
兄さん、登校中に犬に襲われないよう気を付けてくださいね」
　秋葉はそのまま居間を後にした。
　秋葉を玄関まで送るのか、琥珀さんも居間を後にする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I must be going. Take care not to be mauled by any dogs on your way to school, Brother.”
With that, Akiha leaves the sitting room.
Kohaku follows, presumably to see her to the front door.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I am now out of time, so please excuse me, Nii-san.
Please do take care not to get attacked by any dogs on your way to school."
Akiha leaves the sitting room.
Kohaku-san leaves to escort her to the doorway.

entries.japanese:
「…………」
　さて、そろそろ結論を出してもいいころだ。
　昨夜から今までの経過を思い起せば考えるまでもないんだろうけど、
　どうやら俺は、
　秋葉にとてつもなく嫌われているらしい。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
It may be time to accept the obvious.
After everything that has happened since last night,
there can be only one conclusion:
Akiha absolutely detests me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……"
Now seems like a good time to come to a conclusion.
Given what's happened from last night up until now, it's a no-brainer to work out that for some reason, Akiha really, really hates me.

entries.japanese:
琥珀さんが用意してくれた朝食を食べたあと、ロビーに出る。
　と、ロビーには翡翠が鞄を持って待っていた。
「志貴さま、お時間はよろしいのですか？」
「ああ、こっから学校まで走れば二十分ないからね。
いま七時半だろ、寄り道をしても間に合うよ」
　こっちの説明に満足したのか、こくん、と翡翠は頷く。
entries.maoEnglish:
After eating the breakfast Kohaku prepared, I step into the entrance hall.
Hisui is waiting there with my schoolbag.
“Master Shiki, are you certain you have enough time?”
“Sure. If I run, I can make school in under twenty minutes—even with a detour, I have plenty of time.”
Apparently satisfied, Hisui gives one small nod.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I leave for the lobby after I eat the breakfast Kohaku-san made for me.
Hisui is in the lobby, waiting with my bag.
"Will there be enough time, Shiki-sama?"
"Yeah, it's not even twenty minutes to school from here if I run.
It's seven-thirty now, so I could make it even if I take the long way."
Satisfied with my explanation, Hisui nods.

entries.japanese:
「それでは、外までお見送りいたします」
「え―――あ、うん、どうも」
　……やっぱり、自分付きの使用人というのはひどく照れくさい。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Then I shall see you to the gate.”
“Oh—sure, thanks.”
Having a servant assigned especially to me is still painfully embarrassing.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Very well, I will escort you out."
"Eh---Ah, yeah, thanks."
…… It's a terribly embarrassing thing to have a personal servant.

entries.japanese:
「あ、志貴さん！
　ちょっと待ってください！」
　たたたっ、と琥珀さんが二階から降りてきた。
「……………………」
　翡翠は琥珀さんがやってくると、すい、と身を引いて黙ってしまう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Shiki! Please wait!”
Kohaku comes pattering down the stairs.
“…”
The moment Kohaku approaches, Hisui smoothly withdraws a step and falls silent.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah, Shiki-san!
Please wait!"
With pattering footsteps, Kohaku-san runs down from the second floor.
"…………"
Hisui steps back and falls silent as Kohaku-san appears.

entries.japanese:
「あれ、琥珀さんは秋葉と一緒じゃなかったの？」
「秋葉お嬢様はお車で学校に向かわれますから。
今朝は志貴さんにお届け物があるので屋敷に残らさせていただいたんです」
「お届け物って、俺に？」
「はい。
昨日、有間家のほうから荷物が届いたんですよ」
　ニッコリと琥珀さんは笑顔をうかべる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Weren’t you going with Akiha?”
“Miss Akiha travels to school by car. I stayed behind because I have something to give you this morning.”
“Something for me?”
“Yes. A parcel arrived from the Arima family yesterday.”
Kohaku smiles brightly.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Huh?
Weren't you with Akiha?"
"Lady Akiha goes to school by car.
Since I had something to give you this morning, I stayed behind."
"Something to give me?"
"Yes.
This came from the Arima family yesterday."
Kohaku-san smiles.

entries.japanese:
「え───？
