　いや、俺は自分の荷物は全部持ってきたよ。
もともとむこうで使ってたのは有間の家のものだったから、自分の物なんて着てる服ぐらいのものなんだけど……」
「そうなんですか？
　こちらが届けられたお荷物ですけど」
　琥珀さんは二十センチほどの、細い木箱を手渡してくる。
　重量はあまりない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What? But I brought everything of mine. Most of what I used over there belonged to the Arimas, so aside from the clothes on my back, I hardly owned anything…”
“Is that so? This is the parcel they delivered.”
Kohaku hands me a slender wooden box about twenty centimeters long.
It weighs very little.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Eh?
But, I have all my luggage already.
The things I used while I was at the Arimas' house all belonged to them, so all I've got are my own clothes…"
"Really?
But this was sent here, nonetheless…"
Kohaku-san hands me a thin wooden box, perhaps twenty centimeters long.
It's not heavy at all.

entries.japanese:
「───琥珀さん、俺はこんなの見た事もないんだけど」
「はあ。
なんでも志貴さまのお父さまの遺品だそうですけど。
志貴さんに譲られるようにって遺言があったとか」
「……あの親父が俺に？」
　……それこそ実感がわかない。
　八年前、俺をこの屋敷から追い出した親父がどうして俺に形見分けをするんだろう？
entries.maoEnglish:
“───Kohaku, I’ve never seen this before.”
“Yes. I’m told it was among Master Shiki’s father’s effects. Apparently his will instructed that it be left to you.”
“That man left something to me?”
It doesn’t feel real.
Why would the father who cast me out of this estate eight years ago leave me a keepsake?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Kohaku-san, I've never seen this before."
"Well… apparently it was left to you by your departed father.
It was to be given to you in the will."
"…… By my old man?"
…… I can't feel anything about that.
What's the old man who expelled me from this mansion eight years ago doing leaving me things?

entries.japanese:
「まあいいや。
琥珀さん、これ部屋に置いておいて」
「─────」
　琥珀さんはじーっ、と興味深そうに木箱を見つめている。
　なんだか玩具をほしがる子供みたいな仕草だ。
「じーーーーっ」
　いや、子供そのものだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Whatever. Kohaku, leave it in my room for me.”
“─────”
Kohaku stares avidly at the wooden box.
She looks like a child longing for a toy.
“Staaaaare.”
No—she really is a child.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Oh well.
Kohaku-san, please take it to my room for me."
"------"
Kohaku-san is staring intently at the wooden box.
She seems almost like a child who wants a toy.
Staaaaare.
No, she is a child.

entries.japanese:
「……わかりました。
中身が気になるんですね、琥珀さんは」
「いえ、そんなことないです。
ただちょっと気になるなって」
　………だから、十分気になってるじゃないか。
「なら開けてみましょう。
せーのっ、はい」
　スッ、と乾いた音をたてて木箱を開ける。
　中には────十センチほどの、細い鉄の棒が入っていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…I see—you want to know what’s inside, don’t you?”
“Not at all. I’m only a little curious.”
That still means she’s curious.
“Then let’s open it. Ready—and there.”
The wooden lid slides aside with a dry whisper.
Inside lies――――a slender iron rod about ten centimeters long.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I get it.
You want to know what's inside, right?"
"Oh, not at all.
I merely wondered for a moment."
…… Like I said, you do wonder what's inside.
"Alright, let's open it.
One, two… three!"
With a dry sound, the wooden box opens.
Inside, there is----a ten-centimeter bar of thin iron.

entries.japanese:
「………鉄の棒………だ」
　何の飾り気もない、使い込まれて手垢のついた鉄の棒。
　……こんなガラクタが俺に対する形見分けとは、親父はよっぽど俺が気に食わなかったとみえる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“An iron rod…”
Plain, well worn, and darkened by years of handling.
If this piece of junk is all Father left me, he must have disliked me even more than I thought.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… It's… an iron bar."
Undecorated and worn, it has finger marks all over it.
…… The old man must have really hated me to leave me a piece of junk like this.

entries.japanese:
「───違います志貴さん。
これ、果物ナイフですよ」
　琥珀さんは鉄の棒を箱から取り出す。
「ほら、飛び出しナイフってあるじゃないですか。
あれと同じみたいです。
せーの、はいっ」
　パチン、と音がして棒から十センチほどの刃が飛び出す。
　……なるほど、たしかにこれはナイフだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“───No, Shiki. This is a fruit knife.”
Kohaku lifts the iron rod from the box. “You know those spring-loaded
knives? This one seems to work the same way—ready, there!” A snap, and a blade about ten centimeters long leaps from the handle.
She’s right.
It is a knife.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No, Shiki-san.
It's a fruit knife."
Kohaku-san takes the iron bar out of the box.
"See, isn't it one of those folding knifes?
One, two… three!"
With a "pachink!", a ten-centimeter blade pops out from the bar.
…… I see, it certainly is a knife.

entries.japanese:
「ずいぶんと古いものみたいですけど、作りはしっかりしてますよ。
裏に年号がかかれてます」
　琥珀さんは刃をしまってからナイフを手渡してくる。
　たしかに握りの下のほうに数字が刻まれていた。
　七という漢字と、その後には夜という漢字。
entries.maoEnglish:
“It seems very old, but it’s sturdily made. There’s a date engraved on the back.”
Kohaku retracts the blade and hands me the knife.
There are indeed characters carved near the bottom of the grip.
First the character for seven, then the character for night.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"It's old, but it seems pretty solid.
The year and the era it was made in is written on the back."
Kohaku-san replaces the blade, and hands over the knife.
Certainly, there's a number written on the grip.
The character 'seven', and under it, the character 'night'.

entries.japanese:
「姉さん、これは年号じゃないわ。
七つ夜って書かれているだけよ」
「っ！」
　びっくりして振り返る。
　と、今まで黙っていた翡翠が後ろからナイフを覗きこんでいた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Sis, that isn’t a date. It only says Nanatsu-Yoru.”
“!”
I whirl around in surprise.
Hisui, silent until now, has been peering at the knife over my shoulder.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Nee-san, there is no era by that name.
It just says 'Nanatsu-yoru'."
"!"
Surprised, I turn around.
Hisui, who had been silent until now, was looking at the knife over my shoulder.

entries.japanese:
「び、びっくりしたあ……翡翠、人が悪いぞ。
そんな後ろから覗かなくても、見たければ見せてあげるのに」
「あ―――――」
　とたん、翡翠の頬がかすかに赤くなる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You startled me, Hisui… That was mean; you didn’t have to sneak up behind me when I would’ve shown it to you if you asked.”
“Ah—”
A faint blush instantly rises in Hisui’s cheeks.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Y, you surprised me… Hisui, you should say something.
You don't have to look over my shoulder like that, you know.
If you want to see it, I'll show it to you."
"Ah---"
Hisui's cheeks suddenly become a little redder.

entries.japanese:
「し、失礼しました。
あの―――その短刀があまりにキレイでしたから、つい」
「キレイ？
　これ、キレイっていうかなあ。
どっちかっていうとオンボロな感じだけど」
「――――そんな事はありません。
見事な刃文をした、由緒正しい古刀だと思います」
「……そうなの？
　俺にはガラクタにしか見えないけど……」
entries.maoEnglish:
“M-my apologies. I couldn’t help myself—the dagger was so beautiful.”
“Beautiful? I don’t know about that. It looks more battered than anything.”
“――――It is nothing of the kind. Its exquisite temper line marks it as an ancient blade with a distinguished history.”
“Really? It still looks like junk to me…”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"P-please excuse me.
Uh---That knife is so beautiful that I could not help myself."
"Beautiful?
You really think it's beautiful?
It looks kind of beat up to me."
"---Not at all.
The tempering of the blade is masterful.
I think it is a knife with its own proper history."
"Really?
It looks to me like a piece of junk…"

entries.japanese:
翡翠があんまりにも強く断言するもんだから、こっちもその気になってきた。
　……うん。
これはこれで、形見としては悪くないのかもしれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
Hisui insists so firmly that I begin to believe her.
…Yes—perhaps it isn’t such a bad keepsake after all.
entries.mirrorMoon:
But since Hisui seems so convinced, I begin to feel the same thing.
…… Hmmm.
In its own way, I guess it's not such a bad inheritance.

entries.japanese:
「七つ夜……ですか。
その果物ナイフの名前でしょうかね？」
「そうかもね。
ナイフに名前を付けるなんてヤツはそういないと思うけど」
　なんにせよ年代物という事ははっきりしている。
「ま、もらえる物はもらっとくのが俺の信条だし」
　刃を収めて、ズボンのポケットにナイフを仕舞う。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Nanatsu-Yoru… Could that be the fruit knife’s name?”
“Maybe. Not many people bother naming their knives, though.”
Whatever else it may be, the thing is clearly an antique.
“Still, never turn down something free—that’s my creed.”
I fold the blade away and slip the knife into my trouser pocket.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"'Seven nights'…?
Maybe that's the name of this fruit knife?"
"Maybe… though, I can't imagine him naming a knife like that."
Whatever the case may be, it's obvious that it's an antique.
"Well, in any case, I believe in taking what's given to me."
I replace the blade, and put the knife in my trouser pocket.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま。
お時間はよろしいのですか……？」
「まずい、そろそろ行かないと間にあわないか。
それじゃ琥珀さん、届け物ありがとうね」
　いえいえ、と琥珀さんは笑顔で手をふった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki. Are you certain you have time…?”
“Damn, I’d better go or I really will be late. Kohaku, thanks for bringing me the parcel.”
Smiling, Kohaku waves away my thanks.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama, have you enough time…?"
"Ah!
I have to get going.
Well, Kohaku-san, thanks for the delivery."
"You're welcome."
Kohaku-san smiles and waves.

entries.japanese:
玄関を出て、中庭を抜ける。
　屋敷の門に出ると、なにやら騒がしい事に気がついた。
entries.maoEnglish:
I leave through the front door and cross the courtyard.
At the estate gate, I notice some sort of commotion.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Leaving the doorway, I pass through the garden.
As I pass out the mansion gates, I sense a commotion.

entries.japanese:
「……なんだろ。
なんか屋敷の右手のほう、騒がしくないか？」
「それが、今朝方屋敷の東の路面で血痕が発見されたそうです」
「―――血痕……？
　それって、ようするに血のあとってこと？」
「はい。
屋敷の塀にも血の跡がありました。
志貴さまがお眠りになられている間、警察の方々が昨夜の様子を尋ねにもまいられましたが」
「……それって、まさか人が死んでたっていうことなのか……？」
「いえ、発見されたのは血の跡だけだそうです」
entries.maoEnglish:
“…What’s that noise over on the right side of the estate?”
“Bloodstains were discovered on the road east of the estate early this morning.”
“―――Bloodstains…? You mean traces of blood?”
“Yes. There was blood on the estate wall as well. While Master Shiki slept, the police also came to ask about last night.”
“Does that mean somebody died…?”
“No—the only thing found was blood.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… What's going on?
Sounds like something's happening on the right side of the mansion."
"I heard that someone found bloodstains on the road east of the mansion."

"---Bloodstains…?
You mean leftover blood?"
"Yes.
There was blood on the mansion fence, too.
The police came to inquire about what happened last night while you were sleeping, Shiki-sama."
"…… Does that mean someone died…?"
"No, all that has been found are the bloodstains."

entries.japanese:
「――――――」
　屋敷の東側―――それは昨日の夜、黒いコートの男がいたあたりだ。
　血の跡……血のあと。
　血の跡―――赤いあと。
　そういえば、たしかに。
　なにか、赤い色を見た気がしたけれど――――。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――――”
East of the estate―――the place where I saw the man in the black coat last night.
Bloodstains… traces of blood
Bloodstains―――traces of red.
Come to think of it, yes.
I do remember seeing something red――――.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------"
The east side of the mansion---That's around where the man in the black coat was last night.
Bloodstains… traces of blood.
Bloodstains---traces of red.
Come to think of it…
I get the feeling I saw something red----.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま？」
「え………？
　い、いや、なんでもないよ」
　ぶんぶん、と頭をふって不吉なイメージを振り払う。
「それじゃ行ってくる。
見送りありがとう、翡翠」
「行ってらっしゃいませ。
どうか、道々お気をつけて」
　深々とおじぎをする翡翠。
　……何をお気をつけてなのかは不明だけど、おそらくはこっちの体を気遣ってくれてるんだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki?”
“Huh…? N-no, it’s nothing.”
I shake my head hard, shaking off the sinister image.
“I’d better go. Thanks for seeing me out, Hisui.”
“Have a safe journey. Please take great care on the way.”
Hisui bows deeply.
I’m not sure what danger she expects, but she’s probably worried about my health.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama?"
"Eh…?
N-no, it's nothing."
Shaking my head, I shake off the bad images.
"Well, I'll be going now.
Thanks for seeing me off, Hisui."
"Goodbye.
Please take care on the way."
Hisui bows deeply.
…… I'm not sure what to take care about, but she's probably just worried about my health.

entries.japanese:
「ああ、サンキュ。
翡翠も気をつけて」
　好意には好意で返すのは当たり前。
翡翠に元気よく手をふって、屋敷の門を後にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Thanks. You be careful too, Hisui.”
Kindness deserves kindness in return. I wave cheerfully and leave the estate gate behind.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yeah, thanks.
You take care, too, Hisui."
It's only right to repay good intentions with good intentions.
With an energetic wave of the hand at Hisui, I leave the gates of the mansion behind.

entries.japanese:
───見慣れない道を歩く。
　今まで有間の家から高校に通っていたから、この道順での登校は初めてだった。
　単に道が変わっただけなのに、まるで転校生みたいに新鮮な気持ちになる。
entries.maoEnglish:
───I walk along unfamiliar streets.
Until now I always commuted from the Arima house, so this is my first journey to school by this route.
Nothing has changed but the road, yet I feel as fresh and nervous as a transfer student.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---I walk along the unfamiliar streets.
Up until now, I've been going to school from the Arima house, so it's the first time I've taken this route to school.

entries.japanese:
「────あんまりいないな、うちの学生」
　この周辺の家庭にはうちの高校に通っている人間は少ないようだ。
　朝の七時半。
　道を小走りで進んでいく学生服姿は自分しか見あたらない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“────Not many students from our school around here.”
Apparently few families in this neighborhood send their children there.
It is seven-thirty in the morning.
I’m the only uniformed figure jogging down the road.
entries.mirrorMoon:
It's only the path I'm taking that's different, but I feel like I'm going to a new school.
"---There doesn't seem to be a lot of students from my school around."
Apparently, there are not many who live around here.
Half past seven in the morning.
I can't see anyone running along the streets in a school uniform except me.

entries.japanese:
オフィス街は通勤ラッシュで混雑している。
　いつも通り、スーツ服姿の会社員たちが今日もお仕事に励もうと戦闘準備をしている光景。
　いや、いつも通りというのは正しくない。
　ここ数日の街の雰囲気は少し重い。
entries.maoEnglish:
The business district is jammed with the morning rush.
The usual scene: ranks of office workers in suits preparing themselves for another day’s battle.
No—that isn’t quite the usual scene.
A weight has hung over the city these past few days.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The business district is in a rush of activity.
As usual, the scene is one of suited firm employees gearing themselves for today's battle.
No, it isn't quite the same as usual.
For the last few days, the atmosphere has been a little heavier in this town.

entries.japanese:
おそらくは例の連続通り魔の影響だろう。
ここ数日は夕方になると街の人通りも少なくなっているとの事だ。
「───夜遊びはほどほどにって事だぞ、有彦」
　街の雰囲気など気にせず夜遊びをする悪友の顔がうかぶ。
　ま、言ったところでアイツが聞くわけもないんだけど。
entries.maoEnglish:
The recent series of random street killings must be responsible. I have heard that the streets begin to empty by late afternoon.
“───That means you should ease up on the nightlife, Arihiko.”
My incorrigible friend’s face rises in my mind, entirely untroubled by the mood of the city.
Not that he would listen if I told him.
entries.mirrorMoon:
It's probably due to the serial killings.
There are less people in the streets in the evenings now, too.
"---You'd better cut down on the hanging out at night, Arihiko."
The face of my bad friend drifts into mind.
He'd be the sort to carry on hanging out at night regardless of the atmosphere in town.
Well, it's not like he's going to listen to a word I say, anyway.

entries.japanese:
道にちらほらと制服姿が人込みにまざってきた。
　校門が閉まるまであと十分ほど。
　遅刻しないようにとアスファルトの路面を駆ける。
 ───到着。
　屋敷から徒歩で三十分、というより二十分程度か。
途中で何度か走ったから、ゆっくりしたいのなら七時すぎに屋敷を出る必要があるだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
School uniforms begin to appear here and there among the crowd.
Ten minutes until the gates close.
I break into a run over the asphalt, determined not to be late.
───Made it.
They said it was a thirty-minute walk from the estate, but it was closer to twenty. Since I ran part of the way, though, I’ll need to leave just after seven if I want a leisurely walk.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I start to see some people in school uniforms intermingled with the crowd.
There are only about ten minutes until the school gates close.
I dash along the asphalt street so I won't be late.
---I arrive.
It seems like it took twenty minutes rather than thirty from the mansion.
I'll need to leave around seven if I want to go slowly, since I ran several times on the way.

entries.japanese:
ホームルーム数分前の教室はざわざわとこうるさい。
　担任がやってくるまで話し込んでいるクラスメイト達は無秩序に教室に散らばっていて、たった数分ながらもお祭りのような騒がしさをかもしだしている。
　その中をゆったりと歩いて、窓際の自分の席に到着する。
entries.maoEnglish:
With homeroom only minutes away, the classroom buzzes noisily.
My classmates are scattered everywhere, talking until the teacher arrives, and for those brief few minutes the room has the happy disorder of a festival.
I stroll through the chaos and reach my seat by the window.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The classroom, just minutes before homeroom, is full of commotion.
Scattered all over the classroom are my classmates, intent on talking until the teacher arrives.
It's like a festival in here, even though there are only a few minutes left.
I ease my way through to my seat next to the window.

entries.japanese:
────と。
「いょぉう。
遅いぞ、遠野」
　しかも───
「あ、おはようございます遠野くん」
 ───とんでもなく予想外な人物と一緒に、だ。
entries.maoEnglish:
────And there.
“Heeey. Cutting it close, Tohno.”
And worse still───
“Oh, good morning, Tohno.”
───he has someone with him whom I never expected to see here.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Then,
"Yo!
You're late, Tohno."
In stark contrast to the otherwise pleasant classroom, there is someone waiting with a big grin on his face.
And in addition---
"Ah, good morning, Tohno-kun."
---He is accompanied by someone very unexpected.

entries.japanese:
「先輩───なんでうちの教室にいるのさ」
　呆然と、それこそお化けでも見るようにシエル先輩を指差す。
「あれ、そんなに珍しいことですか？
　わたし、遠野くんが教室にいるかなってちょっと寄ってみただけですけど」
「珍しいコトって―――普通、上級生が下級生のクラスには来ないよ。
色々問題はあるけど、なにより場所が離れすぎてる」
　なるほど、と先輩は生真面目に頷いたりする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ciel───what are you doing in our classroom?”
Dumbstruck, I point at her as though I’ve seen a ghost.
“Is it really so strange? I only stopped by to see whether you were here.”
“Of course it’s strange. Upperclassmen don’t normally visit younger students’ classrooms, and whatever else is wrong with it, the distance between them is the biggest problem.”
Ciel nods with perfect seriousness, as though this explains everything.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Senpai---why are you in our classroom?"
Dumbfounded, I point to Ciel-senpai like I'm looking at a ghost.
"Huh?
Is it so unusual?
I was just wondering if you were in class, so I decided to come over to see you, Tohno-kun."
"Unusual?---The seniors never come to the junior classrooms.
There's all sorts of reasons, but the biggest one is that they're just too far apart."
"Oh, I see." Senpai nods with a serious face.

entries.japanese:
「でもその点は大丈夫ですよ。
わたし、こう見えても走るのは速いんです。
下の階の自分のクラスまで、一分もかかりません」
　えっへん、と先輩は力説する。
「…………」
　どうも、この人に世間体というものを問いただすのはあまり意味がないみたいだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“That part is no problem. I may not look it, but I’m a very fast runner. I can reach my classroom downstairs in under a minute.”
She makes the declaration with her chest proudly thrust out.
“…”
Apparently there is little point trying to teach this woman about appearances.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"You don't have to worry about that.
Despite my appearance, I'm a fast runner.
It takes me less than a minute to get to my class downstairs from here."
Senpai emphasizes her point.
"……"
I guess she's just not the kind of person who cares what other people think.

entries.japanese:
「おまえも口やかましいな遠野。
いいじゃんか、先輩が好きで来てるんだからさー」
　有彦は有彦で、人の机にどっかりと腰をおろして先輩と楽しげに話をしている。
「………いいけど。
ホームルームが始まる二分前になったら自分のクラスに帰らないとダメだよ、先輩」
　なんだかどっと疲れてしまって、ため息まじりに椅子に座った。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You nag too much, Tohno. She came because she wanted to, so what’s the harm?”
Arihiko has planted himself squarely on my desk and is chatting merrily with Ciel.
“Fine. But you have to go back to your own classroom two minutes before homeroom, Ciel.”
Suddenly exhausted, I sink into my chair with a sigh.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Quit whining, Tohno.
What's wrong with it, anyway?
Senpai's here because she wants to be."
Arihiko, being Arihiko, plonks himself down on my desk and starts up a merry conversation with Senpai.
"…… I don't mind, but you ought to get back to your class two minutes before homeroom starts, Senpai."
I feel tired for some reason.
Sighing, I sit down.

entries.japanese:
「……乾くん、どうも遠野くんはご機嫌ななめみたいですね」
「……ああ、たぶん引っ越し先の生活が性に合わなくて、カンシャクおこしてるんだろうな。
遠野はたいていのコトは気にしないんだけど、なんかよく解らない事があると暴れ出す悪癖があるからな」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Inui, Tohno seems rather cross this morning.”
“Yeah—his new home probably doesn’t agree with him, so he’s throwing a tantrum. Most things don’t bother Tohno, but when he meets something he can’t make sense of, he has this nasty habit of going berserk.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Inui-kun, it seems Tohno-kun is feeling down."
"…… Yeah, he's probably feeling irritable because he's not used to his life after moving.
Tohno doesn't mind most things, but he's got a bad habit of throwing a fit when faced with things he doesn't understand."

entries.japanese:
「……そうなんですか？
　遠野くん、あんまり怒りそうにないですけど」
「……いやあ、そんなコトはないぜ。
遠野はねー、普段大人しい分、自分で理解できない事に出遭うとプッツーンとイっちまうヤロウなんだって」
「……はあ。
ぷっつーん、ですか」
「……そうそう。
一度キレると見境がなくなるから、先輩もこいつを信用しちゃダメだぜ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Really? Tohno doesn’t strike me as someone who gets angry.”
“Don’t be fooled. He’s usually quiet, but whenever he meets something he can’t understand, he snaps―――completely.”
“Ah. He snaps?”
“Exactly. Once he loses it, he can’t tell friend from foe, so you shouldn’t trust him.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Really?
Tohno-kun doesn't look like the type to get angry."
"…… Nope, that's not true.
Tohno, you see, is usually pretty mature, but when he encounters something he doesn't understand---Kaboom!"
"…… Haah… 'Kaboom', is it?"
"…… Yep.
You'll change your opinion once you see him lose it, so you can't just trust him like that, Senpai."

entries.japanese:
……二人はひそひそと内緒話をしている。
「……あのさ。
内緒話なら廊下でしてくれないか？
人の机でそういうコトされても、全部聞こえてくるから意味がないぞ」
entries.maoEnglish:
The two of them are whispering together in secret.
“…Listen—if you want a private conversation, could you have it in the hallway? Whispering over my desk is pointless when I can hear every word.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… The two of them whisper to each other.
"…… Hey, listen.
If you're going to talk privately, do you mind doing it in the hallway?
I can hear every word you say when you do it on my desk, so there's no real point to it."

entries.japanese:
「なに、聞こえていたのか遠野！？」
　大げさに驚く有彦。
……ここまで芝居をうたれると、怒る前に気が滅入ってくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You heard us, Tohno?!”
Arihiko reels back in theatrical shock. When he lays it on this thick, I lose the will to be angry.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"What!?
You could hear us!?"
Arihiko gives an exaggerated reaction of surprise.
No one could stay angry after being hit with an act like that.

entries.japanese:
先輩はといえば、どこまで本気なのかハッとして口元を手で隠している。
　……この人のことだから、きっと本気で内緒話をしているつもりだったのかもしれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
As for Ciel, she gasps and covers her mouth.
With her, it’s entirely possible she honestly believed they were being discreet.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Senpai puts her hands to her mouth, and I can't tell how serious she is.
…… If it's Senpai, she may have actually intended to talk privately.

entries.japanese:
「ひどいぞ遠野！
　オレと先輩のラブラブな内緒話を盗み聞くなんて、趣味が悪すぎだオマエ！」
　ガガガッ、なんて効果音を出しながら有彦はこちらを指差す。
「―――有彦。
おまえ、もしかして俺に喧嘩を売ってるのか？」
　……ていうか、ぜひ売ってくれ。
今ならどんな値段でも買ってやるから。
　ぶるぶる、と有彦は首をふる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“How could you, Tohno! Eavesdropping on the sweet nothings between me and Ciel is sick!”
Arihiko points at me while making his own dramatic doom-doom-doom sound effects.
“―――Arihiko. Are you trying to pick a fight?”
Please say yes. At the moment, I’ll buy one at any price.
Arihiko shakes his head violently.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"That's terrible, Tohno!
Listening in on the lovey-dovey private conversation between Senpai and me!
You've sure got some nasty hobbies!"
Arihiko points at me.
"---Are you trying to pick a fight with me, Arihiko?"
…… Actually, please do.
Right now, I'm more than willing.
Arihiko shakes his head.

entries.japanese:
「そんなワケないだろ、オレと遠野は親友じゃないか。
オレは親とだって殴り合いはするがね、親友とだけは戦わないってポリシーがあるんだ。
侠に生きる漢なんだよ、基本的に」
　……凄いな、それは。
　侠っていうのは肉親に手をあげていいものだったんだ、こいつの内面世界においては。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Of course not—we’re best friends. I may trade blows with my own parents, but my policy is never to fight a true friend. Fundamentally, I’m a man of honor.”
Remarkable.
In Arihiko’s private moral universe, a man of honor is apparently free to hit his own family.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Of course not.
You're my dear friend, right?
I'd exchange fists with even my parents, but I have a policy of not fighting with my friends.
I'm the very model of chivalry."
…… That's amazing.
I guess chivalrous people could punch their parents in the world that's inside his head.

entries.japanese:
「なるほど―――腐ってるね、おまえのポリシーは」
「ははははは！
　なんだ、元気がないようなフリしやがって、根はいつも通りの遠野じゃないか！
　ったく、心配して損したぜ！」
　バンバン、と背中を叩く有彦。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I see—your code is rotten.”
“Ha ha ha ha! There you are—the same old Tohno underneath that gloomy act. What a waste of my concern!”
Arihiko pounds me repeatedly on the back.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I see---That's a pretty rotten policy."
"Hahahaha!
You pretended to be depressed, but deep down you're the same Tohno as always!
Damn, I had nothing to worry about after all!"
Arihiko hits me a couple of times in the back.

entries.japanese:
「……有彦。
おまえ、もしかして今のは気を使ってくれたのか？」
「ばっか、そんなつまんないコト聞くなっての。
　こういうのはさりげなくやるのが美徳じゃないのサ！」
　ばんばんばん、とさらに背中を叩かれる。
　……長い付き合いだけど、コイツの性格だけはいまだによく掴めない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…Arihiko—were you actually trying to cheer me up?”
“Idiot, don’t ask such embarrassing questions.
The virtue lies in doing this sort of thing without making a show of it!”
He pounds my back even harder.
We’ve known each other for years, and I still can’t quite grasp what sort of person he is.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Arihiko, were you worried about me just then?"
"Don't ask me trivial stuff like that, you dumbass!
It's only good if I do it without you noticing!"
Arihiko hits my back some more.
…… We've been friends for a long time, but I still can't get a hold on this guy's personality.

entries.japanese:
「それで、新しい家はどうなんだ？
　見たところ、けっこうヘヴィにストレス溜まってそうじゃんか」
「さあ、どうだろう。
とりあえず昨日はイヤな夢を見て、家の人達に白い目で見られたけど」
「―――むう。
そうか、それは災難だな」
　有彦は難しい顔をしてうんうんと頷く。
entries.maoEnglish:
“So how’s the new place? You look seriously stressed out.”
“Hard to say. I had a horrible dream last night, and this morning the whole household looked at me as if I’d lost my mind.”
“―――Hmm. I see; what a grim ordeal.”
Arihiko nods gravely.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"So, how's your new house?
Pretty heavy and stressful by the looks of it."
"Mmn.
Can't really say.
I had a bad dream last night, and the people at my house gave me the cold shoulder."
"---Mmm, I see.
Sounds rough."
Arihiko nods with a difficult expression.

entries.japanese:
「…………………」
―――と。
　黙っているかと思ったら、先輩は俺と有彦のくだらないやりとりをじーっと見つめていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
―――And then.
Ciel, whom I thought had simply fallen silent, is staring intently at our idiotic exchange.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"………"
---And,
Senpai is silent, staring at us while we have our trivial conversation.

entries.japanese:
「先輩？」
「遠野くん、やっぱり乾くんと仲がいいんですね」
「本気ですか先輩。
今のを見てそう言えるなんて、そのメガネは度があってないですね」
「そんなコトないです。
遠野くん、乾くんの前だとすごく気を抜いてるじゃないですか。
ものすごく無防備で、乾くんを信頼しきってます」
　なぜか先輩は嬉しそうに笑った。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ciel?”
“Tohno, you really are close to Inui.”
“Are you serious? If that’s what you saw just now, your glasses need a new prescription.”
“They do not. You let your guard down completely around him. You’re utterly defenseless because you trust him without reservation.”
For some reason, Ciel smiles as though that makes her happy.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Senpai?"
"Tohno-kun, you really do get on well with Inui-kun."
"Are you serious, Senpai?
You must need thicker glasses if that's what you think after seeing what just happened."
"Not at all, Tohno-kun.
You look really relaxed when you're with Inui-kun.
You're really open and trust him a lot."
Senpai smiles happily for some reason.

entries.japanese:
「？」
　有彦と顔を合わせて首をかしげる。
「羨ましいなあ。
そうやって何の気負いもしないで分かり合える友人がいるのって、憧れます」
　ほう、と感心する先輩。
entries.maoEnglish:
“?”
Arihiko and I look at each other, equally baffled.
“How enviable—a friend you can understand without either of you needing to pretend or make an effort. I’ve always admired that.”
Ciel gives an impressed little sigh.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"?"
Arihiko and I exchange looks and tilt our heads.
"Oh, I'm so envious.
I really admire how your friendship allows such understanding without you getting worried over each other."
Senpai is impressed.

entries.japanese:
「「そうかあ？」」
　有彦と顔を合わせて眉をよせる。
「そうですよ。
二人とも気がついていないだけです。
あ、でも気がついたら終わってしまうのかもしれません。
……そっか、そうなると遠野くんと乾くんは今のままでいいんでしょうね。
うん、すごく絶妙なバランスです」
「まあ、絶妙といえば絶妙なタイトロープだけどね、俺とこいつの関係は」
　同感だ、と頷く有彦。
こういう所だけは阿吽の呼吸で意見が合う。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You think?”
Arihiko and I say together, exchanging doubtful frowns.
“That’s right. Neither of you has noticed, that’s all. But perhaps noticing would ruin it. In that case, you and Inui should stay exactly as you are. Yes, it’s a wonderfully delicate balance.”
“Delicate is one word for it—the relationship between me and this idiot is more of a tightrope.”
Arihiko nods his complete agreement. Only on points like this do we understand each other without a word.
entries.mirrorMoon:
""Really?""
Arihiko and I exchange looks and raise our eyebrows.
"That's right.
It's just that you two don't realize it.
Ah, but maybe it'll end if you do… Hmmm… In that case, it'd be best if you two just remained as you are.
Yes, truly a miraculous balance."
"Well, I guess you could say our relationship is a miraculous tightrope."
Arihiko nods in agreement.
I guess that's one point we perfectly agree on.

entries.japanese:
「あ、そろそろ時間ですね。
それじゃあわたしは戻りますけど、遠野くん今朝のニュース見ましたか？」
「―――いや。
引っ越した家にはテレビがなくてさ。
朝のニュースは見れないんだ」
「そうですか。
それじゃあ率直に聞きますけど、今朝のニュースで大きなお屋敷が映っていたんです。
あれって遠野くんのお家ですか？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh, I should be going. Before I leave—Tohno, did you see the news this morning?”
“―――No. My new place has no television. I couldn’t watch the morning news.”
“Then I’ll ask you directly. The news showed a very large estate this morning. Was that your home?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah, it's almost time.
I'll be going now.
Did you watch the news this morning, Tohno-kun?"
"---No, the house I moved to doesn't have a television, so I can't watch the morning news."
"Is that so?
Well, I'll just ask you straight out then.
There was a big mansion on today's morning news.
Is that where you live?"

entries.japanese:
「―――――え？」
　今朝のニュース？
　……そういえば警察が事情聴取にきたって翡翠が言っていたっけ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――――What?”
The news this morning?
Hisui did mention that the police had come to ask questions.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Eh?"
This morning's news?
…… Now that she mentions it, Hisui said the police had come to talk.

entries.japanese:
「ああ、それはきっと家のコトだよ。
今朝、警察が話を聞きに来たって言ってたし」
「―――そうですか。
遠野くん、あんまり夜遊びしちゃダメですよ」
　先輩は早足で立ち去っていく。
　その後ろ姿を、俺たちは無言で見送った。
――――と。
「────遠野」
「なんだよ。
つまんない事なら聞かないからな」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Yes, that was probably our estate. I heard the police came by this morning.”
“―――I see. Tohno, please don’t stay out late at night.”
Ciel walks briskly away.
Arihiko and I watch her go in silence.
――――Then.
“────Tohno.”
“What? If it’s something stupid, I’m not listening.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yeah, that must be my house.
I heard the police came this morning to ask us questions."
"---Is that so?
You mustn't be out playing late at night, Tohno-kun."
Senpai leaves quickly.
I watch her silently.
---And,
"Tohno."
"What?
I'm not listening to any more of your trivial garbage."

entries.japanese:
「つまらなくはないぞ。
大きな疑問として、オマエはいつのまにあっちのほうから会いに来るぐらい先輩と親しくなってたんだろうな」
　じっ、と有彦は真剣な眼差しをしてくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“This is not stupid. It is a question of enormous importance: when did you and Ciel become close enough that she comes all this way to see you?”
Arihiko fixes me with an intensely serious stare.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"It's not trivial.
It's becoming a big problem.
You've become so familiar with Senpai that she even comes here to see you."
Arihiko stares at me gravely.

entries.japanese:
「さあ、俺に聞かれたってしるもんか。
話をするようになったのはここ最近だし、今日だって単なる気まぐれなんじゃないか？
　第一、そういうおまえだってえらく親しそうだったじゃないか」
「そうでもない。
オレは七日もかけてやっと名前を覚えてもらったレベルだよ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“How should I know? We only started talking recently, and today was probably a whim. Besides, you seemed awfully friendly with her yourself.” “Not really.
It took me seven full days just to make her remember my name.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Well, I don't know anything about it.
I've only started talking to her recently.
Maybe she just came here on a whim today?
And come to think of it, aren't you pretty familiar with her too?"
"No way, man.
It's taken me seven days to get her to remember my name."

entries.japanese:
「へえ、めずらしいな。
一日でなびかない女はめんどくさいから相手にしないっていうの、おまえのポリシーだったじゃないか」
「並みの女はそうだけど、先輩は別。
秘密にしていたんだけど、実はオレはな────」
「メガネが似合う上級生が好みだっていうんだろ」
　うっ、と有彦は頬を赤らめる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“That’s unusual. I thought your policy was that any girl who didn’t fall for you in one day was too much trouble.”
“That applies to ordinary women, but Ciel is different. I’ve kept this secret, but the truth is────”
“You have a weakness for older girls who look good in glasses.”
Arihiko’s cheeks redden.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Oh?
That's unusual.
Wasn't it your policy not to deal with girls you can't pick up in a day because they're too much trouble?"
"That's for normal girls, but Senpai is different.
I've kept it a secret all this time, but actually, I---"
"You like senior girls who look good with glasses on, don't you?"
"Erk!" Arihiko's face turns red.

entries.japanese:
「わかりましたか、親友」
「わかるよ。
俺たちは親友だからさ。
気が合うし、なにより趣味が似通ってるんだ」
「そうかそうか、遠野も先輩の良さがわかるのか────って、まて」
「ああ、俺たちは趣味が似てるんだろ？
　だから好きな女の子の好みも一緒なんじゃない？」
　有彦はなるほど、と納得すると自分の席に向かっていく。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You understand me, my friend.”
“Of course. We’re best friends. We get along, and above all, our tastes are similar.”
“So you appreciate Ciel’s charms too────wait.”
“Our tastes are alike, aren’t they? Wouldn’t that mean we like the same kind of girl?”
Arihiko considers this, nods, and heads back to his own seat.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"You knew all along, my dear friend."
"Yeah, I knew.
We're friends, after all.
We get along and we've got the same interests."
"I see, I see.
You can understand how good Senpai is too, can't you---hey, wait!"
"Yeah, like I said, we've got similar interests, right?
That's why we're into the same type of woman."
Arihiko nods in agreement, and heads back towards his own seat.

entries.japanese:
「短い友情だったな、遠野」
「ああ、まったくだ」
　ひらひらと手を振って有彦を送り出す。
　それとほぼ同時に、教室に担任が入ってきた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“It was a short friendship, Tohno.”
“Far too short.”
I wave Arihiko away.
At almost the same moment, our homeroom teacher enters the classroom.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I guess it was a short friendship, Tohno."
"Yeah, exactly right."
I wave Arihiko off.
The teacher comes in at about the same time.

entries.japanese:
学食でパンを買ってきて、教室でゆっくり昼食をとる事にした。
　……教室に残っているのは数名の男子と、女子の仲良しグループさんたちだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
I buy some bread from the cafeteria and decide to eat it at leisure in the classroom.
Only a few boys and several tight-knit groups of girls have stayed behind.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I decide to go buy some bread and eat it slowly in my classroom.
…… There are still a few guys and that close group of girls in here as well.

entries.japanese:
「………あれ？」
　今さら気がついた。
　女子の中で一番目立つ存在である弓塚さつきの姿が見えない。
「……欠席、か」
　クラスメイトの一人が休んでいた事を昼休みになって気がつくなんて、我ながら抜けていると思う。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Huh…?”
It takes me until now to notice.
Satsuki Yumizuka, easily the most conspicuous girl among them, is nowhere to be seen.
“Absent, then.”
Not realizing until lunch that one of my classmates is missing—pretty oblivious, even for me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Huh?"
I just noticed.
Yumizuka Satsuki, usually the most eye-catching of all the girls, is nowhere to be seen.
"…… She must be absent."
I must be pretty absent-minded to take until lunchtime to realize one of my own classmates isn't even here.

entries.japanese:
あいかわらず生徒で混雑している食堂で昼食をとることにした。
　うちの学食はどうしてか定食よりうどんやそばといった物のほうがおいしいので、自然にうどんを食べる事が定番になっている。
entries.maoEnglish:
I decide to eat in the cafeteria, as crowded with students as ever.
For some reason, our cafeteria’s udon and soba are much better than its set meals, so udon has naturally become my usual choice.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I decide to eat in the chaotic, student-filled cafeteria as usual.
For some reason, the udon and the soba are better than the meal sets at our school, so naturally I decide to have some udon.

entries.japanese:
テーブルに座って、たぬきうどんを食べる。
　食堂にあるテレビはニュースを映し出している。
　あのテレビはその日の朝のニュースやら昨夜のニュースやらを録画して、昼飯時に生徒たちに見せるという目的のものだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
I sit at a table with a bowl of tanuki udon.
The cafeteria television is showing the news.
It records the morning and late-night broadcasts, then plays them for students during lunch.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Sitting down at the table, I eat my tanuki udon.
The cafeteria's TV is showing the news.
The TV was set up so students can watch the recorded morning news during lunchtime.

entries.japanese:
ニュースは、例の連続殺人事件の特番だった。
　事件が始まってからじき一ヶ月ほど経過するというのに犯人像はまったく浮かび上がっていない。
　痕跡も動機もいっさいなし、という正体不明の殺人鬼。
　こんな狭い街だけで犠牲者が八人も出ているのにいまだ正体不明というのは、さすがにゾッとする、とニュースキャスターが喋っていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
Today it is airing a special on the serial murders.
Nearly a month has passed since they began, yet the police still have no picture of the culprit.
No evidence, no motive—an unidentified killer without so much as a shadow.
Eight people have died in this one small city, and the newsreader remarks that the killer’s continued anonymity is genuinely chilling.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The news is having a special feature on the serial killings.
It's been a whole month since the killings started, but no one yet has any idea who this killer is.
He is an unidentified killer demon, leaving no trace and acting with no motive.
His identity still remains a mystery, even though there has already been eight killings in our little town alone.
It's certainly very frightening, says the newscaster.

entries.japanese:
……茶道室に行ってみようか。
　たしか昨日の放課後、先輩は茶道室で昼食をとるコトがある、とか言っていた。
　もし先輩がいるんなら、先輩と話しながら昼食がとれるかもしれない。
―――なにより。
　先輩と昼食をとれるのは楽しいし、今朝のニュースとやらも気にかかる。
「―――よし」
　善は急げだ。
　有彦に嗅ぎ付けられる前に茶道室に行ってみよう。
entries.maoEnglish:
Maybe I’ll try the tea-ceremony room.
Yesterday after school, Ciel mentioned that she sometimes eats lunch there.
If she’s there today, perhaps we can eat and talk together.
―――More importantly.
I enjoy having lunch with her—and I’m curious about that news she mentioned this morning.
“―――Right.”
No time like the present.
I’ll reach the tea-ceremony room before Arihiko can sniff out my plans.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… I guess I'll go take a look in the tea ceremony room.
I'm sure Senpai said something yesterday after class about having lunch there.
If Senpai is there, maybe I can talk with her while having lunch.
---Most importantly,
I enjoy having lunch with Senpai, and I'm also worried about the news story from this morning.
"---Alright."
Gotta strike while the iron's hot and all.
I head off to the tea ceremony room before Arihiko notices my plan.

entries.japanese:
茶道室のドアをノックする。
　しばらく待つと、がらり、とドアが開いて先輩が顔を出した。
「あれ？
　遠野くんですね」
　不思議そうに先輩は首をかしげる。
　嫌がっている、というのではなく、本当に俺が茶道室に現れた理由がわからない、といった風である。
entries.maoEnglish:
I knock on the door.
After a short wait, it slides open and Ciel peeks out.
“Oh? Tohno.”
Ciel tilts her head in puzzlement.
She doesn’t look displeased; she simply cannot imagine what has brought me here.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I knock on the tea ceremony room door.
After a brief wait, the door creaks open and Senpai pokes out her head.
"Huh?
Tohno-kun?"
Puzzled, Senpai tilts her head.
She doesn't seem annoyed, but it seems like she really doesn't understand why I came here.

entries.japanese:
「先輩。
お昼ごはん、一緒に食べません？」
　購買で買ってきたパンをかかげて、率直に目的を口にした。
「お昼ごはんですか。
遠野くんにお誘いしていただけるのは嬉しいんですけど、その―――」
　うーん、と困ったふうに考え込む先輩。
　……雲行きがよろしくない。
　先輩はどうも乗り気ではなさそうだ。
　仕方ないので、ちょっとした小技を使うことにした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ciel. Would you like to have lunch together?”
I hold up the bread I bought and state my purpose plainly.
“Lunch? I’m happy you invited me, Tohno, but―――”
Ciel lapses into thought with a troubled look.
This isn’t going well.
She doesn’t seem eager.
That leaves me no choice but to try a little trick.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Would you like to have lunch together, Senpai?"
Holding out the bread I purchased at the cafeteria, I tell her why I am here.
"Lunch?
I'm happy to hear you ask me, but---"
Senpai thinks over it looking troubled.
…… Things don't look good.
It seems Senpai isn't very interested.
I guess I've got no choice.
I decide to employ a little strategy.

entries.japanese:
「カレーパン、ありますけど」
「え―――？」
　先輩の顔がほがらかになる。
　……昨日の昼食でなんとなく思っていたんだけど、ここまでわかりやすいリアクションをされるとなんかこっちまで嬉しくなる。
「昨日のお昼ごはんのお返しにあげますから、一緒に食べません？」
「はい、どうぞどうぞ！
　ちょうどお茶をいれてたところですから！」
　先輩はそそくさと中に入っていく。
　その後に続いて、茶道室へと入っていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I have curry bread.”
“What―――?”
Ciel’s face lights up.
I’d gotten an inkling at lunch yesterday, but seeing her react this openly makes me happy too.
“It’s repayment for yesterday, so will you eat with me?”
“Yes, please come in! I was just making tea!”
Ciel hurries back inside.
I follow her into the tea-ceremony room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I have curry bread."
"Eh---?"
Senpai's face becomes bright and cheerful.
…… I had a feeling about this from yesterday's lunch, but I am amused at her reaction.
"I'll give you this in thanks for yesterday's lunch, so why don't we eat together?"
"Yes, please!
I've just put the tea on!"
Senpai hastily vanishes inside.
Following her, I enter the tea ceremony room.

entries.japanese:
「あ……」
　入って、先輩が考え込んだ理由がはっきりした。
　畳の上には、すでに空っぽになったお弁当箱が一つある。
　先輩はとっくに昼食を食べ終えていたらしい。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh…”
Once inside, I understand why she hesitated.
An empty lunch box already rests on the tatami.
Apparently Ciel finished eating some time ago.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah……"
As I enter, it becomes obvious why Senpai was hesitating back then.
On top of the tatami mat is an already empty lunchbox.
It seems like Senpai has long since finished eating her lunch.

entries.japanese:
「遠野くん、お茶と紅茶どっちがいいですか？」
「えっ……ああ、お茶でいいですよ。
それより先輩、もうお昼すませちゃってたの？」
「ええ、ちょっと前に。
今日は寝坊してしまったので、朝ごはんを食べてなくて。
午前中はおなかがペコペコで大変でした」
「……そっか。
じゃあ無理して俺に付き合うコトはないよね。
ごめん、邪魔しちゃって。
　俺は教室で食べるから、どうぞゆっくりしててください」
「え―――パン、いただけないんですか？」
　心底哀しそうに、先輩はそんな言葉を呟いた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Would you prefer green tea or black tea, Tohno?”
“Oh, green tea is fine. More importantly, have you already eaten lunch?”
“Yes, a little while ago. I overslept and missed breakfast today. I was famished all morning.”
“…I see—then there’s no reason to make you keep me company. Sorry for disturbing you.
I’ll eat in the classroom, so please relax.”
“What—don’t I get the bread?”
Ciel murmurs, looking genuinely crushed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Tohno-kun, would you like green or English tea?"
"Eh?
…… Ah, green tea, please.
More importantly, have you already finished lunch, Senpai?"
"Yes, just a little while ago.
I slept in this morning, so I didn't have any breakfast and I was hungry all morning.
It was terrible!"
"…… I see.
Well, you don't have to force yourself to accompany me.
Sorry for intruding on you.
I'll eat in the classroom, so please take your time relaxing."
"Eh---?
You mean you're not going to give me any bread?"
Senpai's sorrow seems to resound from the bottom of her heart.

entries.japanese:
「いや、だって―――おなかいっぱいでしょ、先輩」
「そんなコトないです。
わたし、おなか減ってます」
　……こっちに気を使ってくれている……というワケではなさそうだ。
「そうですか。
じゃあお邪魔しますけど……先輩、ホントに大丈夫？
　うちの購買のパンってボリュームあるよ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“But―――you’re already full, aren’t you, Ciel?”
“Not at all. I’m hungry.”
She does not appear to be saying that out of consideration for me.
“All right, then I’ll stay. But are you sure? The bread from our school shop is pretty substantial.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No, I mean---you must be full, right, Senpai?"
"Not at all.
I'm hungry."
…… It doesn't appear she's just saying this to make me feel better.
"Really?
Well, I'll be intruding then… Is this really okay with you, Senpai?
The bread from our cafeteria really has volume, you know."

entries.japanese:
「ご心配にはおよびません。
わたし、好きなものならわりと限界なくいただけちゃいますから」
　はにかむような笑顔は、照れているのではなくてカレーパンを楽しみにしているためだろう。
「……………」
　……謎な人だ。
　カレーパン一つでここまで喜んでくれるなんて、いまどき貴重な人材かもしれない……。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You needn’t worry. When it’s something I like, I can eat almost without limit.”
Her bashful-looking smile must come from anticipation of the curry bread rather than shyness.
“…”
She is a mysterious person.
Anyone this delighted by a single curry bun may be a rare treasure in this day and age.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No need to worry!
If it's food I like, then I can eat limitless amounts of it."
That bashful smile is most probably not from shyness, but from anticipation of the curry bread.
"………"
…… She is a woman of many mysteries.
Someone who could be so happy over one curry bread in this day and age could be quite precious…

entries.japanese:
先輩はパンを一つ、こっちは二つ食べて、食後のお茶とあいなった。
　畳の上で正座をして、先輩とのんびりお茶をすする。
　これが学校の昼休みじゃなかったら最高なんだけど、そう上手くいかないのが人生か。
entries.maoEnglish:
Ciel eats one bun and I eat two, after which we settle down to tea.
Kneeling on the tatami, I sip in companionable silence with her.
If only this weren’t a school lunch break, it would be perfect—but life never works out quite that neatly.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Senpai eats one while I have two, and we have tea afterwards.
Kneeling on top of the mat, Senpai and I casually sip our tea.
It would have been great if it wasn't during lunchtime at school, but that's life.

entries.japanese:
「遠野くん、新しいお家のほうはどうですか？
　朝はなんかタイヘンな事になってたみたいですけど」
「んー、どうかなあ。
とりあえず家の中はすごく立派で、夜は野犬がうるさかったぐらいだよ。
　しいて言うんなら、テレビがないのと和室がないのがネックかな。
こんなふうにお茶を飲める場所がないから」
「？
　野犬って、なんですかそれ。
遠野さんの家で起きたのは例の通り魔事件なんじゃないですか？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“How is your new home, Tohno? Something rather serious seemed to be happening there this morning.”
“Hard to say. The house itself is magnificent, and the only trouble last night was a pack of noisy wild dogs.
If I had to complain, I’d say it needs a television and a Japanese-style room. There’s nowhere I can sit and drink tea like this.”
“Wild dogs? What do you mean? Wasn’t the incident at your home tied to those random street killings?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"How is your new house, Tohno-kun?
It seems something terrible happened this morning."
"Hmm… yeah.
Well, the inside of the house is really fancy, but there are these really noisy stray dogs at night.
I guess it's also bad that there's no TV and no Japanese-style rooms, so there's nowhere to drink tea like this."
"What, a stray dog?
You mean what happened at your house wasn't related to those serial killings?"

entries.japanese:
「さあ、俺にもよくわからない。
うちの屋敷ってまわりが全部高い塀なんだけど、そこで血痕があったんだって。
けどさ、そこって――――」
―――昨日の夜、野犬を見に行った場所なんだ。
　とは言えなかった。
「……んー、まあいいや。
どうせ俺たちには関係のない話だもんな。
せっかく先輩とのんびりしてるのに、イヤな話をするのはよそうか」
「そんなことありませんっ。
少なくともこの街で暮らしているんですから、通り魔事件は関係あると思います」
entries.maoEnglish:
“I don’t really understand it myself. The entire estate is surrounded by a high wall, and they found bloodstains beside it. But that’s where――――”
―――I went to look for the wild dogs last night.
I cannot bring myself to say it.
“…Well, never mind. It has nothing to do with us, and since I’m finally getting to relax with you, let’s not spoil it with ugly conversation.”
“That isn’t true. We both live in this city, so the random street killings have everything to do with us.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I don't really know.
There's this really high wall all the way around our mansion, and they say they found bloodstains there.
But listen, that's where---"
---I saw the stray dog last night.
I couldn't say it.
"…… Hmm.
Well, anyhow, it's got nothing to do with us.
Let's stop talking about unpleasant topics, now that we've finally got an opportunity to relax."
"Not at all!
We're residents of this town, so I think the killings do have something to do with us."

entries.japanese:
湯呑みを片手に、先輩はじっと真剣な眼差しを向けてきた。
「ああ、そりゃあそうだけどさ、夜に出歩かなきゃいいんじゃないか。
殺されちゃった人たちってもう八人だっけ？
　それだけ犠牲者が出てればもうじき警察が犯人を捕まえてくれるよ」
「―――もうっ。
遠野くん、それって全然危機感がありません。
ニュースだって犠牲者が三人目のころから同じようなコトを言ってましたけど、結局まだ犯人は捕まってないじゃないですかっ」
entries.maoEnglish:
Holding her teacup, Ciel fixes me with a grave stare.
“That’s true, but surely we’ll be safe if we stay indoors at night. Eight people have died now, haven’t they? With so many victims, the police must catch the killer soon.”
“―――Honestly. Tohno, you have no sense of danger at all. The news has been saying exactly that since the third victim, and the killer is still free!”
entries.mirrorMoon:
Holding her cup in one hand, Senpai casts a serious gaze towards me.
"Yeah, I guess that's true, but you'll be okay if you don't go walking in the streets late at night, won't you?
There's been eight people killed so far already, right?
With that many victims, the police ought to catch the guy any day now."
"---Geez, Shiki-kun!
You don't have any sense of danger, do you?
The newscasters have been saying the same thing since the third victim was found, but they haven't caught him yet, have they!?"

entries.japanese:
「ん……まあ、そうだね。
現代の吸血鬼、なんてふざけたテロップをうたれてるから、なんか身近な事件って気がしなくてさ。
　ごめん、たしかに軽率だった。
この街に住んでるんだから気をつけなくちゃいけないのにね」
「はい。
わかってくれればいいんです」
　にこり、と先輩は満足そうに笑った。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Mm… you’re right. The news keeps flashing ridiculous captions about a ‘modern-day vampire,’ so it never felt like an event close
to home. I’m sorry—that was careless, and since I live in this city, I should be more cautious.”
“Yes. As long as you understand.”
Ciel smiles, satisfied.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hmm… Well, that's true.
It's just that I can't really relate to it when they give it such a stupid caption like 'The Modern-Day Vampire'.
I'm sorry, I really did take it too lightly.
We live in this town, so we've got to be careful, right?"
"Yes.
I'm glad you understand."
Senpai smiles in a satisfied manner.

entries.japanese:
「けど先輩。
吸血鬼って言うけど、どうしてそんなあだ名がつくんだろう」
「だって体じゅうの血を抜かれているんですよ？
　そうゆうのって吸血鬼みたいじゃないですか」
「……そうかなあ。
吸血鬼に吸われた人間って、同じように吸血鬼になるっていうのが通説じゃないか。
ちゃんと殺されてしまった人たちの死体はあるんだから、わざわざ吸血鬼なんて名づけなくてもいいのにね」
　ははあ、と先輩は楽しそうに頷く。
「遠野くん、吸血鬼なんかがいるって本気で信じてるんですか？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“But Ciel, why call the killer a vampire in the first place?”
“The victims were drained of every drop of blood. Doesn’t that sound like a vampire?”
“…Does it? The usual story is that anyone bitten by a vampire becomes one too. They’ve found all the victims’ bodies, so there’s no need to drag vampires into it.”
Ciel nods with amused interest.
“Tohno, do you honestly believe vampires exist?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"But Senpai, why are they calling him a vampire anyway?"
"Well, the blood was drained from all the bodies, right?
Isn't that kind of like a vampire?"
"…… You really think so?
Isn't it said that you become a vampire yourself once a vampire sucks your blood?
These victims are all dead, with the corpses to prove it, so they don't really have to go calling him a vampire."
Senpai laughs and nods.
"Do you really believe in things like vampires, Tohno-kun?"

entries.japanese:
「……あのね。
ニュースでそうゆうふうに煽り立てているから、それに合わせただけだよ。
ホントに吸血鬼なんてのがいたら、さっき言った通り死体なんか残らないでしょ」
「そうですね。
けど、こういうふうにも考えられません？
　発見されている死体の方たちは、吸血鬼になれなかったから死んでしまった。
　吸血鬼にはなれる人となれない人とがいて、なれる人は吸血鬼に襲われても死体は発見されないんです。
　今も、どこかで生きているから」
entries.maoEnglish:
“…The news was sensationalizing it, so I played along. Like I said, if a real vampire were responsible, there wouldn’t be any bodies.”
“True. But couldn’t you also see it this way? The bodies they found belonged to people who died because they could not become vampires.
Some people can become vampires and others cannot; when the right kind of person is attacked, no body is ever discovered.
Because that person is still alive somewhere.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Hey now, I'm just saying that's how the news is presenting it.
If there really were vampires, there wouldn't be any dead bodies left, just like I said earlier."
"Yes, you're right.
But can't you think of it like this?
The people who were found dead died because they couldn't become vampires.
There are actually people who can and can't become vampires, and those who can become vampires wouldn't show up as dead bodies after being attacked by one.
Because they're still alive somewhere."

entries.japanese:
「ははあ。
そりゃあホラーだね、先輩」
「はい、わりとホラーな話です。
残念ですがオチはつきませんでした」
　あはは、と笑って、先輩は湯呑みを口にする。
　そんなとりとめのない事を話しているうちに、昼休みは終わってしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Wow. That’s quite a horror story.”
“Yes, it is. Unfortunately, I couldn’t think of an ending.”
Ciel laughs and raises her teacup to her lips.
Lunch break comes to an end as we talk about one thing and another.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Haha, that's what you'd call a horror story, Senpai."
"Yes, exactly.
I'm sorry to say there's no punch line."
Laughing, Senpai sips from her cup.
While we are having our rambling conversation, lunchtime ends.

entries.japanese:
五時限目。
　古文の授業に眠気を誘われつつ、窓の外に視線を移す。
――――と。
　教室のベランダに、鴉がとまっていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
Fifth period.
As classical literature slowly lulls me toward sleep, I turn my eyes to the window.
――――And there.
A crow is perched on the classroom balcony.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Fifth period.
Feeling sleepy at the classics lecture, my gaze drifts outside the window.
----And,
a crow is perched on the classroom veranda.

entries.japanese:
「―――――」
　昨夜の青い鴉じゃなくて、ただの黒い鴉だ。
　鴉は黒一色の目で、ガラスごしに教室の中を見つめている。
　たしかに鴉がとまっているのは珍しいけれど、別段、どうという事はない出来事だった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――――”
Not the blue crow from last night, but an ordinary black one.
Through the glass, it watches the classroom with eyes of seamless black.
A crow perching there is unusual, certainly, but there is nothing especially remarkable about it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-----"
Not the blue crow from last night, but just an ordinary black one.
With its black eyes, the crow stares inside the classroom through the glass window.
It's true that it's unusual for a bird to perch there, but it's not like it's some major event.

entries.japanese:
「あ――――」
　それは唐突にやってきた。
　視界がだんだんと白くなって、平衡感覚がぐるぐるとおかしくなっていく。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ah――――”
It strikes without warning.
My vision slowly bleaches white and my sense of balance begins to spin out of true.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah----"
Suddenly, it comes at me.
My vision gradually goes white as my sense of balance goes crazy.

entries.japanese:
「―――」
　くらり、と視界がゆらぐ。
　頭のうしろのほうに何かがわだかまって、意識がずん、と重くなる感覚。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――”
The world sways.
Something congeals at the back of my head, dragging my consciousness down beneath a sudden, crushing weight.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---"
My field of vision sways.
It feels like something is building up in the back of my head, and my brain feels heavy.

entries.japanese:
「……まず」
　この感覚は知っている。
突発的な眩暈は貧血の前触れだ。
　脳の血管にたまった血液が、黒い塊になってクラクラと頭を揺らして、見えているものを真っ暗にしていってしまう。
　例えるのなら、脳のほうから眼球の方向に闇が押し出されるような感覚。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Damn…”
I know this feeling. Sudden vertigo is the herald of anemia.
Blood pooled in the vessels of my brain thickens into a black mass, rocking my skull and steadily drowning everything I see in darkness.
It feels as though the darkness is being forced forward from my brain into my eyes.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Crap."
I know this feeling.
It's the precursor to an anemia attack.
The blood that's been building up inside the blood vessels in my brain forms black clots and slushes around inside my head, causing my vision to go black.
If I had to describe it, I would say it feels like darkness is pushing from my brain outwards towards my eyes.

entries.japanese:
―――まずいなあ……授業中に倒れるなんて、滅多に、なかったって、いうのに――――
　暗くなっていく視界の中、手探りで机をつかんで寄りかかる。
　それも、すぐに無駄になる。
　指先に力が入らない。
　あとはただ、床に向かって倒れこむだけ―――
entries.maoEnglish:
―――This is bad―――I almost never collapse during class anymore――――
As my sight darkens, I grope for the desk and try to brace myself against it.
That fails almost at once.
There is no strength in my fingers.
All that remains is to fall toward the floor―――
entries.mirrorMoon: ---This is bad… I don't usually collapse in the middle of class, but…

entries.japanese:
「先生、ちょっといいっすか」
―――と。
　どん、と乱暴に背中を叩かれた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Sir, can I interrupt?”
―――Then.
Something thumps me roughly between the shoulders.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Fumbling in a world of darkness, I blindly use my desk for support.
Even that becomes useless…
I can't put any strength into my fingers.
All I can do now is fall towards the floor---

entries.japanese:
「遠野のヤツ、調子が悪そうなんで保健室に連れていきたいんですけど」
「――――有彦」
　いつのまにか有彦がやってきている。
「遠野、本当に具合が悪いのか？」
　教壇から教師の声が聞こえてくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Tohno looks sick, so I’d like to take him to the infirmary.”
“――――Arihiko.”
Somehow Arihiko is standing beside me.
“Tohno, are you truly unwell?”
The teacher calls from the lectern.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Excuse me, Sensei."
---And,
something hits me roughly on the back.

entries.japanese:
「いえ、なんとか大丈夫―――」
「あー、ぜんっぜんダメだそうです。
こりゃあ早退させた方がいいんじゃないっすか？」
　……有彦は大声で、なんだかとんでもない事を言っている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“No, I can manage―――”
“Nope, he says he’s completely done for. Shouldn’t you send him home?”
Arihiko loudly puts an outrageous claim into my mouth.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Tohno's looking pretty bad, so I'd like to take him to the infirmary."
"----Arihiko."
At some point, Arihiko had come up to me.
"Are you really feeling bad, Tohno?"
I can hear the teacher's voice from his lectern.

entries.japanese:
「そうか。
乾がそう言うんじゃ間違いないな。
先生も遠野の体のことは国藤先生から聞いている。
　遠野。
体調が優れないなら保健室で休むか早退していいんだぞ」
　……まったく、人がいいのかなんなのか。
　古典の教師は有彦の言い分を全面的に信じているみたいだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I see. If Inui says so, there can be no doubt. Mr. Kunifuji has told me about your health, Tohno.
If you feel unwell, you may rest in the infirmary or go home.”
Honestly, I can’t tell whether he’s kind or merely gullible.
Our classics teacher seems to accept Arihiko’s every word.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No, I think I'll be fi---"
"Man, he's totally out of it.
Wouldn't it be better for him to leave early?"
…… Arihiko makes this outrageous proclamation loudly.

entries.japanese:
「ほら、帰っていいとよ。
そんな青い顔しやがって、まずいと思ったらすぐにまずいって言わねえとわからねえだろうが」
　有彦は不機嫌そうに人の背中を叩く。
「……それじゃあ早退させてもらいます、先生」
　うむ、と古典の教師は重々しく頷く。
entries.maoEnglish:
“There, you can go home. If you’re going to sit there white as a sheet, say so when you feel yourself going under—how else is anyone supposed to know?”
Arihiko thumps my back, looking annoyed.
“Then I’d like to go home, sir.”
The teacher nods with grave authority.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I see.
If you say so, Inui, then there's no mistake about it.
I've already heard about Tohno's health from Kunifuji-sensei.
Tohno, if you're not well, you may go rest in the infirmary or leave early."
…… Sheesh.
I don't know what's with him.
It seems the classics teacher has complete trust in what Arihiko says.

entries.japanese:
「……悪い、有彦。
いらない心配をかけさせた」
「気にすんな。
中学からの腐れ縁だからな、おまえが貧血でぶっ倒れそうな雰囲気ってのはすぐにわかんだよ」
　有彦は自分の席に戻っていく。
　さんきゅ、と目で礼を言って、まだ重苦しい体を動かして教室を後にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Sorry, Arihiko. I made you worry over nothing.”
“Forget it. We’ve been stuck with each other since middle school, so I can spot the look you get before anemia knocks you flat.”
Arihiko returns to his seat.
I thank him with my eyes, force my leaden body to move, and leave the classroom.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"C'mon, you can go now.
Your face is pale and all, but no one's going to know you're feeling bad until you tell them, you know."
Arihiko hits me in the back grumpily.
"…… I'll be leaving early then, Sensei."
The classics teacher nods solemnly.

entries.japanese:
―――学校を出た。
　本来なら保健室で横になったほうがいいのだが、この時間からだと起きる頃には放課後になってしまっている。
　それなら多少無理をして、屋敷に戻って横になったほうが無駄がないと判断したのだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――I leave the school.
I ought to lie down in the infirmary, but if I sleep now, it will be the end of the day before I wake.
Better to push myself a little farther and rest properly at the estate.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Sorry about making you worry needlessly, Arihiko."
"Don't worry about it.
We've been inseparable since middle school; I can tell when you're about to collapse from anemia."
Arihiko heads back towards his own seat.
Expressing my thanks with a look, I drag my leaden body out of class.

entries.japanese:
「……ふう。
ちょっとは楽になってきたかな」
　外の空気を吸っているうちに気分も持ちなおしてきた。
　……まったく、自分の体の事ながらまいってしまう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Whew. Maybe I’m starting to feel better.”
The outdoor air gradually restores me.
It is exhausting, being at the mercy of my own body.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---I leave school.
It would have been better to go lie down in the infirmary, but at this hour, it'd be after school by the time I wake up.
That being the case, I decide that I'd better go lie down back at the mansion, even if it means pushing myself.

entries.japanese:
八年前。
　命に関わる重症から回復した代償なのか、それからというもの遠野志貴は慢性的な貧血を起こす体質になってしまった。
　病院から退院した当時は一日に一回は貧血で倒れてしまって、眩暈をおこしてしまうなんていうのは日常茶飯事になってしまっていたのだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
Eight years ago, Shiki Tohno recovered from life-threatening injuries.
Perhaps this was the price: from then on, his body became prone to chronic anemia.
When I first left the hospital, I collapsed from anemia at least once a day, and dizzy spells became an ordinary feature of life.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Phew.
I think I'm feeling a little better."
I breathe in the outside air and feel a little rejuvenated.
…… Sheesh.
I'm surprised at my own body.

entries.japanese:
あれからずいぶんと月日がたって、体も成長しきったおかげか突発的な眩暈や貧血を起こしにくくなった。
　けれど、ときおり何かの弾みで眩暈を起こして、そのまま意識を失ってしまう事だけはなくならない。
　今日は有彦が途中で声をかけてくれたから良かったものの、いつもならあのまま地面に倒れていたところだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
Years have passed since then, and perhaps because my body is fully grown, the sudden vertigo and anemia come less often.
Yet every so often, something still sets off a spell and I lose consciousness where I stand.
Today Arihiko caught it in time; ordinarily, I would have gone straight to the floor.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Eight years ago.
The price of recovering from that near-fatal injury was becoming prone to sudden anemia.
When I first left the hospital, it would happen at least once a day.
Collapsing from dizziness became a daily routine for me.
After some time, probably because my body had grown, the spontaneous dizziness and anemia became rarer.
But from time to time, things still trigger dizzy fits, and I still lose consciousness.
Today I was lucky that Arihiko caught me.
Usually, I wind up passed out on the floor.
*sigh*
Taking a slow and deep breath, I draw fresh air into my lungs.
I can feel the blood pooled around the center of my head begin to swirl around again, so I head away from the school.

entries.japanese:
「――――はあ」
　ゆっくりと深呼吸をして、新鮮な空気を肺に送り込む。
　頭の芯に沈澱した血のめぐりをなんとか堪えながら、学校を後にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――Haaah.”
I breathe slowly and deeply, filling my lungs with fresh air.
Enduring the stagnant weight deep inside my skull, I leave the school behind.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I veer onto the main street.
Once I get through here and leave the residential district, it's a direct path to the Tohno mansion.
"--Agh."
…… Crap.
It looks like I haven't fully recovered yet.
Putting my hand to my forehead, I realize it's hotter than usual.

entries.japanese:
大通りに出る。
　ここを抜けて住宅街に出てしまえば、遠野の屋敷まで一直線だ。
「――――う」
　……いけない。
　まだ気分が晴れていないみたいだ。
　額に手を当ててみれば、普段より熱をもっている。
entries.maoEnglish:
I reach the main avenue.
Once I cross it and enter the residential district, the road runs straight to the Tohno estate.
“――――Ugh.”
This is bad.
I’m still not well.
When I touch my forehead, it feels warmer than usual.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……"
I'm not going to do myself any good by pushing myself here until I collapse along the side of the road.
"---I guess there's no helping it."
Disgusted with myself, I lean on the guardrail.
I'll rest for a bit until I manage to calm down.

entries.japanese:
「…………」
　このまま無理をして道端で倒れこんでは元も子もない。
「―――しょうがないな、ほんと」
　自分自身にあきれながらガードレールに腰をかける。
　気分が落ち着くまで少し休む事にしよう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
There is no sense pushing on until I collapse beside the road.
“―――Honestly, what a nuisance.”
Disgusted with myself, I sit on the guardrail.
I’ll rest until the sickness passes.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… I don't have much to do, so I just stare idly around the street.
It's just past noon on a weekday, but the street is filled with passers-by.
Crowds of walking people.
Nameless people without personalities walk straight ahead, without even casting a glance at the people walking beside them.
Even though there are so many people here together in this crowd, in this same space, they see only one thing.

entries.japanese:
……やることもないので、ぼんやりと大通りの様子を眺める。
　平日の午後を過ぎたばかりだというのに、大通りは行き交う人々で賑わっていた。
　歩いていく大勢の人たち。
　名前も素性も知らない彼らは、すぐ隣で歩いている誰かに視線をなげかける事なく前へ前へと歩いていく。
　同じ場所に、これだけ大勢の人間がいるというのに、誰も彼も視界は一つきりだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
With nothing else to do, I stare vacantly at the avenue.
Though a weekday afternoon has barely begun, the avenue is already thronged.
People stream past on foot.
I know none of their names or histories, and none of them spares a glance for the stranger at their side.
So many people occupy the same place, yet each sees the world through a single, solitary pair of eyes.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Everyone is their own main character, so they only live the day from that perspective.
And so, without really interacting with anyone else, they each end the day by themselves.

entries.japanese:
自分が自分の主役であるように、彼らは彼らが主役の一日を過ごしている。
　そして、それぞれの一日はたいていは誰かと交わる事なく、やっぱり自分だけの一日で終わってしまう。
 ───それは、ある意味。
　孤独といえば、ひどく孤独なことだと言えた。
「……………」
　微熱のせいか、感傷的な考え事をしてしまう。
entries.maoEnglish:
Just as I am the center of my own story, each of them is living a day that revolves around them.
Most of those days never truly intersect; each ends, as it began, belonging to one person alone.
───Seen one way.
There is something terribly lonely in that.
“…”
Perhaps the fever is making me sentimental.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---In a way, you could say it's a very lonely thing.
"……"
I begin to think melancholy thoughts, perhaps a result of my fever.
"---Guess I'll go home now."
I feel calmer, and all I'm doing here is wasting my time with pointless thoughts.
Getting up from the guardrail, I resume heading home to the mansion so I can rest.
---That is, until I see her.

entries.japanese:
「―――帰ろ」
　気分も落ち着いてきたし、ここにこうしていても意味のない事を考え込む一方だし。
　さっさと屋敷に帰って休むためにガードレールから腰をあげた。
 ─────その女を、見てしまうまでは。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――Time to go.”
I feel steadier now, and sitting here will only tempt me into more pointless brooding.
I rise from the guardrail, intending to hurry home and rest.
─────That is, until I see that woman.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Casually.
All I did was casually cast my gaze into the crowd, but my vision freezes.

entries.japanese:
なにげなく。
　本当になにげなく、人込みに視線をなげただけだったのに、視界が凍った。
 ───ドクン。
　金の髪と赤い瞳。
　白い、彼女の像を象徴するかのような白い服装。
entries.maoEnglish:
Idly.
Entirely without thought, I merely let my gaze wander across the crowd—and my vision freezes.
───THUMP.
Golden hair and scarlet eyes.
Clothes of white—white as though the color itself were the emblem of her existence.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Thump.
Golden hair and red eyes.
Her clothes are white, as if they are a symbol of herself.
---Thump.
My pulse races.
My veins and arteries spring into action.
My nerves split, one after the other.
My spinal cord goes berserk, as if it is about to leap out of my back.

entries.japanese:
───どくん。
　脈拍がはねあがる。
　静脈と動脈が活性化する。
　神経は次々と破裂していって、脊髄が首の後ろに飛び出してしまいそうなほど、体の中身が暴れだしてる。
entries.maoEnglish:
───thump.
My pulse leaps.
Veins and arteries surge awake.
Nerves burst one after another, everything inside me thrashing so violently that my spinal cord feels ready to tear through the back of my neck.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Thump.
The girl walking in the crowd is just… beautiful.
"------"
The distant dizziness comes back to me.
My consciousness swims, falling.

entries.japanese:
───ドクン。
　人込みの中で歩いている女性は、ただ、美しかった。
「――――――――」
　遠くなっていた眩暈が戻ってくる。
　くらり、と意識が落ちかける。
entries.maoEnglish:
───THUMP.
The woman walking through the crowd is simply beautiful.
“――――――――”
The dizziness that had receded floods back.
My consciousness pitches, almost falling away.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----Thump.
I-I can't breathe.
My fingertips tremble.
The blood isn't reaching them.
My whole body feels cold, like I'm freezing to death.

entries.japanese:
―――――どくん。
　息ができない。
　指先は震えて、血液が届いてない。
　全身のいたるところが寒くて、凍死してしまいそうだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――――thump.
I cannot breathe.
My fingertips tremble, starved of blood.
Every inch of me is cold—as though I might freeze to death.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----THUMP.
My heart beats in a rush, urging me to hurry up.
"Ah--ah!"
I can stand it no longer and unintelligible words escape my mouth.

entries.japanese:
―――――ドクン。
　心臓が急いで、早く早くと命令してくる。
「あ―――――あ」
　耐えきれなくなって、喉から喘ぎ声をもらした。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――――THUMP.
My heart commands me: hurry, hurry.
“Ah―――――ah.”
Unable to endure it, I let a moan escape my throat.
entries.mirrorMoon:
-----I can't think.
My brain tells me only one word.
----TH-U-MP.
Just one word repeating in my brain.
Her.
That girl.
I'm going to----

entries.japanese:
────考えられない。
　ある一つの単語しか、俺の脳味噌は生み出してくれてない。
―――――ド、ク、ン。
　そうして、繰り返される言葉はただ一つ。
　彼女を。
　あの女を。
　オレは、このまま─────
entries.maoEnglish:
────I cannot think.
My brain will give me only a single word.
―――――TH—UM—P.
Only one fragment keeps repeating.
Her.
That woman.
I, like this─────
entries.mirrorMoon:
*wheeze* *wheeze* *wheeze*
I feel sick.
I can't breathe.
It hurts to breathe.
For some reason, I can't remember how to breathe properly.

entries.japanese:
『ぜー、ぜー、ぜー』
　吐き気がする。
　呼吸ができない。
　息がくるしい。
　正しい息の仕方を、どうしても思い出せない。
entries.maoEnglish:
『Haa—haa—haa』
I feel sick.
I cannot breathe.
Every breath is agony.
No matter how I try, I cannot remember the proper way to breathe.
entries.mirrorMoon:
*wheeze* *wheeze* *wheeze*
My throat is burning.
My eyes are about to burst.
My palms are soaked.
I feel so cold--but I'm drenched in sweat.

entries.japanese:
『ぜー、ぜー、ぜー』
　喉がアツイ。
　眼球が砕けそうだ。
　手のひらはぐしょぐしょに濡れている。
　体中が寒いのに────こんなにも、汗をかいてしまっている。
entries.maoEnglish:
『Haa—haa—haa』
My throat is burning.
My eyes feel ready to shatter.
My palms are drenched.
My whole body is freezing—and yet I am sweating this much.
entries.mirrorMoon:
*pant* *pant* *pant*
…… I have to follow her.
I have to follow that girl.
Chase her, chase after her, and talk to her.
My frozen feet begin to move.
My breathing is ragged, like that of a beast.
I chase after the girl in white.

entries.japanese:
「はあ────はあ─────はあ────」
　……追わないと。
　あの女を追わないと。
　追って、追いかけて、話をしよう。
　凍った足を動かして、
　ケモノのように呼吸を荒くして、
　白い女を追いかけた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Haa────haa─────haa────”
I have to follow her.
Follow that woman.
Catch up and speak to her.
I force my frozen legs to move,
panting like an animal—
and pursue the woman in white.
entries.mirrorMoon:
*pant* *pant* *pant*
The girl walks slowly.
She doesn't realize I'm following her.
"Ha----ah."
If I run after her now, I can talk to her.
Talk to her, and ask her name…

entries.japanese:
「はあ────はあ────はあ────」
　女はゆっくりと歩いている。
　尾行しているこっちには気がついていない。
「は―――――あ」
　ここからなら走れば話しかけられる。
　話しかけて、名前を聞こう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Haa────haa────haa────”
The woman walks slowly.
She has not noticed me following her.
“Haa―――――ah”
If I run, I can catch her from here.
I’ll speak to her and ask her name.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ha----ahah, ha."
---Ask her name?
Who am I kidding?
I know very well that that's not what I want to do.
…… I know, but I don't know.
It looks like I want to do something else.
But I can't precisely put "what I want to do" in words.
The inside of my head is misted over, like a rain cloud.

entries.japanese:
「は―――――はは、は」
―――名前を聞く？
　冗談じゃない。
　オレはそんな事をしたいんじゃないって、自分でよくわかってる。
　……よくわかっているつもりなのに、よくわからない。
　オレは他のコトがしたいみたいなのに。
　どうしても、その『やりたいコト』とやらがはっきりと言葉にできない。
　頭の中に、雨雲みたいな霧がある。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Haa―――――ha, ha”
―――Ask her name?
Don’t make me laugh.
I know perfectly well that isn’t what I want.
I think I understand it perfectly, yet I understand nothing.
I want to do something else to her.
But no matter how I reach for it, whatever it is I want refuses to take the shape of words.
There is a fog inside my head, dark and swollen like a raincloud.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-------"
My throat is… hot.
I can't breathe.
But so what?
It's only natural, right?
I've just seen that great woman… it would be impolite not to get excited, wouldn't it?
Stop her and ask her name?
Hah!
Give me a break.
I'm not a kid, after all.
I don't fully understand it, but there is only one thing I must do.

entries.japanese:
「―――――――」
　ノドがアツイ。
　さっきから全然イキがデキナイ。
　だが、それがどうした。
　そんなのは当然だろう？
　あれだけの女を目の前にしたんだ、興奮しないほうが失礼ってもんじゃないか？
　呼び止めて名前を聞く？
　ハッ、ガキじゃあるまいし止してくれ。
　よくわからないけど。
オレがやるべき事は、それこそただ一つだけだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――――――”
My THROAT is BURNING.
I haven’t been able to BREATHE at all.
So what?
Isn’t that natural? With a woman like that before me, it would be an insult not to be excited.
Stop her and ask her name?
Hah. Spare me the childish nonsense.
I don’t understand, but there is only one thing I’m meant to do.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I walk with my hands in my pockets.
My fingers feel steel.
"Ku----huhh.
Hehe."
How fortunate.
The tools are all here.

entries.japanese:
ポケットに手をいれて歩く。
　かつん、と指先には鉄の手触り。
「く──────ク」
　なんて幸運。
　道具は、まさにそろってる。
entries.maoEnglish:
I walk with one hand in my pocket.
Something iron taps against my fingertips.
“Khh──────kh”
What perfect luck.
I have exactly the tool I need.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… She walks.
I leave plenty of room between us.
So she won't notice.
So the other people around us won't suspect.
She and I are complete strangers.
That's why I have to do my best to make following her look natural.

entries.japanese:
……女は歩いていく。
　十分に距離をとろう。
　気付かれないように、周囲の連中に不審に思われないように。
　オレとあの女は赤の他人だ。
　だから出来るだけ自然に、あの女の後をつけなくてはいけない。
entries.maoEnglish:
The woman keeps walking.
I should leave plenty of distance.
She must not notice me; the people around us must see nothing suspicious.
That woman and I are complete strangers.
I have to follow her as naturally as possible.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… She walks into an apartment building.
I don't go in yet, but instead watch from outside.
She takes the elevator up.
The elevator stops at the sixth floor.
I check the common mailbox on the first floor.
There are five mailboxes for the sixth floor.
I touch one of them and feel a sharp sensation.
I smell it.
There's no mistake.
Her room is the third one on the sixth floor.

entries.japanese:
……女がマンションに入っていく。
　まだ中には入らず、外から様子を眺めた。
　女はエレベーターに乗って、上の階へとあがっていく。
　エレベーターは六階で止まった。
　一階にある共通のポストを調べる。
　六階のポストは五つ。
そのうちの一つに触れて、ぞくりときた。
　匂いをかぐ。
　間違いない。
　六階の三号室が、彼女の部屋だ。
entries.maoEnglish:
She enters an apartment building.
I remain outside and watch.
She takes the elevator upward.
It stops on the sixth floor.
I inspect the communal mailboxes on the ground floor.
There are five for the sixth floor. The instant I touch one, a thrill runs through me.
I smell it.
No mistake.
Apartment 603 is hers.
entries.mirrorMoon: I enter the elevator and press six.

entries.japanese: エレベーターに入って、六階のボタンを押した。
entries.maoEnglish: I step into the elevator and press the button for the sixth floor.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I'm excited.
I grip the knife in my pocket tightly while in the small elevator.
She's very close by.
Just a little more, and I can      her.
Ah, just thinking about it makes me feel ecstatic--
My whole body feels like a sexual organ just before climax.

entries.japanese:
わくわくする。
　エレベーターという狭い密室の中で、ポケットの中のナイフを握り締めた。
　すぐそばにあの女がいる。
　あともうすこしであの女を　　　　できる。
　ああ、そう考えるだけでひどい快感────
　体中が、絶頂を控えた生殖器にでもなった気分。
entries.maoEnglish:
I can hardly contain my excitement.
Inside the elevator’s cramped little box, I clutch the knife in my pocket.
That woman is only moments away.
Soon I’ll finally be able to          her.
Ah, just thinking about it is unbearable pleasure────
My entire body feels like one vast sexual organ poised on the brink of climax.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I get off the elevator.
The sixth floor corridor is empty.
This is good.
Quickly----quickly!
I want to do it.

entries.japanese:
エレベーターから出る。
　六階の廊下に人影はない。
　ますます好都合だ。
　早く────早く、ヤリタイ。
entries.maoEnglish:
I leave the elevator.
The sixth-floor corridor is deserted.
Better and better.
Hurry────hurry, I WANT TO DO IT.
entries.mirrorMoon: ----I arrive in front of Room Three.

entries.japanese: ────三号室の前についた。
entries.maoEnglish: ────I reach the door of apartment 603.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I am about to press the doorbell when I stop.
These glasses are in my way.
I can't do what I've come to do with them on.
---It's a promise, Shiki.
You should never cut those lines thoughtlessly---
"……"
Long ago, a woman once told me such a thing.
But right now, neither her name nor her face comes to mind.
Slowly, I remove my glasses.

entries.japanese:
呼び鈴を押そうとして、止めた。
　メガネは邪魔だ。
　こんなものをしていては出来る事も出来やしない。
―――約束よ、志貴。
　決して、軽はずみな気持ちでモノを視ちゃダメだからね―――
「………」
　遠い昔に、そう言ってくれた女の人がいた。
　でも、今は名前も顔も思い出せない。
　ゆっくりとメガネを外した。
entries.maoEnglish:
I reach for the doorbell, then stop.
My glasses will only get in the way.
With them on, I won’t be able to do what I need to.
―――Promise me, Shiki.
Never look at things on a whim―――
“…”
Long ago, a woman said those words to me.
But now I can remember neither her name nor her face.
Slowly, I take off my glasses.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I can see the black lines.
And not just them.
Has something happened to my eyes?
Apart from those abominable lines, I can see 'points', like black holes.
Countless numbers of them.
I don't know myself.
What I'm trying to do.
Why I'm trying to do this.
What does Tohno Shiki-----want to do with that girl?

entries.japanese:
黒い線が、視える。
　それだけじゃない。
　この両目までどうかしてしまったのか。
　視界には、忌まわしい線ばかりか黒い穴のような『点』が、無数に見えてしまっていた。
　自分でもワカラナイ。
　自分は何をしようとしているのか。
　自分はなんだってこんな事をしているのか。
　遠野志貴は────さっきの女を、どうしたいのか。
entries.maoEnglish:
The black lines come into view.
And not only those.
Have even my eyes gone wrong?
Alongside those hateful lines, I can see countless black points, like holes punched through the world.
EVEN I DON’T KNOW.
What am I about to do?
Why am I doing any of this?
What does Shiki Tohno want to do to the woman he has just seen?
entries.mirrorMoon:
I don't know.
Still not knowing, I push the doorbell.

entries.japanese:
ワカラナイ。
　ワカラナイママ、チャイムヲ押シタ。
entries.maoEnglish:
I DON’T KNOW.
STILL NOT KNOWING, I PRESS THE BELL.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yes---?"
I hear the voice behind the door, and the door opens a crack.
In that instant------I slip through it.

entries.japanese:
「はい───」
　扉ごしに声がして、扉がかすかに開く。
　瞬間────そのわずかな隙間から部屋の中に滑り込んだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Yes—?”
A voice comes through the door, and it opens a crack.
In that instant, I slip through the narrow gap and into the room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Eh----"
The girl says.
No, she tries to say.
She will never get to finish what she tried to say.
Because I cut her apart before she could.

entries.japanese:
「え────」
　女の声があがる。
　否、あがろうとした。
　女の声があがりきる事は永遠にない。
　その前に、オレは彼女をバラしていたから。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Wha────”
The woman cries out.
No—she tries to.
Her voice will never finish rising.
Before it can, I have already taken her apart.
entries.mirrorMoon:
In that instant, I slip through the door.
Not taking even a second, I draw the knife across the lines running throughout the girl's body.
Stabbing.
Slashing.
Piercing.
Driving.
Splitting into pieces.
Completely and utterly, I 'kill' her.

entries.japanese:
ドアから中に入った瞬間。
　一秒もかけず、女の体じゅうに走っていた線をナイフでなぞった。
　刺し、
　切り、
　通し、
　走らせ、
　ざっくざっくに切断し。
　完膚なきまでに、「殺した」。
entries.maoEnglish:
The instant I cross the threshold.
In less than a second, I trace every line across her body with the knife.
Stabbing,
slicing,
driving the blade through,
racing it onward,
hacking her to pieces.
until I utterly and completely ‘kill’ her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The black lines that divide her into seventeen pieces.
Through the neck, back of the head, from the right eye to the lips, upper right arm, lower right arm, right ring finger, left elbow, left thumb, left middle finger, left breast, from the rib to the heart, from the stomach to the abdomen in two places, left groin, left thigh, left leg, left toe, all of them.
As I pass by her,
not even taking a second.
Truly, in an instant, entirely.
I "dismantle" her into seventeen pieces of meat.

entries.japanese:
女の体にある計十七個の黒い線、
　首、後頭部、右目から唇まで、右腕上腕、右腕下部、右手薬指、左腕肘、左手親指、中指、左乳房、肋骨部分より心臓まで、胃部より腹部まで同二ヶ所、左足股、左足腿、左足脛、左足指その全て。
　すれ違いざまに、
　一秒の時間さえかけず。
　真実　瞬く間に　ことごとく。
　彼女を、十七個の肉片に『解体』した。
entries.maoEnglish:
The seventeen black lines on her body,
from neck, head, right eye, and lips through arms, fingers, breast, ribs, heart, abdomen, groin, left leg, and toes—all of them.
As we pass each other,
without taking even one second.
truly—in the blink of an eye—every last one.
I ‘disassemble’ her into seventeen pieces of meat.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Eh?"
I can hear an incredibly dumb-sounding voice.
It doesn't feel like the voice is coming from my own throat.
Dizziness.
The minced pieces of the girl lie before my eyes.
Red blood all over the wooden floor, like an overturned bucket of water.

entries.japanese:
『―――え？
』
　すごく間の抜けた声が聞こえた。
　それが自分の喉から出た音だというコトに実感がわかなかった。
　くらり、と眩暈がおこる。
　目の前にはバラバラに散らばった女の体。
　フローリングの床には、バケツの水を引っくり返したように赤い血が広がっていっている。
　むせかえる血の匂い。
　切断面はとてもキレイで、臓物はこぼれていない。
　ただ赤い色だけが、地面を侵食していっている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――Huh?”
A spectacularly stupid voice reaches my ears.
I can’t believe the sound came from my own throat.
A wave of dizziness sweeps over me.
The woman’s body lies scattered in pieces before me.
Red blood spreads across the wooden floor as if someone has overturned a bucket of water.
The smell of blood is suffocating.
The severed surfaces are perfectly clean; no organs have spilled out.
Only the red keeps eating its way across the floor.
entries.mirrorMoon:
There is the choking scent of blood.
The cuts are very clean, so her insides don't spill out.
Only the color of red goes across the ground.
Strange.
There is nothing in the room.
