Nothing but the girl's scattered limbs and me, standing there dumbfounded.

entries.japanese:
不思議なはなし。
　部屋には何もなくて、ただ、バラバラになった女の手足と、自分だけが、呆然と立っている。
entries.maoEnglish:
Strangest of all, the room is empty.
There is nothing here but the woman’s severed limbs and me, standing among them in a daze.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---What---"
A sea of red blood is spreading over the floor.
In my hands, I grip my knife, the murder weapon.
"She's----dead."
Of course she is.
She wouldn't be human if she was alive.

entries.japanese:
『───なに、を───』
　フローリングの床に広がっていく赤い血の海。
　自分の手には凶器のナイフが握られている。
『死ん───でる』
　当たり前だ。
　これで生きていたら人間じゃない。
entries.maoEnglish:
『───What did I───』
A sea of red blood spreads across the floor.
In my hand is the knife that did it.
『She’s───dead』
Of course she is.
If she could survive this, she wouldn’t be human.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Wh----y?"
There's nothing to ask.
I just did it with my own hands.
With my own hands, cleanly and instantly, I cut apart this girl I don't even know.

entries.japanese:
『なん───で？
』
　なんでもなにもない。
　たった今、自分の手で。
　遠野志貴の手で、あっさりと、一瞬にして、見知らぬ女をバラバラにしてしまったんじゃないか。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Why───?”
There is no why.
I have just done it with my own hands.
With the hands of Shiki Tohno, I have casually and effortlessly torn a strange woman to pieces in a single instant.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I----killed her?"
Yes, there's no mistaking it.
Or am I mistaken?
There's no reason for me to do such a thing.
That's why it's a mistake.
It has to be a mistake.

entries.japanese:
『俺が────殺した？
』
　そう間違いなく。
　それとも違うのだろうか。
　自分には、そんなことをする理由がない。
　だから違う、違うはずだ。
　けど理由なんてものは初めからなかった。
　だから違う、違うはずだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I────killed her?”
Without question.
Or could that be wrong?
I have no reason to do such a thing.
So it is not true—it cannot be.
But there was never any reason in the first place.
So it is not true—it cannot be.
entries.mirrorMoon:
But I had no reason from the start.
That's why it's a mistake.
It has to be a mistake.

entries.japanese:
―――フローリングの床に、赤い血が広がっていく。
　ぬらり、と。
　足元に、赤い血が伝わってくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Red blood keeps spreading across the wooden floor.
Slickly.
Red blood creeps toward my feet.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---The red blood flows all over the floor.
Slowly, the dark red stain creeps around my feet.

entries.japanese:
『………………あ』
　驚いて靴をあげるけれど、間にあわない。
　女の赤い血は、コールタールのように、ねっとりと足と床に糸を引いた。
　
『―――――――』
　ああ……あかい、ち、だ
　オレがバラバラにしてしまったから、いまも、だらだらとだらしなく流れ続けている厭な色。
entries.maoEnglish:
『――――――Ah』
I jerk my shoe up, but too late.
The woman’s red blood clings like coal tar, drawing thick threads between my foot and the floor.
『―――――――――』
Ah―――red blood
That hateful color, still spilling without end because I cut her to pieces.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……… Ah!"
Surprised, I lift my shoe, but I'm too late.
Like coal tar, her blood makes a thread connecting the pool on the floor and my foot.
"---------"
It's… red… blood…
The color I hate, still flowing even now.
All because I cut her apart.

entries.japanese:
「―――俺じゃ、ない」
　ソウ、違ウハズ。
　違う。
違う。
きっと違う、ぜったいに違う。
　これは。
　これは、これは、これは、これは、これはこれはこれはこれは―――――――
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――It wasn’t me.”
YES, IT HAS TO BE WRONG.
Wrong. Wrong. It has to be wrong, absolutely wrong.
This was.
This, this, this, this, thisthisthisthis―――――――
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---It wasn't me."
Yes.
It has to be a mistake.
A mistake.
A mistake.
Probably a mistake, definitely a mistake.
This is.
This is, This is, This is, This is, This is This is This is This is This is This is----

entries.japanese:
……こんなのは、悪いユメだ。
　けど、なんだってこう、血の匂いだけがひどくリアルなんだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
This was a nightmare.
But why, then, was the smell of blood so horribly real?
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… This is just a bad dream.
But somehow, this stench of blood smells so horribly real.

entries.japanese:
『……違、う』
　そう。
　違う　違う　違う　違う。
　違う　違う　違う　違う。
　だが。
　自分が殺したというコトが違うのか。
　それとも、自分が殺していないという事が違うのか。
entries.maoEnglish:
『No―――that’s wrong』
Yes.
Wrong, wrong, wrong, wrong.
Wrong, wrong, wrong, wrong.
But.
Was it wrong that I had killed her?
Or was it wrong that I had not?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Wro… ng…"
Yes.
Wrong wrong wrong wrong.
Wrong wrong wrong wrong.
But.
I killed her.
Is that fact wrong?

entries.japanese:
『……だって、理由が、ない』
　いや、理由ならはっきりしてる。
　彼女を見た時、一つの事しか考えられなくなっていたから。
『俺は────』
　そう、俺は───
　　　遠野志貴は　あの女を　殺したい、と。
　それが、あの時の俺の意志だったハズだ。
　ただ、頭の中がドロドロとしていて、あえて、そのイメージを言葉にしようとしなかっただけで。
entries.maoEnglish:
『But―――there was no reason』
No—the reason was perfectly clear.
The moment I saw her, I became incapable of thinking about anything else.
『I────』
Yes, I───
Shiki Tohno wanted to kill that woman.
That must have been what I wanted then.
My thoughts had only been too thick and muddy for me to force that image into words.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I didn't kill her.
Is that fact wrong?

Yes, I---
Tohno Shiki    wanted to kill    that girl.
That's what I wanted to do back then.
Just that, it was all so muddy inside my head, I didn't put it into words.

entries.japanese:
『ちが─────う 』
　血の匂いに、吐き気がする。
『あ―――ぐ』
　胃の中のものが、戻ってくる。
『あ―――あ』
　眼球に、赤い朱色がしみ込んでくる。
　くらり、と眩暈がして。
　そのまま、赤い血の海にひざまずいた。
entries.maoEnglish:
『No─────』
The smell of blood made me sick.
『Ah―――gh』
Everything in my stomach surged back up.
『A―――ah』
Scarlet seeped into my eyes.
The room swayed.
My knees buckled, and I sank into the sea of red blood.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Wro----ng!"
I feel like throwing up from the smell of blood.
"Ah---guh!"
The contents of my stomach rise in my throat.
"Ah---ah!"
The crimson is soaking into my eyeballs.
I feel dizzy.
I fall down on my knees into the red sea of blood.

entries.japanese:
「あ―――ぐっ…………！」
　胃液が逆流する。
　胃の中のものを残らず吐いた。
　食い物も、胃液も、泣きながら吐き出した。
　胃の中には何もない。
　なのに起きてしまった出来事をなかった事に、もとの日常に戻そうとするかのように、体は嘔吐を強制する。
　ご――――ぶ。
　痛い。
　内蔵が焼けてるみたいに、痛い。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ah―――ghh…!”
Acid flooded up my throat.
I vomited everything in my stomach.
Food and bile—I sobbed and brought it all up.
Soon there was nothing left in my stomach.
Even so, my body forced me to retch, as if it could vomit away what had happened and drag me back into my ordinary life.
Ghhhhh.
It hurt.
It hurt as though my insides were on fire.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah---Guh……!"
My gastric juices come up.
I throw everything back up.
My food, my gastric juices, everything, while I cry.
There is nothing left in my stomach.
But my body continues to force me to throw up, as if trying to undo what had occurred and return me to a normal life.
Guuh----burgh!
Pain.
It hurts, like my insides are burning.

entries.japanese:
涙は止まらなくて、体はゴミのように地面に崩れ落ちた。
　広がっていく赤い水たまりに、膝が沈む。
　べちゃりと、体が赤く染まる。
　痛くて赤くて、ユメを見ているみたいだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
The tears would not stop.
My body collapsed like garbage.
My knees sank into the widening red pool; I fell with a wet slap and came away stained crimson.
Everything hurt, everything was red, and it all felt like a dream.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The tears won't stop, and my body collapses to the floor like a pile of garbage.
My knees sink into the red puddle spread all over the floor.
Red starts to stain my body.
It's so painful and red; it's like I'm dreaming.

entries.japanese:
「あ―――――あ………！」
　涙が止まらない。
　人を殺したというコトが、ひどく悲しかった。
　……いや、それは違う。
　人形でもバラすみたいにあっさりと、何の意味もなく、容赦なく殺してしまったコトが、悲しかった。
 ───よくわからない。
　どうしてこんな気分になっているのか、
　どうしてわけもなく殺してしまったのか、
　その理由が解らない。

『────うそだ』
entries.maoEnglish:
“Aaaaaah…!”
I couldn’t stop crying.
It was unbearably sad that I had killed someone.
No—that wasn’t it.
I was grieving because I had killed her so casually, so meaninglessly and mercilessly, as if I had merely pulled apart a doll.
───I didn’t understand.
Why I felt this way,
why I had killed her for no reason,
I understood none of it.
『────It’s a lie』
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah-----Aaah……!"
I keep crying.
The fact that I killed someone is making me sad.
…… No.
That's not right.
I am sad because I killed her without reason, like breaking apart a doll.
---I don't understand.
Why I feel like this,
Why I killed her without reason.
I can't find the reason.

entries.japanese:
現実感がまるでないから。
　だからこれは、いつもみたいに眩暈がして、その間に見ていたユメなんだ────

『────うそだ』
entries.maoEnglish:
None of it felt real.
So this had to be one of those dreams I saw whenever the dizziness took me—
『────It’s a lie』
entries.mirrorMoon:
"--------It's a lie."
It doesn't feel real.
So this is just one of those dreams I have when I faint.

entries.japanese:
だいたい、どうしてナイフ一本で人間をあそこまでバラバラにできるっていうんだ。
　本で読んだ事がある。
　人間一人をバラバラにするのは、ノコギリを使ったって丸一日かかる重労働なんだって。
　だから、こんなナイフ一本であんな事ができるはずがない。
　あの『線』なんて初めからなくって、自分がかってにそう思い込んでいるだけの妄想なんだ――――

『────うそだ』

ご───ふ。
　胃液が唇からもれる。
　口はおろか、あごから下は胃液でベトベトだ。
　胃液には朱色が交ざっている。
　吐き出すものもないくせに胃が蠕動するもんだから、のどが傷ついて出血してるのか。
『い……た────』
　痛い。
　だからきっと。
　これはユメなんかじゃなく、俺は、自分にうそをついている。
entries.maoEnglish:
How could anyone cut a human body into so many pieces with one knife?
I had read about this.
Even with a saw, dismembering a person was backbreaking work that took an entire day.
There was no way a little knife like this could have done it.
Those ‘lines’ had never existed; they were only a delusion I had invented and convinced myself was real――――
『────It’s a lie』
Ghh.
Bile leaked between my lips.
My mouth, my chin, everything below it was sticky with the stuff.
Scarlet threaded through it.
My empty stomach kept convulsing anyway—perhaps the retching had torn my throat open.
『It―――hurts────』
It hurt.
Which meant this probably wasn’t a dream.
I was lying to myself.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------It's a lie."
Besides, how can someone cut apart someone like that with just a knife.
I read it in a book once.
It takes a whole day of strenuous labor to cut someone up, even when using a saw.
That's why there's no way I could have possibly done such a thing with just a knife.
These "lines" never existed in the first place.
Everything was just a delusion I had fallen for--

"------It's a lie."

Guh---ffpt.
Gastric juice drips over my lips.
Passing out of my mouth, dripping down my jaw.
Mixed with the juices is something red.
My throat is probably bleeding because my stomach keeps trying to throw up even when there's nothing left in there.
"O…… u----"
It hurts.
That's why this…
This isn't a dream, and I'm just lying to myself.

entries.japanese:
『───全部、うそだ』

そう、ほんとは理解してる。
　欲情してた。
あの女性を見て興奮してた。
　バラす時なんて、射精しそうなほど刺激的だった。
entries.maoEnglish:
『───It’s all a lie』
Yes. I knew the
truth. I had lusted after her; the sight of her had aroused me.
Cutting her apart had been so thrilling I had nearly come.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---It's all lies."
Yes, actually, I understand everything.
I lusted after her.
Just looking at her aroused me.
When I cut her apart, it was so thrilling I almost ejaculated.

entries.japanese:
この目だってそうだ。
　あの『線』が紙を切るみたいにモノを切断してしまう『線』だってわかっていたのなら。
　遠野志貴は、さっきのように人間だって簡単にバラしてしまうって理解していたはずなのに。
　俺は、そんなことを考えもしないで、ただ普通に暮らしてしまっていた。
　―――自分が、簡単に何かを殺してしまえるような危険な人間なら。
　俺はこの目を潰すか、誰とも会わないような生活をするべきだったのに。
entries.maoEnglish:
The same was true of my eyes.
If I knew those ‘lines’ could let me slice through anything as easily as paper, then Shiki Tohno should have understood that he could tear a human being apart just as easily as he had moments ago.
Yet I had never even considered it.
I had simply gone on living an ordinary life.
―――If I was dangerous enough to kill something so easily.
Then I should have gouged out these eyes or lived where I would never meet another person.
entries.mirrorMoon:
These eyes, too.
If I knew these "lines" could cut things apart like paper being shredded…
I should have understood that even a person could easily be cut apart like I just did to her.
I had lived a normal life without even thinking about something like that.
---If I really am the sort of dangerous person who could easily kill just about anything…
Then I should have put out these eyes or lived a life without seeing anyone.

entries.japanese:
『……ごめん、先生』
―――ほんとうに、ごめんなさい。
　そんな簡単な事さえ、
　遠野志貴は守れなかった────
entries.maoEnglish:
『―――I’m sorry, Teach』
―――I’m so, so sorry.
Shiki Tohno had failed to keep
even that one simple promise—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I'm sorry, Sensei."
---I'm so sorry.
Not even such a simple promise.
Was I able to keep----

entries.japanese:
「俺は────狂って、いるのか」
　わからない。
　さっきまで湧きあがっていた衝動は、もう微塵も残っていないけれど。
　あの時、耐えるとか堪えるとか、そういった意思すら働かなかった。
　我慢する、という考えさえうかばない。
『この女を殺す』
　そんなコトを当たり前のように考えて実行してしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
『Am I────insane?』
I didn’t know.
Not a trace remained of the impulse that had possessed me.
Yet in that moment I hadn’t even tried to resist.
The very idea of restraint had never occurred to me.
『I’ll kill this woman』
I had accepted that thought as naturally as breathing, and then carried it out.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Have I----gone insane?"
I don't know.
There isn't even a trace of that impulse left.
The thought of holding back never crossed my mind.
I didn't even consider trying to stop myself.
"Kill this girl."
It had seemed like the obvious thing to do, and I went through with it.

entries.japanese:
なら答えは簡単だ。
　俺は、きっと狂ってる。
　おそらくは八年前。
　死亡確定といわれた事故から、奇跡的に蘇生したその時から―――――――
entries.maoEnglish:
Then the answer was simple.
I had to be insane.
Probably since eight years ago.
From the moment I miraculously returned from the accident in which I had been declared beyond saving―――――――
entries.mirrorMoon:
Then the answer is simple.
I must be insane.
I've probably been mad since eight years ago, when I miraculously came back to life from a fatal accident-------
…… I can hear the sound of rain coming from somewhere.
It's raining.

entries.japanese:
……どこからか、雨の音が聞こえてくる。
　ザア――――、という雨だれ。
「―――――」
　もうろうとしてる。
　息を吸うと喉が痛んだ。
「い………た」
　声があがる。
「――――志貴さま？」
　とたん、すぐ近くで誰かの声と気配がした―――

「自分の―――部屋だ」
　いつのまにか自分の部屋で横になっている。
「おはようございます、志貴さま」
「翡翠……？」
「はい。
お体の具合はいかかでしょうか？」
「………？」
　翡翠はおかしなコトを聞いてくる。
　お体の具合って、別に悪いところなんて一つもなかったけど―――
entries.maoEnglish:
Somewhere, I can hear rain.
A steady, rushing hiss.
“―――――”
My thoughts are dim and muddled.
Breathing sends pain through my throat.
“It―――hurts.”
The sound escapes me.
“—Master Shiki?”
All at once, there is a voice and a presence close beside me—
“My―――room.”
Somehow, I am lying in my own room.
“Good morning, Master Shiki.”
“Hisui―――?”
“Yes. How are you feeling?”
“―――?”
Hisui is asking a strange question.
How am I feeling? There isn’t anything wrong with me―――
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-----"
I'm in a daze.
My throat hurts when I try to breathe.
"Ou… ch."
I can speak.
"----Shiki-sama?"
Then, I become aware of someone's presence near me--
"My---room."
Somehow, I'm in my own room.
"Good morning, Shiki-sama."
"Hisui…?"
"Yes.
How are you feeling?"
"……?"
Hisui asks me an odd question.
There's not a single thing wrong with my body, but---

entries.japanese:
「なん―――で」
　そう、なんで。
　俺は、こんなところで眠っているんだ――　
「俺は―――ひとを、ころし――」
　ころしたのに、と言いかけて口を塞ぐ。
　その言葉だけは、口にしてはいけないと理性が歯止めをかけてくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
『Why―――』 Yes.
Why?
Why am I asleep
here?――― 『I―――killed some―――』 I almost
say I killed someone, then clamp my mouth shut.
Reason warns me that those words must never leave my lips.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Wh---y?"
Yes, why?
Why am I asleep in a place like this--
"Even though I---kil--"
I was about to say "killed someone", but I stop myself.
My brain tells me I shouldn't say those words.

entries.japanese:
「翡翠、俺―――どうして、ここに」
「……覚えてらっしゃらないのですか？
　学校のほうから志貴さまが早退した、というお電話がありました。
ですが夕方になっても帰ってこられず、姉が探しに行ったところ、公園でお休みになっていたそうです」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hisui, why am I―――here?”
“You don’t remember? The school called to say that Master Shiki had left early. When evening came and he still had not returned, my sister went looking for him and found him asleep in a park.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"What am I---doing here, Hisui?"
"…… Do you not remember?
Your school called to say you left early.
However, you did not come back even after dusk, so when my sister went to look for you, she found you resting in the park."

entries.japanese:
「―――公園って―――近くの公園？」
「はい。
姉が志貴さまを見つけた時には、公園のベンチで休まれていたそうです。
その後志貴さま本人の足で屋敷まで戻られました」
「……うそだろ。
そんな覚え、まったくないんだけど」
「志貴さまの記憶が定かではないのは、そうおかしな事ではないと思います。
姉に連れてこられた時の志貴さまは、言いにくい事ですが呆、としておられましたから」
「………………」
　……まったく記憶がない。
　けど、翡翠の言葉には疑う余地がない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――A park―――the one nearby?”
“Yes. My sister found Master Shiki resting on a bench there. Afterward, Master Shiki walked back to the estate on his own.”
“That can’t be right. I don’t remember any of it.”
“It is not so strange that Master Shiki’s memory should be unclear. Forgive me for saying so, but when my sister brought Master Shiki home, he seemed entirely dazed.”
“………………”
I remember nothing.
But there is no room to doubt Hisui’s account.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Park?---You mean the park near here?"
"Yes, when she found you, you were resting on the park bench.
Then you returned to the mansion on your own feet."
"…… You have got to be kidding.
I don't remember any of that."
"I do not believe it is such an odd thing that your memory is unstable, Shiki-sama.
It is difficult for me to say this, but when my sister brought you back, you were in a daze."
"…………"
…… I don't remember any of this.
But I have no reason to doubt what Hisui says.

entries.japanese:
「……ああ、もう夜の九時なんだ。
……ぜんぜん記憶にないや」
「はい。
お屋敷に戻られた志貴さまが言った言葉は、『眠りたい』というものでした。
姉はお医者様をお呼びしようとしたのですが、志貴さまは『いつものことだから』、と」
entries.maoEnglish:
“It’s already nine at night. I don’t remember a thing.”
“Yes. When Master Shiki returned, the only thing he said was that he wanted to sleep. My sister offered to call a doctor, but Master Shiki told her this happened all the time.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Yeah, it's already nine o'clock… I don't remember anything."
"Yes.
When you returned to the mansion, you said you 'wanted to sleep'.
My sister suggested we call a doctor, but you said 'it happens all the time'."

entries.japanese:
「―――そうか。
たしかに貧血で倒れるのはいつものコトだけど―――」
　……今回はかってが違う。
　俺はひとを殺してしまったんだから―――って、あれ？
「翡翠。
俺、どんな格好をしてたんだ？」
「―――は？」
「だから服装。
俺の制服、その、血で―――」
　ベッタベタに、汚れていたから。
entries.maoEnglish:
“—I see. Fainting from anemia is nothing unusual for me, but…”
This time is different.
I killed someone—wait.
“Hisui. What did I look like when I came home?”
“Pardon?”
“My clothes.
My uniform—there was blood—” It had been drenched in it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---I see.
I guess I do collapse from anemia all the time, but---"
…… This time, it's different.
Because I had killed someone---huh?
"What did I look like, Hisui?"
"---Huh?"
"My clothing, I mean.
Was my uniform… uh, with the blood---"
It was stained with blood.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さまの制服でしたら、汚れてしまっていたので洗濯をしておりますが」
「洗濯って―――あんな血だらけの服を……！？」
「……たしかに泥にまみれてはおりましたが、血液らしきものはありませんでした」
「え……？
　だって、あんなに―――」
　血の海にひざまずいて、足も腕も真っ赤になっていたっていうのに……？
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki’s uniform was dirty, so it is being washed.”
“Washed―――that blood-soaked thing!?”
“It was certainly covered in mud, but there was nothing resembling blood.”
『What―――? But there was so much―――』 I had knelt in a sea of blood.
My arms and legs had been crimson—hadn’t they?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Your uniform was dirty, so I am washing it."
"Washing--you mean those blood-stained clothes…!?"
"…… There was certainly mud on it, but nothing like blood."
"Eh…?
But it was so---"
Even though I was on my knees in a sea of blood, and both my arms and legs had been completely soaked red…?

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま、なにかよくない夢でも見られていたのですか？
　さきほどまでひどくうなされていたようですし、今もお顔の色が優れません」
　翡翠はじっとこちらの顔を見つめてくる。
「夢って――――アレが？」
　夢だったっていうのか。
　あの感覚が。
　あの血の匂いが。
　あの、悪夢みたいにキレイだった白い女が。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki, were you having a nightmare? You were deeply distressed in your sleep, and even now you look very pale.”
Hisui gazes steadily into my face.
“A nightmare――――that?”
Could that have been a dream?
That sensation?
The smell of blood?
That woman in white, as beautiful as a nightmare?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Have you had a nightmare of some sort, Shiki-sama?
You looked like you were having a bad dream until now, and you do not look fine."
Hisui stares at my face.
"A dream?
----That, a dream?"
Was it a dream?
That feeling.
That smell of blood.
That hideously beautiful white girl.

entries.japanese:
「いや―――そうだよな。
あんなのは、悪いユメだ」
　ほう、と長い息がもれる。
――――そうだ。
　あんなものは、悪い夢だ。
　意味もなく理由もなく、幼いころに交わした先生との約束まで破って、俺があんなコトをするわけがなかったんだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“No―――of course. That was only a nightmare.”
A long breath escapes me.
――――Yes.
That was all it had been: a nightmare.
I could never have done such a thing for no reason, no purpose, even breaking the promise I had made in childhood to my teacher.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No---maybe you're right.
That's just a bad dream."
Phew.
I breathe out slowly.
----That's right.
That's got to be a bad dream.
There's no way I would break my childhood promise to Sensei needlessly and for no reason.

entries.japanese:
「ああ――――目が、覚めた」
「はい。
志貴さまのご気分さえよろしければ夕食の支度をいたします」
「夕食、か」
　……ユメだとわかっているのに、まだあの血の色と匂いが脳裏から離れない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ah――――I’m awake.”
“If you feel well enough, Master Shiki, I can prepare supper.”
“Supper…”
…Even now that I know it was a dream, I can’t drive the color or smell of that blood from my mind.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah---I'm finally awake."
"Yes.
If you are feeling better, I will go prepare dinner now."
"Dinner, huh?"
…… I know it's just a dream, but the color and smell of blood still lingers in my mind.

entries.japanese:
「―――いや、いいよ。
今晩はこのまま眠る事にする。
それより翡翠」
「はい、なんでしょうか志貴さま」
「その、さ。
俺、夕方に帰ってきたらしいけど、秋葉はなんて言ってた？」
「秋葉さまなら、その時間はまだお帰りになられていませんでした。
二時間ほど前にお帰りになられたおり、姉のほうから志貴さまのご容体をお伝えしておきましたが」
　それがなにか？
　と翡翠は無言で聞き返してくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――No, thank you. I think I’ll sleep through the night. But Hisui.”
“Yes, Master Shiki?”
“Apparently I came home this evening. What did Akiha say?”
“Miss Akiha had not yet returned at that time. She came home about two hours ago, and my sister informed her of Master Shiki’s condition.”
Hisui is silent. Her look asks whether something is the matter.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---No, it's fine.
I'm just going to sleep like this tonight.
More importantly, Hisui…"
"Yes, what is it, Shiki-sama?"
"Um… well.
It seems like I came back after dusk, did Akiha say anything?"
"Akiha-sama was not home yet at the time.
She came back about two hours ago, and was informed of your condition through my sister."
Hisui seems to silently ask "What about it?"

entries.japanese:
「いや、別になんでもないんだ。
たださ、帰ってきて二日目だっていうのに迷惑をかけたから、呆れてるだろうなって」
「……たしかに秋葉さまはご気分を害されてらっしゃいましたが、呆れているというわけではなさそうでした」
　言って、翡翠は一歩後ろに下がった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“It’s nothing. I’ve only been back two days and I’m already causing trouble, so I thought she must be fed up with me.”
“Miss Akiha was certainly displeased, but she did not seem exasperated with you.”
With that, Hisui takes one step back.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Oh, it's nothing.
I was just wondering if she was disgusted with me for causing her trouble on just the second day after I've come back."
"…… It did seem like Akiha-sama was distressed, but I would not say she was disgusted."
Saying that, Hisui takes a step away from me.

entries.japanese:
「それでは失礼します。
何かご用がおありでしたらお呼びください」
「ああ、ありがとう。
―――と、もう一つ聞き忘れてた」
「はい、なんでしょう志貴さま」
「外、雨が降ってるんだね。
いつから降りはじめたのかな、コレ」
「志貴さまがお帰りになられる前からです。
姉が志貴さまを見つけた時、志貴さまは雨に濡れていたんです」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Then I will excuse myself. Please call if you require anything.”
“Thank you. Oh—one more thing.”
“Yes, Master Shiki?”
“It’s raining outside. When did that start?”
“Before Master Shiki returned. When my sister found Master Shiki, Master Shiki was already soaked.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Well, I will be leaving now.
Please call for me if you need anything."
"Yeah, thanks.
--Oh, one more thing I forgot to ask."
"Yes, what is it, Shiki-sama?"
"It's raining outside.
When did it start?"
"Before you came back, Shiki-sama.
When my sister found you, you were drenched."

entries.japanese:
「……………」
　そうか。
そんなコトさえ、記憶にはない。
どうやらよっぽど重い貧血だったみたいだ。
　……こんなコトなら、無理をせずに学校で休んでいればよかった。
「おやすみ。
今日は本当にすまない。
琥珀さんにもお礼を言っておいてくれ」
「かしこまりました。
―――それではおやすみなさいませ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“……………”
So I can’t remember even that. The anemia must have been exceptionally severe.
……I should have stayed at school and rested instead of pushing myself.
“Good night. I’m truly sorry for today. Please thank Kohaku for me.”
“Very well. ―――Good night.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…………"
I see.
I can't even remember that.
It seems like it was a pretty serious case of anemia.
…… If that's the case, I shouldn't have pushed myself and should have just rested at school.
"Good night.
I'm really sorry about today.
Please express my gratitude to Kohaku-san, too."
"I understand.
--Good night."

entries.japanese:
「――――夢、か」
　まるで実感がわかない。
　あの夢の内容も実感がわかなければ、
　アレが夢なのだという実感も。
　外では、ざああ、という雨の音。
　頭はまだかすかに重い。
　ふと自分の胸を見る。
　……八年前の古傷は、いまも火傷の痕のようにくっきりと残っている。
「あ―――」
　部屋の机の上には、父親からの形見分けであるナイフが置かれている。
　あの、白い女性を十七個に解体した、旧い刃物が。
entries.maoEnglish:
“—A dream.”
None of it feels real.
Not what happened in the dream,
and not the idea that it was a dream at all.
Rain roars outside.
My head still feels faintly heavy.
I glance down at my chest.
The scar from eight years ago remains stark and clear, like the trace of a burn.
“Ah―――”
On the desk lies the knife I inherited from my father.
The old blade that disassembled the woman in white into seventeen pieces.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----A dream, huh."
It's like I don't even know what I felt.
But if I can't understand what happened or how I feel about it,
how do I know it was a dream?
I can hear the sound of the rain outside.
My mind still feels a little heavy.
I glance down at my chest.
…… The old wound from eight years ago is still distinctly there, like a burn scar.
"Ah---"
On top of my desk lies the knife my father left me.
That old blade which had cut that white girl into seventeen pieces.

entries.japanese:
「―――――」
　……あれは夢だ。
　夢以外の何物でもないじゃないか。
　自分自身を誤魔化すようにそう繰り返して眠りにつくことにした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――――”
That was a dream.
It could not have been anything else.
I repeat that to myself as if I might fool myself, then close my eyes and try to sleep.
entries.mirrorMoon:
" ----"
…… That was a dream.
Nothing more.
I repeat this over and over again, trying to placate myself until I sleep.

entries.japanese:
……子供のころ。
　自分自身さえも騙せない嘘はつくな、と誰かが言っていた気がするけれど。
entries.maoEnglish:
…I seem to remember someone telling me as a child
never to tell a lie that cannot fool even me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… But when I was a child,
I think someone once told me, "Don't tell lies that can't even fool yourself."

entries.japanese:
けど、一体なにが違うんだろう？
　自分が殺したというコトが違うのか。
　それとも、自分が殺していないという事が違うのか。
　ああ、もうそんなコトはまったく違う―――
entries.maoEnglish:
But which part, exactly, was the lie?
Was it a lie that I had killed her?
Or was it a lie that I had not?
God, neither of those was it at all—
entries.mirrorMoon:
But just what is wrong about it?
I killed her.
Is that fact wrong?
I didn't kill her.
Is that fact wrong?
No, all that's totally wrong---!

entries.japanese:
違うんだ、違う、違う、違う、
　俺は、だから、なにを、
「……ちが、う」
　だから、なにが
「……違、う」
　それは、だから
「違うって───言ってるのに」
　殺していないというのが、違う。
entries.maoEnglish:
It was wrong, wrong, wrong, wrong,
I had, so, what was I—
“No―――wrong”
Then what
“No―――wrong”
That was, so―――
“I keep saying—that's not it.”
The lie was the claim that I hadn't killed her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Wrong.
Wrong wrong wrong.
So what, am, I,
"…… Wro… ng."
What, is
"…… Wro… ng."
That's, because
"I'm saying---it's wrong."
The fact that I didn't kill her is wrong.

entries.japanese:
「ちがっ……！
　違う、違う違う違う違う違う違う……！
　俺は知らない、こんなヤツ、街で見かけただけのただの他人だ……！
　ほら、おかしいじゃないか志貴……！
　ただの他人をさ、どうして俺が殺さなくちゃいけないっていうんだよ……！」
entries.maoEnglish:
“No―――! No, no no no no no no―――! I don’t know her; I only saw her in the street—she’s a complete stranger―――!
Think, Shiki―――! It doesn’t make any sense—why would I have to kill a total stranger―――?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No…!
Wrong!
Wrongwrongwrongwrongwrongwrong…!
I don't even know her!
She's just some stranger I saw walking down the street……!
See!
Isn't that strange to you, Shiki…!?
She's a complete stranger!
Why would I have to kill her…!?"

entries.japanese:
叫んでも答えはない。
　それに理由ならはっきりしてる。
　彼女を見た時、俺は一つの事しか考えられなくなっていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
No matter how I screamed, no answer came.
Besides, the reason was perfectly clear.
The moment I saw her, I had become incapable of thinking about anything else.
entries.mirrorMoon:
There is no answer to my screams.
Besides, the reason is clear.
From the moment I saw her, I could only think of one thing.

entries.japanese:
「俺は────」
　そう、俺は───
　　　遠野志貴は　あの女を　殺したい、と
　それが、あの時の俺の全ての意志だったハズだ。
　ただ、頭の中がドロドロとしていて、あえて、そのイメージを言葉にしようとしなかっただけで。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I────”
Yes, I───
Shiki Tohno wanted to kill that woman―――
That must have been the whole of my will then.
My thoughts had only been too thick and muddy for me to force that image into words.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I----"
Yes, I----
Tohno Shiki    wanted to   kill    that girl.
That's what I wanted to do back then.
Just that, it was all so muddy inside my head, I didn't put it into words.

entries.japanese:
「ちが─────う 」
　吐き気が、する。
「う、うう、う」
　胃の中のものが、戻ってくる。
「あ、ああ、あ」
　眼球に、赤い朱色がしみ込んでくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“No─────”
Nausea welled up.
“Uh, ugh, ngh”
Everything in my stomach surged back up.
“Ah, aah, ah”
Scarlet seeped into my eyes.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Wro-----ng!"
I feel like throwing up.
"Uh, uggg, uh."
The contents of my stomach are coming back up.
"Ah, aaah, ah!"
The crimson soaks into my eyeballs.

entries.japanese:
「あああああ――――！」
　駆け出した。
　誰かに見られるとか、死体を隠さなくっちゃとか、そんな余分な事は一切考えられない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Aaaaaaah!”
I ran.
I couldn’t spare a thought for someone seeing me, or for hiding the body, or for anything else at all.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Aaaaaaaaah----!"
I dash out.
I don't think for even a moment about how I might be seen, or to hide the body.

entries.japanese:
ただここから逃げ出したくて。
　半狂乱になって、見知らぬマンションの部屋から駆け出した─────
entries.maoEnglish:
I only wanted to escape.
Half mad with terror, I fled the strange apartment—
entries.mirrorMoon:
I just want to escape from here.
Half-crazed, I flee from the unfamiliar apartment-----

entries.japanese:
「ご―――ぼ――」
　胃液が逆流する。
　地面にひざまずいて、胃の中のものを残らず吐いた。
　食い物も、胃液も、泣きながら吐き出した。
「はぁ……はぁ……はぁ……はぁ………」
　胃の中には何もない。
　なのに起きてしまった出来事をなかった事に、もとの日常に戻そうとするかのように、体は嘔吐を強制する。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ghh—blegh—” Acid flooded up my throat.
I dropped to my knees and vomited
everything in my stomach.
Food, bile—I sobbed and brought it all up.
“Hah, hah, hah, hah―――”
Soon there was nothing left in my stomach.
Even so, my body forced me to retch, as if it could vomit away what had happened and drag me back into my ordinary life.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Guuh---burgh!"
My gastric juices rise in my throat.
I throw everything back up.
My food, my gastric juices, everything, while I cry.
*pant*  *wheeze*  *gasp*  *pant*
There is nothing left in my stomach.
But my body continues to force me to throw up, as if trying to undo what had occurred and return me to a normal life.

entries.japanese:
「……はあ……はあ……はあ……は……あ」
　痛い。
　内蔵が焼けてるみたいに、痛い。
　涙は止まらなくて、体はゴミのように地面に崩れ落ちた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hah, hah, hah, ha, ah”
It hurt.
It hurt as though my insides were on fire.
The tears would not stop, and my body collapsed like garbage onto the ground.
entries.mirrorMoon:
*pant*  *wheeze*  *gasp*  *pant*
Pain.
It hurts, like my insides are burning.
The tears won't stop, and my body collapses to the floor like a pile of garbage.

entries.japanese:
「あ、ぐ─────ぐ、ぐぐ、ぐ」
　涙が止まらない。
　……俺は、人を殺した。
　人形でもバラすみたいにあっさりと、何の意味もなく、容赦なく殺してしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ah, gh─────gh, ghh, ngh”
I couldn’t stop crying.
I had killed someone.
I had killed her so casually, so meaninglessly and mercilessly, as if I had merely pulled apart a doll.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah, guh-----gu, guguh, guh!"
I keep crying.
…… I killed someone.
I killed her without reason, without mercy.
Like breaking apart a doll.

entries.japanese:
───なんて事だろう。
　どうしてあんな気分になってしまったのか、
　どうしてほんとうに殺してしまったのか、
　今でもその理由が解らない。
entries.maoEnglish:
───What had I done?
I still didn’t know why
I had felt that way or
why I had truly gone through with killing her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Why?
Why I felt like that,
why I killed her,
even now, I can't find a reason.

entries.japanese:
「ご───ふ」
　胃液が唇からもれる。
　口はおろか、あごから下は胃液でベトベトだ。
　胃液には朱色が交ざっている。
　吐き出すものもないくせに胃が蠕動するもんだから、のどが傷ついて出血してるのか。
「い……た────」
　痛い。
　だからきっと。
　さっきのはユメの筈などなく、俺は、自分にうそをついている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ghh.”
Bile leaked between my lips.
My mouth, my chin, everything below it was sticky with the stuff.
Scarlet threaded through it.
My empty stomach kept convulsing anyway—perhaps the retching had torn my throat open.
“It―――hurts────”
It hurt.
Which meant what had happened could not possibly have been a dream.
I was lying to myself.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Guh---ffpt."
Stomach acid drips over my lips.
Passing out of my mouth, dripping down my jaw.
Mixed with the juices is something red.
My throat is probably bleeding because my stomach keeps trying to throw up even when there's nothing left in there.
"O…… u----"
It hurts.
That's why this…
This isn't a dream, and I'm just lying to myself.

entries.japanese:
「───全部、うそだ」
　そう、ほんとはとっくに理解してる。
　欲情してた。
あの女性を見て興奮してた。
　バラす時なんて、射精しそうなほど刺激的だった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“───It’s all a lie”
Yes. I had known the truth all
along. I had lusted after her; the sight of her had aroused me.
Cutting her apart had been so thrilling I had nearly come.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---It's all lies."
Yes, actually, I understand everything.
I lusted after her.
Just looking at her aroused me.

entries.japanese:
この目だってそうだ。
　あの『線』が紙を切るみたいにモノを切断してしまう『線』だってわかっていたのなら。
　遠野志貴は、さっきのように人間だって簡単にバラしてしまうって理解してたはずなのに。
　俺は、そんなことを考えもしないで、ただ普通にに暮らしてしまった。
　―――自分が、簡単に何かを殺してしまえるような危険な人間なら。
　俺はこの目を潰すか、誰とも会わないような生活をするべきだったのに。
entries.maoEnglish:
The same was true of my eyes.
If I knew those ‘lines’ could let me slice through anything as easily as paper, then Shiki Tohno should have understood that he could tear a human being apart just as easily as he had moments ago.
Yet I had never even considered it.
I had simply gone on living an ordinary life.
―――If I was dangerous enough to kill something so easily.
Then I should have gouged out these eyes or lived where I would never meet another person.
entries.mirrorMoon:
When I cut her apart, it was so thrilling I almost ejaculated.
These eyes, too.
If I knew these "lines" could cut things apart like paper being shredded…
I should have understood that even a person could easily be cut apart like I just did to her.
I had lived a normal life without even thinking about something like that.
---If I really am the sort of dangerous person who could easily kill just about anything…
Then I should have put out these eyes or lived a life without seeing anyone.

entries.japanese:
「……ごめん、先生」
―――ほんとうに、ごめんなさい。
　そんな簡単な事さえ、
　遠野志貴は守れなかった────
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――I’m sorry, Teach.”
―――I’m so, so sorry.
Shiki Tohno had failed to keep
even that one simple promise—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I'm sorry, Sensei."
---I'm so sorry.
Not even such a simple promise,
was I able to keep----

entries.japanese:
「──────」
　でも、自分の事なんてどうでもいい。
　俺はあの人を殺してしまった。
　あの人の今までの人生とか、
　あの人のまわりの人達のこととか、
　あの人がずっと夢見ていた未来とか、
　全部───他人である自分がブチ壊してしまったんだ。
　後悔しても許されない。
　謝っても、絶対に許されない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“—”
But what happened to me didn’t matter.
I had killed her.
Her whole life until now, the people around her,
the future she had always dreamed of—all
of it had been smashed to pieces by me,
a stranger.
Regret could never earn forgiveness.
No apology could ever earn it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------"
But I don't care about myself.
I killed that person.
That person's life up until now.
The people around that person,
the future that person dreamed of,
everything---destroyed by a stranger.
Even if I regret it, I can't be forgiven.

entries.japanese:
「俺は────狂ってるのか」
　わからない。
　あの時沸き上がった衝動は、もう微塵も残っていない。
　けどもし───またあの感覚がやってきたら、自分はどうなるんだろうか？
　耐えるとか、堪えるとか、そういった意思すら働かなかった。
　我慢する、という考えさえうかばない。

『あの女を殺す』
　そんなコトを、当たり前のように考えて実行してしまったのなら、自分でどうにかできる方法なんてありはしない。

なら答えは簡単だ。
　俺は、きっと狂ってる。
　おそらくは八年前。
　死亡確定といわれた事故から、奇跡的に蘇生したその時から。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Am I insane?”
I didn’t know.
Not a trace remained of the impulse that had possessed me.
But if that feeling returned, what would become of me?
In that moment I hadn’t even tried to resist.
The very idea of restraint had never occurred to me.
『I’ll kill that woman』
If I could accept that thought as naturally as breathing and then carry it out, there was nothing I could do to control myself.
Then the answer was simple.
I had to be insane.
Probably since eight years ago.
Since the moment I miraculously returned from the accident in which I had been declared beyond saving.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Even if I apologize, I can't be forgiven.

"Have I----gone insane?"
I don't know.
There isn't even a trace of that impulse left.
The thought of holding back never crossed my mind.
I didn't even consider trying to stop myself.

"Kill this girl."
It had seemed like the obvious thing to do, and I went through with it.

entries.japanese:
……どこからか、雨の音が聞こえてくる。

ザア――――、という雨だれ。
entries.maoEnglish:
Somewhere, I can hear rain.
A steady, rushing hiss.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Then the answer is simple.
I must be insane.
I've probably been mad since eight years ago, when I miraculously came back to life from a fatal accident.

entries.japanese:
「―――――」
　もうろうとしてる。
　息を吸うと喉が痛んだ。
「い………た」
　声があがる。

「――――志貴さま？」
　とたん、すぐ近くで誰かの声と気配がした―――
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――――”
My thoughts are dim and muddled.
Breathing sends pain through my throat.
“It―――hurts.”
The sound escapes me.
“—Master Shiki?”
All at once, there is a voice and a presence close beside me—
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… I can hear the sound of rain coming from somewhere.
It's raining.
"-----"
I'm in a daze.
My throat hurts when I try to breathe.
"Ou… ch."
I can speak.
"----Shiki-sama?"
Then, I become aware of someone's presence near me---

entries.japanese:
「自分の―――部屋だ」
　いつのまにか自分の部屋で横になっている。
「お目覚めになられましたか、志貴さま？」
「翡翠……？」
「はい。
お体の具合はいかかでしょうか」
「………？」
　翡翠はおかしなコトを聞いてくる。
　お体の具合って、別に悪いところなんて一つもなかったけど―――
entries.maoEnglish:
“My―――room.”
Somehow, I am lying in my own room.
“Are you awake, Master Shiki?”
“Hisui…?”
“Yes. How are you feeling?”
“…?”
Hisui is asking a strange question.
As for how I feel, there isn’t anything wrong with me―――
entries.mirrorMoon:
"My---room."
Somehow, I'm in my own room.
"Have you awakened, Shiki-sama?"
"Hisui…?"
"Yes.
How is your body feeling?"
"……?"
Hisui asks me an odd question.
There's not a single thing wrong with my body, but---

entries.japanese:
「なん―――で」
　そう、なんで。
　自分は、こんなところで眠っているんだ――
entries.maoEnglish:
“Why―――”
Yes—why.
Why am I asleep here―――
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Wh---y?"
Yes, why?
Why am I asleep in a place like this--

entries.japanese:
「俺は―――ひとを、ころし――」
　ころしたのに、と言いかけて口を塞ぐ。
　その言葉だけは、口にしてはいけないと理性が歯止めをかけてくる。
「翡翠、俺―――どうして、ここに」
「……覚えてらっしゃらないのですか、志貴さま」
　翡翠はかすかに眉をよせる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I―――killed some―――”
I almost say I killed someone, then clamp my mouth shut.
Reason warns me that those words must never leave my lips.
“Hisui, why am I―――here?”
“You don’t remember, Master Shiki?” Hisui’s brow draws together almost imperceptibly.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Even though I---kil--"
I was about to say "killed someone", but I stop myself.
My brain tells me I shouldn't say those words.
"What am I---doing here, Hisui?"
"…… Do you not remember, Shiki-sama?" Hisui raises her brow slightly.

entries.japanese:
「学校のほうから志貴さまが早退した、というお電話がありました。
ですが夕方になっても帰ってこられず、姉が探しに行ったところ、公園でお休みになっていたそうです」
「―――公園って―――近くの公園？」
「はい。
姉が志貴さまを見つけた時には、公園のベンチで休まれていて、志貴さま本人の足で屋敷まで戻られました」
entries.maoEnglish:
“The school called to say that Master Shiki had left early. When evening came and he still had not returned, my sister went looking for him and found him asleep in a park.”
“―――A park―――the one nearby?”
“Yes. My sister found Master Shiki resting on a bench there, and afterward Master Shiki walked back to the estate on his own.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Your school called to say you left early.
However, you did not come back even after dusk, so when my sister went to look for you, she found you resting in the park."
"---Park?---You mean the park near here?"
"Yes, when she found you, you were resting on the park bench.
Then you returned to the mansion on your own feet."

entries.japanese:
「……うそだろ。
そんな覚え、まったくないんだけど」
「志貴さまの記憶が定かではないのは、そうおかしな事ではないと思います。
　姉に連れてこられた時の志貴さまは、言いにくい事ですが呆、としておられましたから」
「………………」
　……まったく記憶がない。
　けど、翡翠の言葉には疑う余地がない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“That can’t be right. I don’t remember any of it.”
“It is not so strange that Master Shiki’s memory should be unclear.
Forgive me for saying so, but when my sister brought Master Shiki home, he seemed entirely dazed.”
“…”
I remember nothing.
But there is no room to doubt Hisui’s account.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… You have got to be kidding.
I don't remember any of that."
"I do not believe it is such an odd thing that your memory is unstable, Shiki-sama.
It is difficult for me to say this, but when my sister brought you back, you were in a daze."
"…………"
…… I don't remember any of this.
But I have no reason to doubt what Hisui says.

entries.japanese:
「……ああ、もう夜の九時なんだ。
……ぜんぜん記憶にないや」
「はい。
お屋敷に戻られた志貴さまが言った言葉は、『眠りたい』というものでした。
姉はお医者様をお呼びしようとしたのですが、志貴さまは『いつものことだから』、と」
「―――そうか。
たしかに貧血で倒れるのはいつものコトだけど―――」
　……今回はかってが違う。
　俺はひとを殺してしまったんだから―――って、あれ？
entries.maoEnglish:
“It’s already nine at night. I don’t remember a thing.”
“Yes. When Master Shiki returned, the only thing he said was that he wanted to sleep. My sister offered to call a doctor, but Master Shiki told her this happened all the time.”
“―――I see. Fainting from anemia is nothing unusual for me, but―――”
This time is different.
I killed someone—wait.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Yeah, it's already nine o'clock… I don't remember anything."
"Yes.
When you returned to the mansion, you said you 'wanted to sleep'.
My sister suggested we call a doctor, but you said 'it happens all the time'."
"---I see.
I guess I do collapse from anemia all the time, but---"
…… This time, it's different.

entries.japanese:
「翡翠。
俺、どんな格好をしてたんだ？」
「―――は？」
「だから服装。
俺の制服、その、血で―――」
　ベッタベタに、汚れていたから。

「志貴さまの制服でしたら、汚れてしまっていたので洗濯をしておりますが」
「洗濯って―――あんな血だらけの服を……！？」
「……たしかに泥にまみれてはおりましたが、血液らしきものはありませんでした」
「え……？
　だって、あんなに―――」
　血の海にひざまずいて、足も腕も真っ赤になっていたっていうのに……？
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hisui. What did I look like when I came home?”
“Pardon?”
“My clothes.
My uniform—there was blood—” It had been drenched in it.
“Master Shiki’s uniform was dirty, so it is being washed.”
“Washed―――that blood-soaked thing!?”
“It was certainly covered in mud, but there was nothing resembling blood.”
『What―――? But there was so much―――』 I had knelt in a sea of blood.
My arms and legs had been crimson—hadn’t they?
entries.mirrorMoon:
Because I had killed someone---huh?
"What did I look like, Hisui?"
"--Huh?"
"My clothing, I mean.
Was my uniform… uh, with the blood--"
It was stained with blood.
"Your uniform was dirty, so I am washing it."
"Washing---you mean those blood-stained clothes…!?"
"…… There was certainly mud on it, but nothing like blood."
"Eh…?
But it was so--"
Even though I was on my knees in a sea of blood, and both my arms and legs had been completely soaked red…?

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま、なにかよくない夢でも見られていたのですか？
　先ほどまでひどくうなされていたようですし、今もお顔の色が優れません」
　翡翠はじっとこちらの顔を見つめてくる。
「夢って――――アレが？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki, were you having a nightmare? You were deeply distressed in your sleep, and even now you look very pale.”
Hisui gazes steadily into my face.
“A nightmare――――that?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Have you had a nightmare of some sort, Shiki-sama?
You looked like you were having a bad dream until now, and you do not look fine."
Hisui stares at my face.
"A dream?
----That, a dream?"

entries.japanese:
夢だったっていうのか。
　あの感覚が。
　あの血の匂いが。
　あの、悪夢みたいにキレイだった白い女が。
entries.maoEnglish:
Could that have been a dream?
That sensation?
The smell of blood?
That woman in white, as beautiful as a nightmare?
entries.mirrorMoon:
Was it a dream?
That feeling.
That smell of blood.
That hideously beautiful white girl.

entries.japanese:
「いや―――そうだよな。
あんなのは、悪いユメだ」
　ほう、と長い息がもれる。
――――そうだ。
　あんなものは、悪い夢だ。
　意味もなく理由もなく、幼いころに交わした先生との約束まで破って、俺があんなコトをするわけがなかったんだ。

でも、それは。
　その都合のいい思いこみこそが、夢ではないのか。
entries.maoEnglish:
“No―――of course. That was only a nightmare.”
A long breath escapes me.
――――Yes.
That was all it had been: a nightmare.
I could never have done such a thing for no reason, no purpose, even breaking the promise I had made in childhood to my teacher.
But what if that certainty was wrong?
What if it was only a convenient dream?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No---maybe you're right.
That's just a bad dream."
Phew.
I breathe out slowly.
----That's right.
That's got to be a bad dream.
There's no way I would break my childhood promise to Sensei needlessly and for no reason.
But that…
Is it being a dream too good to be true?
"----!"

entries.japanese:
「――――っ」
「……志貴さま？
　ご気分がまだ優れないのですか？」
「―――いや、もう大丈夫。
あれは―――あんなのは、夢に決まってる。
そう、思わないと」
―――とてもじゃないけど、俺はこんなところで眠ってなんかいられない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“—!”
“Master Shiki. Are you still feeling unwell?”
“―――No. I’m all right. That had to be a dream; I have to believe that.”
―――There is no possible way I can lie here and sleep.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Shiki-sama?
Are you still not feeling well?"
"---No, I'm alright now.
That---something like that must have been a dream.
That's what I've got to believe."
---If I don't believe so, I just can't be sleeping here.

entries.japanese:
「それでは、志貴さまのご気分さえよろしければ夕食の支度をいたしますが」
「……夕、食」
　……まさか。
まだあの血の色と匂いが脳裏から離れないのに、食事なんか、とれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“If you feel well enough, Master Shiki, I can prepare supper.”
“Supper.”
Impossible. With the color and smell of that blood still trapped in my mind, I can’t eat a thing.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yes.
If you are feeling better, I will go prepare dinner now."
"…… Dinner?"
…… No way.
I can't eat when the color and smell of blood still lingers in my mind.

entries.japanese:
「―――いや、いいよ。
今晩はこのまま眠る事にする。
それより翡翠」
「はい、なんでしょうか志貴さま」
「その、さ。
俺、夕方に帰ってきたらしいけど、秋葉はなんて言ってた？」
「秋葉さまなら、その時間はまだお帰りになられていませんでした。
二時間ほど前にお帰りになられたおり、姉のほうから志貴さまのご容体をお伝えしておきましたが」
　それがなにか？
　と翡翠は無言で聞き返してくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――No, thank you. I think I’ll sleep through the night. But Hisui.”
“Yes, Master Shiki?”
“Apparently I came home this evening. What did Akiha say?”
“Miss Akiha had not yet returned at that time. She came home about two hours ago, and my sister informed her of Master Shiki’s condition.”
Hisui is silent. Her look asks whether something is the matter.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---No, it's fine.
I'm just going to sleep like this tonight.
More importantly, Hisui…"
"Yes, what is it, Shiki-sama?"
"Um… well.
It seems like I came back after dusk, but did Akiha say anything?"
"Akiha-sama was not home yet at the time.
She came back about two hours ago, and was informed of your condition through my sister."
Hisui seems to silently ask, "what about it?"

entries.japanese:
「いや、別になんでもないんだ。
たださ、帰ってきて二日目だっていうのに迷惑をかけたから、呆れてるだろうなって」
「……たしかに秋葉さまはご気分を害されてらっしゃいましたが、呆れているというわけではなさそうでした」
　言って、翡翠は一歩後ろに下がった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“It’s nothing. I’ve only been back two days and I’m already causing trouble, so I thought she must be fed up with me.”
“Miss Akiha was certainly displeased, but she did not seem exasperated with you.”
With that, Hisui takes one step back.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Oh, it's nothing.
I was just wondering if she was disgusted with me for causing her trouble on just the second day after I've come back."
"…… It did seem like Akiha-sama was distressed, but I would not say she was disgusted."
Saying this, Hisui takes a step away from me.

entries.japanese:
「それでは失礼します。
何かご用がおありでしたらお呼びください」
「ああ、ありがとう。
―――と、もう一つ聞き忘れてた」
「はい、なんでしょう志貴さま」
「外、雨が降ってるんだね。
いつから降りはじめたのかな、コレ」
「志貴さまがお帰りになられる前からです。
姉が志貴さまを見つけた時、志貴さまは雨に濡れていたんです」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Then I will excuse myself. Please call if you require anything.”
“Thank you. Oh—one more thing.”
“Yes, Master Shiki?”
“It’s raining outside. When did that start?”
“Before Master Shiki returned. When my sister found Master Shiki, Master Shiki was already soaked.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Well, I will be leaving now.
Please call for me if you need anything."
"Yeah, thanks.
---Oh, one more thing I forgot to ask."
"Yes, what is it, Shiki-sama?"
"It's raining outside.
When did it start?"
"Before you came back, Shiki-sama.
When my sister found you, you were drenched."

entries.japanese:
「……………」
　そうか。
そんなコトさえ、記憶にはない。
　どうやらよっぽど重い貧血だったみたいだ。
　……こんなコトなら、無理をせずに学校で休んでいればよかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
So I can’t remember even that.
The anemia must have been exceptionally severe.
…I should have stayed at school and rested instead of pushing myself.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…………"
I see.
I can't even remember that.
It seems like it was a pretty serious case of anemia.
…… If that's the case, I shouldn't have pushed myself and should have just rested at school.

entries.japanese:
「おやすみ。
今日は本当にすまない。
琥珀さんにもお礼を言っておいてくれ」
「かしこまりました。
―――それではおやすみなさいませ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Good night. I’m truly sorry for today. Please thank Kohaku for me.”
“Certainly. Good night, Master Shiki.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Good night.
I'm really sorry about today.
Please express my gratitude to Kohaku-san, too."
"I understand.
---Good night."

entries.japanese:
「――――夢、か」
　まるで実感がわかない。
　あの夢の内容も実感がわかなければ、
　アレが夢なのだという実感も。
entries.maoEnglish:
“—A dream.”
None of it feels real.
Not what happened in the dream,
and not the idea that it was a dream at all.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----A dream, huh."
It's like I don't even know what I felt.
But if I can't understand what happened or how I feel about it,
how do I know it was a dream?

entries.japanese:
外では、ざああ、という雨の音。
　頭はまだかすかに重い。
　ふと自分の胸を見る。
　……八年前の古傷は、いまも火傷の痕のようにくっきりと残っている。
「あ―――」
　部屋の机の上には、父親からの形見分けであるナイフが置かれている。
entries.maoEnglish:
Rain roars outside.
My head still feels faintly heavy.
I glance down at my chest.
The scar from eight years ago remains stark and clear, like the trace of a burn.
“Ah—”
On the desk lies the knife I inherited from my father.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I can hear the sound of the rain outside.
My mind still feels a little heavy.
I glance down at my chest.
…… The old wound from eight years ago is still distinctly there, like a burn scar.
"Ah---"
On top of my desk lies the knife my father left me.

entries.japanese:
「―――――」
　……あれは夢だ。
　夢以外の何物でもないじゃないか。
　自分自身を誤魔化すようにそう繰り返して眠りにつく。
　……子供のころ。
　自分自身さえも騙せない嘘はつくな、と誰かが言っていた気がするけれど。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――――”
That was a dream.
It could not have been anything else.
I repeat that to myself as if I might fool myself, then drift to sleep.
…I seem to remember someone telling me as a child
never to tell a lie that cannot fool even me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-----"
…… That was a dream.
Nothing more.
I repeat this over and over again, trying to placate myself until I sleep.
…… But when I was a child,
I think someone once told me, "don't tell lies that you can't even fool yourself with."

entries.japanese:
けど、一体なにが違うんだろう？
　違う　違う　違う　違う。
　違う　違う　違う　違う。
　自分が殺したというコトが違うのか。
　それとも、自分が殺していないという事が違うのか。
　ああ、もうそんなコトはまったく違う―――
entries.maoEnglish:
But which part, exactly, was the lie?
Wrong, wrong, wrong, wrong.
Wrong, wrong, wrong, wrong.
Was it wrong that I had killed her?
Or was it wrong that I had not?
God, neither of those was it at all—
entries.mirrorMoon:
But just what is wrong about it?
Wrong wrong wrong wrong.
Wrong wrong wrong wrong.
I killed her.
Is that fact wrong?
I didn't kill her.
Is that fact wrong?
No, all that's totally wrong---!

entries.japanese:
違うんだ、違う、違う、違う、
　違う、違う、違う、違う、違う違う、
　違う、違う、違う、違う、違う違う違う、
　違う、違う、違う、違う、違う違う違う違う、
　違う違う違う、違う違う違う違う、違う違う違う違う違う、違う違う違う違う違う違う、違う違う違う違う違う違う違う、違う違う違う違う違う違う違う、違う違う違う違う違う違う違う違う違う違う違う違う違う違う違う違う違う違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違違─────
entries.maoEnglish:
It was wrong, wrong, wrong, wrong—wrong, wrong, wrong, wrong, wrongwrong—wrong, wrong, wrong,
wrong, wrongwrongwrong—wrong, wrong, wrong, wrong, wrongwrongwrongwrong—wrongwrongwrong,
wrongwrongwrongwrong, wrongwrongwrongwrongwrong, wrongwrongwrongwrongwrongwrong,
wrongwrongwrongwrongwrongwrongwrong, wrongwrongwrongwrongwrongwrongwrongwrong,
—
entries.mirrorMoon:
That's wrong, wrong, wrong, wrong,
wrong, wrong, wrong, wrongwrong,
wrong, wrong, wrong, wrongwrongwrong,
wrong, wrong, wrong, wrongwrongwrongwrong,
wrongwrongwrong, wrongwrongwrongwrong, wrongwrongwrongwrongwrong, wrongwrongwrongwrongwrongwrong, wrongwrongwrongwrongwrongwrongwrong, wrongwrongwrongwrongwrongwrongwrongwrong, wrongwrongwrongwrongwrongwrongwrongwrongwrongwrongwrongwrongwrongwrongwrongwrongwrongwrongwrongwrongwrongwrongwrongwrong-----

entries.japanese:
「……ちが、う」
　否、否、それこそ否
「違うって───言ってるのに」
　非ず非ず、それこそ非ず。
「ちがうよ───ちがう、ちがう、ちがう、ちがうちがうちがう……！
　俺は知らない、こんなヤツ、街で見かけただけのただの他人だ……！
　ほら、おかしいじゃないか志貴……ただの他人をさ、どうして俺が殺さなくちゃいけないっていうんだよ……！」
entries.maoEnglish:
“No―――that’s not it.”
FALSE FALSE ABOVE ALL FALSE―――
“I keep saying—that's not it.”
It was not—none of it was; above all, it was not.
“No───no, no, no, no no no―――! I don’t know her; I only saw her in the street—she’s a complete stranger―――!
Think, Shiki—does it make any sense that I would have to kill a total stranger―――?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Wr… ong."
No, no, that is wrong.
"I'm saying---it's wrong."
It can't be.
It just can't be.
"Wrong!
---Wrong, wrong, wrong, wrongwrongwrong…!
I don't know her!
She's just some stranger I saw walking down the street……!
See!
Isn't that strange to you, Shiki…!?
She's a complete stranger!
Why would I have to kill her…!?"

entries.japanese:
叫んでも答えはない。
　それに理由ならはっきりしてる。
　彼女を見た時、俺は一つの事しか考えられなくなっていた。
「俺は────」
　そう、俺は───
entries.maoEnglish:
No matter how I screamed, no answer came.
Besides, the reason was perfectly clear.
The moment I saw her, I had become incapable of thinking about anything else.
“I────”
Yes, I───
entries.mirrorMoon:
There is no answer to my screams.
Besides, the reason is clear.
From the moment I saw her, I could only think of one thing.
"I------"
Yes, I----

entries.japanese: 遠野志貴は　あの女を　殺したい、と。
entries.maoEnglish: Shiki Tohno wanted to kill that woman.
entries.mirrorMoon: Tohno Shiki     wanted to  kill that girl.

entries.japanese:
それが、あの時の俺の全ての意志だったハズだ。
　ただ、頭の中がドロドロとしていて、あえて、そのイメージを言葉にしようとしなかっただけで。
entries.maoEnglish:
That must have been the whole of my will then.
My thoughts had only been too thick and muddy for me to force that image into words.
entries.mirrorMoon:
That's what I wanted to do back then.
Just that, it was all so muddy inside my head, I didn't put it in words.

entries.japanese:
「ちが─────う 」
　吐き気が、する。
「う、うう、う」
　胃の中のものが、戻ってくる。
「あ、ああ、あ」
　眼球に、赤い朱色がしみ込んでくる。
「あああああ――――！」

駆け出した。
　誰かに見られるとか、死体を隠さなくっちゃとか、そんな余分な事は一切考えられない。
　ただここから逃げ出したくて。
　半狂乱になって、見知らぬマンションの部屋から駆け出した─────
entries.maoEnglish:
“No─────”
Nausea welled up.
“Uh, ugh, ngh”
Everything in my stomach surged back up.
“Ah, aah, ah”
Scarlet seeped into my eyes.
“Aaaaaaah!”
I ran.
I couldn’t spare a thought for someone seeing me, or for hiding the body, or for anything else at all.
I only wanted to escape.
Half mad with terror, I fled the strange apartment—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Wro-----ng!"
I feel like throwing up.
"Uh, uggg, uh."
The contents of my stomach rise.
"Ah, aaah, ah!"
The crimson is soaking into my eyeballs.
"Aaaaaaaaah----!"
I dash out.
I don't think for even a moment about how I might be seen, or to hide the body.
I just want to escape from here.
Half-crazed, I flee from the unfamiliar apartment--

entries.japanese:
「ご―――ぼ――」
　胃液が逆流する。
　地面にひざまずいて、胃の中のものを残らず吐いた。
　食い物も、胃液も、泣きながら吐き出した。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ghh—blegh—” Acid flooded up my throat.
I dropped to my knees and vomited
everything in my stomach.
Food, bile—I sobbed and brought it all up.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Guuh---burgh!"
My stomach acid rises in my throat.
I throw everything back up.
My food, my gastric juices, everything, while I cry.

entries.japanese:
「はあ、はあ、はあ、はあ………！」
　胃の中には何もない。
　なのに起きてしまった出来事をなかった事に、もとの日常に戻そうとするかのように、体は嘔吐を強制する。
「……はあ……はあ……はあ……は、あ」
　痛い。
　内臓が焼けてるみたいに、痛い。
　涙は止まらなくて、体はゴミのように地面に崩れ落ちた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hah, hah, hah, hah―――”
Soon there was nothing left in my stomach.
Even so, my body forced me to retch, as if it could vomit away what had happened and drag me back into my ordinary life.
“Hah, hah, hah, ha, ah”
It hurt.
It hurt as though my insides were on fire.
The tears would not stop, and my body collapsed like garbage onto the ground.
entries.mirrorMoon:
*pant*, *pant*, *pant*, *pant*…!
There is nothing left in my stomach.
But my body continues to force me to throw up, as if trying to undo what had occurred and return me to my ordinary life.
…… *pant*… *pant*… *pant*… *pant*…
Pain.
It hurts, like my insides are burning.
The tears won't stop, and my body collapses to the floor like a pile of garbage.

entries.japanese:
「あ、ぐ─────ぐ、ぐぐ、ぐ」
　涙が止まらない。
　……俺は、人を殺した。
　人形でもバラすみたいにあっさりと、何の意味もなく、容赦なく殺してしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ah, gh─────gh, ghh, ngh”
I couldn’t stop crying.
I had killed someone.
I had killed her so casually, so meaninglessly and mercilessly, as if I had merely pulled apart a doll.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah, guh----gu, guguh, guh!"
I keep crying.
…… I killed someone.
I killed her without reason, without mercy.
Like breaking apart a doll.

entries.japanese:
───なんて事だろう。
　どうしてあんな気分になってしまったのか、
　どうしてほんとうに殺してしまったのか、
　今でもその理由が解らない。
「────うそだ」
　いや───いくらなんでもおかしすぎる。
　もしかするとさっきのは現実じゃないかもしれない。
ほら、いつもみたいに眩暈がして、その間に見ていたユメなんだ────
entries.maoEnglish:
───What had I done?
I still didn’t know why
I had felt that way or
why I had truly gone through with killing her.
“────It’s a lie.”
No—this was simply too impossible.
Maybe what had just happened wasn’t real. Maybe I had suffered one of my usual dizzy spells and dreamed the whole thing while I was unconscious—
entries.mirrorMoon:
---What was it all about?
Why I felt like that,
Why I killed her,
Even now, I can't find a reason.
"----It's a lie."
No---it's too odd to be true.
That thing that just happened might not be real.
So this is just one of those dreams I have when I faint---

entries.japanese:
「────うそだ」
　だいたい、どうしてナイフ一本で人間をあそこまでバラバラにできるっていうんだ。
　本で読んだ事がある。
人間一人をバラバラにするのは、ノコギリを使ったって何時間もかかる重労働なんだって。
　だから、こんなナイフ一本であんな事ができるはずがない。
　あんな『線』なんて初めからなくって、自分がかってにそう思い込んでいるだけの妄想なんだ────
entries.maoEnglish:
“────It’s a lie.”
How could anyone cut a human body into so many pieces with one knife?
I had read about this. Even with a saw, dismembering a person was backbreaking work that took hours.
There was no way a little knife like this could have done it.
Those ‘lines’ had never existed; they were only a delusion I had invented and convinced myself was real――――
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----It's a lie."
Besides, how can someone cut apart someone else like that with just a knife?
I read it in a book once.
It takes a whole day of strenuous labor to cut someone up, even when using a saw.
That's why there's no way I could have possibly done such a thing with just a knife.
These "lines" never existed in the first place.
Everything was just a delusion I had fallen for----
"----It's a lie."

entries.japanese:
「────うそだ」
「ご───ふ」
　胃液が唇からもれる。
　口はおろか、あごから下は胃液でベトベトだ。
　胃液には朱色が交ざっている。
　吐き出すものもないくせに胃が蠕動するもんだから、のどが傷ついて出血してるのか。
「い……た────」
　痛い。
　だからきっと。
　さっきのはユメなんかじゃなく、俺は、自分にうそをついている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“────It’s a lie.”
“Ghh.”
Bile leaked between my lips.
My mouth, my chin, everything below it was sticky with the stuff.
Scarlet threaded through it.
My empty stomach kept convulsing anyway—perhaps the retching had torn my throat open.
“It―――hurts────”
It hurt.
Which meant what had happened was not a dream.
I was lying to myself.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Guh---ffpt."
Gastric juice drips over my lips.
Passing out of my mouth, dripping down my jaw.
Mixed with the juices is something red.
My throat is probably bleeding because my stomach keeps trying to throw up even when there's nothing left in there.
"O…… u----"
It hurts.
That's why this…
This isn't a dream, and I'm just lying to myself.

entries.japanese:
「───全部、うそだ」
　そう、ほんとは理解してる。
　欲情してた。
あの女性を見て興奮してた。
　バラす時なんて、射精しそうなほど刺激的だった。

この目だってそうだ。
　あの『線』が紙を切るみたいにモノを切断してしまう『線』だってわかっていたのなら。
　遠野志貴は、さっきのように人間だって簡単にバラしてしまうって理解してたはずなのに。
　俺は、そんなことを考えもしないで、ただ普通に暮らしてしまった。
　―――自分が、簡単に何かを殺してしまえるような危険な人間なら。
　俺はこの目を潰すか、誰とも会わないような生活をするべきだったのに。
entries.maoEnglish:
“───It’s all a lie”
Yes. I knew the
truth. I had lusted after her; the sight of her had aroused me.
Cutting her apart had been so thrilling I had nearly come.
The same was true of my eyes.
If I knew those ‘lines’ could let me slice through anything as easily as paper, then Shiki Tohno should have understood that he could tear a human being apart just as easily as he had moments ago.
Yet I had never even considered it.
I had simply gone on living an ordinary life.
―――If I was dangerous enough to kill something so easily.
Then I should have gouged out these eyes or lived where I would never meet another person.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Yes, actually, I understand everything.
I lusted after her.
Just looking at her aroused me.
When I cut her apart, it was so thrilling I almost ejaculated.
These eyes, too.
If I knew these "lines" could cut things apart like paper being shredded…
I should have understood that even a person could easily be cut apart like I just did to her.
I had lived a normal life without even thinking about something like that.
---If I really am the sort of dangerous person who could easily kill just about anything…
Then I should have put out these eyes or lived a life without seeing anyone.
"…… I'm sorry, Sensei."
---I'm so sorry.
Not even such a simple promise,
was I able to keep----

entries.japanese:
「……ごめん、先生」
―――ほんとうに、ごめんなさい。
　そんな簡単な事さえ、
　遠野志貴は守れなかった────

「──────」
　でも、自分の事なんてどうでもいい。
　俺はあの人を殺してしまった。
　あの人の今までの人生とか、
　あの人のまわりの人達のこととか、
　あの人がずっと夢見ていた未来とか、
　全部───他人である自分がブチ壊してしまったんだ。
　後悔しても許されない。
　謝っても、絶対に許されない。
「俺────狂ってるのかな」
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――I’m sorry, Teach.”
―――I’m so, so sorry.
Shiki Tohno had failed to keep
even that one simple promise—
“—” But what happened to me didn’t matter.
I had killed her.
Her whole life until now,
the people around her,
the future she had always dreamed of—all
of it had been smashed to pieces by me,
a stranger.
Regret could never earn forgiveness.
No apology could ever earn it.
“Maybe―――I’m insane.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------"
But I don't care about myself.
I killed that person.
That person's life up until now.
The people around that person,
the future that person dreamed of,
everything---destroyed by a stranger.
Even if I regret it, I cannot be forgiven.
Even if I apologize, I cannot be forgiven.
"Have I----gone insane?"

entries.japanese:
わからない。
　あの時沸き上がった衝動は、もう微塵も残っていない。
　けどもし───またあの感覚がやってきたら、自分はどうなるんだろうか？
　耐えるとか、堪えるとか、そういった意思すら働かなかった。
　我慢する、という考えさえうかばない。
『あの女を殺す』
　そんなコトを、当たり前のように考えて実行してしまったのなら、自分でどうにかできる方法なんてありはしない。
entries.maoEnglish:
I didn’t know.
Not a trace remained of the impulse that had possessed me.
But if that feeling returned, what would become of me?
In that moment I hadn’t even tried to resist.
The very idea of restraint had never occurred to me.
『I’ll kill that woman』
If I could accept that thought as naturally as breathing and then carry it out, there was nothing I could do to control myself.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I don't know.
There isn't even a trace of that impulse left.
But if---that impulse came again, what will happen to me?
The thought of holding back never crossed my mind.
I did not even consider trying to stop myself.
"Kill this girl."
If it had seemed like the obvious thing to do, and I went through with it, then there's nothing I can do.

entries.japanese:
なら答えは簡単だ。
　俺は、きっと狂っている。
――――おそらくは八年前。
　死亡確定といわれた事故から、奇跡的に蘇生したその時から。
entries.maoEnglish:
Then the answer was simple.
I had to be insane.
――――Probably since eight years ago.
Since the moment I miraculously returned from the accident in which I had been declared beyond saving.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Then the answer is simple.
I must be insane.
----I've probably been mad since eight years ago, when I miraculously came back to life from a fatal accident.

entries.japanese:
―――――――さむ、い。
　いつのまにか、日が落ちている。

―――――――いまは、もうどれくらいだろう。
　よくわからない。
　ただ、鼓膜にはざあざあと、なにかノイズめいた音が聞こえてきている。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――――――Cold—so cold.
Somehow, the sun had already gone down.
―――――――What time was it now?
I couldn’t tell.
All I could hear was a ceaseless rushing at my eardrums, like the hiss of static.
entries.mirrorMoon:
-------I'm… cold.
The sun has gone down without me noticing.
-------What time is it now?
I can't tell.
My eardrums are filled with noise, like a static TV.

entries.japanese:
ざあ。
ざあ。
ざあ。
entries.maoEnglish: Shhh. Shhh. Shhh.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Static.
Static.
Static.

entries.japanese:
音はやまず、ひどくさむい。
　このまま――――ベンチに座ったままでいたら、死んでしまうような気がする。
　……死んでしまえるような、気がする。
entries.maoEnglish:
The sound never stopped, and the cold was terrible.
If I stayed sitting on this bench, I felt as though I might die.
As though I might be able to die.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The sound doesn't stop.
It's terribly cold.
If I stay----sitting down on this bench like this, I think I'm going to die.

entries.japanese: ざあ、ざあ、ざあ。
entries.maoEnglish: Shhh, shhh, shhh.
entries.mirrorMoon: Static, static, static

entries.japanese:
なにも感じない。
　繰り返す雑音も、壊死してしまいそうな寒さも、どうでもいい。
entries.maoEnglish:
I felt nothing.
The endless noise, the cold that seemed ready to rot my flesh away—none of it mattered.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I don't feel anything.
I don't care about that repeating noise or the freezing cold.

entries.japanese:
体は震えている。
　きっと原因は寒さか、不安か、恐れか、悔いか。
　けど、いずれかは判別できない。
　俺は人を殺して、そこに理由がないことを、説明できない。
―――お笑いだ。
　理由がないんだから、説明なんてできるはずがない。
entries.maoEnglish:
My body was trembling.
From cold, perhaps, or anxiety, or fear, or regret.
I couldn’t tell which.
I had killed someone, and I couldn’t explain why there had been no reason.
―――What a joke.
If there was no reason, of course I couldn’t explain it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
My body is shivering.
It may be due to the cold, or the uneasiness, or the fear, or regret.
I can't tell which.
I've killed someone, and I can't explain why I did it without any reason.
---What a joke.
There's no reason, so there's no way I can explain it.

entries.japanese:
ただ、殺したいから殺した。
　そんな理由、狂っている。
　……ああ、狂っているのならどんなに楽だろう。
　けどまだココロは正気のまま。
　正気のままだから、こうして麻痺してしまっている。
entries.maoEnglish:
I killed her because I wanted to kill her.
A reason like that was madness.
How much easier it would be if I were insane.
But my mind was still sane.
It was because I remained sane that I had gone numb.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I killed her just because I felt like killing her.
Such a reason is insanity.

…… Yeah, it would be so easy if I was just insane.
But my heart still remains sane.
It's only because I'm still sane that I can feel this numbness.

entries.japanese: ざあざあざあざあ。
entries.maoEnglish: Shhhhhhhhh.
entries.mirrorMoon: Staticstaticstatic.

entries.japanese:
手元には、まだナイフがある。
　死ぬことは。
とりあえず解決するコトはわりと簡単だ。
　けど、それができない。
　正気だからそれができない。
　死を恐れるココロと、
　そんな事は何の解決にも―――償いにもならないと、どこかで解っているココロがある。
　ざあざあ、という雑音。
　坂道を転がるように低くなっていく体温。
entries.maoEnglish:
I still had the knife.
Dying—settling everything for the moment—would be easy enough. But I couldn’t do it.
I was too sane to do it.
Part of me feared death.
Another
part knew that dying would solve nothing—that it would atone for nothing.
The ceaseless hiss.
My body heat tumbling away as if down a steep hill.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The knife is still in my hand.
Resolving this by killing myself, that's pretty easy.
But I can't do it.
I'm still sane, so I can't do it.
My heart fears death,
And somewhere in my heart, I know that doing so will not settle this---or atone for it.
The noise continues.
My body temperature continues to plummet.

entries.japanese:
―――自分で死ぬことはできない。
　　　けど、放っておけばこのまま消える。
　……結局、それがいいのかもしれない。
　俺みたいな人殺しは、生きていても、どうせ。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――I couldn’t kill myself.
But if I did nothing, I could simply fade away here.
Perhaps that was best after all.
There was no point in a murderer like me staying alive.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---I can't kill myself.
But if I leave things as they are, I'll disappear.
…… Maybe that's for the best.
Even if a killer like me survives…

entries.japanese: はやく
entries.maoEnglish: If only
entries.mirrorMoon: If I

entries.japanese: このまま
entries.maoEnglish: I could
entries.mirrorMoon: just quickly

entries.japanese: 死んで、
entries.maoEnglish: hurry up and die
entries.mirrorMoon: die

entries.japanese: しまえば。
entries.maoEnglish: just like this.
entries.mirrorMoon: like this…

entries.japanese:
「遠野……くん？」
　不意に。
　そんな名前を、呼ばれた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Tohno―――?”
Without warning.
Someone called that name.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Tohno… kun?"
Suddenly, my name is called.

entries.japanese:
「―――――――――」
　顔をあげる。
　そこには――――なんだか、もう何十年ぶりぐらいに思える、先輩の姿があった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“—” I raised my head.
She stood there—and somehow it felt as
though I hadn’t seen her in decades.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---------"
I raise my head.
There's Senpai----it feels like decades since I last saw her.

entries.japanese:
「どうしたんですか、こんな雨の中で座り込んじゃって」
「…………あ、め」
　……ああ、なるほど。
　さっきからざあざあとうるさかったノイズは、雨の音、だったのか。
　どうりで寒いはずだ。
　見れば、体中が濡れて冷えきっている。
「もうっ、傘もささないで。
遠野くん、そのままじゃ風邪をひいてしまいますよ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“What are you doing sitting out here in the rain?”
“Rain.”
Oh, of course.
The static that had been roaring in my ears all this time was rain.
No wonder I was cold.
Looking down, I saw that I was soaked through and chilled to the bone.
“Honestly, not even an umbrella. Tohno, you’ll catch cold like this.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"What are you doing sitting out here in the rain?"
"…… R… ain."
…… Ah, I see.
That static noise up until now was the sound of rain.
No wonder it's cold.
I can see now that I'm completely soaked and freezing.
"Oh, you don't even have an umbrella.
You're going to catch a cold like that, Tohno-kun."

entries.japanese:
……先輩の声は、すごく、いたい。
　思えばほんの数時間前まで聞いていた声なのに、今ではなんて―――遠くに聞こえる声なんだろう。

「遠野くん？
　わたしの声、聞こえてます……？」
「ん―――ああ、そうだね。
風邪ぐらい、ひいてみても悪くはないかな」
　なにも考えずに、ただそんな言葉だけを返した。
「だめですよ、いくら十月だっていってもこんな雨の中にいたら、風邪ぐらいじゃすまな―――」
　言いながら俺の体に触れて、先輩は言葉を切った。
entries.maoEnglish:
Ciel’s voice hurt.
I had heard it only a few hours ago, yet now it sounded impossibly far away.
“Tohno? Can you hear me?”
“Mm—yes. Maybe catching a cold wouldn’t be so bad.”
Without thinking, I answer with those words alone.
“Don’t say that—even in October, sitting in rain like this could leave you with far worse than a cold―――”
She touches me and breaks off.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Senpai's voice is so painful.
It was only a few hours ago that I had last heard it, but now---it sounds so distant.
"Tohno-kun?
Can you hear me…?"
"Nn---ah, yeah.
It wouldn't be so bad to catch a cold."
I just reply without thinking.
"That won't do!
You'll catch more than a cold with rain like this, even if it is October---"
Her sentence cuts off as she touches me.

entries.japanese:
「遠野くん、いったいどのくらいこうしてたんですか……！？
　体、こんなに冷たくなってるじゃないですか！」
　先輩は俺の腕を掴んで、強引にベンチから立たせた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Tohno, how long have you been out here…? Your body is freezing!”
She caught me by the arm and dragged me to my feet.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"How long have you been like this, Tohno-kun…!?
You're so cold!"
Senpai pulls my arm and forces me up from the bench.

entries.japanese:
「わたしの傘を貸してあげますから早く家に帰って、体をどうにかしてください。
早く温めないと本当に命にかかわります」
「……ああ、そっか。
けど、家には帰れない。
俺、もうどこにも行けない」
　……あんなコトをしてしまって、家には帰れない。
　もうどこにも―――俺には休んでいい場所なんて、ないと思う。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Take my umbrella and go home. Get warm as quickly as you can—your life could truly be in danger.”
“Oh—right. But I can’t go home. I can’t go anywhere anymore.”
Not after what I had done—I couldn’t go home.
There was nowhere left—nowhere in the world where I had any right to rest.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I'll lend you my umbrella, so please hurry and go home, and do something about your body.
It'll really be a matter of life and death if you don't warm up quickly."
"…… Ah, yeah.
But I can't go home.
I can't go anywhere ever again."
…… I can't go home after doing something like that.
I don't think there's anywhere left where I can rest anymore.

entries.japanese:
「―――――――」
　先輩はじっと、俺を見つめている。
「―――わかりました。
それじゃあわたしの部屋に行きましょう。
遠野くんの家よりは近いですから、ちょうどいいです」
　先輩はぐい、と俺の腕を引っ張っていく。
「……………」
　振り払うことは、できなかった。
　俺は何も考えられなかったし、その―――先輩の体温は、なにもかも麻痺したこのセカイの中で、ただ一つ確かなものだったから。
entries.maoEnglish:
“—” She studied me in silence.
“All right.
Then come to my place. It’s closer than your house, so that works out perfectly.”
She took hold of my arm and pulled me along.
“…”
I couldn’t shake her off.
I was incapable of thought, and her warmth was the one sure thing left in a world where everything else had gone numb.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-------"
Senpai stares at me.
"---I see.
Then let's go back to my room.
It's closer than your house, so it's perfect."
Senpai pulls me by my arm.
"…………"
I can't shake her off.
I can't think about anything at the moment, and---Senpai's warmth is the only certain thing in this world where everything feels numb.

entries.japanese:
……先輩の部屋は、よくある二階建てのアパートの一室だった。
　台所と六畳の部屋が一つあるだけで、本当に狭い。
　部屋は先輩らしく小綺麗で、そんな些細なことが少しだけ、麻痺した神経をほぐしてくれた。
entries.maoEnglish:
Ciel’s apartment was one unit in an ordinary two-story building.
It was tiny, with nothing but a kitchenette and a single room of barely ten square meters.
The place was neat in a way that suited her, and that small, familiar detail eased a little of the numbness in my nerves.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Senpai's room is a common one-room apartment in a two-story building.
Just one really small, cramped room the size of six tatami mats and one kitchen.
As one might expect from Senpai, the room is a neat one.
That trivial fact relaxes my numbed nerves just a little.

entries.japanese:
「はい、これで体を拭いてください」
　バスタオルを手渡される。
「すみません、遠野くんのサイズにあう洋服はないみたいです。
ちょっと、そのままで我慢してください。
すぐにあったかい飲み物を淹れますから」
　……先輩は台所へひっこんだ。
　小綺麗な部屋に、一人きりになる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Here, dry yourself with this.”
She handed me a bath towel.
“I’m sorry, but I don’t seem to have anything in your size. You’ll have to put up with the wet clothes for a moment. I’ll make something hot to drink right away.”
…She disappeared into the kitchen,
leaving me alone in the neat little room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Here, please wipe yourself with this."
She hands me a bath towel.
"Sorry, I don't have any clothes that fit you.
Please just bear with this for a while.
I'll go prepare something warm for you to drink right away."
…… Senpai retreats to the kitchen.
I'm left by myself in the neat room.

entries.japanese:
「―――――――」
　まさか、こんなふうに女の子の部屋にあがるなんて、思ってもみなかった。
　女の子の部屋。
　……女の人の、部屋。
　強引に押し入って、殺してしまった女の部屋。
「っ――――――！」
　吐き気が、する。
　俺は――――なにをしているんだろう。
　こんなところで。
　こんなところで、先輩に気遣ってもらう資格なんて、まったくないのに。
entries.maoEnglish:
“—” I had never imagined I would
enter a girl’s room this way.
A girl’s room.
…A woman’s room.
The room of the woman whose home I had
forced my way into before killing her.
“—!”
Nausea rose in me.
What was I doing here?
I had no right to sit in this place and let her care for me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-------"
I've never imagined coming into a girl's room like this.
A girl's room.
…… The room of a girl.
A girl's room which I forced myself into and killed a girl in.
"-------!"
I feel like throwing up.
What---am I doing here?
In such a place.
I have absolutely no right to receive Senpai's hospitality here.

entries.japanese:
「はい、お待たせしました―――って、遠野くん！」
「早く体を拭かないとダメじゃないですかっ！」
　怒鳴って、先輩はバスタオルで俺の頭をわしゃわしゃと拭き始める。
「ほら、シャツもびしょびしょなんですから脱がないとダメです。
このまま肺炎になってもしりませんからっ！」
　すごい剣幕で先輩はシャツのボタンに手をかける。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Here you are—Tohno!”
“You have to dry yourself right away!”
she shouted, then began vigorously scrubbing my hair with the bath towel.
“Look, your shirt is soaked too, so you have to take it off. Don’t blame me if you end up with pneumonia!”
Still in a fury, she reaches for my buttons.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Thanks for waiting.
Here you g---, Tohno-kun!"
"You've got to wipe yourself down, quickly!"
Senpai scolds me as she begins to rub my head with the bath towel.
"See, your shirt is all soaked too.
You've got to take it off.
You might catch pneumonia like this!"
A very fierce-looking Senpai undoes the buttons on my shirt.

entries.japanese:
と。
　その指がぴたりと止まった。
「………えーと、その」
　先輩はまじまじと俺の胸を見る。
「……これ、もう塞がってる傷、ですよね？」
　……ああ、胸の古傷を見てびっくりしたのか。
　俺の胸の真ん中に火傷みたいな跡があるんだから、知らなかったらびっくりするものなのかもしれない。
「……ああ、それは平気。
もう八年も前のものだから」
「そうですか。
……よかった、遠野くんがおかしい原因がこの傷だったら、今すぐ病院に連れていかなくちゃいけませんものね」
　先輩は淡く、柔らかく微笑む。
　……ずきり、と。
　その笑顔を見て、胸が痛んだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
And then.
Her fingers stop dead.
“Um―――that―――”
She stares at my chest.
“This scar is already healed, isn’t it?”
Oh—the old scar on my chest has startled her.
If you did not know about the burn-like mark in the center of my chest, perhaps it would be alarming.
“It’s fine. That happened eight years ago.”
“I see. Thank goodness—if that wound were the reason you were acting strangely, I’d have to take you to a hospital this instant.”
She gives me a faint, gentle smile.
A sharp ache.
The sight of her smile hurts my chest.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Suddenly, her fingers stop.
"…… Um… er."
Senpai takes a long hard look at my chest.
"…… This is a healed wound, isn't it?"
…… Ah, she must be surprised to see the old wound on my chest.
The burn-like marks are right in the middle of my chest.
She might be surprised at seeing them because she didn't know.
"…… Yeah.
They're fine.
It's already been eight years."
"I see.
…… Thank goodness.
If this wound was the reason you're acting funny, I'd have to take you to the hospital right away."
Senpai gives a faint, soft smile.
…… A twinge.
When I see her smiling face, my chest hurts.

entries.japanese:
「……いいです。
自分でできますから、ほっといてください」
「はい。
それじゃお茶を持ってきます。
あ、シャツを脱いだらそこの毛布を上着代わりにするんですよ」
「………………」
　バスタオルでズボンを拭く。
　それでもズボンは湿っているので、こんな姿で毛布をはおったら濡らしてしまう。
　シャツは脱いで、上半身はバスタオルで包んだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“That’s enough. I can manage by myself, so please leave me alone.”
“All right. I’ll bring the tea. Once your shirt is off, use that blanket as a coat.”
“…”
I wiped down my trousers with the towel.
They were still damp, and wrapping the blanket around myself like this would only get it wet.
I took off my shirt and wound the bath towel around my upper body instead.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… It's alright.
I can do it by myself, so leave me alone."
"Okay.
I'll bring you some tea then.
Oh, if you take your shirt off, please use that sheet there and warm yourself."
"…………"
I wipe my trousers with the bath towel.
But even so, my trousers are still wet.
The sheet is going to get soaked if I cover myself with it.
I take off my shirt, and wrap the top half of my body with the towel.

entries.japanese:
「あ、拭き終わりました？
　それじゃお茶にしましょうか」
　先輩はティーセットを手にして座り込む。
「遠野くんも座ってください。
立ったままでいられるとこっちが落ち着かないじゃないですか」
「……………」
　言われたままに座った。
　先輩は紅茶を淹れて、俺に手渡してくれた。
「――――――――」
「……………………」
　お互い、何も言わない。
　先輩は俺がいることなんて気にしてないように紅茶を飲んでいる。
　俺も、先輩につられるように紅茶を口にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh, you’re done? Then let’s have tea.”
Carrying a tea set, she settled down beside me.
“Sit down, Tohno. If you keep standing there, you’ll make me restless.”
“…”
I sat as instructed.
She poured the tea and handed me a cup.
“—” “…”
Neither of us spoke.
She drank as if my presence required no special notice.
Drawn along by her example,
I raised the tea to my lips.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah, are you finished wiping yourself?
Then let's have some tea."
Senpai sits down, holding a tea set.
"Please sit down too, Tohno-kun.
I can't calm down with you standing up."
"…………"
I do as I'm told and sit down.
Senpai pours some English tea and hands it to me.
"--------"
"…………"
Neither of us say anything.
Senpai drinks her English tea as if she doesn't notice my presence.
Following Senpai's example, I drink some as well.

entries.japanese:
――――あつい。
　舌先がヒリヒリするぐらい熱くて、どくん、と体に脈が入る。
　心臓とか脳とか、止まっていた器官が、少しだけ動いてくれたみたいだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――Hot.
It was hot enough to sting my tongue.
A heavy pulse struck through my body, and it felt as though my heart, my brain, all the organs that had stopped were beginning to move again.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----It's hot.
So hot that it hurts my tongue.
The warmth puts a pulse into me.
It feels like my heart, brain, and all my other organs that stopped begin to move a little again.

entries.japanese:
先輩は何も話さない。
　しばらくして、ティーカップの中が空になる。
　と、先輩は当たり前みたいに紅茶を注いでくれた。
entries.maoEnglish:
She said nothing.
After a while, my cup was empty.
As naturally as anything, she filled it again.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Senpai says nothing.
It's not long before the teacup is empty.
Senpai naturally refills the cup again with more.

entries.japanese:
「…………あ」
　なにか。
口にしないと、いけない気がする。
「遠野くん」
「っ―――――！」
　びくり、と反射的に体が引いた。
「わたし、ちょっと出てきます。
お留守番、頼めますか？」
「あ………う、うん、いいです、けど」
「はい、それじゃあお願いします。
すぐに帰ってきますから、あんまりヘンなことしちゃダメですよ」
　どこまで本気なのか、笑顔でそんなことを言って先輩は出かけてしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…Ah.”
I felt that I had to say something.
“Tohno.”
“―――――!”
My body recoils on instinct.
“I’m going out for a moment. Would you mind watching the place?”
“Ah―――y-yes, that’s fine.”
“Thank you. I’ll be right back, so don’t do anything too strange while I’m gone.”
She said it with a smile, leaving me unable to tell how serious she was, and went out.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……… Ah."
I get the feeling that I have to say something.
"Tohno-kun."
"------!"
I recoil in shock.
