I already know it as a fact that if she catches up to me, I will be killed-----

entries.japanese:
「あっ───」
　無様に地面に倒れこんだ。
　足がもつれてではなく、もう一歩も体が動かなくなって、前のめりに倒れこんだ。
「ぐっ───は、あ」
　倒れたまま這いずって、なんとか壁ぎわに辿り着く。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ah───”
I crashed gracelessly to the ground.
I had not tripped; my body could not take another step, and I pitched forward.
“Gh───hah, ah”
Still prone, I dragged myself toward a wall.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah---!"
Pathetically, I collapse to the ground.
I fall forward, not because I tripped, but because I simply can't move my body a single step further.
"Guh---ha, aah."
Lying there, collapsed, I somehow manage to crawl my way to the wall.

entries.japanese:
「────」
　壁に手をかけて立ち上がろうとしたけれど、ダメだった。
　立ち上がったとたん膝から力を失って、ドスンと尻餅をつく。
　そのまま、体はもう動いてくれなかった。
「はあ────はあ、はあ────」
　顔をあげて息を吸う。
entries.maoEnglish:
“────”
I caught the wall and tried to stand, but it was useless.
The moment I rose, my knees gave way and I landed heavily on my backside.
My body would move no farther.
“Haa────haa, haa────”
I raised my face and tried to breathe.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----"
I try to pull myself up against the wall, but it's no good.
My knees lose their strength as I try to rise, and I collapse back down.
My body won't move anymore.
*pant* *pant* *pant*
I look up as I breathe.

entries.japanese:
────苦しい。
　まったく酸素がぜんぜん足りない。
　おかげで頭がまともに動きやしない。
　自分がなにをしているのかもちんぷんかんぷん。
　どうしてこんなコトをしているのかわからない。
　どうして、なんで、なんで殺した女が生きているのかもわからない。
entries.maoEnglish:
────Agony.
There was nowhere near enough air.
My mind could no longer work properly.
I had no idea what I was doing.
I could not understand why I was doing this.
I could not understand why―――why―――the woman I had killed was alive.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----It hurts.
I don't have enough oxygen.
I can't think properly because of it.
I can't even tell what I'm doing anymore.
I don't know why I'm doing this.

entries.japanese:
間違いなく完璧に、およそ考えられる最終的なカタチで俺はあいつを殺した。
　なのになんで、
　あいつは学校の前で俺を待って、あんなふうに楽しげに笑いかけたり出来るんだろう──？
entries.maoEnglish:
I had killed her beyond question, in the most absolute way imaginable.
So how could she wait outside my school
and smile at me with such delight?
entries.mirrorMoon:
Why?
Why?
I don't even know why the girl I've killed is alive.
Unmistakably, I've utterly and completely killed her in the most final way imaginable.
So why?
How can she be waiting for me in front of my school, smiling--?

entries.japanese:
「……確かに、殺したのに」
―――そうだ。
　たしかに殺したのに、
　たしかに殺したのに、
　たしかにころしたのに、
　たしかにコロシタノニ、
　なんで、なんで、なんで、なんで、なんで、なんで、なんで、なんで、なんで、なんで、なんで、なんで、なんで、なんで、なんで、なんで、なんで、なんで、なんで、なんで、なんで──────！？
entries.maoEnglish:
“But I know I killed her.”
―――Yes.
I know I killed her—
I know I killed her—
i know i killed her—
I KNOW I KILLED HER—
Why, why, why, why, why, why, why, why, why, why, why, why, why, why, why, why, why, why, why, why, why──────!?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I'm sure I killed her."
---That's right.
I'm sure I killed her.
I'm sure I killed her.
I'm sure I killed her.
I'M SURE I KILLED HER, SO
Why why why why why why why why why why why why why why why why why why why why why why why why why why why why-----!?

entries.japanese:
「あれ、追い掛けっこはもう終わり？」
　カツン。
　路地裏に軽やかな足取りでやってきた女は、残念そうに肩をすくめた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh, is our game of chase over already?”
Click.
The woman entered the alley with buoyant steps and gave a disappointed shrug.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Oh?
Is the chase over already?"
With light footsteps, she comes into the alley, shrugging her shoulders in disappointment.

entries.japanese:
「こんにちは。
昨日は本当にお世話になったわ」
　女はにこりと笑顔をうかべて、かつん、と音をたてて路地裏に入ってくる。
――――逃げなくちゃ。
　そう思って後に退こうとして、がつん、とコンクリートの壁に頭をぶつけた。
「追い駆けっこは終わりなんでしょ？
　だってここ袋小路だもん。
くわえて人気もないから、他に邪魔が入る心配もないし」
　よっぽど嬉しいのか、女は笑顔のままだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hello. Thank you ever so much for yesterday.”
Smiling sweetly, she stepped deeper into the alley, her heel striking a light note against the pavement.
――――I had to escape.
I tried to retreat and cracked my head against a concrete wall.
“The game is over, remember? This is a dead end. And there’s no one around, so we don’t have to worry about interruptions.”
She seemed delighted; her smile never faltered.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hello.
You really gave me some trouble yesterday."
With a warm smile, she comes into the alley.
----I've got to run away.
Thinking that, I retreat, only to hit my head against a concrete wall.
"The chase is already over, right?
This is a dead end, after all.
There's no need to worry about anyone coming along or interfering."
She smiles, looking very happy.

entries.japanese:
あわてて周囲を見渡す。
　路地裏に人気はなくて、自分のバカさかげんに本当に愛想がつきた。
　こんなところに逃げ込むなんて───自分から殺してくださいと言っているようなものじゃないか。
entries.maoEnglish:
I looked frantically around.
The alley was deserted, and I was truly disgusted by my own stupidity.
Fleeing into a place like this───wasn’t it practically asking her to kill me?
entries.mirrorMoon:
Panicking, I look around at my surroundings.
A desolate alley.
I'm disgusted at my stupidity.
Running away here is like asking her to kill me.

entries.japanese:
「長かったなぁ。
あれから十八時間、ようやく標的をつかまえた」
　かつん、とさらにもう一歩、女は路地裏に入ってくる。
「お、おまえ────」
「なに？」
「おまえは、たしかに────」
「ええ。
昨日貴方に殺された女よ。
覚えていてくれて嬉しいわ」
「ばっ───」
　嘘だ、そんなバカな話があるもんか……！
entries.maoEnglish:
“What a long wait. Eighteen hours, and at last I’ve caught my target.”
Her heel clicked as she took another step into the alley.
“Y-you────”
“What?”
“You were, I know you were────”
“Yes. I’m the woman you killed yesterday. I’m glad you remember me.”
“Th-that───”
It was a lie—nothing so absurd could possibly happen……!
entries.mirrorMoon:
"It's been a long time.
Eighteen hours since then, I finally found you."
She takes another step into the alley.
"Y-you----!"
"What?"
"I definitely----"
"Yes.
I'm the girl you killed yesterday.
I'm glad you remember."
"Th---"
That can't be true.
There's no way that can happen…!

entries.japanese:
「ふざけるな、死んだ人間が生きてるハズがないだろう！」
「そうだけど、そう驚く必要はないんじゃない？
　たんに生き返っただけなんだから」
　あっさりと答えて、女はかつん、と音をたてる。
　女との距離は、段々と狭くなっていく。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Don’t be ridiculous—dead people don’t come back to life!”
“True, but is it really that astonishing? I simply came back.”
She answered as casually as if it were nothing and took another step.
The distance between us continued to narrow.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Don't be ridiculous!
Dead people can't be alive!"
"That's true, but there's no need for you to be so surprised.
I just revived, that's all."
With that curt response, she takes another step, the sound of it reaching my ears.
The distance between us is gradually decreasing.

entries.japanese:
「……生き……返った？」
　呆然と女の台詞を繰り返す。
　生き返ったって事は、あのあと医者にでもかかって手術のすえに回復したのだろうか……？
entries.maoEnglish:
“Came―――back?”
I repeated her words numbly.
Did that mean a doctor had found her afterward, operated, and somehow restored her?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Re… vived?"
Stunned, I repeat her phrase back to her.
Revived… you mean some doctor saved her with some surgery…?

entries.japanese:
「―――って、罵迦にすんなっ！
　あんなに手足をバラバラにされて生き返る人間なんているはずがないだろ───！」
「うん。
だってわたし、人間じゃないもの」
「─────は？」
　女の言葉の意味は、その、あんまりに簡単すぎて違う解釈ができない。
　わたしは人間じゃない。
　たしかに、目の前の女はそう言い切った。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――Don’t treat me like an idiot! No human being could come back after being cut to pieces───!”
“Exactly. I’m not human.”
“─────What?”
Her words were too simple to mean anything else.
I’m not human.
The woman before me had said it plainly.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Don't be stupid!
There's no way any human could revive from being cut apart like that---!"
"Yeah.
Then again, I'm not human."
"-----Huh?"
Her words are so simple there's no way I could have misinterpreted them.
I'm not human.
That's what the girl in front of me said.

entries.japanese:
「……人間じゃ、ない……？」
「もう、そんなの当たり前でしょ。
手足をバラバラにされて、ひとりでに再生できる人間がいると思う？」
「───────」
　そんな人間、いるわけがない。
　そんなのは人間に似ているだけのまったく違う怪物だろう。
　殺しても蘇る。
　息の根を止めてもおかまいなし。
　ばらばらにしても、すぐに元通りになって動きはじめる人間とは呼べないもの。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Not―――human?”
“Isn’t that obvious? Do you imagine a human could be dismembered and regenerate all by herself?”
“───────”
Of course no such human existed.
Anything like that would merely resemble a person; beneath the likeness, it would be an entirely different monster.
Kill it and it comes back.
Snuff out its life and it carries on as if nothing happened.
Tear it to pieces and it simply puts itself back together and starts moving again—something that could never be called human.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… You're not human…?"
"Geez, isn't that obvious?
Do you think there's a human being out there who can revive after being cut into pieces?"
"-------"
There's no way a human like that could exist.
Something like that is just a monster who looks human.
Something that revives even when killed.
Something that death is irrelevant to.
Something that quickly returns to normal and starts moving even after being cut to pieces isn't something you can call human.

entries.japanese:
「う────そ」
　それが、今自分の目の前にいる女の正体らしい。
　笑おうとして声をあげたけれど、喉は乾いてうまく笑えなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“L────ie”
This, apparently, was the true nature of the woman before me.
I tried to laugh, but my throat was too dry to produce the sound.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No… way."
That seems to be the girl right before my eyes.
I try to laugh, but my throat is so dry, I can't.

entries.japanese:
「……なんだよ、それ」
　笑い話にしてはあんまりに出来が悪い。
　加えて、笑い話にできない材料がとりあえず揃っている。
　だって、確かに。
　この女が人間じゃないのなら、殺したはずなのに生きているってコトに、道理が通るかもしれないじゃないか。
―――頭の芯が落ち着いていく。
　とりあえずよく見て。
　そのあとで色々と考えなくっちゃいけない状況だ、これは。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What the hell is that supposed to mean?”
It was too stupid even to pass for a joke.
Worse, there was too much evidence to dismiss it as a joke.
After all, it was true.
If this woman was not human, then perhaps it made sense that she was alive even though I had killed her.
―――Something at the core of my mind settled.
First, I needed to look at her carefully.
Then I could think through everything else.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… What the hell is that?"
It's not exactly a funny story.
Besides, there's too many things in this story that aren't funny.
Because definitely…
If she's not human, it explains why she's alive even after I've killed her.
---I start to calm down.
This is a situation where I've got to observe everything and think it over.

entries.japanese:
「……人間じゃないって言ったな。
それじゃあナンなんだ、おまえ」
「わたし？
　わたしは吸血鬼って呼ばれてるけど。
あなたたち流に言えば人間の血を吸って生きてる怪物かな」
　……良かった。
　なにが良かったかって、吸血鬼っていう単語は、それなりに解りやすかったから。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You said you aren’t human. Then what are you?”
“Me? People call me a vampire. In your terms, I suppose that means a monster that lives by drinking human blood.”
Good.
The word vampire, at least, was something I could understand.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… You said you're not human.
So what are you?"
"Me?
I'm called a vampire.
To put it in your terms, I'm a monster who lives off human blood."
…… Ah, good.
"Vampire" is at least something I can easily understand.

entries.japanese:
「そう、吸血鬼なんだ───」
　ええ、と女は満足そうに笑った。
　……なんて、ふざけた返答なんだろう。
　吸血鬼って昼間は歩けないっていうのが通説なんじゃないのか。
　まあ、今はそんなコトなんて些細な問題かもしれないが。
「……で。
その怪物が俺なんかに何の用だっていうんだ」
　なぜか、女はびっくりして身をひいた。
　と、それも束の間で、すぐに両手を腰にあてて、むっとした眼差しを向けてくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Right―――a vampire───”
With a satisfied smile, the woman said yes.
What a ridiculous answer.
Wasn’t it common knowledge that vampires couldn’t walk in daylight?
Though perhaps that was a minor issue now.
“…So, what does a monster like you want with someone like me?”
For some reason, the woman drew back in surprise.
It lasted only an instant; then she planted both hands on her hips and gave me an offended glare.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I see.
You're a vampire---"
She smiles in satisfaction to indicate her assent.
…… What a crazy reply.
I've heard that vampires can't walk around during daytime, but I guess that's a trivial matter right now.
"…… So, what does this monster want from me?"
For some reason, she recoils as if surprised.
After a moment, she puts her hands on her hips and looks at me, irritated.

entries.japanese:
「貴方、昨日わたしに何をしたか忘れたの？
　あなたは見ず知らずのわたしを、会った瞬間にバラバラに殺してくれたのよ。
それなのに何の用だ、なんてよっぽど手慣れてるみたいね」
　怒っている、いうより呆れているみたいだ。
　でも、今はこっちだってそんな気分をしている。
　なにしろ自分が殺した女に、よくも殺してくれたわねって恨み言を言われているんだから。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Have you forgotten what you did to me yesterday? You met a perfect stranger and immediately cut her to pieces. And now you ask what I want, as if this happens to you all the time.”
She sounded less angry than appalled.
At the moment, I felt much the same.
After all, the woman I’d killed was standing here complaining that I’d had the nerve to kill her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Have you forgotten what you did to me yesterday?
Even though you didn't know me, you cut me apart the moment we met.
You've got to be pretty used to this to ask me what I want with you now."
She looks more disgusted than angry.
But right now, that's how I feel, too.
Because someone I've killed is complaining to me about me killing her.

entries.japanese:
「ちょっと。
聞いてるの、殺人狂」
「……ああ、聞いてる。
我ながらものすごい悪運持ちだなって、いま噛み締めてるところなんだ。
悪いけど、ちょっと黙っててくれないか」
 ───ったく、ほんとになんて悪い運なんだろう。
　理由もなく、突然殺したくなった女がいて、そのまま勢いにまかせて殺してしまった。
　そのあとの記憶が曖昧で、それは夢だったのかと安心していたらそれはやっぱりホントのことで。
くわえて、実は殺した相手が人間じゃなかったときた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hello? Are you listening, you homicidal maniac?”
“Yeah, I’m listening. I’m just taking in how spectacularly unlucky I am. Sorry, but could you be quiet for a moment?”
───Seriously, what rotten luck.
For no reason at all, I had suddenly wanted to kill a woman, and then I had given in to the impulse and done it.
My memories afterward were blurred, and just when I’d reassured myself that it must have been a dream, it turned out to have been real after all.
And now, to crown everything, the person I’d killed wasn’t even human.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hey!
Are you listening, murderer?"
"…… Yeah, I'm listening.
Sorry, could you shut up for just a minute?
I'm reflecting on how unlucky this is, even for me."
---Sheesh.
I have the worst luck.
There was a girl I wanted to kill for no reason, and I killed her on pure impulse.
My memory wasn't clear after that, so I calmed down, thinking it was just a dream… but it turned out to be real.
What's more, it turns out the person I've killed isn't even human.

entries.japanese:
「――――――ん」
　窓ごしの陽射しで目が覚めた。
　……雨は止んでいるのか、雨音はしない。
　空は曇り模様らしく、陽射しは明るいものとは言えなかった。
「……………え？」
　きょろきょろと周りを見渡す。
　……明らかに、自分の部屋ではない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――――Mm.”
Sunlight through the window awakened me.
The rain must have stopped; I could hear none falling.
The sky remained overcast, and the light was far from bright.
“―――――――Huh?”
I looked around in confusion.
This was plainly not my room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------Nn."
The sunlight streaming through the window wakes me.
…… Maybe the rain stopped; I can't hear it anymore.
It seems the sky outside is cloudy.
The sunlight isn't what you could call bright.
"…… Eh?"
I look around.
…… This is obviously not my room.

entries.japanese:
「あ、おはようございます。
昨夜はぐっすり眠れましたか、遠野くん？」
「あ――――――――」
　思い、だした。
　ここは先輩の部屋で、俺は先輩のベッドを借りて、一泊してしまったんだ――――
「あ―――うん。
おはよう、先輩」
　なにかすごく恥ずかしくなって、ベッドから跳び起きた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh, good morning. Did you sleep well, Tohno?”
“Ah――――――――”
I remembered.
This was Ciel’s apartment, and I had borrowed her bed and spent the night here.――――
“Ah—right. Good morning, Ciel.”
Overcome by embarrassment, I sprang out of bed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah, good morning.
Did you sleep well last night, Tohno-kun?"
"Ah--------!"
I remember now.
This is Senpai's room.
I had borrowed her bed for the night----
"Ah---yeah, good morning, Senpai."
Becoming extremely embarrassed, I hop off the bed.

entries.japanese:
「えっと、昨日はすみませんでした。
色々お世話になっちゃって、その―――」
「はい、一つ貸しにしておきますね」
　先輩は笑顔で返答してくる。
　……なんていうか、すごく大人だな、と思った。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Um, I’m sorry about yesterday. You did so much for me, and―――”
“Then I’ll consider it one favor you owe me.”
Ciel answered with a smile.
She seemed extraordinarily grown-up.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Uh… sorry about yesterday.
I caused you all sorts of trouble, and---"
"Yes, you owe me one."
Senpai replies with a smile.
…… How do I put this… She seems very mature.

entries.japanese:
「と、ともかくありがと。
それじゃあ俺、帰るから」
「あれ、そうなんですか？
　まだ朝の六時になったばかりですよ、遠野くん」
「そうだけど、昨日は無断外泊しちゃったから。
早めに屋敷に戻らないと秋葉になんて言われるかわからない」
「ああ、妹さんのことですね。
えっと、一応昨日は電話しておいたから大丈夫だと思いますよ」
　さらりと、先輩はとんでもない事を口走った。
「ちょっ―――電話したって、先輩が、うちに？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“A-anyway, thank you. I should go home.”
“Already? It’s only just six.”
“I know, but I stayed out all night without permission. If I don’t return early, there’s no telling what Akiha will say.”
“Oh, your sister. I called your house yesterday, so I think it will be all right.”
Ciel casually uttered this catastrophe.
“Wait―――you called my house?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"A-anyhow, thanks.
I'll be going home now."
"Oh, really?
It's barely six o'clock, Tohno-kun."
"Yes, but I didn't get permission to stay the night away from home yesterday, so if I don't hurry back to the mansion, there's no telling what Akiha will say."
"Ah, your little sister.
Well, I've already called her, so it should be okay."
Senpai delivers her earth-shattering statement with a casual air.
"Wh---you called my house, Senpai?"

entries.japanese:
「はい。
遠野くんがうちに泊まるって連絡をいれておかないといけないかなって思ったんですけど、ご迷惑でした？」
「なっ―――――――」
　絶句した。
　シエル先輩がうちに電話したっていう事は、つまり、女の子が『遠野くんはうちに泊まるそうです』なんてことを連絡したっていう事だ。
　それは、なんていうか―――
entries.maoEnglish:
“Yes. I thought someone ought to tell them you were spending the night here; was that a problem?”
“Wh―――――――”
I was speechless.
If Ciel had called my house, that meant a girl had called to tell them, “Tohno will be staying at my place tonight.”
That was―――
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yes.
I thought it wouldn't be right if I didn't contact them about you staying over.
Is that a problem?"
"Wh------!"
I'm at a loss for words.
Ciel-senpai calling my house means a girl has called my house saying, "Tohno-kun is staying over at my place."
That's… well---

entries.japanese:
「―――困る。
それは、すごく困る」
　秋葉が電話に出ていたりしたら、俺はとんでもない女ったらしという誤解をされてしまう。
　ただでさえ遠野家は厳格なんだから、そんなコトをしたってバレたらどうなるか想像したくもない。
「……遠野くん……わたしの部屋に泊まったこと、そんなに嫌だったんですね」
「あ、いや、そういうことじゃなくて、その……うちの家っていうのはすごく厳しくて、決して先輩のことを嫌がってるわけじゃなくて―――」
　しどろもどろになって弁解をする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――A problem. A very serious problem.”
If Akiha had answered, she would think I was some shameless womanizer.
The Tohno family was strict enough already; I did not want to imagine what would happen if they learned I’d done such a thing.
“So—you hated staying in my room that much?”
“No—that’s not it; my family is extremely strict, and this has nothing to do with disliking you―――”
I stumble over myself trying to explain.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Yes, it's a problem.
A big problem."
If Akiha had been the one who picked up the phone, she's going to think I'm some kind of playboy.
Given the severity of the Tohno household, I don't even want to imagine what would happen if she found out about that sort of thing.
"…… Tohno-kun… did you really hate staying at my house that much?"
"Ah, no, that's not it.
It's just that… my house is really strict.
It's definitely not because I don't like you, Senpai---"
Flustered, I try to explain the misunderstanding.

entries.japanese:
「……いいです、言い訳なんかしてもらわなくても」
　先輩は悲しそうに目をふせる。
　……昨夜世話になったせいか、この人にこういう顔をされるとこっちが参ってしまう。
「違うって、俺は本当に先輩には感謝してるんだ。
今だってすごく気持ちが楽になってるし、昨日の夜だって、先輩がいなけりゃどうなってたか解らないぐらいだったんだ……！」
entries.maoEnglish:
“It’s all right—you don’t have to make excuses.”
Ciel lowered her eyes sadly.
After all she had done for me the night before, I could not bear to see her look that way.
“That isn’t what I mean; I truly am grateful. I feel much better now, and last night—without you, I don’t know what would have happened to me.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
Senpai closes her eyes sadly.
…… Is it because I caused her so much trouble last night?
I feel so bad when I see her make an expression like that.
"I'm telling you, that's not it.
I'm really grateful to you, Senpai.
I'm feeling much better now, and if you hadn't been there for me last night, I don't know what would've happened to me…!"

entries.japanese:
「―――はい。
そうですね、遠野くんの顔はいつもの調子に戻ってくれてます。
昨夜どうしたか知りませんけど、元気になってくれて嬉しいです」
　唐突に。
　先輩はこれ以上ないっていうぐらい、満面の笑みをうかべた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――Yes. You look like yourself again. I don’t know what happened last night, but I’m glad you’re feeling better.”
All at once.
Ciel’s face blossomed into the broadest smile imaginable.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Yes, you're right.
You look like you're back to normal now.
I don't know what happened last night, but I'm glad you're feeling better."
Suddenly, Senpai gives the biggest smile anyone could possibly give.

entries.japanese:
「――――え？」
「冗談ですよ。
わたしだって遠野くんの家に直にお電話なんかしません。
乾くんにお願いして、昨夜遠野くんは乾くんの家に泊まった、という電話をしてもらいました。
それでしたら問題はありませんよね？」
「……ああ、それなら問題はないけど……先輩、ちょっと趣味悪い。
いまのは本当に心臓が止まるかと思ったじゃないか」
「はい。
わたし、わりといじわるなんですよ。
好きな子っていじめたくなるじゃないですか。
それといっしょです」
「……え？」
―――好きな子って、それは、その―――
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――What?”
“I was joking. I would never call your house directly. I asked Inui to telephone and say you had spent the night at his home. That won’t cause any trouble, will it?”
“No, that’s fine, but—you have a cruel sense of humor. I honestly thought my heart would stop.”
“I can be rather mean. You know how people want to tease someone they like? It’s the same thing.”
“…What?”
―――Someone she liked—did that mean—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----Eh?"
"I was just joking.
Even I wouldn't directly call your house.
I asked Inui-kun to call your house and tell them that you were staying with him last night.
There should be no problem with that, right?"
"…… Yeah, that should be no problem… but that was kind of a mean joke, Senpai.
I thought my heart was going to stop."
"Yes, I'm actually pretty mean.
Pick on the ones you like, right?"
"…… Eh?"
---Ones you like?
Then that means---

entries.japanese:
「でも、たしかにお家には早めに帰ったほうがいいですね。
ええっと、ちょっと待ってください」
　先輩はなにやらタンスの中をごそごそとあさっている。
「はい、遠野くん。
粗品ですけど、これあげます」
　言って、先輩は古ぼけた指輪を差し出してきた。
「……粗品って……何これ、先輩」
「お守りです。
遠野くん、なんかぽーっとしていて危ないから、持っててください」
「あ、うん―――貰えるものなら何でも貰うけど……わかった、大事にするよ」
　指輪を受け取って、ポケットに入れる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Still, you should probably return home early. Now—wait a moment.”
Ciel began rummaging through a chest of drawers.
“Here, Tohno. It isn’t much, but you may have this.”
She held out an old, tarnished ring.
“What is it, Ciel?”
“A protective charm. You have a dangerous habit of drifting through the world half-awake, so keep it with you.”
“Well—if it’s free, I’ll take it; all right, I’ll treasure it.”
I accepted the ring and slipped it into my pocket.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"But, it's true you should go home early.
Please hold on for a second."
Senpai rummages around in her drawers for something.
"Here you go, Tohno-kun.
It's a little gift for you."
Saying that, Senpai hands me an old-looking ring.
"…… A little gift… what is it, Senpai?"
"It's a protective charm.
You seem to be dangerously spaced out a lot, so please hold on to it."
"Ah… yeah---I'll take anything that's given to me, but… alright.
I'll take good care of it."
Accepting the ring, I put it in my pocket.

entries.japanese:
「それじゃそろそろ行くよ。
……その、さ。
昨日は本当にありがとう。
先輩が言ってたとおり、自分なりに償いっていうのを考えてみるから」
「はい。
それでは学校でお会いしましょう」
entries.maoEnglish:
“I should go. There was one more thing. Thank you—truly. Like you said, I’ll try to work out for myself how I can atone.”
“All right. I’ll see you at school.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Alright.
I'll see you at school."

entries.japanese:
―――先輩は笑顔で送ってくれた。
　けど、その笑顔はもう二度と見れないかもしれない。
　昨日、俺が殺してしまった女性の遺体はとっくに発見されて、屋敷のほうには警察がやってきているかもしれないのだ。
　……けど、それから逃げるわけにもいかない。
　今は先輩の笑顔にお礼をいって、遠野の屋敷に戻るだけだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Ciel saw me off with a smile.
But I might never see that smile again.
The body of the woman I had killed yesterday might already have been discovered; the police might even be waiting at the estate.
Yet I could not run from that.
For now, all I could do was thank Ciel for her smile and return home.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Senpai sees me off with a smile.
But that smile is one I might never see again.
The woman I killed might be found already, and police might already be at the mansion.
…… But I can't run away from it.
All I can do is thank Senpai and return to the Tohno mansion.

To say the results first, the mansion is as it always was.

entries.japanese: 結論から言うと、屋敷の様子は普段どおりだった。
entries.maoEnglish: As it turned out, everything at the estate was perfectly ordinary.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah, welcome home, Shiki-san."
As I enter the lobby, Kohaku-san greets me with a smile.

entries.japanese:
「あ、おかえりなさいませ、志貴さん」
　なんて、ロビーに入るなり琥珀さんに笑顔で挨拶をされてしまった。
「あ……ああ、ただいま。
あの、琥珀さん？」
「ええ、朝ごはんですね？
　すぐに支度をしますから居間で待っていてください。
秋葉さまも先ほど済ませたばかりですから」
　琥珀さんはパタパタと音をたてて居間の方へ去っていってしまった。

……平和すぎる。
　昨日の女性の死体はまだ発見されていないんだろうか。
「………………」
　とりあえず制服を着替えに自室に戻る事にしよう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh, welcome home, Shiki.”
Kohaku greeted me with a smile the instant I entered the lobby.
“Ah… I’m home. Kohaku, is―――” “Breakfast?
I’ll prepare it at once, so please wait in the sitting room. Miss Akiha only just finished hers.”
Kohaku hurried toward the sitting room with quick, pattering footsteps.
It was too peaceful.
Had they still not found the woman’s body from yesterday?
“…”
For the moment, I decided to return to my room and change uniforms.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah… yeah, I'm home.
Um, Kohaku-san?"
"Ah, do you want breakfast?
I'll have it ready soon, so please wait in the sitting room.
Akiha-sama has just finished hers."
Kohaku-san patters off towards the sitting room.
…… It's too peaceful.
Maybe they haven't found the body yet.
"…………"
For now, I head towards my own room to change.

entries.japanese:
自分の部屋に戻ると翡翠がいた。
「―――おはようございます、志貴さま。
お帰りになられたのですね」
「うん、ついさっき。
……あのさ、翡翠。
悪いんだけど、替えの制服ってある？
　いま着ているヤツ、昨日の雨で濡れちゃってさ」
「……かしこまりました。
すぐにご用意いたします」
　翡翠は一礼して、音もなく部屋から出ていく。
　その後、翡翠が持ってきてくれた替えの制服に着替えて、居間へ向かった。
entries.maoEnglish:
Hisui was there when I entered my room.
“―――Good morning, Master Shiki. You have returned.”
“Yeah. I just got back. Hisui, do I have another uniform? The one I’m wearing got soaked in yesterday’s rain.”
“Certainly. I shall prepare it immediately.”
Hisui bowed and left without a sound.
Once she returned, I changed into the fresh uniform and went to the sitting room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Hisui is in my room when I return.
"---Good morning, Shiki-sama.
It seems you have returned."
"Yeah, just now.
…… Listen, Hisui, do I have a spare uniform?
The one I'm wearing now is soaked from yesterday's rain."
"…… I understand.
I will have one prepared immediately."
Hisui bows, and silently leaves the room.
After changing into the uniform Hisui brings me, I head towards the sitting room.

entries.japanese:
居間には秋葉が憮然とした表情でソファーに座っていた。
「――あら、おはようございます兄さん。
いつのまにかお帰りになってたんですね」
　秋葉の声には、どことなく非難の棘がある。
「……ああ、おはよう。
その、朝から機嫌が悪そうだな、秋葉」
entries.maoEnglish:
Akiha sat on the sofa wearing a thoroughly displeased expression.
“――Why, good morning, Brother. I hadn’t noticed you’d returned.”
Her voice carried a faint barb of accusation.
“Morning. You seem to be in a bad mood already, Akiha.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
A disappointed-looking Akiha is sitting on the sofa in the sitting room.
"---Oh, good morning, Nii-san.
It seems you have returned."
Akiha's voice contains thorns filled with blame.
"…… Yeah, good morning.
You look kind of grumpy this morning, Akiha."

entries.japanese:
「ええ。
兄さんが頻繁に外泊をされる方だとは知りませんでしたから。
機嫌を損ねている、というよりは呆れているんです」
　じとり、とした視線を向けてくる秋葉。
「……う」
　外泊したのは事実なので、こっちとしては反論のしようがない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I never knew you made such a habit of spending nights away, Brother. I am not in a bad mood so much as exasperated.” Akiha gave me a long, reproachful look.
“Urk.” I had indeed spent the night
away.
There was no way I could argue.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yes, I was unaware you spend the night elsewhere quite often.
I am more astounded than angry."
Akiha glares at me.
"…… Uhhh."
It's true I spent the night somewhere, so I can't argue.

entries.japanese:
「まあ、体調が悪くなったのでしたら仕方がありませんけど。
乾さん、という方とは中学校の頃からの友人なんですってね」
「そうだけど……そっか、電話をしてくれたのはあいつなんだっけ」
　……トウトツに、不安になった。
　あいつはなんていう口上でここに電話をかけたんだろう……？
entries.maoEnglish:
“Still, if you became ill, it couldn’t be helped. This Inui has been your friend since middle school, I understand?”
“Yeah—right, he was the one who called.”
A sudden anxiety seized me.
What on earth had Arihiko told them?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Well, I suppose there was no helping it if you weren't feeling well.
The one called Inui-san is your friend from middle school, isn't he?"
"Yeah… I see, so he was the one who called you."
…… Suddenly, I feel uneasy.
Just what did he say when he called my house……?

entries.japanese:
「だいたいですね、学校を早退されるにしても、連絡を入れてくだされば迎えの車を送れるじゃありませんか。
　何を遠慮しているか知りませんけど、兄さんは遠野家の長男なんです。
使えるものはなんでも使ってください。
……そうでなくても、兄さんは人より体が弱いんですから」
「――――あ」
　そうか、昨日は学校を早退したんだっけ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Even if you leave school early, Brother, you need only telephone and we can send a car.
I don’t know why you hesitate, but you are the eldest son of the Tohno family. Use whatever is available. Especially when your health is poorer than most people’s.”
“――――Ah.”
Right—I was supposed to have left school early yesterday.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Besides, even if you had to leave school early, you could have just called me and I would have sent a car to pick you up.
I don't know why you are so reserved, but you are the eldest son of the Tohno household, Nii-san.
Please use everything at your disposal…… Besides, your body is weaker than that of a normal person."
"----Ah."
Oh yeah, I left school early yesterday.

entries.japanese:
「雨にうたれたぐらいで貧血を起こすなんて、兄さん、体の具合が悪いんじゃないですか？
　一度主治医に看てもらうにしても、登下校は車で送ってもらったほうがいいんじゃありません？」
「…………」
　なるほど。
そういった理由で有彦の家に泊まった、という事になっているのか。

「大丈夫、秋葉が気にするような事じゃない。
ちゃんと月に一回は病院に通ってるし、車なんかで送られたらそれこそ体が鈍るだろ。
　秋葉が俺のことでそこまで神経質になることはないよ。
ま、心配してくれるのは嬉しいんだけどさ」
「……そんなこと、ないです。
私、兄さんの心配なんてしてません、から」
　ふい、と微妙に秋葉は視線を逸らした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“If being caught in the rain is enough to make you collapse from anemia, perhaps you’re unwell, Brother. You should see your doctor. Perhaps you should even have a car take you to and from
school.”
“…” So that was the story: I had become ill in the rain and stayed at Arihiko’s house.
“I’m fine. I visit the hospital every month, and being driven everywhere would only make me weaker.
You don’t need to be this nervous over me. Though I am glad you care.”
“――That isn’t true. I’m not worried about you, Brother.”
Akiha looked away slightly.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"To collapse from anemia just by getting soaked from the rain… are you not feeling well, Nii-san?
Shall I have the family doctor examine you and send you to and from school in a car from now on?"
"………"
I see.
So that was the reason I was supposedly staying at Arihiko's house.
"It's nothing for you to worry about, Akiha.
I go to the hospital once a month like I'm supposed to.
Taking me to school by car is just going to dull my body even further.
There's no need for you to be that sensitive about my body, though I'm glad you're worried about me."
"…… That's not true.
I'm not worried about you at all, Nii-san."
Akiha subtly avoids looking at me.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さーん、ご用意できましたー」
　食堂から琥珀さんの声が聞こえてくる。
「んじゃ、そういうわけでメシ食ってくる」
「もうっ。
兄さん、その乱暴な言葉づかいはやめてください」
　きりっ、と秋葉は視線を鋭くする。
「……ああ、もとの調子に戻ってきたな。
やっぱり秋葉はそうでなくっちゃ落ち着かない。
俺の事なんか心配しないでいいから、気楽にしてろよ」
「―――しつこいですねっ。
私、兄さんの心配なんてしてませんっ！」
　秋葉はぷい、と顔を背ける。
　それを微笑ましく眺めながら、食堂に移動した。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Shiki, everything’s ready!”
Kohaku called from the dining room.
“Well, I’m off to eat.”
“Honestly, Brother, please stop speaking so crudely.” Akiha’s gaze sharpened.
“Ah.
There you are. You’re finally back to normal. It doesn’t feel right unless you’re like this, so stop worrying about me and relax.”
“―――You are infuriating! I told you I am not worried about you, Brother!”
Akiha jerks her face away.
Smiling at the sight, I went to the dining room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-san, it's ready!"
I can hear Kohaku-san's voice from the dining room.
"Right, so I'm gonna get some grub."
"Oh, Nii-san!
Please refrain from talking in such an unrefined manner!"
Akiha shoots me a sharp glare.
"…… Ah, you're acting normally again.
That's how you should be, Akiha.
You don't have to worry about me, so just relax."
"---You are so persistent!
I am not worried about you, Nii-san!"
Akiha quickly looks away.
Looking at her with a faint smile, I go to the dining room.

entries.japanese:
「いってらっしゃいませ」
　翡翠はいつもどおりの台詞をいった後、じっと視線を向けてきた。
「志貴さま、昨夜はどうなされたのですか」
「……いや、別になにもないよ。
ただ雨にあてられてさ、貧血を起こしただけなんだ。
これからは気をつける」
「責めているのではありません。
ただ、今朝の志貴さまはひどく無理をしているように見えます。
どうか道々、お気をつけくださいませ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Have a safe journey.”
After her customary farewell, Hisui continued to watch me.
“Master Shiki, what happened last night?”
“Nothing. I was caught in the rain and had an anemic spell. I’ll be more careful.”
“I am not reproaching you. Master Shiki merely appears to be forcing himself this morning. Please take great care along the way.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Please take care."
Saying the same thing as she always does, she continues to stare at me.
"Shiki-sama, what happened to you last night?"
"…… Nothing in particular.
I collapsed from anemia when it started to rain on me.
I'll be careful from now on."
"I am not placing any blame on you, Shiki-sama, but you look like you are pushing yourself this morning.
Please take care along the way."

entries.japanese:
翡翠は深々とおじぎをして俺を送り出した。
 ……まいったな。
　できるだけ平静にふるまって、秋葉にも琥珀さんにもボロをださなかったっていうのに、翡翠には通じなかったらしい。
「……もしかして気遣ってくれたのかな、翡翠」
　いつも淡々とした彼女の感情はわかりにくい。
　ともかく、今日が最後の登校になるかもしれないんだ。
　できるだけいつも通りに、悔いの残らないような一日にしよう────。
entries.maoEnglish:
Hisui bowed deeply as she saw me out.
So much for that.
I had behaved as calmly as possible and kept both Akiha and Kohaku from noticing anything, yet Hisui had seen through me.
“Was that her way of worrying about me?”
Her emotions were difficult to read beneath that constant composure.
In any case, this might be my last day of school.
I would live it as normally as possible and leave nothing to regret.──────
entries.mirrorMoon:
Hisui makes a deep bow and sees me off.
…… Oh man.
I tried to act as normally as I could, and although I didn't give myself away to Akiha and Kohaku-san, it didn't seem to have worked on Hisui.
"…… I wonder if Hisui is worried about me."
It's hard to tell when she looks so disinterested all the time.
Today might be my last day of school anyway.
I'll try to spend it as I always do, so I won't have any regrets----

entries.japanese:
どんなにこっちの心境が複雑でも、朝の様子は変わらない。
　学校に近付くにつれ、学生服姿の生徒たちを多く見かけるようになってくる。
　休日前の土曜日。
　遠野志貴にとって、学校というものはこれで最後になるかもしれないかと思うと、歩いている足が止まりそうになる。
　それでもできるだけ平静に、二年間馴染んだ通学路を歩いていく。
　この交差点を抜けてしばらくすれば校門が見えてくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
However tangled my feelings, the morning itself remained unchanged.
As I approached the school, more and more students in uniform appeared.
It was Saturday, the day before a holiday.
The thought that this might be Shiki Tohno’s final day as a student nearly stopped my feet.
Even so, I followed the route I had known for two years, doing my best to remain calm.
Beyond this intersection, the school gate would soon come into view.
entries.mirrorMoon:
No matter how I feel, the morning is always the same.
As I approach the school, I begin to catch sight of more and more students in uniform.
It's Saturday, right before the day off.
My footsteps falter as I think about how this may be my last school day ever.
But still, as calmly as I can, I walk along the road that has become so familiar to me over the last two years.
It's only a little way to the school once I pass this intersection.

entries.japanese:
信号器が赤になって、横断歩道の前で立ち止まる。
　この歩道の向こうはすでに学校の塀がある。
　通学路だから歩道はガードレールに守られていて、今も我先にと生徒たちが校門へと向かっている。
　この時間、道向かいの歩道にはうちの学校の生徒の姿しかない。

……それしか、いない筈だ。
　なのに、車がせわしなく走っていく合間に、白い人影を見た気がした。
entries.maoEnglish:
The signal turned red, and I stopped at the crosswalk.
The school wall already ran along the far side of the road.
Guardrails protected the sidewalk on this busy school route, and students were hurrying toward the gate in a steady stream.
At that hour, the only people on the far sidewalk should have been students from my school.
They should have been the only ones there.
Yet between the ceaselessly passing cars, I thought I saw a figure in white.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The light turns red, and I stop in front of the crosswalk.
The school fence is on the other side of it.
Since it's a school path, the footpath is protected by a guardrail.
Even now, the students in front of me are heading towards the school gate.
There's no one but students from our school on the other side at this time of day.
…… There should be no one but the students.
But between the cars rushing by, I feel like I catch a glimpse of someone in white.

entries.japanese:
「─────な」
　そこにいたのは、彼女だった。
　肩口までの金の髪に白い服。
　細く長い眉と赤い瞳。
　たった一度しか見てはいないけれど、俺がその姿を見間違えるはずがない。
「──────」
　けど、そんな筈はないんだ。
　だって彼女は、昨日俺の手によって、バラバラに殺されたんだから。
entries.maoEnglish:
“─────Wh—”
It was her.
Golden hair brushing her shoulders, and white clothes.
Slender brows and crimson eyes.
I had seen her only once, but I could never mistake that figure.
“──────”
But that was impossible.
Yesterday, with my own hands, I had murdered her and cut her into pieces.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-----Wha……"
She is there.
Dressed in white, with golden hair down to her shoulders.
Long, slender brows and red eyes.
I've seen her only once before, but there's no way I could mistake her for someone else.
"------"
But that's impossible.
I killed her myself yesterday, cutting her into pieces.

entries.japanese:
信号が青にかわる。
　まわりの生徒たちは向こう側へと歩いていく。
　その中で、自分だけが立ち止まったまま呆然としていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
The light turned green.
The students around me crossed to the other side.
I alone remained rooted where I stood, staring.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The light turns green.
The students around me walk towards the other side.
I'm the only one amongst them who stands there, stunned.

entries.japanese:
彼女はガードレールに腰をかけて、足をぶらぶらとゆらしている。
　まるで何か、誰かを待っているような様子。
　どれくらい待っているのかは見当もつかないけれど、彼女の表情に険しいものはない。
 ───誰を待っているのだろう。
　まるで恋人と待ち合わせをしているふうに、彼女はそわそわして落ち着いていない。
entries.maoEnglish:
She sat on the guardrail, swinging her legs idly.
She looked as though she were waiting for someone.
I had no idea how long she had been there, but there was no anger in her face.
───Who could she be waiting for?
She fidgeted with the restless anticipation of someone waiting to meet her lover.
entries.mirrorMoon:
She sits on the guardrail, her legs swinging idly.
As if she is waiting for someone.
I can't tell how long she's been waiting, but her expression isn't a grim one.
---Who is she waiting for?
She fidgets restlessly, as if she were waiting for her lover.

entries.japanese: ───イヤな、予感がする。
entries.maoEnglish: ───Dread crawled through me.
entries.mirrorMoon: ---I have a bad feeling about this.

entries.japanese:
「あ―――――」
　白い女がこっちを見た。
　たぶん、そんなのはただの偶然。
　アレはただ似ているだけの他人で、彼女は別の誰かを待っているに決まってる。
　そうでなければ、この瞬間こそ悪い夢だ。
　だって、彼女はこの手で、完膚なきまでに殺したはずなんだから――――
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ah―――――”
The woman in white looked my way.
It was probably only a coincidence.
She had to be a stranger who merely resembled the dead girl, waiting for someone else.
Otherwise, this very moment was the nightmare.
because I had killed her with these hands—utterly, beyond all hope of survival――――
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah-----"
The girl in white looks over in my direction.
It's probably nothing more than a coincidence.
She's just a stranger who looks like her.
She must be waiting for someone else.
If not, then this moment must surely be a bad dream, too.
After all, I have completely and utterly killed her with my own hands----

entries.japanese:
けれど、女はこっちを見て笑っていた。
『やっと来たわね』と自分を殺した相手を見付けて、心の底から満足そうに――――
　女は親しげに手をあげて笑みをむけると、ガードレールから腰をあげた。
　さらり、と髪をなびかせてこっちに向かってくる。
「───────来る、な」
　悪い、夢だ。
　信号が赤になる。
entries.maoEnglish:
But the woman looked at me and smiled.
She had found the person who killed her, and her face shone with heartfelt satisfaction, as though to say, There you are at last――――
She raised one hand in a familiar greeting and rose from the guardrail.
Her golden hair streamed lightly behind her as she came toward me.
“───────Don’t come any closer.”
This was a nightmare.
The signal turned red.
entries.mirrorMoon:
But she's looking this way and smiling.
Looking very satisfied at having found the person who killed her, her smile seems to say, "you've finally come----"

Giving a familiar wave and a smile, she hops off the guardrail.
Fluttering her hair, she heads towards me.
"-------Don't come."
This… is a bad dream.
The light turns red.

entries.japanese:
「―――――――来るな、よ」
　彼女は気にした風もなく、車が行き交う道路を一直線に横断してくる。
　あと、ほんの数メートルも距離はない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――――――Don’t come any closer.”
Paying no attention, she walked straight across the road through the moving traffic.
Only a few meters remained between us.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-------Don't come near me."
She doesn't even look like she cares, walking straight across the street while the cars pass by.
There's only a few meters between us.

entries.japanese:
「……来るなって言ってるのに――――！！！」
　大声をあげても目の前の現実は変わらない。
　そのまま、俺は自分でもよくわからない声をあげて、白い女から逃げ出していた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I said, don’t come any closer――――!!!”
Shouting changed nothing.
I made some sound I could not understand and fled from the woman in white.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I'm telling you not to come----!!!"
The reality before my eyes does not change even when I scream out.
Screaming in a voice even I don't understand, I run from the girl in white.

entries.japanese:
走った。
　全力で走った。
　恥も外聞もなく、通り過ぎる人達を弾きとばしながら、アスファルトの上を全力疾走した。
「はっ、はっ、はっ、はっ─────！」
　呼吸が乱れて、心臓がばくばくと悲鳴をあげる。
　それでも走った。
　走らないと気が狂いそうだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
I ran.
I ran with everything I had.
With no thought for shame or appearances, I knocked people aside and sprinted flat-out over the asphalt.
“Hah, hah, hah, hah─────!”
My breath broke apart, and my heart screamed against my ribs.
Still I ran.
If I stopped, I felt I would go mad.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I run.
I run with all my strength.
With no regard to embarrassment or shame, I blast through the passersby, running full speed across the asphalt.
*huff* *huff* *huff* *huff*
My breathing is wild, and my heart screams out.
But still, I run.
I feel like I'm going to go crazy if I don't.

entries.japanese:
後ろを見る。
　白い服の女が歩いてくる。
　間違いなく俺を追ってきている。
　俺が殺した女が、俺を追いかけてきている。
　走る理由は、それだけで十分すぎた。
entries.maoEnglish:
I looked back.
The woman in white was walking after me.
There was no doubt: she was pursuing me.
The woman I had killed was coming for me.
That was more than reason enough to run.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I look behind me.
The girl in white is walking towards me.
She's definitely following me.
The girl I've killed is chasing me.
That's more than enough reason for me to run.

entries.japanese:
「はっ、はっ、はあ──────！」
　爆発しそうな心臓を無視して走り続ける。
　振り返るとあの女の姿がある。
　とことこと軽い足取りで逃げる俺を追ってきている。
「はっ、はっ、はっ、はっ─────！」
　顎があがる。
　両腕がだるい。
　足はとっくに千切れそうだ。
　だっていうのに、
　こんなにも全力で走っているのに、どうして歩いているだけの相手をふりきれないんだ──!
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hah, hah—haaah──────!”
Ignoring the heart that felt ready to burst, I kept running.
Whenever I looked back, she was there.
She followed my desperate flight with light, unhurried steps.
“Hah, hah, hah, hah─────!”
My chin lifted.
Both arms hung heavy.
My legs had long since felt ready to tear away.
and yet—even running with everything I had—
why could I not shake someone who was only walking—
entries.mirrorMoon:
*huff* *huff* *huff* *huff*
My heart feels like it's about to explode, but I ignore it and keep running.
When I look back, the girl is still there.
With those light footsteps, she follows me as I run away.
*huff* *huff* *huff* *huff*
My head droops down.
My arms feel heavy.
My legs feel like they're going to tear off.
But despite that,
I'm running with all my strength, and yet, I can't get away from someone just walking after me--!

entries.japanese:
「はっ、はっ、はっ、はっ────」
　息があがる。
　もう何キロ全力で走ったろうか。
　それでも振り返ればあいつが歩いてやってきている。
　自然に、散歩するような足取りでピッタリとくっついてきている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hah, hah, hah, hah────”
I could scarcely breathe.
How many kilometers had I sprinted?
Still, each glance behind showed her walking after me.
She matched me effortlessly with the ease of an afternoon stroll.
entries.mirrorMoon:
*huff* *huff* *huff* *huff*
My breathing is out of control.
I think I've already run several kilometers.
But even so, when I look back, she's always there, walking towards me.

entries.japanese:
「………はっ、はっ、はっ、はは、はははは」
　おかしくもないのに笑って、笑いながらまだ走った。
「はは、ははは、あははははははは！」
　笑いが止まらない。
　それでも走って、これ以上走れば死んでしまうって体が訴えているのに、まだ走った。

走る理由は簡単だ。
　だってあいつに追い付かれたら、俺は間違いなく殺される。
　何を根拠に、と自分自身でそんな妄想を笑い飛ばしても、そんなのが気休めだってのはやっぱり自分自身が一番よくわかっていた。
　理由も根拠も証拠もない。
　ただもう真実として、遠野志貴は、あの女に追い付かれたら殺されるって理解している─────
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hah, hah, hah—ha, ha ha ha.”
Nothing was funny, but I laughed, and kept running as I laughed.
“Ha, ha ha—ahahahahaha!”
The laughter would not stop.
My body screamed that another step would kill me, yet I continued to run.
The reason was simple.
If she caught me, I would unquestionably be killed.
I could ridicule the thought and ask what basis I had for such a delusion, but I knew better than anyone that I was only trying to reassure myself.
No reason, no basis, no proof.
Shiki Tohno simply understood it as truth: if that woman caught him, she would kill him─────
entries.mirrorMoon:
Naturally, like she's taking a stroll, she follows right behind me.
*huff* *huff* "…… Haha, hahaha!"
It's not funny, but I begin to laugh.
"Haha, hahaha, ahahahahahaha!"
I can't stop laughing.
But even so, I run.
My body complains that I'll die if I run any more, but I keep running.
The reason is simple.
If she catches me, she'll kill me for sure.
I ask myself what I base that on, trying to shake it off as mere imagination.
But even as I try to console myself, I am the one who knows best it's true.
There's no reason, no basis, no evidence.
I already know that if she catches up to me, I will be killed-----

entries.japanese:
「あっ───」
　無様に地面に倒れこんだ。
　足がもつれてではなく、もう一歩も体が動かなくなって、前のめりに倒れこんだ。
「ぐっ───は、あ」
　倒れたまま這いずって、なんとか壁ぎわに辿り着く。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ah───”
I crashed gracelessly to the ground.
I had not tripped; my body had simply lost the power to take one more step, and I pitched forward.
“Gh───hah…”
Still prone, I dragged myself toward a wall.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah!
---"
Pathetically, I collapse to the ground.
I fall forwards, not because I tripped, but because I simply can't move my body a single step further.
"Guh---ha, aah."
Lying there, collapsed, I somehow manage to crawl my way to the wall.

entries.japanese:
「────」
　壁に手をかけて立ち上がろうとしたけれど、ダメだった。
　立ち上がったとたん膝から力を失って、ドスンと尻餅をつく。
　そのまま、体はもう動いてくれなかった。
「はあ────はあ、はあ────」
　顔をあげて息を吸う。
entries.maoEnglish:
“────”
I caught the wall and tried to stand, but it was useless.
The moment I rose, my knees gave way and I landed heavily on the ground.
My body would move no farther.
“Haaah────hah, hah────”
I raised my face and tried to breathe.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----"
I try to pull myself up against the wall, but it's no good.
My knees lose their strength as I try to rise, and I collapse back down.
My body won't move anymore.
*pant* *pant* *pant*
I look up as I breathe.

entries.japanese:
────苦しい。
　まったく酸素がぜんぜん足りない。
　おかげで頭がまともに動きやしない。
　自分がなにをしているのかもちんぷんかんぷん。
　どうしてこんなコトをしているのかわからない。
　どうして、なんで、なんで殺した女が生きているのかもわからない。
entries.maoEnglish:
────Agony.
There was nowhere near enough air.
My mind could no longer work properly.
I had no idea what I was doing.
I had no idea why I was doing it.
I had no idea why—why—the woman I had killed was alive.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----It hurts.
I don't have enough oxygen.
I can't think properly because of it.
I can't even tell what I'm doing anymore.
I don't know why I'm doing this.

entries.japanese:
間違いなく完璧に、およそ考えられる最終的なカタチで俺はあいつを殺した。
　なのになんで、
　あいつは学校の前で俺を待って、あんなふうに楽しげに笑いかけたり出来るんだろう──？
entries.maoEnglish:
I had killed her beyond question, in the most absolute way imaginable.
So how could she wait outside my school
and smile at me with such delight?
entries.mirrorMoon:
Why?
Why?
I don't even know why the girl I've killed is alive.
Unmistakably, I've utterly and completely killed her in the most final way imaginable.
So why?
How can she be waiting for me in front of my school, smiling---?

entries.japanese:
「……確かに、殺したのに」
―――そうだ。
　たしかに殺したのに、
　たしかに殺したのに、
　たしかにころしたのに、
　たしかにコロシタノニ、
　なんで、なんで、なんで、なんで、なんで、なんで、なんで、なんで、なんで、なんで、なんで、なんで、なんで、なんで、なんで、なんで、なんで、なんで、なんで、なんで、なんで──────！？
entries.maoEnglish:
“But—I know I killed her.”
―――Yes.
I know I killed her—
I know I killed her—
i know i killed her—
I KNOW I KILLED HER—
Why, why, why, why, why, why, why, why, why, why, why, why, why, why, why, why, why, why, why, why, why──────!?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I'm sure I killed her."
---That's right.
I'm sure I killed her.
I'm sure I killed her.
I'm sure I killed her.
I'M SURE I KILLED HER, SO
Why why why why why why why why why why why why why why why why why why why why why why why why why why why why------!?

entries.japanese:
「あれ、追い掛けっこはもう終わり？」
　カツン。
　路地裏に軽やかな足取りでやってきた女は、残念そうに肩をすくめた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“So, is our game of chase over already?”
Click.
The woman entered the alley with buoyant steps and gave a disappointed shrug.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Oh?
Is the chase over already?"
With light footsteps, she comes into the alley, shrugging her shoulders in disappointment.

entries.japanese:
「こんにちは。
昨日は本当にお世話になったわ」
　女はにこりと笑顔をうかべて、かつん、と音をたてて路地裏に入ってくる。
――――逃げなくちゃ。
　そう思って後に退こうとして、がつん、とコンクリートの壁に頭をぶつけた。
「追い駆けっこは終わりなんでしょ？
　だってここ袋小路だもん。
くわえて人気もないから、他に邪魔が入る心配もないし」
　よっぽど嬉しいのか、女は笑顔のままだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hello. Thank you so much for yesterday.”
Smiling sweetly, she stepped deeper into the alley, her heel striking a light note against the pavement.
――――I had to escape.
I tried to retreat and struck my head against concrete.
“The chase is over, isn’t it? This is a dead end. Better still, no one else is here to interfere.”
She must have been delighted, because her smile never wavered.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hello.
You really gave me some trouble yesterday."
With a warm smile, she comes into the alley.
----I've got to run away.
So thinking, I retreat, only to hit my head against a concrete wall.
"The chase is already over, right?
This is a dead end, after all.
There's no need to worry about anyone coming along or interfering."
She smiles, looking very happy.

entries.japanese:
あわてて周囲を見渡す。
　路地裏に人気はなくて、自分のバカさかげんに本当に愛想がつきた。
　こんなところに逃げ込むなんて───自分から殺してくださいと言っているようなものじゃないか。
entries.maoEnglish:
I looked frantically around.
The alley was deserted; I was disgusted by my own stupidity.
Fleeing into a place like this was the same as asking her to kill me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Panicking, I look around at my surroundings.
A desolate alley.
I'm disgusted at how stupid I am.
To run away here is like asking her to kill me.

entries.japanese:
「長かったなぁ。
あれから十八時間、ようやく標的をつかまえた」
　かつん、とさらにもう一歩、女は路地裏に入ってくる。
「お、おまえ────」
「なに？」
「おまえは、たしかに────」
「ええ。
昨日貴方に殺された女よ。
覚えていてくれて嬉しいわ」
「ばっ───」
　嘘だ、そんなバカな話があるもんか……！
entries.maoEnglish:
“What a long wait. Eighteen hours, and at last I’ve caught my target.”
Her heel clicked as she took another step into the alley.
“Y-you────”
“What?”
“You were, without a doubt────”
“Yes. I’m the woman you killed yesterday. I’m glad you remember me.”
“Id───”
A lie—nothing so absurd could possibly happen…!
entries.mirrorMoon:
"It's been a long time.
Eighteen hours since then, I finally found you."
She takes another step into the alley.
"Y-you----!"
"What?"
"I definitely----"
"Yes.
I'm the girl you killed yesterday.
I'm glad you remember."
"Th---"
That's got to be a lie.
There's no way that can happen…!

entries.japanese:
「ふざけるな、死んだ人間が生きてるハズがないだろう！」
「そうだけど、そう驚く必要はないんじゃない？
　たんに生き返っただけなんだから」
　あっさりと答えて、女はかつん、と音をたてる。
　女との距離は、段々と狭くなっていく。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Don’t be ridiculous—dead people don’t come back to life!”
“True, but is it really that astonishing? I simply came back.”
She answered as casually as if it were nothing and took another step.
The distance between us continued to narrow.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Don't be ridiculous!
Dead people can't be alive!"
"That's true, but there's no need for you to be so surprised.
I just revived, that's all."
With that curt response, she takes another step, the sound of it reaching my ears.
The distance between us is gradually decreasing.

entries.japanese:
「……生き……返った？」
　呆然と女の台詞を繰り返す。
　生き返ったって事は、あのあと医者にでもかかって手術のすえに回復したのだろうか……？
entries.maoEnglish:
“Came―――back?”
I repeated her words numbly.
Did that mean a doctor had found her afterward, operated, and somehow restored her?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Re… vived?"
Stunned, I repeat her phrase back to her.
Revived… you mean some doctor saved her with some surgery…?
"---Don't be stupid!
There's no way any human could revive from being cut apart like that---!"

entries.japanese:
「―――って、罵迦にすんなっ！
　あんなに手足をバラバラにされて生き返る人間なんているはずがないだろ───！」
「うん。
だってわたし、人間じゃないもの」
「─────は？」
　女の言葉の意味は、その、あんまりに簡単すぎて違う解釈ができない。
　わたしは人間じゃない。
　たしかに、目の前の女はそう言い切った。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――Don’t treat me like an idiot! No human being could come back after being cut to pieces───!”
“Exactly. I’m not human.”
“─────What?”
Her statement was too simple to permit any other interpretation.
I’m not human.
The woman before me had said it without qualification.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yeah.
Then again, I'm not human."
"-----Huh?"
Her words are so simple there's no way I could have misinterpreted them.
I'm not human.
That's what the girl in front of me said.

entries.japanese:
「……人間じゃ、ない……？」
「もう、そんなの当たり前でしょ。
手足をバラバラにされて、ひとりでに再生できる人間がいると思う？」
「───────」
　そんな人間、いるわけがない。
　そんなのは人間に似ているだけのまったく違う怪物だろう。
　殺しても蘇る。
　息の根を止めてもおかまいなし。
　ばらばらにしても、すぐに元通りになって動きはじめる人間とは呼べないもの。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Not—human?”
“Isn’t that obvious? Do you imagine a human could be dismembered and regenerate all by herself?”
“───────”
Of course no human could do that.
Such a being would only resemble a person; underneath, it would be an entirely different monster.
Kill it and it comes back.
Snuff out its life and it carries on as if nothing happened.
Tear it to pieces and it simply puts itself back together and starts moving again—something that could never be called human.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… You're not human…?"
"Geez, isn't that obvious?
Do you think there's a human being out there who can revive after being cut up into pieces?"
"-------"
There's no way a human like that could exist.
Something like that is just a monster who looks human.
Something that revives even when killed.
Something that death is irrelevant to.
Something that quickly returns to normal and starts moving even after being cut to pieces isn't something you can call human.

entries.japanese:
「う────そ」
　それが、今自分の目の前にいる女の正体らしい。
　笑おうとして声をあげたけれど、喉は乾いてうまく笑えなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“A────lie.”
This, apparently, was the true nature of the woman before me.
I tried to laugh, but my throat was too dry to produce the sound.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No… way."
That seems to be the girl right before my eyes.
I try to laugh, but my throat is so dry, I can't.

entries.japanese:
「……なんだよ、それ」
　笑い話にしてはあんまりに出来が悪い。
　加えて、笑い話にできない材料がとりあえず揃っている。
　だって、確かに。
　この女が人間じゃないのなら、殺したはずなのに生きているってコトに、道理が通るかもしれないじゃないか。
―――頭の芯が落ち着いていく。
　とりあえずよく見て。
　そのあとで色々と考えなくっちゃいけない状況だ、これは。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What the hell is that supposed to mean?”
It was too stupid even to pass for a joke.
Worse, there was too much evidence to dismiss it as one.
After all, it was true.
If this woman truly was not human, then perhaps it made sense that she lived even after I killed her.
―――Something at the core of my mind settled.
First, I needed to look at her carefully.
Then I could think through everything else.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… What the hell is that?"
It's not exactly a funny story.
Besides, there's too many things in this story that aren't funny.
Because definitely…
If she's not human, it explains why she's alive even after I've killed her.
---I start to calm down.
This is a situation where I've got to observe everything and think it over.

entries.japanese:
「……人間じゃないって言ったな。
それじゃあナンなんだ、おまえ」
「わたし？
　わたしは吸血鬼って呼ばれてるけど。
あなたたち流に言えば人間の血を吸って生きてる怪物かな」
　……良かった。
　なにが良かったかって、吸血鬼っていう単語は、それなりにわかりやすかったから。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You said you aren’t human. Then what are you?”
“Me? I’m called a vampire. In your terms, I suppose I’m a monster that lives by drinking human blood.”
Good.
The word vampire, at least, was something I could understand.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… You said you're not human.
So what are you?"
"Me?
I'm called a vampire.
To put it in your terms, I'm a monster who lives off human blood."
…… That's good.
"Vampire" is at least something I can easily understand.

entries.japanese:
「そう、吸血鬼なんだ───」
　ええ、と女は満足そうに笑った。
　……なんて、ふざけた返答なんだろう。
　吸血鬼って昼間は歩けないって聞いたけど。
まあ、今はそんなコトなんて些細な問題かもしれない。
「……で。
その怪物が俺なんかに何の用だっていうんだ」
　なぜか、女はびっくりして身をひいた。
　と、それも束の間で、すぐに両手を腰にあてて、むっとした眼差しを向けてくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Right.
A vampire───”
She smiled in satisfaction.
What an absurd answer. I had heard vampires could not walk in daylight. Still, that seemed like a
minor concern now. “So what does a monster like you want with me?”
For some reason, the woman drew back in surprise.
It lasted only an instant; then she planted both hands on her hips and gave me an offended glare.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I see.
You're a vampire---"
She smiles in satisfaction to indicate her assent.
…… What a crazy reply.
I've heard that vampires can't walk around during daytime, but I guess that's a trivial matter right now.
"…… So, what does this monster want from me?"
For some reason, she recoils as if surprised.
After a moment, she puts her hands on her hips and looks at me, irritated.

entries.japanese:
「貴方、昨日わたしに何をしたか忘れたの？
　貴方は見ず知らずのわたしを、会った瞬間にバラバラに殺してくれたのよ。
それなのに何の用だ、なんてよっぽど手慣れてるみたいね」
　怒っている、いうより呆れているみたいだ。
　でも、今はこっちだってそんな気分をしている。
　なにしろ自分が殺した女に、よくも殺してくれたわねって恨み言を言われているんだから。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Have you forgotten what you did yesterday? The instant you met a total stranger, you cut me apart and killed me. And now you ask what I want with you, as though this sort of thing were routine.”
She sounded less angry than appalled.
At the moment, I felt much the same.
After all, the woman I had murdered was standing here reproaching me for the murder.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Have you forgotten what you did to me yesterday?
Even though you didn't know me, you cut me apart the moment we met.
You've got to be pretty used to this to ask me what I want with you now."
She looks more disgusted than angry.
But right now, that's how I feel, too.
Because someone I've killed is complaining to me about me killing her.

entries.japanese:
「ちょっと。
聞いてるの、殺人狂」
「……ああ、聞いてる。
我ながらものすごい悪運持ちだなって、いま噛み締めてるところなんだ。
悪いけど、ちょっと黙っててくれないか」
 ───ったく、ほんとになんて悪い運なんだろう。
　理由もなく、突然殺したくなった女がいて、そのまま勢いにまかせて殺してしまった。
　そのあとさんざん悩んで、自暴自棄になったりしたけど、とにかく自分なりの償いをとろうって決意したばかりだったていうのに、殺した相手が実は人間じゃなかったときた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hello? Are you listening, you homicidal maniac?”
“Yeah, I’m listening. I’m just taking in how spectacularly unlucky I am. Sorry, but could you be quiet for a moment?”
───Honestly, what rotten luck.
For no reason at all, I had suddenly wanted to kill a woman I’d never met—and then, carried by that impulse, I had done it.
I had suffered, despaired, and finally resolved to find some way of atoning; now, just as I made that decision, I learned the person I had killed was never human in the first place.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hey!
Are you listening, murderer?"
"…… Yeah, I'm listening.
Sorry, could you shut up for just a minute?
I'm reflecting on how unlucky this is, even for me."
---Sheesh.
I have the worst luck.
There was a girl I wanted to kill for no reason, and I killed her on pure impulse.
I agonized over it in deep despair… and even though I firmly decided to atone for my sins, the one I killed appears out of nowhere and says she isn't even human.

entries.japanese:
「――――――は、はは」
　つい笑ってしまう。
　……けど、そう悲観したことばかりじゃない。
　だって殺した相手が生き返ってるんだから、俺は誰も殺してない事になるじゃないか。
　そりゃあ『殺した』っていう行為は残るけど、彼女はちゃんと生きている。
　―――それだけは。
　　　　正直、喜ぶべきことだと思う―――
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――――Ha, haha”
A laugh escaped me.
But perhaps it wasn’t all hopeless.
If the person I killed had come back to life, then technically I hadn’t killed anyone.
The deed itself remained, but she was standing here alive.
―――That, at least.
I honestly thought I should be glad―――
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------Ha… haha…"
I can't help but laugh.
…… But it's not all bad.
If the person I killed has come back to life, then that means I haven't actually killed anyone, right?
Well, I suppose the fact remains that I "killed" someone, but she's still alive.
---And that's something I should honestly be happy about---

entries.japanese:
ああ、これならとりあえず生活は元通り。
　遠野志貴は今までどおりのスクールライフを送れると思う。
　……まあ、そのかわりになんかとんでもないヤツにこうしてライブで追い詰められてるってワケなんだけど、人殺しになるよりは遥かにラッキーだって言えるかもしれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
Then my life could return to normal.
Shiki Tohno could go back to his ordinary days at school.
Granted, some impossible creature had me cornered in an alley right now, but perhaps that still counted as far better luck than becoming a murderer.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Yeah.
With this, I should be able to get back to living my normal life.
A normal school life, just like I did up until now.
…… Well, in exchange, I seem to have been cornered by this strange person, but you might argue that it's a heck of a lot better than becoming a murderer.

entries.japanese:
「……オーケー、落ち着いた。
言いたい事があったら聞いてやるよ。
文句でも恨み言でも思う存分言ってくれ」
「そりゃあ言いたいコトはいっぱいあるけど……貴方、変わった人ね」
「開きなおってるだけだ。
これでも突飛なことにはそれなりに耐性がついていてね」
　まあ、それでもこんなケースにはついていけないけど。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Okay, I’ve calmed down. If you have something to say, I’ll listen. Complain, curse me—say whatever you want.”
“Oh, I have plenty to say, but you’re a strange one.”
“I’ve simply decided to face it. I’ve developed a reasonable tolerance for the unbelievable.”
Still, not even I could keep up with a case like this.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Okay, I've calmed down.
If you've got something to say, I'll listen: complaints, grudges, whatever.
Talk all you want."
"Yeah, I've got a whole lot of things to say to you… but you're weird."
"I'm just taking everything in right now.
You could say I've built up a resistance to weird stuff like this."
I don't think it's of much help in this case, though.

entries.japanese:
「ふーん………」
　女はじろじろと眺めてくる。
　その視線には敵意というものがない。
　……おかしいな。
やられたらやり返すっていうのは、きっと世界で共通の法則だと思う。
　そうなるとこの女は俺を殺そうとしているはずなんだけど―――
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hmm…”
The woman studied me from every angle.
There was no hostility in her gaze.
Something was odd. I’d always assumed retaliation was a law the whole world shared.
By that logic, this woman ought to be trying to kill me―――
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hmph……"
She stares at me.
It isn't malicious.
…… It's strange.
I'd thought that to get someone back when they got you was one of the common laws of the world.
Then she should be trying to kill me, but---

entries.japanese:
「――なに人のことをじろじろ見てるんだ。
おまえは俺に復讐しにきたってワケなんだろ。
なら――」
「ええ、たしかに殺したら殺し返すっていうのはセオリーよね。
　それがお望みならしてあげるけど、とりあえず今はパスかな。
それ、効率が悪いから」
　女はじっ、と真っ正面から俺を見据えてくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――Why are you staring at me? You came here for revenge, didn’t you? Then—”
“Yes, killing someone who killed you is the usual rule.
If that’s what you want, I could oblige, but I think I’ll pass for now. It would be inefficient.”
The woman looked me squarely in the eye.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"--What are you staring at?
You're here to get revenge, right?
Then--"
"Yeah, I guess I'm supposed to kill you back, in theory.
I'll kill you if you really want me to, but otherwise I'll pass for now.
It's not very efficient that way."
She stares at me head on.

entries.japanese:
「ねっ、反省してる？」
「――――え？」
　一瞬、目が点になった。
　この相手が、なにか―――ひどく場違いな声を出したから。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Well, do you regret it?”
“――――What?”
I could only stare.
The woman had said something so wildly out of place.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"So!
Are you sorry?"
"----Eh?"
I'm stunned for a moment.
The things she says are so… out of place.

entries.japanese:
「わたしを殺しちゃったことを反省してるかって聞いてるの。
　それでね、もし貴方が反省してるっていうんなら許してあげようかなって。
　貴方、人間にしては嘘が下手そうな感じだし」
「反省って―――俺が？」
「うん。
貴方がわたしにごめんなさいって言ってくれれば、わたしとしてはそれでいいよ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’m asking whether you feel any remorse for killing me.
If you do, I thought I might forgive you.
You don’t seem very good at lying, for a human.”
“Remorse—you mean me?”
“Yes. If you tell me you’re sorry, that will be enough for me.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I'm asking you if you're sorry for killing me.
I'm thinking about forgiving you if you are, you see.
Besides, I get the feeling you're a pretty bad liar for a human."
"Sorry---me?"
"Yep.
If you apologize to me, then I'm fine with that."

entries.japanese:
―――信じ、られない。
　なにが信じられないかって、それは。
　自分を殺した相手を許すとか許さないとかじゃなくて、その―――この相手の声が、ひどく優しく聞こえてしまった事が。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――I couldn’t believe it.
Not because she was talking about forgiving the person who had killed her.
What I couldn’t believe was how gentle her voice sounded.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---This is unbelievable.
What's so unbelievable?
Not that the person I killed is forgiving me, but… her voice sounds so kind.

entries.japanese:
「もうっ。
人が真面目に聞いてるんだから、ちゃんと答えるのが筋ってものでしょ。
ほら、早く答えて答えて。
貴方が反省してるのかしてないのか、はっきりさせないと先に進めないんだから」
　女はぷんぷんと怒っている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Honestly! I’m asking you seriously, so the least you can do is answer. Come on, hurry up. We can’t go any further until you tell me clearly whether you’re sorry.”
The woman was fuming.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hey!
You have to give an answer when people ask you seriously, you know.
Come on, hurry up and answer.
We can't get on with things until we make it clear whether or not you're sorry."
She is angry.

entries.japanese:
―――反省しているか、だって？
　そんなの、言われるまでもなく――――
「……そりゃあ後悔してる。
何であれ、俺は、人を殺してしまったんだから」
　容赦なく、なんの理由もなく、ただ自分のためだけに殺してしまった。
「……殺したって事も後悔してるけど。
なにより、俺はあんたを手にかけた。
だから―――」
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Was I sorry?
She hardly needed to ask――――
“…Of course I regret it; whatever the circumstances, I killed someone.”
Without mercy, without reason, solely to satisfy myself.
“…I regret the killing itself, but more than anything, I took your life with my own hands. So—”
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Am I sorry, she asks?
That goes without saying---

"…… Yeah, I regret it.
No matter what the reason is, I did kill someone."
Without mercy or reason.
I killed just for myself.
"…… I do regret the fact that I killed someone.
But more importantly, the person I killed was you, and so---"

entries.japanese:
……ああ、生き返っているから問題ない、とかいうのは嘘だ。
　遠野志貴は、目前の女性を殺してしまった。
　それは究極の略奪というか、これ以上ないっていうぐらいの暴力だと思う。
「だから―――あんたは、俺に復讐していいんだって――こうして俺に復讐に来たんだなって、当たり前のように、思ってた」
　……俯いたまま。
　誰に告白するのでもなく、そんな言葉を呟いた。
entries.maoEnglish:
No—the claim that it was fine because she had come back to life was a lie.
Shiki Tohno had killed the woman before him.
It was the ultimate theft—the most absolute act of violence imaginable.
“So I had simply assumed you had every right to take revenge—that you had come here to do exactly that.”
I kept my head bowed.
I murmured it to no one in particular.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… It's a lie that it's alright if she's alive.
It's a fact that I killed her.
It's the ultimate violation; the greatest violence possible.
"So---you can get your revenge on me--I thought it was only natural you'd be here to get revenge."
…… I hang my head, mumbling, like I'm confessing to someone.

entries.japanese:
「―――そっか。
うん、いい人なんだね、あなた」
　女は、笑った。
　自分のことを吸血鬼だなんて言うクセに、すごくまっすぐで、これ以上ないっていうぐらいの顔で。
「決めた。
やっぱり貴方にはわたしの手伝いをしてもらうわ」
「え―――――？」
　手伝いって、何を言っているんだろう、コイツは。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――I see. Yes, you really are a good person.”
The woman smiled.
She called herself a vampire, yet she wore the most open, honest expression imaginable.
“I’ve decided. You’re going to help me after all.”
“Wha―――――?”
What on earth did she mean by help?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---I see.
Hmm.
You're not a bad person."
She smiles.
Despite calling herself a vampire, she has a very honest face.
"I've decided.
I'm going to make you help me."
"Eh-----?"
Help her?
What is she talking about?

entries.japanese:
「……おい。
手伝いってなんだ」
「簡単よ。
この街に根付いている吸血鬼の始末を貴方に手伝ってもらおうかなってこと」
「――――？」
　……ちょっと、ますますわからない。
「吸血鬼の始末って、だっておまえは―――」
「ああ、ちがうちがう。
確かにわたしも吸血鬼だけど、この街に根付いている吸血鬼はまた別物よ。
　貴方、この街に住んでいる人でしょ？
　なら最近起きている殺人事件も知ってるわよね」
「ああ、もう何人も殺されてる事件だろ……って、ちょっと待った」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hey. What do you mean, help?”
“It’s simple. You’re going to help me dispose of the vampire entrenched in this city.”
“――――?”
Now I understood even less.
“A vampire—but you’re―――”
“No, no, that’s different. I am a vampire, but the one rooted in this city is another creature altogether.
You live here, don’t you? Then you know about the recent murders.”
“That case, where so many people died—wait.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Hey.
What do you mean by helping you?"
"It's simple.
I'm going to get you to help me deal with the vampire which took root in this town."
"----?"
…… Hold on, I'm getting more and more confused.
"Dealing with vampires?
But you're a---"
"Oh, no, no.
I am a vampire, but the vampire in this town is a different kind altogether.
You live here, don't you?
Then you should know about the murders that have been occurring lately, right?"
"Yeah, quite a few people have been killed already… hey, wait."

entries.japanese:
……思い出した。
　そういえば、あの通り魔殺人の犠牲者は、その全てが血液を搾取されていたとかいなかったとか。
「まさか、それって――――」
「まさかもなにも、ちゃんとニュースで『吸血鬼のしわざかっ』って言ってるじゃない。
　おかしな話よね、ちゃんと犯人が何であるかわかってるのに誰も吸血鬼退治をしないんだもの。
だから代わりにわたしがやってあげるしかないじゃない」
「いや、だって―――吸血鬼なんて存在しないだろ」
entries.maoEnglish:
I remembered.
There had been rumors that every victim of those random street killings had been drained of blood.
“You can’t mean――――”
“What do you mean, can’t mean—the news itself is asking whether a vampire did it?
It’s absurd: everyone knows what the culprit is, but no one goes vampire hunting. So I have no choice but to do it for them.”
“But―――vampires don’t exist.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… I remember now.
Come to think of it, all of the killer's victims had their blood extracted or something, didn't they?
"Don't tell me that----"
"Exactly.
Even the news is saying stuff like 'the work of a vampire', right?
It's a funny thing; they obviously know what kind of creature is doing it, but no one is going around trying to vanquish it.
That's why I've got no choice but to do it for them."
"Wait, but---vampires don't exist."

entries.japanese:
「むっ」
　女は不機嫌そうに眉をよせる。
　……そうだった。
　いま自分の目の前にいるのは、自分から吸血鬼を名乗っている正体不明の存在だったっけ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hmph.”
The woman scowled.
Oh, right.
The unidentified being before me had just declared herself a vampire.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hmph!"
She lowers her brows in annoyance.
…… Oh, that's right.
There's an unidentified person standing in front of me claiming to be a vampire herself.

entries.japanese:
「―――よく、わからないけど。
つまり、おまえは街で人を殺している吸血鬼を退治するって言いたいのか……？」
「そうなんだけど、その前になぜか見も知らずの殺人鬼に襲われて、いきなり殺されちゃったのよ。
　うん、アレにはまいったなあ。
もうかんっぺきな不意打ちで、反撃する間もなく十七つに切断されたんだから」
「う――――」
　そうか。
その殺人鬼って、ようするに俺のことを指しているのか。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――I’m not sure I follow, but… you’re saying you want to kill the vampire murdering people in this city?”
“Exactly. But before I could, some murderer I’d never even met attacked me out of nowhere and killed me.
That was a nightmare. He caught me completely off guard and cut me into seventeen pieces before I could even fight back.”
“U――――gh”
So when she said murderer, she meant me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---I don't really understand, but what you're trying to say is that you're here in this town to exterminate vampires, right…?"
"That's right, but before I could, I was attacked and killed by some unknown killer.
Yeah, that really got me.
It was a perfect surprise attack and I was cut into seventeen pieces without a chance to do anything."
"Ugh----"
I see.
She must mean me.

entries.japanese:
「そうよ。
わたしね、こうして復元するまでは本当に貴方を殺すつもりだったわ。
あんな屈辱を受けたのは初めてだったし、復元しきるのに八割以上の力を消費してしまったわけだし」
「けど、それよりなによりほんっっっとうにもの凄く痛かったんだから。
　あんまりにも痛いから気がふれそうになるんだけど、やっぱりあんまりにも痛くて正気に戻るの。
　そんな繰り返しを一晩体験したわたしの気持ち、わかる？」
「……………」
　わからない。
　というか、わかりたくない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Yes. Until I finished restoring myself, I genuinely intended to kill you. No one had ever humiliated me like that, and the restoration consumed more than eighty percent of my strength.”
“But more than anything, it hurt so incredibly much.
The pain was so intense I thought I would lose my mind, then it was so intense it shocked me sane again.
Can you imagine how it felt to spend an entire night trapped in that cycle?”
“……”
I didn’t.
More to the point, I didn’t want to.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"That's right.
Until I was fully recovered like this, I was really planning to kill you, you know.
That's the first time anyone's embarrassed me like that.
And, it took about eighty percent of my power to fully recover."
"But more importantly, it really, really hurt.
It was so painful I thought I was going to go crazy.
However, the pain was so great, it restored my sanity.
Do you know what it's like experiencing that over and over for a whole night?"
"…………"
I don't know.
Actually, I don't want to know.

entries.japanese:
「それでね、もう憎くて憎くて貴方を捜したわ。
目的である吸血鬼のコトも放っておいたぐらい、ただそれだけに熱中したのよ。
　それで貴方があの学校の学生だってわかって、それじゃあってあそこで待つコトにしたの」
「……わからないな。
そこまで憎かったのに、どうして俺のことを許すなんて言うんだ、おまえ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“I hated you so much that I searched everywhere. I became so consumed with finding you that I ignored the vampire I’d come here to hunt.
Once I learned you attended that school, I decided to wait there.”
“I don’t understand. If you hated me that much, why say you’ll forgive me?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"So, full of hatred, I went out to look for you.
I was so worked up that I didn't even care about the vampire, the very reason why I'm here.
I knew you were a student, so that's why I waited over there for you."
"…… I don't get it.
If you hated me so much, why are you forgiving me?"

entries.japanese:
「―――そうね、簡単に言えば時間がたって冷静になったのかな。
　わたしのほうも力を消費しちゃったコトだし、ここは貴方を殺すより盾になってもらったほうが効率的だなって考えたの」
「……ちょっと待て。
いま、なにかよからぬ事を口にしなかったか、おまえ」
「え？
　そんなこと言った、わたし？」
「人のことを盾にするって、言った」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Put simply, I suppose enough time passed for me to calm down.
I’ve lost most of my strength, so using you as a shield seemed more efficient than killing you.”
“…Wait. Didn’t you just say something extremely disturbing?”
“Did I?”
“You said you were going to use me as a shield.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Let's see… to put it simply, I calmed down after a while.
I already used up a lot of power, and I thought that it would be more efficient to use you as a shield than to kill you."
"…… Hold on.
You just said something really bad for me."
"Eh?
Did I say something like that?"
"You said you were going to use me as a shield."

entries.japanese:
「そんなの当然じゃない。
わたしは貴方のことを許したけど、それはわたし個人の感情に整理をつけただけだもの。
貴方が犯した『殺害』っていう行為そのものは、やっぱり気持ちじゃなくて行為で贖うしかないでしょ？」
「―――いや、でしょって言われても」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Of course. Forgiving you only settled my personal feelings. The murder itself still has to be atoned for through action, not sentiment, doesn’t it?”
“You say ‘doesn’t it’ as though that settles everything.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Of course.
I already did forgive you, but that's just my personal feelings.
You've got to atone for your murder through action, not just emotion, right?"
"---Well, even if you ask me…"

entries.japanese:
「なによ、素直なんだかいじわるなんだかわからないひとね。
繰り返すけど、わたしは貴方に殺されたのよ。
　想像できないでしょうけど、一度死んでから蘇生するのにはそれなりに力を消費するんだから。
　まあ単純に殺されただけならどうってコトないんだけど、貴方の方法は今まで見た事もない切断方式で、傷口が繋がらないから体を作り直すしかなかったの。
　その結果、わたしは生き返るのにほとんどの力を使ってしまったわけなんだけど─── 」
entries.maoEnglish:
“I can’t tell whether you’re straightforward or contrary. But I’ll repeat myself: you killed me.
You probably can’t imagine it, but returning to life takes a considerable amount of strength.
An ordinary killing would have been nothing, but your method of dismemberment was unlike anything I had ever seen; the wounds refused to join, so I had to rebuild my entire body.
As a result, reviving consumed nearly all my strength—”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"What's with you?
I can't tell when you're being sincere and when you're not.
Let me repeat it again: you killed me.
You probably can't imagine it, but it takes a lot of energy to regenerate once you've been killed.
Well, actually, it wouldn't be a big deal if you had just killed me, but the way you killed me was something I've never seen before.
I couldn't heal the wounds, so I had no choice but to remake my body parts.
That's why it took so much energy to revive---"

entries.japanese:
ぷんぷん、という擬音が似合いそうなほど、女は腹を立てている。
　……というか、今まで忘れていたけれど、話にした事でその時の怒りを思い出してしまったらしい。
entries.maoEnglish:
The woman was so angry she seemed to be giving off fumes.
Apparently, talking about it had revived an anger she had managed to forget.
entries.mirrorMoon:
She looks angry.
…… It seems like she's recalling her forgotten anger while she talks.

entries.japanese:
「とにかく、今のわたしは弱ってるの！
　二晩も経てば回復すると思うんだけど、その前に『敵』に襲われたら危ないじゃない。
　だからその間、貴方にはわたしの盾になってもらうからね」
「いや、もらうからねって―――なに勝手に決めてるんだよ、おまえ」
「なによ。
貴方のせいでこうなったんだから、それぐらいはして当然でしょう？
「それとも、やっぱり反省なんかしてないっていうの？」
　じっ、とまっすぐな目で女は見つめてくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“The point is, I’m weak right now! I should recover in two nights, but if my enemy attacks before then, I’ll be in danger.
So until I recover, you’re going to be my shield.”
“What do you mean, I’m going to—you can’t decide that on your own.”
“What? You’re the reason I’m like this, so it’s the least you can do.”
“Or were you never sorry after all?”
The woman held me with her clear, unwavering gaze.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Anyhow, I'm weak right now!
I think I'll be able to recover after two nights, but if the enemy attacks before then, I'll be in danger.
That's why for now, I'll have you be my shield."
"You'll have me do it---?
What are you doing, deciding everything by yourself?"
"What?
This is all your fault to begin with, so isn't that much to be expected?"
"Or are you not sorry after all?"
She looks straight at me with honest eyes.

entries.japanese:
「……………う」
　それは、卑怯だ。
　反省とかそういうコト以前に、そんな目をされるのは、卑怯だ。
　……自分のことを吸血鬼だなんて言ってるクセにそんな純粋な目をするのは、反則だと思う―――
「俺は、その―――」
　返答に困って、なんとなく視線を上げた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ugh.”
That was unfair.
Forget remorse—looking at me that way was simply unfair.
Someone who called herself a vampire had no right to look at me with such innocent eyes―――
“I, um…”
Unable to answer, I let my gaze wander upward.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……… Uhh."
This is unfair.
Sorry or not, using those eyes is unfair.
…… It's unfair she has such pure eyes like that when she claims she's a vampire---
"I'm… um---"
Stuck for an answer, I lift my gaze.

entries.japanese:
「……あれ？」
　……なんだろう。
　ビルとビルの切れ間に、なにかおかしなモノがある。
「ちょっと待った。
アレ、なんだろう」
　立ちあがって歩く。
　路地裏の真ん中あたりまで歩いて、ようやくビルとビルの切れ間にいるモノがなんであるかわかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Huh?”
What was that?
Something strange sat in the narrow gap between two buildings.
“Hold on. What’s that?”
I stood and walked to the middle of the alley.
Only then could I make out what occupied the gap between the buildings.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Huh?"
…… What is it?
Something odd is there, in the gap between the buildings.
"Hold on.
What's that?"
I get up and walk.
I walk to the middle of the alley, and I finally realize what it is.

entries.japanese:
そこにいたのは、蒼い鳥だった。
　正確にいうのなら鴉、というべきだろう。
　……蒼い、カラス。
　それは、二日前の夜に見た、不吉なモノではなかったか―――
entries.maoEnglish:
It was a blue bird.
To be precise, a crow.
A blue crow.
Wasn’t that the ominous creature I had seen two nights ago―――
entries.mirrorMoon:
A blue-colored bird.
A crow, to be precise.
…… A blue… crow.
That inauspicious thing I saw two nights ago---

entries.japanese:
「―――まいったな」
　ぽつり、と女が呟く。
　鴉はじぃ、と自分たちの様子を見つめている。
「もうっ。
貴方がいつまでもぐずぐずしてるから見つかっちゃったじゃない」
　女は路地裏の入り口を見ている。
「見つかったって、なにが」
　路地裏の入り口に視線を送る。
―――――、と。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――This is bad”
The woman murmured.
The crow watched us without blinking.
“Honestly! You took so long that we’ve been found.”
The woman was looking toward the mouth of the alley.
“Found by what?”
I turned toward the alley entrance.
―――――And then.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Oh, man…"
The girl murmurs.
The crow just stares at us.
"Geez, thanks to your slowness, he found us."
The girl looks at the entrance to the alley.
"Found us?
Who?"
I cast my gaze towards the alley entrance.
-----Then.

entries.japanese:
「―――――！」
　びくっ、と思わず体が一歩引いてしまった。
　いつのまにか、路地裏の入り口である細い道に一匹の犬がいた。
　どこか歪つフォルムをした強靭な四肢と、ピン、とはりつめた鉄骨のような首。
　
　人間とは大きくかけはなれた、『獲物を狩る』ことだけを追求したそのフォルム。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――――!”
I flinched back a step.
At some point, a dog had appeared in the narrow passage leading into the alley.
Its powerful limbs were subtly misshapen, its neck taut as an iron beam.
Its form was wholly unlike a human body, honed for one purpose alone: hunting prey.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-----!"
I take a step back in shock.
Before I knew it, a dog had appeared in the narrow path running into the alley.
It has four tough legs and a tense neck like steel frame.
That form, far removed from that of a human, is one made solely for hunting.

entries.japanese:
……そこに、言葉による威嚇など必要ない。
　たいていの人間は、この種の『狩猟』動物を見ただけで緊張してしまう。
　その、同じ生物として、絶望的なまでに優れた運動能力への畏敬として。
entries.maoEnglish:
It needed no verbal threat.
Most people tense up at the mere sight of a predator like that.
