Arcueid stares dumbfounded at my hand.
No, more accurately,
she stares at the red blood coating my hand.
"----Arcueid?"
"--------"
Arcueid doesn't respond.
She just, starts to breathe heavier.
Pant, pant.
As if she is trying to withstand pain.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
「おい、アルクェイド……！
　どうしたんだ、また傷が痛んでるのか……！？」
　アルクェイドの肩を掴む。
――――と。
　彼女は、逃げるように俺の腕から跳びすさった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hey, Arcueid…! Are your wounds hurting again?”
I caught her by the shoulder.
――――And then.
She sprang away from my hand as though fleeing from me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hey, Arcueid……!
What's wrong?
Does your wound hurt……!?"
I grab her shoulders.
----And then,
she jumps back as if she was trying to escape.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
「――――」
　ぎろり、と敵を睨むように俺を凝視する。
「……アル……クェイド？」
「志―――――貴？」
　短く。
敵意さえ含んだ声が、そう言った。
「わたし――――そんなコト、思ってない」
　……？
　アルクェイドは気まずそうに視線を逸らす。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
She glared at me as if I were an enemy.
“Ar… cueid?”
“Shi… ki?”
My name came out short and sharp, with something almost like hostility in it.
“I… I wasn’t thinking anything like that.”
What?
Arcueid looked away awkwardly.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----"
She stares at me like I am an enemy.
"…… Ar…… cueid?"
"Shi------ki?"
Short, clipped.
Her voice even contains enmity.
"I----never thought, about it."
……?
She averts her gaze awkwardly.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
「どうしたんだよ、ヘンだぞおまえ。
体、まだ回復してないんじゃないのか？」
「……そうね。
ちょっと無理しすぎたみたい。
だから、わたし帰るね」
「―――あ、うん。
どうせ今夜はこれでおしまいだって言ってたもんな」
「……うん。
また明日、ここで待ってる」
　アルクェイドはこっちの目をまともに見ないまま、早足で去っていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What’s wrong with you—you’re acting strange. Your body still hasn’t recovered, has it?”
“You’re right. I think I pushed myself too far. I’m going home.”
“Oh, right. You said we were finished for tonight anyway.”
“Mm. I’ll wait here again tomorrow.”
Without once meeting my eyes, Arcueid hurried away.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"What's wrong?
You're acting strange.
You still haven't recovered yet?"
"…… Perhaps.
It seems I pushed myself too hard.
So, I'll go back now."
"----Ah, yeah.
I guess we'll call it a night."
"…… Yeah.
I'll be waiting here tomorrow."
Not looking me in the eye, Arcueid leaves quickly.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
……住宅街の坂を昇りきって、屋敷の外周にたどり着いた。
　時刻は午前二時をまわったあたり。
　流石に眠気が襲ってくる。
「……あいつ、あんなんで大丈夫なのかな」
　別れ際のアルクェイドの様子が気にかかる。
　あれは、傷が痛むとかそういったものではない気がするけど―――
entries.maoEnglish:
I finished climbing the hill through the residential district and reached the outer wall of the mansion.
It was a little after two in the morning.
At last, sleepiness was catching up with me.
“I wonder if she’ll be all right…”
I couldn’t stop thinking about Arcueid’s behavior when we parted.
It hadn’t looked like the pain of her wounds, or anything so simple—
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… I go up the residential hill and arrive at the outskirts of the mansion.
It's around two in the morning.
As expected, I'm totally assailed by sleepiness.
"…… I wonder if she's going to be okay."
I'm concerned about how she seemed when we parted.
It seemed like it wasn't pain from her wound, but---
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
「ん？」
　なんだろう。
　街灯の明かりが届かない暗がりに、誰か立っているような気がする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hmm?”
What was that?
In the darkness beyond the streetlamp’s reach, I thought someone was standing still.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hm?"
What is that?
It feels like there's someone lurking in the shadows not illuminated by the streetlights.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
―――どく、ん。
　心臓が、呼吸を停止させる。
　体中の血流が何倍にも速くなって循環していく、この感覚――――
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Thump.
My heart leaped, cutting off my breath.
Blood raced through my body several times faster than before. That sensation—
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Thu,mp.
My heart stops my breath.
My blood rushes through my body, this sensation----
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
たしかに、誰か立っている。
　人影はこちらに段々と近づいてくる。
　かつ、かつ、かつ。
　乾いた足音が聞こえてくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
Someone was definitely there.
The figure drew steadily closer.
Tap. Tap. Tap.
Dry footsteps approached.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Certainly, there's someone standing there.
The figure gets closer and closer.
Footsteps.
The sound of dry footsteps reaches my ears.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
――――どく、ん。
　厭な予感。
　背筋には、なにか、ムカデがはっているような悪寒。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――Thump.
A terrible premonition.
A chill like a centipede crawling down my spine.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----Thu, mp.
I have a bad feeling about this.
Chills race up my spine.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
「――――」
　人影が、すぐそこまでやってきた。
　とたん――――街灯がパリン、と音をたてて割れた。
　月も雲に隠れている。
　世界は、唐突に闇になった。
「！」
　　　　　　　どく、ん………！
　死を告げるように、心臓がはねあがる。
　わけもわからず後ろに跳び退いた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
The figure came within a few steps.
At that instant, the streetlamp shattered with a crystalline crack.
The moon was hidden behind clouds.
Without warning, the world became darkness.
“!”
Thump…!
My heart leaped as though announcing my death.
Without knowing why, I sprang backward.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----"
The figure draws near.
Suddenly----the streetlights shatter loudly.
The moon is hidden by the clouds.
The whole world instantly turns to darkness.
"!"
Thu, mp………!
My heartbeat skips, as if warning me of death.
I jump back for no apparent reason.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
闇に走る刃物。
　かわしきれず、刃物はメガネを掠っていく。
　からん、とメガネが地面に落ちた。
entries.maoEnglish:
A blade flashed through the dark.
I failed to evade it completely; it grazed my glasses.
They clattered to the ground.
entries.mirrorMoon:
A blade runs through the darkness.
Not being able to get away fully, my glasses are grazed by it.
They fall to the ground with a clatter.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
「おま―――え」
　誰だ、と言おうとした瞬間。
　雲の隙間から一瞬だけ月が覗いて、人影の姿が顕になった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You—”
I was about to demand who he was.
Then the moon slipped through a gap in the clouds for an instant and revealed the figure.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Who---"
The instant I start to say "are you?",
The clouds part for a brief moment and the dark figure is illuminated.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
「な――――」
　全身を包帯で巻いた男は、その手にナイフを握っている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What—”
A man wrapped from head to foot in bandages stood there with a knife in his hand.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Wha----"
A man wrapped entirely in bandages is gripping a knife.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
包帯の男は襲いかかってくる。
　とっさにナイフを構えて、男のナイフをやり過ごす。
　ギン、ギン、と音をたてて弾きあう二つの光芒。
「――――！」
　思考が、冷静になってくれない。
　自分が襲われているというコトが混乱を呼んでいる。
entries.maoEnglish:
He lunged.
I raised my own knife on instinct and turned his blade aside.
Clang, clang—the two streaks of light collided and rebounded.
“—!”
My thoughts refused to settle.
Being attacked had thrown me into confusion.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The bandaged man goes to attack me again.
I quickly ready my knife and stop it.
Two slivers of light shoot towards each other.
"----!"
I can't, think calmly.
The fact that I'm being attacked causes my mind to panic.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
ギン、ギン、とナイフとナイフが闇の中で火花を散らす。
「くっ―――」
　思考が、まだ冷静になれないでいる。
　原因は自分が襲われているというコトではなく。
　ギィン―――。
　鋭角的に繰り出されるナイフを、ほぼ同じ角度のスウィングで相殺する。
entries.maoEnglish:
Clang, clang—our knives scattered sparks through the darkness.
“Kh—”
I still couldn’t think clearly.
The cause was not the mere fact that I was being attacked.
Clang!
I met the knife’s sharp thrust with a swing at almost exactly the same angle, knocking it aside.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Clang!
Clang!
Sparks fly from our clashing knives and scatter into the darkness.
"Kk---"
I still can't calm down.
It's not because I'm being attacked.
Clang---.
I swing my knife to cancel out the one attacking me from every angle.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
「なんで――――」
　驚くべきことは。
　この闇の中で、休む暇もなくナイフを振るわれているというのに、その全てを的確に止めている自分自身の体だった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Why…?”
The astonishing thing was my own body.
His knife never stopped, and in this darkness I could scarcely see, yet I was blocking every stroke perfectly.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Why----"
What's surprising is that,
my body is completely stopping all the attacks in this darkness without a pause.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
「かってに、体が―――」
　いや、違う。
　メガネが外れて、この闇の中で。
　たんに裸眼で視えている線と点を、この腕が追っているだけ。
　見えるものはそれだけだから、ただその線に対して闇雲にナイフを振るっている。
　その結果、包帯の男のナイフがかってに俺のナイフを受け止めているだけだ。
　つまり。
　これは俺が防いでいるのではなく、この男が防いでいるということ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“My body is moving on its own—”
No—that wasn’t it.
My glasses were gone, here in the darkness.
My arm was merely following the lines and points visible to my bare eyes.
Because those were all I could see, I slashed blindly at the lines.
The bandaged man’s knife was forced to intercept mine.
In other words.
I wasn’t defending against him; he was defending against me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"My body is moving by itself---?"
No, that's not it.
All my arms are doing,
is seeking out the lines and points that I can see in the darkness with my glasses off.
That's all I can see, so I swing my knife through the dark air after those lines.
As a result, the bandaged man's knife is simply stopping mine.
In other words,
It's not that I'm defending myself, but he's defending himself from me.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
――――勝てる……！
　ドコの誰だか知らないが、間違いない。
　今は、自分が圧している。
　ぞくりと、と血が圧倒的に有利な立場に高揚している。
　勝てる。
俺は、こいつより強い。
　こいつより強いから。
殺されかけたら、殺し返すだけじゃないか――――！
entries.maoEnglish:
――――I could win…!
I had no idea who he was, but there was no mistake: I was driving him back.
A shiver of exhilaration ran through my blood at the overwhelming advantage.
I could win.
I was stronger than he was.
And if I was stronger, then when he tried to kill me, all I had to do was kill him first—!
entries.mirrorMoon:
----I can win……!
I don't know who he is, but there's no doubt.
I'm overwhelming him.
My blood rages forth from my advantage.
I'll win.
I'm, stronger than him.
Because I'm stronger.
Because he's trying to kill me, aren't I just returning the favor----!?
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
ギィン、ギィン。
　鋼をうつような音を響かせて、男を屋敷の塀に追い込んだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
Clang. Clang.
To a sound like hammering steel, I drove him against the mansion wall.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Clang.
Clang.
The sound of ringing metal echoes in the air and I force him back towards the mansion wall.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
「――――！」
　とった。
　その胸に視える『線』めがけて、ナイフを牙のように打ち付ける。
――――刹那。
　血にまみれた少年と、泣いている秋葉の顔が、見えた気がした――――
entries.maoEnglish:
“—!”
I had him.
I struck like a fang at the ‘line’ across his chest.
――――In that instant.
I thought I saw a boy covered in blood—and Akiha’s tearful face—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----!"
There.
My eyes fixate on the "line" on his chest and I thrust my knife forward.
----Momentarily.
For some reason I see a boy painted in blood and Akiha's crying face----
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
「っっっっっ！」
　すんでのところでナイフを引いた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“……!”
I pulled the knife back at the last possible instant.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Gh!"
I pull my knife back before completion.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese: ―――俺は、なにを――自分から、人を殺そうとするなんて、どうして―――
entries.maoEnglish: ―――What was I doing? Why had I tried to kill someone of my own accord—?
entries.mirrorMoon: ---What, am I--I'm, trying to kill someone, why---
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
あたま。
　あたまがいたい。
　足元はおぼつかなくなって、よろよろと後ろにさがる。
　そのまま。
　胃の中のものを、吐き出した。
　じくりと。
胸が、痒い。
　頭がいたい。
胸の古傷が熱い。
　目が、眼孔からこぼれそうで――――
entries.maoEnglish:
My head.
My head hurt.
My footing gave way.
I staggered backward.
Then I vomited everything in my stomach.
A deep itch spread through the scar on my chest.
My head hurt. The old wound in my chest burned.
My eyes felt ready to spill from their sockets—
entries.mirrorMoon:
My head.
My head hurts.
My legs wobble and I stagger backwards.
As I do so,
I empty the contents of my stomach.
My chest starts to itch.
My head hurts, the old wound on my chest burns.
My eyes, feel like they're going to burst out of their sockets----
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
「はあ――――あ、ああ―――！」
　嘔吐がとまらない。
　びしゃびしゃと吐瀉物をアスファルトに撒き散らす。
　そこへ。
　包帯の男が、ナイフを構えて迫ってきた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Haaah—ah, aah!”
The vomiting wouldn’t stop.
Filth splattered wetly across the asphalt.
And then.
The bandaged man approached with his knife raised.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Haa----ah, agh---!"
I can't stop throwing up.
The vomit splatters all over the asphalt.
And there,
the bandaged man comes after me with his knife.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
「―――――！」
　ギィン、という衝撃。
　男のナイフをナイフで弾く。
　今度は、本当に自分で防いだ。
　敵が狙ってくる個所がわかる。
わかるから、次もギィン、と音をたてて弾けた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“—!”
Clang.
The impact ran through me as I knocked his knife aside with mine.
This time I truly had defended myself.
I knew where he intended to strike, so I met the next blow with another ringing clash.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-----!"
Clang!
Another collision.
My knife shoots towards his.
This time, I really defend myself.
I know where he's aiming.
Since I know, I block him once again with another clang.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
ギィンギィンギィン。
　何度も俺なんかの動体視力では捕らえられないほど速いナイフを弾く。
　防げる理由は簡単だ。
　だって、あいつの狙っている個所は俺の体の『線』なんだ。
　だからどこを狙ってくるかは自ずとわかるし、そこを斬られては即死すると解っているので防ぎにまわるしかない。
entries.maoEnglish:
Clang-clang-clang.
Again and again I deflected a knife moving too fast for my eyes to follow.
The reason I could defend myself was simple.
He was aiming for the ‘lines’ on my body.
That told me where every attack would fall, and because I knew a cut there would kill me instantly, I had no choice but to block.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Clang!
Clang!
Clang!
Despite not being able to see his knife due to its speed, I somehow manage to block it over and over.
The reason I can defend myself is simple.
Because, where he's aiming are the "lines" on my body.
So I know where he is aiming at and I understand more than anyone that having them cut would mean instant death, so I have to defend it.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
いや、待て。
　……線を―――狙われて、いる？
entries.maoEnglish:
No. Wait.
He was… aiming at the lines?
entries.mirrorMoon:
No, wait.
…… Aiming---for my lines?
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
「――――――あ」
　さっきとまったく反対だ。
　という事は。
　こいつは、まさか。
――――ク。
　闇の中で、包帯の男が笑った。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ah…”
The exact opposite of before.
Which meant.
Could it really be him?
――――Heh.
The bandaged man laughed in the darkness.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------Ah."
It's the exact opposite of before.
That means,
don't tell me, he.
----Ku.
The bandaged man smiles in the darkness.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
―――ど、く、ん。
　一際心臓が高く動悸する。
　言いようのない恐怖を感じて、逃げるように後ろに下がった。
　包帯の男は追ってこない。
ただ、にやりと笑っている。
　ぎょろりと血走ったその瞳が『ようやく気が付いたのか』と、俺をあざ笑っている。
「視えて――――るのか」
　そう。
　こいつも、『線』が見えているのだ――――
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Th… ump.
My heart pounded harder than ever.
Seized by a terror I couldn’t name, I retreated as if fleeing.
The bandaged man didn’t pursue. He only grinned.
His bulging, bloodshot eyes jeered: So you finally noticed.
“You can… see them?”
Yes.
He could see the ‘lines’ too.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Th, um, p.
My heart rate goes out of control.
Feeling some unnameable fear, I stumble backwards.
He doesn't pursue me.
He just smiles.
His blood-shot eyes seem to be saying "So you've finally realized it?" as he sneers at me.
"You can----see them?"
Yes.
He also, can see the "lines"----
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
なら。
　俺なんか、それこそ一撃で殺されてしまうじゃないか―――
entries.maoEnglish:
Then.
Someone like me could be killed in a single blow—
entries.mirrorMoon:
Then,
He can, also kill with one blow---
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
――――ク。
　男が笑う。
　笑いながら近づいてくる。
　俺は―――ナイフを握る指さえ、がくがくと震えているだけだった。
　ザンザンザン、と肉に刃物が突き刺さる音が三回。
　その後に、ドン、と体が壁に叩きつけられる音。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――Heh.
The man laughed.
He advanced as he laughed.
Even the fingers wrapped around my knife could do nothing but tremble.
Three wet sounds of blades driving into flesh.
Then the crash of a body slammed against the wall.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----Ku.
The man laughs.
He draws near while laughing.
I---even down to my fingers gripping my knife, tremble uncontrollably.
Slice.
Slice.
Slice.
The sound of flesh being pierced by a blade resounds three times.
And then, a thud, a sound of a body hitting the wall.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
「え―――？」
―――事態が、まったく掴めない。
　包帯の男は、突然飛んできた三つの槍みたいなパイプに体を貫かれていた。
　槍は男を貫いただけでなく、そのまま男を壁に突き刺したのだ。
　採集した昆虫を、ピンで串刺しにするように。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What…?”
―――I couldn’t grasp what had happened.
Three pipe-like spears had flown from nowhere and pierced the bandaged man.
They had not merely run him through; they had pinned him to the wall.
Like an insect impaled in a display case.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Eh---?"
---I can't grasp the situation.
The bandaged man was suddenly pierced by three spear-like pipes.
Not just pierced, but stuck onto the wall.
Like an insect pinned in a bug collection.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
「―――ジャマ、ヲ」
　男の声は、しわがれている。
　同時に―――三つの槍は蝋燭みたいに燃え上がり、包帯の男を炎で包み込んでしまった。
「アアアァアアアアアアぁぁぁアぁあああ！」
　苦悶の声と、ごうごうと渦巻く炎。
　闇の中。
その光景は無惨というより、むしろ美しいとさえ感じた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You… interfere…”
His voice was dry and ragged.
At the same moment, the three spears flared like candles, wrapping the bandaged man in fire.
“Aaaaaaaaaaaaaagh!”
His agony mingled with the roar of spiraling flames.
Against the darkness, the sight struck me as beautiful rather than gruesome.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---YOU'RE IN MY WAY."
His voice grates awfully.
At the same time---the three spears alight like candles and engulf him in flames.
"AAAAAaAAAaaaaAaAAAh!"
An anguished voice in the whirlpool of flames.
In the darkness, that scene seems less cruel, and almost beautiful.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
「アアアアアアアアアア！」
　包帯の男―――いや、今ではもう包帯はすべて燃えて、剥き出しの肌がある。
　男は、炎に包まれながら、俺を見ていた。
　血走った、殺意だけしかない瞳。
　遠野志貴だけを呪っているような、凶器みたいな黒い瞳。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Aaaaaaaaaaaaah!”
The bandaged man—no, every bandage had burned away.
His naked skin was exposed as he stared at me from inside the flames.
Bloodshot eyes containing nothing but murder.
Black eyes like weapons, cursing Shiki Tohno alone.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"AAAAAAAAAAH!"
The bandaged man---no, the bandages are burned already, his skin is showing.
Wrapped in the flames, the man stares at me.
His blood-shot eyes filled only with murder.
His black eyes like a weapon bent on cursing Tohno Shiki.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
「―――――な」
　ただ、呆然とするしかない。
　男は炎に包まれながら走り去っていく。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What…”
I could only stare.
Still wrapped in fire, the man fled.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-----Wha…"
Stunned, I can only watch.
He runs off into the distance, still engulfed in flames.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
―――月が出てきた。
　あれだけの炎がたって、あんなに禍禍しい叫び声があがったっていうのに、周囲は何事もなかったように静まり返っている。
「――――」
　がくん、と膝から力を失って、塀にもたれかかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――The moon emerged.
Flames had towered into the night and that monstrous scream had torn through the street, yet everything around me was as quiet as if nothing had happened.
“…”
My knees gave way, and I sagged against the wall.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---The moon re-emerges.
After those flames, and that cursing voice, everything returns to silence like it was before.
"----"
I fall to my knees and lean against the wall.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
空を見上げる。
　あの槍の飛んできた方向。
高く遠いところに、誰かが立っている。
「―――――」
　はるか遠く。
　街灯の上に悠然と、見覚えのある人影が立っていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
I looked up.
In the direction the spears had come from, someone stood high above and far away.
“…”
Far in the distance.
A familiar figure stood serenely atop a streetlamp.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I look up at the sky.
In the direction where those spears flew from, someone is standing high and far off.
"-----"
Far away.
Standing composed on top of the streetlight, I see a familiar figure.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
「……え？」
　外国の神父のような服装。
　手に携えた、大きな釘めいた刃。
　感情がない、青い青い蒼穹の目。
「……先……輩？」
　月明かりの下、シルエットしか見えないのに。
　俺には、それが先輩に似て見えた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What…?”
Clothes like those of a foreign priest.
A great nail-shaped blade in one hand.
Eyes as blue and emotionless as the open sky.
“Ciel…?”
Moonlight showed me nothing but a silhouette.
Even so, I thought it looked like her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Eh?"
Robes like a priest from another country.
Clenched in her hand, large, nail-like swords.
Emotionless, pale eyes.
Blue, sky-blue eyes.
"…… Sen…… pai?"
Under the moonlight, I can only make out the silhouette.
But, she seems to resemble Senpai.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
「――――――」
　視線が合う。
　街灯の上に立った人影は、幽霊のように、唐突に姿を消してしまった。
「あ―――――」
　どさり、と地面に腰が落ちる。
　頭痛が薄れていく心地よさと、緊張が弛緩していくけだるさのせいなのか。
　俺は塀に背中を預けたまま、うっすらと眠りに落ちていく自分自身を見つめていた―――――。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
Our eyes met.
Then the figure atop the streetlamp vanished as abruptly as a ghost.
“Ah…”
I dropped heavily to the ground.
Perhaps it was the pleasure of the headache fading, or the languor that came as all my tension dissolved.
Still leaning against the wall, I watched myself drift softly into sleep.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------"
Our eyes meet.
The standing figure on top of the streetlight suddenly disappears like a ghost.
"Ah-----"
I sit down roughly.
Is it relief from my headache fading or just the lifting of all this tension?
Leaning my back against the wall, I start to drift off to sleep-----.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
……住宅街の坂を上りきって、屋敷の正門にたどり着いた。
　時刻は午前二時をまわったあたり。
　流石に眠気が襲ってくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
I finished climbing the hill through the residential district and reached the mansion’s front gate.
It was a little after two in the morning.
At last, sleepiness was catching up with me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… I go up the residential hill and arrive at the outskirts of the mansion.
It's around two in the morning.
As expected, I'm totally assailed by sleepiness.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
「……あいつ、あんなんで大丈夫なのかな」
　別れ際のアルクェイドの様子が気にかかる。
　あれは、傷が痛むとかそういったものではない気がするけど―――
「ん……しまった、正門が閉まってる」
　当たり前といえば当たり前なんだけど、正門が閉められている。
　……昨日みたいによじ登って中に入ったら、今度こそ警報が鳴り響いてしまうだろう。
「……まいったな……この屋敷、裏門とかなかったっけ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“I wonder if she’ll be all right…”
I couldn’t stop thinking about Arcueid’s behavior when we parted.
It hadn’t looked like the pain of her wounds, or anything so simple—
“Damn, the gate’s locked.”
Naturally enough, the front gate had been shut.
If I climbed over as I had last night, this time the alarm really would sound.
“Great—doesn’t this mansion have a back gate somewhere?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I wonder if she's going to be okay."
I'm concerned about how she seemed when we parted.
It seemed like it wasn't pain from her wound, but---

"Hm…… crap, the front gate is locked."
It's only natural, but it's still locked.
…… If I climb over the wall like yesterday, alarms will probably go off.
"…… Dang…… does this mansion have a rear entrance or something?"
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
……屋敷の周辺をぐるぐると歩きまわる。
　とりあえず、裏口らしきものはあったけど鍵がかかっていて入れなかった。
　あの裏口から無理やり屋敷の庭に入る事は不可能そうだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
I wandered in circles around the grounds.
I did find something resembling a rear entrance, but it was locked.
There seemed to be no way to force my way into the garden through it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… I walk around the mansion perimeter.
Anyway, there is something like a rear entrance, but it's locked so I can't get in.
It's probably not possible to force my way through to the garden.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
「……まいったなあ。
このままじゃ野宿するしかなくなるぞ……」
　できればそれだけは避けたい。
　屋敷の周辺は人気がなく、日が落ちただけで深夜になってしまったような暗さがあるのだ。
　こうして丑三つ時に歩いている、というだけで背筋が寒くなってくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“This is bad. At this rate I’ll have to sleep outside…”
I wanted to avoid that if I possibly could.
No one lived near the mansion, and the neighborhood grew as black as midnight the moment the sun went down.
Merely walking there at two in the morning sent a chill up my spine.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Dang.
If this keeps up I'll have to spend the night out here……"
I want to avoid that if possible.
People don't really go by the mansion, so after the sun sets it's just a deep darkness around here.
Walking around during these hours sends chills down my spine.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
「ん？」
　なんだろう。
　街灯の明かりが届かない暗がりに、誰か立っているような気がする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hmm?”
What was that?
In the darkness beyond the streetlamp’s reach, I thought someone was standing still.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hm?"
What is that?
It feels like there's someone lurking in the shadows not illuminated by the streetlights.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
―――どく、ん。
　心臓が、呼吸を停止させる。
　体中の血流が何倍にも速くなって循環していく、この感覚――――
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Thump.
My heart leaped, cutting off my breath.
Blood raced through my body several times faster than before. That sensation—
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Thu,mp.
My heart stops my breath.
My blood rushes through my body, this sensation---
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
たしかに、誰か立っている。
　人影はこちらに段々と近づいてくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
Someone was definitely there.
The figure drew steadily closer.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Certainly, there's someone standing there.
The figure gets closer and closer.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
かつ、かつ、かつ。
　乾いた足音が聞こえてくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
Tap. Tap. Tap.
Dry footsteps approached.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Footsteps.
The sound of dry footsteps reaches my ears.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
――――どく、ん。
　厭な予感。
　背筋には、なにか、ムカデがはっているような悪寒。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――Thump.
A terrible premonition.
A chill like a centipede crawling down my spine.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----Thu, mp.
I have a bad feeling about this.
Chills race up my spine.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
「――――」
　人影が、すぐそこまでやってきた。
　とたん――――街頭がパリン、と音をたてて割れた。

月も雲に隠れている。
　世界は、唐突に闇になった。
「！」
――――どく、ん………！
　死を告げるように、心臓がはねあがる。
　ずっと屋敷の周辺を歩きまわっていて、体が疲れていたのか。
　後に跳ぼう、とした思考に、肉体が着いてくるのが遅すぎた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
The figure came within a few steps.
At that instant, the streetlamp shattered with a crystalline crack.
The moon was hidden behind clouds.
Without warning, the world became darkness.
“!”
――――Thump…!
My heart leaped as though announcing my death.
Perhaps walking around the mansion for so long had exhausted me.
My mind ordered me to jump back, but my body followed far too slowly.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----"
The figure draws near.
Suddenly----the streetlights shatter loudly.
The moon is hidden by the clouds.
The whole world instantly turns to darkness.
"!"
----Thump………!
My heartbeat skips, as if warning me of death.
Perhaps I was tired after having walked the perimeter of the mansion for so long.
My body gave an all-too-sluggish reaction as I tried to leap backwards.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
闇に走る刃物。
　ざくり、と心臓の上あたりで、肉を裂く音がした。
「あ―――え？」
―――よく、わからない。
　ただ、自分の胸に、ナイフがふかぶかと突き刺さっている、という事ぐらいしか。
entries.maoEnglish:
A blade flashed through the darkness.
There was a wet tearing sound above my heart.
“Ah… what?”
―――I didn’t understand.
All I could grasp was that a knife had sunk deep into my chest.
entries.mirrorMoon:
A knife running through the dark.
The sound of the flesh over my heart being sliced.
"Ah---eh?"
---I don't, understand.
Just… that… there's a knife, sticking through my chest.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
雲の隙間から一瞬だけ月が覗いて、人影の姿が顕になった。
「あ――――」
　全身を包帯でまいた不気味な人影。
　それが、俺の見た最後の光景だった。
entries.maoEnglish:
For one instant, the moon slipped through a gap in the clouds and revealed the figure.
“Ah…”
A sinister shape wrapped from head to foot in bandages.
That was the last thing I ever saw.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The clouds part for a brief moment and the dark figure is illuminated.

"Ah----"
An eerie figure wrapped entirely in bandages.
That's… the last thing I see.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
「申し訳ございません。
知得留先生は昼食の時間なのでお休みです。
お帰りになるまでしばらくお待ちください」
「どうせカレーパンのくせに、職務怠慢ー！」
「でてこーい、ばかシエルー！」
「同感ですが、居ないものは仕方がありません。
　無い袖はふれませんし、姉さんが整理整頓できない事を嘆いても虚しいだけです。
　それでは恒例の救罪コーナーですが」
entries.maoEnglish:
“My apologies. Our Teach Me, Ciel! instructor is away at lunch; please wait until she returns.”
“It’s only going to be curry bread—dereliction of duty!”
“Come out here, stupid Ciel!”
“I share your opinion, but nothing can be done when she is absent.
One cannot give what one does not have, and lamenting my sister’s inability to keep anything in order is equally futile.
Now, for our customary salvation segment…”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I am deeply sorry.
Ciel-sensei is now on her lunch break.
Please wait until she returns."
"She's neglecting her duties and snacking on curry bread!"
"Get over here, stupid Ciel!"
"I feel the same way, but if she is not here, it cannot be helped.
You cannot do anything about someone not here, and it is just too miserable to just complain about how much Nee-san cannot clean or tidy things up.
Now then, we shall begin the customary correction corner."
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
「……時に、志貴さま。
　隠し事はあまりよい結果を生みません。
　これに懲りましたら、次からは翡翠を信頼してください。
　……以上です。
　それでは私はお屋敷に戻ります。
　引き続き、ゲーム本編をお楽しみくださいませ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“A word, Master Shiki.
Secrets seldom lead to desirable outcomes.
Once you have learned your lesson, please place your trust in Hisui next time.
That is all.
I shall return to the estate now.
Please continue to enjoy the main game.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Shiki-sama,
hiding things does not give good results.
If you learned from this experience, please trust Hisui next time.
…… That is all.
I will now return to the mansion.
Please continue enjoying the main storyline."
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese: 「にゃ……なんか今のおんな、おなじネコ属性のかおりがするのにゃ……」
entries.maoEnglish: “Nya—that woman smelled like she had the same cat streak as me…”
entries.mirrorMoon: "Nyaaa…… That woman, I smell another cat-like character……"
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

entries.japanese:
―――白。
　　　白い色は、なつかしい記憶を呼び起こす。
　　　忘れていたもの。
　　　忘れなくてはいけなかったもの。
　　　父に、忘れろと命じられたもの。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――White.
White calls an old memory back.
Something forgotten.
Something that had to be forgotten.
Something Father ordered me to forget.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---White.
The color white summons an old memory.
Something forgotten.
Something I was supposed to forget.
Something my father commanded me to forget.

entries.japanese:
夏の、暑い日。
　青い空と　大きな大きな入道雲。
　じりじりとゆらぐ風景と
　気が遠くなるような蝉の声。
　蝉の声。
entries.maoEnglish:
A hot summer day.
A blue sky and huge, huge thunderheads.
The whole world quivering in the baking heat,
and the endless, dizzying scream of cicadas.
The cicadas’ cry.
entries.mirrorMoon:
A hot, summer day.
A blue sky and large, large columns of summer clouds.
The wafting breeze,
and the droning voice of the cicadas.
The voice of cicadas.

entries.japanese:
みーん　みんみん
　みーん　みんみん
　みーん　みんみん
――――うるさくて死にたくなる。
entries.maoEnglish:
Miiin, min-min
Miiin, min-min
Miiin, min-min
――――They’re so loud I want to die.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Chiiirp.
Chirp Chirp.
Chiiirp.
Chirp Chirp.
Chiiirp.
Chirp Chirp.
----So loud I want to die.

entries.japanese:
広場には蝉のぬけがら。
　たいようはすぐそばにあるようで、
　広場はじりじりと焦げていく。
　真夏のあつい日。
　まるで、セカイがふらいぱんになったみたい。
entries.maoEnglish:
Empty cicada shells litter the clearing.
The sun feels close enough to touch,
and the clearing slowly bakes beneath it.
A hot day in the middle of summer.
Like the whole world is one big frying pan.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Cicada shells are lying in the clearing.
As if the sun is right by my side,
the clearing is roasting.
A hot midsummer's day.
As if the entire world became a frying pan.

entries.japanese:
えーん　えんえん
　えーん　えんえん
　えーん　えんえん
　秋葉が泣いている。
　おとなしくて、いつもボクの後についてきていた秋葉が、ぽろぽろと泣いている。
entries.maoEnglish:
Waaah, waaah
Waaah, waaah
Waaah, waaah
Akiha is crying.
Quiet little Akiha, who always followed right behind me, is crying and crying.
entries.mirrorMoon:
waa, u, uwaaa.
waa, u, uwaaa.
waa, u, uwaaa.
Akiha is crying.

Akiha, who would always obediently stay close behind me, is brimming forth with tears.

entries.japanese:
秋葉の足元には子供がひとり倒れている。
　白いシャツが真っ赤に染まって、ぴくりとも動かない。
　ボクは、それを見下ろしている。
　両手は倒れている子供と同じように赤い。
　いや、違う。
　この両手は、倒れている子供の血で赤いのだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
A child lies at Akiha’s feet.
The white shirt is stained bright red, and the child does not move at all.
I look down at the child.
My hands are red, just like the child lying there.
No—that’s wrong.
My hands are red with the fallen child’s blood.
entries.mirrorMoon:
A child lies collapsed at her feet.
His white shirt is painted red with blood and he doesn't move at all.
I'm, looking down at that.
My hands are red, just like that child on the ground.
No, that's not it.
These hands are red with the blood of that child.

entries.japanese:
「秋葉─────！」
　おとなたちがやってくる。
　この惨状を見つけだして、血相を変えてやってくる。
「なんて事だ─────」
　おとなたちは秋葉を連れていく。
　倒れた子供は死んだまま。
　遠くのそらには、白い白い入道雲。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Akiha—!”
The grown-ups are coming.
They discover the carnage and come running, horror on their faces.
“What a terrible thing—”
The grown-ups take Akiha away.
The fallen child stays dead.
Far off in the sky, a white, white thunderhead towers.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Akiha-----!"
The adults are coming.
After seeing this sight, their expressions change rapidly.
"What in the-----"
The adults take Akiha away.
The child lies there, dead.
In the distant sky, the white, white clouds.

entries.japanese:
ボクは一人残されて、ぼんやりと夏の空を見上げている。
「おまえが殺したのか────」
　おとなたちは叫んでいる。
　子供をころしたボクの名前を叫んでいる。
　たった二文字の言葉を、気がちがったように叫んでいる。
entries.maoEnglish:
They leave me all alone, staring up at the summer sky.
“Did you kill the child—?”
The grown-ups are shouting.
They shout the name of the boy who killed the child.
They scream those two little sounds as if they have all gone mad.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I'm left alone, staring at the sky aimlessly.
"Did you kill him----"
The adults are yelling at me.

They shout my name, the one who killed the child.
Those two syllables, shouting as if they went crazy.

entries.japanese:
たった二文字。
　おとなたちはそろって、両手を真っ赤に染めたボクを、シキと、呼んでいた。
entries.maoEnglish:
Only two sounds.
All together, the grown-ups called me—the child with both hands stained red—SHIKI.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Just those two syllables.
Those adults call me SHIKI, as my hands are stained in red.

entries.japanese:
懐かしいユメを、見ていたような気がして。
　眠りから、目覚めた。
「……………」
　自分の部屋にいる。
　あの後―――屋敷の周りの塀で意識を失ったあと、自分はどうにかしてこの部屋に戻ってきたようだ。
　まだあたまがよく働いてくれない。
　昨夜の事がぐちゃぐちゃになって思い出される。
entries.maoEnglish:
I felt as though I had been dreaming an old, familiar dream.
Then I awoke.
“…”
I was in my room.
After losing consciousness by the wall around the estate, I had somehow managed to make it back here.
My mind still refused to work properly.
Memories of last night churned through it in a tangled mess.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I feel like, I just saw an old, familiar dream.
I open my eyes.
"……………"
I'm in my room.
After that---After losing consciousness by the mansion wall, it seems like I somehow made it back here.
My thoughts still aren't coming together.
I remember the whirling events of last night.

entries.japanese:
体のそこかしこに包帯で巻いた男。
　そいつは自分と同じように『線』が視えている、ということ。
　そいつは剣で全身を貫かれたあと、体中を燃やされて、断末魔の声をあげながら消えてしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
A man wrapped in bandages from head to toe.
The fact that he could see the “lines,” just as I could.
Then swords pierced his entire body, flames consumed him, and he vanished with a dying scream.
entries.mirrorMoon:
That man wrapped entirely in bandages.
And how he could see "lines" just like me.
After he was impaled by those swords, his body burst aflame, and with a voice that sounded like his dying curse, he ran off.

entries.japanese:
「――――」
　そのあとの光景は、本当におぼろげにしか思い出せない。
　街灯の上にいた人影。
　自分を助けてくれた人影は、シエル先輩に似ていたような気がする―――
entries.maoEnglish:
“—”
Everything after that was little more than a haze.
A figure standing atop a streetlight.
The figure who saved me had seemed somehow like Ciel—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----"
After that, I can only remember things vaguely.
The figure on top of the streetlight.
That figure that saved me, that seemed to resemble Ciel-senpai---

entries.japanese:
「……ばかげてる。
そんなコト、あるはずないのに」
　意識がようやく覚醒してくれた。
　メガネをかけて、ベッドから体を起こす。
　時計は午前八時過ぎ。
　いつもならとっくに朝食を済ましている時間だけど、今日はうちの学校は創立記念日で休校だった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ridiculous. That couldn’t possibly have happened.”
My mind finally cleared.
I put on my glasses and sat up.
It was a little after eight.
Ordinarily I would have finished breakfast long ago, but school was closed today for its anniversary.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Yeah right.
That, can't be true."
I finally wake up.
Putting on my glasses, I get up in bed.
The clock says it's past eight.
Normally I would've long since eaten breakfast by now, but today's a school holiday.

entries.japanese:
「翡翠は……いないか」
　いつもなら影のように扉の前で控えている翡翠はいない。
　おそらく朝から何度も起こしに来ていたんだろうけど、こっちが目覚めないもんだからその度に諦めて、今は他の仕事にいっているんだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hisui’s… not here.”
Usually she waited outside my door as silently as a shadow.
She had probably tried to wake me several times that morning, given up each time when I failed to stir, and gone to attend to her other duties.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hisui…… isn't here?"
The figure of Hisui standing before the door like a shadow is nowhere to be seen.
I'm sure she came here many times to wake me up, but I never did, so she probably went off to do other duties.

entries.japanese:
「…………はあ」
　深く息を吐く。
―――昨夜、アルクェイドと別れたあとに起きた出来事は、俺の理解の範疇を超えている。
　あの包帯の男のことも、そいつから助けてくれた人影のことも、自分があれこれ考えたところで何が解るというわけでもない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Haaa…”
I let out a long breath.
―――Whatever happened after Arcueid and I parted last night lay far beyond anything I could understand.
I could turn the bandaged man and the person who saved me over in my mind forever without learning a thing about either one.
entries.mirrorMoon:
………… *sigh*
I let out a deep breath.
---After I parted with Arcueid last night, the events afterwards were beyond my comprehension.
That bandaged man, and that figure that helped me… they're just not things I can understand no matter how much I try.

entries.japanese:
「どのみち今日の夜もアルクェイドに会うんだし。
あいつなら、きっと答えてくれるはずだ」
　異常な出来事はアルクェイドに相談するとして、せめて休みの日ぐらいは自分の日常に戻らないとどうにかしてしまう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’m meeting Arcueid again tonight anyway. She’ll know the answers.”
I could ask Arcueid about the madness later; for now, if I didn’t reclaim some scrap of normal life on my day off, I was going to lose my mind.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Whatever the case, I have to meet Arcueid tonight.
She has to be able to give me some answers."
I'll talk to her about all these strange things, but for now, I have to just return to my normal life or I'll go crazy.

entries.japanese:
「――よし。
なんにせよ、まずは朝飯だな」
　人間、とりあえず何かを食べなくちゃ始まらない。
　起きたばかりのねぼけた頭と体を動かして、居間に向かう事にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Right. Whatever else happens, breakfast comes first.”
Nothing could begin until a person had eaten.
I forced my sleep-heavy body and brain into motion and headed for the sitting room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"--Alright.
First thing's first.
Time for breakfast."
People can't do anything on an empty stomach, after all.
Shaking the sleep from my body, I go to the sitting room.

entries.japanese:
「ん……？」
　二階の東館の廊下に、黒い洋服が見えた。
「翡翠……かな」
　翡翠は秋葉の部屋から出てきたようだ。
　どうせ後で顔を合わすことになるだろうから、ここで朝の挨拶をしても問題はないだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hm…?”
I caught sight of black clothing in the second-floor corridor of the east wing.
“Hisui…?”
She seemed to have just come from Akiha’s room.
We would see each other later anyway, so there was no harm in saying good morning now.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hm……?"
On the second floor east wing hallway, I see a dark uniform.
"It's probably…… Hisui."
It seems like Hisui was leaving Akiha's room.
I guess we'll run into each other anyway, so it won't hurt to give a greeting.

entries.japanese:
「おーい、翡翠―！」
　声をあげて呼びかける。
　翡翠は俺に気がついたのか、トツトツと静かな足取りでやってきた。
「おはようございます、志貴さま」
「うん、おはよう。
わるいね、自分かってな時間に起きちゃって」
「こちらこそ、お目覚めの時におそばにいられず、申し訳ございません」
　翡翠はスッ、と音もなく頭をさげる。
　……ここで謝られると、夜中は街に出歩いて、深夜に自分でも解らないまま帰ってきてベッドにもぐりこむ、なんていう自分がひどく極悪人に感じられる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hey, Hisui!”
I called down the hall.
She noticed me and approached with her usual small, measured steps.
“Good morning, Master Shiki.”
“Morning. Sorry I woke up whenever I felt like it.”
“On the contrary, I apologize for not being at your side when you awoke.”
Hisui bowed without a sound.
…Hearing her apologize made me feel like a hardened criminal for roaming the city at night, stumbling home after midnight with no idea how I had managed it, and crawling into bed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hey, Hisui!"
I call out to her.
Hisui realizes I am here and quietly walks over to me.
"Good morning, Shiki-sama."
"Yeah, morning.
Sorry for just waking up whenever I felt like it."
"I apologize as well.
I should have been there when you awoke.
Please forgive me."
Hisui silently bows her head.
…… Being apologized to like this after I left in the middle of the night and managing to get back to my room, I suddenly feel like the worst person in the world.

entries.japanese:
「翡翠が謝る必要なんかないよ。
決まった時間に起きないこっちが悪いんだから、翡翠は文句の一つでも言ってくれればいいんだ。
そのほうが俺も調子が出る」
「……文句の一つ、ですか……？」
「ああ。
友人が言うには俺って根は怠け者なんだって。
だからバン、と多少強引にでも背中を叩かれたほうがまっとうな人間になれるんだってさ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“You don’t have anything to apologize for. I’m the one who didn’t get up on time, so you ought to complain once in a while. It might keep me in line.”
“Complain—to you?”
“Sure. A friend of mine says I’m lazy at heart. Apparently I need someone to give me a good hard shove now and then if I’m ever going to become a respectable human being.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"There's no need to apologize.
I didn't wake up at the usual time, so it's my fault.
It's okay if you want to voice your complaints."
"…… Voice, my complaints……?"
"Yeah.
My friend always says I'm always a lazy bum, and he always tells me an occasional whack to my back is good to set me straight."

entries.japanese:
「………………」
　翡翠は黙り込んで、じっとこちらの目を見詰めてくる。
　そのまま待つこと一分弱。
　翡翠は眉ひとつ動かさず、ただ俺を見ているだけだ。
　……やっぱり生半可な事じゃ翡翠に人並みのセリフを言わせるのは無理のようだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
Hisui fell silent and stared directly into my eyes.
Nearly a minute passed.
She merely watched me without so much as twitching an eyebrow.
Apparently getting anything remotely ordinary out of Hisui would take more than a casual suggestion.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"………………"
Hisui stands there thinking silently as she stares at me.
It's like that for about a minute.
She doesn't even blink, but just stares at me.
…… I knew forcing Hisui to do such an ordinary thing would be impossible.

entries.japanese:
「いいよ、今のは忘れてくれ。
それより朝飯にしたいんだけど、朝食の準備って出来てる？」
「……姉さんは外に出ています。
志貴さまの朝食でしたら、食堂のほうにすでに用意されておりますが」
「そっか。
んじゃちょっと食べてくる。
仕事中呼び止めて悪かったね」
　それじゃまた後で、と声をかけて一階へと降りていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Never mind; forget I said anything. More importantly, I’m starving—is breakfast ready?”
“My sister is away. Master Shiki’s breakfast has already been laid out in the dining room.”
“Great. I’ll go eat, then. Sorry I stopped you in the middle of your work.”
I told her I would see her later and headed downstairs.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Don't worry about... just forget it.
More importantly, I'm kinda hungry.
Is breakfast ready?"
"…… Nee-san went outside.
Your breakfast is ready in the dining room."
"Oh.
In that case, I'll go have some food.
Sorry to bother you while you were working."
After saying a quick goodbye, I head downstairs.

entries.japanese:
朝食を食べ終わって居間に戻ると、翡翠がぽつんと一人で立っていた。
「あ、ごちそうさま。
毎朝ありがとう、おいしい朝飯を作ってくれて」
　感謝感謝、と手をあわせて黙祷する。
entries.maoEnglish:
When I returned to the sitting room after breakfast, Hisui was standing there all alone.
“Ah, that was delicious. Thank you for making such a good breakfast every morning.”
I pressed my palms together and offered a solemn prayer of gratitude.
entries.mirrorMoon:
After breakfast, I return to the sitting room and come face-to-face with Hisui.
"Ah, that was good.
Thanks for making such a great breakfast every morning."
I bring my hands together in thanks.

entries.japanese:
「食事の支度は姉さんの仕事です。
お誉めの言葉でしたら、わたしではなく姉にお伝えください」
「それはそうなんだけど―――翡翠と琥珀さんの仕事って完全に分かれているの？
　例えばさ、今日みたいに俺だけ休日っていう時は琥珀さんじゃなくて翡翠が朝ごはんを作ってくれるとか」
「志貴さま、今朝の朝食はお口に合わなかったのですか？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Preparing meals is my sister’s responsibility. If you wish to offer praise, please give it to her rather than me.”
“I know, but—are your duties and Kohaku’s divided that strictly? Say I’m the only one with a day off, like today. Couldn’t you make breakfast instead of her?”
“Was this morning’s breakfast not to your taste, Master Shiki?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Preparing meals is Nee-san's duty.
If you wish to compliment the meal, please tell Nee-san instead."
"That's true, but---your duties are really completely separate?
Such as like today when only I slept in, I thought you might make it."
"Shiki-sama, are you saying the breakfast was not to your taste?"

entries.japanese:
「――――へ？」
　翡翠の返答は、その、突飛すぎて困る。
　彼女は今朝の食事がまずかったから、琥珀さんの代わりに翡翠が作れ、と俺が言っているんだと思ったんだろうか？
「そんなコトないよ。
冷めていても琥珀さんのごはんはおいしいです。
　……ただ、やっぱり食べるならあったかいごはんがいいなって。
でもって、それが翡翠の作ってくれたものならなお嬉しいかな、と」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Huh?”
Her answer was so far from what I expected that I had no idea how to respond.
Did she think I was ordering her to replace Kohaku because breakfast had tasted bad?
“Not at all. Kohaku’s cooking is delicious even when it’s cold.
…It’s just that if I’m going to eat, I’d rather the food be warm. And if you’d made it for me, I suppose that would make me happier still.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----Eh?"
Her words are so off topic it's… troubling.
Does she think I was saying I wanted her to make breakfast because the breakfast tasted so bad?
"That's not it.
Even cold, Kohaku-san's cooking is delicious.
…… But, I like it when it's warm.
And, it'd make me really happy if I got to taste your cooking, Hisui."

entries.japanese:
「―――それは出来ません。
志貴さまのために料理をすることはお断りします」
　キッ、と翡翠は挑むような瞳で見据えてくる。
「そ、そっか。
うん、嫌なことは頼めないよな。
身の回りの世話をしてくれてるだけで十分すぎるほど有りがたいんだから」
entries.maoEnglish:
“That is impossible. I refuse to cook for you, Master Shiki.”
Hisui fixed me with a sharp, defiant glare.
“O-oh. Right. I can’t ask you to do something you hate. I’m already more grateful than I can say for everything else you do for me.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---I cannot do that.
Shiki-sama, I refuse to cook for you."
Her eyes suddenly take on a challenging look.
"Oh, I, see.
Yeah, I don't want to force you to do anything you don't want to do.
You do so much for me already."

entries.japanese:
「……………」
　翡翠は黙ったまま、何かいいたげな視線を向けてきている。
　……なんだろう？
　なにか言いにくい事でもあるんだろうか。
「どうかした翡翠。
俺、自分で気がつかないうちにまた悪いことでもやっちゃった？」
　いえ、と首をふる翡翠。
　翡翠はやっぱり黙ったままで、しばらく待ってもなんら変化はない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
Hisui remained silent, but looked at me as though she wanted to say something.
…What was it?
Was there something she found difficult to say?
“What’s wrong, Hisui? Did I do something awful again without noticing?”
She shook her head.
Still she said nothing, and even after I waited, nothing changed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…………"
Still silent, she faces me as if she wants to say something.
…… What could it be?
Is it something that's difficult for her to say?
"What's wrong Hisui?
Did I do something bad without realizing it again?"
Hisui shakes her head "no".
She just stands there silently.

entries.japanese:
「……それじゃあ、いったん部屋に戻るから。
何か用があったら呼んでくれ」
　じゃ、と居間から出ようと歩き出す。
　と―――その前に翡翠がロビーへと歩き出した。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’m going back to my room for a while. Call me if you need anything.”
I said goodbye and started toward the door.
Before I reached it, however, Hisui walked past me into the foyer.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Then, I'll go back to my room.
If you need me, please call for me."
"Later," I say as I start to walk out of the room.
But---before that, Hisui walks towards the lobby.

entries.japanese:
「―――志貴さま」
「ん？」
「失礼とは思いますが、できるかぎり志貴さまのご要望に応えます」
「……はい？」
　翡翠はじっとまっすぐに見つめてくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki.”
“Hm?”
“Impertinent though it may be, I will do my utmost to accommodate Master Shiki’s request.”
“What?”
Hisui looked straight into my eyes.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Shiki-sama."
"Hm?"
"This may be impolite, but I wanted to fulfill your request to the best of my ability."
"…… Huh?"
She looks directly at me.

entries.japanese:
「今朝は、今までで一番自分自身の無力さを思い知らされた日でした」
「え―――う？」
「七回です。
七回も呼びかけてご返事ひとつ返されないのは、いかがなものでしょうか」
「七回って、その、なにが？」
　いまいち翡翠の言っている事が理解できない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“This morning, I was made more painfully aware of my own helplessness than ever before.”
“Eh—what?”
“Seven times. I called to you seven times without receiving a single answer; what am I to make of that?”
“Seven times—what do you mean?”
I still had no idea what she meant.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"This morning, I came to realize how powerless I am."
"Eh---Uh?"
"Seven times.
I called out seven times, but there was no response.
Is this acceptable?"
"Seven times?
What, do you mean?"
I'm totally lost as to what she wants to say.

entries.japanese:
と、翡翠はロビーにむかって踵を返す。
「率直に言わしていただきますと、志貴さまは愚鈍だと思います」
　かつかつ、と足音をたてて翡翠はロビーへと消えていく。
entries.maoEnglish:
With that, Hisui turned back toward the foyer.
“To speak frankly, Master Shiki, I believe you are remarkably dull-witted.”
Her heels clicking sharply, Hisui disappeared into the foyer.
entries.mirrorMoon:
She turns around.
"To say it candidly, I think you are very dense, Shiki-sama."
Hisui disappears into the lobby with her footsteps trailing in the air.

entries.japanese:
「…………はい？」
　一人残されて、間の抜けた声をあげてみる。
　しばらく考えたすえ、ようやく今のが自分に対する文句だという事に気がついた。
―――いいから文句の一つも言ってくれ。
　そんなセリフを、自分はさっき言ったんだっけ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…What?”
Alone again, I managed a thoroughly witless response.
After thinking for a while, I finally realized she had just complained about me.
―――Go on, complain about me for once.
Hadn’t I said something like that earlier?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"………… Huh?"
Left by myself, I blurt out stupidly.
After thinking to myself for a while, I finally realize she was complaining to me.
---It's okay if you want to voice your complaints.
I said that earlier.

entries.japanese:
「―――俺の要望って、アレか」
　ああ、それに間違いはないだろう。
　翡翠は二階で考えこんだあげく、それを言うために居間で俺を待っていたのかもしんない。
「………いや、そりゃまあ文句を言えっていったけどさ」
　言ったけど、いくらなんでも愚鈍です、はストレートすぎると思う。
　……その、あんまり考えたくはないんだが。
　やっぱり俺は、翡翠に嫌われてるんだろうか？
entries.maoEnglish:
“So that was the request she meant.”
Yes, there could be no doubt.
Perhaps Hisui had spent all that time upstairs devising her complaint, then waited in the sitting room just to deliver it.
“Sure, I told her to complain.”
But calling me remarkably dull-witted seemed a little too direct.
I didn’t much care to consider it.
Did Hisui really dislike me after all?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---That was… my request?"
Yeah, there's no mistake.
Hisui was thinking about it the whole time, and was waiting for me in the sitting room just to tell me.
"…………… Well, that is a complaint, but…"
She said it, but saying "dense" is a little too blunt, right?
…… I don't really want to think it,
but does Hisui really hate me?

entries.japanese:
自室に戻ってはみたが、とりあえずやるべき事がない。
　何をしたものかとしばらく考えこんだあげく、八年ぶりに屋敷の中を散歩する事にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
I returned to my room, but had nothing in particular to do.
After wondering how to occupy myself, I decided to take my first walk around the mansion in eight years.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I go back to my room, but I don't really have anything to do there.
Thinking about what I should do next, I decide to walk around the mansion I haven't explored in eight years.

entries.japanese:
ロビーにおりてきた。
　思い返してみれば、子供の頃はよく屋敷の中を探険して怒られたものだ。
　今は屋敷を探険しようなんて子供じゃなくなって、口うるさい父親もいなくなってしまっている。
　昔は屋敷の廊下を歩くだけでどきどきしたっていうのに、今の自分にそんな感動は皆無だ。
　なんとなく、子供の頃の思い出を確かめるために、のんびりと屋敷の中を歩き始めた。
entries.maoEnglish:
I went down to the foyer.
Thinking back, I had often been scolded for exploring the mansion as a child.
Now I was too old to call wandering its halls an adventure, and the father who used to scold me was gone.
Once, merely walking these corridors had set my heart racing, yet now they stirred nothing in me.
With no real purpose beyond retracing my childhood memories, I began a leisurely walk through the mansion.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I arrive at the lobby.
Come to think of it, I was always getting yelled at for playing in the mansion as a kid.
I'm no kid anymore to play in the mansion, and my old man is also gone.
I used to get so excited just walking the hallways when I was a kid, but now I don't feel anything at all.
For some reason, I aimlessly wander around the mansion to confirm my childhood memories.

entries.japanese:
廊下は長く延びている。
　子供のころは、この廊下がどこまでも続いているんだって信じて疑わなかった。
　屋敷は城のように広くて、毎日少しずつ歩き回っては壁や柱、床に自分の名前を刻み付けた。
　当時、秋葉との遊びで陣地取りみたいなゲームが流行ったせいだ。
　名前を刻んだところが自分の領地だ、なんていって二人で屋敷じゅう歩き回っては、自分の名前を刻んでいったんだっけ。
entries.maoEnglish:
The corridor stretched away before me.
As a child, I had believed without question that it went on forever.
The mansion was as vast as a castle, and every day I explored a little farther, carving my name into its walls, pillars, and floors.
Akiha and I had been obsessed with a game of conquest then.
Wherever you carved your name became your territory; we roamed the entire mansion together, carving our names as we went.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The hallway stretches quite a long distance.
When I was a child, I believed this hallway would go on forever.
The mansion seemed as large as a castle and every day, I would walk a bit around the mansion and carve my name on the wall, the pillars, or the floor.
It was sort of a game I would play with Akiha to see who could take over the mansion.
Saying that wherever I put my name became my territory, it really was just the two of us walking around the mansion and carving our names here and there.

entries.japanese:
「お、あったあった」
　階段の手すりにシキ、という名前が刻まれている。
　父親が屋敷の中で遊ぶのを禁じたのは、案外この遊びのせいかもしれない。
　ともかく注意深くして見れば、そこかしこに自分と秋葉の名前が刻まれている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“There it is.”
SHIKI was carved into the stair rail.
Perhaps Father had forbidden us from playing indoors because of this game.
Once I began looking closely, I found my name and Akiha’s everywhere.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Oh, here.
Still here."
On the handrail by the stairs is carved the name SHIKI.

It was probably because of these games that my old man forbade us from playing inside the mansion.
Anyway, if I look closely, I can see both my name and Akiha's all over the place.

entries.japanese:
広い屋敷。
　子供のころ、お城のように思えたこの屋敷も、今ではちょっとしたお化け屋敷ていどの広さしか感じなくなっている。
　時間がたって、大人になって。
　俺と秋葉は、幼かったころの遠野志貴と遠野秋葉ではなくなってきている。
entries.maoEnglish:
The sprawling mansion.
As a child it had seemed like a castle; now it felt no larger than a respectable haunted house.
Time had passed, and we had grown up.
Akiha and I were no longer the little Shiki Tohno and Akiha Tohno we had once been.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The spacious mansion.
While I used to think it was like a giant castle, now it almost seems like an abandoned, haunted house.
Because, I've grown up since then.
Akiha and I, we're not the Tohno Akiha and Tohno Shiki that we were then.

entries.japanese:
外に出る。
―――そういえば、秋葉と遊ぶのはたいていが庭でだったっけ。
　秋葉は俺と違って親父の言いつけを守っていたから、一日に三十分ぐらいしか遊ぶ事ができなかった。
　だっていうのにやる事といったら俺たちの後ろについてきて、じっと言うことを聞いているだけだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
I went outside.
―――Come to think of it, Akiha and I had usually played in the garden.
Unlike me, Akiha obeyed Father, so she was allowed to play for only half an hour a day.
Even then, she mostly trailed behind us and did whatever she was told.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I go outside.
---Come to think of it, most of the time we spent playing was in the garden.
Since Akiha was obedient to that old man, unlike me, she could only play outside for about thirty minutes a day.
And still, she usually just stayed behind us, watching and listening.

entries.japanese:
それでも、いざ遊び出せば元気に走り回って、何をするにしても俺と勝ち負けを競りあってたんだっけ。
「……なんだ。
あいつ、昔っから今の性格の下地はあったんじゃないか」
　親父の手前、猫を五、六匹かぶっていたのかもしれない。
　ま、それにしたって今の秋葉は変わりすぎだ。
八年間という歳月は、こっちが思っている以上に長いものだったのかもしれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
Yet once the games began, she ran about as energetically as anyone and turned everything we did into a contest between us.
“Well, look at that. I guess her present personality was in there all along.”
Perhaps she had been playing the good little girl five or six times over whenever Father was watching.
Even so, the Akiha of today had changed too much. Eight years might have been far longer than I understood.
entries.mirrorMoon:
But she would energetically run out with us and compete with us in whatever games we would play.
"…… Perhaps her personality stems from those times?"
She might have suppressed herself in front of that old man.
But still, Akiha's changed too much since then.
Maybe these eight years were a longer time than I thought.

entries.japanese:
―――中庭に出る。
　屋敷の壁にはまた名前が刻まれていた。
　シキ、志貴、秋葉、シキ、秋葉、シキ、秋葉、志貴、志貴、シキ、志貴。
　割合的にはこんなところで、さすがにシキという名前のほうが多い。
　なんだかんだいっても秋葉は女の子で、男の子であるこっちの行動範囲には敵わなかったということだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――I stepped into the courtyard.
More names had been carved into the mansion wall.
SHIKI, Shiki, Akiha, SHIKI, Akiha, SHIKI, Akiha, Shiki, Shiki, SHIKI, Shiki.
That was about the usual proportion, though naturally SHIKI appeared more often.
Akiha had been a girl, after all; she could hardly compete with the territory a boy could cover.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---I go to the courtyard.
Outside, the walls are also inscribed with names.
SHIKI, Shiki, Akiha, SHIKI, Akiha, SHIKI, Akiha, Shiki, Shiki, SHIKI, Shiki.
The ratios are like that, and the name SHIKI appeared far more times.
I suppose Akiha was just a girl so she couldn't keep up with a boy.

entries.japanese:
「まったく。
手加減ぐらいしてやればよかったのに」
　子供のころの自分をごちてみても、落書きの数は変わらない。
　この様子では、負けず嫌いの秋葉にどれくらい悔し涙を流させたことだろう。
「そうか。
あんがい子供のころの恨みを今になって晴らしてるのかもな、あいつ」
　……まあ、秋葉にかぎってそんな事はないと思うけれど、あったらあったでそれも可愛らしいかもしれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Honestly. You could have let her win once in a while.”
Scolding my childhood self did nothing to change the number of marks.
Knowing how fiercely Akiha hated to lose, I wondered how many tears of frustration I had wrung from her.
“Maybe she’s finally taking revenge for all that now.”
…Not that Akiha would ever do such a thing. Still, if she were, it would be rather cute.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Geez.
It would've been better if I held back a bit."
Cursing myself from that time doesn't change the number of my scribbles.
If this was the case, I probably made Akiha pretty angry, considering how much she hates losing.
"I see.
Maybe she's taking it out on me now."
…… I'm sure she's not the kind to do that, but if she did, that's a little cute.

entries.japanese:
「なんか、俺もとことんバカ兄貴だな」
　うむ、本当にばか兄貴なのだ。
「――――さて」
　なんとなく懐かしい、平和な心持ちになって中庭を散歩していく。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I really am a hopeless big brother.”
Yes, a hopeless big brother indeed.
“Well, then.”
Filled with a strangely peaceful nostalgia, I continued through the courtyard.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I'm an older brother stupid for his little sister."
Yeah, I really am.
"----Well then."
With a nostalgic, peaceful feeling, I stroll through the courtyard.

entries.japanese:
「翡翠……？」
　裏庭にやってくると、ちょうど翡翠の後ろ姿が目に入った。
　翡翠はこちらに気づいていない。
　何をしにいくのか、翡翠は森の中に入っていく。
「？」
　興味をひかれて、少しだけ後についていく。

――――と。
　翡翠が歩いていった先には、ちょっとした広場があるようだった。
「………あれ？
　あんなところに広場なんてあったっけ？」
　首をかしげて思い出そうとしてみるが、どうも記憶はあいまいだ。
　屋敷の森の中、木々をきりとったような広場が見える。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hisui…?”
When I reached the rear garden, I caught sight of her from behind.
She had not noticed me.
Whatever her errand was, it took her into the woods.
“Hm?”
Curious, I followed at a distance.
――――And then.
Beyond the trees where Hisui had gone, there seemed to be a small clearing.
“…Was there always a clearing over there?”
I tried to remember, but the memory would not come into focus.
Amid the mansion woods lay an open space, as though someone had cut it cleanly out of the trees.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hisui……?"
As I come to the rear courtyard, I see Hisui's figure from behind.
Hisui doesn't realize I'm here.
What is she doing, going into the woods like that?
"?"
A bit curious, I follow her from a slight distance.
----And.
Where Hisui headed to, there seems to be a small clearing.
"……… Huh?
There's a clearing in that place?"
Tilting my head to the side, I try to remember, but for some reason, my memory is a bit vague.
In the forest of the mansion, I can see a clearing as if the trees were cut there.

entries.japanese:
―――いや、見えるというのは正しくない。
　普通に歩いている分には決して見えなかったはずだ。
　翡翠があそこに歩いて行かなければ、屋敷に住んでいながら一生気づかなかったぐらい隠れた、木々に囲まれた小さな広場。
「……？
　あんなところ、あったかな。
あったならかっこうの遊び場になってたはずなんだけど」
　少なくとも森の中の広場で秋葉と遊んだ記憶はない。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――No, saying it was visible was not quite right.
No one merely walking through the woods would ever have seen it.
If Hisui had not walked that way, I might have lived in the mansion all my life without discovering that tiny clearing hidden among the trees.
“…Was that really there? If it was, it would have made the perfect playground.”
At least, I had no memory of ever playing with Akiha in a clearing in the woods.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---No, "can see" is not quite right.
If you walk by normally, you probably would never notice it.
If Hisui didn't walk there, hidden enough by the surrounding trees as it is, I would never have noticed even if I lived here all my life.
"…… ?
Was that always there?
If it was, we probably played there as kids."
To say the least, I don't remember ever playing with Akiha in the clearing.

entries.japanese: ―――――――ない、ような、気が、する。
entries.maoEnglish: ―――――――I don’t… think… I do.
entries.mirrorMoon: ----I feel like I've never, been there, before.

entries.japanese:
「…………」
　少しだけ思案してから、その広場に入ってみることにした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
After a moment’s hesitation, I decided to enter.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…………"
After thinking for a bit, I decide to go into the clearing.

entries.japanese:
……広場には特別なにもない。
　先に入っていった翡翠の姿もない。
「なんだ―――ただの空き地じゃないか」
　とことこと広場の真ん中へ歩いていく。
　広場は本当に、なんていうことはない空き地だった。
　きれいにまったいらにされた土の地面と、
　まわりを囲む深い森の木々。
entries.maoEnglish:
…There was nothing remarkable in the clearing.
Hisui, who had gone in ahead of me, was nowhere to be seen.
“It’s nothing—just an empty patch of ground.”
I wandered toward the center.
It truly was an utterly unremarkable clearing.
A perfectly level expanse of bare earth,
encircled by the dense trees of the forest.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… The clearing doesn't strike me as anything out of the ordinary.
I don't see any sign of Hisui.
"What's this---it's just an empty place."
I walk to the middle.
It really is just an empty space.
The perfectly level open ground.
The deep woods enclosing the area.

entries.japanese:
蝉の声と。
　溶けるような、強い、夏の陽射し――――――
entries.maoEnglish:
The cry of cicadas.
Summer sunlight so fierce it seemed to melt the world—
entries.mirrorMoon:
The voice of the cicadas.
And the strong, summer sunshine that feels like it could dissolve------

entries.maoEnglish:
“What…?”
Summer… sunlight?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Eh…………?"
Summer, sunshine---?

entries.japanese:
「い――――痛ぅ…………」
　胸の傷が痛む。
　まるで／ざくりと。
　包丁で胸を刺された／ような／この痛み。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ah—ow…”
The old wound in my chest began to ache.
As though / cut open.
The pain / of a kitchen knife / driving into my chest.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ou----ouch………"
The wound on my chest starts to hurt.
It's like / stabbing
This pain / that feels like / a kitchen knife stabbing my chest.

entries.japanese:
みーん　みんみん
　みーん　みんみん
　みーん　みんみん―――――
　なんだ。
――――どこかで、蝉の声がしている。
　今はもう、秋なのに。
――――白く溶けてしまいそうな夏の陽射し。
entries.maoEnglish:
Miiin, min-min
Miiin, min-min
Miiin, min-min―――――
Oh.
――――Somewhere, cicadas are screaming.
Even though it is already autumn.
――――Summer sunlight so white it might melt everything away.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Chiiirp.
Chirp Chirp.
Chiiirp.
Chirp Chirp.
Chiiirp.
Chirp Chirp----.
What is this?
----From somewhere, I can hear the voice of cicadas.
But it's autumn now.
----The summer sunshine bathes everything in white.

entries.japanese:
遠くのそらには入道雲。
　見えるのは空蝉のこえ。
　足元には蝉のぬけがら。
　ぬけがら。
誰かの、ぬけがら。
entries.maoEnglish:
A thunderhead towers in the distant sky.
I can see the hollow song of cicadas.
Empty cicada shells lie at my feet.
A shell. The empty shell of someone.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Columns of summer clouds in the far sky.
I can practically see the voices.
At my feet, discarded shells of cicadas.

Discarded shell.
Someone's--discarded shell.

entries.japanese:
「――――………」
　傷が開く。
　胸が真っ赤に染まって、この両手まで赤黒く赫灼と。
entries.maoEnglish:
“—…”
The wound tears open.
My chest turns scarlet, and the blood blazes red-black across both my hands.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----…………"
My wound opens.
My chest becomes painted a dark crimson; black vermillion soaks both my hands.

entries.japanese:
……うずくまる誰かの影法師。
　　　近寄ってくる幼い少女の足音。
　　　遠くの空には入道雲。
空蝉の青いそら。
　　　気がつけば、
　　　目の前には血まみれの秋葉の泣き顔。
entries.maoEnglish:
…The shadow of someone huddled on the ground.
A little girl’s footsteps drawing nearer.
A thunderhead in the distant sky. The blue sky of a world left hollow.
And when I realized—
Akiha’s blood-soaked, weeping face is before me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Someone's crouched silhouette.
The approaching footsteps of a young girl.
The columns of clouds in the far sky.
The discarded shells of cicadas.
Then,
In front of me, the crying face of Akiha, who is drenched in blood.

entries.japanese:
みーん、みんみん。
　みーん、みんみん。
entries.maoEnglish:
Miiin, min-min.
Miiin, min-min.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Chiiirp.
Chirp Chirp.

Chiiirp.
Chirp Chirp.

entries.japanese:
―――ああ。
鼓膜を突き破ろうとする、
　　　針みたいな蝉の声。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Ah.
The needle-sharp scream of cicadas, trying to pierce my eardrums.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Ah.
Voices which try to pierce my eardrums,
voices of the cicadas.

entries.japanese:
「あ――――ぐ」
　胸がいたい。
　吐き気がする。
　傷はとうのむかしに塞がっているはずなのに、どうしてこんなにも痛むのか。
　胸が　壊れてる。
　古傷が開いて　セキショクの染みが流れ出す。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ah—gh.”
My chest hurts.
I’m going to be sick.
The wound closed long ago, so why does it hurt this much?
My chest is broken.
The old wound opens, and a RED stain pours out.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah----gu."
My chest hurts.
I feel sick.
My wound has healed a long time ago; why does it hurt so much?
My chest   is broken.
The old wound opens, blood flows forth from the opening.

entries.japanese:
―――なんてこと。
　俺の傷は、ぜんぜん癒えてなんかいない。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――So that’s it.
My wound never healed at all.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---What is this?
My wound, it hasn't healed at all.

entries.japanese:
イタイ。
　　　　　コワイ。
　　　　　　　コレガ、
　　　　　　　　　死トイウ衝動カ。
entries.maoEnglish:
IT HURTS.
/     I’M SCARED.
/         IS THIS—
THE URGE CALLED DEATH?
entries.mirrorMoon:
It hurts.
I'm scared.
This is,
The impulse called Death.

entries.japanese:
意識が沈む。
　傷が痛む。
entries.maoEnglish:
My consciousness sinks.
The wound hurts.
entries.mirrorMoon:
My consciousness sinks.
My wound hurts.

entries.japanese: どさり　と、自身の体が地面に倒れこむ音をきいた。
entries.maoEnglish: I hear my own body strike the ground with a heavy thud.
entries.mirrorMoon: My body collapses to the earth with a large thud.

entries.japanese: ……話し声が聞こえてくる。
entries.maoEnglish: …Voices drift toward me.
entries.mirrorMoon: …… I can hear voices talking.

entries.japanese:
「秋葉さま、お医者さまをお呼びしないのですか？」
「馬鹿なことは言わないで翡翠。
　呼べるわけないでしょう、兄さんの傷は普通の傷じゃないんだから……！」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Miss Akiha, should we not summon a doctor?”
“Don’t be absurd, Hisui.
We can’t. My brother’s wound isn’t an ordinary injury…!”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Akiha-sama, are you not going to call for a doctor?"
"Don't be stupid, Hisui.
There's no way I could do that, since Nii-san's wound isn't normal…!"

entries.japanese:
……あきは　と　ひすい　が話している。
　ここは　シキの　部屋だ。
　どうやら　ベッドの上で　眠っている　らしい。
　よお、と声をあげて起きようとしたけれど、体が思うように動かない。
　胸の痛みはもうないくせに、体は鉛のように重い。
　満足に動くのは、目と口だけのようだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
……akiha and hisui are talking.
this is SHIKI’s room.
it seems i am asleep on the bed.
I tried to sit up and greet them, but my body would not obey.
The pain in my chest was gone, yet every limb felt made of lead.
Only my eyes and mouth seemed willing to move.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Akiha  and  Hisui   are talking.
This  is   SHIKI's room.
It looks   like   I am  sleeping  in the bed.
I planned to say "Yo!" and get out of bed, but I can't move at all.
My chest doesn't hurt anymore, but my body feels as heavy as lead.
All I can move are my eyes and mouth.

entries.japanese:
「一体どういうつもりなの翡翠。
兄さんをあそこに近づけてはいけないって、あなたも知っているでしょうに……！」
「もうしわけ…………ありません」
「謝って済む問題じゃないわ。
あなたを兄さん付きの使用人にしたのは、こういう事態を避けさせるためでしょう？
　それを忘れて、あなたは何をやっていたっていうのよ……！」
entries.maoEnglish:
“What were you thinking, Hisui? You knew you were never to let my brother go near that place…!”
“I am—terribly sorry.”
“Sorry isn’t enough. I assigned you to my brother precisely to prevent this. Did you forget what you were supposed to be doing…?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Just what in the world were you trying to do, Hisui?
You know not to let Shiki go near that place……!"
"Please…… Forgive me."
"This can't be solved by apologizing.
You were assigned to serve Nii-san to avoid this kind of situation.
So what were you doing…!?"

entries.japanese:
秋葉は普段からでは考えられないぐらい、感情を剥き出しにして怒っている。
　対して、叱られている翡翠はうつむいたままずっと黙っていた。
　……俺には、二人がどうしてこうなっているのか全然わからない。
　わからないけれど、翡翠が俺のせいで怒られている、という事ぐらいは読み取れた。
entries.maoEnglish:
Akiha was openly furious, with an intensity I had never seen from her.
Hisui endured the rebuke with her head bowed, saying nothing.
…I had no idea how things had come to this.
But I could at least tell that Hisui was being blamed because of me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Completely different from her usual manner, Akiha gives full vent to her anger.
In comparison, Hisui is accepting the scolding, looking down silently.
…… I'm not sure how this all came about.
But I can at least tell that Hisui is being yelled at because of me.

entries.japanese:
「答えなさい翡翠。
あなたは、今日一日何処で何をしていたっていうの？」
　秋葉の質問に翡翠は答えない。
　二人の間の空気は段々と重苦しくなってくる。
　ぎゅっ、と唇をかみしめて、秋葉が翡翠に一歩だけ近寄る。
　……秋葉が、翡翠に手を上げようとしているのは、俺の目から見てもよくわかった。
　翡翠もわかっているだろうに、うつむいたままそれを黙って受け入れようとしている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Answer me, Hisui. Where were you and what were you doing today?”
Hisui did not answer.
The air between them grew heavier by the second.
Akiha bit down on her lip and took one step toward her.
…Even in my condition, I could see that Akiha was about to strike her.
Hisui must have known as well, yet she kept her head bowed, silently prepared to accept it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Answer me, Hisui.
What were you doing and where were you all day long?"
Hisui doesn't respond.
The air grows tenser between them.
Biting her lip, Akiha takes a step towards Hisui.
…… Even I can understand that Akiha intends to hit her.
Hisui seems to know this as well, but she just stands with her head hung in shame, ready to receive it.

entries.japanese:
「―――ちょっと待て秋葉」
「兄さん――気がついたんですか！？」
「ああ、秋葉があんまりにうるさいんで、いま目がさめた」
「あ…………」
　秋葉は気まずそうに視線をそらす。
　翡翠はやっぱりうつむいたまま、俺のほうを見ようともしなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hold on, Akiha.”
“Brother—you’re awake?”
“Yeah, you were making so much noise you woke me up.”
“Ah…”
Akiha looked away in embarrassment.
Hisui kept her head bowed and would not look at me at all.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Hold on, Akiha."
"Nii-san--You're awake!?"
"Yeah, you were so loud, I woke up."
"Ah…………"
Akiha looks away uncomfortably.
Hisui still keeps looking down, not even trying to look at me.

entries.japanese:
「あのさ、あんまり翡翠にあたるなよ。
事情はしらないけど、ようするに俺が倒れた事でもめてるんだろ？
　なら翡翠に責任なんかないよ。
こんなの俺がかってに倒れただけなんだから」
　よっ、と腕に力をこめて、なんとか上半身だけベッドから起こした。
　今は、それだけでもう指一本だって動かせそうにない。
　けれど翡翠が落ち込んでいる手前、無理をしてでも元気なフリをしなくちゃいけない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Don’t take it out on Hisui. I don’t know the whole story, but this is about me collapsing, right? Then it isn’t her fault. I’m the one who dropped without warning.”
With a grunt, I forced enough strength into my arms to lift my upper body from the bed.
The effort left me unable to move so much as a finger.
But with Hisui already crushed by guilt, I had to pretend I was fine, whatever it cost.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"You know, you shouldn't let it out on Hisui.
I don't know the circumstances, but this has to do with me collapsing, right?
It's not her fault, I just collapsed on my own."
I strain hard and somehow manage to lift the upper half of my body off the bed.
But that's all I can manage, and I don't think I can even move an inch more.
But since Hisui is depressed, I have to force myself to act as fine as possible.

entries.japanese:
「まったく、おまえも俺のコトなんかでケンカなんかするな。
大人びたように見えてまだ子供なんだな」
「でも――――兄さんはあれからずっと気を失っていたんですよ？
　十時間以上も昏睡しているなんて、今までなかったはずです。
　もし―――兄さんがあのまま目が覚めなかったら、私はどうすればいいんですか……！」
「ばか、縁起でもないこというなよ。
こんなのはただの貧血じゃないか。
……って、なんだぁ！？
　もう夜の十時をまわってるじゃないか！」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Honestly, don’t quarrel over someone like me. You may look grown-up now, but you’re still a child.”
“But, Brother—you’ve been unconscious ever since! You’ve never been out for more than ten hours before.
If you had never opened your eyes again, what was I supposed to do?”
“Don’t say things like that. It’s just anemia. Wait—what? It’s already after ten at night!”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Honestly, getting into a fight over me.
Even if you look like an adult, you're still a child."
"But… you completely fainted, Nii-san.
You were out for more than ten hours, and nothing like this has happened before.
If---you never woke up, what would I have done……!?"
"Idiot, don't say things like that.
Wasn't this just anemia?
…… huh?
It's ten o'clock already!?"

entries.japanese:
「ですから、兄さんはお昼から今までずっと気を失っていたんです」
　遠慮がちに秋葉は語る。
　が、こっちの心配事は自分の体のことなんかじゃなくて、夜の十時に公園で待ち合わせ、というアルクェイドとの約束だった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“That is what I have been telling you—you were unconscious from noon until now.”
Akiha’s voice had grown subdued.
My own concern, however, was not my health but the promise I had made to meet Arcueid in the park at ten.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yes, you were unconscious since noon."
She speaks hesitantly.
I wasn't worried about me, but my promise to meet with Arcueid in the park at ten o'clock.

entries.japanese:
「やばい、行かなくっちゃ。
秋葉、俺は出かけるから後のことはよろしくな。
あんまり翡翠をいじめるなよ」
「ば、ばかなことを言わないでください……！
　
　私、兄さんが毎夜どこに行くかなんてコトはもう聞きません。
聞きませんから、どうか今夜ぐらいはご自分の体を大事にしてあげてください……！」
「はは、大丈夫だって。
こんなのはしょっちゅうなんだぞ。
中学のころなんて日に二回は倒れてたって、知ってるだろ秋葉？」
「だから余計に心配なんです。
―――兄さん。
お願いだから、今日ぐらいは私の言うコトを聞いてください」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Damn, I have to go. Akiha, I’m heading out. Take care of things here—and don’t bully Hisui.”
“D-don’t be ridiculous…!
I won’t ask where you go every night anymore. So please, just for tonight, take care of yourself…!”
“I’m fine. This happens all the time. You remember how I used to collapse twice a day in middle school, don’t you, Akiha?”
“That is precisely why I’m worried. Brother… please. Just for tonight, listen to me.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Oh no, I have to go.
Akiha, I have to go so I'll leave the rest to you.
Don't bully Hisui, okay?"
"D, don't say such stupid things……!
I won't ask where you go every night, Nii-san.
I won't ask, so please at least tonight, take it easy on your body tonight……!"
"Haha, I'm okay.
This is pretty regular.
When I was in middle school, I used to collapse twice a day, you know that, right Akiha?"
"That's why I'm more worried.
---Nii-san, please listen to what I say, at least just for tonight."

entries.japanese:
秋葉は真剣な眼差しで俺の目を見つめてくる。
　俺は―――――
entries.maoEnglish:
Akiha held my gaze, utterly serious.
And I—
entries.mirrorMoon:
She looks me in the eye with a serious expression.
I-----

entries.japanese:
「………………」
　……仕方ない。
　これ以上秋葉に逆らうと、なんだか泣かしてしまいそうで怖い。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
…Fine.
If I kept defying Akiha, I was afraid I might make her cry.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"………………"
…… I guess it can't be helped.
I'm afraid I'll make her cry if I keep going against her.

entries.japanese:
「……わかった、今日はおとなしく眠るコトにするよ」
　言って、ベッドに体を横たえた。
「ほんとう……？
　あとになって部屋を抜け出したりするのもナシですよ？」
「ああ、わかってる。
実をいうとさ、どのみち体がまだ重いんだ。
秋葉の目を盗んで外に出ることはできそうにないよ」
「――――よかった」
　ほう、と肩をおとして秋葉は息をはく。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…All right. I’ll be good and go to sleep tonight.”
With that, I stretched out on the bed.
“Really…? You won’t sneak out later?”
“I know. Honestly, my body still feels too heavy anyway. There’s no chance I could slip past you and get outside.”
“Thank goodness.”
Akiha’s shoulders sagged as she let out a long breath.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Alright.
I'll go to sleep for today."
Saying that, I lie down.
"Really……?
You're not going to sneak out of the room later?"
"No, I get it.
To tell the truth, my body feels incredibly heavy.
I don't think I could sneak outside."
"----Thank goodness."
Akiha breathes out and relaxes visibly.

entries.japanese:
「翡翠、琥珀に兄さんが目を覚ました事を伝えにいって。
兄さん、夕食はどうしますか？」
「……そっか。
いや、琥珀さんには悪いけど、食べられそうにない。
今夜はこのまま眠ることにするよ」
「……わかりました。
じゃあ翡翠、そう琥珀に伝えてきて」
　翡翠はうつむいたままコクン、とうなずいて部屋から出て行く。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hisui, go tell Kohaku that Brother is awake. Brother, would you like dinner?”
“…Oh, right. I feel bad for Kohaku, but I don’t think I could eat. I’ll just sleep through the night.”
“…Very well. Hisui, please tell Kohaku that.”
Still looking down, Hisui gave a small nod and left the room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hisui, tell Kohaku that Nii-san is awake.
Nii-san, what about dinner?"
"…… Oh yeah.
No, tell Kohaku-san I'm sorry, but I don't think I can eat right now.
I'm just going to go to sleep."
"…… I understand.
Then Hisui, tell Kohaku that."
Still looking downcast, Hisui nods and leaves the room.

entries.japanese:
……さて。
　ベッドに体を預けたら、また眠気がやってきた。
　このままならあと一分もかからずに眠れるに違いない。
―――と、その前に。
「秋葉。
うちの庭に、あんな場所あったっけ？」
「ええ。
私たちが子供のころ、よく遊んだ場所です」
「そっか。
なんだか、よく覚えてないな」
　……ああ。
本当に、忘れてしまってた。
entries.maoEnglish:
Well, then.
Once I settled back into bed, drowsiness returned.
At this rate I’d be asleep in under a minute.
―――But before that.
“Akiha. Has that place always been in our garden?”
“Yes. We used to play there all the time when we were children.”
“I see. I hardly remember it.”
…No. I truly had forgotten.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Now then.
Lying in bed, I start to feel sleepy again.
Like this, I bet I could fall asleep in less than a minute.
----But, before that,
"Akiha.
There's a place like that in the garden?"
"Yes.
When we were children, we used to play there often."
"Oh.
For some reason, I don't remember it well."
…… Yeah.
I really did forget all about it.

entries.japanese:
「それともう一つ。
……ヘンな事を聞くんだけど、子供のころさ、俺と秋葉と―――もう一人ぐらい、子供がいたとかいう話はしらないか？」
「は？」
　秋葉は見当もつかない、と首をかしげる。
　……そうだよな。
そんな子供、いるはずがない。
　でも―――そうじゃないとおかしいんだ。
　ユメで見た光景と、
　あの広場で見たユメ。
　この二つが同じだっていうんなら――――
　もう一人、殺されてしまった子供がいないと話があわない―――。
entries.maoEnglish:
“One more thing. This is going to sound strange, but when we were children, was there ever another child with us? Someone besides you and me?”
“What?”
Akiha tilted her head, utterly at a loss.
Of course. There couldn’t have been another child.
But if there wasn’t, nothing made sense.
The scene I saw in my dream,
and the dream I saw in that clearing.
If those two were the same—
then there had to have been one more child who was killed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"And one more thing.
…… It's a weird question, but when we were kids----wasn't there another kid with us?"
"Huh?"
She tilts her head, like she doesn't understand what I'm saying.
…… I guess not.
There couldn't have been another kid.
But… if that's true, how strange?
That scene I saw in my dream,
and the dream I saw in the clearing.
If these two are the same----
Then it doesn't make sense unless there's another kid that was killed……

entries.japanese:
「いや、なんでもない。
ただのユメの話だ」
「そうですか。
ではおやすみなさい、兄さん。
今日はゆっくり休んでくださいね」
「ああ、そうする」
　秋葉の声にそう答えたとたん。
　いつもの貧血のように、とうとつに眠りに落ちていっていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Never mind. It was only a dream.”
“I see. Good night, then, Brother. Please get plenty of rest.”
“I will.”
The moment I answered Akiha.
