　じゃあな、と教師は教室から去っていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I know you aren’t the sort of student who stays out carousing, but the matter came up at the staff meeting. The teachers responsible for student discipline want a word with you.
Go to the student guidance office after school. Consider it bad luck and bear with them.”
With that, the teacher leaves the classroom.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I know you're not the kind of student to goof off at night, but there have been concerns voiced by the faculty.
It appears the head of the student council would like to speak to you.
Because of that, please go to the student council room after school.
Just consider yourself unlucky and bear with it."
Saying goodbye, he leaves the classroom.

entries.japanese:
放課後。
　生徒指導室に顔を出すと、指導部の教師はまだ来ていなかった。
　……思い出してみれば、指導部の教師たちはそろって体育系の部活の顧問たちだ。
　もしかすると自分たちの部活が終わるまでやってこないつもりかもしれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
After school.
When I report to the student guidance office, none of the teachers are there yet.
…Come to think of it, every teacher on the discipline committee coaches an athletic club.
Perhaps they intend to keep me waiting until their practices end.
entries.mirrorMoon:
After school.
I stop by the student council room, but the teacher isn't there.
…… Now that I remember, that teacher is also an adviser to the gymnastics team.
He probably won't come until practice is over.

entries.japanese:
「―――――」
　椅子に座って、律儀に待つコトにした。
「………くっ」
　ぎり、と唇を噛む。
　こんなコトをしている場合じゃないってわかってる。
　わかっているけど、俺にはこんなコトしかする事がない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“————”
I sit down and wait dutifully.
“…Ghk.”
I bite hard into my lip.
I know this is no time to be doing something like this.
I know, but this is the only thing I can do.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------"
I sit in my chair and wait faithfully.
"………… Kk."
I bite my lip.
I know this isn't the time to be doing this.
I know, but there's nothing I can do.

entries.japanese:
窓越しの景色は、夕焼けの朱に染まっている。
　校庭からは部活動に励む生徒たちのかけ声や、下校していく生徒たちのざわめきがさざなみのように聞こえてくる。
　その中で、この教室だけが切り取られたように静かだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
Beyond the window, the world is dyed in the scarlet of sunset.
Calls from students practicing on the athletic field and the murmur of those going home reach me like distant ripples.
Amid it all, this one room is silent, as though cut away from the rest of the school.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Outside the window, the sunset paints the sky vermillion.
I can hear the voices of club members practicing outside and the students talking while going home.
Within that, this classroom is the only quiet place.

entries.japanese:
……あたまに、くる。
　なんだって自分はこんなところで、こんなコトをしているんだろう。
　何もできない。
　自分の無力さにどうしようもなく腹がたつ。
　けれどそれを解決する手段がないから、結局はぬけがらみたいに言われたことをこなすしかない。
entries.maoEnglish:
It makes me furious.
What am I doing here?
I can do nothing.
My own helplessness enrages me beyond endurance.
Yet because I have no means of changing it, all I can do is obey whatever I’m told like an empty shell.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… This makes me angry.
Why am I here?
I can't do anything.
I'm angry at my powerlessness.
However, I have no way to solve this myself, so in the end, all I can do is accept everything I'm told emptily.

entries.japanese:
「……なにやってるんだろ、俺」
　答えはない。
　そのまま、ずっと、無人の教室で放課後の音だけを聞いていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What am I doing?”
There is no answer.
I remain alone in the empty room, listening to the sounds of the school after hours.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… What am I doing?"
There's no answer.
I just sit in the empty classroom listening to the sounds outside.

entries.japanese:
かちん。
　長い秒針が音をたてて、夜の七時になったことを告げてくる。
　生徒指導室には誰もやってこない。
　学校の閉鎖時間は六時、教師たちが帰るのが六時半だというから、校舎には誰も残っていないという事になる。
entries.maoEnglish:
Click.
The second hand ticks forward, and the clock announces seven in the evening.
No one has come to the student guidance office.
The school closes at six and the teachers leave at half past, which means no one else remains in the building.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Tick.
The second hand of the clock sweeps by, telling me it's now seven at night.
No one comes by.
The school closes at six and all the teachers leave at six-thirty, so no one else remains on the school grounds.

entries.japanese:
「……忘れられたかな」
　椅子から立ちあがる。
　一人でずっと考えていたせいか、少しはあたまがマトモに戻ってくれたみたいだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Did they forget about me?”
I rise from the chair.
Maybe all those hours alone with my thoughts have brought my head back to something like normal.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I guess I'm forgotten."
I get up from my chair.
After pondering matters so long, my head starts to clear a little.

entries.japanese:
ずっと、考えていた。
　自分はどうするべきか、何を優先すべきかっていうコトを。
　俺は、これから―――
entries.maoEnglish:
I have been thinking all this time.
About what I ought to do, and what matters most.
From here on, I will—
entries.mirrorMoon:
I was thinking all this time.
About what I should do, what I should prioritize.
From here, I should----

entries.japanese:
―――アルクェイドを、見つけ出す。
　どんなにそれが不可能めいていて、無駄なことだってわかっていても、それしか考え付かない。
　見つけるまで探し続ける。
　あいつを一人にしておけないし、かってに―――かってにロアとかいうヤツと決着をつけられてたまるもんか。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――I’ll find Arcueid.
Impossible or not, pointless or not, it was the only answer I could think of.
I would search until I found her.
I couldn’t leave her alone—and I’d be damned if I let her settle things with Roa on her own.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----I should look for Arcueid.
No matter how impossible it might look, no matter how hopeless it seems, it's all I can think of.
I'll keep searching until I find her.
I can't leave her by herself, and I can't let her----settle things with Roa by herself.

entries.japanese:
「――――よし」
　ふんぎりはついた。
　そうと決まればこんなところで時間を無駄にはできない。
　一刻も早く街に出て、藁にすがってでもあいつを探し出さないと――――
entries.maoEnglish:
“All right.”
My mind was made up.
Now that I had decided, I could not waste another moment there.
I had to get out into the city and find her as quickly as possible, even if it meant clutching at straws—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----Alright."
My mind is set.
So I can't waste any more time here.
I have to go in town this very minute, and even if it means looking for a needle in a haystack, I have to find Arcueid----

entries.japanese:
――――屋敷に戻ろう。
　アルクェイドの事を諦めたわけじゃないけど、何のアテもなしであいつを探し出せるとは思えない。
　なら、今は無闇に動き回るより、屋敷に戻って自分に何ができるのかを冷静に考えるべきだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――I’ll go back to the mansion.
I hadn’t given up on Arcueid, but I couldn’t imagine finding her without a single lead. Better to return to the mansion and think calmly about what I could do than run around blindly.
entries.mirrorMoon:
--I'll go back to the mansion.
It's not like I've given up on Arcueid, but without any leads, I don't think I could find her.
Then instead of running around blindly, I should go back to the mansion and think calmly about what I can do.

entries.japanese:
「……そんなことしか、できないのか」
　自分の無力さを痛感する。
　けど、今はそんな方法しか思いつかなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…Is that really all I can do?”
My helplessness stung.
But for now, I had no better answer.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Is that all I can do?"
I am pained by my lack of ability to do anything.
But right now, it is all I can think of.

entries.japanese:
―――ロアっていう吸血鬼を探す。
　アルクェイドは俺の前に出てこない。
こっちからアイツを探し出すのはほぼ不可能だ。
　だから、その逆をとる。
　アルクェイドは絶対にロアを倒すといった。
アルクェイドの目的がロアであるのなら、俺もロアを探し当てる。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――I’ll find the vampire called Roa.
Arcueid refused to appear before me, and finding her myself was all but impossible.
So I would work backward.
She had sworn to defeat Roa. If Roa was her quarry, then I would find him too.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----I should find this vampire Roa.
Arcueid isn't going to come see me, and it's almost impossible for me to find her.
So I'll take the opposite route.
Arcueid said she would defeat Roa no matter what.
If her purpose is Roa, then I'll look for him too.

entries.japanese:
アルクェイドは自分からロアの元へとやってくる。
その時にまで俺がロアを探し出せていればそれでいい。
　それに、それだったら。
　最後の瞬間に、アルクェイドの手助けもできる。
entries.maoEnglish:
Arcueid would come to Roa on her own. All I had to do was find him before she did.
And then, at the final moment,
I could help her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Arcueid will come to Roa, so if I could find him before then, that'll be good.
And with that option,
I can help Arcueid at the last moment.

entries.japanese:
「――――よし」
　ふんぎりはついた。
　そうと決まればこんなところで時間を無駄にはできない。
　一刻も早く街に出て、藁にすがってでも吸血鬼を探し出さないと――――
entries.maoEnglish:
“All right.”
My mind was made up.
Now that I had decided, I could not waste another moment there.
I had to get out into the city and find that vampire as quickly as possible, even if it meant clutching at straws—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----Alright."
My mind is set.
So I can't waste any more time here.
I have to go into town this very minute, and even if it means looking for a needle in a haystack, I have to find this vampire----

entries.japanese:
当然のように、廊下には人影がない。
　電灯の明かりも途絶えて、窓からさしこんでくる月光だけが、青白く廊下を照らしあげている。
「―――――」
　廊下から夜空を見上げて気がついた。
　今夜はこれ以上ないっていうぐらい、真円の月をしている。
entries.maoEnglish:
Naturally, the corridor is deserted.
The electric lights are dead, leaving only the moonlight through the windows to wash the hall in ghostly blue.
“…”
Looking out at the night sky, I finally notice.
Tonight’s moon is as perfectly round as a circle can be.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Naturally, the hallway is empty.
The lights are shut off and the hallway is illuminated solely by the blue moonlight streaming in from the windows.
"------"
I realize as I look up in the sky from the hallway,
tonight is a full moon.

entries.japanese:
「…………」
　一瞬、我を忘れて月を見上げた。
　銀色の月。
　ガラス細工じみた美しさは、手を触れてしまえば崩れてしまいそうなほどに脆く感じられる。
　そんな月を。
　こどものころ。
昏睡の際で。
見つめていた。
きがする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
For a moment, I lose myself staring up at the moon.
A silver moon.
Its glasswork beauty seems fragile enough to crumble if I touch it.
A moon like this.
When I was little. At the edge of a coma. I stared at it. Or so I think.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……………"
I lose myself for a moment gazing at it.
The silver moon.
Delicate beauty like glass, it feels like it will crumble if I were to reach out my hand and touch it.
That moon.
When I was a child.
I feel like.
I saw it.
In a stupor.

entries.japanese:
――――ぞくん。
「ぐっ…………！？」
　突然、胸の古傷が痛んだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――A chill runs through me.
“Ghh…!?”
The old wound in my chest erupts in pain.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----Throb.
"Gah…………!?"
Suddenly, the scar on my chest begins to ache.

entries.japanese:
――――どくん。
　心臓が一際跳ねる。
　体中の血管が活性化して、呼吸が一定しなくなる。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――Thump.
My heart gives a violent leap.
Every blood vessel in my body surges awake, throwing my breath out of rhythm.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----Thump.
My heart skips a beat.
My blood starts to circulate wildly and I can't control my breathing.

entries.japanese:
――――ぞく、ん。
　胸に手を触れてみれば。
　じくり、と制服は真っ赤に染まっていた。
　傷が開いて、出血している。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――A cold pulse.
I touch my chest.
My uniform is already wet with brilliant red.
The wound has opened, and I am bleeding.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----Thro, b.
I place my hand on my chest.
My uniform is soaked in blood.
My scar has opened and is bleeding.

entries.japanese:
――――どく、ん。
「は―――ア、ハア―――ハッ――――」
　呼吸が乱れる。
　背筋は寒くて、背骨がそのまま皮膚を破って外に飛び出しそうなほど、痛い。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――Thump.
“Hah—hah—ha”
My breathing breaks apart.
My back is ice-cold, and my spine hurts as though it might spear straight through my skin.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----Thu, mp.
Panting.
My breathing is out of control.
A chill runs through my back, and my spine painfully feels like it's going to burst open.

entries.japanese:
―――ぞく、ん。
―――どく、ん。
―――ぞ、く
―――ど、く
――――――かつ、ん。
　心音にまぎれて、何か、硬い音がした。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――A cold pulse.
―――Thump.
―――Chi—
―――Thu—
――――――Click.
Amid my hammering heartbeat comes another sound—something hard striking the floor.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----Thro, b.
--Thump.
----Th, ro
--Thum
------Tap.
In between my heartbeats, I hear a sound.

entries.japanese:
「あ――――――」
　誰かが、やってくる。
　廊下の奥から、こちらに向かって歩いてきている。
　かつん、という音は足音だ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ah…”
Someone is coming.
A figure is walking toward me from the far end of the corridor.
That click was a footstep.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah------"
Someone is coming.
From the far end of the hallway, walking towards me.
Tap.
The sounds of footsteps.

entries.japanese:
――――なにか、まずい。
　今までみたいな命にかかわる危険を感じて、体が脈打っているのではない。
　ずきり、と頭痛が走る。
　この痛み。
この危機感は、自分自身に対するものだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――Something is wrong.
This isn’t my body reacting to mortal danger as it has before.
Pain lances through my head.
This pain. This dread is directed at myself.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----There's something… not right.
This isn't the wild beating of my heart which comes from my body sensing danger like before.
A headache runs through my head.
This pain, this sense of danger is directed against me.

entries.japanese: 俺は―――遠野志貴は、あの人影にだけは、会ってはいけない気がしている―――――。
entries.maoEnglish: I—Shiki Tohno—feel that this is the one figure I must never meet.
entries.mirrorMoon: I feel that shadowy figure is something I----Tohno Shiki must not meet------.

entries.japanese:
「ハア……ハア……」
　定まらない息遣いのまま、メガネを外した。
　ナイフは―――ポケットの中に入っている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hah—hah”
With my breath still ragged, I remove my glasses.
The knife is in my pocket.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I breathe harder.
Not even able to breathe properly, I take off my glasses.
My knife---is in my pocket.

entries.japanese:
人影がやってくる。
　月明かりの下、人影はどうやら男性のようだった。
　死の『点』は、カレの体の中心に心臓のように脈動している。
　体内には、機械のコードのように張り巡らされた、数え切れないほどの死の『線』。
entries.maoEnglish:
The figure advances.
In the moonlight, it appears to be a man.
A ‘point’ of death pulses like a heart at the center of his body.
Inside him run countless ‘lines’ of death, tangled together like the wiring in a machine.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The figure draws closer.
The moonlight seems to suggest it's a male.
The "point" indicating death pulsates in the center of his body like a heart.
All around his body are numerous "lines" of death covered like wires for a machine.

entries.japanese:
「―――――――――――――――――――」
　呼吸が止まった。
　……あたまが、どうにしかしている。
　あんな人影、自分は知らない。
　知らないのに―――誰かに似ているような気がしてならない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
My breath stops.
Something is wrong with my head.
I don’t know that shadow.
I know I don’t—and still I cannot escape the feeling that he resembles someone.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------------------"
My breathing stops.
…… There's, something wrong with my head.
I don't know this figure.
Even though I don't know----I can't help but feel like it resembles someone.

entries.japanese:
かつん、かつん。
　男は近づいてくる。
　もうすぐ、その顔がはっきりと見て取れる。
「―――――――――――――――――――」
　誰に似ているのか。
　誰に似ているのか。
　誰に似ているのか。
　誰に似ているのか。
　自分は、誰を忘れているのか――――――
entries.maoEnglish:
Click, click.
The man comes closer.
In another moment, I will see his face clearly.
“…”
Who does he look like?
Who does he look like?
Who does he look like?
Who does he look like?
Who have I forgotten—
entries.mirrorMoon:
Tap, tap.
He approaches.
I'll be able to see his face soon.
"--------------------"
Who does he resemble?
Who does he resemble?
Who does he resemble?
Who does he resemble?
Who am I forgetting------?

entries.japanese:
―――血走った目。
　体中に在る、死。
　大気を凍らすような、異質なまでの静けさ。
　間違いなく、コイツは人間じゃない。
　かつん、とさらに近寄ってくる。
　男はまっすぐに俺だけを凝視して、にやり、と声もなく笑った。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Bloodshot eyes.
Death everywhere inside his body.
An inhuman stillness cold enough to freeze the air.
There is no question—this thing is not human.
Another click brings him closer.
His eyes never leave me, and his mouth spreads into a soundless grin.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----Bloodshot eyes.
The death all over his body.
An alien stillness as if the very air around us was frozen.
There's no mistaking it… he isn't human.
He draws even closer.
He heads straight in my direction looking solely at me, smiling wordlessly.

entries.japanese:
「――――――――――――――――――！」
　ナイフを構える。
　パチン、と音をたてて刃が出る。
　男は歩み寄ってくる。
　考えている時間も、躊躇している余裕もなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“—!”
I bring up the knife.
The blade snaps out.
The man keeps walking.
There is no time to think, no room to hesitate.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------------------!"
I ready my knife.
The blade pops forth.
He continues walking.
There's no time to think or hesitate.

entries.japanese:
白い月の下。
　まるでスローモーションのように、目の前の男に向けてナイフを構えた。
　男は止まらない。
　ゆっくりと。
　まるで、俺の時間だけが止まってしまったみたいに。
　男はこちらの腕からナイフをあっさりと奪い取って、くるん、とナイフを逆手に持った。
entries.maoEnglish:
Beneath the white moon.
I level the knife at the man before me as if moving through slow motion.
He does not stop.
Slowly.
As though time had stopped for me alone.
The man plucks the knife effortlessly from my hand and flips it into a reverse grip.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Under the white moon.
As if in slow motion, I ready my knife.
He doesn't stop.
Slowly,
as if time stopped only for me,
he easily reaches out and takes my knife, holding it upside down.

entries.japanese:
「な―――――」
　体が――――動か、ない―――――
「……志貴。
死を視れるのは、なにもおまえだけの特権じゃあない」
　男は、そう言って腕を動かした。
――――ぞく、ん。
　背筋が凍る。
　脳髄が凍結する。
　以前、同じことをされた体が、その痛みを覚えている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Wh—”
My body—won’t move—
“Shiki… Seeing death is not a privilege reserved for you alone.”
With those words, the man moves his arm.
――――A cold pulse.
My spine freezes.
My brain turns to ice.
My body remembers this pain from the last time the same thing happened.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Wha----"
My body----doesn't move----
"…… Shiki.
Being able to see death isn't just your privilege."
Saying that, he moves his arm.
----Th, rob.
A chill runs through me again.
My brain freezes.
My body remembers the same pain from before.

entries.japanese:
「―――――――――――あ」
　ずざ、と肉を裂く音がして。
　男に奪われた俺のナイフは、俺自身の胸に、深々と突き刺さった―――――
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ah…”
There is a wet rip of flesh.
The knife he stole from me drives deep into my own chest—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------------Ah."
The sound of slashed flesh.
My knife he stole--is now plunged deeply--in my chest------

entries.japanese:
体が倒れこむ。
全身から力が抜けて、床に崩れおちていく。
　はらり、と。
　白い布のようなものが落ちていく。
entries.maoEnglish:
My body pitches forward. All strength drains from me, and I crumple toward the floor.
With a soft flutter.
Something like a strip of white cloth falls.
entries.mirrorMoon:
My body collapses.
All my strength drains as I crumble to the floor.

Fluttering,
a white sheet falls.

entries.japanese:
―――刺される寸前に、男の体に寄りかかった為だろう。
　俺の手は、倒れながら、男の体に巻きついた包帯を解いてしまっていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――I must have fallen against him just before the blade entered me.
As I collapse, my hand catches and unravels one of the bandages wrapped around his body.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----It's because I leaned on him when I fell.
As I fell, my hand took the bandages wrapping his body.

entries.japanese:
「そうか。
俺の素顔が見たいのか、志貴」
　言って。
　男は、自分から包帯をはがしていく。
「――――――」
　目の前が真っ暗になる。
　男の顔。
この男の顔を、俺はたしかに知っている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I see. You want to look upon my true face, Shiki.”
With those words.
The man begins tearing away the bandages himself.
“…”
The world goes black.
That face—I know that face. I know I do.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I see.
You wish to see my face, Shiki?"
Saying that,
he unfurls the bandages.
"------"
Everything turns dark.
His face.
This face before me, I know it.

entries.japanese:
―――似ているはずだ。
　だって、こいつの顔は――――
　あの暑い夏の日に、俺の前で、血にまみれていた少年に似すぎている――――。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Of course he looked familiar.
His face is far too much like the boy who lay
bleeding before me on that sweltering summer day.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----It does resemble that.
Because his face----
It resembles the face of the bloody child before me on that hot summer day----

entries.japanese:
だん、と床に倒れこんだ。
　ナイフは胸に刺さったまま。
　不思議と痛みも出血もない。
　ただ、体温が下がっていく。
意識が段々と薄れていく。
　体の自由が、何もかもが消え去っていく。
entries.maoEnglish:
I strike the floor with a thud.
The knife remains buried in my chest.
Strangely, there is neither pain nor blood.
Only my temperature is falling. My consciousness is fading by degrees.
Control of my body—everything—slips away.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I fall onto the ground,
the knife still embedded in my chest.
Strangely, there is no blood or even pain.
My body just gets colder.

My consciousness drifts away.
My control over my body… everything starts to fade away.

entries.japanese:
「おまえに殺された借り、たしかに返したぞ」
　男は、俺を見下ろしてそう言った。
　見上げる顔。
男の姿には見覚えがある。
―――いや、あって当然のはずだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“The debt I owed you for killing me has now been repaid.”
The man looks down at me as he speaks.
I look up at his face. I have seen this man before.
―――No—of course I had seen him before.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I did pay you back for killing me."
He says this as he looks down at me.
The face I see as I look up.
I recognize him.
----Of course I recognize him.

entries.japanese:
ああ―――どうして今まで忘れていたんだろう。
　こどもの頃。
　遠野の屋敷で遊んだ、自分と、秋葉と、もう一人のこどものことを。
entries.maoEnglish:
How could I ever have forgotten?
When we were children.
There had been three of us playing at the Tohno mansion: me, Akiha, and one other child.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Yeah----why have I forgotten until now?
When I was a kid.
The other child me and Akiha played with at the mansion.

entries.japanese:
いつだって―――いつだって自分たちは一緒だった。
　秋葉と遊ぶときだって、いつも自分はカレと一緒になって秋葉を迎え入れたっていうのに、どうして――――俺は今まで、カレの名前を忘れていたんだろう……？
entries.maoEnglish:
We had always been together.
Whenever Akiha came to play, he and I would welcome her together, so why—why had I forgotten his name until now?
entries.mirrorMoon:
Always----always, we were together.
When Akiha came to play, me and him were always there to welcome her----so why---have I forgotten his name until now……?

entries.japanese:
「シ――――キ」
「そうだよ志貴。
ほんとうに、久しぶりだ」
　男―――シキは、満足そうに口元をつり上げた。
　シキ。
志貴。
秋葉。
シキ。
シキ。
秋葉。
志貴。
　そんな、意味のない、落書きの痕。
entries.maoEnglish:
“SHI—KI”
“That’s right, Shiki. It has been a very long time.”
The man—SHIKI—curls his lips in satisfaction.
SHIKI. Shiki. Akiha. SHIKI. SHIKI. Akiha. Shiki.
The meaningless remains of a child’s scribble.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"SHI----KI"
"That's right Shiki.
It's really been a long time."
He----SHIKI smiles with satisfaction.
SHIKI.
Shiki.
Akiha.
SHIKI.
SHIKI.
Akiha.
Shiki.
Those meaningless scribbles.

entries.japanese:
「そんな――――バカな」
「悪いな志貴。
おまえにはもう少し恨み言を聞いてもらわなくちゃいけないんでね、少しだけ『点』を外させてもらった。
　即死でない分、あとしばらくは意識が保てるだろう。
そう簡単に消えてくれるな」
　厭な笑い声と、ネロとの戦いのおりに厭というほど感じた不快感。
　薄れゆく意識の中で、悟った。
　コイツが―――アルクェイドの“敵”なのだ、と。
entries.maoEnglish:
“That’s—impossible.”
“Sorry, Shiki. I still have a few grievances for you to hear, so I made sure to miss your ‘point’ by a little.
Without instant death, you should remain conscious a while longer. Don’t disappear on me too quickly.”
That hateful laugh carries the same revulsion I learned so well in the battle with Nrvnqsr.
Through my fading consciousness, I understand.
This is Arcueid’s enemy.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"That's----ridiculous."
"Sorry Shiki.
You'll have to listen to my grudges just a little longer, so I just avoided the "point" of death slightly.
It's not fatal, so you'll probably stay conscious for a bit.
Don't fade away that easy."
The unpleasant laugh and the terrible uneasiness I felt when I faced Nrvnqsr.
In the midst of my fading consciousness, I realize something.
He is----Arcueid's "enemy".

entries.japanese:
「さて―――そのナイフは貰っておこうか。
じきに消え去るおまえには不必要なものだからな」
　男の腕が、胸に突き刺さったナイフに伸びる。
　ぐっ、とナイフの柄を握られる。
　それを抜かれれば、間違いなくその瞬間に自分は死ぬだろう。
　けれどどうしようもない。
　体は、もう瞼を閉じる事さえできないほど、まったく動いてはくれなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Now, I think I’ll keep that knife. You’ll have no need of it once you vanish.”
His hand reaches for the knife embedded in my chest.
His fingers close around the hilt.
The instant he pulls it free, I will die—there is no doubt of that.
But I can do nothing.
My body refuses to move so completely that I cannot even close my eyes.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Well then----shall I take that knife?
Someone like you who's about to disappear won't need it."
He reaches for the knife stuck in my chest.
He grips the handle.
The moment he takes it out will be my death.
But I can't do anything.
I can't move even to close my eyes.

entries.japanese:
「ぬっ―――！？」
　飛んだ。
　突然、シキの体が車に撥ねられたように、後ろに飛んだ。
　それと同時に、黒い法衣を着込んだ人影が現れる。
　ここは三階だっていうのに、廊下の窓ガラスを破って、彼女は派手な登場をした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ghh…!?”
He flies backward.
Without warning, SHIKI’s body hurtles away as though struck by a car.
At the same instant, a figure in black vestments appears.
Though we are on the third floor, she has made her entrance by smashing through a corridor window.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Gah----!?"
He flies.
Suddenly, SHIKI flies back as if he was struck by a car.
At the same time, a black-robed figure appears.
Even though this is the third floor, she crashes through the glass window and makes a flashy appearance.

entries.japanese:
「くっ――――――！」
　何メートルも吹き飛んだあと。
　シキはゆっくりと体を立てなおして、床に倒れこんだ俺と――――俺を庇うように立ち尽くすシエル先輩を凝視する。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Damn you…!”
After being thrown several meters, SHIKI slowly rights himself.
His stare moves from me, sprawled on the floor, to Ciel standing over me like a shield.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Kk------!"
After flying back many meters,
SHIKI stands up slowly and stares at me lying on the floor----and Ciel-senpai protecting me.

entries.japanese:
「貴様―――一度ならず二度までも邪魔をしたな」
「………………」
　先輩は何も言わず、ただシキを睨んでいる。
　シキは先輩に襲いかかろうと腰をおとす。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You—you have interfered with me not once, but twice.”
“…”
Ciel says nothing and only glares at SHIKI.
SHIKI lowers his stance, ready to spring at her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Bitch----interfering once and now twice?"
"………………"
Senpai only stares back wordlessly at SHIKI.
He lowers himself as if to attack Senpai.

entries.japanese:
――――と。
　何かに気がついたのか、突然、シキは笑い始めた。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――Then.
As though he has suddenly realized something, SHIKI begins to laugh.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----And then.
As if realizing something, SHIKI suddenly begins to laugh.

entries.japanese: 「ふふ、ははは、あははははははは！」
entries.maoEnglish: “Heh, ha ha, ahahahahahaha!”
entries.mirrorMoon: "Huhu, hahaha, ahahahahahaha!"

entries.japanese:
「そうか、そういうことか女！
　まさかとは思ったが本当にそうとはな！
　おもしろいぞ、このような事態は八百年の繰り返しの中でも初めてだ……！
　これならばたしかに、今回は今までと違う展開が待っているだろう……！」
　心底可笑しそうに、シキは笑い続ける。
　……先輩は、ただ無言で目前の吸血鬼を睨んでいた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“So that’s it, woman! I scarcely believed it possible, but it is true! How fascinating—this has never happened before in eight hundred years of repetition…!
Yes, this time the story may truly unfold differently…!”
SHIKI goes on laughing in wholehearted delight.
Ciel merely stares in silence at the vampire before her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I see, that's how it is, woman!
I can't believe it, but that's how it is!
Interesting, this is the first time such a thing has happened in 800 years……!
If that is the case, then new things truly do await me……!"
SHIKI continues to laugh from the bottom of his heart.
…… Senpai merely stares at the vampire in front of her.

entries.japanese:
「どうした？
　私を殺すためにやってきたのだろう？
　それともなにか？
　やはり脱け殻には何もできないという事なのかい？」
「――――――」
　先輩は答えない。
　ただ、吸血鬼から視線をそらして、倒れこんでいる俺の体を抱き上げてくれた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What is wrong? You came to kill me, did you not? Or what? Is an empty shell incapable even of that?”
“…”
Ciel does not answer.
She turns her eyes from the vampire, bends down, and gathers my fallen body into her arms.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"What is it?
You have come to kill me, right?
Or is it something else?
Or is it that a cast-off shell cannot do anything on it's own?"
"------"
Senpai doesn't respond.
She looks away from the vampire and lifts me up.

entries.japanese:
「ほう。
私との因果を断つより、そのニセモノのほうが大事ということか。
　だが、それは無駄だぞ。
そいつはもう助からない。
今まで遠野志貴が好き放題やってきた事を、そのまま返してやったのだからな。
　死線を裂かれたモノにはどのような治療も無意味だ。
あの姫君でさえ、蘇生するのに八百年の歳月と引き換えにするしかなかった。
―――そいつのようなただの人間に、“死”から逃れる術はない」
　嘲笑う声だけが、聞こえる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“So. That counterfeit matters more to you than severing the bond between us.
Your effort is wasted. He cannot be saved. I have merely returned everything Shiki Tohno has done as he pleased.
Anything whose line of death has been severed is beyond all treatment. Even that princess had no choice but to pay eight hundred years to restore herself.
―――A mere human like him has no means of escaping death.”
Only his mocking voice reaches me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Oh?
That impostor is more important than cutting off the cause behind you?
But, that's useless.
He is beyond help.
It's only payback for him living as Tohno Shiki until now.
No matter what, there is no healing someone whose lines of death are cut.
Even that princess had to exchange her 800 years of time in order to regenerate.
----A human like him can't escape death."
His voice is full of mocking laughter.

entries.japanese:
先輩は何も答えない。
　結局、ただの一言も発せず。
　先輩は俺を抱えたまま、吸血鬼に背を向けて三階の窓ガラスから外に飛び降りた。
entries.maoEnglish:
Ciel says nothing.
In the end, she does not utter a single word.
Holding me in her arms, she turns her back on the vampire and leaps through the shattered third-floor window.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Senpai doesn't say anything in response.
In the end, without a single word,
as she holds me, she goes through the glass window and jumps outside.

entries.japanese:
三階分の高さなんて、先輩にはあまり意味のないモノだったらしい。
　タン、と軽い足取りで地面に降り立つと、先輩は振り返らずに学校から出ようと走り出す。
―――その最中。
　俺は虚ろになっていく目で、夜の校舎だけを眺めていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
Three stories of open air seem to mean little to her.
She touches down with a light tap and races away from the school without looking back.
―――All the while.
My emptying eyes remain fixed upon the school building at night.
entries.mirrorMoon:
She seems to treat the height as if it were nothing.
With a light step, she lands on the ground and runs from the school without even looking back.
----Through it all,
I look only at the school building with empty eyes.

entries.japanese:
さっきまで自分がいた三階の廊下。
　勝ち誇った笑みをうかべて俺たちを見逃す、長い黒髪の吸血鬼の姿を、ぼんやりと、虚ろになっていく意識で見つめていた――――。
entries.maoEnglish:
In the third-floor corridor where I had stood moments ago, a long-haired vampire watches us escape with a triumphant smile.
I gaze back through the haze of my dying consciousness.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The third floor hallway I was in until just now.
I blankly look at the vampire with long, black hair as he victoriously watches us leave------.

entries.japanese:
……アルクェイドはこない。
　考えてみれば当然だ。
　あんな事を―――あいつが信頼してくれたものを全部踏みにじって、俺は無理やりあいつの体を犯した。
entries.maoEnglish:
…Arcueid isn’t coming.
Of course she isn’t.
I trampled over everything she had trusted me with and forced myself on her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Arcueid doesn't come.
It's only natural.
After doing that----after trampling over everything she trusted me with, I forcibly violated her body.

entries.japanese:
アルクェイドは、きっと来ない。
　お互い忘れましょう、というアルクェイドの言葉は、つまるところそういう意味だったんだ。
「くそ……っ！」
　後悔で押しつぶされそうな心のまま、公園を後にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
Arcueid won’t come. I’m sure of it.
When she said we should both forget it ever happened, this was what she meant.
“Damn it…!”
Crushed beneath the weight of my regret, I left the park.
entries.mirrorMoon:
She probably won't come.
This is what she meant when she said for both of us to forget about it.
"Damn it……!"
My heart wrapped in regret, I leave the park.

entries.japanese:
……屋敷まで帰ってきた。
　裏口の門をあけて、屋敷の中へ入る。
entries.maoEnglish:
…I made it back to the mansion.
I opened the rear gate and went inside.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… I return to the mansion.
Opening the rear door, I walk inside.

entries.japanese:
「は――――あ」
　何も考えられず、ベッドに沈みこむ。
　チッ、チッ、チッ、と秒を刻む時計の音だけが部屋に響き渡る。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Haaah…”
Too numb to think, I sank onto the bed.
Tick. Tick. Tick. Nothing filled the room but the clock counting off the seconds.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I yawn.
I sink onto my bed without thinking.
Tick.
Tick.
Tick.
The sound of the clock echoes through the room.

entries.japanese:
「…………」
　……今は、眠ろう。
　朝がきて目が覚めれば、きっと何かが変わっている。
　アルクェイドの事も街を騒がしている吸血鬼の事も、朝になってくれれば、全部――――
entries.maoEnglish:
“……”
…I should sleep.
Once morning came and I woke up, something would surely have changed.
Arcueid, the vampire terrorizing the city—if only morning would come, then all of it would—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…………"
…… Just sleep for now.
When I wake up tomorrow things will be different.
About Arcueid, about the vampire roaming this city, when morning comes all of it will be----

entries.japanese:
ズキリ　　ズキリ　　ズキリ
　ドクン　　ドクン　　ドクン
　ずきり　　ずきり　　ずきり
　どくん　　どくん　　どくん
entries.maoEnglish:
THROB THROB THROB
THUMP THUMP THUMP
throb throb throb
thump thump thump
entries.mirrorMoon:
THROB           THROB           THROB
THUMP           THUMP           THUMP
Throb           Throb           Throb
Thump           Thump           Thump

entries.japanese:
……痛みと鼓動が交互に同期する。
　ずきり、と痛むたびに記憶が剥がれていく。
　どくん、と弾むたびに記憶が塗られていく。
　剥がれていく記憶は、おそらくは余分なものだろう。
　自分には必要のない記憶。
過去。
経験。
　そういったものが剥がれていく。
つまりは忘却だ。
entries.maoEnglish:
…Pain and heartbeat fell into an alternating rhythm.
With every throb, a memory peeled away.
With every pounding beat, another memory was painted over.
The memories being stripped away were probably only excess.
Memories I had no need of. A past. Experience.
They peeled away one after another. In other words, I forgot.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… The pain synchronizes with my pulse.
Every time I feel the throb of pain, my memories fade away.
Every time my heart thumps, memories are plastered on.
The fading away memories are probably extras.
Memories, the past, experiences I don't need.
All of it fades away.
In other words, oblivion.

entries.japanese:
「あ―――――」
　薄れていく記憶、剥がれていく過去を惜しいと感じて、手を伸ばした。
　だが何も掴めない。
　何故なら、俺は。
　その忘れていく記憶がどのような記憶なのかさえ、とっくに忘れてしまっていたからだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ah—”
I mourned the memories fading from me, the past being torn away, and reached for them.
But my hand closed on nothing.
Because I—
because by then, I had already forgotten what those vanishing memories had ever been.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah------"
As regret washes over me, as my memories thin, as my past fades away, I reach out with my hand.
But I can't grasp anything.
Because,
I've already forgot what kind of memories I've lost.

entries.japanese:
ズキリ、ずきり。
　繰り返される頭痛は気持ちが悪くて、ゆめのなかでさえ吐きそうだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
Throb, throb.
The relentless headache sickened me. Even in the dream, I felt ready to vomit.
entries.mirrorMoon:
THROB, throb.
The repeating headaches make me feel sick, and even in my dream, I feel like throwing up.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま、お目覚めですか？」
 ────声がする。
「お気をたしかに。
いま飲み物を持ってまいります」
 ────その後に、たたっ、と駆けていく足音が聞こえた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki, are you awake?”
────A voice.
“Please hold on. I’ll bring you something to drink at once.”
────Then came the quick patter of footsteps running away.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama, are you awake?"
----I hear a voice.
"Please hold on.
I will bring you something to drink."
----After that, the sound of running footsteps.

entries.japanese:
うっすらと目が覚めた。
　自分はベッドに横になっていて、窓からは淡い陽の光が差し込んできている。
「────朝、か」
　ゆっくりと体を起こして、体中が汗をかいている事に気がついた。
「なんだ……？
　なんか、悪い夢でも見てたのかな、俺」
　さっきまでの夢を思い出してみる。
entries.maoEnglish:
I drifted toward wakefulness.
I was lying in bed, pale sunlight spilling through the window.
“—Morning…?”
I slowly sat up and realized I was drenched in sweat.
“What was that…? Was I having a nightmare or something?”
I tried to remember the dream I had just left behind.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I slowly open my eyes.
I'm lying in bed with the radiant sunlight streaming through the window.
"----Morning?"
Slowing lifting myself up, I feel my own sweat drenching me.
"What……?
I must've had a nightmare or something."
I try to remember what I dreamt about.

entries.japanese:
そもそも夢なんていう、意識が覚醒したとたんに融けていく記憶は思い出せるものじゃない。
　ただ、なにか。
　漠然としたイメージで、何かを忘れてしまったような、そんな気がするだけだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
Dreams are memories that melt the instant consciousness returns. They aren’t meant to be recalled.
Only… something remains.
A vague impression that I have forgotten something. Nothing more.
entries.mirrorMoon:
It is the nature of dreams to fade upon awakening.
But, there's still something.
I feel like there's a vague image of something I've forgotten.

entries.japanese:
「ああ起きてるよ。
おはよう翡翠。」
「はい、おはようございます志貴さま」
　翡翠はいつも通り、無表情でベッドに近付いてくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Yeah, I’m awake. Morning, Hisui.”
“Good morning, Master Shiki.”
Hisui approached the bed with her usual unreadable expression.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama?
Have you woken yet?"
"I'm up.
Morning, Hisui."
"Yes, good morning, Shiki-sama."
Hisui approaches the bed, expressionless as always.

entries.japanese:
「お飲み物をお持ちいたしました。
ご気分がすぐれないようでしたらお飲みください」
　見れば、翡翠は銀のトレイを手に持って、飲み物を用意していた。
「いや、別に気分は悪くないからいらないよ。
ぐっすり寝たしね、頭もスッキリしてる」
「───ですが」
　翡翠はめずらしく言い返してきた。
「昨晩はひどくご体調を崩されているようでした」
　……やっぱり昨夜はうなされていたらしい。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I brought you something to drink. Please have it if you are feeling unwell.”
Only then did I notice the silver tray in Hisui’s hands, with a drink already prepared.
“No, I’m fine. I slept like a rock, and my head feels completely clear.”
“—But…”
In a rare display of persistence, Hisui contradicted me.
“You appeared to be seriously ill last night.”
…So I really had been having nightmares last night.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I have brought you something to drink.
If you are not feeling well, please drink."
Hisui carries a silver tray with a drink prepared on it.
"No, I don't feel bad or anything.
I slept deeply, so my head is clear too."
"---However,"
Hisui offers a rare reply.
"It appeared your condition was bad last night."
…… It seems I did have a nightmare last night.

entries.japanese:
「いや、別に体に異状はないから大丈夫だって。
でもまあ、心配してくれるぶんには嬉しいよ、翡翠」
「……はい、志貴さまがお元気でなによりです」
　翡翠はいつもどおり、ガラス細工のような瞳でこっちを見つめている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’m telling you, there’s nothing wrong with me. Still, I’m glad you care, Hisui.”
“…Yes. I am very glad to see you well, Master Shiki.”
As always, Hisui watched me through eyes like glasswork.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Nah, there's nothing wrong with me.
But I'm really grateful you're concerned, Hisui."
"…… Yes, I am glad you are well, Shiki-sama."
Hisui looks at me with her delicate, glass eyes.

entries.japanese:
……なんていうか、間が持たない。
「それじゃすぐに着替えてから食堂に行くからさ。
翡翠は琥珀さんに朝食を頼んでおいてくれ」
「はい、かしこまりました」
entries.maoEnglish:
…This was getting awkward.
“I’ll change and come straight down to the dining room. Could you ask Kohaku to get breakfast ready?”
“Certainly.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Um, I feel uneasy.
"I'll go change and head to the dining room.
Please tell Kohaku-san I'll be having breakfast."
"I understand."

entries.japanese:
……さて。
　時刻は朝の七時前。
　これなら今日はゆっくり朝を迎えられそうだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
…Well, then.
It wasn’t quite seven yet.
For once, I could take my time with the morning.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Well then.
It's seven o'clock.
I can take my time this morning.

entries.japanese:
居間には秋葉と翡翠がいた。
　キッチンのほうから琥珀さんの調子のずれた鼻歌が聞こえてきている。
entries.maoEnglish:
Akiha and Hisui were in the sitting room.
From the kitchen came Kohaku’s cheerfully off-key humming.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Akiha and Hisui are in the sitting room.
From the kitchen, I can hear Kohaku-san's lilting humming.

entries.japanese:
「おはようございます、兄さん」
「おはよ。
なんだ、今朝は元気がなさそうだな秋葉。
朝飯に嫌いなものでもでたのか？」
「……兄さん。
どこをどうしたら、そんな脈絡のない言葉が出るんですか」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Good morning, Brother.”
“Morning. You look a little down, Akiha. Did they serve something you hate for breakfast?”
“Brother… how exactly did you leap to something so completely unrelated?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Good morning, Nii-san."
"Morning.
You don't seem very cheerful today, Akiha.
Was there something you didn't like in your breakfast?"
"…… Nii-san, how did you arrive at that conclusion?"

entries.japanese:
「いや、なんとなく。
たしか秋葉は食べ物に関しちゃ好き嫌いが多かったなって思い出して」
「失礼ですねっ。
子供のころはそうでしたけど、今では好き嫌いなんてありません」
「……そっか。
おかしいな、それならもうちょっと、こう、歳相応に発育がいいはずなんだけど……」
entries.maoEnglish:
“No reason. I just remembered you used to be a really picky eater.”
“How rude! I may have been picky as a child, but I eat everything now.”
“…Really? That’s strange. You’d think you’d be a little more… developed for your age, then…”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Just came to my mind.
I just remembered there were many kinds of food you either liked or disliked."
"That's rude… I was that way as a child, but now I have no dislikes."
"…… I see.
That's odd, cause if that's the case, you should have more physical development for your age……"

entries.japanese:
「兄さん。
今、なにかおっしゃいましたか？」
　じろ、と秋葉は睨んでくる。
　……まずった。
なんだかガラにもなく口を滑らせてしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Brother. Did you just say something?”
Akiha fixed me with a glare.
…That was a mistake. I had let something slip that I normally had more sense than to say.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Nii-san.
Did you just say something?"
Akiha glares at me.
…… Crap.
I should watch my mouth.

entries.japanese:
「……いや、何も言ってない。
ちょっとした独り言だから気にしないでくれ」
「……もう。
どうやら心配する必要なんてなかったみたいね、翡翠。
兄さんは殺したって死にそうにないわ」
「はい、同感です」
　ため息をつく秋葉に、翡翠は無表情のまま同意した。
　話の流れから推測するに、秋葉と翡翠は俺の心配をしていたらしい。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…No. Nothing at all. Just talking to myself, so forget it.”
“…Honestly. It seems we had nothing to worry about after all, Hisui. I doubt Brother would die even if someone killed him.”
“I agree.”
Hisui agreed with the sighing Akiha, her face still expressionless.
Judging from the conversation, the two of them had been worried about me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… No, I didn't say anything.
I was just thinking aloud, so don't worry about it."
"…… Geez.
It seems there was no need to worry, Hisui.
I don't think Nii-san will die even if you kill him."
"Yes, I feel the same way."
Akiha sighs and Hisui expressionlessly agrees.
I can guess from their conversation they were both worried about me.

entries.japanese:
「────なんで？」
　はて、と首をかしげる。
「なんでもなにも、普通は心配します！
　昨日、夜に帰ってきたかと思えばそのまま眠ってしまって、ずっとうなされていたそうじゃないですか。
　起こしても目を覚まさないんですから、何か質の悪い病気なんじゃないかって思うでしょう？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“—Why?”
Puzzled, I tilted my head.
“What do you mean, why? Of course we were worried! You came home late last night, went straight to sleep, and then tossed and moaned until morning.
You wouldn’t wake up no matter what we did. Naturally, we thought you might have some dreadful illness.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Why?"
I wonder why.
"Why?
Normally, you would worry!
After you came home last night, you went straight to bed and had nightmares all night.
Even though we tried to wake you, you never woke up.
Doesn't that sound like you were sick?"

entries.japanese:
「へえ、そうだったのか。
───でも俺、別に風邪とかひいてないけど？」
「風邪のたぐいではなかったと思います。
志貴さまはいつも通り眠っていて、熱も呼吸も正常でした。
ただ、汗を多く分泌していたんです」
「……分泌って、その表現なんかヤだな」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Huh. I had no idea. But I don’t have a cold or anything.”
“I do not believe it was a cold. Master Shiki slept as you normally do, and both your temperature and breathing were normal. You were, however, secreting an unusual quantity of sweat.”
“‘Secreting’ makes it sound really disgusting.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Oh?
Really---But I didn't really catch a cold or anything."
"I do not think you had a cold.
Shiki-sama, you were sleeping as always, and your temperature and breathing were normal.
But you were secreting lots of sweat."
"…… Secreting?
I don't like that word choice."

entries.japanese:
「看病していたこっちはもっと厭だったんですから、少しは感謝してください。
それと、後で琥珀にも一言かけてあげてくださいね。
私一人ではどうにもならなかったでしょうから」
「私一人って……秋葉、俺のこと看ててくれたの？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Try being the one who had to nurse you. A little gratitude would be appropriate. And please remember to thank Kohaku later. I doubt I could have managed alone.”
“Alone…? Akiha, you stayed and looked after me?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"It was worse on me because I was tending you, so please be a little thankful.
And thank Kohaku as well.
I couldn't have done it by myself."
"Yourself…… Akiha, you were caring for me?"

entries.japanese:
「そ、そんなの当たり前でしょう。
私と兄さんは兄妹なんですから。
　それに看病といっても私は様子を見ていただけで、汗を拭いてあげたのは琥珀だけです」
　視線をそらして、秋葉はぶつぶつと独り言のように言った。
　普段は真っ正面から人を見て、はっきりと話をする気の強い秋葉とはとても思えない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“O-of course I did. We are brother and sister.
Besides, I hardly did anything. I merely watched over you. Kohaku was the one who wiped away your sweat.”
Akiha looked aside and muttered the words almost to herself.
It was nothing like the headstrong Akiha who always met a person’s eyes and spoke her mind.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"O-of course I was.
We are siblings.
I was only watching your condition; it was Kohaku who cleaned your sweat."
She looks away and mumbles like she was talking to herself.
This isn't like her as she normally looks at you directly and says things directly.

entries.japanese:
「そっか。
ありがとう秋葉。
心配かけさせてごめんな」
「お礼なんて結構ですっ。
私は当然の義務として看ていただけよ。
兄さん、そういう言葉は琥珀にかけてあげてください」
　秋葉はぷい、と顔を背けてそれきり俺のほうを見ようともしない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I see. Thanks, Akiha. And I’m sorry I worried you.”
“I don’t need your thanks! I only cared for you because it was my natural duty. Brother, save those words for Kohaku.”
Akiha turned sharply away and refused to look at me again.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Really.
Thanks Akiha.
Sorry to worry you."
"You don't have to thank me.
I was just doing my duty.
If you want to thank someone, thank Kohaku."
She looks away and doesn't even try to look at me anymore.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さーん、朝ごはんの支度ができましたよー」
　食堂から琥珀さんの声が聞こえてくる。
「ほら兄さん、早く朝食をお食べになってください」
「あいよ」
　てくてくと居間を横切って食堂に向かった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki, breakfast is ready!” Kohaku called from the dining room.
“There. Go and eat your breakfast, Brother.”
“Right you are.”
I ambled across the sitting room toward the dining room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-san, breakfast is ready," Kohaku-san's voice rings out from the kitchen.
"Nii-san, please hurry up and eat your breakfast."
"Gotcha."
I head to the dining room.

entries.japanese:
「それではいってらっしゃいませ、志貴さま」
「行ってきます。
今日は四時頃に帰ってくるよ」
　ふかぶかとおじぎをして送り出してくれる翡翠に手をふって、屋敷を後にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Have a pleasant day, Master Shiki.”
“I’m off. I should be home around four today.”
I waved to Hisui as she bowed deeply to see me off, then left the mansion.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Please be careful on your way, Shiki-sama."
"I'm off.
I'll be back around four o'clock today."
Raising a hand to the bowing Hisui, I leave the mansion.

entries.japanese:
朝の通学路を歩く。
　月曜日の朝。
理由もなく、学校に向かう足取りが軽い。
　ここ数日まともじゃない生活をしていた分、体がこういった何気ない日常のありがたみをかみ締めているのかもしれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
I walked the morning route to school.
Monday morning. For no particular reason, my steps felt light.
After several days of anything but a normal life, perhaps my body had finally learned to savor the blessing of an ordinary day.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I walk the morning path to school.
Monday morning.
For some reason, my feet feel really light today.
Maybe it's because these past few days were so out of the ordinary, my body welcomes such a normal day.

entries.japanese:
「…………あれ」
　ふと疑問に思った。
　普通じゃない生活っていうけど、それはどんな生活だったんだろう。
「………………」
　なにか大切なことがあったような気がする。
　だが、それが何であるか思い出す事はできなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“……Wait.”
A question occurred to me.
What had been so abnormal about the last few days?
“……”
I felt as though something important had happened.
But I could not remember what it was.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"………… Huh?"
That's strange.
I said 'out of the ordinary', but what kind of life was that?
"………………"
I feel like something very important happened.
But, I can't remember what it was.

entries.japanese:
「いょぉう遠野！」
　バン、と背中を叩いて挨拶をしてくる有彦。
「おはようさん。
今朝は珍しく早いんだな」
「ああ、ちょっとした気紛れってヤツ。
ま、たまにはまじめな学生のフリをするのも悪くないかな、と」
　あはは、と陽気に笑う有彦。
　その笑顔を見て、ここが自分の世界なんだな、と安心する自分がいた。
「………………」
「ん、どうした遠野。
いきなり難しい顔して。
家に忘れ物でもしたのか？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Heeey, Tohno!”
Arihiko greeted me with a smack between the shoulder blades.
“Morning. You’re here surprisingly early.”
“Yeah, just a whim. I figured it couldn’t hurt to impersonate a serious student once in a while.”
Arihiko laughed brightly.
Seeing that smile, I felt a strange reassurance: this was my world.
“……”
“Hm? What’s with the serious face, Tohno? Forget something at home?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yo, Tohno!"
Arihiko whacks me on the back in greeting.
"Mornin'.
You're pretty early today."
"Ah, just a whim of mine.
Well, it doesn't hurt to act like a good student every now and then."
Arihiko laughs brightly.
Seeing that smile assures me that this is my world.
"………………"
"Mmm, what is it, Tohno?
Making such a difficult expression...
Did you forget something at your house?"

entries.japanese:
ワスレモノデモ　シタノカ
　……その言葉が呪いのように頭のなかをかけまわる。
entries.maoEnglish:
DID YOU FORGET SOMETHING
…The words raced through my mind like a curse.
entries.mirrorMoon:
DID YOU FORGET SOMETHING?
…… Those words reverberate through my head like a curse.

entries.japanese:
だが、結局。
　忘れ物がなんであるのかは、思い出せなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
But in the end,
I could not remember what I had forgotten.
entries.mirrorMoon:
But, in the end,
I can't remember what it was I forgot.

entries.japanese:
「……いや、何も忘れてないよ。
そんな事より早く教室に行こう。
せっかく有彦が早起きしたっていうのに遅刻しちゃ大損だろ？」
「はは、そりゃごもっとも」
　そうして友人と校門をくぐり抜ける。
　それで、何かが決定的に終わった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…No, I didn’t forget anything. Come on, let’s get to class. After the miracle of you waking up early, being late would be a terrible waste.”
“Ha! Can’t argue with that.”
And so I passed through the school gates with my friend.
With that, something came to an irrevocable end.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Nah, I didn't forget anything.
Let's hurry on to the classroom.
After waking up this early, it'd be a waste if you were late, right?"
"Haha, you got a point."
I pass the school gate with my friend.
With that, something ends completely.

entries.japanese:
「―――――」
　背後に視線を感じて振り返る。
　振りかえった先には何もない。
　ただ、校庭の木の葉が散っているだけだ。
　遠野志貴は教室に向かっていく。
　今まで通り、平穏で幸福な毎日に戻るように。
entries.maoEnglish:
“—”
Feeling eyes upon my back, I turned.
There was no one behind me.
Only leaves scattering across the schoolyard.
Shiki Tohno went on toward his classroom,
as though returning to the peaceful, happy days he had always known.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------"
I feel someone staring at me and I turn around.
But there's no one there.
Just the scattering leaves in the courtyard.
Tohno Shiki heads to class.
As if returning to a peaceful, happy, and normal everyday life.

entries.japanese:
本日最後の授業になってしまいましたけど、はりきっていきましょう。
　ええ、なにぶん長ーいお話なので眠くなったりお腹減ったり指が痙攣したりしますが、体力とスケジュール等と折り合いをつけて頑張ってください。
　さて、放課後です。
　原因ははっきりしていますね？
　彼女を庇うのは癪にさわるんですけど、ここまできたのならもう、トコトンまで突っ走ってください、ええ！
entries.maoEnglish:
This is our final lesson for today, but let’s give it our best.
It is a very long story, so you may grow sleepy or hungry, and your fingers may even start cramping; pace yourself around your health and schedule, and keep going.
Now, we’re at the end of the school day.
You understand what went wrong, don’t you?
It pains me to defend that woman, but now that you’ve come this far, you may as well follow through to the bitter end!
entries.mirrorMoon:
This is the last lesson for the day, but let's all have high spirits.
Yes, since it is a long story, you might get sleepy, or hungry, or your fingers might get tired, but please plan accordingly so your schedule and energy levels allow you to keep on playing.
Now, it is after school.
The reason is obvious, right?
It irritates me to defend her, but if you've come this far, you have to keep going until the very end!

entries.japanese:
……なんて言いながら、こういった終幕も遠野くんにとっては幸せなのかもしれませんね。
　クリーム、というタイトル名が全てをあらわしていたかもしれません。
　なんて、わりとしんみりしてみたり。
　それでは本日の授業はここまで。
　二日目の授業で会いましょう！
entries.maoEnglish:
Even so, perhaps an ending like this is happiness for Tohno.
Maybe the title Cream told us everything from the start.
And now I’ve gone and made myself rather sentimental.
That concludes today’s lessons.
I’ll see you on day two!
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Saying that, maybe such an end is happiness for Tohno-kun though.
Maybe the title "Cream" defines everything.
It really does tug at the heart strings.
This concludes the day's lessons.
Let's meet again on the second day of lessons!

entries.japanese:
先輩は俺を抱えたまま、一直線に遠野の屋敷にやってきた。
　……なんのつもりか知らないけど、ちょっと、それは困る。
　俺の胸にはまだナイフが刺さったままっていう凄い状況で、間違いなく死にかけている。
　そんなところを秋葉に見せたら、心配させるどころの話じゃなくなるんだから―――――
entries.maoEnglish:
Ciel carries me straight to the Tohno mansion without once slowing down.
I don’t know what she intends, but this is a problem.
There is still a knife sticking out of my chest, and I am unquestionably dying.
If Akiha sees me like this, mere worry will be the least of it—
entries.mirrorMoon:
Still holding me, Senpai heads straight for my mansion.
…… I don't know what she's planning, but this can't be good.
With a knife still embedded in my chest, there's no mistake that my death is near.
If Akiha sees me like this, it won't just be a matter of her worrying------

entries.japanese:
「――――――」
　……くそ、声が出ない。
　やめてくれって言いたいんだけど、喉はかろうじて息をするのがやっとだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
Damn it—I can’t speak.
I want to tell her to stop, but my throat can barely manage the work of breathing.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------"
…… Damn it, I can't speak.
I want to tell her to cut it out, but I can only gasp for air.

entries.japanese:
「遠野くんは黙っていてください。
……大丈夫、遠野くんの妹さんなら、きっと遠野くんを助けることができるはずです」
「――――――」
　……助けるって、そりゃあ無理だよ先輩。
　胸をナイフで刺されて、もう体の自由もきかない。
　……そんな死にかけた人間を助けられるヤツなんて、どこにもいないんだから。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Please don’t try to speak, Tohno. It’s all right—your sister should be able to save you.”
“…”
There’s no way you can save me, Ciel.
There is a knife in my chest, and I can no longer move.
No one can save a man this close to death.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Please be quiet Tohno-kun.
…… It is okay, I am sure your sister can help."
"------"
…… Help?
That's impossible, Senpai.
I'm stabbed in the chest and I can't even move.
…… There isn't anyone who can help a person about to die like this.

entries.japanese:
「いいえ、できます。
そうでなければ理屈が合いません……！
　いいですか、遠野くんの妹さんが遠野くんを助けられないと、そもそも遠野くんは八年前に死んでいるはずなんです。
　だから―――きっと、今回もまだ間に合うはずなんです……！」
　……先輩の言葉は、遠野くんだらけでちょっとわかりづらいと、おもう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“No, she can. Otherwise none of this makes sense…! Listen, Tohno: if your sister couldn’t save you, you would have died eight years ago.
So this time too—we must still have time…!”
I think Ciel’s explanation is a little hard to follow with all those Tohnos in it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No, it's possible.
Otherwise it would not make any sense……!
Look, if your sister couldn't help you, you would have died eight years ago.
That's why----I know we can still make it……!"
…… Her words, they have so many "you's" in them, I can hardly understand.

entries.japanese:
「――――――」
　……先輩、それはどういう――――
「もう、いいから黙っていてくださいっ！
　これ以上喋ると、遠野くん本当に保たないじゃないですかっ！」
　今まで見たこともないほどの真剣な顔で怒られた。
　……なにか、とても悪い気がしたので目を閉じることにした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――――”
Ciel—what does that—
“Enough—please be quiet! If you keep trying to talk, you truly won’t survive!”
She scolds me with a severity I have never seen on her face before.
Somehow I feel terribly guilty, so I decide to close my eyes.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------"
…… Senpai, what do you----
"Geez, just please be quiet already!
If you speak anymore, we may not even be able to help you!"
She gives an unbelievably serious, angry face.
…… I feel terrible, so I close my eyes.

entries.japanese:
…………まあ、どのみち。
　……………………いいかげん。
　　　　　　　　　　　　起きているのが。
　　　　辛くはあった。
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　から
entries.maoEnglish:
—Well, anyway.
—By then.
                        Staying awake.
            Had become too hard.
                                      Because—
entries.mirrorMoon:
………… Well, anyways.
…………………… It's beginning.
to get hard.
staying up.
So

entries.japanese:
――――ずっと、家族とは他人なんだ。
　そんな言葉を、幼いころからもっていた。
　遠野の家から有間の家に預けられた時から。
　いや、正確にはもっと昔から、ずっと、家族とは他人だった。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――I have always been a stranger to my family.
I had carried those words since childhood.
Ever since I was sent from the Tohno family to the Arima family.
No—to be precise, I had been a stranger to my family for much longer than that.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----I was always an outsider to my family.
From an early age, I always thought that.
From the time I was adopted from the Tohno family by the Arima family.
No, actually, long before that, I was an outsider to my family.

entries.japanese:
どうしてなんだろう、なんて考えたこともない。
　気がつけば一人で。
まわりには両親らしき人たちがいたから、そこの子でいようと自分なりに頑張っただけ。
entries.maoEnglish:
I never wondered why.
Before I knew it, I was alone. There were people nearby who seemed to be my parents, so I simply did my best to act like their child.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I never even wondered why.
Before I realized it, I was alone.
There were people around me acting like my parents so I tried hard to act like their child.

entries.japanese:
古い座敷のある家が一番はじめの家だったと思う。
　そこから、何かの事故で大きな洋館に引き取られた。
　……そこには同い年ぐらいの兄妹がいて、自分とは、とても仲がよかったと、思う。
entries.maoEnglish:
I think my first home was an old house with a traditional tatami parlor.
After some kind of accident, I was taken in by a vast Western mansion.
There was a brother and sister there, both around my age, and I think we were very close.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I think the house with the old tatami room was my first house.
From there, after some incident, I was taken to a large western-style mansion.
…… There was a brother and a sister around my same age, and we became good friends, I think.

entries.japanese:
けれどその兄妹の父親とはずっと壁があったままだった。
　……それでもお互いが本当の家族になろうって、努力はしていた。
　血の繋がりなんかなくても、自分たちは親子なんだって信じようとしてはいたのに。
entries.maoEnglish:
But there was always a wall between me and their father.
Even so, we both tried to become a real family.
Though no blood bound us, we tried to believe we were father and son.
entries.mirrorMoon:
But there was always a wall between their father and me.
…… But still, we tried hard to be like a real family.
Even if we weren't related by blood, we tried to believe we were a family.

entries.japanese:
それも、あっけなく終わった。
　大きな事故があって、病院に運ばれて。
　誰も見舞いに来なくて、自分の目がおかしくなって。
　それまでも一人で、けっきょくは一人で。
　もう、そのまま消えてしまおうかと思っていた。
　あの、澄んだ青空みたいにキレイだった、魔法使いに出会うまでは。
entries.maoEnglish:
That ended almost before it began.
There was a terrible accident, and I was taken to the hospital.
No one came to visit, and something went wrong with my eyes.
I had been alone before, and in the end I was alone again.
I thought I might as well disappear.
Until I met the Magician, beautiful as a clear blue sky.
entries.mirrorMoon:
But, that ended abruptly.
After a large accident, I was taken to a hospital.
No one came to see me and my eyes became abnormal.
Until then I was alone, and in the end I was alone.
I thought maybe I should just disappear like that.
Until I met that sorceress who was as beautiful as the clear blue sky overhead.

entries.maoEnglish:
· · · · · · ·
· · · · · A familiar
dream.

entries.japanese:
「生き――――てる」
　ぼんやりと、そんな声が出た。
　体は相変わらず指一本だって動きそうにないけど、声だけはちゃんと出てくれる。
　意識もはっきりとしてきて、ここが自分の部屋だというコトも把握できていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’m—alive.”
The words leave me in a daze.
My body still refuses to move so much as a finger, but at least my voice works.
My thoughts are clearing too, enough for me to recognize my own room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I'm----alive?"
I speak aimlessly.
I don't seem to be able to lift a finger, but at least I can speak clearly.
My mind is clear enough to grasp that this is my own room.

entries.japanese:
「……兄さん？
　気がついたんですね？」
「あきは―――なんだ、そこにいたのか」
　秋葉は枕元に立って、看病をしてくれていたみたいだ。
「秋葉、おまえ―――」
　いまいち状況がわからず秋葉を見つめる。
　秋葉はどこか気まずそうに視線を逸らす。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Brother…? You’re awake?”
“Akiha—so you were here.”
She has been standing at my bedside, nursing me.
“Akiha, you…”
I stare at her, unable to make sense of the situation.
She looks away uneasily.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Nii-san?
Are you awake?"
"Akiha---you're there?"
Akiha is standing by the bedside, apparently having taken care of me.
"Akiha, you---"
I look at Akiha not knowing what happened.
She looks away uneasily.

entries.japanese:
「……その……この傷は、さ」
　あいつに―――シキにやられたんだ、とは言えない。
　そもそも、こんな傷を負った俺を、秋葉はどうして受け入れてくれたんだろう。
　胸にナイフが刺さったままだなんて、普通は病院送りにして家にはあげないと思うんだけど……
entries.maoEnglish:
“About this wound…”
I cannot tell her that he—SHIKI—did it to me.
For that matter, why did Akiha even let them bring me here in this condition?
A man with a knife still buried in his chest would normally be sent to a hospital, not invited inside the house—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… My…… this wound, is…"
I can't say he---SHIKI did it.
In the first place, how did she react when I arrived with this wound?
I would think usually, you'd send someone with a knife in their chest to the hospital……

entries.japanese:
「秋葉、えっと――――」
「……いいんです。
だいたいの事情はあの人に聞きましたから」
「……あの人って……先輩のこと？」
　こくん、と伏し目がちに秋葉は頷く。
「……………」
　……なんか、よけいに混乱してきた。
　だいたいの事情って、先輩は秋葉にどんな事情を説明したっていうんだろう……？
entries.maoEnglish:
“Akiha, I…”
“It’s all right. She told me most of what happened.”
“She—you mean Ciel?”
Akiha lowers her eyes and nods.
“…”
Now I am even more confused.
What exactly did Ciel tell her when she explained ‘most of what happened’?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Akiha, um----"
"…… It's okay.
I heard most of the circumstances from that person."
"…… That person…… you mean Senpai?"
Still looking down, Akiha nods.
"……………"
…… I'm more confused.
What exactly did Senpai tell Akiha by "most of the circumstances"……?

entries.japanese:
「……………む」
　こまった。
先輩が秋葉にどう言い含めたか解らない以上、下手なことは聞けないじゃないか。
「えっ……と、秋葉。
先輩は、どうしたの？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hmm…”
This is awkward. Until I know what story Ciel gave Akiha, I can’t risk asking the wrong question.
“Um—Akiha. Where is Ciel?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…………… Hmph."
This isn't good.
Not knowing what Senpai told her, I can't ask her something wrong.
"Um…… Akiha, where's Senpai?"

entries.japanese:
「あの人でしたら居間のほうでお休みいただいています。
……本来ならあのような人は屋敷には立ち入らせませんけれど、仮にも兄さんを助けてくれた方ですから。
無碍に扱うわけにはいきません」
―――キッ、と。
　秋葉の表情は段々と厳しいものになっていく。
entries.maoEnglish:
“She is resting in the sitting room. Ordinarily I would never permit someone like her to enter the mansion, but she did save you. I could hardly turn her away.”
―――A sharp glare.
Akiha’s expression hardens by degrees.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"If you mean that person, she is resting in the sitting room.
…… Normally I would not let such a person stay in the house, but she has helped you.
So I can't treat her poorly."
---As she speaks,
her expression turns more severe.

entries.japanese:
「兄さん。
その胸の傷は、シキに負わされたものですね」
　きっぱりと。
　秋葉は、その事実を尋ねてきた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Brother. SHIKI was the one who gave you that wound, wasn’t he?”
She states it flatly.
Akiha asks me to confirm the fact.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Nii-san.
The wound in your chest was caused by SHIKI, right?"
Directly,
Akiha cuts to the heart of the matter.

entries.japanese:
「あ、秋葉、おまえ―――」
「言ったでしょう。
あの人から大体の事情は聞いたんです。
……もっとも、聞かなくても兄さんの容体を見れば一目ですべて解りましたけれど」
「――――」
　喉が、動かない。
　秋葉は―――まるで、初めからシキのことを知っていたような口ぶりだ。
「秋葉、おまえ……シキのことを―――」
entries.maoEnglish:
“A-Akiha, you…”
“I told you. She explained most of it. Though one look at your condition would have told me everything even if she hadn’t.”
“…”
My throat locks.
Akiha speaks as though she has known about SHIKI from the beginning.
“Akiha—you knew about SHIKI—”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"A, Akiha, you---"
"Didn't I say so earlier?
I heard most of the circumstances from that person.
…… Although, I would have understood the situation if I looked at you."
"----"
My words… stick in my throat.
Akiha---sounds as if she knew about SHIKI from the beginning.
"Akiha, you…… about SHIKI---"

entries.japanese:
「……ええ、知っています。
私は初めからすべて承知した上で、兄さんを屋敷に呼び戻したんですから」
　くらん、とあたまをトンカチで叩かれたような眩暈が起きた。
「……ちょっ、ちょっと待ってくれ。
すべてを承知した上でって、どういうコトだよそれ。
俺はまだ……正直、ワケが解らないんだ。
　たしかに子供のころ俺と秋葉のほかにもう一人子供がいたっていうのは確かだ。
けど、それを聞いたらおまえは――――」
　三人目のこどもなんて、いないって言ったじゃないか。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Yes. I knew everything from the beginning when I called you back to the mansion.”
The room lurches as though someone has struck me over the head with a hammer.
“W-wait. What do you mean, you knew everything? I still don’t understand any of this.
I know there was another child besides you and me when we were little. But when I asked, you said…”
You said there had never been a third child.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Yes, I know.
From the very beginning, I was aware of everything and called you back to the mansion."
I suddenly get assailed by dizziness like I just got hit in the head with a hammer.
"…… W, wait a minute.
What do you mean you were aware of everything?
I don't…… honestly know what's going on.
Certainly, there was another kid with me and you back then, but when I asked you----"
You said there wasn't a third child.

entries.japanese:
「……ごめんなさい。
私、兄さんには嘘ばかりついていました。
……今回のことも……こうなることが解っていたのに、ずっと、嘘をついてごまかしていたんです」
「ごまかしてたって……じゃあやっぱり、三人目のこどもはいたんだな。
けどどうして、アイツはいきなりいなくなったりしたんだ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’m sorry. I’ve told you so many lies. Even this time, though I knew this would happen, I kept deceiving you and hiding the truth.”
“Then there really was a third child. But why did he suddenly disappear?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I'm sorry.
All I have ever done is lie to you.
…… Even about this…… I knew it would turn out like this, but I lied to you all this time and deceived you."
"Deceived?
…… Then, there was the third kid?
But, why did he disappear suddenly?"

entries.japanese:
……そう、本当に記憶にない。
　三人目の子供……自分と同い年ぐらいの少年がいて、いつも二人で遊びまわっていた事は覚えている。
　俺たちは、そうして時おり父親の目を盗んで外に出てきた秋葉と遊んだんだ。
　けど、どうしても記憶にない。
　アイツがいなくなった理由とか。
　アイツの名前が、俺と同じシキだったという事とか。
　そう、何もかも―――綺麗さっぱり忘れてしまっている。
entries.maoEnglish:
I truly don’t remember.
I remember that there was a third child—a boy around my age—and that the two of us were always running around together.
Sometimes Akiha would slip away from her father, and the three of us would play.
But no matter how I try, I can’t remember.
Why he disappeared.
Or that his name, like mine, was SHIKI.
All of it has been wiped perfectly clean from my mind.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Yeah, I really can't remember.
The third kid…… I remember always playing with another boy my age.
Akiha sometimes would sneak away when her father wasn't looking and come play with us.
But, how come I don't remember?
Things like why he disappeared.
Or like how his name SHIKI was the same as mine.
Yeah, everything---I have clearly forgotten.

entries.japanese:
「……わからない。
覚えていることって言えば、それは――――」
　あの中庭で見た光景。
　この屋敷に帰ってきてから、何かの白昼夢のように脳裏に浮かんだ、あの暑い夏の日の光景だけ。
　あきはがいて、自分がいて。
　目の前には、血にまみれたもう一人の少年の死体があって。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I don’t know. The only thing I can remember is…”
That scene in the courtyard.
Since returning to the mansion, it has surfaced in my mind like a waking dream: a scene from a blistering summer day.
Akiha was there, and I was there.
Before us lay the blood-soaked corpse of another boy.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I don't know.
The only thing I remember is that----"
The scene I saw in the courtyard.
Since I came back, it's only that hot summer day which floats in the back of my mind like a daydream.
Akiha's there, I'm there.
And before me is the bloody corpse of another boy.

entries.japanese:
「――――――あ」
　そう、確かにシキは言っていた。
　“おまえに殺された借り、たしかに返したぞ”、と。
　それは、つまり――――
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ah.”
Yes.
SHIKI had said it clearly: “The debt I owed you for killing me has now been repaid.”
Which meant—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------Ah."
Yes, SHIKI did say so.
"I paid you back for killing me," he said.
So, that means----

entries.japanese:
「あの夢は―――俺は、本当に、あいつを――」
　殺してしまったのか。
　だからアイツはいきなりいなくなって、俺は自分にとって都合の悪い思い出を忘れていたっていうのか。
entries.maoEnglish:
“That dream—had I really killed him—”
Had I killed him?
Was that why he vanished so suddenly, and why I had forgotten a memory merely because it was inconvenient?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"That dream----I, really--"
killed him?
Is that why he suddenly disappeared and I conveniently forgot all those bad memories?

entries.japanese:
「秋葉、俺は――――」
「いいえ、違います。
兄さんは誰も殺してなんかいません。
そう思い込むように遠野槙久……わたしたちのお父様に言いつけられたんです」
「親父……に？」
　……そんなの、よけいにワケがわからない。
　どうして親父が、俺にそんな事を言いつけるっていうんだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Akiha, did I…?”
“No. You didn’t kill anyone. Makihisa Tohno—our father—ordered you to believe that you had.”
“Father did?”
That makes even less sense.
Why would he ever order me to believe such a thing?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Akiha, I----"
"No, you're mistaken.
You did not kill anyone.
Tohno Makihisa…… our father commanded you to think that way."
"My…… old man did?"
…… I don't understand even more.
Why would my old man command me to do something like that?

entries.japanese:
「……秋葉。
おまえ、すべてを了承したままで俺を呼んだって言ったな。
　それ、どういう事だ。
おまえは―――おまえは八年前のことも、あのシキのことも、全部知っているっていうことなのか」
「……はい。
シキの事は、兄さんには思い出してほしくなかった。
出来ることなら、ずっと忘れたままでいてほしかった。
　……けど、それもおしまいですね。
　初めから―――隠し通すことなんて無理な話だったんです」
　そう言って、どこか自嘲ぎみに笑って。
　秋葉はまっすぐに俺の目を見て話を始めた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Akiha. You said you knew everything when you called me back.
What did you mean? Do you know everything about what happened eight years ago—and about SHIKI?”
“Yes. I never wanted you to remember SHIKI. If possible, I wanted you to forget him forever.
But that is over now.
It was impossible to hide the truth from the very beginning.”
She gives a faint, self-mocking smile.
Then Akiha meets my eyes and begins to speak.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Akiha.
You said you were aware of everything when you called me back.
What do you mean?
You----you know about eight years ago, about SHIKI, about everything?"
"…… Yes.
I didn't want you to remember about SHIKI, Nii-san.
If possible, I wanted you to forget about it forever.
…… But it's all over.
From the beginning----it was impossible to hide it."
Saying that, she gives a self-derisive smile.
She looks at me in the eye and starts speaking again.

entries.japanese:
「……兄さん。
遠野の家が特別な血族だという事はあの人に聞いたでしょう？
　信じられないでしょうけど、遠野の血は人間以外の血が混ざっているんです。
……少なくとも、私は幼い頃から父にそう教えられて育ってきました。
　もちろん、それをまっとうに信じてきたわけではありません。
けど、信じざるをえない出来事が起きてしまった。
　……それが八年前の、兄さんがシキに殺された事故なんです」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Brother. She told you the Tohno family possesses a special bloodline, didn’t she? It may be difficult to believe, but something inhuman is mingled with Tohno blood. At least, that is what Father taught me from childhood.
I never truly believed him. Then something happened that gave me no choice.
It was the incident eight years ago—when SHIKI killed you.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Nii-san.
That person told you about the Tohno blood being special, right?
You may not believe it, but there is non-human blood in the Tohno ancestry.
…… At least that is what Father has told me since I was young.
Of course, I did not believe it at first.
But, something happened to make me believe it.
…… That incident was when you were killed by SHIKI eight years ago."

entries.japanese:
「……殺されたって……俺が、シキに……？」
　秋葉は無言で頷く。
　……けど、それはおかしい。
　それでは逆だ。
　血まみれで倒れていたのはシキのほうだし……あいつはたしかに、『おまえに殺された借りを返した』と言ったじゃないか……！？
entries.maoEnglish:
“Killed—SHIKI killed me?”
Akiha nods without a word.
But that is backward.
SHIKI was the one lying there covered in blood.
And he plainly told me he had repaid me for killing him—didn’t he?!
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Killed?
…… me, by SHIKI……?"
Akiha nods wordlessly.
…… But, that's strange.
That's the exact opposite.
SHIKI was the one lying bloody on the ground…… and didn't he say "I paid you back for killing me"……!?

entries.japanese:
「……遠野の人間は、個人差はあれど歳をとるごとに自分の中の“異なる血”が増えていきます。
　この血は、あまりいいものではないんです。
　遠野の血筋に混ざっている異種は、ただのケモノなのかもしれないと思うほど、自己の本能を肥大化させてしまう。
　人間らしい部分を理性とするのなら、ケモノじみた部分である本能が理性を駆逐してしまうんです」
entries.maoEnglish:
“As members of the Tohno family age, the ‘other blood’ within them grows stronger, though the degree varies from person to person.
It is not a benevolent blood.
The inhuman strain mixed into the Tohno line magnifies instinct until one could almost believe it came from beasts.
If reason is the human part of us, then those bestial instincts eventually devour it.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… As the people in the Tohno family grow older, the "inhuman blood" in us increases.
This blood isn't anything good.
I think the type of blood mixed with the Tohno family greatly increases one's instincts and makes me think it's just the blood of a beast.

If you call the human part reason, the instincts of the non-human blood overpower reason."

entries.japanese:
「……………秋葉、それは」
「……わかってます。
にわかには信じられない話でしょうから、今は黙って聞いてください」
―――いや。
　それと同じようなヤツを、俺はよく知っているんだ。
　今だって、シキになんか出会わずに、この体さえ確かに動くのなら、あいつを探しに飛び出しているハズなんだから。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Akiha—that’s…”
“I know. It is difficult to believe without warning, so please listen quietly for now.”
―――No.
I know someone very much like that.
Even now, if I had never met SHIKI and my body could move, I would already be outside searching for her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…………… Akiha, that's……"
"…… I know.
I know you can't believe it because it's so sudden, so please be quiet for now."
----No,
I know someone exactly like that.
Even now, if I could move freely and avoid SHIKI, I'd fly out of here and look for her.

entries.japanese:
「けれど、遠野の血筋の者たちがヒトとして終わってしまうのは年老いてからなんです。
　……私の兄のように……シキのように子供のころに“反転”してしまう例なんて、今までなかった。
　遠野の人間がそれぞれどんな異種の血を混濁させているかは個人差があるそうです。
　外見がまったく変わらないモノもいれば、本当に体の形が変わってしまうモノもいる。
　―――シキは、典型的な後者でした」
entries.maoEnglish:
“But members of the Tohno line ordinarily do not cease to be human until old age.
There had never been a case of someone undergoing ‘Inversion’ in childhood—not until my brother, SHIKI.
The inhuman blood mingled into each Tohno differs from one person to another.
Some retain a perfectly human appearance, while others physically change shape.
―――SHIKI was a classic example of the latter.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"However, the end comes for members of the Tohno family as they grow older.
…… There has not been an instance of 'inversion' as a child like SHIKI did.
The blood in the Tohno family varies from individual to individual.
There are those whose appearance will not change and those whose appearance will.
----SHIKI was a typical case of the latter."

entries.japanese:
「後者って……体の形が変わるっていうこと……？」
「……はい。
シキがどうして、あんな幼いころに狂ってしまったかは解りません。
　ただ、何の前触れもなく反転してしまった。
その時、シキが襲いかかったのが兄さん……貴方なんです」
「シキが……俺に、襲いかかった……？」
　ズキリ、と。
　胸の古傷がうずいた気がした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“The latter—you mean his body actually changed?”
“Yes. I don’t know why SHIKI lost himself at such an early age.
His Inversion came without warning. And the person he attacked was you, Brother.”
“SHIKI—attacked me?”
A stab of pain.
The old scar in my chest seems to ache.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"The latter…… his appearance changed……?"
"…… Yes.
I do not understand why he went crazy at such a young age.
But he inverted without any warning.
When that happened, he attacked you, Nii-san."
"SHIKI…… attacked me……?"
Throb.
The old wound on my chest aches.

entries.japanese:
「その時の場所があの中庭なんです。
兄さんはシキに胸を貫かれて、もう瀕死の状態でした。
そこに父が駆けつけて、シキを止めたんです。
　……理性を失っていたシキを止めるには、息の根を止めるしかない。
　遠野家の当主には、そうやって反転してしまった一族の者を処理する義務があるんです。
　ですから―――兄さんが見た血まみれのシキというのは、父に処理されたあとのシキではないでしょうか」
entries.maoEnglish:
“It happened in that courtyard. SHIKI pierced your chest and left you dying. Then Father arrived and stopped him.
There was only one way to stop SHIKI after he lost his reason: kill him.
The head of the Tohno family has a duty to dispose of any relative who undergoes Inversion.
So might the blood-soaked SHIKI you remember have been SHIKI after Father dealt with him?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"It happened in that courtyard.
You were stabbed in the chest and were on the verge of death when Father came and stopped SHIKI.
…… To stop SHIKI who has lost his mind, you can only kill him.
It is the duty of the head of the Tohno household to deal with members of the family who have inverted.
So----the bloody SHIKI you saw was probably the result of Father dealing with him."

entries.japanese:
「―――――――」
　よく、思い出せない。
　その時、もっと何か。
とても大切なコトがあった気がするのだけど、思い出せない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
I cannot remember clearly.
Something else happened then. I feel it was terribly important, but I cannot remember.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"--------"
I can't remember.

There was something else.
I feel like there was something more important that I can't remember.

entries.japanese:
「……そのあと、兄さんは奇跡的に一命を取り留めました。
あとは兄さんの記憶にあるとおり、遠野志貴は事故に巻き込まれた、という偽証をして病院に運ばれたんです」
「――――」
「……私が次女でありながら当主として育てられたのもそれが原因でした。
　一度でも“反転”した者を当主として迎えるわけにはいきませんから、シキは後継ぎではなくなって、唯一血を継いでいる私が後継ぎになったんです」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Afterward, you survived by a miracle. As you remember, they fabricated the story that Shiki Tohno had been caught in an accident and took you to the hospital.”
“…”
“That was also why I was raised to head the family despite being the younger daughter.
Someone who had undergone Inversion could never be accepted as head, so SHIKI lost his place as heir and I, the only remaining child of the bloodline, inherited it.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Afterwards, you miraculously recovered.
And as you remember, you were taken to the hospital and told you were in a big accident."

"----"
"…… For that reason, I was then raised to be successor of the Tohno family even though I was the second child.
Once "inverted", SHIKI could no longer be the successor, so the only other remaining blood relative had to be chosen."

entries.japanese:
……そうか。
　そういった経緯で秋葉が当主なんていう大きな責任を背負わされたのか……って、アレ？
entries.maoEnglish:
I see.
So that was how Akiha came to shoulder the immense responsibility of heading the family—but wait, what?
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… I see.
That's why Akiha had to take such a heavy burden of becoming the successor…… huh?

entries.japanese:
「秋葉。
それ、おかしい。
だってさ、その、反転しちまったっていうのはシキのほうだろ。
　俺は―――その、まともじゃないのか」
「……驚いた。
兄さん、こんな話を信じてくれるんですか……？」
「―――あのな。
おまえがこんな嘘をつくわけがないし、その……まあ、こういう話には慣れてるんだ。
　っと、そんなコトより！
　その話はおかしいんじゃないかって聞いてるんだけど、秋葉」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Akiha. That doesn’t make sense. SHIKI was the one who underwent Inversion, wasn’t he?
Then does that mean I’m—not normal?”
“I’m surprised. You believe all this, Brother?”
“Listen. You would never invent a lie like this, and besides, I’ve had some experience with stories like these.
But never mind that! I’m asking why your explanation doesn’t add up, Akiha.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Akiha.
That's… weird.
You said it was SHIKI that inverted, right?
Then I'm----not normal?"
"…… I'm surprised.
Nii-san, you believe all of this……?"
"----Hey now.
It's not like you'd lie like this…… Well, I'm used to this kind of talk.
M, more importantly!
I'm asking you if this is a bit strange, Akiha."

entries.japanese:
「そうでしたね。
……でも兄さん、この話はおかしくないんです。
おかしくありませんから、これ以上の事情は、聞かないわけにはいきませんか……？」
「―――ダメだ、秋葉。
　悪いけど、シキの話は俺にとって大事なものなんだ。
あいつは俺にとっても、アイツにとっても共通の敵だ。
無視することはできない。
　だから―――正体を知っておかないと。
そのためには疑問点なんて残しておけないんだ。
　どうして親父に殺されたハズのあいつが生きているのか、どうして―――俺が、そんな大事なことを忘れていたのか。
　頼む。
教えてくれ、秋葉」
entries.maoEnglish:
“You’re right. But, Brother, there is no contradiction. Couldn’t you simply leave the rest unasked?”
“No, Akiha.
I’m sorry, but SHIKI matters too much. He is an enemy to both me and her. I can’t ignore him.
I need to know what he is. To do that, I can’t leave any questions unanswered.
Why is he alive if Father killed him, and why did I forget something so important?
Please. Tell me, Akiha.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I suppose you are right.
…… But Nii-san, there's nothing wrong with the story, so can we not discuss it any further……?"
"----No, Akiha.
Sorry, but finding out about SHIKI is important to me.
He is both my and her mutual enemy, I can't just ignore him.
So----I have to know the truth.
I can't have any traces of doubt left.
Why he is alive if the old man killed him, why----I forgot something so important.
Please.
Tell me, Akiha."

entries.japanese:
「……簡単です。
兄さんには、どうしても遠野家を継げない訳があった。
　本当にそんな事さえ忘れていてくれたんですね、兄さんは。
……その蜃気楼が、ずっと続いていてくれたら良かったのに」
「……秋葉……？」
「………兄さんは、遠野家の人間ではないんです。
ただ父の気まぐれで、私の兄であるシキと同じ志貴という名前だったというコトだけで養子にとられた子供だったんです」
entries.maoEnglish:
“It’s simple. There was a reason you could never inherit the Tohno family.
You truly forgot even that, Brother.
I wish that mirage could have lasted forever.”
“Akiha…?”
“Brother—you are not a member of the Tohno family. Father adopted you on a whim merely because you happened to share the name Shiki with my brother SHIKI.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… It is simple.
You had a reason you could not succeed the Tohno family.
You really even forgot that, didn't you Nii-san?
…… I wish that illusion continued forever."

"…… Akiha……?"
"………… Nii-san, you are not part of the Tohno family.
Because of a whim of Father's, he adopted you just because you had the same name of his son, SHIKI."

entries.japanese:
「……兄さんと私、それにシキ。
私たちは本当の兄妹として育てられました。
　兄さんとシキはとても仲がよくて、わたしも幼心に嫉妬するぐらい、仲が良かった。
　けど、シキがあんなコトになってしまった時に全てが狂ったんです。
　シキは内々に処理したけれど、遠野家の長男を殺してしまうわけにはいかない。
　遠野家は社会的にも地位のある家柄でしょう？
　だから……簡単に後継ぎである長男が居なくなりました、なんて事は周りに報せられなかった」
entries.maoEnglish:
“You and SHIKI and I. We were raised as true siblings.
You and SHIKI were so close that even as a little girl, I was jealous.
But when that happened to SHIKI, everything went wrong.
He was dealt with in secret, but the eldest son of the Tohno family could not simply be allowed to die.
The Tohnos hold considerable social standing. They could hardly announce that their eldest son and heir had suddenly vanished.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… You and I, and SHIKI.
We were raised as true siblings.
You were really good friends with SHIKI, almost enough to make my childish heart feel jealous.
But, after what happened to SHIKI, everything went wrong.
SHIKI was taken care of secretly, but the eldest son of the Tohno household could not be killed.
The Tohno family has important standing in society, doesn't it?
So…… they could not tell society that the heir to the family suddenly just disappeared."

entries.japanese:
「そこで父は思いついたんです。
　シキに殺されかけた兄さんを本当の遠野志貴として扱い、反転して人間でなくなってしまったシキを事故で死亡してしまった養子として扱えばいい、と。
―――つまり、兄さんはシキと入れ替わったんです。
　殺された側が生き残って、殺した側が死んでしまった。
それが兄さんとシキの関係なんです」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Then Father had an idea.
He could pass you, whom SHIKI had nearly killed, off as the real Shiki Tohno—and declare that SHIKI, who had undergone Inversion and ceased to be human, was the adopted child killed in an accident.
―――In other words, he switched the two of you.
The victim survived, and the killer died. That is the relationship between you and SHIKI.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
