entries.mirrorMoon:
"What's going on, Tohno?
I never heard you were skipping class.
It's a lot of trouble.
You have to tell me when you skip school and go play!"
Arihiko says those preposterous words with an unbelievably happy expression.

"…… Why should I have to tell you when I don't go to school?"
"Isn't it obvious?
When you don't show, neither does Senpai, so it's bad unless I think of something ahead of time."
…… What's bad for this guy?

entries.japanese:
「しっかしさ、ホントに土曜はどうしたんだよ。
おまえは中学からこっち、貧血持ちのくせに学校だけは休まなかったじゃないか。
　まあ、そりゃあ登校した瞬間に帰るっていう離れ技は何度かあったけどな」
「それと似たようなものだよ。
交差点あたりまでは登校したんだけ、そこで気分が悪くなって帰ったんだ」
「ふーん。
弓塚といいおまえといい、最近素行が悪いんじゃないか？」
「――まあ、素行が悪いっていうのは否定しないけど……弓塚さん、どうかしたの？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Seriously, what happened Saturday? You’ve been anemic since middle school, but you never missed class.
Sure, you’ve pulled that trick where you arrive and immediately go home a few times.”
“This was nearly the same. I made it as far as the intersection, started feeling sick, and turned back.”
“Huh. First Yumizuka, now you—both of you have been acting up lately.”
“――Well, I won’t deny I’ve been acting up, but did something happen to Yumizuka?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"But seriously--What happened?
Since middle school, you've had anemia, but never skipped school.
Well, you did a cool trick several times, leaving as soon as you arrived."
"It's kind of like that.
I made it to the intersection and felt bad, so I went back home."
"Hmmm… Both you and Yumizuka seem to be acting like bad students lately."
"--Well, I'm guilty as charged, but …… is something wrong with Yumizuka-san?"

entries.japanese:
「うん？
　ああ、ここんとこずっと欠席。
あいつもずっと優等生してたからさ、いいかげんテンパッてたんじゃないか？
　だけどフリテンだから上がれないんだぜ、きっと」
「……………」
　有彦の例え話は、なんというか独特だ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hm? Oh, she’s been absent for days. Maybe the model-student act finally left her one tile from winning. Bet she’d already thrown away her winning tile, though, so she couldn’t go out.”
“…”
Arihiko’s analogies are uniquely his own.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Her?
She's been absent lately.
She was always such an honor student, so I think she might have been stressed out.
But I bet she can't call a raise 'cause she has a bad hand."
"……………"
Arihiko's words are always… very unique.

entries.japanese:
―――そうこう話しているうちに、ホームルーム開始を告げるチャイムが鳴り出した。
「おっと、んじゃオレはこれで。
土曜日さぼった分、まじめに勉学に励むんだぞ」
　有彦はいそいそと自分の机へと戻っていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――While we are talking, the bell sounds for homeroom.
“Oops, I’d better get back. Study hard enough to make up for skipping Saturday.”
Arihiko scurries back to his desk.
entries.mirrorMoon:
--While we are talking, the homeroom chime rings.
"Well, I'm off.
Since you skipped Saturday, make sure you study hard today."
Arihiko goes back to his seat.

entries.japanese:
四時限目が終わって、教室はにわかにざわめきだす。
　食堂に走りだすヤツ、教室で机をくっつけて弁当を広げる女生徒たち、ついでにいうとサンドウィッチを手にしてやってくる乾有彦。
「おう遠野、メシにしようぜメシ」
「―――」
entries.maoEnglish:
Fourth period ends, and the room suddenly erupts into activity.
Some students sprint for the cafeteria, girls push desks together and open lunch boxes—and, for good measure, Arihiko Inui approaches with a sandwich in hand.
“Hey, Tohno, let’s eat.”
“―――”
entries.mirrorMoon:
Fourth period ends and the class erupts into pandemonium all over again.
The guys dash off to the cafeteria, the girls eat their lunches at their desks, and Inui Arihiko's carrying a sandwich and coming over to me.
"Yo Tohno!
Lunch, lunch."
"---"

entries.japanese:
……さて、どうしよう。
　食欲は朝からまったくない。
とりわけ空腹を感じているわけでもないから、無理をして昼食をとる必要はないかもしれない。
　……食べたら食べたで、また吐き出したりしたら面倒だし、ここは―――。
entries.maoEnglish:
What should I do?
I have had no appetite since morning. I do not feel especially hungry, so perhaps there is no need to force down lunch.
If I eat only to vomit again, that will be a nuisance; in that case―――.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… What should I do?
Since morning, I haven't really had an appetite.
I don't feel hungry, so maybe I don't have to force myself to eat.
…… If I eat, I might throw it up again and cause trouble.
I should---.

entries.japanese:
―――それでも多少は栄養をとっておかないとまずい、か。
　ただでさえ眩暈を起こしやすい体質なんだから、無理やりにでも食べ物を口にしておかないと倒れてしまう。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Still, going without any nourishment at all would be a bad idea.
I was prone to dizzy spells even at the best of times; if I did not force myself to eat something, I might collapse.
entries.mirrorMoon:
--Even still, I need to get at least some nutrition.
I'm already prone to passing out as it is; and if I don't push myself to eat, I'll probably just pass out.

entries.japanese:
「わるい、先に食べててくれ。
購買にいってパン買ってくるから」
「そなの？
　んじゃまあ、遠慮なく先に食ってるぜ」
　嬉々としてサンドウィッチの封を開ける有彦を残して、教室を後にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Sorry, go ahead without me. I’m going to buy some bread.”
“Yeah? All right, don’t mind if I do.”
I left the classroom while Arihiko cheerfully tore open his sandwich wrapper.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Sorry, go ahead and eat.
I gotta go buy food."
"Oh yeah?
Guess I'll start eating without you."
I leave Arihiko happily unsealing his sandwich behind me as I exit the classroom.

entries.japanese:
適当なパンと牛乳を買って戻ってくる。
　窓際の自分の席には、有彦とシエル先輩の姿があった。
「あ、遠野くん。
どうも、お邪魔してますね」
「あー、いいっていいって、そんなに気を使わなくっても。
オレたちは先輩が来てくれるだけで嬉しいんだからさ。
な、そうだろ遠野？」
　先輩がいるだけで上機嫌なのか、有彦は楽しそうに同意を求めてくる。
　まあ、その意見には珍しく賛成だ。
entries.maoEnglish:
I bought some bread and milk and returned.
At my window-side desk, I found Arihiko and Ciel.
“Oh, Tohno. Sorry to intrude.”
“Hey, don’t worry about it. We’re happy just to have you here. Right, Tohno?”
Ciel’s mere presence seemed to have put Arihiko in high spirits; he turned to me with a grin, seeking agreement.
For once, I happened to share his opinion.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I buy some bread and some milk, and then go back.
Arihiko and Ciel-senpai are already over at my desk by the window.
"Oh, Tohno-kun.
I'm joining you guys."
"Ah, no, no.
You don't have to mind much.
We're pretty happy when you can join us.
Isn't that right, Tohno?"
Is Arihiko that pleased just to be with Senpai?
He happily asks me for agreement.
Well, for once we do seem to be in agreement.

entries.japanese:
「そうだね、先輩が来てくれると助かる。
なにしろコイツと顔をつきあわせて食事をするのは何かとよろしくない」
　軽く返答をして椅子に座る。
　先輩は大きめのお弁当を、有彦はとっくにサンドウィッチを食べ終わっていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“It does help having you here. Sitting face-to-face with this specimen over lunch is never good for me.”
I answered lightly and sat down.
Ciel had a generously sized lunch box open before her; Arihiko had already polished off his sandwich.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"That's right.
You really helped me out by coming, Senpai.
I don't know what I would've done if I had to eat while staring at this guy's face."
I answer lightheartedly and take my seat.
Senpai's eating from a large lunchbox and Arihiko is long since finished with his sandwich.

entries.japanese:
「………さて」
　いただきます、と手を合わせてパンをかじる。
　食欲がないながらも、とりあえず無理やり牛乳で胃に流し込んだ。
　昼食を終えている先輩と有彦は、なにか物騒な話で盛り上がっている。
　さっきから殺人だの猟奇だの通り魔だの、人が無理して食事を摂っているのもお構いなしだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Well, then.”
I put my hands together over the food and bit into the bread.
I had no appetite, but managed to wash it down with milk by sheer force.
Ciel and Arihiko, both finished with lunch, were absorbed in some gruesome topic.
Murder, mutilation, random attacks—they had been tossing around such words without the least concern for someone struggling to keep his food down.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……… Alright."
I take a bite from my bread.
I still have no appetite, so I forcefully wash it down with some milk.
Arihiko holds a lively conversation with Senpai since they are both done with lunch.
They talk about the strange events like serial murders and whatnot, which really does not help my appetite.

entries.japanese:
「へえ、まだ行方不明者って見つかってなかったんだ」
「そうみたいですねー。
それどころか今朝も新しい届け出があったみたいです。
乾くん、朝のニュースみました？」
「いんや、朝は活動時間じゃないんでテレビは見てないっす」
「ダメですよー、夜更かしばっかりしちゃ。
あんまり夜出歩いてると恐い人にさらわれちゃうんですから」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Huh, so they still haven’t found the missing people?”
“Apparently not. In fact, I heard another report was filed this morning. Did you see the morning news, Inui?”
“Nope; mornings aren’t part of my active hours, so I don’t watch television then.”
“You shouldn’t stay up so late. If you keep wandering around at night, some frightening person might carry you away.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Really?
They haven't found all those missing people yet?"
"It seems that way.
There was even another new report this morning.
Inui-kun, didn't you see the news this morning?"
"Nah, I don't have time to do anything in the morning so I didn't watch it."
"That's no good you know, staying up late at night.
You shouldn't walk around at night, there's some scary people out there."

entries.japanese:
「ああ、その点は問題ないね。
オレ本人が恐い人だったりするから」
「そっか、言われてみればそうですね。
乾くん、なんだか怪しいブローカーみたいですから」
　あはは、と二人は笑いあっている。
　……その、シエル先輩は本気でそう思ってるんだろうが、有彦のほうは冗談のつもりだったんだろう。
　ははは、と笑う有彦の目はちょっと引きつっていたりする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“No problem there. I happen to be a frightening person myself.”
“I see. Now that you mention it, Inui, you do look rather like a disreputable broker.”
The two laughed together.
Ciel probably meant it, though Arihiko had intended the whole thing as a joke.
His laughter continued, but the corners of his eyes had begun to twitch.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"That's no problem.
I'm a scary person myself."
"Well, you might be right.
Inui-kun, you do seem like a shady character."
"Ahahaha." The two of them laugh.
…… Hm, Ciel-senpai might be serious, but Arihiko probably said that as a joke.
"Hahaha." Arihiko's eyes twitch as he smiles.

entries.japanese: それはともかく、今の話は無視できるものではなかった。
entries.maoEnglish: In any case, I could not ignore what they had just said.
entries.mirrorMoon: Anyway, I can't exactly ignore their conversation.

entries.japanese:
「───先輩。
その、今朝の新しい届け出って、どんなものなんですか……？」
「今朝のニュースだと、昨日の夜に買い物にでかけた女性―――といってもわたしたちと同い年の人なんですけど、その人が行方不明になっているそうなんです。
お家は公園の近くらしいんですけど」
「……そう。
公園の近く、か」
　口にして、胃の中のものを戻しそうになった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――Ciel. What exactly was reported this morning?”
“The news said that a woman―――a girl our age, actually, went shopping last night and never came home. Apparently her family lives near the park.”
“I see. Near the park, then.”
The moment I said it, the contents of my stomach surged toward my throat.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Senpai.
You mentioned a new report--what is it……?"
"In the news this morning, a young woman who went shopping last night--about our age--and she went missing.
Her house is close to the park, I heard."
"…… Oh, close to the park."
As soon as I say that, the contents of my stomach threaten to rise up.

entries.japanese:
―――昨日の夜。
　本当に、ただの偶然で公園に通りかかった見知らぬ女の子は、理不尽なまでの暴力の前に、姿を消した。
　死亡した、というより行方不明になった、という表現の方が適切なぐらいの、髪の毛一本残さない凶食の前に。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Last night.
A girl I did not know had happened by pure chance to pass through the park, only to disappear before violence beyond all reason.
Missing was more apt than dead for a ravenous feeding that left not so much as a strand of hair.
entries.mirrorMoon:
--Last night.
That unknown girl who just by chance was by the park, was destroyed by that irrational violence.
Missing might be a better description, since she was devoured without even so much as a hair left behind.

entries.japanese:
「それじゃ行方不明者はこれで九人目、いや十人目だったけか？
　ったく、たった一ヶ月ですげえペースだな」
「そうですね。
けど昨夜に行方不明になった人はなんだか今までとは毛色が違うって話ですけど。
　今まで行方不明になった女の子たちっていうのは、行方不明になってしばらくしてから家の人たちが気付いたっていう話です」
entries.maoEnglish:
“That makes nine missing people, or was it ten? Hell of a pace for a single month.”
“Yes. But I heard last night’s disappearance was somehow different from the others.
With the earlier girls, their families did not realize anything was wrong until some time after they vanished.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"That makes her the ninth victim, no, the tenth?
Damn, what an amazing pace, all in a single month."
"Yes, but I hear last night's disappearance was a little different from the other ones.
The families of all the other girls who disappeared noticed it a short time later."

entries.japanese:
「ところで遠野くんもニュース見てないんですか？
もしかして朝、弱いとか」
「……どうだろう。
朝は弱いとは思わないけど、強くもないみたいだ。
けど、それとは別問題でこの先しばらくは見れそうにない。
うちね、テレビがないんだ」
　ピタリ、と先輩と有彦の動きが止まる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“By the way, didn’t you see the news either, Tohno? Are you bad at mornings too?”
“I don’t know. I wouldn’t say I’m bad at mornings, but I don’t seem particularly good at them either. That’s beside the point, though; I probably won’t be watching the news for a while. We don’t have a television at home.”
Ciel and Arihiko froze in perfect unison.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"By the way, you didn't watch the morning news either Tohno-kun?
Don't tell me you're not a morning person either?"
"…… Hmm.
I wouldn't say I'm a morning person, but I'm not terrible in the morning either.
But, leaving that matter aside, I still won't be able to watch it for a while.
At my house, there's no TV."
Senpai and Arihiko stare blankly.

entries.japanese:
「テレビがないって―――遠野くんのお家って、あのお屋敷ですよね？」
「おう、あの屋敷でテレビがないってコトはねえだろ。
学生の分際で自分の部屋にないんだ、とかいう贅沢は聞かねえぞ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“No television―――but your home is that mansion, isn’t it?”
“Yeah, there’s no way that mansion doesn’t have a television. And don’t give me some spoiled-rich-kid nonsense about not having one in your own room.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No TV--Your house is… that big mansion, right?"
"Heh, there's no way you don't have a TV in that mansion.
I won't let you say you don't have one in your room, being a student and all."

entries.japanese:
「いや、本当にないんだって。
うちの親父はあんな出来の悪い洗脳道具は要らないって断言してた人だったから。
　かろうじて琥珀さんのところに小型のテレビがあるだけなんだけど、朝っぱらから女の人の部屋に行くなんてできないだろ」
　だから報道を識るためには新聞をアテにするぐらいしか方法がない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’m telling you, there really isn’t one. My father used to declare that he had no use for such a shoddy brainwashing device.
There’s just one little set in Kohaku’s room, and I can hardly visit a woman’s bedroom first thing in the morning.”
That left newspapers as my only source of news.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No, there really isn't one.
My old man always said there was no need for such brainwashing machines.
There's a small one in Kohaku-san's room, but I'm not about to barge into a girl's room in the morning."
If I want to get the news, I just have to rely on a newspaper.

entries.japanese:
「遠野くん、女の人って、なんですか？」
「ああ、ちょっと今のは聞き捨てならないな、遠野」
　じろり、と二人して睨んでくる。
　まずい、と手で口を隠しても、今更後の祭だった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What exactly do you mean by ‘a woman,’ Tohno?”
“Yeah, Tohno, we can’t just let that remark pass.”
Both of them glared.
I covered my mouth, realizing my mistake, but it was far too late.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Tohno-kun, what do you mean by a girl?"
"You can't just say that and get away with it, Tohno."
They're both glaring at me.
I slap my hand over my mouth, but it's far too late.

entries.japanese:
「あ、いや―――たんに、うちの使用人の一人が、琥珀さんっていう女の人だっていうだけの、話」
「はあ、使用人さんですか。
いいですねー、身の回りの事を世話してくれる女の人がいてくれて」
「違いますっ！
　屋敷には家事ができる人がいないから働いてもらっているだけなんだってば。
　別に琥珀さんが女の人だろうが男の人だろうが関係はないでしょう」
entries.maoEnglish:
“No, wait―――I only meant that one of our servants is a woman named Kohaku, that’s all.”
“Oh, a servant. How lovely, having a woman to look after your every need.”
“That’s not what it’s like! No one else at the mansion can handle the housework, so she works for us.
It wouldn’t make any difference whether Kohaku was a woman or a man.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Uh, um--simply put, just that there's a servant at my house named Kohaku-san."
"Huh, a servant?
You're really lucky to have a girl around you at all times to take care of your every need."
"That's not it!
There isn't anyone to take care of the mansion, so we have to hire people to do it.
Whether she's male or female is entirely irrelevant."

entries.japanese:
「ふーん。
そのわりには琥珀さん、なんてすごく親しみのあるお言葉でしたよね乾くん」
「そうそう、やけに幸せそうな顔して琥珀さん、なんて口にしやがって。
前から聞こうとは思ってたけどよ、遠野は今どんな生活をしてやがるのかな、一体」
　じろっ、という視線がじとり、というものに変わる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Really? Kohaku sounded awfully familiar on your lips, didn’t it, Inui?”
“Exactly; you practically glowed when you said her name. I’ve been meaning to ask, Tohno, just what kind of life are you living in that place?”
Their sharp glares curdled into long, suspicious stares.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Oh reeeeallly?
Hey Inui-kun, doesn't Tohno-kun sound real intimate with this Kohaku-san?
"Yeah yeah, he looked so happy when he said her name.
I wanted to ask before, but just what kind of a life does Tohno lead right now?"
They trade glances.

entries.japanese:
「………う」
　食べていたパンが喉につまる。
　有彦はともかく、先輩までも冷たい眼差しで問い詰めてくるのは、異様な迫力がある。
「遠野くん、お昼休みはまだたっぷりありますから。
どうぞ、遠慮なくお屋敷での話を聞かせてください」
　有無を言わせぬ笑顔で迫ってくるシエル先輩。
「……………」
　それをあと二十分近くやり過ごさないといけないのか、と思うだけで眩暈がしてきた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Urk.”
The bread lodged in my throat.
Arihiko was bad enough, but being interrogated beneath Ciel’s cold gaze as well gave the pair a terrifying intensity.
“There is still plenty of lunch break left, Tohno. Please, take all the time you need to tell us about life at your mansion.”
Ciel advanced with a smile that permitted no refusal.
“…”
The mere thought of enduring this for another twenty minutes made me dizzy.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……… Ugh."
I choke on the bread I'm eating.
Arihiko, even Ciel-senpai with her cool glance, interrogates me with bizarre intensity.
"Tohno-kun, there is still plenty of time left.
Please tell us all about your life at the mansion."
She approaches with a smile that won't seem to let me get away.
"……………"
Just thinking about the twenty minutes or so I have left to live through this makes my head spin.

entries.japanese:
―――やめよう。
　二食ぐらい抜いても人間は死ぬことはないんだし。
「……ん、今日はパスする。
有彦の好きにしていいよ」
　また食べ物に赤い血がかかっているような錯覚を見るのはゴメンだ。
　正直、有彦のもっているサンドウィッチを見かけただけでうんざりしている。
　だって、ご丁寧に真っ赤なトマトがたっぷりと入っているのだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Forget it.
No one ever died from missing a meal or two.
“I’ll pass today. Do whatever you want, Arihiko.”
I had no desire to hallucinate fresh blood splashed over food again.
The mere sight of his sandwich already made me sick.
Naturally, it was stuffed with bright red tomato slices.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---I won't.
Skipping two meals won't kill me.
"…… Mm, I'll pass.
Do what you want."
Seeing a vision of food with something red on it isn't something I want to do again.
To be honest, I'm already feeling bad looking at Arihiko's sandwich.
Because there are many bright red tomatoes in it.

entries.japanese:
「なんだ、おまえますます不健康になってくな。
そんなに新しい生活は合わないのか？」
「ああ、そうなのかもしれないな。
　朝は七時に起きても遅いと文句は言われるし、門限は八時だし。
おまけに無断外泊すると厳しく詰問されるなんて、監獄生活みたいだろ？」
「いいじゃねえか、規則正しい生活で。
管理体制万万歳、若者はもっとタイトに生きねえとな。
若いうちから楽しちゃろくな大人になれないぞ」
「同感。
……けど、有彦に言われると誰に言われるより説得力があるね」
　その、究極的な反面教師として。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You look less healthy every day. Does your new life disagree with you that much?”
“Maybe it does.
They complain that seven is late to wake up, impose an eight o’clock curfew, and interrogate me if I spend a night away without permission. Sounds like prison, doesn’t it?”
“What’s wrong with that? Long live strict supervision; young people ought to live with a little discipline. Take it easy while you’re young and you’ll never grow into a decent adult.”
“Agreed. Somehow, coming from you, that carries more weight than it would from anyone else.”
As the ultimate cautionary example.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"What's this?
You're becoming more and more unhealthy.
Is your new lifestyle not suiting you that much?"
"That might be it.
They complain about me being late when I wake up at seven o'clock and the curfew's at eight o'clock.
If I spend the night somewhere without asking, they interrogate me afterwards.
It's like a prison, right?"
"Isn't that alright?
It's a proper life.
Early to bed and early to rise, right?
You won't be able to grow up to be a good guy if you burn out when you're young."
"I agree.
…… But, you seem to lend the argument more strength than anyone else can."
As the ultimate counter-example, that is.

entries.japanese:
「そうか？
　なんだ、今日の遠野はやけに素直じゃないか。
よしよし、サンドウィッチを一切れ分けてあげましょう」
「だから食べ物はいいって。
俺のことは気にせず食べろよ。
昼休み、終わっちゃうぞ」
「そう？
　んじゃ遠慮なくいただきます」
　両手を合わせてから有彦はサンドウィッチを食べ始める。
 ───と。
「おじゃましまーす」
　先輩が、お弁当らしきものを手にしてやってきた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Really? You’re awfully agreeable today, Tohno. Here, I’ll share a piece of my sandwich.”
“I said I don’t want any food. Forget about me and eat. Lunch break will be over soon.”
“Yeah? Then don’t mind if I do.”
Arihiko put his hands together and began eating.
───And then.
“Mind if I join you?”
Ciel arrived carrying what appeared to be a packed lunch.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Oh yeah?
You're pretty honest today.
Alright, alright, I'll split the sandwich with you."
"I said, I didn't want to eat.
Don't worry about me and eat; lunch'll end soon."
"Okay, down the hatch."
Arihiko holds his sandwich with both hands and begins to eat.
------And then.
"Hello everyone."
Senpai comes in with something that looks like a boxed lunch.

entries.japanese:
「おっ？
　先輩って学食じゃなかったっけか？」
「いえ、べつに食事は決まってないですよ。
その日の気分でなんでもありです」
　先輩は可愛らしい巾着袋からお弁当を取り出す。
大きさは女の子にしてはやや大きめだ。
「……つまり今日は早起き出来たからお弁当を作ってきた、っていうコト？」
「そうなんです、今朝はめずらしく七時前に起きれたんですよー……って、何を言わせるんですか遠野くんは！」
「……いや、そんなつもりはなかったんだけど……先輩、もしかして朝は弱いほう？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Huh? Don’t you usually eat in the cafeteria?”
“I don’t have a rule about it. I eat whatever suits my mood that day.”
Ciel drew a lunch box from a charming little cloth bag. It was somewhat large for a girl’s lunch.
“So you made a lunch today because you managed to get up early?”
“Exactly; I managed to wake before seven for once—but wait, Tohno, what are you making me admit?!”
“I didn’t mean anything by it, but are you bad at mornings, Ciel?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Oh?
Senpai, I thought you always ate in the cafeteria?"
"No, I don't have a set lunch routine.
It just depends what mood I'm in."
Senpai takes out an boxed lunch wrapped up in a cute handkerchief.
But it seems just a little too big for a girl.
"…… You mean you managed to get up early and make lunch this morning?"
"Yes, that's it.
I managed to wake up before seven this morning and…… wait a minute, what are you making me say, Tohno-kun!?"
"…… No, that's not what I meant, but…… Senpai, you're not a morning person?"

entries.japanese:
「え───？
　あ、はい、実はわたし、早起きって苦手なんです」
　先輩は教師に注意された生徒みたいにかしこまる。
「わたしの実家はパン屋さんでしたから、すっごく朝が早かったんです。
　けどわたしはどうしても朝に弱くて。
もう子供のころからお父さんに怒られてばかりでした」
entries.maoEnglish:
“What───? Oh, yes; actually, I’m terrible at getting up early.”
Ciel sat as stiffly as a student being scolded by a teacher.
“My family owned a bakery, so our days began incredibly early.
But I was hopeless at getting up. Ever since I was little, my father was forever scolding me for it.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Eh----?
Ah, yes, I'm not… not good at waking up early."
Senpai suddenly looks like a student being scolded by a teacher.
"My family owned a bakery, so we'd get up very early every morning.
But I'm terrible in the morning.
My father would always get angry when I was a kid."

entries.japanese:
なんとパン屋！
　有彦は視線があう。
　あいつも今、部屋にカマドがあって、その白い指で小麦粉を練って焼いたりするシエル先輩の姿を想像したに違いない。
entries.maoEnglish:
A bakery, of all things!
Arihiko and I exchanged looks.
He too must have imagined Ciel with a brick oven in her room, kneading flour with those white fingers and baking bread.
entries.mirrorMoon:
What!?
A bakery!?
Me and Arihiko look at each other.
He must be imagining the same thing I am: Ciel-senpai kneading dough with those white fingers of hers and baking it.

entries.japanese:
「お父さんとの戦いは十年ほど続きましたが、最後には『おまえをしつけるのなら二人分働いたほうがましだ』とさじを投げられちゃいました。
　それ以来、わたしは起きる時間に関してはわがまましほうだいなのです」
　えっへん、と発育のいい胸をはるシエル先輩。
「へえー、そうなんだ。
なんか意外だな、先輩ってすっごくしっかりしてそうなのに」
「はい、遠野くんの前では失敗しないように頑張ってますから。
ほんとはですね、どっちかっていうと要領が悪いほうなんです、わたし」
entries.maoEnglish:
“The war between my father and me lasted about ten years.
At last he gave up, declaring he would rather do the work of two people than try to train me; ever since, I’ve been allowed to wake whenever I please.”
Ciel gave a proud little ahem and thrust out her ample chest.
“Wow, really? That’s surprising for someone who always seems so capable.”
“That’s because I work hard not to make mistakes when you’re around, Tohno. The truth is, I’m rather clumsy about most things.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"My daily battle with my father lasted ten years, but in the end, he gave up and told me working two people's worth is better than trying to train me.
Since then, I can wake up when I want to."
Ciel-senpai sticks out her well-developed chest.
"Oh, is that so?
I'm a little surprised; you seem so reliable."
"Yes, I always try hard to not make any mistakes in front of you.
But really, I'm more of a clumsy person."

entries.japanese:
ああ、たしかに要領は悪いほうなのかもしれない。
　思えば先輩と親しくなるきっかけになったのは、上級生が一人きりで中庭の添え木を直しているのをほうっておけなかったからだし。
　要領がいい人間っていうのは、ああいった一文の得にもならない事はやらないものだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
She might be right about that.
After all, we first became acquainted because I could not leave an older student to repair a tree brace in the courtyard all by herself.
People who knew how to play things smart would never do a thankless job like that.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Yeah, maybe she is a bit clumsy.
Come to think of it, I really started to get close to Senpai when I saw her, an upperclassman, all alone in the courtyard fixing those splints and helped her out.
A really clumsy person would never do something that wouldn't benefit them the least bit.

entries.japanese:
「そっか。
───でも俺、要領が悪い人のほうが好きだよ。
一緒にいると安心できる」
　うむ、と隣で同意する有彦。
「それで、朝が弱い先輩はたいてい学食だったってわけなのか」
「ええ、そういうわけなので学食がほとんどなんですけど、たまにはこうやってお弁当ぐらい作ります。
お二人は学食派ですよね？」
「いんや、俺たちもその日の気分だな。
一年の頃は俺も姉貴にメシ作ってもらってたんだけどよ、遠野のやつが学食だったりパン食だったりするから、合わせてるうちにこうなっちまったんだ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“I see. ───But I prefer people who aren’t good at looking out for themselves. They make me feel at ease.”
Beside me, Arihiko nodded solemnly.
“So because mornings defeat you, you usually eat in the cafeteria.”
“That’s why I usually use the cafeteria, though now and then I make myself a lunch like this. You two normally use the cafeteria, don’t you?”
“Nah, we go by mood too. My sister made my lunches in our first year, but Tohno kept switching between cafeteria food and bread from the school shop; I followed his lead, and this is where I ended up.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I see.
---But, I like people that are clumsy.
I can relax better with them."
"Yup." Arihiko agrees next to me.
"So, since you're not a morning person, you usually eat in the cafeteria?"
"Yes, although I usually eat in the cafeteria, there are times when I make lunch.
Aren't you two part of the cafeteria group?"
"Nah, it depends on what mood we're in too.
When we were freshmen, my sister made me something, but Tohno here would always eat in the cafeteria or buy bread, so I end up doing what he does."

entries.japanese:
「はあ。
遠野くんは気分屋さんなんですね」
「そーそー。
こういう男と付き合うと疲れるだけだから、先輩も気をつけな」
　そうですねー、と有彦に同意しながら先輩はお弁当のふたをあける。
　まるい弁当箱にはごはんとおかずが半分半分。
実にオーソドックスなものだけど、それなりに量は多めのようだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I see. So you’re rather fickle, Tohno.”
“Exactly. Dating a man like this would only wear you out, so watch yourself.”
Ciel murmured her agreement as she opened her lunch box.
The round container was divided evenly between rice and side dishes. Entirely conventional, though the portions did appear generous.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I see.
So Tohno-kun is a person of many moods."
"Yeah, yeah.
Being with him will just drain you out, so be careful Senpai."
"That's true," Senpai agrees and she opens her lunch.
The round box is half rice and half side dish.
It's pretty much a normal lunch, but it seems a little large.

entries.japanese:
「ではいただきます。
となりの人の椅子、借りていいでしょうか？」
「いないヤツの椅子はみんなの椅子だよ。
高田クンも先輩に座ってもらえて本望だろうし」
　高田クンはとなりの席の、よく肥えた肉体をした人のいい青年だ。
　たまに、無期限でお金を借りるコトもある。
　先輩は俺の机にではなく、自分の膝の上にお弁当をおいて食べ始める。
　その斜め横では、立ったままで二個目のパンの封をあけている有彦。
　二人の様子を横目に、俺は窓の外の風景を意味もなく眺めたりする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Well, time to eat. May I borrow the chair from the next desk?”
“An absent man’s chair belongs to everyone. Takada would be honored to have you sit in it.”
Takada, who occupied the desk beside mine, was a good-natured young man with a well-padded frame.
Occasionally, I borrowed money from him with no fixed date of repayment.
Ciel set the lunch box on her lap rather than my desk and began to eat.
Beside her at an angle, Arihiko stood opening the wrapper on a second roll.
I watched them from the corner of my eye, then stared aimlessly out the window.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Then, I'll start eating.
Is it okay if I use this person's chair?"
"A person who isn't here has their chair up for grabs.
I'm sure Takada-kun would love for you to have his seat, Senpai."
Takada-kun is a guy who sits next to me.
He's pretty plump, but a good guy.
Sometimes, he borrows money with a grace period which lasts about until the end of eternity.
Senpai doesn't put her lunch on my desk, but puts it in her lap.
Next to her, Arihiko starts opening his second pack of bread while still standing up.
Next to these two, I stare aimlessly out the window.

entries.japanese:
「あれ？
　遠野くん、お昼は食べないんですか？」
「ちょっとね。
昼飯は食べないコトにしたんだ」
「食べないって……それじゃお腹すいちゃいますよ」
「いや、別に腹は減ってないし。
昼をぬいたぐらいでどうにかなるほどやわじゃないよ」
「うわあ、すごいなあ。
わたし、一食でもぬいたら動けません。
おなかがぺこぺこになって倒れちゃいます。
　……恥ずかしいですよね、普通の子よりたくさん食事はとってるほうなのに、すぐお腹が減っちゃうんですから」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh? Aren’t you eating lunch, Tohno?”
“Not today. I decided to skip it.”
“If you skip it, you’ll get hungry.”
“I’m not hungry. Missing lunch won’t do me any harm.”
“That’s amazing. If I miss even one meal, I can’t move. I get so hungry I could collapse.
It’s embarrassing that I get hungry again so quickly even though I already eat more than an ordinary girl.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Huh?
Tohno-kun, are you not eating?"
"No, I thought I'd skip today."
"Not eating…… Won't that make you hungry?"
"No, not really.
I'm not hungry and skipping lunch doesn't affect me that much."
"Wow, that's amazing.
If I skip a single meal, I can't function.
I'd just collapse of hunger.
…… It's a little embarrassing, I always eat more than most people, and I still get hungry."

entries.japanese:
「そんなことはない。
先輩は他のおんなどもに比べて発育いいからな。
胸が大きいぶん燃費が悪いのは致し方あるまい」
　うむ、有彦の意見はもっともだ。
　俺たちとしては、むしろもっと食べて存分に育ってほしい。
　先輩は恥ずかしいのか照れているのか、よくわからない顔をしている。
　……まあ、おそらくは嬉しいんだと思うけど。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Nothing embarrassing about it. You’re better developed than the other girls. A larger chest has to burn more fuel.”
Arihiko’s argument was perfectly sound.
For our part, we hoped she would eat even more and continue to develop without restraint.
Ciel wore an expression I could not quite read as embarrassment or pleasure.
She was probably pleased.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Not at all.
Senpai, you've developed a lot more than other women.
I'm sure you have to eat a lot to maintain that large chest of yours."
Yeah, Arihiko speaks the truth.
To tell the truth, we both want her to eat more and grow more.
Is Senpai embarrassed or shy?
She makes a face I don't quite understand.
…… Well, I'm sure she's probably happy.

entries.japanese:
「でも遠野くん、本当におひるごはんを抜いてだいじょうぶなんですか？」
「大丈夫だよ。
まる一日ぐらい食事を断つのは珍しい事じゃないんだ。
今日は朝食を食べてないだけだから、まだ夜までは元気かな」
「うわあ───遠野くん、そんな生活してちゃ体壊しちゃいますよ」
「壊れないって。
たんに精神的な問題で食事制限してるだけだよ。
……まあ、昔の事故のせいでお医者さんにあんまり体重を増やさないように注意もされてるし、たまにメシを抜いたほうが俺は丁度いいんだってさ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“But are you sure you’ll be all right without lunch?”
“I’ll be fine. Going a whole day without food isn’t unusual for me. I only skipped breakfast today, so I should last until evening.”
“Oh, Tohno───you’ll ruin your health living that way.”
“I won’t. I only restrict my meals when I’m under mental strain. Besides, because of my old accident, the doctor warned me not to gain much weight; missing an occasional meal is about right for me.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"But Tohno-kun, will you really be alright if you skip lunch?"
"I'll be fine.
Skipping meals during the day isn't that rare.
I only didn't eat breakfast, so I'll probably be fine until evening."
"Wow---Tohno-kun, your body will break down with that kind of lifestyle."
"It won't break.
This is more of a mental restriction.
…… Well, thanks to an accident long ago, my doctor told me it wasn't good to gain weight, so it's better for me to skip meals once in a while."

entries.japanese:
「はあ。
おとこのひとでもダイエットって考えるんですね」
　先輩はなにやら上目遣いで俺を見ると、少し考えこんだあげくお弁当のふたを閉じてしまった
「えーと、用事を思い出したんで失礼します」
　テキパキと後片付けをすまして、先輩は風のように去っていく。
「───うむ、かわいい」
　先輩が出ていった扉を未練がましく見つめながら、有彦はそんな言葉を呟いた
entries.maoEnglish:
“I see. So men think about dieting too.”
Ciel looked up at me from beneath her lashes, thought for a moment, then closed her lunch box
“Um, I just remembered something I have to do, so please excuse me.”
She packed everything away with brisk efficiency and vanished like the wind.
“───Mm, adorable.”
Arihiko murmured the words while staring longingly at the door through which Ciel had departed
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Huh.
I guess even guys still think about their diet after all."
Senpai looks up at me for some reason, and after thinking a little bit, closes her lunch.
"Um, I just remembered I had something to do, so excuse me."
Gathering up her things quickly, she disappears like the wind.
"---Mmm, how cute."
Arihiko comments on Senpai regretfully while watching her leave.

entries.japanese:
授業が終わって、教室は急速に黄昏はじめる。
　遠くの地平線に日が沈んでいく。
　教室には誰もいない。
　こうやって、別段やる事もなく教室に残っている物好きは自分ぐらいしかいない。
「―――――」
　茜色に染まっていく教室。
 ───夕焼けは、あまりみたくない。
　鮮烈な血をイメージさせて、ここ数日の出来事を思い返してしまう。
entries.maoEnglish:
Classes end, and twilight steals swiftly into the room.
The sun is sinking beyond the far horizon.
No one else is here.
I’m probably the only person strange enough to linger in an empty classroom with nothing in particular to do.
“―――――”
The classroom deepens toward crimson.
───I don’t want to look at the sunset.
Its vivid red brings blood to mind, and with it everything that has happened these past few days.
entries.mirrorMoon:
After class, the room quickly fills with the gloom of dusk.
The sun is sinking below the horizon.
There's no one else in the classroom.
I'm the only one who likes sitting here and doing nothing.
"-----"
The room is painted red.
---I don't like watching the sunset.
It makes me think of blood, and reminds me of the events in the past few days.

entries.japanese:
「――――――」
　だっていうのに、あまり家に帰る気にはなれなかった。
　ぼんやりと窓の外の緋色を眺める。
　赤い。
　赤い、夕焼け。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――――”
Even so, I can’t bring myself to go home.
I stare absently through the window into the scarlet light.
Red.
A red, red sunset.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------"
Still, I don't particularly feel like going back home.
I stare blankly out the window.
Red.
Red, sunset.

entries.japanese:
「い―――――た」
　ずきりと、胸の古傷が、痛んだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“It―――――hurts.”
The old wound in my chest gives a vicious throb.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah----ow."
The old wound on my chest hurts.

entries.japanese:
赤い色。
　赤いなにか。
　例えば、人の血。
　べったりとはりついて、むせ返るような濃厚な匂いをもった、たくさんの血液。
entries.maoEnglish:
Red.
Something red.
Human blood, for instance.
Great smears of it, clinging thickly, rank with a stench so rich it chokes me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The color red.
Something… red.
Such as, human blood.
Lots of blood… sticky, with a strong smell.

entries.japanese:
「――――くっ」
　痛い。
　メガネをちゃんとかけてるのに、頭が、痛い。
　　　　　　　どうして。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ngh――――”
It hurts.
My glasses are on—they’re on properly—but my head still hurts.
why?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----Gah."
It hurts.
My glasses are on, but, my head hurts.
Why?

entries.japanese:
ずきりと。
　　　　あたまが
　　　どうして。
　　　　　　　　　　　あたまが。
　どうして。
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　ずき
り　　　　と　　　どうして―――――
entries.maoEnglish:
A throb.          my head
    why?
                      my head.
why?
                                  throb
bing          why―――――
entries.mirrorMoon:
Throbbing pain.
My head
Why?
My head.
Why?
Thro
b  w    why----

entries.japanese:
「はあ――――はあ――――は―――――」
　呼吸が荒い。
　なにかひどく―――気が高ぶっている。
　イライラして、何か気に食わなくて、何かにヤツ当たりでもしないとおさまらない――――。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hah――――hah――――haah―――――”
My breathing is ragged.
Something has me terribly―――worked up.
I’m seething. Something is wrong, something is unbearable, and I won’t calm down unless I take it out on something――――
entries.mirrorMoon:
I start to pant heavily.
My breathing is ragged.
I'm horribly----getting worked up.
I'm irritated; there's something I can't stand, and I can't calm down unless I take it out on something----.

entries.japanese:
「……遠野くん、ですか？」
「あれ――――先、輩」
　先輩は何か深刻な顔をして、教室の中に入ってくる。
「いま、机を倒すような音がしたから来たんですけど……それ、遠野くんがやったんですか？」
「――――え？」
　振りかえる。
　そこにはたしかに、乱暴に倒された机や椅子が散乱していた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Tohno, is that you?”
“Oh――――Ciel.”
She enters the classroom with a grave look on her face.
“I came because I heard what sounded like desks falling over; did you do this, Tohno?”
“――――What?”
I look behind me.
Desks and chairs lie scattered everywhere, flung down with unmistakable violence.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Is it--Tohno-kun?"
"Huh----Sen… pai?"
Senpai has a very serious look on her face as she enters the room.
"I just heard a sound like someone knocking over desks…… was that you, Tohno-kun?"
"----Eh?"
I turn around.
Indeed, desks are strewn about and chairs overturned everywhere.

entries.japanese:
「……あ……うん、そうみたいだ。
なんか、ワケもなくムシャクシャしちゃって、その―――」
　俺が、こんなふうに散らかしたんだろうか？
「もう、ダメじゃないですか。
何があったか知りませんけど、物に八つ当たりなんかしちゃだめです」
　先輩は倒れた椅子と机を直していく。
　俺も無言で机を立てなおした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh, yeah, I suppose I did. I got angry for no reason, and then―――”
Did I really make this mess?
“Honestly, you know better than that. I don’t know what happened, but you mustn’t take your anger out on things.”
She begins setting the fallen desks and chairs upright.
Without a word, I join her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Ah…… yeah, it seems so.
I guess I got a little irritated for no reason, um--"
Did I really do this?
"Geez, you can't do that.
I don't know what happened, but you shouldn't take it out on things."
Senpai starts to straighten out the desks and the chairs.
I wordlessly do so too.

entries.japanese:
「……すみません。
なんか、自分でもよくわからなくて」
「はあ。
遠野くん、なんかヘンですよ。
あの時だって雨にうたれてぼーっとしてて、今日は今日で机を倒してぼっーとしているんですから」
「ああ―――うん、ここんところ少し疲れていてヘンなんだ、俺」
　はあ、と深く深呼吸をする。
　……先輩の顔が見れたからだろうか。
　さっきまでの頭痛も、わけのわからない苛だちもキレイさっぱり消えてしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’m sorry. I don’t really understand what came over me.”
“Goodness. You’ve been acting very strangely, Tohno. First I find you standing in the rain in a daze, and now you’re knocking over desks and staring into space.”
“Yeah―――I know; I’ve been tired lately, and I haven’t been myself.”
I draw a long, deep breath.
Maybe it’s because I’ve seen her face.
Whatever the reason, the headache and that senseless fury have vanished without a trace.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Sorry.
I don't… quite know myself."
"Hmm.
Tohno-kun, you're acting weird.
You were spaced out in the rain that time, and today you spaced out in the middle of all these jumbled desks."
"Yeah--yeah, I'm tired and it's making me act weird."
I take a deep breath.
…… Is it because I saw Senpai's face?
That headache and the irritation I had before vanishes like it was never there.

entries.japanese:
「ごめんね、また迷惑かけちゃって。
それじゃ帰るから、また明日」
「あ、遠野くんは今からお帰りなんですか？」
　ああ、と頷く。
　先輩はさっきのコトなんてまるで無かったことのように、淡い笑顔をうかべた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Sorry for causing you trouble again. I’m heading home now, so I’ll see you tomorrow.”
“Oh, are you leaving now?”
I nod.
She gives me a faint smile, as though nothing at all had just happened.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Sorry, I've caused you trouble again.
I'll head out now, so see you tomorrow."
"Oh, Tohno-kun, are you going back now?"
Yeah, I nod.
As if nothing had just happened before, she gives me a hearty smile.

entries.japanese:
「奇遇ですね。
わたしも今日は早めに帰ろうかなぁ、って思ってたんです。
ちょうどいいですから一緒に帰っていいですか？」
「いや、俺は嬉しいけど……先輩の家と俺の家って逆方向じゃないか。
一緒には帰れないよ」
「ですから、校門までご一緒します」
「……まあ、そういうコトなら喜んで」
「はい。
それじゃあ荷物をとってきますから、ちょっと待っててください」
　タッ、と軽快な足音をたてて先輩は走っていく。
　待つ事、実にわずか一分で先輩は帰ってきた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What a coincidence. I was thinking of going home early today too. Since the timing is perfect, may I walk with you?”
“I’d love that, but don’t we live in opposite directions? We can’t exactly walk home together.”
“Then I’ll walk with you as far as the school gate.”
“Well, in that case, I’d be delighted.”
“Wonderful. I’ll fetch my things, so please wait here a moment.”
She darts away, her footsteps quick and light.
A mere minute later, she is back.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"What a coincidence.
I was just thinking that I should go back too.
Since it happens to work out, can I go back with you?"
"No, I really appreciate the offer, but…… isn't your house in the opposite direction?
We can't exactly walk back together."
"I know, so we'll be together until the gate."
"…… Well, in that case, my pleasure."
"Yes.
I have to get my things, so please wait a minute."
With light footsteps, Senpai runs out of the room.
It really was only a minute till she came back.

entries.japanese:
「お待たせしました。
それでははりきって行きましょう！」
　先輩の姿は、本当に明るい。
　なんていうか、見ているだけでさっきまでの陰鬱とした気持ちが晴れていく。
　こんないい人が誘ってくれてるっていうのに、いつまでも暗い顔をしてちゃバチがあたるってもんだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Thank you for waiting. Now, let’s be off!”
She is so full of light.
Just looking at her seems to clear away every gloomy thought I had a moment ago.
When someone this kind has invited me along, keeping a miserable face would be downright ungrateful.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Thanks for waiting.
Now then, let's go!"
She really is cheerful.
How should I say this?
Just seeing her drives away the clouded feelings I had earlier.
Having such a great person ask me to come with her, I ought to be punished if I was still gloomy.

entries.japanese:
「……オッケー、それじゃ行こうか。
けど、そんなにはりきったら校門までなんてあっという間だね」
「あ、そうですよね。
できるだけゆっくり行かないともったいないです」
　先輩はトコトコと歩きだす。
　その後ろについて、夕暮れの教室を後にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“All right, let’s go. But at that pace we’ll reach the gate in no time.”
“Oh, you’re right. We’d better go as slowly as possible, or it would be a waste.”
She sets off at a tiny, deliberate pace.
I follow her out of the classroom and into the dusk.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Okay, let's go.
But, it's a pretty short trip to the front gate."
"Ah, that's right.
We'll have to go as slow as possible to make it worth it."
Senpai starts to walk.
Following her, I leave the darkening classroom behind me.

entries.japanese:
校門を通り抜けた。
　ここからの帰り道はお互い別方向になる。
「それじゃあここでお別れですね。
なんか、あっという間でした」
　……同感。
こっちももう少しうちの学校が広かったら良かったのに、と本気で思っていたりする。
entries.maoEnglish:
We passed through the school gates.
Our routes home split in opposite directions here.
“I suppose this is goodbye. That went by so quickly.”
I feel exactly the same. I find myself sincerely wishing our school grounds had been a little larger.
entries.mirrorMoon:
We walk out the gate.
From here, we have to go our separate ways.
"Well then, this is goodbye for now.
We got here pretty quickly."
…… I feel the same way.
I was really thinking it would be better if the school were a bit bigger.

entries.japanese:
「それじゃ先輩、また明日」
「はい。
また明日、学校でお会いしましょう」
　笑顔で返答して、先輩は別方向の帰り道を去っていく。
　それを軽く見届けてから、自分も屋敷への帰路についた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Well, see you tomorrow.”
“Yes. I’ll see you at school tomorrow.”
She answers with a smile and sets off down the road in the other direction.
After watching her go for a moment, I start home toward the estate.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Well then, Senpai, see you tomorrow."
"Yes, let's meet at school tomorrow."
Smiling as she responds, Senpai disappears in the opposite direction.
After watching her go, I head down the street towards my house.

entries.japanese:
夕暮れの廊下を先輩と歩いていく。
　お互いつまらない事を話しながら、できるだけゆっくりとした足取りで歩いていく。
　なんていうか、すごくいい雰囲気だった。
―――思い返してみれば、俺は先輩の部屋に一泊したんだ。
　あの時は人を殺してしまったっていう事で頭がいっぱいだったし、その後はアルクェイドと過ごしていて忘れていたけど。
entries.maoEnglish:
I walk through the corridors at dusk with Ciel.
We trade idle remarks and make our steps as slow as possible.
There is something wonderfully comfortable about it.
―――Come to think of it, I once spent the night in her room.
At the time I could think of nothing but the person I believed I had killed, and afterward Arcueid occupied all my attention, so the memory had slipped away.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I walk through the hallway bathed in sunset with Senpai.
While talking about pointless things, we walk as slowly as possible.
There's such a wonderful atmosphere here.
---Thinking back, I spent the night in Senpai's room.
Back then, my mind was filled with the fact that I killed someone, and after that, I forgot about it when I was with Arcueid.

entries.japanese:
……あの夜がなかったら、今の遠野志貴はなかったとさえ思う。
　先輩は話題にさえあげないけど、先輩にとってあの夜はどんなものだったんだろう。
　……単に、落ち込んでほっとけない後輩に手を差し伸べただけなんだろうか。
　雨の中、捨てられている子犬を拾う時みたいに。
entries.maoEnglish:
I almost believe that without that night, the Shiki Tohno who exists today would never have come to be.
She has never mentioned it, but what did the night mean to her?
Perhaps she merely reached out to a miserable younger student she could not bear to abandon.
As one might pick up a puppy left shivering in the rain.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… If it wasn't for that one night, I don't think I would be here today as I am now.
She doesn't bring it up, but I wonder what she thinks about that night.
…… Did it feel like she was just lending a hand to a depressed lowerclassman?
Like picking up an abandoned puppy cast out in the rain?

entries.japanese:
「……先輩、あのさ―――」
「はい？」
　先輩が視線を向けてくる。
　……ええいままよ、とあの夜のことを聞こうとした瞬間。
　ぐるうううう。
　と、腹の虫が鳴った。
　いや、鳴ったというより啼いた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ciel, can I ask you something―――”
“Yes?”
She looks over at me.
I steel myself to ask about that night—and just as I open my mouth…
Grrrrrrrrr.
My stomach growls.
No, that was too savage to be called a growl; it howled.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Senpai, um--"
"Yes?"
Senpai looks over to me.
…… Right when I was going to ask about that night,
Guruuuuuu.
My stomach interrupts, growling audibly.
No, not 'growling'… it's more like a roar.

entries.japanese:
「……………う」
「……………」
　沈黙が、すこし気まずい。
「……遠野くん、おなか減ってるみたいですね」
「―――そうみたい。
まいったな、食欲がなくてもおなかっていうのは減っちゃうものなのか」
　はあ、とため息まじりに呟く。
　そんな俺を見て、先輩はクスリと笑った。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ugh.”
“…”
The silence grows a little awkward.
“It sounds as though you’re hungry, Tohno.”
“―――Apparently. That’s inconvenient; I didn’t realize your stomach could be hungry when you have no appetite.”
I mutter it with a sigh.
She gives a quiet laugh.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……………… Uhhh."
"………………"
The silence is a little uncomfortable.
"…… Tohno-kun, it seems you're hungry."
"---I guess so.
Geez, do I get hungry even when I don't have an appetite?"
I let out a sigh.
Looking at me, Senpai smiles.

entries.japanese:
「当たり前ですよ。
なにか食べなくちゃ生きていけないのが人間ですから」
「違いない。
……っと、そう思ったら本当にハラが減ってきやがった」
　……気がつかなかったけど、朝と昼をぬいたのはそれなりに堪えていたらしい。
　この分じゃ夕食まで我慢できそうにないし、途中でパンでも買っていくか────
entries.maoEnglish:
“Of course it can. Human beings have to eat if they want to live.”
“Can’t argue with that. And now that you mention it, I’m suddenly starving.”
I had not noticed, but skipping both breakfast and lunch must have taken its toll.
At this rate I will never last until dinner, so maybe I should buy some bread on the way home────
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Of course.
Being human means you have to eat to live."
"No doubt.
…… Come to think of it, I'm really starving."
…… I hadn't realized it, but skipping breakfast and lunch really did take quite a bit out of me.
I don't think I can last until dinner, so I should buy some bread on the way back-----

entries.japanese:
「遠野くん、これ」
　先輩は手に持った巾着袋を差し出す。
　たしかそれは先輩のお弁当袋だったっけ。
「食べかけだけど、いいですか？」
　わずかに頬をそめて、恥ずかしそうに先輩はそう言った。
　……そういえば先輩、お昼はお弁当を半分だけ食べてフタをしたんだっけ。
　人の食べかけのお弁当を食べる、というのは世間一般の常識では恥ずかしい事だとおもう。
　俺は────
entries.maoEnglish:
“Tohno, here.”
She holds out the drawstring pouch in her hand.
If I remember correctly, that is her lunch bag.
“I’ve already eaten some of it, but would you mind?”
She blushes faintly and says it with embarrassment.
Come to think of it, at lunch she ate only half, then put the lid back on.
By ordinary standards, eating someone else’s leftovers is probably rather intimate.
I────
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Tohno-kun, here."
Senpai presents me a pouch of cloth she is holding.
I think it's her lunch.
"It's partly eaten, but is that okay?"
Blushing a bit, Senpai says this embarrassedly.
…… That's right, Senpai only ate half of her lunch today.
Finishing someone else's half-eaten lunch is a little embarrassing.
I----

entries.japanese:
さすがにそこまで甘える事はできない。
　先輩は好意で言ってくれているんだろうけど、この人にあんまり格好の悪いところを見せたくはない。
entries.maoEnglish:
I cannot impose on her that much.
I know the offer is kindly meant, but I do not want this woman to see too much of me at my most pathetic.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I can't go that far.
Senpai is probably saying it out of goodwill, but I don't want to let her see me like this.

entries.japanese:
「――いや、我慢できそうです。
先輩の言葉だけでおなかが膨らみましたから」
「……そうですか？
　遠野くん、朝から何も食べていないんじゃ途中で倒れちゃうかもしれませんよ……？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“No, I can manage. The offer itself was enough to fill me up.”
“Are you sure? If you haven’t eaten anything since morning, you may collapse on the way home…”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"--No, I think I can make it.
Your words are enough to fill me up."
"…… Is that so?
Tohno-kun, you haven't had anything all day.
Are you sure you won't collapse on the way……?"

entries.japanese:
「ご心配にはおよびません。
俺みたいに何度も貧血で倒れたりしていると、いつ倒れるかなっていうのが解るようになるんです。
で、とりあえず今日はオッケーって体が言ってますから」
「……まあ遠野くんがそう言うんなら大丈夫なんでしょうけど」
　はあ、と呆れた風なため息をこぼしながら、先輩は廊下を歩いていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“There’s no need to worry. Once you’ve fainted from anemia as often as I have, you learn to tell when the next fall is coming. My body says I’m safe for today.”
“Well, if you say so, I suppose you’ll be all right.”
With a sigh of exasperation, she continues down the corridor.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Let your heart not be troubled.
Someone like me who's always fainting sees it coming a mile away.
And today, my body says I'm perfectly okay."
"…… Well.
If you say so, I guess it's alright."
Giving somewhat of an amazed sigh, Senpai continues walking down the hallway.

entries.japanese:
校門を通り抜けた。
　ここからの帰り道はお互い別方向になる。
「それじゃあここでお別れですね。
なんか、あっという間でした」
　……同感。
こっちももう少しうちの学校が広かったら良かったのに、と本気で思っていたりする。
entries.maoEnglish:
We passed through the school gates.
Our routes home split in opposite directions here.
“I suppose this is goodbye. That went by so quickly.”
I feel exactly the same. I find myself sincerely wishing our school grounds had been a little larger.
entries.mirrorMoon:
We walk out the gate.
From here, we have to go our separate ways.
"Well then, this is goodbye for now.
We got here pretty quickly."
…… I feel the same way.
I was really thinking it would be better if the school were a bit bigger.

entries.japanese:
「それじゃ先輩、また明日」
「はい。
また明日、学校でお会いしましょう」
　笑顔で返答して、先輩は別方向の帰り道を去っていく。
　それを軽く見届けてから、自分も屋敷への帰路についた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Well, see you tomorrow.”
“Yes. I’ll see you at school tomorrow.”
She answers with a smile and sets off down the road in the other direction.
After watching her go for a moment, I start home toward the estate.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Well, then, Senpai, see you tomorrow."
"Yes, let's meet at school tomorrow."
Smiling as she responds, Senpai disappears in the opposite direction.
After watching her go, I head down the street towards my house.

entries.japanese:
かまわず食べるサ。
　人の好意は素直に受けとるのが俺の信条なんだし。
entries.maoEnglish:
I’ll eat it, of course.
I have always believed in accepting kindness without making a fuss.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Never mind that and just eat.
I believe kindness should always be accepted.

entries.japanese:
「───食べる。
ハラ減ってますから、いただけるものなら何でも食べます」
　はい、少しぐらいなら正味期限も気になりません。
「それじゃ茶道部に行きましょうか。
部室ならお茶ぐらいだせますから」
　先輩はトテトテと早足で廊下を歩きだした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“───I’ll take it. I’m starving, so if it’s edible, I’ll eat it.”
Yes, even a slightly dubious expiration date would not deter me.
“Then shall we go to the tea club? I can at least make you some tea in the clubroom.”
She patters briskly away down the corridor.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---I'll take it.
I'm hungry, so if you don't mind, I'll eat it."
Yeah, even if it's a bit past the expiration date, I wouldn't mind.
"Then let's go to the tea ceremony room.
If we go there, I can get you some tea."
Senpai trots off down the hallway.

entries.japanese:
「では、いただきます」
　両手をあわせて先輩のお弁当に手をかける。
　ばくばくと遠慮なしで食べていると、先輩はじっーと俺の事を眺めていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Thanks for the food.”
I press my hands together, then attack her lunch.
As I devour it without the least restraint, she sits watching me intently.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Thanks for the meal."
I bring my hands together briefly and start to dig in to Senpai's lunch.
Munch, munch.
I eat without restraint while Senpai stares at me.

Munch munch.

entries.japanese:
ばくばく。
　ばくばぐばく。
　ばくばくばくばくばく。
entries.maoEnglish:
Munch, munch.
Munch-munch-munch.
Munchmunchmunchmunchmunch.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Munch.
Munch.
Munch.
Munch.
Munch.
Munch.
Munch.

entries.japanese:
「────ん」
　ごっくん、とお茶を飲む。
　先輩はまだじっーっとこっちを眺めていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“────Mmm”
I wash it down with a swallow of tea.
She is still staring.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----Mm."
I gulp some tea.
Senpai keeps watching me.

entries.japanese:
「お弁当、おいしいですか？」
「んー、冷めててイマイチです」
　……我ながらこの素直すぎる発言はどうかと思うんだけど、性格なので変えようがない。
　先輩はくすり、と小さく笑ってまっすぐに俺の目を見つめると、
「遠野くんって、達観してる」
　なんて、すごく優しい声で言った。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Is the lunch good?”
“Mmm, it’s cold, so not especially.”
Even I suspect that answer may be too honest, but that is simply how I am.
She laughs softly, meets my eyes, and
“You really are a little sage, aren’t you?”
she says in a remarkably gentle voice.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Does it taste good?"
"Mm, it's cold and not very good."
…… I think that comment was a little too honest myself, but it's my personality, so I can't change it.
Senpai gives a small laugh as she looks directly into my eyes.
"Tohno-kun, you have quite a philosophic outlook."
She says this kindly.

entries.japanese:
「……はあ。
わかんない人ですね、先輩は。
いきなりなんですか、それ」
「だってそうじゃないですか。
普通、人の食べかけのお弁当なんて食べませんよ。
遠野くんは世間体というものを気にしない人なんですね」
「───？
　そうかな、あんまり自覚はないけど」
　俺は、ただ自分に素直に生きているだけだから。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Honestly. I don’t understand you, Ciel. Where did that come from?”
“But it’s true. Most people wouldn’t eat someone else’s half-finished lunch. You don’t seem to care what other people think.”
“───Is that so? I’ve never really noticed.”
I simply live true to myself.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Huh?
I don't get you, Senpai.
Saying something like that all of a sudden."
"But it's true.
Normally, people wouldn't eat another person's half-eaten lunch like that.
But you don't seem to mind what others think of you, do you?"
"---?
Really?
I'm not that self-conscious."
I just live honestly.

entries.japanese:
けど、まわりの事を気にしないで暮らしていく事が達観しているっていうんなら、俺なんかよりこの人のほうがよっぽど達観している。
　俺だったら───みんなが無視してしまうような添え木の修理を、一人きりでやってしまうなんてコトはできない。
entries.maoEnglish:
But if ignoring the world’s opinions makes one a sage, she deserves the title far more than I do.
I could never have repaired that forgotten tree brace alone when everyone else simply walked past it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
But, if living life without caring what others think is philosophical, then this person is much more of a philosopher than I am.
If it was me---I could never mend the splints in the courtyard that everyone else ignores all by myself.

entries.japanese:
「俺から言わせてもらえば、先輩のほうがよっぽど達観してると思うけど。
　先輩はいつだって自分のペースで動いてるじゃないですか。
なんか、見ていて気持ちいいぐらい」
　素直な感想を口にする。
　もちろん誉め言葉だったんだけど、なぜか先輩は『そうですか』なんて、まるでアテにしていた宝くじが外れたみたいにうなだれた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“If you ask me, you’re much more of a sage.
You always move at your own pace. It’s actually refreshing to watch.”
I offer the compliment in complete sincerity.
For some reason, she murmurs a reply and droops like someone whose treasured lottery ticket has failed to win.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"In my opinion, I think you're more philosophical than I am, Senpai.
You're always living at your own pace.
It feels so good just to watch."
I speak openly.
Of course it was a compliment, but Senpai says "Oh, I see," and slumps in disappointment.

entries.japanese:
「あの……先輩？
　俺、なんか悪いこと言っちゃったかな」
「―――はい。
　だって、世間ではそういうのはおばさんくさいって言うじゃないですか。
わたしだって女の子なんですから、ショックうけます」
　……むむ。
先輩の中では達観している、という事はお年よりくさい、というコトらしい。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Um… did I say something wrong?”
“―――Yes.
People say that kind of composure makes a woman look matronly. I’m a girl too, so it hurts.”
Ah. Apparently, to Ciel, sage means old.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Um…… Senpai?
Did I say something bad?"
"--Yes.
Because normally, that's what they call an old spinster.
I'm a girl, so hearing that is a shock."
…… Hmmm.
For Senpai, that must mean she's acting old rather than being philosophical.

entries.japanese:
「なんだ、なら俺はじいさんくさいって事ですか。
失礼ですね、俺は前途多難な高校生です」
「あ、でも否定はできませんよ。
遠野くんはざぶとんとお茶が似合ってますから。
ゆったりしてて、まるでどこかのご隠居さんみたいです」
　くすくすと先輩は笑う。
　……せめて和服の似合う若旦那ぐらいにしてほしかったけど、先輩に言われるとご隠居も悪くはないかな、と思えた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Then you’re saying I seem like an old man? How rude; I’m a high-school student with a difficult future ahead of me.”
“Oh, I can’t deny it. You look perfectly natural on a floor cushion with tea in your hand. So calm and settled, like a retired gentleman.”
She giggles.
I would have preferred a dashing young master in traditional dress, but when she says it, even retired gentleman does not sound so bad.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Oh yeah?
So does that mean I'm acting like an old man now?
Well excuse me, I'm just a high school student bravely facing the dangers of life."
"Ah, but you can't deny it.
Because a sitting cushion and a cup of tea really suit you.
Always calm, you seem like a retired man."
Senpai giggles.
…… I wanted to hear I was more a guy that looks good in Japanese clothing, but if Senpai says a retired man, then maybe that isn't a bad thing.

entries.japanese:
「そっか。
それじゃ年寄同士、お茶でも飲みながら長話しでもするとしますか」
「そうですね。
それじゃあ気のすむまでお付き合いしましょうか、志貴さん」
　こぼれるような満面の笑みをうかべて、先輩は俺の湯呑みにトクトクとお茶を注いでくれた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I see. Then why don’t we two old folks drink tea and talk for a while?”
“Gladly. I’ll keep you company as long as you like, Shiki.”
Beaming, she pours a musical stream of tea into my cup.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Oh.
Well then, fellow old-timer, how about we have a long chat over a cup of tea?"
"I'd love to keep you company, Shiki-san."
With a beaming smile, Senpai pours some tea into my tea cup.

entries.japanese:
それから一時間。
　五時半まで話した俺たちは、校門が閉められる前に学校を出て、交差点で別れる事になった。
entries.maoEnglish:
An hour later.
At half past five, we finally leave before the gates close and part at the intersection.
entries.mirrorMoon:
An hour passes.
We talk together until five-thirty, then we walk out the gate before it closes and go our separate ways at the intersection.

entries.japanese:
坂道を上がりきって、屋敷のまわりを歩いていく。
　しばらく歩いて屋敷の正門に回りこむと、そこに翡翠が一人で立っているのが見えた。
「……？
　なにしてるんだろ、翡翠」
　首をかしげながら正門に向かう。
　と、翡翠はこちらに気がついて、ペコリと頭をさげてきた。
entries.maoEnglish:
I crest the hill and follow the road around the estate.
By the time I reach the front gate, I can see Hisui standing there alone.
“…What’s Hisui doing out there?”
I head toward the gate, puzzled.
Hisui notices me and bows.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I head up the road and draw near the mansion.
After a little more walking I see Hisui standing by herself at the front gate.
"……?
I wonder what Hisui is doing?"
Tilting my head to the side, I head for the front gate.
Hisui realizes I'm here and bows her head.

entries.japanese:
「お帰りなさいませ、志貴さま」
「―――あ、うん―――ただいま、翡翠」
　うやうやしく出迎えをされて、戸惑いながらもなんとか返答する。
「あの―――もしかして、俺が帰ってくるのを待っててくれたの？」
「はい。
主人の出迎えをするのは使用人の務めですから」
　さも当然のように、翡翠は眉ひとつ動かさずに言ってくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Welcome home, Master Shiki.”
“―――Ah, right―――I’m home, Hisui.”
Her ceremonious greeting flusters me, but I manage an answer.
“Um―――were you waiting here for me to come back?”
“Yes. It is a servant’s duty to welcome home the master of the house.”
Hisui says it as though it were obvious, without so much as raising an eyebrow.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Welcome back, Shiki-sama."
"---Ah, yeah---thanks, Hisui."
I can barely reply since I'm bewildered by the respectfulness of it all.
"Um---were you waiting for me to come home?"
"Yes.
Greeting the master is a servant's duty."
Answering very matter-of-factly, she doesn't even bat an eyelash.

entries.japanese:
「いや、あのさ翡翠。
出迎えてくれるのは正直嬉しいんだけど、わざわざ外で待ってなくていいよ。
　俺は勝手に帰ってくるから、帰ってきたなって気づいた時だけ声をかけてくれればいいから」
「―――――」
　翡翠はわずかに顔をくもらせる。
　……もしかすると。
　土曜日も日曜日も、翡翠はこうしてずっと俺の帰りを待っていたのかもしれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Listen, Hisui. I’m honestly glad you want to welcome me home, but you don’t have to wait outside.
I will come back on my own, so just say something whenever you happen to notice I am here.”
“―――――”
A faint shadow crosses Hisui’s face.
Maybe.
She may have waited here like this all through Saturday and Sunday too.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Um, Hisui, I'm truly happy you waited to greet me, but there's really no need to wait outside.
I'll come back on my own, so you can just greet me whenever you realize I'm back."
"-----"
Hisui's face clouds slightly.
…… Oh, maybe…
Maybe she was waiting for me to return like this on Saturday and Sunday.

entries.japanese:
「――翡翠、あのさ――」
「わかりました。
明日からはロビーで志貴さまのお帰りをお待ちいたします」
　ぺこり、と頭をさげて翡翠は屋敷の門を開けた。
　翡翠は門に手をかけたまま、こちらに背中を向けている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――Hisui, listen――”
“Understood. Beginning tomorrow, I shall await Master Shiki’s return in the foyer.”
Hisui bows and opens the gate.
With one hand still on it, she turns her back to me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"--Hisui, um--"
"I understand.
Starting from tomorrow, I will await your return in the lobby."
Hisui gives a quick bow and opens the mansion gate.
Hisui turns around as she does so.

entries.japanese:
「…………はあ」
　なんだか、話しかけられる雰囲気じゃない。
　屋敷の門をくぐると、翡翠は門を閉めて玄関まで歩いていき、やっぱり無言で扉を開けて俺をロビーまで先導した。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Haaah.”
She does not seem inclined to talk.
Once I pass through, Hisui closes the gate, walks to the front door, and silently opens it before leading me into the foyer.
entries.mirrorMoon:
………… *sigh*
For some reason, the atmosphere isn't exactly conducive to conversation.
Hisui closes the gate after I pass through, then she silently walks to the entrance to open the door and leads me into the lobby.

entries.japanese:
自室に帰ってきた。
　秋葉は習い事から帰っておらず、琥珀さんは夕食の支度、翡翠は屋敷の掃除があるとのことだ。
「―――まいったな、やることがない」
　いや、学生なんだから勉強とか復習とか暗記とかやらなくちゃいけない事はたくさんある。
　ただ、なんとなくなーんにもやる気にならない。
entries.maoEnglish:
I return to my room.
Akiha is still at her lessons, Kohaku is preparing dinner, and Hisui has the house to clean.
“―――Damn, I have nothing to do.”
No, I’m a student; I have plenty I should be doing—studying, reviewing, memorizing.
I just do not feel like doing any of it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I get to my room.
Akiha isn't back yet from her lessons, Kohaku-san is preparing dinner, and Hisui is cleaning the mansion.
"---Geez, there's nothing to do."
Well, there's quite a mountain of studying, reviewing, and memorizing a student like me has to do.
But, I just don't feel like doing anything.

entries.japanese:
ちらり、とアルクェイドの顔を思い浮かべた。
　良きにつけ悪きにつけ、忙しい二日間だったことの反動だろうか。
　しばらくは、何かをするよりぼんやりとしていたほうが、心が休まるような気がしていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
Arcueid’s face flits through my mind.
Maybe this is the backlash from two frantic days, for better or worse.
For a while, doing nothing at all seems more restful than trying to occupy myself.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Suddenly, Arcueid's face flashes in my mind.
Whether good or bad, it's probably just a reaction to the crazy two days I just had.
Perhaps spacing out here in my room will be good, giving my mind and heart a break.

entries.japanese:
だだっ広い食堂で一人の夕食を終えた後、琥珀さんに傷口の手当てをしてもらって自室に戻ってきた。
　夕食時になっても秋葉は帰ってこなかった。
習い事が長引いているので、外食をすることになったらしい。
　時計の針は夜の十時を大きく回っている。
　少し早いが体の疲れもあることだし、今夜は早めに眠るとしよう―――
entries.maoEnglish:
After eating alone in the cavernous dining room, I have Kohaku tend my wounds and return to my room.
Akiha still has not come home. Apparently her lesson ran late, so she decided to eat out.
It is well past ten.
A little early, perhaps, but I am exhausted, so I think I will turn in for the night―――
entries.mirrorMoon:
After eating dinner by myself in the large dining room, Kohaku-san treats my wounds and I go back to my room.
Akiha didn't make it back in time for dinner.
Her lesson was apparently going to last a while, so she was going to eat away from home.
It's past ten at night now.
It's a bit too early, but since I'm exhausted, I should sleep early tonight--

entries.japanese:
昼休みになったとたん、今まで授業に一時間も出てなかった男がやってきた。
「よう遠野！
　メシ食おうぜ、メシ！」
　何が嬉しいのか、有彦はとにかく威勢がいい。
entries.maoEnglish:
The instant lunch break begins, a certain boy who has not attended a single class all morning finally shows up.
“Yo, Tohno! Let’s eat—lunch, lunch!”
Whatever has him so delighted, Arihiko is bursting with energy.
entries.mirrorMoon:
At lunch break, that guy who didn't even show up for a single class arrives.
"Yo Tohno!
Food, let's get some food!"
He's happy about something, being even more energetic than usual.

entries.japanese:
「そりゃあメシは当然のように食べるけど、えらく機嫌がいいじゃないか。
なにかあったのか、有彦」
「おう。
ついさっきそこで先輩に昼メシいっしょにどうっすかって声をかけたらさ、断られたんだ」
「………………」
　不思議だ。
　先輩っていうとシエル先輩のことだろうけど、誘いを断られると嬉しいらしい、この友人は。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Obviously I am going to eat, but you are in a suspiciously good mood. What happened, Arihiko?”
“Yeah. I just asked Ciel if she wanted to have lunch with us, and she turned me down.”
“………………”
Strange.
He clearly means Ciel, but apparently this friend of mine enjoys being turned down.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Of course, food.
But you seem to be in a great mood.
Did something happen, Arihiko?"
"Yup.
I just asked Senpai if she wanted to eat lunch together, and she refused."
"………………"
That's odd.
"Senpai" must be referring to Ciel-senpai, but this guy seems to get happy when his offer is refused.

entries.japanese:
「あのさ。
有彦、そういう趣味だったっけ」
「いやいや、話は最後まで聞けって。
でな、先輩にどうしてダメなんだよう、って聞いたら『遠野くんが一緒だと、イヤです』だってさ！
　うわははははははははは！
　愉快だろう、遠野！」
「………………」
　不思議だ。
　どうして俺はこうゆう友達甲斐のない男と、中学時代から友人だったりするんだろう？
entries.maoEnglish:
“Tell me something, Arihiko. Have you always been into that?”
“No, no, hear the whole story. I asked her why not, and she said, ‘Not if Tohno is coming too.’ Wahahahahahaha! Is that not priceless, Tohno?”
“………………”
Strange.
Why have I kept this lousy excuse for a friend around since middle school?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hey, Arihiko, you have that sort of taste?"
"No, no, I'm not finished.
So I asked Senpai why not, and she said 'If Tohno-kun is there, then I don't want to come'!!
Uwahahahahahahahaha!
Isn't that great, Tohno!?"
"……………"
That's odd.
Why have I been friends with this guy since middle school?

entries.japanese:
「いやあ、嫌われたもんだな遠野！
　ライバルが減って嬉しいので、今日の昼メシはオレがおごってやろう！」
　ばんばん、とオレの背中を楽しそうに叩く有彦。
「……いや、おごってくれるのは嬉しいんだけど、先輩、俺のことを怒ってたのか？」
「ん？
　……えっーと、たしか『遠野くんも一緒ですか』って聞いてきて、うなずいたら顔を赤くしてたな。
おまえの名前を聞いた瞬間、怒りで頬が高揚したのかもしれヌ」
「……しれヌ、ってそれ、ちょっと違うんじゃないか有彦」
「さあな。
そうでないかもしれヌ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Boy, she really hates you, Tohno! I am so happy to have one less rival that lunch is on me today!”
Arihiko gleefully pounds me on the back.
“I am glad you are paying, but was Ciel angry with me?”
“Hm. Let me think; she asked, ‘Will Tohno be there too?’ When I nodded, her face turned red; perchance her cheeks flushed with rage the instant she heard your name.”
“Arihiko, I think you are using ‘perchance’ wrong.”
“Who knows? Perchance not.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Oh man, she really hates you Tohno!
A rival's loss is my gain, so I'll treat you to lunch today!"
Arihiko happily slaps my back.
"…… Well, I'm happy you're treating me, but Senpai was angry at me?"
"N?
…… well, after she asked 'will Tohno-kun be with us?' and I nodded, her face turned all red.
As soon as she heard your name, her face probably burned with anger."
"…… Probably?
Isn't that a little different, Arihiko?"
"Maybe.
Maybe not."

entries.japanese:
……有彦の情報はアテにならない。
　たしかに朝の先輩は怒っていたようだったけど、こっちには先輩に怒られる理由がてんでわからない。
「……まさか、俺がどんな夢を見たのか気づいたわけじゃあるまいし」
　あれだけの会話でそれがわかったら、先輩は将来名探偵になれるだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
Arihiko is not a reliable source.
Ciel certainly seemed angry that morning, but I have no idea what I did to offend her.
There is no way she could tell what I dreamed about.
If she worked that out from our brief conversation, she has a brilliant future as a detective.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Arihiko's story can't be trusted.
Certainly Senpai did seem angry this morning, but I don't know why she would be.
"…… No way, she couldn't have realized what kind of dream I had."
If she could figure that out from that one conversation, she'd make a great detective.

entries.japanese:
「ほら、ブツブツ言ってないで行くぞ遠野。
食堂の席は利用客の半分しかないんだからな」
「あ―――いや、俺は―――」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Quit muttering and come on, Tohno. The cafeteria has half as many seats as it has customers.”
“Ah―――no, I―――”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hey, stop whining and let's go, Tohno.
There's only seats enough for half the people using the cafeteria."
"Ah---no, I---"

entries.japanese:
先輩が怒っている理由といったら朝の一件以外思いつかない。
　……先輩が怒っているようには見えなかったけど、怒っているというのならあまりしつこく会いに行くのもなんだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
The only reason I can imagine for Ciel to be angry is what happened this morning.
She did not look angry, but if she is, perhaps I should not keep pestering her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Senpai can't be mad at anything else other than the incident this morning.
…… Senpai didn't seem angry this morning, but if she is angry, then I probably shouldn't go meet her.

entries.japanese:
「……そうだな。
今日はおとなしく食堂に行くとするか」
「おう、そうしろそうしろ。
んじゃあまあ急ぐぞ。
食堂の席は利用客の半分しかないんだからな」
　ずるずる、と有彦は人の腕を強引に引きずっていく。
entries.maoEnglish:
“All right… I will be good and eat in the cafeteria today.”
“That is the spirit. Now move it. The cafeteria only has half as many seats as it has customers.”
Arihiko grabs my arm and forcibly drags me away.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Yeah, maybe I should just go to the cafeteria today."
"Yeah, do that.
C'mon, hurry up.
There's only enough space for half the people using the cafeteria."
Arihiko takes me by the arm and pulls me off.

entries.japanese:
有彦と席を並べて昼食をとる。
　うちの学校の食堂にはテレビが置かれていて、その日の朝のニュースをビデオで流す、という教育にいいんだか悪いんだか紙一重のことをやっている。
　とりあえず、いま流れているニュースはコンビニエンスストアで酔っ払い客が店員を刺殺した、という、とりあえずむこう三日間ぐらいはコンビニに行きたくなくなるような内容だった。
entries.maoEnglish:
Arihiko and I sit together for lunch.
Our cafeteria has a television, and for reasons poised delicately between educational and appalling, it plays a recording of that morning’s news.
The current story concerns a drunken customer stabbing a convenience-store clerk to death—exactly the sort of report that makes you avoid convenience stores for the next three days.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I sit next to Arihiko and eat my lunch.
My school's cafeteria has a television, and for better or worse for our education, they play back the morning news they recorded this morning.
At any rate, the news they are playing back is talking about a drunk customer stabbing to death a convenience store employee, something that makes me not want to go to a convenience store for at least a few days.

entries.japanese:
「ぶっそうな世の中だねえ。
無差別に人を殺してる通り魔はいるわ、酔っ払いは人を刺すわ。
　こんなんじゃ安心して夜遊びもできねえってもんだよな、ほんと」
　有彦は、わりと真剣にニュースを見ているようだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Dangerous world out there. First some lunatic starts killing strangers, then a drunk goes and stabs somebody.
A guy can’t even go out at night in peace anymore.”
Arihiko seems to be watching the news with surprising seriousness.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"What a dangerous world we live in.
Indiscriminate serial killers, drunken people stabbing people.
A man can't even feel safe playing around at night anymore."
Arihiko seems like he is seriously watching the news.

entries.japanese:
「……まあ、たしかに物騒だけど。
とりあえず通り魔事件はもう起きないんだから、いつも通りっていうことじゃないのか」
「そなの？
　通り魔って捕まったんだ？」
「いや、捕まってはいないだろうけど」
―――とりあえず、ネロはもうこの世にはいない。
　だから現代の吸血鬼なんていう俗な見出しがテレビに映ることもないし、もう、意味もなく殺される『誰か』がでることもない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“It’s dangerous, sure. But the random killings are over, so I’d say things are back to normal.”
“Really? They catch the guy?”
“No, I don’t think anyone caught him.”
―――But Nrvnqsr is no longer in this world.
So no cheap headline about a MODERN-DAY VAMPIRE will appear on that screen, and no nameless victim will be murdered for no reason again.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Well, certainly it is dangerous.
But at least those serial killings won't happen anymore, so things should be like usual."
"Oh really?
Did they catch the serial killer?"
"No, they haven't caught him…"
---But Nrvnqsr is no longer in this world.
So the stupid title of the modern day vampire killings shouldn't be showing up in the news anymore and there will be no more of those meaningless killings.

entries.japanese:
「ともかく、もうあんなふざけた事件は起きないし、犠牲者もでないってこと。
この街もようやく以前に戻ったんだよ」
「ふぅん、知らなかった。
やっぱりニュースは見てないとダメなんかなあ」
　難しそうに顔をしかめて、有彦は熱心にニュースを眺めていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“The point is, those ridiculous murders are over, and there will be no more victims. This city is finally back to the way it was.”
“Huh, I did not know that. Guess I really ought to watch the news.”
Frowning as if wrestling with a difficult problem, Arihiko studies the television intently.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Anyway, those terrible incidents won't happen anymore; There won't be any more victims, and the streets will be back to normal."
"Hmmmh, I didn't know.
I guess I should watch the news more often."
Making a strained face, Arihiko earnestly stares at the news.

entries.japanese:
「―――今日はパスする。
パン買って、一人で食べる」
「そなの？
　んじゃ、俺は一人で行くぜ」
　有彦は食堂に向かっていった。
「……さて」
　こっちも席を立って、先輩のいそうな茶道室に行く事にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――I will pass today. I will just buy some bread and eat alone.”
“Oh, yeah? Then I am going without you.”
Arihiko heads for the cafeteria.
“Right…”
I rise too and make my way toward the tea-ceremony room, where Ciel is likely to be.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---I'll pass.
I'm going to buy some bread and eat by myself."
"Really?
Then I'll go ahead."
Arihiko goes off to the cafeteria.
"…… Well then."
I also get out of my chair and head over to the tea club room, where Senpai may be.

entries.japanese:
……茶道室の前にやってきた。
　もちろんここに来る前に購買によって、自分の分の昼食は買ってきてある。
　コンコン。
　茶道室の扉をノックする。
　中でごそごそという音がして、人の気配らしきものがやってきた。
entries.maoEnglish:
I arrive outside the tea-ceremony room.
Naturally, I stopped at the school store on my way and bought my own lunch.
Knock, knock.
I knock on the door.
Something rustles inside, and a presence approaches from the other side.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… I stand before the tea ceremony room.

Of course, I bought some food for myself before I came.
Knock-knock.
I tap on the door.
I hear some scuffling inside and sense a person on the other side.

entries.japanese:
「はい、どなたですか」
　扉ごしに先輩の声が聞こえてくる。
「俺だけど。
先輩、お昼ごはん一緒に食べない？」
　……返事がない。
「先輩、お昼ごはんだってば」
「……遠野くんとは食べません」
　扉ごしの声は元気がない。
　少し迷ってから、
entries.maoEnglish:
“Yes, who is it?”
Ciel’s voice comes through the door.
“It is me. Ciel, want to have lunch together?”
No answer.
“Ciel, I said it is lunchtime.”
“I am not eating with you, Tohno.”
Her voice sounds dispirited.
After a moment’s hesitation
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yes, who is it?"
I can hear Senpai's voice through the door.
"It's me.
Senpai, would you like to eat lunch with me?"
…… There's no answer.
"Senpai, I said lunch."
"…… I'm not eating with you, Tohno-kun."
That voice doesn't sound happy at all.
I'm not sure what to do,

entries.japanese:
「……先輩、俺なにか悪いことしました？」
　と、率直に訊ねてみた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ciel, did I do something wrong?”
I decide to ask her plainly.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Senpai, did I do something wrong?"
I ask her directly.

entries.japanese:
「……………」
　返事はない。
　ただ、扉の向こうで先輩が困っているような、そんな気配だけが伝わってくる。
「あの、先輩？」
　コンコン、と扉をノックする。
　それから数秒。
　どことなくじれったい沈黙のあと、扉ごしに先輩の声が聞こえてきた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
No answer.
I can only sense that she is at a loss on the other side of the door.
“Um, Ciel?”
I knock again.
Several seconds pass.
After a silence that somehow feels painfully drawn out, Ciel’s voice finally comes through the door.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……………"
There's no answer.
I can feel her uneasiness through the door.
"Um, Senpai?"
Knock-knock.
I try again.
After a few seconds…
After a very uncomfortable silence, I hear Senpai's voice once more.

entries.japanese:
「……別に、遠野くんは悪くありません。
遠野くんと顔を合わせられないのはわたしの事情ですから」
「？
　先輩の事情って、なんだよ」
「いいですから、遠野くんはお一人で食事をしてください！
　放課後ぐらいまでには気持ちが落ち着いてくれるでしょうから、それまでは遠野くんとは会いませんっ！」
entries.maoEnglish:
“No, Tohno, you have done nothing wrong. It is my own circumstances that prevent me from facing you.”
“Your circumstances? What do you mean?”
“Never mind, just eat by yourself! I should have my feelings under control by the end of the school day, and until then I refuse to see you!”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Not really, you're not at fault here.
I can't see you right now because of my circumstances."
"?
What's are your circumstances, Senpai?"
"It's okay, so just please eat by yourself!
I'll calm down by the time school ends, so until then, I won't see you!"

entries.japanese:
「…………う」
　なかば叱りつけるような先輩の声に圧されて、仕方なく白旗をあげた。
「わかりました。
それじゃ今は教室に戻ります」
　扉ごしにそう告げて、茶道室の前を後にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ugh.”
Her voice is half a scolding, and it leaves me no choice but to surrender.
“All right. I’ll go back to the classroom for now.”
I say it through the door, then leave the tea-ceremony room behind.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"………… Uh."
Her scolding voice backs me up and I raise the white flag.
"I understand.
Then I'll go back to my classroom."
Telling her through the door, I leave the tea ceremony room behind.

entries.japanese:
「カレーパン、あるよ」
　という、物量作戦に出た。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’ve got curry bread.”
I try the brute-force approach.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I have some curry bread."
I pull out my secret weapon.

entries.japanese:
「遠野くん、わたしが食べ物につられる人間だって思ってるんですかっ！？」
　扉ごしに先輩が怒鳴る。
　……さすがに百円でおつりが来るような食べ物ではつれないらしい
「……………」
　まいったな。
このまま強引に中に入ったらますます怒られそうだし、今日は退散するしかないのかもしれない。
―――と。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Tohno, do you really think I am someone you can lure with food?!”
Ciel shouts through the door.
Apparently, something cheap enough to leave change from a hundred yen will not tempt her
“……………”
Damn; forcing my way inside would only make her angrier. Perhaps I have no choice but to retreat for today.
―――Just then.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Tohno-kun, do you think I can just be bought with food!?"
Senpai shouts from the other side.
…… Maybe this less than one hundred yen bread didn't work.
"……………"
Geez.
I think trying to barge in would make her more angry, so I guess I should just go back.
---And then,

entries.japanese:
「まあ、それはそれでもらっておきます」
　ガラリと扉を開けて、先輩が現れた。
「せ、先輩――？」
「考えてみたら、遠野くんに八つ当たりする言われはないですから。
せっかく来ていただいたお客さんを追い返すなんて、失礼です」
　顔を赤くして、なにやら言い訳めいた事をぶつぶつと言っている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Well, I suppose I can take that off your hands.”
The door rattles open, and there she is.
“C-Ciel――?”
“On second thought, I have no right to take my frustration out on you. It would be terribly rude to turn away a visitor who came all this way.”
Her face bright red, she mutters one excuse after another.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Well, I guess I'll have some though."
She opens the door and stands in front of me.
"Se, Senpai--?"
"Come to think of it, I shouldn't be taking this out on you Tohno-kun.
Turning away a guest that came here would be a little rude."
With a red face, she mumbles something like an excuse.

entries.japanese:
「先輩、それってつまり、一緒にお昼を食べていいってこと？」
「……ええっと、そうとってもらってかまいません。
そんなに和室が好きなんでしたら、どうぞ中に入ってください」
　先輩は茶道室の中に戻っていく。
　その後に続いて、こっちも茶道室に入っていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“So, does that mean I can come in and have lunch with you?”
“Um, you may take it that way if you like. Since you are evidently so fond of Japanese-style rooms, please come inside.”
Ciel retreats into the tea-ceremony room.
I follow her inside.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Senpai, does that mean, we can eat lunch together?"
"…… Ummm, I don't mind if you take it that way.
If you like this room that much, then please come in."
Senpai goes into the tea ceremony room.
Following behind her, I walk inside.

entries.japanese:
先輩と昼食を一緒に食べる。
　有彦の話と、さっきの先輩の態度から考えるに先輩はいたくご機嫌ななめのハズなのだが、どうもそんなコトはないみたいだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
We eat lunch together.
From what Arihiko told me and the way she acted earlier, she ought to be in a foul mood, but now there’s no sign of it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I start to eat with Senpai.
Even though I got the impression that she was in a bad mood from Arihiko and her reaction back then, it certainly doesn't seem that way.

entries.japanese:
「……先輩。
有彦から聞いたんだけど、俺の事を怒ってたって、どうして？」
「え――いえ、べつに遠野くんのことを怒ってたわけじゃないんです。
そのですね、遠野くんに対してというより、遠野くんの背後っていうか、その……たぶん、遠野くんの無神経さに怒ってたんじゃないでしょうか」
「……ちょっと先輩。
いつも難解な人だけど、今日は輪をかけて難しいな。
俺の無神経さに怒るのはいいけど、なんだよそのたぶんって。
　先輩、自分の事わからないのか？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ciel, Arihiko told me you were angry with me. Why?”
“Eh――no, I was not angry with you exactly. It was less about you than what was behind you, or rather, well, perhaps I was angry at how insensitive you were.”
“Hold on, Ciel. You are difficult enough to follow on an ordinary day, but today is a new record. It is fine to be angry at my insensitivity, but what is this ‘perhaps’ business?
Ciel, do you not understand yourself?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Senpai.
I heard this from Arihiko, but you're angry at me?
How come?"
"Eh--no, I'm not really angry at you.
It's more of an indirect thing…… Maybe, it's more your insensitivity?"
"…… Wait a sec Senpai.
You're normally a hard person to understand, but today you're even more so.
If you're angry at my insensitivity, that's fine, but what do you mean by 'maybe'?
Senpai, you don't understand how you feel?"

entries.japanese:
「はあ。
ちょっと自信はありません。
わたし、あんまり自分に関心はありませんから」
　謝るような声で、先輩はそんな事を口にした。
「―――きっと、自分のことなんて好きじゃないんです、わたし」
「……先輩？」
　先輩は黙り込んだまま、こっちを見ない。
