　……本当に、よっぽど嬉しいのか、アルクェイドの笑顔はすごく輝いてる。
「でもいいの？
　志貴、また死ぬような目にあうかもしれないわよ」
「それぐらい覚悟してる。
それにね、もとから俺の目はこういうコトのためにあるようなものなんだ。
―――子供のころ、そう教えてくれた人がいた。
　人にない力があるんなら、人にできない事をするべきだって。
きっと、これがそうなんだ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Yes! If you’re helping me, Shiki, there’s nothing we can’t do!”
She must truly be delighted; her smile is radiant.
“Are you certain? You may come close to dying again.”
“I’m prepared for that. Besides, perhaps these eyes were always meant for something like this. Someone taught me that when I was a child.
If you possess a power no one else has, you should use it to do what no one else can. I think this must be what they meant.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yeah---!
If you help me, there's nothing we can't do---!"
…… Her face beams brilliantly and she seems extremely happy.
"But, is it okay?
Shiki, you may have to face death again."
"I'm ready.
And, I think that's why I have these eyes to begin with.
----When I was a child, someone told me this.
That if I have the power others do not, I should do things that others cannot.
I think this is that kind of thing."

entries.japanese:
「ふーん……志貴の事情は知らないけど」
「なんか、それっていいね」
　……アルクェイドはすごく上機嫌だ。
　かくいう自分も、彼女につられてすごく気持ちが上向きになってはいるんだけど。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hmm… I don’t know your circumstances, Shiki, but…”
“There’s something nice about that.”
Arcueid is in a wonderful mood.
Her high spirits are lifting mine as well.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Oh?
…… I don't really know your circumstances."
"But, that sounds good."
…… Arcueid is in an incredibly good mood.
And being with her puts me in a good mood as well.

entries.japanese:
「さて、それじゃあこれからどうするんだ。
またさっきみたいに街を歩いて死者を探すの？」
「そうね、今はそれぐらいしか手はないかな。
さっきので十二人目だから、そろそろ死者も打ち止めだと思う。
この街にいる死者を全員潰してしまえば親元の吸血鬼が出て来ざるをえなくなるから、それまでは残りの死者を探すって方針だけど」
　それでもいい？
　とアルクェイドは視線で問いただしてくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“So what do we do now? Walk the streets again and look for more of the Dead?”
“For now, that’s about all we can do. The man just now made twelve, so there can’t be many of the Dead left. Once we destroy every one in the city, the vampire who spawned them will have no choice but to come out. Until then, we keep hunting the survivors.”
Arcueid’s eyes ask whether I’m all right with that.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"But, what do we do now?
Do you want to search for more of The Dead like before?"
"Yeah, I think that's all we can do for now.
The one before was the twelfth, so I don't think there's many more.
The parent vampire will have to come out once they all are destroyed, so we have to hunt the remaining ones for now.
Is that still okay?", she asks.

entries.japanese:
「いいもなにも、俺はアルクェイドに付き合うだけだよ。
アルクェイドがそうするっていうんなら、大人しくしたがうさ。
――じゃ、もう一度街に行くか」
「あ、今夜はもういいの。
効率よく死者を操るためにはね、それなりの活動ルートを定めているもので、一晩に複数の死者は活動させないと思う。
　ただでさえ数が減ってきているんだから、むこうも無闇に活動させないでしょうし」
「―――そうなの？
　でも、それじゃあアルクェイドから死者を隠そうとするんじゃないのか、その『敵』ってヤツは」
entries.maoEnglish:
“It isn’t for me to object. I’m following your lead, Arcueid. If that’s what you want, I’ll behave and do as I’m told. So—shall we head back into town?”
“Oh, we’re done for tonight. To control the Dead efficiently, you establish routes for them, and I doubt our enemy would send more than one out in a single night.
Their numbers are already dwindling, so there’s even less reason to waste them.”
“Really? But then wouldn’t this ‘enemy’ just hide the rest from you?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Anything is fine, I'm just with you.
If you lead, then I'll follow.
--Well, shall we start again?"
"Ah, no, that's good for tonight.
They usually follow a fixed route, and the other Dead will probably not be out tonight.
Since they are fewer in number, I don't think he'll let them all come out at once."
"---Oh really?
But, doesn't that mean this 'enemy' will try to hide The Dead from you, Arcueid?"

entries.japanese:
「基本的にはね。
けど、『敵』が吸血鬼である以上、どうしても他者から血や精を搾取しないと存在してられないのよ。
　だから、むこうはわたしに狙われてるってわかっていても、最低限の食料を得るために死者を出すしかないっていうわけ」
―――はあ。
　で、その最低限の死者が、さっきの男性だったわけか。
entries.maoEnglish:
“That would be the sensible thing. But a vampire can’t survive without draining blood and vital essence from others.
Even knowing I’m hunting it, our enemy still has to send out the Dead to secure the bare minimum of food.”
―――I see.
So the man back there was the minimum it could risk sending out.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Basically.
But since this 'enemy' is a vampire, he needs to steal the blood and energy of others.
So, even though he knows I'm searching for them, he has to send The Dead out to get the minimal blood he needs."
---*sigh*
Then, the minimal Dead he sent out was that man from before, huh.

entries.japanese:
「そういうこと。
だから今夜は、これ以上探し回っても無駄だと思う」
「……まあ、俺はどうでもいいけど。
なんだかまだるっこしいな、それ」
「ええ。
もともと吸血鬼退治は面倒なものなの。
この街のどこかにある『敵』の棺を探しあてるんだから、そう簡単には終わらないわ」
　アルクェイドは俺から手を離すと、タン、という軽い足取りでうしろに跳んだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Exactly. Which means there’s no point searching any longer tonight.”
“…Fine by me, but this is awfully slow going.”
“Hunting vampires always is. We have to find our enemy’s coffin somewhere in this entire city. It was never going to end quickly.”
Arcueid releases my hand and springs lightly backward.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"So, searching further tonight will be useless, I think."
"…… Well, I don't mind.
It is tedious though."
"Yeah, hunting vampires is tedious work.
We have to find the coffin of this 'enemy' somewhere in this city, so it won't be easy."
Arcueid lets go of my hand and jumps back softly.

entries.japanese:
「アルクェイド……？」
「今夜はここでお別れにしましょう。
どうせ、またすぐ明日に会えるんだから」
　アルクェイドは踊るようなステップで、こっちを見たまま遠ざかっていく。
「明日って―――ちょっと待て、待ち合わせ場所とかどうするんだよ……！」
「ここでいいよ。
時間は―――そうね、十時ごろがちょうどいいかな」
　笑顔で、実にかってに約束をする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Arcueid…?”
“Let’s say good night here. We’ll be seeing each other again tomorrow anyway.”
She dances away in buoyant little steps, still facing me.
“Tomorrow—wait! Where are we even supposed to meet?”
“Right here is fine. As for the time… I think ten should be perfect.”
Beaming, she makes the arrangement entirely on her own.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Arcueid……?"
"Let's say goodbye for tonight.
We'll meet tomorrow.
With her dance-like steps, she watches me as she gets farther away.
"Tomorrow---wait, where should we meet……!?"
"Here's fine.
The time---yeah, around ten o'clock should be fine."
With a smile, she makes that promise.

entries.japanese:
「おやすみなさい、志貴。
また明日、ここでね！
　と。
　手をふって、アルクェイドは去っていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Good night, Shiki. See you right here tomorrow!”
And with that.
Arcueid waves and leaves.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Good night, Shiki.
I'll see you here tomorrow!"
And,
waving her hand, Arcueid disappears.

entries.japanese:
―――屋敷に帰ってきた。
　時刻は夜の一時半。
　屋敷の明かりは、完全に消え去っている。
「………まずい、かな」
　屋敷の門に手をかける。
　がちん、という音。
　門には頑丈そうな錠が内側からかけられていた。
「―――まいったな。
切るわけにもいかないし」
　少し悩む。
　悩んでから、門を自力でよじのぼる事にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――I made it back to the mansion.
It was half past one in the morning.
Every light in the house had gone out.
“…This could be bad.”
I tried the front gate.
Clank.
A formidable-looking lock had been fastened on the inside.
“Wonderful. It’s not as if I can cut through it.”
I think it over.
Then decide to climb the gate myself.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---I get back to the mansion.
It's about one-thirty in the morning.
The mansion is completely dark.
"……… This can't be good."
I put my hand on the mansion gate.
Ka-chang.
A sturdy chain holds it closed.
"---Dang.
I shouldn't cut this."
I think a bit.
Then, I decide to climb over the gate.

entries.japanese:
……疲れた。
　ドロボウさんよろしくで門をよじ登って、玄関にたどり着く。
　門は鍵がかかっていたが、玄関の扉は開いていた。
「……翡翠、ちゃんと開けててくれたんだ」
　ほう、と感謝の吐息がもれる。
　秋葉や琥珀さんたちを起こさないように、抜き足で屋敷の中へと入っていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
…That was exhausting.
After scaling the gate like a common burglar, I reached the front entrance.
The gate had been locked, but the front door was open.
“…Hisui left it open for me.”
A grateful sigh escaped me.
I crept inside on tiptoe, careful not to wake Akiha, Kohaku, or anyone else.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… I'm exhausted.
After sneaking over the wall like a thief, I quietly make my way to the doorway.
The gate was locked, but the door isn't.
"…… It must have been Hisui."
I give a sigh of thanks.
So as not to wake Akiha, Kohaku-san or Hisui, I sneak my way through the mansion.

entries.japanese:
「――――――ふう」
　一息ついて、ベッドに腰をかける。
「………………」
　アルクェイドとの約束。
　なんの因果か、また厄介なコトに足を踏み入れた遠野志貴。
「――――仕方ないじゃないか。
だってさ、放っておけなかったんだから」
　それとも、放っておきたくなかったのか。
「そりゃあ……アルクェイドのことは、好きだけど」
　けど、それって愛情なんだろうか。
　自分の気持ちがよく解らない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Whew…”
I sat on the edge of the bed and caught my breath.
“……”
My promise to Arcueid.
By some perversity of fate, Shiki Tohno had gone and entangled himself in trouble all over again.
“What else could I do? I couldn’t just leave her to it.”
Or had I simply not wanted to?
“I mean… I do like Arcueid.”
But was that love?
I couldn’t make sense of my own feelings.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------Whew."
Letting out a breath, I lay down on my bed.
"………………"
My promise to Arcueid.
Maybe it's fate, but you've gotten yourself tangled up in trouble again, Tohno Shiki.
"----Could I help it?
I just can't leave her alone."
Or maybe I didn't want to leave her alone?
"Well…… I do like Arcueid."
But is that love?
I don't even know my feelings.

entries.japanese:
ともかく、明日からまたアルクェイドの手伝いをする事になったんだ。
　今は余計なことは考えず、ゆっくりと体を休めて明日にそなえるとしよう――――
entries.maoEnglish:
Whatever the answer, I was going to be helping Arcueid again starting tomorrow.
For now, I would put every other thought aside, rest properly, and save my strength for tomorrow――――
entries.mirrorMoon:
At any rate, it looks like I'll be helping Arcueid once again starting tomorrow.
So for now, I shouldn't think of anything else but getting a good night's sleep----

entries.japanese:
―――眠れない。
　目を閉じると、なにか色々なものが浮かんでくる。
　アルクェイドのこと。
　この街に巣くっている吸血鬼のこと。
　……黒い法衣姿の、先輩のこと。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――I couldn’t sleep.
Whenever I closed my eyes, one thing after another floated into view.
Arcueid.
The vampire nesting somewhere in the city.
And the girl from school, clad in black vestments…
entries.mirrorMoon:
---I can't sleep.
If I close my eyes, so many things come to mind.
About Arcueid.
About this vampire lurking the streets.
…… About the black-clothed Senpai.

entries.japanese:
「――――」
　……眠れない。
　仕方ない、こういう時は読書にかぎる。
　たしかこの前、読みかけの本があったハズだけど――――
entries.maoEnglish:
“……”
I couldn’t sleep.
At times like this, there was nothing for it but a book.
I was sure I had left one half-finished the other day—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----"
…… I can't sleep.
At times like this, reading is good.
I know there was a book I was reading before----

entries.japanese: 一番初めの感情は、むしろ憐憫だった。
entries.maoEnglish: The first emotion I felt was, more than anything, pity.
entries.mirrorMoon: The first feeling was rather one of pity.

entries.japanese:
怒りでも失望でもない。
　ただ、目にうつるすべてのものが哀れに思えた。
（無論、最も哀れなのはこの身ではあるのだが）
entries.maoEnglish:
Not anger. Not disappointment.
Everything my eyes beheld merely struck me as pitiful. Naturally, this body of mine was the most pitiful thing of all.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Not anger, not despair.
Just, I thought everything before my eyes was pitiful.
(Of course, the most pitiful thing is myself.)

entries.japanese:
際限なく壊れていく命。
　際限なく薄れていく営み。
　際限なく忘れていく時間。
　みな落ちるだけだ。
　なのに懸命に存在しようとあがき、それが叶わぬと識ると生み続ける。
　生み出し続ける。
　結局、それらさえ亡くなるというのに、それではあまりにも報われない。
entries.maoEnglish:
Lives breaking without end.
Human endeavor fading without end.
Time forgotten without end.
Everything only falls away.
Yet all things struggle desperately to remain, and when they learn that cannot be, they beget more life.
They go on creating.
Those creations will perish in turn, of course. The whole endeavor is too cruelly unrewarded.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Life which breaks down without limit.
Daily life which fades without limit.
Time which is forgotten without limit.
Everyone only falls.
And yet everyone still struggles desperately to continue existing, and when they judge that it is not possible, they continue to reproduce.
Continuing to reproduce.
In the end, even that dies, but there is no recompensation.

entries.japanese:
無論、死にゆく存在が報われないのではない。
　我々には初めから救いなどない。
　報われないのは、その試み。
　永遠を望もうとする、気高い、およそ一文にもならぬほど需要のない、誰も求めてなぞいない祈りだ。
　壊れていくものには一切の興味はない。
　もし私に死というものが視覚でき理解できるのならば、多少の関心はもてるだろうが。
entries.maoEnglish:
Not that the dying themselves go unrewarded.
There was never any salvation for us to begin with.
What goes unrewarded is the attempt.
A noble prayer for eternity, worth less than a penny because no one has any use for it—a prayer no one ever asked to hear.
Things that break hold no interest for me.
Perhaps they would inspire some small curiosity if I could see death and comprehend it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Of course, it is not those who die who are not recompensated.
We had no hope to begin with.
What is not recompensated are the attempts.
The noble wish, the yearning for eternity which everyone longs for yet can not achieve.
I have no interest whatsoever in the things that break down.
If I could see death and understand it, maybe I'll take a bit of an interest.

entries.japanese:
およそ計測不可能なほど繰り返され、なお繰り返されるその祈り。
　もはや滑稽とさえされるその祈りを、ただ一つの清らかなものに代えようと思った。
　方法は言うまでもない。
　祈りは、叶えられた時点で結果となる。
　それだけを目的として生きてきた。
　別段信念があったわけではない。
　私が最初に覚えた言葉が、永遠という単語であっただけの話だ。
entries.maoEnglish:
That prayer, repeated beyond all measure and then repeated still, had long since become an object of ridicule.
I resolved to transform it into the one pure thing in this world.
The means hardly need stating.
The moment a prayer is granted, it ceases to be a prayer and becomes a result.
I lived for that purpose alone.
Not from any particular conviction.
It merely happened that the first word I ever learned was eternity.
entries.mirrorMoon:
A repetition nearly impossible to measure, yet this wish repeats itself.
I thought to replace this almost-comical cycle of wishes with one pure thing.
There is no need to state the method.
A wish becomes a result after it is granted.
I lived solely for that reason.
It could not be termed "conviction".
Just, the first word I learned happened to be "eternity".

entries.japanese:
……ふうん。
それで、とりあえず一番手近な永遠を手に入れようとするんだね、君は。
entries.maoEnglish: …I see. And so, for the present, you mean to seize the nearest eternity within your reach.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Oh?
So you intend to get the eternity closest to you?

entries.japanese:
まさか。
彼らはただ年老いにくく、死ににくいだけの種ですよ。
彼らの仲間入りをするのは、たんにこの身の限界にいきついてしまったからです。
これ以上先に進むのならば、この器では時間がかかる。
entries.maoEnglish: Hardly. Their kind merely ages slowly and dies with difficulty. I am joining them only because this body has reached its limits. To proceed any farther in this vessel would consume too much time.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Of course not.
They are only a species that age slower and die harder.
I am becoming one of them only because this body has reached its limit.
If I am to go farther on, it will take time in this body.

entries.japanese:
永遠を求める君が生き急ぐとは皮肉な話だね。
　それで、明日にでもココを去るのか。
entries.maoEnglish:
How ironic that a seeker of eternity should be in such a hurry to live.
Will you leave this place as early as tomorrow, then?
entries.mirrorMoon:
It's ironic that you, the one that goes after eternity, hurries with things.
So you plan on leaving here tomorrow?

entries.japanese:
埋葬教室に関しては貴女に一任しますよ。
どうせ司祭の席は一つしか空いていない。
ここに上り詰めるまでで父の遺産はすべて使いきりましたし。
潮時だったんですよ、これが。
entries.maoEnglish: I leave the Department of Burial in your hands. Only one priest’s seat is vacant in any case, and climbing this far has exhausted the whole of my father’s inheritance. It was time for me to leave.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I'll leave the Burial Agency to you.
In the first place, there is only one empty seat for the priesthood.
I used up all my father's inheritance getting this far, so it is about time I quit.

entries.japanese:
……まあいいけどね。
それで君は自分の魔術理論を完成させるわけか。
あたしはここから離れる気はないから、君に合わせて生きていく事はできんな。
　ま、幸いあたしは女だ。
さっさと子供を産んで君の事を伝えるとしよう。
entries.maoEnglish: …Fine by me. So this is how you intend to complete your theory of magecraft. I have no desire to leave this place, so I cannot arrange my life around yours. Fortunately, I am a woman. I shall have a child soon and make certain your story survives.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Well, that's fine.
So you are going to complete your magic theory.
I have no intention of leaving here, and I can't live with you.
Well, fortunately, I am a woman.
I'll quickly bear a child and tell it all about you.

entries.japanese:
ほう。
なんと伝えますか、ナルバレック。
entries.maoEnglish: Indeed? And what story will you tell, Narbareck?
entries.mirrorMoon:
Oh?
What will you tell it, Narbarek?

entries.japanese:
そうだな、あと百年もたてば新参の死徒が台頭してくる。
そいつの相手をするのは無意味だから無視してしまえ、という口伝にしよう。
entries.maoEnglish: Let me see. In another hundred years, a newly risen Dead Apostle will appear. I shall pass down instructions to ignore him, since dealing with the creature would be a waste of time.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Let's see.
I'll tell it something like--After around a hundred years, another newcomer Dead Apostle will appear.
It is pointless to take notice of him, so ignore him.

entries.japanese:
いえ、百年も待つ必要はありません。
私はすぐにあちらでも上り詰めます。
この身は最も優れた吸血種に成るのですから、十年もあれば十分です。
entries.maoEnglish: There will be no need to wait a century. I shall rise to the summit of their world at once. This body will become the finest of all vampiric species. Ten years will be more than enough.
entries.mirrorMoon:
No, you wouldn't need to wait a hundred years.
Just like here, I will rise quickly to the top.
This body will become the most superior vampire, so ten years will be enough.

entries.japanese:
たわけたことを。
いかに君といえど、死者からやり直すのであれば百年はかかろう。
連中の世界の苛烈さはあたしたちの比じゃないぞ。
entries.maoEnglish: What idiocy. Even you would require a hundred years if forced to begin again among the Dead. Their world is more merciless than ours by far.
entries.mirrorMoon:
How foolish.
Even if it is you, you would need at least a hundred years if you start over from The Dead.
Their world's intensity is nowhere as nice as ours.

entries.japanese:
まともな方法ならそうでしょうね。
　しかし初めから最強の吸血種になるのであれば、彼らの世界の法則も通用しない。
entries.maoEnglish:
By ordinary means, yes.
But if I begin as the strongest of all vampiric species, the laws of their world will not apply to me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Using direct methods, then you would be right.
But if I become the strongest vampire from the very beginning, their world's rules will not apply to me.

entries.japanese:
……わからないな。
どういうことだ、それは。
entries.maoEnglish: …I do not understand. What exactly are you proposing?
entries.mirrorMoon: …… What do you mean by that?

entries.japanese:
簡単な話です。
　司祭殿は死徒の能力が、その血を吸った真祖の能力の影響を受けるのはご存知でしょう。
　ですから―――解答は実にシンプルだ。
　己が最強の死徒になりたいのであれば。
　己が血を、
　最強の真祖に吸わせればいいのです―――
entries.maoEnglish:
It is quite simple.
You know, priest, that a Dead Apostle’s abilities are shaped by the power of the True Ancestor who drank their blood.
Therefore—the answer could hardly be simpler.
If one desires to become the strongest Dead Apostle,
one need only offer one’s blood
to the strongest True Ancestor—
entries.mirrorMoon:
It is simple.
As a priest of The Church, you certainly know that Dead Apostles' powers are affected by the True Ancestor that sucked their blood.
Therefore---the solution is very simple.
If I wish to become the strongest Dead Apostle,
this blood of mine,
it must be sucked by the strongest of the True Ancestors---

entries.japanese:
夢を見ている。
　曖昧な、とくに意味などない、灼けたアメのようなユメを見ている。
　彼女のことが、好きなのか。
　感情の正体はわからないけど、どうしても気になってしまうのは、もう否定しようのない事実だと思う。
entries.maoEnglish:
I am dreaming.
A vague and meaningless dream, like sugar scorched to amber.
Do I love her?
I don’t know what this feeling is. But there is no longer any denying that I can’t stop thinking about her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I'm watching a dream.
A vague dream without any particular significance.
Do I like her?
I don't know my true feelings, but I can't deny the reality that I'm always concerned about her.

entries.japanese:
彼女のことが、好きなのか。
　……わからない。
ただ、自分がどうにかしてしまいそうな時、助けてくれたのは彼女だけだ。
　彼女がいなければ。
　雨にうたれて、あのまま本当に死んでいたかもしれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
Do I love her?
…I don’t know. I know only that when I was about to lose myself, she alone saved me.
Without her.
I might truly have died there in the rain.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Do I like her?
…… I don't know.
It's just that when I was completely lost within myself, she helped me.
If she wasn't there,
I may have just died under the pouring rain.

entries.japanese:
――――わからない。
　だから、聞かないと。
　どうしてそんなコトをしているのか。
　どうして、そんな感情のない目をしているのかって――――
entries.maoEnglish:
――――I don’t understand.
So I have to ask.
Why she does such things.
Why her eyes hold no feeling at all—
entries.mirrorMoon:
----I don't know.
That's why I have to ask.
Why she is doing this.
Why her eyes are so devoid of any emotion----

entries.japanese:
「―――志貴さま」
　……朝の光に交じって、翡翠の呼び声が聞こえてくる。
「―――志貴さま、お時間です。
お目覚めください」
　抑揚のない翡翠の声に、意識がはっきりと覚めていく。
entries.maoEnglish:
“—Master Shiki.”
Hisui’s voice reached me through the morning light.
“Master Shiki, it is time. Please wake up.”
Her level, uninflected voice drew me fully into consciousness.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Shiki-sama."
…… I can hear Hisui's voice mingling with the morning light.
"---Shiki-sama, it is time.
Please wake up."
Her inflectionless voice awakens me.

entries.japanese:
「――――――」
　目を覚ましたとたん、厭なモノが視界に入ってきた。
　ずきり、とこめかみには銃創のような頭痛。
「あ――――」
　起きたばかりの意識が、がらり、と足場を失っていく。
　そのまま眩暈を起こしてしまう前に、急いで枕元のメガネを手に取った。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――――”
The instant I opened my eyes, something hateful filled my vision.
Pain shot through my temple like a bullet wound.
“Ah—”
My newly awakened mind lost the ground beneath it.
Before vertigo could take me, I snatched the glasses from my bedside.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------"
As soon as I wake up, terrible things enter my vision.
I get a headache like I was just shot in the head.
"Ah----"
I almost lose my just awakened consciousness.
Before I fade away completely, I quickly grab my glasses.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま……？
　ご気分が優れないのですか？」
「……いや、そういうわけじゃなんだ。
ちょっとした貧血だから」
　軽く頭をふって、さっきまで視えていたものを記憶から振り払う。
「そんなことより、おはよう翡翠。
起こしにきてくれてありがとう」
　ベッドから上半身を起こしながら、できるだけ自然に笑顔を向けた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki…? Are you feeling unwell?”
“…No, it’s nothing like that. Just a little anemia.”
I shook my head, banishing what I had seen from memory.
“Never mind that. Good morning, Hisui. Thanks for waking me.”
Sitting up, I gave her the most natural smile I could manage.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama……?
Are you not feeling well?"
"…… No, that's not it.
It's just my anemia acting up."
Lightly shaking my head, I clear my head of what I was seeing.
"More than that, good morning Hisui.
Thanks for waking me up."
Sitting up in bed, I do my best to smile naturally.

entries.japanese:
「いえ、これがわたしの仕事ですから。
志貴さまに感謝されるほどのことではありません」
「そうかな、俺はすごくありがたいけど。
目覚し時計の音なんかより、何倍もあったかい感じがする」
　ベッドから立ちあがる。
　時刻は朝の七時前―――いつもより十分ほど早い時間。
「……ああ、朝ごはんだろ？
　すぐに行くから先に行っててくれ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“It is only my duty. There is no need for Master Shiki to thank me.”
“Maybe, but I’m really grateful. Waking to your voice feels so much warmer than an alarm clock.”
I rose from bed.
It was not yet seven—about ten minutes earlier than usual.
“…Breakfast, right? I’ll be down in a minute. Go on ahead.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No, this is my duty.
There is no need for you to thank me, Shiki-sama."
"Maybe, but I am grateful.
You are infinitely better than an alarm clock."
I stand up.
It's not yet seven o'clock---about ten minutes earlier than I usually get up.
"…… Hmm, breakfast?
I'll be there soon, so please go ahead of me."

entries.japanese:
「それなのですが、志貴さま。
その―――秋葉さまが、志貴さまに問い詰めたい事がある、と居間でお待ちになっておられます」
　言いにくそうに翡翠はそんなコトを言ってくる。
「……問い詰めたいコトって……あいつ、もしかしてご機嫌ななめ……？」
「……はい。
志貴さまが昨夜遅くに出かけた事を、お気づきになられたようです」
「……あ」
　思わず声をあげてしまった。
　昨夜はつい勢いにまかせてアルクェイドを捜しに行って、夜遅くに帰ってきてしまったんだっけ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“About that, Master Shiki—Miss Akiha is waiting in the sitting room. She says she has something she wishes to question Master Shiki about.”
Hisui looked distinctly uncomfortable.
“You mean she wants to question me because she’s angry?”
“Yes. She appears to have discovered that Master Shiki went out late last night.”
“Oh.”
The sound escaped before I could stop it.
Last night I had rushed off to find Arcueid on impulse and come home in the small hours.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama, about that, um---Akiha-sama is waiting for you in the sitting room.
It seems she has some questions for you."
Hisui says this with some difficulty.
"…… Some things she needs to ask?
…… Is she in a bad mood……?"
"…… Yes.
Akiha-sama seems to have realized that you left late last night, Shiki-sama."
"…… Ah."
I blurt that out without thinking.
Last night, I went to look for Arcueid and came home late.

entries.japanese:
「……まいったな……いちおう見付からないように出ていったのに」
「はい。
わたしも、気がついたのはわたしだけだと思っていました」
　しずしずとした声で翡翠は相づちをうってくれる。
「……？
　翡翠、俺が出ていったコトに気がついてたのか……？」
「あ……」
　翡翠は申し訳なさそうにうつむいてしまう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…That’s not good. I thought I’d slipped out without anyone seeing me.”
“Yes. I also believed I was the only person who noticed.”
Hisui quietly agreed.
“…Wait. You knew I went out?”
“Oh…”
Hisui lowered her head apologetically.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Uh-oh…… I thought no one noticed."
"Yes, I also thought that I was the only one who noticed."
Hisui answers solemnly.
"……?
Hisui, you realized I left……?"
"Oh……"
Hisui looks very apologetic.

entries.japanese:
「そっか、翡翠は知ってたのか。
どうりで屋敷の玄関が開いてたわけだ」
「……………はい」
　ぽつり、と翡翠は答える。
「さんきゅ。
おかげで昨日は助かった。
その、気を遣ってくれてありがとうな」
「ですが、それで姉さんに気づかれてしまいました。
わたしと姉さんは二時間交代でお屋敷の見まわりをするんです。
　それで、玄関の鍵をわたしが外しているのを気がつかれてしまって―――」
entries.maoEnglish:
“So you knew. That explains why the front door was open.”
“……Yes.”
Her answer was scarcely more than a murmur.
“Thanks. You saved me last night. It was kind of you to think of me.”
“But that allowed my sister to notice. She and I take turns patrolling the mansion in two-hour shifts.
She discovered that I had left the front door unlocked, and…”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I see, you knew.
No wonder the mansion's entrance was open."
"……………… Yes."
Hisui answers reluctantly.
"Thanks, it was a big help.
And, thanks for going out of your way to do that."
"But Nee-san realized too because of that.
Nee-san and I have two-hour shifts watching the mansion.
And she found out about me unlocking the entrance---"

entries.japanese:
……なるほど。
　琥珀さんは秋葉つきの人だから、そこから秋葉に昨夜のことが漏れてしまったというコトか。
「翡翠が謝る必要はないよ。
もともと夜中に出歩く俺が悪かったんだから、自業自得なんだ。
　翡翠が玄関を開けていてくれただけで、すごく嬉しい」
「―――――」
　翡翠はじっとこっちを見つめてくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
…Of course.
Kohaku attended Akiha personally, so that was how last night’s escapade had reached her.
“You don’t need to apologize, Hisui. I’m the one who went out in the middle of the night. Whatever happens is my own fault.
Just knowing you left the door open for me makes me happy.”
“……”
Hisui stared at me without a word.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… I see now.
Kohaku-san is Akiha's servant, so she would have leaked it to Akiha about last night.
"Hisui, there is no need to apologize.
It was my fault that I was walking around at night, so I should take the blame.
I'm still very happy that you left the door unlocked."
"-----"
Hisui just looks at me.

entries.japanese:
「……なに？」
「……いえ、なんでもありません。
着替えが済み次第、居間においでください」
　翡翠は何か言いたそうな目のまま、廊下へ出ていってしまった。
「……しかしまいったな。
また秋葉のお説教を聞くことになるなんて」
　独りごちて、制服に着替える。
　そんな暇があるなら―――何か、大切な事をしなくちゃいけない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…What is it?”
“…Nothing. Please come to the sitting room once you have dressed.”
Hisui left for the hallway with something still unspoken in her eyes.
“…Wonderful. Another lecture from Akiha.”
I muttered to myself as I put on my uniform.
But I had no time for that—I had something important to do.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Hm?"
"…… It is nothing.
As soon as you change, please go to the sitting room."
Still looking like she wants to say something, Hisui exits into the hallway.
"…… Dang, I'm going to get scolded by Akiha again."
I mutter to myself as I change.
If I have time for that---there's still something important I have to do instead.

entries.japanese:
「……そうだ。
先輩に話を―――」
「っ――――」
　ずきん、とまた頭痛がした。
　翡翠と話をしていた時はおさまっていたクセに、一人になった途端に頭がズキズキと痛みだす。
「くっ……まず、これ――すぐに、収まりそうに、ない……」
　ベッドに倒れこんで、ただ頭痛に耐える。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…That’s right. I need to talk to Ciel—”
“Ngh—”
Pain stabbed through my head again.
It had stayed quiet while Hisui was here, only to begin throbbing the moment I was alone.
“Damn… This is bad. It isn’t going away anytime soon…”
I collapsed onto the bed and lay there enduring the pain.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… That's right, I have to talk to Senpai---"
"-----"
I get the headache again.
It faded when I was talking to Hisui, but as soon as she left, it started hurting again.
"Gh…… crap, this--doesn't look, like it will end, soon……"
I bear the pain as I collapse on the bed.

entries.japanese:
……痛みは消えない。
　ずきん、ずきん、と頭に釘を打ち込まれるような痛み。
　……おかげで、さっきまで何を思っていたか忘れてしまう。
　振りかえってみれば、事故にあってから八年間。
　遠野志貴は、ずっとこんなポンコツみたいな体と折り合いをつけてきた。
　突発的にやってくる眩暈。
頭痛。
貧血。
　それのおかげでどれだけのコトを諦めなければならなかったのか、数えきれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
…The pain would not fade.
Throb after throb, as though someone were hammering nails into my skull.
…It even drove whatever I had been thinking about from my mind.
Looking back, eight years had passed since the accident. Shiki Tohno had spent all of them bargaining with this defective body.
Sudden attacks of vertigo. Headaches. Anemia.
I couldn’t count how many things they had forced me to surrender.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… It doesn't ease up.
Throb, throb.
A pain like I'm being stabbed in the head.
…… It makes me completely forget what I was thinking about earlier.
Come to think of it, in the eight years since that accident, I've always had to deal with my broken body.
Dizziness, headaches, and anemia occurring unexpectedly.
I can't count how many things I had to give up because of that.

entries.japanese:
医者は奇跡的に命を取り留めたという。
　こうして生きていること事態が奇跡なんだから、多少の痛みは我慢しろっていうことなのか。
　……壊れた目。
この目となんとか折り合いをつけてくれた先生は、その奇跡を大切にしなさいと言っていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
The doctors called my survival a miracle.
Did that mean I was supposed to endure a little pain because being alive at all was miraculous?
The woman who taught me how to live with these broken eyes had told me to treasure that miracle.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The doctor said it was a miracle just surviving it.
Just being able to live is a miracle, so putting up with various pains is perhaps necessary.
…… These broken eyes.
Sensei, who was able to alleviate these eyes, told me to treat that miracle very importantly.

entries.japanese:
……あれは。
　人の命は尊くはないが、戻らないものだから、大事にしなさい、という意味だったんだろうか。
　ここ数日、俺はたくさんの人の死を視てきた。
　あっけない。
笑ってしまうほどあっけない命。
　あんなふうにあっさりと消え去るものならば、もとからその程度だということじゃないのか。
　ならば、それを尊いと考えることなぞ無意味だ。
entries.maoEnglish:
Could she have meant that?
That human life is not precious, but must be treasured because it can never be restored?
Over the last few days, I had witnessed so many people die.
Lives vanished with absurd, almost laughable ease.
If a thing disappeared that readily, hadn’t it been worth that little from the start?
Calling it precious was meaningless.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Those words.
Did she mean that human life is not so much precious as it is not returnable, so I should treat it carefully?
These past few days, I've seen the deaths of many people.
Too easily.
Lives ending so easily, it's almost comical.
If it is something that ends so easily, doesn't it mean that it was only worth that much from the beginning?
If that's the case, it is meaningless to view life as precious.

entries.japanese:
…………あ、れ。
　オレは、　　　　　　　　　　　　オマエは、
　なんで、　　　　　　　　　　　　いつまで、
　　　　そんなコトを考えているんだろう？
entries.maoEnglish:
……What?
Why do I— How much longer will you—
think— keep thinking—
things like that?
entries.mirrorMoon:
………… H, uh?
Why,          Since when,
am I,         did you start,
thinking like that?

entries.japanese:
「……はあ」
　頭痛が収まってくれた。
「……血を見すぎたのかな。
なんか、ひどいことを思っちまった」
　はあ、と大きく深呼吸をする。
　朝の新鮮な空気を肺にとりこんで、イヤな気持ちを洗い流す。
「―――はやく、学校に行かないと」
　行って、シエル先輩に会わないといけない。
　頭の隅にしこりのように残っている頭痛を堪えながら、自分の部屋を後にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hah…”
The headache finally subsided.
“Maybe I’ve seen too much blood. I was thinking something awful.”
I drew one long, deep breath.
I filled my lungs with fresh morning air and washed the ugly feeling away.
“I have to get to school.”
I had to go and see Ciel.
Enduring the ache that lingered like a knot in the corner of my skull, I left my room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… *sigh*
The headache finally stops.
"…… Maybe I saw too much blood.
What a horrible thought."
I take a deep breath.
Filling my lungs with fresh air, I clear away the unpleasantness.
"---I should hurry up and go to school."
I should go and see Ciel-senpai.
Enduring the slight pain lingering in my head, I leave my room.

entries.japanese:
階段を下りて、ロビーにつく。
　すぐ横手には居間に続く廊下。
　正面には外に通じている玄関がある。
「………………」
　どうしよう。
　秋葉が居間で待っているというけど、一刻も早く学校にいって先輩をつかまえたい。
entries.maoEnglish:
I descended the stairs into the lobby.
The hallway to the sitting room lay beside me.
The front door stood straight ahead.
“……”
What should I do?
Akiha was waiting for me in the sitting room, but I wanted to reach school and find Ciel as quickly as possible.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I go down the stairs and into the lobby.
Next to me is the hallway that goes down towards the sitting room.
In front of me is the front door that leads outside.
"………………"
What should I do?
Akiha is waiting in the sitting room, but I want to hurry up and see Senpai.

entries.japanese:
―――だからといって秋葉を無視して学校に行くわけにもいかない。
　……先輩の事は今すぐにでも確かめたいけど、今は秋葉に昨夜の事を釈明するほうが先だろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Even so, I couldn’t ignore Akiha and leave for school.
I wanted to find out about Ciel as soon as possible, but first I owed Akiha an explanation.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---But still, I can't ignore Akiha and go right to school.
…… I want to find out about Senpai right away, but first I should explain to Akiha about last night.

entries.japanese:
居間には秋葉の姿しかない。
　厨房からは琥珀さんの、調子のはずれた鼻歌が響いてきている。
「……………」
　秋葉はこちらを見ても何も言わず、無言で紅茶を飲んでいる。
entries.maoEnglish:
Akiha was alone in the sitting room.
From the kitchen came Kohaku’s cheerfully off-key humming.
“…”
Akiha glanced at me but said nothing, drinking her tea in silence.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Akiha is the only one in the sitting room.
Kohaku-san is in the kitchen, humming away.
"……………"
Akiha doesn't say anything when she sees me and sips her tea quietly.

entries.japanese:
「おはよう、秋葉」
　学校に行こう、とはやる気持ちを抑えて、できるだけ自然に挨拶をする。
　秋葉はぴくっ、と眉を上下させてからティーカップをテーブルに置いて、ゆっくりと俺に視線を向けてきた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Morning, Akiha.”
Suppressing my urge to race straight to school, I greeted her as naturally as I could.
One eyebrow twitched. She set her cup on the table, then turned her gaze toward me with exquisite slowness.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Good morning, Akiha."
Resisting the urge to go to school, I greet her as naturally as possible.
Akiha's eyebrow twitches as she places her teacup down and slowly looks at me.

entries.japanese:
「おはようございます兄さん。
昨夜はずいぶんと遅いお帰りだったようですね」
「……いや、そんなことないんじゃないかな。
　たかだか夜の一時過ぎ、健康な高校生男子ならじゅうぶんに起きてる時間だろう」
「そうね。
私も就寝は日が変わってからだから、その時間は起きてるわ。
もっとも家に帰ってくる時間はもっと早いんですけど」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Good morning, Brother. You came home rather late last night, I see.”
“Was it really that late?
A little after one is a perfectly normal time for a healthy high school boy to be awake.”
“Quite. I don’t go to bed until after midnight either, so of course I’m awake then. I do, however, come home much earlier.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Good morning Nii-san.
It was quite late when you came home last night, wasn't it?"
"…… No, not really.
It was at most a little past one o'clock, quite normal for a healthy young man in high school to be up, right?"
"I see.
My bedtime is also past midnight so I was up at that time.
But I would come home much earlier than that."

entries.japanese:
「ああ、俺だって昨日は早くから家にいたじゃないか。
……ただちょっと、たまたま夜中に用事が出来たから外に出たわけだけど―――」
「無断で、ですか。
何か後ろめたいことをしに行くとしか思えない行動ですね」
「うっ………」
　秋葉の視線は冷たい。
　……こうして注意されるのは二回目だから、冷静そうに見えて秋葉は本当に呆れているのかもしれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I was home early too, wasn’t I? Something just happened to come up in the middle of the night, so I stepped out for a while―――”
“Without telling anyone. It is difficult to imagine a more suspicious way of behaving.”
“Urgh…”
Her gaze was glacial.
This was the second time she had reprimanded me for the same thing; beneath that calm exterior, she might truly be exasperated with me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yeah, even I was home earlier, wasn't I?
…… I just had something to do, so I was out for a little bit---"
"Without permission?
You acted like you were out doing something you felt guilty over."
"Uh……"
Her stare is pure ice.
…… This is the second time, and I'm sure even though Akiha looks calm, she is quite angry.

entries.japanese:
「――兄さん。
　有間の家ではどうだったかしらないけど、ここでの門限は午後八時までです。
これは絶対に守ってもらう規則なんです。
　それ以降は屋敷の門を閉めますから、昨夜のようによじのぼって侵入するなんて事はしないでください」
「あ───知ってたのか、おまえ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Listen, Brother.
I don’t know what rules you kept at the Arima house, but here the curfew is eight in the evening. You will obey it.
The gates are locked after that, so please do not climb over them and break in as you did last night.”
“You knew about that?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"--Nii-san.
I don't know what went on at the Arima house, but here the curfew is eight o'clock.
It is a rule that must not be broken.
The gate will be locked after that, so please don't climb in like a robber."
"Oh----you knew?"

entries.japanese:
「……あのですね、知っていたもなにも、監視カメラにきっかり映っていました。
　琥珀があわてて警報機を切ったからよかったものの、もし兄さんだって気がつかなかったら今頃留置所の中にいるでしょうね、遠野志貴は」
「……そうか。
そりゃあ琥珀さんに感謝しないといけないな。
その、秋葉もごめん。
昨日は黙ってでかけて悪かった」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Of course I knew. The security camera recorded you perfectly.
We were fortunate that Kohaku hurried to disable the alarm. If she hadn’t recognized you, Shiki Tohno would be sitting in a police cell right now.”
“I see. I owe Kohaku my thanks, then. And… I’m sorry, Akiha. I shouldn’t have gone out without telling you.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… The surveillance camera showed me quite clearly.
It is a good thing Kohaku-san realized it was you and turned off the alarm system because otherwise you would probably be detained right now, Tohno Shiki."

"…… Oh.
I should thank Kohaku-san then.
And, um, Akiha, I'm sorry.
I shouldn't have kept quiet about it."

entries.japanese:
「……わかっていただければいいんです。
これにこりたら門限は厳守してくださいね。
今までのことは大目にみてあげますから」
「……それなんだけど、秋葉」
「なんですか？」
「……その、言いにくいんだけどさ。
俺、今日も夜に用事があるんだ。
帰りも何時になるかわからないんだけど、決して悪いことをしてるわけじゃなくて―――」
entries.maoEnglish:
“As long as you understand. Let this be a lesson, and observe the curfew from now on. I will overlook everything up to this point.”
“About that, Akiha…”
“What is it?”
“This is hard to say, but I have something to do tonight too. I don’t know when I’ll be back, but I swear I’m not doing anything wrong—”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… If you understand, then it is fine.
Please make sure you observe your curfew from now on.
I will overlook it this time."
"…… About that, Akiha."
"What is it?"
"…… This is a little hard to say.
I… have something to do tonight too.
I don't know when I will be back, but I'm not going to do anything bad---"

entries.japanese:
「─────────」
　秋葉の視線が厳しくなる。
「琥珀！」
　突然、秋葉は立ち上がった。
　名前を呼ばれて琥珀さんが厨房からやってくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
Akiha’s gaze sharpened.
“Kohaku!”
She shot to her feet.
At the sound of her name, Kohaku came in from the kitchen.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----------"
Her gaze sharpens.
"Kohaku!"
She suddenly stands up.
Kohaku-san comes in from the kitchen.

entries.japanese:
「はい、なんでしょうかお嬢さま」
「学校に行きます。
支度をなさい」
「はあ、ですが志貴さんの朝食の支度がまだできてませんよ」
「こんな人の朝食なんてほっといていいです。
ご自分でなんでも出来るそうですから！」
　秋葉はずかずかとロビーへと行進していく。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Yes, what is it, Miss Akiha?”
“We’re leaving for school. Get ready.”
“But Master Shiki’s breakfast isn’t ready yet.”
“Forget breakfast for someone like him. Apparently he can do everything perfectly well by himself!”
Akiha marches out toward the foyer.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yes, what is it, My Lady?"
"I will be going to school, get the preparations ready."
"Huh?
But I have not yet made Shiki-san's breakfast."
"You can leave this person alone.
It seems he can do everything by himself."
Akiha strides towards the lobby.

entries.japanese:
「はあ……志貴さん、あんまり秋葉さまを怒らせちゃだめですよ。
お兄さんなんですから、ちゃんとかまってあげてくださいね」
　そんな事を言いつつ、琥珀さんは秋葉の後を追いかけていく。
　居間にはまだ、湯気をたてているティーカップが一つきり。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh dear, Master Shiki, you really should not make Miss Akiha so angry. You are her big brother, so give her a little attention, will you?”
With that, Kohaku hurries after her.
Only one teacup remained in the sitting room, still sending up steam.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Kohaku-san sighs.
"…… Shiki-san, you should not make Akiha-sama so upset.
You are her big brother, so please treat her better, okay?"
Saying that, she walks after Akiha.
The teacup sits, still steaming.

entries.japanese:
「……………はあ」
　自業自得とはいえ、今朝は朝食抜きになってしまった。
　が、都合がいいといえば都合がいい。
　まだ時間は七時になったばかりだ。
　今から走って学校に行けば、七時半過ぎには学校に着けるだろう――――
entries.maoEnglish:
“Haaah…”
It was my own fault, but I had lost my breakfast.
On the other hand, that suited me perfectly.
It was only just past seven.
If I ran, I could reach school shortly after seven-thirty—
entries.mirrorMoon:
……………… *sigh*
I know it's my own fault, but I won't have any breakfast today.
But, it is convenient in a way.
It is now just seven o'clock.
If I run to school now, I should be able to get there around half past seven----

entries.japanese:
校門についた。
　時刻は七時半を過ぎたあたりだ。
「…………」
　正門に立って、先輩を待つ。
　ちらほらと登校してくる生徒たちにおかしな目で見られていたけど、そんな事はどうでもよかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
I reached the school gates.
It was a little after seven-thirty.
“…”
I stood at the main gate and waited for her.
The few students arriving this early gave me strange looks, but I couldn’t have cared less.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I make it to the gate.
It's about half past seven.
"…………"
I stand and wait for Senpai by the gate.
It probably looks a little strange to the other students walking by, but I don't really care.

entries.japanese:
「……………」
　先輩はなかなかやってこない。
　校門は登校してくる生徒たちで混雑している。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
She still hadn’t appeared.
The gate was growing crowded with arriving students.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……………"
Senpai doesn't show up.
The school gate is flooded with students as they arrive.

entries.japanese:
校門が閉まるまで、あと五分もない。
　あれから今まで、先輩はやってこなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
Less than five minutes remained before the gate closed.
She hadn’t come.
entries.mirrorMoon:
There's only about five minutes before the gate closes.
But Senpai still does not come.

entries.japanese:
「…………」
　今日は―――来ないのかも、しれない。
　昨日、俺にあんなところを見られたから、今日といわず明日も、明後日も、このまま―――
―――どくん。
「………っ」
　なにか、そう思ったら眩暈がしてきた。
　ふるふると頭をふって、厭な考えを振り払う。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
Maybe she wasn’t coming today.
After what I had seen last night, perhaps not today, or tomorrow, or the day after—perhaps never again—
―――Thump.
“Ngh…”
The thought made me dizzy.
I shook my head hard, driving it away.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"………"
She---might not come today.
Yesterday, I saw all that happened, so she might not come today, or tomorrow, or the day after---
---Thump.
"……… Ah."
Thinking that, I feel a little faint.
I shake my head to clear it of terrible thoughts.

entries.japanese:
……と。
　ぽん、と後ろから肩を叩かれた。
「遠野くん、こんなところで何してるんですか」
「せっ、先輩………！？」
「はい」
　こくん、と先輩は頷いた。
entries.maoEnglish:
And then.
Someone tapped me on the shoulder from behind.
“Tohno, what are you doing out here?”
“C-Ciel…?!”
“Yes.”
She gave a small nod.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… And then,
someone pats me on the shoulder from behind.
"Tohno-kun, what are you doing here?"
"Se, Senpai……!?"
"Yes."
Senpai nods.

entries.japanese:
「ほ、ほんとに……！？
　だって昨日、俺は先輩があんなコトしてたの―――」
　もが。
　最後まで言いきる前に、先輩の手が口を塞いだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You’re really here…?! But yesterday, I saw you doing that—”
Mmph.
Before I could finish, her hand covered my mouth.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"R, really……!?
But yesterday, you were---"
Mph.
Before I can finish, Senpai puts her hand over my mouth.

entries.japanese:
「遠野くん、ここじゃなんですから、ちょっと体育館裏に行きましょう」
　先輩はいつも通りの笑顔で、俺の口を塞いだまま、むんずと腕を掴んでくる。
「っ、っ！」
　ちょっと待ってと抗議をしたんだけど、声にならない。
　そのまま強引に、ずるずると引きずられていってしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“This isn’t the place, Tohno. Let’s go behind the gym.”
Wearing her usual smile, she kept one hand over my mouth and seized my arm with the other.
“Mm! Mmm!”
I tried to protest that she should wait, but no words came out.
She simply dragged me away by force.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Tohno-kun, not here.
Let's go behind the gymnasium."
Senpai gives her usual smile as she keeps her hand over my mouth and pulls my arm.
"…, …!"
I try to tell her to stop, but I can't speak.
She forcefully pulls me away.

entries.japanese:
――――高らかに予鈴の音が鳴り響く。
　……朝のホームルームが始まってしまった。
　くわえて、周りにはまったく人の気配がない。
「はい、ここなら誰にも聞かれません」
　先輩はようやく両手を離してくれた。
　バッ、と後ろに跳びすさって、先輩を正面から見据える。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――The warning bell rang out, loud and clear.
Morning homeroom had begun.
Worse, there wasn’t another soul anywhere nearby.
“There. No one can hear us here.”
At last she released me.
I sprang back and faced her squarely.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----The school bell rings overhead.
…… Homeroom has begun.
Furthermore, no one else is around.
"Yes, no one can hear us here."
Senpai finally releases me.
Jumping back, I face Senpai directly.

entries.japanese:
「昨日の夜の話でしょう？
　言いたいコトがあるんでしたら、遠野くんのほうからどうぞ」
　先輩は冷静にそんな事を言ってくる。
　まるで昨日の夜の事なんて、そう大した事じゃなかったみたいに。
「…………っ！」
　けど、俺にとっては大した事だった。
　先輩のこの態度は、なんだかカチンときてしまう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“This is about last night, isn’t it? If you have something to say, Tohno, go ahead.”
She spoke with perfect composure.
As though nothing particularly important had happened.
“……!”
But it had mattered to me.
Her attitude grated on me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"You want to talk about last night, right?
If there's anything you want to say, please go ahead, Tohno-kun."
Senpai speaks calmly.
As if what happened last night was not a big deal.
"……………!"
But it was a big deal for me.
Her attitude right now makes me mad.

entries.japanese:
「それじゃあ昨日の夜のアレは、本当に先輩なんだな……！」
「はい。
遠野くんの名前も口にしちゃいましたし、もうさすがにごまかしようがありません」
「っ…………！」
　ぎり、と歯を噛む。
　……そりゃあ、別に謝ってもらおうとか思ってたわけじゃないけど、それでも―――
entries.maoEnglish:
“Then that really was you last night…!”
“Yes. I even said your name, so there’s no point denying it any longer.”
“……!”
I ground my teeth.
I hadn’t expected an apology, exactly, but even so—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"So that really was you last night……!?"
"Yes.
I did say your name back then too, so it's impossible to hide it any longer."
"…………!"
I grit my teeth.
…… I didn't expect an apology or anything, but still---

entries.japanese:
―――ダメだ、やっぱり先輩のことが気にかかる。
　朝飯なんてゆっくり食べている場合じゃない。
「―――志貴さま？」
　居間から翡翠がやってきた。
　いつまでたっても居間に現れない俺を迎えに来たのだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――No. I couldn’t stop worrying about her.
This was no time to sit down to a leisurely breakfast.
“Master Shiki?”
Hisui came out from the sitting room.
I had taken so long to appear that she had probably come to fetch me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---No, I have to find out about Senpai.
I don't have time to eat this morning.
"---Shiki-sama?"
Hisui comes from the sitting room.
She must have come to check on me since I did not show up after a while.

entries.japanese:
「……悪い。
俺、このまま学校に行くよ。
秋葉にはごめんって伝えておいてくれ」
「……お待ちください志貴さま。
志貴さまのお顔の色が優れません。
ひどく体調が悪いのではないですか……？」
「―――いいんだ、ただの頭痛だから。
それじゃ行くよ。
……ごめんな、また勝手なコトしちまって」
　……本当に自分勝手なことをいって、返事も聞かずに玄関に手をかけた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Sorry. I’m going straight to school. Tell Akiha I’m sorry.”
“Please wait, Master Shiki. Master Shiki is terribly pale. Are you feeling very ill?”
“It’s fine—just a headache. I’m going now. Sorry for doing whatever I please again.”
After saying something so thoroughly selfish, I reached for the front door without waiting for an answer.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Sorry.
I'm going to school, please tell Akiha I'm sorry."
"…… Please wait Shiki-sama.
You do not look well.
Are you sure you are feeling well……?"
"---I'm fine, just a little headache.
Well, I'm off…… Sorry, I'm being selfish again."
…… I say something really selfish and open the door before she can respond.

entries.japanese:
校門についた。
　屋敷から走ってきたから、時刻はまだ七時半にもなっていないはずだ。
「…………」
　正門に立って、先輩を待つ。
　ちらほらと登校してくる生徒たちにおかしな目で見られていたけど、そんな事はどうでもよかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
I reached the school gates.
I had run all the way from the mansion, so it couldn’t yet have been seven-thirty.
“…”
I stood at the main gate and waited for her.
The few students arriving this early gave me strange looks, but I couldn’t have cared less.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I reach the school gate.
Since I ran from the mansion, it's not even half past seven yet.
"…………"
I stand and wait for Senpai by the gate.
It probably looks a little strange to the other students walking by, but I don't really care.

entries.japanese:
「……………」
　先輩はなかなかやってこない。
　時刻は、七時半を過ぎてしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
She still hadn’t appeared.
Seven-thirty came and went.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……………"
Senpai doesn't show up.
It's past seven thirty already.

entries.japanese:
さらに十分。
　校門は登校してくる生徒たちで混雑している。
entries.maoEnglish:
Another ten minutes passed.
The gate was growing crowded with arriving students.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Ten more minutes pass by.
The school gate is flooded with students as they arrive.

entries.japanese:
校門が閉まるまで、あと五分もない。
　あれから今まで、先輩はやってこなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
Less than five minutes remained before the gate closed.
She hadn’t come.
entries.mirrorMoon:
There's only about five minutes before the gate closes.
But Senpai still does not come.

entries.japanese:
「…………」
　今日は―――来ないのかも、しれない。
　昨日、俺にあんなところを見られたから、今日といわず明日も、明後日も、このまま―――
―――どくん。
「………っ」
　なにか、そう思ったら眩暈がしてきた。
　ふるふると頭をふって、厭な考えを振り払う。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
Maybe she wasn’t coming today.
After what I had seen last night, perhaps not today, or tomorrow, or the day after—perhaps never again—
―――Thump.
“Ngh…”
The thought made me dizzy.
I shook my head hard, driving it away.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"………"
She---might not come today.
Yesterday, I saw all that happened, so she might not come today, or tomorrow, or the day after---
---Thump.
"……… Ah."
Thinking that, I feel a little faint.
I shake my head to clear it of terrible thoughts.

entries.japanese:
……と。
　ぽん、と後ろから肩を叩かれた。
「遠野くん、こんなところで何してるんですか」
「せっ、先輩………！？」
「はい」
　こくん、と先輩は頷いた。
「ほ、ほんとに……！？
　だって昨日、俺は先輩があんなコトしてたの―――」
　もが。
　最後まで言いきる前に、先輩の手が口を塞いだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
And then.
Someone tapped me on the shoulder from behind.
“Tohno, what are you doing out here?”
“C-Ciel…?!”
“Yes.”
She gave a small nod.
“You’re really here…?! But yesterday, I saw you doing that—”
Mmph.
Before I could finish, her hand covered my mouth.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… And then,
someone pats me on the shoulder from behind.
"Tohno-kun, what are you doing here?"
"Se, Senpai……!?"
"Yes."
Senpai nods.

"R, really……!?
But yesterday, you were---"
Mph.
Before I could finish, Senpai puts her hand over my mouth.

entries.japanese:
「遠野くん、ここじゃなんですから、ちょっと体育館裏に行きましょう」
　先輩はいつも通りの笑顔で、俺の口を塞いだまま、むんずと腕を掴んでくる。
「っ、っ！」
　ちょっと待ってと抗議をしたんだけど、声にならない。
　そのまま強引に、ずるずると引きずられていってしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“This isn’t the place, Tohno. Let’s go behind the gym.”
Wearing her usual smile, she kept one hand over my mouth and seized my arm with the other.
“Mm! Mmm!”
I tried to protest that she should wait, but no words came out.
She simply dragged me away by force.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Tohno-kun, not here.
Let's go behind the gymnasium."
Senpai gives her usual smile as she keeps her hand over my mouth and pulls my arm.
"…, …!"
I try to tell her to stop, but I can't speak.
She forcefully pulls me away.

entries.japanese:
――――高らかに予鈴の音が鳴り響く。
　……朝のホームルームが始まってしまった。
　くわえて、周りにはまったく人の気配がない。
「はい、ここなら誰にも聞かれません」
　先輩はようやく両手を離してくれた。
　バッ、と後ろに跳びすさって、先輩を正面から見据える。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――The warning bell rang out, loud and clear.
Morning homeroom had begun.
Worse, there wasn’t another soul anywhere nearby.
“There. No one can hear us here.”
At last she released me.
I sprang back and faced her squarely.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----The school bell rings overhead.
…… Homeroom has begun.
Furthermore, no one else is around.
"Yes, no one can hear us here."
Senpai finally releases me.
Jumping back, I face Senpai directly.

entries.japanese:
「昨日の夜の話でしょう？
　言いたいコトがあるんでしたら、遠野くんのほうからどうぞ」
　先輩は冷静にそんな事を言ってくる。
　まるで昨日の夜の事なんて、そう大した事じゃなかったみたいに。
「…………っ！」
　けど、俺にとっては大した事だった。
　先輩のこの態度は、なんだかカチンときてしまう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“This is about last night, isn’t it? If you have something to say, Tohno, go ahead.”
She spoke with perfect composure.
As though nothing particularly important had happened.
“……!”
But it had mattered to me.
Her attitude grated on me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"You want to talk about last night, right?
If there's anything you want to say, please go ahead, Tohno-kun."
Senpai speaks calmly.
As if what happened last night was not a big deal.
"……………!"
But it was a big deal for me.
Her attitude right now makes me mad.

entries.japanese:
「それじゃあ昨日の夜のアレは、本当に先輩なんだな……！」
「はい。
遠野くんの名前も口にしちゃいましたし、もうさすがにごまかしようがありません」
「っ…………！」
　ぎり、と歯を噛む。
　……そりゃあ、別に謝ってもらおうとか思ってたわけじゃないけど、それでも―――
entries.maoEnglish:
“Then that really was you last night…!”
“Yes. I even said your name, so there’s no point denying it any longer.”
“……!”
I ground my teeth.
I hadn’t expected an apology, exactly, but even so—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"So that really was you last night……!?"
"Yes.
I did say your name back then too, so it's impossible to hide it any longer."
" …………!"
I grit my teeth.
…… I didn't expect an apology or anything, but still---

entries.japanese:
「……どうして。
どうして先輩があんな、ことを」
「どうしても何も、それがわたしの本当の仕事ですから仕方ありません」
　きっぱりと言って、先輩はじろり、と俺を見つめてきた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Why… why would you do something like that?” “Because it’s my real job. I don’t have a choice.”
She said it flatly, then fixed me with a hard stare.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Why?
Why were you doing those things?"
"Why?
I do it because it's my job."
Saying that, she looks directly at me.

entries.japanese:
「わたしは吸血鬼を処理する為にここにいます。
　ですから―――最悪の場合、遠野くんをこのまま放っておくわけにはいきません」
「な――――」
　感情のない瞳に見つめられて、どくん、と心臓が収縮する。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I came here to dispose of vampires.
Which means that, in the worst case, I may not be able to let you walk away.”
“What—”
Under those emotionless eyes, my heart clenched with a heavy thump.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I am here to execute vampires.
So---in the worst case, I cannot leave you like this now, Tohno-kun."
"Wha----"
Being stared at with those emotionless eyes, my heart skips a beat.

entries.japanese:
「聞かせてください、遠野くん。
　どうして遠野くんが彼女のような吸血鬼と関わってしまっているのか。
その内容によっては、わたしは―――」
　ピシリ、と周囲の空気が凍りつくような、気配。
―――質問しようと思っていたのはこっちなのに、今では質問される立場に変ってしまっている。
　けど、ここで答えなかったら、それこそ先輩が何をしてくるかわからなくて、ゾクリとした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Tell me, Tohno.
Why are you involved with a vampire like her? Depending on what you tell me, I—”
A sharp tension ran through the air, as if everything around us had frozen solid.
―――I had come here intending to ask the questions, yet somehow I was now the one being questioned.
A chill ran through me. If I refused to answer, there was no telling what she might do.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Let me ask you, Tohno-kun.
Why you are associated with a vampire like her?
Depending on your answer, I will---"
It feels like the air has literally frozen.
---I thought I would be asking the questions, but our positions have been reversed.
But I don't know what Senpai will do if I don't answer, and a chill runs through me.

entries.japanese:
「さあ、教えてください。
貴方は―――遠野くんは、吸血鬼の仲間になってしまっているんですか」
「あ―――違う、違うよ先輩。
　たしかに俺はアルクェイドに協力してたけど、それはもう終わったハズだったんだ。
　けど昨日はアルクェイドが通り魔事件の犯人かと思って、けどそんなの違うはずだからどうしてもあいつに話を聞きたくて―――」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Now tell me. Are you—are you a vampire’s ally, Tohno?” “No—no, that isn’t it.
I did help Arcueid, but that was supposed to be over.
Last night I thought she might be responsible for the serial killings, but I knew that couldn’t be true, so I had to hear her explanation—”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Now, tell me.
Why you---Tohno-kun is with that vampire."
"Ah---no, no Senpai, that's not it.
Certainly I did agree to help her, but that's already over.
But yesterday, I thought Arcueid was the one behind the serial killings, but that couldn't be right, so I went to ask her and---"

entries.japanese:
あたふたと昨夜の状況説明をする。
　先輩は黙って、およそ説明になんかなっていない俺の独り言を聞いてくれた。
　とりあえず偶然アルクェイドと知り合って、この街に吸血鬼がいるっていう事を教えられて、街を守るために協力してるっていう、今までのいきさつを。
entries.maoEnglish:
I stumbled through an account of the previous night.
She listened in silence to my rambling monologue, which barely qualified as an explanation:
how I had met Arcueid by chance, learned that a vampire was hiding in the city, and agreed to help her protect it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I tell her all about last night.
Senpai listens to it all silently.
How I met her accidentally, how she explained to me about the vampire in this city, how I teamed up with her to save the city, and everything up until now.

entries.japanese:
「……違うって……関係ないって言ったじゃないかっ！」
「なにがですか？」
「三日前の夜のことだよ！
　あの夜、公園で俺を助けてくれたのは先輩かって聞いたら、先輩は違うって言ったのに……！」
「あれ、うそです」
　きっぱりと。
　もう、一人で怒っているこっちがバカに思えるぐらい、気持ち良く先輩は断言した。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You said it wasn’t you… You said you had nothing to do with it!”
“What are you talking about?”
“Three nights ago! When I asked if you were the one who saved me in the park, you said you weren’t…!”
“That was a lie.”
Without hesitation.
She said it so breezily that I felt like an idiot for getting angry all by myself.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… But…… but, you said that wasn't you!"
"What wasn't?"
"Three nights ago!
I asked if you were the one that helped me that night in the park, and you said it wasn't you……!"

"That was a lie."
Succinctly.
Senpai simply says so.

entries.japanese:
「……あの……うそって、先輩？」
「遠野くんのほうこそ、わたしとの約束を守ってくれなかったんですね。
もう夜は出歩かないっていったのに」
「………う」
　先輩はじっと俺を見つめてくる。
　なんか、一瞬にしてこっちが悪人になってしまったみたいな、後ろめたさ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Um… You lied?”
“You’re the one who broke your promise to me, Tohno. You said you wouldn’t go out at night anymore.”
“Urk…”
She fixed me with an unwavering stare.
In the space of a heartbeat, I felt as guilty as if I’d been the villain all along.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Um…… a lie, Senpai?"
"You didn't keep the promise we made.
You told me you wouldn't go out at night anymore."
"……… Uh."
She stares at me.
I start to feel like the bad guy all of a sudden, feeling guilty about what I did.

entries.japanese:
「こうなっちゃうかもしれないから、ちゃんと約束したのに。
遠野くんにとってわたしとの約束なんてそんな程度のものだってなんて、悲しいです」
「あ―――いや、違うんだ。
昨日はだって、アルクェイドが通り魔事件の犯人かと思って、けどそんなの違うはずだからどうしてもあいつに話を聞きたくて―――」
　あたふたと昨夜の状況説明をする。
　先輩は黙って、およそ説明になんかなっていない俺の独り言を聞いてくれた。
　とりあえず偶然アルクェイドと知り合って、この街に吸血鬼がいるっていう事を教えられて、街を守るために協力してるっていう、今までのいきさつを。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I made you promise because I was afraid exactly this might happen. It hurts to learn that a promise to me means so little to you.”
“N-no, that’s not it. Last night, I thought Arcueid might be behind those attacks—but I knew that couldn’t be true, so I had to ask her what was going on—”
I stumbled through an account of the previous night.
She listened in silence to my rambling monologue, which barely qualified as an explanation.
How I had met Arcueid by chance, learned that a vampire was hiding in the city, and agreed to help her protect it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I made the promise with you so something like this wouldn't happen.
Is that how little a promise with me means to you, Tohno-kun?
That makes me sad."
"Ah---no, that's not it.
About last night, I thought Arcueid was the one behind the serial killings, but that couldn't be right, so I went to ask her and---"
I tell her all about last night.
Senpai listens to it all silently.
How I met her accidentally, how she explained to me about the vampire in this city, how I teamed up with her to save the city, and everything up until now.

entries.japanese:
「……どうして。
どうして先輩があんな、ことを」
「どうしても何も、それがわたしの本当の仕事ですから仕方ありません」
「それより遠野くん。
夜は出歩かないって言ってくれたのは、嘘だったんですね」
　ニコリ、と笑顔で先輩は言ってくる。
「あ……」
　そりゃあ先輩とそう約束はしたけど、でも――
entries.maoEnglish:
“Why…? Why were you doing something like that?” “Because that is my real work. There’s nothing else to it.”
“More importantly, Tohno—you were lying when you promised not to go out at night, weren’t you?”
Ciel said with a bright smile.
“Ah…”
Yes, I had promised her that. But—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Why?
Why were you doing those things?
"Why?
I do it because it's my job."
"More importantly, Tohno-kun, you were lying when you told me you would not go out at night, right?"
She grins as she says this.
"Oh……"
I did promise her that, but--

「遠野くん、わたしとの約束を守ってくれなかったんですね。

Senpai simply says so.

entries.japanese:
「……あの……うそって、先輩？」
「あの時は遠野くんの事を思って嘘をついたんです。
わたし、自分の正体を一般人に知られたらその人の口を封じなくてはいけないんです。
　遠野くん、痛いのは嫌いでしょ？」
　明るい声で、先輩はとんでもない事を言ってくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Um—you lied?”
“I lied for your own sake. If an ordinary person learns who I really am, I have to silence them.
You don’t like pain, do you, Tohno?”
She delivered this appalling revelation in the sunniest voice imaginable.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Um…… a lie, Senpai?"
"I lied for your sake, Tohno-kun.
I have to seal the mouth of any ordinary person who finds out my true identity.
Tohno-kun, you don't like pain, right?"
Senpai says such an unbelievable thing with a rather bright and cheerful voice.

entries.japanese:
「口を封じるって、その……」
「解りやすくいうと死人にくちなしっていうところですね。
……えっと、あんまりにも解りやすすぎるとは思いますけど」
「うっ―――」
　思わず腰が引けてしまった。
　先輩の言葉には冗談と真実が半分ずつ混ざり合っている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Silence me—you mean…”
“To put it plainly, dead men tell no tales. Though perhaps that puts it a little too plainly.”
“Ghk—”
I recoiled before I could help it.
Her words were equal parts joke and truth.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Seal the mouth, um……"
"To put it simply, dead people can't talk.
…… Um, I think I put it too simply."
"Uh---"
I step back without even thinking about it.
Senpai sounds like she is only half-joking.

entries.japanese:
「だから、聞く内容によっては遠野くんをこのまま帰すわけにはいきません。
遠野くん、彼女と一体どんな関係なのか聞かせてください」
　じっ、と感情のない眼差しで見つめられて、心臓が縮んだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“So depending on what you tell me, I may not be able to let you leave. Tell me, Tohno—what exactly is your relationship with that woman?”
Her stare held no emotion at all. My heart clenched under it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"So, I cannot let you go free depending on what you tell me.
Tohno-kun, just what is your connection with that woman?"
My heart almost stops as those emotionless eyes stare at me.

entries.japanese:
―――質問しようと思っていたのはこっちなのに、今では質問される立場に変ってしまっている。
　けど、ここで答えなかったら、それこそ先輩が何をしてくるかわからなくて、ゾクリとした。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――I had come here intending to ask the questions, yet somehow I was the one being interrogated.
A chill went through me. If I refused to answer, there was no telling what she might do.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---I thought I would be asking the questions, but our positions have been reversed.
But I don't know what Senpai will do if I don't answer, and a chill runs through me.

entries.japanese:
「あ―――いや、違うんだ。
昨日はだって、アルクェイドが通り魔事件の犯人かと思って、けどそんなの違うはずだからどうしてもあいつに話を聞きたくて―――」
　あたふたと昨夜の状況説明をする。
　先輩は黙って、およそ説明になんかなっていない俺の独り言を聞いてくれた。
　とりあえず偶然アルクェイドと知り合って、この街に吸血鬼がいるっていう事を教えられて、街を守るために協力してるっていう、今までのいきさつを。
entries.maoEnglish:
“N-no, you’ve got it wrong. Last night, I thought Arcueid might be behind those attacks—but I knew that couldn’t be true, so I had to ask her what was going on—”
I stumbled through an account of the previous night.
She listened in silence to my rambling monologue, which barely qualified as an explanation.
How I had met Arcueid by chance, learned that a vampire was hiding in the city, and agreed to help her protect it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah---no, that's not it.
About last night, I thought Arcueid was the one behind the serial killings, but that couldn't be right, so I went to ask her and---"
I tell her all about last night.
Senpai listens to it all silently.
How I met her accidentally, how she explained to me about the vampire in this city, how I teamed up with her to save the city, and everything up until now.

entries.japanese:
「―――わかりました。
　遠野くんは彼女に協力してこの街に根付いている吸血鬼を倒そうとしているんですね」
「まあ、そういうコトに、なるけど」
「……信じられません。
遠野くん、吸血鬼のことなんて本当に信じてるんですか？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“I understand.
You’ve been helping her hunt the vampire entrenched in this city.”
“More or less.”
“I can’t believe it. Do you honestly believe in vampires, Tohno?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---I understand.
So you teamed up with her to defeat the vampire in this city.
Right, Tohno-kun?"
"Well, yeah, that's how it is."
"…… I can't believe it.
Tohno-kun, do you really believe in vampires?"

entries.japanese:
「な……なに言うんだよ先輩。
先輩だって、教会っていうところのエク―――」
　ぴっ、と先輩の指が、俺の唇に当てられた。
「わたしのことはいいです。
それより問題なのは遠野くんのほうでしょう？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Wh-what are you talking about? You’re one of the Church’s exe—”
Her finger darted out and pressed against my lips.
“Never mind me. You are the one we need to discuss, aren’t you?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Wha…… what are you saying Senpai?
Even you, you're one of The Church's exor---"
Senpai puts a finger on my lips.
"Don't worry about me.
Isn't the problem more about you, Tohno-kun?"

entries.japanese:
「俺のほうって、別に俺に問題なんかないよ」
「……はあ。
自覚、ないんですね」
　困ったように先輩はため息をつく。
「一つお聞きしますけど。
遠野くん、彼女にどれくらいの事を聞いてるんですか？」
「どのくらいの事って……この街に、人間の血を吸ってる吸血鬼がいるって事ぐらいだけど」
「つまり彼女本人のことも、彼女が追いかけている『敵』のことも聞かされていないんですね」
「……そりゃあ、詳しくは、聞いてないけど」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Me? There’s nothing wrong with me.”
“…You truly have no idea, do you?”
She sighed helplessly.
“Let me ask you something. How much has she actually told you?”
“How much…? Only that there’s a vampire in this city drinking human blood.”
“So she has told you nothing about herself, or about the ‘enemy’ she is hunting.”
“…Not in any detail, no.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Me?
I don't have any problems."
"…… You have no self-awareness, it seems."
Senpai gives a troubled sigh.
"I have a question… just how much did she tell you about?"
"How much…… well, only that a vampire is in this city sucking people's blood."
"So in other words, you don't know about her or this 'enemy' she is after."
"…… Well, I haven't heard about it.

entries.japanese:
「そうですか。
では、わたしが教えてあげます」
「……へえ。
すごいな、先輩知ってるんですか？」
「あのですね。
わたし、これでも教会の人間なんですから、それぐらい知ってて当たり前じゃないですか！」
「あ、そっか。
……ごめん、なんか忘れてたよ、それ」
　あはは、と誤魔化し笑いをしてみたりする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I see. Then I will tell you.”
“Really? You know about all this?”
“Honestly, I am a member of the Church. Of course I know that much!”
“Oh, right. Sorry—I’d somehow forgotten.”
I tried to laugh it off.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I see.
Then, I will tell you about it."
"…… Wow, that's amazing.
You know about that, Senpai?"
"Well, you know, I am a member of The Church, so of course I know that much!"
"Oh, that's right.
…… Sorry, I kind of forgot.
Ahahaha."
I attempt to laugh it off.

entries.japanese:
「もうっ。
まじめな話をしているんですから、ちゃんと聞いていてください！」
　はい、と反省をこめて頷く。
「……あれ。
けど、そういうのって秘密なんじゃないのか。
アルクェイドは、その……先輩たちは秘密をすごく守るって言ってたけど」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Honestly. This is serious, so please pay attention!”
I nodded contritely.
“Wait. Isn’t all this supposed to be secret? Arcueid said your people guarded their secrets very carefully.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Geez.
I'm trying to be serious here, so please pay attention!"
I nod in assent.
"…… Huh?
But, isn't that a secret?
Arcueid, um…… she said you were all incredibly secretive."

entries.japanese:
「はい。
本来なら口にしていいものではありませんけど、今日は特別です。
　監視役がいるわけでもないですから、遠野くんが誰にも話さないでいてくれればオッケーです」
「……あの。
もし、俺が先輩のコトとかを誰かに話したらどうなるの、かな」
「はい。
遠野くんが思ってるとおりの事をするだけです」
　笑顔で、先輩は恐ろしい返答をする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Yes. Ordinarily I would never be allowed to discuss it, but today is an exception.
No one is here to supervise me, so as long as you tell nobody, it will be fine.”
“…And if I did tell someone about you?”
“Yes. Then I would simply do exactly what you imagine.”
She gave me that horrifying answer with a smile.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yes, it really isn't something to talk about, but today is special.
There isn't anyone watching over us or anything, so as long as you don't tell anyone, then it will be okay."
"…… Um.
What will happen if I tell someone else about you, Senpai?"
"Yes.
I'll just do exactly what you are thinking of, Tohno-kun."
Senpai gives that frightening response with a smile.

entries.japanese:
「それじゃあ簡単に説明しますけど、遠野くんは吸血鬼についてどんな事を教わりました？」
「―――二種類いるっていう事と、死徒っていうヤツが人間の血を吸う吸血鬼だっていうことぐらいかな。
でも、吸血鬼ってのがどんな化け物なのかはわかってるつもりだよ」
「そうでしょうね。
遠野くんは実際に吸血鬼を倒しているんですから」
「はは、最後の最後で先輩に助けられたけど――――って、先輩！」
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’ll keep this brief. What have you been taught about vampires?”
“That there are two kinds, and that the ones called Dead Apostles drink human blood. I think I have a fair idea what sort of monsters vampires are, though.”
“I’m sure you do. You have actually defeated one.”
“Ha. You did save me at the very end, but—wait!”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Well then, I'll keep it very simple.
Tohno-kun, how much was explained to you about vampires?"
"---Just about how there are two types, and how Dead Apostles are the vampires that suck human blood.
But I think I know what kind of monsters they are."
"That's true.
Tohno-kun, you did actually defeat a vampire."
"Haha, but you did help me at the very end-----S, Senpai!"

entries.japanese:
「ええ。
遠野くんが『混沌』を消滅させる所は見せてもらいました。
わたしが駆けつけた時には、もう『混沌』は息絶えていましたけど」
「―――――――」
　驚いた。
それじゃあ先輩は俺の目の事も―――
「ひどい話ですよね。
なんだって遠野くんにあんな真似をさせたんですか彼女はっ。
　『混沌』を滅ぼせるぐらいの概念武装があるんだったら、自分で戦えっていうんです。
　遠野くんをあんなに血だらけにしちゃうなんて、あの場で彼女をこらしめようと思ったぐらいあたまにきました」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Yes. I watched you erase ‘Chaos.’ By the time I reached you, it was already dead.”
“—”
I was stunned. Then Ciel knew about my eyes—
“It’s unforgivable. Why did she make you do something like that?
If she had a conceptual weapon capable of destroying ‘Chaos,’ she should have fought it herself.
Seeing you covered in blood made me so angry I nearly punished her on the spot.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yes.
I watched you annihilate "Chaos".
When I came, "Chaos" was already dying though."
"-------"
I'm surprised.
Then Senpai knows about my eyes---?
"It was terrible.
That woman made you do such a thing.
If she had a conceptual weapon to defeat 'Chaos', she should have used it herself.
After seeing your bloody body, I thought I should punish her then and there."

entries.japanese:
「遠野くんも遠野くんです。
いくら吸血鬼を倒せる武器を貰ったからって、生身で戦うなんて何考えてるんですか。
もしかして彼女に弱みでも握られているんですか？」
　呆れた顔で、先輩はぶつぶつと文句を言う。
entries.maoEnglish:
“And you are hardly blameless, Tohno. Even if she gave you a weapon that could kill a vampire, what possessed you to fight one in the flesh? Does she have some kind of hold over you?”
She continued muttering, visibly exasperated.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"You too, Tohno-kun.
Even if you were given a weapon that can kill vampires, what were you thinking fighting that thing?
Does she have a hold over your weakness or something?"
Still looking surprised, Senpai complains aloud.

entries.japanese:
「……えっと、先輩？
　吸血鬼を倒せる武器って、なに？」
「なにって、遠野くんが持ってたナイフの事ですけど……そっか、彼女が教えてくれるハズありませんよね。
自分にとっても不利なことなんですから」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Um, Ciel? What weapon can kill vampires?”
“The knife you were carrying, of course. I suppose she would never explain it to you, since that knowledge would put her at a disadvantage too.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Um, Senpai?
What's this weapon that can kill vampires?"
"What do you mean?
I'm talking about that knife you have, Tohno-kun.
…… Oh, I guess she wouldn't tell you about it.
It's not good for her either."

entries.japanese:
「えっとですね、吸血種は傷を受けてもたいていは治癒してしまうんです。
　ありきたりの外的要因……つまり凶器ですね。
これでは吸血種の復元速度を上回る破壊力は得られません。
　吸血種を滅ぼすには復元速度を上回る規模の外的要因か、復元速度そのものを無効にする外的要因が必要となります。
「この、彼らの復元呪詛―――傷を治療する、ではなく破損した個所を元通りにしようとする時間の逆行。
この呪詛を無効にする神秘の類を概念武装っていうんです」
entries.maoEnglish:
“You see, vampiric species recover from most wounds.
Ordinary external causes—weapons, in plain language—cannot inflict damage faster than they restore themselves.
To destroy one, you need either an external force vast enough to outpace that restoration or one that nullifies the restoration itself.
“Their curse of restoration is not true healing, but a reversal of time that returns a damaged part to its former state. Mysteries capable of negating that curse are known as conceptual weapons.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Let's see, vampires have the ability to recover from most injuries they receive.
With ordinary outside force…… I mean normal weapons.
With such things, you cannot cause wounds greater than the speed of their recovery.
To kill a vampire, you need an outside force greater than their speed of recovery, or something that nullifies their ability to recover.
This ability of theirs, the curse of restoration---actually isn't treating the wounds.
Instead, it is a reversing of time to restore the damaged body part back to its original state.
An occult artifact which nullifies this effect is called a conceptual weapon."

entries.japanese:
「………………」
　先輩は楽しげに、よく解らない事を言う。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
She cheerfully explained things I could barely understand.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…………………"
Senpai cheerfully says all these things I can't understand too well.

entries.japanese:
「ようするに魔法の武器です。
　わたしたちはあくまで吸血鬼が人だった頃の経歴から彼らを回呪しますからあまり使用しないんですけど、初めから人でない吸血種を処理する時に使用する、言うなれば奥の手です。
　遠野くんのナイフって、彼女が持ち出した対吸血鬼用の武器なんでしょ？」
「あ―――え？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“In short, they are magical weapons.
We generally attack vampires through the histories they possessed while human, so we seldom use them. But against a vampiric species that was never human, a conceptual weapon is our final resort.
Your knife is an anti-vampire weapon she brought with her, isn’t it?”
“Ah… what?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"In short, a magical weapon.
We usually lift their curse looking into their human past, so we do not usually use them.
But for those that were not originally human, we use them, kind of like a secret weapon.
Your knife, is it not an anti-vampire weapon she brought?"
"Ah----eh?"

entries.japanese:
「それとも遠野くんのお家の家宝か何かですか？
　……あ、けど遠野の血筋に退魔の宝具があるのはおかしいですよね」
　ぶつぶつと先輩の独り言は続く。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Or is it some heirloom of your family? …No, it would make no sense for the Tohno bloodline to possess a demon-hunting relic.”
Her private muttering continued.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Or is it a family treasure?
…… Hmmm, but it would be strange for the Tohno family to possess an anti-demon weapon."
Senpai ponders aloud.

entries.japanese:
……先輩の思惑はよく解らないけど、どうも俺の目の事はまったく知らないみたいだ。
「―――あの、先輩。
吸血鬼の話は、どこにいってしまったんでしょう」
「――――――――――――」
　ぴたり、と先輩の独り言が止まった。
　照れ隠しなのか、控えめな笑顔をうかべる。
　……この人の性格は、やっぱり難しい。
entries.maoEnglish:
I could not follow her reasoning, but apparently she knew nothing about my eyes.
“Excuse me, Ciel. What happened to the explanation about vampires?”
“—”
Her monologue stopped dead.
Perhaps to hide her embarrassment, she offered me a small, restrained smile.
…She really was difficult to understand.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… I don't know what she's thinking, but it seems she has no idea about my eyes.
"---Um, Senpai?
Where did our conversation about vampires go?"
"------------"
With a start, Senpai stops mumbling to herself.
She smiles as if to hide her embarrassment.
…… As usual, her personality is hard to understand.

entries.japanese:
「それでは本題に戻ります。
まじめに聞いてくださいね、遠野くん」
「はい、手短にお願いします」
「遠野くんは吸血鬼が真祖と死徒に分けられるという事は知っているんですね。
　なら話は簡単です。
　彼女が追っている『敵』は死徒と区分される吸血種です。
俗称は『蛇』。
死徒たちの中でも異端扱いされている、特別な吸血鬼」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Let us return to the point. Please listen seriously, Tohno.”
“Yes. And please keep it short.”
“You already know that vampires are divided into True Ancestors and Dead Apostles.
Then this will be simple.
The ‘enemy’ she pursues is a vampiric species classified as a Dead Apostle. He is commonly called the ‘Serpent.’ A peculiar vampire regarded as a heretic even by other Dead Apostles.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Let's get back to the main subject.
Please listen carefully, Tohno-kun."
"Yes, please keep it short."
"It seems you already know about how there are the True Ancestors and the Dead Apostles.
So it is very simple.
The 'enemy' she is after is a Dead Apostle, nicknamed 'The Serpent'.
Among the Dead Apostles, he is considered a heretic, a special vampire."

entries.japanese:
「……この吸血鬼は、遠野くんが倒した『混沌』ほど強力な個体ではありません。
　けれど、ある意味『混沌』より滅ぼすのが困難な相手なんです。
なにしろ死んでも生き返ってしまうんですから」
「……あの、先輩。
吸血鬼って不老不死なんだから、殺しても生き返ってくるのは当たり前なんじゃないかな」
entries.maoEnglish:
“This vampire is not as powerful as the ‘Chaos’ you destroyed.
In one sense, however, he is even harder to eliminate. When he dies, he returns to life.”
“…Aren’t all vampires ageless and immortal? I thought coming back after you killed them was part of the package.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… This vampire is not as strong as 'Chaos', whom you defeated.
But, he is more difficult an opponent to eliminate than this 'Chaos' in a way.
Since he comes back to life even after he dies."
"…… Um, Senpai.
Vampires are immortal, so isn't it natural for them to come back to life after dying?"

entries.japanese:
「遠野くんは『混沌』を消滅させたでしょう。
　吸血鬼といえど、その肉体と魂が破壊されれば消滅します。
吸血鬼だって殺されれば死んでしまう。
　けれど、『蛇』はそれを克服してしまった吸血鬼なんです」
entries.maoEnglish:
“You erased ‘Chaos,’ did you not?
Even a vampire ceases to exist if both body and soul are destroyed. Kill a vampire, and it dies. The ‘Serpent,’ however, found a way around that.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"You eliminated 'Chaos', right?
Even if they are vampires, if you destroy their body and soul, they will be vanquished.
If you kill a vampire, they will die.
But 'The Serpent' is a vampire who has conquered even this."

entries.japanese:
「遠野くんは輪廻転生という言葉をご存知ですか？
　仏教用語ですから日本の方には馴染みはあると思うんですけど」
「……ああ、あるよ。
死んでも次の人間として生まれ変わるっていうヤツだろ」
「はい、その通りです」
「ようするにですね。
　『蛇』と呼ばれる吸血鬼は、その輪廻転生を自分の物にしてしまっているんです。
　殺しても生き返る、というのはそういう意味です」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Are you familiar with reincarnation, Tohno? It is a Buddhist concept, so I imagine most Japanese people know it.”
“Sure. You die and are reborn as someone else.”
“Exactly.”
“The point is simple.
The vampire called the ‘Serpent’ has made reincarnation his own.
That is what I mean when I say he returns to life after being killed.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Tohno-kun, are you familiar with the cycle of reincarnation?
It is part of Buddhist doctrine, so I would think a Japanese would be quite familiar with it."
"…… Yeah.
It's that thing where when someone dies, they are reborn again as another human."
"Yes, exactly."
"In other words,
The vampire named 'The Serpent' has made this cycle of reincarnation his own.
That's what I mean when I say he comes back to life even after he is killed."

entries.japanese:
「輪廻転生って―――ようするに、死んだらまた赤ん坊からやり直すっていう、こと……？」
「そうです。
『蛇』は存命している間に、次の自分の肉体をあらかじめ決めておいて、その赤子が誕生した時点で『自分』の全情報を移植します。
　『蛇』の情報はその赤子が成人、ないし自己としての知性を持つまで影を潜めています。
　『自分』を引き継ぐに相応しい知性をもった段階で、その赤子は『蛇』という吸血鬼になってしまうんです」
「―――ちょっと待って先輩。
それってなに、まさか赤ん坊が母親の中にいる時に手術とかをするっていうことなのか……？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Reincarnation… So when he dies, he starts over as a baby?”
“Yes. While still alive, the ‘Serpent’ selects the body that will become his next incarnation, and at the child’s birth, he implants the entirety of himself within it.
That information remains dormant until the child reaches adulthood, or at least develops a mature sense of self.
Once its mind becomes capable of inheriting him, the child becomes the Serpent himself.”
“Wait, Ciel. Are you saying he performs some kind of operation while the baby is still in its mother?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Reincarnation---you mean if he dies he will start over again as a baby……?"
"Yes.
While 'The Serpent' is alive, he chooses his next host and when it is born, he transmits all of the information of his 'self'.
'The Serpent's' information stays deep within the baby until it matures, or until it gains sufficient intelligence.
As soon as that baby has the intelligence to succeed 'his self', the baby becomes a new vampire that is the 'Serpent'."
"---Wait a minute.
What's that?
Don't tell me that he does surgery on it while it's in the mother or something like that."

entries.japanese:
「いいえ、医学的な手段ではないんです。
　だって『蛇』は今の自分の肉体が滅ぼされた瞬間に、あらかじめ『次はこの母体にしよう』と決めておいたモノに転生するんですから。
　さきほどは『全情報』といいましたけど、解りやすく言えば『魂』ですね。
　魂が大気を伝搬して他者に乗り移る、なんていうのは実感が湧かないでしょうけど、ようするに電波と同じなんです。
　この場合、電波を発信するのも受信するのも人間の脳。
　カレの優れたところは、魂なんていう計測不能にして、肉体という器から離れたら霧散してしまうモノを、伝達可能なモノとして加工したことでしょう」
entries.maoEnglish:
“No. There is nothing medical about it.
The instant his current body is destroyed, the ‘Serpent’ reincarnates through the womb he selected in advance.
I called it his ‘complete information,’ but in simpler terms, it is his soul.
A soul passing through the air to possess another person may be difficult to imagine, but it functions much like a radio signal.
In this case, human brains serve as both transmitter and receiver.
His great achievement was turning the soul—something immeasurable that normally disperses when separated from the vessel of the body—into something that could be transmitted.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No, it's not anything medical.
Because the instant his body is destroyed, he reincarnates into the body he chose as his next host.

"I said all of his information earlier, but to say it simpler, think of it as his 'soul'.
It wouldn't be quite correct to say his soul propagates through the air and takes over someone's body, but it's similar to an electro-magnetic wave.
In this case, the human brain is what does the transmitting and the receiving.
