From the beginning, Senpai and I have always lived in different worlds.
"………………"
…… Just go to sleep.
I'll be able to take it tomorrow.
I'll sleep now, so I can calm down---

entries.japanese:
……眠れない。
　胸がイライラして眠れない。
「………しょうがないな」
　ごそごそと枕もとから適当な本を取り出して、眠くなるまで小さな英文を目で追い続けた。
entries.maoEnglish:
I couldn’t sleep.
The restless ache in my chest would not let me.
“I suppose I have no choice.”
I rummaged beside my pillow for some random book and followed the tiny English print until I grew sleepy.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… I can't sleep.
My chest is still bothering me.
"……… Oh well."
I choose a book of English sentences to read so I can drift off to sleep.

entries.japanese:
１９７６年。
　わたしはフランスの片田舎の、一商人の子供として生を受けた。
entries.maoEnglish:
1976.
I was born the child of a merchant in the French countryside.
entries.mirrorMoon:
1976.
I was born as a child of a shopkeeper from a remote countryside village in France.

entries.japanese:
東洋人の母を持つわたしの容姿は母ゆずりで、街のどこにいても異邦人のような違和感を持って育った。
　けれど街の人々はみな一様に陽気で、わたしを笑顔で迎えてくれた。
entries.maoEnglish:
I took after my Asian mother, and grew up feeling like an outsider wherever I went in town.
Yet the townspeople were cheerful without exception, and always welcomed me with smiles.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I looked like my mother, who was Oriental, so I grew up feeling a little out of place wherever I went.
But all the townspeople were great people and would greet me with bright smiles.

entries.japanese: わたしはその笑顔に応えられるように、日々を素直に、前向きに生きていた。
entries.maoEnglish: Wanting to return those smiles, I lived each day honestly and optimistically.
entries.mirrorMoon: To be able to face those smiles, I lived my days honestly and positively.

entries.japanese:
父の手伝いをして、学校に通って、当たり前の片思いをした。
　それがわたしに課せられた義務であり、当然のように許された幸福だと疑わなかった。
　十六歳の誕生日を迎えるまでの、本当にわずかな時間だけの日々ではあったけれど。
entries.maoEnglish:
I helped my father, attended school, and nursed an ordinary unrequited love.
I never doubted that this was the duty expected of me and the happiness I was entitled to enjoy.
Though those days lasted only a painfully brief time, ending with my sixteenth birthday.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Helping my dad, going to school, falling in love like normal.
That was my life and I never doubted my happiness.
It was truly a very short time until my sixteenth birthday.

entries.japanese:
それは、わたしの体に突然訪れた。
　たとえば子供たちと遊んでいるとき。
ワケもなく、そのか細い首をへし折りたくなる。
　たとえば道端に哀れなものごいを見かけたとき。
　おかしくて、その胸にナイフを刺したくなっている。
entries.maoEnglish:
Then, without warning, it came for me.
While playing with children, for example. For no reason at all, I would want to snap their slender necks.
Or when I saw some pitiable beggar by the roadside. I would find the sight absurdly funny and want to drive a knife into his chest.
entries.mirrorMoon:
That came suddenly to my body.
Such as when I would be playing with children.
For no reason, I wanted to snap their necks.
Such as when I saw a poor beggar by the road.
It seemed so funny, I wanted to stab him with a knife.

entries.japanese:
……その感情には理由がなかった。
　誰にも打ち明けられず、わたしは日に日に部屋に閉じこもりがちな人間になっていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
Those feelings had no cause.
Unable to confide in anyone, I withdrew further into my room with every passing day.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… There was no reason for those feelings.
I could not talk to anyone about it, so I started to lock myself away in my room.

entries.japanese:
暗い情念は、わたし本人からくるものだった。
　自分が二重人格になってしまったとか、他の誰かの心がわたしの中に入ってきたわけでもない。
　そもそも、わたしはそんな非科学的なことは信じていない。
entries.maoEnglish:
The darkness came from me.
I had not developed another personality, nor had another person’s mind entered my own.
I did not believe in anything so unscientific.
entries.mirrorMoon:
My dark passions came forth from within me.
It's not like I had two personalities or someone came inside me.
First of all, I don't believe in such unscientific things.

entries.japanese:
わたしの思いは、誰だって思う、ほんのささいな破壊衝動だ。
　夜更かしした次の日、いつもどおり起こしにきた父さんにちょっとした恨み言を口にしたり。
　雨上がりの大通りを歩いていて、道を行く自動車に水たまりの水をかけられて不愉快になったり。
　そんな小さな、ほんの一瞬だけの意識がカタチになって自分を支配してしまう。
entries.maoEnglish:
They were only petty destructive impulses, the kind everyone feels.
A little resentment toward Father when he woke me as usual after I had stayed up too late.
A flash of anger when a passing car splashed me with muddy water on the main street after rain.
Those tiny, momentary thoughts would take form and seize control of me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
My feelings are the small destructive passions everyone has.
Like yelling at your dad after he comes to wake you up after you stayed up all night.
Like feeling angry when you walk along a rainy street and a car passing by splashes you with water.
Such small feelings I feel for an instant solidify inside of my mind and take over.

entries.japanese:
だから。
　わたしはこのままでは、自分が恐ろしいことをしてしまうと理解していた。
entries.maoEnglish:
And so.
I understood that, if nothing changed, I would do something terrible.
entries.mirrorMoon:
That's why.
I knew I would do something terrible if I stayed like this.

entries.japanese:
わたしには、もう自分の部屋に閉じこもることしかできなかった。
　誰にも会わず、何もせず日々を過ごしていくしかできない。
　……そうすれば、誰も恨むことがなくて、何にもいきどおりを感じることがなくなるから。
―――けれど、それは間違いだった。
　部屋という檻の中で息を潜めて過ごしていくうちに精神は磨耗して、やがて、臨界を超えてしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
All I could do was shut myself inside my room.
I had to pass the days without seeing anyone or doing anything.
Then I would have no one to resent and nothing to rage against.
―――But that was a mistake.
As I lived in silence inside the cage of my room, my mind wore away until at last it passed its breaking point.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I could only lock myself away in my room.
I could only not see anyone and do nothing.
…… That way, I wouldn't hate anyone, and I wouldn't have those feelings.
---But, that was a mistake.
Imprisoned in my room, my mind was ground away, and I eventually passed my limit.

entries.japanese:
その日。
　もう、完全に入れ替わったわたしが思ったことは、喉の渇きだった。
　ゆるり、と弱った肉体を引きずって、部屋の外に出る。
entries.maoEnglish:
That day.
The self that had wholly replaced me thought of only one thing: thirst.
Slowly, dragging my weakened body, I left the room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
That day.
After I was completely replaced, what I thought about was how thirsty I was.
I took my weakened body out of my room.

entries.japanese:
サロンでくつろいでいた両親は、何ヶ月かぶりに部屋から出てきたわたしにかけよってくる。
　心配そうによりそってくる父と母を微笑みで迎えて、わたしはふたりを殺害した。
entries.maoEnglish:
When I emerged after months of seclusion, my parents rushed to me from the salon where they had been relaxing.
I welcomed their worried embrace with a smile, then murdered them both.
entries.mirrorMoon:
My parents ran to me, as I came out of my room for the first time in a few months.
Greeting my worried parents with a smile, I killed them.

entries.japanese:
本当に、あっけなかった。
　わたしは衰弱した体のまま、両親の喉に食いついてごくごくと喉をならす。
　二人分の血と命を吸い上げて、わたしは身を起こした。
「―――百年ぶりか。
今回の肉体は、素晴らしく魅力的だ」
　それは、聞いた事もないわたしの声だった。
　くく、と口元をゆがませて、わたしだったものは自らの体を抱きしめた。
entries.maoEnglish:
It was astonishingly easy.
Weak as I was, I fastened my mouth to their throats and drank with great, gulping swallows.
After draining the blood and life of two people, I rose.
“Has it been a century? This body is exceptionally appealing.”
It was my voice, yet I had never heard it before.
With a low chuckle twisting its lips, the thing that had been me embraced its new body.
entries.mirrorMoon:
It really was quick.
With my weakened body, I bit into their necks and sucked their blood.
After sucking out their blood and life, I stood back up.
"---Has it been a hundred years?
This body is very fascinating."
That was my voice that I had never heard before.
My lips shaping a smile, what used to be me hugged itself.

entries.japanese:
―――それはどんな偶然だったのか。
　本来、私が生まれ代わる家柄というのは前回の私があらかじめ定めておいた家柄である。
　しかし前回の私は、それを決定しきる前に『姫』に討たれてしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――What strange chance had brought this about?
Ordinarily, the family into which I will be reborn is selected in advance by my previous incarnation.
This time, however, the Princess destroyed me before I could finish making that choice.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---What kind of coincidence was it?
Originally, the family I was born into was one that I choose beforehand.
But my previous self was destroyed by the "princess" before I could decide that.

entries.japanese:
私は、肉体的に私に相応しい者という条件しか決められず、不完全な転生をした。
　結果として肉体として素質はあるものの、社会的地位の低い、普通の家庭の子供として生を受けてしまった。
　これでは人知れず街を支配下に置くことは難しい。
entries.maoEnglish:
I managed to specify only that my next host be physically suited to me, and so my reincarnation was incomplete.
The result was a child with tremendous bodily potential but little social standing, born into an ordinary family.
Secretly bringing the town under my control would be difficult.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I could only fill the condition that the one I'm reincarnated into has a physical potential, resulting in an imperfect reincarnation.
As a result, I was born into a body with a high potential, but into a normal family without any high social standing.
It will be difficult to take over this town without having people notice.

entries.japanese:
だが、私は悲観しなかった。
　むしろ、この全身をうつ閃光は歓喜であろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
Yet I did not despair.
If anything, the lightning coursing through this body was surely joy.
entries.mirrorMoon:
But, I was not disappointed.
In fact, I was filled with happiness.

entries.japanese:
たしかに普通の家柄ではその時代の権力を掌握するのに時間がかかる。
　この私では社会的に街を掌握するのは困難だろう。
　だが、その不自由さと引き換えに、私は真に優れた肉体を手に入れた。
entries.maoEnglish:
An ordinary family would indeed need time to seize the power of its age.
In this incarnation, it would be difficult to bring the town under my control through social influence.
In exchange for that inconvenience, however, I had obtained a truly exceptional body.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Certainly it would take a long time for a normal family to gain power.
Seizing power socially would be difficult with this self.
But in exchange for that inconvenience.
I found a truly excellent body.

entries.japanese:
今まで。
　私は肉体と家柄を天秤にかけ、その結果として真に優れた肉体には出会わなかった。
　だが―――今回の肉体が持つ魔力回路の多さは過去において最大であり、大本の私―――一人目の私とほぼ同等の素質を有していた。
entries.maoEnglish:
Until then, I had always weighed physical potential against pedigree.
As a result, I had never encountered a body of true excellence.
But this body possessed more Magic Circuits than any before it, and its potential almost equaled that of the original me—my first incarnation.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Until now,
I had always tried to balance the body and the family standing.
Consequently, I was never able to find a truly excellent body.
However----the body this time carries many more Magic Circuits than any of the bodies before----and this body had the same potential as my original.

entries.japanese:
私は、今までの自分の計算高さを嗤った。
　家柄など、いくらでも後から作ることができる。
　だが肉体の素質だけは、後付けのきかない天性の物に他ならない。
　こと十七回目の転生にして、私はようやくその真実にたどり着いた。
entries.maoEnglish:
I laughed at how calculating I had been.
A pedigree could always be manufactured afterward.
The body’s innate potential alone could never be added later.
Only upon my seventeenth reincarnation did I finally arrive at that truth.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I cursed my calculating self up until now.
Things like social standing, they could always be set up later.
But the quality of the body is something natural that cannot be added later.
After my seventeenth reincarnation, I finally realized that truth.

entries.japanese:
目覚めた私は、ごく自然に、水が地面を浸食していくように、ひそやかに街の人々を配下にくわえていった。
　けれどその手段は今までのように乱暴ではなく、むしろあまり血を流さないものだった。
　理由は、ひどく残酷なものである。
entries.maoEnglish:
Once awake, I quietly gathered the townspeople beneath me as naturally as water eating into earth.
Yet my methods were less violent than before, and shed remarkably little blood.
The reason was unspeakably cruel.
entries.mirrorMoon:
My self that finally awoke naturally started to control the people around me like water soaking into the ground.
Not in the wild manner I had done so previously, but rather in a way that didn't spill as much blood.
The reason is horribly cruel.

entries.japanese:
転生した私という意識は、それ単体では存在できない。
　あるのは『～をこうしたい』という意思だけである。
　今、この肉体を動かしているのは私だが、その過程・方法を選ぶのは肉体として育ち、肉体とともに形成された精神であるわたしだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
The reincarnated consciousness called Roa could not exist by itself.
It possessed only a will: the desire to make some particular thing happen.
Roa was the force moving this body, but the mind that chose each means and method was mine—the mind raised within the body and shaped alongside it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The reincarnated will called myself cannot exist by itself.
All I can do is tell the will "I want to do that."
I am the one moving this body, but the method, the process was determined by my mind which has grown along with this body.

entries.japanese:
つまり―――わたしは意思だけは私という転生体のものであるが、意識はもとのわたしのままなのだ。
　わたしの意識はあり、記憶も確かにある。
　わたしは眠ったまま、自分が犯す悪夢を見続けることしかできない。
entries.maoEnglish:
Thus the will belonged to the reincarnation vessel called Roa, while the consciousness remained my own.
My awareness endured; my memories remained intact.
Trapped in sleep, I could do nothing but watch the nightmare my own body committed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
In other words---my will is from the body I am reincarnated into, but my consciousness still remains from my original self.
I have my consciousness, and I have my past memories.
As I sleep, I could only dream of nightmares which I would do myself.

entries.japanese:
覚えている。
　両親の喉に食いついた時の感触を。
　わたしに笑顔を向けてくれた街の人たちを一人一人、じっくりと足元から熔かすように、その魂を陵辱し続けた日々を。
　わたしは、たった一月で。
　街の人たちの命を掌の上に乗せて、ただ己の快楽のためだけに弄ぶようになった。
entries.maoEnglish:
I remember.
The feel of my parents’ throats between my teeth.
I remember the days I spent violating the souls of the townspeople who had smiled at me, one by one, slowly, as though melting them from the feet upward.
Within a single month.
I held all their lives in my palm and toyed with them solely for my own pleasure.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I still remember.
The sensation of biting into my parents' throats.
I took the townspeople who always greeted me, one by one.
as if melting them slowly from their feet, I continued to humiliate and mutilate their souls.
Within just a month.
I held their lives in my fist and played with them however I wanted to.

entries.japanese:
いっそ、狂いたかった。
　狂って、全てを私にゆだねたかった。
　けれどそうすれば、わたしは今以上の罪を犯すだろう。
　わたしは、ずっと。
　このまま正気を保ち続けて、せめて私の行為が最小限に収まるように生きるしかない。
entries.maoEnglish:
I wished I could go mad.
I wanted madness to let me surrender everything to him.
But if I did, I knew I would commit even greater sins.
All that time.
I had to preserve my sanity and live so that Roa’s crimes might at least be kept to a minimum.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I wanted to go crazy.
I wanted to entrust myself completely to insanity.
But if I did that, I would commit even more sins than before.
That's why I kept on.
Trying to preserve my sanity, I tried to minimize the damage I did.

entries.japanese: 救いがあるとすれば、それは。
entries.maoEnglish: If there was any salvation, it was this.
entries.mirrorMoon: If there was such a thing as a relief…

entries.japanese: 悪夢の終わりは、わりあいあっさりと訪れたという事だった。
entries.maoEnglish: The nightmare ended with surprising ease.
entries.mirrorMoon: It was that the end to this nightmare arrived quickly.

entries.japanese: その白い女は、赤い月の夜にやってきた。
entries.maoEnglish: The woman in white came on a night beneath a red moon.
entries.mirrorMoon: That white woman came on a night with a crimson moon.

entries.japanese:
わたしは知らない。
　けれど私はそれが誰であるか解っていた。
　戦いの末、白い吸血姫はわたしを仕留めた。
　すでに転生の準備を進めていた私はまたも転生し、あとに残されたのはわたしの遺体だけとなる。
　白い女は去り、わたしの遺体は、法王庁に運ばれた。
entries.maoEnglish:
I, the girl, did not know her.
But Roa knew exactly who she was.
At the end of the battle, the white vampire princess killed me.
Roa had already begun preparing another reincarnation and departed once more, leaving behind only my corpse.
The woman in white left, and my body was taken to the Holy See.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I didn't know.
But I knew who she was.
After our fight, the white vampire princess killed me.
Since I had already prepared myself for the next reincarnation, I once again reincarnated, leaving my corpse behind.
The white princess left and my body was taken to the Vatican.

entries.japanese:
メルシー！
　なんだかあんまりなデッドエンドを迎えてしまったついてない遠野くんの為のこのコーナー、
“教えて！
知得留先生！
”の時間がやってきちゃいました。
　それではニ時間目の授業を始めます。
entries.maoEnglish:
Merci!
It’s time for Teach Me, Ciel!, the feature for unlucky Tohno,
who has met with a truly appalling dead end.
Let’s begin lesson two.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Merci!
The hint corner for the out-of-luck Tohno-kun who ended up in this terrible Dead End,
It is time for "Teach me, Ciel-sensei!"
And now, we will start the second period lesson.

entries.japanese:
ははあ、これは原因ははっきりしていますねー。
　逃がした魚は大きいというか、大事な先輩なんですからとことんまで話をして和解しちゃいましょう。
　一人では勝てない相手も、二人の愛の力でラクショーです。
　アルクェイドの助けなんて必要ありません！
entries.maoEnglish:
I see—the cause is perfectly obvious.
The one who got away was quite a catch—or rather, she’s precious to you, so talk it out with her until you reconcile.
An enemy you can’t defeat alone will be easy prey for the power of your love.
You certainly don’t need Arcueid’s help!
entries.mirrorMoon:
I see, there is a distinct reason for this.
The fish that got away this time is big.
It's your dear Senpai, so talk your heart out with her and make peace with her.
Even if it's an opponent you can't beat by yourself, it's easy using the power of love between two people.
You don't need Arcueid's help at all!

entries.japanese:
「なによー。
シエルのほうこそ足ひっぱてるじゃんかー」
　そこ、うるさい！
「シカ」
「うにゃー、結局一回しか使われなかった動物さんシリーズにゃー、にゃー、にゃー…………」
entries.maoEnglish:
“What’s that supposed to mean? You’re the one holding Shiki back, Ciel!”
Quiet over there!
“Deer.”
“Mreow—the poor animal series only got used once after all—meow, meow, meow…”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"What?
Aren't you the one dragging him, Ciel?"
You, quiet!
"Deer."
"And nyeow for the only-used-once animal series, nyaa, nyaa, nyaa…………"

entries.japanese:
ほらほら、授業中の私語は禁止ですよー。
　それではうるさいのも蹴飛ばされたコトですし、引き続き本編をお楽しみください。
entries.maoEnglish:
Now, now, no talking during class.
With that noisy creature safely kicked out, please continue enjoying the story.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Hey now, no private conversations during class!
Now that the loud and annoying person has been kicked away, please continue to enjoy the main story.

entries.japanese: 月を見る、夢を見ていた。
entries.maoEnglish: I dreamed I was looking at the moon.
entries.mirrorMoon: In my dream, I'm staring at the moon.

entries.japanese:
何処で、どうして月を見上げているかは思い出せない。
　ただ他に何も見たくなくて夜空を見上げた時、月があっただけなのかもしれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
I could not remember where I was or why I had raised my eyes to it.
Perhaps I had simply looked into the night because I could bear to see nothing else, and the moon had happened to be there.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I can't remember where I am or why I'm looking up at it.
Maybe I looked up into the night sky not wanting to see anything, and the moon happened to be there.

entries.japanese:
ぎちり、と背骨が軋む。
　血脈を駆け巡るのは寒さのイメージ。
　一人きりの暗闇は、眩暈がする。
　眩く、心を病みつかせるような、月。
entries.maoEnglish:
My spine creaked.
An image of cold coursed through my blood.
Alone in the darkness, I grew dizzy.
The moon blazed—bright enough to derange the heart.
entries.mirrorMoon:
My back creaks.
Coursing through my veins is an image of coldness.
A solitary darkness that makes me dizzy.
A radiant moon that sickens my heart.

entries.japanese:
……不思議と。
　息苦しいはずの寒さは、それ以上に懐かしい空気を持っているような気がした。
entries.maoEnglish:
…Strangely,
the cold that should have choked me carried an even stronger air of nostalgia.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Strange.
The overwhelming coldness feels more like a sense of nostalgia.

entries.japanese:
「―――志貴さま」
　……朝の光に交じって、翡翠の呼び声が聞こえてくる。
「―――志貴さま、お時間です。
お目覚めください」
　抑揚のない翡翠の声に、意識がはっきりと覚めていく。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki.”
Hisui’s voice reached me through the morning light.
“Master Shiki, it is time. Please wake up.”
Hisui’s level voice drew me steadily into consciousness.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Shiki-sama."
…… I can hear Hisui's voice mingling with the morning light.
"---Shiki-sama, it is time.
Please wake up."
Her inflectionless voice awakens me.

entries.japanese:
「――――――」
　目を覚ましたとたん、厭なモノが視界に入ってきた。
　ずきり、とこめかみには銃創のような頭痛。
「あ――――」
　起きたばかりの意識が、がらり、と足場を失っていく。
そのまま眩暈を起こしてしまう前に、急いで枕元のメガネを手に取った。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――――”
The moment I woke, something hateful intruded on my vision.
A headache like a gunshot stabbed through my temple.
“Ah—”
My newly awakened mind lost its footing all at once. Before vertigo could take hold, I snatched the glasses from beside my pillow.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------"
As soon as I wake up, terrible things enter my vision.
I get a headache like I was just shot in the head.
"Ah----"
I almost lose my just awakened consciousness.
Before I fade away completely, I quickly grab my glasses.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま……？
　ご気分が優れないのですか？」
「……いや、昨日の疲れがまだ残ってるだけだよ。
すぐによくなるから、心配はしなくていい」
　軽く頭をふって、さっきまで視えていたものを記憶から振り払う。
　……昨夜、無理をしてアルクェイドとの約束を守ったものだから、まだ体は本調子になってくれないらしい。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki? Are you feeling unwell?” “No, I’m only still tired from yesterday. It’ll pass soon, so don’t worry.”
I shook my head, trying to scatter the memory of what I had just seen.
Apparently, I had pushed myself too hard keeping my promise to Arcueid last night, and my body still had not returned to normal.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama……?
Are you not feeling well?"
"…… No, I'm just a little tired from yesterday.
I'll be alright, so don't worry."
Lightly shaking my head, I clear my head of what I was seeing.
…… Last night, I forced myself to keep my promise with Arcueid, so my body isn't back to normal yet.

entries.japanese:
「おはよう翡翠。
今朝も起こしにてきてくれてありがとう」
　ベッドから上半身を起こしながら、できるだけ自然に笑顔を向けた。
「いえ、これがわたしの仕事ですから。
志貴さまに感謝されるほどのことではありません」
「そうかな、俺はすごくありがたいけど。
目覚し時計の音なんかより、何倍もあったかい感じがする」
　ベッドから立ちあがる。
　時刻は朝の七時前―――いつもより十分ほど早い時間。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Good morning, Hisui. Thanks for waking me again.”
As I sat up in bed, I gave her the most natural smile I could manage.
“It is only my duty. There is no need for Master Shiki to thank me.”
“Maybe, but I’m really grateful. Waking to your voice feels so much warmer than an alarm clock.”
I rose from bed.
It was not yet seven—about ten minutes earlier than usual.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Good morning, Hisui.
Thanks for coming to wake me up, as always."
Sitting up in bed, I do my best to smile naturally.

"No, this is my duty.
There is no need for you to thank me, Shiki-sama."
"Really, but I am grateful.
You are infinitely better than an alarm clock."
I stand up.
It's not yet seven o'clock---about ten minutes earlier than I usually get up.

entries.japanese:
「朝ごはんだろ？
　すぐに行くから先に行っててくれ」
「はい。
それでは居間の方でお待ちしております」
　ふかぶかとお辞儀をして翡翠は退室していった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Breakfast, right? I’ll be down in a minute, so go on ahead.”
“Very well. I shall await you in the sitting room.”
Hisui bowed deeply and withdrew.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Hmm, breakfast?
I'll be there soon, so please go ahead of me."
"Yes, I will wait for you in the sitting room."
Giving a bow, Hisui exits the room.

entries.japanese:
―――さて。
　まだ体はだるいけど、学校に行けないほどじゃない。
琥珀さんが作ってくれる朝食を食べれば体力も戻ってくれる事だろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Now, then.
My body still felt sluggish, but not enough to keep me from school. Once I had eaten Kohaku’s breakfast, my strength would surely return.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----Well then.
I'm still feeling a little sluggish, but it's not so bad that I have to skip school.
I'm sure after I eat the breakfast Kohaku-san prepared, I'll feel a lot better.

entries.japanese:
居間にはいつも通り、ソファーに座った秋葉と壁際に控えている翡翠の姿があった。
「おはようございます兄さん。
昨夜はゆっくり休まれましたか？」
　居間に入るなり、秋葉は落ちついた素振りで挨拶をしてきた。
　秋葉は俺が昨夜抜け出した事を知らない。
……あんなに心配してくれたっていうのに、秋葉を騙して外に出てしまった事が後ろめたい。
entries.maoEnglish:
The sitting room held the same familiar tableau: Akiha seated on the sofa, Hisui waiting beside the wall.
“Good morning, Brother. Did you sleep well last night?”
Akiha greeted me with perfect composure the moment I entered.
She did not know I had slipped out last night. After she had worried over me so much, deceiving her and leaving the house weighed heavily on me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
As usual, Akiha is sitting on the sofa, and Hisui is waiting by the wall.
"Good morning, Nii-san.
Did you sleep well last night?"
Akiha greets me calmly as I enter the room.
She doesn't know I left last night.
…… Since she was so worried, I feel guilty for sneaking out.

entries.japanese:
「……うん、おはよう秋葉。
なんていうか、今朝も早いんだな」
「いえ、わたしはいつも通りですけど……兄さん？」
　秋葉は俺の心を見透かすように、まっすぐに見つめてくる。
「あ―――俺の顔になにかついてるのか、秋葉？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Morning, Akiha. You’re up early again.”
“No, this is my usual hour, but—Brother?”
Akiha looked straight at me as though she could see into my mind.
“Ah—do I have something on my face, Akiha?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Yeah, good morning Akiha.
You're up early today, too."
"No, I'm like always…… Nii-san?"
As if reading my mind, she looks directly at me.
"Um----Is there something on my face, Akiha?"

entries.japanese:
「いえ、そういう事ではないんですけど……兄さん、本当に大丈夫なんですか？
　まだ顔色が悪いようですし、気分が優れないのでしたら今日はお休みになったほうが―――」
―――ああ、そういう事か。
　昨夜の事がバレたんじゃないと解って、ホッと胸を撫で下ろす。
entries.maoEnglish:
“No, that isn’t it, but are you truly all right, Brother? You’re still pale, and if you feel unwell, perhaps you should stay home today—”
―――Oh, so that was it.
Relieved that she hadn’t discovered what I had done last night, I let out the breath I had been holding.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No, that isn't it…… Nii-san, are you really alright?
You still do not look well, so if you are still sick, maybe it is better if you just rest today----"
----Oh, that's it.
I relax, realizing she did not find out about last night.

entries.japanese:
「いや、体のほうは大丈夫だよ。
そのうちに治るから、そう心配そうな顔はしないでくれ」
「……はい。
兄さんがそうおっしゃられるのでしたら、私から言うべき事はありませんね」
　秋葉は納得がいかない顔つきで黙り込んだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“No, I’m fine. It’ll pass soon, so please don’t look so worried.”
“Very well. If you say so, Brother, then I have nothing more to add.”
Still plainly unconvinced, Akiha fell silent.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No, I'm really okay.
I'll be better sooner or later, so please don't look so worried."
"…… Okay.
If you say so, Nii-san, then I will not say anything."
She goes quiet, still looking worried.

entries.japanese:
「なんだ、珍しく簡単に納得するんだな。
なんか、秋葉らしくなくて拍子抜けした」
「むっ。
私、普段から物分りはいいほうです。
私が兄さんを注意するのは、兄さんのほうに問題があるからでしょう。
ご自分の至らなさを私のせいにしないでください」
　じとり、と流し目をしてくる秋葉。
「おっ、やっと調子が出てきたな。
やっぱり秋葉がツンケンしてないと朝っていう気がしないよな、翡翠」
「………………」
　急に声をかけられたせいか、それとも返答すべき言葉がみつからないのか。
翡翠は黙ったまま、否定も肯定もしない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“That was easy—you almost never give in so quickly. It’s so unlike you that I don’t know what to do with myself.”
“Hmph. I am ordinarily a very reasonable person. When I reprimand you, it is because you have done something deserving of reprimand. Please do not blame your own shortcomings on me.”
Akiha cut me a sidelong glare.
“Ah, there you are—it doesn’t feel like morning unless Akiha is snapping at me. Right, Hisui?”
“…”
Did I catch her off guard, or could she simply not find an answer? Hisui remained silent, neither agreeing nor denying it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hm, it's quite rare for you to be convinced this quickly.
It's not like you."
"Hey, I'm always sensible.
I only warn you because you're the one with the problems.
So please do not blame me for your imperfections."
She glares at me.
"Oh, that's more like it.
Hey, Hisui, doesn't it not feel like morning unless Akiha gets harsh?"
"……………………"
Is it because I suddenly called out to her or because she doesn't know what to say?
Hisui neither confirms nor denies my statement.

entries.japanese:
「ほら見ろ秋葉。
翡翠もそう思うってさ」
「馬鹿なこと言わないでください。
翡翠は呆れて何も言わないだけでしょう」
　眉間にしわをよせて、秋葉は俺の顔を睨む。
「それにですね、これは前から言おうと思っていたんですけど、兄さんは翡翠に頼りすぎよ。
　今朝だって昨日から眠っていたんだから、もっと早くに起きてきてもいいものなのに結局はいつも通りの時間でしょう。
　翡翠が何も言わないのをいい事に緩みきっているんじゃないですか？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“See, Akiha? Hisui agrees with me.”
“Don’t be absurd. Hisui is silent because she is appalled.”
Akiha knitted her brow and glared at me.
“And there is something else I’ve been meaning to tell you: you rely on Hisui far too much.
You had been asleep since yesterday, yet this morning you still rose at your usual hour instead of waking early.
Aren’t you taking advantage of the fact that Hisui never complains?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"See?
Look, Akiha, Hisui thinks so, too."
"Don't be foolish.
Hisui doesn't say anything because she is surprised."
Wrinkling her forehead in a frown, Akiha glares again.
"Also, I've always wanted to say this, but you rely on Hisui too much.
You have been sleeping since yesterday, so it would have been fine if you woke up earlier.
But you always wake up late.
Are you slacking off because Hisui does not say anything?"

entries.japanese:
「な―――それじゃまるで、俺が翡翠を困らせてるみたいじゃないか！」
「みたい、じゃなくて事実困らせているじゃない。
ね、貴方もそう思うでしょう、翡翠？」
「………………」
　翡翠はやっぱり何も言わず、ただ静かに立ち尽くしているだけだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What—you make it sound as if I’m causing Hisui trouble!”
“It doesn’t merely sound that way. You are causing her trouble, aren’t you, Hisui?”
“…”
Hisui again said nothing, merely standing there in silence.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Wha----You make it sound like I'm causing her trouble!"
"Not 'like', you are causing her trouble.
Hey, don't you think so, Hisui?"
"………………"
Hisui still doesn't say anything and stands there quietly.

entries.japanese:
「ほら。
翡翠もそう思うって言ってます」
「そんなワケあるかっ！
　翡翠は何も言ってないだろ！」
「…………………」
　翡翠は黙っている。
　ただ、その黙り方がどちらかというと、俺より秋葉の意見に賛同しているような、そんな感じだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“There. Hisui says she agrees with me.”
“She does not! Hisui hasn’t said a word!”
“…”
Hisui remained silent.
Yet somehow her particular silence seemed to side more with Akiha than with me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"See?
Hisui says she thinks so, too."
"No way!
She didn't say anything!"
"……………………"
Hisui is silent.
But, her silence feels like she's agreeing more with Akiha.

entries.japanese:
「…………う」
　なんか、気がつかないうちに状況は二対一になってしまっている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Urgh.”
Before I knew it, the situation had become two against one.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"………… Oogh."
I feel like it's now two against one.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さーん、朝食の支度ができましたよー」
　と、そこでタイミングよく琥珀さんの声が響いてきた。
「えっと、それじゃ朝ごはんを食べてくる」
　いそいそと居間を横切って食堂に向かう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki—breakfast is ready!”
Kohaku’s voice rang out with impeccable timing.
“Right, then—I’ll go eat.”
I hurried across the sitting room toward the dining room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-san.
Breakfast is ready~"
With great timing, Kohaku-san's voice echoes through the room.
"Um, I'm gonna go eat."
I quickly head towards the dining room.

entries.japanese:
「…………………」
　なんか、二人の無言の圧力が、背中にどーんとのしかかってきていたりした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
Their silent disapproval landed on my back with crushing weight.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……………………"
I feel the silent pressure of the two behind me drilling into my back.

entries.japanese:
朝食を終えて居間に戻ってくる。
　秋葉の姿はなく、居間には翡翠の姿だけがあった。
entries.maoEnglish:
After breakfast I returned to the sitting room.
Akiha was gone; only Hisui remained.
entries.mirrorMoon:
After breakfast, I head back to the sitting room.
Akiha isn't there, and Hisui is the only one standing.

entries.japanese:
「あれ、秋葉はもう学校？」
「はい。
志貴さまも登校のお時間です」
「あ、もう二十分か。
確かにそろそろ支度をしないとまずいかな」
　……正直、まだ体が本調子じゃないけどしばらくすれば元に戻るだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What, has Akiha left for school already?”
“Yes. It is also time for you to leave, Master Shiki.”
“Oh, it’s twenty past already. I really should get ready.”
To be honest, I still felt far from well, but I would surely recover before long.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Huh?
Akiha left for school already?"
"Yes.
It is also time for you to go to school as well, Shiki-sama."
"Ah, it's already twenty after?
I guess I should get going soon."
…… To be honest, I still don't feel too good, but I'm sure I'll return to normal soon.

entries.japanese:
「それじゃ翡翠、悪いけど部屋から鞄を持ってきてくれないか。
俺は顔を洗ってくるから」
「はい、かしこまりました」
　支度を整えて屋敷を出る。
　翡翠は鞄を持ったまま玄関まで見送りにきてくれる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hisui, would you mind bringing my bag down from my room? I’m going to wash my face.”
“Yes—right away.”
Once I was ready, I left the mansion.
Hisui carried my bag all the way to the entrance to see me off.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Sorry, Hisui, but can you get my bag from my room?
I'm going to wash my face."
"As you wish."
After getting all my preparations done, I leave the mansion.
Holding my bag, Hisui sees me off at the entrance.

entries.japanese:
「それじゃ行ってくる。
何時に帰ってくるかは解らないけど、夕食までには帰ってくるよ」
「はい、お待ちしております」
　しずしずとお辞儀をする翡翠。
　……ただ、その顔はどこか不安そうだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’m off. I don’t know exactly when I’ll be back, but I’ll make it home before dinner.”
“Very well, I shall await your return.”
Hisui bowed with quiet grace.
Yet there was something anxious in her face.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I'll be going.
I'm not sure when I'll be back, but probably by dinner."
"Yes, I will be waiting."
She gives a silent bow.
…… There's a trace of uneasiness in her face.

entries.japanese:
「翡翠？
　どこか具合が悪いのか？」
「いえ―――わたしの事ではなく、志貴さまのお顔の色が優れないので、このまま志貴さまを行かせていいものか、わからなくて」
　ためらいがちにそんな事を言う。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hisui? Are you feeling ill?”
“No—it isn’t me; Master Shiki looks pale, and I’m not sure whether I should allow Master Shiki to leave in that condition.”
She says it reluctantly.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hisui?
Are you feeling sick?"
"No----it is not me, but you do not appear well.
I am unsure if it is a good idea to let you go."
She speaks hesitantly.

entries.japanese:
「大丈夫だよ。
たしかに体調はよくないけど、少し体が重いだけなんだ。
まったく、秋葉も翡翠も昨日の事で心配性になっているんじゃないか？」
「……そう、でしょうか。
わたしたちの気のせいであるのなら、それに越したことはないのですが」
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’ll be fine. I’m not feeling great, but my body is only a little heavy. Honestly, after yesterday, you and Akiha have both become such worriers.”
“Perhaps. Nothing would please me more than for this to be only our imagination.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I'm alright.
I don't feel great, but just a little heavy.
Geez, both you and Akiha like to worry a lot."
"…… Is that so?
If it is just us, then that will be fine, but…"

entries.japanese:
「……しょうがないな。
それじゃ今日は早めに帰ってきて休むから、それでいいだろ。
今日は無茶はしないから、そんな顔はしないでくれ」
「………はい。
申し訳ありません、志貴さま」
　翡翠はますます不安そうな顔をする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“All right. I’ll come home early today and rest; will that satisfy you? I promise I won’t overdo it, so please don’t look at me that way.”
“Yes. Forgive me, Master Shiki.”
If anything, Hisui looked even more anxious.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Geez.
I'll come back early today and rest, so that should be good, right?
I won't overdo anything, so don't look like that."
"………… Yes.
Forgive me, Shiki-sama."
She still looks very worried.

entries.japanese:
「行ってくるよ。
帰ってくるころには元気になっているから、気楽に待っていてくれ」
「あ―――志貴さま――――」
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’m off. By the time I come home, I’ll be perfectly well, so try not to worry while you wait.”
“Ah—Master Shiki—”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I'm off.
I'll be better by the time I get back, so please relax."
"Ah----Shiki-sama----"

entries.japanese:
翡翠をふりきって屋敷を後にする。
　最後まで不安そうに俺を見送る翡翠の姿が、いつになく印象に残っていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
I left Hisui behind and departed the mansion.
The sight of her watching me to the very end, worry plain on her face, remained with me as it never had before.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I ignore her and leave the mansion.
The image of Hisui watching me uneasily remains in my head.

entries.japanese:
学校に向かう。
　手足がまだ重く、他人の体を着ているような感覚で坂道を下りていく。
　……昨夜からの疲れが体の芯に残っているのか。
　すぐに回復すると思っていた体の淀みは、なかなか消え去ってはくれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
I headed for school.
My limbs were still heavy, and I walked down the hill as though wearing someone else’s body.
Perhaps the exhaustion of last night had lodged deep inside me. The sluggishness I had expected to fade quickly refused to leave.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I head towards school.
My feet are heavy and it feels like I'm in another person's body as I head down the hill.
…… It's probably just the weariness from last night.
Even though I thought I would recover right away, the sluggishness doesn't fade.

entries.japanese:
朝の七時五十分。
　正門は登校してくる生徒たちの姿で混雑していた。
「────あ」
　校門をくぐっていく後ろ姿に見知った人影があった。
entries.maoEnglish:
Seven fifty in the morning.
The main gate was crowded with arriving students.
“Ah.”
Among the backs passing through it, I recognized someone.
entries.mirrorMoon:
It's ten minutes until eight.
The school gate is flooded with arriving students.
"---Ah."
By the gate, I see a familiar figure.

entries.japanese:
「……シエル、先輩」
　それは、別段どうという事はない朝の風景だ。
　ただ、あの時の光景―――
　それさえなければ、本当に何気ない朝の出来事だったろう。
「―――――」
　自分でも何をしたいのか分からないまま、先輩の後ろ姿を追いかけた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ciel…”
It should have been an utterly ordinary morning scene.
Except for what I had seen that night—
Without that, it truly would have been nothing more than a chance encounter on an ordinary morning.
“…”
Not knowing what I even meant to do, I hurried after Ciel.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Ciel… Senpai."
It's a completely normal, morning scene.
But, what I saw that time----
If it wasn't for that, it would be a normal morning.
"------"
Not even knowing what I plan on doing, I chase after Senpai.

entries.japanese:
「先輩！」
　声をかけて呼び止める。
「あ、おはようございます遠野くん。
めずらしいですね、校庭で会うなんて」
「……ああ。
先輩の後ろ姿が見えたから走ってきたんだ。
その……ちょっと聞きたい事があってさ」
　ちら、と先輩の顔を盗み見る。
「はい、なんでしょう」
　先輩はいつもの柔らかな笑顔を向けてくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ciel!”
I called out and stopped her.
“Oh, good morning, Tohno. Fancy meeting you in the schoolyard.”
“Yeah. I saw you up ahead and ran after you. There’s something I wanted to ask.”
I stole a glance at her face.
“Of course—what is it?”
Ciel gave me her usual gentle smile.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Senpai!"
I call after her.
"Oh, good morning, Tohno-kun.
It's strange meeting you out here."
"…… Yeah, I saw your figure from behind, so I ran after you, Senpai.
Um…… there was something I wanted to ask."
I sneak a look at her face.

"Yes, what is it?"
She faces me with her usual, gentle smile.

entries.japanese:
「……あのさ先輩。
一昨日の夜、うちの近くにいなかった？
　黒いコートみたいな服を着て、スカートをこうばさばさーとなびかせて」
「……？
　なんですか、それ」
「だから……！
　えっと、それと――そう、編み上げブーツがすごく似合ってたじゃないか。
ちょっと見惚れるぐらい、かっこ良かった」
entries.maoEnglish:
“…Ciel, were you near my house the night before last? Wearing something like a black coat, with your skirt whipping around in the wind?”
“…? What are you talking about?”
“You know…! And—right, the lace-up boots looked fantastic on you. You looked so striking I couldn’t help staring.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Uh Senpai.
Two nights ago, were you near my house?
In a black coat and a skirt flowing in the wind."
"……?
What are you talking about?"
"Um……!
well--yeah, the high-laced boots suited you.
I was kind of fascinated, you looked, really cool."

entries.japanese:
……はい？
　と先輩は首をかしげる。
　俺が何を言ってるのか皆目見当がつかない、というように顔をしかめてから、先輩はきっぱりと否定した。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What?” Ciel tilted her head.
After frowning in utter bewilderment, she gave me a flat denial.
entries.mirrorMoon:
……"Huh?" Senpai tilts her head.
She frowns like she doesn't understand my words completely, and then denies it.

entries.japanese:
「えっと、よくわかりませんけど、一昨日の夜にわたしが遠野くんの家の近くにいて、そうゆうカッコウをしていたんですか？」
「ああ。
あれ、先輩だろ？」
「わけありませんっ。
遠野くん、わたしってそんなに暇な人に見えるんですか？」
―――先輩は、本気で怒ってしまった。
　そこにしらをきっているとか嘘をついているとか、そういったものは一切ない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Let me understand this: you think I was near your house the night before last, dressed that way?”
“Yes. That was you, wasn’t it?”
“Of course not! Tohno, do I really look as though I have that much time on my hands?”
―――Ciel was genuinely angry.
There was no hint that she was feigning ignorance or telling a lie.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Um, I don't quite understand, but you're saying that I was near your house two nights ago, looking like that?"
"Yeah.
Senpai, that was you, right?"
"No way.
Tohno-kun, are you saying I look like I really have that much free time?"
---Senpai is really angry.
She can't be playing dumb or lying.

entries.japanese:
「あ───いや、そんな事はないんだけど、その……昨日、先輩に似た人を公園で見かけたから、それで―――」
　はあ、と先輩はため息をつく。
「遠野くん、それわたしじゃないです。
わたし、そういう趣味はないですから」
「あ───うん、わかってる。
ただちょっと聞きたかっただけなんだ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“No, that isn’t what I meant—it’s just that yesterday I saw someone in the park who looked like you, so—”
Ciel sighed.
“Tohno, it wasn’t me. I have no taste for dressing that way.”
“Ah—right, I understand. I only wanted to ask.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah----No, that's not it, but I just…… saw someone that looked like you in park last night, so---"
Senpai gives a sigh.
"Tohno-kun, that wasn't me.
I don't have that kind of hobby."
"Ah---Yeah, I know.
I just wanted to ask."

entries.japanese:
……たしかに言われて見ればその通りだ。
　シエル先輩と昨日の夜の人物はぜんぜん結びつかない。
　そもそも先輩は普通の人だし、もしあの場に居合わせたのなら───俺がナイフをもって得体の知れない包帯男と殺しあうところを見たハズだ。
　あんな凄惨な場面を見てしまったのなら、俺とこうして今までどおり話なんか出来るはずがない。
entries.maoEnglish:
Now that she had said it, she was obviously right.
I could find no connection at all between Ciel and the figure from last night.
Ciel was an ordinary person, and if she had been there, she would have seen me wielding a knife in a fight to the death against that mysterious bandaged man.
No one who had witnessed something so horrific could stand here speaking to me as normally as ever.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Certainly after having her say that, she is right.
Ciel-senpai and the person that night aren't related at all.
In the first place, Senpai's just a normal person, and if she was actually there---she had to have seen me fight that bandaged guy with my knife.
If she saw such a gruesome scene, there'd be no way she could talk with me normally like this.

entries.japanese:
「……ごめん、今のは忘れて。
なんか他人の空似だったみたいだ」
「いいですけど……そんなにわたしに似てたんですか、そのヘンな人」
「そう言われると自信ないな。
夜だったし、遠かったし………って、あれ？」
　そう、遠くて顔だってよく見えなかった。
　なのにどうして、俺はアレが先輩に似てる、なんて思ったんだろう……？
entries.maoEnglish:
“Sorry, forget I said anything. It must have been someone who happened to look like you.”
“All right, but did that strange woman really resemble me so closely?”
“Now that you ask, I’m not sure. It was dark and she was far away—and, wait?”
Yes, she had been far away, and I had barely seen her face.
Then why had I decided that thing looked like Ciel…?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Sorry, please forget about it.
I guess it was just someone else."
"That's fine, but…… did that person really look like me?
That weird person?"
"Well, I'm not too sure.
It was dark, and far away………… huh?"
Yeah, it was far and I couldn't make out her face.
So why did I think it looked like Senpai……?

entries.japanese:
「……なんだかなぁ。
やっぱりどうかしてたのかもしんない」
　うーん、と腕をくんでうなだれる。
　と、門限十分前の予鈴が鳴り響いた。
「―――やばっ、遅刻する。
それじゃ先輩、またあとで！」
entries.maoEnglish:
“I don’t know. Maybe I really was out of my mind.”
I folded my arms and hung my head, thinking hard.
Then the warning bell rang, leaving ten minutes until homeroom.
“Oh, hell, I’m going to be late. See you later, Ciel!”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Hmm… Maybe there is something wrong with me."
I cross my arms and think.

Then, the ten minute bell rings.
"---Crap, we'll be late.
Bye, Senpai, see you later!"

entries.japanese:
教室に駆け込む。
　ホームルーム五分前、教室の中は未だにがやがやと騒がしい。
「有彦は来てない、か」
　まあ、あいつの事だから二時間目あたりからやってくるに違いない。
entries.maoEnglish:
I dashed into the classroom.
With five minutes left before homeroom, the room was still full of noisy chatter.
“Arihiko isn’t here, huh.”
Knowing him, he would probably stroll in around second period.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I dash into my classroom.
It's still five minutes before class, so it's very noisy inside.
"Arihiko, isn't here."
Knowing him, he'll probably come in around second period.

entries.japanese:
昼休みになった。
　有彦は休みらしい。
　……今日の欠席者は乾有彦と弓塚さつきの二人だ。
弓塚さつきのほうは風邪をこじらせたとかでここのところずっと欠席している。
entries.maoEnglish:
Lunchtime came.
Apparently Arihiko was absent.
Today’s absentees were Arihiko Inui and Satsuki Yumizuka. Yumizuka had supposedly come down with a stubborn cold and had been away for several days now.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Lunch time.
It looks like Arihiko's not coming.
…… Inui Arihiko and Yumizuka Satsuki are the two people absent today.
Yumizuka Satsuki has caught a cold or something and she will be absent for a while.

entries.japanese:
「……先輩も来そうにないし、一人でメシにするか」
　ぼんやりと呟いてみたが、食欲はまったくなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ciel doesn’t look like she’s coming either, so I guess I’ll eat alone.”
I muttered absently, though I had no appetite at all.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Senpai doesn't seem to be coming too, so I guess I'll eat by myself."
I say that, but I'm not hungry.

entries.japanese:
……なんだろう。
　朝から調子は悪かったけど、学校に来てから余計に気持ちが悪くなった気がする。
　それも体の重さだけじゃない。
胸の古傷がチリチリして、痒いような煩わしいような、そんな感覚がしている。
entries.maoEnglish:
What was wrong with me?
I had felt ill since morning, but coming to school seemed to have made it worse.
It was more than the heaviness in my body. The old scar on my chest prickled with an irritating sensation, almost like an itch.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… What is it?
I didn't feel so good to begin with, but after coming to school, I feel a lot worse.
It's not just my body feeling heavy.
The scar on my chest is irritating; it's an annoying sensation.

entries.japanese:
「……学校、休んだほうが良かったかな」
　……一瞬だけ翡翠と秋葉の不安そうな顔が浮かんだ。
　せめて今夜だけは休んでほしい、という秋葉の願いを無視してアルクェイドに会いに行ったのが響いているのか。
　ただ座っているだけで疲れてしまって、俺はよく解らない違和感にさいなまれてしまっている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Maybe I should’ve stayed home.”
For an instant, Hisui’s and Akiha’s worried faces rose in my mind.
Was this the price of ignoring Akiha’s plea that I rest for at least one night and going to meet Arcueid?
Merely sitting upright exhausted me, while an incomprehensible sense of wrongness tormented my body.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Maybe I shouldn't have come to school."
…… For a brief moment, I see the worrying faces of Hisui and Akiha in my mind.
Maybe the fact that I ignored Akiha's wishes for me to rest last night and instead went to see Arcueid might've caused this.
Being worn out by just sitting, I start to feel a strange uneasiness.

entries.japanese:
……授業が始まっている。
　なんの授業だったか。
今日の五時限目の科目が思い出せない。
　黒板を見ても、教師が刻んでいるチョークの跡を見ても、どうしても何の授業なのか。
　俺には、読み取れない。
　文字が、水に流される絵の具のように、ぐちゃぐちゃに混ざっていくような、錯覚。
entries.maoEnglish:
Class had begun.
What subject was this? I couldn’t remember what we had fifth period today.
No matter how I stared at the blackboard or the trails of chalk the teacher carved across it, I couldn’t tell what lesson this was.
I couldn’t read it.
The letters seemed to bleed together like paint washed away by water.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Class has started already.
Which class was it?
I can't remember today's fifth period lesson.
Even though I look at the blackboard and stare at the marks left behind by the teacher's chalk, I still don't know what class this is.
I can't read it.
The letters start to flow like water and mix together like some sort of hallucination.

entries.japanese:
「うっ…………」
　吐き気が、する。
　眩り、と。
意識が病んでいくような、傾斜。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ugh…”
I felt sick.
The world tipped. My consciousness seemed to sicken with it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ugh…………"
I feel like I'm going to throw up.
Dizziness.
My mind starts to slide away.

entries.japanese:
キチキチ。
　　　カタカタ。
　　　　　ギシギシ。
　　　　　　　ガクガク。
entries.maoEnglish:
Creak.
  Rattle.
    Groan.
      Shudder.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Click, click.
Tremble, tremble.
Creak, creak.
Wobble,  wobble.

entries.japanese:
そんな音が、爪弾かれていく。
　違和感。
　その齟齬は、どこからくるのか。
　体中に違和感があって落ち着かない。
　キチキチと歪んでいく。
　まるで骨という骨の接合部分が微妙にズレているみたいだ。
　そう、接合の部分がズレているから無理が生じる。
遠野志貴の躯は、目に見えない煙を吐き出していて、今にもガラガラと崩れていく。
entries.maoEnglish:
The sounds plucked at me one by one.
Something was wrong.
Where did the mismatch begin?
Something felt wrong throughout my body, making it impossible to sit still.
I creaked tighter and tighter.
It felt as though every joint between my bones had slipped slightly out of alignment.
Yes—the displaced joints placed the whole structure under strain. Shiki Tohno’s frame belched invisible smoke and threatened to collapse into pieces at any moment.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Those noises stick out.

Incompatibility.
Where is that inconsistency coming from?
I can't settle this feeling of something being out of place throughout my body.
It fills me to the brim.
As if my bones are sliding out of place in their joints.
Yes, since my joints are out of place, it causes the unnatural feeling.
My corpse is burning unseen smoke and crumbling away.

entries.japanese:
キチキチ。
カタカタ。
ギチギチ。
ガチガチ。
entries.maoEnglish: Creak. Rattle. Grind. Clatter.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Click, click.
Tremble, tremble.
Creak, creak.
Wobble, wobble.

entries.japanese:
ガタン、と椅子から落ちた。
　キャア、という女生徒の声があがる。
　教師がかけよってくる足音が聞こえる。
　俺は。
　完全に気を失ってしまっているのに、どこか離れた所で、冷静に自分が倒れこむ場面を眺めていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
I crashed out of my chair.
A girl screamed.
I heard the teacher running toward me.
I had lost consciousness completely.
Even so, some calm, distant part of me watched my own body fall.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I fall from my chair.
A girl screams.
I hear the footsteps of the teacher running to me.
I…
Even though I've completely passed out, I calmly watch myself from far away.

entries.japanese:
……その後はお決まりの展開だった。
　貧血で気を失った俺は保健室に運ばれて、体調が良くなるまでベッドで眠る事になった。
　夜の七時過ぎ、学校の門限がすぎてもまだ熱が三十八度近くあるため、保険医は遠野の家に誰か迎えに来るように連絡して帰ってしまった。
　で、その結果が。
entries.maoEnglish:
What followed was routine.
After fainting from anemia, I was carried to the infirmary and left to sleep until I recovered.
A little after seven, the school’s closing time had passed, but my fever was still nearly thirty-eight degrees; the nurse called the Tohno residence and asked that someone collect me, then went home.
And the result was this.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… What follows is like always.
Collapsed from my anemia, I was carried to the clinic where I slept until I recovered.
Since I had a fever of over 38 degrees Celsius past seven o'clock, the school's closing time, the nurse called my house for someone to pick me up and went home.
And this resulted in…

entries.japanese:
「あっ、大丈夫ですか志貴さん？
　まだ熱があるんですから、遠慮なさらずにわたしの肩につかまってくださいな」
―――まあ、こういう事である。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh—are you all right, Master Shiki? You still have a fever, so don’t hold back; lean on my shoulder.”
―――Well, that was the result.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Are you okay, Shiki-san?
You still have a fever, so please do not hesitate to lean on my shoulder."
----Yeah, that's how it is.

entries.japanese:
「……いや、大丈夫です。
歩くぐらいはできるから、気を遣わないでください」
　琥珀さんから離れて、精一杯の強がりを口にした。
　……まったく。
琥珀さんに迎えに来てもらっただけでも恥ずかしいのに、その上肩まで貸してもらった日には情けなくて死にたくなる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“No, I’m fine. I can walk, so please don’t trouble yourself.”
I pulled away from Kohaku and bluffed with all the strength I had.
Having her come fetch me was embarrassing enough. If I made her support me too, I would die of shame.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… No, I'm alright.
I can at least walk, so please don't worry."
Stepping away from Kohaku-san, I attempt to bluff my way out of it.
…… Geez.
It's embarrassing enough for Kohaku-san to come pick me up.
The day I lean on her shoulders too, I'll die.

entries.japanese:
「もう、だめですよ無理をしちゃ。
志貴さんのお体が弱いのは志貴さんのせいじゃないんですから、少しぐらい甘えていいんです。
　秋葉さまや翡翠ちゃんには黙っていてあげますから、今ぐらいはわたしに頼っていいんですよ」
　琥珀さんは優しい笑顔のまま、俺の手を握ってくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You mustn’t push yourself. It isn’t your fault that your health is delicate, Master Shiki, so there’s nothing wrong with relying on someone now and then.
I won’t tell Miss Akiha or Hisui, so just for tonight, let me take care of you.”
Still smiling gently, Kohaku took my hand.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Oh that's not good, forcing yourself like that.
It isn't your fault that your body is weak, Shiki-san.
So you can ask for help a little.
I won't tell Akiha-sama or Hisui-chan, so it's okay to depend on me for now."
With a gentle smile, she takes my hand.

entries.japanese:
「あ……はい、すみません」
　ぼっ、と顔が赤くなるのを意識しながら、素直に琥珀さんの言葉に従った。
　……たしかに、これ以上意地を張るとまた倒れかねない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ah—yes, I’m sorry.”
Conscious of my face blazing red, I meekly did as Kohaku said.
She was right: if I kept pretending, I might collapse again.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah…… yes, sorry."
Blushing furiously, I meekly do as she says.
…… Certainly I might collapse if I continue to be stubborn.

entries.japanese:
「外にお車を待たせてありますから、そこまで頑張ってくださいね」
　俺の手を引いて、琥珀さんは歩き始める。
「あ――――」
　……まずい。
歩くだけで眩暈がする。
　朦朧とした意識のまま、琥珀さんに任せて昇降口に向かって歩き出した。
entries.maoEnglish:
“The car is waiting outside, so you only need to make it that far.”
Holding my hand, Kohaku began to walk.
“Ah—”
This was bad. Simply walking made the world spin.
With my thoughts clouded, I let Kohaku lead me toward the entrance.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"There is a car waiting outside, so please hold on until then."
Pulling my hand, Kohaku-san starts to walk.
"Ah----"
…… This isn't good.
Just walking makes me incredibly dizzy.
I depend upon Kohaku-san to lead me to the stairwell as I hold onto my consciousness.

entries.japanese:
あ――――れ？
　なんで―――一階から、二階になんて、あがっているんだろう、俺は。
entries.maoEnglish:
Wai—t.
Why was I climbing from the first floor to the second?
entries.mirrorMoon:
Hu----h?
Why----am I going up… to… the second… floor?

entries.japanese:
「あの……琥珀さん、こっちは、違う」
　声をかける。
　返事はない。
いや、そればかりか―――琥珀さんの手の感触も、琥珀さんの姿さえ、ない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Kohaku, this isn’t the way.”
I called to her.
There was no answer. Worse—there was no warmth of her hand, no sign of Kohaku at all.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Um…… Kohaku-san… this… isn't… the right way."
I call out to her.
There's no response.
No, not only that----I don't feel her hand, or even see her.

entries.japanese:
「琥珀……さん？」
　定まらない意識を総動員してあたりを見渡す。
　廊下には誰もいない。
　ただ、窓から差しこんでくる月明かりだけが、鮮明だった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Kohaku…?”
I marshaled every scrap of my wavering awareness and looked around.
The corridor was empty.
Only the moonlight spilling through the windows remained sharp and clear.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Kohaku…… san?"
I use all of my foggy consciousness to look around me.
There's no one in the hallway.
Only the moonlight streaming from the window is vivid.

entries.japanese:
「―――――――」
　それは、唐突にやってきた。
「あ――――――」
　どくん、と高鳴る鼓動。
　背骨にむかって、縦に、ノコギリをひかれるような寒気。
entries.maoEnglish:
“……”
It came without warning.
“Ah—”
My heart slammed against my ribs.
A chill like a saw dragged lengthwise down my spine.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"--------"
It comes suddenly.
"Ah------"
The sound of my heartbeat.
And a chill that races up my spine.

entries.japanese:
どくん。
かつん。
　どくん。
かつん。
　どくん。
かつん。
　どくん。
かつん。
どくん。
かつん。
どくん。
かつん。
かつん。
かつん。
かつん。
entries.maoEnglish:
Thump. Tap.
Thump. Tap.
Thump. Tap.
Thump. Tap. Thump. Tap. Thump. Tap. Tap. Tap. Tap.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Thump.
Tap.

Thump.
Tap.
Thump.
Tap.
Thump.
Tap.
Thump.
Tap.
Thump.
Tap.
Tap.
Tap.
Tap.
Tap.

entries.japanese:
暗い闇の中、足音が近づいてくる。
―――それは。
　あの時に感じた怖れに類似していた。
entries.maoEnglish:
Footsteps approached through the darkness.
―――It was.
A terror like the one I had felt that night.
entries.mirrorMoon:
In the darkness, the footsteps draw closer.
---This is.
This is similar to the fear I felt from that one time.

entries.japanese:
「琥珀、さん……！」
　名前を呼ぶ。
助けを呼ぶためじゃない。
さっきまで一緒にいてくれた琥珀さんが逃げられるように、必死に名前を呼んだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Kohaku…!”
I called her name. Not for help. I called desperately so that Kohaku, who had been beside me moments ago, would know to run.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Kohaku, san……!"
I call her name.
Not to call for help, but to tell her to escape, I frantically call her name.

entries.japanese:
「琥珀さん、琥珀さん、琥珀さん……！」
　何処にいるのか、俺の目では見つけられない。
　かつん、と足音はもう間近に迫ってきている。
　だから、せめて。
　琥珀さんだけでも、無事にここから逃げ出してほしかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Kohaku, Kohaku, Kohaku…!”
My eyes couldn’t find her anywhere.
Tap—the footsteps were almost upon me.
So, if nothing else.
I wanted Kohaku to escape safely.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Kohaku-san, Kohaku-san, Kohaku-san……!"
Where is she?
I don't see her anywhere.
The footsteps are near me now.
At least…
I want Kohaku-san to escape here unharmed.

entries.japanese:
「無駄だよ志貴。
そいつは、ついさっき用済みになった」
　……声が聞こえる。
　目の前の闇。
そこにいるのは
　あの夜、俺を殺そうとした包帯の男だった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“It’s no use, Shiki. I stopped needing her a moment ago.”
I hear a voice.
In the darkness before me. Standing there is
It was the bandaged man who had tried to kill me that night.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"It's useless Shiki.
She's already done."
…… I hear a voice.
In the darkness in front of me is
the bandaged man who tried to kill me that night.

entries.japanese:
「―――――あ」
　……どうしてだろう。
　俺は、コイツの顔を、よく知っている気がする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ah—”
Why did it feel so familiar?
I felt as though I knew his face intimately.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------Ah."
…… Why is it…?
I feel like I know this person's face.

entries.japanese:
「よくよく運がないんだなおまえは。
こんな事なら、屋敷の前で待ち構える必要なぞなかったか」
　……足音が近づいてくる。
「くっ…………あ」
　体を動かそうとする。
　だが足はずるずると動くだけだ。
　連日の無理が祟ったのか。
俺の体は、最後の最後で、故障してしまったようだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You truly have rotten luck. It seems I needn’t have bothered waiting outside your mansion.”
The footsteps drew closer.
“Ngh—ah.”
I tried to move.
But my feet could only drag uselessly along the floor.
Perhaps the strain of the past several days had caught up with me. At the very end, my body had finally broken down.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"You sure aren't lucky.
If knew it was like this, I wouldn't have waited for you in front of the mansion."
…… The footsteps draw closer.
"Ka…… aah."
I try to move.
But I can only totter along.
I guess I pushed my body too hard every day.
It seems like my body, at the very last moment, broke down.

entries.japanese:
「最後に教えてやるよ。
ココが、今のオレの根城なのさ」
　トス、という音がした。
　男の手にはナイフ。
銀色の刃物は、俺の心臓を確実に貫いていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’ll tell you one last thing. This place is my lair now.”
A soft thunk.
A knife gleamed in the man’s hand. Its silver blade had pierced my heart cleanly.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"This is the end, so I'll tell you.
This is my lair now."
I hear a stabbing sound.
In his hands, a knife.
The silver blade pierces directly into my heart.

entries.japanese:
―――ダン、と倒れこむ。
　身体は指先から死んでいく。
　意識が葡萄のように一つ一つ潰れていって、やがて枝だけの残骸になる。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――I struck the floor.
Death spread inward from my fingertips.
One by one, my thoughts burst like grapes until nothing remained but a bare stem.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----I collapse to the ground.
I feel death working its way from my very fingertips.
My mind fades away, drop by drop.

entries.japanese:
その過程。
　ぷつぷつと消えていく理性の束の中で、網膜は空を見ていた。
　他に見るべき場所がなかったから、そこだけを見ていた。
　夜空には青い月。
　……なんていう間抜けさだ。
　死にいく直前だっていうのに、俺は。
　その、なんの変哲もないモノに惚れ惚れした。
entries.maoEnglish:
During that slow extinction.
While the strands of reason snapped and vanished, my eyes watched the sky.
There was nowhere else left to look.
A blue moon hung in the night.
How stupid.
Here I was, a breath from death.
And I could only stare in wonder at something so ordinary.
entries.mirrorMoon:
In that process.
With my fading mind, I look up at the sky.
I have nowhere else to look, so I just look there.
The blue moon is in the night sky.
…… How stupid.
I'm about to die, but I…
I am charmed by such an ordinary thing.

entries.japanese:
あれは、いつの記憶だっただろう。
　黒いヴェールのような森の中で。
　遠い日の凶った夜。
　こんなふうに、月だけを、見上げていた―――
entries.maoEnglish:
When had that memory been?
In a forest like a black veil.
On a cursed night long ago.
I had gazed up at the moon exactly like this—
entries.mirrorMoon:
When is this memory from?
In a forest like a black veil.
On that terrible night.
Just like this, I was staring only at the moon----

entries.japanese: 月を見る、夢を見ていた。
entries.maoEnglish: I dreamed I was looking at the moon.
entries.mirrorMoon: In my dream, I'm staring at the moon.

entries.japanese:
何処で、どうして月を見上げているかは思い出せない。
　ただ他に何も見たくなくて夜空を見上げた時、月があっただけなのかもしれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
I could not remember where I was or why I had raised my eyes to it.
Perhaps I had simply looked into the night because I could bear to see nothing else, and the moon had happened to be there.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I can't remember where I am or why I'm looking up at it.
Maybe I looked up into the night sky not wanting to see anything, and the moon happened to be there.

entries.japanese:
ぎちり、と背骨が軋む。
　血脈を駆け巡るのは寒さのイメージ。
　一人きりの暗闇は、眩暈がする。
　眩く、心を病みつかせるような、月。
entries.maoEnglish:
My spine creaked.
An image of cold coursed through my blood.
Alone in the darkness, I grew dizzy.
The moon blazed—bright enough to derange the heart.
entries.mirrorMoon:
My back creaks.
Coursing through my veins is an image of coldness.
A solitary darkness that makes me dizzy.
A radiant moon that sickens my heart.

entries.japanese:
……不思議と。
　息苦しいはずの寒さは、それ以上に懐かしい空気を持っているような気がした。
entries.maoEnglish:
…Strangely,
the cold that should have choked me carried an even stronger air of nostalgia.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Strangely.
The overwhelming coldness feels more like a sense of nostalgia.

entries.japanese:
「―――志貴さま」
　……朝の光に交じって、翡翠の呼び声が聞こえてくる。
「―――志貴さま、お時間です。
お目覚めください」
　抑揚のない翡翠の声に、意識がはっきりと覚めていく。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――Master Shiki.”
Hisui’s call reaches me, mingled with the morning light.
“Master Shiki, it is time. Please wake up.”
Hisui's level voice draws me cleanly into consciousness.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Shiki-sama."
…… I can hear Hisui's voice mingling with the morning light.
"---Shiki-sama, it is time.
Please wake up."
Her inflectionless voice awakens me.

entries.japanese:
「――――――」
　目を覚ましたとたん、厭なモノが視界に入ってきた。
　ずきり、とこめかみには銃創のような頭痛。
「あ――――」
　起きたばかりの意識が、がらり、と足場を失っていく。
そのまま眩暈を起こしてしまう前に、急いで枕元のメガネを手に取った。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――――”
The instant I open my eyes, something loathsome enters my vision.
Pain punches through my temple like a gunshot.
“Ah――――”
My newly wakened mind loses its footing. Before vertigo can take me, I snatch the glasses from beside my pillow.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------"
As soon as I wake up, terrible things enter my vision.
I get a headache like I was just shot in the head.
"Ah----"
I almost lose my just awakened consciousness.
Before I fade away completely, I quickly grab my glasses.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま……？
　ご気分が優れないのですか？」
「……いや、疲れが残ってるだけだよ。
すぐによくなるから、心配はしなくていい」
　軽く頭をふって、さっきまで視えていたものを記憶から振り払う。
　……結局。
昨日の夜、アルクェイドを見つけ出せなかった事が心に暗い闇を落としているようだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki…? Are you unwell?” “No, I’m just still tired. It’ll pass soon, so don’t worry.”
I shake my head, trying to scatter the memory of what I had just seen.
In the end. Failing to find Arcueid last night has left a dark shadow over me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama……?
Are you not feeling well?"
"…… No, I'm just a little tired from yesterday.
I'll be alright, so don't worry."
Lightly shaking my head, I clear my head of what I was seeing.
…… It seems that not being able to find Arcueid last night has cast a dark shadow in my heart.

entries.japanese:
「おはよう翡翠。
今朝も起こしにてきてくれてありがとう」
　ベッドから上半身を起こしながら、できるだけ自然に笑顔を向けた。
「いえ、これがわたしの仕事ですから。
志貴さまに感謝されるほどのことではありません」
「そうかな、俺はすごくありがたいけど。
目覚し時計の音なんかより、何倍もあったかい感じがする」
　ベッドから立ちあがる。
　時刻は朝の七時前―――いつもより十分ほど早い時間。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Good morning, Hisui. Thanks for waking me again.”
Sitting up in bed, I give her the most natural smile I can manage.
“It is only my duty. There is no need for Master Shiki to thank me.”
“Maybe, but I’m really grateful. Waking to your voice feels so much warmer than an alarm clock.”
I rise from bed.
It is not yet seven—about ten minutes earlier than usual.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Good morning, Hisui.
Thanks for coming to wake me up, as always."
Sitting up in bed, I do my best to smile naturally.

"No, this is my duty.
There is no need for you to thank me, Shiki-sama."
"Really, but I am grateful.
You are infinitely better than an alarm clock."
I stand up.
It's not yet seven o'clock---about ten minutes earlier than I usually get up.

entries.japanese:
「朝ごはんだろ？
　すぐに行くから先に行っててくれ」
「はい。
それでは居間の方でお待ちしております」
　ふかぶかとお辞儀をして翡翠は退室していった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Breakfast, right? I’ll be there in a minute, so go on ahead.”
“Certainly. I shall await you in the sitting room.”
Hisui bows deeply and leaves.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Hmm, breakfast?
I'll be there soon, so please go ahead of me."
"Yes, I will wait for you in the sitting room."
Giving a bow, Hisui exits the room.

entries.japanese:
―――さて。
　まだ体はだるいけど、学校に行けないほどじゃない。
琥珀さんが作ってくれる朝食を食べれば体力も戻ってくれる事だろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Well, then.
My body still feels heavy, but not enough to keep me from school. Kohaku’s breakfast should restore some of my strength.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----Well then.
I'm still feeling a little sluggish, but it's not so bad that I have to skip school.
I'm sure after I eat the breakfast Kohaku-san prepared, I'll feel a lot better.

entries.japanese:
居間にはいつも通り、ソファーに座った秋葉と壁際に控えている翡翠の姿があった。
「おはようございます兄さん。
昨夜はゆっくり休まれましたか？」
「……おはよう秋葉。
なんていうか、今朝も早いんだな」
「いえ、わたしはいつも通りですけど……兄さん？」
　どうしてか、秋葉は不安げな眼差しをした。
「ん―――俺の顔になにかついてるのか、秋葉？」
entries.maoEnglish:
The sitting room presents its usual tableau: Akiha seated on the sofa, Hisui waiting by the wall.
“Good morning, Brother. Did you sleep well?”
“Morning, Akiha. You’re up early again.”
“No, this is my usual hour—Brother?”
For some reason, Akiha looks at me uneasily.
“Is there something on my face, Akiha?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
As usual, Akiha is sitting on the sofa and Hisui is waiting by the wall.
"Good morning, Nii-san.
Did you sleep well last night?"
"…… Good morning, Akiha.
You're up early today, too."
"No, I'm like always…… Nii-san?"
She looks uneasy for some reason.
"Hm---Is there something on my face, Akiha?"

entries.japanese:
「いえ、そういう事ではないんですけど……兄さん、本当に大丈夫なんですか？
　まだ顔色が悪いようですし、気分が優れないのでしたら今日はお休みになったほうが―――」
「いや、体のほうは大丈夫だよ。
そのうちに治るから、そう心配そうな顔はしないでくれ」
「……はい。
兄さんがそうおっしゃられるのでしたら、私から言うべき事はありませんね」
　秋葉は納得がいかない顔つきで黙り込んだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“No, nothing like that, but are you truly all right? You still look pale, so if you feel ill, perhaps you should stay home today―――”
“I’m fine. It’ll clear up soon, so stop looking so worried.”
“Very well. If you insist, there is nothing more for me to say.”
Akiha falls silent, plainly unconvinced.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No, that isn't it…… Nii-san, are you really alright?
You still do not look well, so if you are still sick, maybe it is better if you just rest today---"
"No, I'm really okay.
I'll be better sooner or later, so please don't look so worried."
"…… Okay.
If you say so, Nii-san, then I will not say anything."
She goes quiet, still looking worried.

entries.japanese:
「なんだ、珍しく簡単に納得するんだな。
なんか、秋葉らしくなくて拍子抜けした」
「むっ。
私、普段から物分りはいいほうです。
私が兄さんを注意するのは、兄さんのほうに問題があるからでしょう。
ご自分の至らなさを私のせいにしないでください」
　じとり、と流し目をしてくる秋葉。
「おっ、やっと調子が出てきたな。
やっぱり秋葉がツンケンしてないと朝っていう気がしないよな、翡翠」
「………………」
　急に声をかけられたせいか、それとも返答すべき言葉がみつからないのか。
翡翠は黙ったまま、否定も肯定もしない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“That was easy; you hardly ever give in so quickly. It’s so unlike you, I feel cheated.”
“Hmph. I am perfectly reasonable as a rule. When I reprimand you, it is because you have done something wrong. Please don’t blame your own shortcomings on me.”
Akiha gives me a sour sidelong look.
“There you are—now you sound like yourself. Morning wouldn’t feel right without Akiha snapping at me, would it, Hisui?”
“…”
Perhaps the sudden question takes her aback. Or perhaps she simply cannot find an answer; Hisui remains silent, neither agreeing nor denying it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hm, it's quite rare for you to be convinced this quickly.
It's not like you."
"Hey, I'm always sensible.
I only warn you because you're the one with the problems.
So please do not blame me for your imperfections."
She glares at me.
"Oh, that's more like it.
Hey Hisui, doesn't it not feel like morning unless Akiha gets harsh?"
"………………"
Is it because I suddenly called out to her or because she doesn't know what to say?
Hisui neither confirms nor denies my statement.

entries.japanese:
「ほら見ろ秋葉。
翡翠もそう思うってさ」
「馬鹿なこと言わないでください。
翡翠は呆れて何も言わないだけでしょう」
　眉間にしわをよせて、秋葉は俺の顔を睨む。
「それにですね、これは前から言おうと思っていたんですけど、兄さんは翡翠に頼りすぎよ。
　習い事をしているわけではないんですから、夜は早くに眠れるでしょう？
　なのにいつも遅くに起きてくるんですから。
翡翠が何も言わないのをいい事に緩みきっているんじゃないですか？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“See, Akiha? Hisui agrees with me.”
“Don’t be absurd. She is only too appalled to answer.”
Akiha knits her brow and glares at me.
“And another thing: I have been meaning to say this for some time—you depend on Hisui far too much.
You have no evening lessons, so you could easily go to bed early. Yet you always sleep late. Aren’t you taking advantage of the fact that Hisui never complains?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"See?
Look, Akiha, Hisui thinks so, too."
"Don't be foolish.
Hisui doesn't say anything because she is surprised."
Wrinkling her forehead in a frown, Akiha glares again.
"Also, I've always wanted to say this, but you rely on Hisui too much.
You don't take lessons or anything, so you can go to sleep early, right?
But you always wake up late.
Are you slacking off because Hisui does not say anything?"

entries.japanese:
「な―――それじゃまるで、俺が翡翠を困らせてるみたいじゃないか！」
「みたい、じゃなくて事実困らせているじゃない。
ね、貴方もそう思うでしょう、翡翠？」
「………………」
　翡翠はやっぱり何も言わず、ただ静かに立ち尽くしているだけだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What—now you’re making it sound as if I’m causing Hisui trouble!”
“It does not merely sound that way; you are causing her trouble. You agree, don’t you, Hisui?”
“…”
Hisui still says nothing; she merely stands there in silence.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Wh----You make it sound like I'm causing her trouble!"
"Not 'like', you are causing her trouble.
Hey, don't you think so, Hisui?"
"………………"
Hisui still doesn't say anything and stands there quietly.

entries.japanese:
「ほら。
翡翠もそう思うって言ってます」
「そんなワケあるかっ！
　翡翠は何も言ってないだろ！」
「…………………」
　翡翠は黙っている。
　ただ、その黙り方がどちらかというと、俺より秋葉の意見に賛同しているような、そんな感じだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“There. Hisui says I’m right.”
“No way! Hisui didn’t say anything!”
“…”
Hisui remains silent.
Somehow, it is the kind of silence that sides with Akiha rather than me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"See?
Hisui says she thinks so too."
"No way!
She didn't say anything!"
"…………………"
Hisui is silent.
But her silence feels like she is agreeing more with Akiha.

entries.japanese:
「…………う」
　なんか、気がつかないうちに状況は二対一になってしまっている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ngh…”
Without my noticing, this has somehow become two against one.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"………… Oogh."
I feel like it's now two against one.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さーん、朝食の支度ができましたよー」
　と、そこでタイミングよく琥珀さんの声が響いてきた。
「えっと、それじゃ朝ごはんを食べてくる」
　いそいそと居間を横切って食堂に向かう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki, breakfast is ready!”
Kohaku’s voice rings out with impeccable timing.
“Right, I’ll go eat.”
I hurry across the sitting room toward the dining room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-san.
Breakfast is ready~."
With great timing, Kohaku-san's voice echoes through the room.
"Um, I'm gonna go eat."
I quickly head towards the dining room.

entries.japanese:
「…………………」
　なんか、二人の無言の圧力が、背中にどーんとのしかかってきていたりした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
Somehow, the combined weight of their silent disapproval lands squarely between my shoulder blades.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…………………"
I feel the silent pressure of the two behind me drilling into my back.

entries.japanese:
朝食を終えて居間に戻ってくる。
　秋葉の姿はなく、居間には翡翠の姿だけがあった。
entries.maoEnglish:
After breakfast, I return to the sitting room.
Akiha is gone; only Hisui remains.
entries.mirrorMoon:
After breakfast, I head back to the sitting room.
Akiha isn't there, and Hisui is the only one standing.

entries.japanese:
「あれ、秋葉はもう学校？」
「はい。
志貴さまも登校のお時間です」
「あ、もう二十分か。
確かにそろそろ支度をしないとまずいかな」
　……正直、まだ体が本調子じゃないけどしばらくすれば元に戻るだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What, has Akiha left for school already?”
“Yes, Master Shiki. It is nearly time for you to leave as well.”
“Oh, it’s already twenty past. I’d better get ready.”
Honestly, I still feel far from normal, but surely that will pass in a little while.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Huh?
Akiha left for school already?"
"Yes.
It is time for you to go to school as well, Shiki-sama."
"Ah, it's already twenty after?
I guess I should get going soon."
…… To be honest, I still don't feel good, but I'm sure I'll return to normal soon.

entries.japanese:
「それじゃ翡翠、悪いけど部屋から鞄を持ってきてくれないか。
俺は顔を洗ってくるから」
「はい、かしこまりました」
　支度を整えて屋敷を出る。
　翡翠は鞄を持ったまま玄関まで見送りにきてくれる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hisui, could you bring my bag down from my room? I’m going to wash my face.”
“Certainly.”
Once ready, I leave the mansion.
Hisui carries my bag and accompanies me all the way to the entrance.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Sorry, Hisui, but can you get my bag from my room?
I'm going to wash my face."
"As you wish."
After getting all my preparations done, I leave the mansion.
Holding my bag, Hisui sees me off at the entrance.

entries.japanese:
「それじゃ行ってくる。
何時に帰ってくるかは解らないけど、夕食までには帰ってくるよ」
「はい、お待ちしております」
　しずしずとお辞儀をする翡翠。
　……ただ、その顔はどこか不安そうだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’m off. I don’t know exactly when I’ll be back, but I’ll return before dinner.”
“Yes, I shall be waiting.”
Hisui bows with quiet grace.
Yet something in her face looks troubled.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I'll be going.
I'm not sure when I'll be back, but probably by dinner."
"Yes, I will be waiting."
She gives a silent bow.
…… There's a trace of uneasiness in her face.

entries.japanese:
「翡翠？
　どこか具合が悪いのか？」
「いえ―――わたしの事ではなく、志貴さまのお顔の色が優れないので、このまま志貴さまを行かせていいものか、わからなくて」
　ためらいがちにそんな事を言う。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hisui? Are you feeling ill?”
“No—it isn’t me; Master Shiki looks pale, and I’m not sure whether I should allow Master Shiki to leave in that condition.”
She says it reluctantly.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hisui?
Are you feeling sick?"
"No---it is not me, but you do not appear well.
I am unsure if it is a good idea to let you go."
She speaks hesitantly.

entries.japanese:
「大丈夫だよ。
たしかに体調はよくないけど、少し体が重いだけなんだ。
まったく、秋葉も翡翠も心配性になっているんじゃないか？」
「……そう、でしょうか。
わたしたちの気のせいであるのなら、それに越したことはないのですが」
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’m fine. I don’t feel great, but my body is only a little heavy. Honestly, you and Akiha have both become such worriers.”
“Perhaps. If it is only our imagination, nothing would please me more.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I'm alright.
I don't feel great, but just a little heavy.
Geez, both you and Akiha like to worry a lot."
"…… Is that so?
If it is just us, then that will be fine, but…"

entries.japanese:
「……しょうがないな。
それじゃ今日は早めに帰ってきて休むから、それでいいだろ。
今日は無茶はしないから、そんな顔はしないでくれ」
「………はい。
申し訳ありません、志貴さま」
　翡翠はますます不安そうな顔をする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“All right. I’ll come home early and rest today. I promise not to overdo it, so please don’t look at me like that.”
“Yes. Forgive me, Master Shiki.”
Hisui looks more anxious than ever.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Geez.
I'll come back early today and rest, so that should be good, right?
I won't overdo anything, so don't look like that."
"……… Yes.
Forgive me, Shiki-sama."
She still looks very worried.

entries.japanese:
「行ってくるよ。
帰ってくるころには元気になっているから、気楽に待っていてくれ」
「あ―――志貴さま――――」
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’m going. I’ll be perfectly well by the time I return, so try not to worry while you wait.”
“Ah―――Master Shiki――――”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I'm off.
I'll be better by the time I get back, so please relax."
"Ah---Shiki-sama----"

entries.japanese:
翡翠をふりきって屋敷を後にする。
　最後まで不安そうに俺を見送る翡翠の姿が、いつになく印象に残っていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
I shake off Hisui’s appeal and leave the mansion.
The image of her watching me go, anxious to the very end, stays with me more vividly than it should.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I ignore her and leave the mansion.
The image of Hisui watching me uneasily remains in my head.

entries.japanese:
学校に向かう。
　手足がまだ重く、他人の体を着ているような感覚で坂道を下りていく。
　……ここ数日の疲れが体の芯に残っているのか。
　すぐに回復すると思っていた体の淀みは、なかなか消え去ってはくれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
I set out for school.
My limbs remain heavy, and I descend the hill with the sensation of wearing someone else’s body.
Perhaps the exhaustion of the past few days has lodged deep inside me.
The sluggishness I expected to pass refuses to clear.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I head towards school.
My feet are heavy and it feels like I'm in another person's body as I head down the hill.
…… It's probably just the weariness from last night.
Even though I thought I would recover right away, the sluggishness doesn't fade.

entries.japanese:
朝の七時五十分。
　正門は登校してくる生徒たちの姿で混雑していた。
「────あ」
　校門をくぐっていく後ろ姿に見知った人影があった。
entries.maoEnglish:
Seven fifty in the morning.
The front gate is crowded with arriving students.
“Ah.”
Among the backs passing through, I recognize someone.
entries.mirrorMoon:
It's ten minutes until eight.
The school gate is flooded with arriving students.
"----Ah."
By the gate, I see a familiar figure.

entries.japanese:
「……シエル、先輩」
　それは、別段どうという事はない朝の風景だ。
　ただ、あの時の光景―――
　それさえなければ、本当に何気ない朝の出来事だったろう。
「―――――」
　自分でも何をしたいのか分からないまま、先輩の後ろ姿を追いかけた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ciel.”
It should have been an utterly ordinary morning sight.
If not for what I had seen that night—
Without that, it truly would have meant nothing at all.
“―――――”
Not knowing what I intended to do, I follow her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Ciel, senpai."
It's a completely normal, morning scene.
But, what I saw that time---
If it wasn't for that, it would be a normal morning.
"-----"
Not even knowing what I plan on doing, I chase after Senpai.

entries.japanese:
「先輩！」
　声をかけて呼び止める。
「あ、おはようございます遠野くん。
めずらしいですね、校庭で会うなんて」
「……ああ。
先輩の後ろ姿が見えたから走ってきたんだ。
その……ちょっと聞きたい事があってさ」
　ちら、と先輩の顔を盗み見る。
「はい、なんでしょう」
　先輩はいつもの柔らかな笑顔を向けてくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ciel!”
I call out and stop her.
“Oh, good morning, Tohno. It’s unusual to meet you out in the schoolyard.”
“Yeah. I saw you ahead of me and ran over. There’s something I wanted to ask.”
I steal a glance at her face.
“Yes—what is it?”
She gives me her usual gentle smile.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Senpai!"
I call after her.
"Oh, good morning, Tohno-kun.
It's unusual to meet you out here."
"…… Yeah, I saw your figure from behind so I ran after you, Senpai.
Um…… there was something I wanted to ask."
I sneak a look at her face.

"Yes, what is it?"
She faces me with her usual, gentle smile.

entries.japanese:
「……あのさ先輩。
三日前の夜、うちの近くにいなかった？
　黒いコートみたいな服を着て、スカートをこうばさばさーとなびかせて」
「……？
　なんですか、それ」
「だから……！
　えっと、それと――そう、編み上げブーツがすごく似合ってたじゃないか。
ちょっと見惚れるぐらい、かっこ良かった」
entries.maoEnglish:
“…Listen, were you near my house three nights ago? Wearing something like a black coat, with your skirt billowing out behind you?”
“…? What are you talking about?”
“I mean…! And—right, those lace-up boots looked incredible on you. You were so striking I couldn’t help staring.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Uh, Senpai.
Three nights ago, were you near my house?
In a black coat and a skirt flowing in the wind?"
"……?
What is that?"
"Um……!
well--yeah, the high-laced boots suited you.
I was kind of fascinated, you looked, really cool."

entries.japanese:
……はい？
　と先輩は首をかしげる。
　俺が何を言ってるのか皆目見当がつかない、というように顔をしかめてから、先輩はきっぱりと否定した。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Excuse me?” Ciel tilts her head.
After frowning in total bewilderment at whatever nonsense I am spouting, she gives me a flat denial.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… "Huh?" Senpai tilts her head.
She frowns like she doesn't understand my words completely, and then denies it.

entries.japanese:
「えっと、よくわかりませんけど、三日前の夜にわたしが遠野くんの家の近くにいて、そうゆうカッコウをしていたんですか？」
「ああ。
あれ、先輩だろ？」
「わけありませんっ。
遠野くん、わたしってそんなに暇な人に見えるんですか？」
―――先輩は、本気で怒ってしまった。
　そこにしらをきっているとか嘘をついているとか、そういったものは一切ない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“If I understand you, you’re saying I was near your house three nights ago dressed like that?”
“Yeah. That was you, wasn’t it?”
“Of course it wasn’t! Tohno, do I really look as though I have that much time to waste?”
―――Ciel is genuinely angry.
There is not the faintest hint that she is feigning ignorance or telling a lie.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Um, I don't quite understand, but you're saying that I was near your house three nights ago, looking like that?"
"Yeah, that was you, Senpai, right?"
"No way.
Tohno-kun, are you saying I look like I really have that much free time?"
---Senpai is really angry.
She can't be playing dumb or lying.

entries.japanese:
「あ───いや、そんな事はないんだけど、その……先輩に似た人を公園で見かけたから、それで―――」
　はあ、と先輩はため息をつく。
「遠野くん、それわたしじゃないです。
わたし、そういう趣味はないですから」
「あ───うん、わかってる。
ただちょっと聞きたかっただけなんだ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“No, not at all—it’s just that I saw someone who looked like you in the park, so…”
Ciel sighs.
“Tohno, that was not me. I have no taste for dressing that way.”
“Yeah, I know. I only wanted to ask.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah---no, that's not it, but I just…… saw someone that looked like you in the park last night, so---"
Senpai gives a sigh.
"Tohno-kun, that wasn't me.
I don't have that kind of hobby."
"Ah---yeah, I know.
I just wanted to ask."

entries.japanese:
……たしかに言われて見ればその通りだ。
　シエル先輩とあの夜の人物はぜんぜん結びつかない。
　そもそも先輩は普通の人だし、もしあの場に居合わせたのなら───俺がナイフをもって得体の知れない包帯男と殺しあうところを見たハズだ。
　あんな凄惨な場面を見てしまったのなら、俺とこうして今までどおり話なんか出来るはずがない。
entries.maoEnglish:
Once she says it, it does seem obvious.
Ciel and the figure from that night do not belong together at all.
She is an ordinary person; if she had been there, she would have seen me fighting to the death with a mysterious bandaged man, knife in hand.
After witnessing something so ghastly, she could never speak to me now as though nothing had changed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Certainly after having her say that, she is right.
Ciel-senpai and the person that night aren't related at all.
In the first place, Senpai's just a normal person, and if she was actually there---she had to have seen me fight that bandage guy with my knife.
If she saw such a gruesome scene, there'd be no way she could talk with me normally like this.

entries.japanese:
「……ごめん、今のは忘れて。
なんか他人の空似だったみたいだ」
「いいですけど……そんなにわたしに似てたんですか、そのヘンな人」
「そう言われると自信ないな。
夜だったし、遠かったし………って、あれ？」
　そう、遠くて顔だってよく見えなかった。
　なのにどうして、俺はアレが先輩に似てる、なんて思ったんだろう……？
entries.maoEnglish:
“Sorry. Forget I asked; I must have mistaken a stranger for you.”
“All right, but did this strange person really look that much like me?”
“Now that you ask, I’m not sure. It was night, and she was far away—wait.”
Yes, she had been too distant for me even to see her face clearly.
Then why had I ever thought she resembled Ciel?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Sorry, please forget about it.
I guess it was just someone else."
