「あはは、シエルったら本気で怒ってるよ、志貴！」
　人の腕を掴んだまま、あくまで陽気にアルクェイドは走っていく。
　……まあ、今シエルに捕まったら何をされるか解らないし、彼女が冷静になるまで逃げた方がいいのかもしれないけど……
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ahaha—Ciel is really furious, Shiki!”
Still gripping my arm, Arcueid ran on in irrepressible high spirits.
Well, there was no telling what Ciel might do if she caught me now, so perhaps fleeing until she calmed down was the wisest course—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ahaha, Ciel is seriously angry, Shiki!"
Still holding my arm, Arcueid runs cheerfully.
…… Well, I don't know what'll happen if Ciel catches up to me right now, so I should probably just keep running until she calms down………

entries.japanese:
「――――――――――はあ」
　アルクェイドに腕を掴まれて、背後にシエル先輩のすごい剣幕に責めたてられながら、ついため息をこぼしてしまった。
　きっと遠野志貴のこれからの生活は、これからずっとこんなふうに展開していくに違いない。
　けどまあ、それも覚悟の上だったのか。
　シエル先輩が大切で、だっていうのにアルクェイドに惹かれてしまった時から、こうなるコトはなんとなく分かっていたんだろうし。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Haa…”
With Arcueid towing me by one arm and Ciel bearing down behind us in a fury, I couldn’t help sighing.
This was probably how life would unfold for Shiki Tohno from now on.
But perhaps I had already accepted that.
From the moment I realized Ciel was precious to me and found myself drawn to Arcueid anyway, some part of me must have known it would end like this.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----------*sigh*
With Arcueid grabbing my arm and having Ciel-senpai chasing us furiously, I can't help but let out a sigh.
Probably, my life from now on would be like this forever.
But, well, I guess I was prepared for this.
Ever since Ciel-senpai became precious to me, but I was still attracted to Arcueid, I think I vaguely knew things might end this way.

entries.japanese:
「と、遠野くんっ！
　なんだってアルクェイドと一緒に逃げてるんですか、あなたは――――！」
　先輩は腕をブンブンと回して追いかけてくる。
　……追いつかれるのは時間の問題だ。
―――――さて。
　その前に汎用性がきいて、うまくシエルを落ち着かせられる言い訳を考えないといけない。
　なにしろこの先。
　何度も何度も何度も何度も、こんな場面に出くわしてしまうんだろうから―――――
entries.maoEnglish:
“T-Tohno! Why are you running away with Arcueid?!”
Ciel charged after us, arms pumping wildly.
It was only a matter of time before she caught up.
―――――Well, then.
Before that happened, I needed a reliable excuse—something versatile enough to calm Ciel down.
After all, from now on.
I was surely going to find myself in this exact situation again and again and again and again—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"To, Tohno-kun!
Why are you running away with Arcueid----!?"
Circling her arms furiously, she chases after us.
…… It's only a matter of time before she catches up.
-----

Well then.
Before that, I have to find a versatile and effective way to calm Ciel down.
Because from now on,
I'll be in this situation over and over and over and over-------

entries.japanese:
メルシー！
　おめでとうございます！
　シエルさんのグッドエンドです！
　……って、え？
　…………あれ？
　…………あれれれ？？
　ちょっと待ったぁ！
　なんですか。
　なんなんですかこの終わり方！
entries.maoEnglish:
Merci!
Congratulations! You’ve reached Ciel’s Good Ending!
Wait, what?
Huh?
Huuuh?
Hold it!
What is this?
What kind of ending is this?!
entries.mirrorMoon:
Merci!
Congratulations!
It's Ciel-san's Good Ending!
…… Eh?
………… Huh?
………… Huh?
Huh???
Wait just a minute!
What is this?
What is this ending!?

entries.japanese:
「………………………………こそこそ」
　そこ！
　まちなさい、この泥棒ネコ――――！
「いったーい、ぼうりょくはんたいー。
シエル先生はすぐ体罰をするのでいけないとおもいまーす」
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――sneak, sneak”
You there! Stop, you thieving cat—!
“Owww—down with violence! I think Teacher Ciel is bad for using corporal punishment all the time!”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……………………………… Sneak, sneak."
Hey you!
Stop, you thief cat----!
"Owieeee!
Don't be so violent!
Ciel-sensei, you shouldn't resort to corporal punishment!"

entries.japanese:
――――却下です。
　……ああもう、えっとですね！
　各ヒロインには二種類のエンディングが用意されています。
　今回のはシエルさんのグッドエンド。
　少し前の選択に戻って、違う物語を歩んでください！
　そっちのほうがトゥルーエンディングですから！
entries.maoEnglish:
――――Rejected.
Oh, honestly!
Each heroine has two endings.
This was Ciel’s Good Ending.
Return to a recent choice and follow the other branch of the story!
That one is the True Ending!
entries.mirrorMoon:
----Dismissed.
…… Oh, geez, okay!
Each heroine has two different kinds of endings.
This is Ciel-san's Good End.
Please return to a previous choice and choose a different story!
That will be the True End!

entries.japanese:
あ、それとですね。
　シエルさんとアルクェイドのルートを表とすると、まったく別展開の裏ルートが存在します。
　秋葉さんを代表する“遠野家”ルートですね。
　中々分岐の条件が解りづらいようですから、ちょっとヒントを。
entries.maoEnglish:
Oh, and one other thing.
Ciel and Arcueid’s routes form the front side of the story.
There is also a reverse side where events unfold completely differently—the Tohno family routes, represented by Akiha.
The conditions for branching there can be rather obscure, so here is a hint.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Oh, and one more thing.
Ciel-san's and Arcueid's routes are the Near Side of the Moon routes.
But there is also a completely different story: the Far Side of the Moon routes.
It is the "Tohno Family" routes, associating with people like Akiha-san.
It seems difficult to know what requirement is needed to be able to choose this path, so I will give you a little hint.

entries.japanese:
一日目は、自分からシエルさんに会ってはいけません。
　昼休みには教室に残ったほうがいいみたいです。
　それと、極めつけ。
　遠野くんはネロという吸血鬼に出会わなければこんな事にはならなかったと思います。
　ですから、まず事の発端。
　あの時、あの行動をしようとさえしなければ、まったく違った展開が待ち受けている事でしょう。
　それではまたいずれ、本編でお会いしましょうね！
entries.maoEnglish:
On day one, do not go out of your way to meet Ciel.
It seems best to remain in the classroom during lunch.
And most importantly.
None of this would have happened if Tohno had never encountered Nrvnqsr.
So begin by returning to the incident that started everything.
If, at that moment, you simply refrain from taking that particular action, an entirely different story should await you.
Until we meet again in the story!
entries.mirrorMoon:
On the first day, you should not go meet Ciel-san.
It might be better to stay in your classroom during lunch.
And most importantly.
I think that if you don't meet the vampire called Nrvnqsr, this current storyline will never happen.
So first, how to cause the new storyline.
During that specific time, if you do not try to perform that one action, a completely different event should be waiting for you.
Well then, let's meet again once more in the main story!

entries.japanese:
シエル・トゥルーエンディング、ごくろうさまでした。
　各ヒロインには（一名だけ例外がありますが）二種類のエンディングが用意されています。
　トゥルーエンディングとグッドエンディングがそれです。
　どちらかのエンディングに辿り着いた後、少しだけ戻ってもう一度物語りを進めてみてください。
　なにか違った展開が待っている事でしょう。
entries.maoEnglish:
Congratulations on completing Ciel’s True Ending.
Each heroine has two endings, with one exception.
They are the True Ending and the Good Ending.
Once you reach either one, go back a little and play through the story again.
A different turn of events should be waiting for you.
entries.mirrorMoon:
You have reached Ciel's True Ending.
Well done.
Each heroine (with one exception) has two different kinds of endings.
A True Ending and a Good Ending.
After reaching one of the endings, please go back a little and readvance through the story.
A different event should await you.

entries.japanese:
それでは、ここまでプレイしていただいてありがとうございました。
　また“月姫”のどこかでお会いしましょうね。
entries.maoEnglish:
Thank you for playing this far.
I hope we meet again somewhere in TSUKIHIME.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Well then, thank you very much for playing up to this point.
Let's meet again somewhere in Tsukihime.

entries.japanese:
……そうだな。
　後悔はしないって決めたんだし、なにより俺を気遣ってくれた琥珀さんの気持ちを大切にしないと。
「賛成にきまってるよ。
自分の歓迎会なんだから、断るはずがないだろ」
entries.maoEnglish:
Right.
I had decided not to live with regrets, and more than anything, I ought to honor Kohaku's concern for me.
“Of course I'm in favor—it's my own welcome party. How could I refuse?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Yeah.
I've decided not to have any regrets, and I don't want Kohaku-san to worry about me.
"I'm in favor.
I'm not about to turn down my own welcome party, am I?"

entries.japanese:
「きまりですね！
　それじゃあわたしはお料理の準備をしますね。
翡翠ちゃんは―――今日のわたしの仕事を任せていいかな？」
「わかりました。
ロビーと東館の掃除ですね」
「それじゃあ私は……どうしよっか、琥珀？」
「秋葉さまと志貴さんはお部屋でお休みくださいな。
ご夕食を早めにして歓迎会を開きますから、ご用がおありでしたらそれまでに済ませてくださいね」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Then it’s settled! I’ll start preparing the food. Hisui, could I ask you to take over my work for today?”
“Understood. The foyer and the east wing require cleaning.”
“And what should I do, Kohaku?”
“Miss Akiha and Shiki should rest in your rooms. We’ll hold the party over an early dinner, so please finish any errands before then.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"It's decided!
Well, then, I'll prepare the food.
Hisui-chan---can you take care of my work for today?"
"That will be fine.
Sweeping the lobby and the east building?"
"Well then, I shall… what should I do, Kohaku?"
"Akiha-sama and Shiki-san should rest in their rooms.
I'll prepare dinner early to make time for the party, so if you have anything you need to do, please try and be done by then, okay?"

entries.japanese:
琥珀さんは厨房に、翡翠は中庭へ向かった。
「それじゃ私は部屋に戻ります」
　さて。
俺はどうしようか？
entries.maoEnglish:
Kohaku headed for the kitchen, while Hisui went toward the courtyard.
“Then I’ll return to my room.”
Now then. What should I do?
entries.mirrorMoon:
Kohaku-san goes into the kitchen, Hisui out to the courtyard.
"Well then, I'll go to my room."
So.
What should I do?

entries.japanese:
「それでは志貴さんが戻ってきた事を祝して、乾杯をしたいと思います。
みなさん、どうかお好きなお飲み物を選んでください」
　琥珀さんはまったく毒気のない笑顔で、並べられた飲み物を勧めてくる。
　その大部分がジュースなどといったものではなく、れっきとしたアルコール飲料だったりした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“To celebrate Shiki’s return, I propose a toast. Everyone, please choose whichever drink you like.”
With a perfectly innocent smile, Kohaku gestures toward the bottles laid out before us.
The great majority of them are not juice or anything of the sort, but genuine alcoholic beverages.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Well then, a toast to Shiki-san's homecoming.
Everyone, please take whatever you would like to drink."
Kohaku lines up drinks in front of us, with a full smile entirely free of malice.
Most of the drinks didn't happen to be juice or anything like that, but proper alcoholic beverages.

entries.japanese:
「……秋葉、あのさ」
「ん？
　なに兄さん？」
　……秋葉は自分のグラスにとくとくと茶色の液体を注いで、オレンジジュースで割ったりしている。
「おま、おまえ、それウイスキーじゃ、ないんですか」
「そうだけど、何かヘンですか？」
「そうだけどって、秋葉」
　その、未成年の飲酒はいけないんじゃなかったっけ……？
entries.maoEnglish:
“Akiha, listen.”
“Hm? What is it, Brother?”
Akiha is pouring a steady stream of brown liquid into her glass and diluting it with orange juice.
“I-isn’t that whiskey?”
“Yes—is something wrong?”
“What do you mean, ‘yes,’ Akiha?”
Wasn’t drinking alcohol forbidden to minors…?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Uh, Akiha?"
"Hm?
What is it, Nii-san?"
…… There's a gurgling as Akiha fills her glass with a tawny liquid, then adds a little orange juice.
"Tha… that wouldn't be whiskey, would it?"
"It would.
Is there something wrong?"
"'It would' …?
Akiha…"
Um, aren't we all too young to be drinking…?

entries.japanese:
「兄さんの歓迎会なんですから、お酒ぐらいは飲まないとつまらないでしょう？
　あ、それとも兄さん。
もしかしてアルコールは弱いほう？」
　秋葉はどことなく嬉しそうだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“It’s your welcome party, Brother, so it would be dull without at least a little alcohol.
Oh. Brother, are you a lightweight?”
Akiha looks oddly delighted by the possibility.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"This is your welcoming party.
We have to have alcohol, don't we?
Or… Nii-san, you're weak when it comes to alcohol?"
Akiha seems… somehow delighted.

entries.japanese:
「あっ、翡翠ちゃん。
珍しいね、今日はジュースじゃないんだ」
「…………………」
　照れているのか、翡翠は無言でお酒をグラスについでいる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh, Hisui—this is unusual. You’re not having juice tonight?”
“……”
Perhaps embarrassed, Hisui silently pours liquor into her glass.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah, Hisui-chan.
That's unusual, not juice today?"
"…………………"
Seeming a little shy, Hisui silently pours wine into her glass.

entries.japanese:
「ほら兄さん、翡翠もお酒を飲むっていうんですから、まさか一人だけジュースですませようってつもりじゃないでしょう？」
「………ったく。
わりとお祭り好きだったんだな、秋葉は」
「ええ。
好きなお祭りは少ないですけど、今日は特別ですから」
――――はあ。
　仕方ない、あんまり純度の高いアルコールは体によくないんだけど、少しぐらいなら大丈夫だろう。
　テーブルに並んだ飲み物の中で一番度数の低いのは―――ワインかな。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Even Hisui is drinking, Brother, so surely you don’t intend to be the only one hiding behind a glass of juice.”
“Honestly. I never knew you loved a party so much, Akiha.”
“There are very few celebrations I enjoy. But tonight is special.”
――――I sigh.
I suppose I have no choice; strong alcohol is bad for my health, but a little should be safe.
The weakest thing on the table is probably the wine.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"See, Nii-san?
Even Hisui is drinking.
Surely you don't intend to be the only one drinking juice?"
"………… Geez.
You really want to get the most out of this party, don't you, Akiha?"
"Yes.
I don't usually like parties, but today is an exception."
----Huh.
Well, it can't be helped.
A lot of alcohol isn't good for my body, but a little bit should be okay.
The weakest drink laid out on the table is---the wine, it looks like.

entries.japanese:
「それではみなさん、グラスをどうぞ。
　せーの、かんぱーいっ！」
　キィン、とガラスとガラスの弾け合う音のあと、琥珀さんはクイッと一気に、秋葉は時間をかけてゆっくり、翡翠はチロチロと舐めるように飲み干していく。
　……あーあ、どうなってもしらないからな、俺は。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Glasses, everyone.
Ready—and cheers!”
The glasses meet with a bright chime; Kohaku tosses hers back in one swallow, Akiha drinks hers slowly and deliberately, and Hisui laps at hers in tiny sips until it is gone.
Oh, well—whatever happens now, it isn’t my fault.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Well then, everyone, raise your glasses, please?
Cheers!"
With a clash, our glasses come together.
Kohaku tosses hers down in a single gulp, Akiha takes her time, and Hisui sips hers quietly.
…… Oh man, I'm not responsible for this.

entries.japanese:
夏の、暑い日。
　青い空と　大きな大きな入道雲。
　じりじりとゆらぐ風景と
　気が遠くなるような蝉の声。
　蝉の声。
　みーん　みんみん
　みーん　みんみん
　みーん　みんみん
―――――うるさくて、死にたくなる。
entries.maoEnglish:
A hot summer day.
A blue sky and enormous, enormous thunderheads.
The landscape wavering in the scorching heat.
The cry of cicadas loud enough to make you faint.
The cicadas’ cry.
Miiin, min-min
Miiin, min-min
Miiin, min-min
―――――So loud it makes me want to die.
entries.mirrorMoon:
A hot, summer day.
A blue sky and large, large columns of summer clouds.
The wafting breeze.
The droning voice of the cicadas.
The voice of cicadas.
Chiiirp.
Chirp Chirp.
Chiiirp.
Chirp Chirp.
Chiiirp.
Chirp Chirp.
----So loud I want to die.

entries.japanese:
広場には蝉のぬけがら。
　たいようはすぐそばにあるようで、
　広場はじりじりと焦げていく。
　真夏のあつい日。
　まるで、セカイがふらいぱんになったみたい。
entries.maoEnglish:
The square is littered with cicada husks.
The sun feels close enough to touch,
and the square slowly scorches beneath it.
A hot midsummer day.
Like the whole WORLD has turned into a frying pan.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Cicada shells are lying in the clearing.
As if the sun is right by my side,
the clearing is roasting.
A hot midsummer's day.
As if the entire world became a frying pan.

entries.japanese:
えーん　えんえん
　　　　　　　えーん　えんえん
　　　　　　　　　　　　　えーん　えんえん
entries.maoEnglish:
Waaah… waaah…
Waaah… waaah…
Waaah… waaah…
entries.mirrorMoon:
waa, u, uwaaa.
waa, u, uwaaa.
waa, u, uwaaa.

entries.japanese:
……あきはが泣いている。
　足元には子供がひとり倒れている。
　子供の白いシャツはまっかに染まって、ぴくりとも動かない。
　ボクは、それを見下ろしている。
　両手は倒れている子供と同じように赤い。
　いや、違う。
　この両手は、倒れている子供の血で赤いのだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
…Akiha is crying.
A child lies at her feet.
The child’s white shirt is bright red, and the child does not move at all.
I look down at the child.
My hands are red, just like the child lying there.
No. That’s wrong.
My hands are red with the fallen child’s blood.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Akiha is crying.
A child lies collapsed at her feet.
His white shirt is painted red with blood and he doesn't move at all.
I'm, looking down at that.
My hands are red, just like that child on the ground.
No, that's not it.
These hands are red with the blood of that child.

entries.japanese:
「秋葉─────！」
　おとなたちがやってくる。
「なんて事だ─────」
　おとなたちは秋葉を連れていく。
　倒れた子供は死んだまま。
　ボクは一人残されて、子供をコロシタ両手をおとなたちにおさえつけられた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Akiha—!”
The grown-ups are coming.
“What a terrible thing—”
The grown-ups take Akiha away.
The child on the ground stays dead.
I am left behind, and the grown-ups pin down the hands that KILLED the child.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Akiha----!"
The adults are coming.
"What in the----"
The adults take Akiha away.
The child lies there, dead.
Alone by myself, the adults press the hands which killed the child to the ground.

entries.japanese:
「おまえが殺したのか────」
　おとなたちは叫んでいる。
　子供をころしたボクの名前を叫んでいる。
　たった二文字の言葉を、気がちがったように叫んでいる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Did you kill the child—?”
The grown-ups are screaming.
Screaming my name—the name of the one who killed the child.
Screaming those two little syllables as if they have all gone mad.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Did you kill him---!?"
The adults are yelling at me.

They shout my name, the one who killed the child.
Those two syllables, shouting as if they went crazy.

entries.japanese:
たった二文字。
　おとなたちをそろって、両手を真っ赤に染めたボクを、シキと、呼んでいた。
entries.maoEnglish:
Only two syllables.
All the grown-ups together call me—the one with blood-red hands—SHIKI.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Just those two syllables.
Those adults call me SHIKI, as my hands are stained in red.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま、このままではご起床のお時間を過ぎてしまいます。
どうかお目覚めください」
　……自分の名前を呼ぶ声で、深い夢から目が覚めた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki, if you sleep any longer, you will be late getting up. Please wake up.”
A voice calling my name drew me out of the depths of the dream.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama, if you do not get up now, you shall be late.
Please, wake up."
…… Hearing my own name called, I awaken from a deep dream.

entries.japanese:
「翡翠……？」
「はい。
おはようございます、志貴さま」
　ふかぶかと一礼をする翡翠。
　窓からは秋の陽射しが差し込んでいて、ここは紛れもなく自分の部屋だ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hisui…?”
“Yes. Good morning, Master Shiki.”
Hisui bowed deeply.
Autumn sunlight streamed through the window, and this was unmistakably my own room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hisui…?"
"Yes.
Good morning, Shiki-sama."
Hisui bows deeply.
Autumn sunlight shines through the window; this is unmistakably my room.

entries.japanese:
「――――翡、翠」
「志貴さま、ご気分が優れないのですか？」
「いや―――そういう、わけじゃなくて」
　……ただ、ひどく懐かしい夢を見た。
　でも内容が思い出せない。
「なんだっけ……よく、思い出せない」
「？」
　翡翠はかすかに首をかしげる。
　……そうか、翡翠に言っても仕方がないよな。
　今のは―――どんな、夢だったんだろう。
　目が潰れるぐらいの眩しい白と、激しく流れ出した赤色のまだら。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hi…sui.”
“Master Shiki, are you feeling unwell?”
“No—it isn’t that.”
I had simply dreamed of something achingly familiar.
But I could no longer remember what it was.
“What was it—I can’t quite remember.”
“?”
Hisui tilted her head a fraction.
Of course—there was no point asking her.
What kind of dream had that been?
A white so bright it could blind me, slashed by red spreading in violent stains.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"--Hi… sui."
"Shiki-sama, are you feeling unwell?"
"Ah… No, I'm fine."
…… I just had a terribly nostalgic dream.
But I can't remember the details that well.
"What was it… I can't remember…"
"?"
Hisui tilts her head slightly.
…… Well, there's no point in telling Hisui.
The dream---what kind of a dream was it?
A dazzling white bright enough to bring tears to my eyes, and furiously gushing spots of red.

entries.japanese:
―――――――なにか。
　　　　　　　ナニカ、不吉ナ夢ヲ。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――――――Something.
SOMETHING—an ominous dream.
entries.mirrorMoon:
-------Something.
SOMETHING, LIKE AN INAUSPICIOUS DREAM.

entries.japanese:
「……シ、キ……」
「はい、なんでしょう志貴さま」
「……なんでもないんだ。
ごめん、起きるから先に食堂のほうに行っていてくれ」
　はい、とうなずいて翡翠はドアのほうへと歩いていく。
　かつ、かつ、かつ。
　いつもより翡翠の足音が高い。
　翡翠はドアを開けて部屋を退室していこうとして、くるりと振り向いた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…Shi…ki…”
“Yes, Master Shiki?”
“…It’s nothing. Sorry. I’m getting up, so go on ahead to the dining room.”
Hisui nodded and walked toward the door.
Click, click, click.
Her footsteps sounded sharper than usual.
She opened the door to leave, then abruptly turned back.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… SHI… KI…"
"Yes?
What is it, Shiki-sama?"
"…… It's nothing.
I'm sorry--I'll go straight to the dining room."
With a nod, Hisui walks to the door.
Clack, clack, clack.
Hisui's footsteps are louder than usual.
Just as she is about to leave the room, she turns back.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま、つかぬ事をお伺いいたします。
　志貴さまは昨夜、何時に帰ってこられたのでしょう」
「え……昨日は……その、夜遅くに」
「……夕方の四時には帰ってこられる、と志貴さまはおっしゃられた筈ですが、予定が変わったのですね」
「―――――あ」
　思い出した。
　そういえば昨日の朝、翡翠には夕方に帰ってくるって言ったんだっけ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki, may I ask you something?
What time did Master Shiki return last night?”
“Yesterday—I came home late.”
“Master Shiki said he would be home by four in the afternoon; I see his plans changed.”
“Ah—”
I remembered.
Yesterday morning, I had told Hisui I would be back that afternoon.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama, forgive me for asking.
What time did you return last night?"
"Ah… yesterday… Quite late at night."
"…… Shiki-sama, you said your return would be at four o'clock.
I assume the schedule changed?"
"----Ah."
I remember.
Yesterday morning, I told Hisui that she should expect me at four.

entries.japanese:
「ごめん。
ちょっと事情があって、昨日は帰って来れなかったんだ。
今日からはちゃんとするから、大目に見てくれ」
「……いえ、志貴さまがそのようにおっしゃられる必要はありません。
主人の予定に合わせるのがわたしたちの仕事ですから。
　ですが、これからはせめてご連絡の一つでもいれてください。
どのような事情であれ、連絡をいれる事はできる筈です」
「―――そうだね。
ごめん、今日からは必ず約束は守る」
「はい。
それでは失礼します」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Sorry. Something came up, and I couldn’t make it home yesterday. I’ll do better from now on, so let me off this once.”
“…No, Master Shiki, you needn’t apologize. It is our duty to accommodate our master’s schedule.
Still, in future, please at least send word. Whatever the circumstances, you should be able to contact us.”
“You’re right. I’m sorry; from today on, I’ll keep my promises.”
“Very well. Excuse me.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I'm sorry.
Things happened, and I didn't make it back.
I will be prompt from now on so it would be great if you could overlook it this time……"
"…… No, it is not necessary for you to say such a thing, Shiki-sama.
It is the duty of us servants to work in accordance with the schedules of our masters.
However, I humbly request that you at least contact us.
Whatever the circumstances, you should still be able to let us know."
"----You're right.
Sorry.
I'll keep my promise from now on."
"I understand.
Then please excuse me."

entries.japanese:
「……珍しく怒ってたな、翡翠」
　普段から無表情だから、翡翠が怒るとすごく怒っているように感じられる。
　……その、まるで俺がとんでもない悪さでもしたみたいだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“It was unusual to see Hisui angry…”
She was always so expressionless. When she did get angry,
she seemed furious—as if I had done something truly terrible.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… That was rare.
Hisui seemed pretty angry."
She's always so expressionless, it seemed she gets extremely angry when she does get angry.
…… As if I did something really terrible.

entries.japanese:
「――――さて、起きるか」
　シーツをはいで、体を起こす。
―――瞬間。
　ずきり、と激しく体が痛んだ。
「ぐっ………！」
　痛み―――痛みは肩の傷口からじゃない。
　もっと奥のほうから、どくん、どくん、と鼓動に合わせるように、響いてくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Well, time to get up.”
I threw back the sheets and sat up.
―――The instant I moved—
A violent stab of pain tore through my body.
“Ngh…!”
It wasn’t coming from the wound in my shoulder.
It echoed from somewhere deeper, throbbing in time with my heartbeat.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----Well then, time to get up."
Pulling away the sheets, I get up.
---At that moment.
My body aches terribly.
"Guh…!"
The pain--it's not from the gash in my shoulder.
It's from a much deeper place, aching with my heartbeat.

entries.japanese:
「あ───ぐ───」
　シーツをつかんで、なんとか痛みに耐える。
「は―――あ」
　……おさまった。
　突発的な発作だったのか、体に異状はない。
「……胸の……傷」
　服の上から胸に触れる。
　そこには大きな傷跡があって、完治した今でも、ときおり今みたいに痛むコトがある。
　お医者さんが言うには、精神的な痛みが完治したはずの肉体の痛みを繰り返させる、というコトだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ah—gh—” I clutched the sheets
and somehow endured it.
“Hah…”
It passed.
Apparently it had only been a sudden attack; nothing seemed physically wrong.
“…The scar… on my chest.”
I touched it through my clothes.
A large scar lay there, and though the wound had healed completely, it still hurt like this from time to time.
According to the doctor, pain in the mind could make an old injury hurt again even after the body had healed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"A---gah---"
Clenching the sheets, I somehow weather the pain.
"Ahhh--"
It fades away.
There's nothing lingering.
Perhaps just a sudden fit?
"…… Chest… wound."
I touch my chest over my cloth.
There is a great scar there, and even now that it has healed, at times it still hurts like it did just now.
The doctor said the physical wound is healed, but that the mind must be replaying the pain over and over again.

entries.japanese:
たいてい胸の傷が痛む時は、交通事故や生き物の死体を見たあとだ。
　血や死のイメージが八年前の事故を思い起こさせているんだろう。
「……昨夜のせいかな」
　赤い路地裏。
　そこで普段通りに話しかけてきた弓塚の笑顔。
entries.maoEnglish:
Usually the scar hurt after I saw a traffic accident or the corpse of an animal.
Images of blood and death must call up the accident from eight years ago.
“…Was it last night?”
A red alley.
Yumizuka’s smile as she spoke to me there as casually as ever.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Usually, the scar begins throbbing after I see a traffic accident or something dead.
The image of blood or death must make me recall the accident eight years ago.
"…… Because of last night, I guess."
The red back alley.
And the normal, smiling face of Yumizuka.

entries.japanese:
「ぐ――――！」
　胸が、痛む。
　弓塚のことが頭から離れない。
　けど、どうすればいいのか、どうするべきなのかさえ、俺には考えつかない。
　俺に出来ることといえば、遠野志貴の日常をとりあえずこなすことぐらいだ。
「く―――そ」
　自分自身に悪態をついて、ベッドから起きあがる。
　寝巻から学生服に着替えて、居間に向かうことにした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ngh—!”
My chest hurt.
I couldn’t get Yumizuka out of my head,
but I had no idea what to do—or even what I ought to do.
All I could manage was to go through the motions of Shiki Tohno’s ordinary day.
“Damn it.”
Cursing myself, I got out of bed,
changed from my pajamas into my school uniform, and headed for the sitting room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Guh--!"
My chest--hurts.
The image of Yumizuka doesn't leave my mind.
But I don't know what I should do, what I can do.
I can only live my everyday life.
"…… Shi… t…"
Swearing at myself, I roll out of bed.
After changing out of my pajamas and into my school uniform, I head to the sitting room.

entries.japanese:
居間には秋葉と翡翠の姿があった。
　琥珀さんは厨房のほうで俺の朝食の支度をしてくれているんだろう。
「おはようございます、兄さん」
　秋葉はソファーに座ったまま、こっちの顔色をうかがうように挨拶をしてくる。
「……ああ、おはよう。
昨日はすまなかった」
　挨拶を返して、そのまま食堂に向かう。
　時間的に秋葉とのんびり居間で話をする余裕はないし―――俺自身にも、誰かと話をする余裕なんてなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
Akiha and Hisui were in the sitting room.
Kohaku was probably in the kitchen preparing my breakfast.
“Good morning, Brother.”
Still seated on the sofa, Akiha studied my face as she greeted me.
“Morning. Sorry about yesterday.”
I returned the greeting and started toward the dining room.
There was no time to sit and talk with Akiha—and I myself was in no state to talk to anyone.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Akiha and Hisui are in the sitting room.
Kohaku-san is probably in the kitchen cooking my breakfast.
"Good morning, Nii-san."
Sitting on the sofa, Akiha greets me and looks at my expression.
"…… Ah, morning.
I'm sorry about yesterday."
Returning her greeting, I head to the dining room.
There really isn't that much time for me to stay and chat with Akiha--and I don't really feel like talking to anyone at all.

entries.japanese:
「兄さん、お話があるのですけど―――少し、よろしいですか」
「……いいよ、時間がないから手短にな」
　秋葉の向かいのソファーに座る。
「昨夜の話の続きですけど。
兄さん、昨日は何をしていたんですか？」
　秋葉はまっすぐな目で問いただしてくる。
「別に。
ただ街を歩いていただけだよ。
遅くなったのは謝るけど、そう大したことじゃないだろ」
　秋葉に嘘をつきたくないから、できるだけ曖昧に返答する。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Brother, I’d like to speak with you. Do you have a moment?”
“…All right, but I’m short on time, so make it quick.”
I sat on the sofa opposite her.
“This is about last night. Brother, what were you doing?”
Akiha questioned me with an unwavering gaze.
“Nothing. I was only walking around town. I’m sorry I came home late, but it’s hardly a catastrophe.”
I didn’t want to lie to her, so I made my answer as vague as possible.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Nii-san, I would like to speak with you a little---is that alright?"
"…… Alright.
But please make it short since I don't have much time."
I sit on the sofa across from her.
"Continuing last night's talk… Nii-san, what were you doing yesterday?"
Akiha asks me with a direct stare.
"Nothing.
Just went for a walk in town.
I'm sorry for getting back late, but it's no big deal."
Since I don't want to lie to Akiha, I answer as evasively as possible.

entries.japanese:
「街を歩いていただけって、それは大した事でしょう。
兄さんはまだ未成年なんですから、夜の街になんか行かないでください。
そうでなくても最近は物騒なのに」
「あ―――――――」
　物騒―――夜の街を徘徊する通り魔。
　なんで。
　なんで、気がつかなかったんだろう。
　人を殺して血を抜き取るという殺人鬼。
　そのフレーズは、昨日の弓塚にぴったり当てはまってしまうじゃないか――――
entries.maoEnglish:
“Only walking around town? That is serious. You’re still a minor, Brother, so please don’t wander the streets at night—especially when the city has become so dangerous.”
“Ah—” Dangerous.
The attacker stalking the city at night.
Why?
Why hadn’t I realized?
A killer who murdered people and drained their blood.
That description fit yesterday’s Yumizuka perfectly—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Just walking the streets IS something.
You are still a minor, so please do not wander out late at night.
Even if you weren't, there have been a lot of disturbances going on."
"Ah------"
Disturbances--the killer skulking around the town at night.
Why?
Why didn't I realize?
The killer that murders people and drinks their blood.
That phrase perfectly matches Yumizuka's behavior yesterday--

entries.japanese:
「……こんなこと私が言うまでもないでしょうけど、兄さんの体は無茶がきかないんです。
　昨夜みたいに、その……ひどく疲れた顔をして帰ってこられたら、困ります。
　何か悩み事があるのでしたら打ち明けてください。
大した力にはなれませんけど、私でよかったら…………」
―――――考えたくないけど。
　弓塚。
弓塚が、この街を騒がしている殺人鬼なのかも、しれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…I shouldn’t have to remind you, but your health can’t bear this kind of strain, Brother.
I can’t simply watch you come home looking as exhausted as you did last night.
If something is troubling you, please tell me. I may not be much help, but if I’m enough…”
―――――I didn’t want to think it,
but Yumizuka—Yumizuka might be the murderer terrorizing this city.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I shouldn't have to say this, but you shouldn't strain your body.
If you come back with an exhausted face like last night's again, I'll get worried.
If you're in trouble, please tell me.
I may not be able to do much, but if you could…"
-----I don't want to think about it, but…
Yumizuka.
Yumizuka could be the killer terrorizing the town.

entries.japanese:
「兄さん？
　ちゃんと話を聞いてますか？」
「え――――いや、うん、聞い、てる」
　秋葉の声が聞こえる。
　けど、こっちの頭の中はただ、昨日の弓塚の姿が思い出されるだけだった。
　秋葉はじっと俺を見つめてくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Brother? Are you listening to me?”
“What—? Yes.
I’m lis…tening.”
I could hear Akiha’s voice, but all my mind could do was replay the sight of Yumizuka the night before.
Akiha stared at me in silence.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Nii-san?
Are you listening to me?"
"Eh----uh, yeah.
I'm listening."
I hear Akiha's voice.
But, the only thing in my mind is the image of Yumizuka from yesterday.
Akiha glares at me.

entries.japanese:
「どうしても事情は話せないっていうんですね、兄さんは」
「ああ。
秋葉には、関係ないことだ」
　今は弓塚のことしか考えられない。
　早く一人になりたくて、そんな言葉を、返していた。
「―――兄さんはあくまで自分だけの勝手を通す、という事ですか？」
「………………」
「わかりました。
では、どうぞご自由になさってください。
兄さんがそうおっしゃるんでしたら、私も自分の勝手を通すだけですから」
entries.maoEnglish:
“You truly refuse to tell me what happened, Brother?”
“Yes. It has nothing to do with you.”
I could think of nothing but Yumizuka.
Desperate to be alone, I gave her that cruel answer.
“So you intend to do exactly as you please, regardless of anyone else, Brother?”
“…”
“Very well. Do as you like. If that is your position, Brother, then I shall do as I please as well.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"So.
You can't talk about your situation, Nii-san?"
"Yeah.
It has nothing to do with you, Akiha."
Right now, I can think only of Yumizuka.
I want to be alone--and so I said that.
"You're going to keep going your own way, is that what you're saying, Nii-san?"
"……………"
"I understand.
Well, please, feel free.
If that's what you want, Nii-san, I'll do the same."

entries.japanese:
秋葉はロビーへと立ち去っていく。
「志貴さま。
よろしいのですか、それで」
「……よろしいって、なにが」
「秋葉さまは志貴さまを深く案じているのだと思います。
……あの方はご自分のお気持ちを口にする方ではありませんから、志貴さまに伝わりにくいとは思いますが―――」
「ちゃんと分かってるよ。
けど、今は頭がいっぱいでダメなんだ。
……秋葉には、悪いと思ってる」
「………………」
entries.maoEnglish:
Akiha left for the foyer.
“Master Shiki. Are you certain that was wise?”
“What do you mean?”
“I believe Miss Akiha is deeply worried for Master Shiki. She is not someone who puts her feelings into words, so they may be difficult for Master Shiki to see…”
“I know. But my head is too full right now. I know I’ve hurt her.”
“…”
entries.mirrorMoon:
Akiha stands, and walks out to the lobby.
"Shiki-sama?
Is this acceptable?"
"…… Acceptable?
Is what acceptable?"
"I believe Akiha-sama is deeply concerned about you, Shiki-sama.
But I think it is difficult for her since she does not often talk about her feelings----"
"I know.
But right now, my head's full, and I can't… I do feel sorry."
"…………"

entries.japanese:
翡翠はそれきり黙りこんだ。
「志貴さーん、朝ごはんですよー」
　食堂から琥珀さんの声が聞こえてくる。
　席を立って、食堂に向かった。
entries.maoEnglish:
Hisui fell silent.
“Master Shiki! Breakfast is ready!”
Kohaku called from the dining room.
I rose and went in.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Hisui falls silent.
"Shiki-saaaan, breakfast!"
Kohaku-san's voice can be heard from the dining room.
I stand up and head towards it.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま、今日のお帰りはいつごろになるでしょうか？」
「ああ、今日は土曜日だから……いや、夕方になると思う。
ちょっと、探し物があるから」
「かしこまりました。
それではどうぞお気をつけて行ってらっしゃいませ」
　ふかぶかと一礼する。
　翡翠に見送られて、屋敷を後にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki, when do you expect to return today?”
“Well, it’s Saturday, so… No, probably this evening. There’s something I need to look for.”
“Understood. Please take care.”
She bowed deeply.
Hisui saw me off as I left the mansion.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama, around what time will you be returning today?"
"Ahh… since today's Saturday… --No.
It'll probably be in the evening.
There's something I want to look for."
"I understand.
Please, take care until then."
She bows deeply.
After Hisui sees me off, I leave the mansion.

entries.japanese:
―――学校に来ても、何の意味もなかった。
　弓塚さつきは欠席者として扱われて、誰も、彼女のことを案じていないように見えた。
　時間はそれこそいつのまにか過ぎてしまっていた。
途中、有彦やシエル先輩がやってきたような気がするけど、よく覚えていない。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Coming to school had accomplished nothing.
Satsuki Yumizuka was treated as just another absent student, and no one seemed worried about her.
The hours slipped away before I knew it. Arihiko and Ciel may have stopped by at some point, but I barely remembered.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---There was no point coming to school.
Yumizuka Satsuki was treated as an absentee, and no one seemed to be the slightest bit concerned about her.
Time passed without my realizing it.
Perhaps Arihiko or Ciel-senpai came by sometime, but I don't really remember.

entries.japanese:
昼になって学校が終わった。
　何のあてもない。
　何のあてもないけど、弓塚を捜さないといけない。
entries.maoEnglish:
School ended at noon.
I had no leads.
None at all—but I had to find Yumizuka.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Noon comes, and school ends.
I have no idea.
I have no idea, but I still have to look for Yumizuka.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま……！」
―――――声がする。
「お気をたしかに。
いま飲み物を持ってまいります」
―――――遠ざかっていく気配。
　カツカツという足音。
　それで、ようやく朝になってくれた事に、気がついた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki…!”
―――――A voice.
“Please hold on. I’ll bring you something to drink at once.”
―――――A presence receding into the distance.
The click of heels.
Only then did I realize morning had finally come.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama……!"
----There's a voice calling me.
"Please remain strong.
I shall bring you something to drink."
----I sense the presence receding.
Footsteps.
It makes me realize that it is morning now.

entries.japanese:
「―――――」
　目が覚めた。
　部屋には誰もいない。
　ゼイゼイ、という音が聞こえる。
「……なんだ……この、音」
　声をだしてみて、それが自分の呼吸の音だという事に気がついた。
「あ……れ」
　見れば、体中が汗まみれだった。
　まるで何十キロっていうマラソンの後みたいに、体が疲れきっている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“—”
I woke.
The room was empty.
I could hear ragged breathing.
“What—is that sound?”
The moment I spoke, I realized it was my own breathing.
“What…?”
My whole body was drenched in sweat.
I was exhausted as if I had just run a marathon.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-----"
I open my eyes.
There isn't anyone else in my room.
I hear something ragged.
"…… What is…… that noise?"
Speaking, I realize that it was my own breathing.
"Hu…… h?"
My body is drenched in sweat.
A tiredness suffocates me, as if I had just ran a long marathon.

entries.japanese:
「くっ………」
　頭痛がする。
　……ひどい夢を見たせいだ。
　血にまみれた弓塚と、それを羨ましそうにずっと眺めていた自分なんていう、どうしようもない悪夢。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ngh…”
My head ached.
It was because of that terrible dream.
A hopeless nightmare of Yumizuka soaked in blood while I stood watching her with envy.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Kgggh……"
My head hurts.
…… Because I saw that hideous dream.
Yumizuka painted with blood, and I, staring at her in envy.
A complete nightmare.

entries.japanese:
「……どうか、してる……」
　荒い呼吸のまま呟く。
　昨夜の夢はまだ頭にこびりついていて、薄れてくれない。
　本当に、酷い悪夢だった。
　夢の中の自分はボウ、としていて、自分一人じゃあの悪夢から目覚められなかったと思うぐらいに。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…Something’s wrong with me…”
I muttered between ragged breaths.
The night’s dream was still stuck fast inside my head, refusing to fade.
It had been a truly hideous nightmare.
In it I had stood vacant and numb, so deeply lost that I doubted I could ever have woken without someone else’s help.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… There's something wrong……"
I manage to say this much, still breathing hard.
Last night's dream still lingers in my head.
It really was a horrific nightmare.
I was just blanked out in my dream, as if I couldn't rouse myself from the nightmare if I tried.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま……！」
　と。
　慌てた様子で、翡翠が部屋にとびこんできた。
「翡翠……？
　どうしたんだ、ノックもしないで入ってくるなんて」
「あ……お目覚めになられたのですか、志貴さま……？」
「うん、いま起きた。
おはよう翡翠。
今朝も起こしに来てくれたんだ」
「あ――はい、おはようございます」
　申し訳なさそうに挨拶を返して、翡翠はベッドまで近づいてくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki…!”
Then.
Hisui burst into the room in a panic.
“Hisui—what’s wrong? You never come in without knocking.”
“Oh—you’re awake, Master Shiki?”
“Yes, I just woke up. Good morning, Hisui. You came to wake me again.”
“Ah—yes. Good morning.”
She returned the greeting almost apologetically and approached the bed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama……!"
And then,
Hisui rushes into my room.
"Hisui……?
Did something happen?
You didn't even knock."
"Um…… Are you awake, Shiki-sama……?"
"Yeah, I just got up.
Good morning, Hisui.
Thanks for coming to wake me."
"Um--yes.
Good morning."
Returning my greeting apologetically, Hisui approaches the bed.

entries.japanese:
「お飲み物をお持ちいたしました。
ご気分が優れないようでしたらお飲みください」
　見れば、翡翠は昨日と同じように銀のトレイに飲み物を用意していた。
「……？
　いや、別に気分は悪くないからいらないよ。
ぐっすり寝たしね、頭もスッキリしてる」
「───ですが」
　じっ、と俺を見つめる翡翠。
「先ほどはひどくご気分が優れていないようでした。
志貴さま、胸の傷が痛んでいるのではないですか？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“I brought you something to drink. Please have it if you feel unwell.”
Just as yesterday, Hisui carried a drink on a silver tray.
“…? I feel fine, so I don’t need it. I slept soundly, and my head’s clear.”
“But…”
Hisui studied me.
“You seemed terribly unwell a moment ago. Master Shiki, is the scar on your chest hurting?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I have brought you something to drink.
You do not appear well, so please drink it."
Looking at it, it seems like she brought a drink on a silver tray like she did yesterday.
"……?
I don't really feel bad or anything.
I slept soundly and I feel refreshed."
"But---"
Hisui stares at me.
"You seemed to be in a very poor state earlier.
Shiki-sama, does the scar on your chest not hurt?"

entries.japanese:
「べつにそんなことはないけど。
……まあ、たしかに夢見が悪くてうなされていたかもしれないな。
さっきまでひどい夢をみてたから」
　……思い出すと眩暈がする。
　翡翠はじっと、そんな俺の顔を見つめている。
「……そっか。
翡翠が起こしてくれたんだ」
「……はい。
申し訳ございません」
「なに言ってるんだ。
ありがとう、翡翠。
起こしてくれて助かった」
　心からの本心でお礼を言う。
　翡翠が起こしてくれなかったら、俺はまだあの悪夢の中で立ち尽くしていただろうから。
entries.maoEnglish:
“No, nothing like that. Though I may have been moaning in my sleep. I was having an awful dream until just now.”
Remembering it made me dizzy.
Hisui kept her eyes fixed on my face.
“…I see. You’re the one who woke me.”
“…Yes. I apologize.”
“What are you apologizing for? Thank you, Hisui. I’m glad you woke me.”
I thanked her from the heart.
If Hisui hadn’t woken me, I would probably still be standing helplessly inside that nightmare.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No, not really…… Well, it may be because of that terrible dream.
I was really having quite a nightmare."
…… I feel dizzy just remembering it.
Hisui looks intently at my face.
"…… I see.
Hisui, you woke me up."
"…… Yes, I am deeply sorry."
"What are you saying?
Thanks, Hisui.
You really helped me a lot."
I really do mean that from my heart.
If she hadn't woken me, I might still be trapped inside that awful nightmare.

entries.japanese:
「それじゃすぐに着替えてから食堂に行くからさ。
わざわざ飲み物まで持ってきてくれたのに、ごめんな」
「いえ、いいんです。
それでは居間のほうでお待ちしております」
　翡翠は静かに退室していく。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’ll change and come straight to the dining room. Sorry you brought the drink all this way.”
“It’s quite all right. I’ll wait for you in the sitting room.”
Hisui quietly withdrew.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I'll change and go to the dining room.
Thanks for everything--and for giving me this drink.
Sorry about that."
"No, you do not need to apologize.
I will wait for you in the sitting room."
Hisui silently leaves the room.

entries.japanese:
正直、ちょっと感動している。
　翡翠は無表情な子なんだなって思っていたけど、もしかして感情表現が下手なだけなのかもしれない。
　俺がうなされているだけであんなに慌てていたなんて、想像するだけでつい笑ってしまう。
　
　この分なら、翡翠の笑顔を見ることもそう難しい事じゃないかもしれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
Honestly, I was a little touched.
I had thought Hisui was simply an emotionless girl, but perhaps she was only bad at showing what she felt.
Imagining her panicking merely because I was having a nightmare brought an involuntary smile to my face.
At this rate, perhaps seeing Hisui smile wouldn’t be so difficult after all.
entries.mirrorMoon:
To be honest, I really am quite moved.
I thought she was truly without emotions, but she may just be poor at expressing them.

She was so distressed over me having a nightmare, it makes me smile imagining her in such a hurry.
Maybe it isn't that hard to see Hisui's smile.

entries.japanese:
「――――さて、起きるか」
　シーツをはいで、体を起こす。
―――瞬間。
　ずきり、と激しく体が痛んだ。
「ぐっ………！」
　痛みは奥のほうから、どくん、どくん、と鼓動に合わせるように、響いてくる。
「あ───ぐ───」
　シーツをつかんで、なんとか痛みに耐える。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Well, time to get up.”
I threw back the sheets and sat up.
―――The instant I moved—
A violent stab of pain tore through my body.
“Ngh…!”
The pain echoed from somewhere deep inside, throbbing in time with my heartbeat.
“Ah—gh—”
I clutched the sheets and somehow endured it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----Well, time to get up!"
I throw off the sheets and get up.
---In that instant.
Pain explodes through my body.
"Gaaah………!"
It's from a much deeper place, aching with my heartbeat.
"Ah---ggghh---"
Clenching the sheets, I somehow weather the pain.

entries.japanese:
「は―――あ」
　……おさまった。
　突発的な発作だったのか、体に異常はない。
「……胸の……傷」
　服の上から胸に触れる。
　そこには大きな傷跡があって、完治した今でも、ときおり今みたいに痛むコトがある。
　主治医が言うには、精神的な痛みが完治したはずの肉体の痛みを繰り返させる、というコトだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hah…”
It passed.
Apparently it had only been a sudden attack; nothing seemed physically wrong.
“…The scar… on my chest.”
I touched it through my clothes.
A large scar lay there, and though the wound had healed completely, it still hurt like this from time to time.
According to my doctor, pain in the mind could make an old injury hurt again even after the body had healed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ahhh--"
It fades away.
There's nothing lingering.
Perhaps just a sudden fit?
"…… Chest… wound."
I bring my hand over my chest.
There is a great scar there, and even though it has healed, at times it still hurts like it did just now.
The doctor said the physical wound is healed, but that the mind must be replaying the pain over and over again.

entries.japanese:
たいてい胸の傷が痛む時は、交通事故や生き物の死体を見たあとだ。
　血や死のイメージが、八年前の事故を思い起こさせているんだろう。
「……昨夜のせい、か」
　赤い路地裏。
　そこで普段通りに話しかけてきた弓塚の笑顔。
entries.maoEnglish:
Usually the scar hurt after I saw a traffic accident or the corpse of an animal.
Images of blood and death must call up the accident from eight years ago.
“…Was it last night?”
A red alley.
Yumizuka’s smile as she spoke to me there as casually as ever.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Usually, the scar begins throbbing after I see a traffic accident or a dead body.
The image of blood or death must make me recall the accident eight years ago.
"…… Because of last night, I guess."
The red back alley.
And the normal, smiling face of Yumizuka.

entries.japanese:
「ぐ――――！」
　胸が、痛む。
　弓塚のことが頭から離れない。
　けど、どうすればいいのか、どうするべきなのかさえ、俺には考えつかない。
　俺に出来る事といえば、遠野志貴の日常をとりあえずこなす事ぐらいだ。
「く―――そ」
　自分自身に悪態をついて、ベッドから起きあがる。
　寝巻から学生服に着替えて、居間に向かうことにした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ngh—!”
My chest hurt.
I couldn’t get Yumizuka out of my head,
but I had no idea what to do—or even what I ought to do.
All I could manage was to go through the motions of Shiki Tohno’s ordinary day.
“Damn it.”
Cursing myself, I got out of bed,
changed from my pajamas into my school uniform, and headed for the sitting room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Guh--!"
My chest--hurts.
The image of Yumizuka doesn't leave my mind.
But I don't know what I should do, what I can do.
I can only live my everyday life.
"…… Shi… t…"
Swearing at myself, I roll out of bed.
After changing out of my pajamas and into my school uniform, I head to the sitting room.

entries.japanese:
居間には秋葉と翡翠の姿があった。
　琥珀さんは厨房のほうで俺の朝食の支度をしてくれているんだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
Akiha and Hisui were in the sitting room.
Kohaku was probably in the kitchen preparing my breakfast.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Akiha and Hisui are in the sitting room.
Kohaku-san is probably in the kitchen cooking my breakfast.

entries.japanese:
「おはようございます、兄さん」
　秋葉はソファーに座ったまま、こっちの顔色をうかがうように挨拶をしてくる。
「……ああ、おはよう秋葉」
　挨拶を返して、そのまま食堂に向かう。
　時間的に秋葉とのんびり居間で話をする余裕はないし―――俺自身にも、誰かと話をする余裕なんてなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Good morning, Brother.”
Still seated on the sofa, Akiha studied my face as she greeted me.
“…Morning, Akiha.”
I answered and continued toward the dining room.
There wasn’t enough time to sit and chat with her—and I had no room in me to talk to anyone anyway.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Good morning, Nii-san."
Sitting on the sofa, Akiha greets me and looks at my expression.
"…… Ah, good morning Akiha."
Returning her greeting, I head to the dining room.
There really isn't that much time for me to stay and chat with Akiha---and I don't really feel like talking to anyone at all.

entries.japanese:
「兄さん、お話があるのですけど―――少し、よろしいですか」
「いいよ、時間がないから手短にな」
　秋葉の向かいのソファーに座る。
「それでは率直に聞きますけど、兄さん昨夜はどこにいっていたんですか？」
　秋葉はまっすぐな目で問いただしてくる。
　……琥珀さんは秘密にしてくれただろうけど、さすがに二時間近く屋敷にいなければ隠し通す事なんかできなかったか。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Brother, I’d like to speak with you. Do you have a moment?”
“All right, but I’m short on time, so make it quick.”
I sat on the sofa opposite her.
“Then I’ll ask you plainly. Brother, where did you go last night?”
Akiha questioned me with an unwavering gaze.
Kohaku had probably kept my secret, but there was no hiding an absence of nearly two hours from the mansion.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Nii-san, I would like to speak with you a little---is that alright?"
"That's fine, but please make it short since I don't have much time."
I sit on the sofa across from her.
"Then I will get straight to the point.
Nii-san, where did you go last night?"
Akiha looks directly at me as she asks.
…… Kohaku-san probably did keep it a secret, but I guess it wasn't possible to hide being gone for two hours.

entries.japanese:
「……別に。
ただ街を歩いていただけだよ。
遅くなったのは謝るけど、そう大したことじゃないだろ」
　秋葉に嘘をつきたくないから、できるだけ曖昧に返答した。
「街を歩いていただけって、それは大した事でしょう。
兄さんはまだ未成年なんですから、夜の街になんかいないでください。
そうでなくても、最近は物騒なんですから」
「―――――――あ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“…Nowhere. I was only walking around town. I’m sorry I came home late, but it’s hardly a catastrophe.”
I didn’t want to lie to Akiha, so I made my answer as vague as possible.
“Only walking around town? That is serious. You’re still a minor, Brother, so please don’t stay out in the city at night—especially when it has become so dangerous.”
“Ah—”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Nothing.
Just went for a walk in town.
I'm sorry for getting back late, but it's no big deal."
Since I don't want to lie to Akiha, I answer as evasively as possible.

"Just walking the streets IS something.
You are still a minor, so please do not wander out late at night.
Even if you weren't, there have been a lot of disturbances going on."
"------Ah."

entries.japanese:
物騒―――夜の街を徘徊する通り魔。
　なんで。
　なんで、気がつかなかったんだろう。
　人を殺して血を抜き取るという殺人鬼。
　そのフレーズは、昨日の弓塚にぴったり当てはまってしまうじゃないか――――
entries.maoEnglish:
Dangerous. The attacker stalking the city at night.
Why?
Why hadn’t I realized?
A killer who murdered people and drained their blood.
That description fit yesterday’s Yumizuka perfectly—
entries.mirrorMoon:
Disturbances--the killer skulking around town at night.
Why?
Why didn't I realize it?
The killer that murders people and drinks their blood.
That phrase perfectly matches Yumizuka's behavior yesterday----

entries.japanese:
「……こんなこと、私が言うまでもないでしょうけど、兄さんの体は無茶がきかないんです。
　昨夜みたいに、その……ひどく疲れた顔をして帰ってこられたら、困ります。
　何か悩み事があるのでしたら打ち明けてください。
大した力にはなれませんけど、私でよかったら…………」
―――考えたくないけど。
　弓塚。
弓塚が、この街を騒がしている殺人鬼なのかも、しれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…I shouldn’t have to remind you, but your health can’t bear this kind of strain, Brother.
I can’t simply watch you come home looking as exhausted as you did last night.
If something is troubling you, please tell me. I may not be much help, but if I’m enough…”
―――I didn’t want to think it, but—
Yumizuka. Yumizuka might be the murderer terrorizing this city.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I shouldn't have to say this, but you shouldn't strain your body.
If you come back with an exhausted face like last night's again, I'll get worried.
If you're in trouble, please tell me.
I may not be able to do much, but if you could…"
---I don't want to think about it, but…
Yumizuka.
Yumizuka could be the killer terrorizing the town.

entries.japanese:
「兄さん？
　ちゃんと話を聞いてますか？」
「あ――――いや、うん、聞い、てる」
　秋葉の声が聞こえる。
　けど、こっちの頭の中はただ、昨日の弓塚の姿が思い出されるだけだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Brother? Are you listening to me?”
“Ah—yes.
I’m lis…tening.”
I could hear Akiha’s voice, but all my mind could do was replay the sight of Yumizuka the night before.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Nii-san?
Are you listening to me?"
"Eh----uh, yeah.
I'm listening."
I hear Akiha's voice.
But, the only thing in my mind is the image of Yumizuka from yesterday.

entries.japanese:
秋葉はじっと俺を見つめてくる。
「どうしても事情は話せないっていうんですね、兄さんは」
「ああ。
秋葉には、関係ないことだ」
　今は弓塚のことしか考えられない。
　早く一人になりたくて、そんな言葉を、返していた。
entries.maoEnglish:
Akiha stared at me.
“You truly refuse to tell me what happened, Brother?”
“Yes. It has nothing to do with you.”
I could think of nothing but Yumizuka.
Desperate to be alone, I gave her that cruel answer.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Akiha glares at me.

"So.
You can't talk about your situation, Nii-san?"
"Yeah.
It has nothing to do with you, Akiha."
Right now, I can think only of Yumizuka.
I want to be alone--and so I said that.

entries.japanese:
「―――あくまで自分だけの勝手を通す、というのですね、兄さんは」
「………………」
「わかりました。
では、どうぞご自由になさってください。
兄さんがそうおっしゃるんでしたら、私も自分の勝手を通すだけですから」
　秋葉はロビーへと立ち去っていく。
entries.maoEnglish:
“So you intend to do exactly as you please, regardless of anyone else, Brother?”
“…”
“Very well. Do as you like. If that is your position, Brother, then I shall do as I please as well.”
Akiha left for the foyer.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"You're going to keep going your own way, is that what you're saying, Nii-san?"
"……………"
"I understand.
Well, please, feel free.
If that's what you want, Nii-san, I'll do the same."
Akiha stands, and walks out to the lobby.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま。
よろしいのですか、それで」
「……よろしいって、なにが」
「秋葉さまは志貴さまを深く案じているんだと思います。
……あの方はご自分のお気持ちを口にする方ではありませんから、志貴さまに伝わりにくいとは思いますが―――」
「ちゃんとわかってるよ。
けど、今は頭がいっぱいでダメなんだ。
……秋葉には、悪いと思ってる」
「………………」
　翡翠はそれきり黙りこんだ。
「志貴さーん、朝ごはんですよー！」
　食堂から琥珀さんの声が聞こえてくる。
　席を立って、食堂に向かった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki. Are you certain that was wise?”
“What do you mean?”
“I believe Miss Akiha is deeply worried for Master Shiki. She is not someone who puts her feelings into words, so they may be difficult for Master Shiki to see…”
“I know. But my head is too full right now. I know I’ve hurt her.”
“…”
Hisui fell silent.
“Master Shiki! Breakfast is ready!”
Kohaku called from the dining room.
I rose and went in.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama?
Is this acceptable?"
"…… Acceptable?
Is what acceptable?"
"I believe Akiha-sama is deeply concerned about you, Shiki-sama.
But I think it is difficult for her since she does not often talk about her feelings----"
"I know.
But right now, my head's full, and I can't… I do feel sorry."
"…………"

Hisui falls silent.
"Shiki-saaaan, breakfast!"
Kohaku-san's voice can be heard from the dining room.
I stand up and head towards it.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま、今日のお帰りは何時になるでしょうか？」
「ああ、今日は土曜日だから……いや、夕方になるかもしれない。
ちょっと、探し物があるから」
「かしこまりました。
それではどうぞお気をつけて行ってらっしゃいませ」
　ふかぶかと一礼する。
　翡翠に見送られて、屋敷を後にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki, what time do you expect to return today?”
“Well, it’s Saturday, so… No, it may be evening. There’s something I need to look for.”
“Understood. Please take care.”
She bowed deeply.
Hisui saw me off as I left the mansion.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama, around what time will you be returning today?"
"Ahh… since today's Saturday… --No.
It'll probably be in the evening.
There's something I want to look for."
"I understand.
Please, take care until then."
She bows deeply.
After Hisui sees me off, I leave the mansion.

entries.japanese:
―――学校に来ても、何の意味もなかった。
　弓塚さつきは欠席者として扱われて、誰も、彼女のことを案じていないように見えた。
　時間はそれこそいつのまにか過ぎてしまっていた。
途中、有彦やシエル先輩がやってきたような気がするけど、よく覚えていない。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Coming to school had accomplished nothing.
Satsuki Yumizuka was treated as just another absent student, and no one seemed worried about her.
The hours slipped away before I knew it. Arihiko and Ciel may have stopped by at some point, but I barely remembered.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---There was no point coming to school.
Yumizuka Satsuki was treated as an absentee, and no one seemed to be the slightest bit concerned about her.
Time passed without my realizing it.
Perhaps Arihiko or Ciel-senpai came by sometime, but I don't really remember.

entries.japanese:
昼になって学校が終わった。
　何のあてもない。
　何のあてもないけど、弓塚を捜さないといけない。
　日が沈む。
　街中を走りまわっても、弓塚さつきの姿は見つけられなかった。
「…………くっ」
　悔しくて歯を噛んだ。
　……弓塚が見つからないのが悔しいんじゃない。
entries.maoEnglish:
School ended at noon.
I had no leads.
None at all—but I had to find Yumizuka.
The sun went down.
Though I had run all over the city, I found no trace of Satsuki Yumizuka.
“Damn…”
I clenched my teeth in frustration.
But I wasn’t frustrated because I couldn’t find Yumizuka.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Noon comes, and school ends.
I have no idea.
I have no idea, but I still have to look for Yumizuka.
The sun sets.
Even after running everywhere in town, there's no sign of Yumizuka Satsuki anywhere.
"………… Gah."
I bite my lip angrily.
…… But it's not anger over not finding her.

entries.japanese:
二日前。
　この道で、あんな約束をした自分が、腹だたしい。
―――ピンチの時は助けてね。
　そう言ってきた弓塚に、俺は気軽に返答した。
　自分に出来ることなら手を貸すよ、と。
　……それは、なんて無責任な返答だったんだろう。
　俺にできることなんて、本当にちっぽけだ。
　痛い、と。
　痛くて暗くて寒い、なんて苦しんでいた弓塚の姿を見つけ出すことさえ、できない。
entries.maoEnglish:
Two days ago.
I was furious with myself for making her that promise on this very road.
―――If I’m ever in trouble, you’ll help me, right?
I had answered Yumizuka so casually.
I told her I would help if there was anything I could do.
What an irresponsible answer that had been.
What I could do was pitifully little.
It hurt, she had said.
Yumizuka had been suffering in pain, in darkness and cold—and I couldn’t even find her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Two days ago.
I'm mad at myself for promising such a thing in the first place.
---Help me when I'm in a pinch, okay?
Yumizuka said that, and I answered lightheartedly.
I would help, as much as I could.
…… Such an irresponsible answer.
There's really nothing I can do.
She said it hurt.
I can't even find Yumizuka, painfully suffering in the cold darkness.

entries.japanese:
「――――――」
　日が沈んでいく。
　……認めたくないけど、夜にならないと弓塚は見つけられないのかもしれない。
「……夕方には戻るって、翡翠に言ったんだっけ」
　時間が早かったのかもしれない。
　いったん屋敷に戻って、冷静に考えてみよう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“—”
The sun continued to sink.
I hated to admit it, but perhaps I wouldn’t find Yumizuka until night.
“I told Hisui I’d be home this evening.”
Maybe I had begun too early.
I should return to the mansion for now and think things through with a clear head.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---"
The sun is setting.
…… I don't want to admit it, but maybe I can only find Yumizuka after nightfall.
"…… I told Hisui I'd be back in the evening."
Perhaps it's too early.
I'll go back to the mansion and calmly think this through.

entries.japanese:
「お帰りなさいませ、志貴さま」
　ロビーでは翡翠が待っていた。
「ただいま。
……翡翠、秋葉はどうしてる？」
「秋葉さまはお帰りになってらっしゃいません。
遅くなるそうですから、夕食は先にとるようにとの事です」
「そうか。
……夕食まで部屋で休んでるから、時間になったら食堂に行くよ」
「はい。
お呼びしますので、ごゆっくりお休みください」
　ふかぶかとお辞儀をする翡翠に背を向けて、自分の部屋へ足を運んだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Welcome home, Master Shiki.”
Hisui was waiting in the foyer.
“I’m back. Hisui, where’s Akiha?”
“Miss Akiha has not yet returned. She expects to be late and asked that you dine without her.”
“I see. I’ll rest in my room until dinner and come down when it’s time.”
“Very well. I’ll call you when it is time, so please rest comfortably.”
I turned away from Hisui’s deep bow and went to my room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Welcome home, Shiki-sama."
Hisui was waiting in the lobby.
"I'm back…… Hisui, where's Akiha?"
"Akiha-sama has not returned yet.
Since she shall be late, we are to have supper first."
"I see…… I'll be resting in my room until dinner, so I'll head to the dining room when it's time."
"Yes.
Please rest until I call you."
I turn my back to the bowing Hisui and walk towards my room.

entries.japanese:
―――夕食が終わって、ベッドに腰をかける。
　時計の針は夜の九時にさしかかろうとしている。
　この屋敷は八時をすぎてからの外出は禁じられているから、もう外に出る事はできない。
「……………」
　だが、そんなものはただのきまりごとだ。
　その気になればいくらでも外には出れる。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――After dinner, I sat on the edge of my bed.
The clock was approaching nine.
No one in this house was allowed out after eight, so I couldn’t leave now.
“…”
But that was only a rule.
If I truly wanted to, nothing could keep me inside.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---After supper, I sit down on my bed.
The clock's hands show nine o'clock.
Since leaving the mansion after eight is forbidden, I cannot go outside any longer.
"…………"
But, that's merely a rule.
If I feel like it, I can easily go outside.

entries.japanese:
―――ばいばい。
また明日学校でね、遠野くん。
entries.maoEnglish: ―――Bye. See you at school tomorrow, Tohno.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Bye-bye.
See you at school tomorrow, Tohno-kun.

entries.japanese:
……なにを……考えてるんだろう、と自分でもバカらしく思う。
　弓塚がいったいどうなっているのか、俺にはてんでわからない。
　アイツが街を騒がしている吸血鬼殺人の犯人だっていう事も、思い知らされてる。
　けど、どうしても。
　夕暮れの帰り道、弓塚の最後の言葉が、どうしても忘れられないでいる――――
entries.maoEnglish:
What am I even thinking? The question felt absurd.
I had no idea what had happened to Yumizuka.
I had also been forced to face the fact that she was behind the vampire murders terrifying the city.
And yet, no matter what I did,
I couldn’t forget her final words on that road at dusk—
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… What…… am I thinking?
It's just foolish.
I just can't comprehend what's happening to Yumizuka.
I do realize she is the vampire serial killer causing all these incidents in town.
But still.
I can not forget her last words she said in the sunset on our way home----

entries.japanese:
……いつのまにか、時刻は十二時にさしかかっている。
　俺はどうするべきかまだ迷ったままで、眠れない夜を過ごしていた。
「……志貴さま、起きていらっしゃいますか……？」
　……翡翠の声だ。
　どうしたんだろう、こんな夜更けに。
entries.maoEnglish:
Before I knew it, midnight was drawing near.
Still unable to decide what I should do, I passed the night without sleep.
“…Master Shiki, are you still awake?”
It was Hisui.
What could she want at this hour?
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Before I realize it, it's almost midnight.
Lost in thinking about what I should do, I've passed some of the night wide awake.
"…… Shiki-sama, are you awake……?"
…… Hisui's voice.
Why is she up this late at night?

entries.japanese:
「起きてるけど、どうしたの翡翠？」
「―――はい、何分このような時間なので迷ったのですが、志貴さまが起きていらっしゃるようでしたらお伝えするべきだと思いまして」
「伝えるって、なにを？」
「先ほど、志貴さま宛に電話がかかってきたのです。
公園で待っている、との言伝でした」
「電話って……こんな時間に？」
「はい。
お名前も言われずにお切りになりましたので、志貴さまに伝えるのはどうかと迷ったのですが―――」
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’m awake. What is it, Hisui?”
“I hesitated because of the hour, but since you were awake, Master Shiki, I thought I ought to tell you.”
“Tell me what?”
“A telephone call came for you a short while ago, Master Shiki. The caller left a message saying they would be waiting in the park.”
“A call at this hour?”
“Yes. The caller gave no name and hung up, so I wasn’t sure whether I should pass the message on to you, Master Shiki.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I'm up, but why, Hisui?"
"---Yes, I was unsure, but if you were awake, I thought that I should tell you."
"Tell me what?"
"Just a while ago, a call came for you, Shiki-sama.
The message was that 'I'll be waiting in the park.'"
"Phone call…… This late at night?"
"Yes, the call ended before I could ask for a name, so I was unsure if I should tell you, Shiki-sama--"

entries.japanese:
「いや―――それは」
　……考えるまでもない。
　その電話は、弓塚からのものだろう。
「……ありがとう。
でも、今夜は遅いからまた明日にする。
その子、学校のクラスメイトだから明日になれば会えるんだ」
「うそです。
そんな辛そうな顔をしていらっしゃるのに、笑われては、困ります」
entries.maoEnglish:
“No—that’s…”
There was nothing to consider.
The call had to be from Yumizuka.
“…Thank you. But it’s too late tonight, so I’ll leave it until tomorrow. She’s a classmate. I can see her at school then.”
“That is a lie. Please don’t smile when you look so miserable.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No--that is……"
…… This doesn't require any thought.
That phone call had to have been from Yumizuka.
"…… Thanks.
But, it's a little late, so I'll wait until tomorrow.
She's one of my classmates, so I'll see her tomorrow."
"That is not true.
There is something wrong with smiling like that with such a strained face."

entries.japanese:
「ばか、うそなんてついてないよ。
大丈夫、こんな時間に外出なんてしない。
秋葉をまた怒らせるだけだし、翡翠にも迷惑をかけるじゃないか。
だから、そんなコトはしないよ」
「…………………」
　翡翠は押し黙る。
　しばらく、俺たちの間には言葉がなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Don’t be ridiculous. I’m not lying. It’s all right—I won’t go out at this hour. I’d only make Akiha angry again, and I’d cause you trouble too. I’m not going anywhere.”
“…”
Hisui said nothing.
For a while, no words passed between us.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Stupid, I'm not lying at all.
I'm fine, I won't go out this late at night.
Akiha would get mad, and you would get in trouble, so there's no reason for me to do that."
"…………………"
Hisui descends into silence.
The conversation between us dies.

entries.japanese:
「……志貴さま。
どうか、ご無理はなさらないでください」
「……やだな、べつに無理なんかしてないって。
これから寝るんだから、翡翠も部屋に戻っていいよ」
「………………」
　翡翠はただ俺を見つめてくるだけだ。
「―――それじゃあ、おやすみ」
　それに耐えきれなくなって、強引にドアを閉めた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…Master Shiki, please don’t push yourself.”
“…Honestly, I’m not. I’m going to bed now, so you can return to your room.”
“…”
Hisui only stood there looking at me.
“Good night, then.”
Unable to endure her gaze any longer, I forced the door shut.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Shiki-sama.
Please do not push yourself too hard."
"…… Nah, I'm not pushing anything.
I'll go to sleep, so please go back to your room."
"…………………"
Hisui just looks at me.
"---Well, good night."
Not being able to endure her stare, I slam the door.

entries.japanese:
「……まいったな。
翡翠に隠し事はできないか」
　机の引き出しからナイフを取り出す。
　……何をするというわけでもないけど、一応用心のために武器を持っていかないと安心できない。
「―――公園か。
こんな時間に呼び出すなんて、どうして―――」
　呟いて、つまらない寓話を思い出した。
　吸血鬼は夜じゃないと活動できない。
　それが本当だっていうんなら、弓塚はこんな時間に俺を呼び出したのではなく。
　こんな時間じゃないと、俺を呼び出せなかっただけじゃないのか。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…So much for hiding anything from Hisui.”
I took the knife from my desk drawer.
I didn’t intend to do anything with it, but I couldn’t feel safe going without some kind of weapon.
“The park… Why call me out at this hour—?”
The words brought an old, silly fable to mind.
Vampires could only move at night.
If that were true, then Yumizuka hadn’t chosen to summon me at this hour.
This was simply the only hour when she could.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Sheesh.
I can't hide anything from Hisui."
I take my knife out of the drawer.
…… I don't intend to necessarily use it, but I just feel better with it by my side.
"---The park?
Why would she call me out at this hour---"
Muttering, I think back to those foolish tales.
Vampires can only move about during night time.
So supposing that's true, then Yumizuka didn't call me out at this hour.
It's more like if it wasn't this hour, then she couldn't call me at all.

entries.japanese:
「……ごめんな翡翠。
自分でもバカだなって思うんだけど、この無理をしないと、どうにも眠れそうにないんだ」
　ここにいない翡翠に謝って、静かに、屋敷を後にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…Sorry, Hisui. I know this is stupid, but unless I do something this reckless, I’ll never be able to sleep.”
Apologizing to the absent Hisui, I quietly left the mansion.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Sorry, Hisui.
Even I think I'm stupid.
You told me not to strain myself, but I can't just sleep like this."
Apologizing to the empty room, I quietly leave the mansion.

entries.japanese:
「はあ―――はあ――――はあ」
　走りどおしで熱くなった体を休める。
　時間はじき午前零時にさしかかろうとしていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hah… hah… hah…”
I stopped to cool my body after running the whole way.
It was almost midnight.
entries.mirrorMoon:
*pant*--*pant*--*pant*
I rest my body, burning from all the running.
It's almost midnight.

entries.japanese:
大通りから離れた公園。
　連日の殺人事件でこのあたりには人影がない。
「………」
　どくん、と心臓が高鳴る。
　緊張で喉が渇く。
　翡翠が受けとった電話が弓塚からのものなら。
　彼女は、この奥で俺を待っているハズだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
The park lay far from the main road.
With the murders night after night, there wasn’t another person anywhere nearby.
“…”
My heart thudded.
Tension dried my throat.
If the call Hisui had answered was from Yumizuka,
she should be waiting somewhere farther inside.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The park located off of the main road.
Because of the serial killings these past several days, there's not a soul to be seen around here.
"………"
Thump.
My heart beats loudly.
My throat dries up from the tension.
If the phone call that Hisui received was from Yumizuka,
then she has to be waiting there for me.

entries.japanese:
夜の公園に人気はない。
　物音一つしない月下。
　わけもなく、全身の体温が下がった気がした。
「―――――――っ」
　首の後ろがしびれる。
　体がシン……と冷えきって、指先さえもかじかんでいくような、悪寒。
entries.maoEnglish:
The park was deserted.
Not a sound disturbed the moonlight.
For no reason I could name, it felt as if every trace of warmth had drained from my body.
“—!”
The back of my neck went numb.
My body went deathly cold, a chill so deep even my fingertips began to stiffen.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The park is empty at night.
There isn't a sound under the moonlight.
I don't know why, but a chill runs through me.
"----------Sst."
The back of my head numbs.
A horrible chill, as if my body freezes to my fingertips.

entries.japanese:
「はっ……はっ……」
　冷めていく体とは正反対に、喉が熱かった。
　カラカラに渇いている。
　ポケットの中に手をいれる。
　ただしきりに―――刃物を、手にしていたかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hah… hah…”
While my body grew colder, my throat burned.
It was parched dry.
I slipped a hand into my pocket.
More than anything, I wanted a blade in my hand.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I try to catch my breath.
In contrast to my cold body, my throat is scorching.
It's dry with thirst.
I put my hand in my pocket.
I just---wanted a blade in my hand.

entries.japanese:
「なん―――だ」
　ギリ………。
　微かな頭痛。
　低くなる体温。
　氷のように冷めていく理性。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What—is this?”
My teeth ground together.
A faint headache.
My temperature falling.
My reason cooling into ice.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Why…?"
Just…
A faint headache.
A low temperature.
My mind is cool like ice.

entries.japanese:
なにか、ヘンだ。
　この公園。
このあたりには、よくないモノが、渦巻いている気がする。
「……いまさら何を恐がってるんだ、俺は」
　頭痛を振り払って、奥へと足を進ませた。
entries.maoEnglish:
Something was wrong.
Something foul seemed to be churning through this park, all around me.
“…What am I afraid of now?”
I shook off the headache and pressed deeper inside.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Something is strange.
This park, it feels like something bad is around here.
"…… Just what am I afraid of?"
I shake the headache off, and walk deeper in.

entries.japanese:
あたりには誰もいない。
　ひどく暗くて、寂しい待ち合わせ場所。
　そこに―――誰かが蹲っていた。
　はあはあという呼吸。
　顔色は真っ青で、苦しそうに喉をかきむしっている姿。
　それは間違いなく、弓塚さつきの姿だった。
entries.maoEnglish:
There was no one around.
A dark, lonely place for a meeting.
And there—someone was crouching on the ground.
Her breath came in harsh gasps.
Her face was deathly pale, and she clawed at her throat in agony.
There was no mistaking Satsuki Yumizuka.
entries.mirrorMoon:
There's no one around.
A terribly dark and lonely place to meet someone.
There--someone is crouched.
Breathing raggedly.
Her face, pale white, as she scratches her throat in pain.
Without a doubt, it is Yumizuka Satsuki.

entries.japanese:
「弓……塚？」
　その姿があんまりにも苦しげだったからだろう。
　俺は昨夜のことなんて考えもせず、弓塚へと駆け出した。
「待って―――！」
　そんな俺の行動を、弓塚は声だけで止めてしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Yumi…zuka?”
Perhaps she simply looked too wretched to leave alone. Without even thinking of the night before, I ran toward her.
“Wait—!”
Her voice alone stopped me in my tracks.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yumi… zuka?"
Her figure is tormented.
Without a thought for what happened last night, I run towards her.
"Wait… !"
Yumizuka stops me with just a word.

entries.japanese:
「……待って、志貴くん。
来てくれたのは嬉しいけど、今は近くにこられると困っちゃうんだ。
お願いだから、それ以上は近寄らないで」
　苦しげな呼吸で。
　今にも倒れそうに体を震わせながら、弓塚はそんなことを言ってくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Wait, Shiki. I’m glad you came, but I can’t have you close to me right now. Please, don’t come any nearer.”
Her breath came in tortured gasps.
Her body trembling as if she might collapse at any moment, Yumizuka told me to stay back.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Wait, Shiki-kun.
I'm glad you came, but I don't want you any nearer right now.
Please, don't come any closer."
Her breathing looks painful.
Her body convulses as she speaks, as if she's about to collapse any second now.

entries.japanese:
「ばか、そんな顔色をしてるヤツを放っておけるわけがないだろ……！」
「ううん、わたしは、大丈夫……志貴くんが来てくれたから、もう元気になっちゃった」
　無理やり体をあげて、弓塚は笑顔をうかべる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Don’t be stupid; you look half dead—how am I supposed to leave you like this…?”
“No, I’m all right… You came, Shiki, so I’m feeling better already.”
Forcing herself upright, Yumizuka smiled.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Don't be stupid!
I'm not going to leave someone looking as painful as you alone…!"
"No, I'm okay… You came, so I'm fine now."
Forcing herself up, Yumizuka smiles at me.

entries.japanese:
「……いったいどうしたんだよ弓塚。
どうして家に帰ってないんだ。
昨日のアレは一体なんだったんだ。
どうして、あんな――――」
「ん？
　あんな、なに？」
「あんな―――あんなことを、していたんだ……！」
「あんなことって、昨日のことは見たまんまだよ。
わたしがあの人たちを殺したって言ったでしょ？」
　あっさりと返答する。
　……それを否定したいっていう俺の気持ちを、嘲笑うみたいに。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…What happened to you, Yumizuka? Why haven’t you gone home? What was all that yesterday? Why were you doing something so—?”
“Something so what?”
“Something so… so horrible…!”
“Yesterday was exactly what it looked like. I told you I killed those people, remember?”
She answered without hesitation.
As if mocking my desperate wish to deny it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… What's going on, Yumizuka?
Why haven't you been home?
What was that about, yesterday?
Why, that----"
"Hm?
That what?"
"That---you know what I'm talking about!"
"If you mean yesterday---well, you saw what happened.
I told you, 'I killed those people,' didn't I?"
She answers frankly.
…… It's almost as if she's laughing at my feelings of denial.

entries.japanese:
「それじゃあ……街で起きている殺人事件は、弓塚の仕業だっていうのか」
「あんまし答えたくないけど。
そういう事になるよ、うん」
「―――そういう事になるって、なんで！？」
「そういう事はそういう事だよ。
わたしはあの人たちを殺したし、きっとこれからも同じ事をしていくんだもん。
嘘をついたって仕方ないでしょ？」
「弓……塚、おまえ―――」
「その呼び方、やめてくれないかな。
わたしだって志貴くんって呼んでるんだから、志貴くんも名前で呼んでくれないと不公平だよ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Are you saying the murders in the city were your doing?”
“I’d rather not answer. But yes, I guess that’s what it means.”
“What do you mean, ‘that’s what it means’—why?!”
“It means what it means. I killed those people, and I’m sure I’ll keep doing the same thing. There’s no point lying about it, is there?”
“Yumizuka—you—”
“Could you stop calling me that? I call you Shiki, so it’s only fair that you call me by my first name too.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Then… the recent killings in town were all your doing, Yumizuka…!"
"I don't like to say it, but… that's the way it is, yeah."
"What the hell do you mean, 'That's the way it is' …!?"
"It's just the way it is.
I killed those people, and I'll keep on doing the same thing.
I can't just lie about it, can I?"
"Yumi… zuka, you--"
"Please.
Stop calling me that.
I'm calling you Shiki-kun, so it's only fair for you to call me by my first name too."

entries.japanese:
「なっ――――」
　ごくりと息を飲む。
　弓塚はやっぱり以前のままだ。
　以前のままの仕草で―――ひどく恐ろしいことを、口にする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What—?”
I swallowed hard.
Yumizuka was just as she had always been.
With the same familiar gestures, she spoke of things too horrible to imagine.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Wha…"
I take a deep breath.
Yumizuka is still like before.
Even though she acts like she used to----she says some pretty scary things.

entries.japanese:
「考えてみると、わたしってばかみたいだよね。
 こんなふうに志貴くんって呼ぶこともできないで、何年間もあなたのことを遠くから見てるだけだった」
「え――――弓、塚…………？」
「ずっと志貴くんのことを見てた。
あの倉庫で助けられる前から、ずっと志貴くんの事を見てた。
　わたし、本当は臆病なんだ。
だから周りの人たちに合わせて、無理をして笑ったり話を合わせたりしてたらね、いつのまにかアイドルみたいに扱われちゃった」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Looking back, I was such an idiot.
For years I couldn’t even call you Shiki; all I did was watch you from far away.”
“What—Yumizuka?”
“I was always watching you. Even before you saved me in that storehouse, I’d been watching you for ages.
I’m actually a coward. I forced myself to smile and agree with everyone so I could fit in, and before I knew it, people were treating me like some kind of class idol.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"When I think about it, I look foolish.
I could never talk to you like this, for all the years I watched you from afar."
"Eh--Yumi… zuka……?"
"I was always watching you, Shiki-kun.
Even before I was saved in that warehouse, I was always watching you.
I'm… really a coward.
I always just agreed with the people around me, and smiled when it seemed right.
Before I knew it, everyone was treating me like an idol."

entries.japanese:
「だから、学校はあんまり楽しくなかったんだ。
でも中学二年生になったばかりの時にね、志貴くんに話しかけられてから変わったんだよ」
「え―――？」
「ううん、志貴くんは覚えてなんかないよ。
なんていうのかな、あなたはいつも自然で、飾らない人だから。
たぶんあの時の言葉も、志貴くんにとってなんでもない一言だったんだろうなあ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“That’s why school was never much fun. But just after we started our second year of middle school, you spoke to me, and everything changed.”
“I did?”
“No, you wouldn’t remember. You’re always so natural, so completely yourself. Whatever you said probably meant nothing at all to you.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"So school wasn't fun for me.
But that changed, after you talked to me in the second year of junior high, Shiki-kun."
"Eh--?"
"Nah.
It's not something you'd remember.
How can I put it… You were always natural, never showing off.
Probably you didn't even think about what you said back then."

entries.japanese:
「――――――――」
　なんていえばいいんだろう。
　弓塚の言うとおり、俺は何も覚えていない。
　弓塚と何を話したのか、いや、弓塚と話したことがあるなんていうことさえ、覚えてない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“—”
What could I say?
She was right—I remembered nothing.
Not what we had talked about—I didn’t even remember ever speaking to her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------"
What can I say.
Just as Yumizuka says, I remember nothing.
I don't know what I said to her, or even if I had talked to her back then.

entries.japanese:
「いいよ、そんな顔しなくても。
志貴くんはあの頃から乾くんに付きっきりだったから、他のクラスメイトには興味がなさそうだったし」
「けど、それでも良かったんだ。
志貴くんと同じ教室にいるんだって思うだけで、すごく嬉しかった。
　いつかあなたにちゃんと話しかけて、弓塚さんって呼ばれることを目標にしてたなんて、今思うとすごく損してたなって笑っちゃうけど」
　懐かしむように彼女は言った。
　とても昔。
……とても遠い昔のことを思い出すように。
entries.maoEnglish:
“It’s all right. Don’t look like that. You were always off with Arihiko back then, so you never seemed interested in anyone else in class.”
“But I didn’t mind. Just knowing I was in the same classroom as you made me so happy. I dreamed of finally speaking to you properly and hearing you call me by name. Looking back, I can’t help laughing at how much time I wasted.”
She spoke with aching nostalgia,
as though remembering something ancient—something impossibly far away.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"It's okay.
Don't make a face like that.
You were only hanging out with Inui-kun, so it was normal for you to ignore other classmates."
"But that was okay.
I was happy just being in the same class as you, Shiki-kun.
It was my goal to talk to you and let you call me Yumizuka-san.
Now that I think about it, it was too small of a wish."
She recalls nostalgically.
Those ancient days.
…… Like she is remembering something that happened a long time ago.

entries.japanese:
「わたし、ずっとあなたのことを見てた。
気付いてくれないってわかってたけど、ずっと見てたんだよ」
「――――――」
　それは―――正直嬉しいけど。
「ね。
志貴くんはわたしのこと、好き？」
　今の彼女に、俺はなんて答えてあげればいいんだろう―――？
entries.maoEnglish:
“I watched you all that time. I knew you’d never notice, but I still kept watching.”
“—”
To be honest, it made me happy. But—
“Tell me, Shiki. Do you like me?”
What answer could I possibly give the girl standing before me now?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I… was always watching you.
I knew you'd never notice me, but I watched you anyway."
"------"
Well--to be honest, I'm happy, but…
"Do you like me, Shiki-kun?"
How can I answer her right now---?

entries.japanese:
日が沈む。
　街中を走りまわっても、弓塚さつきの姿は見つけられなかった。
「…………くっ」
　悔しくて歯を噛んだ。
　……弓塚が見つからないのが悔しいんじゃない。
entries.maoEnglish:
The sun went down.
Though I had run all over the city, I found no trace of Satsuki Yumizuka.
“Damn…”
I clenched my teeth in frustration.
But I wasn’t frustrated because I couldn’t find Yumizuka.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The sun sets.
Even after running everywhere in town, there's no sign of Yumizuka Satsuki anywhere.
"………… Gah."
I bite my lip angrily.
…… But it's not anger over not finding her.

entries.japanese:
二日前。
　この道で、あんな約束をした自分が、腹だたしい。
―――ピンチの時は助けてね。
　そう言ってきた弓塚に、俺は気軽に返答した。
　自分に出来ることなら手を貸すよ、と。
　……それは、なんて無責任な返答だったんだろう。
　俺にできることなんて、本当にちっぽけだ。
　痛い、と。
　痛くて暗くて寒い、なんて苦しんでいた弓塚の姿を見つけ出すことさえ、できない。
entries.maoEnglish:
Two days ago.
I was furious with myself for making her that promise on this very road.
―――If I’m ever in trouble, you’ll help me, right?
I had answered Yumizuka so casually.
I told her I would help if there was anything I could do.
What an irresponsible answer that had been.
What I could do was pitifully little.
It hurt, she had said.
Yumizuka had been suffering in pain, in darkness and cold—and I couldn’t even find her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Two days ago.
I'm mad at myself for promising such a thing in the first place.
--Help me when I'm in a pinch, okay?
Yumizuka said that, and I answered lightheartedly.
I would help, as much as I could.
…… Such an irresponsible answer.
There's really nothing I can do.
She said it hurt.
I can't even find Yumizuka, painfully suffering in the cold darkness.

entries.japanese:
「――――――」
　日が沈んでいく。
　……認めたくないけど、夜にならないと弓塚は見つけられないのかもしれない。
「……夕方には戻るって、翡翠に言ったんだっけ」
　時間が早かったのかもしれない。
　いったん屋敷に戻って、冷静に考えてみよう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“—”
The sun continued to sink.
I hated to admit it, but perhaps I wouldn’t find Yumizuka until night.
“I told Hisui I’d be home this evening.”
Maybe I had begun too early.
I should return to the mansion for now and think things through with a clear head.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---"
The sun is setting.
…… I don't want to admit it, but maybe I can only find Yumizuka after nightfall.
"…… I told Hisui I'd be back in the evening."
Perhaps it's too early.
I'll go back to the mansion and calmly think this through.

entries.japanese:
―――学校を捜してみよう。
　弓塚が欠席しているって事はわかってるけど、それでも―――何のアテもない今、自分と弓塚の接点はこの学校だけだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――I would search the school.
I knew Yumizuka was absent, but with no other lead, the school was the only point of connection between us.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---I'll search at school.
I know she's absent, but… right now, this school is the only connection I have to her.

entries.japanese:
日が沈む。
　校舎を走りまわっても、弓塚さつきの姿は見つけられなかった。
「…………くっ」
　悔しくて歯を噛んだ。
　……弓塚が見つからないのが悔しいんじゃない。
　二日前、あんな約束をした自分が、腹だたしい。
entries.maoEnglish:
The sun went down.
Though I had run through every corner of the school, I found no trace of Satsuki Yumizuka.
“Damn…”
I clenched my teeth in frustration.
But I wasn’t frustrated because I couldn’t find Yumizuka.
I was furious with myself for making that promise two days ago.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The sun sets.
Even after looking everywhere at school, there's no sign of Yumizuka Satsuki anywhere.
"………… Gah."
I bite my lip angrily.
…… But it's not anger over not finding her.

Two days ago, I'm mad at myself for promising such a thing in the first place.

entries.japanese:
―――ピンチの時は助けてね。
　そう言ってきた弓塚に、俺は気軽に返答した。
　自分に出来ることなら手を貸すよ。
　……それは、なんて無責任な返答だったんだろう。
　俺にできることなんて、本当にちっぽけだ。
　痛い、と。
　痛くて暗くて寒い、なんて苦しんでいた弓塚の姿を見つけ出すことさえ、できない。

entries.japanese:
―――弓塚のいそうなところなんて見当もつかない。
　ただ家とかマンションが多いあたりを中心に捜してみよう。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――I had no idea where Yumizuka might be.
All I could do was concentrate my search on areas with lots of houses and apartment buildings.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---I have no idea where she could be.
But let's search around the area where there are lots of houses and apartments.

　この道で、あんな約束をした自分が、腹だたしい。

"…… I told Hisui I'd be back in the evening."
Perhaps it's too early.
I'll go back to the mansion and calmly think this through.

entries.japanese:
「お帰りなさいませ、志貴さま」
「ただいま。
……翡翠、秋葉はどうしてる？」
「秋葉さまは学校の手続きに行かれました。
遅くなるそうですから、夕食は先にとるようにとの事です」
「………？」
　学校の手続き、か。
　秋葉の通っている高校は名高いお嬢様学校だから、なにかと複雑な手続きがあるのだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Welcome home, Master Shiki.”
“I’m back. Hisui, where’s Akiha?”
“Miss Akiha has gone to take care of some school formalities. She expects to be late and asked that you dine without her.”
“…?”
School formalities?
Akiha attended a prestigious girls’ academy; perhaps it had all sorts of complicated procedures.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Welcome home, Shiki-sama."
"I'm back… Hisui, where's Akiha?"
"Akiha-sama has remained at school for certain formalities.
Since she shall be late, we are to have supper first."
"…?"
Certain formalities, huh.
Akiha's school probably has lots of formalities as it is a top tier school for young ladies.

entries.japanese:
「夕食まで部屋で休んでるから、時間になったら食堂に行くよ」
「はい。
お呼びしますので、ごゆっくりお休みください」
　ふかぶかとお辞儀をする翡翠に背を向けて、自分の部屋へ足を運んだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’ll rest in my room until dinner and come down when it’s time.”
“Very well. I’ll call you. Please rest comfortably.”
I turned away from Hisui’s deep bow and went to my room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I'll go wait in my room till suppertime and I'll head down when it's ready."
