兄さんはシエルという人とどれくらい親しいんですか？」
　唐突に、突拍子もない質問をしてくる。
「いや、別に親しいっていうほどじゃないけど。
シエル先輩とは先輩と後輩の間柄だよ。
なんていうか、話してると落ち着く友達って感じだけど」
　そうですか、と秋葉は目を背けて玄関に向かっていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
We reach the mansion.
Akiha steps ahead to open the gate, then turns back to me as though something has just occurred to her.
“One question. How close are you to this Ciel?”
The question comes completely out of nowhere.
“We’re not especially close. She’s a year above me, and that’s all. I suppose she’s a friend I can relax around.”
Akiha says, “I see,” then looks away and heads for the front door.
entries.mirrorMoon:
We arrive at the mansion.
Akiha steps forward to open the gate, but as if remembering something, turns to me.
"…… I have one question.
How close are you to that person called Ciel, Nii-san?"
Abruptly, she asks an extremely forward question.
"Not especially close.
We're just friends from school.
She… feels like someone I can talk to."
"Really?" Akiha says, turning away and going through the gates.

entries.japanese:
庭を通り過ぎて玄関に着く。
　翡翠が門で待っていたり、庭で琥珀さんがホウキを手にして掃除していたりする事はなく、今日は申し合わせたように二人の姿は見当たらなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
We cross the garden and reach the entrance.
Hisui is not waiting at the gate, nor is Kohaku sweeping the garden with her broom; today, as if by prior agreement, neither of them is anywhere to be seen.
entries.mirrorMoon:
We cross the courtyard and arrive at the door.
As Hisui is not waiting at the gates and Kohaku is not sweeping the garden, there is no sign of either of them today.

entries.japanese:
「あ」
「はい？
　何か言いましたか兄さん」
「いや、ちょっとした事なんだけど。
あのさ、秋葉が言っていた例の和風の離れに入ってみたいんだけど、いいかな」
「――――離れに、ですか？」
　呟いて、秋葉は難しそうに眉をよせた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh.”
“Yes? Did you say something, Brother?”
“Nothing important. Could I take a look inside that Japanese-style annex you mentioned?”
“――――The annex?”
Akiha murmurs, knitting her brows.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah."
"Yes?
Did you say something, Nii-san?"
"Well, nothing much but… I'd like to go and take a look at the Japanese-style building you were talking about, if that's okay."
"----The detached building?"
Murmuring, Akiha's brow creases with concern.

entries.japanese:
「やめてください。
あそこはもう何年も前に封鎖したところです。
兄さんといえど、あそこ立ち入ることは許しません」
　きっぱりと言って、秋葉は屋敷の中に入っていってしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Please don’t. That building was sealed off years ago. Even you are not permitted to enter it.”
With that flat refusal, Akiha disappears into the mansion.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Please, do not.
It was sealed up many years ago.
Nii-san, even you are not permitted to go there."
Having stated this, Akiha goes into the mansion.

entries.japanese:
時刻は夕方の五時すぎ。
　夕食まではあと一時間ほど余裕がある。
　このまま夕食まで部屋で過ごすべきか、それとも―――
entries.maoEnglish:
It is a little past five in the evening.
Dinner is still an hour away.
I could spend the time in my room, or else―――
entries.mirrorMoon:
It's a bit past five in the evening.
There is about an hour of free time before dinner.
Between now and dinner, should I spend time in my room, or---

entries.japanese:
―――居間に行けば誰かいるだろう。
　一人でいるよりは大勢でいたほうが楽しいにきまっている。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Someone was bound to be in the sitting room.
It was bound to be more fun with everyone than sitting alone.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---If I go to the sitting room, there should be someone there.
Being with company is surely more pleasant than being alone.

entries.japanese:
居間に入ると琥珀さんの姿があった。
「あら志貴さん。
どうしたんです、夕食まではまだ時間がありますよ」
「いや、食事にきたんじゃなくてくつろぎにきたんだ。
お邪魔するけど、いいかな」
「はい、どうぞごゆっくり。
えっと、それじゃ……」
entries.maoEnglish:
When I entered the sitting room, I found Kohaku there.
“Oh, Master Shiki, what brings you here? Dinner is still a while away.”
“I didn’t come to eat, just to relax. Mind if I stay?”
“Of course, make yourself comfortable. Now, let me see…”
entries.mirrorMoon:
I enter the sitting room and see Kohaku-san.
"Ah, Shiki-san.
What can I do for you?
Supper isn't for another hour."
"No, I came here to relax, not for a meal.
I hope I'm not intruding?"
"Oh, no, please come in.
Let's see…"

entries.japanese:
「姉さん、離れの屋敷の事ですけど―――」
「やっ。
お邪魔してるよ、翡翠」
「――はい。
お帰りなさいませ、志貴さま。
お出迎えができず、申し訳ありませんでした」
「いいって、そんなこと気にしなくて。
こっちこそ帰ってきたのに声をかけなくてごめんな」
「―――――――」
　翡翠はかすかに頬を赤くする。
　翡翠の感情表現が少しだけわかるようになってきて、嬉しい。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hisui, about the annex―――”
“Hey, Hisui. I’m making myself at home.”
“――Yes. Welcome home, Master Shiki. Forgive me for not being here to greet you.”
“Don’t worry about that. I’m the one who should apologize for coming home without letting you know.”
“―――――――”
Hisui’s cheeks colored faintly.
I was beginning to understand those tiny displays of feeling, and it made me happy.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Nee-san, about the detached building…"
"Hi.
Sorry to intrude, Hisui."
"…… Welcome home, Shiki-sama.
I am sorry I was not able to welcome you home."
"It's okay, don't worry about it.
I'm sorry for not saying hi as soon as I got back."
"-------"
Hisui's cheeks become faintly red.
Little by little, I'm coaxing expressions out of her.
I'm pleased.

entries.japanese:
「ちょうどよかった。
翡翠ちゃん、志貴さんにお飲み物を用意してくれる？」
「はい。
志貴さま、何を飲まれますか」
「そうだね、ごはんの前だからお茶だけでいいよ。
ただみんなと話をしにきただけだから、あんまりお構いなく」
「はい、かしこまりました」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Perfect timing. Hisui, would you bring Master Shiki something to drink?”
“Certainly. What would you care for, Master Shiki?”
“Just tea, I think. Dinner’s soon, and I only came to talk with everyone, so please don’t go to any trouble.”
“Very well.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Excellent timing.
Hisui-chan, would you prepare a drink for Shiki-san?"
"Yes.
Shiki-sama, what would you like to drink?"
"Hm.
Since it's before dinner, I guess just tea would be great.
I only came down to chat, so I don't want to be any trouble."
"Please wait a moment, then."

entries.japanese:
翡翠が三人分のお茶を持ってきて、なんとなく会話がないままのまったりとした時間がすぎる。
「ああ、そういえば翡翠。
さっき離れの屋敷がどうしたって言ってなかった？」
「はい、口にしましたがそれがなにか？」
「んー、別にどうこうってワケじゃないんだけど、あそこには入るなって秋葉にきつく言われたから。
もしかして俺がいない間に、あそこで事故でも起きたのかなって」
entries.maoEnglish:
Hisui brought tea for the three of us, and a pleasantly lazy silence settled over the room.
“That reminds me, Hisui. Weren’t you saying something about the annex earlier?”
“I did; is there some concern?”
“Not really. Akiha gave me strict orders not to go inside, so I wondered if there had been an accident there while I was away.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
Hisui returns with three teacups, and time passes by slowly and silently.
"Ah, by the way, Hisui, you were talking about the detached house earlier?"
"Yes.
Did you have a question about it?"
"Mm, not particularly, but Akiha was saying no one can go there anymore.
Did something happen there while I was gone, by any chance?"

entries.japanese:
「いえ、そんな事はありませんよ。
あそこは使用人用にあてがわれた屋敷ですから、志貴さんが足を運ぶ必要がないだけですね」
「使用人用の屋敷……？」
「はい。
今はわたしと翡翠ちゃんしかいませんけど、ちょっと前までは十人以上の使用人がお屋敷で働かせていただいてましたから。
お屋敷のお部屋もそう多くはありませんから、使用人用にと建てられたのが離れのお屋敷なんです」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Nothing of the kind. The annex was allotted to the servants, so there is simply no reason for Master Shiki to visit it.”
“The servants lived there?”
“Yes. Hisui and I are the only ones left now, but until fairly recently more than ten servants worked here. The main house could not accommodate everyone, so the annex was built as servants’ quarters.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No, nothing like that.
It merely houses servants' quarters, so there's no reason for you to go there, Shiki-san."
"Servant's quarters……?"
"Yes.
Although it's only me and Hisui-chan now, a little while ago there were more than ten servants working in the mansion.
Since there isn't room for so many people in the mansion, the detached building was built."

entries.japanese:
「姉さん―――その話は、してはいけないと」
「あ」
　翡翠に言われて、琥珀さんはきょろきょろとあたりを見渡す。
　……幸い秋葉の姿はなく、琥珀さんはホッと息をついた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Sister―――we were told not to discuss that.”
“Oh.”
At Hisui’s warning, Kohaku glanced anxiously around the room.
Fortunately Akiha was nowhere in sight, and Kohaku breathed a sigh of relief.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Nee-san---you must not speak about this."
"Ah."
Hisui says this, and Kohaku-san looks around guiltily.
…… There is no sign of Akiha.
Kohaku-san lets out a sigh of relief.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さん！」
「あ、はい、なんでしょう」
「………今のお話は、ないしょです」
　琥珀さんはぐっ、とこっちの手を握ってくる。
「あ、うん―――秋葉には言わないよ」
「はい、ありがとうございます」
　ほう、と胸を撫で下ろす琥珀さん。
　よっぽど秋葉に離れの屋敷の話は禁じられていたのだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki!”
“Y-Yes?”
“What I just told you is a secret.”
Kohaku seized my hand tightly.
“Yes―――I won’t tell Akiha.”
“Thank you.”
Kohaku pressed a hand to her chest in relief.
Akiha must have forbidden the subject of the annex in the strongest possible terms.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-san!"
"Ah… Yes, what is it…?"
"…… Our talk just now is a secret!"
Kohaku-san grips my hand hard.
"Ah, yeah---I won't tell Akiha about it."
"Yes, thank you."
Kohaku-san sighs with relief once more.
It seems like Akiha forbids talking about the detached building.

entries.japanese:
――――けど、なんでだろう。
　使用人たちの家だったという離れの屋敷。
　そこへ立ち入る事を嫌う秋葉。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――But why?
The annex had once housed the servants.
And Akiha hated the thought of me entering it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----But, why?
The detached building that used to be the servants' quarters.
Akiha doesn't want people to go there.

entries.japanese:
「……ねえ琥珀さん。
あの離れはいつから使用されなくなったんだ？」
「えっと……ね、翡翠ちゃん？」
「………………」
　翡翠は無言で首を横にふる。
　どうやらそれさえも『話してはいけないこと』であるらしい。
「なんで？
　それって秘密にするほどのことなのか？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Kohaku. When did they stop using the annex?”
“Well, Hisui?”
“……”
Hisui silently shook her head.
Apparently even that was forbidden territory.
“Why? Is it really something you have to keep secret?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hey, Kohaku-san.
How long has the detached building been unused?"
"Uhhh… Hisui-chan?"
"…………"
Hisui silently shakes her head.
It seems that even this cannot be spoken of.
"What?
Is it a secret?"

entries.japanese:
「―――はい。
あの離れに関するお話は、志貴さまのお体によい影響を与えません」
　そうきっぱりと返答されて、離れの屋敷の話はそれきりになってしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――Yes. Discussing the annex would be detrimental to your health, Master Shiki.”
Her answer was so final that the subject died there.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Yes.
Talking about the detached building would be bad for your health, Shiki-sama."
And with that final response, talk of the detached building ceases.

entries.japanese:
……どうも、さっきの秋葉の言いぶりが気にかかる。
　離れの屋敷には絶対に入るな、と秋葉は言った。
　そう言われると余計気になるし、第一―――この屋敷に和室がそこにしかないというのなら、行ってみたいという気もする。
「……見付からなければオッケーだよな」
　心の中で秋葉に謝って、そろそろと忍び足で出口に向かう事にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
Something about Akiha’s warning still bothered me.
She had told me never, under any circumstances, to enter the annex.
That only made me more curious, and besides―――if it contained the mansion’s only Japanese-style rooms, I wanted to see them.
“If nobody catches me, it should be fine.”
After apologizing silently to Akiha, I crept toward the exit.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… It's bugging me how Akiha said that.
She said not to enter the detached building under any circumstances.
The way she said it gets me more curious.
Besides-----if a Japanese-style room is only located there, I do feel like I want to take a look at it.
"…… I guess it's alright if I don't get caught."
I silently apologize to Akiha and decide to walk to the exit quietly.

entries.japanese:
―――すっかり日が沈んで、あたりは真夜中のように暗い。
　林というよりもはや森に近い庭を歩いていく。
　……いまいちどこにあるのか覚えてなかったけど、森に入るなり足がかってに離れの屋敷を目指し出した。
　頭のほうで忘れかけていても、体が覚えていたということだろうか。
　ともかく、少しも迷わずに離れの屋敷に到着できた。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――The sun had set completely, leaving the grounds dark as midnight.
I walked through a garden so densely wooded it was almost a forest.
I barely remembered where the annex stood, yet as soon as I entered the trees, my feet began carrying me toward it on their own.
Perhaps my body remembered what my mind had nearly forgotten.
In any case, I reached the annex without taking a single wrong turn.
entries.mirrorMoon:
------The sun has set and it is pitch black outside.
I walk through the woods which seem more like a forest.
…… I didn't remember quite where it was, but as I enter the forest, my feet automatically head toward the detached building.
Even if I forgot where it was, I guess my body remembers how to get there.
At any rate, I am able to get to the detached building without getting lost.

entries.japanese:
「―――――――」
　使われなくなってどれほどの年月が経っているのか、離れの屋敷はところどころが老朽化している。
　玄関に手をかけると、鍵はかかっていなかった。
　中は当然のように暗い。
　畳や障子の匂いがして、まったく何も見えない闇だというのに安心できた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――――――”
However many years the annex had stood unused, parts of it had visibly fallen into decay.
The entrance was unlocked when I tried it.
Naturally, the interior was dark.
The smells of tatami and paper screens greeted me, and despite the absolute blackness, I felt at ease.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-------"
It must have been many years since this building was put out of use, as many parts are deteriorated.
As I put my hand on the door, I notice that it is unlocked.
It is dark inside, as expected.
I smell the tatami mats and the shoji, and somehow feel comfortable even though I can't see anything.

entries.japanese:
「―――――あ」
　その和室に入ったとたん、ぞくりと、背中が震えた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――――Ah”
The moment I entered the room, a shiver ran down my back.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-----Ah."
As I enter the Japanese-style room, a chill runs through my spine.

entries.japanese:
「―――――ここ、知ってる」
　子供のころ、本館のほうにはない和室が珍しくて遊びにきたんだろう。
「――――――」
　けど、ヘンだ。
　屋敷に帰ってきて、自分の部屋に案内された時に感じていた違和感と似たものを、肌が感じ取っている。
「……有間の家が和室だったからかな」
　なんだか、ずっとここで暮らしてきたような気がする。
　いや、それとも―――
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――――I know this place.”
As a child, I must have come here to play because the main house had no rooms like it.
“――――――”
But something was wrong.
My skin sensed the same strange dissonance I had felt when first shown to my bedroom after returning to the mansion.
“Maybe it’s because the Arima house had rooms like this.”
I felt as though I had lived here all my life.
Or perhaps―――
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----------I know this place."
I guess I came here as a kid since this japanese-style room was interesting.
"------------"
But it's weird.
I feel the same sense of incompatibility I had when I was first shown my room after I came back to this mansion.
"…… Maybe because the Arimas' house was Japanese-style."
I feel like I've lived here all my life.
Or maybe-----

entries.japanese: そういえば、昔
entries.maoEnglish: Come to think of it, long ago
entries.mirrorMoon: If I recall, in the past…

entries.japanese: 庭で遊んでいる時にいたのは、
entries.maoEnglish: When I played in the garden, there had been
entries.mirrorMoon: When we were playing in the yard…

entries.japanese: 自分と、秋葉、だけではなかったような、
entries.maoEnglish: Someone besides Akiha and me
entries.mirrorMoon: Maybe it wasn't just me and Akiha.

entries.japanese:
「痛っ――――」
　ズキリ、と首筋が痛んだ。
　貧血の前触れか、体も鉛のように重く感じる。
「……まずいな……部屋に戻らないと」
　頭を軽くふって、本当に倒れてしまう前に部屋に戻ることにした時。
「あら、志貴さんじゃないですか。
何をしているんですか、こんなところで」
　いきなり、琥珀さんが入ってきた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ow――――”
Pain stabbed through the back of my neck.
Perhaps anemia was coming on; my body felt heavy as lead.
“This is bad; I need to get back to my room.”
I shook my head and was about to leave before I collapsed for real.
“Why, Master Shiki. What are you doing in a place like this?”
Kohaku suddenly walked in.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ouch------"
I feel a pain in my neck.
It might be my anemia, but my body feels like lead.
"…… This is bad…… I have to go back to my room."
I shake my head lightly, and I decide to go back to my room before I really faint.
"Oh hello, Shiki-san.
What are you doing at a place like this?"
Kohaku-san suddenly enters the room.

entries.japanese:
「―――――っ！」
　ど、どうしようとあたりを見渡す。
　……隠れる場所なんてないし、そもそもとっくに見付かってしまっているじゃないか、俺。
「もう、ダメですよココに入っちゃ。
秋葉さまから志貴さんだけはここに入れてはいけないって言われてるんですから」
「……ああ、今日言われた。
言われたんだけど、その―――」
「気になってしまったんですね。
わかりました、今回だけは大目に見ますから、今後はココには来ないでください。
この屋敷、もともと古いものですからちょっと危ないんです」
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――――!”
I frantically looked around for some escape.
There was nowhere to hide, and she had already found me in any case.
“You know you aren’t allowed in here. Miss Akiha gave us strict instructions that Master Shiki, in particular, must never enter.”
“I know. She told me today, but, well―――”
“You couldn’t help being curious, could you? Very well, I’ll overlook it this once, but please don’t come here again. This building is quite old, and parts of it are dangerous.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----------!!!"
I look around to see what I can do.
…… There's no place to hide.
Besides, she's already seen me.
"Hey now, you can't come in here.
Akiha-sama told us never to let you in here."
"…… Yeah, she told me today.
She told me but-----"
"You got curious?
I understand.
I'll let you go this time, but please don't come here again.
This building is old and a bit dangerous."

entries.japanese:
……もともと古い建物だから危ない、か。
　なんかヘンな理由だけど、一応スジは通っている。
「……ごめん。
けど琥珀さん、ここっていったい何に使ってた建物なんだ？
　今は使ってないっていうけど、昔は使ってたのか？」
「ええ、ここはもともと使用人の住居だったんです。
志貴さんが有間の家に預けられる前まで、屋敷には十数人の使用人がおりました。
　それだけの数の人間をお屋敷のほうに住まわせる事はできなかったので、槙久さまがこの離れをお作りになられたんです」
「そう。
使用人の住居だったのか」
entries.maoEnglish:
The building was old and therefore dangerous.
It sounded odd, but it made a certain amount of sense.
“Sorry. But Kohaku, what was this building used for? Everyone says it’s abandoned now, so it must have been used for something before.”
“It was originally the servants’ residence. Until you were sent to live with the Arima family, more than a dozen servants worked at the mansion.
There was no room for so many people in the main house, so Master Makihisa had this annex built.”
“I see. So it was servants’ quarters.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… This building is old and a bit dangerous, huh.
It's a weird reason but, it still makes sense.
"…… I'm sorry.
But what was this building used for?
You say it's not used now but did someone use it before?"
"Yes, this used to be the servants' residence.
Before you went to the Arimas, this mansion had many servants.
It was impossible to let all the servants live in the mansion, so Makihisa-sama constructed this detached building."
"I see, this place was the servants' residence."

entries.japanese:
言われてみれば納得できる。
　たしかにこれほどの大屋敷になるとそれぐらいのものは必要になってくるだろう。
　だけど、どうして。
　秋葉は俺をここに入らせないようにしているんだろう―――？
entries.maoEnglish:
Once she explained it, the arrangement seemed obvious.
An estate this large would naturally have needed something of the sort.
But why.
Why was Akiha so determined to keep me out―――?
entries.mirrorMoon:
It does make sense now that she mentions it.
If you have a mansion this big, such a thing would be certainly needed.
But, why?
Why is Akiha trying to get me away from this place------?

entries.japanese:
「志貴さん、そろそろお屋敷のほうに戻らないと秋葉さまに気付かれてしまいます」
「あ―――そうだね、悪かった」
　かすかな疑問を振り払って、琥珀さんと一緒に屋敷に戻る事にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki, we should return to the main house before Miss Akiha notices.”
“Ah―――right, sorry.”
I pushed the faint misgiving aside and went back with Kohaku.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-san, we should go back to the mansion or Akiha-sama might find out."
"Oh-----I'm sorry."
I shake off the faint doubt remaining and decide to go back to the mansion with Kohaku-san.

entries.japanese: まあ、これといってやる事もないし部屋でゆっくりしていよう。
entries.maoEnglish: Well, there was nothing in particular I needed to do, so I might as well relax in my room.
entries.mirrorMoon: Well, I don't exactly have anything in particular to do, so I'll just take it easy in my room.

entries.japanese:
夕食はいつもどおり、俺と秋葉だけの静かなものだった。
　琥珀さんは秋葉の後ろに、翡翠は俺の後ろに立って、一言も話さないというお決まりのディナー。
entries.maoEnglish:
Dinner is the customary quiet affair shared by Akiha and me.
Kohaku stands behind her, Hisui behind me, and neither says a word—the same ritual every evening.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Dinner, as usual, is a quiet affair with just me and Akiha.
Kohaku-san stands behind Akiha, and Hisui stands behind me during our wordless dinner.

entries.japanese:
「……………」
　ただ、いつもと違って秋葉の様子はおかしかった。
　今までは俺が食器の音をたてるたびにじろりと睨んできたっていうのに、今日は秋葉本人もカチャカチャと耳障りな音をたてる。
　しまいには、
「―――部屋に戻ります。
夕食はさげてください」
　なんて言って、途中で食堂を後にしてしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
Tonight, however, Akiha is behaving strangely.
Ordinarily she glares whenever my cutlery makes the slightest noise, but now she herself keeps producing an irritating clatter.
Finally,
“―――I am returning to my room. Please clear my dinner.”
With that, she leaves the dining room halfway through the meal.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…………"
The only thing different is the way Akiha is acting.
Until now, whenever my tableware would make noise, Akiha would look up with a scowl.
Today, however, Akiha makes quite a lot of clattering herself.
In the end,
"---I am going back to my room.
Please clean up my dinner."
Saying so, she leaves the dining room behind.

entries.japanese:
「……どうしたんだろう、あいつ。
一緒に帰ってくる時まではあんなんじゃなかったのに」
「………………」
　翡翠は黙ったまま、何も言わない。
　琥珀さんはいつも通りに笑顔で食器を片付けている。
――――と。
　ロビーのほうから、何かが倒れる音がした。
「―――秋葉！？」
　ただそんな予感だけがして、ロビーへと駆け出した。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What’s gotten into her? She was fine when we walked home together.”
“…”
Hisui remains silent.
Kohaku clears the dishes with her usual smile.
――――Then.
Something crashes in the foyer.
“―――Akiha!?”
With nothing but a terrible premonition to guide me, I sprint toward the sound.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… What's with her?
She wasn't like that when we were walking back together…"
"…………"
Hisui says nothing.
Kohaku-san collects the tableware, smiling as ever.
----And then.
From the lobby, I hear the sound of someone falling.
"---Akiha!?"
Fearing the worst, I race towards the lobby.

entries.japanese:
「―――――！」
　そこには、階段にもたれかかった秋葉の姿があった。
　秋葉の呼吸は乱れていて、離れていてもぜいぜいという音が聞こえてくる。
　顔色は真っ青で、額や腕に玉のような汗が浮かんでいた。
　……その姿は、一目見ただけで尋常ではないと判る。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――――!”
Akiha is slumped against the staircase.
Her breathing is so ragged that I can hear her wheezing from across the foyer.
Her face is deathly pale, and beads of sweat stand out on her forehead and arms.
One glance is enough to tell me this is no ordinary illness.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-----!"
There, I see Akiha leaning on the stairs.
Her breathing is irregular, and I can hear her wheezing from here.
Her face is pale, and there are beads of sweat on her skin.
…… I can see with a single glance that she is not okay.

entries.japanese:
「おい、秋葉！」
「近寄らないで……！」
「っ！」
　足を止める。
　秋葉は、階段にもたれかかったままで、激しく俺を拒絶した。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Akiha!”
“Don’t come any closer…!”
“—!”
I stop.
Still propped against the stairs, Akiha rejects me with startling violence.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hey, Akiha!"
"Don't come near me…!"
"…!"
I stop.
Leaning on the stairs, Akiha refuses me violently.

entries.japanese:
「なっ―――近寄らないでって、なに言ってるんだよ。
何があったか知らないけど、そんな苦しそうなヤツを放っておけるわけないだろ」
「―――いいから、兄さんだけは、近寄らない、で」
　はあはあ、という声。
「な――――」
　どくん、と心臓が跳ねる。
　ただ、苦しげに息をはく秋葉の姿。
　……どうかしている。
　それが弓塚さつきの姿にひどく似ていると、一瞬だけでも思ってしまったなんて。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What―――do you mean, don’t come closer? I don’t know what happened, but I can’t abandon you when you’re suffering like this.”
“―――Please, Brother, just don’t come near me.”
Her breath rasps in and out.
“What――――”
My heart bucks.
Akiha stands there, breathing in torment.
I must be losing my mind.
How could I think, even for an instant, that she looked so much like Satsuki Yumizuka?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Wha---don't come near you…?
What are you talking about!?
I don't know what happened, but I can't just leave you like that!"
"---I'm fine, just… don't come any closer… Nii-san."
Akiha breathes heavily.
"Hey----"
My heart pounds.
Akiha just breathes painfully.
…… There's something wrong with me.
For a moment, I feel it resembles the figure of Yumizuka Satsuki.

entries.japanese:
「秋、葉―――」
「いいから来ないでくださいっ。
いま近くにこられたら、私はきっとダメになる。
……だから、こないで。
わたしは兄さんなんかいなくたって、大丈夫なんだから―――」
　ずるり、と。
　階段にもたれかかっていた秋葉の体が倒れこむ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Akiha―――”
“Please, just stay away! If you come near me now, I know I’ll lose control. So don’t. I don’t need you, Brother; I’ll be perfectly fine without you―――”
Akiha slips.
Her body falls away from the staircase and crumples.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Aki… ha---"
"I'm fine, so please, don't come near me.
If you come near me, there's no way I'll be able to… so don't come any closer.
As long as you are not around, I'll be fine, so…"
With an audible sound,
Akiha collapses once more.

entries.japanese:
「秋葉さま？」
　と、俺の横をすり抜けて琥珀さんが秋葉にかけよる。
　琥珀さんは秋葉と何やら小さな声で話し合うと、秋葉に肩をかして立ちあがらせた。
　そのまま、秋葉は琥珀さんに助けられて、自分の部屋へと戻って行ってしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Miss Akiha?”
Kohaku slips past me and rushes to her.
After exchanging a few quiet words with Akiha, Kohaku lends her a shoulder and helps her stand.
Supported by Kohaku, Akiha returns to her room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Akiha-sama?"
Kohaku-san passes me, running toward Akiha.
She whispers something to Akiha, and helps her up.
With Kohaku-san's help, Akiha returns to her room.

entries.japanese:
「な――――なんだよ、それ」
　わけがわからない。
　苦しそうな秋葉の容体といい、俺に近寄るなって言っておきながら、琥珀さんには安心して肩を貸してもらうなんて。
「―――志貴さま」
「翡翠……今のは、なんだ。
秋葉があんなになるなんて、どうして」
entries.maoEnglish:
“What――――was that?”
None of it makes sense.
Akiha is suffering, refuses to let me near, and then calmly accepts Kohaku’s support.
“―――Master Shiki”
“Hisui, what just happened? Why would Akiha become like that?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Wha----what was that about?"
I really don't understand.
Akiha's tormented condition, telling me not to come near her, yet she lets Kohaku-san help her.
"---Shiki-sama."
"Hisui… what was that?
Why was Akiha like that?"

entries.japanese:
「……はい。
秋葉さまは突発的な呼吸困難におちいる事があるのです。
志貴さまが貧血ぎみであるように、秋葉さまも、遠野家の人間ですから」
「あ――――」
―――遠野の人間にはそういった特色がありますから。
　昼休み、秋葉はたしかにそう言っていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Yes. Miss Akiha sometimes suffers sudden attacks that leave her unable to breathe. Just as Master Shiki is prone to anemia, Miss Akiha too belongs to the Tohno family.”
“Ah――――”
―――The Tohnos have certain inherited peculiarities.
Akiha had indeed said that at lunch.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"At times, Akiha-sama lapses into sudden dyspnea.
Just as with your anemia, Akiha-sama too is a member of the Tohno family."
"Ah----"
---Members of the Tohno family do have such conditions.
Akiha said that during lunch.

entries.japanese:
「……そんな。
けど、秋葉はいつも元気そうだったじゃないか」
「秋葉さまは志貴さまにはくれぐれも内密にするように、と気を配っておられましたから。
わたしたちも志貴さまには黙っているように命じられておりました」
「――――――――」
　言葉がない。
　俺は呆然と、秋葉が去っていった階段を見上げることしかできなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“But… Akiha always seemed so healthy.”
“Miss Akiha took great pains to keep the matter from Master Shiki. We were also ordered not to tell Master Shiki.”
“――――――――”
I have no answer.
All I can do is stare blankly up the staircase where Akiha disappeared.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"It can't be… Akiha always seems so healthy."
"Akiha-sama tried her best to keep it a secret from you.
We were also ordered not to speak to Shiki-sama about it."
"--------"
There's nothing to be said.
I can only look aghast up the stairs Akiha just ascended.

entries.japanese:
「それではおやすみなさいませ。
……秋葉さまのことでしたら、姉さんにまかせてあげてください。
　姉さんは何年も前から槙久さまのお体を任されていましたから、医学の心得もあるのです」
「そうだね。
秋葉も琥珀さんを信頼しきっているみたいだったし、琥珀さんに任せてあげて大丈夫だろう」
　……だいたい俺がついていても何もできないんだから、琥珀さんに任せるしかないだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Good night, then. Please entrust Miss Akiha to my sister.
For many years she was responsible for Master Makihisa’s health, and she has some medical training.”
“You’re right. Akiha seemed to trust Kohaku completely, so she should be safe in her hands.”
I could do nothing for her even if I stayed, so there is no choice but to rely on Kohaku.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Well then, good night.
Please leave Akiha-sama's condition to Nee-san.
As Makihisa-sama was under her care for many years, she has medical experience."
"I guess so.
If we leave Akiha to Kohaku-san, I'm sure she'll be fine."
…… Since there doesn't seem to be anything else I can do, it seems I'll have to just leave her to Kohaku-san.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま、秋葉さまがあのようなご容体になるのは稀なんです。
それも、きちんと薬で持ちなおせるものですから心配はいらないと思います。
　……秋葉さまは原因と治療方法が判っているご自分のことより、志貴さまのお体のほうを気にかけているのです」
「―――わかってる。
くそ、こんなんじゃ兄貴失格だな。
俺は本当に、何もわかってなかったみたいだ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki, attacks that severe are rare for Miss Akiha, and the proper medicine will restore her. I do not believe you need to worry.
Miss Akiha is more concerned about Master Shiki’s uncertain health than her own condition, whose cause and treatment she already knows.”
“I know. Damn it, I’m a failure as a brother. I really didn’t understand anything.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama, it is rare for Akiha-sama to be like that.
Since it can be easily relieved with medication, I do not think that you need to worry.
…… Rather than being concerned with her treatable condition, Akiha-sama is concerned more about your health, Shiki-sama."
"---I know.
Damn it, I'm a crappy older brother.
I guess I really didn't realize anything at all."

entries.japanese:
「何も―――わかっては、いないのですか」
　翡翠はうつむいて、そんな事を呟いた。
「……翡翠？
　どうしたんだ、まさかきみまで体調が悪いとか言わないでくれよ」
「―――いえ。
ただ、志貴さまは本当に、あの離れの屋敷を思い出せないのですか？」
「―――――え？」
　……思い出せないって、何、を。
「……翡翠、それって―――」
「―――志貴さまは、本当に遠野志貴になられてしまったのですね」
entries.maoEnglish:
“You―――truly understand nothing?”
Hisui lowers her head as she whispers it.
“Hisui? What’s wrong—don’t tell me you’re ill too.”
“―――No. But can Master Shiki truly remember nothing about the annex?”
“―――――What?”
Remember nothing about what?
“Hisui, that means―――”
“―――Master Shiki, you truly have become Shiki Tohno.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"You---do not know anything?"
Hisui murmurs to herself, looking down.
"Hisui?
What is it?
Don't say that even you feel bad."
"---No, it is just… Shiki-sama, do you really remember nothing about the detached building?"
"-----Eh?"
…… Remember… what?
"…… Hisui, that's…"
"---You really became Tohno Shiki, did you not, Shiki-sama?"

entries.japanese:
「翡翠？」
「……あの離れが使われなくなったのは、志貴さまが有間の家に預けられてすぐです。
槙久さまは取り壊すと決定されましたが、秋葉さまがひどく嫌がったのでああして今も残っているのです。
　―――ですから、志貴さまが本当に秋葉さまのことを思うのなら、あの離れに近づかないでください」
　言って、翡翠は走り去るように部屋から出ていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hisui?”
“The annex fell out of use soon after Master Shiki was sent to live with the Arima family. Master Makihisa decided to demolish it, but Miss Akiha protested so fiercely that it remains standing even now.
―――Therefore, if Master Shiki truly cares for Miss Akiha, please stay away from the annex.”
With that, Hisui hurries from the room as though fleeing.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hisui?"
"…… That detached building fell into disuse right after you left for the Arima family.
Makihisa-sama decided to demolish it, but as Akiha-sama objected strongly, it remains standing today.
---So, Shiki-sama, if you think anything at all of Akiha-sama, please do not approach that detached building."
Saying so, Hisui leaves the room as if she were running.

entries.japanese:
十時を過ぎて、屋敷じゅうの電気が消えた。
「………………」
　目が冴えて眠れない。
　秋葉のこと。
　秋葉が秘密にしたがっている離れの屋敷のこと。
entries.maoEnglish:
After ten, every light in the mansion goes out.
“…”
I am too wide awake to sleep.
Akiha.
The annex she is so desperate to keep secret.
entries.mirrorMoon:
It's ten o'clock, and all the mansions lights go off.
"…………"
I can't sleep.
Akiha.
The detached building she wants to keep a secret from me.

entries.japanese:
―――って、ちょっと待った。
　翡翠の言葉は気になるけど、離れならさっき行ったじゃないか。
　あそこには何もないってわかっている。
　今夜はこのまま、大人しく眠る事にしよう。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Wait a moment.
Hisui’s words bothered me, but I had already visited the annex earlier.
I knew there was nothing there.
I would behave myself and go to sleep.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---But, hold on.
Hisui's words bother me, but I went to the detached house earlier.
I know there's nothing there.
I'll keep quiet tonight and sleep.

entries.japanese: ――――喉が、カラカラに渇いて、熱い。
entries.maoEnglish: ――――My throat is parched dry and burning hot.
entries.mirrorMoon: ----My throat, dry with thirst, hot.

entries.japanese:
――――――このままでは眠れない。
　　　　　　起きて、水を飲みに行こう。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――――I can’t sleep like this.
I should get up and find some water.
entries.mirrorMoon:
------I can't sleep like this.
I'll go and get a drink of water.

entries.japanese:
夜の街に出たようだ。
　目を血走らせて誰か通りかからないか待っているのか。
entries.maoEnglish:
It seems someone has gone out into the city at night.
Eyes bloodshot, they wait for someone—anyone—to pass.
entries.mirrorMoon:
It seems I went into town at night.
It seems like I'm waiting with bloodshot eyes for someone to pass by.

entries.maoEnglish: ――――――Everything burned.
entries.mirrorMoon: ------It is hot.

entries.japanese:
ふと、窓ガラスに映った顔が見えた。
　目は血走っていて、とても正気には見えなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
A face appeared suddenly in a pane of glass.
Its bloodshot eyes looked anything but sane.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Suddenly, I see a face reflected in the window.
The eyes are bloodshot, and the face looks quite insane.

entries.japanese: ――――――ただ、熱かった。
entries.maoEnglish: ――――――There was nothing but the heat.
entries.mirrorMoon: ------It is just so hot.

entries.japanese:
獲物を見つけたようだ。
　背後から首をしめて、それで終わり。
　見知らぬ女性はそれで死んでしまったみたいだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
A victim, found.
A chokehold from behind, and it was over.
A woman I’d never seen before seemed to die just like that.
entries.mirrorMoon:
It seems I found my prey.
Strangling her from behind, it's all over.
It seems that the unknown woman has died just from that.

entries.japanese: ―――俺は、ただ、熱かった。
entries.maoEnglish: ―――I was only burning hot.
entries.mirrorMoon: ---I am just, so hot.

entries.japanese:
死体を連れこんで、喉元に食らいついたのか。
　じゅるじゅる、という音が聞こえる。
　喉もとから、肉ごとかみ切るように血を飲んで、喉の渇きを癒している。
entries.maoEnglish:
The corpse must have been dragged somewhere, then bitten at the throat.
Wet, sucking sounds.
Blood gulped down from the neck, teeth shearing through flesh along with it, slaking that terrible thirst.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Taking the dead body, perhaps I bit into its throat.
There's a gurgling sound.
Drinking the blood flowing out of the rended neck, my thirst is quenched.

entries.japanese: ―――わからない。
entries.maoEnglish: ―――I don’t understand.
entries.mirrorMoon: ---I don't understand.

entries.japanese:
はあはあという呼吸音。
　よほど。
　よほどその行為は興奮するのか。
　死体の胸に指をつきいれた。
　肉を潰していく音、骨を崩していく音。
　心臓を素手でえぐりだす、音。
entries.maoEnglish:
Panting.
So much.
Was the act truly that exciting?
Fingers plunged into the corpse’s chest.
The sound of flesh pulping, the sound of bones breaking.
The sound of a heart being torn out with bare hands.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The sound of heavy breathing.
Does this act…
Does this act really excite me so much?
I stick my finger in the chest of the dead body.
The sound of crushing meat, the sound of breaking bones.
The sound of a heart being ripped out with my bare hand.

entries.japanese: ―――見ているだけで、頭が真っ白になる。
entries.maoEnglish: ―――The mere sight of it wipes my mind clean.
entries.mirrorMoon: ---As I watch, my head fills with pure white.

entries.japanese:
その、究極の略奪。
　頂点に位置する背徳性。
　それが、見ているものさえ熱くさせる。
　たとえそれがマイナスの快楽にしたって、熱くなるということには、かわりはないらしい。
entries.maoEnglish:
The ultimate act of plunder.
Transgression at its absolute height.
It sets even the watcher burning.
Pleasure with a minus sign before it is still pleasure enough to burn.
entries.mirrorMoon:
This, the ultimate pillage.
The height of immorality.
Just gazing at it, I feel hot.
You might say it's negative pleasure, but for making one hot, it's still the same.

entries.japanese: ―――俺には、わからない。
entries.maoEnglish: ―――I don’t understand it.
entries.mirrorMoon: ---I don't understand.

entries.japanese:
熱い血液を口からたらして、恍惚とした目で、夜空を見上げていた。
　長い髪が乱れる。
　頭上には螺旋の空。
　なんてキレイな、銀色の月。
entries.maoEnglish:
Hot blood trailed from the mouth as ecstatic eyes lifted to the night sky.
Long hair streamed wild.
Above, the heavens spiraled.
What a beautiful silver moon.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Hot blood dripping from my mouth, I gaze up at the night sky entranced.
My long hair waves around.
Above is the spiraling sky.
Such a beautiful, silver moon.

entries.japanese:
―――だから、わからない。
　　　俺は、ただ、熱かっただけなのに――――
entries.maoEnglish:
―――That’s why I don’t understand.
I was only burning hot, and yet――――
entries.mirrorMoon:
---And so, I don't understand.
I am just, only, hot----

entries.japanese:
「……行ってみるか」
　ベッドから出て、足音を立てないように部屋を後にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’ll go and see”
I slipped out of bed and left the room without making a sound.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Shall I take a look?"
Getting out of bed, I leave my room silently.

entries.japanese:
―――庭の林には月光さえ届かない。
　林というよりもはや森に近い庭を歩いていく。
　……いまいちどこにあるのか覚えてなかったけど、森に入るなり足がかってに離れの屋敷を目指し出した。
　頭のほうで忘れかけていても、体が覚えていたということだろうか。
　ともかく、少しも迷わずに離れの屋敷に到着できた。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Not even moonlight reached the trees in the garden.
I walked through a garden so overgrown that it was closer to a forest.
I could not clearly remember where the annex stood, yet the moment I entered the trees, my feet began carrying me toward it on their own.
Perhaps my body remembered what my mind had almost forgotten.
Whatever the reason, I reached the annex without losing my way once.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----Even the moonlight does not penetrate the woods of the garden.
I walk through the woods which seem more like a forest.
…… I didn't remember quite where it was, but as I enter the forest, my feet automatically head toward the detached building.
Even if I forgot where it was, I guess my body remembers how to get there.
At any rate, I am able to get to the detached building without getting lost.

entries.japanese:
「―――――――」
　使われなくなってどれほどの年月が経っているのか、離れの屋敷は所々が老朽化している。
　玄関に手をかけると、鍵はかかっていなかった。
　中は当然のように暗い。
　畳や障子の匂いがして、まったく何も見えない闇だというのに安心できた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――――――”
However many years had passed since it fell out of use, the annex had begun to decay here and there.
When I tried the front door, I found it unlocked.
Naturally, the interior was dark.
The smells of tatami and paper screens greeted me, and despite the absolute blackness, I felt at ease.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-------"
It must have been many years since this building was put out of use, as many parts are deteriorated.
As I put my hand on the door, I notice that it is unlocked.
It is dark inside, as expected.
I smell the tatami mats and the shoji, and somehow feel comfortable even though I can't see anything.

entries.japanese:
「―――――あ」
　その和室に入ったとたん、ぞくりと、背中が震えた。
「―――――ここ、知ってる」
　子供のころ、本館のほうにはない和室が珍しくて遊びにきたのだろうか。
「――――――」
　けど、ヘンだ。
　屋敷に帰ってきて、自分の部屋に案内された時に感じていた違和感と似たものを、肌が感じ取っている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――――Ah”
The instant I entered the Japanese-style room, a chill ran down my spine.
“―――――I know this place”
Perhaps, as a child, I had come to play here because the main house had no rooms like this one.
“――――――――”
But something was wrong.
My skin sensed the same dissonance I had felt when I returned to the mansion and was shown to my room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-----Ah."
As I enter the Japanese-style room, a chill runs through my spine.

entries.japanese:
「……有間の家が和室だったからかな」
　なんだか、ずっとここで暮らしてきたような気がする。
　いや、それとも―――
entries.maoEnglish:
“Maybe it’s because the Arima house had rooms like this.”
I felt as though I had lived here all my life.
Or perhaps―――
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----------I know this place."
I guess I came here as a kid since this Japanese-style room was interesting.
"------------"
But it's weird.
I feel the same sense of incompatibility I had when I was first shown my room after I came back to this mansion.

entries.japanese: そういえば、昔
entries.maoEnglish: Come to think of it, long ago—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Maybe because the Arimas' house was Japanese-style."
I feel like I've lived here all my life.
Or maybe-----

entries.japanese: 庭で遊んでいる時にいたのは、
entries.maoEnglish: when I played in the garden, I don’t think—
entries.mirrorMoon: If I recall, in the past…

entries.japanese: 自分と、秋葉、だけではなかったような、
entries.maoEnglish: Akiha and I were the only ones there—
entries.mirrorMoon: When we were playing in the yard,

entries.japanese:
「痛っ――――」
　ズキリ、と首筋が痛んだ。
　貧血の前触れか、体も鉛のように重く感じる。
「……まずいな……部屋に戻らないと」
　頭を軽くふって、本当に倒れてしまう前に部屋に戻ることにした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ow――――”
Pain stabbed through the side of my neck.
Perhaps it heralded another fainting spell; my limbs felt heavy as lead.
“This is bad, I need to get back to my room”
I shook my head and started for my room before I could actually collapse.
entries.mirrorMoon: maybe it wasn't just me and Akiha…

entries.japanese:
「は――――あ」
　なんとか部屋に戻ってこれた。
　いくらなんでも、立ち入り禁止のあの離れで倒れてしまったら、秋葉のかみなりが落ちてしまう。
「――――ん」
　くらり、と眩暈がする。
　そのまま、着替えもせずにベッドに倒れこんだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hah――――ah”
Somehow, I made it back.
If I collapsed in the annex after being forbidden to enter it, Akiha’s wrath would be terrifying.
“――――Nn”
The room tilted.
Without even changing my clothes, I fell onto the bed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ouch------"
I feel a pain in my neck.
It might be my anemia, but my body feels like lead.
"…… This is bad…… I have to go back to my room."
I shake my head lightly, and I decide to go back to my room before I really faint.
I take a deep breath.
Somehow, I made it back to my room.
No matter what, if I collapsed in the off-limits building, Akiha's wrath would pour down on me.
"------Mn."
I feel a little dizzy.
I fall onto my bed without even changing.

entries.japanese: ――――喉が、カラカラに渇いて、熱い。
entries.maoEnglish: ――――My throat is parched dry and burning hot.
entries.mirrorMoon: ----My throat, dry with thirst, hot.

entries.japanese:
――――――このままでは眠れない。
　　　　　　起きて、水を飲みに行こう。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――――I can’t sleep like this.
I should get up and find some water.
entries.mirrorMoon:
------I can't sleep like this.
I'll go and get a drink of water.

entries.japanese:
夜の街に出たようだ。
　目を血走らせて誰か通りかからないか待っているのか。
entries.maoEnglish:
It seems someone has gone out into the city at night.
Eyes bloodshot, they wait for someone—anyone—to pass.
entries.mirrorMoon:
It seems I went into town at night.
It seems like I'm waiting with bloodshot eyes for someone to pass by.

entries.maoEnglish: ――――――Everything burned.
entries.mirrorMoon: ------It is hot.

entries.japanese:
ふと、窓ガラスに映った顔が見えた。
　目は血走っていて、とても正気には見えなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
A face appeared suddenly in a pane of glass.
Its bloodshot eyes looked anything but sane.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Suddenly, I see a face reflected in the window.
The eyes are bloodshot, and the face looks quite insane.

entries.japanese: ――――――ただ、熱かった。
entries.maoEnglish: ――――――There was nothing but the heat.
entries.mirrorMoon: ------It is just so hot.

entries.japanese:
獲物を見つけたようだ。
　背後から首をしめて、それで終わり。
　見知らぬ女性はそれで死んでしまったみたいだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
A victim, found.
A chokehold from behind, and it was over.
A woman I’d never seen before seemed to die just like that.
entries.mirrorMoon:
It seems I found my prey.
Strangling her from behind, it's all over.
It seems that the unknown woman has died just from that.

entries.japanese: ―――俺は、ただ、熱かった。
entries.maoEnglish: ―――I was only burning hot.
entries.mirrorMoon: ---I am just, so hot.

entries.japanese:
死体を連れこんで、喉元に食らいついたのか。
　じゅるじゅる、という音が聞こえる。
　喉もとから、肉ごとかみ切るように血を飲んで、喉の渇きを癒している。
entries.maoEnglish:
The corpse must have been dragged somewhere, then bitten at the throat.
Wet, sucking sounds.
Blood gulped down from the neck, teeth shearing through flesh along with it, slaking that terrible thirst.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Taking the dead body, perhaps I bit into its throat.
There's a gurgling sound.
Drinking the blood flowing out of the rended neck, my thirst is quenched.

entries.japanese: ―――わからない。
entries.maoEnglish: ―――I don’t understand.
entries.mirrorMoon: ---I don't understand.

entries.japanese:
はあはあという呼吸音。
　よほど。
　よほどその行為は興奮するのか。
　死体の胸に指をつきいれた。
　肉を潰していく音、骨を崩していく音。
　心臓を素手でえぐりだす、音。
entries.maoEnglish:
Panting.
So much.
Was the act truly that exciting?
Fingers plunged into the corpse’s chest.
The sound of flesh pulping, the sound of bones breaking.
The sound of a heart being torn out with bare hands.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The sound of heavy breathing.
Does this act…
Does this act really excite me so much?
I stick my finger in the chest of the dead body.
The sound of crushing meat, the sound of breaking bones.
The sound of a heart being ripped out with my bare hand.

entries.japanese: ―――見ているだけで、頭が真っ白になる。
entries.maoEnglish: ―――The mere sight of it wipes my mind clean.
entries.mirrorMoon: ---As I watch, my head fills with pure white.

entries.japanese:
その、究極の略奪。
　頂点に位置する背徳性。
　それが、見ているものさえ熱くさせる。
　たとえそれがマイナスの快楽にしたって、熱くなるということには、かわりはないらしい。
entries.maoEnglish:
The ultimate act of plunder.
Transgression at its absolute height.
It sets even the watcher burning.
Pleasure with a minus sign before it is still pleasure enough to burn.
entries.mirrorMoon:
This, the ultimate pillage.
The height of immorality.
Just gazing at it, I feel hot.
You might say it's negative pleasure, but for making one hot, it's still the same.

entries.japanese: ―――俺には、わからない。
entries.maoEnglish: ―――I don’t understand it.
entries.mirrorMoon: ---I don't understand.

entries.japanese:
熱い血液を口からたらして、恍惚とした目で、夜空を見上げていた。
　長い髪が乱れる。
　頭上には螺旋の空。
　なんてキレイな、銀色の月。
entries.maoEnglish:
Hot blood trailed from the mouth as ecstatic eyes lifted to the night sky.
Long hair streamed wild.
Above, the heavens spiraled.
What a beautiful silver moon.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Hot blood dripping from my mouth, I gaze up at the night sky entranced.
My long hair waves around.
Above is the spiraling sky.
Such a beautiful, silver moon.

entries.japanese:
―――だから、わからない。
　　　俺は、ただ、熱かっただけなのに――――
entries.maoEnglish:
―――That’s why I don’t understand.
I was only burning hot, and yet――――
entries.mirrorMoon:
---And so, I don't understand.
I am just, only, hot----

entries.japanese:
……いや、秋葉との約束を守ろう。
　秋葉が行くなっていうんだから、些細な好奇心で約束を破るわけにはいかない。
「……ん」
　ゆったりとした眠気が体に浸透していく。
　今夜はこのまま、大人しく眠る事にしよう。
entries.maoEnglish:
No, I would keep my promise to Akiha.
Akiha had told me not to go, so I could not break my word over idle curiosity.
“Nn.”
A gentle drowsiness seeped through my body.
I decided to behave myself and go to sleep.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… no, I'll keep my promise with Akiha.
Akiha told me not to go there, and I can't break a promise just because of trifling curiosity.
"…… Nn."
A calm drowsiness permeates my body.
I'll keep quiet tonight and sleep.

entries.mirrorMoon:
---And so, I don't understand.
I am just, only, hot----

entries.japanese:
「――――――！」
　たまらず、ベッドから跳ね起きた。
「はあ―――はあ、はあ――――」
　口元に込み上げる吐き気を手の平で押さえて、はあはあと呼吸を整える。
「な――――――」
　なんだ、今のは。
　夢。
夢を見てた。
けど、今のはなんだ。
　あんな酷い、人を殺して血を吸う夢を見るなんて、どうかしてる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――――!”
I could bear it no longer and shot upright in bed.
“Hah―――hah, hah――――”
I clapped a hand over my mouth to contain the nausea and struggled to steady my breathing.
“Wh――――――”
What had that been?
A dream. I had been dreaming. But what kind of dream was that?
Dreaming of murdering someone and drinking their blood; something had to be wrong with me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…!"
Unable to take it, I leap out of bed.
I start to breathe heavily.
I press my hand over my mouth and resist the urge to throw up.
"Wh-----"
What, was that?
A dream.
It was a dream.
But, what was that?
Why did I have such a terrible dream, of killing people and drinking their blood?

entries.japanese:
「はあ……はあ……はあ」
　喉元の渇き。
　肉をかみきる感触。
　人を殺した時の、脳髄が焼き切れそうな快感。
　……それらの単語が、なんてリアルに思えるんだろう。
　音をたてて心臓をつかみ出した時の感触さえ、たしかに思い出せる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hah, hah, hah”
The thirst in my throat.
The feel of teeth severing flesh.
The pleasure of killing someone, fierce enough to sear my brain away.
How could those things feel so real?
I could even remember wrenching the heart free with that hideous sound.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I try and catch my breath.
The thirst in my throat.
The feeling of biting flesh.
The pleasure burning through my brain as I killed.
…… These things, why do they seem so real?
I can even remember perfectly the feel and sound of the heart as it was ripped out.

entries.japanese:
「は、あ――――――」
　あれが『快感』だったのかはてんでわからない。
　ただ、弾丸のように凝縮された興奮が、耳元からトリガーをひいて脳髄に叩き込まれたような衝撃だけがあった。
「ぐ―――っ」
　思い出しただけで息が止まる。
　なら―――あの衝撃は、やはり『快感』と呼べるものだったのかもしれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hah――――――”
I had no idea whether it truly deserved the name pleasure.
There had only been the impact of excitement compressed like a bullet, a trigger pulled beside my ear and the charge fired straight into my brain.
“Gh―――!”
The memory alone stopped my breath.
Then―――perhaps that impact really could be called pleasure after all.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I continue to gasp hungrily for air.
I don't know if it was really "pleasure".
It was just excitement condensed like a bullet, fired straight into my head.
"Guh…"
My breath stops as I remember.
Then---perhaps that impact could be something called "pleasure".

entries.japanese:
「俺は―――なんて、夢を」
　自らの両手を見る。
　当然、自分の手は真っ白で血の赤色なんて微塵もない。
　俺はベッドで眠っていて、窓からはさわやかな朝の陽射しが差し込んできている。
　……あの時。
吸血鬼になってしまった弓塚と初めて出会った路地裏の光景が、まだ脳裏に残っているのか。
　だからあんな、凄惨な夢を見てしまうんだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What kind of―――dream was that?”
I looked down at my hands.
Naturally they were clean and white, without the faintest trace of blood.
I had been asleep in my bed, and fresh morning sunlight streamed through the window.
…Perhaps the alley where I first encountered Yumizuka after she became a vampire was still branded into my mind.
That must have been why I dreamed something so atrocious.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Why did I… that kind of dream…"
I look down at my hands.
Of course, they are pure white, without a trace of red blood on them.
I am sleeping on the bed, and fresh morning sunlight shines in through the window.
…… That time.
That first meeting with the vampire Yumizuka in a back alley… is it still in my mind?
Maybe that's why I had such a ghastly dream.

entries.japanese:
「いた――――」
　ズキリ、と弓塚にかまれた首筋が痛む。
―――吸血鬼にかまれた者は、同じように吸血鬼になる。
　そんな有名すぎる俗説を、無闇にも思い出してしまった。
「……まさか。
考えすぎだ、そんなの」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ow――――”
The place on my neck where Yumizuka had bitten me throbbed with pain.
―――Anyone bitten by a vampire will become a vampire in turn.
The most hackneyed superstition imaginable rose unbidden into my mind.
“No way. I’m overthinking it.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ow----"
My neck hurts where Yumizuka bit it.
---Those who are bitten by a vampire become vampires as well.
Unexpectedly, that common phrase pops into my head.
"…… Can't be.
I'm overthinking this."

entries.japanese:
失礼します、と翡翠が部屋に入ってくる。
　いつも通りの姿で、いつも通りの声をして。
「おはようございます、志貴さま」
　丁寧な翡翠の口調。
　いつからか、翡翠がやってくれば平穏な朝を迎えられるような、そんな日課が出来上がっている。
　そう思えた途端、さっきまで頭に渦巻いていた悪い夢は簡単に掻き消えてくれた。
entries.maoEnglish:
Hisui entered, politely announcing herself as usual.
She looked and sounded exactly as she always did.
“Good morning, Master Shiki.”
Hisui’s unfailingly courteous voice.
Somehow, her arrival had become a ritual that assured me the morning would be peaceful.
The instant I realized that, the nightmare still churning through my mind simply dissolved.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Excusing herself, Hisui enters the room.
The same figure, the same voice as always.
"Good morning, Shiki-sama."
Hisui speaks politely.
Since I arrived here, Hisui has brought a calm tranquility with her every morning.
As I think this, the tumult of bad dreams simply fades from my head.

entries.japanese:
「……志貴さま？
　お体の具合がよろしくないのですか？」
「―――ああ、違う違う。
ちょっと見惚れていただけだって。
……うん、おはよう翡翠。
今朝もいつも通りだね」
「あ―――はい、変わり映えがなく申し訳ありません」
「そういう意味じゃないんだ。
ただ、翡翠がいつも通りだからさ。
今日もいつも通り穏やかな朝だなって、実感できた」
　よし、と勢いよくベッドから起きあがる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki? Are you feeling unwell?”
“―――No, no. I was only staring because you looked so beautiful. Good morning, Hisui. You’re the same as ever this morning.”
“Ah―――yes; I apologize for never changing.”
“That isn’t what I meant. It’s just that you’re your usual self, Hisui. It makes me feel that today will be another ordinary, peaceful morning.”
With a decisive breath, I climbed out of bed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Shiki-sama?
Is there something wrong?"
"---Ah, no.
I was just enraptured for a moment.
…… Morning, Hisui.
This morning's just like always, huh."
"Ah---yes.
I am sorry it is no better than usual."
"I don't mean it like that.
I just feel, since you are the same as always, today is as peaceful a morning as always."
Alright!
With vigor, I throw myself out of bed.

entries.japanese:
「着替えたら居間に行くから。
翡翠は先に行ってていいよ」
「はい。
それでは失礼します」
　翡翠は静かにドアを閉めて去っていく。
「さて―――ばかなコト考えてないで学校に行くか」
　気を取りなおして、大きく深呼吸をしてみたりする。
　時刻は七時十分前。
　昨日と同様、今日もそう急がなくてよさそうだけど―――
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’ll come to the sitting room once I’m dressed. You can go on ahead.”
“Very well. Please excuse me.”
Hisui quietly closed the door behind her.
“All right―――enough stupid thoughts; time for school.”
I drew a deep breath and pulled myself together.
It was ten minutes to seven.
Just like yesterday, I had no need to hurry, but―――
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I'll change and go to the sitting room.
You can go now."
"Very well.
Please excuse me."
Hisui leaves and shuts the door calmly.
"Right---stupid thoughts aside, I should go to school…"
Taking charge of my thoughts, I breathe deeply.
It's ten before seven.
Like yesterday, there's no hurry today, so I'll---

entries.japanese:
――そうだな、夢見が悪かったせいで胸がムカムカしているし、すぐに朝食は食べられない。
　あと十分ぐらいぼんやりしてから居間に行こう。
entries.maoEnglish:
――Right; that nightmare has left my stomach churning, so breakfast is out of the question just yet.
I’ll sit here in a daze for another ten minutes, then go to the sitting room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
--That's right.
Having just had a bad dream, my chest's still a little jumpy.
I can't have breakfast right away.
I'll go to the sitting room in about ten minutes.

entries.japanese:
「あ、おはようございます志貴さん。
朝ごはんの支度でしたら出来ていますよ」
　琥珀さんは俺の顔を見て、すぐに笑顔で挨拶をしてくれる。
「うん、おはよう。
いつもすみません」
　と挨拶を返して、ちらりとソファーに視線を移す。
　と、そこにはいかにも文句がありそうな秋葉の姿があった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh, good morning, Master Shiki. Breakfast is ready whenever you are.”
The moment Kohaku sees me, she greets me with her usual smile.
“Morning. Thanks, as always.”
I return the greeting, then glance toward the sofa.
Akiha is there, plainly ready with a list of complaints.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah, good morning, Shiki-san.
Breakfast is already made."
Seeing my face, Kohaku-san immediately greets me with a smile.
"Yeah, morning.
Sorry, as always."
I return the greeting, and glance over at the sofa.
And there is Akiha, looking like she has something to complain about.

entries.japanese:
「おはよう秋葉。
その、今日も早いな」
「おはようごさいます。
兄さんは今日も遅いですね」
「……そっか。
秋葉もすっかり元気になったみたいで、安心したよ」
　その、心身ともに本当に回復してるみたいで。
「あら、心配してくれてたんですか。
そのわりにはただの一度も様子を見にきてくれなかったようですけど？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Morning, Akiha. You’re up early again.”
“Good morning. And you’re late again, Brother.”
“I see. You seem fully recovered, Akiha, and that’s a relief.”
In both body and spirit, she really does seem fully recovered.
“Oh, so you were worried about me. Strange that you never came to see me even once, though?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Morning, Akiha.
You're… up early again today."
"Good morning.
You're up late again, Nii-san."
"…… Ahh.
It looks like you're completely recovered, Akiha; I'm glad."
She really does seem much better, mind and body.
"Ah, you were worried?
It still seems like you didn't come to check on me even once."

entries.japanese:
「あのな秋葉。
俺だって見舞いぐらいはしたかったけど、おまえのほうが俺に近寄るなって言ったの、覚えてないのか？」
「そんなの状況次第です。
私の発作なんてすぐに納まるんですから、あんまり言葉を鵜呑みにしないでください」
　……秋葉の言い分はムチャクチャだ。
　どうも今朝は機嫌が悪いらしく、なんでもいいから俺に文句を言いたいだけなのかもしれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Come on, Akiha. I wanted to visit you, but you were the one who told me to stay away; have you forgotten?”
“That depends entirely on the circumstances. My attacks pass quickly, so please don’t take every word I say quite so literally.”
Her argument makes no sense whatsoever.
She must have woken up in a foul mood and decided that any excuse to criticize me will do.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hold on, Akiha, I did want to come watch over you.
Don't you remember ordering me not to come near you?"
"That was depending on the situation.
I was having only a temporary fit so you should not have really listened to what I said."
…… Akiha's words are unreasonable.
She seems to be in a bad mood this morning, so maybe she wants to yell at me for whatever reason.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま。
朝食を済ませていただかないと、学校に遅れてしまいますが」
　やばい、そういえば時間ギリギリだったんだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki. Unless you finish breakfast soon, you will be late for school.”
Damn, that’s right; I was already cutting it close.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama.
If you don't eat breakfast soon, you'll be late for school."
Crap, come to think of it, I was already running late.

entries.japanese:
朝食をすませて居間に戻ると、秋葉はまだ優雅にお茶なんかを飲んでいた。
　……俺を待っていた……っていうのは、都合のいい解釈なんだろうか。
「秋葉、もしかして学校までは車で行くのか？」
「あのですね。
兄さんの高校に自動車で登校したら厭味になるでしょう。
私でもそれぐらいは分かりますっ」
　そっか。
それじゃあ、やっぱりそういうコトなのか。
entries.maoEnglish:
When I return to the sitting room after breakfast, Akiha is still there, sipping tea with perfect elegance.
Would it be shamelessly convenient to think she has been waiting for me?
“Akiha, are you going to school by car?”
“Listen, Brother. Arriving at your school in a chauffeured car would be an appalling display. Even I understand that much.”
I see. So she really was waiting, then.
entries.mirrorMoon:
When I finish breakfast and return to the sitting room, Akiha is still drinking tea gracefully.
…… Waiting for me… is that the right explanation, I wonder?
"Akiha, will you be taking a car to school by any chance?"
"Now wait a minute.
To take a car to your school would be in poor taste.
Even I can understand that."
Ahh.
I guess it was that, after all.

entries.japanese:
「それじゃ行こうか。
この時間だと少し走るけど、仕方ないよな」
「え……兄さん？」
「だから、一緒に学校に行くぞって言ってるんだ。
学校までの近道教えてやるからこいよ。
……ま、俺と行くのがイヤだっていうんなら、別にいいけど」
「―――兄さんがそう言うのでしたら、私は、いいです、けど」
「きまりだな。
ほら、支度はできてるんだろ？
　急がないと遅刻するぞ」
　ソファーに座っている秋葉の手を取って、立ちあがらせる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Then let’s go. We’ll have to run a little at this hour, but we have no choice.”
“Brother?”
“I’m saying we should go to school together. I’ll show you a shortcut, so come on. Unless you’d rather not go with me, in which case, never mind.”
“―――If that’s what you want, Brother, then I suppose I don’t mind.”
“Settled. You’re ready, aren’t you? Come on, we’ll be late.”
I take Akiha’s hand and pull her up from the sofa.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Well then, shall we go?
At this time we might have to run a bit, but it can't be helped."
"Eh… Nii-san?"
"I'm saying, let's go to school together.
I'll show you the best route to take…… Well, if you don't want to go with me, I don't really mind."
"…… If you say so, I don't mind, but…"
"Then it's settled.
C'mon, you're ready, right?
We'll be late if we don't hurry."
I take Akiha's hand from the sofa, and pull her up.

entries.japanese:
「あ――――」
「翡翠、玄関までの見送りはいらないよ。
今日も夕方に帰ってくるから、よろしく」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ah――――”
“Hisui, you don’t need to see us to the door. I’ll be back this evening as usual, so take care of things while we’re gone.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah…"
"Hisui, we won't need to be seen off.
I'll be back in the afternoon today too, so take care."

entries.japanese:
―――というわけで、屋敷から出て坂道を一気に駆け下りて、そのまま学校まで駆けてきた。
　秋葉のスピードに合わせていたからいつもよりは遅れたけど、それでも十五分たらずで到着できた。
「よし、到着。
これならなんとかホームルームに間に合うぞ、秋葉」
「ええ、十分すぎるぐらい間に合うわ、こんなに走りどおしできたんですから！」
―――あ。
　なんか、秋葉が怒ってる。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――And so we dash out of the mansion, race headlong down the hill, and keep running all the way to school.
Matching Akiha’s pace makes me slower than usual, but we still arrive in under fifteen minutes.
“There, we made it. We can still catch homeroom, Akiha.”
“Yes, with time to spare—after you made me run the entire way!”
―――Oh.
Akiha seems to be angry.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---And so, we come out of the mansion, descend the slope at a run, and race on to school.
Matching my speed to Akiha's, even though it takes longer, we still make it in just under fifteen minutes.
"Right, we're here.
You should just about make it to homeroom, Akiha."
"Yes, we're going to make it in plenty of time, since we ran all the way!"
---Ah.
For some reason, Akiha seems to be angry.

entries.japanese:
「どうしたんだ秋葉、そんなに怒っちゃって。
……その、やっぱり車で来たほうがよかったとか？」
「―――あのですね、そんなわけないでしょう。
私が怒っているのは、もっと単純な理由です」
　はあはあ、と肩で息をしながら秋葉はこちらを睨んでくる。
「もしかして走るスピードが速かった、とか？」
「ええ、それも理由の一つだけど、正解じゃないわ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“What’s wrong, Akiha? Did you decide we should have taken the car after all?”
“―――Of course not. I’m angry for a much simpler reason.”
Akiha glares at me, shoulders heaving as she pants for breath.
“Was I running too fast, then?”
“Yes, that’s part of it, but it isn’t the answer.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"What's wrong, Akiha?
Such an angry face.
Maybe you should have come by car after all?"
"---Oh please.
Not at all.
I'm angry for a much simpler reason."
Breathing heavily, shoulders heaving, Akiha glares at me.
"Then, did I run a little too fast?"
"Yes.
Not a complete answer, but that is one of the reasons."

entries.japanese:
「それじゃあアレか。
二人で走っているところを登校中のやつらに見られて、指差されたりしたこととか？」
「そうね、おかげでものすごく恥ずかしかったけど、そんなのはどうでもいいわ」
――――？
　……わからないな、秋葉なんでこんなに怒っているんだろう。
　別に疲れたから怒っているんでもないし、ちゃんと時間には間に合ったし。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Then is it this? Were you upset because all those students pointed at us when they saw us running together?”
“That was mortifying, yes, but it hardly matters.”
――――?
I don’t get it; why is Akiha so angry?
It isn’t because she’s tired, and we arrived on time.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Well, perhaps it's that?
Two of us running together to school, being seen and pointed at?"
"True.
Although I was really embarrassed, I don't really care about that."
----?
…… I don't get it, then.
Why is Akiha so angry?
She's not angry because she's tired, and we made it to school on time.

entries.japanese:
「いいんです、私がかってに舞い上がっていただけですから。
考えてみれば、兄さんが早起きなんかするわけないんですよね。
……ほんと、私なにを期待してたんだろ」
　はあ、とうなだれる秋葉。
　……よくわからないけど、秋葉はもっとゆっくり登校したかったっていう事なんだろうか。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Never mind; I merely got carried away. Thinking about it sensibly, there was never any chance you would wake up early. Honestly, what was I expecting?”
Akiha hangs her head with a sigh.
I still don’t quite understand, but perhaps she wanted us to take our time walking to school.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Never mind, I am making an issue out of it on my own.
Thinking about it, you have no reason to get up early… Really, I don't know what I was hoping for."
With a sigh, Akiha hangs her head.
…… I don't really get it, but I guess Akiha's saying she wanted to go to school more leisurely?

entries.japanese:
「けど、少し意外でした。
私、足は速いほうですけど兄さんには追いつけなかった。
……部活動をしないわりには速いんですね、兄さんは」
「……まあ、やたらめったら運動できない体だから部活には入れないけど、体はちゃんと動かしてるから。
これでも運動神経はいいほうなんだ」
「ええ。
翡翠から聞いてはいましたけど、これほどだとは思っていませんでした。
　まあ、だからといって毎朝こんなペースで学校にいくのは遠慮したいですけど」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Still, you surprised me. I’m a fast runner, but I couldn’t keep up with you. You’re remarkably quick for someone who doesn’t play sports.”
“My health keeps me from joining a club, but I do exercise. Believe it or not, I’m fairly athletic.”
“Yes. Hisui told me as much, but I never imagined you were this fast.
That does not mean, however, that I care to come to school at this pace every morning.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"But, I'm surprised.
I'm a fast runner, but I wasn't able to keep up with you, Nii-san.
Even though you don't do any clubs, you're quite fast, aren't you."
"…… Well, vigorous activity isn't good for my body, so I can't do clubs, but I still move around.
Actually, I'm pretty athletic."
"Yes.
I heard from Hisui, but I wasn't expecting this.
But, I still would like to refuse going to school at such a pace every morning."

entries.japanese:
正門を抜けて昇降口に向かう。
　秋葉とはここで別れて、秋葉は四階、俺は三階の教室に向かう事になる。
「……それじゃあ兄さん、私は一年の教室ですから。
放課後まで、お別れですね」
「なに言ってるんだ、その前に昼休みがあるだろ。
中庭で待ってるから、早めにこいよ」
「あ―――――はい、お待ちしています」
entries.maoEnglish:
We pass through the front gate and head for the entrance hall.
This is where Akiha and I part ways: her classroom is on the fourth floor, mine on the third.
“Well, Brother, the first-year classrooms are upstairs. I suppose this is goodbye until after school.”
“What are you talking about? Lunch comes first; I’ll wait in the courtyard, so don’t be late.”
“Ah―――――yes; I’ll be there.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
Passing the main gate, we come to the entrance.
Here I part from Akiha; she goes to the fourth floor, and I go to my classroom on the third.
"…… Well then, Nii-san, I shall go to the first year classrooms.
I shall see you after school."
"What are you talking about?
There's lunch break before that.
I'll be waiting in the courtyard, so come quickly."
"Ah----yes.
I'll be waiting."

entries.japanese:
ぺこり、と柄にもなくかわいらしいお辞儀をして、秋葉は昇降口に駆けていく。
―――と。
　思い出したように立ち止まって、秋葉は振り向いた。
「兄さん、今朝の追いかけっこは楽しかったわ。
毎日はお断りだけど、たまにはああゆうのも悪くはありませんね！」
　息を弾ませて、今度こそ秋葉は昇降口へと消えていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
Akiha gives an unexpectedly sweet little bow and hurries toward the entrance.
―――Then.
As if remembering something, she stops and turns back.
“Brother, I enjoyed our race this morning. I refuse to do it every day, but once in a while, it might not be so bad!”
Still breathless, Akiha disappears through the entrance at last.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Giving a cute little bow, she runs inside.

---Then.
As if remembering something, Akiha stops and turns.
"Nii-san, this morning's race was enjoyable.
Though I wouldn't want to do it every day, perhaps it's not so bad once in a while!"
Her breath bouncing, Akiha disappears inside.

entries.japanese:
「――――――」
　……なんだ、かわいいとこあるじゃないか、あいつ。
「いいなあ、仲がいいんですね二人とも」
　！？
「し、シエル先輩！
　いきなり後ろから声をかけないでください……！」
「はい、これからは気をつけます」
　にっこりと笑って、先輩は楽しそうにこちらを見つめてくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――――”
Well, she does have a cute side after all.
“How lovely that you two are so close.”
Wha—!?
“C-Ciel! Please don’t suddenly speak to me from behind…!”
“Very well, I’ll be more careful in future.”
She beams at me, plainly amused.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……"
…… Well, I guess she does have a cute side.
"How nice!
The two of you get along well, don't you?"
!?
"Ci… Ciel-senpai!
Please don't sneak up on me like that…!"
"Yes, I'll be careful from now on."
Smiling sweetly, Senpai gazes at me happily.

entries.japanese:
「……なんだよ先輩。
言いたい事があるんだったら、はっきり言ってくれ」
「いえいえ、わたしがいまさら言う必要もないみたいです。
遠野くん、すごく幸せそうな顔してますから」
「―――なっ」
「そんな顔のままで教室にいったら乾くんにからかわれますよ。
それじゃ遠野くん、またお昼休みにお邪魔しますね」
　先輩はクスクスと笑いながら昇降口へと歩いていく。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What is it? If you have something to say, just say it.”
“Oh, there’s no need for me to say anything now. You already look perfectly happy, Tohno.”
“―――What?”
“If you go to class wearing that expression, Inui will never let you hear the end of it. Well then, Tohno, I’ll come bother you again at lunch.”
She walks toward the entrance, laughing softly to herself.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… What is it, Senpai?
If you want to say something, say it."
"No, no; I don't think I need to say anything.
You look really happy, Tohno-kun."
"---Wha…!"
"If you go into the classroom with a face like that, Inui-kun will surely tease you.
Well, Tohno-kun, I'll see you at lunch again."
Senpai walks indoors, laughing to herself.

entries.japanese:
「――――――」
　ふに、と自分の頬をつねってみた。
「……そんなににやけてたかな、俺」
　……まあ、にやけてたんだろう。
　秋葉のあんな笑顔一つで、なんだか幸せな気分になってたりしたんだから。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――――”
I pinch my own cheek.
“Was I really grinning that much?”
Well, I suppose I was.
One smile from Akiha had been enough to leave me absurdly happy.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------"
I pinch my cheek.
"…… Did I look that happy?"
…… Well, I guess I did.
Since just seeing Akiha smile made me feel real happy inside.

entries.japanese:
―――四時限目の授業が終わった。
　昼休みになって、学校中がざわざわと騒がしくなる。
「――――さて」
　秋葉と中庭で待ち合わせだったっけ。
　……あいつの事だから琥珀さんにお弁当でも作ってもらったんだろうけど、一応、適当に購買で買っていくとするか。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Fourth period ends.
Lunchtime begins, and the whole school swells with noise.
“――――Right, then.”
I promised to meet Akiha in the courtyard.
Knowing her, she probably had Kohaku prepare a lunch for her, but I’ll pick up something from the school store just in case.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----Fourth period ends.
Lunch break comes, and the school fills with noise.
"----Right."
Akiha should be waiting in the courtyard.
…… Since it's Akiha, I think she probably got Kohaku-san to make her lunch, but I should go buy something just in case.

entries.japanese:
たまに早起きした事だし、わざわざ時間を潰す必要もないだろう。
　昨日の夕食の一件―――秋葉が顔を真っ青にして部屋に引きこもってしまった事も気にかかる。
　秋葉の体調がよくなっているんなら、あいつも居間にいる事だろうし。
entries.maoEnglish:
Since I’ve managed to wake early for once, there’s no reason to waste the time.
I’m also worried about what happened at dinner yesterday―――how Akiha went deathly pale and shut herself in her room.
If she’s feeling better, she should be in the sitting room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Occasionally I get up early so there's no need to kill time.
I'm concerned about last night's dinner incident---when Akiha's face turned pale and she withdrew to her room.
If she is feeling better, then she is probably in the sitting room.

entries.japanese:
「あら、おはようございます志貴さん。
今朝はお早いんですね」
　琥珀さんは俺の顔を見て、すぐに笑顔で挨拶をしてくれる。
「おはよう琥珀さん。
ところで秋葉はもう起きてるの？」
「ええ、もうすぐいらっしゃいますよ。
今朝はお二人ともご一緒に朝食がとれますね」
　琥珀さんは楽しそうな足取りで台所へ行ってしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Good morning, Master Shiki. You’re up early today.”
Kohaku greets me with a smile the moment she sees me.
“Morning, Kohaku. Is Akiha awake yet?”
“Yes, she’ll be here shortly. You’ll be able to have breakfast together this morning.”
Kohaku skips cheerfully away toward the kitchen.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Oh, good morning, Shiki-san.
You are up pretty early today."
Seeing my face, Kohaku-san immediately greets me with a smile.
"Morning, Kohaku-san.
By the way, is Akiha up yet?"
"Yes, she will be here shortly.
You can have breakfast together this morning."
Kohaku-san walks happily to the kitchen.

entries.japanese:
「兄さん……？」
「よっ、おはよう秋葉。
体の調子、ちゃんと良くなったのか？」
「え―――あ、はい。
おかげさまで発作も治まりましたけど……兄さん、気にしてらっしゃったんですか？」
「まあその、それなりに気にはしてた。
　……昨日はすまなかった。
秋葉があんなふうになるなんて知らなかったから、つい動転しちまって、秋葉に無理させただろ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Brother…?”
“Hey, good morning, Akiha. Are you feeling all right now?”
“Oh―――yes. The attack has passed, thanks to you, but were you worried about me?”
“Well, yes; I was worried.
I’m sorry about yesterday. I had no idea that could happen to you, so I panicked and ended up pushing you too hard.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Nii-san……?"
"Yo, morning, Akiha.
Are you feeling better?"
"Eh----Y, yes.
Thanks to you, my spasms have passed…… Nii-san, were you worried?"
"Well, yeah.
I was worried a bit.
…… I'm sorry about last night.
I didn't know you had that condition, so I panicked and I guess I made you push yourself."

entries.japanese:
「いえ、あの時は私のほうこそ怒鳴ったりして申し訳ありませんでした。
……私、ああなってしまうと周りが見えなくなって、言動が雑になってしまうんです」
　昨夜の自分を思い返して、恥ずかしそうに秋葉は視線を泳がせる。
「……ごめんなさい兄さん。
昨夜ははしたない所をお見せしてしまって」
「そんな事はないだろ。
秋葉、体調が悪い時はみんなそうなんだから、そんな事を気に病むことはないよ」
「あ……うん、兄さんがそう言ってくれるのなら、ちょっとは救われるんですけど」
　よほど昨夜の事が気になっているのか、秋葉はそわそわとして落ち着かない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“No, I’m the one who should apologize for shouting. When an attack takes hold, I lose sight of everything around me and become terribly coarse.”
Remembering last night, Akiha looks away in embarrassment.
“I’m sorry, Brother. You had to see me behave so disgracefully.”
“It wasn’t disgraceful. Everyone loses their composure when they’re ill, so you don’t need to torment yourself over it.”
“If you say so, Brother, I suppose that helps a little.”
Last night must still be weighing heavily on her; she can’t seem to settle.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No, I am the one who must apologize for being upset…… When I have that condition, I tend to get tunnel-visioned and my conduct becomes a little rude."
Akiha starts to look embarrassed as she recalls her actions.
"…… I'm sorry, Nii-san.
I showed you an unpleasant side of me yesterday."
"That's not true.
Everyone is like then when they feel sick.
There's no need to beat yourself up over it."
"Ah…… okay.
If you say so, it makes me feel a little better."
She must still be bothered by it because she doesn't seem relaxed.

entries.japanese:
そこへ、
「志貴さーん、秋葉さまー、朝食の支度が整いましたよー」
　という、底抜けに明るい琥珀さんの声が聞こえてきた。
entries.maoEnglish:
Then,
“Master Shiki, Miss Akiha, breakfast is ready!”
Kohaku’s irrepressibly bright voice rings out.
entries.mirrorMoon:
And,
"Shiki-saan, Akiha-samaaa, breakfast is reaaady!"
Kohaku-san's boundless, cheerful voice rings out.

entries.japanese:
「……とりあえず朝食にしようか。
考えてみると秋葉と朝食をとるの、今日が初めてだな」
「そうですね。
学校が変って、私も朝の時間がゆっくりになりましたから。
これからはずっとこうできればいいんですけど」
―――そうか、言われてみればその通りだ。
　俺たちは同じ学校になったんだから、たった十分早起きするだけで余裕をもって秋葉と朝食をとれることになっているんだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Let’s eat for now. Come to think of it, this will be the first time we’ve had breakfast together.”
“Yes. Now that I’ve changed schools, my mornings are less hurried. I hope we can do this every day from now on.”
―――Come to think of it, she’s right.
Now that we attend the same school, all I have to do is wake ten minutes earlier and there will be plenty of time to eat breakfast with her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Shall we eat now?
Come to think of it, I haven't had breakfast with you yet."
"That is true.
After changing schools, my morning schedule has become more flexible.
I wish we could always do this."
---Now that she mentions it, that's right.
Since we're both going to the same school, if I get up ten minutes early, I can eat breakfast with Akiha.

entries.japanese:
朝食を終えて居間に戻ってきた。
　時刻は七時二十分。
余裕をもって登校するのなら、もう屋敷を出ないといけない時間だ。
　秋葉は準備が出来ているのか、ソファーに座って時計を眺めていたりする。
　……というより、秋葉は今まで車で学校に通っていた。
もしかするとうちの学校にも車で向かうつもりなのかもしれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
Breakfast over, I return to the sitting room.
It is seven twenty. If we want an easy walk to school, we need to leave now.
Apparently ready already, Akiha sits on the sofa watching the clock.
Then again, Akiha has always traveled to school by car. Perhaps she intends to do the same here.
entries.mirrorMoon:
After breakfast I return to the sitting room.
It is twenty past seven.
If we want to walk to school slowly, we have to leave soon.
Akiha must be all prepared as she is sitting on the sofa, staring at the clock.
…… Actually, she's been going to her school in a car this whole time.
Maybe she intends to do so to go to my school as well.

entries.japanese:
「秋葉。
念のために聞いておくけど、学校までは歩いていくんだろ？」
「当たり前です。
兄さんの高校に自動車で登校したら厭味になるでしょう。
私でもそれぐらいはわかります」
　そうか。
それなら一緒に屋敷を出る事になるな。
「それじゃそろそろ行こうか。
この時間ならゆっくり歩いていけるだろ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Akiha. Just to make sure—you’re walking to school, aren’t you?”
“Of course. Arriving at your school in a chauffeured car would be an appalling display. Even I understand that much.”
I see. Then we’ll be leaving together.
“We should get going. At this hour we can take our time.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Akiha.
Just to make sure, but you're walking to school, right?"
"Of course.
To take a car to your school would be in poor taste.
Even I can understand that."
I see.
Then we'll be leaving together.
"Then shall we get going?
If we leave now, we can take our time."

entries.japanese:
「え……兄さん？」
「だから、一緒に学校に行くぞって言ってるんだ。
学校までの近道教えてやるからこいよ。
……ま、俺と行くのがイヤだっていうんなら、別にいいけど」
「―――いえ、こちらこそよろしくお願いします。
兄さんが付いていてくれるのなら心配ありません」
「決まりだな。
それじゃそろそろ行くぞ」
「翡翠、玄関までの見送りはいらないよ。
今日も夕方に帰ってくるから、よろしく」
　翡翠にそう告げて、秋葉と一緒に屋敷を後にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Brother?”
“I’m saying we should go to school together. I’ll show you a shortcut, so come on. Unless you’d rather not go with me, in which case, never mind.”
“―――No, I’d be glad to. If you’re with me, Brother, I have nothing to worry about.”
“Settled, then. Let’s go.”
“Hisui, you don’t need to see us to the door. I’ll be back this evening as usual, so take care of things while we’re gone.”
With that, Akiha and I leave the mansion together.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Eh…… Nii-san?"
"I'm saying, let's go to school together.
I'll show you the best route to take…… Well, if you don't want to go with me, I don't really mind."
"----No, I would love to.
I have no worries if I go with you, Nii-san."
"It's decided, then.
Well, we gotta head out now."
"Hisui, you don't need to send us off.
We will be back in the afternoon, so take care."
After instructing Hisui, I leave the mansion with Akiha.

entries.japanese:
秋葉のペースに合わせて、ゆっくり歩いて学校に到着した。
　時刻は七時五十分前。
ホームルームまで余裕で間に合う時間帯だ。
「時間通りだな。
もうちょっと速く歩けば七時半に出ても間に合うんだけど―――っても秋葉？」
「………………」
　何か不思議なものでも見るように、秋葉は校門の様子を見つめている。
entries.maoEnglish:
Matching Akiha’s pace, I walk leisurely to school.
We arrive at ten to eight. There is plenty of time before homeroom.
“Right on time. If we walked a little faster, we could leave at seven thirty and still―――Akiha?”
“…”
Akiha stares at the school gate as though she has never seen anything like it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Matching her pace, we arrive leisurely at school.
It's just before seven fifty.
We have plenty of time before homeroom.
"Right on time.
We could probably even leave at seven thirty and still make it----uh, Akiha?"
"………………"
Akiha looks at the school gate as if there was something odd about it.

entries.japanese:
「どうした？
　何かおかしなモノでも見つけたか？」
「あ―――いえ、別に何でもありません。
ただ、昨日は生徒の方々が登校する前に登校していたから、こういった光景は初めて見るなって」
　……そうか。
子供の頃から全寮制の学校にばかり通っていたものだから、こういうふうに大勢の生徒が学校にやってくる、という光景に秋葉は慣れていないらしい。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What is it? See something odd?”
“Oh―――no, nothing. Yesterday I arrived before the other students, so this is my first time seeing the school like this.”
I see. She attended boarding schools from childhood, so the sight of a crowd of students arriving for the day is unfamiliar to her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"What is it?
Do you see something weird?"
"Ah----no, it's nothing.
Yesterday I came before everyone else was arriving, so this is the first time I've seen all the students arriving in a clutter like this."
…… I see.
She's always been at a boarding school so many students walking into school like this would be unfamiliar.

entries.japanese:
「バカだな、なにを他人行儀なコト言ってるんだ。
昨日から秋葉はうちの生徒なんだぞ。
別に遠慮する必要なんてないだろ」
「………………」
　なにか後ろめたい事でもあるのか、秋葉はいまいち元気がない。
「どうしたんだよ秋葉。
なんだからしくないぞ、おまえ」
「……そんなの、仕方ないじゃないですか。
兄さんと一緒に学校に行けるだけで十分なのに、こんな当たり前の生活をしてしまったら、私―――」
　秋葉は気まずそうに顔を伏せる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Don’t be silly; why talk as if you’re an outsider? You’ve been a student here since yesterday. There’s no need to hang back.”
“…”
Whether from guilt or something else, Akiha seems uncharacteristically subdued.
“What’s wrong with you? This isn’t like you, Akiha.”
“I can’t help it. Walking to school with you is already more than enough, and if I let myself enjoy an ordinary life like this, I―――”
Akiha lowers her face, suddenly awkward.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Stupid, why are you being so reserved?
Starting yesterday, you became one of us.
There's no need to hold back."
"………………"
Is she holding something back?
She doesn't seem really lively.
"What's wrong, Akiha?
You don't look too well."
"…… That, that can't be helped, can it?
I thought just going to school with you would be enough, but such a normal lifestyle, I----"
Akiha averts her gaze, looking sad.

entries.japanese:
「…………？」
　秋葉の言いたい事はよく解らない。
　ただ、こうして正門で立ち尽くしていると目立って仕方がない。
　さっきから登校してくる生徒たちの視線が秋葉に集まっていて、こっちが照れてしまうぐらいだ。
「ほら、ともかく中に入るぞ」
　秋葉の手をとって正門をくぐり抜ける。
　正門を抜けて昇降口に向かう。
　秋葉とはここで別れて、秋葉は四階、俺は三階の教室に向かう事になる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…?”
I don’t really understand what she means.
But standing frozen at the gate is drawing far too much attention.
Every student who passes has been staring at Akiha, enough to make even me self-conscious.
“Come on; let’s get inside.”
I take her hand and lead her through the gate.
We head toward the entrance hall.
This is where Akiha and I part ways: her classroom is on the fourth floor, mine on the third.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…………?"
I don't know what she's trying to say.
Just that we kind of stand out standing here in front of the gate.
The students who arrive all stare at Akiha and I'm getting a little embarrassed.
"C'mon, let's go inside for now."
I take Akiha's hand and pass through the gate.
We go through the gate and head for the entrance.
We split up here as Akiha has to go to the fourth floor while I am on the third floor.

entries.japanese:
「それじゃあ兄さん、私は一年生の教室ですから。
放課後まで、お別れですね」
「なに言ってるんだ、その前に昼休みがあるだろ。
中庭で待ってるから、早めにこいよ」
「あ―――――はい、お待ちしています」
　ぺこり、と柄にもなくかわいらしいお辞儀をして、秋葉は昇降口に駆けていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Well, Brother, the first-year classrooms are upstairs. I suppose this is goodbye until after school.”
“What are you talking about? Lunch comes first; I’ll wait in the courtyard, so don’t be late.”
“Ah―――――yes; I’ll be there.”
Akiha gives an unexpectedly sweet little bow, then hurries into the entrance hall.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Well then, Nii-san, I shall go to the first year classrooms.
I shall see you after school."
"What are you talking about?
There's lunch break before that.
I'll be waiting in the courtyard, so come quickly."
"Ah------Yes, I will be there."
Giving a cute little bow, she runs inside.

entries.japanese:
「――――――」
　……なんだ、かわいいとこあるじゃないか、あいつ。
「いいなあ、仲がいいんですね二人とも」
　！？
「し、シエル先輩！
　いきなり後ろから声をかけないでください……！」
「はい、これからは気をつけます」
　にっこりと笑って、先輩は楽しそうにこちらを見つめてくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――――”
Well, she does have a cute side after all.
“How lovely that you two are so close.”
Wha—!?
“C-Ciel! Please don’t suddenly speak to me from behind…!”
“Very well, I’ll be more careful in future.”
She beams at me, plainly amused.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------"
…… well, I guess she does have a cute side.
"How nice!
The two of you get along well, don't you?"
!?
"Ci… Ciel-senpai!
Please don't sneak up on me like that…!"
"Yes, I'll be careful from now on."
Smiling sweetly, Senpai gazes at me happily.

entries.japanese:
「……なんだよ先輩。
言いたい事があるんだったら、はっきり言ってくれ」
「いえいえ、わたしがいまさら言う必要もないみたいです。
遠野くん、すごく幸せそうな顔してますから」
「―――なっ」
「そんな顔のままで教室にいったら乾くんにからかわれますよ。
それじゃ遠野くん、またお昼休みにお邪魔しますね」
　先輩はクスクスと笑いながら昇降口へと歩いていく。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What is it? If you have something to say, just say it.”
“Oh, there’s no need for me to say anything now. You already look perfectly happy, Tohno.”
“―――What?”
