“If you go to class wearing that expression, Inui will never let you hear the end of it. Well then, Tohno, I’ll come bother you again at lunch.”
She walks toward the entrance, laughing softly to herself.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… What is it, Senpai?
If you want to say something, say it."
"No, no; I don't think I need to say anything.
You look really happy, Tohno-kun."
"---Wha…!"
"If you go into the classroom with a face like that, Inui-kun will surely tease you.
Well, Tohno-kun, I'll see you at lunch again."
Senpai walks indoors, laughing to herself.

entries.japanese:
「――――――」
　ふに、と自分の頬をつねってみた。
「……そんなににやけてたかな、俺」
　……まあ、にやけてたんだろう。
　秋葉のあんな笑顔一つで、なんだか幸せな気分になってたりしたんだから。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――――”
I pinch my own cheek.
“Was I really grinning that much?”
Well, I suppose I was.
One smile from Akiha had been enough to leave me absurdly happy.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------"
I pinch my cheek.
"…… Did I look that happy?"
…… well, I guess I did.
Since just seeing Akiha smile made me feel real happy inside.

entries.japanese:
―――四時限目の授業が終わった。
　昼休みになって、学校中がざわざわと騒がしくなる。
「――――さて」
　秋葉と中庭で待ち合わせだったっけ。
　……あいつの事だから琥珀さんにお弁当でも作ってもらったんだろうけど、一応、適当に購買で買っていくとするか。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Fourth period ends.
Lunchtime begins, and the whole school swells with noise.
“――――Right, then.”
I promised to meet Akiha in the courtyard.
Knowing her, she probably had Kohaku prepare a lunch for her, but I’ll pick up something from the school store just in case.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----Fourth period ends.
Lunch break comes, and the school fills with noise.
"----Right."
Akiha should be waiting in the courtyard.
…… Since it's Akiha, I think she probably got Kohaku-san to make her lunch, but I should go buy something just in case.

entries.japanese:
―――そうだな、夢見が悪かったせいで胸がムカムカする。
　時間もある事だし、もう少しだけ休んでいこう。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Right; that nightmare has left my stomach churning.
Since I still have time, I’ll rest a little longer.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----That's true.
Thanks to my nightmare, I'm still a little unsettled.
I have a little time, so I should rest.

entries.japanese:
いつのまにかベッドで二度寝してしまっていた。
　まだふらふらしている頭を振って、まわりを見渡す。
　と。
「志貴さま」
「うわぁ！」
　枕元に、俺を覗きこむように翡翠が立っていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
At some point I must have fallen back asleep.
I shake my still-swimming head and look around.
Then.
“Master Shiki.”
“Wah!”
Hisui is standing beside my pillow, leaning over to peer at me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
At some point, I realize that I've slept in.

I shake my groggy head and look around.
And then,
"Shiki-sama."
"Uwaa!"
Hisui is standing right by my bed looking into my face.

entries.japanese:
「な、な―――」
「志貴さま、お時間のほうはよろしいのですか？
　すでに八時を過ぎておりますが」
「――――え？」
　時計を見る。
　たしかに、長針は八時を指していた。
「しまった、寝過ごした……！」
　ベッドから跳ね起きる。
　慌てて着替えようとして、部屋に翡翠がいることに気がついた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Wh-what―――”
“Master Shiki, are you certain you have time to spare? It is already past eight.”
“――――What?”
I look at the clock.
Sure enough, the minute hand points to the eight on the dial.
“Damn it, I overslept…!”
I spring out of bed.
I’m about to tear off my clothes when I remember that Hisui is still in the room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Wha, wha----"
"Shiki-sama, is the time acceptable?
It is past eight o'clock."
"----Eh?"
I look at the clock.
Certainly, the arm is pointing towards eight.
"Crap, I overslept……!"
I jump up from bed.
Flustered, I start to change and then realize Hisui is still here.

entries.japanese:
「翡翠。
悪いんだけど、その」
「承知しております。
それではどうか、今度こそ居間のほうにおいでください」
　部屋から退室していく翡翠。
……その目はあきらかに怒っているように見えた。
「……そりゃそうだよな。
せっかく起こしに来てくれたのに、その後に二度寝したら翡翠の立場がないもんな……」
　一人反省して、とにかく急いで着替えをすませた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hisui. Sorry, but, um…”
“I understand. Please come to the sitting room this time, once you are dressed.”
Hisui leaves the room. Her eyes look unmistakably angry.
“Well, of course. She came all the way here to wake me, and then I went straight back to sleep; that makes her effort rather pointless…”
After a moment of solitary repentance, I dress as fast as I can.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hisui.
Um, sorry, but…"
"I understand.
Please go to the sitting room this time."
Hisui exits my room…… Her eyes were obviously showing she was upset.
"…… Well, of course.
She already came to wake me up, so for me to fall asleep again like that……"
Ruminating to myself, I quickly change.

entries.japanese:
……どうにかして学校までやってきた。
　とっくに一時限目が始まっていて、校門には誰もいない。
「はあ………」
　ため息をこぼして校舎へと向かっていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
Somehow, I make it to school.
First period has long since begun, and the gate is deserted.
“Haa…”
With a sigh, I trudge toward the building.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… I manage to make it to school.
First period has started a while ago and no one is at the gate.
I give a sigh as I enter the school building.

entries.japanese:
―――四時限目の授業が終わった。
　昼休みになって、学校中がざわざわと騒がしくなる。
「――――さて」
　中庭に行けば秋葉もやってくるだろう。
　あいつの事だから琥珀さんにお弁当でも作ってもらったんだろうけど、一応、適当に購買で買っていくとするか。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Fourth period ends.
Lunchtime begins, and the whole school swells with noise.
“――――Right, then.”
Akiha will probably come to the courtyard.
Knowing her, she likely had Kohaku prepare a lunch for her, but I’ll pick up something from the school store just in case.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----Fourth period ends.
Lunch break comes, and the school fills with noise.
"----Right."
Akiha should be waiting in the courtyard.
…… Since it's Akiha, I think she probably got Kohaku-san to make her lunch, but I should go buy something just in case.

entries.japanese:
――――で。
「いょぉう遠野、遅かったな」
「ほんと、遅かったですね兄さん」
―――どうゆうわけなのか、有彦は俺より先に中庭にやってきていて、秋葉の相手をしていたみたいだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――And so.
“Heeey, Tohno, took you long enough.”
“You certainly did take your time, Brother.”
―――For some unfathomable reason, Arihiko had reached the courtyard before me and had apparently been keeping Akiha company.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----And there,
"Yo, Tohno.
You're late."
"Indeed; you are rather late, Nii-san."
---For some reason, it seems that Arihiko has come to the courtyard ahead of me, and was keeping Akiha company.

entries.japanese:
「……朝から姿が見えないと思ったら、こんなところにいたのか有彦」
「おう！
　四時間目からここではってた甲斐があったってもんだぜ！」
　誇らしげに胸をはって豪語する有彦。
　……ここまで幸せなヤツだと、文句のもの字もうかばない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“So this is where you’ve been hiding all morning, Arihiko.”
“Damn right! Camping out here since fourth period finally paid off!”
Arihiko throws out his chest in triumph.
When a man is this blissfully pleased with himself, even the first syllable of a complaint refuses to come.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I was wondering where you've been all morning, Arihiko.
I guess you've been here."
"Oh!
I knew if I waited here after fourth period it would be worth it!"
Arihiko boasts, puffing out his chest.
…… If he's that happy, I guess I can't complain.

entries.japanese:
「で、秋葉。
今日の昼食はどうなってるんだ？
　琥珀さんにお弁当でも作ってもらったのか？」
「え……オベントウ、ですか？」
「……いや、いい。
そんな一般的なことを尋ねた俺が間違いだった」
　買ってきたパンのなかから、比較的まともなサンドウィッチといちご牛乳を差し出す。
entries.maoEnglish:
“So, Akiha. What are you doing for lunch? Did Kohaku pack something for you?”
“A packed lunch?”
“Never mind. My mistake for asking such a commonplace question.”
From the things I bought, I offer her the comparatively respectable sandwich and a carton of strawberry milk.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"So, Akiha.
What'll we do for lunch today?
Did you have Kohaku-san make you a boxed lunch?"
"Eh?
…… a 'boxed lunch'…?"
"…… Never mind.
I shouldn't have asked such a common thing."
From the bread I bought, I offer her the best sandwich and a strawberry milk.

entries.japanese:
「ほら、今日の昼食。
昨日のよりはマシだから、安心して食べられるぞ」
「……うん、わかった」
　おずおずとサンドウィッチといちご牛乳を手に取る秋葉。
　……この先、秋葉がうちの学校に昼食に慣れる時がくるのか、少しだけ不安になる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Here, today’s lunch. It’s safer than yesterday’s, so you can eat without fear.”
“All right…”
Akiha gingerly accepts the sandwich and strawberry milk.
I am beginning to worry that she may never adapt to the food at this school.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Here, today's lunch.
It's better than yesterday, so eat it in comfort."
"…… Alright."
Akiha timidly accepts the sandwiches and strawberry milk.
…… I wonder uneasily whether Akiha will ever get used to having lunch at our school.

entries.japanese:
「あー、いいないいなー。
なあ遠野、オレっちにはないの？」
「……うん。
まあ、なぜか、買ってある」
　ほら、とソーセージパンと適当な飲み物を手渡した。
「うっわー、なんだよそれ！
　ゴーヤドリンクなんて哺乳類の飲むモンじゃねーだろうが！」
「しょうがないだろ、他のはもうなかったんだから。
ま、サボテンミキサーならいくらでも余ってたけど、いくらなんでもアレはね、すでに飲み物じゃないから」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Aw, lucky! Hey, Tohno, don’t I get anything?”
“Yeah. Somehow, I bought something for you too.”
I hand him a sausage roll and a random drink.
“What the hell is this? Bitter-melon juice isn’t fit for mammalian consumption!”
“I had no choice; everything else was gone. There was plenty of Cactus Mixer left, but that stuff stopped qualifying as a beverage long ago.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Aw, nice, nice!
Hey, Tohno, nothing for me?"
"…… Well, yeah, for some reason there is."
I hand him a sausage roll and a suitable drink.
"Hey, what is this!
'Balsam Pear Drink'?
This stuff isn't even fit for animals to drink!"
"Can't be helped, the rest were all gone already.
Well, there were some Cactus Mixer's, but that's not what you would call a drink."

entries.japanese:
「………むっ。
まだおまえにも人の情けというものがあったんですか、遠野」
「おまえ以外にはいくらでもあるよ。
ほら、昨日の借りはこれでチャラだからな」
　ちぇっ、と舌打ちしながらも有彦は楽しげに飲み物パックにストローを挿している。
「ナプキンももらってきたから、秋葉も―――」
「――――！」
　びっ、びっくりした。
　なんて顔してるんだ、秋葉のヤツ。
「ど、どうした秋葉。
毛虫でもいたのか？」
「……別になんでもありません。
ただ、兄さんと乾さんって本当に仲がいいんだなあって思っただけです」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hmph. So some shred of human mercy still survives in you, Tohno.”
“I have plenty for everyone but you. Anyway, that settles what I owed you from yesterday.”
Arihiko clicks his tongue, yet cheerfully punches the straw into the carton.
“I brought napkins too, so Akiha, you can―――”
“――――!”
I—I nearly jumped out of my skin.
What kind of face is Akiha making?
“Wh-what’s wrong, Akiha? Did you find a caterpillar?”
“Nothing. I was merely thinking how remarkably close you and Mister Inui seem to be.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Muh.
I guess you still had a bit of compassion, Tohno."
"I have loads for anyone but you.
This makes us even for yesterday."
Though he clicks his tongue in irritation, Arihiko puts the straw into the drink pack happily.
"I got a napkin for you too, Akiha…"
"…!"
Wha, what a shock.
Why's Akiha making such a face?
"Wha, what is it, Akiha?
Is there a bug on you?"
"…… It's nothing at all.
I just thought, Nii-san and Inui-san seem to be really close."

entries.japanese:
「あははは！
　秋葉ちゃん、そりゃあいくらなんでも持ち上げすぎだって。
オレと遠野は友人は友人でも仇敵と書いてトモと呼ぶ友人なんだからな！」
　がははは、と愉快そうに笑う有彦の横で、秋葉は何か言いたそうな視線を向けてくる。
――――と。
「あ、こんなところにいたんですね、遠野くんたち」
　お弁当を片手に、先輩がやってきた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ahahaha! Come on, Akiha, that’s giving us way too much credit. Tohno and I may be friends, but we’re the kind where ‘friend’ is spelled ‘mortal enemy’!”
As Arihiko roars with laughter beside her, Akiha fixes me with a look that seems to have something to say.
――――And then.
“Ah, so this is where you all were.”
Carrying her lunch, Ciel joins us.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hahaha!
Akiha-chan, you're giving us too much credit.
Tohno and I are best friends and bitter enemies, so just call us pals!"
Arihiko laughs happily, and Akiha looks at me as if wanting to say something.
----And then.
"Ah, you were all here, then?"
Boxed lunch in hand, Senpai appears.

entries.japanese:
「あっ、シエル先輩じゃん！
　やった、今日はスリーセブンだぞ遠野！」
「…………」
　……悪いけど有彦、俺はそこまで素直に喜べない。
　だって、その―――
　秋葉が、とっても恐い顔をしているんだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hey, it’s Ciel! Jackpot, Tohno—three sevens today!”
“….”
Sorry, Arihiko, but I can’t celebrate quite that innocently.
Because, well―――
Akiha is wearing an absolutely terrifying expression.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah, it's Ciel-senpai!
Today's a jackpot, right, Tohno?"
"……"
…… Sorry, Arihiko, I can't be as easily pleased as that.
That's because---
Akiha has a really scary expression right now.

entries.japanese:
「みなさん、わたしもお昼をご一緒していいですか？」
　うんうん、とうなずく有彦。
　俺だってそれには賛成だけど―――
「嫌です」
　なんて、秋葉はきっぱりと断言した。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Would everyone mind if I joined you for lunch?”
Arihiko nods eagerly.
I am in favor too, but―――
“I would.”
Akiha’s refusal is absolute.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"May I join you all for lunch?"
Arihiko nods eagerly.
I don't mind either, but---
"No."
For some reason, Akiha refuses directly.

entries.japanese:
……中庭の空気が寒い。
　十月も末だから、そりゃあ暖かいとは言えないけど、とにかく寒い。
　秋葉のお嬢さまなところしか知らなかった有彦なんて、『あ』と口を開けたまま固まっている。
「…………はあ」
　が、兄として秋葉の今の発言は注意してやらないといけないだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
The courtyard has gone cold.
Granted, it is late October and hardly warm to begin with, but this is a different sort of cold.
Arihiko, who has seen only Akiha’s polished young-lady façade, stands petrified with his mouth hanging open.
“Hah.”
Still, as her brother, I ought to reprimand her for that.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The air in the courtyard is cold.
It's not going to be warm in October, but it's still quite cold.
Arihiko, who until now knew only the ladylike Akiha, gapes silently.
"…… Ahh."
Well, as an older brother, it would be bad if I didn't respond to what Akiha just said.

entries.japanese:
「秋葉、なんてコト言うんだ。
たとえ冗談にしたって、今のは失礼だぞ」
「兄さん。
私、冗談は口にしません。
今のは偽りのない私の本心です」
「な―――なんて事を言うんだおまえ！
　秋葉は先輩とまだ会ったばっかりじゃないか！
　だっていうのにいきなり嫌ですって、それはどういう了見だ！」
「嫌なものは嫌なんですっ。
私、その人とは絶対的に相性が悪いんです。
「あなただってそうでしょう？
　私とは相容れないってわかってるんじゃない、先輩？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Akiha, what was that? Even as a joke, it was terribly rude.”
“Brother. I do not make jokes. What I said was my honest opinion.”
“Wh―――what a thing to say! You only just met her! How can you reject her on sight like that?”
“Because I don’t want her here! She and I are fundamentally incompatible.”
“You know it too, don’t you? You and I could never get along, Ciel.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"What're you talking about, Akiha.
That was rude, even for a joke."
"Nii-san, I am not joking.
I meant what I said."
"Wha---what are you saying!
You've only just met Senpai!
You've no reason to dislike her, so why…!?"
"I don't like what I don't like.
She and I are entirely incompatible.
You feel the same, don't you?
You know there's no way we can get along, don't you, Senpai?"

entries.japanese:
「いえいえ、そんなコトはありませんよ。
たしかにお互い苦手なタイプみたいですけど、わたしはなんとか我慢できますから」
「「――――っ」」
　ザザッ、と有彦といっしょに身を引いた。
　……すごい。
　はっきりとケンカを売っている秋葉も秋葉だけど、それを笑顔で受け流す先輩も先輩だ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh, I wouldn’t say that. We do seem to be precisely the sort of people each other dislikes, but I think I can endure it.”
“――――!”
Arihiko and I recoil together.
Impressive.
Akiha openly picks the fight, and Ciel parries with a smile.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No, no, not at all.
Certainly we seem to be incompatible types, but I think I can somehow restrain myself."
""---Erk.""
Arihiko and I pull ourselves back.
…… Amazing.
Akiha spoiling for a fight is amazing, and Senpai's smiling face turning it aside is also amazing.

entries.japanese:
「ふうん……それって、つまりお互いのことは相殺しあいましょう、っていう提案なのかしら」
「てっとり早く言うとそうですね。
わたしが用があるのは秋葉さんじゃなくて遠野くんや乾くんですから」
　ばちばちばち、と二人の間で火花が散っている。
　古い言い方でいうと龍虎相搏つ、というヤツかもしれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I see, so you’re proposing that we simply cancel each other out.”
“That is the simplest way to put it. I came to see Tohno and Inui, not you.”
Sparks crackle between them.
To borrow an antique phrase, it is the clash of tiger and dragon.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hm.
So, you're suggesting we merely counterbalance each other, then?"
"To sum it up, yes.
My business is not with you, Akiha-san, but with Tohno-kun and Inui-kun."
Sparks crackle between the two of them.
It's like a face-off between a dragon and a tiger, as they used to say.

entries.japanese:
……結局、もう破滅的に（自称）相性が悪いシエル先輩と秋葉を囲んで、昼食がはじまってしまった。
「でも、遠野くんにこんな歳の近い妹さんがいるなんて知りませんでした。
わたし、てっきり遠野くんって一人っ子だと思ってましたから」
「……あれ？
　俺、前に先輩には妹がいるって話さなかったっけ」
「ええ、聞きましたよ。
遠野のお屋敷には妹さんが一人残っている、っていう話でしたよね」
　……？
　なんだ、やっぱり先輩は秋葉のことを前から知ってたんじゃないか。
entries.maoEnglish:
In the end, we start lunch gathered around Ciel and Akiha, whose self-professed incompatibility is already catastrophic.
“Still, I never knew Tohno had a sister so close to his own age. I had always assumed he was an only child.”
“Wait. Didn’t I tell you I had a sister?”
“You did. You said one younger sister remained at the Tohno estate.”
What?
Then she did know about Akiha already.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… At last, with the allegedly incompatible Ciel-senpai and Akiha, lunch began.
"But, I never knew Tohno-kun had a sister almost his age.
I always thought Tohno-kun was an only child."
"…… Huh?
Didn't I mention that I had a younger sister before?"
"Yes, I heard about a little sister living alone in the Tohno mansion."
…?
What, so she already knew about Akiha?

entries.japanese:
「私も兄さんにこんな知り合いがいるとは思いませんでした。
シエル先輩はいつからこの学園にいらっしゃるんですか？」
「ん？
　秋葉ちゃん、先輩は三年だからずっと前からいるぜ。
今年で卒業なのは残念だけどな」
「そうですか。
あまり制服慣れしていなさそうでしたので、私と同じように転校してきたのかと思いました」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Nor did I imagine my brother had an acquaintance like you. Ciel, how long have you attended this school?”
“Huh? She’s a third-year, Akiha, and has been here ages. Shame she’s graduating this year, though.”
“I see. You seemed so unaccustomed to the uniform that I assumed you had transferred here, as I did.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I did not know that Nii-san's friends were like you, either.
When did you join this school, Ciel-senpai?"
"Mm?
Akiha-chan, Senpai's been here for three years.
It's a shame that she graduates this year."
"Really.
She doesn't seem accustomed to the school uniform yet, so I thought she might have transferred from another school, like me."

entries.japanese:
「そうですねー、わたしもホントは秋葉さんみたいな制服が着たかったかなあ。
秋葉さん、その制服は前の学校のものですか？」
「ええ、こちらの学校の制服は好みじゃありませんから、前の学校のものを着ているんです」
　さらりと、秋葉はとんでもないコトを言ってのける。
　……そっか、てっきりまだ制服が出来てないのかなって思ったけど、初めっからうちの学校の制服を着る気はなかったんだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You know, I think I’d rather have worn a uniform like yours. Is that from your previous school, Akiha?”
“Yes; I dislike this school’s uniform, so I continue to wear my old one.”
Akiha delivers that outrageous statement as casually as the weather.
So that was it: I thought her new uniform simply wasn’t ready, but she had never intended to wear it at all.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah, yes… I really wanted to wear a uniform like Akiha-san's.
Akiha-san, is that the uniform of your last school?"
"Yes.
Since the uniform here isn't to my liking, I wear the uniform from my old school."
Akiha says such an outrageous thing casually.
…… I see.
I had assumed the uniform simply hadn't been made yet, but it seems she never intended to wear our school's uniform at all.

entries.japanese:
「はあ。
秋葉さん、どうも活発そうですからこっちのほうが似合うとは思いますよ。
ね、遠野くんはどう思います？」
「え？
　な、なにがですか？」
「ですから、秋葉さんの制服の話です。
どっちの制服が似合うかなって」
「……どっちの制服が似合うか、か……」
　そうだな、俺は―――
entries.maoEnglish:
“Well. You seem rather spirited, so I think this school’s uniform might suit you better. What do you think, Tohno?”
“Huh? Wh-what about?”
“Akiha’s uniform. Which one do you think suits her?”
“Which uniform suits her, huh?”
Well, I―――
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ahh.
Well, I think this one suits your level of activity well.
What do you think, Tohno-kun?"
"Eh?
Uh, about what?"
"About Akiha-san's uniform.
Which one would suit her better?"
"…… Which one suits her better, huh…"
I would have to say---

entries.japanese:
「……どうだろう。
俺は今のままの秋葉がいいと思うけど。
秋葉の髪ってキレイだからさ、あんまり明るい色彩の服には合わないと思うんだ」
「へえー、珍しいね、遠野が女のコの容姿を誉めるなんて。
っていうか、初めてじゃないか、それ」
「うるさいな、たんにそう思っただけだよ。
秋葉にはセーラー服のが似合うから、ブレザーはイヤだって言ってるだけだろ」
　ふーん、とにやにや笑いをする有彦。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I don’t know. I think Akiha looks best as she is. Her hair is beautiful, and I don’t think bright-colored clothes would suit it.”
“Well, look at that—Tohno complimenting a girl’s appearance! Is this a historic first?”
“Oh, shut up; I’m only saying what I think. A sailor uniform suits Akiha, and a blazer wouldn’t.”
Arihiko grins knowingly and hums in amusement.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I wonder.
I think Akiha looks good the way she is now.
Since she has such beautiful hair, I don't think bright colors would suit her."
"Hmm, that's rare, Tohno praising a woman's appearance like this.
First time, isn't it?"
"Shut up.
That's just what I think.
I'm saying the sailor suit suits her so I don't want her in a blazer."
"Hmm." Arihiko grins at me.

entries.japanese:
「――――あ」
　……しまった。
有彦に、のせられた。
　ちらりと秋葉を見ると、秋葉もなんだかそっぽを向いて黙っている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――Ah.”
Damn it. Arihiko baited me into that.
I glance at Akiha and find that she has turned her face away and fallen strangely silent.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----Ah."
…… Damn it, Arihiko got me.
Glancing over, Akiha seems to be silently looking the other way.

entries.japanese:
「なるほどねー、遠野に女っけがないワケだ。
そりゃあ秋葉ちゃんを毎日見てれば、うちの学校の女どもになんか目もくれないもんな――――って、げふぅうう！？」
「あ、ごめんなさい乾くん。
手、滑っちゃいました」
　有彦の横腹に肘鉄を鋭角に叩きこんで、シエル先輩はニコリと笑った。
　…………はあ。
　こんな胃に穴があきそうな時間を、あと十分近く過ごさないといけないのか…………。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Now I understand why Tohno never has a girl around. If you get to look at Akiha every day, of course you wouldn’t spare a glance for the girls at our school――――ghuuuh!?”
“Oh, I’m sorry, Inui. My arm slipped.”
Ciel smiles sweetly after driving an elbow at a sharp angle into Arihiko’s ribs.
Hah.
I still have nearly ten minutes of this stomach-destroying ordeal to survive.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I see… No wonder Tohno has no eye for women.
Because, after looking at Akiha-chan every day, the girls at our school must hardly compaaaaahhhhhh!!?"
"Ah, I'm sorry, Inui-kun.
My hand slipped."
Ciel-senpai laughs gently as she drives her elbow into Arihiko's side at a sharp angle.
…… Man.
I have to live through this stressful situation for almost ten more minutes…………

entries.japanese:
「わりとうちの制服のが合ってるんじゃないかな。
ほら、秋葉って大人しそうに見えて芯が強いからさ、無理して清楚な服を着る必要も―――」
「―――いや、まあ、イメージの払拭という事で、たまには明るい感じの服を着てもいいんじゃないかなって」
　……危ない危ない。
　うかつに下手な事は、口にしないほうが安全だ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Actually, our uniform might suit her better. Akiha looks quiet, but she has a will of iron, so there’s no reason to force herself into something so prim and proper―――”
“―――Or rather, a brighter outfit now and then might help soften that impression.”
That was close.
Much safer not to let careless opinions escape my mouth.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I think our school's uniform would match her well.
See, Akiha already looks mature enough, so you don't have to force her to wear such a prim and proper----"
"----Uh, well, maybe sweeping away the old image and a fresh change might be nice."
…… Danger!
Danger!
It would be better if I just don't force myself to say things too much.

entries.japanese:
「ふーん、そんなものかね。
そりゃあ秋葉ちゃんぐらいの美人なら、うちの野暮ったいブレザーでも似合うとは思うけど」
「あら。
乾さんはこの学校の制服がお嫌いなんですか？」
「んー、嫌いってわけじゃないけど、当たり前すぎて色気がないっていうか、つまんないっていうか。
うちの学校の女どものレベルじゃ制服の統一性に埋もれちまって、みんな同じ顔に見えるんだよな―――って、むはぁあああ！？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Huh, I guess so. A beauty like Akiha could probably make even our dowdy blazer look good.”
“Oh? You dislike this school’s uniform, Mister Inui?”
“Not dislike, exactly; it’s just ordinary, with no charm or excitement. The girls here don’t have enough personality to stand out through all that uniformity, so they end up looking exactly the same―――mwaagh!?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hm?
Is that how it is?
Well, Akiha-chan is a beauty, so I think even in a blazer she would look good."
"That's surprising.
Do you not like our school uniform, Inui-kun?"
"Hm, it's not that I don't like it, it just isn't sexy enough, or at least it's kind of bland.
When you get girls at the level they are in our school all in the same uniform, everyone will start to look the same and iiiooooooowww!?"

entries.japanese:
「あ、ごめんなさい乾くん。
手、滑っちゃいました」
　有彦の横腹に肘鉄を鋭角に叩きこんで、シエル先輩はニコリと笑った。
　…………気がめいる。
　こんな胃に穴があきそうな時間を、あと十分近く過ごさないといけないのか…………。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh, I’m sorry, Inui. My arm slipped.”
Ciel smiles sweetly after driving an elbow at a sharp angle into Arihiko’s ribs.
This is depressing.
I still have nearly ten minutes of this stomach-destroying ordeal to survive.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Oh, I'm sorry Inui-kun.
My hand slipped."
Ciel-senpai laughs gently as she drives her elbow into Arihiko's side at a sharp angle.
………… This is depressing.
I have to live through this stressful situation for almost ten more minutes…………

entries.japanese:
放課後になった。
　秋葉を迎えに一年の教室に行こう。
　……と、廊下に出たとたん、秋葉とバッタリ会った。
entries.maoEnglish:
Classes are over.
I should go meet Akiha outside the first-year classrooms.
The moment I step into the corridor, however, I run straight into her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
School ends.
Let's go meet Akiha at the first year classrooms.
…… But just as I leave the classroom, I run into her.

entries.japanese:
「あれ、兄さん。
どこかに行かれるんですか？」
「いや、これから秋葉を迎えに行こうと思ってたところだ。
そっちこそどこか寄っていくのか？」
「いえ、私は兄さんと帰ろうかなって、こっちに来てみたんですけど……」
「そうか、行き違わないでよかった。
それじゃ行こうか、琥珀さんたちが待ってる」
「そうですね。
家に帰りましょう、兄さん」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh, Brother. Were you going somewhere?”
“No, I was just coming to get you. Were you planning to stop somewhere on the way home?”
“I thought I might go home with you, Brother, so I came looking.”
“Good thing we didn’t miss each other, then. Let’s go; Kohaku and Hisui will be waiting.”
“Yes. Let’s go home, Brother.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah, Nii-san.
Are you going somewhere?"
"No, I was just on my way to get you.
What about you?
Are you on your way anywhere?"
"No.
I just thought I might go home with you, Nii-san, so I came here…"
"I see.
It's lucky we didn't miss each other.
Well then, let's go.
Kohaku-san and Hisui are waiting."
"You're right.
Let's go home, Nii-san."

entries.japanese:
「そうだ、秋葉に聞こうと思ったことがあった」
「私に聞きたいこと、ですか……？」
「ああ。
秋葉ってさ、どうして先輩のことをあんなに毛嫌いしてるんだよ。
もしかして顔見知りだったのか？」
「いえ、あの人とは昨日が初めてです。
私があの人を好きになれないのは生理的なものですから、兄さんには関係ありません」
「……生理的って、なんだいそれ」
「自分の感情では制御できない、という事です。
兄さんがお父様を嫌っていたのと同じようなものですから、あまり気にしないでください」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Right, there was something I wanted to ask you.”
“Something you wanted to ask me…?”
“Yeah. Why do you dislike Ciel so much? Did you two know each other before yesterday?”
“No, yesterday was the first time I met her. My aversion is instinctive, so it has nothing to do with you.”
“What do you mean by instinctive?”
“It means I cannot control how I feel. It is much like the way you disliked Father, so please do not concern yourself with it.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Oh, that's right, there's a question I've been wanting to ask you, Akiha."
"A question for me…?"
"Yeah.
Why did you have that dislike for Senpai?
Did you know her already, by any chance?"
"No, I met her for the first time yesterday.
My dislike for her is simply psychological, so you don't need to worry about it."
"Psychological?
What do you mean?"
"I mean, I can't control how I feel.
It's the same as how you felt about father, so please don't worry about it."

entries.japanese:
「―――あのな、秋葉。
俺は親父が苦手だっただけで、別に嫌ってはいなかったよ」
「私だってあの人のことが嫌いってわけじゃありません。
……まあ、今日のはたしかに言いすぎでした。
自分でも反省しているんですから、昼間の一件は大目に見てください」
「……そっか。
それならいいんだけど」
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――Now listen, Akiha. I may have found Father difficult, but I never hated him.”
“I don’t hate her either. Admittedly, I went too far today. I regret it, so please overlook what happened at lunch.”
“I see. Then I suppose it’s all right.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Hold on, Akiha.
I just disliked the old man, I didn't hate him."
"I don't hate her, either.
…… I suppose I exaggerated things today.
I'll reflect on it, so please look leniently upon the affair at lunchtime."
"…… Right.
I guess that's okay, then."

entries.japanese:
……まあ、そうゆうことなら問題はないかな。
　昼休みはシエル先輩が来る方が多いんだから、秋葉とシエル先輩の仲が悪いままでは困る。
　秋葉もこう言っているし、明日からは俺も有彦も横でハラハラしなくてすみそうだ―――
entries.maoEnglish:
Then I suppose there’s nothing to worry about.
Ciel joins us for lunch more often than not, so having her and Akiha at each other’s throats would be a problem.
If Akiha means what she says, perhaps Arihiko and I won’t have to sit there sweating bullets from tomorrow on―――
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Well, I guess it might not be a problem.
Ciel-senpai often comes by at lunch, so if relations between Akiha and her are bad, it'd be a problem.
At this rate, with Akiha saying things like this, me and Arihiko might not end up on pins and needles on the sidelines----

entries.japanese:
「――――ふう」
　鞄を机に放り投げて、ベッドに腰を下ろす。
　さて、どうしようか。
　秋葉は習い事があるそうで、帰ってくるなり車でどこかに出かけてしまった。
　……そういえば、琥珀さんも翡翠もなにやら忙しそうに屋敷の庭を歩いていたな。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――Whew.”
I toss my bag onto the desk and sit on the bed.
Now what?
Akiha had another lesson and left by car almost as soon as we got home.
Come to think of it, Kohaku and Hisui both looked busy as they crossed the garden.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----Ahh."
I toss my bag on the desk, and sit down on the bed.
Well, what should I do?
It seems Akiha has lessons, and as soon as we got back, she went somewhere by car.
…… That's right, Hisui and Kohaku-san were busily walking about too.

entries.japanese:
――――そうだな。
　いつもお世話になっているんだし、翡翠の手伝いをしにいこう。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――That settles it.
Hisui is always looking after me; I’ll go lend her a hand.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----That's right.
Since I'm always in her debt, I'll go and help Hisui out.

entries.japanese:
「ただいま翡翠。
忙しそうだけど何してるの？」
「あ―――お帰りなさいませ、志貴さま。
私でしたら、これから槙久さまのお部屋の整理をさせていただきます」
　翡翠の足元には何十という本が置かれている。
　本っていうのは、一冊一冊は軽いんだけどこれが十冊単位になるととたんに重くなる。
　翡翠の足元にある本は五十冊を優に超えている。
　とてもじゃないけど、翡翠の細腕でどうにかできるものとは思えない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’m home, Hisui. You look busy—what are you doing?”
“Ah―――welcome home, Master Shiki. I am about to put Master Makihisa’s room in order.”
Dozens of books lie at Hisui’s feet.
A single book weighs next to nothing, but stack ten together and the weight mounts quickly.
There must be well over fifty here.
There is no possible way Hisui’s slender arms can manage them all.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I'm home, Hisui, You look busy; what are you doing?"
"Ah---welcome home, Shiki-sama.
I am going to take these to Makihisa-sama's room."
Hisui is surrounded by dozens of books.
Though each of them is light, a dozen of them is pretty heavy.
There must be at least fifty books around her.
It's not too much, but I don't think Hisui's slender arms are up to the task.

entries.japanese:
「親父の部屋の整理、か―――たしか西館の一階だったよな」
　よっ、と本の束を抱える。
「いけません、志貴さま。
そのようなことは私が行いますから、どうかお部屋でお休みください」
「いいっていいって。
部屋にいても体が鈍るだけだしさ、こんなんじゃいつも世話してくれるお礼にもならないけど手伝わせてよ」
「ですが――――」
「……しっかし、重いなコレ。
秋葉のヤツも翡翠にこんな力仕事をまかせるなんて、何考えてるんだろうね」
「あ―――――」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Father’s room―――that was on the first floor of the west wing, wasn’t it?”
With a grunt, I gather up a stack of books.
“Please don’t, Master Shiki. This is my work, so please rest in your room.”
“It’s fine. Sitting around will only make me stiff, and though this barely begins to repay everything you do for me, at least let me help.”
“But――――”
“These really are heavy. What was Akiha thinking, leaving this kind of lifting to you?”
“Ah―――――”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"The old man's room, huh… that's on the west wing of the first floor, isn't it?"
Saying so, I pick up a pile of books.
"You must not, Shiki-sama.
I will take care of this, so you should go and rest in your room."
"It's fine, it's fine.
If I just lay around in my room my body'll go dull, so I thought I'd repay you by helping out a bit."
"However----"

"…… But these are heavy, aren't they?
What's Akiha thinking, making you do this kind of heavy labor?"
"Ah----"

entries.japanese:
「翡翠は先に親父の部屋に行っててよ。
本を持っていくからさ、翡翠は中の整理に専念してくれ。
適材適所っていうワケだし、それならいいだろ？」
「―――はい、それではお願いします、志貴さま」
　翡翠は申し訳なさそうに階段を昇っていく。
―――さて。
　こっちはこっちで、この本の山を二階に運ばなくちゃいけない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Go on ahead to Father’s room, Hisui. I’ll carry the books, and you can concentrate on arranging everything inside. Division of labor should make sense, right?”
“―――Very well, then I leave them in your care, Master Shiki.”
Looking apologetic, Hisui climbs the stairs.
―――Now, then.
That leaves me to haul this mountain of books up to the second floor.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"You go on to the old man's room; I'll bring the books, you can sort them out once they're there.
Everyone should work where they'll be the most use, right?"
"…… Yes.
Well then, please do, Shiki-sama."
Apologizing, Hisui goes up the stairs.
---Alright.
Now I've just got to get this mountain of books up to the second floor.

entries.japanese:
「へえ―――これが親父の部屋、か。
翡翠、ちょっと本とか見ていいかな」
「はい、鍵のかかっていないものならかまわないと思います」
　翡翠は運んできた本を本棚に入れていっている。
　ジャンル別に整頓しているのか、忙しく部屋の中を往復していた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“So―――this was Father’s room. Hisui, do you mind if I look through some of the books?”
“I believe you may examine anything that is not locked.”
Hisui shelves the books I carried in.
Apparently sorting them by subject, she moves briskly back and forth across the room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ohh… this is the old man's room, huh?
Hisui, is it okay if I take a look at some of the books?"
"Yes.
I think it is alright if they are not locked up."
Hisui is placing the books onto a bookshelf.
She's busily going back and forth, arranging the books by genre.

entries.japanese:
「……鍵のかかってないものって、机に鍵でもかかっているのかな」
　親父の机の引き出しに手をかける。
　引くと、がつん、と引っかかる感触。
「ほんとだ、鍵がかかってる」
　親父が死んだ後だっていうのに、一体なにを守っているんだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Anything that isn’t locked—does the desk have locks or something?”
I tug at one of Father’s desk drawers.
It catches with a hard clunk.
“It really is locked.”
What could it still be protecting now that Father is dead?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… What does she mean by locked up?
Maybe there's a lock on the desk drawer or something."
I take the handle of the drawer on the old man's desk.
As I pull, I feel a click.
"She's right, it is locked."
The old man's already dead, so what is it protecting?

entries.japanese:
「―――――」
　翡翠はこっちを見ていない。
　親父の机の上にはペーパーナイフが一つ。
　都合よく道具はそろっていたりした。
「…………………」
　少しだけメガネを下にズラして、机を視る。
「―――――そこ」
　音もなく鍵を切った。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――――”
Hisui isn’t looking.
A letter opener lies on Father’s desk.
Everything I need is conveniently at hand.
“……”
I lower my glasses just enough to see the desk.
“―――――There.”
Silently, I sever the lock.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-----"
Hisui isn't looking.
There's a letter opener on his desk.
It's the perfect opportunity.
"…………"
I lower my glasses a little, and look at the desk.
"-----There."
Silently, I cut the lock.

entries.japanese:
「―――なんだ、紙しか入ってないじゃないか」
　引き出しの中にあるのは古びた紙の束だった。
　どれ、と一枚だけ手にとって見てみる。
「あれ―――これ、うちの家系図だ」
　間違いない。
　遠野マキヒサの後には遠野シキ、遠野アキハという名前がある。
　あるけど―――
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――It’s only paper.”
The drawer contains a bundle of yellowed sheets.
I pick one up for a closer look.
“Wait―――this is our family tree.”
There is no mistaking it.
Beneath Makihisa Tohno are the names SHIKI Tohno and Akiha Tohno.
They are there, but―――
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---What, only papers?"
There's only a bundle of old papers in the drawer.
I take out a sheet and look at it.
"Huh?
This is… our family tree."
There's no mistake.
After Tohno MAKIHISA, the names Tohno SHIKI and Tohno AKIHA are written.
But there's---

entries.japanese:
「……うそ。
親父のヤツ、十年前に養子をとってる。
……あ、けどすぐに病死しちゃってるな」
　十年前っていえば、俺が小学一年生の頃だ。
　そんな大昔のことなら、覚えていないのも当然か。
「……けどうちの当主って、わりと短命なんだな。
親父も五十前に病死してるし、その前は三十歳の時に事故死してる。
……うわっ、その前なんか十八歳で自殺してるじゃないか」
――――いや、待て。
　いくらなんでも、これは、おかしい。
entries.maoEnglish:
“No way. Father adopted a child ten years ago. Oh, but the child died of an illness soon afterward.”
Ten years ago, I would have been in first grade.
No wonder I can’t remember something that old.
“The heads of our family don’t seem to live very long. Father died of illness before fifty, and the one before him died in an accident at thirty. God, the one before that killed himself at eighteen.”
――――No, wait.
This is too strange.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… No way.
That old man adopted a son ten years ago… ah, but he passed away shortly thereafter."
Ten years ago, that would mean I was just in elementary school.
That long ago, it's only natural that I wouldn't remember.
"But, the heads of the household have had pretty short lifespans.
My old man died before he was fifty, and before that, before thirty in an accident… Wow, before that, eighteen years of age, suicide…!?"
----No, wait a second.
No matter how you look at it, this is strange.

entries.japanese:
しっかりと家系図に目を通すと、遠野家の人間はみな異状な死に方をしていた。
　発狂死。
事故死。
他殺。
行方不明。
死産。
　……誰一人として、寿命で静かに他界したものがいない。
「な…………」
　その一連の記録は、呪われているとしか言いようがない。
　とくにその大半の死は発狂死。
自らの命を断つことで他界してしまっている。
entries.maoEnglish:
Reading the family tree carefully, I find that every member of the Tohno family met an unnatural end.
Death by madness. Accident. Murder. Disappearance. Stillbirth.
Not one of them died quietly of old age.
“What…”
There is no other word for this history but cursed.
Most of the deaths are attributed to madness. They ended their own lives.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Looking through the family tree, all members of the Tohno household have died strangely.
Madness.
Accidents.
Murder.
Disappearances.
Still birth.
…… Not one of them lived a long life or died peacefully.

"Wha…………"
This entire document is filled with horrible fates.
Even worse, most of the deaths are death by madness.
Taking one's own life.

entries.japanese:
「あ――――」
　視界から光が薄れていく。
　後頭部にぐらぐらと血液が溜まっていくような感じ。
　手足に力が入らなくなって、息が、できなくなるような、錯覚。
「志貴さま……！」
　翡翠……翡翠がかけよってきた。
　―――なんとか本棚に手をかけて、体を持ちなおす。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ah――――”
The light drains out of my sight.
It feels as though blood is pooling and swaying at the back of my skull.
Strength leaves my limbs, and I suffer the illusion that I can no longer breathe.
“Master Shiki…!”
Hisui—Hisui runs toward me.
―――I catch the bookcase and somehow steady myself.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah----"
The light seems to fade.
I feel as if blood is collecting in the back of my head.
My limbs feel weak, and breathing becomes impossible.
"Shiki-sama…!"
Hisui… Hisui runs toward me.
---Somehow I hold myself up, grabbing onto a bookshelf.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま！
　お気を確かに、志貴さま……！」
　心配そうな、翡翠の声。
　けど彼女の手は、決して俺の体には触れてこない。
「大丈夫―――ちょっと、吐き気がしただけだから」
「志貴さま、無理はしないでください……！
　どうぞ、椅子に座ってください。
そのように青い顔をなさっているのに、無理をして立っている必要なんかないでしょう……！？」
　……珍しい、な。
　翡翠が必死になって、俺に呼びかけてきてる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki! Please stay conscious, Master Shiki…!”
Hisui’s voice is full of concern.
But her hands never touch me.
“I’m all right―――I just felt a little sick.”
“Please don’t strain yourself, Master Shiki…! Sit down. You’re white as a sheet—there is no reason to force yourself to remain standing…!”
That’s unusual.
Hisui is pleading with me in earnest.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama!
Hold on, Shiki-sama…!"
Hisui's worrying voice.
But her hands never touch my body.
"It's alright… I just, felt a little sick for a moment, so…"
"Shiki-sama, please do not push yourself…!
Please, sit down.
As pale as your face is, you should not be trying to stand…!"
…… That's, new.
Hisui is becoming frantic, calling out to me.

entries.japanese:
「……うん……大丈夫、だから―――」
　なんとか意識を整える。
　それでも眩暈は納まらない。
　赤と黒が明滅する視界のなか。
　白い。
　ひどく温かそうな、翡翠のうなじが見えた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’m all right, so―――”
I struggle to pull my thoughts together.
But the dizziness won’t pass.
Red and black pulse across my vision.
White.
Hisui’s nape comes into view, looking terribly warm.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yeah… I'm okay… so…"
I try to regain my senses.
But the dizziness doesn't fade.
My vision flickers red and black.
White.
I gaze at the nape of Hisui's neck, a terribly warm white.

entries.japanese:
「―――――あ」
　なんて艶めかしい。
　この体がちゃんと動くんなら、俺は今すぐにでも翡翠の体を押さえつけて―――
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――――Ah.”
How alluring.
If my body would only move, I would pin Hisui down this instant and―――
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-----Ah."
It's captivating.
If my body could move properly, I would seize Hisui's body and----

entries.japanese:
さっきまで貧血で暗くなっていた視界が、一転して真っ赤に染まる。
　翡翠の、白い首筋。
　真っ赤だった、昨夜の夢。
―――殺人の夜の。
　心臓が飛び出しそうなほどの、痛い快感。
entries.maoEnglish:
The darkness of anemia vanishes, and my whole field of vision floods crimson.
Hisui’s white throat.
Last night’s dream, drenched in red.
―――The night of murder.
Pleasure so sharp and painful my heart seemed ready to tear free of my chest.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The black vision from my anemia all of sudden turns deep red.
Hisui's, white neck.
Last night's crimson dream.
---From the night of killing.
Painful pleasure, as if my heart would rip itself out.

entries.japanese:
「くっ―――――！」
　たまらなくなって、翡翠から逃げ出した。
「志貴さま……？」
「いや―――大丈夫―――大丈夫だから、一人にしてくれ」
「お断りします。
志貴さまは今のご自分の体をわかっていらっしゃいません。
そんな―――そんなお体の方を、一人にはできません」
　そうして、翡翠は近寄ってくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Damn―――――!”
Unable to bear it, I flee from Hisui.
“Master Shiki?”
“No―――I’m fine―――I’m fine, so leave me alone.”
“I cannot. Master Shiki does not understand the state he is in. I cannot leave someone in such―――such a condition alone.”
And Hisui comes closer.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Kuhh…!"
Unable to bear it, I pull back from Hisui.
"Shiki-sama…?"
"No… it's alright… I'm alright, so, just leave me alone."
"I refuse.
You do not seem to realize the state of your body, Shiki-sama.
With… with your body like this, I cannot leave you alone."
And Hisui approaches.

entries.japanese:
―――まずい。
　　　それは、恐い。
　そんな手の届く範囲にこられたら、自分がなにをしてしまうか解らなくて、恐い。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――This is bad.
It terrifies me.
If she comes within reach, I don’t know what I might do, and that terrifies me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Bad.
This is, bad.
If she comes within reach of my hands, I'm afraid I don't know what I'll do.

entries.japanese:
「いいから放っておいてくれ、翡翠……！」
「聞けません。
志貴さま、どうか落ちついてください」
　……だから、やめてくれ。
　近づいたら危ないのに。
　近づくなっていってるのに。
　どうして。
　どうして俺の言う事を聞かないんだ、この女。
―――なんで俺の邪魔をする。
　　　なんで俺の思い通りにならないんだ……！
entries.maoEnglish:
“Just leave me alone, Hisui…!”
“I cannot obey. Master Shiki, please calm yourself.”
Please stop.
It’s dangerous to come closer.
I told you not to.
Why?
Why won’t this woman do as I say?
―――Why are you getting in my way.
      Why won’t anything go the way I want…!
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I'm fine, so go, Hisui…!"
"I cannot listen to you.
Shiki-sama, please, calm down."
…… So, stop.
It's dangerous if you come near me.
I told you not to come near me.
Why.
Why won't this woman listen to me?
---Why does she get in my way.
Why does it never go the way I want…!

entries.japanese:
「うるさい……！
　近寄るなって言っているのがわからないのか、翡翠！」
「あ―――」
　だん、という鈍い音。
　翡翠は本棚に弾かれて、苦しそうに顔をゆがませている。
「あ―――」
　……その顔で、正気に戻れた。
　眩暈も急速に薄れていく。
　残ったのは眩暈でもなんでもなく、ただの罪悪感だけだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Shut up…! Don’t you understand me when I tell you to stay away, Hisui?”
“Ah―――”
A heavy crash.
Hisui rebounds against the bookcase, her face twisting in pain.
“Ah―――”
The sight of her face brings me to my senses.
The dizziness ebbs almost at once.
What remains has nothing to do with vertigo; it is only guilt.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shut up…!
Don't you understand I'm telling you to get away, Hisui!"
"Ah---"
A dull, thumping sound.
Hisui is thrown against the bookshelves, her face distorted in pain.
"Ah---"
…… Her expression causes my sanity to return.
The dizziness fades quickly.
After just a moment, all dizziness disappears, leaving only a feeling of guilt.

entries.japanese:
「――すまない。
俺は、何を――」
「―――――――――――――」
　翡翠はうつむいたまま、顔をあげない。
「―――翡翠、俺は―――すまない、自分でも、どうしてこんなコトをしたのか―――」
「申し訳ありません。
志貴さまの言いつけを守れず、志貴さまを不快にさせてしまいました」
「……違う、謝るのは俺のほうだ。
俺は翡翠に、ひどいことを、したんだから」
entries.maoEnglish:
“――I’m sorry. What did I――”
“―――――――――――――”
Hisui keeps her head bowed.
“―――Hisui, I―――I’m sorry, I don’t even know why I did that―――”
“I apologize. I disobeyed Master Shiki’s instruction and caused you distress, Master Shiki.”
“No, I’m the one who should apologize. I did something terrible to you.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"--I'm sorry.
What was… I…"
"-------------"
Hisui looks down, not meeting my gaze.
"---Hisui, I'm---I'm sorry, I don't know why I did such a thing…"
"I apologize.
I disobeyed your orders, and caused you discomfort."
"…… No, I'm the one who should apologize.
I did something horrible to you…"

entries.japanese:
「……志貴さま、どうかお部屋にお戻りください。
志貴さまはお疲れなんです。
体を休めれば、すぐに元通りになると思います」
「――――――」
　翡翠は顔をあげない。
「……わかった、部屋に戻るよ。
すまなかった、翡翠」
　返答はない。
　自己嫌悪で押しつぶされそうになりながら、部屋を後にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Please return to your room, Master Shiki. Master Shiki is exhausted. I believe rest will soon restore you to yourself.”
“――――――”
Hisui still won’t look up.
“All right, I’ll go back. I’m sorry, Hisui.”
She gives no answer.
Nearly crushed beneath my self-loathing, I leave the room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama, please return to your room.
You are tired; if you rest, I believe you will recover immediately."
"-----"
Hisui will not show me her face.
"…… I understand; I'll go back to my room.
I'm sorry, Hisui."
There's no answer.
I leave the room behind, being crushed by self-loathing.

entries.japanese:
―――夕食をすませて、部屋に戻ってくる。
　ベッドに倒れこんで翡翠の顔を思い出す。
「――――」
　わからない。
　なんであんな気分になって、あんな事をしてしまったのか。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――After dinner, I return to my room.
I fall onto the bed and see Hisui’s face again.
“――――”
I don’t understand.
I don’t know why that feeling came over me, or why I did such a thing.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---After dinner, I return to my room.
I fall on the bed, and remember Hisui's face.
"----"
I don't understand.
Why I felt that way, and why I did that.

entries.japanese:
あの時。
　俺は、翡翠の首筋を見て、欲情した。
　まるで昨日の夢のように、翡翠の首筋にかじりつきたいと思っていた。
　けど、今はそんな考えはこれっぽっちも浮かんでこない。
　昨夜の夢と、さっきの自分。
　自分の中に、自分でない自分がいるような、そんな感覚。
entries.maoEnglish:
At that moment.
The sight of Hisui’s throat aroused me.
Just as in last night’s dream, I wanted to fasten my teeth into it.
Yet now the thought holds no appeal at all.
Last night’s dream and the person I became today.
It feels as though someone who is not me lives inside me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Back then…
Looking at Hisui's neck, I was lusting.
Just like in last night's dream, I wanted to bite into her neck.
But, I can't even think about that right now.
Last night's dream, and myself a while ago.
I feel like there's someone inside me that isn't me.

entries.japanese:
「――――」
　首筋に手を当てる。
　吸血鬼にかまれた者は吸血鬼になる、という話。
「……そんな馬鹿な。
だって昼間でも歩いてられるじゃないか、俺」
　……そう、それは本当にありえない。
　あれは、たんに眩暈に襲われて、朦朧とした意識が見せた錯覚だ。
　弓塚との出来事が脳裏に焼き付いていて、それが貧血の時に思い出されるだけだと思う。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――”
I touch my throat.
They say anyone bitten by a vampire becomes one in turn.
“That’s absurd. I can walk around in broad daylight.”
Yes, it’s impossible.
Dizziness clouded my mind and showed me a hallucination, nothing more.
What happened with Yumizuka was burned into my memory, and the anemia merely brought it back.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----"
I touch my neck.
Those who are bitten by a vampire become vampires in turn, they say.
"…… That's stupid.
I'm walking around in the daytime, after all."
…… Yes, it's impossible.
It was just dizziness and my fading consciousness contributing to the imagination.
What happened with Yumizuka is burnt into my mind, so I think I just remember it when I suffer from anemia.

entries.japanese:
「翡翠の言うとおり、疲れてるのかな、俺」
　……そうかもしれない。
　さっさとぐっすり眠って、疲れた体を休めるとしよう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Maybe Hisui is right and I’m just exhausted.”
Perhaps so.
I should get a good night’s sleep and let my worn-out body recover.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Like Hisui said, maybe I'm just tired."
…… Perhaps.
I should hurry up and get to sleep, and rest my tired body.

entries.japanese:
――――一度昂ぶった体は、
　　　　　眠りなどでは治まらない。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――Once the body has been roused,
          sleep cannot quiet it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----My body, once aroused,
can't be calmed with something like sleep.

entries.japanese:
――――さあ。
　　　　今夜も、この渇きを癒しにいこう。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――Come, then.
        Tonight, too, let us go and slake this thirst.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----So.
Tonight too, I shall relieve my thirst.

entries.japanese:
夜の街に出たようだ。
　目を血走らせて、誰か通りかからないか待っているらしい。
entries.maoEnglish:
Apparently I’ve gone out into the sleeping city.
Eyes bloodshot, I seem to be waiting for someone to pass by.
entries.mirrorMoon:
It seems I went into town at night.
It seems like I'm waiting with bloodshot eyes for someone to pass by.

entries.maoEnglish: ――――Again.
entries.mirrorMoon: ----Again.

entries.japanese:
ふと、窓ガラスに映った顔が見えた。
　目は血走っていて、とても正気には見えなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
My face appears suddenly in a darkened window.
Its bloodshot eyes look anything but sane.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Suddenly, I see a face reflected in the window.
The eyes are bloodshot, and the face looks quite insane.

entries.japanese: ――――また、この夢。
entries.maoEnglish: ――――This dream again.
entries.mirrorMoon: ----This dream, again.

entries.japanese:
獲物を見つけたようだ。
　獲物が悲鳴をあげる間もなく、死んだという事さえ気付かせずに、仕留めてしまう。
entries.maoEnglish:
The prey seems to have been found.
It is killed before it can scream—before it can even realize that it has died.
entries.mirrorMoon:
It seems I found my prey.
I bring it down without a chance to scream, without it even realizing it has died.

entries.japanese: ――――またこの悪夢を、見せられる。
entries.maoEnglish: ――――I am being made to witness this nightmare again.
entries.mirrorMoon: ----I'm seeing this nightmare again.

entries.japanese:
死体を連れこんで、喉元に食らいつく音。
　じゅるじゅる、という音が聞こえる。
　喉もとから、肉ごとかみ切るように血を飲んで、喉の渇きを癒している。
entries.maoEnglish:
The corpse is dragged away, and teeth close on its throat.
I hear wet sucking.
Blood is swallowed straight from the neck, flesh torn away with it, until the thirst subsides.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Taking the dead body, and the sound of biting into the throat.
A gurgling sound.
Drinking the blood flowing out of the rended neck, my thirst is quenched.

entries.japanese: ――――昨日と同じ出来事。
entries.maoEnglish: ――――The same thing as yesterday.
entries.mirrorMoon: ----The same scene as last night.

entries.japanese: 血だけではあきたらず、死体の手の指を、一本一本噛み千切っていく。
entries.maoEnglish: Unsatisfied with blood alone, one finger after another is bitten from the corpse’s hand.
entries.mirrorMoon: Getting bored with just blood, I take the hand of the dead body and bite off the fingers one by one.

entries.japanese: ――――昨日と同じ出来事。
entries.maoEnglish: ――――The same thing as yesterday.
entries.mirrorMoon: ----The same scene as last night.

entries.japanese: 指だけではあきたらず、死体の手足を、一本一本噛み千切っていく。
entries.maoEnglish: Unsatisfied with fingers alone, one limb after another is bitten from the corpse.
entries.mirrorMoon: Getting bored with just the fingers, I take the limbs of the dead body, and bite them off one by one.

entries.japanese: ――――昨日と同じ出来事。
entries.maoEnglish: ――――The same thing as yesterday.
entries.mirrorMoon: ----The same scene as last night.

entries.japanese:
と。
　邪魔が、入った。
　死体を捨てて跳びあがる。
　誰か。
誰かが見ているようだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
Then.
An interruption.
The corpse is cast aside, and I leap away.
Someone. Someone is watching.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Then,
an obstruction appears.
I throw the dead body aside and jump.
Someone.
Someone is watching me.

entries.japanese: ――――昨日とは、違うのか。
entries.maoEnglish: ――――So tonight is different.
entries.mirrorMoon: ----Is it different from last night…?

entries.japanese:
なにか巨大な釘のようなモノが飛んでいる。
　それをかわすために跳びあがる。
　ビルの側面をかけあがって、屋上から屋上へ。
entries.maoEnglish:
Something like an enormous nail comes hurtling through the air.
I leap aside to avoid it.
I race up the face of a building and bound from rooftop to rooftop.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Something like a vast nail is flying through the air.
To dodge it, I leap aside.
I run up the side of a building, and jump from rooftop to rooftop.

entries.japanese: ――――黒い人影が、吸血鬼を追っていく。
entries.maoEnglish: ――――A black silhouette pursues the vampire.
entries.mirrorMoon: ----The figure in black chases the vampire.

entries.japanese:
屋根から屋根へ。
　闇から闇へ。
　人影は追ってくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
Roof to roof.
Darkness to darkness.
Still the figure follows.
entries.mirrorMoon:
From rooftop to rooftop.
From shadow to shadow.
The figure follows.

entries.japanese: ――――仕方ない。
entries.maoEnglish: ――――It can’t be helped.
entries.mirrorMoon: ----It can't be helped.

entries.japanese:
仕方あるまい、と呟いて。
　今夜の食事は終わりを告げた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“It can’t be helped,” someone murmurs,
and tonight’s meal comes to an end.
entries.mirrorMoon:
It can't be helped, it murmurs.
And tonight's meal ended.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま――――？」
 ────声がする。
「お気をたしかに。
お飲み物を持ってまいりますから……！」
 ────たたっ、と駆けていく足音。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki――――?”
────A voice reaches me.
“Please stay with me. I’ll bring you something to drink…!”
────Quick footsteps hurry away.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama----?"
----A voice.
"Please get a hold of yourself, I will bring you a drink right away…!"
----The sound of running footsteps.

entries.japanese:
「あ――――」
　暗い夢から、目が覚めた。
「……自分の部屋、だ」
　俺は紛れもなく自分の部屋にいる。
　ベッドで横になって、こうして朝を迎えている。
　……また、あの夢を見た。
　誰かの血を吸う夢。
　夢だって分かっているのに、ひどくリアルな夢。
　手には肉を引き千切る感触が残っていて、鼻にはまだ生臭い血の匂いが残留している―――
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ah――――”
I wake from the dark dream.
“My room.”
There can be no doubt that I am in my own room.
I am lying in bed, greeting the morning.
I dreamed it again.
A dream of drinking someone’s blood.
I know it was a dream, yet it was hideously real.
My hands still remember tearing flesh, and the raw smell of blood still clings inside my nose―――
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah----"
I awaken from the nightmare.
"…… My own room."
I am definitely in my own room.
Just lying in bed, and morning has come.
…… I saw that dream again.
The dream of sucking someone's blood.
Though I know it's just a dream, it still feels terribly real.
My hands retain the feel of ripping meat; my nose, the smell of fresh blood…

entries.japanese:
「―――どうなってるんだ、俺は」
　そっと首もとに触れてみた。
　……弓塚に噛まれた傷はとうに塞がっている。
　俺はまっとうな人間なままだ。
　誰かの血を飲みたいなんて思った事ないし、太陽の陽射しを疎ましいとも思わない。
「――――あ」
　違う。
昨日、俺は。
　翡翠の首筋を見て、なんて、思っただろう。
―――白い首筋。
　そこから流れる赤い血を、俺は心の底から欲しいと――――
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――What is happening to me?”
I touch my throat.
The wound where Yumizuka bit me has long since closed.
I am still an ordinary human being.
I have never wanted to drink anyone’s blood, and sunlight does not repel me.
“――――Ah.”
No. Yesterday was different. I―――
When I saw Hisui’s throat, what did I think?
―――A white throat.
From the bottom of my heart, I wanted the red blood that would flow from it――――
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---What's happening to me?"
I touch my neck gently.
…… Yumizuka's bite marks are long gone.
I'm still a normal human being.
I don't want to drink people's blood, and I don't have a problem with the sun.
"----Ah."
No.
Yesterday, I…
What did I think when I saw Hisui's neck?
---Her white neck.
From the bottom of my heart, I wanted to drink the blood flowing in there----

entries.japanese:
―――よし。
　いつもお世話になっているんだし、琥珀さんの手伝いをしに行こう。
「あれ……？」
　中庭に琥珀さんの姿は見当たらない。
　きょろきょろとあたりを見渡す。
　一瞬だけ、林のほうで琥珀さんの着物の色がちらついた。
「あっちにあるのは離れの屋敷か」
　……少し迷ったあと、琥珀さんの後を追っていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――All right.
Kohaku is always taking care of me; I’ll go lend her a hand.
“Huh…?”
Kohaku is nowhere in the courtyard.
I look around.
For a moment, I catch a glimpse of her kimono among the trees.
“That’s the detached house over there.”
After a moment’s hesitation, I follow her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----Alright.
I'm always in her debt, so I'll go help Kohaku-san.
"Huh……?"
I don't see her anywhere in the courtyard.
I glance around.
For just an instant, I see the color of her kimono in the forest.
"Is that where the detached building is?"
…… After a little internal debate, I follow after Kohaku-san.

entries.japanese:
琥珀さんはそのまま中に入っていった。
　ここまできて戻るのも馬鹿らしいので、思いきって中に入る事にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
Kohaku goes straight inside.
Turning back now would be ridiculous, so I summon my nerve and follow.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Kohaku-san continues and enters inside.
I would be pretty stupid if I came all the way here only to go back, so I force myself to go inside.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さん？
　どうしたんですか、こんな所までやってきて」
「いや、その―――琥珀さんの手伝いをしようと思って来たんだけど、迷惑でした？」
「志貴さん、お気持ちは嬉しいんですけど、わたしはお仕事をしにきたわけじゃないんですよ。
秋葉さまに言われて離れの電源を確かめにきただけなんです」
「えっ？
　電源って、この屋敷ってまだ使えるの？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Shiki? What brings you all the way out here?”
“Well―――I came to help you, but am I getting in the way?”
“The thought is very sweet, Shiki, but I didn’t come here to work. Miss Akiha asked me to check the power in the detached house.”
“The power? This place is still usable?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-san?
Why did you come here?"
"Um, well----I was thinking maybe I should give you a hand.
Am I in the way?"
"Shiki-san, I am happy you feel that way, but I didn't come here to work.
I only came here to check the electricity according to Akiha-sama's orders."
"Eh?
Electricity?
This place is still used?"

entries.japanese:
「ええ、電源が生きているのはこの部屋だけですけど、一応はまだ人が住める環境を保っていますよ。
お風呂も使えますし、お布団だって用意してありますから」
「へえ、そうなんだ。
……けどここ、随分前から使ってないんだろ？
　なんだってそんなふうにしてあるんだろう」
「そうですね、きっと秋葉さまも未練が残っているのかもしれません。
ここは昔、槙久さまが養子にとった子供の住居でもありますから」
――――は？
　槙久……親父が昔、養子にとっていた、子供？
entries.maoEnglish:
“Yes, only this room still has electricity, but the house remains fit to live in. The bath works, and we keep bedding ready.”
“Huh, I see. But no one has used this place for years, have they? Why keep it like this?”
“Perhaps Miss Akiha still feels attached to it. This was once the home of a child Master Makihisa adopted.”
――――What?
A child Makihisa—my father—once adopted?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yes, this is the only room with electricity.
This building is still maintained at a level for people to live in.
The bath is still able to be used and there are futons ready."
"Really?
But this place hasn't been used for a while, right?
Why is it maintained like that?"
"Let's see, maybe Akiha-sama is just fond of this place.
A long time ago, this was where Makihisa-sama's adopted child used to live."
----Huh?
Makihisa…… my old man, adopted a child… a long time ago?

entries.japanese:
「……ちょっと待って琥珀さん。
その、親父が養子をとったって、どういう事だ」
「あら、憶えてないんですか？
　十年ほど前に槙久さまが引き取られた子供がいたじゃないですか。
両親を事故で亡くしてしまったとかで、槙久さまが養子になさったんです」
「そんな―――こと、あった、っけ」
「はい。
もっとも二年ほどで亡くなられてしまったんです。
些細な事故だったらしいんですけど、お屋敷に勤めていた使用人の人たちはやっぱり遠野の家は呪われてるんだとか、よく口にしていましたから」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Wait, Kohaku. What do you mean Father adopted a child?”
“Oh, don’t you remember? About ten years ago, Master Makihisa took in a child whose parents had died in an accident. Master Makihisa adopted the child.”
“Did―――that really happen?”
“Yes. Sadly, the child died about two years later. It was only a minor accident, apparently, but the servants employed here then often said it proved the Tohno family was cursed.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Wait a sec, Kohaku-san.
My old man adopted a child?"

"Oh, you don't remember?
About ten years ago, he brought a child here.
His parents both died in an accident, so he adopted the child."
"That---happened?"
"Yes.
But two years later, the child passed away.
It was a trivial accident, but a lot of the servants began to say that the Tohno family was cursed."

entries.japanese:
―――――ちょっと、待って。
　なにか……琥珀さんの言葉は、恐い。
　聞いているだけで視界がぐにゃりと歪む。
　まるでこの和室が飴で出来ているみたいに、どろどろと溶けていくような、不安定さ。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――――Wait.
Something about Kohaku’s words frightens me.
Just hearing them makes my sight buckle.
The tatami room seems made of candy, melting into a syrupy blur around me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
-----Wait a minute.
Something about her words seems scary.
Just hearing them, my vision starts to warp.
It's like the whole room is made entirely of dissolving sugar.

entries.japanese:
「こ、琥珀、さん」
　十年前にとられた養子。
二年後に事故死したという養子。
　つまり、それは。
　八年前――――俺が事故にあって、入院した年じゃない、のか。
entries.maoEnglish:
“K-Kohaku.”
Adopted ten years ago. Killed in an accident two years later.
That means.
Eight years ago――――the year I had my accident and was hospitalized.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ko, Kohaku, san."
A child adopted ten years ago.
Two years later, the child died.
In other words, eight years ago… That's when I had my accident and was sent to the hospital.

entries.japanese:
――――――事故。
　それはどんな事故だ。
　俺が大怪我をするぐらいの事故。
　その養子とやらが、死んでしまうぐらいの、事故。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――――The accident.
What kind of accident was it?
One that injured me so badly.
One that killed that adopted child.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Accident.
What kind of accident was it?
An accident that seriously wounded me.
An accident, that the adopted child was killed in?

entries.japanese:
夏の暑い日。
――――――よく思い出せない。
　ただあの時、俺の腕は、赤い血にまみれていたような――――
entries.maoEnglish:
A sweltering summer day.
――――――I can’t remember.
Only that my arms seemed to be covered in red blood—
entries.mirrorMoon:
A hot summer day.
---I can't remember.
All I know is at that time, my arms seemed to be soaked in blood----

entries.japanese:
「琥珀、さん。
呪われてるって、どういう、こと」
「いえ、別にそう大した事じゃないんですよ。
ただ遠野家の方々は、代々早くにお亡くなりになっているだけです。
　ただそれが事故死であったり自殺であったり病死であったり、みなさん天寿をまっとうするようなカタチではないので呪われている、と噂されただけです」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Kohaku… What do you mean, cursed?”
“Oh, it’s nothing so dramatic. Members of the Tohno family have simply tended to die young, generation after generation.
Whether by accident, suicide, or illness, none lived out a natural span; that is all that gave rise to the rumor of a curse.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Kohaku, san.
You said 'cursed'?"
"No, it isn't anything important.
It is just that a lot of the members of the Tohno family have died young.
Such as in accidents, or suicide, or illness; a curse that does not allow them a natural death.
Well, that was the rumor, anyway."

entries.japanese:
「―――自殺って……なに、それ」
「はい。
なんでも遠野家の方……男性に多いのだそうですけど、幼いころから精神を病んでしまって、成人してから自殺なさってしまった方が十人以上いるそうなんです。
　あくまで噂話なんですけど、戦前には殺人の罪を犯してしまった方もいらっしゃったとか」
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――Suicide, what do you mean?”
“They say members of the Tohno family—mostly the men—often developed mental illnesses in childhood. More than ten went on to kill themselves as adults.
It is only gossip, of course, but supposedly one man even committed murder before the war.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----Suicide…… what?"
"Yes.
Whatever the case, the members of the Tohno family…… mostly male, carried some mental illness and committed suicide when they became adults.
These are just stubborn rumors, but it is said some of them were murderers before the war."

entries.japanese:
……精神を病んでいる？
　……殺人の、罪？
　……例えば、毎夜人を殺すユメを見たり？
　……例えば、毎夜人を殺すユメに憧れたり？
entries.maoEnglish:
Mental illness?
The crime of murder?
Does that include dreaming of killing people every night?
Longing for those dreams every night?
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Mental illness?
…… Murderers?
…… Such as, seeing dreams of killing people every night?
…… Such as, feeling a sense of longing as I see dreams of killing people every night?

entries.japanese:
「琥珀さん、それは―――」
「あ、申し訳ありません。
こんな、遠野の家をおとしめるような噂話なんかしちゃって」
「いや、いいんだ。
いいから……もう少し、詳しい話をしてくれないか、琥珀さん」
「……かまいませんけど、わたしも詳しく知っているわけではないんです。
ただ、その……槙久さまには、たしかにそういう気がありました」
「親父―――親父が？」
　ぐらり、と。
　視界が、回転していく。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Kohaku, does that mean―――”
“Oh, I’m sorry. I shouldn’t be repeating rumors that disparage the Tohno family.”
“No, it’s all right. Please, Kohaku, tell me a little more.”
“If you like, though I don’t know all the details. But―――Master Makihisa certainly had those tendencies.”
“Father―――Father did?”
The world lurches.
My vision begins to spin.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Kohaku-san, that---"
"Oh, I'm very sorry.
Those are just dark rumors about the Tohno family."
"No, that's fine.
It's okay…… could you tell me in more detail, Kohaku-san?"
"…… I do not mind, but I do not necessarily know all the details.
Just that, well…… Makihisa-sama did have that kind of air about him."
"My old man----my old man did?"
Blurring.
My vision whirls around.

entries.japanese:
「はい。
槙久さまがお亡くなりになる二年前から、わたしは槙久さまの容体を管理させていただいておりました。
　……志貴さんを有間の家に預けた頃から槙久さまはひどく落ち込むようになってしまわれて、精神を安定させるお薬を服用しなければならなかったんです」
「精神を安定させる薬って―――親父はそんなにひどかったのか、琥珀さん」
「……はい。
夜になると屋敷の庭を出歩くようになって、その日に買ってきた犬や猫を殺してしまわれたり、ご自分のお体を傷つけたりするのは珍しい事ではなかったほどです」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Yes. For the final two years of Master Makihisa’s life, I was entrusted with managing Master Makihisa’s condition.
After Master Makihisa sent you to live with the Arima family, he fell into a severe depression and had to take medicine to steady his mind.”
“Medicine to steady his mind―――was Father really that unwell, Kohaku?”
“Yes. At night he would wander the grounds; it was not unusual for him to kill dogs or cats he had bought that day, or to injure himself.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yes.
I took care of Makihisa-sama's condition two years before he passed away.
…… While you were living with the Arima family, Makihisa-sama would become very depressed and I would have to prepare his medicine to calm him."

"Medicine to calm him----was my old man that bad, Kohaku-san?"
"…… Yes.
It would not be uncommon for him to walk into the garden at night and kill the pet dogs and cats, or to hurt his own body."

entries.japanese:
――――な。
　なんだ、それは。
　それじゃほとんど狂ってる。
　ユメのなかの俺みたいに、正気じゃない。
　……いや、それとも。
　俺のほうが、親父みたいに、正気じゃないのか。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――Wha.
What was that?
That was practically madness.
As mad as I am in the dream.
Or else.
Am I the one who has gone mad, just like Father?
entries.mirrorMoon:
----Wha-
What is this?
That's pretty much crazy.
As crazy as I am in my dreams.
…… No, that is backwards.
Am I crazy just like my old man?

entries.japanese:
「志貴さん……！？」
　……琥珀さんの声が聞こえる。
　俺は―――いつのまにか、畳に膝をついていた。
「志貴さん、顔が真っ青じゃないですか！
　体調が悪いのでしたら、お部屋で休んでないとダメです……！」
　言いながら、琥珀さんは肩をかしてくれる。
　それに助けられて立ちあがる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Shiki…!?”
Kohaku’s voice reaches me.
Before I know it―――my knees are on the tatami.
“Shiki, you’re white as a sheet! If you’re ill, you should be resting in your room…!”
As she speaks, Kohaku offers me her shoulder.
With her support, I rise.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-san……!?
…… I hear Kohaku-san's voice.
I---don't know when it happened, but I'm on my knees on the tatami floor.
"Shiki-san, you look terrible.
If you are feeling poorly, you should rest in your room……!"
Kohaku-san says this as she grabs my shoulder.
With her help, I can stand.

entries.japanese:
「……うん……大丈夫、だから―――」
　なんとか意識を整える。
　それでも眩暈は治まらない。
　赤と黒が明滅する視界のなか。
　白い。
　ひどく温かそうな、琥珀、さん、のうなじが見えた。
「―――――あ」
　なんて艶めかしい。
　この体がちゃんと動くんなら、俺は今すぐにでも琥珀の体を押さえつけて―――
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’m all right, so―――”
I struggle to pull my thoughts together.
But the dizziness won’t pass.
Red and black pulse across my vision.
White.
Kohaku’s nape comes into view, looking terribly warm.
“―――――Ah.”
How alluring.
If my body would only move, I would pin Kohaku down this instant and―――
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Yeah…… I'm fine, so---"
I am somehow able to focus again.
But I am still dizzy.

In the red and white swirl of my vision,
white.
Kohaku… san's… terribly warm… looking neck.
"------Ah."
How captivating.
If my body could move properly, I would seize Kohaku's body and----

entries.japanese:
さっきまで貧血で暗くなっていた視界が、一転して真っ赤に染まる。
　琥珀の、白い首筋。
　真っ赤だった、昨夜の夢。
――――――殺人の夜の。
　心臓が飛び出しそうなほどの、痛い快感。
entries.maoEnglish:
The darkness of anemia vanishes, and my whole field of vision floods crimson.
Kohaku’s white throat.
Last night’s dream, drenched in red.
――――――The night of murder.
Pleasure so sharp and painful my heart seemed ready to tear free of my chest.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The black vision from my anemia all of sudden turns deep red…
Kohaku's white neck.
Last night's crimson dream.
------The nighttime killings.
Painful pleasure, as if my heart would rip itself out.

entries.japanese:
「くっ―――――！」
　たまらなくなって、琥珀さんから逃げ出した。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Damn―――――!”
Unable to bear it, I flee from Kohaku.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Gg------!"
Unable to bear it, I pull away from Kohaku-san.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さん……？」
「いや―――大丈夫―――大丈夫だから、一人にしてくれ」
「だめです。
ここで志貴さんに倒られてはわたしが秋葉さまに叱られちゃいます。
第一、志貴さん苦しそうじゃないですか」
　言って、琥珀さんは近づいてくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Shiki?”
“No―――I’m fine―――I’m fine, so leave me alone.”
“I can’t do that. If you collapse here, Miss Akiha will scold me. Besides, you’re clearly suffering.”
With that, Kohaku comes closer.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-san……?"
"No----I'm fine----I'm fine, so leave me alone."
"That won't do.
If you collapse here, Akiha-sama will get very angry.
In the first place, you look like you are in a lot of pain."
Kohaku-san says this and draws closer.

entries.japanese:
――――――まずい。
　それは、恐い。
　そんな手の届く範囲にこられたら、自分がなにをしてしまうか解らなくて、恐い。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――――This is bad.
It terrifies me.
If she comes within reach, I don’t know what I might do, and that terrifies me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
------This isn't good.
It's scary.
If she comes within reach of my hands, I'm afraid I don't know what I'll do.

entries.japanese:
「―――いいから放っておいてくれ、琥珀、さん」
「だめですっ。
志貴さん、どうか落ちついてください」
　……だから、やめてくれ。
　近づいたら危ないのに。
　近づくなっていってるのに。
　どうして。
　どうして俺の言う事を聞かないんだ、この女。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――Just leave me alone, Kohaku.”
“No. Shiki, please calm down.”
Please stop.
It’s dangerous to come closer.
I told you not to.
Why?
Why won’t this woman do as I say?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----I'm fine, just leave me alone, Kohaku… san…"
"I can't.
Shiki-san, please calm down."
…… Please, stop.
It's dangerous if you come near me.
I told you not to come near me.
Why?
Why won't this woman listen to me?

entries.japanese:
―――なんで。
　　　なんで俺の邪魔をする。
　　　なんでこう、
　　　俺の思い通りにならないんだ……！
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Why?
Why are you getting in my way.
      Why is it that
      nothing will go the way I want…!
entries.mirrorMoon:
----Why?
Why are you getting in my way?
Why are you like this,
Not doing what I want you to……!?

entries.japanese:
「うるさい……！
　近寄るなって言っているのがわからないのか、琥珀！」
「きゃっ―――！」
　だん、という鈍い音。
　琥珀さんは壁に弾かれて、苦しそうに顔をゆがませている。
「あ―――――――」
　……その顔で、正気に戻れた。
　眩暈も急速に薄れていく。
　残ったのは眩暈でもなんでもなく、ただの罪悪感だけだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Shut up…! Don’t you understand me when I tell you to stay away, Kohaku?”
“Eek―――!”
A heavy crash.
Kohaku rebounds against the wall, her face twisting in pain.
“Ah―――――――”
The sight of her face brings me to my senses.
The dizziness ebbs almost at once.
What remains has nothing to do with vertigo; it is only guilt.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shut up……!
Don't you understand I'm telling you to get away, Kohaku!"
"Kyaa----!"
Thud, a thick sound.
Kohaku-san slams into the wall, her face distorting in pain.
"Ah-------"
…… Her expression causes my sanity to return.
The dizziness fades quickly.
After just a moment, all dizziness disappears, leaving only a feeling of guilt.

entries.japanese:
「――ごめん。
俺は、何を――」
「いいんです、お気になさらないでくださいな。
志貴さんのご機嫌が悪い時に、出過ぎた真似をしただけですから」
　ニコリ、と。
　いつも通りに、彼女は笑った。
「顔色も良くなりましたし、もう大丈夫のようですね。
それじゃあもう少しお話を続けましょうか？」
「いや――今日はもういい。
ごめん、琥珀さん。
俺、どうかしてる」
entries.maoEnglish:
“――I’m sorry. What did I――”
“It’s quite all right; please don’t trouble yourself. I only overstepped while you were in a temper, that’s all.”
A smile.
She smiles as she always does.
“Your color has returned, so you seem to be all right now. Shall we continue our conversation?” “No―――not today. I’m sorry, Kohaku. There’s something wrong with me.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"--Sorry.
What was… I…"
"It is okay, please do not worry about it.
I only provoked you when you were in a bad mood."
She gives her usual smile.
"You are no longer pale and seem to have recovered.
Shall we continue our conversation?"
"No--that's enough for today.
Sorry Kohaku-san.
There's, something wrong with me."

entries.japanese:
「そうですか？
　志貴さんは男の人なんですから、ちょっと乱暴でもどうかしてはいないと思いますけど。
普段の志貴さんは大人しすぎるんですよ、きっと」
　琥珀さんは笑顔のままで言う。
「……………っ」
　そんな笑顔を向けられると、胸が痛い。
　……琥珀さんは俺のことを信用しきっている。
　だっていうのに俺は、たった今、この人に対してなにをしようとしていたんだろう―――？
entries.maoEnglish:
“Do you think so? You’re a man, Shiki; a little roughness hardly means there’s something wrong with you. If anything, you’re usually too gentle.”
Kohaku says it without losing her smile.
“…!”
That smile makes my chest ache.
She trusts me completely.
And only moments ago, what was I about to do to her―――?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Oh?
You are a man, so I don't think it is unnatural to be a little rough.
In fact, I think you are usually too calm, Shiki-san."
She says that, smiling.
"………………"
Seeing that smile makes my chest hurt.
…… Kohaku-san trusts me.
But what was I about to do to her just earlier----?

entries.japanese:
「……琥珀さんの言うとおり、部屋に戻ります。
さっきは、すみませんでした」
　言って、逃げ出した。
　自己嫌悪で押しつぶされそうになりながら、離れの屋敷を後にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’ll take your advice and go back to my room. I’m sorry about what happened.”
With that, I flee.
Nearly crushed beneath my self-loathing, I leave the detached house.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Like you say, Kohaku-san, I will go back to my room.
I really am sorry about earlier."
I say this and run away.
I leave the detached building behind, being crushed by self-loathing.

entries.japanese:
―――夕食をすませて、部屋に戻ってくる。
　ベッドに倒れこんで琥珀さんの顔を思い出す。
「――――」
　わからない。
　なんであんな気分になって、あんな事をしてしまったのか。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――After dinner, I return to my room.
I fall onto the bed and see Kohaku’s face again.
“――――”
I don’t understand.
I don’t know why that feeling came over me, or why I did such a thing.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---After dinner, I return to my room.
I collapse on my bed and remember Kohaku-san's face.
"----"
I don't understand.
Why I felt that way, and why I did that.

entries.japanese:
あの時。
　俺は、琥珀さんの首筋を見て、欲情した。
　まるで昨日の夢のように、琥珀さんの首筋にかじりつきたいと思っていた。
　けど、今はそんな考えはこれっぽっちも浮かんでこない。
　昨夜の夢と、さっきの自分。
　自分の中に、自分でない自分がいるような、そんな感覚。
entries.maoEnglish:
At that moment.
The sight of Kohaku’s throat aroused me.
Just as in last night’s dream, I wanted to fasten my teeth into it.
Yet now the thought holds no appeal at all.
Last night’s dream and the person I became today.
It feels as though someone who is not me lives inside me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Back then…
Looking at Kohaku-san's neck, I was lusting.
Just like in last night's dream, I wanted to bite into her neck.
But, I can't even think about that right now.
Last night's dream, and myself a while ago.
I feel like there's someone inside me that isn't me.

entries.japanese:
「――――」
　首筋に手を当てる。
　吸血鬼にかまれた者は吸血鬼になる、という話。
「……そんな馬鹿な。
だって昼間でも歩いてられるじゃないか、俺」
　……そう、それは本当にありえない。
　あれは、たんに眩暈に襲われて、朦朧とした意識が見せた錯覚だ。
　弓塚との出来事が脳裏に焼き付いていて、それが貧血の時に思い出されるだけだと思う。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――”
I touch my throat.
They say anyone bitten by a vampire becomes one in turn.
“That’s absurd. I can walk around in broad daylight.”
Yes, it’s impossible.
Dizziness clouded my mind and showed me a hallucination, nothing more.
What happened with Yumizuka was burned into my memory, and the anemia merely brought it back.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----"
I touch my neck.
Those who are bitten by a vampire become vampires in turn, they say.
"…… That's stupid.
I'm walking around in the daytime, after all."
…… Yes, it's impossible.
It was just dizziness and my fading consciousness contributing to the imagination.
What happened with Yumizuka is burnt into my mind, so I think I just remember it when I suffer from anemia.

entries.japanese:
「琥珀さんの言うとおり、疲れてるのかな、俺」
　……そうかもしれない。
　さっさとぐっすり眠って、疲れた体を休めるとしよう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Maybe Kohaku is right and I’m just exhausted.”
Perhaps so.
I should get a good night’s sleep and let my worn-out body recover.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Like Kohaku-san said, maybe I'm just tired."
…… Perhaps.
I should hurry up and get to sleep, and rest my tired body.

entries.japanese:
――――一度昂ぶった体は、
　　　　　眠りなどでは治まらない。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――Once the body has been roused,
          sleep cannot quiet it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----My body, once aroused,
can't be calmed with something like sleep.

entries.japanese:
――――さあ。
　　　　今夜も、この渇きを癒しにいこう。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――Come, then.
        Tonight, too, let us go and slake this thirst.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----So.
Tonight too, I shall relieve my thirst.

entries.japanese:
夜の街に出たようだ。
　目を血走らせて、誰か通りかからないか待っているらしい。
entries.maoEnglish:
Apparently I’ve gone out into the sleeping city.
Eyes bloodshot, I seem to be waiting for someone to pass by.
entries.mirrorMoon:
It seems I went into town at night.
It seems like I'm waiting with bloodshot eyes for someone to pass by.

entries.maoEnglish: ――――Again.
entries.mirrorMoon: ----Again.

entries.japanese:
ふと、窓ガラスに映った顔が見えた。
　目は血走っていて、とても正気には見えなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
My face appears suddenly in a darkened window.
Its bloodshot eyes look anything but sane.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Suddenly, I see a face reflected in the window.
The eyes are bloodshot, and the face looks quite insane.

entries.japanese: ――――また、この夢。
entries.maoEnglish: ――――This dream again.
entries.mirrorMoon: ----This dream, again.

entries.japanese:
獲物を見つけたようだ。
　獲物が悲鳴をあげる間もなく、死んだという事さえ気付かせずに、仕留めてしまう。
entries.maoEnglish:
The prey seems to have been found.
It is killed before it can scream—before it can even realize that it has died.
entries.mirrorMoon:
It seems I found my prey.
I bring it down without a chance to scream, without it even realizing it has died.

entries.japanese: ――――またこの悪夢を、見せられる。
entries.maoEnglish: ――――I am being made to witness this nightmare again.
entries.mirrorMoon: ----I'm seeing this nightmare again.

entries.japanese:
死体を連れこんで、喉元に食らいつく音。
　じゅるじゅる、という音が聞こえる。
　喉もとから、肉ごとかみ切るように血を飲んで、喉の渇きを癒している。
entries.maoEnglish:
The corpse is dragged away, and teeth close on its throat.
I hear wet sucking.
Blood is swallowed straight from the neck, flesh torn away with it, until the thirst subsides.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Taking the dead body, and the sound of biting into the throat.
A gurgling sound.
Drinking the blood flowing out of the rended neck, my thirst is quenched.

entries.japanese: ――――昨日と同じ出来事。
entries.maoEnglish: ――――The same thing as yesterday.
entries.mirrorMoon: ----The same scene as last night.

entries.japanese: 血だけではあきたらず、死体の手の指を、一本一本噛み千切っていく。
entries.maoEnglish: Unsatisfied with blood alone, one finger after another is bitten from the corpse’s hand.
entries.mirrorMoon: Getting bored with just blood, I take the hand of the dead body and bite off the fingers one by one.

entries.japanese: ――――昨日と同じ出来事。
entries.maoEnglish: ――――The same thing as yesterday.
entries.mirrorMoon: ----The same scene as last night.

entries.japanese: 指だけではあきたらず、死体の手足を、一本一本噛み千切っていく。
entries.maoEnglish: Unsatisfied with fingers alone, one limb after another is bitten from the corpse.
entries.mirrorMoon: Getting bored with just the fingers, I take the limbs of the dead body, and bite them off one by one.

entries.japanese: ――――昨日と同じ出来事。
entries.maoEnglish: ――――The same thing as yesterday.
entries.mirrorMoon: ----The same scene as last night.

entries.japanese:
と。
　邪魔が、入った。
　死体を捨てて跳びあがる。
　誰か。
誰かが見ているようだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
Then.
An interruption.
The corpse is cast aside, and I leap away.
Someone. Someone is watching.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Then,
an obstruction appears.
I throw the dead body aside and jump.
Someone.
Someone is watching me.

entries.japanese: ――――昨日とは、違うのか。
entries.maoEnglish: ――――So tonight is different.
entries.mirrorMoon: ----Is it different from last night…?

entries.japanese:
なにか巨大な釘のようなモノが飛んでいる。
　それをかわすために跳びあがる。
　ビルの側面をかけあがって、屋上から屋上へ。
entries.maoEnglish:
Something like an enormous nail comes hurtling through the air.
I leap aside to avoid it.
I race up the face of a building and bound from rooftop to rooftop.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Something like a vast nail is flying through the air.
To dodge it, I leap aside.
I run up the side of a building, and jump from rooftop to rooftop.

entries.japanese: ――――黒い人影が、吸血鬼を追っていく。
entries.maoEnglish: ――――A black silhouette pursues the vampire.
entries.mirrorMoon: ----The figure in black chases the vampire.

entries.japanese:
屋根から屋根へ。
　闇から闇へ。
　人影は追ってくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
Roof to roof.
Darkness to darkness.
Still the figure follows.
entries.mirrorMoon:
From rooftop to rooftop.
From shadow to shadow.
The figure follows.

entries.japanese: ――――仕方ない。
entries.maoEnglish: ――――It can’t be helped.
entries.mirrorMoon: ----It can't be helped.

entries.japanese:
仕方あるまい、と呟いて。
　今夜の食事は終わりを告げた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“It can’t be helped,” someone murmurs,
and tonight’s meal comes to an end.
entries.mirrorMoon:
It can't be helped, it murmurs.
And tonight's meal ended.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま――――？」
 ────声がする。
「お気をたしかに。
今お飲み物を持ってまいりますから……！」
 ────たたっ、と駆けていく足音。
「あ――――」
　暗い夢から、目が覚めた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki――――?”
────A voice reaches me.
“Please stay with me. I’ll bring you something to drink right away…!”
────Quick footsteps hurry away.
“Ah――――”
I wake from the dark dream.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama----?"
----A voice.
"Please get a hold of yourself, I will bring you a drink right away…!"
----The sound of running footsteps.

"Ah----"
I awaken from the nightmare.

entries.japanese:
「……自分の部屋、だ」
　俺は紛れもなく自分の部屋にいる。
　ベッドで横になって、こうして朝を迎えている。
　……また、あの夢を見た。
　誰かの血を吸う夢。
　夢だって分かっているのに、ひどくリアルな夢。
　手には肉を引き千切る感触が残っていて、鼻にはまだ生臭い血の匂いが残留している―――
entries.maoEnglish:
“My room.”
There can be no doubt that I am in my own room.
I am lying in bed, greeting the morning.
I dreamed it again.
A dream of drinking someone’s blood.
I know it was a dream, yet it was hideously real.
My hands still remember tearing flesh, and the raw smell of blood still clings inside my nose―――
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… My own room."
I am definitely in my own room.
Just lying in bed, and morning has come.
…… I saw that dream again.
The dream of sucking someone's blood.
Though I know it's just a dream, it still feels terribly real.
My hands retain the feel of ripping meat; my nose, the smell of fresh blood…

entries.japanese:
「―――どうなってるんだ、俺は」
　そっと首もとに触れてみた。
　……弓塚にかまれた傷はとうに塞がっている。
　俺はまっとうな人間なままだ。
　誰かの血を飲みたいなんて思った事ないし、太陽の陽射しをうとましいとも思わない。
「――――あ」
　違う。
昨日、俺は。
　琥珀さんの首筋を見て、なんて、思っただろう。
―――白い首筋。
　そこに流れる赤い血を、俺は心から欲しいと――
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――What is happening to me?”
I touch my throat.
The wound where Yumizuka bit me has long since closed.
I am still an ordinary human being.
I have never wanted to drink anyone’s blood, and sunlight does not repel me.
“――――Ah.”
No. Yesterday was different. I―――
When I saw Kohaku’s throat, what did I think?
―――A white throat.
From the bottom of my heart, I wanted the red blood flowing through it――
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---What's happening to me?"
I touch my neck gently.
