--I didn't want Akiha to drink anyone's blood except mine.
I guess Akiha really likes my blood.
She has never gone outside since then.
But it is really dangerous for my body too.

entries.japanese:
もともと血の気が多くない遠野志貴は、秋葉に血を与え続けられるほど健康じゃない。
　こうして日に一度秋葉に血を与える時、そのまま気を失ってしまう事の方が多いぐらいだ。
　失った分を輸血で補ってはいるものの、本来自分の血液でないものが体に馴染むのにも時間がかかる。
entries.maoEnglish:
Shiki Tohno had never had much blood to spare, nor was he healthy enough to keep feeding Akiha indefinitely.
More often than not, I lost consciousness during her daily feeding.
Transfusions replaced what I lost, but blood that had not begun as mine took time to settle into my body.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I do not have much blood to start with, and I am not healthy enough to keep feeding Akiha blood.
I faint most of the time when I come here once a day to feed Akiha.
Although I'm getting blood from transfusion, it takes my body a while to get used to other people's blood.

entries.japanese:
……遠野志貴の体力は日増しに弱まってきている。
　翡翠が俺の顔を見るたびに言葉を飲むのは、自分の体のほうを労ったほうがいい、という事なんだろう。
　けど、そんなものは。
　痛いと思えるだけ、秋葉の何倍も易しい事だ。
entries.maoEnglish:
Shiki Tohno was growing weaker by the day.
Whenever Hisui looked at my face and swallowed her words, she was probably trying to tell me that I ought to care for myself as well.
But that was nothing.
The very fact that I could feel the pain made my burden many times easier than Akiha’s.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… My body is getting weaker by the day.
I guess the reason for Hisui trying to say something every time she sees my face is to tell me I should care more about myself.
But such a thing…
It's many times easier since I can feel the pain, unlike Akiha.

entries.japanese:
――――秋葉の腕が下がる。
　満足したのか、秋葉は俺の腕から唇を離した。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――Akiha’s arm fell.
Apparently satisfied, she lifted her lips from my arm.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----Akiha lowers her arm.
I guess she's happy now, as she lets go of my arm.

entries.japanese:
そうして、秋葉は人形に戻った。
　口元から垂れた血の跡を拭ってやって、汚れた着物を替える。
　秋葉は何も抵抗しない。
ただされるがままに俺のすることを受け入れるだけだ。
―――そこに。
　以前の、毅然とした秋葉の面影は皆無だった。
entries.maoEnglish:
And then Akiha became a doll again.
I wiped the trail of blood from her mouth and changed her stained kimono.
She offered no resistance. She merely accepted whatever I did to her.
―――There.
Not a trace remained of the proud, resolute Akiha she had once been.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Then she goes back to being being a doll once more.
I clean the dripping blood off her face and change her dirty kimono.
Akiha does not fight back.
She just accepts everything I do.
---There,
Akiha's proud look is nowhere to be seen.

entries.japanese:
「――――――――」
　辛くないと言ったら嘘になる。
　けれどそれでも―――嬉しいという気持ちのほうが大きいんだ。
　秋葉は生きている。
　生きて、こうして存在している。
　それならいつか元の秋葉に戻れる日だって来るだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“……”
I would be lying if I said it didn’t hurt.
And yet—my happiness was greater.
Akiha was alive.
Alive, here, existing before me.
If that was true, then surely a day might come when she became herself again.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---------"
I'd be lying if I said this isn't hard on me.
But still---my feeling of happiness is greater.
Akiha is alive.
She is alive and she is here right now.
Then, someday, Akiha might return to the previous Akiha she once was.

entries.japanese:
「よし。
それじゃあな秋葉。
また明日来るから、夜は琥珀さんの言う事を聞くんだぞ」
　昨日と同じ、いや、いつもと同じ言葉を口にして、ぎゅっと、秋葉の手を握った。
entries.maoEnglish:
“All right. I’ll see you tomorrow, Akiha. Be good tonight and do what Kohaku tells you.”
I repeated the same words as yesterday—the same words as always—and squeezed Akiha’s hand.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Alright.
See you Akiha.
I'll come back tomorrow so listen to Kohaku-san at night."
I say the same phrase as yesterday, no… the same phrase as always, as I hold Akiha's hands.

entries.japanese:
細い指先。
小さな手の平。
　それを隙間なく、自分の掌で埋める。
　そのぬくもり。
　生きているんだっていう感触が痛くて。
　不意に、こみあげそうになった。
entries.maoEnglish:
Slender fingertips. A tiny palm.
I covered it completely with my own hand.
That warmth.
The painful sensation of knowing she was alive.
Something suddenly surged into my throat.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Slender fingers, small hands.
I cover them in my hands.
The warmth.
The fact that she is alive.
It almost makes me cry.

entries.japanese:
「っ…………………！」
　それをかみ殺して笑った。
　だって、悲しいことなんて入らないように、笑っていたい。
　俺がこんな事で悲しむなんていうのは簡単すぎる。
　たとえ解っていなくても、秋葉の前では笑い続けていないといけない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ngh…!”
I crushed it down and smiled.
I wanted to keep smiling, leaving no room for sadness to enter.
It would be too easy for me to grieve over this.
Even if Akiha understood nothing, I had to go on smiling in front of her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…………………!!"
I suppress that feeling and smile.
I want to laugh so that I won't have room for any sadness.
It's easy to feel sad about the situation I'm in.
Even if Akiha doesn't understand, I have to keep on smiling in front of her.

entries.japanese:
いつか秋葉が自分を取り戻した時に、俺が悲しんでいる所ばかり思い出したら可哀相だ。
　こんな事なんでもなかったって―――これも楽しい事だったって秋葉には、思ってもらいたい。
　だから笑っていないと。
　秋葉が解っていなくても、秋葉が自分を取り戻した時、今までの時間を悔やまないように。
entries.maoEnglish:
If Akiha someday regained herself and remembered nothing but the sight of me grieving, that would be too cruel.
I wanted her to believe it had been nothing—that even this time had held some happiness.
So I had to smile.
Even if she understood nothing now, when she returned to herself, I did not want her to regret the time we had spent this way.
entries.mirrorMoon:
One day, if Akiha ever finds herself again, I don't want her to remember how I was sad.
I want her to think that this was nothing----that this was one of the happy times too.
So I have to keep on laughing.
Even if Akiha doesn't understand right now, so that Akiha wouldn't regret the past when she finds herself again.

entries.japanese:
―――手を握って待ち続ける。
　秋葉の瞳が何も見ていなくとも、この世界で最後まで笑って見せよう。
　いつか、秋葉が目を覚ました時。
　やあ、と普段どおりの、なんでもなかったような、挨拶で迎えられるために。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――I would hold her hand and wait.
Even if Akiha’s eyes saw nothing, I would keep smiling in this world until the very end.
Someday, when Akiha opened her eyes.
So I could welcome her with the same ordinary ‘Hey’ as always, as though nothing had happened.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---I keep on waiting, holding her hands.
Even if Akiha's eyes are not staring at anything, I will keep smiling until the end of the world.
So that one day, when Akiha wakes up,
I would be able to greet her like it was another normal day and say "Hi".

entries.japanese:
……できない。
　俺にそんな事ができる筈がない。
　秋葉は何も悪くないんだ。
　何も悪くないのに、どうして――――そんな、理不尽な終わりを迎えさせなくっちゃいけないんだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
…I can’t.
There is no way I could do that.
Akiha hasn’t done anything wrong.
She’s innocent—so why should I be the one to condemn her to such a senseless end?
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… I can't do it.
There's no way I can do that.
Akiha didn't do anything wrong.

She didn't do anything wrong, so why-----does she have to end like this?

entries.japanese:
「………………」
　トス、という音。
　知らず、俺の腕は力を失っていたらしい。
　掌から落ちたナイフは、そのまま畳に突き刺さった。
　血に濡れた部屋。
　昔、俺が七夜志貴だったころ住んでいた部屋。
　……幼い秋葉が、親父の目を盗んで何度も見舞いにきてくれた和室。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
A soft thunk.
At some point, all the strength must have left my arm.
The knife slipped from my hand and buried itself in the tatami.
The room was drenched in blood.
The room where I had lived when I was Shiki Nanaya.
The tatami room where little Akiha had slipped past Father time and again to visit me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"………………"
The sound of my knife dropping.
My arm has lost all strength without me knowing it.
The knife that fell out of my hand sticks in the tatami floor.
The room is drenched in blood.
The room I was living in when I was still Nanaya Shiki a long time ago.
…… The room she came to see me in so many times when my old man wasn't looking.

entries.japanese:
「――――――」
　たった、一日前。
　ここでお互いの肌を確かめ合った。
　あの時、秋葉はもうこの結末を受け入れていたんだろうか。
　俺は、否定するだけだった。
　秋葉の口から全てを聞かされても、それを押しのけようとした。
　認める事ができなくて、漠然と、そんな事にはならないと希望を抱いていただけ。
――――それが、罪だった。
　俺は秋葉を愛しているなんて言いながら、あいつの事を守れなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“—”
Only one day ago.
Here, we had felt each other’s skin.
Had Akiha already accepted this ending then?
All I had done was deny it.
Even after she told me everything herself, I tried to push it away.
Unable to accept it, I simply clung to the vague hope that it would never come to this.
――――That was my sin.
I said I loved Akiha, and still I failed to protect her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------"
Just a day ago.
We felt everything about each other here.
Had Akiha already accepted this outcome back then?
All I could do was refuse.
Even though Akiha told me everything, I tried to push it away.
I didn't want to accept those facts and vaguely, I was wishing it wouldn't happen.
----That is my crime.
I told Akiha I loved her, yet I couldn't protect her.

entries.japanese:
「秋―――――葉」
　……その償いを、しなくちゃいけない。
　俺はこれから、どんな事になっても秋葉を守って生きていくしかない。
　たとえ秋葉が人を殺すだけの生き物になってしまって、俺の事をただの生き物としか認識できなくなっても。
　俺はこれから、おそらくは死に至るまで。
　秋葉を繋ぎとめて、秋葉のために生きていく。
　……それが結局、何一つとして救えなかった、遠野志貴としての、或る終劇のカタチだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Aki—ha.”
Now I had to atone.
Whatever came, I had no choice but to devote the rest of my life to protecting her.
Even if she became a creature that did nothing but kill—even if she could no longer recognize me as anything more than another living thing.
From this day until, in all likelihood, the day I died.
I would hold Akiha to this world and live for her.
In the end, that was how one ending took shape for Shiki Tohno, who had failed to save a single thing.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Aki-----ha."
…… I have to compensate for the crime I've committed.
I can only protect Akiha from now on, no matter what happens.
Even if Akiha has become a creature that only kills people, and even if she could only recognize me as another creature.
Starting now, probably until I die, I will…
Live for Akiha and tie her to this world.
…… That is the way to end the show for Tohno Shiki, who could not save anything.

entries.japanese:
目を開けた。
　まどろんだ意識に果てしのない青が染み入ってくる。
　かすかに暖かい陽射しと、かすかに肌寒い空気。
　草の匂いと木々のざわめきしかない世界。
　この屋敷の森は季節が違っているのか、じき冬だというのに大気は秋の残滓を含んだままだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
I opened my eyes.
Endless blue seeped into my drowsy mind.
Sunlight faintly warm, air faintly cold.
A world made only of the scent of grass and the whisper of trees.
Perhaps the woods around the mansion lived by another calendar; winter was nearly here, yet the air still held the last traces of autumn.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I open my eyes.
Endless blue soaks my sleepy mind.
Slightly warm sunlight and a slightly cool breeze.
A world with only the smell of grass and the sound of trees.
It might be that this mansion's forest is in a different season.
It's almost winter, but this place still feels like autumn.

entries.japanese:
「―――――――――」
　地面に寝そべったまま青い空を見上げる。
太陽はすでに空の真中に昇っていた。
　……どうも、眠ってしまっていたらしい。
　朝食を終えて散歩がてらに森に入った後、草むらに横になったのがいけなかったのか。
　まあ、かといって別にやる事があったわけじゃない。
　ここで、こうして。
　自分の名前さえ忘れて午睡するのも、そうおかしな事ではないだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“—”
I lay on the ground gazing up at the blue sky. The sun had already climbed to the center of the sky.
Apparently I had fallen asleep.
After breakfast I had wandered into the woods, then made the mistake of lying down in the grass.
Not that I had anything else to do.
Here, like this.
Even an afternoon nap deep enough to forget my own name did not seem so strange.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---------"
I look up at the blue sky as I lie on the ground.
The sun is already way up in the sky.
…… I guess I fell asleep.
I guess it was my fault for lying down here on the grass after breakfast.
Well, I didn't have anything to do anyway.
Doing this here.
Falling asleep deeply, even forgetting my name, can't be that bad.

entries.japanese:
―――――底のない青。
　衛生的すぎるその空が遠いなあ、と。
　子供のころに思うような感傷を抱いて、飽きることなく見つめ続けた。
　夢に見るような、遠すぎる空。
　視界いっぱいに広がる景色は意味もなく綺麗すぎて、ため息をつく事さえ、できなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――――Bottomless blue.
That sterile sky was so far away.
I watched it without tiring, seized by the sort of wistfulness a child might feel.
A sky as distant as one seen in dreams.
The view filling my eyes was beautiful beyond all reason, so beautiful I could not even sigh.
entries.mirrorMoon:
-----Bottomless blue.
The clean sky is far away.
Thinking like a child, I keep on watching the sky.
A far sky like in a dream.
The view is so beautiful, I can't even let out a sigh of amazement.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま……？
　こちらにいらっしゃいますか、志貴さま」
　中庭のほうから翡翠の声が聞こえてくる。
「…………」
　もうそんな時間なのか。
　自分はまた眠っていたらしい。
　この青空に憑かれて忘我していたのなら、それは眠っていた事となんら変わりはないのだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki…? Are you here, Master Shiki?”
Hisui’s voice came from the courtyard.
“…”
Was it that late already?
I must have fallen asleep again.
If the blue sky had bewitched me into losing myself, perhaps that was no different from sleep.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama……?
Are you over here, Shiki-sama?"
I hear Hisui's voice from the courtyard.
"…………"
It's that time already.
I guess I fell asleep again.
If I forgot time while watching this blue sky, it makes no difference if I was sleeping or not.

entries.japanese:
息を切らした風もなく翡翠はやってきた。
「志貴さま、秋葉さまがお呼びです」
「そっか、いつのまにか眠ってたみたいだ。
悪いね翡翠、ここのところずっと手間をかけさせて」
「いえ、そのような事はないのですが……」
　翡翠は何か言いたそうに目を伏せる。
　……翡翠が何を言いたいのかは解っている。
ただそれは言葉にされても返答できない物だった。
entries.maoEnglish:
Hisui arrived without the slightest sign of being out of breath.
“Master Shiki, Miss Akiha is asking for you.”
“Oh. I must have dozed off without noticing. Sorry, Hisui. I’ve been putting you to an awful lot of trouble lately.”
“No, it is no trouble, but…”
Hisui lowered her eyes, plainly wanting to say more.
…I knew what she wanted to tell me. Even if she put it into words, though, I would have no answer.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Hisui arrives, composed.
"Shiki-sama, Akiha-sama is calling you."
"Alright.
I guess I was asleep.
Sorry for being so troublesome, Hisui."
"Not at all, it is nothing of the sort……"
Hisui looks down as if she wants to say something.
…… I know what Hisui wants to say, but even if she did, I wouldn't be able to give her an answer.

entries.japanese:
「それじゃ行ってくる。
一時間経ったら琥珀さんに声をかけておいてくれ」
「あ―――――」
　翡翠に背を向けて、秋葉の居る離れの屋敷に向かった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’d better go, then. When an hour has passed, tell Kohaku.”
“Ah—”
I turned my back on Hisui and headed for the detached house where Akiha waited.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I'll get going.
Can you tell Kohaku-san in about an hour or so?"
"Ah-----"
I turn my back to Hisui and head to the detached building where Akiha is waiting.

entries.japanese:
和室には一人の少女がいる。
　いや、いる、という表現は正しくはない。
　少女は自分だけでは動いてくれない。
ただ食事を摂る時にだけ生き物として活動して、それ以外は彫像のように止まってしまう人形だった。
　だから、それは居る、というより。
　おそらくは在る、という表現のほうが相応しい、人形そのものだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
There was a girl in the tatami room.
No—that was not quite the right way to put it.
The girl never moved of her own accord. She came alive only when she fed; the rest of the time she was a doll, still as a statue.
She was not someone who lived there so much as something that existed there.
A doll in the truest sense.
entries.mirrorMoon:
In the room lives a girl.
No, the term "lives" is not right.
The girl cannot move of her own will.
She only moves as a living thing when she eats, and she just sits there like a statue when she isn't.
So instead of "live",
"exists" is a more correct term, since she is more like a doll.

entries.japanese:
「ごめんな秋葉。
ちょっと昼寝しててさ、いつもの時間に遅れちまった」
　障子を閉めて部屋に入る。
　秋葉は座ったまま動かない。
「なんだ、髪がグシャグシャじゃないか。
着替えもまだ終わってないみたいだし、琥珀さんは今朝こなかったのか？」
　秋葉は何も言わない。
　ただ焦点のない瞳で、ぼんやりとこちらを眺めている。
　……いや。
　眺めているような、気がするだけだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Sorry, Akiha. I took a nap and missed our usual time.”
I slid the paper screen shut behind me.
Akiha remained seated and motionless.
“Look at you. Your hair’s a mess, and you’re not even dressed properly. Didn’t Kohaku come this morning?”
Akiha said nothing.
Her unfocused eyes only stared vaguely in my direction.
…No.
It merely felt as though she were looking at me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I'm sorry Akiha.
I fell asleep and couldn't make it in time."
I enter the room and close the shouji.
Akiha sits there and does not move.
"Whoa, your hair is messed up.
It looks like you haven't changed yet either.
Didn't Kohaku-san come by this morning?"
Akiha does not say anything.
She looks in my direction with a blank stare.
…… No,
it just seems like she's looking.

entries.japanese:
「しょうがないな。
ほら、髪ぐらい綺麗にしないと」
　秋葉の髪に手をかける。
　抵抗する素振りはない。
　静かに、できるだけ柔らかに、赤い髪を梳る。
　ざあ、と長い髪が流れていく。
　秋葉は何も言わない。
　しばらくそんな時間が続いたあと。
　不意に、秋葉の腕が動いた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Honestly. At least let me make your hair presentable.”
I reached for it.
She showed no resistance.
Slowly, as gently as I could, I combed her red hair.
The long strands poured through my hand with a soft rush.
Akiha said nothing.
After a while had passed that way—
Akiha’s arm suddenly moved.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Alright, let's at least make your hair look good.
I touch Akiha's hair.
She makes no motion to fight it.
Quietly, as softly as I can, I let my hands go through her hair.
Her long hair flows in my hand.
Akiha does not say anything.
After some time like that,
Akiha suddenly moves her arm.

entries.japanese:
「秋葉―――？」
　返事はない。
　ただ秋葉の指がこちらの腕を掴んで、口まで持っていく。
　ガツ、という感触のあと。
　秋葉は俺の腕に噛み付いて、無表情のまま、血を飲んだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Akiha—?”
No answer.
Her fingers closed around my arm and drew it to her mouth.
There was a hard impact.
Then Akiha bit into my arm and, without changing expression, began to drink my blood.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Akiha---?"
There's no answer.
She just takes my arm and brings it to her mouth.
After a hard sensation,
Akiha bites on my arm and starts to suck out my blood expressionlessly.

entries.japanese:
白い喉が、ごくごくと赤い血を嚥下していく。
　口元からこぼれた血は秋葉の喉を伝って、着物を赤く汚していく。
entries.maoEnglish:
Her white throat worked as she swallowed the red blood in great gulps.
Blood spilled from her lips, ran down her neck, and stained her robe crimson.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Her white throat gulps down my blood.

The blood that spills out of her mouth drips down her throat and stains her kimono red.

entries.japanese:
「ぐっ――――う」
　歯を食いしばって秋葉が満足するまで耐える。
　……秋葉には適量というものがない。
　満腹になれば吸うのを止めるだけで、それがどの程度の量なのかは統計できない。
　だからこうして、秋葉が自分から止めるのを待つ事しか、俺にはできない。
「っ…………ぁ」
　くらりと意識が点滅する。
　それでも自分から腕を引く事はしない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ghh—”
I clenched my teeth and endured until she was satisfied.
Akiha had no sense of how much was enough.
She stopped only when she was full, and there was no predicting how much that might take.
All I could do was wait for her to stop of her own accord.
“Ngh—ah…”
My consciousness flickered.
Still, I did not pull my arm away.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ghu----u"
I grit my teeth and hold on until Akiha is full.
…… There is no proper quantity for Akiha.
She stops only when she's full, and I can't predict when that is.
So all I can do is wait like this for her to be full.
"………… Ah."
I feel dizzy.
But I don't pull back.

entries.japanese:
……そういえば、この事を最後まで反対していたのは翡翠だったっけ。
　秋葉が人の血しか受け付けなくなってから、俺は自分の血を与える事に決めた。
　それは責任感、なんてものじゃない。
　秋葉が人の血を口にしなければ生きていけないというのなら、その被害者は最低限に抑えたかったし、何より―――俺は、秋葉に俺以外の人間の血なんかを飲んでほしくはなかったのだ。
　秋葉にとって俺の血は相性が良かったのか、それ以来秋葉が独りでに外に出る事はなくなった。
　反面、それは俺の体にしてみれば危険な事だった。
entries.maoEnglish:
…Come to think of it, Hisui had opposed this to the bitter end.
Once Akiha became unable to take anything but human blood, I decided to give her mine.
It wasn’t some noble sense of duty.
If she could only survive by drinking human blood, I wanted as few people as possible to suffer for it. More than anything—I couldn’t bear the thought of Akiha drinking anyone’s blood but mine.
Perhaps my blood suited her unusually well, because from then on Akiha never wandered outside on her own again.
The price was that every feeding placed my own body in danger.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Hisui was against this until the very last minute.
I decided to give Akiha my own blood ever since she could only take in human blood.
It wasn't a sense of responsibility.
If Akiha could only survive by taking in blood, I wanted to limit the amount of victims, and most of all---
--I did not want Akiha to drink anyone's blood except mine.
I guess Akiha really likes my blood.
She has never gone outside since then.
But, it is really dangerous for my body.

entries.japanese:
もともと血の気が多くない遠野志貴は、秋葉に血を与え続けられるほど健康じゃない。
　こうして日に一度秋葉に血を与える時、そのまま気を失ってしまう事の方が多いぐらいだ。
　失った分を輸血で補ってはいるものの、本来自分の血液でないものが体に馴染むのにも時間がかかる。
entries.maoEnglish:
Shiki Tohno had never had much blood to spare, nor was he healthy enough to keep feeding Akiha.
More often than not, I lost consciousness during our daily sessions.
Transfusions replaced what I lost, but blood that had not been mine to begin with took time to settle into my body.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I do not have much blood to start with, and I am not healthy enough to keep feeding Akiha blood.
I faint most of the time when I come here once a day to feed her.
Although I'm getting blood from transfusion, it takes my body a while to get used to other people's blood.

entries.japanese:
……遠野志貴の体力は日増しに弱まってきている。
　翡翠が俺の顔を見るたびに言葉を飲むのは、自分の体のほうを労ったほうがいい、という事なんだろう。
　けど、そんなものは。
　痛いと思えるだけ、秋葉の何倍も易しい事だ。
entries.maoEnglish:
…Shiki Tohno was growing weaker by the day.
Whenever Hisui looked at my face and swallowed what she meant to say, she was probably trying to tell me to take better care of myself.
But this was nothing.
The simple fact that I could still feel the pain made it far easier to bear than what Akiha endured.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… My body is getting weaker by the day.
I guess the reason for Hisui trying to say something every time she sees my face is to tell me I should care more about myself.
But such a thing…
It's many times easier since I can feel the pain, unlike Akiha.

entries.japanese:
――――秋葉の腕が下がる。
　満足したのか、秋葉は俺の腕から唇を離した。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――Akiha’s arm fell.
Apparently satisfied, she drew her lips away from my arm.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----Akiha lowers her arm.
I guess she's happy now, as she lets go of my arm.

entries.japanese:
そうして、秋葉は人形に戻った。
　口元から垂れた血の跡を拭ってやって、汚れた着物を替える。
　秋葉は何も抵抗しない。
ただされるがままに俺のすることを受け入れるだけだ。
―――そこに。
　以前の、毅然とした秋葉の面影は皆無だった。
entries.maoEnglish:
And then Akiha became a doll again.
I wiped the trail of blood from her mouth and changed her stained robe.
She offered no resistance. She merely accepted whatever I did to her.
―――There.
Not a trace remained of the proud, resolute Akiha she had once been.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Then she goes back to being a doll once more.
I clean the dripping blood off her face and change her dirty kimono.
Akiha does not fight back.
She just accepts everything I do.
---There,
Akiha's proud look is nowhere to be seen.

entries.japanese:
「――――――――」
　辛くないと言ったら嘘になる。
　けれどそれでも―――嬉しいという気持ちのほうが大きいんだ。
　秋葉は生きている。
　生きて、こうして存在している。
　それならいつか元の秋葉に戻れる日だって来るだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“—”
I would be lying if I said it didn’t hurt.
Even so—my happiness was greater.
Akiha was alive.
Alive, here with me.
As long as that was true, surely a day would come when she returned to herself.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"--------"
I'd be lying if I said this isn't hard on me.
But still---my feeling of happiness is greater.
Akiha is alive.
She is alive and she is here right now.
Then, someday, Akiha might return to the Akiha she once was.

entries.japanese:
「よし。
それじゃあな秋葉。
また明日来るから、夜は琥珀さんの言う事を聞くんだぞ」
　昨日と同じ、いや、いつもと同じ言葉を口にして、ぎゅっと、秋葉の手を握った。
entries.maoEnglish:
“There we are. I’ll see you tomorrow, Akiha. Be good tonight and do what Kohaku tells you.”
I repeated the words I had used yesterday—the words I always used—and clasped Akiha’s hand tightly.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Alright.
See you, Akiha.
I'll come back tomorrow so listen to Kohaku-san at night."
I say the same phrase as yesterday, no, the same phrase as always, as I hold Akiha's hands.

entries.japanese:
細い指先。
小さな手の平。
　それを隙間なく、自分の掌で埋める。
　そのぬくもり。
　生きているんだっていう感触が痛くて。
　不意に、こみあげそうになった。
entries.maoEnglish:
Slender fingers. A tiny palm.
I closed my own hand completely around hers.
That warmth.
The painful proof that she was alive.
Suddenly, I felt something welling up inside me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Slender fingers, small hands.
I cover them with mine.
The warmth.
The fact that she is alive.
It almost makes me cry.

entries.japanese:
「っ…………………！」
　それをかみ殺して笑った。
　だって、悲しいことなんて入らないように、笑っていたい。
　俺がこんな事で悲しむなんていうのは簡単すぎる。
　たとえ解っていなくても、秋葉の前では笑い続けていないといけない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ngh…!”
I bit it back and smiled.
I wanted to keep smiling, leaving sorrow no room to enter.
It would be far too easy for me to grieve over this.
Whether she understood or not, I had to keep smiling whenever I was with her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…………………!"
I suppress that feeling and smile.
I want to laugh so that I won't have room for any sadness.
It's easy to feel sad about the situation I'm in.
Even if Akiha doesn't understand, I have to keep on smiling in front of her.

entries.japanese:
いつか秋葉が自分を取り戻した時に、俺が悲しんでいる所ばかり思い出したら可哀相だ。
　こんな事なんでもなかったって―――これも楽しい事だったって秋葉には、思ってもらいたい。
　だから笑っていないと。
　秋葉が解っていなくても、秋葉が自分を取り戻した時、今までの時間を悔やまないように。
entries.maoEnglish:
If Akiha ever found herself again and remembered nothing but my sorrow, it would only hurt her.
I wanted her to believe that none of this had been terrible—that even these days had held happiness.
So I had to smile.
Even if she understood nothing now, I had to make sure that when she awakened, she would not regret the time we had spent this way.
entries.mirrorMoon:
One day, if Akiha ever finds herself again, I don't want her to remember how I was sad.
I want her to think that this was nothing---that this was one of the happy times too.
So I have to keep on smiling.
Even if Akiha doesn't understand right now, so that Akiha wouldn't regret the past when she finds herself again.

entries.japanese:
―――手を握って待ち続ける。
　秋葉の瞳が何も見ていなくとも、この世界で最後まで笑って見せよう。
　いつか、秋葉が目を覚ました時。
　やあ、と普段どおりの、なんでもなかったような、挨拶で迎えられるために。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――I would hold her hand and wait for as long as it took.
Even if Akiha’s eyes saw nothing, I would smile for her until the very end of this world.
So that someday, when Akiha opened her eyes,
I could welcome her with the same ordinary “Hey” as always—as though nothing had happened at all.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---I keep on waiting, holding her hands.
Even if Akiha's eyes are not staring at anything, I will keep smiling until the end of the world.
So that one day, when Akiha wakes up,
I will be able to greet her like it was another normal day and say "Hi".

entries.japanese:
秋葉・ノーマルエンディング、ごくろうさまでした。
　各ヒロインには（一名だけ例外がありますが）二種類のエンディングが用意されています。
　通常はトゥルーエンディングとグッドエンディングと呼ばれますが、秋葉さんだけはノーマルエンディング、トゥルーエンディングと呼ばれています。
　秋葉さんのルートは他のルートとは違っていて、好感度さえクリアしていればグッド・トゥルー、共に特別な条件を必要としません。
entries.maoEnglish:
Congratulations on completing Akiha’s Normal Ending.
Each heroine—with one exception—has two endings.
Ordinarily they are called the True Ending and the Good Ending, but Akiha’s are instead called the Normal Ending and the True Ending.
Akiha’s route differs from the others: once you meet the affection requirement, neither ending has any additional special condition.
entries.mirrorMoon:
You have reached Akiha's Normal Ending.
Well done.
Each heroine (with one exception) has two different kinds of endings.
Usually, they are called "True Ending" and "Good Ending", but Akiha-san's are called "Normal Ending" and "True Ending".
Akiha-san's route is different from everyone else's in that how much Akiha-san likes you does not determine which ending you receive.

It also differs from all other routes in that it has an extra Normal Ending, which is what you are reading right now.
While this ending is called Akiha's Normal Ending, it will not register as an ending in the game.
"Nya?
What is this?
You're talking nonsense!
Take it up with the game designers if you must.
Tohno-kun, please proceed to play through Akiha-san's route to reach her real Normal Ending.

entries.japanese:
それでは、ここまでプレイしていただいてありがとうございました。
　また“月姫”のどこかでお会いしましょう。
entries.maoEnglish:
Thank you for playing this far.
I hope we meet again somewhere in TSUKIHIME.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Well then, thank you very much for playing up to this point.
Let's meet again somewhere in Tsukihime.

entries.japanese:
居間にはソファーに座った秋葉と、その相手をしている琥珀さん、それに壁際で控えている翡翠の姿があった。
「おはようございます、志貴さん」
「おはよう琥珀さん。
悪いんだけど、ごはん作ってもらえるかな。
ずいぶんと眠ってておなかが減っちゃってさ」
「はい、かしこまりました。
いま支度をしますからしばらく待っていてくださいね」
　琥珀さんはパタパタと食堂へと去っていく。
entries.maoEnglish:
Akiha sat on the sofa in the sitting room, with Kohaku keeping her company and Hisui standing in attendance by the wall.
“Good morning, Shiki.”
“Morning, Kohaku. Sorry to ask, but could you make me something to eat? I slept forever, and I’m starving.”
“Of course. Give me a few minutes to prepare something.”
Kohaku hurried away toward the dining room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
In the sitting room, Akiha is on the sofa, Kohaku-san is keeping her company, and Hisui is standing by the wall.
"Good morning, Shiki-san."
"Morning, Kohaku-san.
Sorry to be a bother, but could you fix me something to eat?
I'm a little hungry from all that sleeping."
"Yes, right away.
I will get it ready, so please wait a little bit."
Kohaku-san quickly patters away towards the dining room.

entries.japanese:
これで居間に残ったのは秋葉と、彫像のように無言を通している翡翠だけになる。
「……やっ。
秋葉も、おはよう」
「……………………」
　秋葉は不機嫌そうな顔で俺を一瞥するだけで、挨拶を返してこない。
「…………う」
　翡翠の教えてくれたとおり、昨夜のことを怒っているらしい。
　朝に『夜遊び厳禁！
』って注意されたのに、その日の深夜に外出すれば、そりゃあ秋葉だって怒って当然か。
entries.maoEnglish:
That left only Akiha and Hisui, who stood in silence like a statue.
“Hey, Akiha. Good morning.”
“……”
Akiha merely gave me a displeased glance, refusing to return the greeting.
“Urgh.”
Just as Hisui had warned me, she was angry about last night.
She had expressly forbidden late-night outings that morning, and then I had gone out after midnight the very same day. Of course she was angry.
entries.mirrorMoon:
That leaves Akiha and Hisui, who is standing wordlessly like a statue.
"…… Yo, Akiha.
G'morning."
"……………………"
Akiha just looks at me with a dissatisfied look on her face and doesn't return my greeting.
"…………… Uh."
Like Hisui warned me, she seems angry about last night.
Telling me in the morning that leaving late at night is forbidden only to find me leaving late at night.
It's only natural for her to be angry.

entries.japanese:
「秋葉。
昨日は、その―――」
「兄さん。
いくらなんでもこんな時間に起きてくるなんて、なにを考えているんですか」
「え―――いや、その、だから、ごめん」
「……もうっ、そんなコトを怒っているんじゃありません。
せっかくの休日なのにこんな時間まで眠っている、兄さんの緩みようを怒っているんです、私は！」
　ふん、と顔をそむけて怒る秋葉。
　……っていうか、怒っているというよりは拗ねているように見えるのは、気のせいだろうか。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Akiha. About yesterday…”
“Brother. What could you possibly be thinking, getting up at this hour?”
“Uh—sorry.”
“Oh, honestly—that isn't what I'm angry about. I'm angry because you wasted half your day off in bed and have grown far too lax!”
Akiha turned away with an offended huff.
Was it my imagination, or did she look less angry than sulky?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Akiha.
Last night, was---"
"Nii-san.
Sleeping in this late… just what were you thinking?"
"Eh---um, well, I… Sorry."
"…… Geez, I'm not mad about that.
It's your day off, and you've chosen to sleep in until now.
It's your laziness that angers me!"
With a "hmph", Akiha angrily turns her face away.
…… Well, it may just be my imagination, but "peevishly" is a better word than "angrily".

entries.japanese:
「いや、だって仕方ないだろう。
昨日は遅かったんだし、体だって疲れきってたんだから」
「そんなのは自業自得です。
だいたい夜の十二時すぎに出かけるなんて、いったい有間の家でどういう生活をしていたんですか、兄さんはっ！」
「うっ……あっちでだって門限は厳しかったぞ。
夜の外出も禁じられてたし……」
entries.maoEnglish:
“It couldn’t be helped. I was up late, and my body was completely exhausted.”
“That was entirely your own doing! Sneaking out after midnight—what sort of life did you lead with the Arima family?”
“Urgh—they had a strict curfew too. Going out at night was forbidden—”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Well, I couldn't help it.
I got in late last night, and my body was just tired."
"That is entirely your fault.
Staying out until way past midnight… Just what kind of lifestyle did you have when you lived with the Arimas, Nii-san!?"
"Uh…… I had a strict curfew there, too.
I wasn't allowed to leave at night, and……"

entries.japanese:
「へえ、それはそれは。
有間の家では規則を守っていたのに、こっちにきてからは守ってくださらないんですね。
　……つまり兄さんは私の注意なんて微塵も気にとめていないっていうコトなんだ。
ふーん、そうなるとこっちもそれなりの体罰を考えないといけませんね」
　意地の悪い流し目をする秋葉。
　……なんていうか、秋葉のセリフは冗談を言っても冗談には聞こえないあたり、恐ろしい。
entries.maoEnglish:
“How fascinating. You obeyed the rules at the Arima home, yet refuse to obey them here.
So my warnings mean absolutely nothing to you. In that case, perhaps I’ll have to devise an appropriate corporal punishment.”
Akiha gave me a sidelong look full of malice.
The terrifying thing about Akiha was that even her jokes never sounded like jokes.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Oh, so that's it.
At the Arimas' house, you followed the rules, but you come here and break them?
…… In other words, you won't even follow my simplest request?
In that case, I may have to resort to corporal punishment."
The fury of her intent also flows through her eyes.
…… How do I say this?
She has to be joking, only she doesn't sound like she's kidding, and it's pretty frightening.

entries.japanese:
「……体罰って、秋葉。
おまえ、なんか恐いぞ」
「あのですね、あくまで例え話ですっ。
夜は夜更かししほうだい、朝は気の済むまで眠ってる、なんていう人をしつけるには厳しくしないといけないでしょ」
　むー、とうなる秋葉。
　……悔しいけど、秋葉の言うことはまったくの正論なので反論のしようがない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Corporal punishment? Akiha, you’re starting to scare me.”
“It was only an example! Anyone who stays up as late as he pleases and then sleeps as long as he pleases needs strict discipline.”
Akiha made an irritated little growl.
Infuriatingly, she was also entirely right, leaving me no room to argue.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Corporal punishment, Akiha?
You're starting to frighten me."
"That was just an example.
Staying up real late like that and just sleeping until you feel like getting up?
Of course I should be very strict."
Akiha gives an audible groan.
…… I hate to admit it, but she is right.

entries.japanese:
「だいたいね、兄さん。
朝起きるだけだったら翡翠に起こしてもらえばいいだけでしょう？
　
　今日は日曜日だからよかったものの、なんだっていつもいつも時間ぎりぎりで起床するのよ、兄さんは」
「……あのさ、秋葉。
いちおう言っておくんだけど、俺だって好きで寝過ごしてるわけじゃないよ」
「なによ、それじゃあどうしていつも余裕のない朝を過ごしてるの？
　私がいつもどんな思いで、時間ぎりぎりまで待って――――」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Besides, Brother, waking up is easy. All you need is to have Hisui wake you, isn't it?
Today happened to be Sunday, but why must you always sleep until the last possible minute?”
“Listen, Akiha. It's not as if I oversleep because I enjoy it.”
“Then why are your mornings always such a mad rush? Do you have any idea how I feel, waiting until the very last moment for you to—”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Besides, Nii-san.
Shouldn't you let Hisui wake you up in the morning?
It is a good thing today is Sunday, but you always, always laze around in bed too long, Nii-san."
"…… Um, Akiha.
Maybe it's not my place to say, but it's not like I'm sleeping in because I want to."
"What?
So how come you always sleep in until the last minute every morning?
You don't know how I feel when I wait for you until the last minute, and----"

entries.japanese:
「秋葉さま」
「あ――――」
「………？」
　さっきまでの剣幕はどこにいったのか、秋葉は唐突に黙ってしまう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Miss Akiha.”
“Ah…”
“……?”
Akiha's fury vanishes as she abruptly falls silent.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Akiha-sama."
"Ah----"
"………?"
Where did the dire, threatening atmosphere go?
All of a sudden, Akiha descends into silence.

entries.japanese:
「あのな、秋葉。
言っとくけど俺が起きるのがいつも七時過ぎなのはワザとじゃないよ。
　俺だって早起きはしたいけど、体が言うことをきかないんだからしょうがないだろ。
そんなに早起きさせたいんならすっごく強力な目覚まし時計を買ってくれ。
それなら、まあなんとか早起きできるかもしれないから」
「……あの、兄さん？
　ふと疑問に思ったんですけど、兄さんは翡翠に何時に起こしてほしい、といった事は伝えてないの？」
「―――――あ」
　そっか、そんな単純なことをど忘れしてた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Look, Akiha. I don’t deliberately sleep past seven every morning.
I’d like to wake earlier, but my body simply won’t cooperate. If you want me up that badly, buy me some monstrously powerful alarm clock. Then I might just manage it.”
“Brother? A thought just occurred to me: have you ever told Hisui what time you want her to wake you?”
“Ah.”
Of course, I had forgotten the most obvious thing imaginable.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hey, Akiha.
I said so before, but waking up past seven o'clock in the morning isn't intentional.
Even I would like to get up earlier, but my body doesn't listen to what I tell it.
If you want to help me wake up earlier, please buy me a really powerful alarm clock.
I'm sure that'd get me up."
"…… Uh, Nii-san?
This may be a stupid question, but did you ever tell Hisui what time you wanted her to wake you up?"
"----Ah."
That's right, I forgot such a simple thing as that.

entries.japanese:
「そうだよな、せっかく毎朝翡翠が起こしにきてくれるんだから、翡翠に起こしてもらえばいいんだ。
そういうわけなんで翡翠、これからは朝の六時半ごろに起こしてくれると助かるんだけど……」
　ちらり、と背後の翡翠に視線を投げる。
　と、翡翠はじっ、と俺の顔を睨みつけた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You're right—since Hisui comes to wake me every morning anyway, I can just have her do it. Hisui, from now on, could you wake me at about six-thirty?”
I glanced back at her.
Hisui fixed me with an unblinking glare.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Oh yeah.
Hisui comes every morning to wake me, so it's alright for her to do that.
So… Hisui, could you please wake me up at six-thirty each morning?
It would really help me out……"
I swing around to face Hisui.
She stares right back at me.

entries.japanese:
「お断わりします」
「え？」
「ですから、志貴さまを起こすのはお断わりします、と申しあげたのです」
「えーと、その」
　なんて言っていいものか、あまりのショックで思考が働かない。
　見れば秋葉もびっくりしたような顔で翡翠を呆然と見つめていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I refuse.”
“What?”
“I said that I must decline to wake you, Master Shiki.”
“Er—well.”
The shock was so great that my mind stopped working.
Akiha looked equally stunned as she stared at Hisui.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I refuse."
"Eh?"
"Forgive me, but I refuse to wake you up, Shiki-sama."
"Well, um--"
I don't know what to say.
The shock put my brain on hold.
Looking at the situation, Akiha is also gaping at Hisui in surprise.

entries.japanese:
「翡翠。
どうして兄さんを起こすのは出来ないの」
「出来ない事はお引き受けできません。
志貴さまを私の意志で起こすのは、おそらく無理だと思います」
「───無理って、どうして」
　思わず二人の会話に口を挟む。
　と、またも翡翠は俺をじっと睨んできた。
「今までの三日間、すべて無理でしたから。
　志貴さま、今朝はわたしが幾度お呼びしたか覚えてらっしゃいますか？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hisui. Why can’t you wake my brother?”
“I cannot accept a duty I am unable to perform. I do not believe it is possible for me to wake Master Shiki by my own efforts.”
“Why wouldn’t it be possible?”
I broke into their conversation without thinking.
Hisui turned that level glare on me again.
“Because I have failed every day for the past three days.
Master Shiki, do you remember how many times I called to you this morning?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hisui, why can't you wake up Nii-san?"
"I am unable to undertake things I cannot do.
I do not think I am able to wake up Shiki-sama with my own power."
"----Unable?
Why not?"
I unthinkingly enter their conversation.
Hisui continues staring at me.

"These past three days, all my efforts were fruitless.
Shiki-sama, do you remember how many times I called your name this morning?"

entries.japanese:
「いや、覚えてらっしゃいますかって───俺は翡翠の声で目が覚めるか、自分でかってに起きるだけなんだけど……」
「それ以前のわたしの声は記憶にも留まっていない、という事ですね。
───秋葉さま、つまりこういう事です」
　なるほどねー、と秋葉はいじわるな眼差しを向けてくる。
　……なんていうか、一瞬にして俺の立場は最悪なものになってしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I either wake up to your voice or happen to wake on my own—”
“Which means that you retain no memory of all the times I called before that. Miss Akiha, that is precisely the difficulty.”
Akiha gave me a wicked look that said, Now I understand.
In a single instant, my position had become indefensible.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No, I don't remember----I woke up from your voice?
I thought I woke up by myself……"
"That means there is no memory of me even calling out.
----Akiha-sama, that is the situation."
"Oh, I see," Akiha says and looks over at me teasingly.
…… How do I say this…… it would seem my standing here has just been lowered quite a bit.

entries.japanese:
「ようするに翡翠がいくら起こしても、兄さんは自分の起きたい時間でなければ反応さえしてくれない───そういう事なの、翡翠？」
　翡翠は無言でうなずく。
「………………」
　俺も無言でうなずく。
　……そっかー、実は朝早くからちゃんと起こされてたのか。
　自分でいうのもなんだけど、俺の熟睡ぶりもここまでくると神業の域に到達してしまっているかもしんない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“In other words, no matter how often Hisui tries, you won’t even respond until the time you have decided to wake—is that right, Hisui?”
Hisui nodded silently.
“……”
I nodded too.
So she had been trying to wake me properly all along.
If I did say so myself, sleeping this soundly might qualify as a supernatural talent.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"In short, you have tried repeatedly to wake up Nii-san, but there isn't even the slightest reaction on his part---that's how it is, Hisui?"
Hisui nods silently.
"………………"
I nod silently as well.
…… I see.
The truth is, Hisui has already been trying to wake me up early in the morning.
I don't want to say it myself, but I must be really good at sleeping in.

entries.japanese:
「………兄さん。
どうして、そこで得意げな顔をなさるんですか」
「いや、つい。
自分の大物ぶりに呆れてたとこ」
「……はあ。
わかりました、翡翠は今までどおり、兄さんが起きそうになったらなんとか起きてもらえるように努力してちょうだい」
　はい、と翡翠はうなずく。
　話はまとまったようだ。
　結局、俺は今までどおり自由気ままに朝を迎えるしかないってコトだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Brother. Why do you look so proud of yourself?”
“I couldn't help it. I was marveling at what a formidable man I am.”
“I see. Hisui, continue as before; when he appears ready to wake, do your best to coax him the rest of the way.”
Hisui nodded and said, “Very well.”
That settled it.
Apparently I had no choice but to keep greeting the morning whenever my body happened to feel like it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……… Nii-san.
Why are you looking so proud of yourself?"
"Nothing.
I was just surprised by how daunting it is to wake me."
"…… Hmm.
I understand.
Hisui, just like before, please try and wake up Nii-san as much as you can."
Hisui nods in assent.
It seems like the conversation is finished.
In the end, it may be just me waking up whenever I feel like it again.

entries.japanese:
「ねえ。
ところで翡翠」
「はい、なんでしょうか」
「その、兄さんったら本当に起きないの？
　呼びかけてもまったく反応しないの？」
「────はい。
志貴さまの眠りはとても静かで、彫像のようですから分かりやすいんです」
「………………？」
　……彫像のようって、なんだいそれ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hey. By the way, Hisui.”
“Yes, what is it?”
“Does he truly never wake? He doesn’t react at all when you call him?”
“That is correct. Master Shiki sleeps so quietly—like a statue—that it is quite easy to tell.”
“……?”
What was that about being like a statue?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hey, by the way, Hisui?"
"Yes, what is it?"
"Um.
Does Nii-san really not wake up?
Even if you call his name, he doesn't respond?"
"---Yes.
Shiki-sama's sleep is very quiet, and he sleeps like a statue."
"……………?"
…… Like a statue?
What?

entries.japanese:
「へえ。
兄さん、寝相いいんですね」
「いえ、そうではなくて───なんと申しますか、その、お眠りになられている志貴さまは別人のような気がいたします。
　あんな静かな寝顔は見た事がなかったから、初めて見た時はお亡くなりになられたんじやないかって、その───」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Really? You’re a quiet sleeper, Brother.”
“No, that is not quite what I mean; I suppose Master Shiki seems like another person when he sleeps.
I had never seen such a still sleeping face, so the first time I thought he might have died—”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Oh?
Nii-san has a great sleeping posture, huh?"
"No, that is not it---how do I say it… um, Shiki-sama is like a completely different person when he sleeps.
I have never seen such a peaceful sleeping face, so when I first saw him, I thought that he had passed away, I---"

entries.japanese:
「ですから起こしにくい、というのではなくて、起こすのがとても失礼な気がして、強く起こせないんです。
　志貴さまがご自分でお目覚めになられる時は、白い頬に体温が戻っていって、ああ、お目覚めになられるんだな、とすぐに分かるんですが───」
　翡翠は目を伏せたまま、人の寝相の感想をもらしている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“It is not that he is difficult to wake; rather, waking him feels like a terrible discourtesy, so I cannot bring myself to be forceful.
When Master Shiki begins to wake on his own, warmth returns to his pale cheeks, and I can always tell at once that he is about to wake—”
Hisui keeps her eyes lowered as she describes my sleeping face.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"So it is not quite that he is hard to awaken, but that it seems very rude to do so, so I can not help but be very gentle.
Once Shiki-sama is about to wake up by himself, warmth returns to his white face, and I know he will wake up soon, but---"
Looking down, Hisui talks about how I look when I sleep.

entries.japanese:
「……………」
　……なんか、すごく恥ずかしい。
　考えてみれば寝相っていうのは人間のもっとも無防備な姿なわけで、それをこう微にいり細にいり説明されると、裸を見られたみたいで赤面してしまう。
　翡翠はそのまま黙ってしまうし、秋葉もなぜか顔をそむけて見当違いのところを見ていたりする。
「……………」
　なんか、ヘンに場が重い。
entries.maoEnglish:
“……”
This was mortifying.
Sleep left a person utterly defenseless, and hearing every detail of mine described like this made me flush as though she had seen me naked.
Hisui fell silent; for some reason, Akiha turned away too, staring fixedly at nothing in particular.
“……”
The atmosphere had become strangely oppressive.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……………"
…… I can't help but feel embarrassed.
Come to think of it, a sleeping person is completely defenseless, and after listening to that explanation, I flush as red as if she said she saw me naked.
Hisui descends into silence, and Akiha is obviously trying not to look in my direction.
"…………"
The air has become a little, heavy.

entries.japanese:
「はい、お待たせしました。
志貴さん、朝食が出来ましたよー」
　そこへ、明るい声で救世主が登場した。
「あ、ありがとう。
それじゃあごちそうになります」
「はい、ゆっくり召し上がってくださいね」
　琥珀さんの笑顔に背中をおされて、一人で食堂へ足を向けた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Thank you for waiting! Shiki, your breakfast is ready.”
A savior arrived on a tide of good cheer.
“Thanks. I’ll go eat, then.”
“Please take your time.”
Urged onward by Kohaku’s smile, I escaped alone to the dining room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Thanks for waiting!
Shiki-san, breakfast is reaaadyyyy!"
A bright voice saves the situation.
"Th, thanks.
Well, I'll eat up!"
"Yes, please take your time eating."
Turning my back to Kohaku-san's smile, I head to the dining room alone.

entries.japanese:
昼食を済ませて戻ると、秋葉も翡翠も居間に残っていた。
　二人を無視して部屋に戻るのも気まずいので、秋葉の向かい側のソファーに座ってみたりする。
entries.maoEnglish:
When I returned after lunch, Akiha and Hisui were still in the sitting room.
Ignoring them and going straight upstairs would have been awkward, so I sat on the sofa opposite Akiha.
entries.mirrorMoon:
After I eat lunch, Akiha and Hisui are still in the sitting room.
It wouldn't be good to ignore them and go back to my room, so I sit on the sofa across from Akiha.

entries.japanese:
「どうぞ、志貴さんはお茶のほうが好きなんですよね」
　琥珀さんが食後のお茶をテーブルに置いてくれた。
「うん、ありがと。
遠慮なくいただきます」
「いえいえ、遠慮なんかしないでくださいな。
ここは志貴さんのお家なんですから、もっと楽にしてください」
　琥珀さんは俺に気を遣ってくれているのか、細かいところまで世話を焼いてくれる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Here you are—tea is what you prefer, isn't it, Shiki?”
Kohaku set a cup of after-lunch tea on the table.
“Thanks. Don't mind if I do.”
“No need to stand on ceremony. This is your home, Shiki, so please make yourself comfortable.”
Perhaps she was trying to put me at ease; Kohaku attended to every little detail.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Here, Shiki-san.
You prefer green tea, right?"
Kohaku-san places an after meal cup of tea on the table beside me.
"Yeah, thanks.
If you don't mind, then."
"No, not at all.
This is your home, so please relax a little more."
Kohaku-san must be trying to make me feel more comfortable here because she takes good care of me.

entries.japanese:
「……まいったな。
俺、これでも屋敷には慣れたつもりなんだけど、まだ緊張してるように見える？」
「そうですねー、まだ両肩に力が入っている感じです。
昔みたいに、とはいかないでしょうけど、もう少しゆったりしていいと思いますよ」
「琥珀、あんまり兄さんを甘やかしちゃだめよ。
ただでさえ有間の家の暮らしで鈍っているんだから、初めは緊張しているぐらいがちょうどいいのよ、この人には」
entries.maoEnglish:
“That's discouraging. I thought I'd finally grown used to this house, but do I still look tense?”
“A little—your shoulders are still rather stiff. It may not be possible to act exactly as you did when you were young, but you can relax a bit more.”
“Kohaku, don't coddle him. Life with the Arima family has already made him soft, so a little tension is exactly what he needs while he settles in.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Geez.
I'm thinking I'm already used to this place.
Do I still look a little strained?"
"Yes, just a little bit.
Your shoulders seem a little tense.
I wouldn't say you should be like back then, but you certainly can relax a bit more."

"Kohaku, you shouldn't spoil Nii-san.
He's been living like a sloth at the Arimas' house so long, it's probably good for him to be a little tense just at first."

entries.japanese:
「ふふ、秋葉さまは志貴さんにだけ厳しいんですね」
「私だって好きで厳しくしてるんじゃないわ。
兄さんがあんまりにものんびりしてるから、こっちが気を配らないといけないだけだもの」
entries.maoEnglish:
“My, Miss Akiha—you only ever seem strict with Shiki.”
“It isn’t as if I enjoy being strict. He’s so hopelessly easygoing that someone has to look after him.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Heehee.
Akiha-sama, you are really strict with Shiki-san, are you not?"
"I don't want to be strict.
It's just that he is always so spaced out, I have to watch out for him."

entries.japanese:
「………ふうん」
　少し驚いた。
　秋葉は琥珀さんと話していると、どことなくいつもの凛とした雰囲気がなくなっている。
　同じ年頃だという事もあるんだろうけど、この二人はすごく仲がいいのかもしれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Huh.”
That surprised me a little.
When Akiha spoke to Kohaku, some of her usual austere composure fell away.
Perhaps it was because they were close in age, but the two of them might genuinely be very good friends.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……… Huh?"
I'm a little surprised.
When Akiha talks to Kohaku-san, there isn't any hint of her usual coldness.
Maybe it's because they're so close in age, but they seem to be really good friends.

entries.japanese:
「………」
　ちらり、と翡翠に視線を移す。
　秋葉が何人もいた使用人を解雇して翡翠と琥珀さんを残した以上、翡翠だって秋葉に信頼されていると思う。
　けど、やっぱり琥珀さんとは正反対の性格のためか、翡翠と秋葉が気軽に会話をする場面は少ない気がする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“……”
I glanced over at Hisui.
Akiha had dismissed the estate’s many servants but kept Hisui and Kohaku, so she must trust Hisui too.
Yet perhaps because Hisui’s temperament was the exact opposite of Kohaku’s, I rarely saw Akiha and Hisui chatting so freely.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"………"
I glance over at Hisui.
Since Akiha dismissed all of the other servants except for Hisui and Kohaku-san, I think Hisui must be trusted by Akiha as well.
But, since Kohaku-san is her complete opposite in personality, I have a feeling that there isn't much talk between Hisui and Akiha.

entries.japanese:
「なんでしょうか、志貴さま」
　俺が見ている事に気がついて、翡翠が用事を聞いてくる。
「いや、別に用事はないんだ。
ただ翡翠は大人しいなって思っただけで」
「―――はい。
そのように槙久さまにお教えいただきました」
　きっぱりと返答する翡翠。
　……なんていうか、きっぱりしすぎていて会話が続いてくれない。
「………………」
　気まずくなって黙り込む。
　と、そんな俺に気を使ってか、琥珀さんが話しかけてきた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Did you need something, Master Shiki?”
Noticing my gaze, Hisui asked whether I had some business with her.
“No, nothing. I was only thinking how quiet you are.”
“Yes. Master Makihisa taught me to be so.”
Hisui delivered the answer with absolute certainty.
Too much certainty, really; it left the conversation nowhere to go.
“……”
I fell silent in awkward defeat.
Perhaps taking pity on me, Kohaku spoke up.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"May I be of service, Shiki-sama?"
Hisui realizes I was looking at her and asks me if there is anything she can do.
"No, it's nothing.
I was just thinking that you're really calm."
"---Yes.
It is something that Makihisa-sama taught to me."
She answers very distinctly.
…… The answer is so distinct, I can't continue the conversation.
"………………"
An uncomfortable silence ensues.

As if sensing this, Kohaku-san starts up a conversation.

entries.japanese:
「そういえば志貴さん、一つお聞きしてよろしいですか？」
「え―――ああ、いいけど、なに？」
「ええ、志貴さまは昨夜もお出かけになられたようですけど、深夜になると定期的に出かけるような用があるのかなって」
「あ―――いや、そんな事はないよ。
ちょっとここ二日間は特別だっただけだから」
　ちらり、と翡翠に視線を移す。
　翡翠は無言で、俺と琥珀さんのやりとりを見つめている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“By the way, Shiki, may I ask you something?”
“Sure—what is it?”
“Master Shiki, you appear to have gone out again last night; I wondered whether you had some regular business that required you to leave after midnight.”
“No, nothing like that. These past two nights were special circumstances, that's all.”
I glanced toward Hisui.
Hisui silently watched the exchange between Kohaku and me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-san.
Is it okay if I ask a question?"
"Eh---ah, yeah.
What is it?"
"It seems like you left last night again, so I was wondering if you had some usual, scheduled routine to take care of every night."
"Ah---no, I don't have anything like that.
The past two days were just something special."
I look over at Hisui.
She just quietly watches the two of us.

entries.japanese:
「大丈夫だよ琥珀さん。
もう夜遅くに外出することはないから。
それにさ、子供じゃないんだから夜出歩くぐらいそう危険なことじゃないだろ？」
「もうっ、なにのんきなコトを言ってるんですか志貴さんはっ！
　ね、翡翠ちゃんもそう思うでしょ？」
「姉さんの言うとおりです。
志貴さまは遠野家の長男なのですから、そのような無用心な行動はお控えください」
entries.maoEnglish:
“It's all right, Kohaku. I won't be going out late anymore. Besides, I'm not a child, so walking around at night is not so dangerous, is it?”
“Honestly, Shiki, how can you be so complacent? Hisui, you agree with me, don’t you?”
“My sister is correct. As the eldest son of the Tohno family, Master Shiki, please refrain from exposing yourself to needless danger.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"It's alright, Kohaku-san.
I won't go out late at night anymore.
Besides, I'm not a kid anymore, so it's not like there's any danger or anything."
"Oh!
Are you still saying that sort of thing, Shiki-san!?
Hisui-chan, don't you feel the same way?"
"It is as Nee-san says.
Shiki-sama, you are the eldest son of the Tohno family, so please refrain from doing anything careless."

entries.japanese:
「ほら、翡翠ちゃんだって怒ってるじゃないですか。
いいですか、志貴さんは貧血持ちなんですから、あんまり無理をしちゃいけないんです。
　わたし、志貴さんの主治医さんにも注意されてるんですからね」
「……いや、それはそうだけど、それと夜の外出は関係ないよ。
一人で出歩くのがいけないんなら、俺は学校にだって行けないじゃないか」
「関係ありますねー。
昼間は明るいから誰かが助けてくれるでしょう？
　けど夜は別です。
とくに最近は吸血鬼殺人とか流行ってるんですから、貧血で倒れたところを襲われる、なんてコトがあったらどうするんですか」
「あ…………」
entries.maoEnglish:
“There, even Hisui is upset. You suffer from anemia, Shiki, so you mustn't overexert yourself.
Your doctor has warned me about it too.”
“I know, but that has nothing to do with going out at night. If being alone is the problem, I wouldn't even be able to attend school.”
“It has everything to do with it. During the day there’s light, and someone would come to your aid. Night is different—especially with all these vampire murders lately. What if you collapsed from anemia and someone attacked you?”
“Ah…”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"See, even Hisui-chan is angry.
You are anemic, so you shouldn't strain yourself, you know?
I was told this by your personal physician too, Shiki-san."
"…… Well, that's true, but it has nothing to do with going out late at night.
If I can't walk by myself, I shouldn't go to school either, right?"
"It does have something to do with it.
During the day it is bright outside and someone could help you, right?
But at night it's different.
There's been all these vampire murders recently, so if you go outside and collapse, what do you think will happen?"
"Ah…………"

entries.japanese:
びくり、と思わず体が震えた。
　こうして、自分以外の誰かから『吸血鬼』という単語を聞くと、本当に弓塚が人を殺していたんだというコトを再認識してしまって。
entries.maoEnglish:
I flinched.
Hearing someone else say vampire forced me to acknowledge all over again that Yumizuka truly had killed people.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Without thinking, my body shudders.
Just hearing someone else use the word "vampire" like this really reminds me that it was Yumizuka killing those people.

entries.japanese:
「……いや、大丈夫だよ琥珀さん。
夜の街に吸血鬼なんていない。
……あの事件は、もう二度とおきないから」
　弓塚さつきは、もうこの世にはいないんだから。
「はい？
　そうなんですか秋葉さま？」
「わたしに聞かれてもわかるわけがありません。
断言しているのは兄さんなんですから、兄さんには何か根拠でもあるんでしょう。
　そういえば、兄さんの高校では殺人事件の犠牲者になった方がいたらしいけど。
二年三組といったら兄さんのクラスではなかったかしら」
「え……？
　俺のクラスで犠牲者なんていないけど」
entries.maoEnglish:
“It's all right, Kohaku. There are no vampires in the streets at night. Those murders will never happen again.”
Because Satsuki Yumizuka was no longer in this world.
“Really? Is that true, Miss Akiha?”
“How should I know? He is the one making such a categorical claim, so presumably he has some basis for it.
Come to think of it, I heard a student at your school fell victim to the murders. Wasn’t Class Two-Three your class?”
“What? Nobody in my class was a victim.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… No, it's okay, Kohaku-san.
There isn't a vampire out there anymore.
…… Those incidents, they won't happen ever again."
Because Yumizuka Satsuki… is no longer in this world.
"Oh?
Is that true, Akiha-sama?"
"I haven't heard anything about it.
The one to ask is Nii-san, since he seems to know something about it.
Oh yeah, there was a victim from your high school, Nii-san.
Year 2 Class 3 is your class, right?"
"Eh……?
There wasn't a victim from my class."

entries.japanese:
「あ、志貴さんは今朝のニュースを見てないんですね。
なんでも一昨日の夜、弓塚さつきという方の血痕が大通りの路地裏で発見されたそうなんです。
　血痕自体はもっと前についたものらしいんですけど、現場に残された出血量からして死亡しているのはまず間違いないという話ですよ」
「―――――――」
　……動悸が激しい。
　彼女。
弓塚さつきが死亡しているなんて、そんな事は誰よりもよくわかっている。
　けれど、こうはっきりと“死亡している”と言われると、“おまえが殺したんだろう”と言われている気がして――――
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh, you didn’t see the news this morning. Apparently blood belonging to a girl named Satsuki Yumizuka was found the night before last in an alley off the main avenue.
The blood itself appears to have been there longer, but from the volume lost at the scene, the authorities say there can be little doubt that she is dead.”
“…”
My heart began to pound.
She was dead. Satsuki Yumizuka was dead, and I knew it better than anyone.
But hearing it declared so plainly made it sound like an accusation—You killed her
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah, Shiki-san, you didn't see the news this morning.
Last night, they found a large quantity of blood from someone named Yumizuka Satsuki in an alley off the main street.
The blood seems to have been there for a while, but from the amount of blood there, they say she is more than likely dead."

"-------"
…… My heart starts to throb violently.
The fact that Yumizuka Satsuki is dead, I know that better than anyone else.
But when they say that she's dead, it sounds like, "you killed her, didn't you?" to me----

entries.japanese:
「―――兄さん？
　どうしたのよ、顔色が悪いわよ」
「―――いや、別に、なにも―――」
　気分が沈む。
　せっかく翡翠のおかげで心が落ち着いてくれたのに、こんな些細なことで倒れそうになるなんて、なんて、この心は弱いのか。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Brother? What's wrong—you've gone pale.”
“It's nothing, really.”
My spirits sank.
Hisui had only just calmed me, yet something so small had nearly brought me down again—how could my heart be this weak?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Nii-san?
What's wrong, you're really pale."
"---No, it's, nothing---"
My mood starts to sink.
Thanks to Hisui, my heart was able to be calm, but with just this conversation, I almost collapse.
Is my heart really this weak?

entries.japanese:
「みなさん、今夜は歓迎会をいたしましょう！」
　と。
　いきなり、琥珀さんがはしゃぐような大声をあげた。
――――はい？
　と、俺と秋葉と、あまつさえ翡翠までもが首をかしげる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Everyone, let's hold a welcome party tonight!”
And then.
Kohaku cried out with breathless enthusiasm.
――――Huh?
Akiha, Hisui, and I all tilted our heads in unison.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Everyone, let's have a welcome party tonight!"
Just like that,
Kohaku-san makes an announcement in a loud voice.
----Huh?
Akiha and I say the same thing aloud, and even Hisui tilts her head.

entries.japanese:
「ですから志貴さんの歓迎会をしましょう！
　せっかくみんなそろっているんですし、志貴さんの引っ越し祝いもまだしてないじゃないですか。
　ですから、今夜は志貴さんの歓迎会なんです」
　ね、と琥珀さんは俺ににっこりと笑顔をむけてくる。
「…………………」
　……まいった。
　翡翠といい琥珀さんといい、どうしてこう、俺が弱っているコトに敏感なんだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“A welcome party for Shiki! We’re all together, and we haven’t even celebrated his moving home yet.
So tonight is Shiki’s welcome party.”
Kohaku turned a brilliant smile on me, inviting my agreement.
“……”
I was helpless.
Hisui and Kohaku both seemed uncannily sensitive to every moment of weakness in me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"A welcome party for Shiki-san!
Everyone is here, and we haven't even celebrated Shiki-san's arrival yet.
So, tonight should be Shiki-san's welcome party."
"Right?" Kohaku-san looks at me and smiles.
"………………"
…… Crap.
Why are Hisui and Kohaku-san so able to read my feelings?

entries.japanese:
「秋葉さま、よろしいですか？
　お許しがいただければ、いまから腕によりをかけてご馳走をお作りしますけど」
「そうね、せっかく兄さんが帰ってきたのに何もしないっていうのもなんだし。
わたしは賛成だけど、翡翠はどう？
　もちろん賛成でしょ？」
「あ―――はい、志貴さまがよろしいというのでしたら、わたしも、悪くはないと思います」
　じっ、と三人の目がこっちにむけられる。
　俺は―――
entries.maoEnglish:
“Would that be all right, Miss Akiha? If you give me permission, I’ll start now and make a proper feast.”
“Yes, we should do something now that Brother has finally come home. I'm in favor, but what about you, Hisui? You agree, of course?”
“If Master Shiki approves, I suppose I would not object.”
All three pairs of eyes settled on me.
I—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Akiha-sama, is that acceptable?
If you allow it, we can start the preparations right away."
"Yes, Nii-san has finally come back and we haven't even done anything.
I think it's a good idea but… Hisui?
You agree, right?"
"Ah---yes, if it is acceptable to Shiki-sama, I do not think it will be a bad thing."
The three of them turn to stare at me.
I---

entries.japanese:
ぎい、と音をたてて扉が開く。
　重い身体と鈍い思考のまま屋敷に帰ってきた。
　ずっ、ずっ、という足音。
　月明かりに伸びる自身の影は、くたびれた亡霊じみている。
entries.maoEnglish:
The door creaks open.
I have made it back to the mansion, though my body is leaden and my thoughts barely move.
My footsteps scrape and drag.
In the moonlight, my long shadow looks like the ghost of some exhausted man.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The door opens with a creak.
With a heavy body and dulled mind, I make it back to the mansion.
My footsteps drag behind me.
The moonlight illuminates my figure, making it look like an exhausted ghost.

entries.japanese:
「―――――――――――っ」
　……弓塚に裂かれた左腕が痛む。
　出血はとうに止まっている。
軋むような痛みは残留しているものの、傷自体はそう深いものではなかったらしい。
「―――――――――――」
　階段に向かう。
　傷の手当てなんて知らない。
　今はただ、一秒でも早く部屋に戻って、泥のように眠りたかった―――――
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ngh—!”
My left arm throbs where Yumizuka tore it open.
The bleeding stopped long ago. A grinding ache remains, but the wound itself cannot be very deep.
“……”
I make for the stairs.
I do not know the first thing about treating a wound.
All I want is to reach my room one second sooner and sink into dreamless sleep—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-----------"
…… My left arm hurts where Yumizuka wounded me.
The bleeding has stopped, and the gradual lessening of the pain tells me it couldn't have been too deep.

"-----------"
I reach the stairs.
I don't even care about treating my wounds.
Right now, I just want to stumble back to my room and sleep like a rock----

entries.japanese:
長い眠りから目が覚めた。
　窓から入ってくる陽射しは、すでに朝というより昼の陽射しだった。
　昨夜、夜遅くに帰ってきたせいだろう。
　昼近くになって、ようやく俺は目が覚めたらしい。
entries.maoEnglish:
I wake from a long sleep.
The sunlight coming through the window belongs more to noon than morning.
I must have slept late because I came home so late last night.
It seems I have only just awakened, with midday almost here.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I wake from a long sleep.
The sunshine from the window looks closer to mid-day than morning.
It must be because of how late I got back last night.
It seems I've overslept.

entries.japanese:
「……………」
　ベッドから体を起こして、自分の手を見る。
――――まだ、弓塚を刺した時の感触が残っている。
　二日前の夜。
　弓塚に出会って、その晩にひどい悪夢を見た。
「……いっそ昨日のことも……夢なら、よかったのに」
　そんな都合のいい話はない。
　弓塚が吸血鬼だった理由もわからなければ、アイツを助けてやる事もできなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“……”
I sit up in bed and stare at my hand.
――――I can still feel the moment I stabbed Yumizuka.
Two nights ago.
I met Yumizuka, and that night I had a terrible nightmare.
“I only wish yesterday had been a dream.”
But nothing could be that convenient.
I never learned why Yumizuka had become a vampire, and I could do nothing to save her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……………"
Dragging myself up from bed, I look down at my hand.
----The sensation of how I stabbed Yumizuka remains.
Two nights ago.
When I met Yumizuka and saw that hideous dream.
"…… If only yesterday…… was just a dream."
But wishing it won't make it so.
I've no clue why or how Yumizuka became a vampire, and I couldn't do anything to help her.

entries.japanese:
―――いや。
　ああなってしまった弓塚を助ける方法なんてなかったのかもしれない。
　彼女は、とっくに生きてはいなかった。
　俺がした事は、人並みに動き回れる死体を、ちゃんとした死体に戻しただけの事だって、それぐらいのことは考えられる。
　だが、それでも―――
「失礼します、志貴さま」
　もう馴染みになった声がして、翡翠が部屋に入ってきた。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――No.
Maybe there had been no saving Yumizuka after what she became.
She had stopped being alive long before.
I can understand that much: all I did was turn a corpse that could still walk around like anyone else into a corpse that behaved properly.
And yet—
“Excuse me, Master Shiki.”
Hisui enters the room, her voice already familiar to me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---No.
Once Yumizuka had become like that, there was probably no way for anyone to help her.
She was already dead.
All I did was return that corpse somehow moving about as if it were a living thing back to being a dead body.
That's the only way I can think of it.
But, still---
"Please excuse me, Shiki-sama."
With that voice I have become accustomed to, Hisui enters the room.

entries.japanese:
「おはようございます志貴さま。
今日は体調のほうはよろしいですか？」
「ん……ああ、よく眠ったおかげかな、体の調子は悪くないよ」
「そうですか。
それを聞いて安心しました」
　……眉一つ動かさないで言われても、翡翠が安心しているようにはとても見えない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Good morning, Master Shiki. How are you feeling today?”
“Mm—I think all that sleep helped, because I don’t feel bad.”
“I see. I am relieved to hear it.”
With her expression perfectly still, she hardly looks relieved.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Good morning, Shiki-sama.
How are you feeling today?"
"Hm…… ah, I slept well, so I don't feel bad at all."
"Is that so?
Hearing that makes me feel very relieved."
…… Even though she says that, I don't see her even relax her shoulders, or give any other indication of it.

entries.japanese:
「…………」
　けど、俺は安心できた。
　昨夜の出来事から、たった一晩しか明けていない。
俺は、もうあの異常な世界から抜け出せないだろうって、心のどこかで諦めていた。
「……ありがとう翡翠。
きみの事だから、朝から何度も様子を見に来てくれたんだろ？
　気を遣ってくれて、感謝してる」
「――――いえ。
志貴さまのお世話をさせていただくのがわたしの仕事ですから」
　かすかに嬉しがっているような翡翠の表情。
entries.maoEnglish:
“……”
But I found relief.
Only one night had passed since it happened. Somewhere inside, I had resigned myself to never escaping that mad world.
“Thank you, Hisui. Knowing you, you probably checked on me again and again this morning, didn’t you? I appreciate your concern.”
“No. It is my duty to attend to you, Master Shiki.”
Something in Hisui’s expression looks almost pleased.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……………"
But, I feel relieved as well.
Because of what happened last night, the long night is over.
Because I don't have to enter that unnatural world any longer, my heart can relax.
"…… Thanks, Hisui.
You've always come to check up on me from early in the morning, right?
Your concern means a lot to me."
"----Not at all.
It is my duty to be concerned with your welfare."
There is a hint of happiness in Hisui's expression.

entries.japanese:
……それに、幾分救われた気がした。
　こうしてベッドに眠っていて、いつも通り翡翠が起こしに来てくれる。
　そんな些細な事だけで、自分はちゃんとした日常に戻ってこれたって実感できたんだから。
entries.maoEnglish:
That tiny change in her face saves me a little.
I slept here in my own bed, and Hisui came to wake me as she always does.
Something so small is enough to make me feel that I have truly returned to an ordinary life.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Moreover, I feel like I've been somewhat rescued.
While I've been sleeping in bed like this, Hisui came as always to wake me up.
With just that trivial thing, I honestly feel like I have returned to my normal life.

entries.japanese:
「あの……志貴さま、申し上げにくいことなのですが、よろしいでしょうか？」
「……？
　なに、言いにくい事って。
昼過ぎまで寝てた事には弁解のしようがないから、平謝りするしかないけど」
「いえ、そのようなことではないのですが、多少は志貴さまの睡眠時間が関係あることかもしれません」
　翡翠は言いにくそうにもじもじと指を絡ませている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki, there is something difficult for me to say; may I?”
“Hm? What could be difficult? If this is about sleeping past noon, I have no excuse and can only apologize.”
“No, not that, although it may have something to do with how long Master Shiki slept.”
Hisui fidgets, uneasily lacing and unlacing her fingers.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Um…… Shiki-sama, this is somewhat difficult for me to say, but… can I?"
"……?
Difficult to say?
If it's about me sleeping in till noon, I really can't do anything but apologize."
"No, that is not what I meant, but it is perhaps related to when you went to sleep."
Hisui fidgets with her fingers as she struggles to come up with the right words.

entries.japanese:
「……その、わたしがいたらないばかりに、昨夜のことを秋葉さまに知られてしまいました」
「え……昨夜のことって……なに？」
「ですから、志貴さまがお出かけになられた事です」
「う――――」
　思わず翡翠から目を逸らす。
　自分ではうまくやり過ごしたつもりだったけど、やっぱり翡翠にはバレてしまっていたか。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Through my own failings, Miss Akiha learned about last night.”
“Last night—what do you mean?”
“That you went out, Master Shiki.”
“Urk—”
I look away without meaning to.
I thought I had covered my tracks, but Hisui saw through me after all.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Um, I did not say anything, but Akiha-sama found out about last night."
"Eh…… about last night…… what?"
"I mean when you left late last night, Shiki-sama."
"Oh----"
I unconsciously turn my eyes away from her.
I thought I'd managed to slip away undetected, but I should have known Hisui would still find out.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さまは夜のうちに戻られましたから秋葉さまもそう気に留めてらっしゃらないようですが、のちほど何か聞かれることは確実です。
　居間のほうにいかれるのでしたら、どうか気を引き締めてください」
「………そっか。
まあ仕方ないよな、文句の一つや二つぐらい。
門限を破っているのはこっちのほうなんだから」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Because Master Shiki returned before the night was over, Miss Akiha does not seem overly concerned, though she is certain to question you later.
If you intend to go to the sitting room, please prepare yourself.”
“I see. Well, I can hardly complain if she gives me an earful. I’m the one who broke curfew.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama, your return late at night has gained the attention of Akiha-sama, so I believe you will be asked to explain yourself sooner or later.
She is in the sitting room and may be angry, so please be prepared."
"……… I see.
Oh well, I can't complain, since it was me that went out past curfew."

entries.japanese:
「その件ですが、今後もこのような事があるのですか？
　わたしは志貴さまをお止めすることはできませんが、昨夜のような事が続くようでしたら秋葉さまにお報せしなくてはなりません」
「――――いや、昨日みたいな事はもうないよ。
全部、昨日で終わったんだ。
……もう、電話がかかってくることなんて、ない」
entries.maoEnglish:
“On that subject, should I expect this to happen again? I cannot prevent you from leaving, Master Shiki, but if nights like the last one continue, I will be obliged to inform Miss Akiha.”
“—No, nothing like yesterday will happen again. It all ended yesterday. There won’t be any more phone calls.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"About that, will it be occurring again?
I cannot stop you, but if you continue doing such things, I must tell Akiha-sama."
"----No, nothing like last night will happen again.
Everything…… has ended last night…… There won't be any phone calls anymore."

entries.japanese:
―――そう。
本当に、決着がついた。
　こうして言葉にして、ようやく終わった。
　弓塚さつきはもういない。
　街を騒がしていた吸血鬼は消えて、俺は、自分のことを好きだったと言ってくれたクラスメイトを、自らの手で、永久に喪った。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Yes. It really is over.
Only after saying it aloud does the ending become real.
Satsuki Yumizuka is gone.
The vampire that terrorized the city has disappeared, and with my own hands I have lost forever the classmate who told me she loved me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Yes.
It really has ended.
With these words, it truly is over.
Yumizuka Satsuki is no more.
The vampire skulking the streets has vanished.
I, with my own hands, sent away a classmate who said she liked me, for all eternity.

entries.japanese:
「…………………」
　翡翠は痛ましそうな顔で俺を見る。
　……まったく、翡翠にあんな顔をさせるぐらい、今の自分はひどい顔をしてるってコトか。
「―――さ、時間も時間だしいいかげん起きないとな。
翡翠、秋葉は今日は屋敷にいるの？
　なにかと忙しいヤツだから、やっぱり休日も習い事をしてるとか」
「はい、秋葉さまは休日も予定が入っておりますが、今日は屋敷に残っておられます」
「………？」
　予定はあるけど、屋敷には残ってる……？
entries.maoEnglish:
“……”
Hisui watches me with pain in her eyes.
Do I really look so awful that even Hisui has to make that face?
“Well, it’s getting late, so I should get up. Hisui, is Akiha home today? She’s always busy—does she have lessons even on holidays?”
“Miss Akiha has an engagement today despite the holiday, but she will remain at the mansion.”
“……?”
She has plans, but she is staying here?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……………………"
Hisui looks at me with a painful expression on her face.
…… Geez, if Hisui is making that sort of face, then I must look terrible right now.
"---Well, I should get up sooner or later.
Hisui, is Akiha still here?
She's an awfully busy person, so does she have a routine on her day off?"
"Yes, she does have plans during her day off, but today she is still in the mansion."
"………?"
She has plans, but she's still here……?

entries.japanese:
「よくわからないけど……ま、とにかく着替えたら居間に行くから、先に行っていてくれ」
「はい。
それでは失礼します」
　翡翠はいつも通り、足音一つたてず立ち去っていく。
―――と、大事なコトを忘れていた。
「翡翠」
entries.maoEnglish:
“I don’t quite follow, but I’ll come to the sitting room when I’m dressed, so go on ahead.”
“Very well. If you will excuse me.”
As always, Hisui departs without making a sound.
―――Wait—I nearly forgot something important.
“Hisui.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I don't quite get it, but…… well, I'll go and get changed, so please head to the sitting room before me."
"Yes.
Well then, please excuse me."
As usual, Hisui walks away without a sound.
---But, I forgot something really important.
"Hisui."

entries.japanese:
「はい？
　なんでしょうか、志貴さま」
「うん、言い忘れてた。
起こしにきてくれてありがとう。
遅れたけど、おはよう翡翠」
「―――はい。
どうかよい一日を、志貴さま」
　さて。
　こっちも手早く着替えて居間に向かうことにしよう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Yes? What is it, Master Shiki?”
“I forgot to say it. Thanks for coming to wake me. And though it’s late—good morning, Hisui.”
“Yes. I hope you have a pleasant day, Master Shiki.”
Well, then.
I had better dress quickly and head for the sitting room myself.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yes?
What is it, Shiki-sama?"
"Yeah, I forgot to say something.
Thanks for coming to wake me up.
It's a little late, but good morning, Hisui."
"---Yes.
Please have a nice day, Shiki-sama."
Well then.
I should hurry up and change, and head to the sitting room.

entries.japanese:
ぎい、と音をたてて扉が開く。
　重い身体と鈍い思考のまま屋敷に帰ってきた。
　ずっ、ずっ、という足音。
　月明かりに伸びる自身の影は、くたびれた亡霊じみている。
entries.maoEnglish:
The door creaks open.
I have made it back to the mansion, though my body is leaden and my thoughts barely move.
My footsteps scrape and drag.
In the moonlight, my long shadow looks like the ghost of some exhausted man.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The door opens with a creak.
With a heavy body and dulled mind, I make it back to the mansion.
My footsteps drag behind me.
The moonlight illuminates my figure, making it look like an exhausted ghost.

"-----------"
…… My left arm hurts where Yumizuka wounded me.
The bleeding has stopped, and the gradual lessening of the pain tells me it couldn't have been too deep.

entries.japanese:
「―――――――――――っ」
　……弓塚に裂かれた左腕が痛む。
　出血はとうに止まっている。
軋むような痛みは残留しているものの、傷自体はそう深いものではなかったらしい。
「―――――――――――」
　階段に向かう。
　傷の手当てなんて知らない。
今はただ、一秒でも早く部屋に戻って、泥のように眠りたかっ―――
「え………？
　兄、さん…………？」
―――と。
　階段の中頃から、秋葉の声が聞こえてきた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ngh—!”
My left arm throbs where Yumizuka tore it open.
The bleeding stopped long ago. A grinding ache remains, but the wound itself cannot be very deep.
“……”
I make for the stairs.
I do not know the first thing about treating a wound. All I want is to reach my room one second sooner and fall asl—
“Huh…? Bro—ther?”
―――Then.
Akiha’s voice comes from halfway down the stairs.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-----------"
I reach the stairs.
I don't even care about treating my wounds.
Right now, I just want to stumble back to my room and sleep like a rock----

"Eh………?
Nii--san…………?"
--And then.
From the middle of the stairs, I hear Akiha's voice.

entries.japanese:
「………………秋葉？」
　顔をあげる。
　そこには―――たった今階段から降りてきた秋葉の姿があった。
「あ…………」
　……秋葉は黙っている。
　なにか様子がおかしいと思う反面、そんな事なんてどうでもよくて、ふらふらと歩いていく。
　帰るべき場所は自分の部屋だ。
　それには階段を使わないといけない。
　ぼんやりと立ち尽くしている秋葉の横をぬけて、階段を上らないと―――
entries.maoEnglish:
“Akiha?”
I raise my head.
There she stands, having just come down the stairs.
“Ah.”
Akiha says nothing.
Some part of me notices that something is wrong with her, but I cannot bring myself to care.
I stagger onward.
My room is where I need to go.
To reach it, I have to pass the dazed Akiha and climb the stairs—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……………… Akiha?"
I raise my head.
In front of me---I see Akiha who has just now made it to the bottom of the stairway.
"Ah…………"
…… Akiha is silent.
Something about her appearance is a little strange, but I don't even care right now and continue stumbling up the steps.
Right now I should just go to my room.
So I have to keep going up the stairs.
I dazedly make my way past Akiha's still figure.
I have to get up the stairs---

entries.japanese:
「ちょ……ちょっと待ってください兄さん！
　こんな夜更けに何処に行っていたんですか？」
「―――――――」
　さあ。
そういう秋葉こそ、こんな時間にどうしてこんな所にいるんだろう。
　足音を忍ばせて階段を下りるなんて、まるで今から外に出かけようとしていたみたいだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“W-wait, Brother! Where have you been at this hour of the night?”
“……”
Who knows. For that matter, what is Akiha herself doing here so late?
She was creeping down the stairs without a sound, almost as if she had been about to slip outside.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"H…… Hey, please wait, Nii-san!
Just where did you go this late in the evening?"
"-------"
Who knows?
Besides, what is Akiha doing standing here at this hour anyway?
Trying to glide down the stairs as quietly as possible, it seems like she was going to go outside just now.

entries.japanese:
「……秋葉には関係ない。
部屋に戻るから、邪魔しないでくれ」
「邪魔って、私は―――」
　言いかけて、ハッと秋葉は息を飲んだ。
「兄さん、その体―――」
　さっきまで驚いていた秋葉の目が静かになる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“It’s none of your business, Akiha. I’m going to my room, so get out of my way.”
“You say I’m in your way, but I was only—”
Halfway through, Akiha catches her breath.
“Brother, your body—”
The shock drains from Akiha’s eyes, leaving them suddenly still.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… It doesn't have anything to do with you, Akiha.
I'm going to my room, so don't bother me."
"Bother, I---"
Akiha gasps and cuts off mid-sentence.
"Nii-san, you look---"
Her previously shocked eyes become calm.

entries.japanese:
「左腕に傷がありますね。
よく見れば洋服も所々汚れています」
「……気にしないでくれ。
もう痛くないんだ、そこは」
「痛くないって、そんなハズはないでしょう。
今にも倒れそうな顔をして、左腕には血の跡があるんです。
もうっ、今まで一体何をしていたんですか兄さんは」
「……………」
　答えられず、秋葉から視線を逸らした。
　今夜起きた出来事を説明する事なんてできないし、何より―――弓塚との事を誰にも話したくなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Your left arm is wounded. And now that I look, your clothes are filthy in places.”
“Don’t worry about it. That arm doesn’t hurt anymore.”
“How could it not hurt? You look ready to collapse, and there is blood on your left arm. Honestly, Brother—what have you been doing all this time?”
“……”
Unable to answer, I turn my eyes away from her.
I could never explain what happened tonight; more than that, I did not want to tell anyone what passed between Yumizuka and me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Your left arm is injured, right?
Your clothes are pretty dirty too."
"…… Don't worry about it.
It doesn't even hurt anymore."
"It doesn't hurt?
That can't be true.
You look like you could collapse at any moment, and there's blood clotted all over your left arm.
Goodness, just what in the world were you doing, Nii-san?"
"……………"
I can't answer, and only avert my gaze.
I couldn't possibly explain everything that happened tonight, and more than that---I don't ever want to talk about Yumizuka to anyone.

entries.japanese:
「……別に。
街を歩いてたら酔っ払いにからまれただけだ。
ただのケンカ」
　簡潔に言って、秋葉の横を通りすぎる。
　そこを、ぐっ、と。
　秋葉に首根っこを掴まれてしまった。
「兄さん。
私、怒りますよ」
　どこか弱々しい声で、秋葉はまっすぐにこちらを見つめてくる。
「……………」
　そんな顔をされると、ますます本当の事なんて言えなくなる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Nothing. Some drunk picked a fight with me while I was walking through town. That’s all.”
I give her the barest answer and walk past.
Then—yank.
Akiha grabs me by the back of the collar.
“Brother. I am going to lose my temper.”
Her voice sounds strangely frail, and she looks straight into my eyes.
“……”
With a face like that, she only makes it harder for me to tell her the truth.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Nothing much.
I was just walking around and got sucked into a little drunken brawling."
Answering simply, I climb past her.
But with a pull,
Akiha places her hands on my shoulders.
"Nii-san, I'll get mad."
With a weak voice, Akiha looks directly at me.
"……………"
With her face like that, I become even more unable to tell her what really happened.

entries.japanese:
「―――――」
「……………」
　俺と秋葉はそのまま、言葉もなく時間を過ごす。
　……数分が経って、はあ、と秋葉は諦めた様に肩をさげた。
「いいわ。
事情は聞かない事にします」
　秋葉は傷ついていない右腕を掴んで、居間に向かって歩き出す。
entries.maoEnglish:
“……”
“……”
Akiha and I remain there in silence.
Several minutes pass before she sighs and lets her shoulders fall in surrender.
“Fine. I won’t ask what happened.”
Akiha takes hold of my uninjured right arm and starts toward the sitting room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-----"
"……………"
Just like that, time passes without either of us speaking.
…… After some minutes pass, Akiha lets out a breath and drops her shoulders in resignation.
"Fine.
I will let it go."
Akiha grabs my uninjured right arm and heads towards the sitting room.

entries.japanese:
「……ちょっと、秋葉。
俺、部屋に戻って眠りたいんだけど」
「だめです。
何も聞かない事にしたんですから、かわりに手当てぐらいはさせてもらっていいでしょう？
　ほら、こっちです。
そんな格好のまま眠られては心配で仕方がないわ」
　秋葉は俺の腕を掴んだまま、ズカズカとロビーを横切っていく。
「………………」
　こうなっては仕方がない。
　諦めて秋葉の言い分に従う事にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Wait, Akiha. I want to go to my room and sleep.”
“No. If I am not to ask any questions, you can at least allow me to tend your wounds, can’t you? Come along. I could never rest knowing you had gone to sleep in that condition.”
Still gripping my arm, Akiha marches across the lobby.
“……”
There is no arguing with her now.
I give up and let her have her way.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Hey, Akiha.
I wanna go back to my room and sleep."
"No.
I won't ask you any more about it, so you have to let me treat your injuries, okay?
So come this way.
I can't help but be worried if you go to sleep looking like that."
Still holding on to my arm, she drags me with her to the lobby.
"…………………"
Oh well.
This is just how it is.
I resign myself to doing as Akiha says.

entries.japanese:
―――手当てはわりと簡単だった。
　もともと大した傷ではなかったのか、消毒をして薬を塗って、ガーゼを当てて包帯を巻くという必要最小限の手当て。
　それを一人でこなした後、秋葉はお湯で絞ったタオルで俺の顔を拭いて、ようやく一段落ついたらしい。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――The treatment proves simple enough.
Perhaps the wound was never serious, because her treatment was minimal: disinfectant, ointment, gauze, then a bandage.
After handling it all herself, Akiha wipes my face with a towel wrung out in hot water and at last seems satisfied.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---The treatment was quite simple.
I guess it was really not that bad to begin with.
After applying some disinfectant and wrapping the wound in gauze, my treatment is over.
After finishing that simple care by herself, Akiha takes a towel soaked in warm water and wipes my face.

entries.japanese:
「はい、これでおしまいです。
その学生服はもう駄目ですね。
