“I wasn’t suffering. Akiha was cheerful, and we all had a wonderful evening. People must tell you that you worry too much.”
Still gazing vaguely into the trees, I make my voice as gentle as I can.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"It wasn't tough at all.
Akiha was so happy, and it was fun.
Kohaku-san, you're just thinking about it too much."
Staring blankly into the forest, I try to make my voice sound as gentle as possible.

entries.japanese:
…………。
　………………………。
　……………………………………。
　……………………………………………………。
　少しの、沈黙の後。
　突然、それこそ草むらから出てきた兎のように、ぴょこんと琥珀さんが俺の視界に入ってきた。
entries.maoEnglish:
…
……
………
…………
After a short silence.
Kohaku suddenly pops into my field of vision like a rabbit springing from the undergrowth.
entries.mirrorMoon:
………
…………………………
…………………………………
…………………………………………
A brief silence ensues.
Suddenly, like a rabbit poking its head out of a bush, Kohaku-san comes into view.

entries.japanese:
「琥珀さん？」
「あっ、やっぱりちゃんと起きてたんですね志貴さん。
急に黙り込んだりするから、眠っちゃったのかと思ったじゃないですか」
　めっ、と叱ってくる。
　どうも、ここで眠ったらいけませんよー、という事を言いたいらしい。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Kohaku?”
“Ah, so you were awake after all, Shiki. You suddenly went quiet, and I thought you had fallen asleep.”
She gives me a playful scolding.
Evidently she means to say that sleeping out here is forbidden.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Kohaku-san?"
"Ah, so you are awake, Shiki-san.
You got so quiet all of a sudden, I thought you fell asleep."
She says this, scolding me.
It sounds like she wants to tell me that I shouldn't sleep here.

entries.japanese:
「……大丈夫だよ琥珀さん。
ちゃんと起きてるから、心配しなくていい。
酔いが冷めたら部屋に戻るから、琥珀さんは部屋に戻ってなよ」
「んー、お断りします。
わたしも涼みたかった所ですし、志貴さんがお部屋に戻られるまでお付き合いさせてくださいね」
　いつも通りの笑顔で言って、琥珀さんは森の中で落ち葉を楽しそうに眺めたりする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’m fine, Kohaku—I’m awake, so you don’t need to worry. Once I sober up, I’ll go inside. You should return to your room.”
“No, thank you. I wanted some fresh air myself, so please allow me to stay until you go back inside, Shiki.”
Smiling as she always does, Kohaku begins happily studying the fallen leaves beneath the trees.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I'm fine, Kohaku-san.
I'm awake, so don't worry.
I'll go back to my room once I'm done cooling off, so you can go back inside."
"Mm, I refuse.
I wanted to cool off as well, so I will keep you company until you are done."
With her usual smile, Kohaku-san looks longingly at the fallen leaves in the forest.

entries.japanese:
「……まあ、涼むのは琥珀さんの勝手だからいいんだけど」
　琥珀さんは答えず、カシュカシュと音をたてて落ち葉を踏んだりしている。
　…………。
　………………………。
　……………………………………。
　……………………………………………………。
　また、しばしの沈黙のあと。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Well, it’s your business if you want some air.”
Kohaku does not answer, merely crunching through the fallen leaves.
…
……
………
…………
Another brief silence passes.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Well, if you feel like it, then that's fine, Kohaku-san."
Kohaku-san doesn't answer, and she walks over the leaves, which crinkle as she takes each step.
…………
………………………
…………………………………
……………………………………………………
Silence ensues again.

entries.japanese:
「……ありがとう琥珀さん。
今日は楽しかった」
　椅子に座ったまま、心からの本心を告げた。
「どうしたんですか？
　今日の事なんて、そんなお礼を言われるほどの事ではないですよ」
「……そうかな。
でも本当に楽しかった。
考えてみると、こういうふうに家族で騒ぐのは初めてだったし、きっと、こういうのに憧れていたから」
　……有間の家でこういう席がなかったわけじゃない。
ただ自分は有間の家で誰にも迷惑をかけないいい子でいたから、今日のように気がねなく楽しむ事はなかっただけ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Thank you, Kohaku. I had a wonderful time tonight.”
Still seated, I tell her exactly what I feel.
“What brought this on? Tonight was hardly anything worth thanking me for.”
“Maybe not, but I really did enjoy it. Thinking about it, this was the first time I’d ever let loose with my family. I suppose I’d always wanted something like this.”
It is not as though the Arima family never held gatherings like this. I simply spent my time there being the good boy who never inconvenienced anyone, so I never relaxed and enjoyed myself as freely as I did tonight.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Thanks, Kohaku-san.
It was really fun today."
I really do mean it.
"What do you mean?
Today wasn't something you should thank us for."
"…… Maybe, but it really was fun.
Come to think of it, it was the first time we did something like that, and I finally felt like part of the family."
…… It isn't like we didn't do things like that when I stayed at the Arimas'.
It's just that when I lived there, I didn't ever want to be a bother, and I couldn't concentrate on having fun like today.

entries.japanese:
「家族……ですか？」
　首をかしげて、静かに呟く。
　琥珀さんはほんのわずかだけ能面じみた貌をした後、いつもの調子で顔をあげた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Family…?”
Kohaku tilts her head and murmurs the word.
For the briefest instant, her face goes blank as a Noh mask; then she looks up in her usual manner.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Family?"
Tilting her head to the side, she asks in a soft voice.
For a very brief instant, it looked like Kohaku-san removed her usual mask, but she returns to her usual self.

entries.japanese:
「でも志貴さん。
貴方はこの屋敷にいるかぎり、志貴さんが憧れているような家族というものは手に入りませんよ。
　遠野家の親戚の方々はみな志貴さまを疎んじておられます。
志貴さんの味方は秋葉さまだけです。
　ですから、これからの生活は志貴さんにとって心苦しいものになるでしょう」
　……琥珀さんの言う事はもっともだ。
　八年前、俺は親父や親戚会議で勘当寸前にまで扱われたわけだから、そんな自分の立場が今になって良くなるとは思っていない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“But, Shiki. As long as you remain in this mansion, you will never have the kind of family you long for.
Every one of the Tohno relatives resents Master Shiki. Miss Akiha is the only person on his side.
Life here will therefore become very painful for you.”
Kohaku is right.
Eight years ago, my father and the family council came close to disowning me, so I have no reason to think their opinion will have improved since then.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"But Shiki-san, as long as you stay at the mansion, you won't ever have the family you are dreaming about.
All your relatives shun you and your only ally is Akiha-sama.
That means that your life here will be very painful."
…… What she says is correct.
Eight years ago, I was treated badly enough to get me out of this house, so it's natural that they still think badly of me.

entries.japanese:
「……まあ、それぐらいは覚悟してるよ。
でも、そんな事はどうでもいいんだ。
秋葉はそれを八年間も耐えてきたじゃないか。
俺は兄貴なんだから、秋葉が耐えてきた事ぐらい余裕でこなさないと悪いだろ」
　八年間。
　秋葉は子供の頃から、一人で遠野家の厳格な教えに耐えてきた。
　それに比べれば親戚連中からの嫌味なんて、顧みるに値しないだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’m prepared for that much. But it doesn’t matter. Akiha endured it for eight whole years. I’m her older brother; it would be shameful if I couldn’t handle what she did with ease.”
Eight years.
From the time she was a child, Akiha endured the rigid discipline of the Tohno family alone.
Compared with that, a few spiteful remarks from our relatives are not worth considering.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Well, I'm prepared for that, but it doesn't really matter.
Akiha put up with it for eight years.
I'm her big brother, so I should be able to put up with it easily."
Those eight years.
Since she was little, Akiha had to endure a very strict upbringing.
Compared to that, my relatives disliking me really isn't that much.

entries.japanese:
「そうですか。
秋葉さまは幸せですね。
こんなに妹思いのお兄さんが傍にいてくれるんですから」
「それはどうかな。
秋葉にとって、俺はいい兄貴じゃないと思うけど」
　琥珀さんは笑顔のまま、ただクスクスと笑い続けた。
　……なんていうか、そう嬉しそうにされるとこっちまで恥ずかしくなる。
その、くすぐったくて。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I see. Miss Akiha is very fortunate. She has such a devoted brother beside her.”
“I don’t know about that. I doubt Akiha considers me a particularly good brother.”
Kohaku keeps smiling, laughing softly to herself.
Her delight makes me self-conscious too. The feeling is warm, embarrassing, and strangely pleasant.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I see.
Akiha-sama is really lucky, having a brother that thinks so much of her."
"I don't know.
I don't think I'm a good brother to Akiha."
Still smiling, she continues to giggle.
…… Seeing her laugh so much makes me feel a little embarrassed.

entries.japanese:
「けどおかしいですね。
志貴さんは秋葉さまの事ばっかりで、ご自分の事を考えてあげていないんですから」
「――――――え？」
「志貴さんだって、そう幸せな日々ではなかったでしょう。
遠野家から勘当された志貴さんには、辛いことだってたくさんあったはずです。
　そうしてやっと有間の家に馴染めてきたのに、志貴さんは戻ってきてしまわれました。
　志貴さんは志貴さんがずっと憧れていた普通のご家族から、遠野の家の勝手な事情でまた離されてしまったんです」
entries.maoEnglish:
“But that is strange, Shiki. You think only of Miss Akiha and spare no thought for yourself.”
“What?”
“Your own life cannot have been a happy one. After the Tohno family cast you out, you must have suffered many painful things.
You finally found a place in the Arima household, only to return here.
The Tohno family’s selfish circumstances tore you away once again from the ordinary family you had always longed for.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"But, that is strange.
Thinking only of Akiha-sama and not thinking of yourself like that."
"------Eh?"
"You too, have lead a bad life.
Being disinherited and sent away, there had to have been some hard times for you, too.
And when you finally start to really get along with the Arima family, you come back here.
You were made to leave a normal family that suited you the most, due to a mere whim of the Tohno house."

entries.japanese:
「………………………」
　それは―――答えられない、言葉だった。
　三日前の朝。
有間の家の玄関で別れた啓子さんの顔が思い出される。
　あの、いつも気丈な人があんな悲しそうに笑うのを、見たかったワケではなかった。
　琥珀さんの言うとおり―――俺はようやく自分に馴染んでくれた半身を、自分から切り捨てたようなものなんだから―――
entries.maoEnglish:
“…………”
There is no answer I can give.
Three mornings ago. I remember Keiko’s face at the Arima family’s front door.
I never wanted to see that indomitable woman smile with such sorrow.
Kohaku is right—just when that family had finally become another half of me, I severed it with my own hands—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……………………"
I don't even know how to respond.
That morning three days ago.
I remember the face of Keiko-san standing in the doorway as we parted.
I didn't want to see that always steadfast person smile so sadly.
Like Kohaku-san said---I left a big part of me behind that was so attached to them when I left---

entries.japanese:
「ほら。
志貴さんだって、それを考えなかったわけではないんですよね？」
「――――――」
　違う。
それは、考えてはいけない事だ。
「……琥珀さん……どうして、そんな―――」
　コトを、今になって言うんだろう。
　出来れば琥珀さんや秋葉、翡翠には、俺は望んでこの屋敷に帰ってきたと、それだけを思っていてほしかったのに。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You see, Shiki? It isn’t as though you never thought about it.”
“————”
No. That is something I must not think about.
“Kohaku—why would you say something like that now—”
Why bring it up now?
I had wanted Kohaku, Akiha, and Hisui to believe only one thing: that I returned to this mansion because I wanted to.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"See, Shiki-san.
Don't tell me that you never thought of that?"
"------"
No, that's something I shouldn't think about.
"…… Kohaku-san…… why are you---"
I wanted to ask her why she was bringing all this up now.
I wanted Kohaku-san, Akiha and Hisui to think that I came back here because I wanted to.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さん」
　琥珀さんの声が聞こえる。
　その声を無視する事ができない。
誘われるまま、視線をあげた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Shiki.”
Kohaku’s voice reaches me.
I cannot ignore it. Drawn by the sound, I lift my eyes.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-san."
I hear her voice.
I can't ignore her voice, so I look up.

entries.japanese:
「わかっているはずです。
志貴さんは有間の家で暮らしていたほうが幸せだった」
――――それは。
　けどどうして、そんな――――
「どうして？
　どうして今になってこの屋敷に戻ってきてしまったんですか？
　志貴さんは、ここに来ては不幸になるだけなのに」
―――どうしてそんな―――泣き出しそうな顔を、しているんだろう――――
entries.maoEnglish:
“You already know, Shiki. You would have been happier living with the Arima family.”
――――That.
But why would she—
“Why? Why did you come back to this mansion after all these years, Shiki? Being here can only make you unhappy.”
―――Why does she look as though she is about to cry—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"You know it, too.
You would have been happier staying with the Arima family."
----That.
But, why is she---
"Why?
Why did you come back to the mansion now, when there is only unhappiness waiting for you here?"
---Why is she saying that---with that almost crying face---

entries.japanese:
「……………………」
　俺に答えはない。
　ただ魅入られたように琥珀さんの姿を見続けて、静かに、視線を落とした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…………”
I have no answer.
I can only stare at Kohaku as though transfixed, then quietly lower my gaze.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……………………"
I can't answer.
I just stare at Kohaku-san, as if I was in some sort of a trance.

entries.japanese:
「……ひどいな。
琥珀さんは言いにくい事を聞いてくる」
「はい、申し訳ありません。
わたしも酔ってしまっているみたいですね。
こんな事を尋ねるなんて、どうかしています」
　琥珀さんは笑顔だった。
　……なんだかそんな顔をされると、さっきの質問がまるで嘘だったかのように思える。
entries.maoEnglish:
“That’s cruel, Kohaku. You ask such difficult questions.”
“Yes, I’m sorry. It seems I may be drunk as well. I must be out of my mind to ask such things.”
Kohaku is smiling.
Her smile makes the question she just asked feel like a lie.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… You're mean, asking me to talk about such difficult things."
"I am sorry.
I guess I must be drunk as well.
Saying such things, there must be something wrong with me."
She is smiling.
…… Smiling like that, it makes it seem like she didn't even ask me something so serious.

entries.japanese:
「……琥珀さん。
さっきの話だけど。
やっぱりさ、自分の家に戻ってくるのは当たり前の事じゃないか。
秋葉を一人きりにしておけないし、有間の人たちに迷惑もかけられないだろ」
「では、それが志貴さんが戻られた理由なんですね」
　なるほど、と納得してくれる琥珀さん。
―――けど、それは嘘だ。
　本当はもう一つ―――秋葉の事より大切な出来事が、確かにあった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Kohaku. About what you asked… It’s only natural to return to your own home. I couldn’t leave Akiha all alone, and I couldn’t keep burdening the Arimas.”
“Then that is why you came back, Shiki.”
Kohaku nods, apparently satisfied.
―――But it is a lie.
There was one other reason—an event that mattered even more to me than Akiha.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Kohaku-san.
About that subject earlier, isn't it natural for me to come back here to my own home?
I couldn't leave Akiha all alone, and I couldn't burden the Arimas forever."
"So, that is your reason for coming back."
Kohaku-san seems like she understands.
---But, that is a lie.
There is another reason---something more important than Akiha.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さん？
　どうしたんですか？」
「……いや、違うんだ琥珀さん。
ホントはね、もう一つだけ大事な理由がある」
「へえ、それってもしかして秘密なコトなんですか？」
「……どうだろう。
秘密っていうわけじゃないけど、人には話したくない大事な思い出。
　俺はね、ここを出るときに借り物をしちゃたんだ。
それをきちんと返したくて、ここに帰ってきたんだよ」
「――――――――――」
　……それも、翡翠は覚えていなかった事だけど。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Shiki? What is it?”
“No, that wasn’t the whole truth. There’s one more important reason.”
“Oh—is it a secret?”
“I’m not sure. It isn’t exactly secret, but it’s a precious memory I don’t like sharing.
When I left this place, I borrowed something. I came home because I wanted to return it properly.”
“————”
Though Hisui herself did not remember any of it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-san?
What is it?"
"…… Oh, it's different, Kohaku-san.
Really, there is another important reason."
"Really?
Does that mean it is a secret?"
"…… I don't know.
It isn't that it's a secret, but it's an important memory I have that I don't want to talk about.
I borrowed something when I left here, so I came back to return it."
"----------"
…… But, it seems like Hisui doesn't remember it, though.

entries.japanese:
椅子から立ちあがる。
「酔いも冷めたし、部屋に戻ります。
それじゃ、また明日」
　片手をあげて中庭から立ち去る。
　琥珀さんは呆然と、そんな俺をいつまでも見送っていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
I rise from the chair.
“I’ve sobered up, so I’m going back to my room. See you tomorrow.”
With one hand raised in farewell, I leave the courtyard.
Kohaku remains there, stunned, watching me until I disappear.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I get up from the chair.
"I've cooled down, so I'm going back to my room."
Raising a hand, I exit the courtyard.
Kohaku-san just looks at me, dumbstruck.

entries.japanese:
ベッドに倒れこむ。
　アルコールのおかげか、すぐさま眠気がやってきてくれた。
「……………………」
　琥珀さんにあんな事を言ったせいだろう。
　とりとめもなく、八年前の約束が思い出される。
entries.maoEnglish:
I collapse onto the bed.
Thanks to the alcohol, drowsiness takes me at once.
“…………”
Perhaps it is because of what I told Kohaku.
The promise from eight years ago returns in scattered fragments.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I collapse on the bed.
It's probably the fault of the alcohol, as I start to feel very sleepy.
"……………………"
It's probably because I said those words to Kohaku-san.
I start to think about the promise I made eight years ago.

entries.japanese:
――――二度とこの屋敷に入る事はできない。
　そう父親に断言されて部屋を出た時の気持ちを、今でもまだ覚えている。
　事故にあって、ずっと一人きりで、先生に出会った後、結局は一人に戻ったのだと知った時。
　俺は先生との約束を守れないで、無感動な人間になっていたと思う。
　その時、ただ一度だけ話しかけてきてくれた少女。
　……それが、唯一つの救いだった。
　あの言葉にどんな魔法がかかっていたのかは知らない。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――I would never be allowed inside this mansion again.
Even now, I remember how I felt when my father declared that and sent me from the room.
After the accident, after being alone for so long, after meeting my teacher only to discover that in the end I had been left alone once more.
I think I had become numb, unable to keep my promise to her.
Then a girl spoke to me, just once.
That alone saved me.
I do not know what magic those words possessed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----You can never come back to this mansion ever again.
I still remember the time when my father said those words to me, and my feelings as I left my room.
That time when I realized that I would be all alone, just like I was before I met Sensei.
Not being able to keep my promise with Sensei, I guess I became empty inside.
That time, the girl I spoke with only once.
…… that was my only saving grace.
I don't know what kind of magic was in those words.

entries.japanese:
“返してね”なんていう、ただそれだけの言葉。
　けどそれは、あの時の自分には大切な言葉だった。
　それを―――ただ大事に思い続けてきただけ。
　……まあ、その約束をしてくれた当の本人である翡翠は忘れてしまっていたわけだけど。
entries.maoEnglish:
Just the words, “Give it back, okay?”
But to the child I was then, those words mattered.
I have simply treasured them ever since.
Though Hisui, the very person who made me that promise, had forgotten it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Give it back, okay?" …… Just those words.
But to me, those words meant so much back then.
I---always thought those words were important.
…… Well, it seems that Hisui forgot she ever said them though.

entries.japanese:
「……仕方ないよな。
子供のころの約束なんだし」
　それは本当に仕方のない事だと思う。
　八年間は長い。
　それが子供の頃の約束だとしたら、覚えているほうがおかしいんだ。
「……寝るか」
　はあ、と深呼吸をして瞼を閉じる。
――――後には、深い水底に沈むような眠りがあった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“It can’t be helped. It was a promise between children.”
I truly believe that.
Eight years is a long time.
For a promise made in childhood, remembering would be stranger than forgetting.
“Time to sleep.”
I draw a deep breath and close my eyes.
――――Then sleep takes me, like sinking to the bottom of deep water.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Oh well, it can't be helped.
It was just a promise we made as children."
It is a shame, but it really can't be helped.
Eight years is a long time.
Actually remembering a promise from your childhood is stranger than forgetting it, I suppose.
"…… Well, I should sleep."
Taking a deep breath, I close my eyes.
----I sink into a deep sleep.

entries.japanese:
―――熱さを覚えて体を起こした。
　灼い。
喉が燃えている。
触れてみると血が滲んでいた。
　あまりに灼かったため、何度も掻き毟った跡だろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――I sit up at the sensation of burning heat.
Scalding. My throat is on fire. When I touch it, my fingers come away bloody.
I must have scratched it raw again and again because the burning was unbearable.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---I feel the heat and my body wakes.
Roasting.
My throat is burning.
My blood is evaporating.
The roasting must be leaving scars all over.

entries.japanese:
「―――――」
　灼い。
　灼くてうまく辻褄が合わない。
　部屋には誰か、自分以外の気配の汚濁がある。
　灼い。
　灼くて部屋から出る事にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“————”
Scalding.
So hot the facts refuse to fit together.
Someone else’s presence fouls the room.
Scalding.
It is so hot that I decide to leave the room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-----"
Roasting.
I can't think clearly.
I feel the dirty presence of someone else in my room.
Burning.
I decide to leave my room.

entries.japanese: ―――時刻はとうに零時を過ぎていた。
entries.maoEnglish: ―――It is long past midnight.
entries.mirrorMoon: ---The clock says it is past midnight.

entries.japanese:
体の灼さは治まらない
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　／錯乱。
　どくん、どくん、という脈動
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　／発情。
　視界が鼓動に合わせて跳ねていく
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　／妄想。
　灼い。
紅い。
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　／燃料チューブ。
　硝える。
殖える。
　　　　　　　　　　　　　／昆虫ノ黒イ羽根。
　まるで眼球に
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　／狂想血液。
　動脈があるかのように。
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　／タイプ、死異。
entries.maoEnglish:
The burning in my body will not subside
　　　　　　　　　　　　／delirium.
Throb, throb, the pulse
　　　　　　　　　　　　／arousal.
My vision leaps in time with every beat
　　　　　　　　　　　　／delusion.
Scalding. Scarlet.
　　　　　　　　　　　　／fuel line.
Combust. Multiply.
　　　　　　　　　　　　／an insect’s black wings.
As though the eyeball itself
　　　　　　　　　　　　／rhapsodic blood.
possessed an artery.
　　　　　　　　　　　　／type: death anomaly.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The burning won't stop.
/Confusion.
Thump, Thump.
My heart pounds.
/Sexual excitement.
The whole world pulsates in unison.
/Delusion.
Burning.
Crimson.
/Fuel tube.
Exploding.
Multiplying.
/The black wings of insects.
It's as if my eyes,
/Blood of mad desire.
have a pulse.
/Type, different death.

entries.japanese:
闇に入る。
　心臓の活動は自己を苛烈に責めたてる。
　さらにさらに。
　どくん　　　　　　　どくん、!w1000
　　　　　　ドクン　　　　　　　　ドクン。
　自己の存在を希薄にするほどの鼓動音。
　心臓は双子に増えて、ざむざむと脈うつが故に一つしかない我が身は灼い。
　さあ、彼女が望む結末をかなえなければ。。。
entries.maoEnglish:
I enter the dark.
My heart’s labor drives me forward without mercy.
Further and further.
Thump　　　　　　　　　thump,!w1000
THUMP　　　　　　　　　THUMP.
A heartbeat so loud it thins my very existence.
My heart has doubled into twins, pounding and pounding; my single body burns because it cannot contain them.
Now I must grant her the ending she desires.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I enter the darkness.
My exploding heart scourges me forward.
More and more.
Thump    Thump,
Thump     Thump.
The beating that makes my existence pale in comparison.
My heart doubles, burning my single body with their fierce pulsation.
Now, time to fulfill her wish…

entries.japanese:
―――そして、
　　　目の前には見知らぬ誰かの死体があった。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――And then, before me,
lies the corpse of someone I have never seen.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---And then,
there were the corpses of strangers in front of me.

entries.japanese:
「―――――一人、二人、三人……か」
　口にだして数える。
　人差し指で確認したのだが、その人差し指は真っ赤だった。
　いや。
　俺の両手は、赤いペンキを塗りたくったように赤い。
　無論、周囲に赤いペンキなどない。
　あるのはできそこないのスパゲッティ（無論、ソースはミートソースだ）にしか見えない、人間の死体が三つ。
　地面には俺の―――七つ夜と刻まれたナイフが落ちている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“One, two, three.”
I count aloud, checking with my index finger.
My index finger is bright red.
No.
Both my hands are red, as though slathered in crimson paint.
Naturally, there is no paint anywhere nearby.
There are only three human corpses resembling badly made spaghetti—served, of course, with meat sauce.
On the ground lies my knife, engraved with the words Nanatsu-Yoru.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------One, two, three people……"
I count aloud.
I point out each one with my finger, my red finger.
No.
Both of my hands seem painted red.
Of course, there isn't any paint anywhere around me.
The only thing here is the flayed spaghetti (with meat sauce, of course) of three dead bodies.
On the ground---is my knife, engraved with "Nanatsu Yoru".

entries.japanese:
「…………つまり、これは」
　考えるまでもないと思うのだが。
「…………俺が、やったワケか」
　ナイフを拾う。
　……信じられないが、やってしまったものは仕方がない。
　気がつけばあれだけ灼かった体も冷めている。
　用は済んだのだし、さっさと屋敷に帰るとしよう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“So that means…”
There is hardly any need to think about it.
“So—I’m the one who did this.”
I pick up the knife.
I can hardly believe it, but what’s done is done.
Only now do I notice that the terrible heat has left my body.
My business here is finished, so I may as well hurry home to the mansion.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"………… This means……"
It doesn't even require thought.
"………… I, did this."
I pick up my knife.
…… I can't believe it, but what's done is done.
Now that I realize it, my once burning body has cooled down.
Now that I'm done, I should go back to the mansion.

entries.japanese:
「―――――――チッ。
誰かくる」
　通路から誰かがやってくる。
　まいった。
　ただでさえここはスパゲッティでごった返しているのに、この上また新しいミートソースをブチまけなくてはいけないのか。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Tch. Someone’s coming.”
A person approaches through the passage.
What a nuisance.
The place is already overflowing with spaghetti, and now I will have to splash fresh meat sauce over everything.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-------Kk.
Someone's coming."
Someone comes down the pathway.
Great.
This place is already overflowing with spaghetti, and now I have to make some more meat sauce on top of that.

entries.japanese:
かつん、かつん、と足音が近づいてくる。
　闇でしかなかった人影が露になる。
「――――――」
　ナイフを握る。
　人影は、路地裏に入ってきた。
entries.maoEnglish:
Footsteps draw closer—click, click, click.
The figure that had been nothing but darkness takes shape.
“————”
I tighten my grip on the knife.
The stranger enters the alley.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The footsteps approach.
The dark shadow becomes a little clearer.
"------"
I grip my knife.
That shadow enters the alley.

entries.japanese:
キィィィン、という音。
――――信じられない。
　有無を言わさず踏み込んだ俺を、人影は迎撃してきた。
　敵のエモノもナイフ。
　俺たちは互いに、相手の喉元を狙った必殺の一撃を相殺しあった。
entries.maoEnglish:
A piercing clang of metal.
――――Impossible.
I lunge without warning, and the figure meets me head-on.
My enemy’s weapon is another knife.
We each aim a killing stroke at the other’s throat, and the two attacks cancel each other perfectly.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Kiiin!
The sound of metal clashing.
----I can't believe it.
Without any indication at all, that shadow totally intercepted my attack.
The enemy also uses a knife.
Our attacks cancelled each other's fatal strikes to the throat.

entries.japanese:
「「―――――驚いたな」」
　闇に声が重奏する。
　俺はナイフを仕舞い、敵もナイフを仕舞った。
「戻ってきてみれば同類に出くわすとはな。
まったく、殺人鬼なんて初めて見た」
　言って、男は笑った。
　嫌味のない笑み。
減量の果てにリングにあがったボクサーが、生涯最高の敵と対峙した時のような、悦びに満ちた笑いだ。
　おそらく。
　俺も、それと同じ笑みをうかべていたのだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Well, that’s a surprise.”
Our voices speak in unison through the dark.
I put away my knife, and my enemy does the same.
“I come back and immediately meet one of my own kind. Never thought I’d see another murderer.”
The man laughs.
There is no mockery in the smile. It is pure delight, like a boxer who has starved himself down to weight and entered the ring to find the finest opponent of his life.
Most likely.
I am wearing the same smile.
entries.mirrorMoon:
""-----That's surprising!""
Our voices overlap in the darkness.
We both put away our knives at the same time.
"I didn't expect to see my kind here after coming back.
It's my first time seeing a killer."
He laughs as he says this.
A pure laugh without any bad intentions.
It's like the laugh of a boxer that finally cut weight and steps into the ring to face his greatest lifetime rival.
Probably,
I have the same smile on my face.

entries.japanese:
「――――ふん」
　男は鼻をならして背を向けた。
　大通りに向けて歩いていく。
「ここいらにするか。
大の男が二人、突っ立っているのもなんだろ？」
　道端に座りこむ。
　男は思い立ったように自動販売機まで歩いていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hmph.”
The man snorts and turns his back on me.
He walks toward the main road.
“How about here? Two grown men standing around together would look strange, wouldn’t it?”
I sit down by the roadside.
As though struck by an idea, the man walks over to a vending machine.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----Heh."
He snorts as he turns around.
We walk out to the main street.
"This looks like a good spot.
It's a bit odd for two grown men to be standing about, isn't it?"
I sit down on the sidewalk.
As if he just thought of something, he keeps walking… to the vending machine.

entries.japanese:
「おい、金だせ。
金もってねえんだ、オレ」
　こっちも財政状態はよろしくないが、一際大きいコインを投げた。
「一度ぐらいは試してみたかったんだ、コレ」
　嬉しげに言って、男は缶コーヒーを二つ買った。
「投げるぞ」
「あいよ」
　缶コーヒーとつり銭を受け取る。
　男は俺の隣に座って、缶コーヒーを一口飲む。
　……なんていうか、今日はこんなんばっかりだな、と思った。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hey, give me some money. I’m broke.”
My finances are hardly thriving either, but I toss him a large coin.
“Always wanted to try one of these.”
Delighted, the man buys two cans of coffee.
“Heads up.”
“Right.”
I catch the coffee and the change.
The man sits beside me and takes a sip from his can.
What is it with today—this kind of thing keeps happening to me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hey, gimme some money.
I don't have any."
I'm not exactly rich right now, but I give him the biggest coin I have.
"I always wanted to try this."
He says this happily and buys two cans of coffee.
"Catch."
"Alright."
I get the change and a can of coffee.
He sits by my side and takes a drink out of the can.
…… For some reason, I think this is all I've been doing all day.

entries.japanese:
「……まず。
なんだかなあ、煙草も珈琲もあんまりいいもんじゃねえんだな。
なんだってこんなもん口にすんだろうなあ、大人ってヤツは」
「そりゃあ我慢強さを鍛えてるんだよ。
大人になったら、まあ色々と大変だからね」
「ああ、なるほど。
オマエ頭いいな」
　けけけ、と愉快そうに男は笑う。
　こっちも缶コーヒーを飲んだ。
　……まったく同感だ。
こんな毒物めいたものを飲む連中は自殺願望が多分にありすぎる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ugh. Cigarettes and coffee aren’t much good, are they? Why do adults put this stuff in their mouths?”
“They’re training their endurance. Adulthood is difficult in all sorts of ways.”
“Oh, I get it. You’re smart.”
The man cackles happily.
I take a drink as well.
I agree completely. Anyone willing to consume something this poisonous must harbor a considerable death wish.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Yuck.
I don't think cigarettes and coffee are that great.
I wonder why adults even drink these things?"
"They're training their endurance.
Being an adult is pretty hard work."
"Ah, I see.
You're pretty smart."
He chuckles, delighted.
I take a drink as well.
…… I can't help but agree with him.
They must be awfully suicidal, wanting to drink something that tastes like poison.

entries.japanese:
「しかしまあ、なんだね。
オマエは酷いヤツだな。
いきなり喉元にナイフ突きつけてくるか、フツー」
「よく人の事が言えるな。
アンタこそ俺を殺す気だったじゃないか」
「そうだっけ？
　まあいいじゃんか、昔の事は。
お互い命があったんだからチャラにしようぜ」
　……まあ、確かに。
　お互いが殺し合ったんだから、どちらが死んでいようと結果はチャラだ。
　競技として、差し引きはそれなりに合っている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Still. You’re a nasty piece of work. Who lunges straight for a man’s throat with a knife?”
“You can talk. You were trying to kill me too.”
“Was I? Forget it—ancient history. We both survived, so let’s call it even.”
He has a point.
We both tried to kill each other, so whichever one of us had died, the result would have been fair.
Considered as a contest, the accounts balance well enough.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Well, anyway, you're a pretty awful guy.
How could you just suddenly strike at someone's throat like that?"
"You're one to talk.
You were trying to kill me too."
"Is that so?
Well, what's done is done.
We're both alive, so we'll call it even."
…… Well, he's right.
We both tried to kill each other, so even if one of us died, we'd still be even.
As a competition, that sounds right.

entries.japanese:
男は不味い不味いといいながら、嬉しそうに缶コーヒーをあおっている。
「……んー、まあこれも慣れれば悪くないねえ。
なんていうかさ、世間から外れた不良仲間って感じ」
　男は笑いをかみ殺しながら、そんな事を呟いていた。
「そう？
　なら煙草にしよっか」
　そのほうが不良少年、というイメージは強い。
entries.maoEnglish:
The man keeps calling the coffee disgusting while drinking it with obvious pleasure.
“Mm, maybe it isn’t bad once you get used to it. Makes us feel like fellow delinquents cast out by society.”
He murmurs it while suppressing a laugh.
“You think so? Then maybe we should smoke instead.”
That would fit the image of juvenile delinquents rather better.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Even though he keeps saying it is disgusting, he keeps happily drinking the coffee.
"…… Well, this isn't bad once you get used to it.
This feels like a get-together of bad boys kicked out of society."
He says so, killing his smile.
"Really?
Well, you wanna smoke?"
We'd look more like the bad boys that way.

entries.japanese:
「あー、いらね。
ありゃ思考を鈍らせる。
純粋でありたかったら、毒物は摂らぬが吉だ」
「……そう言いながらもコーヒーを飲んでいる」
「なんだオマエ、殺人鬼のくせに細かいな。
人間なんて毒食って生きてるようなもンなんだから、これぐらいはまだ許容範囲じゃないか。
オマエだって耐性ぐらいついてんだろ」
　ケタケタと男は笑う。
　まったく同意見なので、缶コーヒーを口に運んだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Nah—don’t want one. They dull the mind. If you want to stay pure, best not put poison in you.”
“You say that while drinking coffee.”
“You’re awfully particular for a murderer. Humans live by eating poison anyway, so this much is still within tolerance. You must have built up some resistance too.”
The man cackles.
Since I agree entirely, I raise the coffee to my lips.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah, I'll pass.
They numb the brain.
If you want to remain pure, you shouldn't take any poison."
"…… So says the guy drinking coffee."
"What's with you?
You're pretty nit-picky for a killer.
Humans eat poison every day, so isn't this alright?
You have some tolerance against it too, right?"
He laughs loudly.
I feel the exact same way, so I take another sip.

entries.japanese:
それから一時間ばかり、男と話した。
　道行く車を眺めながら、とりわけ意味のない事を語る。
　中でも意味がなかったのは、お互いの能力についてだった。
　モノの死が視えるという俺の眼と、
　中々死に難いという男の体。
　お互いその原理を語り合っているうちに、
「……そっか。
それじゃあさ、オマエってもしかして五感を殺せるってコト？」
　なんて、意味不明なコトを言い出した。
entries.maoEnglish:
I talk with the man for roughly an hour.
We watch the passing cars and discuss one meaningless subject after another.
The most meaningless subject of all is our respective abilities.
My eyes, which can see the death of things,
and his body, which is exceedingly difficult to kill.
As we compare their workings—
“Wait. Does that mean you could kill the five senses?”
It makes no sense at all.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I speak with him for another hour.
We ramble about nothing as we watch cars go by.
The most pointless thing was probably our special powers.
My eyes that can see death.
His body that dies with great difficulty.
We began by discussing their principles.
"…… I see.
Well, does that mean you can kill the five senses?"
He says such nonsense.

entries.japanese:
「できない。
そんな曖昧な、表現でしか表現できないものは殺せない」
「そんなワケねえだろ。
いいか、視覚なら眼、聴覚なら耳を殺せばいいだけの話じゃんか。
けどそんな事ならオレにでもできる。
　けどオマエは違うだろ。
モノを潰さずに殺すコトができる。
オマエはさ、その線とやらが見えている時点で物体じゃなくて意味を殺しているんだよ。
　だから――――五感の上にあるもの、第六感とかそういった便宜上のモノ……魂とか感情とか、そういったモノだって削り取れるハズだぜ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“No. I can’t kill something so vague that it can only be described as an abstraction.”
“Bullshit. To kill sight, destroy the eyes; to kill hearing, destroy the ears. Even I could do that.
But you’re different. You can kill a thing without crushing it. If you can see those lines, then what you’re killing isn’t the object—it’s the meaning.
So you ought to be able to scrape away things beyond the five senses too—whatever people call a sixth sense for convenience, souls, emotions, things like that.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I can't do that.
I can't kill something so vague that needs an expression to be understood."
"Not at all.
Look, if you wanted to kill sight, kill the eyes.
Hearing, kill the ears.
I can do at least that much…
But you're different.
You can kill things without crushing them.
The moment you see those lines, you can kill.
Not the object, but its very meaning.
That's why----something beyond the five senses, like the sixth sense…… spirit and emotion, you should be able to kill those things too."

entries.japanese:
「………………………ふうん」
　……それは、確かにそうだ。
　もともと俺の眼はそれ自体が異状なもの。
　それをまっとうな理屈で考える事自体、前提を間違えている。
　……なら俺はアレを殺せるだろうか。
　子供の頃に一度だけ見かけた蜃気楼。
　たしか、くれないせきしゅ、とか言う憑き物。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Huh.”
He may be right.
My eyes are intrinsically abnormal.
Trying to explain them with ordinary logic was a mistake from the outset.
Could I kill that, then?
The mirage I saw once as a child.
The possessing spirit called something like kurenai sekishu.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……………………… Hmm."
…… Well, he has a point.
My eyes themselves are an aberration.
Using logic to understand them is a mistake from the start.
…… Then can I kill that too?
That apparition that I saw once in my childhood.
That haunting thing called Crimson Red Vermillion.

entries.japanese:
「けど、それはタイヘンそうだ。
そんなモノまで視えてしまったら、俺はマトモな思考ができなくなると思う」
「だな。
人間の頭脳しかもってないくせに、神様の計算をしようってコトだもんな。
そりゃあ廃人になるぜ、普通」
　言って男は立ちあがると、また自動販売機まで歩いていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“But that sounds difficult. If I started seeing things like that, I don’t think I could remain capable of rational thought.”
“Naturally. You’d be trying to perform God’s calculations with nothing but a human brain. Anyone normal would end up a vegetable.”
With that, the man stands and returns to the vending machine.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"But, that seems hard.
If I do that, I don't know how much longer I could stay sane."
"Yeah.
It's like trying to calculate as a god using the mind of a human.
You'd cripple yourself for sure."
He says this as he walks toward the vending machine again.

entries.japanese:
「おい」
　自販機を見たまま、後ろにいる俺に手を差し出す。
　コインを投げると、男は器用に受け取ってまた缶コーヒーを買ってきた。
　男は缶コーヒーを飲んだあと、
「久しぶりに人間と話してる」
　なんて事を口にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hey.”
Still facing the machine, he holds a hand out behind him.
I toss another coin, which he catches neatly, and he buys more canned coffee.
After taking a drink, the man says,
“Been a long time since I talked to a human being.”
That is the peculiar thing he chooses to say.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hey."
Still looking at the vending machine, he holds his hand behind him towards me.
I toss him a coin, which he catches skillfully and uses to buy another can of coffee.
After drinking this, he turns to me again.
"It really has been a long time since I talked to another person."
That's really weird.

entries.japanese:
「……おかしな事を言うね。
アンタ、今まで無人島にでも住んでいたのか？」
「あー？
　今も住んでるぜ、この無人島にさ。
なんでもオレは世間とズレているらしい。
意味もなく人殺しをするようなヤツは正気じゃないんだとよ。
　だからまあ、ズレてるオレはズレてないヤツラと話しても会話が成立しないわけ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“That’s an odd remark. Have you been living on a deserted island?”
“Still am. This deserted island right here. Apparently I’m out of step with society. They say anyone who kills for no reason can’t be sane.
So when someone out of step like me talks to people who aren’t, no real conversation happens.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… That's strange, were you stranded on an island somewhere?"
"Huh?
I'm still stranded on this island.
It seems I'm out of alignment with society.
They say someone who kills people for no reason is just crazy.
There's really no way someone like me, who's out of tune, could have a conversation with someone in tune."

entries.japanese:
「……ふうん。
ズレてるんだ、俺たち」
「そっ。
どっちが異常なのかは問題じゃない。
ようは世間から外れているほうがズレてるワケ」
「そう？
　異状なのは世間のほうかもしれないよ」
「へえ、そりゃあどういう意味だ」
「言葉通り。
アンタだって言ってたじゃないか。
　多数決と一緒。
大部分の意見に賛同しなかった小数意見は“使えない”と除外されるじゃないか。
　どっちが正しいかなんて、関係ないんだ。
みんなに合っていないヤツは、正しかろうがなんだろうが仲間はずれにされるだけ。
ズレてるなんていう表現には普遍的な基準は当てはまらないよ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“I see. So we’re out of step.”
“Right. Which side is abnormal doesn’t matter. The side standing outside society is the one that’s out of step.”
“Is that so? Perhaps society is the abnormal one.”
“Oh—what do you mean by that?”
“Exactly what I said. You mentioned it yourself.
It’s like a majority vote. The minority who disagree with everyone else are discarded as ‘useless.’
It doesn’t matter which side is right. Anyone who fails to fit with the majority gets shut out, right or wrong. There can be no universal standard for being out of step.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Hmm.
So we're out of tune?"
"Yeah.
It's not a matter of who's off tune.
Those out of tune with society are the ones out of tune."
"Really?
Maybe society is the one out of tune instead."
"What do you mean by that?"
"Exactly what I said.
Didn't you say that just now?
It's like majority rule.
The views of the minority that aren't the same as the views of the majority are said to be "unusable" and rejected.
It doesn't matter who is right or wrong.
If you don't fit in, you're left out, regardless of if you are right or wrong.
The term 'out of tune' doesn't follow universal rules."

entries.japanese:
「―――――フン。
じゃあ何か、オレたちみたいな殺人鬼は悪党じゃない、って言ってるワケ？」
「……さあ。
事の善悪なんて知らないよ。
ただ理屈で考えるとズレているのは俺たちじゃないだろ。
　……そうだな、例えばボクサーっているじゃない。
別にボクサーじゃなくてもいいんだけど、とりあえず解りやすいから例にあげる」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hmph. So what—murderers like us aren’t villains?”
“Who knows. I don’t know anything about good or evil. I only mean that, logically, we aren’t the ones out of step.
Take boxers, for example. It doesn’t have to be boxing, but that makes the idea easy to explain.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-----Heh, so are you trying to say that killers like us aren't evil?"
"…… Who knows?
I don't know about good or evil.
But if you think about it logically, we aren't the ones out of tune.
…… Let's see, how about using boxers as an example?
It doesn't have to be boxers, but it is an easy example to understand."

entries.japanese:
「ボクサーっていうのはさ、殴り合うのが仕事なんだって。
それもただ殴り合うだけじゃないんだ。
減量っていう苦しい思いをして、毎日毎日人を殴る訓練をする。
いかにうまく人を殴るか。
いかに効率よく人を倒すか。
それだけを毎日、刃物を研ぐように鍛え上げていくんだ。
　これってさ、どう思う？」
「……ふうん。
そんな連中がいるんだ。
で、続きは？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“A boxer’s job is to trade blows. But that isn’t all. They put themselves through the misery of cutting weight and train every day to hit people. How to strike more skillfully. How to bring someone down more efficiently. Day after day they hone that single ability like a knife.
What do you think of that?”
“Huh. People like that exist? Go on.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Boxers, their job is to punch people.
But not just to punch people.
They painfully cut weight, and train every day to skillfully punch people.
To effectively punch others, to efficiently defeat others.
They diligently work on it every day, like sharpening a blade.
What do you think of that?"
"…… Huh.
There are people like that.
And?"

entries.japanese:
「いや、それだけだよ。
　ただね、彼らは殴り合うだけで相手の息の根は止めない。
そりゃあ事故で死んでしまう場合もある。
けどその場合は一般的な殺人罪には問われない。
なんかさ、これってすごくない？」
「―――殺してもいいってコトかよ、それ」
「違う違う。
殺しちゃ駄目。
けど殺してもいいんだ。
すごい矛盾だろ。
それだけじゃない。
ボクサーっていうのは拳が凶器として認められるから、ケンカをしちゃいけないんだって」
entries.maoEnglish:
“That’s all.
They fight, but they aren’t supposed to finish the other person off. Accidents happen, of course, and sometimes somebody dies. Yet when that happens, it generally isn’t treated as murder. Isn’t that incredible?”
“You mean they’re allowed to kill?”
“No, no. They aren’t allowed to kill. But they are allowed to kill. Quite a contradiction, isn’t it? And there’s more. A boxer’s fists are legally considered weapons, so apparently boxers aren’t allowed to get into street fights.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No, that's all.
They just punch each other, but they don't kill their opponents.
Sure, some could die from accidents, but it isn't considered murder.
Isn't that incredible?"
"---You mean it's okay to kill?"
"No, no.
You aren't supposed to kill.
But you could.
Isn't that a huge contradiction?
That's not all, because a boxer's fist is considered a weapon, they aren't allowed to fight outside the ring."

entries.japanese:
「……これってすごいぜ。
ボクサーの拳が凶器だって解ってるのにさ、どうしてボクサーなんていう職業があるのかな。
人を殺しかねない凶器ならさ、ボクサーっていうモノを無くすべきだろ。
　殺しちゃ駄目、殺しちゃ駄目。
　そのくせ世界にはね、人殺しの道具があふれているんだ。
法律でさえ容認されている。
なのに人殺しは駄目だっていうんだから、これはもう混沌というしかない。
常識というものが多くの人間が考えているような善良なものであるのなら、俺たちはズレてないんだよ。
　だって、常識からズレているとしたらそれはこの世界のほうなんだから」
entries.maoEnglish:
“That’s remarkable. Everyone knows a boxer’s fists are weapons, so why does boxing exist at all? If something can kill people, shouldn’t society abolish it?
Killing is wrong.
Yet the world overflows with instruments for killing, and even the law approves of them. Then it turns around and says murder is forbidden. You can only call that chaos. If common sense is truly as decent as most people imagine, then we aren’t out of step at all.
The world is the thing that has strayed from common sense.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… This is incredible.
They know a boxer's fist is a weapon, so why is there such a profession in the first place?
If it's a weapon that can kill, they should abolish it.
Killing is wrong, killing is wrong.
But this world is full of tools to kill.
Even the law allows it.
But they say it's not alright to kill; this can only be considered chaos.
If common sense is what is thought of as good by a majority of people, then we aren't out of tune.
If there is anything out of tune, it's this world."

entries.japanese:
……とは言っても、ボクサーという職業を敵視しているわけではない。
　色々な職業はあるけど、あれほど自己の目的のためにストイックになれるモノはないだろう。
　一切の誘惑を断ちきって自身を鍛え上げる。
　人間は解りやすい強さに興味を示す生き物だ。
だから競技はなくならない。
　その中でも他者を傷つけ合う競技を選ぶものは、一種憑かれている。
entries.maoEnglish:
Not that I bear any hostility toward boxing.
Of all the professions in the world, few demand such merciless devotion to a personal goal.
A boxer rejects every temptation and forges his own body.
Human beings are fascinated by strength they can readily understand. That is why contests will never disappear.
Among all competitors, those who choose a sport built on hurting others are possessed by something special.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… All that said, I don't necessarily hate boxing.
There are a lot of professions out there, but there aren't any others where you can be so stoic about your objectives.
You strengthen yourself by cutting yourself off from all temptations.
Humans are interested in strength they can easily comprehend.
That's why competitions will never go away.
Of all of these competitions, the ones people like the most are where the contestants hurt each other.

entries.japanese:
強さへの憧憬。
　強さにしか執着できなかった思考。
　それはきっと、とても健全な精神だ。
　俺やこの男のように結果でしか意味を求められない思考とは、色彩こそ似通ってはいるもののそのカタチは異なるだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
A longing for strength.
A mind capable of caring for nothing else.
Surely that is an exceedingly healthy spirit.
It may share the same colors as the way this man and I think—we can find meaning only in results—but its form is altogether different.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Admiration of the strong.
A mindset that can only be drawn towards strength.
That is probably a very healthy mind.
As guys like him and I can think only of results, our colors might be similar, but our shapes should be completely different.

entries.japanese:
何か、自己さえ忘れて打ち込める嗜好。
　それはその個人の自由にはならない。
　学問を崇拝する者、芸術に焼身する者、商業に邁進する者。
　それを個人で決定できるのなら、この世界はもう少し解りやすい、キレイなパズルになっているだろう。
　だがこのパズルは穴だらけだ。
　所々欠けているし、中にはまったく規格の異なるピースが混ざっている。
entries.maoEnglish:
A calling one can throw oneself into so completely that everything else disappears.
That is not something a person is free to choose.
Some worship scholarship, some immolate themselves for art, and some throw themselves into commerce.
If each person could choose that calling, the world would make a cleaner, more comprehensible puzzle.
But this puzzle is riddled with holes.
Pieces are missing everywhere, while others belong to a wholly different design.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Something you can concentrate on and forget yourself.
That doesn't become an individual's free will.
Those that worship education, those who immolate themselves in art, those who advance themselves in business.
If an individual could decide that, then this world would be a pretty puzzle that could be understood.
But this puzzle is full of holes.
Pieces are missing, and a lot of pieces don't fit.

entries.japanese:
「ふうん。
オマエ、よくしゃべるヤツだな。
昔さ、オマエみたいな友人がオレにもいたんだぜ。
　そいつはなんていうか……そうだな、何も持っていなかったんだ。
だから何も求めていなかったように見えたんだろう。
　それはなんていうか、ひどく孤高でさ。
孤高っていうのは孤独の別名だろ。
だからオレは、それが気になって仕方がなかった」
「……ふうん。
何も求めていない、か。
アンタはどうなんだ？
　何か欲しいものはある？」
「……どうだろう。
あった気がするが、思い出せない。
そういうオマエはどうだ？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Huh. You talk a lot. I had a friend like you once.
How can I put it? He had nothing, so perhaps that was why he seemed to want nothing.
There was something fiercely aloof about him. But aloofness is only another word for loneliness, isn’t it? I could never stop thinking about him.”
“I see. Wanting nothing. What about you? Is there anything you want?”
“I don’t know. Feels like there was, but I can’t remember. How about you?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I see.
You like to talk a lot, don't you.
I had a friend like that once.
How do I say this…… well, he didn't have anything, which is why he looked like he didn't want anything.
To me, he seemed very isolated.
Isolation is just another name for loneliness, right?
That is why it bugged me."
"…… Hmm.
Didn't want anything?
What about you?
Is there something you want?"
"…… I don't know.
I think I used to, but I can't remember now.
What about you?"

entries.japanese:
「求めているものは誰にだってあるだろ。
けど夢中になれるような事はなかった。
　自己を見失うほどの白熱は、そうだな―――今夜のこれが初めてだったかもしれない」
「あはは。
つまるところおまえも殺人鬼って事だよな、それは」
「……どうだろう。
まだ断定はできない。
そういうアンタはどうなんだ？
　人殺しは楽しいかい？」
「――――バカかオマエ。
楽しかったら休むことなくやってるだろ。
こんなのにはさ、理由はねえんだよ。
ただやり始めたら夢中になる。
それだけの話だ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Everyone wants something. I had simply never found anything that could consume me.
The kind of fever in which you lose yourself—tonight may have been my first.”
“Ha! Then when all is said and done, you’re a murderer too.”
“I don’t know. There still isn’t enough evidence to be certain. What about you? Is killing people enjoyable?”
“Are you stupid? If it were fun, I’d never stop doing it. There’s no reason behind this. Once I begin, I become absorbed. That’s all.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Everyone wants something, but I haven't found anything worth dreaming for.
A fire within me that caused me to lose my mind---tonight was maybe my first time feeling that."
"Hahaha.
That means you're a killer too."
"…… I don't know.
I can't be sure yet.
What about you, is killing fun?"
"----Are you stupid?
If it was fun, I'd be doing it non-stop.
There isn't any reason.
Once you start, you just get hooked."

entries.japanese:
……なるほど。
　それは少しだけ理解できた。
　ようするに、殺人行為を嗜好しているワケではなく、殺人を行為してしまった場合、その作業に没頭できるかどうか。
　それがズレているかいないかの違いという事らしい。
entries.maoEnglish:
I see.
That, at least, I can partly understand.
It is not a matter of enjoying murder, but of whether one can lose oneself completely in the work once the act has begun.
Apparently, that is the distinction between being out of step and being ordinary.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… I see.
I think I understand a little bit.
In other words, it's not a matter of liking or disliking the murder.
It's a matter of when he does kill someone, whether he can devote himself to that action.
That's probably the difference between being in or out of tune.

entries.japanese:
「アンタさ。
子供の頃、ラジオとか解体してた口じゃない？」
「螺字男……？
　いや、そんなヤツをバラした事はねえけど」
「―――オーケー、つまらないボケをありがとう。
ついでに言うと、今のは冗談だよ。
有機と無機は対極だからね。
俺たちみたいなのは、わりと医者とかが向いてるかもしれない」
「医者、か。
オレ、クスリは嫌いだ。
射たれると自分が希薄になるだろ。
なんだかさ、傀儡になりさがる気がするじゃんか」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hey. Were you the sort of child who took radios apart?”
“Raydio? Never cut up a man by that name.”
“All right, thank you for that appalling joke. For the record, mine was a joke too. Living things and machines are opposites. People like us might actually make fairly good doctors.”
“A doctor, huh? I hate drugs. When they inject you, you can feel yourself thinning away. It’s as if you’ve been reduced to somebody else’s puppet.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hey, didn't you ever take apart a radio when you were a kid?"
"Ray Dio……?
I never killed any one like that."
"---Right, thanks for being a moron.
To be honest, that was a joke.
Animate objects and inanimate objects are completely different.
Maybe people like us should be doctors instead."
"A doctor?
I hate medicine.
When you get a shot, don't you feel yourself getting diluted?
It's like you're becoming a puppet, right?"

entries.japanese:
……そんなものか。
　こっちは主治医までいる体だから、クスリなんてもう日常茶飯事なものだけど。
entries.maoEnglish:
Perhaps that is how it feels.
I already have my own doctor, so medicine has been an everyday matter for me for years.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Is that so?
I have my own doctor, so I take medicine like it was nothing.

entries.japanese:
「―――――あーあ。
楽しかったぜ、ほんと」
　男は腰をあげる。
　そうして――――感情のない目で俺を見下ろした。
「―――さて。
同じ街に二人はいらねえよな。
こんな狭い檻の中にライオンが二匹もいたんじゃ縄張りさえ作れない」
　男はナイフを取り出そうとする。
　無機質な殺気。
　男は本気で、俺と殺し合いを望んでいる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ah, well. That really was fun.”
The man rises.
Then he looks down at me with eyes emptied of all emotion.
“Now then. There isn’t room for two of us in one city. Put two lions in a cage this small and neither can even claim a territory.”
His hand moves toward his knife.
His killing intent is cold and inorganic.
He genuinely means to fight me to the death.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-----Ahh, it really was a lot of fun."
He stands up.
And----with empty eyes, he looks down at me.
"---Well.
We don't need two of us in this town, right?
Two lions in a cage this small won't even be able to mark their own territory."
He looks like he is going for his knife.
The inorganic reek of murder.
He really does want a fight to the death.

entries.japanese:
「やめておいたほうがいいよ」
　至極自然に、そんな声が出た。
「なぜ？」
「そりゃあ、生き物としてアンタのほうが強いけど」
――――だが、それが殺し合いなら。
「アンタより、俺のほうが優れてる」
entries.maoEnglish:
“You shouldn’t.”
The words leave me with perfect ease.
“Why not?”
“As living creatures go, you’re stronger than I am.”
――――But if what we are measuring is the ability to kill.
“I’m better than you.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"You shouldn't."
I say quite naturally.
"Why?"
"Well, as a living creature, you're stronger than me, but…"
----If it's a fight to the death.
"I'm superior to you."

entries.japanese:
「――――――、――――――」
　ぎり、という歯が軋む音。
　男はひきつった笑みを浮かべたあと、
「ハ……あは、あっーはっはっは……ッ！！」
　なんて、大声で笑い出した。
entries.maoEnglish:
“————”
His teeth grind together.
A twisted smile forms on his face, and then—
“Ha—ha, ah—hahahahaha!”
He bursts into thunderous laughter.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------,------"
He grinds his teeth.
After a twitching smile,
"Ha…… aha, aahahhaha……!!"
He laughs extremely loudly.

entries.japanese:
「なんだよ。
そんなに可笑しかったのか、殺人鬼」
　ひひ、ひひひ、と男は神経質に笑い続ける。
　……仕方がないのでこのまま放っておこうとした矢先、男はピタリと笑い止んで俺を見た。
「――――そうだな。
オマエは、正しい」
　それだけ言うと、男は一人で歩き出してしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What? Was it really that funny, murderer?”
He keeps giggling in short, nervous bursts.
Just as I decide to leave him to it, the laughter stops dead and he looks at me.
“Yes. You’re right.”
With that, the man turns and walks away alone.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"What?
Was it that funny, killer?"
Hee hee hee, heeheehee.
The man continues to laugh.
…… Just when I thought I'd just have to leave him, he stops laughing and looks at me.
"----You're right, you know."
Saying that, he starts to walk away.

entries.japanese:
「これで潮時になっちまった。
おまえみたいなヤツが出てきた以上、オレの方がこの街を出て行くしかないもんな」
「……別に俺はアンタの後釜につく気はないけど」
「いやいや無理だって。
今夜、初めて夢中になれたんだろ？
　ならもう明日からは同じ事さ。
オマエはもう一日だって我慢する事なんてできねえよ。
　それじゃあまあ、二度と会わない事を祈ってるぜ」
　片手をあげて、男は去っていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“This means my time is up. Now that somebody like you has appeared, I’m the one who has to leave town.”
“I have no intention of taking your place.”
“No, no, you won’t have a choice. Tonight was the first time you ever lost yourself in something, wasn’t it? Tomorrow will be the same. You won’t endure even one day without it.
Well, here’s hoping we never meet again.”
He raises one hand and departs.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I guess this is a good opportunity.
Now that someone like you is here, I should probably leave town."
"…… I don't really intend to take your place."
"No, no, it's useless.
You got hooked tonight, right?
Then it'll be the same tomorrow.
You won't be able to endure, even for a day.
Well, I hope we won't meet again."
Raising a hand, he disappears.

entries.japanese:
「――――――――」
　二度と会わない、と聞いて少しだけ残念に思った。
　足元には男が飲み干した缶コーヒーが十缶ほど。
　つまり、この借りを返してもらえる事はないという事だった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“————”
Hearing that we will never meet again leaves me faintly disappointed.
Roughly ten empty coffee cans lie at my feet.
Evidently he will never repay what he owes me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"--------"
Hearing that we wouldn't meet again, I get a little sad.
At my feet, there are about ten cans of coffee that he drank.
In other words, he'll never pay me back for these.

entries.japanese:
――――さて、部屋に戻ってきた。
　じき夜も明ける。
　言われたとおり全てを忘れて、このまま眠ることにしよう――――
entries.maoEnglish:
――――And now I am back in my room.
Dawn will come soon.
As I was told, I will forget everything and go to sleep—
entries.mirrorMoon:
----I make it back to my room.
It is almost dawn.
I should just forget everything and go to sleep----

entries.japanese:
何事もなく教室について、いつものように授業が始まった。
　……弓塚の机はなくなっている。
　クラスメイトが一人いなくなってしまったぐらいで学校の時間割に変動はない。
「………………」
　少し、不安になる。
　翡翠のおかげで忘れていられた事。
　あんな出来事を経験してしまったためだろうか。
　ここにいる事に違和感をうけて、何もかもが上の空に思えてしまっていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
I reached the classroom without incident, and lessons began as usual.
Yumizuka’s desk was gone.
The school timetable did not change merely because one student had disappeared.
“…”
Unease crept over me.
Hisui had helped me forget.
Perhaps it was because I had lived through something so terrible.
Being here now felt wrong, and everything around me seemed distant and unreal.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I get to the classroom, and the class starts uneventfully, as always.
…… There's no one at Yumizuka's desk.
Even though a classmate is gone forever, class life remains unchanged.
"………"
I become a little uneasy.
Because of Hisui, I had forgotten all about that.
Perhaps because of that incident?
With that uneasiness, my thoughts drift towards the sky.

entries.japanese:
気がつけば一日が終わっていた。
「…………はあ」
　有彦や先輩に会いに行く気分でもない。
　今の自分は学校より、遠野の屋敷のほうが気分が落ち着いてくれるみたいだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
Before I knew it, the day was over.
“…”
I was in no mood to see Arihiko or Ciel.
These days, the Tohno mansion seemed to put me more at ease than school did.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Before I realized it, the school day was over.
I let out a sigh.
I don't really feel like seeing Arihiko or Senpai.
Right now, it seems I'm just more at ease in the Tohno mansion than in school.

entries.japanese:
ロビーに入ると、すぐに翡翠の姿があった。
「お帰りなさいませ、志貴さま」
「ただいま翡翠。
琥珀さんと秋葉は留守？」
「秋葉さまはお帰りになられていらっしゃいません。
姉さんでしたら裏庭の掃除をしておりますが」
「いつもと同じか。
それじゃ部屋に戻るから、翡翠も仕事に戻っていいよ」
「はい。
それでは失礼いたします」
entries.maoEnglish:
Hisui was there as soon as I entered the foyer.
“Welcome home, Master Shiki.”
“I’m back, Hisui. Are Kohaku and Akiha both out?”
“Miss Akiha has not yet returned. My sister is cleaning the rear courtyard.”
“So, same as always. I’m going to my room, so you can get back to work.”
“Yes. Excuse me.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
I enter the lobby and immediately encounter Hisui.
"Welcome back, Shiki-sama."
"I'm home, Hisui.
Are Kohaku-san and Akiha here?"
"Akiha-sama has not returned yet.
Nee-san will most likely be in the rear courtyard sweeping."
"As usual.
Well, I'll be in my room; please continue whatever you were doing."
"Yes.
Please excuse me."

entries.japanese:
二階への階段に足をかける。
「あ、志貴さま」
「ん？」
　
「わたしは槙久さまのお部屋の整理をしていますから、何かご用でしたらお呼びください」
　翡翠は東館のほうに早足で去っていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
I set one foot on the stairs.
“Oh, Master Shiki.”
“Hm?”
“I shall be putting Master Makihisa’s room in order, so please call me if you require anything.”
Hisui hurried away toward the east wing.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I head up the stairs to the second floor.
"Ah, Shiki-sama?"
"Hm?"
"I will be in Makihisa-sama's room sorting things out.
If you need me, please call for me."
Hisui disappears towards the east end of the mansion.

entries.japanese:
鞄を置いて、上着を脱ぐ。
「……さて」
　夕食まで時間があるし、何をしようか。
entries.maoEnglish:
I set down my bag and removed my jacket.
“Well.”
There was still time before dinner, so what should I do?
entries.mirrorMoon:
Putting down my bag, I take off my jacket.
"…… Well, then."
There's still time until evening, so what should I do?

entries.japanese:
―――翡翠に会いにいく、か。
「……けど翡翠、仕事は手伝わせてくれないし、わざわざ会いにいって翡翠の仕事を邪魔するのもな……」
　……困った。
　翡翠に迷惑をかけるのは避けたい。
　けど、なんとなく会いに行きたい。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Maybe I should go see Hisui.
“But Hisui won’t let me help with her work, and going out of my way to see her would only interrupt it…”
A problem.
I didn’t want to inconvenience her.
Even so, for some reason, I wanted to see her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---I'll go see Hisui.
"…… But Hisui doesn't let me help her, and I don't want to get in her way……"
…… What should I do?
I don't want to be a burden.
But for some reason, I want to see her.

entries.japanese:
「……………あ」
　そういえば、まだ翡翠にリボンを返してあげていなかった。
　翡翠は忘れたって言っていたけど、もともとあのリボンは翡翠のものだ。
いつまでも俺が持っていても仕方がないし、返しに行こう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh…”
I still hadn’t returned Hisui’s ribbon.
She had said she had forgotten it, but it had belonged to her in the first place. There was no point in my keeping it forever, so I would take it back to her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Ah."
That reminds me.
I still need to give her back the ribbon.
Hisui said she'd forgotten about it, but the ribbon is hers.
There's really no point in me holding on to it, so I should give it back.

entries.japanese:
親父の部屋で、翡翠は本の整理をしているらしかった。
　もう主人はいないというのに、親父の部屋は昔のままで保管されている。
entries.maoEnglish:
Hisui appeared to be sorting books in Father’s room.
Though its owner was gone, the room had been preserved exactly as it was.
entries.mirrorMoon:
In the old man's old room, Hisui is arranging books.
Even though it is no longer being used, his room is still being cleaned like before.

entries.japanese:
「翡翠、ちょっといい？」
「あ―――志貴さま。
はい、なんでしょうか」
「その、前にも言ったけど、これを返しておこうと思って」
　八年前に翡翠から渡されたリボンを差し出す。
「……………………」
「翡翠？
　やっぱり、もういらない……？」
「……いえ、お預かりします。
それは、大切なものですから」
　リボンを受け取ると、翡翠は黙り込んでしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hisui, do you have a moment?”
“Ah—Master Shiki. Yes, what is it?”
“I mentioned it before, but I thought I should return this.”
I held out the ribbon Hisui had given me eight years ago.
“…”
“Hisui? Do you not want it anymore?”
“No, I’ll take it. It is something precious.”
Hisui accepted the ribbon, then fell silent.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hisui, can I have a minute?"
"Ah---Shiki-sama.
Yes, what is it?"
"I know we talked about this earlier, but I thought I should give this back."
I pull out the ribbon Hisui gave me eight years ago.
"………………"
"Hisui?
So, you honestly don't want it……?"
"……No, I will take it.
It is important to me, after all."
Taking the ribbon, Hisui becomes silent.

entries.japanese:
「……………」
　話しかけられない。
　今の翡翠は八年前の頃のように、周りの人間を拒絶しているように見えて。
「志貴さま、用件はこれだけでしょうか」
　声も出せず、ただ頷く。
「それでは、どうかお部屋にお戻りください。
まだ仕事が残っておりますから」
　部屋の奥に歩いていく翡翠。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
I couldn’t bring myself to speak.
Hisui looked as she had eight years ago, shutting every other human being out.
“Master Shiki, was that all you required?”
Unable to find my voice, I merely nodded.
“Then please return to your room. I still have work to complete.”
Hisui walked away toward the far end of the room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…………"
I can't talk to her.
The Hisui in front of me right now looks very much like the Hisui from eight years ago, distant from the ones around her.
"Shiki-sama, is this all you came to do?"
I can't seem to speak, so I just nod.
"In that case, please return to your room.
I still have some work remaining."
Hisui walks towards the center of the room.

entries.japanese:
「……翡翠」
　なにか、あのリボンには特別な意味でもあったのんだろうか。
　この八年間。
自分は本当に、遅すぎた約束を果たしただけなのかもしれない。
「……それじゃ、部屋に戻るよ。
また後で、翡翠」
　言って、部屋を後にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hisui…”
Had that ribbon held some special meaning?
Eight years had passed. Perhaps all I had truly done was fulfill a promise far too late.
“I’ll go back to my room, then. See you later, Hisui.”
With that, I left.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Hisui."
Did that ribbon have any special meaning?
This eight year period.
I think I may have finally fulfilled my promise, even if it was too late.
"…… Then, I'll go to my room.
See you later, Hisui."
With that, I leave the room.

entries.japanese:
―――琥珀さんの手伝いをしにいこう。
　中庭に出ると、ホウキを持った琥珀さんの姿があった。
　裏庭での掃除は終わったのか、陽気な鼻歌を口ずさみながら中庭の落ち葉を払っている。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――I’ll go help Kohaku.
In the courtyard I found Kohaku holding a broom.
Apparently finished with the rear garden, she was humming cheerfully as she swept the fallen leaves.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---I'll go help Kohaku-san.
I go out to the courtyard and see Kohaku-san holding a broom.
I suppose she is done with the rear courtyard, and is now humming in the courtyard while sweeping the leaves.

entries.japanese:
「あら、どうしたんですか志貴さん。
こんな時間に中庭に出てくるなんて」
「あ……いや、ヒマだから琥珀さんの手伝いでもしようかなって思ったんだけど、もしかして終わっちゃった？」
「ええ、裏庭の手入れは先ほど済ませてしまいました。
もうちょっとしたら夕食の準備をしなくちゃいけないんですけど、それまでは中庭の手入れをしておこうと思いまして」
　琥珀さんは働きものらしく、中庭の落ち葉もほとんどが整理されていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Why, Shiki. What brings you into the courtyard at this hour?”
“I was bored and thought I might help you, but have you already finished?”
“Yes, I completed the rear garden a little while ago. I’ll need to begin preparing dinner soon, but until then I thought I would tidy the courtyard.”
Industrious as ever, Kohaku had already gathered nearly all the leaves.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Huh?
What is the matter, Shiki-san, coming out to the courtyard at this time?"
"Ah…… Nothing.
I was just bored, so I thought I'd come help you.
Are you done already?"
"Yes, I just finished the rear courtyard.
Since there was some time before I had to prepare dinner, I thought I should sweep the courtyard as well."
It seems Kohaku-san is rather industrious, as she has already taken care of most of the leaves.

entries.japanese:
「……よけいなお世話だったか。
琥珀さん、庭の掃除はほんとうにテキパキとしてるんだね」
「はい、お庭の整理は昔からわたしの管轄でしたから。
裏庭のガーデンも、林の楠や楓の管理も任されているんです」
「へえ、裏の花壇だけじゃなくて林のほうも琥珀さんの仕事なんだ」
　……あれ。
　っていうことは、もしかして。
「あの、琥珀さん。
林の奥のほうに大きな木があるよね。
あれもやっぱり琥珀さんが世話をしてるの？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“So much for being useful. You’re incredibly efficient at this, Kohaku.”
“I’ve always been responsible for the grounds. The garden behind the mansion, and even the camphors and maples in the woods, are all under my care.”
“The woods too, not just the flower beds?”
Wait.
In that case.
“Kohaku. There’s a huge tree deep in those woods. Do you care for that one as well?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I guess I'm no help.
Kohaku-san, you almost cleaned up all the leaves in the whole courtyard already."
"Yes, taking care of the garden has always been my job.
Taking care of the garden in the rear courtyard, the woods, and the maples to the south are also my responsibility."
"Wow, your job is not just to take care of the flower bed, but also the woods?"
…… Hold on a minute here.
Does that mean…?
"Um, Kohaku-san.
There is this huge tree in the middle of the woods.
Do you take care of that too?"

entries.japanese:
「まさか、そんなワケないじゃないですか志貴さん。
あの大木はずっと昔からお屋敷にあるものです。
あれだけのものになってしまうとわたしでは手入れはできませんよ」
　なにが楽しいのか、嬉しそうに琥珀さんは笑う。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Of course not, Shiki. That tree has stood on the estate since long before my time. Something that enormous is beyond my ability to tend.”
For some reason, Kohaku laughed as though the question had delighted her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No, how could I, Shiki-san?
That tree has been at the mansion for a long time.
I can't take care of something that big."
As if she was having a lot of fun, Kohaku-san smiles happily.

entries.japanese:
「けど、あの木は大切なものなんです。
一際大きくて、お屋敷の二階の廊下からならすぐに見付かるでしょう？
　子供の頃はあの木を目印にして色々と探したものです」
「ふぅん―――俺も一度だけ、あの木には思い出があるんだけど」
　……それも、今では無意味なものになってしまった。
　あの時の少女―――翡翠は、あの時の約束をどうとも思っていなかった。
まあ、八年も前の事だから仕方ないといえば仕方のない事なのかもしれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“But it is an important tree. It rises above all the others, so you can spot it at once from the second-floor corridor, can’t you? When I was little, I used it as a landmark whenever I went searching for things.”
“I see—I have one memory tied to that tree myself.”
But now it had become meaningless.
The girl from that day—Hisui—had thought nothing of our promise. But after eight years, perhaps that was only natural.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"But that tree is very important.
From the second floor of the mansion in the hallway, you can see that tree very well.
As a child, I would use it as a landmark to find many things."
"I see---I too have memories of that tree, although it was just once."
…… But it seems like there isn't any meaning to it anymore.
The girl from that time---Hisui didn't think much about the promise we made.
It was eight years ago, so I guess it can't be helped if she thinks differently now.

entries.japanese:
「あ、そろそろ時間ですね。
それじゃ志貴さん、お夕食の時間になったら食堂にきてくださいね」
　琥珀さんはパタパタと足音をたてて去っていった。
　きっと夕食の仕込みはとっくに終わっていて、あとは準備をするだけなんだろう。
「……こっちも一度部屋に戻るかな」
　少しだけ林の奥にある大木を眺めて、中庭を後にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh, look at the time. Shiki, please come to the dining room when dinner is ready.”
Kohaku hurried away, her footsteps pattering over the stones.
She had probably finished the actual cooking preparations long ago and needed only to put everything together.
“I suppose I’ll go back to my room.”
After one last glance at the great tree deep in the woods, I left the courtyard.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah, it's almost time.
Well then, Shiki-san, when it's time for dinner, please come to the dining room."
With that, Kohaku-san disappears, her footsteps echoing in the air.
I'm sure all the ingredients are set, and all that remains is preparing the food.
"…… I guess I should head back to my room."
After staring a little more at the big tree in the middle of the woods, I leave the courtyard.

entries.japanese:
――――秋葉の部屋に行ってみよう。
　……秋葉がまだ帰ってきていない、という事は聞いている。
　と、ゆうことは。
いま秋葉の部屋に行っても誰もいないハズだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――I’ll have a look at Akiha’s room.
I had already heard that Akiha wasn’t home yet.
Which meant. Her room ought to be empty right now.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----I'll go to Akiha's room.
…… I heard that Akiha hasn't returned yet.
Which means that if I go to her room, no one will be there.

entries.japanese:
……やってきてしまった。
　秋葉の部屋は二階の東奥にある。
俺の部屋とは四十メートル以上は離れた場所にある、まず入る機会のない部屋だ。
「―――――」
　ごくり、と喉が動く。
　……冷静に考えてみると、なにかものすごくヤバイ事をしようとしている。
「――ええい、ここまできて引き下がれるか！」
　意を決して、秋葉の部屋の扉を開けた。
entries.maoEnglish:
And yet here I was.
Akiha’s room lay at the far eastern end of the second floor, more than forty meters from mine. It was a place I would ordinarily have no reason to enter.
“―――――”
I swallowed hard.
Looked at calmly, what I was about to do was incredibly dangerous.
“I’ve come this far—I’m not turning back now!”
Summoning my courage, I opened her door.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… I arrive at her room.
Akiha's room is in the middle of the east wing.
My room is about forty meters away, so this a rare opportunity.
"-----"
I gulp anxiously.
…… If I think about it calmly, I'm doing something extremely dangerous.
"--I can't go back now!"
Making up my mind, I open the door to Akiha's room.

entries.japanese:
「―――――」
　……予想していた事とはいえ、言葉がない。
　とても高校生の部屋とは思えない部屋の内装に、しばらく無言で見惚れてしまった。
「……ベッドはないけど……寝室は別っていう事か」
　その贅沢さに毒気が抜かれた。
　秋葉の留守中に秋葉の部屋を探索だ、なんて思ったけど、ここは軽い気持ちで立ち入れる場所じゃないみたいだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
Though the sight was more or less what I had expected, it left me speechless.
The room looked nothing like a high school girl’s bedroom, and for a while I could only admire it in silence.
“No bed—so she has a separate bedroom?”
The sheer luxury took all the mischief out of me.
I had come intending to explore while Akiha was away, but this did not feel like a place one trespassed in lightly.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-----"
…… I expected this… but still, I'm at a loss for words.
I am fascinated by the room that looks nothing like any high schooler's room.
"…… There's no bed…… it must be in a separate room."
I almost forget myself looking at all the luxury.
I thought I'd explore Akiha's room while she isn't here, but this isn't a place where you can come in like that.

entries.japanese:
「………秋葉に見つかる前に戻るか」
　はあ、とため息とともに踵を返す。
――――と。
「あら、もう少しゆっくりしていいのに、兄さん」
―――扉の前に、腕組みをした秋葉の姿があった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’d better leave before Akiha catches me.”
With a sigh, I turned back toward the door.
――――Then.
“Oh, Brother, you needn’t hurry away; please make yourself at home.”
―――Akiha stood before the door with her arms folded.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I better go before Akiha finds me."
With a sigh, I turn to leave the room.
----And.
"Oh no, please, take your time, Nii-san."
---Akiha is standing in front of the door with her arms crossed.

entries.japanese:
「あ、秋葉――――か、帰ってきてたのか、おまえ……！？」
「ええ、たったいま帰ってきたところです。
それより兄さん、何か重要なお話でもあるのでしょう？
　そうでもなければ私の部屋に、一人で、断りもなく入る理由なんてありませんものね」
「あ――――う」
　じろり、と睨まれて思わずあとじさる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“A-Akiha――――you’re back already――――!?”
“Yes, I returned this very moment. More importantly, Brother, you must have something terribly important to discuss with me. Otherwise there could be no reason for you to enter my room alone and without permission.”
“Uh――――”
Her glare drove me back a step.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah, Akiha----You've come back already……!?"
"Yes, I just got back.
More importantly, Nii-san, is there something you want to talk to me about?
There has to be, otherwise there would be no reason for you to be in my room alone, now, would there?"
"Ah----um."
I back up as Akiha glares at me intently.

entries.japanese:
「いや、その―――別に大した用件じゃなくて、秋葉と少し話そうかなって思っただけなんだけど―――」
「ふうん、おかしいですね。
私にお話があるのでしたら、私の部屋に入る意味はないじゃないですか。
私は不在だったんですから、すぐにご自分のお部屋に戻るのが道理ではありませんか？」
「そうなんだけど……ちょっと、秋葉の部屋で待っていようかなって、思ったり、思わなかったり……」
「―――――――」
　秋葉の視線の圧力が増してくる。
　……うう、ここは素直に謝ったほうがいいみたいだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“It’s nothing important—I only thought I might talk to you for a while―――”
“How strange. If you wished to speak with me, entering my room served no purpose while I was away. Surely the reasonable thing would have been to return to your own room.”
“That’s true, but I may or may not have thought I could wait for you in here……”
“…”
The pressure of Akiha’s gaze intensified.
Yes, surrender and an honest apology were probably my only options.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No, I---it's not really important… I just thought I'd talk with you for a bit---"
"Oh really?
That's strange.
If you wanted to talk to me, going into my room when I'm not there is rather pointless, isn't it?
It makes perfect sense that if you saw I was not in my room, you would go back to your room, right?"
"That's true, but…… I thought maybe I should just wait a while in your room or maybe I didn't……"
"-------"
Akiha's stare becomes even harder.
…… Ugh, I think it's best if I just apologize right now.

entries.japanese:
「……悪かった。
秋葉の部屋ってどうなってるのか気になってさ」
「つまり興味本位で私の部屋に忍び込んだ、という事ですか」
「うっ―――いや、そんな悪気はなかったんだけど―――」
「なかった、では済まされません！
　女性の部屋に断りもなく入室するなんて、有間の家でどんな教育を受けていたんですか兄さんは！」
「―――面目ない。
これはあくまで俺の修行不足っていうか、悪戯心でした」
「―――――――」
　秋葉の視線が痛い。
　が、こっちには非しかないので、とにかく平謝りするしかなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’m sorry. I was curious what your room looked like.”
“In other words, you sneaked into my room to satisfy your curiosity.”
“Well―――I didn’t mean any harm―――”
“Meaning no harm does not excuse it! What did the Arima family teach you, Brother, if you think you may enter a woman’s room without permission?”
“I have no defense. Call it a failure of training—or a childish impulse.”
“…”
Akiha’s stare hurt.
Since I was wrong in every conceivable respect, all I could do was keep apologizing.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Sorry.
I just was wondering what your room was like."
"In other words, you sneaked into my room out of curiosity?"
"Uh---no, I had no bad intentions---"
"It doesn't matter!
Sneaking into a girl's room like that, what kind of upbringing did you have at the Arima household!?"
"---I'm sorry.
I guess you can call this my stupidity, or my mischievous mind."
"-------"
Akiha's gaze is painful.
Since I'm the only one at fault, I only can apologize.

entries.japanese:
「……いいわ、今回の事はなかった事にしてさしあげます。
もうじき琥珀もやってくるし、その前に兄さんはご自分のお部屋に戻ってください」
「う……すまん、秋葉」
　お兄ちゃん、イタズラがすぎたみたいだ。
「ですけど決してこれで済んだと思わないでくださいね。
この貸しはきちんと贖ってもらいますから、兄さん」
　みょうにドスの入った、どこか愉しそうな声でそう言って、秋葉はドアの前から離れてくれた。
「…………」
　なんか、すごい弱みを握られたなー、と思いつつ、秋葉の部屋から脱出した。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Very well, I will pretend this never happened. Kohaku will be here shortly, so return to your own room before she arrives, Brother.”
“Right—sorry, Akiha.”
Big brother had clearly taken his little prank too far.
“But do not imagine that settles the matter. You will repay this debt in full, Brother.”
Speaking in an oddly menacing voice with an equally odd note of pleasure, Akiha moved away from the door.
“…”
Reflecting that she had acquired devastating leverage over me, I escaped from her room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Fine, I will overlook it this time.
Please go back to your room before Kohaku comes."
"S…… sorry, Akiha."
It seems that Onii-chan is just a mischievous brat after all.
"But don't think that this matter is over.
I expect to be compensated for this, Nii-san."
For some reason, there is a hint of both amusement and threat in Akiha's voice as she steps away from the door.
"…………"
I leave Akiha's room thinking that she has grasped my terrible weakness.

entries.japanese:
―――夕食が終わって、部屋に戻ってきた。
　時刻は夜の十時になろうとしている。
　今日はめずらしく食後のお茶会なんてものを秋葉たちと過ごしたもんだから、いつのまにか就寝時間になってしまっていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――After dinner, I returned to my room.
It was almost ten.
We had done something unusual tonight and lingered over tea after dinner, so by the time I left Akiha and the others, bedtime had crept up on me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---After dinner, I return to my room.
It's ten at night.
Since I had tea with Akiha and the others after dinner, it's already time for bed.

entries.japanese:
「ん………」
　あまり疲れているわけでもないのに、どことなく体がだるい。
　屋敷の生活に慣れてきた証拠だろうか。
　無反応な翡翠や明るい琥珀さん、なんだかんだと俺のことを気遣ってくれる秋葉。
　……たしかに、慣れてくるとこの生活は楽しいと思う。
それこそ八年前の自分に戻ったような気さえしてくるぐらいだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Mm…”
I wasn’t particularly tired, yet a vague heaviness hung over my body.
Maybe it meant I was settling into life at the mansion.
Impassive Hisui, cheerful Kohaku, Akiha, who always found one way or another to look after me…
Once I grew accustomed to it, this life truly was pleasant. Pleasant enough to make me feel as though I had become my eight-year-old self again.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Nnn……"
I'm not really tired, but my body feels sluggish.
It seems like I've finally gotten used to life in this mansion.
Expressionless Hisui, bright and cheery Kohaku, and Akiha, who worries over me constantly.
…… Certainly, getting used to this lifestyle… is fun.
It seems like I've returned to the me that existed eight years ago.

entries.japanese:
有間の家では、ここまでくつろぐ事はできなかった。
　おばさんにも中学生の子供がいたけど、どうも敬遠されているようで話をする機会も少なかったし。
「ん……ほんとに、眠くなってきた」
　寝巻に着替えてベッドに横になる。
　早く眠って早起きして、明日こそ秋葉を驚かせてやろう―――
entries.maoEnglish:
I had never been able to relax this completely with the Arima family.
My aunt had a child in middle school, but they seemed wary of me, and we rarely spoke.
“Mm, I really am getting sleepy.”
I changed into my pajamas and lay down.
I’d go to sleep early, wake up early, and tomorrow I would finally be the one to surprise Akiha—
entries.mirrorMoon:
I never had a chance to relax this much when living with the Arimas.
The Arimas have a child in middle school as well, but we were always distant and we never really had a chance to talk.
"Nnn…… I really am sleepy."
Changing into my pajamas, I lie down in bed.
I'll go to bed early, wake up early, and give Akiha quite a surprise---

entries.japanese:
「――――あれ」
　気がつくと、街にいた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What…?”
When I came to, I was in the city.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----Huh?"
All of a sudden, I find myself in town.

entries.japanese:
午前零時。
　人通りの途絶えた街の中を、歩いている。
entries.maoEnglish:
Midnight.
I am walking through streets emptied of people.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Midnight.
I walk through the empty town.

entries.japanese:
「ハア―――ハア――――ハア」
　どうしてか息があがっている。
　オレは。
　ぎょろぎょろと血走った目で、道行く人間を見定めている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hah―――hah――――hah”
For some reason I’m panting.
I am.
My bloodshot eyes roll from side to side, appraising every person who passes.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I pant heavily.
For some reason, I'm out of breath.
I.
With bloodshot eyes, I am looking at people walking down the street.

entries.japanese:
バカな連中。

――――自分だけはそんな目にあわないっていう自己の特別性を信じているのか、それとも死にたくても自殺する手段がなくて、誰かに殺してほしいのか。
　まあ、恐らくは後者だろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
Idiots.
The murderer hasn’t even been caught, yet they keep wandering the streets as though nothing has happened.
――――Do they believe in their own special exemption—that such a fate could never befall them—or do they long for death but lack the means to kill themselves and hope someone else will do it for them?
Probably the latter.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Foolish people.
Walking the streets so carelessly even though the killer has not been caught.
----Do they think that they're special and won't get killed?
Or maybe, they want to die but are unable to kill themselves and want someone to kill them?
Well, it's probably the latter.

entries.maoEnglish:

Decision made.
Tonight, I’ll change the plan.
Anyone will do now.
Anyone I can kill.
One more time.
I want to taste that feeling one more time—
entries.mirrorMoon:

Anyone will do.

Once more.

I WANT THAT
A sister belongs to her brother.
She is mine alone.

Holding her long hair, I drag her body.

entries.maoEnglish:

Fakes make me furious.
entries.mirrorMoon:

I'm angry.

Impostor.

entries.japanese:
「ハア――――ハア――――ハア――――」

「今夜は、疲れた。
また明日、やろう」
　うん、それがいい。
そうしよう。
　さあ。
　朝が来る前に、誰にも気付かれないように、自分の寝床に戻らなければ――――
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hah――――hah――――hah――――”
I wasted too much strength.
The night isn’t endless.
When morning comes, Shiki will wake.

Yes. Let’s do that.
Now.
Before morning comes, I must return to my bed without anyone noticing――――
entries.mirrorMoon:
*pant*----*pant*----*pant*----
I've used up extra energy.
The night isn't that long.
Once it becomes morning, Shiki will awaken.
"I'm tired tonight.
I'll start again, tomorrow."
Yeah, that'll do.
That's what I'll do.
Now then.
Before the morning comes, before anyone realizes, I must go back to my own bed----

entries.japanese:
……ダメだ、そんな気分じゃない。
　気を遣ってくれた琥珀さんには悪いけど、弓塚との事が忘れられないうちはとてもじゃないけどそんな気分にはなれない。
　この二日間。
　あんなに他人の血を見てきた自分が、琥珀さんや秋葉、翡翠に歓迎されていいはずが、ない。
entries.maoEnglish:
No, I couldn't celebrate.
I felt bad after Kohaku had gone out of her way for me, but until I could forget what had happened with Yumizuka, I couldn't possibly be in the mood.
These past two days, I had seen so much of other people’s blood.
Someone like me had no right to be welcomed by Kohaku, Akiha, and Hisui.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… No, I don't feel like it at all.
I know Kohaku-san just wants me to feel good, but I can't forget about Yumizuka right now.
These past two days.
After I've seen so much of other people's blood, I can't be welcomed by them.

“What…?”
――――――thump.

the room began to spin.
entries.mirrorMoon:

------My head is pounding.
