Pound.
I feel, very dizzy.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま―――？」
　控えめに翡翠が呼びかけてくる。
　……秋葉も琥珀さんも気付かない、俺本人だって気付かないような、突然の眩暈に、翡翠は気がついてくれたみたいだ。
　だがそれで薄れていく意識が止まってくれるワケでもない。
　ばたん、と。
　糸の切れた人形のように、体が床に倒れこんだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki…?”
Hisui called to me softly.
Neither Akiha nor Kohaku had noticed the sudden dizziness—apparently even I hadn’t recognized it until it struck—yet Hisui had.
But her voice could do nothing to arrest the darkness swallowing my mind.
My body struck the floor.
I fell like a puppet whose strings had been cut.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama---?"
Hisui hesitantly calls my name.
…… Hisui seems to have noticed my sudden dizziness which neither Akiha nor Kohaku-san realized, and which I barely realized myself.
But that doesn't stop it from getting worse.
Thud.
Just like a puppet without any strings, I collapse to the floor.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま、お気を確かに、志貴さま……！」
　翡翠の声が遠くなっていく。
　……ああ、まったく自分でもイヤになる。
　ただ弓塚との事を思い出しただけで、遠野志貴は意識を失おうとしてしまっているんだから――――
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki, please stay with me, Master Shiki…!”
Hisui's voice receded into the distance.
God, I disgusted myself.
Merely remembering Yumizuka was enough to make Shiki Tohno lose consciousness—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama, get a hold of yourself, Shiki-sama……!"
Hisui's voice grows distant.
…… Ah, I really am pretty pathetic.
Just thinking about Yumizuka and what happened, I lose consciousness like this----

entries.japanese:
「あ―――――」
　気がつくと、自分の部屋で横になっていた。
　俺はベッドに眠っていて、目の前には秋葉の姿がある。
「秋、葉？」
「兄さん？
　気がつかれたんですね」
　秋葉はほっと胸を撫で下ろす。
「俺は……そうか、また貧血で倒れたんだっけ」
「ええ。
あれから七時間近く眠っていたんですよ、兄さんは」
「―――そうか。
最近なにかと寝不足だったから、その反動なのかな。
……悪い。
また秋葉に迷惑をかけちまった」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ah…”
When I came to, I was lying in my own room.
I was in bed, and Akiha was sitting before me.
“Akiha?”
“Brother? You're awake?”
Akiha released a breath of relief.
“I see—I collapsed from anemia again.”
“Yes. You slept for almost seven hours, Brother.”
“I see. Perhaps all the sleep I've missed lately caught up with me. Sorry. I've caused you trouble again.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah-----"
When I come to, I'm lying in my room.
While I was sleeping, Akiha must have been watching me because she is there in front of me.
"Aki, ha?"
"Nii-san?
You finally got up."
Akiha visibly relaxes.
"I…… that's right, I must have passed out from my anemia again."
"Yes.
You slept for about seven hours, Nii-san."
"---Really.
I haven't been sleeping enough recently, that might be why.
…… Sorry.
I've caused you trouble again."

entries.japanese:
「何を言うんですか。
兄さんの体が不安定なのは兄さんの責任ではないでしょう？
　兄さんは私の兄さんなんですから、看病をするのは当たり前です。
迷惑だというのでしたら、そう思われるほうがよっぽど迷惑です」
「……そっか。
それじゃお礼を言うのはやめとく。
兄妹なら当然のことだもんな、こんなの」
「なんだ、それだけ言えるんでしたらもう大丈夫みたいですね」
　言って、秋葉は俺の熱を計った。
　熱は三十七度六分。
平熱より一度ばかり高い程度。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Don't be absurd, Brother. Your poor health is hardly your fault. You are my brother, so of course I will nurse you. If anything is troublesome, it is hearing you call yourself a burden.”
“All right. Then I won't thank you. This is only natural between siblings.”
“If you can say that much, you must be fine.”
Akiha took my temperature.
It was 37.6 degrees—barely a degree above normal.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"What are you saying?
Your condition isn't your fault, right?
It is only natural for me to take care of my own brother, Nii-san.
You saying that you are a trouble to me is actually more troublesome than me watching over you."
"…… I see.
Well, I won't say thanks then.
It's only natural, since we are brother and sister."
"Well, if you can say all that, then I suppose you must be alright."
saying that, she takes my temperature.
Thirty seven degrees Celsius.
That's just one more degree than normal.

entries.japanese:
「……少し不満ですけど、顔色も良いみたいだしこれなら兄さん一人でも安心かな。
それじゃ私も部屋に戻りますけど」
「……ん？
　けど、なんだよ秋葉」
「私はともかく、翡翠にお礼を言っておいてあげてください。
あの子、兄さんが倒れてから今までずっと看病していてくれたんですから」
　お大事に、と残して秋葉は退室していった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I'm not entirely satisfied, but your color is good, so I think you'll be safe alone. I'll return to my room.”
“Hm? But what is it, Akiha?”
“Never mind me. Be sure to thank Hisui, who has been caring for you without a break since you collapsed.”
Akiha told me to take care and left the room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I still feel a little uneasy, but you look fine, so I guess it is okay for me to leave you by yourself.
I'll be in my room then."
"……?
What, Akiha?"
"Please give your thanks to Hisui.
She is the one that cared for you all this time."
After wishing me well, she leaves the room.

entries.japanese:
「……翡翠が……看ててくれたのか」
　そういえば、気を失う直前に聞こえたのは翡翠の声だけだった。
　秋葉や琥珀さんも何か言っていたようだけど、聞こえたのは駆け寄ってくる翡翠の声だけだった気がする。
　くらり、と心地よい眩暈がする。
「っ………まだ、本調子じゃないみたいだ」
　はあ、と深く呼吸をする。
　せっかくの休日は、いつのまにか終わってしまっていた。
　……まあ、それも一日じゅう翡翠が看ていてくれたのなら、そう悪いことではなかったかもしれない――――
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hisui was looking after me?”
Come to think of it, hers had been the only voice I heard just before losing consciousness.
Akiha and Kohaku must have said something too, but Hisui's voice rushing toward me was the only one I remembered.
A pleasant dizziness washed over me.
“I'm still not quite myself.”
I drew a long breath.
Somehow my entire holiday had vanished.
Still, if Hisui had spent the whole day beside me, perhaps it hadn't been wasted after all—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Hisui…… was the one who cared for me?"
Come to think of it, I heard her voice before I passed out.
Even though I'm sure Akiha and Kohaku-san must have said something, Hisui's was the only voice that I heard coming towards me.
I start to get dizzy.
"……… I guess I'm not fully well yet."
I take a deep breath.
My day off ended before I knew it.
…… Well, if Hisui was watching over me all day, then I suppose it wasn't a bad thing----

entries.japanese: ―――懐かしい、匂いが、する。
entries.maoEnglish: ―――There was a familiar scent.
entries.mirrorMoon: ---Something seems… very familiar.

entries.maoEnglish:
An old tatami room.
A dark room.
entries.mirrorMoon:

A dark room.

had that been?

that's an extremely old memory.

新しく連れてこられて周りの人たちになれなくて、一人でずっと閉じこもっていた子供のころ。

　その先に何もないってわかっていても、ずっとそうしていたかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
Back when I had just been brought there, when I couldn’t grow used to the people around me and spent every day shut away alone.
I hated everything and didn't want to speak to anyone.
I wanted to remain alone forever, sealed inside the cocoon of that happy childhood.
Even knowing there was nothing beyond that cocoon, I wanted to stay inside forever.
entries.mirrorMoon:
When I was very young, I wasn't used to the new people that took me in, so I locked myself up in my room.
I didn't care for anything; I didn't want to talk to anyone.
Always, always alone, and I wanted to be swaddled in a cradle of my happy memories.

Even if I knew there would be nothing like that for me ever again, I still wanted to do so.

entries.japanese:
トントン、という音。
「―――だれ？」
「あたしだよ」
　ああ、またやってきた。
　同い年ぐらいの女の子が、この部屋の扉を叩いている。
「シキちゃん、遊ぼ。
そんなとこにいたらかびが生えちゃうんだからね」
「ヤだ。
外は、ヤだ」
　膝を抱えて、あかりのない部屋のすみで、ずっと小さくなっていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
Knock, knock.
“―――Who is it?”
“It’s me.”
She had come again.
A girl about my age was knocking on the door.
“Shiki, come play. If you stay in there, you’ll grow mold.”
“No. I don’t wanna go outside.”
Hugging my knees, I stayed curled into a tiny ball in the unlit corner.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Knock knock, came a sound.
"…… Who is it?"
"It's me."
Ah, she came again.
That girl around my age was knocking on the door again.
"SHIKI-chan, let's play.
You'll get moldy if you stay in a place like that."
"I don't wanna.
I don't like going outside."
Hugging my knees, I huddled in a corner of the dark room.

entries.japanese:
……女の子は毎日やってきた。
　飽きもしないでノックをする。
　少女は、決して無理強いはせず、扉を開けようともしないで、ただ自分に呼びかけ続けていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
The girl came every day.
She never tired of knocking.
She never forced me or tried to open the door, but simply kept talking to me through it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… That girl came every day.
She would always knock, never getting tired of it.
She would never force me out, so she would not open the door, but just continued to call my name.

entries.japanese:
「どうして外に出てこないの？」
　だって、外には知らない人しかいないもの。
みんな、ボクのことを憎んでいるんだ。
「そんなことないよ。
みんな、シキくんのこと好きになりたがってるよ」
　うん。
それはわかるけど、しんじられない。
だって、ボクのお父さんは、そうして―――
entries.maoEnglish:
“Why won’t you come outside?”
Because everyone outside is a stranger. They all hate me.
“That’s not true. Everyone wants to like you, Shiki.”
I know. But I can’t believe it. Because my father was like that, and then—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Why won't you come outside?"
Because there's no one that I know outside.
Everyone hates me outside.
"That's not true.
Everyone wants to like you, SHIKI-kun."
Yes.
I knew that, but I couldn't believe it.
Because my father went outside, and---

entries.japanese:
そうして。
　自分の父親は、そうして、バラバラにされてしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
And then.
My father was, just like that, torn to pieces.
entries.mirrorMoon:
And.
He was torn to pieces.

entries.japanese:
「……そっか。
そうだよね、それじゃあ誰もしんじられないよね」
　そうなんだ。
だから、ずっとここにいる。
もうこわい思いはしたくないんだ。
「でも、それじゃいつまでもひとりきりだよ。
ひとりきりはつまんないよ」
　つまんなくても、こわいよりは楽しいとおもうけど。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I see. Then of course you can’t trust anybody.”
That’s right. So I’m staying here forever. I don’t want to be scared again.
“But then you’ll always be alone. Being alone is boring.”
Even if it’s boring, I think it’s nicer than being scared.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I see.
No wonder you can't trust anyone."
Yeah, that's why I will always stay here.
I don't want any more scary things happening.
"But, you will just be by yourself all the time.
Being by yourself is no fun."
Even if it's no fun, it is better than being scared.

entries.japanese:
「そんなの、ぜんぜんたのしくなんかない。
もう、ほんとにしょうがないなあ。
じゃあ、シキちゃんはあたしをしんじていいよ」
　……しんじていいよって、なにそれ。
あべこべだよ、ふつーはボクがしんじてあげてもいいってゆわない？
「いいのっ！
　シキちゃんはあたしをしんじて出てくるの！」
　……いいけど。
けど、しんじるってなにをしんじるの？
entries.maoEnglish:
“That isn’t nice at all. Honestly, you’re hopeless. Fine, then—you can trust me, Shiki.”
What does that mean, I can trust you? That’s backwards—aren’t I supposed to be the one who says I might trust you?
“That’s just how it is! Trust me, Shiki, and then come outside!”
All right. But what am I supposed to trust?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"That's, that's not fun at all.
Then, SHIKI-chan, you can believe in me."
…… You say I can believe in you.
That's a little backwards.
Don't people normally say, "I believe you?"
"It's okay!
SHIKI-chan, you can trust me and come out!
…… Fine, but, believe, what should I believe in?

entries.japanese:
「かんたんだよ。
もしみんながシキちゃんを嫌っても、あたしはきっとシキちゃんを好きだってこと。
　あたし、シキちゃんのことが好きだから、こうやって遊びにいこうって言ってるんだもん」
　…………そとは、たのしい？
「うん！
　ひとりでいるより、きっときっと楽しいよ―――――」
―――明るい光に意識が冴えていく。
　窓からさしこんでくる朝の光に目が覚めていく。
「………ん」
　夢からさめる。
　……よくわからない、ひどく曖昧な夢を見た気がする。
　懐かしい匂いをかんじた。
　あれは畳の匂い―――だろうか。
entries.maoEnglish:
“It’s easy. Even if everybody hates you, I’ll still like you, Shiki. I keep coming to ask you to play because I like you, Shiki.”
Is it fun outside?
“Yes! It’ll be much, much more fun than being alone—”
―――Bright light sharpened my mind.
Morning streamed through the window and drew me awake.
“Nn.”
I surfaced from the dream.
I had dreamed something confused and terribly vague.
There had been a familiar scent.
The smell of tatami, perhaps.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Simple.
Even if everyone hates you, I will still like you, SHIKI-chan.
Because I like you, I always come and ask you to play."
……… Is outside, fun?
"Yeah!
It's much, much more fun than being by yourself-----!"
---A bright light floods my consciousness.
As I open my eyes, the morning light shines through the window.
"……… Nnn."
I wake from my dream.
…… I don't quite remember it, but I remember vaguely watching a dream.
It was very nostalgic.
The smell of tatami---is that what it was?

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま、お目覚めでいらっしゃいますか？」
　と。
コンコン、というノック音と一緒に翡翠の声が聞こえてきた。
「ああ、起きてるから中に入ってきていいよ」
「はい。
それでは失礼します」
　一礼して部屋に入ってくる翡翠。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki, are you awake?”
Then came a knock. Hisui's voice sounded through the door at the same time.
“Yes, I’m up, so you can come in.”
“Very well. Excuse me.”
Hisui bowed before entering.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama, are you awake?"
Knock knock.
I hear Hisui's voice.
"Yeah, I'm up, so you can come in."
"Yes.
Please excuse me."
With a bow, Hisui enters the room.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま、ご気分のほうはいかがですか？
　体調が優れないようでしたら、どうか遠慮なさらずにおっしゃってください」
　翡翠はじっとベッドに横になったこちらを見つめてくる。
　……どうも、昨日突然倒れた事をまだ心配してくれているみたいだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“How are you feeling, Master Shiki? If you are at all unwell, please don’t hesitate to tell me.”
Hisui studied me as I lay in bed.
Apparently my sudden collapse yesterday was still troubling her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama, how are you feeling?
If you feel bad, please do not hesitate to tell me."
Hisui stares over at me as I lay in bed.
…… It seems she is still really worried about me collapsing so suddenly yesterday.

entries.japanese:
「大丈夫、体のほうは問題ないって。
昨日倒れたのだって、今までちょっと無理しすぎただけなんだし、これからはもうあんなコトにはならないよ」
　弓塚―――吸血鬼はもういない。
　だから、この数日間のように深夜に出歩くなんていう事は、もうないんだから。
「志貴さまがそうおっしゃるのでしたらよろしいのですが―――」
　何か他に心配事でもあるのか、翡翠は珍しく不安そうな顔をする。
「――――まあ、心配してくれるのは有り難いけど」
　言って、勢いよくベッドから立ちあがる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I'm fine—there's nothing wrong with me. I only collapsed because I'd been pushing myself too hard, and it won't happen again.”
Yumizuka—the vampire—was gone.
There would be no more wandering the streets after midnight as I had these past several days.
“If you say so, Master Shiki…”
Hisui looked unusually anxious, as though something else still concerned her.
“I appreciate you worrying about me, but—”
I sprang briskly out of bed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I'm fine, there's nothing wrong with me.
I collapsed yesterday because I've been pushing myself recently, but that won't happen again."
Yumizuka---the vampire does not exist anymore.
Therefore, I won't have to walk the streets late at night anymore, like I did these past few days.
"If you say that is the case, then---"
I don't know what else she is worried about, but she looks at me uneasily.
"----Well, thank you for worrying about me."
I jump out of bed.

entries.japanese:
「ごらんの通り体のほうは元気一杯だよ。
すぐに着替えて居間に行くから、翡翠は先に行っていてくれ」
　翡翠は何か言いたそうな顔つきのままこちらを見つめる。
　と、それもすぐに終わってしまった。
「……かしこまりました。
それでは失礼します」
　翡翠は着替えの学生服を置いて退室した。
entries.maoEnglish:
“As you can see, I’m full of energy. I’ll change and come to the sitting room in a minute, so go on ahead.”
Hisui continued to watch me, looking as though there were something she wanted to say.
Then the moment passed.
“Very well. Please excuse me.”
Hisui left my school uniform and withdrew.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"As you can see, I'm just fine.
I'll change real quick, so please go ahead of me to the sitting room."
Hisui still stares at me with an expression that looks like she wants to say something more.
But, that look passes.
"…… As you wish.
Well then, please excuse me."
Hisui places my fresh clothes down and exits the room.

entries.japanese:
「……どうしたんだろ。
そんなに顔色悪いのかな、俺」
　窓ガラスに映った自分の顔は普段とそう変りは無い。
　とにかく、学生服に着替えて居間に向かわないといけない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What was that about? Do I really look so pale?”
My reflection in the window looked no different from usual.
In any case, I needed to put on my uniform and head downstairs.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… What was that all about?
Do I look that pale?"
My reflection on the window glass looks pretty normal to me.
Anyways, I should hurry up and change, then head to the sitting room.

entries.japanese:
居間に行くと、すでに翡翠の姿があった。
　秋葉はすでに朝食を済ませて紅茶を飲んでいるし、琥珀さんは台所にいるらしい。
entries.maoEnglish:
Hisui was already in the sitting room when I arrived.
Akiha had finished breakfast and was drinking tea, while Kohaku appeared to be in the kitchen.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I go to the sitting room and see Hisui standing there.
Akiha has already eaten breakfast and is now drinking tea.
Kohaku-san seems to be in the kitchen.

entries.japanese:
「おはようございます兄さん。
お体のほうはすっかり良くなったようですね」
　あわだたしい俺とは対照的に、秋葉は落ちつき払っている。
「ああ、おはよう秋葉。
昨夜は、その、手間をかけさせてすまなかった」
「……兄さん、同じことを何度も言わせないでください。
あの程度の事は手間と呼べるものではありませんし、感謝するのでしたら私にではなく翡翠にでしょう」
　むっ、と不愉快そうに目を閉じて秋葉は言う。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Good morning, Brother. You seem to have recovered completely.”
In contrast to my hurried entrance, Akiha was perfectly composed.
“Morning, Akiha. About last night—I’m sorry I put you to so much trouble.”
“Don’t make me repeat myself, Brother. What I did hardly qualifies as trouble, and if you intend to thank anyone, it should be Hisui.”
Akiha closed her eyes with a displeased frown.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Good morning, Nii-san.
You seem like you've recovered."
In contrast to me, she seems very calm and collected.
"Yeah, good morning Akiha.
Sorry for being such a burden last night."
"…… Nii-san, don't make me repeat myself.
I didn't consider that a burden, and if you are to thank someone, thank Hisui."
She closes her eyes in displeasure.

entries.japanese:
「――――そうか」
　言われて、まだ翡翠にお礼を言ってなかった事に気がついた。
「……翡翠。
遅くなったけど、昨日はありがとう。
俺はこんなだから、色々と手間をかけさせて申し訳ない」
「いえ、わたしのほうこそ志貴さまのお体を気遣えず、申し訳ありませんでした」
　ふかぶかと一礼をする翡翠。
「いや、だから情けないのは俺のほうなんだって。
翡翠が謝る必要なんてないだろ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Right.”
Only then did I realize I still hadn’t thanked Hisui.
“…Hisui, I know it’s late, but thank you for yesterday. I’m sorry someone as unreliable as me keeps creating work for you.”
“Master Shiki, I must apologize for failing to consider your health.”
Hisui bowed deeply.
“No, I’m the pathetic one here. You have nothing to apologize for.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----I see."
Those words remind me that I haven't thanked Hisui yet.
"…… Hisui.
This is a little late, but thanks for what you did yesterday.
Since my body's this way, I'm sorry I caused you a lot of trouble."
"No, I am the one who should apologize.
I was not attentive to your condition."
Hisui bows.
"No, it's really my fault.
You don't need to apologize."

entries.japanese:
「ですが志貴さまのご健康をお守りするのもわたしの仕事です。
志貴さまのお体のことを考えず、あのような申し出をしたのはわたしですから」
「…………う」
　あのような申し出、というのは昨日の歓迎会の事なんだろう。
　もともとあの話を持ち出したのは琥珀さんで、翡翠は同意しただけだったのに。
entries.maoEnglish:
“But safeguarding Master Shiki’s health is also part of my duty. I was the one who made such a proposal without considering Master Shiki’s condition.”
“Urgh.”
She presumably meant yesterday’s welcome party.
Kohaku had suggested the whole thing, and Hisui had merely agreed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"But protecting your health is my duty.
It is my fault for suggesting things without thinking about your health."
"………… Uh."
That suggestion, she must mean last night's welcome party.
Actually, it was Kohaku-san's suggestion, and Hisui only agreed with it.

entries.japanese:
「いや、だからそうゆう事じゃなくて―――」
「兄さん、それ以上は水掛論になるだけですよ。
翡翠がそう言っているのならそれでいいじゃないですか」
　言って、秋葉はソファーから立ちあがった。
「時間ですのでお先に失礼します。
兄さんも早く食堂にいって、朝食を済ませたらどうですか？」
「むっ……そりゃあ、朝食は食べるけど」
「朝食でしたらもう用意されています。
そろそろ七時半になるんですから、早くしないと遅刻なさってしまいますよ」
　優雅な足取りで居間から立ち去っていく秋葉。
entries.maoEnglish:
“No, that isn’t what I mean—”
“Brother, any further argument will only go in circles. If Hisui chooses to see it that way, let her.”
Akiha rose from the sofa.
“It’s time for me to leave. Why don’t you go to the dining room and finish breakfast, Brother?”
“I will, but…”
“It has already been prepared. It’s nearly seven thirty, so unless you hurry, you’ll be late.”
Akiha departed the sitting room with graceful steps.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"That has nothing to do with it, so---"
"Nii-san, this is starting to get a little pointless.
If Hisui says that is the case, then let it be."
Akiha stands up from the sofa.
"Well, it is now time, so I'll excuse myself.
Nii-san, can you hurry to the dining room and eat your breakfast?"
"Wh…… Of course I will eat breakfast."
"Breakfast is already prepared.
It's almost seven-thirty, so you should hurry up or you'll be late."
Akiha elegantly strolls out of the sitting room.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま、どうぞお食事をなさってください。
秋葉さまのおっしゃられたとおり、時間はあまりありません」
「……だな。
それじゃ食堂に行ってくる」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Please have your breakfast, Master Shiki. Miss Akiha is correct; there is little time.”
“Right. I’ll go to the dining room.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama, please eat.
As Akiha-sama stated, you do not have much time."
"…… Right.
I'll go to the dining room."

entries.japanese:
朝食を終えて、玄関に出る。
　翡翠は先に俺の鞄を持ってきて、すでに玄関で待っていた。
「今日はまっすぐ帰ってくるから、帰りは四時ごろになる。
あ、それとここで出迎える、なんて事はしなくていいから」
「かしこまりました。
それでは志貴さま、どうかお気をつけて」
「ありがとう。
それじゃ行ってくるよ、翡翠」
　ふかぶかとおじぎをしてくれる翡翠に手をふって、坂道へと走り出した。
entries.maoEnglish:
After breakfast, I went to the entrance hall.
Hisui had brought my bag ahead of me and was already waiting.
“I’ll come straight home today, so I should be back around four. And you don’t need to stand here waiting to greet me.”
“Understood. Please take care, Master Shiki.”
“Thanks. I’m off, Hisui.”
I waved to Hisui as she bowed deeply, then ran down the hill.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I eat breakfast and go to the entrance of the mansion.
Hisui already went to get my bag and has it when I get there.
"I'll come back right after school, so I should be home around four o'clock.
Oh, and you don't have to wait for me here."
"I understand.
Shiki-sama, please be careful on your way."
"Thanks.
I'll get going, Hisui."
Waving a hand to the bowing Hisui, I dash down the street.

entries.japanese:
「あ―――――――！」
　あ―――――――
「はあ――――はあ――――」
　あさ、に、なってる。
　ここは自分の部屋。
　俺はいままでここで、
　こうして、
　眠っていた、ハズ―――――――――
entries.maoEnglish:
“Aaaaaah!”
Ahhhhhhh—
“Hah――――hah――――”
It’s morning.
This is my room.
I’ve been here,
like this,
asleep, or so I thought―――――――――
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah-------!"
Ah-------.
I gasp for air.
It's---morning… now.
This is my room.
Up until now, I've been here,
just like this,
and I should have been sleeping---------

entries.japanese:
「痛ッ………」
　ズキリ、とこめかみが痛む。
「ゆ………め」
　酷い夢を見た。
　人を殺す夢。
　殺しながら、何度も絶頂を迎えていた夢を。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ow…”
Pain spikes through my temple.
“A…
dream.”
A horrible dream.
A dream of murdering someone—and climaxing again and again as I killed her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ahh……"
My forehead is hurting.
"Dre…… am."
I had a terrible dream.
A dream where I killed someone.
A dream where I ejaculated over and over as I killed.

entries.japanese:
「あ…………つ」
　喉が、熱い。
　体中がだるくて、両手には、ごきり、と。
　人の首を、折る感触が、付着したまま。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hot…”
My throat is burning.
My whole body feels leaden, and a single sensation clings to both hands.
The crunch of a human neck breaking.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ho…… t…"
My throat is burning.
My body feels like lead, and my hands…
The feeling of breaking someone's neck still lingers on my hands.

entries.japanese:
「ちが……う」
　違う。
　あんなのは夢だ。
間違いなく夢だ。
　だが、あんなはっきりした夢があるのか。
　何もかも鮮明に覚えている。
　夜の街も、
　首を折る感触も、
　喉にはりつく血の粘つきも、
　無惨に殺してしまった女の顔も―――――
entries.maoEnglish:
“No…”
No.
That was a dream. Unquestionably a dream.
But can a dream be so vivid?
I remember every detail.
The city at night,
the neck snapping in my hands,
the sticky blood clinging to my throat,
the face of the woman I butchered—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"That… can't be."
That can't be.
That was a dream.
Unmistakably a dream.
But are dreams really that vivid?
I remember it so vividly.
The street in the dead of night,
the feeling of snapping someone's neck,
the stickiness of blood gurgling down my throat,
the face of the woman so cruelly killed-----

entries.japanese:
だが夢だ。
実際に遠野志貴はここにいたんだから、あんなものは夢にすぎない。
　ただ、問題は。
　俺が、人を殺して悦ぶような、夢を見てしまっているということ。
entries.maoEnglish:
But it was a dream. Shiki Tohno was here in this room, so it could have been nothing else.
The only problem was this.
I had dreamed of taking pleasure in murder.
entries.mirrorMoon:
But it's merely a dream.
Since I'm here, it had to have been a dream.
But the problem is…
I am dreaming that I am having fun killing people.

entries.japanese:
―――志貴くんはわたしと同じ
　目の前が、ぐらくらとスライドしていく。
―――人殺しが大好きでたまらない人なんだよ
　その、おかしくなるようなスピード。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Shiki, you’re the same as me
The world before me pitches and slides.
―――You love killing people more than anything
It moves fast enough to drive me mad.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---You and I are the same, Shiki-kun.
Before my eyes, the world starts spinning.
---Someone who can't resist the pleasure from killing.
And that crazy speed.

entries.japanese:
失礼します、と声をあげて翡翠が部屋に入ってきた。
「おはようございます。
今朝はもうお目覚めでいらしたんですね、志貴さま」
「………ああ。
おはよう、翡翠」
　スライドが収まる。
　自分が立っている角度から滑っていく錯覚は、翡翠の声のおかげで止まってくれた。
entries.maoEnglish:
Hisui announced herself and entered the room.
“Good morning, Master Shiki. You’re already awake this morning.”
“Yeah. Morning, Hisui.”
The sliding stops.
Her voice arrests the sickening illusion that the floor is slipping away beneath the angle of my body.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Excuse me," Hisui says as she enters the room.
"Good morning.
It seems that you have already awakened, Shiki-sama."
"……… Ah.
Morning, Hisui."
The world stops spinning.
As soon as Hisui spoke, the whirlpool I was trapped in disappeared like an illusion.

entries.japanese:
「……志貴さま？」
「え―――――なに、翡翠？」
「なに、ではありません。
お体の具合がよろしくないのですか？
　さきほどから何もおっしゃられません」
「……いや、ちょっと翡翠に見惚れてただけだ。
わかってる、学校に行かないとね。
すぐ居間に行くから、先に行っていてくれる？」
「志貴さま。
お体の具合がよろしくないようでしたら、どうか無理はなさらないでください。
学校も大事ですが、志貴さまのお体には代えられません」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki?”
“What is it, Hisui?”
“That is what I should be asking you. Are you unwell? You have not said a word since I came in.”
“No, I was just admiring you. I know, I have to get to school. I’ll be in the sitting room in a minute, so could you go on ahead?”
“Master Shiki. If you are feeling unwell, please do not overexert yourself. School is important, but not more important than Master Shiki’s health.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Shiki-sama?"
"Eh-----what is it, Hisui?"
"How are you feeling this morning?
You are not saying anything."

"…… Ah, sorry, I was just staring at you.
I understand; I have to go to school.
I'll go to the sitting room right away, so wait for me there."
"Shiki-sama.
If you are not feeling well, please do not push yourself.
Your health is more important than school."

entries.japanese:
「はは、やだな翡翠。
学校は休まないよ。
なんでもないんだから、あんまり甘やかさないでくれ」
「いえ、秋葉さまにはわたしのほうからお伝えいたしますから、どうかお休みください」
　翡翠は珍しく食い下がってくる。
　……そんな情けない顔をしているんだろうか、俺は。
「もう、翡翠ってわりと心配性だったんだな。
本当になんでもないんだから、気にしないでいいんだ。
　……ちょっと顔を洗っていくから、先に居間のほうに行っててくれ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Come on, Hisui. I’m not missing school. There’s nothing wrong with me, so don’t spoil me too much.”
“I’ll explain everything to Miss Akiha myself, so please remain in bed.”
Hisui presses the point with unusual determination.
Do I really look that pathetic?
“Honestly, Hisui, I never knew you worried this much; I’m fine, so you don’t have to fuss. I’m just going to wash my face. Go on to the sitting room without me.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Haha, no way, Hisui.
I can't skip school.
It's nothing---really.
So don't spoil me like that."
"No, please rest.
I will tell Akiha-sama so please rest."
Hisui is unusually persistent.
…… Does my face look that haggard?
"Hisui, you worry too much.
It really is nothing at all, so don't worry about it… I'll just wash my face, so please wait for me in the sitting room."

entries.japanese:
ベッドから出て、まだ何か言いたそうにしている翡翠の横を通りすぎる。
　部屋を出る時。
　不安そうにこっちを見つめる翡翠の視線が、少しだけ痛かった。
entries.maoEnglish:
I climb out of bed and pass Hisui, who still looks as though she wants to object.
As I leave the room.
The anxious gaze she fixes on my back hurts more than it should.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Getting out of bed, I walk past Hisui, who seems like she wants to say more.
Leaving the room,
it is a little painful seeing Hisui watch me with such uneasiness in her eyes.

entries.japanese:
脱衣場にいって、鏡を見る。
「……顔色は悪くないよな。
翡翠、どうしてあんなに不安そうな顔してたんだろ」
　バシャ、と冷たい水で顔を洗う。
―――昨夜の夢を思い返すと、たしかに吐き気がするし学校に行く気が失せていく。
　けどそんな事で学校を休めば、それこそ何かを認めるような気がして、不安だった。
entries.maoEnglish:
I go to the washroom and examine myself in the mirror.
“I don’t look pale. Why did Hisui seem so worried?”
I splash cold water over my face.
―――The memory of last night’s dream certainly makes me nauseous enough to lose all desire to go to school.
But staying home because of it would feel like admitting something, and that frightens me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I look in the mirror in the bathroom.
"…… I don't look like I'm sick.
Why is Hisui worrying so much?"
I splash cold water onto my face.
---Just thinking about the dream I had last night makes me want to puke and not go to school.
But if I stay home from school because of that, that will just be like confirming something, which makes me feel uneasy.

entries.japanese:
居間には秋葉と琥珀さん、翡翠がそろっていた。
　毎度のことながら、ここに入ってくる順番は俺が最後である。
entries.maoEnglish:
Akiha, Kohaku, and Hisui are all in the sitting room.
As usual, I’m the last one to arrive.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Akiha and Kohaku-san are in the sitting room, and Hisui is standing nearby.
As usual, I'm the last one to enter the room.

entries.japanese:
「あ、おはようございます志貴さん」
「うそ！？
　まだ六時半になったばかりじゃない！」
　柔らかな笑顔を向けてくれる琥珀さんと、失礼にもソファーから身を乗り出して俺を見る秋葉。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh, good morning, Shiki.”
“You can’t be serious! It’s only half past six!”
Kohaku greets me with her gentle smile, while Akiha has the poor manners to lean halfway off the sofa and stare.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah, good morning, Shiki-san."
"No way!?
It isn't even six-thirty yet!"
Kohaku-san looks towards me with a soft smile while Akiha gets up from the sofa and gapes at me in surprise.

entries.japanese:
「おはようございます琥珀さん。
ああ、ついでに秋葉もおはよう」
「む。
ついでにってなんですか、ついでにって」
「ついでにはついでにだよ。
日ごろから朝早く起きろー、なんて言っておきながら、いざ早起きしたら驚くようなヤツなんかそれで十分だ」
「――――フン。
たまに早起きしてきたからって、鬼の首でもとったような勢いですね、兄さんは」
「鬼の首って、秋葉―――」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Good morning, Kohaku. Oh, and morning to you too, Akiha.”
“Excuse me? What do you mean, ‘you too’?”
“Exactly what it sounds like. You’re always telling me to get up earlier, then acting astonished when I do; ‘you too’ is plenty for someone like that.”
“Hmph. You get up early once and act as proud as if you’d taken an ogre’s head.”
“An ogre’s head, Akiha―――”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Good morning, Kohaku-san, oh, and Akiha too."
"Wha… What do you mean, 'Akiha too?'"
"Well, 'Akiha too' means 'Akiha too'.
That should be enough for someone who's so surprised to see me get up early when you tell me to get up early every day."
"----I see.
Nii-san, you wake up early for once and now you triumphantly walk around with your head held high."
"Head held high, Akiha---"

entries.japanese:
首。
　首……？
　ぞわり、と夢の中の感触を思い出して、吐き気がしてきた。
entries.maoEnglish:
A neck.
A neck…?
The sensation from my dream crawls back through me, and nausea rises in my throat.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Head.
Neck.
Neck……?
I remember the sensations from my dream and feel like vomiting.

entries.japanese:
「……ごめん、琥珀さん。
悪いんだけど、ごはんの前に冷たい飲み物でももらえない？」
「はい、炭酸ものと果汁もの、どちらがよろしいですか？」
「えーっと、炭酸ものでお願いします」
「はい、かしこまりました」
　琥珀さんはパタパタと台所に向かっていく。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Sorry, Kohaku. Could I have something cold to drink before breakfast?”
“Would you prefer something carbonated or fruit juice?”
“Um, carbonated, please.”
“Right away.”
Kohaku hurries off to the kitchen.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Sorry, Kohaku-san.
I don't mean to be a bother, but could you get me something cold to drink before I eat?"
"Not at all.
Would you like soda or fruit juice?"
"Ummm, I'll have a soda please."
"Coming right up."
Kohaku-san disappears towards the kitchen.

entries.japanese:
「……兄さん？
　どうしたんですか、言い返しもしないで大人しくなるなんて。
もしかして、どこか具合でも悪いの？」
「……まったく。
翡翠といい秋葉といい、俺のことをなんだと思ってるんだ。
ただ起きたばっかりで喉が渇いているだけなんだから、体のほうに問題なんかないっ……！」
　自分の中の吐き気を否定するように、ただ、反射的に怒鳴ってしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Brother? What’s wrong? You never go quiet without answering back; are you feeling ill?”
“Honestly. What do you and Hisui think I am? I only just woke up and my throat is dry; there’s nothing wrong with me!”
I shout without thinking, as though the force of my denial could drive out the nausea.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Nii-san?
You're not arguing back.
Are you feeling alright?"
"…… Geez.
You and even Hisui, what do you think I am?
I just woke up early and my throat is dry, there isn't anything wrong with me…!"
Trying to resist the urge to vomit, I shout back.

entries.japanese:
「……ごめんなさい、兄さん。
確かにあまり気分のいいものではありませんよね、いちいち気を遣われるのは」
「あ―――いや、そういう事じゃない。
その、心配してくれるのはすごく嬉しいんだ。
ただちょっと、今日は夢見が悪くて苛々してた。
　……ごめんな秋葉。
謝るのは俺のほうだ」
　ソファーに腰を下ろす。
　自分でもどうかしているとわかっているけど、こればっかりはどうしようもなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’m sorry, Brother. I suppose being fussed over at every turn cannot be pleasant.”
“Ah―――no, that’s not it. I’m glad you’re worried about me. I just had a bad dream and woke up irritable.
I’m sorry, Akiha. I’m the one who should apologize.”
I sit down on the sofa.
I know I’m behaving strangely, but knowing does nothing to stop it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I'm sorry, Nii-san.
But there is obviously something wrong, and I want to help."
"Ah---no, that's not it.
The fact that you're worried about me makes me really happy.
I just had a really bad nightmare last night and my mind is elsewhere, that's all.
…… I'm sorry, Akiha.
I'm the one who should apologize."
I sit down on the sofa.
I know that something's wrong with me, but I can't do anything about it.

entries.japanese:
「兄さん、なにか悩み事でもあるんですか？
　この屋敷に関する事でしたら、相談していただければ少しは力になれると思いますけど……」
「いや、別に家に慣れてないとかそういう問題じゃないんだけど―――」
　……そうだな。
　例え話で秋葉に相談してみるのも気分転換になるかもしれない。
　ここは―――
entries.maoEnglish:
“Is something troubling you, Brother? If it concerns life in this house, perhaps I can help if you tell me.”
“No, it isn’t that I’m having trouble settling in, but…”
Maybe so.
Perhaps asking Akiha through a hypothetical would help clear my head.
So I should—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Nii-san, is there something bothering you?
If it's something to do with this mansion, please tell me, and I'm sure I can be of help…"
"No, it isn't that I'm not used to living here---"
…… That's right.
Maybe if I ask her indirectly, it might help me feel better.
I decide to---

entries.japanese:
しないよりはしたほうがいいに決まっている。
　だいたい自分一人で悩みを抱えているから、よけい暗く考えてしまうんだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
Of course it’s better to ask than not.
Keeping everything bottled up only drives my thoughts into darker places.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I decide that it's better to do it than not.
Besides, I keep on thinking for the worst since I'm keeping this to myself.

entries.japanese:
「……じゃあ聞くけど。
例えばさ、自分がやってはいけないって思う事をやってしまう、なんていうのはストレスのせいなのかな」
「自分がしてはいけないと思うこと、ですか。
それは慢性的なものでしょうか、それとも突発的なものでしょうか」
「……そうだな、突発的なものなんじゃないかな。
本人はあんまり意識していないみたいだから」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Then let me ask you this. Could stress cause someone to do things they know they shouldn’t?”
“Things they believe they shouldn’t do? Is this an ongoing pattern, or does it happen in sudden episodes?”
“I’d say sudden. The person doesn’t seem especially conscious of it.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Well, then let me ask you a question.
If someone does things they know they shouldn't do, would that be a result of stress?"
"Doing something they know they shouldn't do?
Is it a recurring problem or just an accident?"
"…… Well, it's more like an accident.
It seems that the person really isn't that conscious."

entries.japanese:
「意識していないでその行動をしてしまう、という事は本人の意思でその『してはいけないこと』を止める事はできないんですね？」
「―――そう、止められない。
止めるっていう考えさえ浮かばなくなる」
「だとすると、その人は性格が一時的に反転しているとしか思えませんね」
「……性格が反転するって……裏返るっていうこと？」
「ええ。
何かのきっかけでその人の道徳観念というか、物の優先度という天秤が逆になってしまうんです」
entries.maoEnglish:
“If they act without being conscious of it, then they can’t stop themselves by force of will?”
“―――Right. They can’t stop; the very idea of stopping no longer occurs to them.”
“Then I can only think their character is being temporarily inverted.”
“Inverted—you mean turned inside out?”
“Yes. Something triggers it and reverses their moral compass—the balance by which they decide what matters most.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"So you mean they're doing things while unconscious, so they can't stop themselves from doing it?"
"---That's right, they can't stop.
They can't even get themselves to think about stopping."
"In that case, it sounds like a personality inversion."
"…… Personality inversion…… you mean their personality gets reversed?"
"Yes.
For whatever reason, something triggers a change in the person and their entire moral spectrum, their whole attitude gets reversed."

entries.japanese:
「それは心の病、とも言えるものかもしれない。
　ほら兄さん、覚えてない？
　お父さまは優しい方でしたが、ときおり人が変わったように冷たくなってしまっていた事を」
「親父が―――？」
　……言われてみれば……たしかに、遠野槙久は極端に優しかったり、極端に厳しかったりしていた気がする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“It may be a kind of mental illness. Don’t you remember, Brother?
Father was a kind man, but there were times when he suddenly turned cold, almost as if he had become someone else.”
“Father did—?”
Now that she mentions it, Makihisa Tohno did seem to swing between extraordinary kindness and extraordinary severity.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"It may be termed a disease of the mind.
Don't you remember, Nii-san?
Father was usually a very kind person, but sometimes he would just turn cold as ice."
"The old man was---?"
…… Come to think of it…… Tohno Makihisa was extremely kind one day and extremely strict the next.

entries.japanese:
「……よく覚えてないな。
翡翠は覚えてる？」
　壁際の翡翠を見る。
―――と。
　翡翠は、何かに耐えるように俯いて、俺の声が聞こえていないようだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I don’t remember very well. Do you, Hisui?”
I look toward Hisui, standing by the wall.
―――And then.
Hisui has bowed her head as if enduring some private agony and does not appear to have heard me at all.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I don't remember that well.
Do you remember, Hisui?"
I look at Hisui, who is standing by the wall.
---And.
It looks like Hisui is trying to contain herself and can't hear my voice.

entries.japanese:
「秋葉さま、あんまり極端なお話はしないでください。
槙久さまは躁鬱の気が激しかっただけですよ」
　と、琥珀さんが銀のトレイにグラスを乗せてやってきた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Miss Akiha, you shouldn’t make it sound so dramatic. Master Makihisa simply had severe mood swings, that’s all.”
Kohaku enters carrying glasses on a silver tray.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Akiha-sama, please don't talk about any of that.
Makihisa-sama was just a little manic-depressive, that's all."
Kohaku-san says this as she brings a silver tray with a glass on it.

entries.japanese:
「だめですよ、秋葉さま。
亡くなられた方のことを悪く言っては。
そうでなくても槙久さまは秋葉さまのお父上なんですから」
「わ、わかってます……！
　あなたに言われるまでもありません……！」
　翡翠に続いて秋葉まで押し黙ってしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“That won’t do, Miss Akiha. You mustn’t speak badly of the dead. After all, Master Makihisa was Miss Akiha’s father.”
“I-I know that…! I don’t need you to tell me…!”
Now Akiha falls silent as well, joining Hisui.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"You shouldn't say bad things about those who have departed.
And besides, Makihisa-sama is your father, too."
"I, I know……!
I don't need you to tell me that……!"
Akiha joins Hisui in silence.

entries.japanese:
「はい志貴さん、お待たせしました」
　レモンスカッシュをそそいだグラスをテーブルに置く琥珀さん。
「どうも、いただきます」
　ストローをさして、冷たい液体を飲み込む。
　……それきり、翡翠と秋葉が口をひらく事はなかった。
　朝の居間で元気なのは琥珀さんだけ。
　……暗くなってしまった理由こそ分からないものの、親父の話が原因だという事だけは、はっきりと実感できた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Here you are, Master Shiki—sorry to keep you waiting.”
Kohaku sets a glass of lemon soda on the table.
“Thanks.”
I slip in the straw and swallow the cold drink.
After that, neither Hisui nor Akiha speaks again.
Kohaku alone remains cheerful in the morning sitting room.
I may not understand why the mood has turned so grim, but I can feel with absolute certainty that talking about Father caused it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Here you go, Shiki-san.
Thanks for waiting."
Kohaku-san puts the glass of Lemon Squash onto the table.
"Thanks."
Using a straw, I let the cool drink fill my body.
…… The rest of the time, Akiha and Hisui never open their mouths.
The only cheerful one in the sitting room is Kohaku-san.
…… I don't understand why everyone became so depressed, but the old man is definitely connected to it.

entries.japanese:
「それでは行ってらっしゃいませ、志貴さま」
「ああ、行ってくるけど……翡翠」
「……はい、なんでしょうか志貴さま」
「さっきの話。
親父のことが出たとたん、翡翠は黙りこんだだろ。
翡翠だけじゃなくて、自分から話しておいて秋葉も黙り込んじまった」
「なあ。
俺がいなかった八年の間、親父に何かあったのか？
　さっきの翡翠と秋葉は普通じゃなかっただろ」
「……………………」
　翡翠は答えない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Have a safe day, Master Shiki.”
“Right―――I’m off, but―――Hisui”
“Yes―――what is it, Master Shiki?”
“About what happened earlier. The moment Father came up, you stopped talking. And it wasn’t only you—Akiha brought him up herself, then went silent too.”
“Listen. Did something happen to Father during the eight years I was gone? Neither you nor Akiha was acting normally.”
“…”
Hisui gives no answer.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Please be careful on your way, Shiki-sama."
"Ah, I'll be going…… Hisui?"
"…… Yes, what is it, Shiki-sama?"
"When we were talking earlier, about my old man.
You were deathly quiet.
Not just you, but Akiha as well."
"Did something happen to that old man in the eight years I was gone?
You and Akiha were both acting strange earlier."
"……………………"
Hisui doesn't answer.

entries.japanese:
「……そっか。
ま、無理に聞こうとは思わないよ。
機会があったら話してくれ」
「―――いえ。
あれは志貴さまには関係のない事です。
「志貴さま。
これからこのお屋敷で暮らすのなら、二度と槙久さまの事は口にしないでください」
　一瞬、火のような目をして、翡翠は屋敷へと戻っていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I see. I won’t force you. Tell me someday, if the chance comes.”
“―――No. It has nothing to do with Master Shiki.
“Master Shiki. If you intend to go on living in this house, never speak of Master Makihisa again.”
For one instant, Hisui’s eyes blaze like fire as she turns and goes back inside.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I see.
Well, I won't force you to answer.
If you ever feel like it, we can talk about it."
"---No.
This is not something that concerns you, Shiki-sama.
"Shiki-sama, if you are going to live in this mansion, please do not ever mention Makihisa-sama again."
After Hisui's eyes flash for a brief instant, she heads back to the mansion.

entries.japanese:
―――いや、いたずらに秋葉たちを不安にさせる事はできない。
　この事は―――あの夢のことは、俺だけで解決すべき問題だ。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――No—I cannot frighten Akiha and the others for no reason.
This—the matter of that dream—is something I have to resolve alone.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---No, I really shouldn't make Akiha and the others worry about any of this.
This problem---that dream, I should take care of it myself.

entries.japanese:
「―――ちょっと、ここのところ学校のほうが忙しいんだ。
十一月になれば学園祭だし、その前には体育祭もあるしね」
「……そうですか。
学校の事で悩んでいるのなら、たしかに私では相談には乗れませんね」
　どこか残念そうに秋葉は視線を下げる。
　……秋葉に嘘をついて誤魔化すのは、正直心苦しかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“School has just been keeping me busy lately. The school festival is in November, and we have the athletics festival before that.”
“I see. If it’s a school problem, then I suppose I really can’t offer much advice.”
Akiha lowers her eyes, looking faintly disappointed.
Lying to her and hiding behind an excuse honestly makes me feel wretched.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---It's just that things at school are keeping me busy.
In November, there's the school festival, and before that, the athletic festival."
"…… Is that so?
Since it's a school problem, then there isn't really anything I can do to help, I suppose."
Akiha lowers her gaze, a little disappointed.
…… Deceiving Akiha by telling her a lie is very painful.

entries.japanese:
「はい志貴さん、お待たせしましたー」
　トレイにグラスをのせて琥珀さんがやってくる。
「どうも、いただきます」
　ストローをさして、琥珀さんが用意してくれたレモンスカッシュを飲み下す。
　……それで、なんとなく会話が途絶えてしまった。
　朝の居間で元気なのは琥珀さんだけで、結局そのままいつも通りの朝食を済ませる事になった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Here you are, Master Shiki—sorry to keep you waiting.”
Kohaku arrives with a glass on her tray.
“Thanks.”
I slip in the straw and drink the lemon soda she prepared.
Somehow, the conversation dies there.
Kohaku is the only cheerful person in the morning sitting room, and in the end we finish breakfast much as usual.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Here you go, Shiki-san.
Thanks for waiting."
Kohaku-san comes carrying a glass on a tray.
"Thanks."
Using a straw, I drink the Lemon Squash that Kohaku-san got for me.
…… With that, the conversation ends.
The only cheerful one in the sitting room is Kohaku-san, and I end up eating breakfast like always.

entries.japanese:
翡翠に見送られて門までやってくる。
　さっきの居間での沈黙がまだ続いていて、なんとなく居心地が悪い。
「それでは行ってらっしゃいませ、志貴さま」
「ああ、行ってくるけど……翡翠」
「はい、なんでしょうか志貴さま」
　まっすぐに見つめてくる翡翠。
―――どうしてだろう。
　その、俺を信じきった目を前にすると、ひどく自分が邪なものに思えてしまって、落ち着かない。
entries.maoEnglish:
Hisui sees me as far as the gate.
The silence from the sitting room seems to have followed us, leaving the air awkward and uncomfortable.
“Have a safe day, Master Shiki.”
“Right―――I’m off, but―――Hisui”
“Yes―――what is it, Master Shiki?”
Hisui looks directly into my eyes.
―――Why is it?
Faced with eyes so utterly trusting, I feel horribly unclean and cannot settle down.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Hisui walks with me to the gate to see me off.
Just like before in the sitting room, Hisui continues her silence, which makes me uneasy.
"Please take care on your way, Shiki-sama."
"Yeah, I'll be on my way…… Hisui?"
"Yes, what is it, Shiki-sama?"
Hisui looks at me directly.
---Why is it?
Being stared at by those pure eyes, I get this uncomfortable feeling, like I was very dirty.

entries.japanese:
「……なんでもない。
くれぐれも留守中は気をつけてくれ」
　胸の中の不安をそのまま言葉にして、逃げるように屋敷に背を向けた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Never mind. Just be careful while I’m gone.”
I put the fear in my heart into those words, then turn my back on the mansion as though fleeing.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… It's nothing.
Just be careful at home."
With a deep uneasiness in my chest, I leave the mansion.

entries.japanese:
―――昼休みになった。
　有彦はいつものように学校を休んでいる。
「……学食にいくか」
　一人で昼飯を食べても塞ぎこむだけだ。
　生徒たちでごったがえしている食堂に行けば、よけいなことを考えなくてもすむだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Lunchtime arrives.
Arihiko is absent from school, as usual.
“Maybe I’ll go to the cafeteria.”
Eating alone would only leave me brooding.
In a dining hall packed with students, I shouldn’t have room to think about anything unnecessary.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---It's lunch time.
As usual, Arihiko is skipping school.
"…… I'll go eat at the cafeteria."
If I eat by myself, I'll just end up being depressed.
If I go eat in the cafeteria full of people, it should help me get my mind off of things.

entries.japanese:
予想通り、食堂は派手に賑わっていた。
　何十人という行列に並んで、手堅いＡ定食を買ってテーブルにつく。
　生徒たちの話し声がやかましいおかげで、とりあえず食事に専念できた。
　黙々とフォークを動かして栄養を摂取する。
――――と。
　一瞬、なにかイヤな映像が見えた。
entries.maoEnglish:

entries.maoEnglish:
“Something on television…?”
A memory of a television screen flashes through my mind.
The school records the morning news and plays it here at lunchtime, and something in the broadcast must have caught my eye.
“――――No.”
The report leaves me stunned.
The screen shows the same back alley I saw in yesterday’s dream.
A newscaster is speaking.
Across the picture, huge letters the color of blood read: VAMPIRE MURDERS—NINTH VICTIM.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… The television screen……"
I gape at the large television mounted on the wall at the end of the cafeteria.
At my school, they record the morning news and replay it at lunch.
My eyes fixate on what is playing.
"----No way…"
I watch the news in amazed horror.
Shown on the television is the alley that I saw last night in my dream.
The newscaster is talking.
On the screen, the words "Vampire Serial Killer's Ninth Victim" appear in bloody lettering.

entries.maoEnglish:

“――――――”
I feel consciousness slipping away.
“Why…?”
It was a dream. I know it was a dream.
Yet the same person has been murdered in the same place, in exactly the same way.
entries.mirrorMoon:

“Father’s room is still just as he left it…”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……… Ah."
Come to think of it, Akiha said something like that earlier.
That was about---my old man would have extreme personality shifts…… it sounds almost like me right now.
…… Of course, like father, like son.
It might even be hereditary.
"My old man's room… I think they still keep it like before…"

entries.japanese:
親父の部屋は当時のままだ。
　並べられた書籍はその大部分が学術書で、これといって興味を引くものはない。
　今の自分がほしいものは親父の日記や手記だ。
　几帳面だった親父のことだから、まず間違いなくそういった類のものを遺していると思うんだけど―――
「……さすがに目の届く場所には見あたらないか」
　あるとしたら鍵のかかった所か。
　机の引き出しあたりを、とりあえず見てみよう。
entries.maoEnglish:
Dad’s room was exactly as he had left it.
Most of the shelves were filled with academic texts, none of which interested me.
What I wanted was a diary or personal journal.
Dad had been meticulous, so I felt certain he must have left something of the kind―――
“Nothing in plain sight, naturally.” If it existed, it would be somewhere locked.
I decided to try the desk drawers first.
entries.mirrorMoon:
My old man's room is just like it always was.
Nearly all of the rows of books are educational reports, and nothing catches my attention.
What I want right now is my old man's journal or notes.
The old man was extremely methodical.
There certainly has to be something like that lying around here somewhere---
"…… Of course, they're not just lying about where anyone can see them."
Maybe they're locked away somewhere.
I should probably look in these desk drawers first.

entries.japanese:
親父の机にあったペーパーナイフを使って、引き出しの鍵の『線』を切る。
　机の中には紙を紐で束ねた古い記録書と、手記らしい本だった。
entries.maoEnglish:
Using the letter opener from Dad’s desk, I cut the lock’s line.
Inside the drawer lay old records bundled with string and a book that appeared to be a journal.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Using a letter opener lying on the desk, I cut the "line" of the drawer lock.
Inside, there appears to be some old documents bundled together and what seems to be a journal.

entries.japanese:
まず古い記録書に目を通す。
「……これ、うちの家系図かな」
　間違いない。
　遠野マキヒサの後には遠野シキ、遠野アキハという名前がある。
「え……親父のヤツ、十年前に養子をとってる。
……あ、けどすぐに病死してるのか」
　十年前っていえば、俺が小学一年生の頃だ。
　そんな大昔のことなら、覚えていないのも当然か。
entries.maoEnglish:
I examined the records first.
“Is this our family tree?”
There was no mistaking it.
Beneath Makihisa Tohno were the names SHIKI Tohno and Akiha Tohno.
“What, Dad adopted a child ten years ago…? But the child died of an illness almost immediately.”
Ten years ago, I had been in first grade.
It was so long ago that forgetting was hardly surprising.
entries.mirrorMoon:
First, I'll look at the old documents.
"…… This is… my family tree?"
Definitely.
Right after Tohno MAKIHISA is written Tohno SHIKI and Tohno AKIHA.
"Huh…… my old man, he adopted a son ten years ago?
…… Ah, but he passed away shortly thereafter."
Ten years ago; that would be when I was just in elementary school.
That long ago, it's only natural I wouldn't remember.

entries.japanese:
「ふうん……うちの当主ってわりと短命なんだな。
　親父も五十前に病死してるし、その前は三十歳の時に事故死、か。
……その前は十八歳で、自殺してる―――」
――――いや、待て。
　いくらなんでも、これは、おかしい。
　しっかりと家系図に目を通すと、遠野家の人間はみな異状な死に方をしていた。
　発狂死。
事故死。
他殺。
行方不明。
死産。
　……誰一人として、寿命で静かに他界したものがいない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Huh, the heads of our family tended to die young. Dad died of illness before fifty. His predecessor died in an accident at thirty, while the one before that committed suicide at eighteen―――”
――――No, wait.
This is far too strange.
Reading the family tree more carefully, I saw that every Tohno had met an unnatural end.
Death by madness. Accidents. Murder. Disappearances. Stillbirths.
Not one had died peacefully of old age.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"But, the heads of the household have had pretty short lifespans.
My old man died before he was fifty, and before that, before thirty in an accident…… Wow, before that, eighteen years of age, suicide…!?"
----No, wait a second.
No matter how you look at it, this is strange.
Looking through the family tree, all members of the Tohno household have died strangely.
Madness.
Accidents.
Murder.
Disappearances.
Stillbirth.
…… Not one of them lived a long life or even died peacefully.

entries.japanese:
「な…………」
　その一連の記録は、呪われてるとしかいいようのない。
　とくに、その大半の死因は発狂。
　遠野の人間は、その大部分が自らの命を断つことで他界してしまっている。
「おかしい―――おかしいぞ、これ」
　だが、一体なにがおかしいのかが解らない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What…?”
The record could only be called cursed.
Most of the deaths had followed madness.
Generation after generation of Tohnos had ended their own lives.
“This is wrong―――something is terribly wrong.”
Yet I couldn’t say exactly what.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Wha…………"
This entire document is filled with horrible fates.
Even worse, most of the causes of death are madness.
Most of them ended up taking their own lives.
"That's strange---it's just strange."
But I can't exactly tell what's strange about it.

entries.japanese:
「……あとは……親父の手記か」
　わりと新しい装丁をした手記を手にとる。
――――どくん。
　鼓動が響く。
　この中身を見てはいけないと、心のどこかで悟っている。
　けど、いまさら戻れない。
　ごくりと唾を飲みこんで、親父の手記を開いた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“That leaves Dad’s journal.”
I picked up the comparatively new-looking volume.
――――Thump.
My heartbeat echoed through me.
Some part of me understood that I must not read what was inside.
But it was too late to turn back.
I swallowed hard and opened Dad’s journal.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Next is…… my old man's journal."
I pick up the journal, which has a relatively new binding.
----Thump.
My heart starts to pound.
My heart seems to understand that I shouldn't be opening this.
But I can't turn back now.
Swallowing hard, I open my old man's journal.

entries.japanese:
――――――遠野の血筋には魔が宿る。
!w1500
entries.maoEnglish: ――――――A demon dwells in the blood of the Tohnos.!w1500
entries.mirrorMoon: ------There is a demon lurking inside the Tohno bloodline.

entries.japanese:
書き出し文は、そういった類のものだった。
　それは、比喩ではない。
　遠野の祖先は本当に『人間でないモノ』との混血で、子孫にあたる自分たちにも、その『人間でないモノ』の血が混ざっている、という事だった。
entries.maoEnglish:
That was how the account began.
It was not a metaphor.
The ancestors of the Tohno family had truly been born of unions with nonhuman beings, and their descendants still carried that inhuman blood.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The opening statement is in those lines.
And that isn't just a simple metaphor.
The ancestors of the Tohno were a mixed breed of "something nonhuman" and human.
We, being their descendants, also have this element of "something nonhuman" in our blood.

entries.japanese:
血は。
　濃い者と薄い者に分かれる。
　血が薄い者なら普通の人間として問題なく暮らしていけるが、濃い者であるのなら、人間として生きていく事はできない。
　遠野の血が濃い者は、すべからく特別な力を身体に宿して生まれてくる。
　それは死ににくい体であったり、
　手を使わず物を動かす力であったり、
　他人から体液を搾取する牙であったりした。
entries.maoEnglish:
In some, the blood ran thick.
In others, thin.
Those with thin blood could live without difficulty as ordinary humans; those with thick blood could not live as human beings at all.
All those in whom the Tohno blood ran thick were born with some extraordinary power.
A body that resisted death
The power to move objects without touching them
Fangs that drained bodily fluids from others.
entries.mirrorMoon:
In regards to our blood…
There are those with strong and those with weak nonhuman blood.
Those with weak nonhuman blood can live their lives as ordinary people, but those with strong nonhuman blood can never live a normal life.
Those with strong Tohno blood are born with special powers.
It could be a body that is resistant to death,
it could be an ability to move things without touching them,
or it could be fangs used to take bodily fluids from other people.

entries.japanese:
この血。
　この血が濃く現れだした遠野の人間は、段々と理性を失っていく。
　そうして理性を失ってしまった遠野の人間はその大部分が人を食う悪鬼になりはてる。
　故に、遠野の当主は、そうなってしまった同族を処罰する責任があるという。
entries.maoEnglish:
That blood.
When it began to manifest strongly in a Tohno, the person gradually lost all reason.
Most Tohnos who succumbed became man-eating demons.
It was therefore the family head’s duty to execute any relative who suffered that fate.
entries.mirrorMoon:
This blood.
When this blood becomes too strong, the members of the Tohno House start to gradually lose their sanity.
And the majority of the members of the Tohno House that lose their sanity become demons that feed on human flesh.
So, the head of the Tohno household carries the responsibility of punishing those who have turned into such monsters.

entries.japanese:
「――――――――は」
　……どうかしてる。
　親父は、なにを。
　夢物語みたいなことを、こんなに真面目に書き記しているんだろうか。
　手記は、いつのまにか親父の語りに移り変わっていた。
　日付はおよそ九年前。
　手記には乱れた文字が続いている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――――――Hah”
This was madness.
What had Dad been thinking.
Why had he recorded this fantasy with such grave sincerity?
At some point, the journal shifted into Dad’s own personal account.
The entry is dated roughly nine years ago.
The handwriting that follows is erratic.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"--------Ha."
…… It's messed up.
My old man, what was he trying to say?
Writing so seriously about something that's more like a fairy tale.
The journal turns more into the old man's rant.
The date is roughly nine years ago.
The handwriting starts to get erratic.

entries.japanese:
……ついに自分の血の昂ぶりが抑えられなくなってきた。
　共感者の一族の孤児を手に入れ、自らの意志を強化したところで、それもいずれは効かなくなるだろう。
私が私でいられる時間は、あと僅かなものかもしれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
At last, I can no longer suppress the fever in my blood.
I acquired an orphan from a family of empaths and used the child to reinforce my will, but in time even that will cease to work. Little time may remain in which I can still be myself.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… I am no longer able to suppress my raging blood.
I was able to obtain an orphan from a family of Synchronizers, so this should help me strengthen my mind.
However, it really is only a matter of time before I go insane.

entries.japanese:
……恐ろしくなる。
　気がつけば、一日の半分がまったく記憶にない。
　私は、私の知らないところで、自身の反転している衝動をあの子供に押し付けてしまっている。
　このままでは。
　いずれ完全に理性をなくして、ただのケモノに成り果てるだろう。
　私が私としていられる時間はあとどれほど残っているのか。
entries.maoEnglish:
I am terrified.
Half of each day has vanished entirely from my memory.
Without even knowing it, I am forcing the impulses born of my inversion upon that child.
If this continues.
I will eventually lose all reason and become nothing but a beast.
How much longer can I remain myself?
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… It is terrifying.
When I come to, I find that I can't even remember half of the day.
During that time, I'm forcing my inversion impulse on that child.
If this keeps up,
it is only a matter of time before I completely lose my sanity and turn into a beast.
I don't even know how much time I have left to remain as myself.

entries.japanese:
いや、あの子供がいればあと数年は保つだろう。
　だがあの子供のほうは私の行為に耐えきれまい。
　おそらく、あの子供が壊れた後、私は自らの手で自分の命を絶たなければなるまい。
　だがそれまでは―――私は子供たちを守らなければならない。
　アキハの血は薄い。
アキハは自分から望まないかぎり、私のようにはならないだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
With that child, I may endure for several more years.
But the child cannot withstand what I am doing. Once the child breaks, I will most likely have to end my life with my own hands.
Until then―――I must protect my children.
Akiha’s blood is thin. Unless she desires it herself, she will never become what I am.
entries.mirrorMoon:
No.
If that child is here, then I can probably last for a few more years.
But that child will not be able to bear that.
After that child breaks, I will have to take my own life.
But until then---I must protect my children.
Akiha's blood is weak.
Unless she wishes it herself, she does not have to suffer the same fate.

entries.japanese:
問題はシキだ。
　あの子は、私にひどく近い。
　せめてあの子だけには、私と同じ苦しみを味わわせたくはない。
　……遠野の血が異状な血だというのなら、あの子を遠野という名前から遠ざけて、様子を見るしかないだろう―――――
entries.maoEnglish:
The problem is SHIKI.
That child resembles me too closely.
I want to spare him, at least, from suffering as I have.
If the Tohno blood itself is the cause, I have no choice but to remove him from the Tohno name and observe what follows―――――
entries.mirrorMoon:
The real problem is SHIKI.
That child is incredibly close to me.
More than anything, I do not want that child to suffer my fate.
…… If the Tohno blood is unnatural, I need to distance him as much as possible from the Tohno name and see how he will fare-----

entries.japanese:
「―――――――――」
　読み終わって、愕然とした。
　親父の手記の内容は、あまりに非現実すぎていて、気味が悪い。
　親父は躁鬱が激しかったわけじゃない。
　ただ、自分でも分からないうちに凶暴になっていただけだ。
　今の―――遠野志貴と同じように。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――――――――”
When I finished, I could only stare.
Dad’s journal was so grotesquely unreal that it left me sick with unease.
Dad had not suffered violent swings between mania and depression.
He had simply become savage without realizing it.
Just like―――Shiki Tohno now.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---------"
I finish reading in a state of horror and amazement.
The contents of my old man's journal are so far away from reality that it's outright bizarre.
My old man didn't just have manic-depression.
Rather, he just became violent without his knowing.
Just like Tohno Shiki right now.

entries.japanese:
「……いや」
　違うか。
　親父が俺と同じなんじゃない。
　俺が、親父と同じなんだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“No.”
That was backward.
Dad wasn’t like me.
I was like Dad.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… No."
That's wrong.
That old man isn't like me.
I'm like him.

entries.japanese:
それを恐れて親父は俺を屋敷から出した。
　けど俺は屋敷に戻ってきて、今まで眠っていた遠野の血とやらが目覚めてしまったとでもいうのか。
「はっ……バカげてる、そんな話」
　笑おうとして、笑い声さえあげられなかった。
　遠野の人間には人間ではない血が混ざっている。
　遠野の人間には特別な力がある。
　……それが、もう笑いとばせない。
　人と違う力。
そんなバカげた力なら、俺は八年も前から持ってしまっている。
　モノの死が視えるなんていう、この異状な眼。
entries.maoEnglish:
That fear was why he had sent me away.
Had returning to the mansion awakened this Tohno blood that had lain dormant inside me?
“Hah, what a ridiculous story.”
I tried to laugh, but no sound came.
The Tohnos carried inhuman blood.
The Tohnos possessed unnatural powers.
I could no longer laugh those claims away.
An inhuman power. I have had such an absurd power for eight years.
These abnormal eyes that can see the death of things.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Fearing that, he sent me from the mansion.
But now I've returned, and my sleeping blood has awoken.
"Heh…… nonsense, all of this."
I try to laugh but find myself unable to laugh it off.
The Tohno blood is mixed with the blood of something nonhuman.
Those of the Tohno blood have special powers.
…… I can't laugh it off.
Supernatural power.
I've been carrying that for eight years.
Being able to perceive the death of things, my unnatural eyes.

entries.japanese:
「ぐ………………………」
――――――吐き気がする。
　とてもじゃないけど立っていられない。
　早く。
　早く部屋に戻って眠らないと、頭がどうにかしてしまいそうだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ghh…”
――――――Nausea surged through me.
I could barely remain standing.
Quickly.
I had to return to my room and sleep before my mind came apart.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"G………………………"
------I feel like vomiting.
I can't stay standing up.
Hurry.
I must hurry back to my room and sleep; it feels like there is something wrong with my head.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま、お帰りになられているのですか？」
　……翡翠みたいな声が聞こえる。
「志貴さま、失礼します」
　……翡翠が部屋に入ってきた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki, have you returned?”
I could hear what sounded like Hisui’s voice.
“Master Shiki, may I come in?”
Hisui entered the room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama, you have returned already?"
…… I can hear a voice that sounds like Hisui.
"Shiki-sama, please excuse me."
…… Hisui enters my room.

entries.japanese:
「申し訳ございません。
志貴さまがお帰りなっていた事に気付かず、お出迎えが遅れてしまいました」
「……いや、いいんだ。
俺のほうがかってに早く帰ってきたんだから。
それより翡翠、悪いんだけどしばらく一人にしてくれないか。
今は人と話せる気分じゃないんだ」
「志貴さま、お気分が優れないのですか……？」
「―――さあ。
自分でもよく解らない」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Please forgive me. I failed to notice that Master Shiki had returned and was late in greeting you.”
“It’s all right. I came home early without warning. Hisui, I’m sorry, but could you leave me alone for a while? I don’t feel up to talking to anyone.”
“Are you feeling unwell, Master Shiki?”
“―――I don’t know. I can’t even tell anymore.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Please forgive me.
I did not realize that you had returned, so I was unable to greet you at the door."
"…… Don't worry about it.
I came early on my own.
Hisui, can you leave me alone?
I just don't feel like talking to anyone."
"Shiki-sama, are you feeling sick…?"
"---I don't know.
I don't understand it myself."

entries.japanese:
「…………………」
　翡翠はこっちの体を気遣うような目を向けてくる。
　……くそ、俺は何をしているんだろう。
　翡翠は俺の心配をしてくれているのに、翡翠にヤツ当たりしても仕方がないだろう……！
entries.maoEnglish:
“……”
Hisui studied me with concern.
Damn it, what was I doing?
She was worried about me; taking my anger out on her accomplished nothing.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…………………"
Hisui looks at me with worried eyes.
…… Damn it, what am I doing?
Hisui is worrying about me; there's no reason to take it out on her……!

entries.japanese:
「……ごめん。
たしかに体調が悪いんだ。
その、夕食まで眠りたいんだけど、何か薬とかあるかな。
頭痛薬があれば一番いいんだけど」
「はい、それではお持ちしいたします」
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’m sorry. I really am unwell. I’d like to sleep until dinner, so do we have any medicine? Something for the headache would be best.”
“Certainly, I will bring it at once.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Sorry, I just feel a bit bad.
I want to sleep until dinner; is there some medicine I can take?
Headache medicine would be the best."
"Yes, I will go get some."

entries.japanese:
「お待たせいたしました。
どうぞ、お飲みください」
「ありがとう。
いつもすまない」
　翡翠の持ってきてくれた水と、粉末薬の入った包みを手に取る。
　包みはなぜか二つあった。
「あれ、二つあるんだけど、これってなに？」
「はい、姉に志貴さまの具合が悪いと相談したところ、志貴さまの主治医から指示されていた安定剤を分けていただきました。
　そちらの包み睡眠薬だそうです。
ベンゾジアゼピン系のものだから、仮眠をとるには安全性が高いと言っていましたけど」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Thank you for waiting. Please take these.”
“Thanks. Sorry to keep troubling you.”
I accepted the water and a paper packet of powdered medicine.
For some reason, there were two packets.
“There are two packets; what is the other one?”
“I consulted my sister about Master Shiki’s condition, and she gave me a sedative that Master Shiki’s physician had instructed her to keep for you.
The second packet is a sleeping medicine. She said it was a benzodiazepine and should be comparatively safe for a short nap.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Thank you for waiting.
Please drink this."
"Thank you, as always, and sorry."
I take the water and the powdered medicine that Hisui brought me.
For some reason, there are two kinds of medicine.
"Huh?
Two?
What are they?"
"Yes, I told my sister that you were not feeling well, and she gave me some medicine she had prescribed from your doctor.
This one is to help you sleep.
This contains benzodiazepine, which is known for being able to produce a relaxed sleep."

entries.japanese:
「…………？」
　琥珀さんは頼りになるけど、そういう専門的な単語を翡翠に言いつけるのも問題ありだ。
「……あれかな、琥珀さんは将来薬剤師になるのかな」
　言いつつ、二つの薬を飲む。
　水で薬を喉に流し込む。
　と、本当に即効性なのか、ほどなくして眠気がやってきてくれた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“……?”
Kohaku was certainly capable, but expecting Hisui to relay technical jargon like that seemed a little much.
“Maybe Kohaku plans to become a pharmacist.”
Muttering to myself, I took both medicines.
I washed them down with water.
Perhaps they really were fast-acting, because drowsiness came over me within moments.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…………?"
I trust Kohaku-san, but she doesn't have to tell Hisui all this in-depth knowledge…
"…… Wow, does Kohaku-san plan on becoming a licensed pharmacist?"
Saying that, I drink the medicine.
I drink the water to gulp down my medicine.
Apparently, it works fast; I feel sleepy already.

entries.japanese:
「……それじゃ少し眠るから。
夕食になったら起こしてくれ」
「はい。
それでは失礼します」
　翡翠が去っていく。
　くらり、と意識がかすんでいく。
　……少し、眠ろう。
　まだ外は明るい。
　この時間になら―――あんな、たちの悪い夢は見ないハズだろうから―――
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’m going to sleep for a while. Wake me when dinner is ready.”
“Very well. Excuse me.”
Hisui departed.
The room swayed, and consciousness began to cloud.
I would sleep for a little while.
