Her hands trembled. Akiha buried her face against my shoulder, smothering her sobs.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Her nails rip into me.
Despite this, I embrace her shoulders.
"………… Akiha.
It's okay, I'm here."
"Ah…… a, ah-----"
Her shaking hands.
Resting her face against my shoulder, she muffles a sob.

entries.japanese:
「―――秋葉。
そんなに苦しいなら、無理しなくていいんだ。
我慢するコトなんて、ない」
「……ちがう……ちがうの、兄さん。
　私は、そんな―――兄さんに言ってもらえる資格なんて、ない」
　言って。
　がくん、と秋葉の体から力が抜けた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Akiha. If it hurts this much, you don’t have to force yourself. You don’t have to endure it.”
“No—that isn’t it, Brother.
I don’t deserve to hear those words from you.”
With that.
All the strength abruptly left Akiha’s body.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Akiha.
If it hurts that much, don't push yourself.
You don't have to hold back."
"…… No…… that's not it, Nii-san.
I---I don't deserve anything from you."
Saying that,
her strength drains from her body.

entries.japanese:
「……お父様、私は――――私は、兄さんを、どうしても」
　こぼれる嗚咽。
　それに隠れるように、
「どうしても、この手にかけないと、いけないんですか」
―――と。
　吐き出すような悲哀が、聞こえた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Father—I—I can’t, Brother, no matter what—”
A sob escaped her.
Almost hidden beneath it—
“Do I truly have to kill him with my own hands?”
―――And then.
I heard the anguish wrenched out of her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Father, I----I must, to Nii-san…"
She sobs.
As if trying to hide it,
"Must I, kill him with my own hands?"
---With that,
I hear her sobbing.

entries.japanese:
「―――――――秋、葉？」
「嫌―――私、どうすれば…………！」
　震える声で、秋葉は涙をこぼす。
　嗚咽は堰をきってこぼれだす。
「…………………」
　何も言えず、ただ秋葉を抱きしめた。
―――そうして、どれくらいの時間がたっただろう。
　泣きつかれた子供のように秋葉は眠って、そのか細い体を、俺はベッドに横たわらせた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Akiha?”
“No—I don’t know what to do…!”
Her voice shook as the tears spilled over.
Then the dam broke, and her sobs came pouring out.
“…”
Unable to say anything, I simply held her.
―――How long did we remain that way?
At last Akiha fell asleep like a child exhausted from crying, and I laid her frail body upon the bed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-------Aki, ha?"
"I don't want to---what, what should I do……!"
Speaking with a wavering voice, Akiha cries.
No matter how hard she tries, she can't hold it in.
"……………………"
I just hold her, not saying anything.
---How long did it last?
Akiha sleeps like a child who cried herself to sleep, and I lay her slender body onto the bed.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さん。
秋葉さまは落ち着かれましたか？」
　廊下で待っていたのか、琥珀さんは秋葉の寝室の前で待っていた。
「……ああ。
今は眠ってる。
けど琥珀さん、秋葉はどうして、あんな―――」
「いえ、志貴さんが心配する事はありませんよ。
秋葉さまは突発的な呼吸困難におちいる事があるんです。
志貴さまが貧血ぎみであるように、秋葉さまも遠野家の人間ですから」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Shiki. Has Miss Akiha settled down?”
Kohaku must have been waiting in the corridor; she stood outside Akiha’s bedroom.
“Yes. She’s asleep now. But Kohaku, why did she—?”
“There’s no need for you to worry, Shiki. Miss Akiha sometimes suffers sudden attacks of breathlessness. Just as Master Shiki is prone to anemia, Miss Akiha too is a member of the Tohno family.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-san.
Has Akiha-sama calmed down?"
Kohaku-san must have been waiting in the hallway as she was standing outside the door.
"…… Yeah.
She's sleeping.
But Kohaku-san, why is Akiha---"
"No, it is nothing you need to worry about.
At times, Akiha-sama lapses into sudden dyspnea.
It is the same as your anemia; Akiha-sama is a member of the Tohno family after all."

entries.japanese:
「……なんだよそれ。
秋葉はいつも元気そうだったじゃないか」
「はい。
けど遠野家の方々は、みなそういった疾患を持っているんですよ。
　遺伝的な欠陥なのか、秋葉さまも志貴さんも、お二人の父親である槙久様も何らかの身体的な発作を持病としてお持ちなんです。
　その中でも秋葉さまの病状は軽い方なんです。
楽観はできませんが、志貴さんと違って決して命に関わる物ではありませんから、そう怖い顔をしないでくださいな」
entries.maoEnglish:
“What is that supposed to mean? Akiha has always looked perfectly healthy.”
“Yes. But everyone in the Tohno family suffers from some such complaint.
Whether it is a hereditary defect or something else, Miss Akiha, Shiki, and their father, Master Makihisa, have all been subject to physical attacks of one kind or another.
Miss Akiha’s condition is among the milder cases. It cannot be dismissed, but unlike yours it poses no danger to her life, so please don’t look so frightened.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… What do you mean?
She's always healthy."
"Yes.
But those of the Tohno family all have that sort of illness.
Maybe it's inherited, but both you and Akiha-sama carry a variation of Makihisa-sama's condition.
Akiha-sama's condition is not very serious.
It isn't something to be taken lightly, but it's not life-threatening, as your condition is, so please don't make such a worried face."

entries.japanese:
「―――怖い顔って、仕方ないだろ。
さっきまで秋葉があんなに苦しんでたんだ。
　俺は何もできないし、今まで―――秋葉がそんな体だったなんて、知りもしなかった」
「ええ。
秋葉さまは志貴さんにはくれぐれも内密にするように、と気を配っていましたから。
　わたしたちも志貴さまには内緒にするよう、きつく言われてましたからね」
「――――そんな、どうして」
「秋葉さまは志貴さんに不快な思いをさせたくないんです。
ですからどうか、志貴さんも秋葉さまのお心遣いを無下にするような事はしないでください」
entries.maoEnglish:
“How am I supposed to look? Akiha was in agony a few minutes ago.
I couldn’t do anything for her, and until tonight I never even knew she had a condition like this.”
“Yes. Miss Akiha has always taken great care to keep it from you, Shiki.
She gave us strict instructions not to tell Master Shiki either.”
“But why?”
“Miss Akiha did not want to distress you. So please, Shiki, do not repay Miss Akiha’s consideration by treating it lightly.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---I can't help it.
She seemed to be in such pain.
I couldn't even do anything.
Until now---I didn't even know she had that condition."
"Yes.
Akiha-sama tried her best to keep it a secret from you.
We were also told to keep it a secret from you."
"----But, why?"
"Akiha-sama didn't want to worry you.
So please, do not concern yourself and do as Akiha-sama wishes."

entries.japanese:
「……………っ」
　言葉がない。
　琥珀さんの言う事は正しすぎて反論できない。
　結局は俺は、一人だけ何も知らないまま、自分だけ悩みを持っている気になっていただけだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
I had no answer.
Kohaku was so plainly right that there was nothing to argue.
In the end, I alone had known nothing, all the while imagining that I alone carried some great burden.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"………………"
I don't know what to say.
What she says is true; I can't dispute it.
In other words, I was the only one who didn't know.
I just thought I was the only one with problems.

entries.japanese:
「………すみません。
秋葉をよろしくお願いします、琥珀さん」
　琥珀さんに頭をさげて、秋葉の部屋の前から立ち去った。
「――――――――」
　部屋に戻っても眠る事などできなかった。
　何かを怖がっていた秋葉の姿が目蓋に焼き付いてしまって、心が穏やかになってくれない。
「い……………た」
　背中の傷が痛む。
　秋葉の爪が掻き毟った背中には、血が滲んでいた。
　爪は肌を裂いて、カッターで切りつけたような跡を何十と残している。
　……だが、こんな傷はそう痛いものではなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’m sorry. Please take care of Akiha, Kohaku.”
I bowed to her and walked away from Akiha’s room.
“…”
Even back in my room, sleep was impossible.
The sight of Akiha frightened of something had burned itself behind my eyelids, and my heart refused to settle.
“Ow…”
The wounds on my back stung.
Blood had seeped from the places Akiha’s nails had raked.
They had split the skin and left dozens of marks like slashes from a box cutter.
But those wounds hardly hurt at all.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……… Sorry.
Please take care of Akiha, Kohaku-san."
Bowing to Kohaku-san, I walk away.
"--------"
I go back to my room, but I can't sleep.
The frightened figure of Akiha burns in my mind, and I can't calm down.
"Ah…………… ow."
My back hurts.
Blood oozes where her nails dug into my back.
Her nails left numerous knife-like marks in my skin.
…… But, they don't hurt that much.

entries.japanese:
窓から遠い月を眺める。
　秋葉を心配する心は、それでも穏やかになってくれない。
　……あんなに苦しんでいた秋葉。
　……体に疾患を持つという遠野の一族。
「―――――――」
　脈拍があがる。
　それを思うだけで、何も知らなかった自分に対する怒りが湧き上がる。
entries.maoEnglish:
I gazed through the window at the distant moon.
My fear for Akiha would not subside.
Akiha, suffering so terribly.
The Tohno bloodline, said to carry illness in its flesh.
“…”
My pulse quickened.
Merely thinking about it sent anger surging through me—anger at myself for knowing nothing.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I look out my window to the distant moon.
My worrying heart still cannot calm down.
…… She was in such pain.
…… The illness of the Tohno family.
"-------"
My pulse increases.
Just thinking about it, I get mad at myself for not knowing anything.

entries.japanese:
「―――――――」
　赤い。
唇から雫れた赤い血。
　わずか一瞬だけ、赤く―――血のように赤く見えた、秋葉の髪。
「―――――――く、そ」
　自分に対する怒りで穏やかになれない？
　そんなのは嘘だ。
　あの髪。
あの色彩を思い出すだけで、ドクンドクンと心臓が鼓動する。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
Red. The red blood that had dripped from my lip.
Akiha’s hair, which for one instant had looked red—red as blood.
“Damn it.”
I could not calm down because I was angry with myself?
That was a lie.
That hair. Merely remembering that color made my heart pound and pound.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-------"
Red.
Blood drips from my lip.
It was only for an instant, but her hair was blood red.
"-------Damn, it."
I can't calm down because I'm angry at myself?
That's a lie.
That hair.
Just remembering that color makes my heart beat like a drum.

entries.japanese:
……俺はどうしてしまったんだろう。
　あの、赤い髪の秋葉を思い出すだけで、血が昂ぶって、息が苦しくなる。
　だから考えないようにしているのに、どうしてもそれができない。
　あの秋葉の姿は、美しすぎた。
　こんなにも。
　こんなにも何かに夢中になったのは、これが初めてだった。
――――いや、それとも。
　この頭の中が真っ白に燃えるような感覚を、何日か前に、体験したような気がする。
entries.maoEnglish:
What was happening to me?
The thought of Akiha with red hair sent my blood racing and tightened my breath.
I tried not to think about it, but I could not stop.
That vision of Akiha had been too beautiful.
This much.
Never before had anything consumed me so completely.
――――No. Or perhaps—
I had felt this before—the sensation of my mind burning white—perhaps only a few days earlier.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… What's wrong with me?
Just remembering her red hair causes my blood to boil and my breathing to become difficult.
I try not to think about it, but I can't even manage that.
Back then, Akiha was just too beautiful.
Even now.
This was the first time I was so into something.
----No, or…
I think I felt this burning sensation in my head a few days ago.

entries.japanese:
「……まったく。
これじゃ秋葉に恋をしているみたいじゃないか」
　……それも、また嘘。
　この昂ぶりは恋なんて優しいものじゃない。
　思い出して、呼吸を乱す。
それは欲情と呼ばれるモノだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“God. It’s as if I’m in love with Akiha.”
Another lie.
This fever was nothing so gentle as love.
The memory alone left me panting. What I felt was lust.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Jeez.
I'm acting like I'm in love with Akiha."
…… That, is also a lie.
This excitement isn't anything as gentle as love.
Remembering, and breathing out of control.
That is what you call lust.

entries.japanese:
「――――――――」
　顔を手で覆って、ベッドに倒れこんだ。
　気分は収まらない。
　今夜はこのまま、ずっとこんな気持ちのまま過ごさないといけないんだろうか―――!w1000
　トントン、というノックの音。
「志貴さん？
　起きてらっしゃいますか？」
「えっ……起きてるけど、琥珀さん？」
「はい。
失礼しますね、志貴さん」
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
I covered my face and fell back onto the bed.
The feeling would not abate.
Was I going to spend the entire night like this—!w1000
A soft knock sounded at the door.
“Shiki? Are you awake?”
“Huh—yes, Kohaku?”
“Yes. Pardon me, Shiki.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"--------"
Slapping my face, I collapse on my bed.
I can't settle down.
Do I have to stay like this the whole night---?
Knock.
Knock.
"Shiki-san?
Are you awake?"
"Eh…… I'm up.
Kohaku-san?"
"Yes.
Please excuse me, Shiki-san."

entries.japanese:
琥珀さんは銀のトレイを持って部屋に入ってきた。
　トレイには水の入ったグラスと、薬らしき錠剤がある。
「あ、やっぱりご気分が優れないみたいですね。
さっきの志貴さん、すごく思いつめてましたから。
もしかしたら眠れないのかなー、って老婆心ながらもやってきてしまいました」
　琥珀さんはトコトコとベッドまで歩いてくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
Kohaku entered carrying a silver tray.
It held a glass of water and a tablet of some kind.
“Oh, you really aren’t feeling well. Shiki, you looked so troubled earlier that I wondered if you might have difficulty sleeping. I’m afraid I came to meddle.”
She padded over to the bed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Kohaku-san enters my room, carrying a silver tray.
There is a glass of water and something that looks like medicine.
"Ah, you look like you're not feeling well after all.
Before, you looked very worried.
I thought that maybe you wouldn't be able to sleep and was a little concerned."
Kohaku-san steps over to my bed.

entries.japanese:
「……琥珀さん。
それ、もしかして睡眠薬か何かですか？」
「いえ、そこまで強いものではありません。
ちょっとした安定剤ですけど、志貴さんがよろしいのでしたらお勧めしようと思って」
　琥珀さんは控えめな口調だった。
　薬は勧められないけど、俺がどうしても眠れないのなら使ってください、という意味。
　……その心遣いは、本当に助かる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…Kohaku, is that a sleeping pill?”
“Nothing so strong—it’s only a mild sedative. I thought I might offer it, if you wished, Shiki.”
Her tone was careful.
She did not want to press medicine on me, but if I truly could not sleep, it was there.
That thoughtfulness was a genuine relief.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Kohaku-san.
Is that, something like a sleeping pill?"
"No, it isn't anything that strong.
It's something that only helps to relax.
If you don't mind, then please take it."
Kohaku-san sounds a bit hesitant.
In other words, she doesn't want to offer the medicine, but if I can't sleep, I should take it.
…… That kindness really helps.

entries.japanese:
「―――ありがとう。
ちょうど眠れなかったところなんだ。
薬、貰うよ」
「……いいんですか？
　志貴さん、お薬の服用はあまり好きではない、と主治医さんから伺っていますけど」
「別に薬嫌いなわけじゃないよ。
あの主治医はね、薬の副作用とか説明しないで、人をモルモット扱いしてやがんだ。
　けど琥珀さんは別。
琥珀さんのくれた薬なら安心できるよ」
　グラスを受け取って、錠剤を飲みこんだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Thank you. I was lying here unable to sleep. I’ll take it.”
“Are you certain, Shiki? Your doctor told me you dislike taking medicine.”
“I don’t dislike medicine. That doctor treats me like a guinea pig without even explaining the side effects.
You’re different. If it came from you, I can trust it.”
I accepted the glass and swallowed the tablet.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Thanks.
I couldn't sleep, so I'll take it."
"…… Is it okay?
Shiki-san, I heard from your doctor that you do not usually like medicine."
"It's not that I hate it.
It's just that the doctor gives me medicine without telling me what it's for.
I feel like I'm a guinea pig.
But, you're different.
If it's from you, then I can safely take it."
I take the glass and down the pill.

entries.japanese:
水で薬を胃まで流し込む。
　……別に即効性というワケではないだろうけど、冷たい水の感触が昂ぶった心を落ち着けてくれたみたいだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
I washed the tablet down with water.
It could hardly have taken effect at once, but the cold water seemed to soothe my fevered mind.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The water carries the pill down to my stomach.
…… I don't think it's because it works that fast, but the cool water seems to already calm my agitated mind.

entries.japanese:
「ありがと。
これならすぐに眠れそうだ」
「はい。
それでは失礼しますね。
どうか良い夢を、志貴さん」
　琥珀さんはおじぎをして退室していった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Thanks. I think I’ll be able to sleep now.”
“Yes. Then I shall leave you. Sweet dreams, Shiki.”
Kohaku bowed and left the room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Thanks.
With this, I should be able to sleep soon."
"Yes.
Well then, I will be going.
Sweet dreams, Shiki-san."
With a bow, Kohaku-san exits the room.

entries.japanese:
「――――――ふぁ」
　両腕を伸ばして、大きく息を吐く。
　……今夜は秋葉の事を考えるのは止めよう。
　今はともかく眠って、やるべきことは明日になったら―――――
entries.maoEnglish:
“Haaah…”
I stretched both arms and exhaled deeply.
I would stop thinking about Akiha tonight.
For now I would sleep, and whatever needed doing could wait until tomorrow—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------Haa."
Stretching out my arms, I let out a deep breath.
…… I should just stop thinking about Akiha.
I should go to sleep and wait until tomorrow-----

entries.japanese:
目が醒めた。
　琥珀の薬のおかげが、この上ないほど頭の中がクリアになっている。
　四角い窓から見上げる空は、同じようにクリアな空だ。
　なにか、今日はいいコトがありそうな気がする。
entries.maoEnglish:
I woke.
Perhaps thanks to Kohaku’s medicine, my mind was clearer than I could remember it ever being.
The sky through the square window was just as clear.
I had a feeling something good would happen today.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I open my eyes.
Thanks to Kohaku-san's medicine, my head has cleared perfectly.
I look out the window to the sky, which is clear too.
I feel like something good might happen today.

entries.japanese:
朝食を済ませて学校に向かう。
　今日は秋葉の顔ぐらいは見ておこうと思ったが、やめておいた。
　何事も急いては台無しにしてしまう。
　今日は大人しく学校にいる事にしよう。
entries.maoEnglish:
After breakfast, I set out for school.
I considered at least looking in on Akiha, but decided against it.
Rushing things only ruins them.
Today I would behave myself and remain at school.
entries.mirrorMoon:
After breakfast, I head to school.
I thought that I would see how Akiha is doing, but I stopped myself.
Hurrying things just makes things worse.
I decide to just go to school.

entries.japanese:
――――学校はいつも通りだった。
　とりわけ変化もなく、自分を脅かすものもない。
　夕方になれば生徒たちは下校していって、校舎はとたんに静かになる。
　意味もなく日没まで時間を潰す事にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――School was the same as ever.
Nothing had changed; nothing threatened me.
By evening the students had gone home, and the building fell abruptly silent.
For no particular reason, I killed time until sunset.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----School's just the same as always.
Nothing is especially different, nothing threatens me.
In the afternoon, everyone leaves and the school building becomes quiet.
For no reason, I just kill time until sunset.

entries.japanese:
夜になった。
　まだ屋敷に帰る気にはなれない。
　少し遊んでから、どうするか考えよう。
entries.maoEnglish:
Night came.
I still had no desire to return to the mansion.
I would amuse myself for a while, then decide what to do.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Night falls.
I don't feel like going back to the mansion.
I should play around a bit and then decide what to do.

entries.japanese:
――――はっ、はっ、はっ、はっ――――
　コトを済ませて、呼吸を再開した。
　目の前には真新しい女の死体。
　両手はやはり血に染まっている。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――Hah, hah, hah, hah—
Once it was done, I began breathing again.
A woman’s fresh corpse lay before me.
My hands were stained with blood, as usual.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----*pant* *pant* *pant* *pant*---.
Finishing it up, I resume breathing.
In front of me is a new girl's dead body.
Both my hands are painted with blood.

entries.japanese:
――――はっ、はっ、はっ、はっ――――
　またやってしまったらしい。
　やる気はなかったのに、始めてしまうとつい白熱してしまう。
　悪い癖だ。
　さて、死体はどうしようか。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――Hah, hah, hah, hah—
I had done it again.
I had not meant to, but once I started, I always got carried away.
A bad habit.
Now, what to do with the corpse?
entries.mirrorMoon:
----*pant* *pant* *pant* *pant*---.
It looks like I did it again.
I didn't really feel like it, but once I started, I just got into it.
It's a bad habit.
Well, what should I do with the dead body?

entries.japanese:
――――はっ、はっ、はっ、トン――――
　自分の呼吸音だけが夜に響く。
　なのに、今、最後におかしな音がした。
「――――――――誰だ！？」
　振り返る。
　大通りに通じる小道から、足音が聞こえてくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――Hah, hah, hah, tap—
Only my breathing echoed through the night.
Yet that last sound had been wrong.
“Who’s there?!”
I spun around.
Footsteps came from the narrow lane leading to the main road.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----*pant* *pant* *pant*, Thud---.
My voice is the only thing that echoes in the air.
But I hear a weird sound at the end.
"--------Who is it!?"
I turn around.
I hear footsteps along the path leading to the main street.

entries.japanese:
――――はっ、はっ、はっ、はっ――――
　ぽたり、と額から汗がこぼれた。
　……緊張しているワケではない。
　身体が、ひどくあつかった。
　どうかしている。
あまりの暑さに喉が乾く。
　死体を、ひどくあつかった。
　死体の首筋に歯をたてて、血を飲む。
　喉の乾きはそれぐらいでは収まらない。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――Hah, hah, hah, hah—
A drop of sweat fell from my brow.
It was not tension.
My body was terribly hot.
Something was wrong. The heat had parched my throat.
The corpse was terribly hot.
I sank my teeth into its neck and drank the blood.
It was nowhere near enough to quench my thirst.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----*pant* *pant* *pant* *pant*---.
Sweat trickles from my forehead.
…… It's not that I'm nervous.
My body is just so hot.
There's something wrong.
It's so hot, I'm thirsty.
The dead body is horribly hot.
Biting its neck, I drink the blood.
But that isn't enough.

entries.japanese:
――――はっ、はっ、はっ、はっ――――
　ゆらりと視界が歪む。
　気のせいではない。
　この周辺の気温が異状。
　大気の冷たさに比べて、地面の温度が高すぎる。
　煙る蒸気が、この上ないほどの危険を告げている。
「―――――――チッ」
　死体に噛みついたまま走った。
　ここにいては危険だと本能が告げていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――Hah, hah, hah, hah—
My vision warped in the shimmering air.
It was no illusion.
The temperature here was unnatural.
The ground was far too hot beneath the cold night air.
Rising steam warned of mortal danger.
“Tch.”
Still biting into the corpse, I ran.
Instinct told me it was dangerous to remain.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----*pant* *pant* *pant* *pant*---.
My world starts to waver.
It isn't my imagination.
There is something unnaturally hot in the air.
And the ground is much hotter than the air.
This burning heat is screaming a warning at me.
"---------Sst."
I run, still gnawing at the body.
My head tells me that staying here is incredibly dangerous.

entries.japanese:
――――はっ、はっ、はっ、はっ――――！
　学校まで逃げてくる。
　ここなら他人の目につく事はない。
　さっきのが何だったのかは解らないが―――
entries.maoEnglish:
――――Hah, hah, hah, hah!—
I fled as far as the school.
No one would see me here.
I had no idea what that had been, but—
entries.mirrorMoon:
----*pant* *pant* *pant* *pant*----!
I escape to school.
No one will see me here.
I don't know what that was but---

entries.japanese: アイツが、笑っている。
entries.maoEnglish: It was laughing.
entries.mirrorMoon: It is smiling.

entries.japanese:
「――――――――！」
　背後に言いようのない熱さを感じた。
　振り返ると、そこには。
#ff0000
　赤い熱気のようなものが。
#ffffff
　何か、得体の知れないモノの気配が近づいてきていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“!”
An indescribable heat gathered behind me.
I turned.
Something like a red haze.
The presence of something I could not begin to identify was drawing near.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"--------!"
Behind me, I feel an indescribable heat.
I turn around and see what is there.
#ff0000
The something that is like red heat.
#ffffff
I feel something moving towards me.

entries.japanese:
「くそ――――――」
　追いかけられている。
　……面倒くさいので殺そう、とナイフを握る。
#ff0000
　赤い熱気が広がっていく。
#ffffff
　足音をたてて、堂々と『誰か』がやってくる。
　隙だらけの歩き方だ。
　得体が知れないが、格好の獲物だと唇を舐めた後。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Damn it…”
I was being hunted.
Annoyed by the pursuit, I gripped my knife and decided to kill it.
The red haze spread.
Someone approached openly, footsteps ringing without the least attempt at concealment.
Every stride left them exposed.
Whatever it was, I licked my lips at the sight of such easy prey.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Damn it------"
It chases after me.
…… It's a real bother, so I'll just kill it.
I grip my knife.

#ff0000
The red heat expands.
#ffffff
The footsteps of "someone" approach me.
A careless gait.
I don't know what it is, but I lick my lips in anticipation.

entries.japanese:
「あ―――――――――」
　どくん、と。
　心臓が、アレには絶対に敵わない、と告げてきた。
「はっ――――――はは、は」
　汗が流れる。
　熱さのためではない。
　本能に次いで、理性も悟った。
　自分は、アレに捕まったら始末される、と。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ah…”
With a single thud.
My heart told me I could never defeat that thing.
“Hah—ha, ha.”
Sweat ran down me.
Not from the heat.
Reason followed instinct to the same conclusion.
If it caught me, it would dispose of me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah---------"
Thump.
My heart screams at me, telling me that I'm no match for whatever that is.
"Ha-------haha, ha."
I sweat.
Not because of the heat.
After instinct, my mind understands as well.
If that catches me, I'm finished.

entries.japanese:
「はは、ははは、ははははははははは！」
　怖くなって、校舎の中へ逃げ出した。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ha—ha ha—hahahahahaha!”
Terror drove me into the school building.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Haha, hahaha, hahahahahahahahaha!"
Scared, I escape into the school building.

entries.japanese:
――――はっ、はっ、はっ、はっ――――
　四階まで上がってきた。
　ここまで来れば、アレが追ってくる事もないだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――Hah, hah, hah, hah—
I made it to the fourth floor.
Surely it would not follow me this far.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----*pant* *pant* *pant* *pant*---.
I run up to the fourth floor.
If I come up here, it won't follow me this far.

entries.japanese: おまえ―――どうして、笑っているんだ。
entries.maoEnglish: You—why are you laughing?
entries.mirrorMoon: Why---are you smiling?

entries.japanese:
「はぁ………は、はは、は」
　ようやく一息つけて、自分がまだ死体を噛んでいる事に気がついた。
　口をあける。
　ぼと、と廊下に死体が落ちる。
　手足はまだついたままだ。
　ちょうどハラが減った事だし、ここで処理する事にしよう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hah—hah—ha, ha.”
At last I caught my breath and realized the corpse was still clenched between my teeth.
I opened my mouth.
It dropped onto the corridor with a wet thud.
All four limbs were still attached.
I was hungry anyway, so I decided to dispose of it here.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Haa……… ha, haha, ha."
Taking a deep breath, I realize I'm still biting that dead body.
I open my mouth.
The dead body falls to the ground with a thud.
The arms and legs are still attached.
I am hungry right now, so I guess I'll take care of this right here.

entries.japanese:
――――――カツン。
「―――――――！？」
　振り返る。
　そこには―――あの、得体の知れないヤツが立っていた。
「やっぱり貴方だったんですね、兄さん」
　誰かが言う。
　この両手は血で濡れている。
足元には新しい死体。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――――Click.
“?!”
I turned.
There stood that same incomprehensible thing.
“So it was you after all, Brother.”
Someone spoke.
Both my hands were drenched in blood. A fresh corpse lay at my feet.
entries.mirrorMoon:
------Creak.
"-------!?"
I spin around.
There---there is that unknown person.
"I knew it was you, Nii-san."
That person speaks.
These hands are bloody.
At my feet is the dead body.

entries.japanese:
見られた。
　人を殺している所を見られた。
　なら、もう怖がってなんかいられない。
　相手が誰であろうと、ここでコイツを始末するだけだ。
「はっ――――――！」
　ナイフを握って、敵へと走る。
　その途端。
　きぃぃぃぃん、という音がして、片手が消滅した。
entries.maoEnglish:
I had been seen.
Someone had seen me kill.
There was no room left for fear.
Whoever this was, I had only to dispose of them here.
“Hah!”
Knife in hand, I charged.
The instant I did—
A piercing whine split the air, and one of my hands ceased to exist.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I've been seen.
I've been seen where I killed someone.
There's no more reason to be afraid.
No matter who this is, I have to finish it here and now.
"Ha------!"
Gripping my knife, I run towards the enemy.
In that instant.
Kreeeeee!
My arm disintegrates.

entries.japanese:
「なっ…………！？」
　足を止めて、後ろに跳ぶ。
#ff0000
　赤い熱気めいたものを、間一髪でかわす。
#ffffff

「貴様、何を――――」
　肘から先がなくなっていた。
　痛みもない。
　出血もない。
　断面からは肉と骨が見えていて、そこから―――吐き気がするぐらいの冷気が体内に侵入してくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What…?!”
I stopped and sprang backward.
I barely evaded the red haze.
“What did you—?”
My arm ended at the elbow.
There was no pain.
No blood.
Flesh and bone showed in the stump, and through it a nauseating cold invaded my body.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Wha…………!?"
Stopping, I leap backwards.
#ff0000
I barely avoid that red heat.
#ffffff

"You, what the----"
There is nothing past my elbow.
It doesn't hurt.
There is no blood.
I can see the cross-section of flesh and bone, from there---a chill nausea enters my body.

entries.japanese:
「はっ……は、あ……！？」
　解らない。
　敵は何もしていない。
ただ、今はもう無くなってしまった片腕を睨んだだけ、のようだった。
　つまり―――睨んだだけで、殺せるという事か。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hah—ah?!”
I did not understand.
The enemy had done nothing. It seemed only to have looked at the arm that was no longer there.
Did that mean a glance alone was enough to kill?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Haa…… ha, ah……!?"
I don't understand.
The enemy didn't do anything.
It seemed like it only stared at my now missing arm.
In other words---just a look can kill.

entries.japanese:
#ff0000

　いや、それは違う。
entries.maoEnglish: No—that was not it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
#ff0000

No, that's not right.

entries.japanese:
#ffffff


　かつん、と乾いた足音が響く。
　敵がやってくる。
　それは、拙い。
　敵の視界に入れば成す術もなく殺される。
「ひ…………ひひ、ひ…………！」
　闇にまぎれて、見られないように廊下を走った。
entries.maoEnglish:
A dry footstep rang out.
The enemy was coming.
Bad.
If I entered its sight, I would be killed without any chance to resist.
“Hee—hee hee!”
I fled down the corridor, hiding in the darkness from its gaze.
entries.mirrorMoon:
#ffffff


Dry footsteps echo through the air.
The enemy is coming.
That's foolish.
If I fall in the enemy's line of vision, I will die.
"Hee………… heehee, heee…………!"
In the dark, I run down the hallway.

entries.japanese:
階段までついた。
　足音は近づいてくる。
「はっ――――はは、は――――」
　窓を開ける。
ここは四階だが、かまわない。
　敵と自分とではスキルが違いすぎる。
　こっちは近づかなくちゃ殺せないのに、敵は見るだけでいいときた。
　そんな手合いを殺すには、完全な奇襲以外はありえない。
　今はここから逃げて、違う日にこっちから殺しにいってやる。
entries.maoEnglish:
I reached the stairs.
The footsteps kept drawing closer.
“Hah—ha ha—hah.”
I opened a window. It was the fourth floor, but that hardly mattered.
The difference in our abilities was absurd.
I had to get close to kill; the enemy only had to look.
Nothing short of a perfect ambush could kill an opponent like that.
I would escape now and come back to murder it another day.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I make it to the stairs.
The footsteps sound closer.
"Ha-----haha, ha----"
I open the window.
This is the fourth floor, but I don't care.
The difference between my skills and the enemy's are just too great.
I have to get close to kill, but the enemy merely has to look.
The only way to kill such a thing would be through a surprise attack.
For now, I have to get away and kill the enemy later.

entries.japanese:
#ff0000
　窓の外には。
　無数の赤い糸が張り巡らされていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
Outside the window,
countless red threads had been woven across the night.
entries.mirrorMoon:
#ff0000
Outside the window,
is a web of countless red threads.

entries.japanese:
#ffffff

　窓を開けて外に身を乗り出す。
「っ―――あ、ああああああああ！」
　途端、体が燃えた。
　火がつく前に廊下に転がる。
「な……なん、だ―――」
#ff0000
　だから、校舎を赤い糸が包んでいる。
#ffffff
　解らない。
　窓の外には何もないのに、外に出ようとすると体が発火してしまう。
entries.maoEnglish:
I opened the window and leaned out.
“A-Aaaaaagh!”
My body ignited at once.
I threw myself back into the corridor before the flames could catch.
“What is this?”
Red threads enclosed the entire building.
I did not understand.
Nothing stood outside the window, yet whenever I tried to leave, my body burst into flame.
entries.mirrorMoon:
#ffffff

I stick my body out the window.
"---Ah, aaaaaaaaaah!"
Instantly, my body burns.
Before I burst into flames, I roll back in the hallway.
"Wha…… what was----"
#ff0000
The red threads are wrapped around the school building.
#ffffff
I don't understand.
There is nothing outside the building, but if I go outside, I'll go up in flames.

entries.japanese:
――――かつん、という足音が聞こえる。
「くそ……窓はだめだ……！」
　逃げなければ。
　とにかく逃けないと殺される。
　転がるように階段を駆け下りた。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――A single footstep clicked in the corridor.
“Damn—the windows are no good!”
I had to run.
If I did not escape, I would be killed.
I raced headlong down the stairs.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----I hear the footsteps.
"Damn it…… the window is no good……!"
I need to escape.
If I don't, I'll die.
I roll down the stairs.

entries.japanese:
三階を駆け下りて二階に来た。
　……いける。
敵よりこちらの足が速い。
#ff0000
　違う。
もう、すぐ後ろに赤い髪が。
#ffffff
「……………っ！」
　転がった。
　唐突に、片足が蒸発した。
「がっ――――あ、あ………！？」
　転がる。
階段の方とは逆に転がった。
　上からは、階段を降りてくる敵の足音。
「はっ――――は、はっ、はっ…………！」
　残された片腕と片足で、廊下を這って逃げた。
entries.maoEnglish:
I raced down through the third floor and reached the second.
“I can make it. I am faster than the enemy.”
No. The red hair was already behind me.
“…!”
I pitched forward.
Without warning, one leg evaporated.
“Gah—ah?!”
I rolled. Away from the stairs.
Above me came the enemy’s measured descent.
“Hah—hah, hah!”
With one arm and one leg remaining, I dragged myself down the corridor.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I make it past the third floor to the second.
…… I can make it.
I'm faster than the enemy.
#ff0000
No.
There's already the red hair behind me.
#ffffff
"………!"
I roll.
All of a sudden, my leg is vaporized.
"Gah----ah, ah………!?"
I roll again.
Backwards, away from the stairs.
From above, I hear the footsteps of the enemy walking down the stairs.
"*pant*----*pant* *pant* *pant*………………!"
With my remaining arm and leg, I escape down the hall.

entries.japanese:
「ぐっ………なんだってんだ、チクショウ………！」
　這いながら、叫んだ。
　敵はまだ階段にいるハズなのに、体のいたる所が寒い。
#ff0000
　廊下には、赤い熱気。
#ffffff
　廊下は汗がでるほど熱いのに、体は冷たい。
　そうして、冷たいと感じた部分が、次の瞬間には蒸発していた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What the hell is this?!”
I screamed as I crawled.
The enemy should still have been on the stairs, yet cold spread through my body.
The corridor swam with red heat.
The air was hot enough to draw sweat, but my flesh was freezing.
Every place that turned cold evaporated in the next instant.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"G……… What's this?
Shit……!"
I scream.
Even though the enemy is still by the stairs, my body feels so cold.
#ff0000
Down the hall, that red heat.
#ffffff
The hallway is hot enough to sweat, but my body is cool.
And then, the part that still felt cool, evaporates.

entries.japanese:
「はっ――――はっ、あ……………！」
　だがこの程度では死なない。
　そのまま、身近な教室に入った。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hah—hah—ah!”
This was not enough to kill me.
I pulled myself into the nearest classroom.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ha-----ha, ah…………!"
But I won't die with such a wound.
Like that, I enter a nearby classroom.

entries.japanese:
……かつん、かつん、かつん、かつん。
　足音が近づいてくる。
　……敵がどんなカラクリをしているのかは解らない。
#ff0000
　いや、だから。
#ffffff
　敵の殺傷能力は、どう考えてもこっちより数倍は優れている。
#ff0000
　あの赤い熱気だろう。
#ffffff
　だが―――それを扱っている本体は最低だ。
　気配の消し方も出来なければ、相手を察知する能力もない。
entries.maoEnglish:
Click, click, click, click.
The footsteps approached.
I did not know what trick the enemy was using.
No—of course.
Its power to kill was many times greater than mine.
It had to be that red heat.
But the one wielding it was pathetic.
It could not conceal its presence or even sense another’s.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Clomp, clomp, clomp, clomp.
The footsteps come closer.
…… I don't know how the enemy does it.
#ff0000
No, that's not it.
#ffffff
The enemy's ability to kill, no matter how I think of it, is so many times superior to mine.
#ff0000
It's probably that red heat.
#ffffff
But----the one controlling the power is awful.
It can't hide its presence, and it can't even sense its enemy.

entries.japanese:
かつん、と。
　敵はこちらに気がつかず、そのままこの教室を通り過ぎようとしている。
entries.maoEnglish:
Click.
Unaware of me, the enemy was about to pass the classroom.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Footsteps.
The enemy is about to walk past the classroom without noticing me.

entries.japanese:
「――――――――――」
　落ち着いてきた。
　素人が飛び道具を持っているだけなら、どうという事はない。
　……敵は教室を通りすぎた。
　なら、後は簡単だ。
その隙だらけの背中を仕留める。
　片足がなくとも仔細ない。
　敵が振り返るより早く、確実に、敵の脳髄を切り取ってやる――――――！
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
Calm returned.
If this was merely an amateur armed with a projectile, there was nothing to fear.
The enemy passed the classroom.
The rest was simple. I would take that defenseless back.
One missing leg made no difference.
Before it could turn, I would slice out its brain—cleanly, certainly.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----------"
I calm down.
If it's only an amateur with a ranged weapon, it's nothing.
…… The enemy passes the classroom.
Then it's simple.
I just have to kill from behind.
I only have one leg, but that's fine.
I'll certainly slice open the brain faster than the enemy can turn around------!

entries.japanese:
廊下に出る。
　敵は背中を見せている。
　……なんて無様。
まだこちらの気配さえ察していない。
　確信して、跳躍した。
entries.maoEnglish:
I slipped into the corridor.
The enemy’s back was exposed.
“How pathetic. It had not sensed me even now.”
Certain of victory, I leapt.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I go out in the hallway.
I see the enemy's back.
…… How careless.
The enemy doesn't even notice my presence yet.
Full of confidence, I jump.

entries.japanese:
「―――――！？」
　敵が驚いて振り向く。
　時間にして五秒はあったろう。
　それなら七回は殺せる時間だった。
　だった。
だった。
だった。
だった。
だった、ハズだ。
　敵は。
　無慈悲な目をして、振り返った。
entries.maoEnglish:
“?!”
The enemy turned in surprise.
I must have had five whole seconds.
Enough time to kill it seven times over.
It had been. Had been. Had been. Had been. It should have been.
The enemy.
It turned with merciless eyes.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------!?"
The enemy turns, surprised.
I had at least five seconds.
It was enough time to kill the enemy seven times.
Was.
Was.
Was.
Was.
Was.
Supposed to.
The enemy.
The enemy turns to face me with merciless eyes.

entries.japanese:
「―――驚いたわ。
そんな体でまだ動けるなんて」
　敵が言う。
　からん、とナイフが廊下に落ちた。
　……ア・ツ・イ。
　なんて、コト。
　コイツは、別に、気配を察知する必要も、身を守る必要も、なかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’m impressed. You can still move in that condition.”
The enemy spoke.
My knife clattered onto the corridor floor.
Hot.
What—?
It had never needed to sense my presence or defend itself.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---I'm surprised.
You can still move with that body."
The enemy speaks.
Clang!
My knife falls to the ground.
…… H   o   t.
What is this?
This enemy did not need to feel anyone's presence or to protect itself.

entries.japanese:
#ff0000

　敵の周囲は、密度すら感じる熱気で充満している。
#ffffff
　近づくだけで―――肌が灼けて、動けなく、なった。
#ff0000
　それは、赤い髪が手足にまとわりついている為だろうに。
entries.maoEnglish:
The air around the enemy was packed with heat so dense it seemed almost solid.
Merely drawing near had scorched my skin and stolen the power to move.
Of course—red hair had wound itself around my limbs.
entries.mirrorMoon:
#ff0000

The enemy's surrounding is filled with heat.
#ffffff
Just getting close---my skin roasts, and it stops my movement.

#ff0000
It's because that red hair is wrapping around my limbs.

entries.japanese:
#ffffff
「は――――――あ」
　見上げる。
　雲は途切れる。
解放された月光が、敵の姿を映し出す。
#ff0000
　全て終わったと確信したのか。
ゆらめいていた敵の髪が、さらりと落ちた。
entries.maoEnglish:
#ffffff


“Hah—ah.”
I looked up.
The clouds parted. Freed moonlight revealed my enemy.
Perhaps convinced it was over. The hair that had writhed around her settled softly into place.
entries.mirrorMoon:
#ffffff
"Ha------ah."
I look up.
The clouds part.
The freed moonlight illuminates the enemy.
#ff0000
Is the enemy confident it's over?
The fluttering hair falls down.

entries.japanese:
#ffffff
――――秋葉、だった。
「―――――」
　あまりの事に声が出ない。
　ただ、それで――――これが夢だと、ようやく悟った。
entries.maoEnglish:
#ffffff


――――It was Akiha.
“…”
The revelation struck me speechless.
And only then did I finally understand that this was a dream.
entries.mirrorMoon:
#ffffff
----It is Akiha.
"-----"
I can't speak.
But, with that----I realize that this is a dream.

entries.japanese:
「さよなら兄さん。
さんざん逃げ回ってくれたけど、これで終わりね」
　秋葉の視線が向けられる。
#ff0000
　赤い髪が絡み付こうと伸びてくる
#ffffff
　視線から逃げる事はできない。
#ff0000
　違う。
それは、違う
#ffffff
　骨の芯から凍りつくような悪寒。
そのあと、何もかも奪われてしまうような感覚。
#ff0000
　だから、違う。
まだ間に合う。
切れ。
その髪を切れ。
それとも、やはり
entries.maoEnglish:
“Goodbye, Brother. You’ve led me quite a chase, but it ends here.”
Akiha’s gaze fell upon me.
Red hair reached out to coil around my body,
There was no escaping her eyes.
No—that was wrong.
A chill froze me to the marrow. Then came the sensation of everything being torn away.
Wrong. There was still time. Cut it. Cut the hair. Or was it still—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Goodbye, Nii-san.
You led me on quite the chase, but it is now over."
She looks directly at me.
#ff0000
The red hair shoots forth.
#ffffff
I can't escape from her gaze.
#ff0000
No.
That is, wrong.
#ffffff
The piercing chill from the center of my spine.
And then, the feeling of everything being taken.
#ff0000
So this is, wrong.
I can still make it.
Cut it.
Cut that hair.
Or, maybe…

entries.japanese:
#ffffff
　成す術もなく。
意識が、薄れていく。
#ff0000
　これは夢だから、今の俺には見えていないのか
entries.maoEnglish:
#ffffff



Helpless. I felt consciousness ebb away.
Was it only because this was a dream that the waking me could not see it—
entries.mirrorMoon:
#ffffff
Not being able to do anything, my consciousness fades.
#ff0000
This is a dream, so I can't see it right now.

entries.japanese:
#ffffff



「どうして、こんな事に」
　呪うような秋葉の呟き。
　そこへ。
「当主としてのお役目、ご苦労様でした」
　と。
笑顔で、琥珀さんが告げていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“How did it come to this?”
Akiha’s whisper sounded like a curse.
Then.
“Your duty as head of the family is complete.”
With a smile. Kohaku told her she had done well.
entries.mirrorMoon:
#ffffff



"Why, did it end this way?"
Akiha mutters this like a curse.
Then.
"Good work fulfilling your duty as the head of the household."
With a smile, Kohaku-san says this.

entries.japanese:
悪い夢。
　これは悪い夢。
　これはもう少し先の未来。
　これはまだ決定していない先の時間。
　だから早く、もとの時間に戻らなくっちゃ―――
entries.maoEnglish:
A bad dream.
This was a bad dream.
A future a little way ahead.
A future that had not yet been decided.
I had to hurry back to my own time—
entries.mirrorMoon:
A nightmare.
This is a nightmare.
This is just a glimpse of the future.
This is an undecided future.
So I have to hurry, back to my own time---

entries.japanese: ――――そうして、ベッドから跳ね起きた。
entries.maoEnglish: ――――And then I shot upright in bed.
entries.mirrorMoon: ----And then, I jump up from my bed.

entries.japanese:
「ハッ―――ハァ、ハ――――」
　ぜいぜいと空気を吸う。
　今のは、夢だった、らしい。
「はあ―――はあ、あ…………」
　呼吸を整えながら、自分の体を抱いた。
　……体は依然として存在し、肌が灼けた跡も、失われている部分もない。
　背中に指を当てると、びしゃりと音がした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hah—haaah—hah.”
I dragged air into my lungs.
That had apparently been a dream.
“Hah—hah—ah.”
As I steadied my breathing, I wrapped my arms around myself.
My body still existed, with no burns and no missing pieces.
When I touched my back, my fingers landed with a wet slap.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ahh---ah, ha----"
I suck in air.
That, was just, a dream.
"*pant*---*pant*, *pant*………"
Hugging myself, I try to control my breathing.
…… My body is still all here; there are no burn marks on my skin.
I feel my back with my fingers.
It's wet.

entries.japanese:
「……すごい……汗……」
　口にして、なんだか他人事のように思えた。
　全身が汗をかいていて、寝巻は水をかぶったように水気を帯びている。
　今の夢―――あの悪夢から覚めた今でも、額からはポタポタと汗がこぼれていた。
「……気持ち……悪い」
　吐き気を堪えながらベッドから起きあがる。
　窓際まで歩いて外の風を浴びて、少しだけ気分が落ち着いてくれた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“So much sweat.”
The words sounded as though they concerned somebody else.
My whole body was drenched; my nightclothes clung to me as if soaked in water.
Even awake now, free of that nightmare, sweat continued to drip from my brow.
“I feel sick.”
Fighting nausea, I climbed out of bed.
I staggered to the window, and the outside air calmed me a little.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… All this…… sweat……"
I speak as if it is happening to someone else.
My entire body is drenched in sweat, as if someone covered me in water.
That dream----even after I woke up from it, sweat pours from my forehead.
"…… I feel…… terrible."
I get up from bed and suppress the urge to vomit.
Walking towards the window, the wind calms me down a little bit.

entries.japanese:
「……なんて夢を見てるんだろう、俺は」
　あの悪夢を反芻して、自分の両手を確認する。
　両手には血の染み一つない。
　それは当然の事だ。
　さっきのは夢にすぎないんだから、俺が殺人の返り血を浴びる事も、人の血を吸うような真似をするハズもない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What kind of dream was that?”
I went over the nightmare again and examined my hands.
Not a speck of blood stained them.
Naturally.
It had only been a dream, so I could not have bathed in a murder victim’s blood or drunk blood from a human body.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… What a dream."
Recalling the dream, I check both my hands.
There isn't any blood on my hands.
Well, of course.
That was just a dream, so I wasn't covered in blood, nor did I suck any blood.

entries.japanese:
―――だが。
　　　昨日の朝、遠野志貴は何をしただろう。
　　　確か赤いペンキに塗れた両手を、
　　　誰にも見つからないようにと、
　　　洗い流しにいったのではなかったか。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――But.
What had Shiki Tohno done yesterday morning?
Those hands stained with red paint—
—somewhere no one would find him—
—and washed them clean?
entries.mirrorMoon:
---But.
Yesterday morning, what did I do?
Didn't I take my hands drenched in red paint,
while trying not to let anyone see them,
and wash them clean?

entries.japanese:
――――志貴くんはわたしと同じだよ。
　　　　そう言っていた少女がいた。
　　　……よく思い出せない。
　　　遠野志貴は彼女に噛まれた。
　　　……よく思い出せない。
　　　血を吸う病があるのなら。
　　　……よく考えられない。
　　　それは、噛まれる事によって伝染する。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――You’re just like me, Shiki.
There had been a girl who told me that.
I could not remember clearly.
Shiki Tohno had been bitten by her.
I could not remember clearly.
If there were a disease that made people drink blood.
I could not think clearly.
It would spread through a bite.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----You and I are the same, Shiki-kun.
That's what she said.
…… I can't remember that well.
Tohno Shiki was bit by her.
…… I can't remember that well.
If there is a habit of drinking blood.
…… I can't think well.
It spreads by being bitten.

entries.japanese:
「――――――違う………っ！！」
　言って、脳内に巣くう暗い情念を払拭した。
　だが今の夢は消えてくれない。
　人殺しをする自分がいた。
　きっと問題はそこだ。
　俺は、たとえ夢の中だとしても殺人をして、それに何の罪悪感も抱いていなかった。
　ただ、当たり前のように殺して、それを眺めていただけ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“No…!”
I shouted down the dark conviction nesting in my mind.
But the dream would not disappear.
I had seen myself murder someone.
That was the real problem.
Even in a dream, I had killed without the slightest guilt.
I had murdered as naturally as breathing, then merely gazed at what I had done.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------No……!!"
I sweep away the dark passions in my brain.
But that dream doesn't disappear.
There was a me that killed someone.
There's the problem.
Even though it's in my dreams, I killed someone and didn't feel any guilt.
All I did was kill naturally, and watch.

entries.japanese:
それは異常だ。
　夢の中の自分は正気じゃなかった。
　アレは、こうしている自分とはまったくの別人だ。
　だが、あの夢は遠野志貴が見たものだ。
　なら―――正気じゃなかった遠野志貴も、自分である事に間違いはない。
entries.maoEnglish:
It was monstrous.
The person in that dream had not been sane.
He was utterly different from the self standing here now.
But Shiki Tohno had dreamed it.
Therefore the mad Shiki Tohno had also, unquestionably, been me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
That's abnormal.
Inside my dreams, I wasn't sane.
That is different from this me right now.
But, that's a dream that Tohno Shiki saw.
So---even that insane Tohno Shiki has to be me.

entries.japanese:
「―――――違う」
　……そうして、そんな遠野志貴を罰しに来た秋葉。
　夢かと言われれば夢だろう。
　だがアレは悪夢というよりは、そう遠くない未来のような気がして、吐き気がする。
　と。
控えめな、ノックの音がした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“No.”
And then Akiha had come to punish that Shiki Tohno.
A dream was still a dream.
Yet it had felt less like a nightmare than a glimpse of the near future, and the thought turned my stomach.
Then. A restrained knock sounded at the door.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-----No."
…… And, the Akiha that came to punish me.
It might be a dream.
But for some reason, I feel like it's a glimpse of the future, and start to get nauseous.
I hear a knock at the door.

entries.japanese:
「失礼します。
……志貴さま？
　お目覚めになられていたのですか？」
「ああ。
ちょっと夢見が悪くて、ついさっき目が醒めた。
……ちょうど良かった。
すごく汗をかいたから、早く着替えたいって思ってたんだ」
　翡翠はいつも通り、学生服を用意してくれている。
　それを受け取る為に翡翠へ近づこうとして、
　くらりと、眩暈がした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Pardon me. Master Shiki? You are already awake?”
“Yeah. A nightmare woke me a minute ago. Your timing’s perfect. I sweated so much I’ve been dying to change.”
Hisui had brought my school uniform as usual.
I started toward her to take it—
The room lurched around me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Excuse me.
…… Shiki-sama?
Are you already awake?"
"Yeah I just had a bad dream, so I just woke up…… Thank goodness.
I sweated a lot, so I wanted to change quickly."
As usual, Hisui has prepared my uniform.
I draw nearer to her to get them, and,
I get real dizzy.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま！？」
　……翡翠の声が聞こえる。
駆け寄ってくる気配がして、手をあげてそれを止めた。
「ぁ――――大丈夫。
ちょっとした眩暈だから、すぐに持ちなおすよ」
　深呼吸をして、自分の中でトントン、というリズムをとる。
　そうして頭の奥にわだかまった血が薄れていくのを待った。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki?!”
I heard Hisui’s voice. Sensing her rush toward me, I raised one hand to stop her.
“Ah—I’m fine. Just a little dizzy; it’ll pass in a moment.”
I breathed deeply, beating out a steady rhythm inside myself.
Then I waited for the blood knotted behind my eyes to drain away.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama!?"
…… I can hear her voice.
I sense her coming closer, and raise my hand to stop her.
"Ah----I'm fine.
I just was a little dizzy, I'll be fine in a bit."
Taking a deep breath, I focus on my heart's rhythm.
I wait for the blood to stop pounding in my head.

entries.japanese:
「ほら。
すぐに治っただろ」
　こんな事で翡翠を心配させたくないから、できるだけ明るく笑いかける。
「…………う」
　が、今回は失敗してしまったみたいだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“See? Gone already.”
Not wanting Hisui to worry over something so minor, I gave her the brightest smile I could manage.
“Oh.”
This time, it seemed I had failed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"See?
All better."
I say this with my best attempt at a bright smile to calm Hisui's worries.
"………… Ugh…"
But I guess I failed.

entries.japanese:
「……志貴さま、無理をなさらないでください。
そのようなお顔のまま笑われると、困ります」
　翡翠は辛そうな表情で、そんな事を言った。
「え――――」
　そんなふうに感情を露にした翡翠を見るのは初めてのような、気がする。
　……いや、そんな事はないか。
　よく思い返してみれば、翡翠は無表情に見えるだけで、わりと感情表現はストレートだ。
　八年前の、いつも窓際にいた頃の彼女に比べると違和感を覚えるぐらい、思っている事が顔にでている気がする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki, please do not overexert yourself. When you smile with such a look on your face, I do not know what to do.”
Hisui said it with an expression of quiet pain.
“What—?”
I felt as though I had never seen her show emotion so openly before.
No, that could not be right.
When I thought about it, Hisui only appeared expressionless; her feelings were often quite plain.
Compared with the girl who had always sat by the window eight years ago, her face now revealed so much that it was almost disconcerting.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Shiki-sama.
Please do not overexert yourself.
Smiling with a face like that troubles me."
Hisui says this with a pained expression.
"Eh----"
I think this is the first time I've seen her show emotion like this.
…… No, that's not true.
If I recall in detail, Hisui just looks expressionless, but you can see her emotions if you study her face.
I think she shows her feelings too much, so that when I compare her to that girl standing by the window, I feel a big contradiction.

entries.japanese:
「……志貴さま？
　やはりお体の具合が―――」
「いや、違うんだ翡翠。
ただちょっと意外に思っただけなんだ。
翡翠は昔に比べると変わったじゃないか。
いつも俺たちを見ていた頃に比べると元気になってくれた気がする」
「―――――そう、でしょうか。
それは志貴さまの思い違いだと思います」
　翡翠は言いにくそうに視線を逸らす。
　……うん。
やっぱり昔の、人形みたいに静かだった翡翠とはイメージが違っている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki? Are you certain you are well—?”
“No, it isn’t that. I was only surprised. You’ve changed since we were children, Hisui. You seem happier than when you used to sit and watch the rest of us.”
“Is that so? I believe you are mistaken, Master Shiki.”
Hisui turned her eyes aside, plainly uncomfortable.
Yes. She was nothing like the doll-still girl I remembered.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Shiki-sama?
Are you feeling bad after all---"
"No, that's not it, Hisui.
I just found it surprising.
You've changed a lot since back then.
I think you're more cheerful than the time when you were just watching us."
"-----Is, that so?
I think your memory is mistaken."
Hisui averts her gaze.
…… Yeah, she's different from the quiet, doll-like Hisui from my memory.

entries.japanese:
「それよりも志貴さま。
本当にお体のほうはよろしいのですか？」
「ああ、大丈夫だよ。
翡翠と話してたら元気になった」
「……わかりました。
ですが志貴さま、次の休日にはお医者さまに診ていただくべきです。
　志貴さまはこのお屋敷に帰ってきてから、明らかに体調を崩していますから」
「…………う」
　それは、確かにその通りだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“More importantly, Master Shiki. Are you truly feeling well?”
“I’m fine. Talking to you has already made me feel better.”
“Very well. But Master Shiki, you should see a doctor on your next day off.
Since returning to this mansion, Master Shiki’s health has plainly deteriorated.”
“…”
I could hardly deny it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"More importantly, Shiki-sama.
Are you really feeling well?"
"Yeah, I'm fine.
Speaking with you made me feel better."
"…… I understand.
But Shiki-sama, I think you need to see a doctor.
It seems like you are not feeling well since you came back to the mansion."
"…………… Um."
Well, that's true.

entries.japanese:
「なんだ、翡翠まで琥珀さんと同じような事を言うんだな。
それじゃあさ、まるでこの屋敷に帰ってこなかったほうがいいみたいだ」
　それは、軽い冗談のつもりだった。
「はい。
わたしも姉さんと同意見です」
「な―――――――」
　瞬間。
目の前が、くらりと歪んだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You sound just like Kohaku. The way you two talk, I’d almost think I was better off never coming back here.”
I meant it as a harmless joke.
“Yes. I agree with my sister.”
“What—?”
For an instant. The world swayed before my eyes.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"What's this?
You're saying the same thing as Kohaku-san.
You sound like it would've been better if I never came back."
I meant that as a joke.
"Yes.
Nee-san and I share the same view."
"Wha-------"
For an instant, my vision flickers.

entries.japanese:
「――――――――」
　言葉さえ喉を通らない。
　俺は八年前の約束を守るために帰ってきた。
　なのに、それを。
　あのリボンを手渡してくれた翡翠本人が、否定するのか。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
I could not even force words through my throat.
I had returned to fulfill a promise made eight years ago.
And now, that promise.
Was Hisui herself—the girl who had placed that ribbon in my hand—denying it?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"--------"
I can't even speak.
I came back to fulfill the promise.
But that.
The one who gave the ribbon disagrees.

entries.japanese:
「……翡翠。
きみが、それを言うのか。
俺が一体誰のために帰ってきたと―――」
「……違います。
志貴さまは志貴さまの為にこの屋敷に帰ってきたのです。
　ですから―――昔の約束になど縛られる必要はありません。
……今ならまだ間にあいます。
志貴さまは志貴さまの意思でやってこられた。
　だからいつだって、志貴さまはご自分の意思で自由になる事ができるんです」
　翡翠は学生服を机に置くと、足音も立てず扉へと歩いていく。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hisui. How can you be the one to say that? Who do you think I came back for—?”
“That is not true. Master Shiki returned to this mansion for Master Shiki’s own sake.
So you need not remain bound by a promise from long ago. It is not too late. Master Shiki came here of Master Shiki’s own will.
That means Master Shiki may also set himself free whenever he chooses.”
Hisui laid the uniform on my desk and walked soundlessly toward the door.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Hisui.
You say that?
Who do you think I came to the mansion for---"
"…… No.
Shiki-sama, you came back here for your own sake.
Therefore---there is no need to be bound by any promise from the past.
…… There is still time.
You decided yourself to come here.
So you can decide on your own to become free at any time."
Hisui places my uniform on the desk and walks away.

entries.japanese:
「……失礼しました。
どうか、ご無礼をお許しください」
　…………翡翠は去っていった。
「…………………」
　一人残されて、なぜか胸が痛んだ。
　……翡翠に対する怒りはない。
いや、逆に申し訳ないような、そんな感情しか湧いてこない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Forgive me. Please excuse my impertinence.”
Hisui left.
“…”
Alone, I felt an inexplicable ache in my chest.
I was not angry with her. If anything, all I felt was guilt.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Excuse me.
Please forgive my rudeness."
………… Hisui leaves.
"………………"
Left alone, my chest hurts for some reason.
…… I'm not angry at her.
No, I can only feel apologetic.

entries.japanese:
――――昔の約束に縛られる必要はない。
　翡翠にとってはどうでもいい約束。
　俺にとっては大切だった約束。
　その違いをこうハッキリと言われても、怒りが湧いてこない。
　理由はわかりきっている。
「……なんで。
そんな、泣きそうな顔をするんだ、翡翠」
　それが、ただ申し訳なくて、彼女を責める事なんて、できなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――You need not remain bound by a promise from long ago.
A promise that meant nothing to Hisui.
A promise precious to me.
Even after she stated the difference so plainly, no anger came.
The reason was obvious.
“Why. Why did you look as though you were about to cry, Hisui?”
I felt only sorry for her and could never have blamed her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
-----There is no need to be bound by a promise from the past.
The promise Hisui doesn't seem to care about.
The promise that was very important to me.
Even when she tells me directly this difference, I feel no anger.
The reason is obvious.
"…… Hisui.
Why did you look like you were going to cry?"
Because of that, I could not blame her.

entries.japanese:
居間には誰もいなかった。
　いつもは当然のように朝食を済ませている秋葉も、彫像のように壁際に立っている翡翠の姿もない。
entries.maoEnglish:
The sitting room was empty.
Akiha was not there eating her customary early breakfast, nor was Hisui standing against the wall like a statue.
entries.mirrorMoon:
There isn't anyone in the sitting room.
Neither Akiha, who usually has already finished eating by now, nor Hisui, who usually stands like a statue by the wall, are there.

entries.japanese:
「あ、おはようございます志貴さん。
今朝はまた早いんですね」
「……ああ、おはよう琥珀さん」
　挨拶をして居間を見渡す。
　居間は秋葉と翡翠がいないだけで、ひどく味気ない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh, good morning, Shiki. You’re up early again.”
“Morning, Kohaku.”
I greeted her and looked around.
Without Akiha and Hisui, the sitting room felt painfully bare.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah, good morning, Shiki-san.
You're up early today again."
"…… Yeah, morning, Kohaku-san."
Greeting her, I glance around the sitting room.
It bothers me that they're not there.

entries.japanese:
「琥珀さん。
秋葉はあれからよくなった？」
「はい。
もう体調も戻られて、大事はありませんでした。
ですがまだご気分が優れないようなので、今日はお休みになられるそうです」
「……そうか。
大事がなくて良かった」
「はい。
なんでしたら声をかけてきたらどうですか？
　秋葉さま、きっと寝起きの顔を見られたくなくて枕を投げてきますから」
　琥珀さんは遠まわしに、秋葉とケンカをして来いと言っている。
　確かに枕を投げつけてくるぐらい慌てる秋葉を見るのは楽しそうだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Kohaku. Did Akiha recover?”
“Yes. Miss Akiha’s condition has stabilized, and there was no serious harm. She is still feeling unwell, however, so she intends to rest today.”
“I see. Thank God it wasn’t serious.”
“Yes. Why not go say hello? Miss Akiha won’t want you to see her just after waking, so she’s sure to throw a pillow at you.”
Kohaku was indirectly suggesting that I go pick a fight with Akiha.
Admittedly, seeing her flustered enough to hurl a pillow sounded entertaining.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Kohaku-san.
Has Akiha recovered since then?"
"Yes.
She's healthy now, so there is nothing to worry about.
But she is still feeling a bit tired, so she will be resting today."
"…… I see.
Thank goodness it was nothing too bad."
"Yes.
Maybe you should go see her?
She probably wouldn't want you to see her when she just woke up, so she'll probably throw a pillow at you."
Kohaku-san tells me indirectly to go have a fight with Akiha.
Certainly, seeing Akiha panic so much that she would throw a pillow at me sounds fun.

entries.japanese:
「――――――あ」
　けど、あんな夢を見てしまった自分が、普段通りに秋葉と話せる自信なんか、なかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ah…”
But after that dream, I had no confidence I could speak to Akiha as though nothing had happened.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------Ah."
But, after seeing that dream, I just don't think I can face her.

entries.japanese:
「……いや、止めておくよ。
今朝は気分が悪いから、秋葉と言い合う体力がない」
「そうですね。
秋葉さまも気を使わなくていい、と申されていましたから、志貴さんはいつも通り学校に行ってください。
　それと、志貴さん？
　翡翠ちゃんに何かしましたか？」
　じっ、と。
　琥珀さんは笑顔のまま、なんかとんでもない事を聞いてきた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“No. I’d better not; I feel ill this morning, and I don’t have the strength to argue with her.”
“That may be best. Miss Akiha said you needn’t worry about her, so please go to school as usual.
One other thing, Shiki. Did you do something to Hisui?”
With an intent stare.
Still smiling, Kohaku asked something outrageous.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… No, I don't think I will.
I don't feel good today, so I don't have the strength to fight her."
"I see.
Akiha-sama also said you don't have to worry too much about her, so you go to school as usual.
Oh, Shiki-san?
Did you do something to Hisui-chan?"
She stares.
With a smile, Kohaku-san asks such a thing.

entries.japanese:
「翡翠ちゃん、今朝は志貴さんに合わせる顔がないからって部屋に引きこもってしまったんです。
　あの翡翠ちゃんが仕事を休みたがるなんてよっぽどの事だと思いませんか、志貴さん」
　ふふふ、とどこか怖い笑いをこぼす琥珀さん。
　……間違いなく、俺が翡翠に酷い事をしたと思いこんでいる顔だった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hisui shut herself in her room this morning, saying she couldn’t face you.
Don’t you think it must be something very serious for Hisui of all people to want a day off, Shiki?”
Kohaku gave a soft, somehow frightening laugh.
Her face said she had already concluded that I had done something terrible to Hisui.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hisui-chan said she could not possibly see you today, so she locked herself up in her room.
Something must have really happened in order to make her skip work like that, Shiki-san."
Hehehe, Kohaku-san laughs with a frightening smile.
…… Without a doubt, she must think I did something horrible to Hisui.

entries.japanese:
「―――な、何かしたかって、別に何もしてませんっ……！
　どっちかっていえば、俺のほうがきつく叱られたようなものなんですっ」
「翡翠ちゃんが志貴さんを叱ったんですか？」
「あ―――いえ、そういう訳じゃないんだけど、なんて言うか……いつまでもつまらない事に執着するなって、そういう事です」
「ふーん……翡翠ちゃんもよく解らない事をするんですね。
　けど安心しました。
もしかしたら志貴さん、槙久さまに似ているのかなって心配したんですよ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“D-Did something—I didn’t do anything! If anything, I was the one who got a severe scolding.”
“Hisui scolded you, Shiki?”
“Well—no, not exactly; she told me to stop clinging to something that didn’t matter.”
“Hmm—Hisui does the strangest things.
Still, that’s a relief. For a moment I was worried that you might take after Master Makihisa, Shiki.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Wha, what?
I didn't do anything……!
If anything, she's the one that scolded me."
"Hisui-chan scolded you?"
"Ah---no, well, that's not it, it's just…… she told me I shouldn't be too persistent over small things."
"Hmmm…… Hisui-chan is doing some weird things.
But, I'm relieved.
I was worried that you were going to be like Makihisa-sama."

entries.japanese:
「はい？
　親父と似てるって、なにが？」
「あ………」
　しまった、と琥珀さんは視線を逸らす。
「いえ、何でもないんです。
些細な事ですから、どうかお気になさらないでくださいな」
「……あのね、琥珀さん。
そういうふうに言われると余計気になるんですけど」
　さっきの仕返し、とばかりに琥珀さんをじっと見つめる。
　……。
　…………。
　………………。
　………………………。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What? In what way am I like my father?”
“Ah…”
Kohaku looked away with the unmistakable expression of someone who had said too much.
“Oh, it’s nothing. Something trivial, so please don’t concern yourself.”
“…Kohaku, saying that only makes me more curious.”
In retaliation for her earlier interrogation, I stared her down.
…
…
…
…
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Huh?
Like my old man?
How?"
"Ah………"
Kohaku-san looks away like she didn't mean to say that.
"No, it isn't anything.
It's a trivial matter, so please do not worry about it."
"…… Hey, Kohaku-san.
It makes me more curious if you say it like that."
As revenge for before, I stare at her.
……
…………
………………
……………………

entries.japanese:
「……はあ、わかりました。
けど秋葉さまや翡翠ちゃんには内緒ですよ。
槙久さまのお話は、あまりしていいものではありませんから」
「？
　親父の事って、別に隠すような事じゃないだろ」
「そうですけど、あまりいい話ではありませんから。
　ほら志貴さん、覚えていませんか？
　槙久さまに躁鬱の気があった事を」
「躁鬱……？」
　躁鬱というのは、ようするに気分が極端に明るかったり極端に暗かったり、と頻繁に変わる事を言う。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Very well. But you must keep this from Miss Akiha and Hisui. Master Makihisa is not someone we should discuss lightly.”
“Why? There’s nothing secret about my father.”
“No, but it isn’t a pleasant subject.
Shiki, don’t you remember? Master Makihisa was prone to manic depression.”
“Manic depression…?”
That meant his moods swung frequently between extreme elation and extreme darkness.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I understand.
But keep this a secret from Akiha-sama and Hisui-chan.
It isn't too good to speak about Makihisa-sama."
"?
There isn't anything to hide about my old man, is there?"
"Well no, but it isn't a good story to talk about.
Don't you remember, Shiki-san?
About Makihisa-sama's manic depression?"
"Manic depression……?"
Manic depression means that someone changes mood all of a sudden, from extreme happiness to utter despair, and vice versa.

entries.japanese:
「……ああ、そういえば親父はそういう所があったっけ。
優しい時はすごく優しいんだけど、機嫌が悪い時は些細な事で怒ってたな」
「ええ。
それもまだ志貴さんがいらした頃は良かったんです。
ですが志貴さんが有間のお家に預けられた頃から、槙久さまはご気分を害される事が多くなりました。
　意味もなく秋葉さまを叱ったり、翡翠ちゃんに手を上げる事が多くなったんです」
「な――――ちょっと待って。
確かに親父は厳しい人だったけど、そんな理不尽な真似は―――」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Now that you mention it. When he was kind, he was incredibly kind, but when he was in a foul mood, the smallest thing could enrage him.”
“Yes. Even that was not so bad while you still lived here, Shiki. But after you were sent to the Arima family, Master Makihisa’s dark moods became more frequent.
He would scold Miss Akiha for no reason and often strike Hisui.”
“What—wait. My father was strict, but he would never do anything so unreasonable—”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Yeah, well, I guess he was like that.
He was very kind when he was kind, but he would get extremely angry over little things when he was in a bad mood."
"Yes.
But it was still alright when you were here.
But after you were adopted by the Arima family, his condition grew a lot worse.
He would yell at Akiha-sama for no reason and often abuse Hisui-chan."
"Wha----wait a minute.
I know my old man was strict, but he would never do such a---"

entries.japanese:
「……ですから、志貴さんが行かれた後の話です。
　槙久さまの躁鬱は、日に日に悪化していきました。
それは躁鬱と呼べるものではなく、すでに二つの違う人格がある段階にまでなってしまったんです。
　槙久さまは些細な事で感情を昂ぶらせるのですが、気分が落ち着かれると以前ご自分が何をしていたか覚えていない、というのです。
　その頃からわたしは槙久さまのお体を看させていただいていたんですが、槙久さまはわたしにだけおっしゃいました」
entries.maoEnglish:
“As I said, this happened after you left, Shiki.
Master Makihisa’s condition worsened by the day. Eventually it could no longer be called manic depression; it was as if two distinct personalities lived inside him.
The smallest thing would excite Master Makihisa into a frenzy, yet when he calmed down he could not remember what he had done.
I began tending to Master Makihisa’s health around that time, and Master Makihisa once confided something to me alone.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Like I said, this is after you left, Shiki-san.
Day by day, Makihisa-sama's manic depression worsened.
It was so bad it was more like having two different personalities rather than having manic depression.
He would be set off by the littlest things, but after he calmed down, he wouldn't even remember what he did.
During that time, I was taking care of him, and Makihisa-sama told me."

entries.japanese:
―――自分の中には狂暴な自分がいる。
　こうしている普段の自分にはソレを抑える事はできなくて、ソレが現れると自分は眠ってしまう。
　理由もなく、目に映る物全てを壊したくなる。
　その時の自分は、悪い夢を見ているようだ―――
entries.maoEnglish:
―――There is a violent self inside me.
His ordinary self could not restrain it, and whenever it emerged, he fell asleep.
For no reason at all, he wanted to destroy everything he saw.
At such times, he said, it felt as though he were trapped in a nightmare—
entries.mirrorMoon:
---I have a violent me within myself.
I cannot suppress it with my normal self, and when it appears, I go to sleep.
Without reason, I want to destroy everything I see.
Back then, it felt like I was watching a bad dream.

entries.japanese:
「……槙久さまはご病気で亡くなられましたが、病状を悪化させたのは槙久さまの心の病による所が大きかったんです。
　……人間の精神面での病は難しいものです。
　ですから志貴さんも、もしかしたら槙久さまの体質が遺伝しているのかもしれない、と心配したんです。
遠野家の人たちは何らかの疾患を遺伝するそうですから。
　けど、志貴さんに関してはわたしの杞憂でしたね。
だって志貴さんの疾患は貧血でしょう？
　槙久さまのように、ご自分のお心が自由にならないという訳ではないんですもの」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Makihisa died of physical illness, but Master Makihisa’s mental condition played a large part in its decline.
Afflictions of the human mind are difficult things.
That was why I worried you might have inherited Master Makihisa’s disposition, Shiki. Members of the Tohno family are said to inherit illnesses of one sort or another.
But in your case, I was worrying over nothing. Your condition is anemia, isn’t it? It isn’t as though you lose command of your own mind, as Master Makihisa did.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Makihisa-sama passed away from illness, but the illness was worsened by the illness in his mind.
…… Mental illnesses are a very difficult thing.
So I worried, thinking that you might have inherited some of that characteristic.
It seems that everyone in the Tohno family has some sort of illness.
But, I guess I was worrying for no reason in your case.
Because your illness is anemia, right?
It's not like you can't control yourself like Makihisa-sama."

entries.japanese:
良かった、と安心するように、琥珀さんは笑いかけてきた。
　俺は。
「―――――」
　　　　俺は。
「――――――――違う」
　　　　俺は、そんなふうに。
　安心して、笑う事なんて、出来ない。
entries.maoEnglish:
Kohaku smiled at me in relief.
I.
“…”
I.
“No.”
I could not feel that way.
I could not smile in relief.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Thank goodness," Kohaku-san smiles at me.
I.
"-----"
I.
"--------No."
I can't do it like that.
I can't feel relieved and smile.

entries.japanese:
昨夜の夢。
　秋葉に対して欲情していた自分。
　殺人の夢を当然のように見る、正気ではない遠野志貴。
entries.maoEnglish:
Last night’s dream.
The self that had lusted after Akiha.
The insane Shiki Tohno who dreamed of murder as though it were the most natural thing in the world.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Last night's dream.
My lust over Akiha.
Watching a dream of killing people as if it was natural, the insane Tohno Shiki.

entries.japanese:
「あ、もうこんな時間ですね。
それでは朝食の支度をしてきます」
　琥珀さんは食堂へ去っていく。
　その後ろ姿を、ただ呆然と眺める事しかできなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh, look at the time. I should prepare breakfast.”
Kohaku left for the dining room.
I could only stare blankly after her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah, it's already this late.
I'll go prepare breakfast now."
Kohaku-san disappears towards the dining room.
I can only stare at her in shock.

entries.japanese:
朝食はあまり味がしなかった。
　琥珀さんが話してくれた親父の事がグルグルと頭の中で渦巻いて、気がつくと屋敷の門までやってきていた。
「志貴さん、忘れ物はありませんか？」
　翡翠ちゃんが部屋に引きこもっているから、と琥珀さんが見送りにきてくれている。
「もう、志貴さんっ！
　今日はこんなにいいお天気なんですから、もっと元気をださないとダメですっ。
　そんな顔をされたままだと、送り出す事ができないじゃないですかっ」
「あ―――うん。
……そう、だね。
ごめん、ちょっと考え事をしていたんだ」
　軽く頭をふって、頭の中にわだかまった影を振り払う。
entries.maoEnglish:
Breakfast scarcely had a taste.
What Kohaku had told me about my father spun endlessly through my head, and before I knew it I was standing at the mansion gates.
“You haven’t forgotten anything, have you, Shiki?”
Since Hisui had shut herself in her room, Kohaku had come to see me off instead.
“Honestly, Shiki! The weather is beautiful today, so you must show a little more spirit.
I can’t possibly send you out looking like that.”
“Ah—right. Sorry. I was thinking.”
I shook my head lightly, trying to dislodge the shadow lodged there.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I ate breakfast, but I didn't taste anything.
What Kohaku-san said about my old man kept circling in my head and before I knew it, I was at the gate in front of the mansion.
"Shiki-san, you didn't forget anything?"
Hisui-chan is still in her room, Kohaku-san says as she sends me off.
"Geez, Shiki-san!
The weather is so nice today so you have to cheer up.
I can't send you off when you look like that."
"Ah---yeah.
…… You're right.
Sorry, I was just thinking about some things."
Giving my head a little shake, I banish the shadows in my mind.

entries.japanese:
「あ、少しはいつもの志貴さんに戻ってくれましたね。
はい、これなら安心です」
　……不思議だ。
　こう、まっすぐに笑顔を向けられると、本当に元気になれるような気がする。
「いってらっしゃい志貴さん。
お帰り、お待ちしておりますね」
　ぺこり、とお辞儀をする琥珀さん。
　それで、さっきまで自分を支配していた暗い感情は消えてくれた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“There—you look a little more like yourself again, Shiki. Now I can stop worrying.”
How strange.
When she smiled at me so openly, I felt as though strength truly returned.
“Have a good day, Shiki. I’ll be waiting for you to come home.”
Kohaku bowed.
That dispelled the dark feelings which had ruled me until then.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah, now that's more like the normal Shiki-san.
Yes, I can relax now."
…… That's odd.
Seeing that smile, I really do feel better.
"Goodbye, Shiki-san.
I'll be waiting for your return."
Kohaku-san bows.
With that, all of my worries seem to disappear.

entries.japanese:
「――サンキュ、琥珀さん。
おかげで元気が出た」
「はい。
志貴さんにはやっぱり、明るいお顔が似合っていますから」
「……ありがとう。
それじゃ行ってきます、琥珀さん」
　心からのお礼を言って、学校に向かって走り出した。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Thanks, Kohaku. I feel much better.”
“Good. A bright face suits you best, Shiki.”
“Thank you. I’m off, then.”
I thanked her from my heart and set off at a run for school.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"--Thanks, Kohaku-san.
I feel better already."
"Yes.
A bright face suits you better, Shiki-san."
"…… Thanks.
Well, then, I'm off, Kohaku-san."
Thanking her from the bottom of my heart, I run down the road to school.

entries.japanese:
いつもより余裕をもって教室に着いた。
　有彦は今日も遅刻らしく、おかげで静かにホームルームを迎えられる。
　かすかに騒がしい教室の中、席に座って担任がくるのを待つ事にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
I reached the classroom with more time to spare than usual.
Arihiko seemed to be late again, which meant I could greet homeroom in peace.
I sat amid the low classroom chatter and waited for our teacher.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I arrive in the classroom with more spare time than usual.
Arihiko is late as usual, so I can wait quietly for homeroom.
I decide to sit in my seat in the noisy classroom and wait for the teacher.

entries.japanese:
―――何のトラブルもなく一日が終わった。
　旅にでも出ているのか、有彦は欠席だった。
　旅、とは比喩表現でもなんでもなく、あいつは突発的に旅行に出かける、という奇癖をもっている。
　それもバイクに乗って気ままに放浪する、という格好のいいものではない。
平日のツアーパックは安いんだ、とご年配の方々にまぎれての観光旅行らしい。
　……まったく。
小学校からの付き合いになるが、あいつの趣味はいまいち掴めない。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――The day ended without incident.
Arihiko was absent, perhaps off traveling.
That was not a figure of speech; he had the peculiar habit of taking sudden trips.
Nor did he do anything glamorous, like roaming wherever his motorcycle carried him. Weekday package tours were cheap, he said, so apparently he joined sightseeing groups full of elderly travelers.
…I had known him since elementary school, and still could not make sense of his tastes.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---The day passes without any trouble.
Maybe he went on a trip?
Arihiko didn't show up.
"Trip" isn't a metaphor or anything.
He does have this strange habit of spontaneously taking trips.
It isn't anything cool like roaming the country on a motorcycle.
He goes on sightseeing tours on weekdays with the old people.
…… Geez.
I've known since elementary school, but I've never completely understood his hobbies.

entries.japanese:
――――屋敷に帰ってきた。
　学校にいる間は考えないようにしていた事が脳裏をよぎる。
　朝、琥珀さんが話してくれた親父の二面性。
　遠野家の人間が持つという、遺伝的な疾患。
　……翡翠の言うとおり、屋敷に帰ってきてからの俺はどこかおかしい。
　なにか、自分でも解らない所で記憶が曖昧になっている気がする。
　……琥珀さんの言っていたように、自分があの親父と同じとは思えない。
　だが事実として、この屋敷に帰ってきてから、俺は遠野志貴という自分に自信が持てなくなりつつある。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――I returned to the mansion.
The thoughts I had suppressed at school returned.
My father’s two faces, as Kohaku had described them that morning.
The hereditary afflictions of the Tohno family.
Hisui was right: something had been wrong with me since I returned here.
Somewhere beyond my own awareness, my memories seemed to be growing indistinct.
As Kohaku said, I could not believe I was the same as my father.
Yet the fact remained: since returning to this mansion, I had begun to lose faith in myself—in Shiki Tohno.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----I arrive at the mansion.
What I didn't think about at school comes back into my mind.
What Kohaku-san said about my old man's split personalities.
The hereditary illnesses of the Tohno family.
…… Like Hisui said, ever since I came back, there's been something wrong with me.
It feels like my memories are vague about something.
…… Like Kohaku-san said, I don't think I'm like my old man.
But, ever since I came back to this mansion, I no longer have full confidence in myself as Tohno Shiki.

entries.japanese:
「本当に―――親父はおかしかったのか」
　確かにそんな記憶もあるが、はっきりとは断定できない。
　こんな事を気にするなんて自分でも馬鹿げていると解っている。
　だが、それでも―――遠野志貴は、遠野家というものについて知っておくべきなのかもしれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Was there really something wrong with Father?”
I had memories that supported it, but nothing clear enough to be certain.
I knew it was ridiculous to obsess over this.
Even so—perhaps Shiki Tohno needed to learn the truth about the Tohno family.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Was my old man---really that crazy?"
I do have a vague memory like that, but I can't say for sure.
I understand that it's stupid of me to even be troubled by it.
But, still---I should probably know about the Tohno family.

entries.japanese:
「ただいま―――」
　声をあげてみるが、とりあえず返事はなかった。
　秋葉はまだ自室で休んでいるんだろう。
　琥珀さんと翡翠もそれぞれ仕事についているんだと思う。
「………………さて」
　考えてみると、これはいい機会かもしれない。
　俺は―――
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’m home.”
I called out, but received no answer.
Akiha was probably still resting in her room.
Kohaku and Hisui would each be occupied with work.
“Well.”
On reflection, this might be the perfect opportunity.
I―――
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I'm back---"
I call out, but there's no response.
Akiha is probably still resting in her room.
Kohaku-san and Hisui are probably doing their jobs right now.
"…………… Well then."
Come to think of it, this might be a good opportunity.
I--.

entries.japanese:
琥珀さんに話を聞こう。
　朝の様子からいって、琥珀さんはもっと詳しい事情を知っているようだった。
　秋葉がこの手の話をしてくれるとは思えないし、親父の部屋を調べるのも時間がかかる。
琥珀さんに直接問いただした方が、なにより効率的だろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
I would ask Kohaku.
Judging from this morning, she knew more than she had told me.
Akiha would never discuss this, and searching Father’s room would take time. Questioning Kohaku directly was by far the most efficient course.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I'll go ask Kohaku-san.
She seemed pretty knowledgeable about all those things this morning.
I don't think Akiha would want to talk about it, and searching my old man's room would take time.
I'll probably have the best luck with Kohaku-san.

entries.japanese:
「琥珀さん、この時間なら庭の掃除だよな」
　中庭に出てみる。
「あれ……？」
　中庭に琥珀さんの姿は見当たらない。
　きょろきょろとあたりを見渡す。
―――と。
　一瞬だけ、森のほうで琥珀さんの着物の色がちらついた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Kohaku should be cleaning the garden around now.”
I stepped into the courtyard.
“Huh…?”
She was nowhere in sight.
I looked around.
―――Then.
For an instant, I caught a flicker of her kimono among the trees.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"She's probably sweeping in the back."
I enter the courtyard.
"Huh……?"
I don't see her anywhere.
I glance around.
---And then.
For just an instant, I see the color of her kimono in the forest.

entries.japanese:
「……？
　あの方角に掃除するような場所、あったっけ？」
　あの方角には何もない。
　子供の頃はあの森で遊んでいたんだから、それに間違いはないんだ。
　とくにあの方角は自分にとって庭のような物だったから、あそこには―――
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hm. Was there anything to clean in that direction?”
There was nothing that way.
I had played in those woods as a child, so I knew that much for certain.
That particular part had been like my own private garden, and there was nothing there except—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……?
Is there anything to clean over there?
There isn't anything over there.
I played in that forest as a child, so I would remember.
I used to play a lot in that direction, so over there---

entries.japanese:
「―――――え？」
　……なんだ、ろう。
　あそこには何もない筈だ。
　けどそれもおかしな話。
　何もないような場所が、どうして。
　子供の頃の遠野志貴にとって、庭のような特別性を持っているのか。
「…………い、た………」
　こめかみに軽い頭痛。
　……少し迷ったあと、琥珀さんの後を追う事にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What…?”
What was this?
There should have been nothing there.
But that made no sense either.
Why would an empty place.
Hold such special meaning for the child Shiki Tohno—enough to feel like his own garden?
“Ow.”
A faint pain stirred in my temple.
After a moment’s hesitation, I followed Kohaku.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-----Eh?"
…… What was that?
There should be nothing there.
But there's something odd about that.
If there's nothing there, then why?
Did this garden-like area hold some special significance to me?
"……… Ou, ch………"
I get a light headache.
…… After a little debate with myself, I follow after Kohaku-san.

entries.japanese:
「―――――――――」
　森の奥には、ちょっとした大きさの屋敷があった。
　……離れ、というヤツだろうか。
　本館である屋敷からは木々に隠れて見えないような作りをしている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
Deep in the woods stood a mansion of modest size.
An annex, perhaps.
The trees had been allowed to conceal it completely from the main house.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---------"
Deep in the forest, there is another mansion.
…… Detached, I suppose.
Deep within the trees, it seems to be hidden from sight from the main building of the mansion.

entries.japanese:
「―――――――うそ」
　どくん、と心臓が痙攣する。
　初めて見る筈の離れは、ひどく―――懐かしい気がして、眩暈がする。
「…………………………」
　……琥珀さんはこの中に入っていった。
　この離れが何なのかは思い出せない。
　ただ不吉な予感がして、足を踏み入れたくないだけだ。
　それでも、ここまできて戻るのも馬鹿らしいので、思いきって中に入る事にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Impossible.”
My heart convulsed.
I should never have seen this annex before, yet it felt so terribly familiar that the sight made me dizzy.
“…”
Kohaku had gone inside.
I could not remember what this place was.
I only felt a sinister foreboding and wanted no part of it.
But turning back after coming this far seemed absurd, so I forced myself through the entrance.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-------No way."
My heart convulses.
This is the first time I've seen it, but---it seems horribly familiar, and I start to get dizzy.
"………………………"
…… Kohaku-san went inside.
I don't remember what this detached building is.
I just have a bad feeling about all of this and I don't want to go inside.
But, it would be pretty stupid if I came all the way here only to go back, so I force myself to continue.

entries.japanese:
……離れの中を歩く。
　もう何年も使われていないのだろう、建物は所々痛んでいた。
　それでも手入れはされているのか、汚いという事はない。
「……琥珀さんがいるとしたら奥の和室かな」
　ぼんやりとそんな事を思って、自然に足が和室に向かった。
entries.maoEnglish:
I walked through the annex.
It had plainly gone unused for years, and parts of the building had fallen into disrepair.
Yet someone still maintained it; nothing was filthy.
“If Kohaku is here, she’ll be in the tatami room at the back.”
The thought rose vaguely, and my feet carried me there as if they already knew the way.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… I walk around inside.
It's a little run-down here and there, probably because it hasn't been used in years.
But it seems like someone may have been doing some maintenance because it isn't dirty.
"…… Kohaku-san is probably in the Japanese-style room in the back."
I absent-mindedly think that aloud and automatically walk towards the room.

entries.japanese:
―――そこは懐かしい。
　　　畳の匂いがする、小さな部屋だった。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――The room was familiar.
A small space filled with the scent of tatami.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---This is all so familiar.
The smell of tatami fills the small room.

entries.japanese:
「あれ、志貴さん？
　どうしたんですか、こんな所までやってきて」
　琥珀さんはちょっと意外そうに首をかしげる。
　俺は―――
「いえ、琥珀さんに聞きたい事があったから、追いかけてきたんです」
―――自分でも不思議なぐらい、落ち着いた気分でそう返答していた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh, Shiki? What brings you all the way out here?”
Kohaku tilted her head, mildly surprised.
I—
“I wanted to ask you something, so I followed you.”
―――Somehow, even to my own surprise, I answered with perfect calm.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Huh?
Shiki-san?
Why did you come here?"
Kohaku-san tilts her head in surprise.
I---
"I wanted to ask you about something, so I followed you here."
---Strangely enough, I respond calmly.

entries.japanese:
「わたしにお話、ですか？」
「うん。
朝の事で、もうちょっと話を聞きたいんです。
……えっと、ここじゃなんですから中庭のほうに行きませんか？」
　ちらり、と部屋の天井に視線をおくる。
　外はじき日没で、すぐに暗くなってしまう。
　この部屋には電灯なんかつかないだろうし、早めに明かりのある所に移動したほうがいいだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You wished to speak with me?”
“Yes. I wanted to hear more about what you said this morning. Shall we go back to the courtyard?”
I glanced at the ceiling.
Sunset was near, and the room would soon be dark.
I doubted the lights worked here, so we ought to move somewhere illuminated while we still could.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"A talk, with me?"
"Yeah.
I wanted to talk more about this morning.
…… If this isn't a good place, should we go to the courtyard?"
I look up to the ceiling.
It is almost sunset, so it'll get dark soon.
The light in this room probably doesn't work, so we should head somewhere else.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さん、そのお話でしたらここでしたほうがいいと思いますよ。
屋敷に戻ると秋葉さまがいらっしゃいますから、槙久さまのお話はできません」
「あ―――そうか。
秋葉がやってくる事だってあるもんな。
……けど琥珀さん、別に俺は秋葉に内緒で話を聞くつもりはないんだけど」
「うーん、それはちょっと難しいですね。
秋葉さまは槙久さまのお話をしたくないんです。
　ですから、志貴さんが朝のお話の続きを聞きたい、というのでしたら、それは秋葉さまの目の届かない所でないといけません」
entries.maoEnglish:
“If that is what you wish to discuss, Shiki, we should remain here. Miss Akiha will be at the mansion, and I cannot speak about Master Makihisa there.”
“Ah—right. She could walk in on us. But Kohaku, I wasn’t planning to hide this from her.”
“That may be difficult. Miss Akiha does not wish us to discuss Master Makihisa.
If you want to hear the rest of what I began this morning, Shiki, it must be somewhere beyond Miss Akiha’s notice.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-san, if you want to talk about that then here is probably better.
If we go back to the mansion, we might run into Akiha-sama and will not be able to talk about Makihisa-sama."
"Ah---that's right.
She'll probably see us.
…… But Kohaku-san, I don't like keeping things secret from Akiha."
"Hmm, that is a little difficult.
Akiha-sama does not like talking about Makihisa-sama.
So if you wish to continue our talk from this morning, then we have to do it where Akiha-sama will not overhear us."

entries.japanese:
