「………琥珀さん。
それってつまり、秋葉には秘密にしなくちゃいけないってコト、ですか」
「はい。
秋葉さまにも翡翠ちゃんにも知られちゃいけない、志貴さんとわたしだけの秘密です」
　なぜか楽しそうに琥珀さんは笑う。
　……まあ。
　なんていうか、琥珀さんと二人きりの秘密、という単語には確かにドキドキするものがあるんだけど……。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…Kohaku, are you saying we have to keep this secret from Akiha?”
“Yes. A secret known neither to Miss Akiha nor Hisui—just between you and me, Shiki.”
For some reason, Kohaku smiled as though the idea delighted her.
Well.
The phrase just between Kohaku and me admittedly sent a little thrill through my chest.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Does that mean, we have to keep it a secret from Akiha?"
"Yes.
A secret between me and you, Shiki-san.
We can't let Akiha-sama or Hisui-chan know about it."
Kohaku-san smiles like she's having a lot of fun.
…… Well.
Having a secret just between the two of us does seem a little exciting, but……

entries.japanese:
「けど琥珀さん。
もうじき日が落ちるんだし、ここじゃ話はできないだろ」
「いえ、そんなコトはありませんよ。
この離れはですね、一応はまだ人が住める環境を保っているんです。
電源も生きてますし、お布団だって用意してありますから」
「へえ、そうなんだ。
……けどここ、随分前から使ってないんだろ？
　なんだってそんなふうにしてあるんだろう」
entries.maoEnglish:
“But Kohaku, the sun’s almost down. We can’t talk here in the dark.”
“Oh, that won’t be a problem. The annex is still kept fit for habitation. The electricity works, and there is bedding as well.”
“Really? But no one has used this place for years, have they? Why keep it ready?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"But Kohaku-san, the sun is almost setting.
We can't talk here, right?"
"Not at all.
This building is still maintained at a level for people to live in, so it has futons already prepared and electricity."
"Really?
But this place hasn't been used for a while, right?
Why is it maintained like that?"

entries.japanese:
「そうですね、きっと秋葉さまも未練が残っているのかもしれません。
ここは昔、槙久さまが養子にとった子供の住居でもありますから」
――――は？
　槙久……親父が昔、養子にとっていた、子供？
「……ちょっと待って琥珀さん。
その、親父が養子をとったって、どういうこと？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Perhaps Miss Akiha still feels attached to it. This was once the home of a child Master Makihisa adopted.”
――――What?
A child whom Makihisa—whom Father—had once adopted?
“Wait, Kohaku. What do you mean, my father adopted a child?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Let's see, maybe Akiha-sama is just fond of this place.
A long time ago, this was where Makihisa-sama's adopted child used to live."
----Huh?
Makihisa…… my old man, adopted a child, a long time ago?
"…… Wait a sec, Kohaku-san.
My old man adopted a child?"

entries.japanese:
「あら、憶えてないんですか？
　十年ほど前に槙久さまが引き取られた子供がいたじゃないですか。
両親を事故で亡くしてしまったとかで、槙久さまが養子になさったんです」
「そんな―――こと、あった、っけ」
「はい。
もっとも二年ほどで亡くなられてしまったんです。
些細な事故だったらしいんですけど、お屋敷に勤めていた使用人の人たちはやっぱり遠野の家は呪われてるんだとか、よく口にしていましたから」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh, don’t you remember? About ten years ago, Master Makihisa took in a child whose parents had died in an accident. Master Makihisa adopted the child.”
“Did―――that really happen?”
“Yes. Sadly, the child died about two years later. It was only a minor accident, apparently, but the servants employed here then often said it proved the Tohno family was cursed.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Oh, you don't remember?
About ten years ago, he brought a child here.
His parents both died in an accident, so he adopted the child."
"That---happened?"
"Yes.
But two years later, the child passed away.
It was a trivial accident, but a lot of the servants began to say that the Tohno family was cursed."

entries.japanese:
―――――ちょっと、待って。
　なにか……琥珀さんの言葉は、恐い。
　聞いているだけで視界がぐにゃりと歪む。
　まるでこの和室が飴で出来ているみたいに、どろどろと溶けていくような、不安定さ。
「こ、琥珀、さん」
　十年前にとられた養子。
二年後に事故死したという養子。
　つまり、それは。
　八年前――――俺が事故にあって、入院した年じゃない、のか。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――――Wait.
Something about what Kohaku was saying terrified me.
Merely listening made my vision buckle and warp.
The tatami room seemed as unstable as if it were made of candy, sagging as it slowly melted around me.
“K-Kohaku.”
Adopted ten years ago. Killed in an accident two years later.
That means.
Eight years ago――――the year I had my accident and was hospitalized.
entries.mirrorMoon:
-----Wait a minute.
Something about her words seems scary.
Just hearing them, my vision starts to warp.
It was as if the room was made completely of dissolving sugar.
"Ko, Kohaku, san."
A child adopted ten years ago.
Two years later, the child died.
In other words,
eight years ago----that's when I had my accident and was sent to the hospital.

entries.japanese:
―――事故。
　それはどんな事故だ。
　俺が大怪我をするぐらいの事故。
　その養子とやらが、死んでしまうぐらいの、事故。
　夏の暑い日。
―――よく思い出せない。
　ただあの時、俺の腕は、赤い血にまみれていたような――――
entries.maoEnglish:
―――An accident.
What kind of accident had it been?
One bad enough to leave me gravely injured.
Bad enough to kill that adopted child.
A scorching summer day.
―――I couldn’t remember it clearly.
Only that my arms had seemed drenched in scarlet blood――――
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Accident.
What kind of accident was it?
An accident that seriously wounded me.
An, accident that the adopted child, was killed in?
A hot summer day.
---I can't remember.
All I know is at that time, my arms seemed to be soaked in blood----

entries.japanese:
「琥珀、さん。
呪われてるって、どういう、こと」
「いえ、別にそう大した事じゃないんですよ。
ただ遠野家の方々は、代々早くにお亡くなりになっているんです。
　それが事故死であったり自殺であったり病死であったり、みなさん天寿をまっとうするようなカタチではないので呪われている、と噂されてしまったんですね」
「―――自殺って……なに、それ」
「ですから遠野家の方―――槙久さまもそうであったように、幼いころから精神を病んでしまって、成人してから自殺なさってしまった方が十人以上いるそうなんです。
　あくまで噂話なんですけど、戦前には殺人の罪を犯してしまった方もいらっしゃったとか」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Kohaku… what do you mean, cursed?”
“No, it’s nothing so dramatic. It’s simply that the Tohnos have tended to die young, generation after generation.
Whether by accident, suicide, or illness, hardly any lived out their natural span, so people began to call the family cursed.”
“Suicide—what do you mean?”
“More than ten members of the family are said to have become mentally ill as children, as Master Makihisa did, then taken their own lives after reaching adulthood.
It’s only rumor, of course, but one of the Tohnos supposedly even committed murder before the war.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Kohaku, san.
You said 'cursed'?"
"No, it isn't anything important.
It is just that a lot of the members of the Tohno family have died young.
Such as in accidents, or suicide, or illness; a curse that does not allow them a natural death.
Well, that was the rumor, anyway."
"----Suicide…… what?"
"Some members of the Tohno family---like Makihisa-sama, carried mental illnesses and committed suicide when they became adults.
These are just rumors, but it's said some of them were murderers before the war."

entries.japanese:
……精神を病んでいる？
　……殺人の、罪？
　……例えば、人を殺すユメを見たり、
　……例えば、自分の記憶が曖昧だったり？
entries.maoEnglish:
Mentally ill?
Guilty of murder?
Like dreaming that you killed someone―――
Like finding holes in your own memory…?
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Mental illness?
…… Murderers?
…… Such as, seeing dreams of killing people?
…… Such as, my memory being extremely vague?

entries.japanese:
「琥珀さん、それは―――」
「あ、申し訳ありません。
こんな、遠野の家をおとしめるような噂話なんかしちゃって」
「……いや、いいんだ。
もとからその話が聞きたくて来たんだから。
……かまわないから、もう少し詳しい話をしてくれないか、琥珀さん」
「―――槙久さまのお話、をですか？」
　琥珀さんは声のトーンを落としてそう言った。
「………………ん」
　無言で頷く。
　琥珀さんはわずかだけ目を伏せて、それでは、とまっすぐに俺を見つめた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Kohaku, does that mean—”
“Oh, forgive me. I shouldn’t be repeating ugly rumors about the Tohno family.”
“No, it’s all right. This is what I came to ask you about. Please—tell me more, Kohaku.”
“You mean—about Master Makihisa?”
Kohaku’s voice dropped.
“Mm.”
I nodded without another word.
Kohaku lowered her eyes for only a moment, then looked straight at me and said, “Very well.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Kohaku-san, that---"
"Oh, I'm very sorry.
Those are just dark rumors about the Tohno family."
"…… No, that's fine.
That is what I wanted to ask about.
…… If you don't mind, can you continue?"
"---About Makihisa-sama?"
Her tone lowers.
"……………… Yeah."
I nod.
Kohaku-san lowers her eyes, and then looks directly at me.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さん。
朝にもお話しましたが、槙久さまがお亡くなりになる二年前から、わたしは槙久さまの容体を管理させていただいていたんです。
　……志貴さんを有間の家に預けた頃から槙久さまはひどく落ち込むようになってしまわれて、精神を安定させるお薬を服用しなければならなかったんです」
entries.maoEnglish:
“You remember what I told you this morning, Shiki. For the last two years of Master Makihisa’s life, I was put in charge of Master Makihisa’s condition.
Around the time he sent you to live with the Arima family, Master Makihisa fell into a terrible depression and had to take medication to keep his mind stable.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-san.
We spoke about it this morning, but I took care of Makihisa-sama's condition two years before he passed away.
…… While you were living with the Arima family, Makihisa-sama would become very depressed at times and I would have to prepare his medicine."

entries.japanese:
「……ちょっと待って琥珀さん。
朝にもそんな事を言ってたけど、精神を安定させる薬を使うほど親父はひどかったんですか」
「―――はい。
夜になると屋敷の庭を出歩くようになって、その日に買ってきた犬や猫を殺してしまわれたり、ご自分のお体を傷つけたりするのは珍しい事ではなかったほどです。
　そうして、そういった夜が明けた朝には決まって何も覚えていらっしゃらなくて、血に塗れたご自分の手を不思議そうに眺めてらっしゃいました」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Wait. You mentioned that this morning, but was he really ill enough to need medication?”
“Yes. At night he would wander the grounds, and it was not unusual for him to kill dogs or cats he had bought that very day, or to injure himself.
The next morning he would invariably remember nothing, merely staring in bewilderment at his own blood-soaked hands.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Wait.
You said it this morning too, but was he that bad that he had to take medicine?"
"---Yes.
It would not be uncommon for him to walk into the garden at night and kill the pet dogs and cats, or to hurt his own body.
And when the night was over, he wouldn't remember a thing, only thinking that it was strange that his hands were painted in blood."

entries.japanese:
――――な。
　なんだ、それは。
　それじゃほとんど狂ってる。
　ユメのなかの俺みたいに、正気じゃない。
　……いや、それとも。
　俺のほうが、親父みたいに、正気じゃないのか。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――What…?
What the hell was that?
He had practically been insane.
Out of his mind—like me in those dreams.
Or was it the other way around?
Was I the one who was out of his mind, just like him?
entries.mirrorMoon:
----What---
What is this?
That's pretty much crazy.
As crazy as I am in my dreams.
…… No, that is backwards.
Am I crazy just like my old man?

entries.japanese:
「志貴さん……！？」
　……琥珀さんの声が聞こえる。
　俺は―――いつのまにか、畳に膝をついていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Shiki…!?”
Kohaku’s voice reached me.
Somehow, without noticing, I had fallen to my knees on the tatami.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-san……!?"
…… I hear Kohaku-san's voice.
I---I don't know when it happened, but I'm on my knees on the tatami floor.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さん、顔が真っ青じゃないですか！
　体調が悪いのでしたらお部屋で休んでないとダメです……！」
　言いながら、琥珀さんは肩をかしてくれる。
　それに助けられて立ちあがれた。
「……うん……大丈夫、だから―――」
　なんとか意識を整える。
　それでも眩暈は納まらない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Shiki, you’re white as a sheet! If you’re ill, you should be resting in your room…!”
As she spoke, Kohaku offered me her shoulder and helped me back to my feet.
“I’m…
all right.
Really…”
I forced my thoughts into order, but the dizziness refused to pass.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-san, you look terrible.
If you are feeling poorly, you should rest in your room……!"
Kohaku-san says this as she grabs my shoulder.
With her help, I can stand.
"…… Yeah…… I'm fine, so---"
I'm somehow able to focus again.
But I'm still dizzy.

entries.japanese:
乱舞する赤と黒。
　視界は血と夜の色に明暗する。
　さっきまで貧血で暗くなっていた視界が、一転して真っ赤に染まる。
　血を想起させるその色彩。
　無造作に死体の首筋に噛みついた、昨夜の夢。
―――喉に滑り落ちる。
　　　熱い、粘液のような、血の味わい。
entries.maoEnglish:
Red and black wheeled in a frenzy.
My sight pulsed between the colors of blood and night.
My vision, darkened moments ago by anemia, flooded scarlet.
The color of blood.
Last night’s dream, in which I had sunk my teeth carelessly into a corpse’s throat.
―――Something slid down my throat.
The taste of blood, hot and thick as slime.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Swirling red and black.
My vision strobes between blood and night.
The darkness brought about by my anemia now turns into just one sheet of red.
A red reminiscent of blood.
The ease with which I bit the neck of the dead body in last night's dream.
---It slides down my throat.
The taste of warm blood.

entries.japanese:
「――――――――――ぁ」
　ばたん、という音。
　それが自分の倒れた音だという事は、なんとなく理解できた。
「志貴さん――――！？」
　駆け寄ってくる琥珀さん。
「志貴さん、苦しいんですか、志貴さん……！？」
　……いや。
そう苦しくはない、と言おうとして、意識が途絶えかけた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Aah…”
A heavy thud.
Dimly, I understood that it was the sound of my own body hitting the floor.
“Shiki—!?”
Kohaku rushed toward me.
“Shiki, are you in pain, Shiki!?”
I tried to tell her no, that it didn’t hurt that badly. But consciousness almost deserted me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----------Ah."
Thud.
Somehow, I understand that was the sound of my body hitting the floor.
"Shiki-san----!?"
Kohaku-san dashes towards me.
"Shiki-san, are you in pain?
Shiki-san……!?"
…… No.
It doesn't hurt.
I want to tell her, but my consciousness is fading.

entries.japanese:
「……………………」
　声が出せない。
　指先も動かない。
　なにか余分な事をすれば、それだけで意識が刈り取られてしまいそうだった。
　畳に倒れたまま、明暗する意識を必死に支える。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
No voice came.
I couldn’t move so much as a fingertip.
The slightest unnecessary movement felt as though it would snuff out what little consciousness I had left.
Sprawled on the tatami, I fought desperately to keep the light from going out.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……………………"
I can't speak.
I can't even move a finger.
It seems that if I exert myself even the slightest bit, I'll completely lose consciousness.
Collapsed on the floor, I try as hard as I can to resist the coming darkness.

entries.japanese:
「―――無理はしないで。
このまま、少し横になっていてください」
　琥珀さんの声がする。
　そのままスウ、と。
　琥珀さんの手が俺の頭を抱いて、とん、と枕らしき物の上に乗せてくれた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Don’t strain yourself. Just lie still for a while.”
Kohaku’s voice.
Then something moved softly beneath me.
Her hands cradled my head and settled it, gently, on what felt like a pillow.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Don't strain yourself, please lie down."
Kohaku-san speaks to me.
She slides me over.
With one hand holding my head, Kohaku-san slides a pillow underneath me.

entries.japanese:
「……どうぞ、このままでいてください。
こうしていれば血の気が引いてくれるでしょう？」
「…………………ん」
　琥珀さんの声は、すごく近くから聞こえた。
　それで、なんとなく。
　自分が琥珀さんに膝枕をしてもらっている事が解ってしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Please stay like this. It should help the blood drain from your head.”
“Mm…”
Her voice came from very close by.
Slowly, I understood.
The pillow beneath my head was Kohaku’s lap.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Please relax.
This will help the blood to flow, right?"
"………………… Nn."
Her voice sounds so close.
I piece together my situation.
It seems I am resting on her lap.

entries.japanese:
……静かに時間が流れていく。
　お互いなにも会話はない。
　その沈黙が、今の自分には心地良かった。
entries.maoEnglish:
Time passed in silence.
Neither of us spoke.
In my present state, that silence was comforting.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… The time passes quietly.
Neither of us say anything.
Right now, that silence relaxes my heart.

entries.japanese:
「……静かだな。
こうしていると、なんだか……ひどく懐かしい、気分になる」
　横になったまま、ぼんやりと畳を見つめる。
　琥珀さんは頷いたあと、投げ出された俺の手の脈を診た。
entries.maoEnglish:
“It’s so quiet. Lying here like this makes me terribly nostalgic.”
Still on my side, I gazed vaguely at the tatami.
Kohaku nodded, then took the wrist lying loose at my side and checked my pulse.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… It's so quiet.
For some reason…… this seems so familiar."
Lying down on my side, I stare at the tatami mat floor.
After nodding, Kohaku-san checks my pulse.

entries.japanese:
「うーん、ちょっとまずいですね。
志貴さん、体温が下がったまま戻らないようですから、お薬をとってきます」
「いや、別に大丈夫。
こういうのならもう慣れっこだからさ、もうすぐ血の巡りがよくなるってわかるんだ。
今回はいつもより辛かったけど、もうじきに良くなってくれる。
……だから、このままでいてくれないか。
そのほうが安心できる」
　まだこうしていたくて、そんな事を口にした。
　そういう事でしたら、と琥珀さんは留まってくれた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hmm, this isn’t good. Your temperature still hasn’t recovered, Shiki, so I’ll fetch some medicine.”
“No, I’m all right. I’m used to this, and I can tell my circulation will pick up again soon. This spell was worse than usual, but it will pass. So please, could you stay like this? I feel safer with you here.”
I said it because I wasn’t ready for this to end.
Kohaku said she would stay if that was what I wanted.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Well, this isn't good.
Shiki-san, your body temperature has fallen.
I should go back and bring you some medicine."
"No, I'm fine.
I'm used to this, so I'll be fine soon.
Today was a little harder than before, but I'll be alright.
…… So can we stay like this a little longer?
I can relax better like this."
I tell her that, wanting to stay like this a little longer.
"In that case", Kohaku-san says as she stays in place.

entries.japanese:
――――――――――そうして。
「志貴さんは恐くはないんですか？」
　そう、琥珀さんが問うてきた。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――――――――And then…
“Aren’t you afraid, Shiki?”
That was what Kohaku asked me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----------And then.
"Shiki-san, you are not scared?"
Kohaku-san asks me this.

entries.japanese:
「……え？
　恐いって、なにが？」
「志貴さんのお体の事です。
わたし、志貴さんがお屋敷に帰ってくる二日ほど前、主治医の方から志貴さんの診断書を受け取ったんです。
その時は驚いたというより、騙されているのかなあって思いました」
「？
　騙されてるって、どうして」
「どうしても何もないです。
志貴さんは再生不良性貧血に極めて近い症状なのに、普通の人と同じように生活しているんですもの。
本来ならずっと病院のベッドの上なんですよ、志貴さんは」
　それは心配というより、何か、こう……怒っているような、そんな声だったと思う。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Afraid? Of what?”
“Of your own body, Shiki. Two days before you returned to the mansion, I received your medical report from your physician. I wasn’t so much shocked as convinced someone must be playing a joke on me.”
“Why would you think that?” “Why wouldn’t I?
There is no why. Your symptoms are almost indistinguishable from aplastic anemia, yet you live as though you were perfectly healthy. By rights, you should spend your whole life in a hospital bed.”
She sounded less worried than angry, somehow.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Eh?
Of what?"
"About your health.
About two days before you returned here, I received all your information from the doctor.
I was not surprised, but felt more like he was deceiving me."
"?
Deceiving you?
Why?"
"Because you are so close to wavering between life and death, but you can live a normal life.
Normally, with a condition like yours, you would be confined to bed."
That voice seems not so much full of worry, but more…… full of anger, almost.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さんは普通の人とは違います。
眠ったら、次の日の朝に当たり前のように目覚める、なんて断言できない体なんです。
なのに普通に暮らしていて、そんな自分を恐れてもいない。
　……それが、わたしには解らない。
　聞かせてください。
どうして、志貴さんは怖くはないんですか」
entries.maoEnglish:
“You aren’t like other people, Shiki. You can’t go to sleep certain that you’ll wake the next morning as a matter of course. And yet you live an ordinary life without seeming frightened of yourself at all.
I don’t understand that.
Please tell me. Why aren’t you afraid, Shiki?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-san, you're different from most people, who can rest assured at night that they'll wake up the next morning.
But you still live normally and do not have fear.
…… I can't understand it.
Please answer me.
Why are you not scared?"

entries.japanese:
「…………………」
　その質問は、うまく答えられない。
　死にやすい体。
　いつも身近にある死。
　……死が視えるという現実。
　その事実に、ただ、俺は麻痺しているだけなのかもしれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
I had no good answer.
A body that died too easily.
Death forever close at hand.
The simple fact that I could see death.
Maybe I had merely grown numb to it all.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…………………"
I can't come up with a good answer.
My weak body.
The death that's always close.
…… My eyes that can see death.
Maybe that's why I'm just numb to it.

entries.japanese:
「さあ。
きっと実感がわかないだけなんじゃないかな、俺は」
「……解りません。
志貴さんは死というものを感じていないんですか。
　それともいつ死んでしまってもおかしくない体だから、生きているという事にさえ、関心がないんですか」
「……どうだろうね。
ただ確かに、他の人より死という事柄について、俺は不感症なのかもしれない。
　なまじ敏感でそれなりに視えてしまうと、それも日常になってしまうんだ。
だから、俺は開き直っているだけなのかもしれない」
entries.maoEnglish:
“I don’t know. Maybe it just doesn’t feel real to me.”
“I don’t understand, Shiki. Can’t you feel what death means?
Or, because you could die at any moment, have you stopped caring whether you’re alive?”
“I’m not sure. I may be more numb to death than most people.
When you’re sensitive enough to see it everywhere, even death becomes part of ordinary life. Maybe I’ve simply resigned myself to that.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Who knows?
Maybe I just don't feel it as being real."
"…… I don't get it.
Do you not feel how close death is?
Or is it because your body could die at any moment so living does not concern you?"
"…… It's hard to say.
Maybe I'm desensitized to death.
Being sensitive and seeing it that close every day, it just becomes normal."

entries.japanese:
「……それでも確かに言える事はね、琥珀さん。
　俺はいつも死と隣り合わせだから、以前より強く生を実感しているんだ。
生きている、という事はそれだけで幸運なんだって解ってる。
　琥珀さんの言うとおり、俺の体はあんまり俺の自由になってくれない。
……けど、そんな人形のような体だからこそ、こんなふうに話ができる今が素晴らしい事だって信じたいんだ」
　……そう。
　自分の体をどうこう思うより、こうしていられる事を大事にしたい。
　いつ死ぬかなんて恐れる暇があるんなら、少しでも、こうしていられる事を大切にするべきなんだろうから。
entries.maoEnglish:
“But there is one thing I know, Kohaku.
Because death is always beside me, I feel life more keenly than I used to. I know that merely being alive is an incredible stroke of luck.
You’re right—my body hardly ever obeys me. But precisely because it’s like a doll, I want to believe that a moment like this, when I can lie here talking to you, is something wonderful.”
Yes.
What mattered wasn’t what I thought of my body, but treasuring the time it still gave me.
If I had time to fear when death might come, I ought to spend it cherishing every moment I could remain like this.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… But I can still say this, Kohaku-san.
Since I'm so close to death all the time, I can feel life more strongly.
I know that living itself is happiness.
Like you said, my body isn't that free.
…… But, with such a puppet-like body, I want to believe that even talking right now is such a wonderful thing."
…… That's right.
More than thinking about my body, I want to treasure the present.
If I have time to worry about dying, I should be enjoying the present more.

entries.japanese:
「……そう。
自由なんですね、志貴さんの心は」
　静かに、歌うような呟きのあと。
　琥珀さんの指が、優しく俺の髪を撫でた。
「―――――琥珀さん？」
　視線を上げる。
　そこには―――
　―――とても穏やかな、彼女の笑顔があった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I see. Your heart is free, Shiki.”
Her murmur was quiet, almost songlike.
Then Kohaku’s fingers began to stroke my hair.
“Kohaku…?”
I raised my eyes.
Above me—
―――was her smile, quiet and infinitely gentle.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I see.
Your heart is free, isn't it?"
Quietly, as if she's singing, Kohaku-san says this to herself.
Her fingers run through my hair gently.
"-----Kohaku-san?"
I look up.
I see---
---her smiling very peacefully.

entries.japanese:
見慣れているはずの琥珀さんの笑顔。
　なのに、初めて。
　この人の笑顔を、見ている気がする。
entries.maoEnglish:
A smile I ought to have seen a thousand times.
And yet this felt like the first.
I felt as though I were truly seeing her smile.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Her smile that I should be so used to seeing.
But it seems like it's the first time,
the first time I've ever seen her smile.

entries.japanese:
「…………………」
　……ただ時間だけが流れていく。
　軽く髪を撫でる彼女の指先。
　膝から伝わってくる確かな体温。
　懐かしい畳の匂い。
　その全てがあまりにも心地よくて、目蓋がゆっくりと落ちていく。
　……温かな琥珀の眼差し。
　それを受けたまま眠れるのなら、それはどんなに―――
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
Time alone drifted on.
Her fingertips lightly combing my hair.
The sure warmth of her lap.
The familiar scent of tatami.
It was all so soothing that my eyelids slowly sank.
Kohaku’s warm gaze rested on me.
If I could fall asleep beneath it, how wonderful that would be―――
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……………………"
…… Time just passes by.
She lightly runs her fingers through my hair.
I feel the warmth of her body from her legs.
The nostalgic smell of the tatami mats.
It's all so comforting, my eyelids slowly start to close.
…… She has such a gentle look on her face.
If I can sleep like this, it would be---

entries.japanese:
「……なんだか―――」
　本当に、このまま。
「……初めて、琥珀さんの笑顔を見たような、気がする」
　眠りに、落ちてしまいそう。
「そうですか？
　志貴さん、寝ぼけてらっしゃいますね」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Somehow—”
Truly, just like this.
“I feel as though this is the first time I’ve ever seen you smile.”
I was about to slip into sleep.
“Do you? You must be half asleep, Shiki.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… That's funny---"
Really, like this.
"…… I feel like, this is the first time, I've seen you smile, Kohaku-san."
I feel like I'm falling asleep.
"Is that right?
Shiki-san, you must be really sleepy."

entries.japanese:
「……いいよ。
それで琥珀さんが喜んでくれるなら、それで――――」
　それでこの人が笑ってくれるのなら、いくらでもこうしていたい。
　……仄暗い和室の中。
　ただ、もっと近くに琥珀さんを感じたくて手を伸ばす。
entries.maoEnglish:
“That’s fine. If it makes you happy, then――――”
If it would make her smile, I could stay this way forever.
In the dim tatami room.
I reached out, wanting only to feel Kohaku a little closer.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… That's fine.
If you're happy, then---"
If this makes her smile, I want to do this forever.
…… In the middle of this dark room.
I want to feel her closer to me and I reach out my hand.

entries.japanese:
「……志貴さん……？」
　指が触れた。
　彼女の頬をなぞるように指を当てる。
　きめ細かな肌に触れた指は、そのまま琥珀の髪に絡まって、そのまま―――!w3000
「―――琥珀、先に来てるの？」
　勢いよく障子が開いて、秋葉が和室に入ってきた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Shiki…?”
My fingers found her.
They traced the curve of her cheek.
From the fine softness of her skin they slipped into Kohaku’s hair, tangled there, and then—!w3000
“Kohaku, are you already here?”
The shoji flew open, and Akiha strode into the room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Shiki-san……?"
My fingers touch her.
My fingers trace the lines of her face.
They brush her smooth skin, and reach her hair, then---
"---Kohaku, you came here ahead of me?"
Vigorously opening the screen door, Akiha enters the room.

entries.japanese:
「な――――――――」
　ビクン、と。
　琥珀さんの指が、凍った。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What――――――――”
Kohaku’s fingers jerked.
Then they froze.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Wha--------"
Kohaku-san's fingers suddenly stop moving.

entries.japanese:
「――――何をしてるの、あなたたち」
　感情のない秋葉の声。
「あ、秋葉……！？
　ちが、これは誤解だって……！」
　慌てて立ちあがって、待てよ、と落ち着いた。
　別に誤解も破戒も奇奇怪怪もないんだ。
　俺と琥珀さんはやましい事なんてしていないんだし、琥珀さんは倒れた俺を看病していただけなんだから。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What are the two of you doing?”
Akiha’s voice was utterly without emotion.
“A-Akiha…!? No, you’ve got the wrong idea…!”
I scrambled upright, then stopped myself.
There was no misunderstanding, wrongdoing, or anything bizarre about this.
Kohaku had only been caring for me after I collapsed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----What are you two doing?"
Akiha's emotionless voice.
"A, Akiha……!?
This, it's not what you think……!"
I stand up in a hurry.
I'll just tell her to calm down.
There's nothing wrong, or anything suspicious.
We haven't done anything, and all Kohaku-san did was watch over me after I collapsed.

entries.japanese:
「ちょっと待った秋葉。
今のは単に、俺が倒れたもんだから琥珀さんが―――」
　と、俺が言いきる前に。
　秋葉は琥珀さんを睨みつけ、和室に足を踏み入れた。
　そのあと。
　パン、と乾いた音が、響いた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hold on, Akiha. I only collapsed, and Kohaku was―――”
Before I could finish.
Akiha fixed Kohaku with a glare and stepped into the room.
Then.
A dry crack rang out.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Wait, Akiha.
I just collapsed, so Kohaku-san was---"
It's over before I can finish.
Akiha stares at Kohaku-san and enters.
It's only a moment after.
Slap!
The dry sound echoes through the room.

entries.japanese:
「なっ…………」
　止める間も、なかった。
　秋葉は琥珀さんに歩み寄ると、そのまま、ためらわずに琥珀さんの頬に平手打ちをしたのだ。
　よほど力がこもっていたのか、琥珀さんは数歩よろめいている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What…?”
I had no time to stop her.
Akiha walked straight up to Kohaku and slapped her across the face without the slightest hesitation.
The blow must have carried tremendous force; Kohaku staggered several steps.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Wha………"
There wasn't even time to stop it.
Akiha just walked in and slapped her.
Kohaku-san takes a few steps back.
It must've been pretty hard.

entries.japanese:
「秋葉、おまえ――――！」
「兄さん、ここは立ち入り禁止です。
お体がよくなったのならすぐに屋敷に戻ってください」
「っ……！
　そんな事どうでもいいっ！
　おまえ、なんで琥珀さんに手を上げたんだ！」
「当然でしょう。
ここは老朽化が進んでいる建物です。
そんな所で兄さんを休ませるなんて何を考えているんだか」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Akiha, you—!”
“Brother, this building is off limits. If you’ve recovered, return to the mansion at once.”
“What…!? Who cares about that? Why did you hit her?”
“It was only natural. This building is falling apart. What was she thinking, letting you rest in a place like this?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Akiha, you----!"
"Nii-san, this place is off limits.
If you are feeling well, please go back to the mansion."
"……!
I don't care about that!
Why'd you hit her!?"
"Why not?
This is an old, decrepit building.
What was she thinking, having you rest here?"

entries.japanese:
「そ、そんな事ぐらいで手を上げるのかおまえは！
　琥珀さんは俺の事を気遣ってくれただけじゃないか！」
「―――そんな事？
　そんな事ってどんな事ですか、兄さん。
　この建物はいつ崩れてもおかしくない物です。
もし兄さんが休まれていた時、大きな地震が起きていたら天井が崩れていたかもしれない。
そんな危険な場所で遠野家の長男を介抱するなんて、使用人としての気遣いが足りない証拠です」
entries.maoEnglish:
“You hit her over that!? Kohaku was only trying to help me!”
“Over that? What exactly do you mean by ‘that,’ Brother?
This building could collapse at any time. If a strong earthquake had struck while you were lying here, the ceiling might have come down on you. Nursing the eldest son of the Tohno family in such a dangerous place shows an inexcusable lack of judgment in a servant.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Just for that?
She was just taking care of me!"
"---Just that?
What do you mean, Nii-san?
It would not be surprising if this place collapses.
An earthquake could cause the ceiling to collapse.
To take care of the eldest son of the Tohno household in such a place means she doesn't have the discretion proper for a servant."

entries.japanese:
「秋葉……！
　おまえ、言っていい事と悪い事があるぞ。
琥珀さんは何も悪くない。
　ここだって、俺のほうから琥珀さんを呼んだんだから！」
「―――そう。
そんなに琥珀を庇うっていうんですか、兄さんは」
　秋葉の視線が鋭くなる。
「―――――――――」
　それは、あの夢に出てきた秋葉に、似ていた。
　悪意や憎悪に近い視線。
　そんなものを―――現実として秋葉に向けられている、悪夢。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Akiha…! There are some things you have no right to say. Kohaku did nothing wrong.
I’m the one who asked her to meet me here!”
“I see. So you intend to defend Kohaku that fiercely, Brother.”
Akiha’s gaze sharpened.
“…”
She looked like the Akiha from my dream.
A gaze close to malice, close to hatred.
A nightmare in which Akiha was turning such a look on me—not in a dream, but in reality.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Akiha……!
There's some things you shouldn't say.
Kohaku-san didn't do anything wrong.
I was the one that called her here anyway!"
"---Oh?
You're going this far to protect Kohaku, Nii-san?"
Her gaze sharpens.
"---------"
She looks just like she did in that dream.
A gaze that looks close to malice and hatred.
In front of me---in reality, there's a nightmarish Akiha.

entries.japanese:
「え――――――――？」
　ギリ、と血脈が搾られた。
　目の錯覚か。
一瞬、秋葉の周りに、何か―――よくないモノが、視えた気がした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What…?”
Something clenched tight around my veins.
A trick of the eye? For one instant, I thought I saw something—something wrong—around Akiha.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Eh--------?"
My pulse tightens.
Was I hallucinating?
For an instant, around Akiha---I thought that I saw something terrible.

entries.japanese:
「――――わかりました。
兄さんがそうおっしゃるのでしたら、私からは何も言いません。
　ですが兄さん。
今後は決してここには近づかないでください。
それさえ守れないようでしたら、私にも考えがありますから」
―――やはり目の錯覚だったのか、秋葉に異常らしきものはない。
　ただ、どうしてか、今の秋葉を見ていると危うい感じがして、不安になる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Very well. If that is what you insist, Brother, I have nothing more to say.
But, Brother. You must never come near this place again. If you cannot obey even that, I have measures of my own.”
―――Perhaps it really had been an illusion, for there was nothing visibly wrong with Akiha.
Even so, something about her now seemed precarious, and the sight of her filled me with unease.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----I understand.
If you say that, then I will not say anything else.
But, Nii-san.
From now on, please do not come here.
If you can not even do that, then I have some ideas, too."
---It must have been an illusion.
There isn't anything strange around her.
But why?
The danger I feel from her makes me uneasy.

entries.japanese:
「戻るわよ琥珀。
兄さんもすぐに部屋に戻ることね」
　……そうして、秋葉は立ち去った。
「琥珀さん」
　……秋葉に叩かれて、俯いたままの琥珀さんに声をかける。
entries.maoEnglish:
“We’re going back, Kohaku. Brother, return to your room immediately.”
With that, Akiha left.
“Kohaku.”
I called to Kohaku, who still stood with her head bowed after Akiha’s slap.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"We're going back, Kohaku.
Nii-san, go back to your room."
…… Akiha walks away.
"Kohaku-san."
…… I call out to Kohaku-san, who is still looking down.

entries.japanese:
「琥珀さん……？
　あの、大丈夫……？」
「はい？
　大丈夫って、なにがですか？」
　けろりと。
　いつもの笑顔で、琥珀さんは顔をあげた。
　……それは強がりとか、空元気といった笑顔じゃない。
　この人は本当に笑っている。
　秋葉に叩かれた事が、まるでなかった事のように。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Kohaku…? Are you all right?”
“What? What do you mean, all right?”
Without a care in the world.
Kohaku looked up with her usual smile.
It wasn’t bravado or forced cheer.
She truly was smiling.
It was as though Akiha had never struck her at all.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Kohaku-san……?
Are, you alright……?"
"Yes?
Alright about what?"
She says this casually.
With her usual smile, she looks up.
…… That isn't a forced, empty smile.
She really is smiling.
As if Akiha never even hit her.

entries.japanese:
「……いや、何って、その―――」
「それでは志貴さん、お屋敷に戻りましょうか。
秋葉さまにも見つかってしまいましたし、もうこの離れに来ちゃダメですよ。
　秋葉さま、本気で志貴さんを矯正しかねませんからねー」
　あはは、と冗談を言って、琥珀さんは和室を後にする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“No, what I mean is―――”
“Then shall we return to the mansion, Shiki? Miss Akiha found us, so you mustn’t come to the annex again.
Miss Akiha might seriously try to reform you, you know.”
Kohaku laughed off her own joke and left the room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Um, well, that---"
"Well then, Shiki-san.
Let's go back.
Akiha-sama found out, so you shouldn't come back here again.
Akiha-sama would really punish you for sure."
"Ahaha," laughing at her own joke, she leaves the room.

entries.japanese:
「―――――――――」
　秋葉も秋葉なら、琥珀さんも琥珀さんでどこか普通じゃなかったせいだろうか。
　俺は二人のように、すぐには屋敷に戻る事ができなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
Perhaps it was because neither Akiha nor Kohaku had seemed quite normal.
Whatever the reason, I couldn’t follow them back to the mansion right away.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---------"
It's probably because both of them are acting strange.
I can't go back right away.

entries.japanese:
食堂で一人で夕食を済ませて部屋に戻ってきた。
　秋葉はまだ体調が悪いらしく、部屋で夕食を摂った。
　……琥珀さんは、やっぱりいつも通りの明るさで俺の夕食を作ってくれて、秋葉の世話をしているみたいだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
I ate dinner alone in the dining room and returned to my room.
Akiha still seemed unwell and took her meal upstairs.
Kohaku, as bright as ever, had prepared my dinner and apparently gone on to tend to Akiha.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I eat dinner alone and go back to my room.
I guess Akiha was still feeling poorly because she wasn't there.
…… Kohaku-san made me dinner with her usual cheery mood and then went to take care of Akiha.

entries.japanese:
「………琥珀さん、気まずくないのかな」
　少なくとも琥珀さんは秋葉に不満はないようだった。
　翡翠は朝の一件から気を取り直したのか、とりあえず俺の世話をしてくれていた。
　……翡翠は気を取り直すのに半日かかったわけだから、琥珀さんは翡翠より精神面で強い人なのかもしれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Doesn’t Kohaku feel awkward at all…?”
At the very least, she seemed to bear Akiha no resentment.
Hisui, meanwhile, had recovered from that morning’s incident enough to resume looking after me.
It had taken Hisui half a day to pull herself together, so perhaps Kohaku was simply much stronger than her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I wonder if Kohaku-san is feeling uneasy."
It would seem that Kohaku-san doesn't resent Akiha at all.
It seems like Hisui is over what happened this morning and is taking care of me.
…… Hisui took half a day to get over it, so maybe Kohaku-san is a lot stronger.

entries.japanese:
「――――――――」
　ベッドに横になって、はあ、と大きくため息をした。
　……疲れているんだろうか。
　最近は夜になると、すぐにベッドに倒れこんでしまう。
　色々と考えなくてはいけない事がある筈なのに、そんな事は自分には関係のない事のような気がして、すぐに眠ろうとしてしまう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
I lay on the bed and let out a long breath.
Was I tired?
Lately I collapsed onto the bed as soon as night came.
There ought to have been so many things to think about, yet they all felt as though they belonged to someone else, and all I wanted was sleep.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"--------"
Lying down on my bed, I let out a big sigh.
…… I must be tired.
Recently, as soon as night falls, I've been falling into bed.
Even though there are a lot of things I should think about, I feel like nothing concerns me and try to go to sleep.

entries.japanese:
「……おかしいな。
こんなに集中力がなかったっけ、俺――――」
　天井を眺めながら、ぼんやりと口にする。
　うっすらと目蓋が閉じていく。
　結局、今夜も何一つ疑問に思う事なく、深い眠りに落ちていった――――
entries.maoEnglish:
“Something’s wrong. Was I always this bad at concentrating…?”
I murmured vaguely at the ceiling.
My eyelids drifted shut.
And once again that night, without questioning a single thing, I sank into a deep sleep――――
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… That's odd.
I can't concentrate----"
I stare at the ceiling.
My eyes start to close.
Again, I don't think about anything and fall into a deep sleep----

entries.maoEnglish: ――――Burning.
entries.mirrorMoon: ----Burning.

entries.maoEnglish: ――――Burning.
entries.mirrorMoon: ----Burning.

entries.maoEnglish: ――――Burning.
entries.mirrorMoon: ----Burning.

entries.japanese: ――――肌が、チリチリと焦げて、灼い。
entries.maoEnglish: ――――My skin crackles and chars with burning heat.
entries.mirrorMoon: ----My skin is burning.

entries.japanese:
――――このままでは眠れない。
　　　　起きて、水を飲みに行かないと。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――I can’t sleep like this.
I have to get up and find water.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----I can't sleep like this.
I have to get up and drink some water.

entries.japanese:
夜の街。
　はぁはぁと熱っぽい吐息を繰り返して、通りを歩いていく人たちを見る。
　今夜にかぎって二人や三人といった人しかいない。
　できれば、一人きりの、自分と同い年の女の子がほしかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
The city at night.
I watch the people passing through the streets, my breath feverish and ragged.
Tonight, of all nights, everyone seems to be walking in twos and threes.
What I want is a girl alone—someone my own age.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The city at night.
Repeating my hot breathing, I look at the people passing by.
There are only two or three of them tonight.
If possible, I want to find a lone girl who is about my age.

entries.maoEnglish: ―――Hot.
entries.mirrorMoon: ---Hot.

entries.japanese:
ふと、窓ガラスに映った顔が見えた。
　呼吸は乱れて、まるで四十度ぐらいの熱病にうなされているみたい。
entries.maoEnglish:
My face catches suddenly in a shop window.
My breathing is wild, as though I were delirious with a forty-degree fever.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I see my reflection in the mirror.
Breathing wildly, it looks like I'm running a high fever.

entries.japanese: ―――あつ――こんなに灼いと、堪えきれない。
entries.maoEnglish: ―――Hot—this heat is more than I can bear.
entries.mirrorMoon: ---Hot--I can't stand this burning.

entries.japanese:
……いた。
　こちらから近づく必要なんかない。
　後ろから少女を引き寄せて、そのまま気を失わせた。
　ずるり、と音をたてて、少女の体を運んでくる。
―――なんか、笑ってしまう。
　ちゃんと、今まで我慢してきたのに、それもこれでおしまいになってしまったんだから。
entries.maoEnglish:
There.
No need to approach her from the front.
I pull the girl against me from behind and knock her unconscious.
Her body drags along with a wet, scraping sound.
―――It almost makes me laugh.
I had held myself in check all this time, and now that is over.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… There.
I don't need to get any closer.
I grab her from behind and make her pass out.
I pick her up and take her with me.
---I start to smile.
I endured it for so long, and now everything is over.

entries.japanese:
……結局、ここですることにした。
　理由は簡単。
　だって、ここが殺人鬼の根城だったから。
entries.maoEnglish:
In the end, I decide to do it here.
The reason is simple.
This is the murderer’s lair.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… I decide to do it here in the end.
The reason is simple.
Because, this was the killer's lair.

entries.maoEnglish: ―――Burning.
entries.mirrorMoon: ---Burning.

entries.japanese:
はあはあという呼吸音。
　もうすぐ。
　もうすぐ、この子を口にできる。
entries.maoEnglish:
The rasp of panting.
Soon.
Soon I can feed on this girl.
entries.mirrorMoon:
My breathing fills the air.
Soon.
Soon I can taste her.

entries.japanese:
そうして、食事を始めた。
　首筋に口をつけて、血液を吸い上げる。
entries.maoEnglish:
Then the meal begins.
I press my mouth to her throat and draw out the blood.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Then I start my meal.
Biting into her neck, I suck the blood.

entries.japanese: ―――なんて、甘い。
entries.maoEnglish: ―――So sweet.
entries.mirrorMoon: ---It is unbelievably sweet.

entries.japanese:
その感覚は本当に恐ろしかった。
　こんなに甘くて、こんなに気持ちがいいのなら。
　きっと、自分はあの殺人鬼のかわりに、この感覚の虜になると予感してしまったからだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
That sensation was truly terrifying.
If it could be this sweet and feel this good.
Then I knew that it—not the murderer—would make me its slave.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The sensation is really terrifying.
If it is this sweet and feels this good,
I may just become a captive to this sensation, in place of that killer.

entries.japanese:
―――夜が深い。
頭上には罪を咎める銀の瞳。
entries.maoEnglish: ―――The night is deep. Overhead hangs a silver eye that condemns my sin.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---The night is deep.
Above my head is the silver eye bearing witness to my sin.

entries.japanese:
熱い血液で唇をぬらして、恍惚とした目で、夜空を見上げていた。
　髪が乱れる。
　頭上には螺旋の空。
　なんてキレイな、銀色の月。
entries.maoEnglish:
Hot blood wetting my lips, I gaze at the night sky in rapture.
My hair tumbles loose.
Above me, the heavens turn in a spiral.
What a beautiful silver moon.
entries.mirrorMoon:
With blood-smeared lips, I look up at the night sky with eyes full of amusement.
Fluttering hair.
Above is the spiraling sky.
What a beautiful, silver moon.

entries.japanese:
―――蛇の如く。
血を吸う鬼を、見つめている。
entries.maoEnglish: ―――Like a snake. It watches the blood-drinking fiend.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Like a snake.
Watching the blood-sucking demon.

entries.japanese:
「――――――！」
　たまらず、ベッドから跳ね起きた。
「あ―――はあ、は――――あ」
　込み上げてくる吐き気を堪えてケモノのような息吹をあげる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“—!”
I could bear no more and sprang upright in bed.
“Ah―――hah, ha――――ah”
Fighting down the nausea surging through me, I panted like an animal.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------!"
I leap out of bed, unable to take it any longer.
"Ah---haa, ha----ah."
Holding back the urge to vomit, I breathe like some sort of animal.

entries.japanese:
「な――――――」
　なんだ、今のは。
　夢。
夢を見てた。
けど、今のはなんだ。
　二日前に見たおかしな夢とは違う。
　夜の街を歩く感覚。
　鼻腔に残る血の匂い。
　ずるずると。
自分と同い年の女の子を引きずっていた音。
―――その全てが、はっきりと記憶として残っている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What――――――”
What had that been?
A dream. I had been dreaming. But what had that been?
Nothing like the strange one from two days ago.
The sensation of walking through the city at night.
The smell of blood still lodged in my nose.
Dragging. The sound of a girl my own age scraping along behind me.
―――Every detail remained with the clarity of a real memory.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Wha------"
What was that just now?
A dream.
It was a dream.
But, what was that?
It's different than what I saw two days ago.
The feeling of walking the streets at night.
The smell of blood lingering in my nose.
The sound of dragging that girl who was close to my age.
---All of it is fresh in my memory.

entries.japanese:
「は、あ――――――」
　あれは快感と呼ばれるモノだったのだろうか。
　弾丸のように凝縮された興奮が、耳元からトリガーをひいて脳髄に叩き込まれたような衝撃だけがあった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hah…”
Could that have been what people called pleasure?
There had only been the impact: excitement compressed into a bullet, its trigger pulled beside my ear, firing it straight through my brain.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ha, ah-------"
Was that something you could call pleasure?
It was pure excitement condensed like a bullet, fired straight into my head.

entries.japanese:
「ぐ―――っ」
　思い出しただけで息が止まる。
　なら―――あの衝撃は、やはり『快感』と呼べるものだったのかもしれない。
「俺は―――なんて、夢を」
　自らの両手を見る。
　当然、自分の手は真っ白で血の赤色なんて微塵もない。
　なのに一瞬だけ。
　自分の両手が、真っ赤に染まっているように、見えた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ghh…!”
The memory alone stopped my breath.
Then perhaps that impact truly had been what people called ‘pleasure.’
“What kind of dream―――”
I stared at my hands.
Naturally, they were bloodless and pale, without the faintest trace of red.
Yet, for one instant.
I saw both hands stained scarlet.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"G---"
My breathing stops just thinking about it.
Then… perhaps that impact could be something called "pleasure".

"Why did I… that kind of dream…"
I look down at my hands.
Of course, they are pure white, without a trace of red blood on them.
But, for an instant,
I saw both of my hands covered in red.

entries.japanese:
―――なんだ、おまえは同類か。
　……あれ。
―――自分以外の殺人鬼なんて、初めて見たぜ。
　……ああ、確かにそんな話をした。
―――同じ街に殺人鬼は二人はいらない。
　　　ここは、おまえに譲ってやるよ
　……ただ、それは、いつのコトだったろうか。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――So you’re one of my kind.
Wait…
―――You’re the first murderer I’ve ever met besides myself.
Yes, I had certainly had a conversation like that.
―――One city doesn’t need two murderers.
I’ll leave this place to you
But when had that conversation taken place?
entries.mirrorMoon:
---What, you too?
…… Huh?
---This is the first time I've seen another killer besides myself.
…… That's right.
I did have that conversation.
---The same city doesn't need two killers.
I'll give you this place.
…… But, when was that?

entries.japanese:
「……なんで……思い、出せない――――？」
　確かに、俺は誰かとそんな話をした気がする。
　けどまったく思い出せない。
　それが現実の事だったのか、それともやっぱり空ろな夢だったのか。
　ただはっきりと、殺人鬼っていうヤツが、俺の事を同類と呼んでいた事だけが思い出せる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Why…
can’t I remember…?”
I felt certain I had had a conversation like that with someone, but I couldn’t recover a single detail.
Had it happened in reality, or in another hollow dream?
All I could remember clearly was that a murderer had called me one of his own kind.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Why, can't I remember----?"
Certainly, I feel like I had that conversation with someone.
But I just can't remember.
Was it real, or was it just an empty dream?
I just remember that the killer said I was the same as him.

entries.japanese:
「―――おかしいぞ、おい……なんでこう……頭の中が、ぐちゃぐちゃに、なってるんだ――――」
　必死に昨夜の夢を思い出そうとする。
「がっ――――！？」
　ガン、と音がしそうなぐらいの頭痛。
「はっ―――ぁ、はっ…………！」
　思い、出せない。
　無理に昨日の事を思い出そうとすると、吐き気がする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“This is wrong—why is everything in my head such a mess――――”
I fought to recall last night’s dream.
“Gah—!?”
Pain slammed through my skull hard enough to make a sound.
“Hah―――ah, hah…………!”
I couldn’t remember.
Every attempt to force yesterday back into my mind made me want to vomit.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---That's strange.
…… Why is it…… all mixed up in my head----"
I earnestly try hard to remember about last night's dream.
"Ga----!?"
My head pounds.
"Agh---ah, agh………!"
I can't, remember.
When I try to remember about yesterday, I feel the urge to vomit.

entries.japanese:
怖い。
　思い出せないという事は、怖い。
　なんだかそれは。
　俺の知らない遠野志貴が人殺しをして、その事実を隠すために、俺という遠野志貴を、騙している、よう。
――――と。
　廊下のほうで、人の気配を感じ取った。
「誰だ――――！？」
　声をかける。
entries.maoEnglish:
I was afraid.
There was nothing more frightening than being unable to remember.
It felt something like this.
Another Shiki Tohno, one I knew nothing about, had murdered someone—and was deceiving the Shiki Tohno I knew in order to conceal the crime.
――――Then.
I sensed someone in the corridor.
“Who’s there!?”
I called out.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I'm scared.
I'm scared of the fact that I can't remember.
It feels like…
A Tohno Shiki I don't know is killing people, and in order to hide it, is deceiving the Tohno Shiki that is me.
----And.
I sense someone in the hallway.
"Who's there----!?"
I call out.

entries.japanese:
コンコン、というノックの音がした。
　失礼します、と翡翠が部屋に入ってくる。
　それはいつも通りの、なんていう事はない朝の光景だった。
「あ―――――――――」
　翡翠の姿があまりにも自然だったからなのか。
　ドクドクとリズムを乱していた心臓は、あっけないぐらい静かになってくれた。
entries.maoEnglish:
A quiet knock answered me.
Hisui excused herself and entered the room.
It was an utterly ordinary morning scene, exactly like any other.
“Ah…”
Perhaps it was because her presence felt so natural.
My heart, hammering wildly moments before, quieted with almost laughable ease.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Knock.
Knock.
"Please excuse me," Hisui says as she enters the room.
It's just a normal morning scene.
"Ah---------"
Is it because she is acting so naturally?
My pounding heart instantly calms down.

entries.japanese:
「おはようございます、志貴さま」
「………ひす、い？」
「はい、お時間ですので着替えをご用意いたしました。
……あの、志貴さま？
　お体の具合がよろしくないのですか？」
「いや、そんな事はないよ。
俺はいつも通りだし、何もおかしな所なんて、ない」
　自分に言い聞かせるように言って、ベッドから起きあがった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Good morning, Master Shiki.”
“Hisui?”
“Yes. It is time to rise, so I have brought your clothes. Master Shiki, are you feeling unwell?”
“No, nothing like that. I’m the same as always, with nothing wrong at all.”
As if repeating it could make it true, I climbed out of bed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Good morning, Shiki-sama."
"……… Hisu, i?"
"Yes, it is time, so I have prepared your change of clothes already.
…… Um, Shiki-sama?
Are you not feeling well?"
"No, that's not it.
I feel fine.
There's nothing wrong."
I get up from bed, as if to prove my words.

entries.japanese:
「おはよう翡翠。
着替えたら居間に行くから、翡翠は先に行ってていいよ」
「はい。
それでは失礼します」
　翡翠は静かにドアを閉めて去っていく。
　それを見送ってから、はあ、と大きく深呼吸をした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Morning, Hisui. I’ll come to the sitting room once I’m dressed, so you can go on ahead.”
“Very well. Excuse me.”
Hisui quietly closed the door behind her.
Once she was gone, I drew one long, deep breath.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Morning, Hisui.
I'll go to the sitting room after I change, so please go ahead of me."
"Yes.
Well then, please excuse me."
Hisui quietly closes the door and leaves.
After watching her go, I take a deep breath.

entries.japanese:
「なにを弱気になってるんだろうな、俺は」
　昨日、親父の病気の事を知ったせいだろう。
　今の自分と遠野槙久の病状が少しだけ似ている、というだけで被害妄想ぎみになっているのかもしれない。
「……だよな。
たんに帰ってきたばっかりで、俺は疲れてるだけなんだし。
あんな夢、気にする必要なんてない」
―――さて。
　時刻は七時になろうとしている。
　昨日と同様、今日もゆっくりとした朝が迎えられそうだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What am I getting so frightened about?”
It had to be because I had learned about my father’s illness yesterday.
My symptoms bore a slight resemblance to Makihisa Tohno’s, and I was letting paranoia do the rest.
“Right. I’ve only just come home, and I’m tired. There’s no reason to worry about some stupid dream.”
―――Enough of that.
It was almost seven.
Just like yesterday, this promised to be another leisurely morning.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Why am I feeling down like this?"
Probably because I found out about my old man's illness yesterday.
Just because my symptoms are similar to his, maybe I'm being too paranoid.
"…… Yeah.
Ever since I came back, I've been so tired.
I shouldn't think about that dream."
---Well then.
It's almost seven.
Like yesterday, I should be able to enjoy the morning.

entries.japanese:
――――と。
　何も考えずに居間に足を踏み入れて、大事な事を忘れている事に気がついた。
「しまっ―――――」
　た、という声をなんとか飲みこむ。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――Then.
I stepped into the sitting room without thinking and realized I had forgotten something important.
“Damn―――――”
I somehow swallowed the rest of the word.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----And then…
Unthinkingly, I step into the sitting room and it hits me that I forgot something very important.
"Oh cra-----"
I swallow my words.

entries.japanese:
居間には秋葉と翡翠、琥珀さんの姿があった。
　いつもならどうって事はないこの光景も、昨日の一件の後だと実に気まずいシーンとなる。
　秋葉と琥珀さんは和解していたようだけど、あいにく俺はまだ秋葉と話すらしていない。
　昨日の秋葉の様子からして、まだ俺に対して怒っているであろう事は明白だった。
entries.maoEnglish:
Akiha, Hisui, and Kohaku were all there.
Ordinarily there would have been nothing remarkable about that, but after yesterday it made for an excruciating scene.
Akiha and Kohaku appeared to have made peace, while I had yet to exchange so much as a word with Akiha.
Judging by how she had behaved yesterday, she was plainly still furious with me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Akiha, Hisui, and Kohaku-san are in the sitting room.
Everything seems just like normal, but after what happened yesterday, I'm sure it'll be really awkward.
Akiha and Kohaku-san seemed to have reached an understanding, but I haven't spoken with Akiha yet.
Thinking how Akiha acted yesterday, I'm pretty sure Akiha's still mad at me.

entries.japanese:
「おはようございます、兄さん。
昨夜はよく眠れましたか？」
「――――――――はい？」
　と。
　秋葉は、これ以上にないっていうぐらい、さわやかな笑顔で挨拶をしてきてくれた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Good morning, Brother. Did you sleep well?”
“Excuse me?”
Then.
Akiha greeted me with the brightest, freshest smile imaginable.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Good morning, Nii-san.
Did you sleep well?"
"--------Huh?"
And.
Akiha greets me with a big smile.

entries.japanese:
「あ…………う？」
　あまりの出来事に思考が石化した。
　呆、と立ち尽くす俺に、秋葉はやっぱりにこやかな視線を向けてきている。
　……こいつ、何か企んでいるんじゃないだろうな……なんて邪推してしまうぐらい、秋葉は上機嫌すぎる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Uh—what?”
The shock petrified my thoughts.
I stood there blankly while Akiha continued smiling at me.
She was in such an impossibly good mood that I couldn’t help wondering what she was plotting.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Uh………………?"
My mind freezes at such an unexpected event.
Akiha still has a big smile as I just stand there.
Akiha is way too cheerful and it makes me think she is planning something.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま、お座りになられないのですか？」
「あ……うん、座れと言われれば、座るけど」
　恐る恐る秋葉の向かいのソファーに腰を下ろす。
「おはよう秋葉。
今朝は、その、えらく機嫌がいいんだな」
「そうですか？
　確かに今朝は体調がいいから、顔色はいいかもしれませんね」
　……いや、顔色がいいとか、そういったレベルの話ではないと思う。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki, will you not sit down?”
“Yes, if you’re telling me to sit.”
With extreme caution, I lowered myself onto the sofa opposite Akiha.
“Morning, Akiha. You’re unusually cheerful today.”
“Am I? I do feel well this morning, so perhaps I simply look healthier.”
No, this was not merely about looking healthier.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama, would you care to sit down?"
"Ah…… yeah, if you want me to sit, I will."
I fearfully look at Akiha as I sit down across from her.
"Morning, Akiha.
You seem to be in a good mood today."
"Is that so?
Certainly I feel much better, so I probably look less pale than before."
…… No, it is far beyond not looking pale.

entries.japanese:
「それより兄さん、この前はお世話になりました。
本当なら昨日のうちにお礼を言いたかったんだけど、昨日は私おかしかったから機会がなくて」
　秋葉はまっすぐに俺の目を見つめてくる。
　そこには昨日見せた冷たさらしきものがまったく存在しない。
　……あの、どことなく“危うい”と思わせるような雰囲気も、どこかに行ってしまったみたいだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“More importantly, Brother, thank you for the other night. I meant to say so yesterday, but I wasn’t myself and never had the chance.”
Akiha looked straight into my eyes.
Not a trace remained of yesterday’s coldness.
Even that indefinable air of danger around her seemed to have vanished.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Anyway, first I have to thank you.
I really wanted to thank you yesterday, but I was feeling rather ill and did not have an opportunity."
Akiha looks directly at me.
There isn't even a trace of yesterday's coldness.
…… It also seems that the air of danger has disappeared.

entries.japanese:
「お礼って、別に秋葉に感謝されるようなコトはしてないよ、俺は」
「そんなコトありません。
兄さんは倒れた私を看病してくれて、ずっと傍にいてくれたじゃないですか。
　兄さんが抱きしめてくれたから、私は決心がついたんです。
あの夜は、本当に嬉しかった」
「っ――――――！」
　目の前でトンデモナイ事を言われて咳き込みそうになった。
――――と。
　背後から、なにやら重いプレッシャーを感じる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You don’t have anything to thank me for.”
“Of course I do. You looked after me when I collapsed, and stayed beside me the whole time.
When you held me, Brother, I finally found the courage to make my decision. That night made me so happy.”
“—!”
I nearly choked at hearing something so outrageous announced in front of everyone.
――――Then.
A crushing pressure gathered behind me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Thank me?
I didn't really do anything to deserve that."
"That's not true.
You took care of me when I was sick, right?
Because you embraced me, I was determined.
I was extremely happy that night."
"-------!"
She says something that catches me totally off guard.
----And then.
I feel incredibly heavy pressure against my back.

entries.japanese:
ちらりと後ろを向く。
　……そこにはどう見ても普段通りなのに、どう見ても普段通りとは思えない、琥珀さんと翡翠の視線があった。
entries.maoEnglish:
I glanced over my shoulder.
Kohaku and Hisui were watching me; both looked exactly as always, yet neither looked remotely normal.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I glance behind me.
…… There, Hisui and Kohaku-san stare at me in a manner far different than usual.

entries.japanese:
「―――秋葉。
あんまり誤解を招くような表現はやめよう。
あの夜は秋葉が苦しそうだったから、体を支えてあげただけだろ」
「あら。
私の背中に両腕まわして、そのままでいる事は支えるというんですか？」
　クスクスと秋葉は笑う。
　じーーーーーっ、と。
　背中には二人分の視線が加重してくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Akiha. Stop phrasing it in ways people might misunderstand. You were in pain that night, and I only held you up.”
“Oh. Is wrapping both arms around my back and holding me there what you call supporting me?”
Akiha giggled.
A long, unbroken stare.
Two pairs of eyes pressed against my back, steadily gaining weight.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Akiha.
Don't say things that might give people the wrong impression.
You were in so much pain, I just supported you, that's all."
"Oh?
I suppose wrapping your arms around me is just supporting me?"
Akiha giggles softly.
Staring.
They're staring at me.
The stares of the two behind me get even heavier.

entries.japanese:
「―――あのな。
おまえ、なんかヘンだぞ。
そんなふうに俺をからかって楽しいのかよ」
「ええ、とっても。
兄さんの困った顔を見るのも悪くはありませんね」
「………………」
　おかしすぎる。
秋葉ってこんなキャラクターしてたっけ？
entries.maoEnglish:
“Listen. You’re acting weird. Is tormenting me like this really that much fun?”
“Very much so. Seeing you flustered has a charm of its own, Brother.”
“…”
This was beyond strange. Had Akiha always been this kind of person?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Now look.
You're acting odd.
Are you enjoying making fun of me?"
"Yes, a lot.
Looking at your troubled face is fun."
"……………"
This is just too weird.
Is this really Akiha's personality?

entries.japanese:
「悪趣味なヤツだな。
朝から兄貴を困らせるわ、昨日は昨日で叱りつけてくるわ。
　……まあ、まず間違いなくそうだとは思うんだけど、おまえ俺に恨みでもあるんだろ」
　ため息まじりに切り返す。
　と、秋葉は突然、気まずそうに視線を逸らしてしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What a nasty streak. You spend the morning tormenting your brother, after spending yesterday lecturing him.
I’m almost certain I know the answer already, but you’ve got some kind of grudge against me, don’t you?”
I returned her teasing with a weary sigh.
At that, Akiha suddenly looked away, embarrassed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"You have some strange hobbies.
Bothering me in the morning and lecturing me last night.
…… Well, I thought so at first, but you really must have something against me."
I end with a sigh.
All of a sudden, Akiha averts her gaze.

entries.japanese:
「……ごめんなさい。
昨日のことは悪かったって反省してるわ。
昨日はその、具合が悪くてどうかしてたんだって、琥珀にも謝ったし―――」
「琥珀さんに謝ったって、秋葉が！？」
　いや、秋葉が謝ってくる事も意外なら、琥珀さんに謝るなんていう事も意外すぎて、思わず声をあげてしまう。
「―――むっ。
兄さん、私のことをなんだと思っているんですか。
自分に非があるんだから琥珀に謝るのは当然でしょう」
　……いや、なんだと言われると、使用人に厳しい女主人とかそういったモンを、こう漠然と。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’m sorry. I know I behaved badly yesterday. I was ill and out of my mind, and I even apologized to Kohaku―――”
“You apologized to Kohaku!?”
Her apologizing to me was surprising enough; the idea of her apologizing to Kohaku was so astonishing that I shouted without meaning to.
“Hmph. What sort of person do you think I am, Brother? I was at fault, so naturally I apologized to Kohaku.”
I vaguely imagined something like a stern mistress ruling her servants.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I'm very sorry.
What I did yesterday was stupid.
There was something wrong with me, and I've already apologized to Kohaku---"
"You apologized to Kohaku-san!?"
I blurt this out in surprise.
Not only did she apologize, but she apologized to Kohaku-san.
"---Hey.
Nii-san, just what kind of person do you think I am?
I was at fault, so it is only natural that I apologized to Kohaku, right?"
…… When she says that, I get a vague mental image of her acting as a strict mistress.

entries.japanese:
「兄さん。
今良からぬ事を考えたでしょう」
　……鋭い。
上機嫌でハイになっていても、秋葉の勘の良さは鈍っていないようだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Brother. You were just thinking something unkind about me.”
Sharp as ever. Even giddy with good humor, Akiha’s instincts had not dulled in the least.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Nii-san.
You're thinking of something bad, aren't you?"
…… She's sharp.
As happy as she is, it doesn't do anything to dull her sense of perception.

entries.japanese:
――――親父の部屋に行ってみよう。
　はっきりと何があると期待はできないけど、遠野という血筋について何か調べられるかもしれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――I’ll try Father’s room.
I had no particular reason to expect anything, but I might find some clue about the Tohno bloodline.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----I'll go to my old man's room.
I can't say for sure that I expect to find anything, but I might be able to investigate something about the Tohno lineage.

entries.japanese:
「―――、………お帰りなさいませ、志貴さま」
　………と。
　親父の部屋にはすでに先客がいた。
　翡翠は持っていた本の山を置いて、ふかぶかとおじぎをしてくる。
「―――――翡翠」
　……翡翠の様子はいつも通りだ。
　今朝の一件でなんとなく気まずいものがあったけど、翡翠は朝の出来事を引きずっていないように見えた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“W-welcome home, Master Shiki.”
And so.
Father’s room already had a visitor.
Hisui set down the stack of books she was carrying and bowed deeply.
“Hisui.”
Hisui appeared entirely herself.
Although that morning had left some awkwardness between us, she showed no sign of dwelling on it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---, ……… Welcome back, Shiki-sama."
……… And.
There is already someone in the old man's room.
Hisui puts down the mountain of books she is carrying and bows.
"-----Hisui."
…… She looks like she always does.
I was uneasy about seeing her because of this morning, but it seems she is over it already.

entries.japanese:
「先ほどはお迎えが出来ず、申し訳ありませんでした。
―――何かご用でしょうか」
「いや、用ってほどの事じゃないんだけど、ちょっと親父の部屋で調べものがあって。
　翡翠の仕事の邪魔にならなければ、少しここに居ていいかな」
「……はい。
ですが志貴さま、鍵のかけられている机や棚は秋葉さまが管理しています。
鍵を開ける事はわたしにはできませんが、それでよろしいでしょうか？」
「鍵、か……ああ、かまわないよ。
別に目的があるわけでもなし」
「―――――――？」
　不思議そうに首をかしげる翡翠。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I apologize for not being there to welcome you earlier. Is there something you require?”
“Nothing important, but I wanted to look into a few things in Father’s room.
If I won’t be in your way, may I stay for a while?”
“Yes. However, Master Shiki, Miss Akiha keeps the keys to the locked desks and cabinets. I cannot open them for you; will that be acceptable?”
“The keys…? That’s fine; I’m not searching for anything specific.”
“―――――――?”
Hisui tilted her head, plainly puzzled.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I deeply apologize for not being able to welcome you earlier.
---May I help you with anything?"
"No, I just thought that I'd look around my old man's room.
As long as I'm not in the way, could I stay here a bit?"
"…… Yes, but Akiha-sama has the keys to the locked shelves and drawers, so I cannot open them.
Is that acceptable?"
"Locked?
…… That's fine.
I'm not really looking for anything in particular."
"-------?"
Hisui tilts her head questioningly.

entries.japanese:
「じゃ、勝手に見てるから翡翠は仕事を続けてくれ。
俺の我が侭で翡翠の邪魔したくないし」
「かしこまりました。
それでは、何かありましたらお声をかけてください」
　翡翠は部屋の掃除を再開する。
―――――さて。
　こっちも始めるとしようか。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’ll look around by myself, so carry on with your work. I don’t want my whim getting in your way.”
“Understood. Please call me if you need anything.”
Hisui resumed cleaning.
―――――All right, then.
Time for me to begin as well.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I'll just look around myself, so please continue.
I don't want to get in your way."
"As you wish.
Well then, if you need anything, please call me."
Hisui resumes cleaning the room.
-----Well then.
I should start too.

entries.japanese:
……しばらく本棚を調べて、こんな事をしても無意味な事が判明した。
　親父の本棚にあるものは既成の著作物だけで、遠野の家に関するものは並べられていない。
　見たいものは遠野家の家系図とか、親父の手記とかそういったものだ。
「……やっぱりその手のヤツはこの中かな……」
　親父の机の引き出しに手をかける。
　引くと、がつん、と引っかかる感触。
「……けど鍵がかかってるんだよな……」
　鍵を開けるためには秋葉に相談しないといけない。
……が、翡翠の口ぶりからすると秋葉が鍵を開けてくれるとは思えない。
entries.maoEnglish:
After searching the bookcase for a while, I realized the whole exercise was pointless.
It held nothing but published books, nothing about the Tohno family itself.
What I needed was a family tree, or Father’s journals—something of that kind.
“I suppose those would be in here…”
I tugged at a drawer in his desk.
It struck the lock with a solid clunk.
“Locked, of course…”
Opening it properly would mean asking Akiha. Judging from Hisui’s warning, there was no chance she would agree.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… I spend a little time searching the bookshelves, but realize it's useless.
The shelves are all full of books, but nothing about the Tohno family.
What I want to see is something like my family tree or my old man's journal.
"…… I guess things like that are in here……"
I pull the drawers to my old man's desk.
I feel it catch.
"…… But they are locked……"
If I want the key, I have to talk to Akiha.
…… But from what Hisui says, I don't think she'll open them for me.

entries.japanese:
「―――――」
　翡翠はこっちを見ていない。
　親父の机の上にはペーパーナイフが一つ。
　都合よく道具はそろっていたりした。
　……まあ、場合が場合だし、この際手段は問わずにしよう。
「…………………」
　少しだけメガネを下にズラして、机を視る。
「―――――そこ」
　音もなく鍵を切った。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
Hisui wasn’t looking.
A letter opener lay on Father’s desk.
Conveniently, every tool I needed was already at hand.
Given the circumstances, I could afford to be flexible about my methods.
“…”
I lowered my glasses slightly and looked at the desk.
“There.”
Without making a sound, I cut through the lock.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-----"
Hisui isn't looking this way.
There is a letter opener on the desk.
This is convenient.
…… Well, might as well use what's given to me.
"………………"
Lowering my glasses a bit, I look at the desk.
"-----There."
Without a sound, I cut the lock.

entries.japanese:
「ん―――紙しか入ってないな」
　引き出しの中にあるのは古びた紙の束だった。
　どれ、と一枚だけ手にとって見てみる。
「―――なんだろう、これ」
　流れるような筆文字のため、よく読めない。
　なんとなく読み取れるのは遠野マキヒサという文字で、その後には遠野シキ、遠野アキハという名前がある。
　そうして、その終わりに。
　七夜という、見なれない単語があった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hm—nothing but paper.”
The drawer contained a bundle of yellowed sheets.
I picked up the first and examined it.
“What is this…?”
The flowing calligraphy was difficult to decipher.
I could just make out the name Makihisa Tohno, followed by Shiki Tohno and Akiha Tohno.
Then, at the very end.
There was an unfamiliar word: Nanaya.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hmm---there's only some papers."
Inside the drawer is only a bundle of old papers.
I pick up a sheet.
"---What is this?"
The flowing script is difficult to read.
My eyes come to the names Tohno MAKIHISA followed by Tohno SHIKI and Tohno AKIHA.
And after that,
I see an unfamiliar name: Nanaya.

entries.japanese:
―――――――不意に。
　理由もなく、暗い森の映像が、浮かんだ。
「あ――――」
　視界から光が薄れていく。
　後頭部にぐらぐらと血液が溜まっていくような感じ。
　手足に力が入らなくなって、息が、できなくなるような、錯覚。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――――――Without warning.
For no reason, the image of a dark forest rose before me.
“Ah…”
Light bled out of my vision.
It felt as though blood were pooling and sloshing in the back of my skull.
Strength deserted my limbs, and I suffered the illusion that I could no longer breathe.
entries.mirrorMoon:
-------Suddenly.
For no reason, I see a vision of a dark forest.
"Ah----"
My vision thins.
I feel the blood welling in the back of my head.
Strength drains from my limbs, and I feel like I can't breathe.

entries.japanese:
――――なんで？
　なんでこんな、理由もなく息が苦しいのか。
　何があったわけでもない。
　何を見たわけでもない。
　なのにどうして、俺はこんなにも―――ガタガタと、子供のように震えているん、だろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――Why?
Why was I choking when nothing had happened?
I hadn’t experienced anything.
I hadn’t seen anything.
Then why was I trembling so violently—shaking like a terrified child?
entries.mirrorMoon:
----Why?
Why is it hard to breathe all of a sudden?
It's not like anything happened.
I didn't see anything.
So why am I---shaking like a small kid?

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま……！」
　翡翠……翡翠がかけよってきた。
　―――なんとか本棚に手をかけて、体を持ちなおす。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki…!”
Hisui—Hisui runs toward me.
―――I catch the bookcase and somehow steady myself.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama……!"
Hisui…… Hisui rushes over to me.
---Placing a hand on a bookcase, I somehow manage to stay standing.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま！
　お気を確かに、志貴さま……！」
　心配そうな、翡翠の声。
　けど彼女の手は、決して俺の体には触れてこない。
「大丈夫―――ちょっと、吐き気がしただけだから」
「志貴さま、どうかご無理はなさらないよう。
椅子に座って、お体を休めてください」
「……ああ……大丈夫、だから―――」
　なんとか意識を整える。
　それでも眩暈は納まらない。
　赤と黒が明滅する視界のなか。
　白い。
　ひどく温かそうな、翡翠のうなじが見えた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki! Please stay with me, Master Shiki…!”
Hisui’s voice was tight with worry.
But her hands never touched my body.
“I’m fine—it was only a little nausea.”
“Master Shiki, please do not strain yourself. Sit down and rest.”
“I’m all right―――”
I forced my thoughts into order.
But the dizziness refused to pass.
Red and black pulsed across my vision.
White.
Hisui’s nape came into view, looking unbearably warm.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama!
Please, hold on, Shiki-sama……!"
Hisui's voice is full of worry.
But her hand does not touch me.
"I'm fine---I just got a little nauseous."
"Shiki-sama, please do not strain yourself.
Please have a seat and rest."
"…… Yeah…… I'm fine, so---"
I manage to hold onto consciousness.
But I'm still dizzy.
In my flickering red and black vision.
White.
I see her terribly warm neck.

entries.japanese:
「―――――あ」
　なんて艶めかしい。
　この体がちゃんと動くんなら、俺は今すぐにでも翡翠の体を押さえつけて―――
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――――Ah.”
How alluring.
If my body would only move, I would pin Hisui down this instant and―――
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-----Ah."
I'm captivated.
If my body could move properly, I would seize Hisui's body and----

entries.japanese:
さっきまで貧血で暗くなっていた視界が、一転して真っ赤に染まる。
　翡翠の、白い首筋。
　真っ赤だった、昨夜の夢。
―――殺人の夜の。
　心臓が飛び出しそうなほどの、痛い快感。
entries.maoEnglish:
The darkness of anemia vanishes, and my whole field of vision floods crimson.
Hisui’s white throat.
Last night’s dream, drenched in red.
―――The night of murder.
Pleasure so sharp and painful my heart seemed ready to tear free of my chest.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The black vision from my anemia all of a sudden turns deep red.
Hisui's, white neck.
Last night's crimson dream.
----The nighttime killing.
Painful pleasure, as if my heart would rip itself out.

entries.japanese:
「くっ―――――！」
　たまらなくなって、翡翠から逃げ出した。
「志貴さま……？」
「いや―――大丈夫―――大丈夫だから、一人にしてくれ」
「いけません。
そのようなお顔で、どうかご無理はなさらないでください」
　翡翠は近寄ってくる。
今にも倒れそうな俺の体を支えようとやってくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ghh—!”
Unable to endure it, I fled from Hisui.
“Master Shiki…?”
“No—I’m fine, so please leave me alone.”
“I cannot; not when you look like that. Please don’t force yourself.”
Hisui came closer. She meant to support me before I fell.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"K------!"
Unable to bear it, I get away from Hisui.
"Shiki-sama……?"
"No---I'm fine---I'm fine, so leave me alone."
"I cannot do that when you look that ill.
Please do not strain yourself."
Hisui draws close.
She comes to support my collapsing body.

entries.japanese:
―――まずい。
　　　それは、恐い。
　そんな手の届く範囲にこられたら、自分がなにをしてしまうか解らなくて、恐い。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――This is bad.
It terrifies me.
If she comes within reach, I don’t know what I might do, and that terrifies me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---This isn't good.
This is, bad.
If she comes within reach of my hands, I'm afraid I don't know what I'll do.

entries.japanese:
「やめ―――いい、から……、一人、に―――」
　眩暈がする。
　気が遠くなる。
　……でも、今はそれでいい。
　倒れてしまえば、それで―――翡翠の血を吸いたいなんて、そんな錯覚に揺れるコトがなくなるんだから―――――
entries.maoEnglish:
“Stop―――I’m fine, just leave me―――alone―――”
The room spun.
Consciousness receded.
But perhaps that was best.
If I collapsed, then at least I would no longer be tormented by the delusion that I wanted to drink Hisui’s blood―――――
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Sto---I'm, fine…… leave, me---"
Dizziness assails me.
I feel very faint.
…… But that's fine.
If I collapse, then---I won't feel the urge to suck Hisui's blood-----

entries.japanese:
「翡翠？
　昨日のコトだけど、あれから琥珀と兄さんって――――」
　え……秋、葉……？
「兄さん？
　どうしてこんな所に――――」
　途端、秋葉はまっすぐに俺のところまでやってきて、無言で遠野家の家系図を奪ってしまった。
「兄さん。
鍵を、壊したんですか」
「――――――――」
　秋葉が睨んでくる。
　俺は―――眩暈に襲われていて、うまく秋葉を見る事さえ、できずにいた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hisui? About yesterday—afterward, did Kohaku and Brother…?”
Akiha…?
“Brother? What are you doing in here—?”
The instant she saw me, Akiha marched straight over and silently snatched the Tohno family tree from my hands.
“Brother. Did you break the lock?”
“…”
Akiha glared at me.
Dizziness still had me in its grip; I could barely focus on her face.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hisui?
About yesterday, Kohaku and Nii-san----"
Eh…… Aki, ha……?
"Nii-san?
Why are you here----"
Akiha comes straight to me and snatches the Tohno family lineage away from me.
"Nii-san.
You broke the lock?"
"--------"
Akiha stares at me angrily.
I---fighting my dizziness, can't look at her right.

entries.japanese:
「……そう。
見てしまったものは仕方がありません。
今回は大目に見てさしあげますが、次は相応の処罰を覚悟してください」
　そうして、秋葉は翡翠へと視線を向けた。
　……鋭い視線は、翡翠を憎んでいるようにさえ、とれる。
「ぁ―――――――――」
　それは、あの夢に出てきた秋葉に、似ていた。
　悪意や憎悪に近い視線。
　火炎じみた熱さを感じさせる、秋葉の髪。
「え――――――――？」
　ギリ、と血脈が搾られた。
　目の錯覚か。
一瞬、秋葉の周りに、何か―――よくないモノが、視えた気がした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I see. What’s done is done. I will overlook it this once, but next time you should expect an appropriate punishment.”
Then Akiha turned her gaze on Hisui.
It was sharp enough to look almost hateful.
“Ah―――――――――”
She looked like the Akiha from my dream.
A gaze close to malice, close to hatred.
Akiha’s hair, seeming to radiate the heat of flame.
“What…?”
Something clenched tight around my veins.
A trick of the eye? For one instant, I thought I saw something—something wrong—around Akiha.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I see.
It can't be helped if you saw it already.
I will let it go this time, but be prepared for a deserving punishment next time."
Akiha then stares at Hisui.
…… She looks like she almost hates Hisui.
"Ah---------"
She looks like the Akiha in that dream.
A gaze that looks close to malice and hatred.
I almost feel burning heat emanating from her hair.
"Eh---------?"
My heart skips a beat.
Was I hallucinating?
For an instant, around Akiha---I thought that I saw something terrible.

entries.japanese:
「――――翡翠。
あなた、何をしていたの。
兄さんは体が弱いんですから、せめて心労だけでも無くしてあげないといけないのよ。
　だっていうのに兄さんをお父様のお部屋に入れるなんて、考えが足りないんじゃない？」
「――――はい。
申し訳、ございません」
「……今後は気をつけなさい。
それと琥珀に話があるから、すぐに私の部屋に来るように伝えておいて」
　秋葉は立ち去っていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hisui. What did you think you were doing? Brother is frail enough already; the least we can do is spare him needless distress.
Yet was it not thoughtless to let him into Father’s room?”
“Yes. I am very sorry.”
“Take greater care in future. I also need to speak with Kohaku, so tell her to come to my room at once.”
Akiha left.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----Hisui, what were you doing?
Nii-san's body is weak, so you have to at least take away his mental burden.
But letting Nii-san enter Father's room, were you not thinking?"
"----I am, deeply sorry."
"…… Be more careful from now on.
I have to speak with Kohaku, so tell her to come to my room immediately."
Akiha walks away.

entries.japanese:
「……志貴さま、お部屋にお戻りください。
お体の具合も良くないようですし、夕食までお休みください」
　翡翠は顔をあげずに言う。
「……そうだね、部屋に戻るよ。
すまない、翡翠。
俺のせいで秋葉に怒られるはめになって」
「いえ、これはわたしの落ち度です。
……秋葉さまのおっしゃるとおり、志貴さまはまだお屋敷に慣れておられません。
志貴さまが落ち着かれるまで、この部屋に志貴さまを招くべきではなかったのです」
「………………………………」
　そう言われると、返答するべき言葉がない。
　俺は眩暈が残る頭のまま、親父の部屋を後にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki, please return to your room. You appear unwell, so you should rest until dinner.”
Hisui spoke without lifting her face.
“You’re right. I’m sorry, Hisui. Akiha only scolded you because of me.”
“No, the fault was mine. As Miss Akiha said, Master Shiki is not yet accustomed to life in the mansion. I should not have permitted Master Shiki into this room until Master Shiki had settled in.”
“…”
Put that way, there was nothing I could say.
My head still spinning, I left Father’s room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Shiki-sama, please return to your room.
Your condition is not good, so please rest until dinner."
Hisui says this, still looking down.
"…… You're right, I'll go to my room.
Sorry, Hisui.
Because of me, Akiha was mad at you."
"No, it was my fault.
…… As Akiha-sama says, you are still not used to this mansion.
Until you are settled in, you should not enter this room."
"…………………………"
I don't know what to say.
Still dizzy, I exit my old man's room.

entries.japanese:
食堂で一人で夕食を済ませて部屋に戻ってきた。
　秋葉はまだ体調が悪いらしく、部屋で夕食を摂った。
entries.maoEnglish:
I ate dinner alone in the dining room and returned to my room.
Akiha still seemed unwell and took her meal upstairs.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I eat dinner alone and go back to my room.
I guess Akiha was still feeling poorly because she wasn't there.

entries.japanese:
「――――――――」
　ベッドに横になって、はあ、と大きくため息をした。
　……疲れているんだろうか。
　最近は夜になると、すぐにベッドに倒れこんでしまう。
　色々と考えなくてはいけない事がある筈なのに、そんな事は自分には関係のない事のような気がして、すぐに眠ろうとしてしまう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
I lay on the bed and let out a long breath.
Was I tired?
Lately I collapsed onto the bed as soon as night came.
There ought to have been so many things to think about, yet they all felt as though they belonged to someone else, and all I wanted was sleep.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"--------"
Lying down on my bed, I let out a big sigh.
…… I must be tired.
Recently, as soon as night falls, I fall into bed.
Even though there are a lot of things I should think about, I feel like nothing concerns me and try to sleep.

entries.japanese:
「……おかしいな。
こんなに集中力がなかったっけ、俺――――」
　天井を眺めながら、ぼんやりと口にする。
　うっすらと目蓋が閉じていく。
　結局、今夜も何一つ疑問に思う事なく、深い眠りに落ちていった――――
entries.maoEnglish:
“Something’s wrong. Was I always this bad at concentrating…?”
I murmured vaguely at the ceiling.
My eyelids drifted shut.
And once again that night, without questioning a single thing, I sank into a deep sleep――――
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… That's odd.
I can't concentrate----"
I stare at the ceiling.
My eyes start to close.
Again, I don't think about anything and fall into a deep sleep----

entries.maoEnglish: ――――Burning.
entries.mirrorMoon: ----Burning.

entries.maoEnglish: ――――Burning.
entries.mirrorMoon: ----Burning.

entries.maoEnglish: ――――Burning.
entries.mirrorMoon: ----Burning.

entries.japanese: ――――肌が、チリチリと焦げて、灼い。
entries.maoEnglish: ――――My skin crackles and chars with burning heat.
entries.mirrorMoon: ----My skin is burning.

entries.japanese:
――――このままでは眠れない。
　　　　起きて、水を飲みに行かないと。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――I can’t sleep like this.
I have to get up and find water.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----I can't sleep like this.
I have to get up and drink some water.

entries.japanese:
夜の街。
　はぁはぁと熱っぽい吐息を繰り返して、通りを歩いていく人たちを見る。
　今夜にかぎって二人や三人といった人しかいない。
　できれば、一人きりの、自分と同い年の女の子がほしかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
The city at night.
I watch the people passing through the streets, my breath feverish and ragged.
Tonight, of all nights, everyone seems to be walking in twos and threes.
What I want is a girl alone—someone my own age.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The nighttime city.
Breathing out in warm gasps, I look at the people passing by.
There are only two or three of them tonight.
If possible, I want to find a lone girl who is about my age.

entries.maoEnglish: ―――Hot.
entries.mirrorMoon: ---Hot.

entries.japanese:
ふと、窓ガラスに映った顔が見えた。
　呼吸は乱れて、まるで四十度ぐらいの熱病にうなされているみたい。
entries.maoEnglish:
My face catches suddenly in a shop window.
My breathing is wild, as though I were delirious with a forty-degree fever.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I see my reflection in the mirror.
Breathing wildly, it looks like I'm running a high fever.

entries.japanese: ―――あつ――こんなに灼いと、堪えきれない。
entries.maoEnglish: ―――Hot—this heat is more than I can bear.
entries.mirrorMoon: ---Hot--I can't stand this burning.

entries.japanese:
……いた。
　こちらから近づく必要なんかない。
　後ろから少女を引き寄せて、そのまま気を失わせた。
　ずるり、と音をたてて、少女の体を運んでくる。
―――なんか、笑ってしまう。
　ちゃんと、今まで我慢してきたのに、それもこれでおしまいになってしまったんだから。
entries.maoEnglish:
There.
No need to approach her from the front.
I pull the girl against me from behind and knock her unconscious.
Her body drags along with a wet, scraping sound.
―――It almost makes me laugh.
I had held myself in check all this time, and now that is over.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… There.
I don't need to get near her.
I grab her from behind and make her pass out.
I pick her up and take her with me.
---I start to smile.
I endured it for so long, and now everything is over.

entries.japanese:
……結局、ここですることにした。
　理由は簡単。
　だって、ここが殺人鬼の根城だったから。
entries.maoEnglish:
In the end, I decide to do it here.
The reason is simple.
This is the murderer’s lair.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… I decide to do it here in the end.
The reason is simple.
Because, this was the killer's lair.

entries.maoEnglish: ―――Burning.
entries.mirrorMoon: ---Burning.

entries.japanese:
はあはあという呼吸音。
　もうすぐ。
　もうすぐ、この子を口にできる。
entries.maoEnglish:
The rasp of panting.
Soon.
Soon I can feed on this girl.
entries.mirrorMoon:
My breathing fills the air.
Soon.
Soon I can taste her.

entries.japanese:
そうして、食事を始めた。
　首筋に口をつけて、血液を吸い上げる。
entries.maoEnglish:
Then the meal begins.
I press my mouth to her throat and draw out the blood.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Then I start my meal.
Biting into her neck, I suck the blood.

entries.japanese: ―――なんて、甘い。
entries.maoEnglish: ―――So sweet.
entries.mirrorMoon: ---It is unbelievably sweet.

entries.japanese:
その感覚は本当に恐ろしかった。
　こんなに甘くて、こんなに気持ちがいいのなら。
　きっと、自分はあの殺人鬼のかわりに、この感覚の虜になると予感してしまったからだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
That sensation was truly terrifying.
If it could be this sweet and feel this good.
Then I knew that it—not the murderer—would make me its slave.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The sensation is really terrifying.
If it is so sweet and feels so good,
I may just become a captive to this sensation, in place of that killer.

entries.japanese:
―――夜が深い。
頭上には罪を咎める銀の瞳。
entries.maoEnglish: ―――The night is deep. Overhead hangs a silver eye that condemns my sin.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---The night is deep.
Above my head is the silver eye bearing witness to my sin.

entries.japanese:
熱い血液で唇をぬらして、恍惚とした目で、夜空を見上げていた。
　髪が乱れる。
　頭上には螺旋の空。
　なんてキレイな、銀色の月。
entries.maoEnglish:
Hot blood wetting my lips, I gaze at the night sky in rapture.
My hair tumbles loose.
Above me, the heavens turn in a spiral.
What a beautiful silver moon.
entries.mirrorMoon:
With blood-smeared lips, I look up at the night sky with eyes full of amusement.
Fluttering hair.
Above is the spiraling sky.
What a beautiful, silver moon.

entries.japanese:
―――蛇の如く。
血を吸う鬼を、見つめている。
entries.maoEnglish: ―――Like a snake. It watches the blood-drinking fiend.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Like a snake.
Watching the blood-sucking demon.

entries.japanese:
「――――――！」
　たまらず、ベッドから跳ね起きた。
「あ―――はあ、は――――あ」
　込み上げてくる吐き気を堪えてケモノのような息吹をあげる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“—!”
I could bear no more and sprang upright in bed.
“Ah―――hah, ha――――ah”
Fighting down the nausea surging through me, I panted like an animal.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------!"
I leap out of bed unable to take it.
"Ah---haa, ha----ah."
Holding back the urge to vomit, I breathe like a beast.

entries.japanese:
「な――――――」
　なんだ、今のは。
　夢。
夢を見てた。
けど、今のはなんだ。
　二日前に見たおかしな夢とは違う。
　夜の街を歩く感覚。
　鼻腔に残る血の匂い。
　ずるずると。
自分と同い年の女の子を引きずっていた音。
―――その全てが、はっきりと記憶として残っている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What――――――”
What had that been?
A dream. I had been dreaming. But what had that been?
Nothing like the strange one from two days ago.
The sensation of walking through the city at night.
The smell of blood still lodged in my nose.
Dragging. The sound of a girl my own age scraping along behind me.
―――Every detail remained with the clarity of a real memory.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Wha------"
What was that just now?
A dream.
It was a dream.
But, what was that?
It's different than what I saw two days ago.
The feeling of walking the streets at night.
The smell of blood lingering in my nose.
The sound of pulling that girl who was close to my age.
