---All of it is fresh in my memory.

entries.japanese:
「は、あ――――――」
　あれは快感と呼ばれるモノだったのだろうか。
　弾丸のように凝縮された興奮が、耳元からトリガーをひいて脳髄に叩き込まれたような衝撃だけがあった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hah…”
Could that have been what people called pleasure?
There had only been the impact: excitement compressed into a bullet, its trigger pulled beside my ear, firing it straight through my brain.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ha, ah-------"
Was that something you could call pleasure?
It was pure excitement condensed like a bullet, fired straight into my head.

entries.japanese:
「ぐ―――っ」
　思い出しただけで息が止まる。
　なら―――あの衝撃は、やはり『快感』と呼べるものだったのかもしれない。
「俺は―――なんて、夢を」
　自らの両手を見る。
　当然、自分の手は真っ白で血の赤色なんて微塵もない。
　なのに一瞬だけ。
　自分の両手が、真っ赤に染まっているように、見えた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ghh…!”
The memory alone stopped my breath.
Then perhaps that impact truly had been what people called ‘pleasure.’
“What kind of dream―――”
I stared at my hands.
Naturally, they were bloodless and pale, without the faintest trace of red.
Yet, for one instant.
I saw both hands stained scarlet.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"G---"
My breathing stops just thinking about it.
Then… perhaps that impact could be something called "pleasure".

"Why did I… that kind of dream…"
I look down at my hands.
Of course, they are pure white, without a trace of red blood on them.
But, for an instant,
I saw both of my hands covered in red.

entries.japanese:
―――なんだ、おまえは同類か。
　……あれ。
―――自分以外の殺人鬼なんて、初めて見たぜ。
　……ああ、確かにそんな話をした。
―――同じ街に殺人鬼は二人はいらない。
　　　ここは、おまえに譲ってやるよ
　……ただ、それは、いつのコトだったろうか。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――So you’re one of my kind.
Wait…
―――You’re the first murderer I’ve ever met besides myself.
Yes, I had certainly had a conversation like that.
―――One city doesn’t need two murderers.
I’ll leave this place to you
But when had that conversation taken place?
entries.mirrorMoon:
---What, you too?
…… Huh?
---This is the first time I've seen another killer besides myself.
…… That's right.
I did have that conversation.
---The same city doesn't need two killers.
I'll give you this place.
…… But, when was that?

entries.japanese:
「……なんで……思い、出せない――――？」
　確かに、俺は誰かとそんな話をした気がする。
　けどまったく思い出せない。
　それが現実の事だったのか、それともやっぱり空ろな夢だったのか。
　ただはっきりと、殺人鬼っていうヤツが、俺の事を同類と呼んでいた事だけが思い出せる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Why…
can’t I remember…?”
I felt certain I had had a conversation like that with someone, but I couldn’t recover a single detail.
Had it happened in reality, or in another hollow dream?
All I could remember clearly was that a murderer had called me one of his own kind.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Why, can't I remember----?"
Certainly, I feel like I had that conversation with someone.
But I just can't remember.
Was it real, or was it just an empty dream?
I just remember that the killer said I was the same as him.

entries.japanese:
「―――おかしいぞ、おい……なんでこう……頭の中が、ぐちゃぐちゃに、なってるんだ――――」
　必死に昨夜の夢を思い出そうとする。
「がっ――――！？」
　ガン、と音がしそうなぐらいの頭痛。
「はっ―――ぁ、はっ…………！」
　思い、出せない。
　無理に昨日の事を思い出そうとすると、吐き気がする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“This is wrong—why is everything in my head such a mess――――”
I fought to recall last night’s dream.
“Gah—!?”
Pain slammed through my skull hard enough to make a sound.
“Hah―――ah, hah…………!”
I couldn’t remember.
Every attempt to force yesterday back into my mind made me want to vomit.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---That's strange.
…… Why is it…… all mixed up in my head----"
I earnestly try hard to remember about last night's dream.
"Ga----!?"
My head pounds.
"Agh---ah, agh………!"
I can't, remember.
When I try to remember about yesterday, I feel the urge to vomit.

entries.japanese:
怖い。
　思い出せないという事は、怖い。
　なんだかそれは。
　俺の知らない遠野志貴が人殺しをして、その事実を隠すために、俺という遠野志貴を、騙している、よう。
――――と。
　廊下のほうで、人の気配を感じ取った。
「誰だ――――！？」
　声をかける。
entries.maoEnglish:
I was afraid.
There was nothing more frightening than being unable to remember.
It felt something like this.
Another Shiki Tohno, one I knew nothing about, had murdered someone—and was deceiving the Shiki Tohno I knew in order to conceal the crime.
――――Then.
I sensed someone in the corridor.
“Who’s there!?”
I called out.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I'm scared.
I'm scared of the fact that I can't remember.
It feels like…
A Tohno Shiki I don't know is killing people, and in order to hide it, is deceiving the Tohno Shiki that is me.
----And.
I sense someone in the hallway.
"Who's there----!?"
I call out.

entries.japanese:
コンコン、というノックの音がした。
　失礼します、と翡翠が部屋に入ってくる。
　それはいつも通りの、なんていう事はない朝の光景だった。
「あ―――――――――」
　翡翠の姿があまりにも自然だったからなのか。
　ドクドクとリズムを乱していた心臓は、あっけないぐらい静かになってくれた。
entries.maoEnglish:
A quiet knock answered me.
Hisui excused herself and entered the room.
It was an utterly ordinary morning scene, exactly like any other.
“Ah…”
Perhaps it was because her presence felt so natural.
My heart, hammering wildly moments before, quieted with almost laughable ease.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Knock.
Knock.
"Please excuse me," Hisui says as she enters the room.
It's just a normal morning scene.
"Ah---------"
Is it because she is acting so naturally?
My pounding heart calms down immediately.

entries.japanese:
「おはようございます、志貴さま」
「………ひす、い？」
「はい、お時間ですので着替えをご用意いたしました。
……あの、志貴さま？
　お体の具合がよろしくないのですか？」
「いや、そんな事はないよ。
俺はいつも通りだし、何もおかしな所なんて、ない」
　自分に言い聞かせるように言って、ベッドから起きあがった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Good morning, Master Shiki.”
“Hisui?”
“Yes. It is time to rise, so I have brought your clothes. Master Shiki, are you feeling unwell?”
“No, nothing like that. I’m the same as always, with nothing wrong at all.”
As if repeating it could make it true, I climbed out of bed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Good morning, Shiki-sama."
"……… Hisu, i?"
"Yes, it is time, so I have prepared your change of clothes already.
…… Um, Shiki-sama?
Are you not feeling well?"
"No, that's not it.
I feel fine.
There's nothing wrong."
I get up from bed, as if to prove my words.

entries.japanese:
「おはよう翡翠。
着替えたら居間に行くから、翡翠は先に行ってていいよ」
「はい。
それでは失礼します」
　翡翠は静かにドアを閉めて去っていく。
　それを見送ってから、はあ、と大きく深呼吸をした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Morning, Hisui. I’ll come to the sitting room once I’m dressed, so you can go on ahead.”
“Very well. Excuse me.”
Hisui quietly closed the door behind her.
Once she was gone, I drew one long, deep breath.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Morning, Hisui.
I'll go to the sitting room after I change, so please go ahead of me."
"Yes.
Well then, please excuse me."
Hisui quietly closes the door and leaves.
After she leaves, I take a deep breath.

entries.japanese:
「なにを弱気になってるんだろうな、俺は」
　昨日、親父の病気の事を知ったせいだろう。
　今の自分と遠野槙久の病状が少しだけ似ている、というだけで被害妄想ぎみになっているのかもしれない。
「……だよな。
たんに帰ってきたばっかりで、俺は疲れてるだけなんだし。
あんな夢、気にする必要なんてない」
―――さて。
　時刻は七時になろうとしている。
　昨日と同様、今日もゆっくりとした朝が迎えられそうだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What am I getting so frightened about?”
It had to be because I had learned about my father’s illness yesterday.
My symptoms bore a slight resemblance to Makihisa Tohno’s, and I was letting paranoia do the rest.
“Right. I’ve only just come home, and I’m tired. There’s no reason to worry about some stupid dream.”
―――Enough of that.
It was almost seven.
Just like yesterday, this promised to be another leisurely morning.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Why am I feeling down like that?"
Probably because I found out about my old man's illness yesterday.
Just because my symptoms are similar to his, maybe I'm being too paranoid.
"…… Yeah.
Ever since I came back, I've been so tired.
I shouldn't think about that dream."
---Well then.
It's almost seven.
Like yesterday, I should be able to enjoy the morning.

entries.japanese:
――――と。
　何も考えずに居間に足を踏み入れて、大事な事を忘れている事に気がついた。
「しまっ―――――」
　た、という声をなんとか飲みこむ。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――Then.
I stepped into the sitting room without thinking and realized I had forgotten something important.
“Damn―――――”
I somehow swallowed the rest of the word.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----And then.
Unthinkingly, I step into the sitting room and it hits me that I forgot something very important.
"Oh cra-----"
I swallow my words.

entries.japanese:
居間には秋葉と翡翠、琥珀さんの姿があった。
　いつもならどうって事はないこの光景も、昨日の一件の後だと実に気まずいシーンとなる。
　秋葉と翡翠は和解していたようだけど、あいにく俺はまだ秋葉と話すらしていない。
　昨日の秋葉の様子からして、まだ俺に対して怒っているであろう事は明白だった。
entries.maoEnglish:
Akiha, Hisui, and Kohaku were all there.
Ordinarily there would have been nothing remarkable about that, but after yesterday it made for an excruciating scene.
Akiha and Hisui appeared to have made peace, while I had yet to exchange so much as a word with Akiha.
Judging by how she had behaved yesterday, she was plainly still furious with me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Akiha, Hisui and Kohaku-san are in the sitting room.
Everything seems just like normal, but after the thing yesterday, I'm sure it'll be really uneasy.
Akiha and Kohaku-san seemed to have reached an understanding, but I haven't spoken with Akiha yet.
Thinking how Akiha acted yesterday, I'm pretty sure Akiha's still mad at me.

entries.japanese:
「おはようございます、兄さん。
昨夜はよく眠れましたか？」
「――――――――はい？」
　と。
　秋葉は、これ以上にないっていうぐらい、さわやかな笑顔で挨拶をしてきてくれた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Good morning, Brother. Did you sleep well?”
“Excuse me?”
Then.
Akiha greeted me with the brightest, freshest smile imaginable.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Good morning, Nii-san.
Did you sleep well?"
"--------Huh?"
And.
Akiha greets me with a big smile.

entries.japanese:
「あ…………う？」
　あまりの出来事に思考が石化した。
　呆、と立ち尽くす俺に、秋葉はやっぱりにこやかな視線を向けてきている。
　……こいつ、何か企んでいるんじゃないだろうな……なんて邪推してしまうぐらい、秋葉は上機嫌すぎる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Uh—what?”
The shock petrified my thoughts.
I stood there blankly while Akiha continued smiling at me.
She was in such an impossibly good mood that I couldn’t help wondering what she was plotting.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Uh……………?"
My mind freezes at such an unexpected event.
Akiha still has a big smile as I just stand there.
Akiha is way too cheerful and it makes me think she is planning on something.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま、お座りになられないのですか？」
「あ……うん、座れと言われれば、座るけど」
　恐る恐る秋葉の向かいのソファーに腰を下ろす。
「おはよう秋葉。
今朝は、その、えらく機嫌がいいんだな」
「そうですか？
　確かに今朝は体調がいいから、顔色はいいかもしれませんね」
　……いや、顔色がいいとか、そういったレベルの話ではないと思う。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki, will you not sit down?”
“Yes, if you’re telling me to sit.”
With extreme caution, I lowered myself onto the sofa opposite Akiha.
“Morning, Akiha. You’re unusually cheerful today.”
“Am I? I do feel well this morning, so perhaps I simply look healthier.”
No, this was not merely about looking healthier.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama, would you care to sit down?"
"Ah…… yeah, if you want me to sit, I will."
I fearfully look at Akiha as I sit down across from her.
"Morning, Akiha.
You seem to be in a good mood today."
"Is that so?
Certainly I feel much better, so I probably look less pale than before."
…… No, it is far beyond not looking pale.

entries.japanese:
「それより兄さん、この前はお世話になりました。
本当なら昨日のうちにお礼を言いたかったんだけど、昨日は私おかしかったから機会がなくて」
　秋葉はまっすぐに俺の目を見つめてくる。
　そこには昨日見せた冷たさらしきものがまったく存在しない。
　……あの、どことなく“危うい”と思わせるような雰囲気も、どこかに行ってしまったみたいだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“More importantly, Brother, thank you for the other night. I meant to say so yesterday, but I wasn’t myself and never had the chance.”
Akiha looked straight into my eyes.
Not a trace remained of yesterday’s coldness.
Even that indefinable air of danger around her seemed to have vanished.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Anyway, first I have to thank you.
I really wanted to thank you yesterday, but I was feeling rather ill and did not have a chance to."
Akiha looks directly at me.
There isn't even a trace of yesterday's coldness.
…… It also seems that the air of danger has disappeared.

entries.japanese:
「お礼って、別に秋葉に感謝されるようなコトはしてないよ、俺は」
「そんなコトありません。
兄さんは倒れた私を看病してくれて、ずっと傍にいてくれたじゃないですか。
　兄さんが抱きしめてくれたから、私は決心がついたんです。
あの夜は、本当に嬉しかった」
「っ――――――！」
　目の前でトンデモナイ事を言われて咳き込みそうになった。
――――と。
　背後から、なにやら重いプレッシャーを感じる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You don’t have anything to thank me for.”
“Of course I do. You looked after me when I collapsed, and stayed beside me the whole time.
When you held me, Brother, I finally found the courage to make my decision. That night made me so happy.”
“—!”
I nearly choked at hearing something so outrageous announced in front of everyone.
――――Then.
A crushing pressure gathered behind me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Thank me?
I didn't really do anything to deserve that."
"That's not true.
You took care of me when I was sick, right?
Because you embraced me, I was determined.
I was extremely happy that night."
"-------!"
She says something that catches me totally off guard.
----And then.
I feel some heavy pressure against my back.

entries.japanese:
ちらりと後ろを向く。
　……そこにはどう見ても普段通りなのに、どう見ても普段通りとは思えない、琥珀さんと翡翠の視線があった。
entries.maoEnglish:
I glanced over my shoulder.
Kohaku and Hisui were watching me; both looked exactly as always, yet neither looked remotely normal.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I glance back.
…… There, Hisui and Kohaku-san stare at me in a manner far different than usual.

entries.japanese:
「―――秋葉。
あんまり誤解を招くような表現はやめよう。
あの夜は秋葉が苦しそうだったから、体を支えてあげただけだろ」
「あら。
私の背中に両腕まわして、そのままでいる事は支えるというんですか？」
　クスクスと秋葉は笑う。
　じーーーーーっ、と。
　背中には二人分の視線が加重してくる。
明かに過重気味だ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Akiha. Stop phrasing it in ways people might misunderstand. You were in pain that night, and I only held you up.”
“Oh. Is wrapping both arms around my back and holding me there what you call supporting me?”
Akiha giggled.
A long, unbroken stare.
Two pairs of eyes pressed against my back, steadily gaining weight. Far more than my back was rated to carry.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Akiha.
Don't say things that might give people the wrong impression.
You were in so much pain, I just supported you, that's all."
"Oh?
I suppose wrapping your arms around me is just supporting me?"
Akiha giggles softly.
Staring.
They're staring at me.
The stares of the two behind me get even heavier.

entries.japanese:
「―――あのな。
おまえ、なんかヘンだぞ。
そんなふうに俺をからかって楽しいのかよ」
「ええ、とっても。
兄さんの困った顔を見るのも悪くはありませんね」
「………………」
　おかしすぎる。
秋葉ってこんなキャラクターしてたっけ？
entries.maoEnglish:
“Listen. You’re acting weird. Is tormenting me like this really that much fun?”
“Very much so. Seeing you flustered has a charm of its own, Brother.”
“…”
This was beyond strange. Had Akiha always been this kind of person?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Now look.
You're acting odd.
Are you enjoying making fun of me?"
"Yes, a lot.
Looking at your troubled face is fun."
"……………"
This is just too weird.
Is this really Akiha's personality?

entries.japanese:
「悪趣味なヤツだな。
朝から兄貴を困らせるわ、昨日は昨日で叱りつけてくるわ。
　……まあ、まず間違いなくそうだとは思うんだけど、おまえ俺に恨みでもあるんだろ」
　ため息まじりに切り返す。
　と、秋葉は突然、気まずそうに視線を逸らしてしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What a nasty streak. You spend the morning tormenting your brother, after spending yesterday lecturing him.
I’m almost certain I know the answer already, but you’ve got some kind of grudge against me, don’t you?”
I returned her teasing with a weary sigh.
At that, Akiha suddenly looked away, embarrassed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"You have some strange hobbies.
Bothering me in the morning and lecturing me last night.
…… Well, I thought so at first, but you really must have something against me."
I end with a sigh.
All of a sudden, Akiha averts her gaze.

entries.japanese:
「……ごめんなさい。
昨日のことは悪かったって反省してるわ。
昨日はその、具合が悪くてどうかしてたんだって、翡翠にも謝ったし―――」
「翡翠に謝ったって、秋葉が！？」
　いや、秋葉が謝ってくる事も意外なら、翡翠に謝るなんていう事も意外すぎて、思わず声をあげてしまう。
「―――むっ。
兄さん、私のことをなんだと思っているんですか。
自分に非があるんだから翡翠に謝るのは当然でしょう」
　……いや、なんだと言われると、使用人に厳しい女主人とかそういったモンを、こう漠然と。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’m sorry. I know I behaved badly yesterday. I was ill and out of my mind, and I even apologized to Hisui―――”
“You apologized to Hisui!?”
Her apologizing to me was surprising enough; the idea of her apologizing to Hisui was so astonishing that I shouted without meaning to.
“Hmph. What sort of person do you think I am, Brother? I was at fault, so naturally I apologized to Hisui.”
I vaguely imagined something like a stern mistress ruling her servants.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I'm very sorry.
What I did yesterday was stupid.
There was something wrong with me, and I've already apologized to Hisui---"
"You apologized to Hisui!?"
I blurt this out in surprise.
Not only did she apologize, but she apologized to Hisui.
"---Hey.
Nii-san, just what kind of person do you think I am?
I was at fault, so it is only natural that I apologized to Hisui, right?"
…… When she says that, I get a vague mental image of her acting as a strict mistress.

entries.japanese:
「兄さん。
今良からぬ事を考えたでしょう」
　……鋭い。
上機嫌でハイになっていても、秋葉の勘の良さは鈍っていないようだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Brother. You were just thinking something unkind about me.”
Sharp as ever. Even giddy with good humor, Akiha’s instincts had not dulled in the least.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Nii-san.
You're thinking of something bad, aren't you?"
…… She's sharp.
As happy as she was, it didn't do anything to dull her sense of perception.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さん、お楽しみのところ申し訳ありませんが、朝ごはんはどうなさいますか？
　そろそろ時間ですから、支度をしようと思いますけど」
「そっか、忘れてた。
……けどあんまり食欲はないんだ。
喉は乾いているんだけど、なんかお腹がいっぱいでさ」
「あ、ダメですよ志貴さんっ。
昨日もお倒れになったんですから、朝ごはんを摂らないとまたお体を悪くしますっ。
　ここは多少食欲がなくても、キチンと食事をなさっていただきますからね」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Shiki, I’m sorry to interrupt while you’re enjoying yourself, but what would you like for breakfast? It’s nearly time, so I thought I should start preparing it.”
“Oh, right. I forgot. But I don’t have much of an appetite; I’m thirsty, yet somehow I feel full.”
“Oh, that won’t do, Shiki. You collapsed yesterday, so if you skip breakfast, you’ll only make yourself ill again.
Even if you don’t feel hungry, I’m going to see that you eat a proper meal.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-san, I hate to ruin your fun, but would you like some breakfast?
It is almost time, so I thought I should make some."
"Oh, I forgot.
…… I'm not so much hungry as I am thirsty though."
"Oh, that won't do, Shiki-san.
You collapsed yesterday so you need to eat to regain your strength.
Even if you don't feel like eating, you should have some food."
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「うっ……」
　琥珀さんの言う事はもっともなんだけど、こればっかりはどうしようもない。
　そもそもあんな夢を見た後で、まともな食事なんて摂れる筈がなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ugh…”
Kohaku was perfectly right, but that didn’t make eating any more possible.
After a dream like that, there was no way I could stomach a normal meal.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Uh……"
What she says is true, but I just don't feel like it right now.
After seeing that dream, I can't bring myself to eat.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「……姉さん。
志貴さまは朝からご気分が優れないようでしたから、あまり無理を言うのもどうかと思います」
「もう、翡翠ちゃんは志貴さんに甘いんですから――――って、あれ？」
「志貴さん、今朝もご気分が優れないんですか？」
　じっ、と琥珀さんが見つめてくる。
　それに釣られてなのか、翡翠と秋葉もまじまじと見つめてきた。
　……なんていうか、あんまりその場しのぎの誤魔化しが通じる雰囲気じゃない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Sister. Master Shiki has seemed unwell since this morning, so I don’t think we should force him.”
“Honestly, Hisui, you’re far too soft on Shiki—wait, what?”
“Shiki, are you feeling ill again this morning?”
Kohaku fixes me with an unwavering stare.
As if drawn in by her, Hisui and Akiha begin studying me just as intently.
Somehow, this does not feel like an atmosphere where a flimsy excuse will survive.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Nee-san.
If Shiki-sama does not feel well, I do not think you should force him."
"Hisui-chan, you are too indulgent when it comes to Shiki-san----huh?"
"Shiki-san, you're not feeling well again this morning?"
Kohaku-san stares at me.
As if on cue, Hisui and Akiha add their serious stares on me as well.
…… I guess I really can't go on fooling myself.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「―――実をいうと、あまりいい気分じゃないんだ。
朝食は食べるけど、できれば流動食にしてもらえないかな。
ここんところ体調も悪くて、あまり味を感じられないぐらいだし」
　本当の事を告白すると、琥珀さんはそうですか、と残念そうに俯いてしまった。
　……料理担当として、きっと思うところがあるんだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“—To tell you the truth, I do feel pretty bad. I’ll eat breakfast, but could you make it something I can drink? I haven’t been well lately, and I can barely taste anything.”
When I confess the truth, Kohaku lowers her eyes in disappointment.
As the one who does the cooking, she must have feelings about that.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---To tell the truth, I do feel a little under the weather.
I can eat, but could you make it something I don't need to chew?
I feel pretty bad, and I can't really taste anything."
After telling the truth, Kohaku-san says "Oh, I see," and looks a little downcast.
…… As the one in charge of cooking, she probably feels something about what I said.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「……あの、志貴さま？
　志貴さまの体調不良は、生活環境が変わったからだと思います。
　ですからその、お屋敷の生活が合わないようでしたら、しばらく有間の家に戻って養生なされてはどうでしょう……？」
「………………」
　翡翠の意見は、純粋に俺の体を心配しての事だった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki? I think Master Shiki’s health may have suffered because his living situation changed so suddenly.
If life at the mansion doesn’t agree with you, perhaps you should return to the Arima family for a while and recuperate…?”
“…”
Hisui’s suggestion comes from nothing but genuine concern for me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Um, Shiki-sama?
I think you are not feeling well because there was a change in your environment.
So, if the mansion is not suitable for you, maybe you should go back and live with the Arima family for a while……?"
"………………"
Hisui's opinion is driven by a sincere concern about my health.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
……確かにこの屋敷に帰ってきてから、遠野志貴の日常はおかしくなってきている。
　それに八年前の約束が消えてしまった事もあるし、無理をして残るよりは数日だけでも有間の家に戻って、体の調子を元通りにしたほうがいいのかもしれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
It’s true that Shiki Tohno’s ordinary life has begun to unravel ever since he returned to this mansion.
The promise from eight years ago has vanished as well; rather than force myself to stay, perhaps I should spend a few days with the Arimas and give my body a chance to recover.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Ever since I came back, my life has been strange.
Since that promise from eight years ago has apparently been forgotten; maybe it's better for my health if I go back and live at the Arimas'.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「……そうだね。
それもいいかもしれない。
　まだ一週間しかたってないけど、このまま合わないようだったらしばらく家を離れて、体調を戻してくるよ」
　まぁそれもまだ先の話だけど、と付け足す。
―――と。
　唐突に、秋葉がソファーから立ちあがった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Yes. That might be a good idea.
It’s only been a week, but if I still can’t adjust, I’ll leave for a while and get my health back.”
Though that wouldn’t be for some time yet, I add.
―――At that.
Akiha abruptly rises from the sofa.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Yeah.
That may be good too.
Although I've only been here for a week, if I don't seem to get used to it soon, I'll leave for a while and go regain my health."
"Well, that may be jumping the gun a little bit," I add.
---And then.
Suddenly, Akiha stands up from her sofa.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「あら、だめよ兄さん。
やっと帰ってきたんですから、もう二度とこの屋敷から外には行かないでください。
　それでもまた出ていくというのでしたら、私、兄さんを殺しちゃうんだから」
　にこり、と冗談を言って秋葉はロビーへと去っていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh no, Brother, you’ve only just come home. Please don’t ever leave this mansion again.
If you try to leave us again, I’ll have to kill you.”
With a bright smile at her little joke, Akiha walks out into the lobby.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Oh, that will not do, Nii-san.
You finally came back, so please do not leave again.
If you say you are going to leave one more time, I will kill you, Nii-san."
Akiha smiles as she says that joke and disappears towards the lobby.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「翡翠ちゃん。
秋葉さまは登校の時間ですから、付いていてあげて。
わたしは志貴さんの朝ごはんの支度をするから」
　はい、と返事をして翡翠は秋葉を追いかけていく。
「それじゃ朝ごはんは食べやすいものにしますから、もうちょっとだけ待ってください」
　琥珀さんは早足で厨房へ移動していく。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hisui. It’s time for Miss Akiha to leave for school, so go with her. I’ll prepare Shiki’s breakfast.”
Hisui answers yes and hurries after Akiha.
“I’ll make you something easy to eat, then, so please wait just a little longer.”
Kohaku strides quickly toward the kitchen.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hisui-chan.
It's time for Akiha-sama to go to school, please accompany her to the door.
I'll be taking care of Shiki-san's breakfast."
With a simple "yes", Hisui walks after Akiha.
"Well then, I'll make you something easy for you to eat.
Please wait just a moment."
Kohaku-san walks quickly toward the kitchen.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「―――――――」
　俺はと言うと、ソファーに座ったまま呆然としたままだった。
―――兄さんを殺しちゃうんだから。
　……その言葉が頭から離れない。
　冗談のハズなのに、どうしても、それが冗談には聞き取れなかったせいだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
I remain on the sofa, too stunned to move.
―――I’ll have to kill you, Brother.
Those words refuse to leave my mind.
It was supposed to be a joke, yet somehow I couldn’t make myself hear it as one.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-------"
I sit on the sofa, dumbstruck.
---I will kill you, Nii-san.
…… Those words won't leave my head.
It's probably because even though it was a joke, it didn't sound like a joke to me.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
―――昼休みになった。
　有彦はいつものように学校を休んでいる。
「学食にいくか」
　一人で昼飯を食べてもつまらない。
　にぎやかな食堂に行けば、一人きりの昼食も少しは味がでるだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Lunchtime arrives.
Arihiko is absent from school, as usual.
“May as well go to the cafeteria.”
Eating lunch alone is dull.
At least the bustle of the cafeteria might make eating alone a little less dull.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Noon arrives.
As usual, Arihiko is skipping school.
"I guess I'll go to the cafeteria."
I don't feel like eating by myself here.
Maybe if I go to the lively cafeteria, my appetite may pick up.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
予想通り、食堂は派手に賑わっていた。
　何十人という行列に並んで、手堅いＡ定食を買ってテーブルにつく。
　生徒たちの話し声を聞きながら昼食を食べる。
――――と。
　一瞬、なにかイヤな映像が見えた。
entries.maoEnglish:
As expected, the cafeteria is roaring with activity.
I join a line dozens deep, buy the safe Set A, and find a table.
I eat amid the chatter of the other students.
――――Then.
For an instant, an ugly image flashes before me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
As expected, the cafeteria is full of people.
After waiting in a long line, I buy the tried and true meal set A and walk to a table.
Listening to the voices of everyone else, I begin to eat.
----And then.
For a moment, I see a terrible image.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「……？
　テレビの映像かな」
　食堂の奥にでーん、と鎮座する大型テレビを眺める。
　うちの学校はその日の朝のニュースを録画しておいて、昼休みに食堂で流すという紙一重のサービスを実施している。
　今日も今日とて数時間遅れのニュースを映し出しているテレビをぼんやりと眺める。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What was that? Something on television?”
I look toward the enormous television enthroned at the back of the cafeteria.
Our school records the morning news and replays it during lunch—a service of distinctly questionable value.
Today, as ever, I gaze blankly at news already several hours old.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……?
Is it the television screen?"
I gape at the large television mounted on the wall at the end of the cafeteria.
At my school, they record the morning news and replay it at lunch.
I just stare dumbfounded at the news broadcast that is several hours late.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「――――うそ」
　そのニュースを見て、愕然とした。
　テレビに映し出されているのは、昨日、夢で見た少女の顔だった。
　ニュースキャスターが喋っている。
　画面には大きく、吸血鬼殺人・新しい犠牲者、なんていう血文字のテロップ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“—No.”
The broadcast leaves me frozen.
The face on the screen belongs to the girl from last night’s dream.
The screen bears a huge blood-red caption.
VAMPIRE MURDER—ANOTHER VICTIM.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----No way…"
I watch the news in amazed horror.
Shown in the television is the alley that I saw last night in my dream.
The newscaster is talking.
On the screen, the words "Vampire Serial Killer's New Victim" appears in bloody lettering.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
……少女は、とりあえず命を取り留めたらしい。
　体の血液を搾取された少女は病院で治療を受けているという。
　意識は不明。
回復の見込みも不明。
　……誰が少女を襲い、その血を奪ったのかも不明。
　画面に映し出された少女の写真は、間違いなく昨夜の少女だ。
―――なら、不明ではない事が一つだけある。
　　　彼女を襲った犯人は、紛れもなく――――
entries.maoEnglish:
Apparently the girl survived, for now.
The report says she is in the hospital after having the blood drained from her body.
Her consciousness is unknown. Her prospects for recovery are unknown.
Who attacked her and stole her blood is also unknown.
But the photograph on the screen is unmistakably the girl from last night.
―――Then there is one thing that isn’t unknown.
The person who attacked her was beyond any doubt—
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… It appears that the girl was saved.
The girl is in the hospital recovering from having her blood drained.
She is still unconscious.
Chances of recovery are unknown.
…… The identity of who attacked and stole her blood is also unknown.
The picture of the girl on the television is unmistakably that girl from last night.
---That means there's one thing that isn't unknown.
The criminal who attacked her is, without a doubt----
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「――――――」
　気が、遠くなったような。
「なん………で？」
　アレは夢だ。
間違いなく夢だった。
　なのに実際夢と同じ人間が、同じように、血を吸われてしまっている。
「吸血鬼は、もう、いないのに」
　弓塚は俺がこの手で殺した。
　吸血鬼事件なんていうものは、もう二度と起こらないはずじゃないのか。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
I feel consciousness slipping away.
“Why?”
That was a dream. There can be no doubt that it was a dream.
Yet the same person has suffered the same fate in reality, her blood taken exactly as I saw it.
“But there aren’t any vampires left.”
I killed Yumizuka with my own hands.
Wasn’t that supposed to mean the vampire murders could never happen again?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------"
I start to feel faint.
"How……… come?"
That was a dream.
It had to be a dream.
But in reality, the same person in my dream, had her blood sucked out the same way in my dream.
"That vampire should be gone already."
I killed Yumizuka with my own hands.
Those killings, they shouldn't be happening anymore.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「俺が――――殺した？」
　そう、殺した。
　弓塚をこの手で刺した時のように。
　はあはあと息をあげて、昨日の夜も見知らぬ少女を―――
entries.maoEnglish:
“I――――killed her?”
Yes, I killed her.
Just as I stabbed Yumizuka with my own hand.
Panting for breath that same way, last night I took that unknown girl and―――
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I----killed?"
Yes, I killed.
Just like the time when I killed Yumizuka.
While breathing hard, last night, that woman I've never met---
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
だから言ったでしょう志貴くん？
　我慢したって、無駄なんだって。
entries.maoEnglish:
I told you so, Shiki.
Holding back never did any good.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Didn't I tell you, Shiki-kun?
It's useless to resist it.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
何をとぼけてやがる。
　オマエは俺以上の殺人鬼じゃないか。
entries.maoEnglish:
Who are you kidding?
You’re an even worse killer than I am.
entries.mirrorMoon:
What are you talking about?
You're more of a killer than I am.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「うっ―――」
　吐き気を堪えて席を立つ。
　教室には戻れない。
　そのまま街へと走り出していた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Urgh―――”
Fighting the urge to vomit, I stagger to my feet.
I can’t go back to the classroom.
Before I know it, I’m running out into the city.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ugh---"
Resisting the urge to throw up, I get up from my seat.
I can't go back to class.
I find myself running into the city.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
―――夢で見た場所にやってきた。
　まわりには警察官が何人かいて、路地裏へは立ち入り禁止のテープがはられていた。
「―――同じだ」
　たしかに夢の中でここを通った。
―――いや、アレは夢じゃない。
　もう、夢だって誤魔化すことなんてできない。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――I reach the place from my dream.
Several police officers are standing nearby, and tape seals off the alley.
“—It’s the same.”
I passed through this place in the dream.
―――No—that wasn’t a dream.
I can’t hide behind that excuse any longer.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---I come to the place I saw in my dream.
There are several policemen around the area, and tape reading "Police Line Do Not Cross" is stretched across the alley.
"---Exactly the same."
Without a doubt, this is the place I went to in my dream.
---No, it wasn't a dream.
I can't delude myself into thinking it is a dream any longer.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「…………」
　ここに長くいても警察の人たちに睨まれるだけだ。
　……今さら学校には戻れない。
このまま、屋敷に戻るしかなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
Staying here will only draw suspicion from the police.
It’s too late to return to school. I have no choice but to go back to the mansion.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"………"
Even if I stay here longer, the cops will only stare at me.
…… I can't go back to school now, so I guess I'll go back to the mansion.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
まだ午後二時になったばかりのためか、ロビーには誰も待ってはいなかった。
「………………」
　都合がいいといえば都合がいい。
今は誰にも会いたくない。
　ふと、窓ガラスに視線を移す。
　そこにいるのは青ざめた顔をした、別人のような遠野志貴だった。
　別人のような自分。
　別人のようなユメ。
　意識には表れない、
　記憶にだけ残る殺人の跡。
entries.maoEnglish:
Perhaps because it is only just after two in the afternoon, no one is waiting in the lobby.
“…”
That suits me. I don’t want to see anyone.
My eyes drift to the window.
Reflected in the glass is Shiki Tohno, pale-faced and looking like a stranger.
A self like someone else.
A dream belonging to someone else.
A murder absent from consciousness,
leaving its traces only in memory.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Since it's not even two o'clock yet, Hisui isn't waiting in the lobby.
"……………"
I can say I got lucky.
I don't feel like seeing anyone right now.
I glance at my reflection in the window.
The pale face looks like a completely different Tohno Shiki.
My self that seems like another person.
That dream that seemed like it belonged to another person.
That which cannot be noticed,
the traces of the killing that only remains in my memory.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
くらりと。
　目の前が、闇に変わっていく。
entries.maoEnglish:
The world sways.
Darkness spreads across my sight.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Dizziness.
Before me, my vision goes black.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「違う――――！
　俺は親父と同じなんかじゃないっ……………！！！」
　必死に眩暈をこらえて、倒れそうになる体を立て直した。
「――――――親父だ」
　親父の部屋に行って、親父がどんな病状だったのか調べてみればいい。
　そうすれば俺は遠野槙久とは違う事がはっきりするし、もし同じなら――――何か、解決策のようなものが残っているかもしれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“No—! I’m nothing like my father…!”
I fight the vertigo and wrench my collapsing body upright.
“—Father.”
I can search his room and find out what illness he had.
Then I’ll know whether I’m different from Makihisa Tohno—and if I’m not, perhaps he left behind some kind of cure.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No----!
I'm not the same as my old man…………!!!"
Desperately fending off the dizziness, I try to stay upright.
"------My old man."
I can go to my old man's room, and I can find out about his illness.
If I do that, I can confirm that I'm not the same.
If I am the same----there might be a way to help myself.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
……遠野槙久の部屋は一階の西館、琥珀さんの部屋の隣にある。
　学校を抜け出してきた事が幸いした。
　この時間、琥珀さんも翡翠も秋葉の姿もない。
　ナイフを取り出して、メガネを外す。
　扉の鍵を『切断』しようとして、メガネを戻した。
　部屋に、鍵はかかっていなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
Makihisa Tohno’s room is in the west wing of the first floor, beside Kohaku’s.
For once, cutting school has worked in my favor.
At this hour, Kohaku, Hisui, and Akiha are all gone.
I draw my knife and remove my glasses.
I’m about to cut the lock on the door when I put the glasses back on.
The door isn’t locked.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… His room is on the first floor in the western part of the mansion, next to Kohaku-san's room.
It was fortunate that I left school early.
At this time, no one else is around.
I pull out my knife and take off my glasses.
I try to cut the "line" of the door's lock and put my glasses back on.
The room was not locked.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
親父の部屋は当時のままだ。
　並べられた書籍はその大部分が学術書で、これといって興味を引くものはない。
　今の自分がほしいものは親父の日記や手記だ。
　几帳面だった親父のことだから、まず間違いなくそういった類のものを遺しているハズ―――

「……くそ。
さすがに目の届く場所には見あたらないか」
　あるとしたら鍵のかかった所だろう。
　机の引き出しあたりを、とりあえず見てみよう。
entries.maoEnglish:
My father’s room is exactly as it was.
Most of the books lining the shelves are academic texts, nothing that interests me.
What I need is a diary or personal journal.
Knowing how meticulous he was, he must have left something of the kind—
“Damn. I suppose he wouldn’t leave it lying in plain sight.”
If anything exists, it will be somewhere locked.
I’ll start with the desk drawers.
entries.mirrorMoon:
My old man's room is just like it always was.
Nearly all of the rows of books are educational reports, and nothing catches my attention.
What I want right now is my old man's journal or notes.
The old man was extremely methodical.
There certainly has to be something like that lying around here somewhere---

"…… Of course, they're not just lying about where anyone can see them."
Maybe they're locked away somewhere.
I should probably look in these desk drawers first.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
なりふりかまっている場合じゃない。
　メガネを外して『線』を視る。
　ナイフを使って、引き出しの鍵の『線』を切った。
　机の中には紙を紐で束ねた古い記録書と、手記らしい本があった。
entries.maoEnglish:
This is no time for scruples.
I remove my glasses and look for a line.
With the knife, I cut the line on the drawer’s lock.
Inside the desk are an old bundle of records tied with string and a book that looks like a journal.
entries.mirrorMoon:
This isn't time to be fooling around.
Taking off my glasses, I look at the "lines".
Using my knife, I cut the "lines" on the drawer.
Inside, there appears to be some old documents bundled together and what seems to be a journal.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
まず古い記録書に目を通す。
「……これ、うちの家系図かな」
　間違いない。
　遠野マキヒサの後には遠野シキ、遠野アキハという名前がある。
　そのすぐ後ろに、ナナヤという単語があった。
「……親父のヤツ、十年前に養子をとってる。
……けど、それもすぐに病死してるのか」
　十年前っていえば、俺が小学一年生の頃だ。
　そんな大昔のことなら、覚えていないのも当然か。
entries.maoEnglish:
I examine the old records first.
“Could this be our family tree?”
There is no mistake.
After Makihisa Tohno come the names Shiki Tohno and Akiha Tohno.
Immediately behind them appears the word Nanaya.
“Father adopted a child ten years ago. But the child died of illness soon afterward.”
Ten years ago, I would have been in first grade.
If it happened that long ago, no wonder I don’t remember.
entries.mirrorMoon:
First, I look at the old documents.
"…… This is, my family tree?"
Definitely.
Right after Tohno MAKIHISA is written Tohno SHIKI and Tohno AKIHA.
And right after that, the word "Nanaya" is written there.
"Eh…… my old man, he adopted a son ten years ago?
…… Ah, but he passed away shortly thereafter."
Ten years ago, that would mean I was just in elementary school.
That long ago, it's only natural that I wouldn't remember.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「……しかし、うちの当主ってのは本当に短命なんだな。
親父も五十前に病死してるし、その前は三十歳の時に事故死、か。
……その前は十八歳で自殺している―――」
――――いや、待て。
　いくらなんでも、これは、おかしい。
entries.maoEnglish:
“The heads of this family really do die young. Father died of illness before he reached fifty, and the head before him died in an accident at thirty. The one before that committed suicide at eighteen―――”
――――No, wait.
This is too strange.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Let's see…… the heads of the household have had pretty short lifespans.
My old man died before he was fifty, and before that, before thirty in an accident… before that, eighteen years of age, with suicide---"
----No, wait a second.
No matter how you look at it, this is strange.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
しっかりと家系図に目を通すと、遠野家の人間はみな異常な死に方をしていた。
　発狂死。
事故死。
他殺。
行方不明。
死産。
　……誰一人として、寿命で静かに他界した者がいない。
「な…………」
　その一連の記録は、呪われてるとしかいいようのない。
　とくに、その大半の死因は発狂。
遠野の人間は、その大部分が自らの命を断つことで他界してしまっている。
entries.maoEnglish:
When I study the family tree more closely, I find that every member of the Tohno family died abnormally.
Death by madness. Accident. Murder. Disappearance. Stillbirth.
Not one of them reached the end of a natural life and died in peace.
“What…”
The record reads like the history of a cursed family.
Madness accounts for most of the deaths. The greater part of the Tohno line ended by taking their own lives.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Looking through the family tree, all members of the Tohno household have died strangely.
Madness.
Accidents.
Murder.
Disappearances.
Still birth.
…… Not one of them lived a long life, or even died peacefully.

"Wha…………"
This entire document is filled with horrible fates.
Even worse, most of the causes of death are madness.
Most of these ended up taking their own lives.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「おかしい―――おかしいぞ、これ」
　だが、一体なにがおかしいのかが解らない。
「……あとは……親父の手記か」
　わりと新しい装丁をした手記を手にとる。
――――どくん。
　鼓動が響く。
　この中身を見てはいけないと、心のどこかで悟っている。
　だが、今さら戻れない。
　ごくりと唾を飲みこんで、親父の手記を開いた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“This is wrong—something is wrong here.”
Yet I can’t say what is wrong.
“That leaves Father’s journal.”
I pick up the comparatively new-looking volume.
――――Thump.
My heartbeat reverberates through me.
Somewhere inside, I know I must not read what is written here.
But I’ve come too far to turn back.
I swallow and open my father’s journal.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"That's strange---all of this is strange."
But I can't exactly place my finger on it.
"…… Next is…… my old man's journal."
I pick up the journal which has a relatively new binding.
----Thump, Thump.
My heart starts to pound.
My heart seems to understand that I shouldn't be opening this.
But I can't turn back now.
Swallowing hard, I open my old man's journal.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
―――遠野の血筋には魔が宿る。
　書き出し文は、そういった類のものだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Something demonic dwells in the Tohno bloodline.
That is how it begins.
entries.mirrorMoon:
------There is a demon lurking inside the Tohno bloodline.
The opening statement is in those lines.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
それは、比喩ではない。
　遠野の祖先は本当に『人間でないモノ』との混血で、子孫にあたる自分たちにも、その『人間でないモノ』の血が混ざっている、という事だった。
　血は。
　濃い者と薄い者に分かれる。
　血が薄い者なら普通の人間として問題なく暮らしていけるが、濃い者であるのなら、人間として生きていく事はできない。
entries.maoEnglish:
It is no metaphor.
The Tohno ancestors truly mingled their blood with things that were not human, and that inhuman blood still runs in us, their descendants.
That blood manifests in some more strongly than in others.
Those in whom it runs thin can live without difficulty as ordinary humans.
Those in whom it runs thick cannot live as human beings.
entries.mirrorMoon:
And that isn't just a simple metaphor.
The ancestors of the Tohno were a mixed breed of "something nonhuman" and human.
We, being their descendants, also have this element of "something nonhuman" in our blood.
In regards to our blood…
There are those with strong and those with weak nonhuman blood.
Those with weak nonhuman blood can live their lives as ordinary people, but those with strong nonhuman blood can never live a normal life.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
遠野の血が濃い者は特別な力を身体に宿して生まれてくる。
　それは死ににくい体であったり、
　手を使わず物を動かす力であったり、
　他人から体液を搾取する牙であったりした。
　この血。
　この血が濃く現れだした遠野の人間は、段々と理性を失っていく。
　そうして理性を失ってしまった遠野の人間はその大部分が人を食う悪鬼に成り果てる。
　故に、遠野の当主は、そうなってしまった同族を処罰する責任があるという。
entries.maoEnglish:
Those born with a strong inheritance of Tohno blood bear special powers within their bodies.
Flesh that is difficult to kill,
The ability to move objects without touching them,
Or fangs that drain bodily fluids from others.
That blood.
When it begins to manifest strongly in a Tohno, reason slowly erodes.
Most who lose it altogether become man-eating demons.
The head of the Tohno family is therefore charged with punishing any member of the clan who falls that far.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Those with strong Tohno blood are born with special powers.
It could be a body that is resistant to death,
it could be an ability to move things without touching them,
or it could be fangs used to take bodily fluids from other people.

This blood.
When this blood becomes too strong, the members of the Tohno family start to gradually lose their sanity.
The majority of those become demons that feed on human flesh.
So, the head of the Tohno household carries the responsibility of punishing those who have turned into such a monster.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「――――――――」
　……どうかしてる。
　親父は、なにを。
夢物語みたいなことを、こんなに真面目に書き記しているんだろうか。
――――手記は、いつのまにか親父の語りに移り変わっていた。
　日付はおよそ九年前。
　手記には乱れた文字が続いている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
This is insane.
What could Father have been thinking? Why record such fairy-tale nonsense with such deadly seriousness?
――――Without my noticing, the journal has shifted into my father’s own voice.
The entry is dated roughly nine years ago.
The handwriting that follows is erratic.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"--------"
It's messed up.
My old man, what was he trying to say?
Writing so seriously about something that's more like a fairy tale.
-----The journal turns more into the old man's rant.
The date is roughly nine years ago.
The handwriting starts to get erratic.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
ついに、自分の血の昂ぶりが押さえられなくなってきた。
　共感者の一族の孤児を手に入れ、自らの意志を強化したところで、それもいずれ効かなくなるだろう。
　私が私でいられる時間は、あとわずかなものかもしれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
At last, the rising of my blood has grown impossible to contain.
I acquired an orphan of a resonator clan and used the child to reinforce my will, but in time even that will cease to suffice.
Little time may remain in which I can still be myself.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I am no longer able to suppress my raging blood.
I was able to obtain an orphan from a family of Synchronizers, so this should help me strengthen my mind.
However, it really is only a matter of time before I go insane.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
……恐ろしくなる。
　気がつけば、一日の半分がまったく記憶にない。
　私は、私の知らないところで、自身の反転している衝動をあの子供に押し付けてしまっている。
　このままでは。
　いずれ完全に理性をなくして、ただのケモノに成り果てるだろう。
　私が私としていられる時間はあとどれほど残っているのか。
entries.maoEnglish:
I am afraid.
When awareness returns, I find half the day entirely missing from my memory.
Without knowing it, I am forcing the impulses of my Inversion onto that child.
At this rate.
I will eventually lose all reason and become a mere beast.
How much longer can I remain myself?
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… It is terrifying.
When I come to, I find that I can't even remember half of the day.
During that time, I'm forcing my inversion impulse on that child.
If this keeps up,
it is only a matter of time before I completely lose my sanity and turn into a beast.
I don't even know how much time I have left to remain as myself.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
いや、あの感応者の子供がいればあと数年は保つだろう。
　だがあの子供のほうは私の行為に耐えきれまい。
　おそらく、あの子供が壊れた後、私は自らの手で自分の命を絶たなければなるまい。
　……皮肉なものだ。
　自身を守るために多くの障害を排除してきた私は、結局は自身の手で命を絶たなければならないらしい。
　それとも、これは七夜の呪いなのか。
　戯れでヤツの息子を飼ってみたが、その程度ではヤツの怨念は断ち切れなかったという事か。
entries.maoEnglish:
No—with that resonator child, I may endure for several years yet.
But the child cannot withstand what I am doing. Once the child breaks, I will most likely have to end my life with my own hands.
How ironic.
After removing so many obstacles to preserve myself, I am apparently destined to die by my own hand.
Or is this the curse of Nanaya?
I kept his son as a pet on a whim, but perhaps even that was not enough to sever the father’s hatred.
entries.mirrorMoon:
No.
If that child is here, then I can probably last for a few more years.
But that child will not be able to bear that.
After that child breaks, I will have to take my own life.
…… It is incredibly ironic.
I eliminated so many things in order to preserve myself, but in the end, I will probably have to commit suicide.
Or maybe this is the curse of the Nanayas.
I end up adopting his son, but I guess I could not lift their grudge with such a thing.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
だが、今更過去の行為を贖う事などできない。
無様な死が待つというのならば潔く受け入れよう。
　だがそれまでは―――私は子供たちを守らなければならない。
　アキハの血は薄い。
アキハは自分から望まないかぎり、私のようにはならないだろう。
　問題はシキだ。
あの子は、私にひどく近い。
せめてあの子だけには、私と同じ苦しみを味あわせたくはない。
　……遠野の血が異常な血だというのなら、あの子を遠野という名前から遠ざけて、様子を見るしかないだろう―――――
entries.maoEnglish:
But it is too late to atone for what I have done. If a shameful death awaits me, I will accept it without protest.
Until then, however—I must protect the children.
Akiha’s blood is thin. Unless she chooses otherwise, she will never become what I have.
The problem is SHIKI. That child is very like me. If nothing else, I would spare him the same suffering.
If the Tohno blood itself is the source of this abnormality, I can only remove the child from the Tohno name and observe what follows―――――
entries.mirrorMoon:
But, I can't make up for the events of the past.
If death is waiting for me, then I must accept it when the time comes.
But until then---I must protect my children.
Akiha's blood is weak.
Unless she wishes it herself, she does not have to suffer the same fate.
The problem is SHIKI.
That child is incredibly close to me.
More than anything else, I do not want that child to suffer my fate.
…… If the Tohno blood is unnatural, I need to distance him as much as possible from the Tohno name and see how he will fare----
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「は――――――あ」
　まだ途中である手記から目を逸らして、肺に沈澱した厭な空気を吐き出した。
　……気分が悪くなる。
　親父の手記の内容は、あまりに非現実すぎていて、気味が悪い。
　親父は躁鬱が激しかったわけじゃない。
　ただ、自分でも解らないうちに凶暴になっていただけだ。
　今の―――遠野志貴と同じように。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Haaah…”
I look away from the unfinished journal and expel the foul air congealed in my lungs.
I feel sick.
What Father has written is so unreal that it turns my stomach.
Father hadn’t suffered violent swings between mania and depression.
He had simply become violent without knowing it.
Just like—Shiki Tohno now.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I let out a deep breath and expel the air from my lungs.
I take a break from reading.
…… It makes me sick.
The contents of my old man's journal are so far away from reality that it's plain weird.
My old man didn't just have manic-depression.
Rather, he just became violent without his knowing.
Just like Tohno Shiki right now.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「――――おかしい」
　だが、気になったのはその事ではなかった。
　親父はシキとアキハ、とおかしな表記をしている。
　気になって先ほどの家系図を見返すと、アキハは秋葉となっているがシキは、四季、なんていうふうに記されていた。
「四季……たしかにシキって読む、けど」
　これ以上考えるのはまずいと直感したが、思考の奔流は止まらない。
「……この感応者って何のコトだろう。
養子にとった子供の事……なのかな」
　それもどこか違う気がする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“—Something’s wrong.”
But that isn’t what troubles me.
Father wrote the names SHIKI and Akiha phonetically, in an odd manner.
I check the family tree again; Akiha’s name is written normally, but SHIKI’s is given with the characters for ‘four seasons.’
“Four Seasons—that can be read Shiki, but――――”
Instinct warns me not to think any further, yet the torrent won’t stop.
“What does this word resonator mean? Does it refer to the adopted child?”
Somehow that feels wrong too.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----That's strange."
But, that isn't what concerns me.
He writes SHIKI and AKIHA strangely.
Looking back to the family tree, I see that he writes "Akiha" using the Chinese characters for "Autumn Leaves", while "SHIKI" is written using the characters for "Four Seasons".
"The characters for 'Four Seasons' can certainly be pronounced as 'SHIKI', but the characters in my name are 'Intention' and 'Esteemed'."
I have a feeling that thinking too hard about that will be bad, but my train of thought does not stop.
"…… What are these 'Synchronizers'?
Maybe the adopted child?"
But, I feel that's wrong too.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
ともかく、手記はまだ半分だ。
　最後まで目を通せばこの疑問も解決するだろう。
　だがそれは―――本当に、解決していい疑問なのか。
「……………」
―――吐き気がする。
　とてもじゃないけど立っていられない。
　早く。
　早く部屋に戻って眠らないと、頭がどうにかしてしまいそうだった。
　それでも、手記のページをめくる事にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
In any case, half the journal remains.
If I read to the end, these questions may be answered.
But are they—truly questions I should answer?
“…”
―――I’m going to be sick.
I can barely stay on my feet.
Quickly.
If I don’t return to my room and sleep, I feel as though my mind will come apart.
Even so, I turn the page.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Anyway, I've only read half-way through all of this.
If I read through it completely, I might come up with a solution.
But---do I really want to find out?
"………"
------I feel like vomiting.
I can't stay standing.
Hurry.
I must hurry back to my room and sleep; it feels like there is something wrong with my head.

But still, I decide to go back reading the journal.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
―――手記の残りは、何かの記録だった。
　日付は八年前の夏の日から始まって、その後は少しずつ月日が経過しているようだ。
「…………」
　意味が解らないまでも、とりあえず目を通してみることにする。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――The remainder of the journal is some kind of record.
The entries begin on a summer day eight years ago, then advance little by little through the months and years.
“…”
Though I don’t understand what they mean, I begin to read.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---The rest of it seems to be a record of some sort.
The date starts in the summer of eight years ago, and about a month after that.

"…………"
I don't understand it yet, but I continue to look through it.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
〇月〇日。
　息子のシキが遠野の血に傾斜する。
　シキ、その場に居あわせた養子を殺害。
（養子は七夜の跡取り息子である。
琥珀、翡翠といった感応者の一族ではないのは不幸中の幸いだった）
　シキは反転が酷い。
よって処罰するしかないと判断した。
遠野の当主の役割といえ、我が子を殺すのは辛い。
entries.maoEnglish:
Month ○, Day ○.
My son SHIKI succumbs to the Tohno blood.
SHIKI kills the adopted child present at the scene.
It is a small mercy that he is the Nanaya heir rather than a member of a resonator clan such as Kohaku and Hisui’s.
SHIKI’s Inversion is severe. I therefore judge that he must be punished. Even as part of my duty as head of the Tohno family, it pains me to kill my own son.
entries.mirrorMoon:
~ Month ~ Day
My son SHIKI succumbed to his Tohno blood.
SHIKI, he killed my adopted son who happened to be there.
(The adopted son is the heir of the house Nanaya. I guess it is a blessing in all the unfortunate events that he isn't in the same family as the Synchronizers, like Kohaku and Hisui.)
SHIKI's inversion impulse is terrible.
So it was determined that he must be eliminated.
I have my duty as the head of the Tohno household, but killing my own son is so difficult.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
遠野の血は、アキハよりシキのほうが濃い。
　潜在的なレヴェルではアキハにより旧い起源を感じるが、血の濃さではシキが上回っていた。
　そのために、シキは成人する前に反転してしまったのだろう。
　シキの能力は『不死』と『共融』である。
　シキは蘇った自己の能力を持て余し、結果として近くにいた七夜の養子を殺害し、その命を奪い取った。
　初めての能力行使にしては素晴らしいと言わざるをえまい。
entries.maoEnglish:
The Tohno blood runs more strongly in SHIKI than in Akiha.
On a latent level I sense an older Origin in Akiha, but SHIKI’s blood is the more concentrated.
That must be why he underwent Inversion before reaching adulthood.
SHIKI possesses ‘immortality’ and ‘coalescence.’
Unable to control the powers that awakened when he revived, he killed the nearby Nanaya adoptee and took the boy’s life for himself.
For a first exercise of his abilities, the result was undeniably impressive.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The Tohno blood is stronger in SHIKI than in AKIHA.
Talking about potential, I feel an older origin in Akiha's blood, but SHIKI's Tohno blood runs much stronger.
I assume that is why SHIKI inverted before he became an adult.
SHIKI's powers are "immortality" and "fusion".
SHIKI could not manage the awakened powers and as a result, killed the adopted Nanaya child, taking his life.
I have to say it was a superb job for using his powers for the first time.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
〇月×日
　シキ、養子、ともに一命を取りとめる。
entries.maoEnglish:
Month ○, Day ×
Both SHIKI and the adopted child survive.
entries.mirrorMoon:
~ Month x Day
Both SHIKI and the adopted son managed to escape death.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
〇月〇日
　社会的な処理が残る。
　シキは七夜の養子を殺害してしまった。
　事実は隠蔽したが、シキは表に出せる状態ではない。
まだ私がつけた傷も癒えていおらず、姿カタチも変貌してしまっている。
　とても遠野シキとして人前に出せる状態……人間として表現できる生命ではない。
　七夜の養子はまだ生きている。
　アレが存命している間、まだ役にたってもらう事にした。
　反対意見があるのなら返答を願う。
entries.maoEnglish:
Month ○, Day ○
The matter must still be settled in the eyes of society.
SHIKI killed the Nanaya adoptee.
I concealed the truth, but SHIKI is in no condition to appear in public. The wound I inflicted has yet to heal, and his very shape has transformed.
He cannot be presented as Shiki Tohno, nor can the life he has become be described as human.
The Nanaya adoptee remains alive.
As long as that thing survives, I intend to put it to use.
If there are objections, I request a reply.
entries.mirrorMoon:
~ Month ~ Day
The problem of maintaining appearances to normal society still remains.
SHIKI has killed the adopted Nanaya child.
I have covered up the incident, but SHIKI cannot be shown to the public.
The wound I gave him hasn't healed and his figure has transformed.
He is not in a condition to be brought in front of others as Tohno SHIKI…… he cannot be called a human either.
The Nanaya child still lives.
As long as he lives, I've decided to use him.
If there are any disagreements, I would like to hear them.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
補足。
　七夜の血筋は、ある種殺人鬼を輩出する一族である。
　もしあの養子が生き残ってしまった場合、命を共有して繋がっているシキに悪影響を及ぼすだろう。
　折角理性を取り戻したシキが、七夜の養子に引きずられて『殺人鬼』になってしまう可能性も否定できない。
　そのような事態が起きないよう、養子は目の届く範囲で飼わなければならない。
だが遠野の屋敷に近づける事も許されない。
　管理に適切な分家筋を選んでほしい。
entries.maoEnglish:
Addendum.
The Nanaya bloodline produces a particular breed of killer.
Should the adoptee survive, he may exert a harmful influence on SHIKI, to whom he is joined through their shared life. We cannot dismiss the possibility that SHIKI, having finally regained his reason, will be dragged along by the Nanaya adoptee and become a ‘killer’ himself.
To prevent that outcome, the adopted child must be kept on a short leash and under observation. He must not, however, be allowed anywhere near the Tohno mansion.
Select a suitable branch family to manage him.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Complementarity.
The Nanayas are a family that produces killers.
If that adopted son happens to stay alive, the link between him and SHIKI may corrupt SHIKI's mind.
Even if SHIKI regains his sanity, I cannot deny the possibility of the Nanaya child's influence turning him into a killer.
To prevent this from occurring, we must have him somewhere where we can keep an eye on him.
But we cannot allow him near the Tohno mansion either.
I should have him raised by an appropriate branch of the family.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
〇月×日。
　……遠野の血に目覚めてしまったシキ。
　一度臨死体験をしたためか、今では以前のような理性が戻ってくれた。
　だが、いつ何かの拍子で反転してしまうかはわからない。
不本意ではあるが、シキも遠野の屋敷に近づける事はできない。
　シキの世話は信頼できる使用人に一任する。
entries.maoEnglish:
Month ○, Day ×.
SHIKI has awakened to the Tohno blood.
Perhaps because he passed so close to death, his former reason has returned for now.
But there is no knowing what stimulus might send him into Inversion again. Much as I regret it, SHIKI cannot be allowed near the Tohno mansion either.
His care will be entrusted entirely to a reliable servant.
entries.mirrorMoon:
~ Month x Day
…… The Tohno blood that has awakened within SHIKI.
Maybe it is because he was so close to death, but he has regained his sanity like before.
But I don't know if something will cause him to invert again.
Even though it tears me apart, I cannot allow SHIKI near the Tohno mansion either.
I place him in the care of a trusted servant.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
〇月×日。
　七夜の息子を分家筋に預ける。
　アキハが私を嫌う。
　アキハにしてみれば二人の兄を同時に失った事になる。
私が嫌われるのは当然かもしれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
Month ○, Day ×.
The son of Nanaya is placed with a branch family.
Akiha has come to hate me.
From her perspective, she lost both her brothers at once. Perhaps her hatred is only natural.
entries.mirrorMoon:
~ Month x Day
I put my adopted son from the Nanaya family into the care of another branch of our family.
AKIHA hates me.
AKIHA has lost both of her brothers at the same time, so I suppose it is only natural.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
○月×日。
　アキハを次期当主として教育する。
　一族を管理する当主として必要な能力に関しては、アキハは十分すぎるほど才能があった。
　シキが“不死”であるのならば、
　アキハは“略奪”である。
（兄妹故、共融能力は共に備えている）
　悔やまれる。
アキハが十年早く生まれていれば、軋間の手など借りずに七夜を始末できただろうに。
entries.maoEnglish:
Month ○, Day ×.
Akiha’s education as the next head begins.
In the abilities required to govern the clan, she possesses more talent than she could ever need.
If SHIKI is ‘immortality,’ then
Akiha is ‘plunder.’
(As brother and sister, both possess coalescence)
It is regrettable. Had Akiha been born ten years earlier, I could have disposed of Nanaya without borrowing Kishima’s hand.
entries.mirrorMoon:
~ Month X Day
I start to raise Akiha as the next head of the household.
AKIHA has more than enough talent to carry out her duties as the head of the household.
SHIKI may have the ability of "Immortality",
but Akiha has the power to "plunder."
(As siblings, both of them have the ability to share and take life energy.)
It is regretful.
If only she had been born ten years ago, I would have been able to eliminate the Nanayas without the help from the Kishimas.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
だが注意せねばならない。
　略奪は諸刃だ。
相手の熱を奪うおり、その想念さえも摂り込みかねない。
　私のように―――殺した相手の呪いを招き寄せるような事がないよう、教育しなければならないだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
But caution is essential.
Plunder is a double-edged gift. When she takes another’s heat, she may absorb their thoughts as well.
She must be trained so that she does not, as I did, draw down the curse of one she has killed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
But I have to be careful.
Her ability to "plunder" is a double-edged sword.
She might plunder someone's entire concept while plundering their heat.
Like me--I have to teach her how not to attract the curse of an enemy.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
○月×日。
　アキハが有間の家に行こうとした。
　アキハと七夜の息子を会わせる訳にはいかない。
　アキハは全寮制の学校に転入させ、行動を制限させる。
entries.maoEnglish:
Month ○, Day ×.
Akiha attempted to visit the Arima family.
Akiha and the son of Nanaya cannot be allowed to meet.
She will be transferred to a boarding school and her movements restricted.
entries.mirrorMoon:
~ Month X Day
AKIHA tried to visit the Arima residence.
I cannot let her and my adopted son see each other.
I placed her in a boarding school so that her freedom is limited.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
○月×日。
　近頃、体の具合がおかしくなってきた。
　感応者の娘だけでは限界になったのだろうか。
entries.maoEnglish:
Month ○, Day ×.
My health has begun to fail of late.
Has the resonator girl alone reached the limit of what she can do?
entries.mirrorMoon:
~ Month X Day
Recently, my condition has been getting worse.
It seems like the daughter of the Synchronizers is not enough now.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
○月×日。
　……久しぶりに自分に戻れた。
　こうして筆を持つのは何ヶ月ぶりか。
おそらく次はないだろう。
筆はここで止める事にする。
　私の死後、これはアキハに渡すよう娘に言いつけた。
　アキハがこれを読むかどうかは解らない。
だが一度でも目を通したのなら、必ず処分する事。
　それが私、遠野槙久が我が娘にあてる、ただ一つの遺言である。
entries.maoEnglish:
Month ○, Day ×.
For the first time in many months, I have returned to myself.
How long has it been since I last held a pen? There will probably be no next time. I will lay it down here.
I have instructed the girl to give this to Akiha after my death.
I do not know whether Akiha will read it. If she so much as looks through it once, however, she must destroy it.
This is the sole testament I, Makihisa Tohno, leave to my daughter.
entries.mirrorMoon:
~ Month X Day
…… For the first time in a long time, I've come back to my self.
How many months has it been since I last picked up this pen?
There probably will not be a next time.
I will have to finish writing here.
I gave instructions for this to be given to my daughter AKIHA after my death.
I don't know if AKIHA will ever read this, but if she does read it, it is to be destroyed.
That is my only request for my daughter to fulfill.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「―――――――なんだ、これ」
　十年前に引き取られた養子。
　そんな大昔のこと、俺はまるっきり覚えていない。
　……そいつを、俺が殺した？
　八年前の夏の日、あの傷がつけられた時。
　……そいつが、俺を殺した？
　八年前の夏の日、この傷がつけられた時。
!w3000
entries.maoEnglish:
“—What is this?”
An adopted child taken in ten years ago.
I remember absolutely nothing from so long ago.
I killed him?
On that summer day eight years ago, when I received this wound.
Or did he kill me?
On that summer day eight years ago, when I received this wound.!w3000
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-------What is this?"
The child adopted ten years ago.
I completely forgot about that.
…… I killed him?
That summer day eight years ago, when I received that wound.
…… He, killed me?
That summer day eight years ago, when I received this wound.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「―――――」
　吐きそうだ。
　気持ちが悪い。
　今まで忘れていた記憶が、グチャグチャになって頭の中で跳ねまわっている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
I feel like I’m going to throw up.
I feel sick.
Memories I had forgotten until now are thrashing through my skull, mangled beyond recognition.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-----"
Nausea wells within me.
I feel sick.
That memory that I had forgotten until now runs through my head.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「―――――くっ」
　……解っている。
　ここまで決定的に書かれていたら、潔く認めざるをえないじゃないか。
　そもそも、それなら辻褄は合うんだ。
　俺が有間の家に預けられた理由。
　跡取りである長男を勘当したワケ。
　なんて事はない。
　ようするに、俺は―――志貴という名前をした、シキという人間の代わりでしかなかったワケだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“—Damn it.”
I understand.
When the truth is written this plainly, I have no choice but to accept it.
Besides, it makes everything fit.
Why I was sent to the Arima family.
Why the eldest son and heir was disowned.
It was nothing complicated.
I was only a substitute—a boy named Shiki filling the place of someone named SHIKI.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------"
…… I understand.
Everything has been written down, so I have to accept it.
Besides, everything falls into place.
The reason I was adopted by the Arimas.
The reason I was disinherited as the eldest son.
It's nothing.
In other words, I---Shiki was only a replacement for the one named SHIKI.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「はっ―――なんて、無様」
　自己を呪う呟きをこぼして、手記を投げ捨てた。
　……もう、これ以上知るべきものなんてない。
　ここにいても、ただ時間を無駄にするだけだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ha—how pathetic.”
I whisper the curse at myself and fling the journal away.
There is nothing else here I need to know.
Staying any longer would only waste time.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---What is, this?"
Cursing myself, I toss the journal to the side.
…… There's no need for me to investigate any further.
Staying here any longer is just a waste of my time.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
―――日が落ちる。
　ベッドに倒れこんだまま、あることを考え続けている。
　……冷静になって考えてみると、あの手記から解った事は二つだけだ。
　俺が遠野家の人間ではないこと。
　七夜という家系が殺人鬼を輩出しているということ。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――The sun goes down.
Sprawled across the bed, I keep circling the same thought.
Considered calmly, the journal told me only two things.
I am not a member of the Tohno family.
The Nanaya bloodline produces killers.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---The day ends.
Collapsed on my bed, I just keep on thinking about the same thing.
…… Thinking calmly, there were only two things I found out from that journal.
That I am not a part of the Tohno family.
That the Nanaya lineage turns out a large number of killers.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
俺は遠野槙久とは血の繋がりを持っていない。
　殺人の夢を見るのはあくまで自分だけが原因だった。
　なら、もうするべき事ははっきりとしている。
――――ロビーの方で話し声がした。
「……秋葉、帰ってきたのか」
　ベッドから立ちあがる。
　最後に秋葉の口から真実が聞きたかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
I share no blood with Makihisa Tohno.
The dreams of murder are entirely my own doing.
Which means what I have to do is finally clear.
――――Voices come from the lobby.
“Akiha must be home.”
I rise from the bed.
There is one last thing I want—to hear the truth from Akiha herself.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I don't have any blood ties to Tohno Makihisa.
In other words, those dreams of murder have to be my own.
If that is the case, there's only one thing left to do.
----I hear voices coming from the lobby.
"…… I wonder if Akiha is back."
I get up from bed.
I want to hear the truth from Akiha.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「―――――」
　意を決して扉を叩く。
「秋葉、話がある」
「えっ、兄さんですか？
　どうぞ、お入りになってください」
　秋葉の声は明るい。
　それに決心が鈍りながらも、一息でドアを開けた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
I steel myself and knock.
“Akiha, I need to talk to you.”
“Oh, Brother? Please, come in.”
Her voice is bright.
It weakens my resolve, but I open the door in one motion.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-----"
Gathering up my courage, I knock on the door.
"Akiha, I want to talk."
"Eh, Nii-san?
Please come in."
Her voice is bright and cheerful.
Taking a breath to compose myself, I open the door.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「めずらしいですね。
兄さんが私の部屋を訪ねにきてくれるなんて」
　朝と同じように、秋葉は笑顔をうかべている。
　それを見ていると、このまま無言で立ち去りたくなってしまう。
　……なんだかんだって、俺は。
　遠野志貴である自分も、遠野秋葉っていう妹も、離れがたいほど大切なものだって感じていたのか。
――――それでも。
　問いたださなければいけない事がある。
entries.maoEnglish:
“How unusual. I never expected you to come and visit my room, Brother.”
Akiha is smiling, just as she was this morning.
Seeing that smile makes me want to turn around and leave without a word.
For all my doubts, I…
Perhaps I felt that both my life as Shiki Tohno and Akiha Tohno as my sister were too precious to let go.
――――Even so.
There is something I have to ask.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"It certainly is rare for you to come to my room like this, Nii-san."
Just like this morning, Akiha has a smile on her face.
Seeing that, I just stand there wordlessly, wanting to go back.
…… I guess after all,
I have felt that my self as Tohno Shiki and my sister, Tohno Akiha, are important to me.
----But still.
There is something I have to ask her.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「秋葉――――」
「はい、なんでしょうか兄さん」
　秋葉は何か、楽しい会話を期待するように見つめてくる。
「―――――っ」
　ギリ、と歯を軋ませて、秋葉の目だけを真剣に見返した。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Akiha—”
“Yes, what is it, Brother?”
Akiha looks at me as though expecting some pleasant conversation.
“—”
I grind my teeth and force myself to meet Akiha’s eyes without flinching.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Akiha----"
"Yes, what is it Nii-san?"
Akiha appears to be looking forward to a fun conversation.
"------"
Gritting my teeth, I look her seriously in the eye.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「七夜っていう家の事を教えてくれ。
俺には、その権利があると思う」
「――――――――」
　瞬間。
まるでゼンマイの切れた人形のように、秋葉は全ての動きを止めた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Tell me about the Nanaya family. I think I have a right to know.”
“…”
In that instant. Every movement in Akiha stops, like a clockwork doll whose spring has snapped.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Please tell me about the Nanaya family.
I think I have a right to know."
"--------"
In that instant, Akiha freezes like a puppet whose strings were cut.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「―――――――」
　秋葉は無言で俺を見つめてくる。
「答えないのか。
それじゃあ質問を変えるよ。
　親父―――遠野槙久は二重人格だったんだろ。
それも親父だけじゃない。
遠野家の人間の多くは体になんらかの疾患を抱えている。
……だから俺も自分の体がそうなんだって思ってた。
　けど、それは違う。
俺の貧血は八年前の事故が原因にすぎない。
だって、俺は」
「知ってるわ。
遠野家に養子にとられた子供だから、でしょう？」
　言って。
　一体なんのつもりなのか、秋葉はくすりと笑った。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
Akiha stares at me in silence.
“You won’t answer? Then I’ll ask something else.
Father—Makihisa Tohno—had two personalities, didn’t he? And it wasn’t only him. Many members of the Tohno family suffered from some kind of disorder. That was why I assumed my body was the same.
But I was wrong. My anemia is only the result of the accident eight years ago. Because I—”
“I know. Because you were adopted into the Tohno family, weren’t you?”
She says it.
Akiha gives a quiet laugh for reasons I can’t begin to understand.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-------"
Akiha wordlessly stares at me.
"If you won't answer, then I'll rephrase my question.
My old man---Tohno Makihisa had two personalities, right?
And not just him.
Almost all members of the Tohno family have some sort of illness.
…… I used to think that's what I had.
But, that's wrong.
My anemia came from that incident eight years ago.
Because I…"
"I know.
You were adopted by the Tohno family, right?"
Saying that,
she smiles for some reason.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「秋葉―――？」
　秋葉はゆっくりと、芝居がかったような優雅さで窓際まで歩いていく。
　さあ、とカーテンが風になびく。
　秋葉は窓に手をかけて、くるりと振り返った。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Akiha…?”
With slow, theatrical grace, she crosses to the window.
The curtains lift in the breeze.
Resting one hand on the sill, she turns to face me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Akiha---?"
Akiha slowly and elegantly walks to the window as if she was in a play.
The curtains billow in the breeze.
Placing her hand on the window, she turns around.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「兄さんは遠野家に引き取られた養子で、本当の名前は七夜志貴と言います。
　兄さんの言うとおり、貴方の体が不安定なのも八年前の事故が原因。
……ふぅん。
その様子だと、遠野の人間がみんな人とは違うという事も知ってしまわれたみたいですね」
　秋葉ははっきりと、一番聞きにくかった事実を口にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You were adopted into the Tohno family, Brother; your true name is Shiki Nanaya.
And as you said, your health is unstable because of the accident eight years ago. I see. Judging by your expression, you’ve also learned that none of the Tohnos are entirely human.”
Akiha states the hardest truth of all without the slightest hesitation.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Nii-san, you were adopted by the Tohno family.
Your real name is Nanaya Shiki.
As you say, your health condition is due to that accident eight years ago.
You appear to know already that the members of the Tohno family are different than most humans."
Akiha succinctly says the thing that I would have had the most difficulty asking.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「……秋葉。
それは――――」
「いいのよ。
どうせいつかは知られてしまう事だし、回りくどい事は嫌いだもの。
兄さんが知ってしまったのなら隠す事なんてしない。
　……いいえ、むしろ初めからこうするべきだったんでしょうね。
だって、そうすれば我慢する必要なんてなくなんだもの」
　ね、そうでしょう、兄さん。
　と。
秋葉は自信に満ちた声で、言った。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Akiha. That means—”
“It’s all right. You were bound to discover it one day, and I hate beating around the bush. Now that you know, I won’t try to hide it.
No. In fact, I should have done this from the start—then I would never have needed to hold back.”
“Isn’t that right, Brother?”
So Akiha says. Her voice is brimming with confidence.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Akiha.
That----"
"It is okay.
It was only a matter of time, and I did not like hiding it.
Now that you know, there is no need.
…… No, maybe there never was a need.
Then there's no need to put up with any of this."
"Is that not right, Nii-san?"
Akiha says this with her voice full of confidence.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「秋葉。
それじゃあやっぱり、俺は―――」
「はい。
十年前にお父様によって引き取られた養子です。
けど兄さんはその事を覚えていない。
　兄さん、私たちにはシキというもう一人の遊び仲間がいた事を覚えていますか？」
「――――――いや。
思い出せない」
「でしょうね。
それはお父様が兄さんに暗示をかけたからです」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Akiha. Then I really am—”
“Yes. Father adopted you ten years ago. But you don’t remember that.
Brother, do you remember that we once had another playmate named SHIKI?”
“—No. I can’t remember.”
“Of course not. Father placed a suggestion in your mind.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Akiha.
So like I thought, I---"
"Yes.
You are the one Father adopted ten years ago, but you do not remember it.
Do you remember the SHIKI who used to play with us?"
"------No.
I don't."
"That's right.
It is because Father hypnotized you."
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「……シキは、遠野家の血に耐えられなかった人でした。
兄さんは覚えていないでしょうけど、八年前のあの日、兄さんはシキから私を守ってくれたんですよ。
あの、血に飢えた人殺しになったシキから、身を呈して守ってくれたんです。
　それで兄さんはシキに殺されて、シキもお父様に処分された。
“外れて”しまった一族の者を処分するのは遠野家の当主の義務ですから」
entries.maoEnglish:
“SHIKI was unable to endure the Tohno blood. You won’t remember, but on that day eight years ago, you protected me from him. You put your own body between me and SHIKI after he became a blood-starved murderer.
He killed you, and Father disposed of him in turn. Punishing those members of the clan who stray beyond the bounds is the duty of the Tohno family head.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… SHIKI was someone who could not resist his Tohno blood.
You may not remember it, but that day eight years ago, you protected me from SHIKI.
You sacrificed yourself to protect me from the bloodthirsty SHIKI.
That is how you were killed by SHIKI and SHIKI was killed by Father.
It is the duty of the head of the Tohno household to dispose of those who are no longer human."
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「……？
　殺されたって言うけど、俺は生きてるじゃないか」
「―――はい。
兄さんは奇跡的に一命をとりとめました。
その後の事は覚えているでしょう？
　兄さんは病院に運ばれて、屋敷に帰ってきたその日に有間の家へ預けられた。
　その時にお父様は兄さんに暗示をかけたんでしょう。
兄さんはまだ傷も治りきっていなくて、心身ともに不安定な状態だった。
だから簡単に、本当に根深くお父様の暗示を信じてしまったんだわ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“What? You say he killed me, but I’m alive.”
“—Yes. By some miracle, you survived. You remember what followed, don’t you? You were taken to the hospital, and on the very day you returned to the mansion, you were sent to the Arima family.
Father must have placed the suggestion in you then. Your wounds had not yet healed, and both your body and mind were terribly unstable. That made it easy for his suggestion to take root in you—deeply, completely.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……?
Killed?
But I'm still alive, right?"
"---Yes.
By a miracle, you survived.
You remember what happened afterwards, right?
You were taken to a hospital and the day you returned, you were adopted by the Arima family.
That is when Father hypnotized you.
You were not fully healed so your heart and mind was weak.
So you easily believed what Father told you."
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「……そうか。
なら、もういい。
秋葉が解っているなら、こんな話をする必要なんかない。
　俺は遠野家の人間じゃないんだろ？
　なら、もう―――無理をして、俺の事を兄だなんて、呼ばなくていい」
　すぐに。
　他人である俺は、この家から出て行くから。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I see. Then that’s enough. If you already know, there’s nothing more to discuss.
I’m not one of the Tohnos, am I?
So you don’t have to force yourself to call me your brother anymore.”
At once.
I am a stranger, so I will leave this house.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I see.
Then, that's enough.
If you understand, then there is no more need to talk.
I'm not a member of the Tohno family, right?
Then, you don't---have to force yourself to call me brother."
Soon.
Soon I, an outsider, should leave this place.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「……誤解しないで兄さん。
　私は世間体のために貴方を兄さん、と呼んでいたんじゃないわ。
　覚えてないの？
　私、兄さんがシキに殺される前から貴方の事を兄さんと呼んでいた。
だから貴方が養子であろうと何であろうと関係ないんです。
　私は初めから兄さんが実の兄でない事は知っていました。
　兄さんもそれを受け入れてくれた。
　だから―――兄さんがどんなに否定しようと、兄さんはもう遠野志貴なんです。
ですからずっと、貴方はこの屋敷にいてください」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Don’t misunderstand me, Brother.
I never called you that for appearances’ sake.
Don’t you remember? I called you Brother even before SHIKI killed you. Whether you were adopted or anything else never mattered.
I knew from the beginning that you weren’t my brother by blood.
You accepted it.
So no matter how fiercely you deny it, you are already Shiki Tohno. Please stay in this mansion with me forever.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Don't get me wrong, Nii-san.
I do not call you Nii-san for the sake of society.
Do you not remember?
Even before you were killed by SHIKI, I called you Nii-san.
It had nothing to do with you being adopted.
I knew from the very beginning you were not my true brother.
And you accepted that too.
So---no matter what you think, you are Tohno Shiki.
So please stay here in this mansion."
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
秋葉の言葉は純粋に嬉しかった。
　けど、俺には解らない。
　どうして秋葉はそんなに、他人である俺を受け入れてくれるのか。
entries.maoEnglish:
Akiha’s words make me genuinely happy.
But I don’t understand.
Why is she so willing to accept me, when I’m nothing but a stranger?
entries.mirrorMoon:
Akiha's words make me happy.
But, I don't understand.
Why does she accept me, an outsider?
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「―――なんで。
俺は秋葉にとって、本当の兄貴じゃないのに」
「……もう。
ここまで言っているのに、兄さんはまだ解ってくださらないんですね。
　私にとって兄と呼べる人は貴方だけなんだし、たとえ兄さんがそれを認められなくても、ただ傍にいてほしいんです。
　私は、兄さんの事を愛していますから」
entries.maoEnglish:
“—Why? I’m not really your brother.”
“Honestly. After everything I’ve said, you still don’t understand.
You are the only person I could ever call my brother; even if you cannot accept that, I still want you beside me.
Because I love you, Brother.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Why?
I'm not even your real brother."
"…… Goodness, after I have said all this, you still do not understand?
You are the only one I will call Nii-san.
Even if you do not wish it, I just want you by my side.
Because, I love you, Nii-san."
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「な―――――――」
　さらりと、秋葉は凄い事を言ってくる。
　秋葉が俺を、兄として好いてくれるのは嬉しい。
　だが、そうであればあるほど――――俺は、この屋敷にはいられない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Wha—”
Akiha says something astonishing as casually as if it were nothing.
I’m happy that she cares for me as her brother.
Yet the more she does, the more impossible it becomes for me to remain in this mansion.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Wha------"
