Akiha says something totally unbelievable.
I'm happy that she likes me as her brother.
But, as long as this situation remains----I can't be here.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「……違う。
俺は秋葉が思っているような人間じゃないんだ。
秋葉はシキを人殺しというけど、俺だって―――シキと同じような、人殺しかもしれないんだ」
「人殺しって、それはどういう事ですか？」
「………………」
　ここまできた以上、隠しとおす事はできない。
　俺は今までの出来事――――昨夜の殺人の夢や自分に覚えのない血の跡の事、そして、秋葉に殺される夢を見た事。
entries.maoEnglish:
“No. I’m not the person you think I am. You call SHIKI a murderer, but I might be one too—someone no different from him.”
“What do you mean by a murderer?”
“…”
After coming this far, I can’t keep hiding it.
I tell her everything that has happened—the dream of murder last night, the bloodstains I couldn’t remember leaving, and the dream in which Akiha killed me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… No, I'm not the kind of person you think I am.
You see SHIKI as a killer, but I---I'm just a killer like him."
"A killer, what do you mean?"
"………………"
I can't keep it a secret any longer.
Everything I did up until now----the dream I had last night, the bloodstains I can not explain, and that dream where Akiha killed me.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「……俺は、自分に自信が持てない。
どうしてもアレが夢だとは思えないんだ。
　親父は七夜の人間は殺人鬼を輩出していると言っていた。
だから俺もシキのようになって、いつか秋葉に迷惑をかける事になる」
　心臓を絞るような思いで、全てを告白した。
　だっていうのに、秋葉のヤツは目を白黒させたあと、可笑しそうに笑いをかみ殺した。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I can’t trust myself. No matter what I tell myself, I can’t believe that was only a dream.
Father wrote that the Nanaya family produced killers. So one day I’ll become like SHIKI and bring you nothing but misery.”
I wrench the confession from the depths of my heart.
Yet Akiha only widens her eyes, then struggles to suppress an amused laugh.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I can't trust myself.
I thought those were just dreams.
But my old man wrote that the Nanaya were a family that produced killers.
If I become like SHIKI, I don't know what I will do to you, Akiha."
I lay it all out to her from the bottom of my heart.
But, after blinking in surprise, she tries not to laugh.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「な、なにがおかしいんだよ。
これは冗談なんかじゃないんだ。
……信じられないだろうけど、俺は確かに人の血を吸う夢を見たんだ……！」
　秋葉はまだくすくすと笑っている。
　……なんだか。
　そうされると、一人で悩んでいた自分がバカみたいに思えてくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“W-what’s so funny? This isn’t a joke. You may not believe me, but I really dreamed that I drank someone’s blood…!”
Akiha is still laughing softly.
Somehow.
It makes all the hours I spent suffering alone feel ridiculous.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Wha, what's so funny?
This isn't a joke.
…… You may not believe me, but I really have dreams of sucking people's blood……!"
Akiha is still giggling.
…… What is this?
She makes me look stupid, worrying about all of this.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「ああ、おかしい。
いい？
　兄さんは決して吸血鬼なんかじゃないのよ。
兄さんは七夜という、あくまで人として優れた血を持つだけなんだから。
　それに七夜の方たちは殺人鬼なんかじゃないわ。
　……確かにお父様から見れば殺人鬼でしょうけど、七夜の方たちが殺人衝動を覚えるのは人間外のヒトにだけなんです。
　だから、兄さんが見ているのは只の夢にすぎない。
その夢だって、シキという殺人鬼から流れてしまった想念みたいなものだから、兄さん本人の嗜好じゃない」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh, it is funny. Listen to me, Brother. You are not a vampire. The Nanaya blood is exceptional, but entirely human.
And the Nanayas are not killers.
Father might have seen them that way, certainly, but the Nanayas feel a murderous impulse only toward things that look human yet are not.
So what you saw was nothing more than a dream. Even that dream was only a residue of thought that leaked into you from the killer called SHIKI, not a reflection of your own desires.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yeah, it is funny.
See, you can't be a vampire.
Because you are from the Nanaya family, your blood is only human.
Besides, the Nanayas are not killers.
…… Certainly from Father's point of view, they are, but the only ones that the Nanaya feel a homicidal impulse towards are nonhumans.
So what you saw had to be just dreams.
And even those dreams are probably SHIKI transmitting to you, so it isn't that you want to see them."
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
……シキから流れてきた想念？
　そういえば親父の手記にもそんな事が書かれていたっけ。
　シキは俺の命とやらを奪って、それを共融しているから、俺たちは互いに影響しあうとかなんとか。
entries.maoEnglish:
Thoughts leaking from SHIKI?
Now that she mentions it, Father’s journal did say something like that.
SHIKI stole my life and joined it to his through coalescence, so the two of us affect each other—or something along those lines.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… SHIKI transmitted them?
Come to think of it, my old man did write something about that.
SHIKI stole some of my life, so there is like a link between us.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「……そうか。
けどそれじゃあ誰が街で人を殺しているんだ。
俺の見ているものが夢だとしても、実際に街で犠牲者が出ているんだから―――」
―――殺人鬼は実在する。
　俺はそいつと会った事がある気がする。
　アレも夢の中の出来事だったのか。
　いや、その真偽は別にしても、もしこの街に殺人鬼がいるとしたら、それは―――
entries.maoEnglish:
“I see. But then who is killing people in the city? Even if what I’m seeing is a dream, there are real victims out there—”
―――The killer exists.
I feel as though I have met him before.
Did that happen in a dream too?
No, whether it did or not, if a killer is loose in this city, then he must be—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I see.
Then who is killing on the streets right now?
Even if what I saw was just a dream, there are victims showing up on the streets in reality---"
---The killer is real.
I feel like I've met him before.
Or was that a dream too?
No, putting that off to the side.
If there's a killer on the streets, then---
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「……シキが、生きている……？」
「え？」
　今までクスクスと忍び笑いをこぼしていた秋葉も、流石に深刻な顔をした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“SHIKI is still alive…?”
“What?”
Even Akiha, who had been hiding her laughter until now, turns grave.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… SHIKI is still alive……?"
"Eh?"
Akiha, who was just giggling until now, becomes serious.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「秋葉。
親父の手記だと、シキは生きていたって書かれてた。
それってつまり―――」
「お父様の手記……？」
　はて、と不思議そうに首をかしげる秋葉。
「親父は俺とシキは繋がっていると言ってた。
なら俺が見ている夢っていうのはシキの夢なのかもしれない」
　……いや、というよりシキが行っている殺人行為そのものか。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Akiha. Father’s journal said SHIKI survived. That means—”
“Father’s journal…?”
Akiha tilts her head in genuine puzzlement.
“Father wrote that SHIKI and I were connected. Then the dreams I’m seeing may be SHIKI’s.”
No, more likely, they are the murders SHIKI himself is committing.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Akiha.
In my old man's journal, he wrote that SHIKI was still alive.
In other words---"
"Father's journal……?"
Akiha tilts her head, curious.
"My old man wrote that SHIKI and I were connected.
Then maybe what I saw were really his dreams."
…… No, it's more likely what he's actually doing.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「……確かにその可能性はあります。
お父様の死因も不審な点が多々ありましたし、屋敷の地下牢には誰かを匿っていた跡がありましたから」
「……ちょっと秋葉。
屋敷の地下牢って、この家ってそんな物騒なものがあるのか」
「あら、それは当然でしょう？
　遠野家の人間の多くは精神に異常をきたすんですもの。
外の世界に害を及ぼさないよう、そういった結界は用意してあります。
　まあ、用途はそれだけじゃありませんけど。
私も子供の頃、お父様の言いつけを破った時はよく閉じ込められましたし」
　なぜか楽しそうに、秋葉はこちらを流し見てくる。
　……なんか、背筋がぶるっときた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“That is possible. Father’s death was suspicious in several respects, and there were signs that someone had been hidden in the cells beneath the mansion.”
“Wait, Akiha. There are underground cells in this house?”
“Why, of course. Many members of the Tohno family suffer mental disturbances. We need such facilities to prevent them from harming the outside world.
Though that isn’t their only use. Father often locked me there when I disobeyed him as a child.”
For some reason, Akiha gives me a sidelong look of delight.
A chill runs down my back.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… That may be a possibility.
Father's death was suspicious, and it did seem like someone was being raised in the underground cell."
"…… Wait a minute, Akiha.
Do we have such a thing like an underground cell here?"
"Oh, of course.
There are a lot of members of the Tohno family who lose their sanity, so it is only natural to lock them away before they can hurt the outside world, right?
Well, that isn't all it is used for.
When I got in trouble, Father would lock me up down there."
For some reason, Akiha sounds like she is having fun.
…… A chill runs down my spine.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「……わかった。
地下牢の話はいいから、今はシキの事をなんとかしないと。
　もし本当にシキが街で人殺しを繰り返しているんなら、なんとか止めないといけないだろ」
「そうですか？
　シキがなんであれ、私たちが関わる必要はないでしょう？
　警察という組織があるのですから、殺人鬼なんていう輩は彼らに任せておくべきじゃない？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Fine. Forget the cells; we need to do something about SHIKI.
If he really is murdering people in the city, we have to stop him.”
“Do we? Whatever SHIKI has become, why should we involve ourselves? The police exist for precisely this reason, so wouldn’t it be better to leave murderers to them?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I get it.
We'll stop talking about it.
We have to do something about SHIKI, though.
If SHIKI really is wandering the streets killing people, then we have to stop him."
"Is that so?
We really do not have to concern ourselves about him, do we?
Is it not the job of the police to take care of killers?"
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「な―――――秋葉、何をいうんだ。
いくら人殺しになったからって、シキはおまえの兄さんだろ。
そりゃ罪は償わないといけないけど、それでも―――」
「……はぁ。
もう、兄さんはどこまで人がいいのかしら」
　呆れたふうにため息をこぼすと、秋葉は髪をかきあげた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What are you saying, Akiha? Murderer or not, SHIKI is still your brother. He has to answer for his crimes, but even so—”
“Good grief. How can you possibly be this kindhearted, Brother?”
With an exasperated sigh, Akiha sweeps back her hair.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Wha----Akiha, what are you saying?
He's killing people, but he is your brother.
He has to pay for his crime, but still---"
"…… Goodness, Nii-san.
You are really too nice of a person."
Taking a breath, she brushes her hair back.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「私にとって肉親は兄さんだけです。
シキの事なんて知らないし、兄さんが心を痛める必要もありません」
「ばか、そういうわけにはいかないだろ。
今まで警察に捕まらなかったヤツが、そう簡単に捕まるもんか。
その間にもまた新しい被害者が出たらどうするんだ」
「どうもしません。
そんなの、私たちの責任じゃありませんから」
　言って、秋葉は俺の目を見つめてくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You are my only family, Brother. SHIKI means nothing to me, and you have no reason to grieve over him.”
“Idiot, we can’t just ignore this. He’s evaded the police until now—what makes you think they’ll suddenly catch him? What if he claims another victim in the meantime?”
“Then he does. That would not be our responsibility.”
Akiha says it while staring directly into my eyes.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"You are my only relative.
I do not care about SHIKI, so you do not have to worry about him."
"No, we can't just do that.
Do you think the police can catch him so easily?
And before then, there will be more victims!"
"I will not do anything.
That is, not our responsibility."
She says this and looks me directly in the eye.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「ね、もうこんな話はよしません？
　人殺しとか殺人鬼とか、そんな話はつまらないわ」
「な――――――」
　けどこれは俺たちの身内の問題だ、と言おうとして、言えなかった。
　……深い、こちらの心まで見透かすような秋葉の目。
　そんな目をされると、なぜか秋葉には敵わないような気がして、気合がそがれてしまう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Can’t we stop talking about this? Murder and killers make for such tedious conversation.”
“Wha—”
I try to say this concerns our own family, but the words won’t come.
Akiha’s eyes are fathomless, as though they can see through to the center of my heart.
Under that gaze, I feel inexplicably incapable of opposing her, and my resolve drains away.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hey, let's not speak of these matters any longer.
Talking about murder and killers is boring, isn't it?"
"Wha-----"
I try to tell her that it has to do with our family, but I can't.
…… Her eyes pierce into me deeply.
Staring at me like that, her eyes seem to take away my resolution.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「分かってくれたみたいですね。
それじゃそろそろお部屋に戻ってもらえますか？
　学校から帰ってきたばかりですから、やらなくちゃいけない事があるんです」
「―――――」
　……秋葉の言う通り、とりあえず、これ以上話をする事がない。
　納得がいかないまま頷いて、秋葉に背中を向けた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I see you understand. Would you return to your room now? I’ve only just come home from school, and I have things to do.”
“…”
For the moment, Akiha is right: there is nothing more to say.
Still unconvinced, I nod and turn my back on her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"It seems you understand.
Well then, will you return to your room?
I just came back from school so there are things I have to do."
"-----"
…… Like Akiha says, there isn't anything else to talk about.
Still not convinced, I turn away from her.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
秋葉の部屋から立ち去ろうとする。
――――と。
　後ろから、呼び止める声がした。
「……なんだ。
もう話すことはないんだろ、秋葉」
「―――――――」
　秋葉は黙って、じっと俺の目を見つめてくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
I start to leave Akiha’s room.
――――Then.
A voice calls after me.
“What is it? I thought we had nothing left to talk about, Akiha.”
“…”
Akiha says nothing and only holds my gaze.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I go to leave her room.
----And all of a sudden,
from behind me, a voice tells me to stop.
"…… What is it?
Aren't we done talking Akiha?"
"-------"
Akiha stares at me silently.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「―――兄さん。
私にとって、一番大切なものは貴方です。
この八年間、兄さんとの思い出がなければ私は私でなくなっていた。
　……兄さんがいてくれたから、秋葉は秋葉のままでいられたんです。
私にとって兄さんは自分以上に大切な人だから、ずっと、私を好きでいてほしかった」
　真摯に。
　視界には俺しかいないようなひたむきさで、秋葉は俺を見つめている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“—Brother. You are the most precious thing in the world to me. Without my memories of you to sustain me through these eight years, I would have ceased to be myself.
Because you existed, Akiha was able to remain Akiha. You matter more to me than my own life, so I wanted you to go on loving me forever.”
In all sincerity.
Her eyes are fixed on me with a devotion so complete it is as though nothing else exists.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Nii-san.
You are the most important thing to me.
If I had lost my memories of you over these eight years, I would not be who I am.
…… Because you were here, I was able to be myself.
You are more important to me than myself, so I wanted you to like me, always."
True sincerity.
Akiha looks at me like I'm the only thing she sees.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「けどそれは私の自分勝手な願いでしょう？
　兄さんにとっては遠野の家も私も、重荷でしかないんですから。
　ですから兄さんは私を疎んじているんだろうって、ずっと恐れていました。
　けど、それは杞憂だったんですよね？
　だって兄さんはこの屋敷に戻ってきてくれた。
他の誰でもない、私のために戻ってきてくれたんだから」
　そう、嬉しそうに秋葉は笑う。
　……その笑顔を見て、胸が痛んだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“But that was only my own selfish wish, wasn’t it? To you, both the Tohno family and I must be burdens.
I spent all those years afraid that you despised me.
But there was never anything to fear, was there? You came back to the mansion. You returned for me—not for anyone else.”
Akiha smiles, radiant with happiness.
The sight sends a pain through my chest.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"But that is just a selfish request, right?
This family and I are just a burden to you.
That is why I always feared that you would distance yourself from me.
But that's just me worrying, right?
Because you came back here.
Because you came back for my sake."
She says happily.
…… Seeing her smile, my chest hurts.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「……そうだ。
俺は秋葉を放っておけなくて戻ってきた。
それは、今でも間違いじゃないって思ってる」
　その、どこか危うい今の秋葉を見守るためにも、戻ってきた事は間違いじゃない。
　けど、違うんだ。
　秋葉の目があまりにも真摯だから、嘘はつけない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…Yes. I came back because I couldn’t leave you alone, and I still believe that was the right choice.”
Coming back was the right choice, if only so I could watch over Akiha in her present, precarious state.
But that isn’t the whole truth.
Her gaze is too earnest for me to lie.
entries.mirrorMoon:
" …… That's right.
I came back because I could not leave you alone here.
But now, I'm beginning to think I was wrong."
I did come back because I wanted to watch over her.
But, she's wrong.
Her eyes are so sincere that I can't lie.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「けど秋葉。
俺が戻ってきた理由はそれだけじゃないんだ。
俺は―――」
　八年前のあの子との約束を果たす為に戻ってきた。
　それは秋葉に対する愛情より大切な、偽れないモノだと思う。
entries.maoEnglish:
“But Akiha. That wasn’t my only reason for coming back. I—”
I came back to fulfill the promise I made to that girl eight years ago.
That promise feels more precious than my affection for Akiha—something I cannot deny without betraying myself.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"But, Akiha.
That isn't the only reason why I came back.
I---"
I came back for the sake of the child I made a promise with.
That is something that's even more precious than my feelings towards Akiha, and something I can't lie about.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「やめて。
そんな話は聞きたくありません。
兄さんは戻ってきてくれた。
事実はそれだけでしょう？
　なら、それ以外の事なんて―――兄さんの事情なんて、私には不必要です」
　秋葉の視線が外れる。
　視線をそらした秋葉は、どこか―――意味もなく、危うい物を感じさせる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Stop. I don’t want to hear this. You came home, Brother. That is the only fact that matters, isn’t it?
Everything else—your reasons, your circumstances—means nothing to me.”
Akiha looks away.
With her eyes averted, she gives off an inexplicable air of fragility.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Stop it.
I do not want to hear it.
You came back, so that is that.
So anything else---such as your feelings, I do not need."
She looks away.
Akiha looking down like that just---for no real reason, seems very dangerous.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「部屋に戻って。
そんな顔のまま、私の前に立たないでください、兄さん」
「………………」
　返す言葉が見つからず、無言で秋葉の部屋を後にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Go back to your room. Please don’t stand before me with that expression, Brother.”
“…”
Unable to find any answer, I leave Akiha’s room in silence.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Go back to your room.
Please do not look like that in front of me, Nii-san."
"………………"
Not knowing what to say, I silently leave her room.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
夜もふけて、もうじき午前零時になろうとしていた。
　いつもの就寝時間はとっくに過ぎている。
　ベッドに横たわったまま、窓ごしの月を見上げる。
「……………」
　眠れずに夜を過ごす。
　また殺人の夢を見るのが怖い、という訳ではない。
　街を徘徊しているシキという殺人鬼。
　どこか崩れてしまいそうな、危うい雰囲気がある秋葉。
　そういった事が気になって、いつまでも眠れずに月を見上げているだけだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
The night deepens, and midnight draws near.
My usual bedtime is long past.
Lying on the bed, I stare at the moon through the window.
“…”
I spend the night unable to sleep.
It isn’t that I’m afraid of another dream of murder.
SHIKI, the killer wandering the city.
Akiha, seeming always on the verge of coming apart.
Those thoughts keep me awake, staring endlessly at the moon.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The night wears on, and it's almost midnight.
It's already way past the time I would usually go to sleep.
I lie down and look up at the moon through the window.
"…………"
The night goes by without me sleeping.
It isn't that I'm scared of seeing another dream of murder.
The killer SHIKI wandering the streets.
The somehow dangerous looking Akiha.
Thinking of that, I cannot sleep and just look up at the moon.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「…………喉、乾いたな」
　最後に水を飲んだのが夕食時から、かれこれ四時間が経っている。
　我慢するのもなんだし、台所にいって水を飲む事にした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’m thirsty.”
Nearly four hours have passed since I last drank anything at dinner.
There is no point enduring it, so I decide to go down to the kitchen for some water.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"………… I'm so thirsty."
The last time I drank anything was about four hours ago at dinner.
I don't want to endure it, so I go to the kitchen to get something to drink.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
コップに水を汲んで、一息で飲みほした。
　どうしてか、妙においしい。
「……おかしいな。
ただ喉が乾いているだけなのに」
　昨夜の夢の中の自分のように、喉を通っていく液体の感覚が心地よかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
I fill a glass and drain it in one breath.
For some reason, it tastes extraordinarily good.
“That’s strange. I’m only thirsty.”
As in last night’s dream, the sensation of liquid sliding down my throat is almost blissful.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I down a cup of water in one gulp.
Why is it so delicious?
"…… That's odd.
I was just thirsty."
The sensation of fluid going down my throat is just like it was last night in my dream.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「ん……？
　誰かやってくる」
　カツン、カツン、という足音が近づいてくる。
　とても小さな足音で、深夜でなければ聞き取れないぐらいの静かさだ。
「……志貴さま？
　こんな時間に何をしてらっしゃるんですか？」
「翡翠か。
いや、喉が乾いたから水を飲みにきただけだよ」
「志貴さま。
そのような事でしたら、お呼びしてくだされば用意いたします。
どうか、夜はお部屋でお休みください。
……夜にこの屋敷を歩かれるのは、あまりいい事ではありません」
　淡々と翡翠は言う。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hm…? Someone’s coming.”
Tap, tap—footsteps approach.
They are so faint that I could never have heard them outside the silence of midnight.
“Master Shiki? What are you doing at this hour?”
“Oh, Hisui. I was thirsty, so I came down for some water.”
“Master Shiki, if you require something, please call for me and I will bring it to you. At night, I ask that you remain in your room and rest. …It is unwise to walk through this mansion after dark.”
Hisui delivers the warning without inflection.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hm……?
Someone's coming."
I can hear the footsteps coming closer.
Soft, small footsteps that barely echo in the deep night.
"…… Shiki-sama?
What are you doing this late at night?"
"Hisui?
I was just thirsty so I thought I'd get something to drink."
"Shiki-sama.
If that is the case, please call for me.
At night, you should be resting in your room.
…… Walking around here at night is not good."
Hisui speaks plainly.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「……？」
　けど、その言葉はどこかおかしい。
　夜に屋敷を歩くのはいい事ではない、という言葉は、裏を返せば部屋から出るな、という事になる。
　……いや、そんな事より。
　翡翠と琥珀さんは子供の頃からこの屋敷で働いている。
　なら―――俺が遠野家の養子という事を知っていてもおかしくはない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…?”
There is something odd in her choice of words.
Her warning that I should not walk through the mansion at night amounts to telling me not to leave my room.
No, more importantly.
Hisui and Kohaku have worked in this mansion since they were children.
It would hardly be strange if they knew I was adopted into the Tohno family.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……?"
There's something wrong with her words.
Telling me it's not good to walk around at night means she's telling me not to get out of my room at night.
…… No, more than that.
Hisui and Kohaku-san have worked here since they were very young.
So---it would not be strange for them to know that I was adopted.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「……翡翠。
聞きたい事があるんだけど、いいかな」
「はい。
それでしたら志貴さまのお部屋に戻りましょう。
ここはお話をするような場所ではありません」
「いや、ここでいい。
ちょっとした事を聞くだけだから」
「―――――？」
　翡翠はかすかに首をかしげる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hisui. May I ask you something?”
“Certainly, Master Shiki. Let us return to your room first. This is not a suitable place for a conversation.”
“No, here is fine. It’s only a small question.”
“—?”
Hisui tilts her head almost imperceptibly.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Hisui.
There is something that I want to ask.
Is it okay?"
"Yes.
If that is the case, then let us go back to your room.
This is not somewhere to be having a conversation."
"No, this is fine.
It is just something small, anyway."
"-----?"
Hisui tilts her head.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「…………」
　はぁ、と深呼吸をする。
　翡翠が知らなかった場合、聞いてしまう時点で秘密をばらしてしまう事になる。
　だが、今更この事を隠そう、なんていうつもりもない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
I draw a long breath.
If Hisui doesn’t already know, merely asking will give the secret away.
But at this point, I have no intention of hiding it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…………"
I take a deep breath.
If she doesn't know, then asking her will be revealing a secret.
But, I don't intend to hide it anyway.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「手短に聞くけど。
翡翠は、俺が養子だっていう事を知ってたのか」
「――――――――」
　びくん、と翡翠の肩が震える。
　……それで、翡翠も知っていたという事が解ってしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’ll be direct. Did you know I was adopted?”
“…”
Hisui’s shoulders jerk.
That alone tells me she knew.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I'll make it short.
Did you know that I was adopted?"
"--------"
Her shoulder shakes.
…… That tells me that she did know.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「……そっか。
翡翠が知ってるっていう事は琥珀さんも知ってるっていう事だよな。
　なんだ。
こんなの、別に秘密でもなんでもないじゃないか」
「志貴さま、それは―――」
　翡翠はそこで言葉をきって、目を伏せた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I see. If you knew, then Kohaku must have known too.
So that’s it. This was never any secret at all.”
“Master Shiki, that is—”
Hisui breaks off and lowers her eyes.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I see.
If you know, then Kohaku-san must know too.
What's this?
This really isn't a secret after all."
"Shiki-sama, that is---"
She says that as she lowers her eyes.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「……申し訳、ありません。
ですが志貴さま、志貴さまは養子であっても紛れもなく遠野家のご長男です。
秋葉さまが志貴さまを肉親と受け入れているように、わたしや姉さんにとっても志貴さまはわたしたちの主です」
「……ありがとう。
そう言ってくれると、この屋敷に残っていいんだなって信じられる」
entries.maoEnglish:
“I am sorry. But Master Shiki—adopted or not—Master Shiki is unquestionably the eldest son of the Tohno family. Just as Miss Akiha accepts Master Shiki as her own family, both my sister and I recognize Master Shiki as our master.”
“Thank you. Hearing that makes me believe I’m allowed to remain in this mansion.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I am so very sorry.
Even if you are adopted, there is no doubt that you are the eldest son of the Tohno family.
Akiha-sama accepts you as her relative and you are mine and Nee-san's master."
"…… Thanks.
If you say that, then I believe that I can stay here."
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま……どうか、そのような事はおっしゃらないでください。
志貴さまにとって、このお屋敷は本当の家なのですから」
「わかってる。
俺だってそのつもりだよ。
短かったけど、子供の頃にここで過ごした時間は大切なものだ。
それを捨てる事なんてできないだろ」
　翡翠は安心したように胸をなでおろす。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki, please do not speak that way. This mansion is Master Shiki’s true home.”
“I know. That’s how I feel too. I didn’t spend many years here as a child, but the time I did have is precious to me. I could never throw it away.”
Hisui lets out a breath of relief.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama…… Please do not say things like that.
This really is your true home."
"I know.
That's what I think too.
Even though it was for a short while, what happened here when I was a child is very important to me.
I can't throw it away."
Hisui looks visibly relieved.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「……けど、それでも知りたいんだ。
　俺がこの家に来る前、えっと……ナナヤ、だっけ。
そういった頃、どんな子供だったのかっていう事を。
翡翠がそれを知っているなら教えてほしい」
「……申し訳ありません。
志貴さまは七夜という、旧い家系のご長男だという事以外、わたしは知らされておりません。
全ては槙久さまが処分してしまいましたから」
　……そうか。
まあ、俺を遠野志貴として偽るのなら、七夜志貴だった頃の記録なんて全て処分してしまっているだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“But I still want to know.
Before I came here—when I was, um, Nanaya, wasn’t it? I want to know what kind of child I was. If you know, please tell me.” “I am sorry, Master Shiki. I was told only that you were the eldest son of an ancient family called Nanaya. Master Makihisa destroyed everything else.”
I see. If he intended to pass me off as Shiki Tohno, he would have destroyed every record of Shiki Nanaya.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… But I still want to know.
Before I came here, um…… it was Nanaya…?
If you know, could you tell me what kind of child I was?"
"…… I am sorry.
Other than that you were the eldest son of the Nanaya line, I do not know.
Makihisa-sama completely destroyed all the records."
…… I see.
Well, if he made me act as Tohno Shiki, then all the records of me as Nanaya Shiki probably were destroyed.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「ですが志貴さま。
姉さんなら何か知っているかもしれません」
「え……？
　翡翠、どうして琥珀さんなら知っているんだ？」
「姉さんは子供の頃から槙久さまのお世話をしていましたから。
遠野という家の事情でしたら、ある意味秋葉さま以上に教え込まれているはずです」
「……………？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“However, Master Shiki. My sister may know something.”
“What…? Hisui, why would Kohaku know?”
“My sister attended Master Makihisa from childhood. When it comes to the affairs of the Tohno family, she may in some respects have been taught more than Miss Akiha herself.”
“…?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"But Shiki-sama, Nee-san may know something."
"Huh……?
Hisui, why would Kohaku-san know anything?"
"Nee-san took care of Makihisa-sama ever since she was young.
She may know more about the Tohno family than even Akiha-sama does."
"………………?"
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
そういうば琥珀さんも、自分が槙久付きの使用人だったとか話していた。
　けどそれは、たまに槙久の健康を看るだけの事だって思ってたけど……そんな子供の頃から槙久付きだったとは知らなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
Come to think of it, Kohaku did mention that she had once been Makihisa’s personal attendant.
I had assumed that meant she only checked on his health from time to time; I never knew she had attended Makihisa since childhood.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Come to think of it, Kohaku-san did say that she was Makihisa's servant.
But I thought that was just to take care of his condition once in a while.
…… I didn't realize she was his servant from that young of an age.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「……あの琥珀さんがねぇ……あんなに毎日俺と遊んでたから、親父の傍にいたっていうイメージはないんだけど――――」
　……どちらかといえば、槙久付きの使用人は翡翠のほうがイメージに合う。
　いつも屋敷の中にいて、俺と秋葉と琥珀さんが遊んでいる所を眺めていたって、いう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Kohaku, of all people—she played with me every day, so I can’t picture her spending all that time beside Father—”
If anything, Hisui fits the image of Makihisa’s attendant.
The child who was always inside the mansion, watching while Akiha, Kohaku, and I played together.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… That Kohaku-san?
…… Since she played with us every day, I just can't picture her being near my old man all the time------"
…… To be honest, Hisui seems like she was more suited for that.
Always looking down at me, Akiha, and Kohaku-san from the inside of the mansion.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「……そうなのか。
けどおかしいよ翡翠。
秋葉にだって伝えなかった事を、親父はどうして琥珀さんに伝えたんだろう」
「いえ、伝えた、という訳ではないと思います。
姉さんはこの屋敷に引き取られてからずっと槙久さまの傍におりましたから、槙久さまの独り言を聞く事も多かったのでしょう」
「―――――――ずっと、親父の傍にいた？」
　だから。
　それはいつも屋敷の中にいた翡翠の方―――
entries.maoEnglish:
“I see. But that’s strange, Hisui. Why would Father tell Kohaku things he never told Akiha?”
“I do not think he told her intentionally. My sister was always at Master Makihisa’s side after she was brought to this mansion, so she must often have overheard Master Makihisa speaking to himself.”
“—She was always beside Father?”
That was why.
It was Hisui who had always remained inside the mansion―――
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Is that true?
But that's odd.
Why would my old man tell Kohaku-san all the things he would not even tell Akiha?"
"No, I do not think he told her directly.
Since Nee-san was always near Makihisa-sama's room in the mansion, I believe she had many chances to overhear Makihisa-sama thinking out loud."
"-------Always near my old man?"
But.
But that's what Hisui, who stayed in the mansion all the time, did---
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「待って。
琥珀さんは、子供の頃から親父の傍にいたっていうのか」
「あ――――」
　視線を逸らす翡翠。
―――今、何かズレた。
　今まではただの違和感にすぎなかった物が、カチリと音をたててはまり直した。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Wait. Are you saying Kohaku was beside Father from the time she was a child?”
“Ah—”
Hisui looks away.
―――Something just shifted.
What until now had been only a vague sense of unease clicks back into place with an audible snap.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Wait.
Kohaku-san was always with my old man as a child?"
"Ah----"
Hisui looks down.
---Something just went wrong here.
The feeling of inconsistency comes back and everything falls back into place.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
琥珀さんは翡翠しか知らない筈の約束を知っていた。
　翡翠は八年前の約束を忘れていた。
　けどそれは、単に。
　二人の位置付けが、そのまま逆になっていただけなんじゃないのか。
　だとしたら――――
entries.maoEnglish:
Kohaku knew the promise only Hisui should have known.
Hisui had forgotten the promise from eight years ago.
But perhaps it simply meant this.
Their places had been reversed all along.
If so――――
entries.mirrorMoon:
Kohaku-san knew about the promise that only Hisui should know about.
Hisui forgot about the promise made eight years ago.
But it might just be…
That I just reversed their roles in my memory.
If that's true then----
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「……翡翠。
もう一度訊くけど、八年前の事は覚えてる？」
「―――はい。
リボンを志貴さまにお渡しした、という事ですね」
「……そうだ。
俺が自分の部屋を出たあと、玄関で呼び止めて餞別にリボンをくれた。
ところでリボンの色が何色だったか覚えてる？」
「白でしたが、なにか」
　翡翠の返答は淀みがない。
　けど、それはすでに間違えてしまっている。
「――――――」
　がたん、と。
　膝の力が抜けて、倒れるように椅子に座る。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hisui. Let me ask again: do you remember what happened eight years ago?”
“—Yes. You mean the ribbon I gave you, Master Shiki.”
“Right. After I left my room, you stopped me at the front entrance and gave me the ribbon as a farewell gift. Do you remember what color it was?”
“It was white, but why do you ask?”
Hisui answers without the slightest hesitation.
But she has already made a mistake.
“…”
With a clatter.
My knees give way, and I collapse heavily into a chair.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Hisui.
I'll ask one more time, but do you remember about eight years ago?"
"---Yes.
About how I gave you that ribbon, right?"
"…… That's right.
After I left my room, you stopped me by the entrance and gave me a ribbon.
Do you remember what color it was?"
"It was white, but what about it?"
There is nothing wrong with her answer.
But, she is already wrong.
"------"
Thud.
The power drains from my legs and I collapse onto the chair.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「―――――なんて」
　なんて間違いを、今までしていたんだろう、俺は。
「志貴さま……？」
「―――違うんだ翡翠。
俺は庭の木の下でリボンを手渡されたんだ。
玄関じゃない」
「―――――――――」
　翡翠は息を飲んで、それきり黙り込んでしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“How could I――――”
How could I have been so terribly wrong all this time?
“Master Shiki…?”
“No, Hisui. I was given the ribbon beneath the tree in the garden. Not at the front door.”
“…”
Hisui catches her breath, then falls utterly silent.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-----How--"
How could I have been so wrong up until now?
"Shiki-sama……?"
"---That's wrong Hisui.
I was given the ribbon under that tree in the garden.
Not by the entrance."
"---------"
Hisui gasps and falls into silence.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「なんで――――」
　解らない。
　どうして琥珀さんは俺を騙すような事ばかりしていたのか。
　どうして―――はっきりと、あの約束の相手は自分だと言ってくれなかったのか。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Why――――”
I don’t understand.
Why had Kohaku done so much to deceive me?
Why hadn’t she simply told me that she was the girl I’d made that promise to?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Why----"
I don't get it.
Why did Kohaku-san try to trick me?
Why---why didn't she just tell me that she was the one I made the promise with?
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま―――どうか姉さんにはこの事は黙っていてあげてください。
志貴さまが知られたと知れば、姉さんは行き場をなくしてしまいます」
　不意に。
　翡翠は、そんな事を言ってきた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki―――please don’t tell my sister what you’ve discovered. If she learns that Master Shiki knows, she’ll have nowhere left to turn.”
Without warning.
Hisui says that to me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama---please do not tell Nee-san about this.
If she finds out, she will have nowhere else to go."
All of a sudden,
Hisui says this.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「知られたって、琥珀さんと翡翠が入れ替わっていたっていう事、をか」
　無言で翡翠は頷く。
「……それじゃやっぱり、翡翠が俺たちと遊んでいた子で、琥珀さんのほうが―――屋敷の中にいた子だっていうのか、翡翠」
　無言で翡翠は頷く。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You mean that you and Kohaku traded places?”
Hisui nods without a word.
“Then it’s true—you were the girl who used to play with us, and Kohaku was the one who stayed inside the mansion; is that what you’re saying, Hisui?”
Again, Hisui nods in silence.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"If she finds out that I knew you two changed places?"
She silently nods.

"…… Then it was you who played with us, and Kohaku-san---was the one in the mansion, right?"
She silently nods.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「どうして……？
　どうしてそんな入れ替わるような真似をしてるんだ、翡翠たちは。
そんな事したって、何の意味もないじゃないか。
それとも俺をからかっていたっていうんじゃないだろうな」
「志貴さまを欺こうとした訳ではありません。
わたしたちも、どうしてこんな事になってしまったのかはっきりと説明はできないんです」
entries.maoEnglish:
“But why…? Why would the two of you switch places like that? What could it possibly accomplish? Don’t tell me this was all some kind of joke at my expense.”
“We never meant to deceive you, Master Shiki. The truth is, neither of us can clearly explain how it came to this.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Why……?
Why did you act like you traded places?
There's no point.
Or were you guys playing around with me?"
"It was not our intent to deceive you, Shiki-sama.
We cannot even fully describe it ourselves how it came to be."
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「……八年前の話です。
志貴さまが有間の家にいかれた後、わたしは以前に比べて大人しくなったんだと思います。
　姉さんはそんなわたしを励まそうと明るく振る舞うようになって、いつのまにか、わたしたちはそっくり立場が入れ替わっていただけなんです」
「それが解らない。
翡翠、キミはあんなに元気な子だったじゃないか」
「……違います。
わたしはもともと、あまり活動的な子供ではありませんでした。
ただ志貴さまがいらしたから、精一杯駆け足で志貴さまを追いかけていただけなんです」
「――――――――――」
entries.maoEnglish:
“It began eight years ago, Master Shiki. After you went to live with the Arima family, I think I became much quieter than I had been.
My sister began acting cheerful to lift my spirits, and before we knew it, our roles had completely reversed.”
“That’s what I don’t understand. You were such a lively child, Hisui.”
“No. I was never very energetic by nature. I only ran so hard because Master Shiki was there, and I was doing everything I could to keep up with Master Shiki.”
I have no answer.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… It started eight years ago.
After you were adopted by the Arima family, I think I just became calmer than before.
Nee-san tried to cheer me up by acting very happy, and then, we gradually traded our roles."
"But why…… why did it happen……?
Hisui…… you were always so energetic."
"…… That is not true.
I am naturally not active.
But when you were there, I tried to follow you as hard as I could."
"----------"
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
……ああ、覚えている。
　いつも元気で、笑顔をたやさなかった少女。
　俺たちの誰よりも自由で、危なっかしくて、なのに一番しっかりしていた、琥珀さんの子供時代のような少女の姿を。
entries.maoEnglish:
Yes, I remember her.
The girl who was always full of life, always smiling.
Freer and more reckless than any of us, yet somehow the most dependable of all—a child who looked exactly like the Kohaku I know now.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Yeah, I remember.
That girl who was always cheerful, always smiling.
The most free-spirited, who would always worry over us, who put up with the most, who acted like Kohaku-san would, if she was younger.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「……そうかな。
翡翠は俺がいなくても、やっぱり元気だったと思うよ。
アレはさ、間違いなく地だったからね。
さんざん翡翠に振り回された俺が言うんだから間違いないって」
「……はい。
あの頃はとても楽しかった。
志貴さまがいらした二年間は、わたしにとって一番いい季節だったと思います」
entries.maoEnglish:
“I don’t know about that. I think you’d have been just as lively without me, Hisui. That was the real you. Believe me—I’m the one you dragged into every one of your adventures.”
“Yes. I was very happy then, Master Shiki. I think the two years you spent here were the finest season of my life.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Really?
I think you would be cheerful even if I wasn't there.
That was your character.
Trust me since I, the one who followed after you, am saying this."
"…… Yes.
Those days were very fun.
I think those were the best two years of my life."
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「ですが、志貴さまがいなくなってから何かが崩れてしまったんです。
　秋葉さまは槙久様を嫌うようになって、槙久様は姉さんにきつくあたるようになりました。
　楽しかったお屋敷の生活は、そこで終わってしまったんです。
わたしは段々と無口になっていって、仕事ができない状態になってしまいました」
entries.maoEnglish:
“But after you left, Master Shiki, something in the household broke apart.
Miss Akiha began to hate Master Makihisa, and Master Makihisa began treating my sister cruelly.
That was the end of our happy life here. I spoke less and less, until eventually I could no longer perform my duties at all.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"But something crumbled after you left, Shiki-sama.
Akiha-sama started to hate Makihisa-sama, and Makihisa-sama became very strict with Nee-san.
The happy days were then over.
I gradually became very quiet and could not even work anymore."
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「そうして、姉さんは仕事ができなくなってしまったわたしの代わりに働くようになったんです。
　以前のわたしのように笑って、以前のわたしのように振る舞う。
その代わりに、わたしは以前の姉さんの役割を受け入れました。
　……わたしにはそれが一番楽でした。
同時に、それがただ一つきりの姉さんの望みだったんです」
entries.maoEnglish:
“So my sister began working in my place.
She smiled the way I used to smile and behaved the way I used to behave. In return, I took on the role that had once been hers.
For me, that was the easier life. It was the only thing my sister had ever wanted.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"So Nee-san took over for me.
Smiling like I always used to, running around like I used to.
In turn, I took over Nee-san's old role.
…… That was the easiest for me.
At the same time, it fulfilled Nee-san's only wish."
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「……琥珀さんの望み……？」
　翡翠の言う事は俺には解らない。
　ただ、翡翠は本当に琥珀さんの事を案じている。
　それだけは、こんな自分にもはっきりと感じ取れた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What Kohaku wanted…?”
I can’t understand what Hisui means.
But she is truly afraid for her sister.
Even someone as insensitive as me can see that much.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Kohaku-san's wish……?"
I don't understand what she said.
Only that Hisui really thinks about Kohaku-san.
That is the only thing I could feel.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「翡翠。
琥珀さんが望んだって、どういう事なんだ」
「……姉さんは、ずっと翡翠になりたかったんです。
けどわたしのためにそれをずっと我慢してきました。
　姉さんにとって、わたしの代わりに働く事はただの芝居にすぎないのだと思います。
　姉さんは昔の翡翠に成りきって、姉さん自身の意思を殺している。
姉さんは自分の意思ではなく、あくまで“昔の翡翠”として日々を過ごしているだけの、人形なんです」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hisui. What do you mean when you say Kohaku wanted this?”
“My sister always wanted to be Hisui. For my sake, she denied herself that wish for years.
I think working in my place is only a performance to her.
She has become the Hisui I used to be and smothered every desire of her own. She no longer lives by her own will, passing each day as ‘the old Hisui’—nothing more than a doll.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hisui.
What do you mean by her wish?"
"…… Nee-san always wanted to be like me.
But for my sake, she held back.
I think it is just an act for her to work in my place.
She pretends to be me and kills her own will.
She is just a doll that only acts like a 'Hisui from the past'."
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「……わたし、そんな姉さんが怖かった。
姉さんには自分というものがもう無くなっていて、ただ誰かになりきって過ごしているだけなんだって気づいてしまったんです。
　……姉さんはきっと、わたしが以前の翡翠に戻ればすぐに以前の、本当の姉さんに戻ってくれると思います。
　……わたしと姉さんが初めて入れ替わった時、姉さんはこう言いました」
entries.maoEnglish:
“That frightened me. I realized there was no self left inside her—that she only lived by becoming someone else.
I’m sure that if I returned to being the girl I once was, she would immediately return to being her old, true self.
When we first exchanged places, she said this to me.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I was scared of that Nee-san.
Nee-san lost her identity and I realized that she was just living by acting out someone's role.
…… I think that if I go back to my old self, Nee-san will return to her old, true self.
…… Nee-san said this when we first traded places."
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
大丈夫よ、翡翠ちゃん。
　翡翠ちゃんが元気になるまで、わたしが代わりになってあげるから。
　だからいつでも、翡翠ちゃんが元気になったら翡翠は返してあげるからね。
entries.maoEnglish:
“It’s all right, Hisui.
I’ll take your place until you feel better.
And whenever you’re ready—whenever you’re well again—I’ll give Hisui back to you.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
It's okay, Hisui-chan.
Until you become cheerful again, I will take your place.
So no matter when, once you are cheerful again, I will give you back your role.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「――――その言葉が怖くて、わたしは少しでも早く元の自分に戻ろうって自分に言い聞かせました。
　……でも、そんな時に偶然、庭を楽しそうに歩いている姉さんを見かけたんです。
　姉さんは本当に嬉しそうだった。
……昔の自分がそんな笑顔で庭を歩いているなんて知らなかったぐらい、姉さんは嬉しそうだったんです。
姉さんはただ独りきりで、庭を歩いているだけだったのに」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Those words frightened me, and I kept telling myself I had to become my old self again as soon as possible.
But then, quite by chance, I saw my sister walking happily through the garden.
She looked so happy. I had never known that the girl I used to be could walk through the garden with such a smile. My sister looked happier than I had ever seen her, though she was only walking there alone.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----I was scared of those words and I thought that I should return to my self right away.
…… But then, by accident, I saw her walking around happily in the garden.
…… Nee-san really looked happy.
…… I did not know I looked that way back then, but she really was happy.
And all she was doing was walking by herself."
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「姉さんの行為は、すべて“翡翠”という役割を演じているだけだって解っています。
けれど、その芝居はあまりにも幸せそうだったんです。
　だから―――姉さん自身が気がついていないだけで、今の琥珀は姉さんがずっと憧れてきた夢なんだって、解ってしまった。
　それを崩すことなんて、わたしにはできませんでした」
　……そうして、翡翠は唇を噛んで、涙を堪えるように黙り込んだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I know that everything she does is only part of her performance as ‘Hisui.’ But she looked so happy in that role.
And then I understood: though my sister herself didn’t realize it, the Kohaku she is now was the dream she had longed for all her life.
I could not bring myself to destroy it.”
Hisui bites her lip and falls silent, struggling to hold back her tears.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Nee-san was only pretending to be 'Hisui'.
Even still, she looked so happy.
So---Nee-san just does not realize it, but I understood that Nee-san always wanted to be like that.
I just could not destroy that."
…… Biting her lip, Hisui holds back her tears in silence.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「……志貴さま。
姉さんは今の姉さんのままでいさせてあげてください。
……そうでなければ、姉さんは自分の居場所を失ってしまうんです」
　……翡翠の言葉に頷くしかない。
　だけどそれは、決して正しい選択じゃない。
　琥珀さんはいつまでも昔の翡翠を演じて、翡翠はそれを守るために、昔の琥珀を演じなくてはいけないのか。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki, please let my sister remain as she is. …Otherwise, she will lose the only place she has left.”
I can only nod.
Yet I know it can never be the right choice.
Is Kohaku to spend the rest of her life playing the Hisui of long ago, while Hisui plays the old Kohaku simply to protect that illusion?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Shiki-sama.
Please let Nee-san stay the way she is.
…… If you do not, she will lose her place."
…… I can only nod to her words.
But that definitely is not the correct choice.
Kohaku-san has to pretend to be the Hisui from the past, and Hisui has to pretend to be the Kohaku-san from the past to protect that.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
―――そんな、偽りしか知らない琥珀さんを見て、翡翠はずっと傍にいるという。
　それは―――とても辛い事の筈だ。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――And Hisui means to remain beside Kohaku all that time, watching a sister who knows nothing but falsehood.
That has to be unbearably painful.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Hisui has been watching Kohaku-san who only knows how to live a lie, but still says she will live with her.
That---has to be so difficult.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま。
どうか約束してください。
姉さんには何も言わないと」
「……わかった。
けど翡翠。
君はそれでいいのか」
「…………………」
　翡翠は答えない。
　……行き場のない感情を飲みこんで椅子から立ち上がる。
　俯いたままの翡翠を残して、台所を後にする事しか、できなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki. Please promise me you won’t tell my sister. Promise me.”
“All right. But Hisui. Is this truly what you want?”
“…”
Hisui gives no answer.
I swallow everything I have no way to express and rise from the chair.
All I can do is leave the kitchen, abandoning Hisui there with her head bowed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama.
Please promise me that you will not say anything to Nee-san."
"…… Fine.
But, Hisui, are you okay with this?"
"……………………"
Hisui doesn't answer.
…… Full of conflicting emotions, I get up from the chair.
All I can do is leave the downcast Hisui behind in the kitchen.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「―――――――？」
　部屋に戻ろうとして、玄関の扉がわずかに開いている事に気がついた。
「……誰か外に出たのか？」
　……翡翠はまだ台所にいる筈だ。
　だとしたら琥珀さんか秋葉が外に出た、という事になる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hm…?”
On my way back to my room, I notice that the front door stands slightly ajar.
“Did someone go outside?”
Hisui should still be in the kitchen.
That means either Kohaku or Akiha has left the house.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-------?"
Going back to my room, I notice that the door is open.
"…… Did someone go outside?"
…… Hisui must still be in the kitchen.
That means that it's either Kohaku-san or Akiha.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「………………」
　正直、今はもう眠りたい。
　体も心も疲れきっていて、すぐに眠らなければ倒れてしまいそうだ。
　今夜だけは。
このまま静かに眠らないと、遠野志貴は壊れてしまう。
　ここは――――
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
I want nothing now but sleep.
Body and mind alike are spent; if I don’t lie down at once, I feel I might collapse.
Just for tonight. If I don’t sleep quietly now, Shiki Tohno will break.
So I should――――
entries.mirrorMoon:
"………………"
To be honest, I want to sleep.
My body and my heart are tired; I feel like I could collapse if I don't sleep.
Just tonight.
I feel like if I don't sleep, I'll break.
I should----
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese: ―――少しだけ様子を見に行こう。
entries.maoEnglish: ―――I’ll only take a quick look.
entries.mirrorMoon: ---I should check it out.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
外に出た。
　いつのまに雲が出てきたのか、先ほどまで出ていた月が隠れている。
「ん………？」
　誰かが門を開けようとしている。
　声をかけようとした瞬間、
「…………秋葉？」
　秋葉は後ろをチラリと見て、外に出ていってしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
I stepped outside.
Clouds had gathered without my noticing, hiding the moon that had shone only moments before.
“Hm…?”
Someone was opening the gate.
Just as I drew breath to call out,
“Akiha?”
She glanced back once, then slipped outside.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I go outside.
The previously present moon is now obscured by clouds.
"Hm………?"
Someone is opening the front gate.
I start to say something,
"………… Akiha?"
Akiha looks quickly over her shoulder and exits the gate.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「え―――――？」
　どくん、と。
　何の前触れもなく、胸がキシンだ。
　どくん。
　ドクン。
　どくん。
　ドクン。
　あれだけ弱っていた心臓は、まるで新生したかのように激しく活動する。
　血液は過度に流動して、指先まで震えていた。
「あ――――つ」
　背中には悪寒。
　なのに全身は火のように熱い。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What…?”
Thud.
Without warning, my heart gave a painful throb.
Thump.
THUMP.
Thump.
THUMP.
My heart, so weak only moments ago, hammered as though newly born.
Blood raced violently through me until even my fingertips trembled.
“Hot――――”
A chill crawled along my back.
Yet the rest of me burned like fire.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Eh-----?"
Thump.
Out of nowhere, my chest starts to pound.
Thump.
THUMP.
Thump.
THUMP.
My heart seems to pulse with new life.
I can feel the blood coursing through my body, and the shaking of my fingers.
"Ah-----"
A chill runs down my back.
Despite that, my body feels like it's on fire.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「秋葉――――あいつ、こんな夜更けに―――」
　眩暈がする。
　冷静に物事を整理しようとして、止めた。
　ともかく。
今は、秋葉を追いかけよう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Akiha—what is she doing out this late―――”
Dizziness washed over me.
I began trying to think it through, then stopped.
None of that mattered now. I had to follow her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Akiha----what is she doing this late?---"
I feel dizzy.
I try to sort things out rationally, but I stop.
Right now, I have to follow Akiha.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「は――――」
　あふれそうになる呼吸を殺して、秋葉の後を付いていく。
　どくん、どくん。
　早鐘の音が心地良い。
　秋葉に見つからないように、こっそりと後を付けていく。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hah――――”
I stifled the breath threatening to spill from me and followed Akiha.
Thump, thump.
The racing beat felt wonderful.
I kept to the shadows, careful not to let her notice me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Haa----"
Stifling my breath, I follow after her.
Thump, Thump.
My beating heart.
I follow her quietly to avoid being noticed.

Thump, thump, thump.
I feel regret.
I don't have my knife tonight.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
どくん、どくん、どくん。
　悔やまれる。
どうして今夜にかぎって、俺はナイフを持っていないのか。
entries.maoEnglish:
Thump, thump, thump.
Of all nights, why had I left my knife behind tonight? The thought filled me with regret.
entries.mirrorMoon:
There's no moonlight and it's now midnight.
There isn't a sign of anyone else on the streets.
Thump,
Thump.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
月は無く、時刻は零時。
　大通りには人気はない。
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　どくん、
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　どくん。
　秋葉はふらふらとした足取り。
　息を殺して、チャンスを待つ。
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　どくん、
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　どくん。
　秋葉は中々一人にならない。
　何処に向かっているかは、まあ瑣末事。
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　どくん、
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　どくん。
entries.maoEnglish:
It was midnight beneath a moonless sky.
The main avenue was deserted.
Thump,
Thump.
Akiha walked unsteadily.
I held my breath and waited for my chance.
Thump,
Thump.
Akiha still hadn’t found herself alone.
Where she was headed hardly mattered.
Thump,
Thump.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Akiha walks unsteadily.
I try to silence my breathing and await my chance.
Thump,
Thump.
It's taking her a while to be alone.
Where she's going is trivial.
Thump,
Thump.

I'm terribly thirsty.
I'm incredibly excited.
Thump,
Thump, thump.
---All of a sudden, I lose sight of her.
Where'd she go?
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
ひどく、喉が乾く。
　すごく、刺激的だ。
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　どくん、
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　どく、どく。
―――と。
秋葉を見失ってしまった。
　どこで見失ったのか。
entries.maoEnglish:
My throat was parched.
This was exhilarating.
Thump,
Thud, thud.
―――And then. I lost sight of Akiha.
Where had she disappeared?
entries.mirrorMoon:
I return to the main street.
I feel instinctively that I'll see her again if I wait here.
I let out a deep breath.
My heart is still burning.
"-------"
That's odd.
This isn't a dream.
This isn't a dream, then why---is my blood burning as I'm following Akiha?
It's like, I want to kill Akiha.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
大通りに戻ってきた。
　なんとなく、ここで待っていれば秋葉を見つけられると直感した。
　はあ、と大きく息を吐く。
　心臓はいまだに過熱している。
「―――――――」
　おかしい。
　これは夢じゃない。
　夢じゃないのに、どうしてこう―――俺は、血を昂ぶらせて、秋葉の後を付けているのか。
　これじゃあまるで、俺が秋葉を、殺したがっているみたい。

どくん!w1000
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　どくん!w1000
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　どくん!w750
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　どくん!w750
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　どくん!w750
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　どく!w500
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　どく!w500
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　どく!w500
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　どく!w250
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　どく!w250
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　どく!w250
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　どく
entries.maoEnglish:
I returned to the main avenue.
Some instinct told me that if I waited here, I would find her again.
I breathed out heavily.
My heart was still overheating.
“…”
Something was wrong.
This wasn’t a dream.
It wasn’t a dream—so why was I stalking Akiha through the night with my blood singing like this?
It was almost as though I wanted to kill her.
Thump!w1000
Thump!w1000
Thump!w750
Thump!w750
Thump!w750
Thud!w500
Thud!w500
Thud!w500
Thud!w250
Thud!w250
Thud!w250
Thud
entries.mirrorMoon:
Thump
Thump
Thump
Thump
Thump
Thump
Thump
Thump
Thump
Thump
Thump
Thump
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
気配を感じて、咄嗟に身を隠した。
　秋葉がやってくる。
　きょろきょろと周囲を見渡している所をみると、秋葉は何かを探しているようだった。
「………ここには居ないみたいね」
　なんていう独り言が聞こえてくる。
　独り言が聞こえるぐらい、距離が近くなっているという事か。
　物陰から顔を出して、大通りを見た。
entries.maoEnglish:
I sensed someone and ducked out of sight.
Akiha approached, looking restlessly from side to side.
She seemed to be searching for something.
“It doesn’t seem to be here.”
I heard her murmur to herself.
If I could make out a whisper, she had come dangerously close.
I peered from my hiding place onto the avenue.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Sensing something, I instantly conceal myself.
Akiha is coming.
She looks around from side to side, as if searching for something.
"……… There isn't anyone here, I guess."
I hear her thinking aloud.
I must be that close if I can hear her.
Peering from the shadows, I look out into the street.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「―――」
　頭痛。
　バキンという音がした。
――――地面に倒れる。
　こんな頭痛は体験した事がない。
　頭が割れて死んでしまったか、と真剣に思ったほどだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
Pain split my head.
Something inside it cracked.
――――I fell to the ground.
I had never known a headache like it.
For one earnest instant, I believed my skull had burst and killed me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---"
My head aches.
The air around me tenses.
----I collapse to the ground.
I've never felt such pain before.
It's so bad it makes me seriously think my skull just split open and I'm going to die.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「あ―――――痛…………」
　頭をふって立ち上がる。
　どのくらい倒れていたのか、さっきより夜の静けさが深い。
―――って、ちょっと待った。
「な、なんでこんな所にいるんだ、俺！？」
　いつのまにか大通りまでやってきている。
　屋敷の門で秋葉を見かけて、その後―――そう、秋葉を追いかけてきたんだっけ。
「……なにしてんだよ、俺は」
　自分で自分の行為に呆れてしまう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ah―――――it hurts”
I shook my head and forced myself up.
I couldn’t tell how long I had lain there, but the night had grown even deeper and stiller.
―――Wait a moment.
“W-why am I all the way out here?”
Somehow I had reached the main avenue.
I had seen Akiha at the mansion gate and then―――yes, I had followed her.
“What the hell am I doing?”
My own behavior left me appalled.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah-----ouch…………"
Shaking my head, I stand up.
I don't know how long I was out, but the night is quiet.
---Wait a minute.
"Wh, why am I here!?"
I am out on the main street.
I saw Akiha by the gate, and after that---that's right, I followed her.
"…… What am I doing?"
I'm surprised at what I'm doing.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「――――――あれ」
　なにか、嫌な匂いが鼻をついた。
　今までは知らなかった匂い。
ここ数日、夢の中で何度も口にした匂いだ。
「……あっちの路地裏から……？」
　何か嫌な予感がして、路地裏へと走り出した。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What is that――――?”
A foul odor caught in my nose.
An odor I had never known before. One I had tasted again and again in my dreams.
“From that alley…?”
Dread seized me, and I ran toward it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------Huh?"
An unpleasant smell pricks at my nose.
A smell I've never known until now.
The smell that stuck to my mouth during my dreams these past few days.
"…… From that alley……?"
Getting a bad feeling, I run towards that alley.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
―――それは、昨夜見た夢の焼き直しだ。
　路地裏には見知らぬ他人が倒れていた。
　首筋から血を流しているが、息はある。
「―――――――――」
　目の前が真っ赤になる。
　だがこれは夢ではない。
　何度も殺人の光景を見てきたせいか、思考はあくまで冷静だった。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――It was a reprise of last night’s dream.
A stranger lay crumpled in the alley.
Blood ran from the person’s neck, but they were still breathing.
“…”
My vision flooded red.
This was no dream.
Perhaps because I had witnessed murder so many times, my thoughts remained perfectly calm.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---It's like a rehash of my dream last night.
In the alley there is a collapsed stranger.
Despite the blood flowing from the neck, the person is still breathing.
"---------"
Everything before me turns crimson.
But this isn't a dream.
Maybe it's because I've had all those dreams of murder, but I can think calmly.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
大通りに出る。
　公衆電話にかけよって、一番近くの緊急病院に電話をする。
　適当な名前をでっちあげて、路地裏の正確な住所と怪我人の状態を告げて、電話を切った。
　後は救急車が来る前に、誰にも見られないように屋敷に戻らなくてはいけない。
entries.maoEnglish:
I hurried back to the main avenue.
I ran to a public telephone and called the nearest emergency hospital.
I invented a name, gave them the exact location of the alley and the victim’s condition, then hung up.
Now I had to return to the mansion before the ambulance arrived, without letting anyone see me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I go out to the street.
I go to the nearest public phone and call the nearest hospital.
After giving a fake name, I tell the location and condition of the victim, and I hang up the phone.
Now, before the ambulance comes, I should head back to the mansion so no one sees me.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「はぁ、はぁ、は――――――」
　休みなく走り抜けて、ようやく体を休められた。
　やましい事なんて何もなかったが、関わり合いになるのは危険な気がして、とりあえず自分にできる最善の行動をとったと思う。
　……路地裏に倒れていた人はまだ息があった、
　出血もそう大したものではなかったし、命に別状はないと思う。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hah―――hah―――hah――――――”
Only after running the whole way without rest could I finally stop.
I had done nothing wrong, yet involvement felt dangerous, and I believed I had taken the best course available to me.
The person in the alley had still been breathing,
the blood loss hadn’t looked severe, so their life probably wasn’t in danger.
entries.mirrorMoon:
*pant* *pant* *pant*------
After running without stopping, I can finally relax.
I don't have anything to feel bad about, but I felt that getting involved would be dangerous, and I did the best I could.
…… The person in the alley was still breathing,
and the bleeding wasn't that bad, so I don't think it was life-threatening.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「あ―――――」
　……流石に街からここまでの全力疾走は応えたか。
途中、心臓破りめいた坂道も休み無しだったから、体中に酸素がまるで足りていない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ah…”
The flat-out sprint from the city had taken its toll. I hadn’t even slowed on the murderous uphill road, and now there was nowhere near enough oxygen in my body.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah-----"
…… As expected, running here with all my strength, including up the big hill, was a little much.
I'm completely out of breath.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「まず―――」
　……強い眩暈。
　意識が段々と削れていって、頭の中から消え去っていくような感覚。
　それは、いつもの軽い眩暈じゃない。
　これだけの重さだと、倒れたらしばらくは起きあがれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“This is bad…”
A savage wave of dizziness struck.
My consciousness felt as though it were being scraped away, vanishing piece by piece from inside my skull.
This was no ordinary faint spell.
If I fell now, I wouldn’t be getting up for some time.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Cra--"
…… Dizziness assails me.
I can feel my consciousness withdrawing.
This isn't a normal dizziness.
If it's this bad, if I collapse, I won't be able to get back up for a while.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「くそ………倒れる前に、部屋に、戻らない、と――――」
　階段の手すりに体を預ける。
　足を一歩だけあげる。
　そこが限界。
　手すりに寄りかかったまま、ずるりと体が倒れこんだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Damn it—have to reach my room before I fall――――”
I sagged against the banister.
I raised one foot to the first step.
That was my limit.
Still leaning against the banister, I slid helplessly to the floor.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Damn……… I have to, get back, to my room, before----"
I lean up against the stairs.
I manage to take one step up the stairs.
That's it though.
I collapse.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
強い陽射しを感じて目蓋を開けると、そこは自分の部屋だった。
　俺はきちんと寝巻に着替えて、ベッドに横になっている。
entries.maoEnglish:
When I opened my eyes to strong sunlight, I was in my own room.
I was properly dressed in pajamas and lying in bed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Strong rays of sunshine cause me to open my eyes.
I'm in my room.
I'm now wearing my pajamas and lying in bed.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「失礼します」
　ノックの音がして、扉が開く。
　やってきたのは洗面器やらタオルやらを持った琥珀さんだった。
「あ、おはようございます志貴さん。
お体の具合はどうですか？」
　いつもと変わらない笑顔で琥珀さんは近寄ってきた。
「―――――――」
　昨夜の翡翠との会話が思い出される。
　それをなんとか思考の隅においやって、出来るだけいつも通りに笑ってみせた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Excuse me.”
A knock sounded, and the door opened.
Kohaku entered carrying a basin, towels, and an assortment of other things.
“Oh, good morning, Shiki. How are you feeling?”
Kohaku approached with her usual smile.
“…”
Last night’s conversation with Hisui came rushing back.
I shoved it into a distant corner of my mind and returned as normal a smile as I could manage.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Excuse me."
With a knock, the door opens.
Kohaku-san enters carrying a towel and a bucket.
"Ah, good morning Shiki-san.
How are you feeling?"
Kohaku-san draws near with her normal smile.
"-------"
I think back to last night's conversation with Hisui.
Tucking that away into the back of my mind, I try to make my usual smile.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「おはよう琥珀さん。
あの―――もしかして、琥珀さんがここに運んできてくれたんですか？」
「あれ、志貴さん覚えてないんですか？
　志貴さんは階段でうなされていて、お声をかけたら一人で立ちあがって。
　いや、よく寝た、とか言って歩き出したんですよー。
肩をお貸ししましたけど、志貴さんはご自分でここまで戻ってきたんです」
「………はあ。
なんか、まったく記憶にないんだけど。
ここんところ疲れてるのかな。
自分が何をしていたのか、よく思い出せなくなるんだ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Morning, Kohaku. Were you the one who carried me here?”
“What, don’t you remember, Shiki? You were moaning in your sleep on the stairs.
When I called to you, you stood up all by yourself and said, ‘Ah, what a wonderful nap!’ Then you started walking.”
“Huh. I don’t remember any of that. Maybe I’ve been too tired lately. I keep losing track of what I’ve been doing.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Morning Kohaku-san.
Um---did you carry me up here?"
"Huh?
Don't you remember Shiki-san?
I found you alone on the stairs and you stood up once I called you.
You said you had a nice nap and started to walk.
I did lend you my shoulder, but you walked here by yourself."
……… *sigh*
"I don't remember.
I must've been so tired that I forgot what I did."
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「はあ。
それじゃ昨夜の事も覚えていないんですか？」
「……多分。
俺の記憶は屋敷に帰ってきた所で止まってます」
「あはは、それは残念ですねー。
志貴さん、ずっとわたしに謝っていたんですよ。
　どうして謝るんですかって尋ねるんですけど、俺はばかだ、とうへんぼくだ、としか答えてくださらないんです。
　志貴さん、とうへんぼくなんですか？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh? Then don’t you remember last night either?”
“Probably not. My memory stops when I returned to the mansion.”
“Ahaha, what a shame, Shiki. You spent the whole time apologizing to me.
I kept asking what you were sorry for, but all you would say was that you were an idiot and a blockhead.
Shiki, are you really a blockhead?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"So you don't remember anything about last night?"

"…… Maybe.
I don't remember anything after I came back to the mansion."
"Ahaha.
That's unfortunate.
Shiki-san, you kept apologizing to me.
I inquired why you kept apologizing, and you kept saying that you were an idiot and a blockhead.
Shiki-san, are you a blockhead?"
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「いや。
いちおう人間のつもりだけど」
　……まあ、それでもそろそろ本気で朴念仁だの甲斐性なしだのと、石を投げられるような気はしているけど。
entries.maoEnglish:
“No. I’m fairly sure I’m human.”
Although at this rate, I did expect people to start throwing stones at me for being a hopelessly insensitive good-for-nothing.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No, I don't think so."
…… Well, I am really starting to get the idea that they think my brain is made out of wood.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「……ともかく助かった。
あのまま階段で寝てたら風邪を引いてたし、学校だって―――」
　あれ？
　目の錯覚が、時計は午前十時を余裕で過ぎてしまっている。
「あ―――！
　こ、琥珀さん、学校っ！」
「はい。
志貴さんの学校でしたら、今日は創立記念日でお休みですね」
「――――――――」
　そう、か。
そういえば、そんな日もあったっけ。
　ここんところ学校に行っても上の空だったから、そんな事さえ忘れていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Anyway, thank you. If I’d slept on the stairs all night, I’d have caught a cold, and school―――”
Wait. Unless my eyes deceived me, the clock was well past ten.
“School! Kohaku, school!”
“Yes. Your school is closed today for its anniversary.”
“…”
I see. Come to think of it, there was such a day.
I had been so distracted at school lately that even that had slipped my mind.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Anyway, thanks a lot.
If I slept on the stairs, I'd have caught a cold, and school---"
Huh?
Are my eyes playing tricks on me?
The clock tells me it is already past ten in the morning.
"Ah---!
Ko, Kohaku-san, School!"
"Yes.
Today is your school's founding holiday, so you don't have school."
"--------"
That's right.
Come to think of it, it was.
I completely forgot about it since I have been spacing out at school lately.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「ま、ともかく起きないと。
こんな時間まで寝てたら秋葉になんて言われるか―――」
　ベッドから体を起こす。
「あれ――――うまく、体が」
　動いてくれない。
　腕をたてて体を起こそうとするんだけど、その腕に力が入らない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Well, I should still get up. If Akiha hears I slept this late―――”
I pushed myself upright.
“What――――my body won’t move”
It refused to move properly.
I braced my arms to sit up, but no strength would enter them.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Well, I should get up anyway.
If I sleep any longer Akiha will---"
I sit up on my bed.
"Huh-----I can't really."
My body won't move.
I try to get up with my arms, but they have no strength.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「どうやらまだお体の具合が悪いみたいですね。
今朝は三十八度ほど熱がありましたし、まだ顔色が優れてませんし。
退屈でしょうけど、今日はベッドの上でお休みしてくださいね、志貴さん」
　琥珀さんは冷たい水で絞ったタオルを俺のおでこに乗せてくる。
　……冷たくて、気持ちがいい。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You still seem unwell. Your temperature was around thirty-eight degrees this morning, and you’re still rather pale. I know you’ll be bored, but please stay in bed and rest today, Shiki.”
Kohaku laid a towel wrung out in cold water across my forehead.
It was wonderfully cool.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"It seems your condition is still bad.
You have a slight fever and you look a little pale.
It may be boring, but please rest in bed today, Shiki-san."
Kohaku-san wipes my forehead with the cold, wet towel.
…… It feels good and cold.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「んー、とりあえず熱は下がっていますねー。
汗はだいぶ引いてくれたようですし、お顔の色もよくなってきてるから、夜には元気になってますよ」
　琥珀さんは体温計や氷枕をテキパキと繰り出してくる。
　……最後には口をあけさせられて、舌の具合まで確かめられてしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hmm, your fever has come down for now. You’ve mostly stopped sweating, and the color is returning to your face, so you should be feeling much better by tonight.”
Kohaku briskly produced a thermometer, an ice pillow, and one instrument after another.
By the end, she even made me open my mouth so she could examine my tongue.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hmm, it seems your fever is down.
You're not sweating as much and your face looks much better.
You should be well by the evening."
Kohaku-san crisply brings out a thermometer and an ice pillow.
…… In the end, she makes me open my mouth and checks the condition of my tongue.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「それではすぐにお粥を持ってまいりますね。
志貴さん、今日は大人しくしてないとダメですよ」
「あ―――琥珀さん」
「はい？
　なんですか志貴さん？」
　……琥珀さんはやっぱり琥珀さんだ。
　見ているとこっちまで元気が出てきそうなその笑顔に変わりはない。
　俺には―――この人が、ただ笑顔を演じているだけだなんて思えない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’ll bring you some rice porridge right away. You must behave yourself today, Shiki.”
“Wait—Kohaku.”
“Yes? What is it, Shiki?”
Kohaku was still Kohaku.
That smile, bright enough to restore the spirits of anyone who saw it, had not changed.
I could not believe it was merely an act.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Well, I'll bring you some rice porridge right away.
Shiki-san, you better behave today."
"Ah---Kohaku-san."
"Yes?
What is it, Shiki-san?"
…… As expected, she is like always.
Her usual cheerful smile doesn't change.
I---I can't bring myself to think that her smile is just an act.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「……いや、なんでもないんだ。
お粥、楽しみにしてます」
「はい、それでは失礼しますね」
　琥珀さんはパタパタと足音をたてて廊下へ去っていく。
　その後ろ姿を、ただ黙って見つめていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“No, it’s nothing. I’m looking forward to the porridge.”
“All right, I’ll leave you to rest.”
Kohaku pattered out into the corridor.
I watched her go without a word.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Nothing.
I'm looking forward to the rice porridge."
"Yes, well then, excuse me."
Kohaku-san disappears down the hall, her footsteps padding after her.
I just stare at that figure silently.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
正午になった。
　琥珀さんはお粥を持ってきた後、屋敷の仕事に戻っていった。
「…………………はぁ」
　こうして一人になると、今の自分が置かれた状況の異常さにため息が出てしまう。
　……養子だった自分。
　……それでも構わないと言ってくれた秋葉。
　……翡翠と琥珀さん。
　……そして、いまだ野放しになっている殺人鬼。
entries.maoEnglish:
Noon arrived.
After bringing my porridge, Kohaku returned to her work around the mansion.
“Haaah…”
Alone again, I could only sigh at the madness of my situation.
I was adopted.
Akiha had said it didn’t matter.
Hisui and Kohaku.
And somewhere outside, the murderer still roamed free.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Noon arrives.
After bringing the food, Kohaku-san went back to her duties.
…………………… *sigh*
Being alone, I let out a sigh as I think of my strange circumstances.
…… Myself being adopted.
…… Akiha saying that she doesn't care about it.
…… Hisui and Kohaku-san.
…… And the killer that's still on the loose.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
琥珀さんに尋ねた所、今朝のニュースで新しい死者が出た、というものはなかったそうだ。
　昨夜の被害者は助かったのだろうが、シキが野放しになっている以上、犠牲者はなくならない。
「……この体がもう少し思い通りになってくれれば、俺が―――」
　シキを止める、と言いかけて、枕に頭をうずめた。
　あんな夢を見続けた影響だろうか。
俺もシキに負けず劣らず物騒な思考をしている。
「……何をするにしても、とにかく体を治さないとダメだよな」
　目蓋を閉じる。
entries.maoEnglish:
Kohaku said the morning news had reported no new deaths.
Last night’s victim must have survived, but as long as SHIKI remained at large, there would be more.
“If only this body would do what I tell it, I could―――”
I nearly said I would stop SHIKI, then buried my face in the pillow.
Perhaps those dreams had infected me. My thoughts were as dangerous as SHIKI’s.
“Whatever I do, I need to get well first.”
I closed my eyes.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I asked Kohaku-san, but it doesn't seem like there was a new victim in the news today.
I guess last night's victim was saved, but while SHIKI is on the loose, there will be more victims.
"…… If only this body did what I told it to, I---"
I could stop SHIKI.
I lay my head back down on the pillow as I start to say that.
Maybe it's because I've been seeing those dreams, but I'm beginning to have violent thoughts like SHIKI.
"…… Whatever I do, I should heal up first."
I close my eyes.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
――――部屋に戻ろう。
　翡翠が語ったコトバが、頭の中で渦を巻いてしまっている。
　ただでさえ重い体は、目に見えない言霊の鎖でよけいギクシャクと稼動する。
「………………………っ」
　階段を上ろうとして、体が軋んだ。
　……足があがらない。
歩くことしか、できそうにない。
「……………………どうしたんだ、これ」
　……仕方がない。
台所に戻って、翡翠に肩を貸してもらって――――
entries.maoEnglish:
――――I should go back to my room.
Hisui’s words churned endlessly inside my head.
My body was heavy enough already; now invisible chains forged from those words made every movement stiff and awkward.
“…”
I tried to climb the stairs, and my body creaked in protest.
My legs wouldn’t rise. Walking on level ground was all I could manage.
“What’s wrong with me?”
There was no choice. I would return to the kitchen and ask Hisui for her shoulder――――
entries.mirrorMoon:
----I should go back to my room.
Hisui's words echo inside my head.
My leaden body weakens more, weighed down by those chains.
"…………………………"
I try to go up the stairs and my body stops.
…… My legs can't go far up enough.
It looks like I can only walk.
"…………………… What is this?"
…… Oh well.
I should go back to the kitchen to ask Hisui to lend me her shoulder----
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「あ――――――れ」
　台所に戻ろうとして、絨毯に倒れこんだ。
「―――――ちょっ、と」
　声もあげられない。
　ずるずると腕だけで這って、すぐに力尽きた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What…?”
I turned toward the kitchen and collapsed onto the carpet.
“Wait―――just”
I couldn’t even raise my voice.
Dragging myself by my arms, I crawled a short distance before my strength deserted me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"H------uh?"
I start to go back and collapse on the carpet.
"-----H, hey."
I can't even shout.
I exhaust myself crawling on my arms.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
カツカツ、という足音が聞こえてくる。
　台所から翡翠がやってくる。
　……助かった。
ともかく、これで翡翠に肩を貸してもらえ―――
　カツカツ、カツカツ、カツ。
「……………………うそ」
　階段から這って進んだ事が裏目に出たのか。
　ちょうど俺は物陰に入ってしまって、翡翠は気がつかずに階段を上がっていってしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
Sharp footsteps approached from the kitchen.
Hisui was coming.
Saved. Now she could help me up―――
Click, click, click, click, click.
“You’re kidding.”
Crawling away from the stairs had worked against me.
I had ended up behind an obstruction, and Hisui passed without noticing me, then climbed the stairs.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Clomp, clomp.
I hear footsteps.
Hisui comes from the kitchen.
…… I'm saved.
Now Hisui can help me out---
Clomp-clomp, clomp-clomp, clomp.
"…………………… No way."
Crawling away from the stairs backfired.
I have hidden myself in the shadows and Hisui goes up the stairs without even noticing me.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「……………………なんか、すごく間抜けじゃないのか、俺」
　ぼんやりと呟いた瞬間、ぞくり、と。
　近くに、自分以外の気配を感じた。
「―――――――――――！」
　倒れたまま視線を後に向ける。
　そこには。
　幽霊のような、人影が。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I look unbelievably stupid right now, don’t I?”
The moment I muttered it, a chill ran through me.
I sensed someone nearby.
“―――――――――――!”
Still sprawled on the floor, I wrenched my gaze behind me.
There.
A human shape stood there, pale and insubstantial as a ghost.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"………………………… That was incredibly stupid of me."
As soon as I voice my thoughts, something catches my attention.
The feeling of something close to me.
"-----------!"
I look behind me as I'm lying on the ground.
Over there,
a ghost-like figure.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「――――――――――」
　そこで、ようやく今の自分の状態を悟った。
　動かない体。
　あげられない声。
　明かりのない暗い洋館。
　……そして、エモノをじっと凝視する誰か。
　これだけお膳立てが揃っていたら、まず殺されてしかるべきだ。
　そこいらのホラー映画なみの状況に、吐き気というより笑いがこみ上げた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
Only then did I understand my situation.
A body that wouldn’t move.
A voice that wouldn’t come.
A dark Western mansion without a light burning anywhere.
And someone staring fixedly at their prey.
With the stage set so perfectly, being murdered was practically mandatory.
The scene belonged in a cheap horror film, and instead of nausea, laughter welled up inside me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----------"
Then I really realize my situation.
I can't move.
I can't even call out.
The dark mansion.
…… That "someone" looks at me as if staring at its prey.
Under all these conditions, it's no surprise if I die here.
This situation seems like such a bad horror movie that I almost start to laugh instead of being scared.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「………………は、はは」
　“誰か”は足音一つ立てずにやってくる。
　殺される、という緊迫感のためか、眩暈はさらに加速していく。
「―――――――――」
　気配が止まった。
　“誰か”は倒れた俺を見下ろして、そのまま、無防備な背中に向けて――――
「志貴さん、こんな所で寝てると風邪ひいちゃいますよー」
―――なんて、この上なく陽気なコトバを、投げかけてきた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ha――――ha, ha”
The figure drew near without making a sound.
Perhaps it was the tension of impending death; the world began spinning faster still.
“…”
The presence stopped.
The figure looked down at me, then turned toward my defenseless back――――
“Shiki, you’ll catch cold if you sleep in a place like this.”
―――and called down to me in the most cheerful voice imaginable.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……………… Ha, haha."
That "someone" takes a step towards me.
Is it fear of being killed?
My dizziness starts to increase.
"---------"
The presence stops.
It looks down at me and my defenseless back----
"Shiki-san, if you sleep there, you will catch a cold you know."
---and throws me those cheerful words.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「………………………琥珀、さん？」
「はい、わたしですけど何ですか？」
　………………どっと力が抜けた。
「志貴さん？
　ホントにどうしたんですか、こんなところで横になって」
　……あくまで陽気な声が聞こえる。
　それで安心してしまったのか、そのまま―――
　眩暈に揺れていた意識は、完全に途絶えてしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Kohaku?”
“Yes, it’s me—what is it?”
Every ounce of strength left me at once.
“Shiki? Why are you lying here?”
Her voice remained relentlessly bright.
Perhaps the relief was too much, because then―――
My consciousness, already rocking with vertigo, went out completely.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…………………… Kohaku, san?"
"Yes, it is me.
What is it?"
……………… I let my tension go.
"Shiki-san?
Really, just what exactly are you doing lying down like that?"
…… Her voice is really cheerful.
With that, I relaxed, and I---
completely overwhelmed by dizziness, my consciousness shuts down.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
強い陽射しを感じて目蓋を開けると、そこは自分の部屋だった。
　俺はきちんと寝巻に着替えて、ベッドに横になっている。
「―――――――――そうか、昨日」
　昨日の夜、ロビーで倒れてしまったんだ。
　翡翠は俺に気がつかずに行ってしまって、琥珀さんが物音を聞いてやってきてくれた。
「……ってコトは、出ていったのは秋葉のヤツか」
　……おそらく。
責任感の強い秋葉の事だから、夜の街にシキを捜しに行ったんだろう。
「……あいつ。
シキの事は俺に任せろって言ったのに……」
entries.maoEnglish:
When I opened my eyes to strong sunlight, I was in my own room.
I was wearing pajamas and lying in bed.
“That’s right―――――yesterday”
I had collapsed in the foyer.
Hisui had passed me, and Kohaku had come afterward.
“Then Akiha must have been the one who went out.”
Probably. Knowing Akiha’s sense of responsibility, she had gone looking for SHIKI.
“Idiot. I told her to leave SHIKI to me…”
entries.mirrorMoon:
Strong rays of sunshine cause me to open my eyes.
I'm in my room.
I am now wearing my pajamas and lying in bed.

"---------That's right, last night."
I collapsed in the lobby last night.
Hisui did not realize I was there and Kohaku-san heard something and came.
"…… That means that Akiha was the one that left."
…… Probably.
Akiha always had a strong sense of responsibility, so she must have gone looking for SHIKI on the streets.
" …… Akiha.
I told her to leave him to me……"
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「失礼します」
　ノックの音がして、扉が開く。
　やってきたのは洗面器やらタオルやらを持った琥珀さんだった。
「あ、おはようございます志貴さん。
お体の具合はどうですか？」
