　いつもと変わらない笑顔で琥珀さんは近寄ってきた。
「―――――――」
　昨夜の翡翠との会話が思い出される。
　それをなんとか思考の隅においやって、出来るだけいつも通りに笑ってみせた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Excuse me.”
A knock sounded, and the door opened.
Kohaku entered carrying a basin, towels, and an assortment of other things.
“Oh, good morning, Shiki. How are you feeling?”
Kohaku approached with her usual smile.
“…”
Last night’s conversation with Hisui came rushing back.
I shoved it into a distant corner of my mind and returned as normal a smile as I could manage.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Excuse me."
With a knock, the door opens.
Kohaku-san enters carrying a towel and a bucket.
"Ah, good morning Shiki-san.
How are you feeling?"
Kohaku-san draws near with her normal smile.
"-------"
I think back to last night's conversation with Hisui.
Tucking that away into the back of my mind, I try to make my usual smile.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「おはよう琥珀さん。
あの―――昨日の夜、あれから琥珀さんが運んできてくれたんですか？」
「あれ、志貴さん覚えてないんですか？
　志貴さんロビーで横になっていて、お声をかけたら一人で立ちあがって。
いや、よく寝た、とか言って歩き出したんですよー。
肩をお貸ししましたけど、志貴さんはご自分でここまで戻ってきたんです」
「………そう。
なんか、まったく記憶にないんだけど。
ここんところ疲れてるのかな。
自分が何をしていたのか、よく思い出せなくなるんだ」
「はあ。
それじゃ昨夜の事も覚えていないんですか？」
「……多分。
俺の記憶は台所で―――――」
　……翡翠と、琥珀さんの関係を、聞かされたんだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Morning, Kohaku. Were you the one who brought me here after I collapsed last night?”
“What, don’t you remember, Shiki? You were lying in the foyer when I called to you. You stood up by yourself, said you had slept well, and started walking. I lent you my shoulder, but you made it back here on your own.”
“I see. I don’t remember any of that. Maybe I’ve been too tired lately. I keep losing track of what I’ve been doing.”
“Oh. Then don’t you remember last night either?”
“Probably not. My memory stops in the kitchen, when―――――”
That was when Hisui told me the truth about herself and Kohaku.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Mornin', Kohaku-san.
Um---did you carry me up here after last night?"
"Huh?
Do you not remember, Shiki-san?
I found you collapsed in the lobby and you stood up once I called you.
You said you had a nice nap and started to walk.
I did lend you my shoulder, but you walked here by yourself."
"……… Oh.
I don't even remember it.
I must have been so tired that I forgot what I did."
"So you don't remember anything about last night?"
"…… Maybe.
I remember being in the kitchen-----"
…… And hearing about Hisui and Kohaku-san's connection.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「あはは、それは残念ですねー。
志貴さん、ずっとわたしに謝っていたんですよ。
　どうして謝るんですかって尋ねるんですけど、俺はばかだ、とうへんぼくだ、としか答えてくださらないんです。
　志貴さん、とうへんぼくなんですか？」
「いや。
いちおう人間のつもりだけど」
　……まあ、それでもそろそろ本気で朴念仁だの甲斐性なしだのと、石を投げられるような気はする。
「……ともかく助かった。
あのままロビーで寝てたら風邪を引いてたし、学校だって―――」
　あれ？
　目の錯覚が、時計は午前十時を余裕で過ぎてしまっている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ahaha, what a shame, Shiki. You spent the whole time apologizing to me.
I kept asking what you were sorry for, but all you would say was that you were an idiot and a blockhead.
Shiki, are you really a blockhead?”
“No. I’m fairly sure I’m human.”
Although at this rate, I did expect people to start throwing stones at me for being a hopelessly insensitive good-for-nothing.
“Anyway, thank you. If I’d slept in the foyer all night, I’d have caught a cold, and school―――”
Wait. Unless my eyes deceived me, the clock was well past ten.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ahaha.
That is unfortunate.
Shiki-san, you kept apologizing to me.
I inquired why you kept apologizing, and you kept saying that you were an idiot and a blockhead.
Shiki-san, are you a blockhead?"
"No, I don't think so."
…… Well, I am really starting to get the idea that they think my brain is made out of wood.

"…… Anyway, thanks a lot.
If I slept on the stairs, I'd have caught a cold, and school---"
Huh?
Are my eyes playing tricks on me?
The clock tells me it is already past ten in the morning.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「あ―――！
　こ、琥珀さん、学校っ！」
「はい。
志貴さんの学校でしたら、今日は創立記念日でお休みですね」
「――――――――」
　そう、か。
そういえば、そんな日もあったっけ。
　ここんところ学校に行っても上の空だったから、そんな事さえ忘れていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“School! Kohaku, school!”
“Yes. Your school is closed today for its anniversary.”
“…”
I see. Come to think of it, there was such a day.
I had been so distracted at school lately that even that had slipped my mind.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah---!
Ko, Kohaku-san, School!"
"Yes.
Today is your school's founding holiday, so you don't have school."
"--------"
That's right.
Come to think of it, it was.
I completely forgot about it since I have been spacing out at school lately.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「ま、ともかく起きないと。
こんな時間まで寝てたら秋葉になんて言われるか―――」
　ベッドから体を起こす。
「あれ――――うまく、体が」
　動いてくれない。
　腕をたてて体を起こそうとするんだけど、その腕に力が入らない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Well, I should still get up. If Akiha hears I slept this late―――”
I pushed myself upright.
“What――――my body won’t move”
It refused to move properly.
I braced my arms to sit up, but no strength would enter them.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Well, I should get up anyway.
If I sleep any longer Akiha will---"
I sit up on my bed.
"Huh?-----I can't really."
My body won't move.
I try to get up with my arms, but they have no strength.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「どうやらまだお体の具合が悪いみたいですね。
今朝は三十八度ほど熱がありましたし、まだ顔色が優れてませんし。
退屈でしょうけど、今日はベッドの上でお休みしてくださいね、志貴さん」
　琥珀さんは冷たい水で絞ったタオルを俺のおでこに乗せてくる。
　……冷たくて、気持ちがいい。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You still seem unwell. Your temperature was around thirty-eight degrees this morning, and you’re still rather pale. I know you’ll be bored, but please stay in bed and rest today, Shiki.”
Kohaku laid a towel wrung out in cold water across my forehead.
It was wonderfully cool.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"It seems your condition is still bad.
You have a slight fever and you look a little pale.
It may be boring, but please rest in bed today, Shiki-san."
Kohaku-san wipes my forehead with the cold, wet towel.
…… It feels good and cold.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「んー、とりあえず熱は下がっていますねー。
汗はだいぶ引いてくれたようですし、お顔の色もよくなってきてるから、夜には元気になってますよ」
　琥珀さんは体温計や氷枕をテキパキと繰り出してくる。
　……最後には口をあけさせられて、舌の具合まで確かめられてしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hmm, your fever has come down for now. You’ve mostly stopped sweating, and the color is returning to your face, so you should be feeling much better by tonight.”
Kohaku briskly produced a thermometer, an ice pillow, and one instrument after another.
By the end, she even made me open my mouth so she could examine my tongue.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hmm, it seems your fever is down.
You're not sweating as much and your face looks much better.
You should be well by the evening."
Kohaku-san crisply brings out a thermometer and an ice pillow.
…… In the end, she makes me open my mouth and checks the condition of my tongue.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「それではすぐにお粥を持ってまいりますね。
志貴さん、今日は大人しくしてないとダメですよ」
「あ―――琥珀さん」
「はい？
　なんですか志貴さん？」
　……琥珀さんはやっぱり琥珀さんだ。
　見ているとこっちまで元気が出てきそうなその笑顔に変わりはない。
　俺には―――この人が、ただ笑顔を演じているだけだなんて思えない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’ll bring you some rice porridge right away. You must behave yourself today, Shiki.”
“Wait—Kohaku.”
“Yes? What is it, Shiki?”
Kohaku was still Kohaku.
That smile, bright enough to restore the spirits of anyone who saw it, had not changed.
I could not believe it was merely an act.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Well, I'll bring you some rice porridge right away.
Shiki-san, you better behave today."
"Ah---Kohaku-san."
"Yes?
What is it, Shiki-san?"
…… As expected, she is like always.
Her usual cheerful smile doesn't change.
I---I can't bring myself to think that her smile is just an act.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
「……いや、なんでもないんだ。
お粥、楽しみにしてます」
「はい、それでは失礼しますね」
　琥珀さんはパタパタと足音をたてて廊下へ去っていく。
　その後ろ姿を、ただ黙って見つめていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“No, it’s nothing. I’m looking forward to the porridge.”
“All right, I’ll leave you to rest.”
Kohaku pattered out into the corridor.
I watched her go without a word.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Nothing.
I'm looking forward to the rice porridge."
"Yes, well then, excuse me."
Kohaku-san disappears down the hall, her footsteps padding after her.
I just stare at that figure silently.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
正午になった。
　琥珀さんはお粥を持ってきた後、屋敷の仕事に戻っていった。
「…………………はぁ」
　こうして一人になると、今の自分が置かれた状況の異常さにため息が出てしまう。
　……養子だった自分。
　……それでも構わないと言ってくれた秋葉。
　……翡翠と琥珀さん。
　……そして、いまだ野放しになっている殺人鬼。
entries.maoEnglish:
Noon arrived.
After bringing my porridge, Kohaku returned to her work around the mansion.
“Haaah…”
Alone again, I could only sigh at the madness of my situation.
I was adopted.
Akiha had said it didn’t matter.
Hisui and Kohaku.
And somewhere outside, the murderer still roamed free.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Noon arrives.
After bringing the food, Kohaku-san went back to her duties.
…………………… *sigh*
Being alone, I let out a sigh as I think of my strange circumstances.
…… Myself being adopted.
…… Akiha saying that she doesn't care about it.
…… Hisui and Kohaku-san.
…… And the killer that's still on the loose.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
琥珀さんに尋ねた所、今朝のニュースで新しい死者が出た、というものはなかったそうだ。
　それでもシキが野放しになっている以上、犠牲者はまた出てきてしまうだろう。
「……この体がもう少し思い通りになってくれれば、俺が―――」
　シキを止める、と言いかけて、枕に頭をうずめた。
　あんな夢を見続けた影響だろうか。
俺もシキに負けず劣らず物騒な思考をしている。
「……何をするにしても、とにかく体を治さないとダメだよな」
　目蓋を閉じる。
entries.maoEnglish:
Kohaku said the morning news had reported no new deaths.
Even so, as long as SHIKI remained at large, there would be more victims.
“If only this body would do what I tell it, I could―――”
I nearly said I would stop SHIKI, then buried my face in the pillow.
Perhaps those dreams had infected me. My thoughts were as dangerous as SHIKI’s.
“Whatever I do, I need to get well first.”
I closed my eyes.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I asked Kohaku-san, but it doesn't seem like there was a new victim in the news today.
But as long as SHIKI is still on the loose, there will be more victims.
"…… If only this body did what I told it to, I---"
I could stop SHIKI.
I lay my head back down on the pillow as I start to say that.
Maybe it's because I've been seeing those dreams, but I'm beginning to have violent thoughts like SHIKI.
"…… Whatever I do, I should heal up first."
I close my eyes.
entries.scriptLabel: 7 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour I

entries.japanese:
よっぽど今まで疲れていたのか、気を抜くとすぐに眠気がやってきた。
　……耳をすませていると、自分の鼓動がよく聞こえる。
　どくん、どくん、どくん、どくん。
　体の内側から響いてくる音がうるさくて、まどろみから現に戻る。
entries.maoEnglish:
I must have been far more exhausted than I knew, because the moment I relaxed, sleep came for me again.
When I listen, I can hear my heart with unnatural clarity.
Thud, thud, thud, thud.
The noise reverberating through my body is so loud it drags me back from sleep into waking.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Was I this tired all along?
My energy just drains from me and I feel sleepiness overcome me.
…… I can hear my pulse in my ears.
Thump, Thump, Thump, Thump.
It echoes inside my whole body noisily and jerks me away from dozing off.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「あ………つ」
　また、喉が乾いている。
　喉がカラカラに渇いて、頭がぼーっとかすんできた。
　目を覚ます。
　体はまだ鈍い。
少し熱がぶり返してきた。
　それでも、食堂にいって水を飲むぐらいなら、体を動かしてもいいだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hot…”
My throat is dry again.
It is parched raw, and a haze spreads through my head.
I force myself awake.
My body is still sluggish. The fever has begun to return.
Even so, surely I can manage the walk to the dining room for a drink of water.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ho……… t."
I'm thirsty again.
My throat is dry, my mind is foggy.
I open my eyes.
My body still feels sluggish and my fever has slightly increased.
But still, I should be able to at least go to the dining room and get some water.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
廊下には誰もいない。
　昔。
　思い出せないぐらい昔か、それとも思い出す必要がない昔に見た、映画に出てくる廃墟みたいに、静かだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
The corridor is deserted.
Long ago.
As quiet as the ruins in some film I saw long ago—so long ago I can no longer remember it, or perhaps simply have no need to.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The hallway is empty.
A long time ago.
So long ago I don't remember or something I don't need to remember…… this place is quiet like ruins you might see in a movie.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
暑い。
　陽射しが暑い。
　ただ水を飲みたいだけなのに、どうして。
　何かに引き寄せられるように足が動く。
entries.maoEnglish:
Hot.
The sunlight is hot.
I only wanted water, so why…?
My feet carry me onward as if something is drawing them.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Hot.
The sunlight is hot.
I just want some water, so why?
Something compels my legs to move.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
……離れは強い陽射しにかすみそうだった。
　まるで、ここだけ砂漠にでもなったように暑くて、白くて、目がかすむ。
　……ごと、と物音がした。
　……離れの中からだ。
　……誰か。
　……中に、いるのだろうか。
entries.maoEnglish:
The detached building shimmers in the fierce sunlight.
It is as if this one place has become a desert—hot, white, blurring before my eyes.
Something knocks softly inside.
Inside the annex.
Is someone…
in there?
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… It seems like the detached building is bathed in sunlight.
Completely, like I'm in a hot desert, my vision dims, white.
…… Thud.
I hear a noise.
…… It's from this detached house.
…… Someone.
…… Is there someone in there?
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
縁側から障子を少しだけあけて、中を覗いた。
　そこには秋葉と琥珀の姿があった。
　二人の様子はどこかおかしい。
　しゅるり、という、帯の外れる音。
―――――なに、を。
　無言のまま、琥珀は着物をはだけさせて、その胸をさらけだした。
entries.maoEnglish:
From the veranda, I ease the shoji open a crack and peer inside.
Akiha and Kohaku are there.
Something about them is wrong.
Silk whispers as an obi comes undone.
―――――What are they doing?

entries.japanese:
背骨にたかった昆虫は、ずぶずぶと、首のあたりから脳内に入ってくる。
　何十という昆虫が爪をたてて、キィキィと鳴いて、背中にたかっている。
　その虫が入るたびに――――いいようのない衝動に支配されかける。
　コロセ、と。
　遠野秋葉を殺し尽くせと、頭の中で繰り返される。
　その昆虫の名は、殺意というモノに違いなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
The insects clinging to my spine burrow wetly through the base of my neck and into my brain.
Dozens dig in their claws, squealing as they swarm across my back.
With every insect that enters, an indescribable impulse comes closer to consuming me.
KILL HER.
The command repeats inside my skull: kill every last part of Akiha Tohno.
Those insects could have only one name: murderous intent.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The insects gathered around my spine crawl into my brain through my neck.
Countless insects claw my back, crying out.
As the insects enter----a sick impulse almost seizes me.
KILL.
The command to kill Tohno Akiha fills my brain.
There can be no mistake, the name of these insects is "The Urge to Kill".
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「うる、さい―――うるさい、うるさい、うるさい、うるさい……………！！！！！」
　うなじを手で抑えた。
　そうでもしなければ狂いそうだ。
　血を啜っていた秋葉に対する憎悪なんてない。
　ただ、秋葉を殺せと繰り返す自分自身に対する、憎悪しか、存在しない――――
entries.maoEnglish:
“Shut up—shut up, shut up, shut up, shut up!”
I clamp a hand over the nape of my neck.
Without that, I will go mad.
I feel no hatred for Akiha because she drank blood.
There is only hatred for myself—for the self that will not stop demanding Akiha’s death――――
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shut, up---shut up, shut up, shut up, shut up………………!!!!!"
I slap the back of my neck with my hand.
I felt like I'd go crazy if I didn't.
I don't hate Akiha for sucking blood.
I only hate myself.
I hate being filled with the command to kill her----
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「はぁ………はっ、あ、はあ―――――」
　首筋にたかる虫どもを振り払って、自分の部屋に逃げ込んだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Haa―――hah, ah, haaah―――――”
I beat away the insects swarming at my neck and flee into my room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Haa……… ha, ah, haa-----"
Shaking off the insects from the back of my neck, I escape to my room.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「――――あ――――は、あ―――――」
　壁に背中を預けて、途切れそうになる息を継いだ。
　俺は自分自身の行動を抑制できない。
　こんなもの、シキという殺人鬼と一体どこが違うというのか。
　……いや。
　そんなコト、本当はどうだっていい。
　俺は、どうして―――解って、あげられなかったんだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ah――――hah, ah―――――”
I lean against the wall, fighting for each failing breath.
I cannot control my own actions.
What difference is there between this and the murderer called SHIKI?
No.
That does not truly matter.
Why couldn’t I understand her―――?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----Ah-----ha, ah-----"
Leaning my back against the wall, I catch my breath.
I can't control myself.
Just what's different between SHIKI and the way I am now?
…… No.
That isn't really important.
Why---why couldn't I understand her?
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「―――――――琥珀、さん―――――」
　……槙久の手記にあった言葉。
　感応者という単語。
養子としてではなく、ただの道具として扱われる為に引き取られた琥珀と翡翠。
　その意味。
　槙久付きという事の意味を、俺はまったく理解していなかった。
理解、しようとさえしなかった。

―――毎日毎日、飽きる事なく―――
　秋葉はそう言った。
　槙久が何をしていたか、俺には考えるまでもない。
　槙久が俺と同じように暴力的な衝動に支配される人間なら、琥珀に何をしたかなんて、わかりきってる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Kohaku―――――”
Words from Makihisa’s journal.
Resonator. Kohaku and Hisui, taken in not as adopted children but as tools to be used.
What that meant.
What it meant for Kohaku to be assigned to Makihisa. I had understood none of it, never even tried.
―――Day after day, without ever tiring—
That was what Akiha said.
I do not need to wonder what Makihisa did.
If violent impulses ruled him as they rule me, then what he did to Kohaku is obvious.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-------Kohaku, san-----"
…… The word in Makihisa's journal.
The word "Synchronizer".
Kohaku and Hisui weren't adopted, they were just brought here as tools.
The meaning.
I didn't know the meaning of what it meant by being Makihisa's servant.
I didn't even try to understand.
---Every, every day, without end---
Akiha said that.
I don't have to think too hard about what Makihisa did.
If Makihisa was subject to the same violent urges as me, I understand all too clearly what he must have done.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
―――いつも。
いつも窓際にいた少女。
　外に出る事も、助けを求める事も、知らなかった。
　まだ幼い琥珀に対して、槙久は情けなんてもたなかった。
　あの手記に書かれていた事だ。
　槙久は、琥珀を道具としか見ていなかった。
　ただ、子供のように。
自分の欲情を、少女に叩きつけていただけだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Always. The girl who was always at the window.
She knew neither how to go outside nor how to ask for help.
Makihisa showed no mercy to a Kohaku who was still only a child.
His journal made that clear.
To him, she was nothing but a tool.
Like a child himself. He simply battered the girl with his lust.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Always.
That girl was always by the window.
Not knowing how to leave, or even how to beg for help.
Makihisa had no sympathy for Kohaku still being a little girl.
It was written in the journal.
Makihisa only saw Kohaku as a tool.
Just like a child.
Placing all his emotions onto her.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
―――ずっと、ただ庭で遊ぶ自分たちを眺めているだけだった少女。
　槙久の事を責められない。
　俺だって。
槙久以上に、彼女に責め苦を負わせていた。
　翡翠は言った。
　琥珀さんは、ずっと翡翠になりたかったんだと。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――The girl who could only watch us playing in the garden, day after day.
I cannot condemn Makihisa.
I did it too. I inflicted a torment on her even worse than his.
Hisui told me.
Kohaku had always wanted to become her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---That girl would perpetually just stare at us while we played in the garden.
I can't condemn Makihisa.
I also tortured her, more than Makihisa.
Hisui said it.
That Kohaku-san always wanted to become "Hisui".
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「―――――――――」
　俺には想像すらできない。
　子供の頃から、ずっと屋敷に閉じ込められていた少女。
　たった一枚の窓を隔てて遊んでいた俺たちを眺めるだけの毎日。
　それなのに。
　屋敷を離れる俺に、大事なものを預けてくれた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
I cannot even imagine it.
A girl imprisoned in the mansion since childhood.
Every day spent behind a single pane of glass, watching the rest of us play.
And yet.
When I left the mansion, she entrusted me with something precious to her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---------"
I can't even imagine it.
That girl being locked in the mansion ever since childhood.
Looking down at us playing behind that clear wall of a window every day.
Despite this,
she gave me something important to her as I left.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
その後。
　働けなくなった妹の為に妹の役割を演じた彼女は、その芝居の中で笑った。
――――ひどい、道化だ。
　……そんな、自分で作り物と解っている芝居の中でしか、彼女は笑えなかったのか。
entries.maoEnglish:
Afterward.
When her sister could no longer work, she assumed Hisui’s role—and learned to smile inside that performance.
――――What a hideous farce.
Could she smile only inside a performance she knew perfectly well was false?
entries.mirrorMoon:
After that.
For the sake of her younger sister, she began smiling in her own play.
----A terrible farce.
…… Only, inside the play even she knows is a lie, all she can do is laugh?
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「――――――なんて」
　なんていう仕打ちを、俺はしてしまったのか。
　……俺は琥珀さんが翡翠だと思いこんで、琥珀さん相手に、あの頃の思い話なんかをしてた。
　歓迎会の日。
　琥珀さんと料理をしながら、俺は幸せそうに翡翠との思い出話を語っていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“How could I…”
How could I have done that to her?
I mistook Kohaku for Hisui and reminisced to her about those days.
At my welcome party.
While Kohaku and I cooked together, I happily told her all my treasured memories of Hisui.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------What---"
What a terrible thing I've done.
…… Thinking that Kohaku-san was Hisui, I've spoke to her about my memories of the past.
The day of the welcome party.
While cooking with Kohaku-san, I spoke so happily about memories with Hisui.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese: ―――傷ついた指を、彼女は痛くないと言った。
entries.maoEnglish: ―――When she cut her finger, she said it did not hurt.
entries.mirrorMoon: ---She said she didn't feel pain when she cut her finger.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「――――愚か、な」
　……胸がつまる。
　呼吸ができない。
　秋葉を殺したくなる自分。
　こんなにも無神経な自分。
「ごめん――――ごめん、琥珀さん―――――」
　意識がゆらぐ。
　そのまま体は昏睡する。
　俺は、初めて。
　自分のこの力で、自分自身を、殺したいと思った。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What a fool.”
My chest closes.
I cannot breathe.
The self that wants to kill Akiha.
The self so callous it could do this.
“I’m sorry――――Kohaku, I’m sorry―――――”
My consciousness sways.
My body sinks into oblivion.
For the first time.
I wish I could turn this power upon myself and die by my own hand.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----Foolish."
…… My chest constricts.
I can't breathe.
My self that wants to kill Akiha.
My self that couldn't even understand what was going on.
"Sorry----sorry, Kohaku-san------"
My consciousness wavers.
My body enters a stupor.
For the first time,
I want to kill myself using my ability.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「……秋葉さま、お医者さまをお呼びしないのですか？」
「無駄よ。
兄さんの体は病気という訳ではないんだもの。
原因を解決しないかぎり治ってくれるものじゃないわ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Miss Akiha, shouldn’t we call a doctor?”
“It would be pointless. Brother is not ill. He cannot recover until the cause itself is removed.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Akiha-sama, won't you call a doctor?"
"That is pointless.
He isn't sick.
He won't get better unless we take away what's causing it."
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
……あきは　と　ひすい　が話している。
　ここは　シキの　部屋だ。
　どうやらベッドの上で　眠っている　らしい。
entries.maoEnglish:
akiha and hisui are talking.
this is Shiki’s room.
apparently he is asleep on the bed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Akiha  and  Hisui   are talking.
This  is   SHIKI's room.
It looks   like   I am  sleeping  on the bed.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
あきは、と声をあげて起きようとしたが、体が思うように動かない。
　体は鉛のように重い。
満足に動くのは目と口だけ。
　一瞬。
　まだ、夢のなかにいるのかと、思った。
entries.maoEnglish:
I try to call out, akiha, and sit up, but my body refuses to obey.
My body weighs as much as lead. Only my eyes and mouth move properly.
For an instant.
I wonder whether I am still dreaming.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I try to get out of bed, but I can't move at all.
My body is heavy like lead.
All I can move freely are my mouth and eyes.
For an instant,
I think I am still dreaming.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「失態ね、翡翠。
今日一日は兄さんをいたわってあげて、と言ったでしょう？
　こんな事じゃ兄さんを任せる事はできないわよ」
「もうしわけ…………ありません」
「謝るのなら兄さんに謝って頂戴。
私に謝られても不愉快なだけよ」
entries.maoEnglish:
“You failed him, Hisui. I told you to take care of Brother all day, did I not? If this is the result, I cannot entrust him to you.”
“I am deeply sorry.”
“If you wish to apologize, apologize to Brother. Hearing it from you only irritates me.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"You failed, Hisui.
I told you to pay attention to Nii-san today, right?
I can't even trust you to take care of Nii-san like this."
"I am………… very sorry."
"If you want to apologize, apologize to Nii-san.
Apologizing to me will just make me angry."
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
……俺には、二人がどうしてこうなっているのか全然わからない。
　わからないけれど、翡翠が俺のせいで怒られている、という事ぐらいは読み取れた。
entries.maoEnglish:
I don’t understand what brought them to this.
But I can at least tell that Hisui is being blamed because of me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… I don't understand why they're like that.
But I understand that Hisui is being scolded because of me.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「……秋葉さま。
わたしでは志貴さまがお倒れになった時、咄嗟にお助けする事ができません。
どうか姉さんと役割を替えていただけないでしょうか」
「……だめよ。
しばらく琥珀は兄さんには近づけさせません。
翡翠もそのつもりでいて。
琥珀を呼ぶ時は貴方も同伴して、兄さんと琥珀を二人きりにしないこと」
entries.maoEnglish:
“…Miss Akiha, when Master Shiki collapses, I am unable to support him quickly enough. Would you please allow my sister and me to exchange duties?”
“No. Kohaku will not be allowed near Brother for some time, so remember that, Hisui. If you must call her, you will remain present. Never leave Brother and Kohaku alone together.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Akiha-sama.
I cannot help Shiki-sama if he collapses.
Please give Nee-san my duty."
"…… That won't do.
I can't let Kohaku near Nii-san.
You shouldn't, either.
Be with Kohaku every time she's here and never let her alone with Nii-san."
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「ですが秋葉さま。
志貴さまの容体は日に日に悪くなってきています。
姉さんに薬を処方してもらわないと、志貴さまは立ち上がる事もできなくなるのではないですか？」
「……そうね。
けど、それはそれで都合がいいわ」
　小さく呟いて、秋葉は思案する。
「翡翠、兄さんが起きたらしばらくは学校を休むように言って。
ここ数日元気がなかったみたいだし、顔色が良くなるまで部屋から出してはダメよ。
　学校には私のほうから連絡を入れておきます」
entries.maoEnglish:
“But, Miss Akiha. Master Shiki’s condition is worsening by the day. Unless my sister prepares medicine for him, Master Shiki may soon be unable even to stand.”
“True. But that may be convenient in its own way.”
Akiha murmurs, considering.
“Hisui, when Brother wakes, tell him he is to stay home from school for a while. He has looked unwell for days, so do not let him leave this room until his color improves.
I will notify the school myself.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"But Akiha-sama, Shiki-sama's condition is getting worse.
If he does not receive medicine from Nee-san, he will not even be able to stand."
"…… That is true.
But, that's better for me."
Akiha murmurs this as she ponders.
"Hisui, tell Nii-san to skip school for a few days when he wakes.
He has not been well the past few days, so do not let him out of the room until he gets better.
I will contact his school."
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
……秋葉の姿が見えなくなった。
　部屋には、押し黙ったままの翡翠だけが、いる。
「……志貴さま。
お目覚めでいらっしゃいますか？」
　……驚いた。
　秋葉は気がついていなかったようだけど、翡翠は俺が起きている事に気がついていたらしい。
「……ああ、ちょっと前から目が醒めてた。
……すまない。
俺のせいで秋葉に怒られてたんだろ」
entries.maoEnglish:
Akiha disappears from view.
Only Hisui remains in the room, silent and still.
“…Master Shiki, are you awake?”
That surprises me.
Akiha apparently failed to notice, but Hisui knew I was conscious.
“Yeah. I woke up a little while ago. Sorry—Akiha was angry with you because of me, wasn’t she?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… I can no longer see Akiha's figure.
A subdued Hisui is the only one in the room.
"…… Shiki-sama, are you awake?"
…… I'm surprised.
Akiha didn't even realize it, but Hisui must have known I was awake.
"…… Yeah, I woke up just a little bit ago.
…… Sorry.
Because of me, Akiha was mad at you."
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「いえ、秋葉さまがお怒りになられるのは当然の事です。
志貴さまがお倒れにになっていたのに、わたしは気がつかないでいたのですから」
「―――ったく。
そんなのもう慣れっこだろ。
秋葉もなんだって、こんな事ぐらいで学校を休めなんていうんだ。
　こんなの朝になればすぐに治るんだから、あんなに過保護になる必要なんかないのに」
entries.maoEnglish:
“No. Miss Akiha had every right to be angry; you had collapsed, Master Shiki, and I failed to notice.”
“Come on. I’ve done that often enough. Why is Akiha making such a fuss about this and ordering me to miss school?
I’ll be fine by morning, so there’s no need to be so overprotective.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No, it was only natural for her to be angry.
I did not realize that you had collapsed, Shiki-sama."
"----Geez.
I'm used to it.
And what's with Akiha wanting me to skip school?
I'm fine, so I don't really need intensive care or anything."
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「……志貴さま。
その件ですが、どうか秋葉さまのおっしゃる通りにしていただけないでしょうか」
「は？
　秋葉の言う通りって、明日から学校を休めっていう事？」
　はい、と頷く翡翠。
　その目は秋葉に叱られる事ではなく、本当に俺の体を案じている眼差しだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki. Regarding that matter, would you please do as Miss Akiha asks?”
“What? You mean stay home from school starting tomorrow?”
Hisui nods.
Her gaze holds no fear of Akiha’s displeasure—only genuine concern for me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Shiki-sama.
About that, can you not do as she tells you to do?"
"Huh?
You mean not going to school tomorrow?"
Hisui nods.
She looks as if she is not worried about being scolded by Akiha.
Rather, she is really concerned over me.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「う――――――――」
　そんな目をされたら嫌だ、なんてとても言えない。
「…………わかったよ。
とりあえず明日ぐらいは学校を休む。
それでいい？」
　翡翠は申し訳なさそうに、微かに笑顔をうかべる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Urgh…”
I cannot possibly refuse while she looks at me like that.
“All right. I’ll stay home tomorrow, at least. Will that do?”
Hisui gives me the faintest apologetic smile.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Oo--------"
I can't say no to those eyes.
"………… I understand.
I'll rest from school tomorrow, is that acceptable?"
Hisui gives a weak, apologetic smile.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「……それでは失礼します。
何かありましたら、すぐにお呼びください」
―――翡翠は一礼して立ち去っていった。
　一人になった途端、急速に眠気が襲ってきた。
「っ――――」
　深刻な話、俺の体はどうかしてしまっているらしい。
　起きていようと努力しているのに、まったく抑えがきかない。
　俺は天井の模様を睨みつけながら、それでも呆気なく眠りに落ちてしまっ――――
entries.maoEnglish:
“Then I will leave you to rest. If you need anything, please call me at once.”
―――Hisui bows and departs.
The instant I am alone, sleep rushes over me.
“Ngh…”
Something is seriously wrong with my body.
I fight to remain conscious, but I have no control over it at all.
Glaring at the pattern on the ceiling, I fall helplessly, absurdly easily, into sleep—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Well then, please excuse me.
If anything happens, please call for me."
---Hisui disappears with a bow.
The instant I become alone, sleepiness assails me.
"-----"

In all seriousness, there does seem to be something wrong with my body.
I'm trying to stay awake, but it's no use.
Staring at the pattern on the ceiling, I easily fall asleep----
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
――――どうしてこんなにも悲しいのか。
　その理由が解らない。
　別に、誰がどうなろうとそれはその個人の運命だ。
　他人である自分に分け与えられる物ではない。
　痛みも喜びも、感情も肉体も、別に。
　なにが、悲しいというわけじゃない。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――Why does this make me so unbearably sad?
I do not understand.
Whatever happens to someone is that person’s own fate.
None of it can be shared with an outsider like me.
Not pain or joy, emotion or flesh.
There is nothing for me to grieve.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----Why is there this much sadness?
I don't understand the reason.
Whatever happens to anyone, it is their fate.
It's not something that I can receive as a stranger.
Neither pain, nor happiness, nor feelings, nor flesh.
It's not that I'm sad.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
―――なのにどうして、こんなにも悔しいのか。
　あの少女の事を何も知らなかったくせに。
　今の彼女の事しか見ていなかったくせに。
　自分にとって、二つの事柄には繋がりなんてありはしない。
　なのにどうして。
　今まで見もしなかった過去を思うと、胸が張り裂けそうになるのか。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Then why does it fill me with such bitter anguish?
I knew nothing about that little girl.
I saw only the woman she is now.
To me, those two lives had never been connected.
And yet.
Why does a past I never once looked at feel as though it will tear my heart apart?
entries.mirrorMoon:
---So why this relentless regret?
Even though I never knew about that girl.
Even though I only looked at her now.
For me, there isn't a connection between the two.
So why?
After thinking of the past I did not see until now, why does my chest feel like it is tearing apart?
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
―――なあ。
一番悲惨なヤツってどんなのかな。
　月の夜。
　偶然街で出会った殺人鬼は、ふとそんな事を尋ねてきた。
　それはとりとめのなかった、意味などない会話の中のヒトコマだ。
　……それに、自分はどう答えただろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Tell me. What kind of person has the most wretched life of all?
On a moonlit night.
The murderer I happened to meet in the city asked me that question.
It was only a fragment of an aimless conversation without any meaning.
What answer did I give him?
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Hey, I wonder what is the most miserable?
That moonlit night.
The killer I happened to meet that one night asked that question.
That was just one of the many, rambling and meaningless scenes.
…… And how did I respond?
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
悲しい事は簡単に目に付くし、倖せは難しすぎて解らない。
　悲惨な状況といったらそれこそ限りなく下を見るしかない。
　この上なく悲しい思い、耐えられないほど辛い生き方を強制される事が悲惨だというのなら、生まれてこなければいい事になる。
―――自分にとっては。
　その、生まれえないという事が、一番悲しい事だと思った。
entries.maoEnglish:
Misery is easy to recognize, while happiness is too difficult to understand.
If you measure wretchedness by circumstances, there is always someone lower.
If the worst fate means suffering unbearable grief and being forced into an intolerably painful life, then the answer would simply be never to have been born.
―――To me.
The inability ever to be born seemed saddest of all.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Sadness is easy to see and happiness is hard to understand.
To find miserable situations, you have to look way down.
If being miserable is living a life so painful and full of suffering that makes you wish you were dead, then it would mean that it was better if you were never born.
---As for me,
I thought the saddest thing was to never have been born.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
そう言うと、殺人鬼だと名乗っていた男は笑った。
　のけぞるぐらいに笑って、おまえはいいヤツだな、とかノタマッタ後。
!w1000
―――なにが悲惨かって、そりゃあさ。
　その悲惨なヤツ本人が自分が悲惨だって気がついていないで、自分が幸せなんだって思ってる事なんじゃないか。
entries.maoEnglish:
At that, the man who called himself a murderer laughed.
He laughed until he threw back his head, then called me a good person. After that―――!w1000
―――The truly wretched one?
Isn’t it someone so wretched they don’t even realize it—someone who believes they’re happy?
entries.mirrorMoon:
After I said that, the killer laughed.
After laughing so hard, he said something along the lines that I was really a nice guy.
---What is misery?
Not even realizing your misery and mistaking it for happiness, I think.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
なるほど、と頷いた記憶がある。
　確かにそれはどうしようもない。
　自分が悲しいのだと思う事もできない。
　唯一、権利として与えられる同情でさえその本人には意味がない。
　彼女は自身が幸福だという幻想を信じたまま、誰が見ても滑稽な生を送る。
　苦痛を分け合えない他人として。
　悲惨といえば、きっとそういう在り方が、一番悲しいのだろう、と同意した。
entries.maoEnglish:
I remember nodding.
Yes, that would be beyond saving.
Such a person cannot even recognize her own sorrow.
Even pity—the one thing she is entitled to—means nothing to her.
Believing in the illusion of her own happiness, she lives a life that seems absurd to anyone watching.
As an outsider unable to share her pain.
I agreed that if any way of living deserved to be called wretched, that must surely be the saddest.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I remember nodding to that.
That really can't be helped.
Not being able to think that you're miserable.
The only thing that is granted to them will be that sympathy is meaningless.
Believing the illusion that she's happy, she will live a laughable life.
As a stranger that can't feel her pain,
I agreed that kind of misery was the worst.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「―――――――」
　何に起こされる訳でもなく、ゆっくりと目が醒めた。
　窓から入ってくる陽の光も、肌をさらう冷たい風も心地良い。
　外は、この上ないぐらいの晴天ぶりだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
Nothing in particular wakes me; my eyes simply open, slowly.
The sunlight through the window and the cool breeze brushing my skin are both pleasant.
Outside, the weather could not possibly be finer.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-------"
I slowly wake up for no apparent reason.
The combination of the cool breeze and the sunlight streaming from the window feels great.
The weather is simply exquisite.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
いつまでも横になっていられる天気じゃない。
　上半身だけでも体を起こして背伸びをしよう、と力をいれる。
「ありゃ――――やっぱりだめか」
　腕の感覚がまだ鈍い。
　一人で立ち上がれない、という程ではないが、歩きまわるには無理があるという感じだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
It is no day to spend lying down.
I tense my body, intending at least to sit up and stretch.
“Well――――I guess I still can’t”
My arms remain numb.
I could probably stand without help, but walking around would be too much.
entries.mirrorMoon:
It's not the kind of weather to spend all day in bed.
I lift my upper body.
"Aww----still no good."
My arms are still sluggish.
It's not like I can't stand up, but I probably won't be able to walk.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
トントン、という聞きなれたリズムのノックがした。
「失礼します、志貴さま。
お体の具合はよろしいですか？」
「ああ、調子はいいよ。
この分なら夜には動けるようになってる」
　……なんか昨日もそんなセリフを口にした気がするけど、今度こそ大丈夫だろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
A familiar two-beat knock sounds at the door.
“Excuse me, Master Shiki. How are you feeling?”
“Pretty good. At this rate, I should be moving again by tonight.”
I have a feeling I said the same thing yesterday, but surely this time I’m right.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I hear the gentle rhythm of knocking.
"Please excuse me, Shiki-sama.
How are you feeling?"
"Ah, I feel fine.
I bet I'll be able to move by evening."
…… I kind of remember saying that last night, but it should be fine this time.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「……志貴さま。
一つ、お聞きしていいでしょうか？」
「ん？
　なに？」
「志貴さまは有間の家で暮らしていた頃も、今回のようにお倒れになった事があるのですか？」
　翡翠の声は弱々しい。
　……この屋敷に帰ってきてから俺の体調が崩れたのでは、と心配しているみたいだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…Master Shiki, may I ask you something?”
“Hm? What?”
“While Master Shiki lived with the Arima family, did he ever collapse as he did this time?”
Hisui’s voice is frail.
She seems afraid that returning to this mansion is what ruined my health.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Shiki-sama.
May I ask you a question?"
"Hm?
What is it?"
"Shiki-sama, while you were living with the Arima family, did you ever collapse like this before?"
Hisui's voice is weak.
…… She seems worried that my declining condition is due to me coming back here.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「翡翠が責任を感じる事なんてないよ。
有間の家でもこういう事は何度かあったんだ。
……まあ、中学にあがってからは年に一回ぐらいになって、高校になってからは無かったからな。
　くるとしたらそろそろかなって、それなりに覚悟はしてた」
「では、その時もすぐに治られたのですか？」
「一日二日で治ったよ。
だからあんまり大事にとらないでくれ。
そんな顔をされると、なんだか俺まで重病なんだって勘違いするじゃないか」
entries.maoEnglish:
“You don’t have to blame yourself, Hisui. This happened a few times at the Arimas’ too. After I started middle school, it fell to about once a year, and it hasn’t happened at all since I entered high school.
I knew I was probably due for another spell, so I was more or less prepared.”
“Did you recover quickly then as well?”
“Within a day or two. So please don’t treat this as something grave. When you look at me like that, even I start imagining I’m seriously ill.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"You don't need to feel responsible, Hisui.
This happened to me while I lived with the Arimas.
…… Well, maybe once a year during middle school, but that stopped once I entered high school.
But, I was ready thinking that if it was going to come, it should be pretty soon."
"And did you recover quickly at those times?"
"In a day or two, so it's not a big deal.
You act like I have some serious illness or something."
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「………………志貴さまは、重症だと思います。
　貧血を起こす、とは聞いていましたが、そのようにお倒れになるとは聞いていませんでした。
　志貴さまはご自分のお体がおかしい、と思われた事はないのですか？」
「あはは。
キミの体はデタラメだね、とは主治医によく言われるぞ。
考えてみればこうして倒れてもすぐに回復するあたり、人より驚異的な体力といえるかもしんない」
「………………………」
　……あ。
笑って茶化したら、翡翠が怒った。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki, I believe you are seriously ill.
I knew you suffered from anemia, but no one told me you collapsed like this.
Has Master Shiki never wondered whether there is something truly wrong with his body?”
“Ha ha. My doctor often says my body makes no sense. Come to think of it, recovering so quickly after collapsing might mean I have extraordinary stamina.”
“…”
Ah. I laughed it off, and now Hisui is angry.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……………… Shiki-sama, I think it is a serious illness.
I have heard that you have anemia, but nothing like this.
Have you never thought that your body was strange?"
"Ahaha.
My doctor always says my body is just totally weird.
Come to think of it, collapsing like this and recovering so quickly, I could say my strength is much more amazing than most people's."
"……………………"
…… Ah.
I tried to laugh it off and made her angry.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま。
人より優れた体力を持つ方は、夜のうちに何度も熱をだしたりはいたしません。
昨夜、志貴さまが何度発熱したのか覚えておられますか？」
「え―――俺、なんかしたのか」
「……昨夜の話です。
志貴さまがお眠りになられた後、すぐに熱を出されました。
発汗もひどく、頻繁にお体を拭いて、一時間ごとに様子を見にきたほどです」
――――我ながら、それは凄い。
　凄いんだけど、こうも翡翠に迷惑をかけていると少しはしっかりしなくては、と恥じいってしまいそうだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki. A person with extraordinary stamina does not develop repeated fevers through the night. Does Master Shiki remember how many times his fever returned?”
“What happened to me?”
“This happened last night. Soon after Master Shiki fell asleep, his temperature rose. He perspired so heavily that we had to wipe him down repeatedly and check on him every hour.”
――――Even by my standards, that is impressive.
Though after causing Hisui so much trouble, I’m beginning to feel ashamed enough to try taking better care of myself.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama.
People whose strength is much more amazing do not have many fevers during the night.
Do you remember how many times you had a fever last night?"
"Eh---I, did something happen?"
"…… It was last night.
As soon as you fell asleep, you had a fever.
You began to sweat profusely and I had to come check on you every hour."
----If I do say so myself, that's amazing.
It is amazing, but I am a bit embarrassed to have been such a burden to her.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「……あれ？
　そういえば寝巻が昨日とは違うな。
翡翠……は無理だから、琥珀さんが着替えさせてくれたのか？」
「いえ、それは秋葉さまです。
昨夜はわたしと秋葉さまが交代で志貴さまを看ていました。
　朝方になって志貴さまが落ち着かれたので、秋葉さまもお部屋にお戻りになられましたが」
「―――――秋葉が？」
　口にして、昨日の光景が頭に浮かんだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Wait, these aren’t the pajamas I wore yesterday. You couldn’t have changed me. Was it Kohaku?”
“No, that was Miss Akiha. Last night, Miss Akiha and I took turns watching over you, Master Shiki.
Toward morning, once Master Shiki’s condition had settled, Miss Akiha returned to her room.”
“Akiha did?”
As I say her name, yesterday’s scene rises in my mind.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Huh?
Come to think of it, these are different pajamas then I wore last night.
Hisui…… did Kohaku-san change my clothes?"
"No, Akiha-sama did it herself.
Last night, Akiha-sama and I took turns caring for you.
After you calmed down this morning, Akiha-sama returned to her room."
"-----Akiha did?"
As I blurt this out, I flash back to what I saw yesterday.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
―――琥珀さんの血を吸っていた秋葉。
　　　翡翠に辛くあたっていた秋葉。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Akiha drinking Kohaku’s blood.
Akiha treating Hisui harshly.
entries.mirrorMoon: ---Akiha, who was sucking Kohaku-san's blood.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま……？」
　翡翠が声をかけてくる。
　知らず、俺の顔は強張っていたのかもしれない。
「いや―――なんでもない。
……そっか、秋葉が看ててくれたのか」
「はい。
一時間ごとに志貴さまのお部屋の前にやってきて、志貴さまの看病をなさってくださいました。
　……その、志貴さまのお体に触れるような事は不得手ですので、秋葉さまが来てくれて助かりました」
「―――――――」
　……なんて馬鹿。
　秋葉がそんなに心配していてくれたのに、俺はなんて事を思ってたんだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki…?”
Hisui calls to me.
Perhaps my face tightened without my noticing.
“No—it’s nothing. So Akiha looked after me.”
“Yes. Every hour she came to Master Shiki’s door, Master Shiki, and helped nurse you.
I am unaccustomed to touching Master Shiki’s body, so I was grateful Miss Akiha came.”
“…”
What an idiot I am.
Akiha was that worried about me, and what was I thinking of her?
entries.mirrorMoon:
Akiha, who was yelling at Hisui.

"Shiki-sama……?"
I vaguely hear Hisui's voice.
Maybe I showed my tension on my face.
"Um---it's nothing…… I see, Akiha took care of me, huh."
"Yes.
She would come every hour and take care of you.
…… Um, since I was unable to contact you physically, it was very fortunate that Akiha-sama came."
"-------"
…… How stupid of me.
Akiha was so worried about me, but what did I think about her?
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「……ありがとう翡翠。
秋葉にもお礼を言っておいてくれ」
「はい。
それでは志貴さま、朝食をお持ちいたしますので、お待ちください」
　翡翠が退室して、今度こそ体を起こした。
　壁に背を預けて、はあ、と大きく深呼吸をする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Thank you, Hisui. Please thank Akiha for me too.”
“Of course, Master Shiki. I will bring your breakfast now, so please wait here.”
After Hisui leaves, I finally manage to sit up.
I brace my back against the wall and draw one long, deep breath.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Thanks, Hisui.
Please tell Akiha thanks, too."
"Yes.
Well then, Shiki-sama, I will bring you breakfast, so please wait a moment."
Hisui leaves the room and I lift myself up.
Leaning my back against the wall, I take a deep breath.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
……体の具合はそれなりに良くなっているし、外はこんなにもいい天気だ。
　加えて、一晩中秋葉と翡翠が看ていてくれた事は純粋に嬉しい。
　だっていうのに、気分は曇ったままで晴れ渡らない。
「……昨日から琥珀さんに会ってないな」
　顔を会わせれば、きっと今までのように話せなくて困るって解ってる。
　それでも、今は琥珀さんの顔が見たかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
My body is recovering, and the weather is beautiful.
The knowledge that Akiha and Hisui watched over me all night makes me genuinely happy.
Yet the clouds inside me refuse to clear.
“I haven’t seen Kohaku since yesterday.”
I know that if we met, I would no longer be able to speak to her as I once did.
Even so, I want to see her face.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… My body has gotten a little better and the weather outside is excellent.
To add to that, I am truly happy that Hisui and Akiha took care of me last night.
Still, I feel down.
"…… I haven't seen Kohaku-san since yesterday."
I know that if I see her face, I won't be able to talk to her normally.
But still, I just want to see her face.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
正午を過ぎて、太陽もその頂点を下り始めた。
　体の調子は相変わらずで、良くなる事はないかわりに悪くなる事もない。
　半端に不自由な体を持て余しながら、窓の外の空を眺める。
「―――――――」
　こうして何も考えないようにしても、頭にうかぶのは一人だけ。
　シキという殺人鬼をどうにかしなくちゃいけないっていうのに、俺は琥珀さんの事ばかりを考えてしまっている―――
entries.maoEnglish:
Noon passes, and the sun begins its descent.
My condition remains unchanged—neither improving nor worsening.
Trapped in a body too weak to use yet not weak enough to ignore, I stare out at the sky.
“…”
No matter how hard I try to empty my mind, only one person appears there.
I should be worrying about the murderer SHIKI, yet I can think of nothing but Kohaku―――
entries.mirrorMoon:
It passes noon and the sun starts its dip from the top of the sky.
My condition does not improve, but it doesn't get worse either.
Not knowing what to do, I just stare out the window.
"-------"
Even though I try not to think, one person pops into my mind.
I know the killer SHIKI has to be dealt with, but I'm thinking of Kohaku-san---
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
硬いノック音がした。
「兄さん。
私ですけど、中に入っていいですか？」
―――声は秋葉のものだ。
　別に秋葉を避ける事はない。
　……確かに昨日の事は気になる。
　けど琥珀さんが嫌がっていた訳ではなさそうだったし、アレは秋葉にとって必要な事なのかもしれない。
　遠野という血族は感応者と呼ばれる者を必要としている。
　……秋葉は親父のように琥珀さんを苦しめている訳ではないんだから、今は、あの出来事は自分の胸の中にしまっておくべきだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
A hard knock strikes the door.
“Brother, it’s me. May I come in?”
―――Akiha’s voice.
There is no reason to avoid her.
Yesterday certainly troubles me.
But Kohaku did not seem unwilling, and perhaps it was something Akiha needed.
The Tohno bloodline requires people called resonators.
Akiha is not tormenting Kohaku as Father did, so for now I should keep what I saw to myself.
entries.mirrorMoon:
A solid knock at the door.
"Nii-san.
It is me, can I come in?"
---Akiha's voice.
I don't really have any reason to avoid her.
…… Obviously I'm concerned about yesterday.
But, it didn't look like she hated Kohaku-san, and it might be something she has to do.
Those of the Tohno blood need Synchronizers.
…… Akiha isn't hurting her like my old man did, so I should keep quiet about it for now.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「俺に断る必要なんかないだろ。
立ってないで早く入れよ」
「はい。
失礼します、兄さん」
　部屋に入ってくる秋葉。
「秋葉、学校は？
　まだ一時になったばかりだろ」
「そんなものは休みました。
兄さんが苦しんでいる時に外になんか出ていられないでしょ？」
　秋葉は笑顔のまま、ベッドまで近寄ってくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You don’t need my permission. Don’t stand out there—come in.”
“Very well. Excuse me, Brother.”
Akiha enters.
“Akiha, what about school? It’s barely one.”
“I stayed home. You cannot expect me to go out while you’re suffering.”
Still smiling, Akiha approaches the bed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"You don't need to ask me.
Come on in."
"Yes, excuse me, Nii-san."
Akiha enters my room.
"Akiha, what about school?
It's not even one o'clock, right?"
"I took off today.
If you are suffering, I should not leave, right?"
With a smile, Akiha comes over to my bed.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「それじゃ体温を測るから、これを口にくわえて。
終わったらシーツを替えるけど、少しぐらいなら立っていられるでしょ？」
　はい、と秋葉は体温計を差し出してくる。
　……どうやら翡翠のかわりに軽い診察をしにきたらしい。
entries.maoEnglish:
“First I’ll take your temperature, so put this in your mouth. After that I’ll change the sheets; you can stand for a minute or two, can’t you?”
She holds out the thermometer.
Apparently she has come to give me a simple examination in Hisui’s place.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I will take your temperature, so please put this in your mouth.
After that, we need to change your sheets, so can you get up for a just a moment?"
She sticks the thermometer in my mouth.
…… It looks like she came in place of Hisui.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
秋葉は体温を測った後、シーツを替えたり新しい寝巻を用意したりとテキパキと動いていた。
　……そういえば琥珀さんも無駄のない行動をする人だったけど、秋葉のように素早い、という印象はなかった。
　琥珀さん自体はいつも穏やかだけど、やるべき事を順序だてているから無駄がないんだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
Once she has taken my temperature, Akiha moves briskly through changing the sheets and laying out clean pajamas.
Kohaku is efficient too, but never gives an impression of speed as Akiha does.
Kohaku herself is always serene; perhaps she wastes no motion because she plans each task before beginning.
entries.mirrorMoon:
After checking my temperature, she smartly changes my sheets and gets out a fresh set of pajamas.
…… Come to think of it, Kohaku-san was efficient too, but she didn't have Akiha's air of swiftness.
Even though Kohaku-san is relaxed normally, she probably has things ordered so there's nothing unnecessary done.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「兄さん、終わったから横になっていいですよ」
　立ったついでに、ちらりと中庭を見てみた。
「―――――――ぁ」
　琥珀さんが、ホウキをざっざっと動かして落ち葉を集めている。
　ここからなら声をかけられるし、挨拶をしてみようか―――
「兄さん。
新しいシーツに替え終わったんですけど」
「え……？
　あ、そうか。
ごめん、ぼけっとしてた」
　だるい手足を動かしてベッドに横になる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’m finished, Brother, so you can lie down now.”
Since I am already standing, I glance into the courtyard.
“Ah…”
Kohaku is there, sweeping fallen leaves into a pile.
I could call to her from here and say hello―――
“Brother. I said the fresh sheets are ready.”
“Hm? Oh, right. Sorry, I was staring into space.”
I drag my sluggish limbs back onto the bed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"All finished.
Nii-san, please lay down."
Still standing, I steal a glance out the window.
"-------Ah."
Kohaku-san is gathering the fallen leaves with her broom in the garden.
I could probably say hi from here so---
"Nii-san, I have finished putting new sheets on your bed."
"Eh……?
Ah, sorry.
I spaced out a little."
I sluggishly lie back down on my bed.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
秋葉は椅子に腰をかけると、慣れない手つきでリンゴの皮むきを始めていた。
　難しい顔つきでナイフを扱うのだが、時折勢いあまってベッドにナイフが突き刺さりそうになる。
　……花嫁修行だろうか。
　そういう危ない事は、できれば台所でやってほしい。
entries.maoEnglish:
Akiha sits in a chair and begins peeling an apple with hands plainly new to the task.
She scowls in concentration as she wields the knife, which occasionally comes perilously close to burying itself in the bed.
Is this some kind of bridal training?
I would prefer her to practice dangerous arts like that in the kitchen.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Sitting down on a chair, she starts to peel an apple rather clumsily.
With an intense look on her face, she intently works the knife, but sometimes, she uses too much strength and the knife almost flies toward my bed.
…… Is she practicing to be a good housewife?
I wish she would do such dangerous things in the kitchen.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「……秋葉。
あんまり無理しなくていいぞ」
　控えめに、慣れない事はするなと言ってみた。
「……………」
　秋葉は不満そうな顔で、しぶしぶとナイフとリンゴを床に置いた。
　持ってきた盆には皿やフォークがあった所を見ると、やっぱり慣れない事をするつもりだったらしい。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…Akiha, you don’t have to try so hard.”
I gently suggest she not force herself to do something she isn’t used to.
“…”
Akiha frowns, then reluctantly sets both apple and knife on the floor.
Judging by the plate and fork on her tray, she really had intended to attempt the whole performance.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Akiha, you don't have to force yourself."
Indirectly, I tell her not to do things she's not good at.
"………………"
Akiha, a little dissatisfied, puts down the apple and the knife on the floor.
Seeing her with the plate and fork, it's obvious that she was going to do something she's not good at.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「………………く」
　結果はどうあれ、秋葉の気持ちは嬉しい。
　というか、妙におかしくてつい笑ってしまった。
「……むっ。
何がおかしいんですか兄さん。
私、兄さんを笑わせるような事はしていないでしょう」
「いや、昔と変わらないなって。
子供の頃に一度、俺が風邪を引いた時があったじゃないか。
その時も不器用な看病をしてたなあって」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Pfft…”
Whatever the result, her thoughtfulness makes me happy.
More than that, the sight is so strangely funny that I cannot help laughing.
“Hmph. What is so amusing, Brother? I haven’t done anything that should make you laugh.”
“No, I was thinking you haven’t changed. Remember when I caught a cold as a child? Your nursing was just as clumsy then.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……………………"
Despite the result, I'm happy for Akiha's care.
But it's funny, so I start to laugh.
"…… Hey.
What is so funny, Nii-san?
I did not do anything to make you laugh."
"I was just thinking that this is just like back then.
When I was sick as a child, you used to clumsily take care of me back then, too."
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
……ああ、思い出した。
　まだ俺が養子として暮らしていた頃の話だ。
　親父の目を盗んで秋葉と遊んでいた時、いきなり熱をだしてダウンしてしまった。
　俺はそのまま離れの和室で養生していたんだけど、秋葉は屋敷を抜け出して看病に来た事があった。
entries.maoEnglish:
Now I remember.
It was when I still lived here as an adopted child.
I was secretly playing with Akiha behind Father’s back when a fever struck me without warning.
They put me to bed in the annex, but Akiha slipped out of the mansion to nurse me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Yeah, I remember.
When I was still living as an adopted child.
When I was playing with Akiha, I caught a fever and collapsed.
I was resting in that detached house after that, but Akiha escaped the mansion to come care for me.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「…………懐かしいな。
初めは手を握っているだけだったのに、段々と看病の真似事をし始めてさ。
　おまえ、最後には屋敷から注射器を持ち出して、空のまま俺に射とうとしてただろ」
「うっ……悔しいけど、否定できない事実ですね」
「ふざけろ。
時南さんが気がついて止めなかったら、俺はとっくにお亡くなりになってたんだからなっ」
　ちなみに時南さんは当時遠野家の専属医をしていた医者の助手だった人だ。
今ではその頃の縁で、俺の主治医をやってくれている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“That takes me back. At first you only held my hand, but then you started pretending to be a nurse.
By the end, you’d stolen a syringe from the mansion and were about to stick me with it empty.”
“I hate to admit it, but I can’t deny that.”
“You’re telling me. If Tokinan hadn’t noticed and stopped you, I’d have died years ago.”
At the time, Tokinan was assistant to the Tohno family’s private physician. That old connection is how he became my own doctor.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"………… It sure brings back memories.
At first you just held my hand, but you started to try and take care of me.
At the end, you even took some empty syringes and were going to inject me, right?"
"Uu…… I regret it now, but it's the truth I cannot take back."
"No kidding.
If Jinan-san hadn't realized it and stopped you, I probably would have died."
Incidentally, Jinan-san was the assistant of the family doctor.
After that time, he became my personal physician.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「時南先生ですか。
そういえば医者嫌いの兄さんもあの人には根負けしていましたね」
「……そりゃそうだろ。
あの人はマッドがつくほうの医者だからな。
下手に逆らうと倍返ししてくるんだぞ。
医者の倍返しがどれくらい怖いか解るか？」
　さあ、と秋葉は笑う。
　他人事だと思って、実に可愛くない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Doctor Tokinan? Come to think of it, even you eventually surrendered to him despite your hatred of doctors.”
“Of course I did. He’s the kind of doctor you put ‘mad’ in front of. Cross him, and he gives back twice what you dish out. Do you have any idea how terrifying a doctor’s payback can be?”
Akiha laughs.
Easy for her to find it funny.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Jinan-sensei?
Come to think of it, even though you didn't like doctors, you always ended up losing to him."
"…… Of course.
That person is a mad doctor.
If you disobey him, he'll pay you back twice as much.
Do you understand how scary that is?"
"Who knows?" Akiha says as she smiles.
She knows it doesn't concern her and she isn't being cute at all.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「あ、医者っていえば琥珀さんっていつ薬剤師の資格をとったんだ？
　琥珀さん、年齢的に俺たちとわりと近いだろ。
アレって年齢制限とかないの？」
「……そうですね、それに関しては少々お父様が無理をしました。
　琥珀と翡翠は正確な生年月日が解らないんです。
ですからお父様は琥珀の戸籍に少しばかり細工をして、書類上での琥珀の年齢を引き上げたそうです」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Speaking of doctors, when did Kohaku qualify as a pharmacist? She can’t be much older than us. Isn’t there some sort of age requirement?”
“Father forced the matter somewhat.
Kohaku’s and Hisui’s exact birth dates are unknown, so he altered Kohaku’s family register. He made her older on paper.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah, speaking of doctors, when did Kohaku-san get her pharmacist license?
She seems to be very close to our age, but doesn't that sort of thing have an age limit?"
"…… That is true, but it is Father's doing.
We don't know the exact date of Kohaku and Hisui's birth, so Father did a little manipulation of the documents and made her older."
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「―――――げ」
　流石金持ち。
やる事がイリーガルだ。
「けど、翡翠は兄さんと同い年だと思いますよ。
翡翠と琥珀は双子なんですから、当然琥珀も兄さんと同い年という事になりますね」
「―――――うそ」
　……同い年って、琥珀さんと俺が……？
　いや、そりゃあ確かに考えない事もなかったけど、どうしてか琥珀さんは年上のような気がしていた。
　……まあ、確かに『年上の人』っていうイメージは無かったんだけど、それでも同い年とは思えない。
　だって、それだと……琥珀さんは八歳か九歳の頃から遠野槙久に―――
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ugh.”
Rich people. Even their solutions are illegal.
“But I believe Hisui is the same age as you. Since she and Kohaku are twins, Kohaku must naturally be your age as well.”
“You’re joking.”
Kohaku and I are the same age?
I had considered that she might be close, but for some reason she always seemed older.
Not exactly an older woman, perhaps, but certainly not my age.
Because if that is true, Kohaku was only eight or nine when Makihisa Tohno began―――
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------Whoa."
As expected of a rich man, his methods are a bit illegal.
"But, I think that Hisui is about your age.
Kohaku and Hisui are twins, so that would naturally make her around your age, right?"
"-----No way."
…… Kohaku-san and I, the same age……?
Well, it's not like I really gave it much thought, but I always felt she was older.
…… Well, she certainly doesn't act older, but I never thought of her as the same age.
Because, if that's true…… Then from when Kohaku-san was eight or nine, Tohno Makihisa did---
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
ぎしりと。
　体にヒビが入ったような、錯覚。
entries.maoEnglish:
A creak runs through me.
The illusion of a crack splitting my body.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Crack.
I imagine a crack in my body.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「兄さん……？
　どうしました、体の具合が悪いんですか……？」
「―――いや、なんでもない。
俺の体なんて、別に、どうでもいい」
　所詮こんなものは、瞬間的な痛みにすぎない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Brother? Are you feeling worse?”
“No. It’s nothing; what happens to my body doesn’t matter.”
This is only a moment’s pain.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Nii-san……?
What is wrong, are you feeling alright……?"
"---Nah, it's nothing.
No need to worry."
After all, this is just a brief pain.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「どうでもいい事はないでしょう。
そんなに汗をかいて、今にも倒れそうじゃないですか……！」
「――――そんなの―――――琥珀さんに、比べれば――――」
「――――――――――」
　比べれば、いくらでも耐えられる痛みだ。
　俺はやっぱり琥珀さんに会いたい。
　会って何を言っていいか解らないけど、会って、何かをしなくちゃいけない。
　八年前の約束だってまだ果たしていないんだ。
　俺は、こんな所でいつまでも休んでいる訳にはいかな―――
entries.maoEnglish:
“Of course it matters. You’re drenched in sweat and look ready to collapse!”
“This is nothing―――――compared with Kohaku――――”
“…”
Compared with her, I could endure any pain.
I still want to see Kohaku.
I do not know what I could say to her, but I have to see her and do something.
I have not even fulfilled the promise we made eight years ago.
I cannot keep lying here forever—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"There is a need to worry.
Sweating like that, you seem like you will collapse any moment now……!"
"----But-----compared to Kohaku-san-----"
"----------"
Compared to that, this pain is nothing.
I really want to see Kohaku-san after all.
I don't know what I will say after I meet her, but I have to see her and do something.
I still haven't fulfilled my promise from eight years ago.
This isn't the time for me to be lazing around here---
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
―――と。
　突然、眩暈は止まってくれた。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――And then.
Without warning, the vertigo stops.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---And just like that.
Suddenly, my dizziness comes to a complete stop.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「どう？
　少しは落ち着きました？」
　額に秋葉の手の平が置かれている。
　冷たい指。
　その冷たい感触が、俺の眩暈を止めてくれたらしい。
entries.maoEnglish:
“How is that? Do you feel calmer?”
Akiha’s palm rests against my forehead.
Her fingers are cold.
That cool touch seems to have dispelled the dizziness.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"How is that?
Have you calmed down?"
Akiha is placing her palm on my forehead.
Her cool fingers.
It seems the cool sensation has doused away my dizziness like soothing water.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「―――兄さん。
体の具合はどうですか？」
「？」
　どうって、そんなのはさっきも言ったけど。
　秋葉の目は真剣だ。
……何か、もっと違う事を尋ねてきているような、そんな視線。
「……いいわ。
私の方で調べてみるから、少しじっとしていて」
　言って、秋葉は額に当てた手の平を下にずらした。
　ペタペタと、寝巻の上から手の平を当ててくる。
「……特別おかしな所はないようね。
なのに体温が一定しないのは私がまだ慣れていないせいなのかな……」
　秋葉はそう呟いて手の平を離した。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――Brother. How are you feeling?”
“Hm?”
I told her how I felt a moment ago.
Akiha’s eyes are grave. It is as though her real question lies somewhere else entirely.
“Never mind—I’ll find out for myself. Hold still a moment.”
Akiha slides the hand from my forehead downward.
Her palm pats me here and there through my nightshirt.
“Nothing seems especially wrong… Yet perhaps your temperature won’t stay steady because I’m still not used to this…”
Akiha murmurs, then removes her hand.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Nii-san.
How are you feeling?"
"?"
Didn't I already tell her?
Her eyes are dead serious.
…… Her gaze seems to be asking something different.
"…… Fine, I will just have to investigate myself."
After saying this, she lowers her hand from my forehead.
Her palm smoothly glides down to the top of my shirt.
"…… It doesn't seem like there is anything wrong in particular.
But your fluctuating temperature might be due to me simply not being used to it."
Murmuring to herself, she draws back her hand.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「兄さんはどちらかというと健康な体をしていますよね。
なのにこうして、突発的に貧血を起こしてしまうのはおかしいと思わない？」
「……ああ。
そりゃあ医者からさんざん言われた事だよ。
でも、それがどうしたっていうんだ」
「当然ですね。
医学では兄さんの貧血の原因はわからない。
　……ねえ兄さん。
その理由を、知りたくはありませんか？」
「え――――――？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“You’re generally quite healthy, aren’t you? Don’t you find it strange that you should suddenly collapse from anemia like this?”
“Yeah… Every doctor I’ve seen has told me the same thing. So what?”
“Naturally. Medicine can’t explain what causes your anemia.
Tell me, Brother… wouldn’t you like to know the reason?”
“What…?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Nii-san, you have a normally healthy body, but you have anemia like this very often.
Do you ever think that is strange?"
"…… Yeah, well, the doctor told me that many times, but what about it?"
"Of course.
Doctors cannot know the reason for your anemia.
…… Hey, Nii-san, do you want to know the reason for it?"
"Eh-----?"
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
どくん、と心臓が躍動した。
　俺が長年知ろうとして知りえなかった事。
　この不安定な自分の体。
　その原因を秋葉が知っている……？
entries.maoEnglish:
My heart gives a violent thud.
The answer I have sought for years and never found.
The reason this body of mine is so unstable.
Does Akiha know…?
entries.mirrorMoon:
My heart skips a beat.
What I haven't known for all these years.
This unstable body of mine.
Akiha knows……?
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「冗談……じゃなさそうだな」
「ええ。
兄さんが知りたい、というのでしたら教えてさしあげます。
これは元々、私の肉親が犯した罪です。
ですから兄さんには知る権利があるわ」
　秋葉の言葉にはどこか―――危ういものを感じる。
　けれどそこまで言われて、首を横にふる事はできなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“This isn’t a joke, is it?”
“No. If you wish to know, I’ll tell you. This began with a crime committed by one of my own blood. You have every right to hear the truth.”
Something about Akiha’s words feels dangerous.
But after hearing all that, I cannot bring myself to say no.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"It…… doesn't seem like you're joking."
"Right.
If you want to know, then I will tell you.
It is due to the sins of my family, so you have a right to know."
For some reason---her words seem very dangerous.
But I can't shake my head in denial after all this.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「……知りたい。
知っているのなら教えてくれ、秋葉」
「解りました、それでは教えてさしあげますね。
　といっても、だいたいの事は兄さんだって知っている事よ。
兄さんは八年前の事故からそうなってしまったでしょう？
　なら、原因は全てそこにあるのは当然の事だもの」
「八年前―――つまり、俺がシキに殺されかけたっていう事？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“I want to know. If you know the truth, tell me, Akiha.”
“Very well.
Though you already know most of it yourself. Your body became this way after the accident eight years ago, didn’t it? The cause must lie there.”
“Eight years ago―――in other words, when SHIKI nearly killed me?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I want to know.
Please tell me, Akiha."
"I understand.
Then, I will tell you.
I say that, but you already know most of it.
After that accident eight years ago, you became this way, right?
So that has to be the root of all this."
"Eight years ago---you mean, when I was almost killed by SHIKI?"
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「そうよ。
その時に兄さんは、シキに命の大半を奪われてしまったんです。
　シキはお父様に処断された後、地下牢で生き延びていたのでしょう？
　なら、シキは無くしてしまった自分の命の代わりに、兄さんの命を使って存在しているのよ。
　だから兄さんは、自分の命で自分の体を補う事ができず、結果として今みたいに死に直面してしまう。
　ようするにシキが生きているかぎり、兄さんはずっとそのままなんです。
もう、元には戻れない」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Yes. That was when SHIKI stole most of your life.
He survived in the dungeon after Father passed judgment on him, didn’t he? He has been sustaining his existence with your life in place of the life he lost.
That leaves you without enough life to sustain your own body, which is why you keep coming so close to death.
In short, as long as SHIKI lives, nothing will change. You can never return to the way you were.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Exactly.
At that time, SHIKI stole the majority of your life.
After Father carried out sentence on SHIKI, he was kept alive in the basement, right?
So SHIKI is using your life in place of the life he lost to stay alive.
That's why, Nii-san.
That's why you cannot move around freely with your own life.
And as a result, you are always teetering on the brink of death.
So as long as SHIKI is alive, you will always be like this.
You can never go back to the way you were before."
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「なっ……死に直面してるって、そんな事ないだろ。
こんなのはただの―――」
　ただの貧血、のハズはない。
　自分の体の自由がきかず、頻繁に意識を失うなんてものは貧血とは呼べない。
　なら、秋葉の言うとおり。
　これは死に至る過程と大差はない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“C-close to death? That can’t be right—this is just―――”
But it cannot be just anemia.
Losing control of my body and blacking out so often cannot be called anemia.
Then Akiha is right.
This is little different from the process of dying.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Wha…… on the edge of death?
That's ridiculous, it's just---"
It can't be just anemia.
Not being able to move freely and losing consciousness this frequently can't be called anemia.
So it's just like she says.
There's not much difference between this and drifting into death.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「……なんで？
　それでも今までやってこれたじゃないか。
八年間もこうしていられたんだから、これからだって―――」
「違うわ。
今まではシキが地下牢に閉じ込められていたから、兄さんはなんとかやってこれただけよ。
　けどシキは外に出て、本来兄さんが自分に使うべき命を使って、好きなように徘徊している。
　その分の負荷が全て兄さんだけにやってきているんだから、兄さんはもう以前のように生活はできない」
entries.maoEnglish:
“But why? I’ve managed all this time. I’ve lived this way for eight years, so surely I can keep―――”
“No. You survived until now only because SHIKI was confined underground.
But he is free now, wandering wherever he pleases and spending the life that should be sustaining you.
That entire burden is falling on your body, so you cannot go on living as you did before.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Why?
But I made it this far.
If I lived like this for eight years, then I can surely---"
"No.
Until now, SHIKI was locked away so you were able to live barely.
But now SHIKI is going outside and is using your life to do as he pleases.
The burden for whatever he does is on you, so you will not be able to live like before."
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「―――――――」
　どくん、という鼓動。
　秋葉の言葉は遠慮がない。
　それが真実であるが故に、よけい鋭い刃になって心臓に突き刺さる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――――――”
My heart thuds.
Akiha shows no mercy with her words.
Because they are true, they become an even sharper blade, driven straight into my heart.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-------"
My pulse surges.
Her words hold nothing back.
Since they are the truth, they pierce my heart like a sword even more.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「兄さん。
恨むのでしたらシキと、シキを外に出した誰かを恨んで。
　たとえシキが生きていても、シキが大人しくしているままだったら兄さんはこんな体にはならなかったんだから」
　言って、ぎり、と秋葉は唇を噛んだ。
　……俺の命を奪っているというシキに対する怒りなのか、唇に血が滲むほど強く。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Brother. If you must hate someone, hate SHIKI—and whoever let him out.
Even with SHIKI alive, you would never have come to this if he had remained quietly imprisoned.”
Akiha bites hard into her lip.
Perhaps she is furious with SHIKI for stealing my life, but whatever the reason, she bites down hard enough to draw blood.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Nii-san.
If you want to hate someone, hate SHIKI or the one who set him free.
Because even if he is alive, if SHIKI was quiet, this would have never happened to you."
She bites her lip as she says this.
…… Is she that angry at SHIKI for stealing my life?
She bites so hard that blood flows from her lips.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「…………秋葉」
　秋葉の視線は俺には向いていない。
　見えるはずのない敵を睨むように、秋葉は虚空を凝視している。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――Akiha.”
She is not looking at me.
She stares into empty space as though glaring at an enemy no one can see.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"………… Akiha."
But she isn't looking at me.
She is staring into emptiness as if staring at an enemy.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「けれど安心して。
どんな事をしても、兄さんは私が守ってさしあげます。
……兄さんがいつも笑顔でいられるよう、私が―――」
―――シキを殺す、というのか。
　……親父の手記を思い出す。
　遠野家の当主は外れてしまったモノを処罰しなくてはいけない、という記述。
entries.maoEnglish:
“But don’t be afraid. Whatever it takes, I will protect you so that you can always smile. I will―――”
―――Is she saying she will kill SHIKI?
I remember Father’s journal.
The passage saying that the head of the Tohno family must punish whatever has strayed beyond the bounds.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"But rest assured.
I will do anything to protect you, Nii-san……
So you can always smile, I---"
---will kill SHIKI, you want to say?
…… I remember my old man's journal.
The responsibility of the head of the Tohno household is to exterminate all those who stray from a human existence.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「―――――――あ」
　いつかの夜。
　俺に抱きついて、必死に涙を堪えていた秋葉。
　あの時、秋葉は確かに言っていた。
　自分の手で兄を殺さなくてはいけないのか、と。
　……秋葉は、俺に打ち明ける事もできず、泣いていたのか―――
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――――――Ah.”
That night.
Akiha had clung to me.
She had fought desperately to hold back her tears.
She had said it clearly then: would she have to kill her own brother with her own hands?
Had she been crying because she could tell no one—not even me―――
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-------Ah."
That one night.
Akiha was hugging me, desperately fighting back her tears.
That time, I know she said those words.
She said she didn't want to kill her brother with her own hands.
…… She was crying, not being able to tell me that---
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「……いい。
秋葉が責任を感じる必要なんて、ない」
「いいえ……私は遠野家の当主です。
ですから遠野の者が犯した罪は、私が必ず―――」
「……ばか。
そう辛そうな顔するなよ秋葉。
大丈夫、こんなのは以前にもあったんだ。
シキが何をしようと、このぐらいなら明日には治ってる。
　だから、おまえは何も心配するな」
entries.maoEnglish:
“You don’t have to. None of this is yours to answer for, Akiha.”
“No—I am the head of the Tohno family. Any crime committed by a Tohno is mine to―――”
“Idiot. Don’t look so miserable, Akiha—it’s all right. This has happened before. Whatever SHIKI may be doing, something this minor will clear up by tomorrow.
So stop worrying.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… It's fine.
You don't have to feel any responsibility."
"No…… I am the head of the Tohno family.
So all the crimes any member of the Tohno house has committed, I will definitely---"
"…… Hey, you don't have to make such a painful face.
It's okay, this has happened before.
Whatever SHIKI does, I'll recover in a matter of days.
So you don't have to worry."
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「兄さん、だけどそれでは繰り返すだけじゃないですか。
私は兄さんにそんな、いつ死んでしまうか解らない体でいてほしくなんかない……！
　だから、そのために私は―――」
「何も心配するなって言ってるだろ。
　シキの事は―――俺がなんとかするから。
秋葉は何もしなくていいんだ」
「……………兄、さん」
entries.maoEnglish:
“But then it will only happen again! I don’t want you trapped in a body that might die at any moment…!
That’s why I have to―――”
“I told you not to worry.
As for SHIKI―――I’ll deal with him myself. You don’t have to do anything, Akiha.”
“―――――Brother.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Nii-san, you are just repeating yourself.
I cannot bear you to be like this, not even knowing if you may die any minute……!
So, I---"
"I told you not to worry.
SHIKI is---my responsibility.
You don't have to do anything."
"……………… Nii, san."
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
……ああ。
　秋葉に兄殺しなんかさせられない。
　それにこれは俺とシキの問題だ。
　遠野の血が忌まわしいもので、八年前からそれに踊らされていたのなら。
　それなら全て―――自分自身の手で、八年前の決着をつけてやる。
　琥珀さんも秋葉も、これ以上―――遠野の血なんかで、苦しませてたまるものか。
entries.maoEnglish:
Yes.
I cannot make Akiha kill her own brother.
Besides, this is between SHIKI and me.
If the Tohno blood is truly accursed—if it has toyed with all of us since that day eight years ago—then I will settle everything with my own hands.
I will bring those eight years to an end.
I will not let that blood torment Kohaku or Akiha any longer.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Yeah.
Akiha doesn't have to kill her brother.
This is just between me and him.
If the Tohno blood is cursed and I've been forced into this ridiculous dance for eight years,
then I---with my own hands, will end all of this that started eight years ago.
Neither Kohaku-san nor Akiha, can be---should suffer any longer from that blood.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「――――兄さん」
　安心したのか、秋葉はようやく肩の力を抜いてくれた。
「……よかった。
兄さんは、やっぱり私の兄さんなんですね。
八年前のあの時と同じ、私の事だけを守ってくれる」
　秋葉は濡れた瞳で、まっすぐにこちらを見つめてくる。
　…………なんていうか。
　すごく、いい雰囲気になりつつ、ある。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――Brother.”
At last, perhaps reassured, Akiha lets the tension leave her shoulders.
“I’m so glad. You really are still my brother. You’re the same brother who protected only me eight years ago.”
Her tear-filled eyes gaze straight at me.
How should I put this?
The mood between us is becoming awfully intimate.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----Nii-san."
Has she relaxed?
She finally eases her shoulders.
"…… Thank goodness.
You are definitely my Nii-san.
Just like eight years ago, you only protect me."
Her brimming eyes look directly at me.
………… How do you say this?
The atmosphere has become incredibly intimate.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
――――、と。
　そんな雰囲気を台無しにするように、ぐー、と秋葉のおなかが鳴った。
「――――――――」
「……………………」
　……そういえば、秋葉が昨夜から寝ずに俺の看病をしていてくれたんだっけ。
　さっきの思いつめた表情といい、俺が倒れたのは自分のせいだって思いこんで、食事もとっていないのかもしれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――And then.
As if determined to ruin the moment, Akiha’s stomach gives a long, loud growl.
“――――――――”
“…”
Come to think of it, Akiha has stayed beside me since last night without sleeping.
Judging by that tormented expression earlier, she may have convinced herself my collapse was her fault and gone without eating as well.
entries.mirrorMoon:
-----, and.
As if to spoil this great mood, Akiha's stomach lets out a growl.
"--------"
"………………………"
…… Come to think of it, Akiha stayed up all night watching over me.
She must have been so worried over me that she didn't eat.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「そういえば、おなか減ったな」
　と、とりあえずフォローをいれてみる。
「……もう。
安心したら気が抜けてしまいました」
　秋葉は恥ずかしそうに弁明する。
　ま、こっちはそれで助けられたかもしれない。
　あのままだったら、雰囲気に流されて何をしていたか解らないし。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You know, I’m getting hungry too.”
It is the best rescue attempt I can manage.
“Oh, honestly… I suppose the relief made me lose my composure.”
Akiha offers the excuse with an embarrassed look.
Maybe her stomach has rescued me as well.
If things had gone on like that, who knows what the mood might have swept me into.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I think I'm getting hungry."
I try to follow her up.
"…… Geez.
I was so relaxed I let down my guard."
Akiha gives an embarrassed excuse.
Well, maybe it helped me out.
I don't know what would have flowed from that mood.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「秋葉、俺はしばらく大丈夫だから、秋葉も少しは休んでくれないか。
昨日の夜、ずっと看ててくれたんだろ？」
「あ――――うん。
大した事はできなくて、兄さんを助ける事はできなかったけど、私に出来る事はそれぐらいだけですから」
「それで十分だって。
翡翠にその事を聞いて、純粋に嬉しかった。
いい妹をもったなってさ」
「……はい。
それじゃ少しだけ休みますね。
夕食後にまた来ますから、兄さんもゆっくり休んでください」
　椅子から立ちあがって秋葉は部屋を出ていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Akiha, I’ll be all right for a while, so will you get some rest too? You stayed with me all night, didn’t you?”
“Ah――――yes. I couldn’t do much or make you better, but staying with you was at least something I could do.”
“That was more than enough. When Hisui told me, I was honestly happy. I thought I was lucky to have such a good sister.”
“Thank you. Then I’ll rest for a little while. I’ll come back after dinner, so please get some proper sleep yourself.”
Akiha rises from the chair and leaves the room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Akiha, I'm fine right now, so please rest.
You took care of me all night, right?"
"Ah----yes.
It was really nothing at all.
I could not help you, and I only did the best that I could."
"That's enough.
I heard it all from Hisui.
I really am happy to have such a great little sister."
"…… Yes.
Then I suppose I will rest a little bit.
I will come here again after dinner, so please rest and relax."
Getting up from the chair, Akiha leaves the room.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
軽やかなノック音がして扉が開く。
「お待たせしましたー。
志貴さん、ご夕食の時間ですよー」
「―――――――え？」
　意外な事に、やってきたのは琥珀さんだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
A brisk knock sounds, and the door opens.
“Sorry to keep you waiting! It’s dinnertime, Master Shiki!”
“―――――――What?”
To my astonishment, it is Kohaku who comes in.
entries.mirrorMoon:
A light knock and the door opens.
"Thanks for waiting.
Shiki-san, time for dinner."
"--------Eh?"
Kohaku-san's arrival takes me completely by surprise.
