entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「あれ、琥珀さん……？」
「はい？」
　と琥珀さんは首をかしげる。
「だって、秋葉はしばらく琥珀さんを近寄せないって言ってたのに」
　あんまりに不意打ちだったせいか、思っている事が口に出てしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Kohaku…?”
“Yes?”
She cocks her head.
“But Akiha said she wasn’t going to let you near me for a while.”
Her arrival catches me so completely off guard that the thought slips straight out of my mouth.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Huh?
Kohaku-san……?"
"Yes?"
She tilts her head.
"I thought Akiha said she wouldn't let you near me."
Still off-kilter with surprise, I blurt out what I was thinking.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「はい、わたしもそう仰せつかっていますよ。
けどさすがに点滴だけは秋葉さまにも翡翠ちゃんにも出来ないですから。
　志貴さん、ごはんを食べ終わったらお注射ですからねー」
　琥珀さんはいつも通りの笑顔でそう言って、ガラガラと荷台のようなものを部屋に入れて、ぱたんと扉を閉めた。
　……琥珀さんの持ってきた荷台の一番上には夕食。
下の台には注射器と点滴の準備が整っていたりする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Yes, I received the same instructions. But neither Miss Akiha nor Hisui can administer an IV.
Once you’ve finished eating, Master Shiki, it will be time for your injection.”
With her usual smile, Kohaku wheels a service cart into the room and clicks the door shut.
Dinner occupies the top shelf. Below it wait a syringe and everything needed for the IV.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yes, I was ordered the same thing, but Akiha-sama and Hisui-chan do not know how to do an IV.
Shiki-san, after dinner, you'll have to get a shot, you know."
With her usual smile, she wheels in a cart and shuts the door.
…… On top of the cart there is food.
On the lower shelf, there is a syringe and everything needed for an IV.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「あの、琥珀さん」
「えーと、まずはご夕食ですね」
　どうぞ、と食事をトレイに乗せて差し出してくる。
　琥珀さんの笑顔は、満ち足りている。
　……それを無くす事なんて、どうしてできるだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Um, Kohaku.”
“Um, first things first: dinner.”
With a “Here you are,” she sets the meal on a tray and offers it to me.
Kohaku wears a deeply contented smile.
How could I possibly take that away from her?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Uh, Kohaku-san?"
"Ummm, first is dinner, right?"
Here you go, she says as she presents the meal on a platter.
Kohaku-san's smile is full of contentment.
…… How could I destroy it?
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
―――今まで通りに接してあげてください。
　翡翠の言葉が思い出される。
　俺だって、琥珀さんにはいつも笑っていてほしい。
　こんなふうに、幸せそうに笑っていてほしいんだ。
　それを―――壊すことなんて、できない。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Treat her exactly as you always have.
Hisui’s words come back to me.
I want Kohaku to keep smiling.
To smile as happily as she does now.
I cannot destroy that―――I just cannot.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Please act like before.
I remember Hisui's words.
Even I want her to keep smiling like this.
I want to see her smile happily, just like this.
I---I can't destroy that.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「……それじゃ、いただきます」
「はい。
よく噛んで食べてくださいね」
　琥珀さんから目を逸らして、ただ箸を動かした。
　……すぐ隣には琥珀さんの笑顔がある。
　それが無性に悲しくて、正視する事ができなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“All right, then—thank you for the meal.”
“Of course. Be sure to chew properly.”
I turn away from Kohaku and move my chopsticks mechanically.
Kohaku’s smile is right beside me.
It makes me so unbearably sad that I cannot bring myself to face her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Well, I'll dig in."
"Yes.
Please chew everything well."
Lowering my eyes, I pick up my chopsticks.
…… Kohaku-san stands nearby with that smile.
It's all so sad, I just can't look at her.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
かちゃかちゃと、食器の音だけが響く。
　隣で幸せそうに笑顔でいる彼女を見ていると、他の誰でもない自分を、殺したくなってくる。
　……どうして悲しいんだろう、俺は。
　すぐ近くに琥珀さんがいる。
　昨日から会いたかった人が傍にいるんだから、悲しい事なんて何も無いはずだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
Only the clatter of dishes fills the room.
Seeing her sit beside me with that happy smile makes me want to kill myself.
Why am I so sad?
Kohaku is right here.
With the person I have wanted to see since yesterday at my side, I should have nothing to be sad about.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Clink.
Clank.
The sound of my utensils echo through the room.
Seeing her so close to me and smiling makes me want to kill myself.
…… Why am I so sad?
Kohaku-san is right here.
The one I wanted to meet since yesterday is here, so there can't be any reason to be sad.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
―――悲しい事は簡単に目に付くし、
　　　倖せは、難しすぎて解らない。
　例えばそれは、
　幼いころからずっと屋敷に閉じ込められていた少女だったり。
　それでも去り際に、遠野志貴にリボンを渡してくれた彼女だったり。
　……何も知らずに。
琥珀さんに、楽しかった屋敷の生活を語っていた俺だったり。
　……そんな事が、痛かった。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Sorrow is easy to notice,
but happiness is too hard to understand.
For example,
a girl who had been shut inside the mansion since childhood.
The girl who, even so, gave Shiki Tohno a ribbon when he left.
And me, knowing nothing. Telling Kohaku how happy my life in the mansion had been.
That was what hurt.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Sadness is easy to see,
happiness is difficult to understand.
For example,
a girl who was locked away in the mansion since she was very young.
The girl giving Tohno Shiki her ribbon despite all that.
…… The stupid me that spoke so happily about the past in this mansion.
…… Such things caused me pain.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
かちゃかちゃという食器の音。
　ごちそうさま、と両手を合わせる。
　おかわりを二杯した事が嬉しかったのか、琥珀さんは喜びながら食器を下げる。
　……その喜びが芝居ではなく本当の事だったら、俺はどんなに嬉しいんだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
The dishes clattered.
I pressed my palms together and thanked her for the meal.
Delighted that I had taken two extra helpings, Kohaku cheerfully cleared everything away.
If only that delight were real, and not another performance—how happy would that make me?
entries.mirrorMoon:
Clink.
Clank.
The sound of my utensils.
Bringing my hands together, I thank her for the meal.
As if she was so happy that I had seconds, she cheerfully takes the dishes.
…… If that was true happiness, maybe I would be happy as well.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「―――――なんだ、簡単な事じゃないか」
　悲しい理由を探してみて、ようやく思い知った。
　こんな事が解らなかったなんて、本当にどうかしてる。
　遠野志貴は、単にこの人が好きなだけだ。
　この人の傷ついた姿を想像するのが耐えられないぐらい、俺は彼女の事を愛しているだけなんだと。
　そんな単純なコトに、俺は、今さらながら、ようやく気がついてくれたらしい――――
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――――Why, it’s simple.”
Only after searching for the source of my sadness do I finally understand.
How could I have failed to see something so obvious?
Shiki Tohno simply likes this woman.
I love her so deeply that even imagining her in pain is more than I can bear.
Now, far too late, I seem finally to have realized something so simple――――
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-----That's pretty simple, isn't it?"
I suddenly find the reason for my sadness.
There must be something wrong with me to not have seen it earlier.
I just like this person.
I love her to a point where I can't even imagine seeing her in pain.
It seems I've finally realized this simple fact----
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「それでは点滴の前に注射ですね。
志貴さん、シャツの袖をめくっていただけますか？」
「…………………」
　肘まで袖をめくる。
「あまり痛くない注射ですから安心してください。
槙久さまも時折体調を崩しましたから。
　わたし、こういうのには慣れているんですよー」
　アルコールで濡らした脱脂綿で腕を拭く。
　……どうかしそうだ。
　琥珀さんは遠野槙久の名前を、なんでもない事のように口にする。
　そんなに完璧に―――芝居をする必要なんて、どこにあるっていうんだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Now, an injection before the IV. Would you roll up your sleeve, Master Shiki?”
“…”
I roll it up to my elbow.
“Don’t worry; this injection barely hurts. Master Makihisa also fell ill from time to time.
I have plenty of practice with this sort of thing.”
Kohaku swabs my arm with alcohol-soaked cotton.
I feel as though I might lose my mind.
Kohaku says Makihisa Tohno’s name as though it means nothing at all.
Why does she need to perform so perfectly―――?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Well then, a shot before your IV.
Shiki-san, can you roll up your sleeve for me?"
"……………………"
I roll it up to the elbow.
"This won't be too painful, so just relax.
Makihisa-sama would sometimes fall ill, too.
So, I've had a lot of practice, you know."
She rubs my arm with a swab of cotton drenched in alcohol.
…… I don't know what to do.
Kohaku-san says Tohno Makihisa's name as if it was nothing.
This perfect---act, is there a reason for it?
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「あ、そういえば志貴さんも子供の頃は怪我ばかりなさっていましたね。
槙久さまのお叱りなんか気にしないで、庭を元気に走り回ってました」
　懐かしそうに言う。
「――――――――っ」
　その笑顔を、直視できない。
　一瞬だけ彼女の笑顔は普段と違っていた。
　にこやかな笑みではなく、夢を語るような遠い笑顔。
　それでも今の彼女を守るためには、騙されていなければならなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh, come to think of it, you were always getting hurt as a child, Master Shiki. You would ignore Master Makihisa’s scolding and run cheerfully around the garden.”
She says it nostalgically.
“――――――――!”
I cannot look directly at that smile.
For one instant, her smile is different from usual.
Not her cheerful smile, but a distant one, as if she were talking about a dream.
Even so, to protect the person she is now, I have to let myself be deceived.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah, come to think of it, you were always injuring yourself as a little kid.
You would ignore Makihisa-sama's scolding and run around the garden."
She speaks nostalgically.
"---------Tss."
I just can't look at her smile directly.
For an instant, her smile changes from its usual form.
It isn't her cheerful smile, it is a smile that comes from describing a distant, longed-for dream.
But to protect the Kohaku-san of the present, I have to play along with this charade.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「…………そう、だったな。
　でも、琥珀、さんも――――楽しそう、だった」
「はい、志貴さんと一緒に走り回りました。
　……ええ、本当に楽しかったですね。
日が落ちるまでずっとあの庭ではしゃぎまわって。
　けど遊び終わるといつも泥だらけで、志貴さんは家長さんにいつも怒られていましたっけ」
――――それも芝居。
　　　　そんな笑顔は、本当は存在しない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Yes—that’s right.
But you—you looked happy too, Kohaku.”
“I was. I ran all over the garden with you, Master Shiki.
It truly was wonderful—we played there until the sun went down.
Though by the end we were always covered in mud, and the head of the house would scold you every time.”
――――That too was an act.
That smile had never truly existed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"………… That's, right.
But, Kohaku-san, you----also seemed to be having, a lot of fun."
"Yes, running around with you, Shiki-san.
…… Yeah, it really was fun.
Playing in the garden until sunset.
But after it was all over, you would always get yelled at for being covered in mud."
----That's another act, too.
That smile is just fake.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「っ………………！」
　夢を語る彼女が、ただ耐えられなくて、その体を抱き寄せた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ngh…!”
Unable to bear hearing her speak of that dream any longer, I pull her into my arms.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"………………!"
Not being able to stand it anymore, I wrap my arms around this girl speaking of her dream.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese: ―――強く抱きしめる事さえできない。
entries.maoEnglish: ―――I could not even hold her tightly.
entries.mirrorMoon: ---I can't even hold onto her tightly.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「あっ………えっと、志貴さん？」
　どこか間の抜けた琥珀の声。
　何も言わず、ただ体を寄せて髪を梳いた。
「………………」
　顔を見られないようにしないといけない。
　俺はたぶん、ひどい顔をしている。
　そんな顔を見せたら、勘のいい琥珀さんの事だ。
　きっと、俺が知ってしまったって、悟ってしまう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Ah… um, Master Shiki?”
Kohaku’s voice sounds almost comically bewildered.
Without answering, I draw her against me and run my fingers through her hair.
“…”
I have to keep her from seeing my face.
My face must look terrible.
Kohaku is too perceptive; one glance,
and she will know that I have learned the truth.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah……… um, Shiki-san?"
Her questioning voice reaches me.
I just wordlessly hold her close to me and stroke her hair.
"………………"
I can't let her see my face.
I probably have a horrible expression.
I can't meet her gaze, her sharp perception.
If I did that, she would know that I know everything.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「…………………っ」
　それでも。
　堪えていたはずなのに、どうしようもなくて、歯を噛んだ。
「志貴さん……？
　痛いんですか、志貴さん？」
「…………………いや。
そんな事は、ないんだ」
　このままで、指先にだけ力をいれた。
　強く抱きしめる事はできなくても、こうして少しでも、この人を抱きとめていたかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
Even so.
Though I mean to endure it, I cannot, and I clench my teeth.
“Master Shiki…? Does it hurt, Master Shiki?”
“――――No. That’s not it.”
Still holding her, I tighten only my fingertips.
Even if I cannot hold her tightly, I want to keep her in my arms like this, if only a little longer.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…………………………"
But still.
I try to hold back and bite my lip.
"Shiki-san……?
Does it hurt that much, Shiki-san?"
"………………………… No.
It isn't, that."
All I can do is grip with my fingers.
I can't hold her tightly, but I want to embrace her as much as I can.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「……もう。
だめですよ、志貴さん。
男の子なんですから、痛くてもがまんしないと」
　言って、彼女の腕が俺の髪をさすった。
　琥珀は静かに、そっと頭をなでてくる。
　それが。
俺にとってのトドメになった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Honestly. That won’t do, Master Shiki. You’re a boy—you have to be brave even when it hurts.”
As she speaks, her hand brushes through my hair.
Quietly, tenderly, Kohaku strokes my head.
That was it. The final blow.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Aw.
That's no good, Shiki-san.
You're a boy, so you have to endure some pain."
Her arm brushes against my hair.
She quietly rubs my head.
That breaks my limit.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「―――――――いい」
「志貴さん？
　何かおっしゃいました？」
　問い返してくる琥珀。
　それに、止めろと自身に叫びながら、それでも言葉が口に出た。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――――――You don’t have to.”
“Master Shiki? Did you say something?”
Kohaku asks.
I shout at myself to stop, but the words come out anyway.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-------It's okay."
"Shiki-san?
Did you say something?"
Kohaku-san asks.
No matter how much my mind screams at me to stop, the words just come out.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「―――もう、笑わなくて、いい」
「え？」
「―――もう、無理に笑わなくて、いいんだ」
　唇を噛み締めて、血を吐くような思いで言った。
「―――――――――」
　なでていた手が止まる。
　琥珀さんはピタリと、呼吸さえ止めて固まっている。

――――カタ。
　という、何かの音。

「っ………………！」
　琥珀さんの体が離れる。
「困りましたね。
点滴がこぼれてしまいました」
　いつもの笑顔。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――You don’t have to smile anymore.”
“What?”
“―――You don’t have to force yourself to smile anymore.”
I bite down on my lip and force out each word as though it were blood.
“―――――――――”
The hand stroking my hair stops.
Kohaku goes utterly still, as if even her breathing has stopped.
――――Clatter.
Something made a small, hard sound.
“Ngh…!”
Kohaku pulls away from me.
“Oh dear. I’ve spilled the IV solution.”
Her usual smile.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---It's okay.
You don't have to smile any longer."
"Eh?"
"---It's okay, you don't have to force yourself to smile."
My voiced feelings spurt forth from my clenched lips.
"---------"
Her hand stops moving.
Kohaku-san freezes.
She doesn't even breathe.

----Kacha.
I hear a noise.

"……………………!"
Kohaku-san pulls away.
"Oh no, it looks like the IV spilled."
The usual smile.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「あいにくと替えの物は明日にならないと届きませんから、今日は点滴はやめましょう。
　それでは志貴さん、何かありましたら呼んでくださいね」
　何事もなかったように琥珀さんは荷台を押していく。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Unfortunately, the replacement won’t arrive until tomorrow, so we’ll have to skip the IV tonight.
If you need anything, please call for me, Master Shiki.”
As though nothing has happened, Kohaku wheels the cart away.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Unfortunately the next one will not arrive until tomorrow, so we'll stop for today.
Well then, Shiki-san, if anything happens, please call me."
Kohaku-san pushes the cart as if nothing just happened.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
彼女はドアも開けずに部屋から出て行った。
「っ――――」
　何をしているんだろう、俺は。
　翡翠との約束も破って、あんな真似をして。
　これじゃ槙久と変わらない。
　俺は自分の気持ちさえ抑えられないのか。
　開けられたままのドアは俺の愚かさを嘲笑うようにユラユラと揺れている。
entries.maoEnglish:
She leaves the room without opening the door.
“Ngh――――”
What am I doing?
I have broken my promise to Hisui and behaved like that.
I am no better than Makihisa.
Can I not even control my own feelings?
The open door sways gently, mocking my stupidity.
entries.mirrorMoon:
She leaves without opening the door.
"-----"
What was I doing?
Acting like that and breaking my promise to Hisui.
It's no different than Makihisa.
I couldn't even control my feelings.
The open door flutters at me in ridicule.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
―――待て。
　琥珀さんはドアを開けずに退室していった…？
「……それはおかしい。
確かに琥珀さんはドアを閉めていたはずだ」
　なのにドアは開いていた。
　それはつまり、琥珀さんと抱き合っていた時、誰かがドアを開けた、という事ではないのか。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Wait.
Kohaku had left without opening the door…?
“That doesn’t make sense. I’m sure Kohaku shut it.”
Yet now it stood open.
Which meant that while Kohaku and I were embracing, someone else had opened the door.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Wait.
Kohaku-san left without opening the door…?
"…… That's odd.
I know Kohaku-san closed it when she came in."
So why was the door open?
That has to mean that someone was watching when I was hugging Kohaku-san.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
―――夕食後にもう一度来ますね、兄さん。
　……そう、秋葉は俺に言っていた。
「秋葉に、見られたのか――――――――」
　一人呟く。
　それはどうという事のない事実の筈だ。
　なのにどうしてか―――何か取り返しのつかない事をしてしまったような、そんな不安だけが胸に渦巻いていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――I’ll come back after dinner, Brother.
Akiha had told me so.
“Did Akiha see us――――――――?”
I whisper to myself.
It should mean nothing.
Yet an inexplicable dread churns in my chest—the sense that I have just done something that can never be undone.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---After dinner I will return, Nii-san.
…… That's what Akiha said.
"Akiha, saw it---------"
I ponder aloud.
That wasn't really a big deal.
So why---why do I have this whirlpool of uneasiness in my chest like I just did something I can never take back?
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
――――日付が変わった。
　日中に晴れていた空には黒い天蓋。
　雨雲は群れをなして空を蹂躙して、月の明かりは皆無といっていい。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――Midnight came and went.
A black canopy now covered the sky that had been clear by day.
Storm clouds massed overhead and trampled out nearly every trace of moonlight.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----Night falls.
The clear daytime sky turns into a black dome.
The swarm of clouds carouse across the sky and obscure the moonlight.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
はあ、と大きく息を吸って、ベッドから起きあがった。
「……ほらな。
夜になれば治るっていっただろ」
　体の調子は、まあ八分という所。
それでも走り回る事に支障はない。
　……引き出しをあけてナイフを取り出す。
　それをポケットにしまって、よし、と気合をいれた。
entries.maoEnglish:
I draw a deep breath and sit up.
“See? I told you I’d recover by night.”
I feel perhaps eighty percent myself. Even so, I can run without trouble.
I open the drawer and take out my knife.
I slip it into my pocket and steel myself.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I take a deep breath and get out of bed.
"…… See?
I told them I'd be better by evening."
I'm pretty much better.
There isn't anything to stop me from running about.
…… I take my knife from the drawer.
"Alright."  I place it in my pocket and psyche myself up.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
……問題は山積みになっている。
　それでも出来る事と、やらなければならない事を間違える事はしない。
　街を騒がしている殺人鬼。
　おそらくは今夜も徘徊しているであろうシキを止める。
「……これぐらいしか兄貴として出来る事はないからな」
　秋葉に実の兄であるシキと争わせるなんて、そんな惨い事はさせられない。
　この体がまだ動くうちに、シキをなんとか止めなければいけないだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
The problems are piling up.
Even so, I will not confuse what I can do with what I have to do.
The killer terrorizing the city.
I have to stop SHIKI, who is probably roaming again tonight.
“It’s about the only thing I can do as her brother.”
I cannot force Akiha to fight SHIKI, her brother by blood.
I have to stop him while this body can still move.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… The problems really have piled up.
But I won't mistake what I can do and what must be done.
The killer wandering the streets.
Tonight I will have to end SHIKI's wanderings once and for all.
"…… As her big brother, it's the least I can do."
I can't allow Akiha to be forced into fighting her real brother.
I have to stop SHIKI while I can still move my body.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
闇雲に街を歩いてもシキの姿は見つけられなかった。
「……チッ。
見通しが甘かったか」
　なんとなく夜の街に出れば、シキとはそれだけで出会えると心のどこかで思っていた。
　まだ実際に出会った事がないくせに、シキとは磁石の両端が引き合うように、望まなくても出会える予感はあったんだが――――
entries.maoEnglish:
I wandered the city at random, but found no sign of SHIKI.
“Damn. Guess I didn’t think this through.”
Some part of me had assumed that simply entering the city at night would bring us face-to-face.
I had never actually met him, yet I had felt certain that, like opposite ends of a magnet, SHIKI and I would be drawn together whether we wished it or not――――
entries.mirrorMoon:
I don't see SHIKI anywhere under the clouded night streets.
"…… Damn.
I guess I was thinking too optimistically."
I thought I would meet SHIKI if I just walked the streets at night.
Even though I have never seen him, I thought I'd be able to meet him like two magnets coming together-----
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「……無闇に動き回るより、どこかで張っていた方が効率的か」
　……見張るのなら路地裏だろうか。
　夢の中であそこは何度も殺害現場になっている。
　かなりの確率で今夜もシキが現れるだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“It may be more efficient to stake out one place than keep wandering blindly.”
The alley seemed the obvious choice.
In my dreams, it had served as the murder scene again and again.
There was a good chance SHIKI would appear there tonight.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… It's probably better if I just wait somewhere instead of randomly walking about."
…… The alley would probably be a good idea.
I witnessed so many murders there in my dreams.
That's probably the best bet if I want to find SHIKI.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
―――――さて。
　物陰に隠れて息を潜める。
　いつ襲われてもいいよう、ナイフはすでに握り締めていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――――All right.
I hid in the shadows and held my breath.
The knife was already clenched in my hand, ready for an attack at any moment.
entries.mirrorMoon:
-----Well then.
I hide in the darkness and take a deep breath.
Ready for an attack at any moment, I grip my knife.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II
8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「――――――っ」
　心臓がやけに速い。
　……不謹慎だとは思うのだが、心はそう乱れていなかった。
　俺はこれからシキと戦う。
　それは殺し合いに極めて近い。
　俺に殺すつもりがなくとも、結果としてそうなってしまう可能性の方が大きいだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――――Ngh.”
My heart is beating absurdly fast.
Shameful as it is, my mind is not particularly disturbed.
I am about to fight SHIKI.
It will be perilously close to a fight to the death.
Even if I have no intention of killing him, that outcome is more likely than not.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-------"
My heart is beating furiously.
…… This may be imprudent, but my mind isn't out of control.
Soon I will be battling SHIKI.
This will be extremely close to a fight to the death.
I don't intend to kill, but the possibility of ending that way is high.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「――――――く」
　だっていうのに、心はまったく乱れていない。
　あんな夢を見続けたせいで、こと殺人という一点にのみ、俺の感情が壊れてしまったのか。
　……正常なのは心臓だけだ。
　正しく活動し、殺人という行為に緊張し、どくどくと早鐘をうつ心臓だけが、七夜志貴にとっての正常か。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――――Kh.”
Yet my mind remains perfectly calm.
Have those dreams broken something in me—destroyed my emotions where murder alone is concerned?
Only my heart is normal.
Is this heart—functioning as it should, tensing before the act of killing, and hammering madly—the only normal thing left in Shiki Nanaya?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------Kk."
Even still, my mind is calm.
Has watching those dreams truly desensitized me towards killing?
…… The only thing that is normal is my heart.
It is the only thing that feels the tension of the upcoming killing and beats a warning bell inside of me.
Maybe it is the only true normalcy of Nanaya Shiki.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「――――――く、う」
　はあ、と大きく息を吐く。
　心臓はいまだに過熱している。
「―――――――」
　おかしい。
　感情は乱れていないのに、どうしてこう―――俺は、血を昂ぶらせて吸血鬼を待っているのか。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――――Kh, ah.”
I let out a long breath.
My heart is still overheating.
“―――――――”
Something is wrong.
If my emotions are calm, why am I waiting for the vampire with my blood racing like this?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-------"
I let out a deep breath.
My insides are still overheating.
"-------"
Strange.
My feelings are completely calm, so why---why is my blood racing to meet this vampire?
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
どくん
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　どくん!w1000
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　どくん
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　どくん!w1000
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　どくん
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　どく!w750
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　どく!w750
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　どく!w500
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　どく!w500
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　どく!w250
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　どく!w250
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　どく!w250
――――以前。
　こんなふうに、誰かを、探していた気がする。
entries.maoEnglish:
Thump
Thump!w1000
Thump
Thump!w1000
Thump
Thump!w750
Thump!w750
Thump!w500
Thump!w500
Thump!w250
Thump!w250
Thump!w250
――――Once before.
I feel as though I searched for someone like this.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Thump
Thump
Thump
Thump
Thump
Thump
Thump
Thump
Thump
Thump
Thump
Thump
----Once before.
I think I was searching for someone like this.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「―――――――――」
　気配を感じて、咄嗟に身を隠した。
　……足音が気配がやってくる。
　脈拍はさらに高く。
　訪れた相手が、自分が倒すべき『敵』だと確実に照合した。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――――――――”
I sense a presence and instantly conceal myself.
Footsteps approach; the presence draws nearer.
My pulse climbs higher.
Without doubt, the newcomer matches the “enemy” I must destroy.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---------"
I sense someone and instantly hide myself.
…… The sound of footsteps.
My pulse reaches new heights.
The one who is coming is the one "enemy" I know I came here to defeat.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
―――足音が近づいてくる。
　あと数歩。
　一歩。
　二歩。
　三歩。
　四歩――――――――！
entries.maoEnglish:
―――The footsteps come closer.
Only a few more steps.
One.
Two.
Three.
Four—now!
entries.mirrorMoon:
---The footsteps come closer.
Only a few more steps.
One step.
Two steps.
Three steps.
Four steps--------!
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
そのまま、敵へと走った。
　敵が突然の襲撃者に振り向く。
　とっさに後ろに逃げようとするが、こちらのほうが何倍も迅い。
　躊躇わず、ナイフを敵の喉へと振る――――
entries.maoEnglish:
I charge straight at the enemy.
The enemy turns toward the sudden attacker.
They try to leap backward, but I am many times faster.
Without a moment’s hesitation, I swing the knife at the enemy’s throat――――
entries.mirrorMoon:
I dash towards the enemy.
The enemy suddenly whirls to face me.
The enemy tries to jump back, but I am many times faster.
I swing my knife at the enemy's throat without the slightest hesitation----
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「「！？」」
――――寸前、紙一重で軌跡をズラした。
　ざん、とナイフが秋葉の髪を切る。
　俺たちは互いに大きく吐息をこぼしたあと、同時に指差しあう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“!?” “!?”
――――At the last possible instant, I twisted the blade’s path aside by a hair.
The knife sliced through Akiha’s hair with a sharp hiss.
We both let out a long breath, then pointed accusing fingers at each other in perfect unison.
entries.mirrorMoon:
""!?""
----Right before impact, I manage to pull back.
The knife breezes through Akiha's hair.
We both take a deep breath and point at the other at the same time.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「兄さん、どうしてこんな所に！？」
「秋葉、なんで所にいるんだよ！？」
　………………まあ、それでなんとなく自分たちが同じ目的で、同じようにここに来た事が解ってしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Brother, what are you doing here!?”
“Akiha, what are you doing here!?”
That exchange made it more or less obvious that we had come here in exactly the same way, for exactly the same reason.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Nii-san, what are you doing here!?"
"Akiha, what are you doing here!?"
……………… Well, I guess it's pretty obvious we're after the same thing.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「…………………」
　秋葉は何か、すっごく文句がありそうな目で俺を見ている。
　……琥珀さんを抱きしめていた事を怒っているんだろうが、今ばっかりはそんな事に怯んではいられない。
「秋葉。
おまえ、こんな時間に何をしているんだ」
「決まっているでしょう。
遠野家の当主として、シキを捜しているんです」
「……………」
　悪びれた様子もなく、きっぱりと秋葉は答えてくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
Akiha looks at me as though she has a serious complaint to make.
She is probably angry about seeing me embrace Kohaku, but this is no time to let that intimidate me.
“Akiha. What are you doing out at this hour?”
“Isn’t it obvious? As head of the Tohno family, I’m searching for SHIKI.”
“…”
She answers without the slightest sign of remorse or hesitation.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"………………"
Akiha looks at me with eyes almost brimming with complaint.
…… I think she's still mad at me for hugging Kohaku-san, but I can't worry about that right now.
"Akiha.
Just what are you doing here at this time of night?"
"Is it not obvious?
I am looking for SHIKI so I can fulfill my duty as head of the Tohno family."
"……………"
Akiha answers me.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「―――秋葉。
シキの事は俺がなんとかするって言っただろ。
いくら決まりだからって、おまえがこんな危険な真似をする事はないんだ。
おまえだってそれは解ってくれたんじゃないのか」
「そうですけど、気が変わったんです。
　兄さんは何かと忙しいようですから、代わりに私がやるしかないでしょう」
　ふん、と視線を逸らす秋葉。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――Akiha. I told you I would deal with SHIKI. I don’t care what the family rules say—you don’t need to put yourself in danger like this. I thought you understood that.”
“I did, but I changed my mind.
You seem to have so many other demands on your time, Brother, so I have no choice but to do it in your place.”
With a huff, Akiha turns her eyes away.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Akiha.
I told you I'd take care of it, so there's no need for you to put yourself in danger like this.
Didn't you agree to that?"
"That may be true, but I changed my mind.
Nii-san, you seemed a little busy, so I thought I would go in your place."
With a "hmph," Akiha looks away.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「……秋葉。
おまえが何に怒っているかは聞かないけど、それとシキの問題は別だろう？
　これはシキと俺の問題だ。
秋葉を―――こんな、命にかかわる争いに巻き込む事はできない」
「あきれた。
まだそんな悠長な事を言っているなんて、兄さんは甘いのよ。
　いい？
　こうしている間にも兄さんの体は衰弱していってしまう。
　……だから私は、どんな事をしてでも兄さんを元気にしてさしあげなくちゃいけないんです。
それを止めろ、なんて言われても聞けません」
　……秋葉はまっすぐに俺の目を睨んでくる。
　それは引く事を知らない、真剣な眼差しだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Akiha. I won’t ask what you’re angry about, but that has nothing to do with SHIKI.
This is between him and me. I cannot drag you―――drag you into a fight where you might lose your life.”
“Unbelievable. You’re still talking as though we had all the time in the world.
You’re much too naïve, Brother—listen to me. Your body is wasting away even as we speak.
That is why I have to make you well again, whatever it takes. You can order me to stop all you like—I will not obey.”
Akiha glares straight into my eyes.
It is a serious gaze that will not yield.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Akiha.
I won't ask what you're angry about, but isn't that a different matter?
This is between me and SHIKI.
Akiha---I won't let you get involved in such a dangerous fight."
"Give it up.
You are very naive if you keep saying that, Nii-san.
Look.
Even now your body is getting weaker.
…… So I will do whatever it takes to make you better.
I will not listen to you if you tell me to stop."
…… Akiha looks intently at me.
She's dead serious.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「……秋葉の言う事は正しいよ。
俺の体を気遣ってくれる気持ちも嬉しい。
　けど、それは辛いだけだろう。
シキはおまえにとって、その……」
「兄さん。
私にとって兄と呼べるのは兄さんだけです。
……たしかにこれは辛い役割ですが、誰かがしなくてはいけない事でしょう？
　私は物心ついた時から、遠野家の当主として教育されてきました。
だから、こんな事は覚悟の上なんです」
entries.maoEnglish:
“You’re right, Akiha. And I’m grateful that you care so much about me.
But doing this will only hurt you. SHIKI is your…”
“Brother. You are the only person I consider my brother. This may be a painful duty, but someone must perform it. I have been raised to be head of the Tohno family since I was old enough to understand anything. I accepted long ago that this might be required of me.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… What you say is right.
I really am happy that you worry over me this much.
But, isn't it tough?
SHIKI is your, um……"
"Nii-san.
You are the only one I call Nii-san.
…… Certainly this is a difficult task, but someone has to do it, right?
I was raised to fulfill my duty as head of the Tohno family, so all of this is under my own resolution."
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「そんな事より！
　兄さん、そんな体で何をしているんですかっ。
兄さんのほうこそ、シキに襲われでもしたらどうするんです！？」
「うっ―――――」
　秋葉はすごい剣幕でずかずかと歩いてくると、ツン、と指で俺の喉元をつついた。
　あまりの迫力におされて、思わず数歩よろめいてしまう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Never mind that! Brother, what are you doing out here in that condition? What if SHIKI attacks you!?”
“Urk―――――”
Akiha storms up to me and jabs a finger against my throat.
Her sheer force of personality makes me stagger back several steps.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"More importantly!
Nii-san, at your current health, what are you doing?
Aren't you the one who is in danger from SHIKI!?"
"Uu-----"
Akiha adopts an incredibly commanding pose as she walks toward me with her finger pointed right at my throat.
I unconsciously take a few steps back under this attack.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「ほら、私なんかに怒鳴られたぐらいで気合負けしてるじゃない。
いい？
　兄さんは普通の人なんですから、シキのような怪物に敵うわけがないんです。
　ほら、今夜は送ってさしあげますから、明日からはご自愛してくださいね」
　ぐい、と俺の腕を掴んで歩き出す秋葉。
「ちょっ―――ちょっと秋葉、待てってば……！」
「やかましいわね、深夜なんだから騒ぐと警察が来ちゃうじゃない……！」
entries.maoEnglish:
“There, you see? A little shouting from me is enough to make you retreat. Brother, you are an ordinary human being, so you cannot possibly defeat a monster like SHIKI.
I’ll escort you home tonight, and from tomorrow onward you will take proper care of yourself.”
Akiha grabs my arm and starts walking.
“H-hey―――wait, Akiha…!”
“Keep it down—it’s the middle of the night, and if you make a scene, the police will come…!”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"See, you're already losing to me mentally.
Look, you are just a normal human so a monster like SHIKI is too far above your level.
I will escort you this night, but from now on, you have to take care of yourself."
Akiha grabs my arm and walks off.
"Wa---wait Akiha, wait up……!"
"Oh quiet, if you make a racket this late at night you will just attract the police……!"
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「―――――――う」
　またも気合負けして黙り込む。
　……仕方がない。
　まだ体も本調子じゃないし、ここは秋葉の言う通り屋敷に戻る事にしよう――――
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――――――Ugh”
Once again, her momentum crushes all resistance.
I have no choice.
My body still is not fully recovered, so I might as well do as Akiha says and return to the mansion――――
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-------Ugh."
I lose once again.
…… Oh well.
My body still isn't fully well so I should just go back like she says----
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「それじゃ兄さん、大人しく部屋にいてくださいね。
私も今日はもう戻りますから」
　不機嫌なままで秋葉は背中を向ける。
―――ざあ、と流れる黒髪。
　理由もなく。
　秋葉を見て、唐突に不安になった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Now stay quietly in your room, Brother. I’m going back to mine for the night as well.”
Still in a foul mood, Akiha turns her back on me.
―――Her black hair streamed behind her in a dark cascade.
For no reason I can name.
Looking at Akiha fills me with sudden unease.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Nii-san, please go back to your room.
I am also done for the night."
Akiha turns away, still a bit perturbed.
---Her black hair swishes in the air.
For no reason whatsoever,
I see her and feel this incredible uneasiness.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「……秋葉」
「はい？
　なんですか、兄さん？」
「……信じても、いいよな」
　……？
　何を信じるのか自分でも解らないまま、そんな言葉を口にする。
　秋葉は呆然としてから、
「はい、兄さんが気に病むような事は決してありませんから、どうかお休みになってください」
　なんて、曇りのない笑顔で言った。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Akiha…”
“Yes? What is it, Brother?”
“I can believe you, can’t I?”
…?
Not even knowing what I am asking her to believe, I say it anyway.
Akiha stares at me in astonishment, then―――
“There is nothing for you to worry about, Brother, so please get some rest.”
She says it with an open, cloudless smile.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Akiha."
"Yes?
What is it, Nii-san?"
"…… I can trust it, right?"
……?
I say that without really even knowing what I want to trust in.
Akiha looks surprised for a moment.
"Yes, you have not done anything you need to worry about, so please rest."
She says this with a completely unclouded smile.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「…………………」
　秋葉の姿が遠くなっていく。
　俺の部屋は二階の西奥。
秋葉の部屋は東奥。
　同じ屋根の下にいながら、遠く離れた距離が不安にさせるのか。
　結局、胸の不安は消えないまま、何が不安なのか定まらないまま、自分の部屋のドアを開けた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
Akiha recedes into the distance.
My room is at the western end of the second floor. Akiha’s is at the eastern end.
Is the span between us enough to frighten me, even under the same roof?
The unease remains, shapeless and unresolved, as I open my bedroom door.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…………………"
Akiha walks away.
My room is on the second floor in the western part of the mansion.
Akiha's is in the eastern part.
Does living under the same roof but being so far away make me that uneasy?
With this lingering uneasiness that I still can't define, I open the door to my room.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
――――葦切りの声が聞こえた。
　遠い月。
　夜は暗く、木々のヴェールは世界を覆い。
　地面はギザギザにとがって、ノコギリのように連なっている。
　人影はなく。
　大きな葦切りの声だけが、叢から聞こえてくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――I heard the cry of a reed warbler.
A distant moon.
The night was dark, and a veil of trees covered the world.
The earth rose in jagged points, an endless row of sawteeth.
No human figure could be seen.
Only the reed warbler’s loud cry came from the thicket.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----I hear the voices of reed warblers.
The distant moon.
The night is dark, the veil of trees shrouds the entire world.
The ground is jagged like the teeth of a saw.
There isn't anyone around.
All I can hear is the reed warblers.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
黒い、野原だった。
　本能が郷愁する。
子供の頃、ずっと子供の頃、この森を駆け回った。
　外に出る時は決まって真夜中。
　両親やその兄妹たちはヒトメにつく事が苦手で、日中に出歩く事は滅多に無かったのだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
It was a black field.
My instincts ache with nostalgia. As a child—a very small child—I raced through these woods.
We always went outside at midnight.
My parents and their siblings disliked being seen by people and seldom ventured out by day.
entries.mirrorMoon:
A black field.
I instinctually feel homesick.
As I child, a small child, I always played in this forest.
I always go out in the dead of night.
Since my parents and siblings feel uneasy about getting seen by people, we usually don't go out during the day too much.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
だから、その日も当然夜だった。
　一人きりで庭に出て、黒い森の中で、見知らぬ他人と遭遇した。
　黒い野原は、その日に限ってのみ一層黒い。
　尋常の暗色ではなかった。
　どちらかというと鈍く燈るような暗み。
　鮮血の絨毯は、蛇苺の実に類似する。
entries.maoEnglish:
So of course it was night that day as well.
I went into the garden alone and met a stranger in the black woods.
Only that night, the black field was blacker still.
It was no ordinary darkness.
It was a darkness that seemed to glow dully from within.
The carpet of fresh blood looked like mock strawberries.
entries.mirrorMoon:
So, this is just like any other day.
I walk out of the garden alone into that forest and I encounter those people I don't know.
The black field is an even darker shade today.
It isn't a natural darkness.
It's as if it was being radiated from a dull lamp.
The fresh carpeting of blood looks like wild berries.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
やけに熱かった。
　空気を吸いこむと、火を呑んだように肺がビリビリと爛れる。
　ここは真夏のように熱い。
　だからだろうか。
　今夜はこんなにも凍えるのに、葦切りの鳴き声が聞こえるのは。
entries.maoEnglish:
It was terribly hot.
Each breath scorched my lungs as though I had swallowed fire.
The place burned like high summer.
Was that why?
Why, on a night this bitterly cold, could I hear the reed warbler?
entries.mirrorMoon:
It is awfully hot.
As I take each breath it feels like I'm bringing fire into my lungs.
The heat is as intense as summer.
Is that why?
I keep hearing those reed warblers in the chilled air.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
蛇苺の実でしきつめられた野原。
　その中で、一際アカイ目があった。
　見知らぬ他人が野原に立っている。
　そいつは一つ目だった。
　目は赤く光っている。
　空に虚が孔いたかと思うほど、まわりのモノとは異質すぎる存在色。
　独眼であるが故に、その色は倍化するのか。
　そいつの目に比べれば、野原の鮮血は気の抜けた山吹にすぎないだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
The field is paved with mock strawberries.
Amid them is one eye redder than all the rest.
A stranger stands in the field.
He has one eye.
That eye glows red.
Its color is so alien to everything around it that it seems a hole has opened in the sky.
Does having only one eye double that color’s intensity?
Beside it, the fresh blood covering the field is no more than washed-out yellow ocher.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The wild berries are strewn all over the field.
In the middle, a single, bright red eye.
A stranger is standing in the field.
It only has one eye.
The eye shines with red light.
Looking like it's floating in empty air, its very existence screams abnormally.
Since there is only one eye, its color doubles?
Compared to that eye, the fresh blood seems like the chrome yellow of a far-off mountain.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
赤より緋い赤。
　七夜では紅赤朱と口伝される。
　くれないせきしゅ。
　一言にいえば極めて旧い、先祖還りを起こした混血の事を指す。
　小我としてのリセイが大我としてのリセイに飲まれて正気ではなくなってしまった者の事だ。
entries.maoEnglish:
A red more scarlet than red.
Among the Nanaya, it is handed down by word of mouth as Crimson Vermilion.
Kurenai Sekishu.
Put simply, it refers to an ancient mixed-blood overcome by atavism.
It means someone whose reason as an individual self has been swallowed by the reason of the greater self, driving them insane.
entries.mirrorMoon:
A scarlet deeper than red.
A name for that has been passed down in the Nanaya oral tradition.
Crimson Red Vermillion.
A name that points to an existence that has awakened to the nonhuman blood of its ancestors.
It describes a person whose ego is subsumed by a transcendental self and loses all sanity.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
赤い凶眼は、憑かれたモノの証だという。
　そいつの背には蜃気楼のように何かが煙っている。
　そいつは狂ったようにワラッテいた。
　楽しい事があったわけではないだろう。
　葦切りの声に、そいつの姿が霞んでいく。
　そいつは叢に食われるように消えていった。
entries.maoEnglish:
That murderous red eye is said to mark one who has been possessed.
Something shimmers behind the stranger like a mirage.
He is LAUGHING like a madman.
It is not because anything joyful has happened.
As the reed warbler cries, his figure blurs.
He vanished as though the thicket had devoured him.
entries.mirrorMoon:
It is said that the red Evil Eye is a sign of being possessed.
Like a mirage, something shimmers behind it.
Laughing around aimlessly as if insane.
It doesn't look like it's having any fun.
With the reed warbler's cry, its body becomes hazy.
It disappears as if eaten by the surrounding bush.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
……遠くで呼ぶ声がする。
　一人きりは怖いから、もっと奥の森に行かなくてはいけない。
　木々のヴェールの向こうでは、がちゃがちゃ・ばきばき・どんどん・ぐちゃり、と、祭りめいた騒ぎが繰り返されている。
　七夜志貴は、森の奥へと歩いていく。
entries.maoEnglish:
Someone is calling in the distance.
Being alone is frightening, so I have to go deeper into the forest.
Beyond the veil of trees, the same festive uproar repeats itself: clatter, crack, boom, squelch.
Shiki Nanaya walks deeper into the forest.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… A voice calls me from the distance.
I'm scared to be alone, so I should go towards the forest.
Within the veil of trees, I hear sounds like they are having a festival.
Crash!
Crunch!
Smash!
Splat!
Nanaya Shiki walks toward the back of the forest.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
野原を通り過ぎた時、さっきの赤色について考えた。
　可哀相に。
　アイツは背中でゆらめいていた蜃気楼に憑かれて、いつか疲れて、あんなふうになってしまったのだろう。
　アイツは強そうだったけど、同時にとても危うく見えた。
　アレでは長く生きられないな、と結論を出して、森の奥へと進んでいった。
entries.maoEnglish:
As I leave the field behind, I think of that red stranger.
Poor thing.
The mirage flickering at his back must have possessed him; eventually it wore him down and reduced him to that.
He looked powerful and terribly fragile at once.
Having concluded that he would not live long, I continue into the depths of the forest.
entries.mirrorMoon:
After passing through the field, I think back about that redness I saw earlier.
How pitiful.
When did it become so tired and hazy like that?
It seemed incredibly strong, but at the same time, very fragile.
After finding out that it doesn't have much longer to live, I continue towards the heart of the forest.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
窓から差しこんでくる朝日で目が覚めた。
「―――――――あつ」
　寝ている時にまた熱でも出したのか、寝巻が濡れている。
　……それにしてもおかしな眠りだった。
　大昔に作られた音のない喜劇……よく知らないけど、黒い山高帽をかぶった髭の役者がアレコレと酷い目に会う、あんな感じの映画を見せられたような夢だった。
entries.maoEnglish:
Sunlight through the window wakes me.
“―――――――Hot.”
My nightclothes are soaked, as though I ran another fever in my sleep.
What a strange dream.
It felt like being shown one of those ancient silent comedies—I hardly know the genre, but the kind where a mustached actor in a black bowler hat suffers one disaster after another.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I open my eyes to the morning sun streaming from my window.
"-------Hot."
My pajamas are drenched with sweat.
…… It seems I had a weird dream.
It was like that really old silent comedy film…… I'm not too sure, but that one where that actor with a black derby hat and a mustache keeps getting in all sorts of situations… it was a dream where it felt like I was watching a movie.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「……そういえば、有間の家にいたころは夢なんかみなかったっけ」
　というか、子供の頃から夢というものには無縁だった気がする。
　俺の眠りは深すぎて夢を見る深度じゃない、と主治医は言っていた。
　なら、この屋敷に帰ってきてから続けてみる夢は、夢というより記憶の断片なのかもしれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Come to think of it, I never dreamed when I lived with the Arimas.”
In fact, dreams seemed to have been absent from my life since childhood.
My doctor said I slept too deeply to dream.
Perhaps the dreams I had kept having since returning to this mansion were less dreams than fragments of memory.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Come to think of it, I never did dream when I stayed at the Arimas'."
Actually, I never did dream since I was a kid.
My doctor said that I sleep so deeply that I can't dream.
Then, maybe the dreams I see since coming back to this mansion are actually my memories instead.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「……って。
それを夢っていうんじゃなかったけ」
　ま、そういった小難しい事を考察するのは学者さんに任せて、一学生である遠野志貴は学校に行くべきだろう。
「―――よし、起きるか」
　ベッドから体を起こす。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Wait. Isn’t that still what you call a dream?”
Well, scholars can wrestle with questions like that while Shiki Tohno, ordinary student, goes to school.
“―――All right, time to get up.”
I raise myself from the bed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Wait, isn't that what you call a dream?"
Well, I'll leave these little things for scholars to debate.
As a student, I should go to school.
"---Alright, time to get up!"
I get up from bed.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「―――――え」
　体が動かない。
「なっ……動かないって、どうして！？」
　歯を食いしばって体に力をこめる。
　力みすぎて頭に血が上って、軽い眩暈が起きるぐらいまで努力して、ようやく上半身を起こせた。
「ぁ………あ、つ…………」
　体中が熱い。
「くそ……昨日より、悪くなってる……」
　昨日はただ全身が重いだけだった。
なのに今は、腕を動かすなんて事さえ辛い。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――――What?”
My body will not move.
“It won’t move—why!?”
I clench my teeth and force strength into every muscle.
Only after straining until blood rushes to my head and dizziness washes over me do I manage to raise my upper body.
“Ah―――hot”
My whole body is burning.
“Damn—this is worse than yesterday.”
Yesterday, my limbs merely felt heavy. Now it is an effort just to move one arm.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-----Eh?"
Actually, my body does not move.
"Wha…… Why can't I move!?"
I clench my teeth and summon all my strength.
The blood rushes to my head causing dizziness and I manage to lift my upper body.
"H……… Ho, t…………"
My body is on fire.
"Damn…… This is worse, than yesterday……"
Yesterday my body was just heavy.
But now, just moving my arm is incredibly difficult.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「――――っ、く――――」
　片腕を垂直に上げてみる。
　……。
　…………。
　………………。
「――――はっ……あ」
　ようやく上がった。
　たったそれだけの事をするのに、体中の力をつかって、一分近くかかってしまっている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――Kh――――”
I try to lift one arm straight into the air.
…
……
………
“――――Hah――ah”
At last it rises.
That tiny movement takes every ounce of strength in my body and nearly a full minute.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-----, Da----"
I see if I can lift my arm vertically.
……
…………
………………
"----Gaa…… argh."
I finally lift it up.
Just doing this expends all of my energy and takes me about a minute.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「……どうなってるんだ、これ」
　これじゃ死体だ。
　それとも動力のきれたロボットか。
　ともかく体が動かない。
　けど、そのわりには意識ははっきりしているし、痛みはまったく感じない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What the hell is happening to me?”
I might as well be a corpse.
Or a robot whose power has run out.
Whatever the comparison, my body refuses to move.
Yet my mind remains perfectly clear, and I feel no pain at all.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… What's going on?"
This is like a dead body.
Or maybe like a robot without any power.
Either way, I can't move.
But still, my mind is sharp and I don't feel any pain.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「琥珀さん―――――」
　そう、彼女を呼ぼうとして思いとどまった。
　昨日、俺は琥珀さんを抱きよせて、あんな事を言ってしまった。
　琥珀さんがどう思ったかは知らない。
　……琥珀さんと翡翠の入れ替わりを俺が知っている、という事までは気がついていないとは思うけど、それでも今は会いにくい。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Kohaku―――――”
I almost call for her, then stop myself.
Yesterday I pulled her into my arms and said those things.
I do not know what she made of it.
She probably has not realized that I know she and Hisui traded identities, but facing her now would still be awkward.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Kohaku-san-----"
I start to call her then stop.
Yesterday I said those things while I embraced her.
I don't know what Kohaku-san thought of that.
…… I don't think she knows that I know about her and Hisui trading places, but it's still difficult for me to face her now.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「翡翠―――秋葉、ちょっと―――」
　来てくれ、と言おうとして止まった。
　声は出せるけど、大声をあげようとすると眩暈がする。
　……大声をあげるにも筋力を使うから、その負荷で脳に血がたまっていくような感覚。
「はっ―――――」
　軽く息を吐く。
　こうなったら翡翠が起こしに来てくれるまで、こうして待っているしかないだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hisui―――Akiha, could one of you―――”
I stop before I can ask them to come.
I can speak, but trying to raise my voice brings on dizziness.
Shouting requires muscle, and the strain feels as though it is forcing blood to pool inside my brain.
“Hah―――――”
I breathe out weakly.
At this point, all I can do is wait for Hisui to come wake me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hisui---Akiha, hey---"
I try to say "come", but I stop.
Speaking loudly brings another wave of dizziness crashing into me.
…… Shouting requires muscle use, and that probably puts a strain on the blood to my brain.
"Ahh-----"
I breathe shallowly.
All I can do is just wait like this until Hisui comes to wake me.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
―――結局、俺は今日も学校を休んだ。
　俺を起こしに来た翡翠は顔を蒼白にして秋葉を呼びにいった。
　話を聞きつけた秋葉が駆けつけてきて、これは秋葉や琥珀さんでも対処できないと判断したのか、わざわざ医者を呼んで検査をしてもらった。
　検査結果はいつも通り原因不明。
　あとはお決まりの、ベッドで一日休むべし、という秋葉のご命令が下された。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――In the end, I missed school again.
Hisui went white when she came to wake me and ran for Akiha.
Akiha rushed in, decided that neither she nor Kohaku could handle this, and actually summoned a doctor to examine me.
As always, the tests found no cause.
Then came Akiha’s customary decree: I was to spend the entire day in bed.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---In the end, I take off from school today.
When Hisui came to wake me, she immediately turned pale and called for Akiha.
As soon as she heard, Akiha came running, and I guess neither Akiha nor Kohaku-san knew what to do because they called the doctor in to perform an examination.
As usual, it came up with nothing.
As expected, Akiha ordered me to rest in bed afterwards.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
……日が沈む。
　ベッドに横たわったまま、何もできずに窓の外を眺める。
「………………くそ」
　こんな事になるのなら、やはり昨夜のうちにシキと決着をつけておくんだった。
　こうしている間にも吸血鬼の犠牲者は増えていく。
……いや、昨夜だって俺と秋葉が屋敷に戻った後、シキは誰かの血を吸っていたかもしれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
The sun goes down.
Unable to do anything but lie in bed, I stare through the window.
“Damn it…”
If this is going to happen, I should have settled matters with SHIKI last night.
Every moment I remain here means more victims for the vampire. For all I know, SHIKI drank someone’s blood after Akiha and I returned home.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… The sun sinks below the horizon.
Lying on my side, I gaze emptily out the window.
"…………………… Damn it."
I knew I should have settled things with SHIKI last night, especially now that I became like this.
While I'm like this the number of victims will increase.
…… No, even last night after I came back with Akiha, SHIKI may have already sucked another person's blood.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「―――――――」
　俺は判断を間違えたのか。
　昨日の夜。
秋葉がなんて言おうと、俺はあのまま路地裏に残ってシキを待ち伏せるべきではなかったのか。
「………今夜こそ、やらないと」
　体が動かない、なんて泣き言は言っていられない。
　今は一刻も早くシキを止める事だ。
　そのために、夜に備えて少しでも体力を蓄えておかないといけない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――――――”
Have I chosen wrong?
Last night. No matter what Akiha said, should I have remained in the alley and waited for SHIKI?
“Tonight―――I have to do it tonight.”
I cannot afford to whine that my body will not move.
I have to stop SHIKI as soon as possible.
Until night, I need to conserve every scrap of strength I have.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-------"
Was it the wrong decision?
Last night.
Maybe I should have stayed in that alley waiting for SHIKI no matter what Akiha said.
"……… I have to go tonight."
I can't cry over the fact that I can't move.
I have to stop SHIKI as soon as possible.
I have to save up all my strength until tonight so I can do that.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「志貴さん、起きていらっしゃいますか？」
　扉が開いて、琥珀さんが入ってきた。
「琥珀――――さん」
「はい。
一日ぶりですね、志貴さん」
　笑顔で言って、琥珀さんは扉を閉める。
「……そっか。
そういえば、そうだよね」
　気まずくて視線を逸らす。
　今は琥珀さんとまっすぐに話をする事ができない。
シキの事で余裕がないっていう事もあるけど、俺は昨日のポカを誤魔化すための言い訳を思いついていなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki, are you awake?”
The door opens and Kohaku comes in.
“Kohaku――――”
“Yes. It has been a whole day, Master Shiki.”
Smiling, she shuts the door behind her.
“Right… I suppose it has.”
Awkwardly, I look away.
I cannot face Kohaku properly now. SHIKI has left me little room for anything else, but the real problem is that I still have not devised an excuse for yesterday’s blunder.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-san, are you awake?"
Kohaku-san opens the door and walks in.
"Kohaku----san."
"Yes.
It's been a whole day, hasn't it, Shiki-san?"
She closes the door with a smile.
"…… That's right.
Yeah, that's right."
I suddenly feel awkward and look away.
I can't speak to her directly now.
Not only am I worried too much about SHIKI, but I also haven't figured out a excuse yet for my stupidity last night.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「志貴さん？
　どうしたんです、うつむいたりして？
　やっぱりまだ元気が出ないんですか？」
「っ……………！」
　ひょい、と俺の顔を覗き込んでくる。
「――――いや、そんな事はない、けど」
　赤面しながら、なんとか平静を保って返答した。
　……まずい。
　会いにくいとか言っておいて、琥珀さんの顔を見ると高揚している自分がいる。
　一日会えなかった分、こうして琥珀さんが傍にいてくれるだけで、シキの事を忘れてしまうぐらい、嬉しい。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki? Why are you hanging your head? Are you still feeling poorly?”
“Ngh…!”
She leans in and peers up at my face.
“――――No, I’m fine, mostly.”
Blushing furiously, I somehow keep my voice level.
This is bad.
I told myself she would be difficult to face, yet one look at Kohaku fills me with exhilaration.
After a day apart, merely having her beside me makes me so happy I can forget about SHIKI.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-san?
Why do you look so down?
You really don't feel well?"
"…………!"
She looks into my face.
"----No, that's not it, but…"
Blushing furiously, I somehow manage a calm response.
…… This is bad.
I said it would be difficult to meet her, but just seeing her face uplifts me.
Since I could not see her for a whole day, just having her beside me makes me so happy, I forget about SHIKI.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「……琥珀さん、どうしたの。
点滴ならさっき終わったけど」
　……それでも、彼女とは距離をとらないといけなかった。
　俺は翡翠との約束を破って、琥珀さんを抱き寄せた。
琥珀さんが昨日の事をどう思っているかは解らない。
けどこっちは、昨日で自分の気持ちを思い知らされたんだ。
　こうして傍にいられると、今度は何をするか自分でも解らない――――
entries.maoEnglish:
“Why are you here, Kohaku? The IV finished a while ago.”
Even so, I have to keep my distance.
I broke my promise to Hisui and pulled Kohaku into my arms. I do not know what she thinks of yesterday. But I have been forced to recognize my own feelings.
If she stays this close, I cannot trust what I might do next――――
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Kohaku-san, I thought the IV was already done?"
…… All the same, I need to keep my distance from her.
I broke my promise to Hisui and held her.
I don't know what she thinks about what happened yesterday, but as for me, I've finally realized how I feel.
I have no clue what I'll do now if she's close to me----
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「用がないなら出ていってくれ。
秋葉がやってきたら、琥珀さんが叱られる」
「用ならありますよ。
夕食の献立を決めるんですけど、志貴さん食べたいものがありますか？」
「食べたいものって……今はこんなだから、消化のいいものがほしいけど」
「ふふ、それがですねー、志貴さんは細かい事を気にしなくていいんですよ。
　なんと、お医者さまから食事は自由にとっていい、と許可がおりたんです。
ですから今夜は、志貴さんの好きなものを作ってさしあげられます」
entries.maoEnglish:
“If you don’t need anything, please leave. Akiha will scold you if she finds you here.”
“But I do need something. I’m deciding tonight’s menu, so is there anything you’d like to eat?”
“In this condition, I’d like something easy to digest.”
“That’s the wonderful part, Master Shiki—you don’t need to worry about such details.
The doctor has given you permission to eat whatever you like. So tonight, Master Shiki, I can make your favorite meal.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"If there's nothing, please leave.
If Akiha sees you, you'll be in trouble."
"I do have something.
I thought that I would ask if you wanted anything special tonight to eat?"
"To eat?
…… Since I'm like this, I think something easily digestible would be best."
"Heehee, don't worry about such delicate matters, Shiki-san.
The doctor said you could eat as you please.
So tonight I'll make you whatever you want to eat."
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
……俺の好きなものって、そりゃあたいていの物は好きだけど、今は味より栄養がほしかった。
「―――そうだな、栄養がつくものがいい。
　少しでも体力をつけて、今夜こそシキを止めないといけないから―――」
「はい？
　志貴さんを止めるんですか？」
　琥珀さんは不思議そうに首をかしげた。
「あ―――――」
　まずい、つい思っていた事が口に出てしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
I liked most foods, but right now I cared less about flavor than nourishment.
“―――Then make it something nourishing.
I need to recover as much strength as I can, because tonight I have to stop SHIKI once and for all―――”
“Stop Shiki? You mean yourself?”
Kohaku tilts her head, puzzled.
“―――――Ah”
Damn it—I let my thoughts slip out again.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… I do have foods I like, but I think right now nutrition is more important than taste.
"---I see, then something really nutritious.
I have to get as much power as possible to stop SHIKI tonight---"
"Huh?
Stop yourself, Shiki-san?"
Kohaku-san confusedly tilts her head.
"Ah-----"
Crap.
I let that slip without even thinking about it.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
……って、ちょっと待った。
そういえば琥珀さんはシキの事を知っている筈だ。
秋葉が琥珀さんの血を啜っている時、確かに二人はシキの話をしていたんだから。
　……それに翡翠だって、俺が養子だという事を知っていた。
なら琥珀さんがシキの事を知らない筈がない。
entries.maoEnglish:
Wait. Kohaku had to know about SHIKI. When Akiha was drinking her blood, the two of them had clearly spoken about him.
Hisui knew I was adopted as well. There was no chance Kohaku knew nothing.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… Wait a minute.
She has to know about SHIKI.
When Akiha was drinking Kohaku-san's blood, they were discussing SHIKI.
…… Even Hisui knew I was adopted.
Then there's no way Kohaku-san does not know about SHIKI.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「―――そうか。
琥珀さんも、知っているのか」
「はあ。
知っているって何をですか？」
「……だから俺が養子で、秋葉にはシキっていう人殺しの兄貴がいる事だよ」
　笑顔が凍る。
「……そうですか。
志貴さん、知ってしまわれたんですね」
　でも、それは一瞬だけ。
　“昔の翡翠”という役割を演じる琥珀は、この程度では崩れない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――I see. So you know too?”
“Um. Know what?”
“That I was adopted, and that Akiha has a murderous brother named SHIKI.”
Her smile froze.
“I see. So you have found out, Master Shiki.”
But the lapse lasts only an instant.
Kohaku, playing the role of the Hisui I knew as a child, will not break over something so small.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---I see, you know about it."
"Um.
Do I know what?"
"…… That I was adopted, and that Akiha has a killer brother called SHIKI."
Her smile freezes.
"…… I see.
Shiki-san, you found out about it."
But, that's just for an instant.
Kohaku's act of "Hisui from the past" doesn't crumble.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「ですがシキ様はもう他界されています。
　今の遠野家の長男は志貴さんだけなんですから、その事はお忘れになったほうがいいと思いますけど」
　琥珀さんは笑顔だった。
　それはさっきの、夕飯の献立をどうしようか、という時と同じ笑顔だ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“But Master SHIKI has passed away.
You are the Tohno family’s only son now, Master Shiki, so I think it would be best if you forgot the matter.”
Kohaku is smiling.
It is the same smile she wore when asking what I wanted for dinner.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"But SHIKI-sama is no longer in this world.
You are the only eldest son of the Tohno family now.
I think it's best to forget about it."
She keeps smiling.
The same smile she had when discussing the evening menu.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「……俺だって忘れたいよ。
けど、今は忘れるわけにはいかない。
遠野の血ってヤツがしでかした事が、俺には許せないんだ」
　親父が。
　君を、笑うだけの人形にしてしまった事が。
「……それにシキの事は放っておけない。
　アイツが街で吸血鬼騒ぎを起こしているかぎり、俺は秋葉の兄貴にもなれないし、」
　あの少女に、約束のリボンを返す事も、できない。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’d like to forget it too. But I can’t—not now. I can’t forgive what the Tohno blood has done.”
What Father had done.
How he had turned you into a doll that could do nothing but smile.
“And I can’t leave SHIKI alone.
As long as he keeps stirring up vampire attacks in the city, I can’t truly be Akiha’s brother, and…”
Nor can I return the ribbon to that girl, as I promised.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I want to forget it, but I can't.
I can't forgive what the Tohno blood did."
My old man.
He turned you into nothing more than a smiling doll.
"…… And I can't leave SHIKI alone.
As long as he is being a vampire, I can't ever be Akiha's brother."
I can't give that girl back her ribbon, either.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
―――俺には、そんな事しかできない。
　この人をどうすれば救えるのか、どうすれば遠野槙久の罪を贖えるのかは解らない。
　ただ今は、シキという殺人鬼を止めて、遠野の血というモノを消すしかできない。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――That is the only thing I can do.
I do not know how to save this woman, or how to atone for Makihisa Tohno’s sin.
All I can do now is stop the killer SHIKI and eliminate the Tohno blood itself.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---This is the only thing I can do.
I don't know how to save this person or erase the sin of Tohno Makihisa.
All I can do right now is to stop the killer SHIKI and extinguish that Tohno blood.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「……だから、俺の手でなんとかしたいんだ。
　俺はシキを放っておけないけど、それ以上に、その―――琥珀さんを、助けたくて」
　……ばか。
また俺は、ワケの解らない事を口にしてる。
　かってに思いこんで、かってに、琥珀を助けられるんだって、そんな自分勝手な事を―――
「……はは、何言ってるんだろ、俺。
　けどまあ、ともかくそういう事なんだ。
これは遠野の問題だから、俺だけで決着をつける。
琥珀さんと翡翠は何も心配しなくていいんだ」
　琥珀さんは何も言わない。
　あの笑顔も途絶えている。
entries.maoEnglish:
“That’s why I want to settle it with my own hands.
I can’t ignore SHIKI, but more than that, I―――I want to save you, Kohaku.”
Idiot. Once again, I’m spouting nonsense.
Deciding everything for myself, arrogantly imagining I can save Kohaku―――
“Hah—what am I even saying.
Anyway, that’s how it is. This is a Tohno problem, so I’ll settle it alone. You and Hisui don’t have to worry about anything.”
Kohaku says nothing.
Even her smile is gone.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… I want to do this with my own hands.
I can't leave him alone, but more than that, I---I want to help you, Kohaku-san."
…… Idiot.
I keep saying these stupid things.
Thinking selfishly, thinking that I can save Kohaku by doing that.
Such selfish things---
"…… Haha, what am I saying?
But, anyway, this is a problem of the Tohno family, so I will end it.
There is no need for you or Hisui to worry."
Kohaku-san doesn't say anything.
Her smile also ceases.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「琥珀さん？
　俺、また何か気に障る事でも言っちゃった？」
「―――違うんです。
あの、志貴さんは本当に、そう思われているんですか？」
―――――――？
　そう思われてるって、何が……？
entries.maoEnglish:
“Kohaku? Did I say something to upset you again?”
“―――No, that isn’t it. Master Shiki, do you truly mean what you just said?”
―――――――?
Which part is she asking whether I mean?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Kohaku-san?
Did I say something wrong?"
"---No.
Um, do you really mean that?"
-------?
What does she mean……?
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「志貴さん。
秋葉さまが毎晩お屋敷を抜け出している事は知っていますか」
「知ってるよ。
秋葉は遠野家の当主としてシキを捜しているんだろ。
止めろって言ってるんだけど、秋葉のヤツは俺の言う事なんて聞きやしないんだ」
「うそです。
志貴さんは秋葉さまから何も聞いていないんですか！？」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki. Do you know that Miss Akiha leaves the mansion every night?”
“I know. She’s searching for SHIKI as head of the Tohno family. I keep telling her to stop, but Akiha never listens to a word I say.”
“That isn’t true! Has Miss Akiha told you nothing?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-san.
You know that Akiha-sama leaves the mansion every night?"
"Yeah.
It's her responsibility as head of the Tohno family to look for SHIKI.
I told her to stop, but she doesn't listen."
"I don't believe it.
You didn't hear from Akiha-sama!?"
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「……待ってくれ琥珀さん。
聞いてないって、何が」
「………………」
　琥珀さんは答えない。
　……ただ、琥珀さんの様子は普通じゃない。
鈍感な俺にだって解る。
　どくん、と。
　落ち着いていた心臓が拍子をあげた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Wait. Kohaku.
What haven’t I heard?”
“―――――――――”
Kohaku does not answer. Something is wrong.
Even someone as oblivious as me can see it.
My calm heart quickens with a thump.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Wait, Kohaku-san…… hear what?"
"………………"
Kohaku-san doesn't answer.
…… But she isn't acting normal.
Even someone thick-headed like me can tell.
Thump.
My pulse starts to increase.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「秋葉さまは、志貴さんに嘘を言っておられます。
　……元々シキ様は血を吸う鬼ではないんです。
　他者の体温。
　血という温もりを必要としているのは」
　どくん、どくん。
　脈拍が乱れていく。
　琥珀さんの真剣な目と、ふと、ある事実が重なって、厭なコトを、想像してしまった。
―――ちょっと待った。
　　　頼むから、ちょっと待ってほしい。
　それは。
　俺が無意識に、考える事を避けていた事じゃないか。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Miss Akiha has been lying to you.
Master SHIKI was not originally a blood-drinking fiend.
Another person’s body heat.
The one who needs the warmth carried in blood is―――”
Thump, thump.
My pulse breaks into chaos.
Something in Kohaku’s grave eyes suddenly connects with a fact I already know, and a hideous possibility forms in my mind.
―――Wait, please.
Just wait a moment.
That.
This is what I have unconsciously refused to consider.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Akiha-sama is lying to you, Shiki-san.
…… SHIKI-sama was not exactly a blood sucking demon.
It's the body warmth of others.
Not the blood, but the heat."
Thump, Thump.
My pulse goes crazy.
The combination of those facts and her serious eyes make me imagine something bad.
---Wait.
Please, just wait.
That is.
Unconsciously, something I avoided thinking about.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「……待ってくれ。
……いい。
今は、そんな話、言わなくていいんだ」
「――――志貴さん。
遠野シキと呼ばれていた人は、すでに他界しているんです。
　確かにシキ様は血を吸う鬼となって、街を騒がしていた殺人鬼でした。
　でもそれも終わりました。
　……五日前。
他ならぬ秋葉さまの手で、シキ様は処罰されたんです」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Wait. It’s all right. You don’t have to tell me now.”
“――――Master Shiki. The man once called SHIKI Tohno is already dead.
He did become a blood-drinking fiend, and he was the murderer who terrorized the city.
But that has ended.
Five days ago. Miss Akiha herself passed judgment on him.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Please wait.
…… It's okay, you don't have to say anything."
"----Shiki-san.
The one known as Tohno SHIKI is no longer in this world.
Certainly SHIKI-sama was a blood sucking demon and killed people on the streets.
But that is all over.
…… Five days ago, by Akiha-sama's hand, SHIKI-sama was exterminated."
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
―――あの夢。
　　　秋葉に殺される殺人鬼の夢。
　　　アレは俺が見たものではなく、
　　　シキが見ていた、最後の光景。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――That dream.
The dream of a murderer being killed by Akiha.
It was not something I had seen,
but the final sight witnessed by SHIKI.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---That dream.
The dream of the killer being killed by Akiha.
That wasn't what I saw.
It was what SHIKI was watching in his final moments.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「人を殺して血を吸っていたシキという者はもういないんです。
　ですから……今街で起こっている事件は、全て―――」
entries.maoEnglish:
“The SHIKI who murdered people and drank their blood no longer exists.
Which means that every incident happening in the city now is…”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"The SHIKI that killed people and drank their blood is no longer alive.
So…… that means that all the recent incidents, they are all---"
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
―――シキはもういない。
　　　とっくの昔に退場していた。
　　　残っているのは。
　　　毎夜屋敷を抜け出して街を徘徊している、
　　　遠野秋葉という血を吸う鬼だけだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――SHIKI is already gone.
He had left the stage long ago.
The only one left.
The blood-drinking fiend who slipped from
the mansion each night and roamed the city—a woman named Akiha Tohno.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---SHIKI is no longer alive.
Long gone.
The only one that is left.
Leaving every night to walk the streets,
the blood sucking demon named Tohno Akiha.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「志貴さん――――！？」
　呼びとめる琥珀さんの声を振り切って、部屋から飛び出した。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki――――!?”
I tear free of Kohaku’s call and bolt from the room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-san----!?"
Ignoring her voice, I fly out of the room.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
――――走る。
　体が痛んだが、そんな事はどうでもいい。
　何も考えられない。
　これ以上は考えたくない。
　秋葉の口から本当の事を聞くまでは、もう何も。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――Run.
My body screams, but that means nothing.
I cannot think.
I do not want to think any further.
Nothing more until I hear the truth from Akiha herself.
entries.mirrorMoon:
----Running.
My body is engulfed in pain but that doesn't matter.
I don't think about anything.
I don't want to think about anything.
Until I hear the truth from Akiha's mouth, nothing else.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
走る。
　東館の奥、秋葉のいる部屋へと走る。
　息を乱して、半狂乱になって、ノックもせずに重い両開きの扉を開けた。
「はぁ――――はあ、は――――」
　部屋を見渡す。
　秋葉は――――俺を見るなり、優雅に椅子から腰をあげた。
entries.maoEnglish:
I ran.
I ran to Akiha’s room at the far end of the east wing.
Gasping, half frantic, I threw open the heavy double doors without knocking.
“Hah――――hah, hah――――”
I sweep my gaze across the room.
The moment she sees me, Akiha rises gracefully from her chair.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Running.
Running toward her room at the east end of the mansion.
Breathing wildly, I open her heavy double door without knocking.
*pant*----*pant*, *pant*----
I look around the room.
Akiha----elegantly gets up from her chair as soon as she sees me.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「どうしたんですか兄さん。
ノックもしないで部屋に入ってくるなんて失礼ですよ」
「は――――――あ」
　乱れた呼吸を整えて秋葉を凝視する。
　いや、自分でも意識していないが俺は秋葉を睨んでいるんだろう。
　害意をこめた視線を受けて、秋葉は何かを察したようだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What is it, Brother? It’s terribly rude to enter someone’s room without knocking.”
“Hah…”
I brought my ragged breathing under control and fixed my eyes on her.
No—even if I had not realized it, I must have been glaring.
Meeting the hostility in my gaze, Akiha seemed to understand.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"What is it, Nii-san?
Entering without knocking is pretty rude, you know."
"Ah------haa……"
I catch my breath as I stare at her.
No, I'm definitely glaring at her without realizing it.
Akiha senses the emotion in my look.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「兄さん………？
　何かあったんですか？」
「――――――――」
　一度だけ深呼吸をして、乱れた呼吸を正した。
　胸の動悸を抑えて、秋葉を睨んだまま、口を開けた。
「――――秋葉。
どういう、事だ」
　秋葉の顔がこわばる。
　……その言葉だけで俺が何を聞きたいのか悟ったのか。
　秋葉は無言で俺を見つめた後、くるりと、何事もなかったように窓際まで歩き出した。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Brother…? Has something happened?”
“――――――――”
I take one deep breath and steady myself.
Suppressing the pounding in my chest, I keep my glare fixed on Akiha and open my mouth.
“――――Akiha. What is going on?”
Akiha’s face stiffened.
Had those few words told her exactly what I wanted to know?
She watched me in silence, then turned and walked toward the window as though nothing were amiss.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Nii-san………?
Did something happen?"
"--------"
I take one more deep breath and calm my breathing.
Suppressing the pulse in my chest, I glare as I speak.
"----Akiha.
What is the meaning of this?"
Her face tightens.
…… With just those words she probably figured out what I was going to say.
After staring at me wordlessly, she walks casually over to the window sill.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
外は深空。
　茜に染まった陽射しが、空とこの部屋を燃え上がらせる。
　その中で、三日前の夕暮れと同じように、秋葉は紅の空を背にして振り返った。
entries.maoEnglish:
Outside, the sky was fathomless.
Madder-red sunlight set both heaven and room ablaze.
As she had at sunset three days before, Akiha turned with the crimson sky at her back.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The deep sky.
The red rays of sun glaring through the sky and into the room.
Like three days ago, she turns her back to the crimson sky.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「そんな聞き方じゃ何の事だか解らないわ、兄さん。
もう少し具体的に言ってくれない？」
「――――――」
　刹那、眩暈がした。
　目の錯覚なのか、秋葉のまわりに靄のようなモノが見えた。
―――危うい、と感じさせる空気。
　背後にあんな、燃えるような空があるせいだ。
　秋葉の髪が真紅に見えて、ギシリと、全身の機構が軋む。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I can’t possibly know what you mean when you ask like that, Brother. Couldn’t you be more specific?”
“…”
Dizziness struck.
Perhaps it was only an illusion, but something like haze wavered around Akiha.
―――The air itself warned me of danger.
It had to be the burning sky behind her.
Her hair looked scarlet, and every mechanism in my body creaked.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I'm not sure what you mean, Nii-san.
Could you be a little more specific?"
"------"
Dizziness assails me.
Is it just a trick of the eyes?
I thought I saw something hazy around her.
---Danger fills the air.
It must be the fault of that glowing sky behind her.
Akiha's hair looks crimson and my whole body creaks.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「兄さん？
　黙ったままじゃどうしようもないでしょう。
それとも今更―――何もなかった事にして、お部屋に戻ってくれるのかしら」
　クスクスと秋葉は笑う。
　それで本当に。
秋葉が俺を騙していたのだと、解ってしまった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Brother? Silence won’t get us anywhere. Or have you decided, even now, to pretend nothing happened and return to your room?”
Akiha gives a soft, amused laugh.
And that was it. I know beyond doubt that she has deceived me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Nii-san?
If you don't say anything I can't help.
Or---will you go back to your room and pretend nothing happened?"
Akiha giggles.
With that, I understand she was really deceiving me all along.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「秋葉、なんで―――」
「なんでシキを殺したのかなら、理由は解っているでしょう。
　私は遠野家の当主です。
その役目は遠野よりのモノになってしまった一族の処理が第一だもの。
　私がシキを殺すのは一族の総意だし、兄さんだってシキを殺したがっていたじゃない」
　ぞわり、と全身が総毛立つ。
―――なんだ。
　今、目の前にいるのは誰だ。
　この、見ているだけで息が止まりそうな重圧は誰のものだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Akiha, why―――”
“If you’re asking why I killed SHIKI, you already know.
I am the head of the Tohno family. My foremost duty is to dispose of those among us who become more Tohno than human.
Killing SHIKI was the will of the entire family—and you wanted him dead too, didn’t you?”
Every hair on my body rises.
―――What was this?
Who stood before me now?
Whose presence was this, so crushing that merely looking at her threatened to stop my breath?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Akiha, why---"
"You already know why I killed SHIKI.
I am the head of the Tohno family.
It is my responsibility to exterminate those that become controlled by the Tohno blood.
What I did was by consensus of the family, and even you wanted to kill him."
The hairs on my body stand on end.
---What is this?
Who is this person in front of me?
Who is this that takes away my breath through sheer pressure?
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「違う―――俺が言いたいのは、そんな事じゃない」
「ふうん。
それじゃ問題なんかないじゃない。
ヒトでないものを処理した所で罪じゃないでしょう？
　たとえ飼い犬だって、人を噛んでしまったら殺さなくてはいけない。
私がした事は、それと同じレベルの話よ」
「違うって言ってるだろ……！
　俺が言いたいのは、どうして俺にその事を隠していたのかって事だ……！」
entries.maoEnglish:
“No—that isn’t what I mean.”
“Oh. Then there’s no problem. Disposing of something inhuman is hardly a crime.
Even a pet dog must be put down once it bites a person. What I did was no different.”
“I said that isn’t it! I want to know why you hid it from me!”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No---that's not, what I meant."
"Oh?
Well then, there's no problem.
Killing someone who isn't human isn't a sin, right?
It is just like killing a dog that attacks people.
It is on the same level."
"I said that it's not about that……!
What I want to say is, why did you hide it from me……!"
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「ああ、そのコトなんだ。
つまらないなあ、そんな解りきった事を聞かれるなんて。
　ねえ兄さん、ご自分でも気がついている事を尋ねるのは質問ではなく確認よ。
そういう事なら、私は頷くしかないんだけど」
　秋葉の周囲がゆらぐ。
　蜃気楼のようにゆれるカーテン。
　赤い、夕暮れに染まった長い髪。
　ギシリ、と。
　今にも秋葉をコロソウとするこの躯。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh, that. How dull—to be asked something so obvious.
Brother, asking what you already know isn’t a question—it’s a request for confirmation. If that’s all you want, I can only nod.”
The air around Akiha ripples.
Curtains sway like a mirage.
Her long hair is red with sunset.
Creak.
This body, ready even now to KILL Akiha.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Ah, that.
It's boring, asking me such an obvious question.
Hey Nii-san, asking something you know the answer to is not a question, but a confirmation.
If that's the case, I can only nod."
The air around her shimmers.
The curtains waver like a mirage.
Her long hair illuminated red by the setting sun.
Creak.
My body screams at me to kill her.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「―――シキを殺したのは、五日前だな」
　はい、と秋葉は頷く。
　五日前―――その夜、秋葉が倒れた日。
　泣きながら抱きついた秋葉は、何かを必死に拒んで、涙を流していた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You killed SHIKI five days ago.”
Yes, Akiha said with a nod.
Five days ago—the night she collapsed.
She had clung to me in tears, desperately rejecting something as she wept.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---You killed SHIKI five days ago."
"Yes," Akiha nods.
Five days ago---that night when she collapsed.
Hugging me while she was crying, trying to hold something back.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「なら、その後に起こった吸血鬼騒動はシキの仕業じゃない。
アレは、おまえがやった事なのか」
　はい、と秋葉は頷く。
　森の中の離れの屋敷。
　そこで琥珀さんの血を啜ってた秋葉。
　あの時に、もう――シキは消えていて、秋葉は吸血鬼じみた行為を繰り返していた。
　琥珀さんが言っていたじゃないか。
どうして自分の血だけで満足してくれないのか、と。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Then the vampire attacks after that weren’t SHIKI’s work. Were they yours?”
Yes, Akiha said with another nod.
The detached house in the forest.
Akiha drinking Kohaku’s blood.
SHIKI had already been gone, and Akiha had continued those vampiric acts.
Kohaku had said it herself. Why could Akiha not be satisfied with her blood alone?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Then the recent vampire incidents aren't the work of SHIKI…… they are all your doing."
"Yes," Akiha nods.
The detached building in the forest,
where Akiha was sucking Kohaku-san's blood.
At that time--SHIKI was already gone and Akiha was still committing those acts.
Kohaku-san even asked why Akiha wasn't satisfied with just her blood.
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「―――どうして。
　シキはともかく、おまえは―――何も、おかしな所なんてないじゃないか」
「ええ、私はまだシキのように外れてはいません。
そうならないように琥珀から血を貰っていたんだから、そんなのは当然でしょう？」
「……なら！
　どうして琥珀さんだけで満足しなかったんだ！？
　今までそうしていたって言うんなら、どうして今になってあんな―――」
　シキと同じ、吸血鬼じみた事をしてしまったんだ、おまえは……………！！
entries.maoEnglish:
“Why?
SHIKI may have been twisted, but there’s nothing wrong with you.”
“No. I haven’t strayed as far as SHIKI—not yet. That was why I took blood from Kohaku in the first place.”
“Then why wasn’t Kohaku enough? If her blood sustained you all this time, why would you suddenly do something like that?”
You did something vampiric, just like SHIKI…!!
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Why?
SHIKI was, but you---you don't seem strange."
"Yes, I am not like SHIKI.
It's obvious because I'm drinking Kohaku's blood so I don't become like him."
"…… Then!
Why aren't you satisfied with just her blood!?
You said it yourself, so why---"
Why are you doing the same things as SHIKI………………!!
entries.scriptLabel: 8 / Crossroads at the Witching Hour II

entries.japanese:
「それはシキの影響です。
これは私にとっても失敗だったんです、兄さん。
　……私の力は単に物を排除するモノではなくて、対象を壊すのではなく、対象から奪う、という類の力だった。
　私はシキからシキの命を奪いました。
けどその時に、何かよくないモノまで摂りこんでしまったみたい」
「―――――？」
　何かよくないモノ？
　以前の秋葉にはなくて、今の秋葉にはあるもの。
　それは、あの―――
