Nii-san, are you looking forward to playing with Inui-san so much?"
"Why do you sound like that?
Of course a trip is fun."
"I see.
You seem almost drunk with happiness.
You've been waiting for this day since the start of summer, right?
I don't know where you are going with Inui-san, but there has to be something really good waiting for you there, right?"

entries.japanese:
「秋葉さま。
その言い回しはおかしいと思います。
いいコトは有るもので、待っているものではありません」
「あ、そっか。
待ってるっていう形容詞は人に対して使うものだものね。
兄さんに一時間も待たされたものだから、私ったらどうかしてるみたい」
「………………………………」
　……この二人。
最近、すごく息があってる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Miss Akiha. I believe that expression is incorrect. Good things are found somewhere; they do not wait there.”
“Oh, of course. People wait; good things don’t. Being kept waiting for an hour must have scrambled my grammar.”
“…”
…Those two had become alarmingly good at working together lately.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Akiha-sama.
I do not think that is quite right.
Something good is something that is there, not something that is waiting."
"Ah, that's right.
It would have to be a person to be 'waiting'.
There must be something wrong with me.
I guess I was just waiting for Nii-san too long."
"……………………"
…… These two.
They seem to be in harmony all of a sudden.

entries.japanese:
「それで兄さん。
旅行は何日でしたっけ」
「……七日間だけど。
それが、なに」
「へえ、短いんですね。
たまにしか会えないんだから、私はてっきり休みの間はずっとあちらに居ると思ってたのに。
　兄さん。
そんなんじゃ琥珀、可哀相なんじゃない？」
「な―――なな、なにを言ってんだおまえ！
　俺は乾とアテのない旅に出るんであって、決して琥珀さんの所になんか行かないぞ……っ！
　だいたいな、琥珀さんとならすぐに会えるじゃないか。
今だって土日はこっちに来てくれるんだから、別に、俺から会いにいく必要なんて……………」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Now then, how long was this trip again?”
“…Seven days. Why?”
“Oh, how short. Since you so rarely see her, I assumed you would spend the entire vacation there.
Don’t you think Kohaku will be lonely?”
“Wh-what the hell are you talking about! I’m going on an aimless journey with Inui. I am absolutely not going to visit Kohaku…! Besides, I can see her whenever I want. She already comes here on weekends, so there’s no reason I need to go all the way to see her…”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Well then, Nii-san.
How long will you be gone?"
"…… Seven days.
Why do you ask?"
"Oh really?
That's pretty short.
Since you can only see her once in a while, I thought that you would spend your whole summer break there.
Nii-san.
Don't you feel sorry for Kohaku like that?"
"Wh---wh, wh, what are you saying?
I'm just going on a random trip with Inui, I'm not going to see Kohaku-san at all……!
Anyway, I see her all the time.
She's still coming here every weekend, so there's really no need for me to go see her…………"

entries.japanese:
「――――――――――――――」
「…………必要なんて、ないけど……やっぱり寂しいかなっ、と………」
　視線に耐えきれなくなって、床を見つめてみたりする。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――――――――――――”
“No reason, exactly, but I suppose I would still be lonely”
Unable to endure their stares any longer, I found myself studying the floor.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"--------------"
"………… There's really no need, but…… she probably is lonely, and………"
I stare down at the floor.

entries.japanese:
―――くそ、いいじゃんか。
　夏休みなんだから、琥珀さんの所に泊まりに行くぐらい、見てみぬふりをしてくれても。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Damn it, what was wrong with that?
It was summer vacation; they could at least pretend not to notice that I was going to stay with Kohaku.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---Damn it, what's wrong with it?
It is summer vacation after all, so they should pretend to not notice that I'm going to go see Kohaku-san.

entries.japanese:
「―――と、もうこんな時間か。
これ以上先方をお待たせするワケにはいかないし、今日はここで許してさしあげますね、兄さん」
　秋葉は楽しげに言ってソファーから立ちあがる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“―――Oh, look at the time. We mustn’t keep the other party waiting any longer, so I’ll show mercy for today, Brother.”
Akiha rises from the sofa, plainly enjoying herself.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Oh, it's already late.
I can't let her wait any longer, so I'll let you go for today, Nii-san."
Akiha sounds like she's having fun as she rises from the sofa.

entries.japanese:
「それじゃ翡翠、あとはよろしくね。
今日は夕方には帰ってくるから、二人で仲良く陰口でも叩きましょう」
「はい。
それは、是非」
　……だから。
　秋葉はともかく、翡翠まで性格が変わってきたのはどういう事なのか。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Hisui, I’ll leave the rest to you. I’ll be back this evening, and then the two of us can enjoy talking behind his back.”
“Yes. I would be delighted.”
Honestly.
Akiha is one thing, but when did Hisui’s personality begin changing too?
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I'll leave it up to you, Hisui.
I will be back in the evening, so we can maliciously gossip about Nii-san then."
"Yes, let's."
…… So……
What's with all these shifts in Akiha's personality, and even Hisui's?

entries.japanese:
「行ってきます。
兄さんも行ってらっしゃい。
お土産は期待してませんから、どうぞごゆっくり」
　秋葉はロビーへと去っていく。
　と。
「あーあ、私も早くいい男みつけたいなー」
　なんて、大声で最後のアテツケを残していった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’m off. Have a pleasant trip yourself. I’m not expecting a souvenir, so please, take all the time you like.”
Akiha departs for the foyer.
Then.
“Oh, I wish I could find myself a good man soon, too.”
She left that final barb behind in a voice loud enough to fill the mansion.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I will be going.
Nii-san, you should be going as well.
I'm not hoping for any souvenirs, so please relax."
Akiha disappears towards the lobby.
And then.
"Man, I want to find a good man too!"
She leaves her last complaint loudly.

entries.japanese:
「………アイツ、日増しに元気になっていくな」
　ほんと、まさかこんなふうに事が運ぶとは思わなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“She gets more energetic by the day.”
Honestly, I never imagined things would turn out like this.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"……… She seems to be getting more cheerful each day."
I really didn't think things would end up this way.

entries.japanese:
……あの事件から、もう一年ほど経っている。
　変わった事は沢山あるけど、その中でも特筆すべきなのは秋葉と琥珀さんの事だろう。
　ぶっちゃけて言うと、秋葉は以前のままである。
　髪は赤いままで、普段は黒く染めているらしい。
……いや、薬品によるモノではなく、本人の意思で変えられるのだそうだ。
擬態かもしれない。
　……吸血衝動もそれなりにあるらしくて、たまに輸血用のパックをちゅーちゅー吸っている。
これも擬態かもしれない。
entries.maoEnglish:
Nearly a year has passed since that incident.
Many things have changed, but the most remarkable changes concern Akiha and Kohaku.
To put it bluntly, Akiha remains much as she was.
Her hair is still red, though she usually makes it black. Not with dye, apparently; she can change it by force of will. Perhaps it is some form of camouflage.
Her vampiric impulse seems to remain as well, and every so often she can be found slurping from a transfusion pack. Perhaps that is camouflage too.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… It's been about a year since then.
There's been a lot that has changed, but the biggest changes were in Akiha and Kohaku-san.
Simply put, Akiha is still like back then.
Her hair is still red, but she dyes it black…… No, it's not like she uses any chemicals, but it seems she can change it with her will.

…… She still has the urge to drink blood, so every once in a while she will suck on a blood pack used for transfusions.

entries.japanese:
秋葉はシキから、何かの悪霊じみたモノを受け継いでしまった。
　それが原因で秋葉は暴走してしまったワケだけど、あの一件の後、秋葉はソレの手綱を握ってしまったらしい。
　簡単に言うと、ソレは秋葉に移った時点でとても薄くなっていて、秋葉の性格が少し強気になる程度の影響で収まった、というのだ。
　……強気というよりはいじわるになった、というのが正しいと思うのだが、本人に言うと怒るのでやめておく。
entries.maoEnglish:
Akiha inherited something from SHIKI that resembles an evil spirit.
It drove her berserk, but after the incident she apparently managed to seize its reins.
Put simply, the Thing became greatly diluted when it passed into her, and its influence stopped at making her a little more assertive.
I would say meaner rather than assertive, but she gets angry if I tell her that, so I keep it to myself.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Akiha absorbed some sort of evil spirit from SHIKI.
That's why she originally went on a rampage, but since then, I guess she has control over it.
Simply put, it weakened when it transferred to Akiha, and its only influence is making Akiha strong-willed.
…… Well, she's more like a bully than strong-willed, but if I tell her that, she will get angry, so I'm not going to.

entries.japanese:
ソレは秋葉の性格をちょっと素直にさせただけではなく、どうも秋葉の力そのものも強くさせた。
　秋葉一人では抑えきれなかった遠野という『血』を、ソレのおかげで秋葉はうまくコントロールできてしまっている。
髪の色を隠せるのもそれのおかげだろう。
　……結論から言えば敵無し状態で、お兄ちゃんとしてはタイヘン扱いに困っている。
entries.maoEnglish:
The Thing does more than make Akiha a little more forthright; it also seems to have increased her power.
Thanks to it, Akiha can now control the Tohno blood she once could not contain alone. It must also be what lets her hide her hair color.
In short, she has become unbeatable, and as her brother I have no idea how I am supposed to handle her.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Not only did it make her a bit more honest, but it also increased her power.
Thanks to that, Akiha can exert better control over her Tohno blood.
That's probably why she can hide the color of her hair.
…… To say the results, she's pretty much invincible, and as her dear Onii-chan, it's pretty troublesome to keep her under control.

entries.japanese:
―――一方琥珀さんはと言うと、年が明けた頃に独立してしまった。
　秋葉が一人でも大丈夫になった事と、何か思う所があったのか、琥珀さんは長野の山奥にある遠野の分家の屋敷で働く事になった。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――Kohaku, meanwhile, struck out on her own around New Year’s.
Perhaps because Akiha could now manage by herself, perhaps for reasons of her own, Kohaku took a position at the mansion of a Tohno branch family deep in the mountains of Nagano.
entries.mirrorMoon:
---With regards to Kohaku-san, she became independent after the new year started.
Because Akiha is now fine by herself, and maybe because she is planning something, Kohaku-san left to work in a mansion of a branch of the Tohno family in the mountain recesses of Nagano.

entries.japanese:
……それでも週の終わりにはここに帰ってきて、四人で以前のように過ごしている。
　以前、どうしてそんな事をするんだと問いただしたら、なんでも向こうで調べたい事があるから、それが終わるまで我が侭を聞いてください、と返されてしまった。
　そう言われると惚れた弱みで、こっちとしては待つしかない。
　以来、俺と琥珀さんは週の終わりに再会するんだけど、屋敷では秋葉や翡翠がいるので二人きりにはなりにくかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
Even so, she returns here at the end of every week, and the four of us spend our time together just as before.
When I once pressed her to explain why she had left, she said there was something she wanted to investigate there and asked me to indulge her until she had finished.
I am the one in love, so all I can do is wait.
Since then, Kohaku and I reunite every weekend, but with Akiha and Hisui always at the mansion, finding time alone together is difficult.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… But at the end of the week, she comes back here and the four of us pass the time together like always.
Before, I asked her why she decided to do that, and she answered that there was something she wanted to investigate and that I should wait patiently until she is done.
Because I love her, I couldn't refuse, so all I can do now is wait.
Since then, even though Kohaku-san and I can meet at the end of every week, being alone together is difficult because of Akiha and Hisui.

entries.japanese:
ついでに言うと、琥珀さんと秋葉の中は良好だ。
　琥珀さんは秋葉の事を好いているし、秋葉も琥珀さんの事を気に入っている。
　……俺と琥珀さんの事は、秋葉も認めている、と公言はしていた。
公言はしているんだけど、
「いいわよ、別に。
兄さんは兄さんの勝手にするんだから、私だって私の勝手にするだけだもの」
　なんて、どうとっていいか解らない発言を付け足していた。
entries.maoEnglish:
For the record, Kohaku and Akiha get along extremely well.
Kohaku loves Akiha, and Akiha is very fond of Kohaku.
Akiha has publicly declared that she accepts Kohaku and me as a couple. She has declared it, certainly, but—
“I don’t mind. You do as you please, so I’ll simply do as I please.”
—she had added, leaving me with no idea how to interpret it.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Also, Kohaku-san and Akiha are on very good terms.
Kohaku-san likes Akiha, and Akiha cares for Kohaku-san.
…… About me and Kohaku-san, Akiha has acknowledged it openly.
She did, but…
"That's fine.
If you're going to do as you please, Nii-san, then I will just do as I please."
She added that random exclamation which can really mean anything.

entries.japanese:
「…………………はあ」
　という訳で、色々と込み入っている現状の中、琥珀さんから手紙がきた。
　俺に見せたいものがあるから夏休みを利用して長野まで出てきてほしい、という手紙を見て、すぐに今回の狂言旅行を計画したわけである。
　一応、俺はこれから有彦と一週間旅行をする事になっている。
　だっていうのに、秋葉と翡翠はよからぬ疑いをかけてくる。
……まったく。
二人とも、人の事をなんだと思っているんだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Haaah”
In the midst of this complicated state of affairs, a letter arrives from Kohaku.
The letter says she has something to show me and wants me to come to Nagano during summer vacation; the moment I read it, I begin planning this trip as a cover.
Officially, Arihiko and I are about to leave on a week-long trip.
Yet Akiha and Hisui persist in entertaining all sorts of improper suspicions. Honestly. What kind of person do those two imagine I am?
entries.mirrorMoon:
……………… *sigh*
That's how it was, and in the midst of all that complexity, I received a letter from Kohaku-san.
The letter said that there was something she wanted to show me, so she wants me to go to Nagano during summer break.
After seeing that, I planned this insane trip immediately.
I am supposed to be spending the week with Arihiko.
But Akiha and Hisui doubt me…… Geez, those two, what do they think of me?

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま」
「うわあ！」
　……心臓に、悪い。
　翡翠も、後ろから気配を殺して声をかけるのは止めてほしい。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki.”
“Wah!”
Bad for the heart.
I wish Hisui would stop erasing her presence before speaking to me from behind.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama."
"Uwaaa!"
…… My heart skipped a beat.
I wish Hisui would stop sneaking up on me and suddenly speaking like that.

entries.japanese:
「志貴さま、急がないと電車の時間に間に合わないのではないですか？」
「あ―――まず、そういえばのんびりしてる場合じゃなかった」
　用意のいい琥珀さんは、長野までの交通手段をきっかりと準備してくれていた。
　電車は指定席なので、時間を逃すと自腹で電車に乗らないといけなくなる。
……バイトもさせてもらえない貧乏学生には、それは切腹と同意語だ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki, will you not miss your train unless you hurry?”
“Ah―――damn, I forgot this is no time to dawdle.”
Ever-thorough Kohaku has arranged my transportation to Nagano down to the last detail.
The train has reserved seating, so if I miss it, I’ll have to buy another ticket myself. For a penniless student who is not even permitted a part-time job, that is synonymous with ritual suicide.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama, if you do not hurry, will you not miss the train?"
"Ah---crap, this isn't the time to be spacing out."
Always one to be prepared, Kohaku-san arranged transportation for me out to Nagano.
I have a reserved seat on the train, so if I miss it, I'll have to pay out of pocket to ride…… For a poor student without a job, that would be like suicide.

entries.japanese:
「わるい、俺もそろそろ行くよ。
ごめんな、朝っぱらから慌ただしくしちゃって………！」
　バッグを持って居間を後にする。
　その背中に、
「はい。
それでは、姉さんによろしく言っておいてください」
　なんていう、柔らかな翡翠の声がかけられた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Sorry, I’d better get going. I didn’t mean to make the whole morning so hectic…!”
I grabbed my bag and left the sitting room.
Behind me—
“Yes. Please give my sister my regards.”
Hisui’s gentle voice followed me out.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Sorry, I'll be off.
Sorry for being in a rush this morning………!"
Carrying my bag, I exit the sitting room.
From behind me,
"Yes, please send my best regards to Nee-san."
Hisui's soft voice reaches my ears.

entries.japanese:
―――――――汽車は走る。
　白く消え去ってしまいそうな陽射しの中、山間の田園を駆けていく。
entries.maoEnglish:
―――――――The train runs on.
Through mountain farmland it races beneath sunlight so white the world seems ready to vanish.
entries.mirrorMoon:
-------The train continues forward.
Bathed in the fragile, white sunlight, it runs past the mountain countryside.

entries.japanese:
あまりに田舎だからだろうか、車両には自分しかいなかった。
　窓際に座って、流れていく景色を眺める。
　暑い陽射しが視界を眩ませて、風の心地よさだけが頬に触れていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
Perhaps the countryside was simply that remote, but I had the entire carriage to myself.
I sat beside the window and watched the scenery flow past.
The blazing sun dazzled my eyes; only the pleasant wind touched my cheek.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Maybe it's because this is a really rural area, but I'm the only one in this car.
Sitting by the window, I stare at the flowing scenery.
The radiant sun illuminates my vision while the wind wafts comfortably on my cheeks.

entries.japanese:
「――――――――」
　手紙に視線を落とす。
　手紙には写真が同封されていて、あとは待ち合わせるべき場所の住所しかない。
　……住所といっても、それは『この街からこれこれこういった道順で行けます』といった、住所なんてない場所の標だ。
　同封された写真は、きっとその場所のものなのだろう。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――――――”
I lower my eyes to the letter.
A photograph is enclosed, along with nothing but the address where we are to meet.
Address is hardly the word; these are directions from the nearest town to a place with no address at all.
The photograph must show that place.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"--------"
I glance down at the letter.
There is a picture included in the letter, and the address of where we're meeting.
…… I say address, but there really isn't one.
It's more of "take a left here, a right there, and down this path" sort of place without an address.
This picture has to be of that place.

entries.japanese:
「――――――帰るべき場所、か」
　そこがどこであるのか、言われなくても予感はしていた。
　……琥珀さんは、きっと覚えていたんだろう。
　遠野槙久が口にしていた些細な言葉。
それを頼りにして、あの森を見つけ出したのかもしれない。
　黒い森。
　誰の目にもつかない、山奥にひっそりとあった古い屋敷。
　昔。
　七夜志貴という子供が暮らしていた、その場所を。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――――――The place I’m meant to return to.”
No one has to tell me where it is; I have already guessed.
Kohaku must have remembered.
A trivial remark once made by Makihisa Tohno. Perhaps she used it as a clue to find that forest.
The black forest.
The old mansion hidden deep in the mountains, unseen by anyone.
Long ago.
This was the place where a child named Shiki Nanaya lived.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------A place to return to, huh?"
Where it is, I do have a feeling without it being said.
…… Kohaku-san probably remembered where it was.
Those trivial words that Tohno Makihisa said.
Just working off that information, she must have found that forest.
That black forest.
Hidden from sight, the old mansion in the heart of the mountains.
Long ago.
The place where Nanaya Shiki spent his childhood.

entries.japanese:
「――――――――――」
　……目的地までにはあとしばらくかかる。
　陽射しがあんまりにも強すぎたせいだろう。
　目を閉じて椅子に背中を預けて、そのまま―――
―――そのまま、夢に落ちた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――――――――”
My destination is still some distance away.
Perhaps the sunlight is simply too fierce.
I close my eyes, lean back in my seat, and―――
―――fell into a dream.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----------"
…… It'll still be a while until I reach my destination.
Is it because the sunshine is unusually strong?
Closing my eyes, I lean back against the seat---
---like that, I fall into a dream.

entries.japanese:
白く霞むような太陽。
　人の手垢に汚れていない空気の匂い。
　空はどこまでも澄んで、ゆらめく陽炎が風を弾く。
　春は野草。
秋は星空。
冬は冷たい土だけの故郷。
　あと、夏は、たしか―――目を奪うような、明るい花。
―――そこに、彼女が待っている。
entries.maoEnglish:
A sun blurred white with haze.
The scent of air unstained by human hands.
The sky clear to its furthest reach, the trembling heat turning back the wind.
Wild grasses in spring. Stars in autumn. A homeland of nothing but cold earth in winter.
And in summer, if memory serves―――brilliant flowers bright enough to steal the eye.
―――There, she waits for me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The sunshine that is so white.
The smell of the air untainted by the touch of civilization.
The endlessly pure sky, the shimmering summer air that rides on the wind.
The wild grass of spring.
The starry sky of autumn.
The cold ground during winter of my home.
In summer, it was---the bright flowers that steal your breath away.
---There, she is waiting.

entries.japanese:
一面の花畑。
　むせ返る夏の匂い。
　明るい向日葵に負けないぐらいの華やかな笑顔。
　焦げるほどの熱さの中で、彼女は出迎えてくれる。
entries.maoEnglish:
A field of flowers stretching in every direction.
The heady scent of summer.
A radiant smile bright enough to rival the sunflowers.
Amid heat fierce enough to scorch, she welcomes me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
In front of a sea of flowers.
The overwhelming scent of summer.
A radiant smile that outshines even those sunflowers.
In the midst of the burning heat, she greets me.

entries.japanese:
――――――おかえりなさい、と。
　　　　　　今度こそ、本当に。
　　　　子供の頃の約束を叶えるように。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――――And says, “Welcome home.”
This time, truly.
At last making good on the promise we made as children.
entries.mirrorMoon:
------Welcome back.
This time, it is for real.
As if fulfilling that childhood promise at last.

entries.japanese:
琥珀・トゥルーエンディング、ごくろうさまでした。
　琥珀さんにはエンディングは一つしかありません。
　ここまで物語を進めてくれた遠野くんなら、琥珀さんの物語は“月姫”の裏方、残った全ての出来事を括る物と理解しているでしょう。
entries.maoEnglish:
Congratulations on completing Kohaku’s True Ending.
Kohaku has only one ending.
Having followed the story this far, Tohno will understand that her tale reveals what lay behind TSUKIHIME and gathers together every remaining thread.
entries.mirrorMoon:
You have reached Kohaku's True Ending.
Well done.
There is only one ending for Kohaku-san.
If you have come this far, you should understand that Kohaku-san's story is the propman of "Tsukihime", the story to tie up all the remaining events.

entries.japanese:
本当に、お疲れ様でした。
　長い長い時間をへて、彼女たちの物語は幕を下ろしたのです。
entries.maoEnglish:
Truly, thank you for all your effort.
After so very long, the curtain has fallen on the stories of these women.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Thank you so much for all your hard work.
After a long time, their stories have ended.

entries.japanese:
――――――ですが、待ってください。
　まだ一人だけ残された人物がいます。
　それはそう、この物語の主人公です。
　彼の物語は終わっていません。
　天には冴え凍える真円の月。
　けれどその月も永劫不変ではありえない。
　全ての物語の終幕のあと。
　遠野志貴の物語は、そこで終わりを迎える事を待っています―――――
entries.maoEnglish:
――――――But wait.
One person still remains.
Yes—the protagonist of this story.
His tale is not yet over.
A perfect full moon hangs clear and frozen in the heavens.
But even that moon cannot remain unchanged forever.
After every other story’s curtain has fallen.
The tale of Shiki Tohno waits there to meet its own ending—
entries.mirrorMoon:
------But, please wait.
There is still one person remaining.
Yes, that is this story's main character.
His story is not over yet.
In the heavens is the cold, round moon.
But even that moon cannot be eternally the same.
After the end of all stories,
the story of Tohno Shiki is waiting to be finished there-----

様子を見にいこう。
entries.maoEnglish: 2. …I can’t let it go. I’ll see what’s happening.

entries.japanese:
犬の遠吠えはまだ続いている。
　このままじゃはっきりいって眠れない。
　……眠れないけど、まあ、それは常人の神経のレヴェルの話だ。
「………………眠いので、パス」
　シーツをかぶって、ベッドに横になる。
　犬の遠吠えなんて、道を走る自動車の音だと思えばいい。
entries.maoEnglish:
The dogs were still howling.
There was no way anyone could sleep through this.
That was true only for someone with normal nerves.
“I’m too sleepy, so I’ll pass.”
I pulled the sheet over my head and lay down.
I could pretend the howling was only traffic passing on the road.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The howling continues.
There's no way I can sleep like this.
…… I can't sleep, but that's just normal.
"……………… I'm sleepy, so I'll pass."
Pulling the sheets over me, I stretch out on the bed.
I can just think of the howling as the sound of something mundane, like cars driving by on the street.

entries.japanese:
「………はあ」
　今日はなんだか長い一日だった。
　慣れない屋敷での夕食や秋葉たちとの会話で精神も疲れきっている。
その前には犬の遠吠えなんて、ただの雑音に他ならない。
　目を閉じてしまえば、あとはゆるやかに眠りの中へと落ちていけた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Haa…”
It had been an awfully long day.
Dinner in the unfamiliar estate and all those conversations with Akiha and the others had exhausted me. Against that, the dogs were nothing but background noise.
Once I closed my eyes, I slipped gently into sleep.
entries.mirrorMoon:
*sigh*
Today's been a very long day.
I'm mentally tired from eating dinner in this unfamiliar mansion and my conversations with Akiha and everyone else.
After all that, the howling is just background noise.
I close my eyes and gently fall asleep.

entries.japanese:
「――――ん」
　なにか、物音が聞こえた気がした。
　ねぼけまなこで時計を見てみると、時刻は午前二時になったばかりだ。
　……さっきの野犬の騒ぎから、二時間ほど経っている。
　野犬の鳴き声はとっくにやんでいた。
　屋敷の夜は時計の秒針の音が響くぐらい、静かだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――Mm?”
I thought I heard something.
Peering blearily at the clock, I saw that it had just turned two in the morning.
About two hours had passed since the uproar with the stray dogs.
Their howling had long since stopped.
The estate was so quiet that the ticking clock carried through the night.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----Nng."
I think I just heard something.
Half-awake, I look at the clock.
It's just past two.
…… It's been about two hours since I heard the dogs howling.
The dogs' howling has already stopped.
The mansion is so quiet, I can hear the clock ticking in the silence.

entries.japanese:
「――――――？」
　また物音が聞こえた。
　……屋敷の中……ロビーのほうだろうか。
「―――――まさか、泥棒？」
　ありえない話じゃない。
　この屋敷は金目のものでしか構成されていないとんでもない屋敷だ。
くわえて、今は俺と秋葉、琥珀さんと翡翠しかいないっていう無用心ぶりである。
「……………」
　ベッドから出て、足音を立てないように部屋を出る。
entries.maoEnglish:
“――――――?”
There it was again.
Somewhere inside the estate—perhaps near the foyer.
“―――――A burglar?”
It was not impossible.
This enormous estate seemed to be made entirely of valuables. On top of that, only Akiha, Kohaku, Hisui, and I were living here.
“…”
I slipped out of bed and left the room without making a sound.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------?"
I hear it again.
…… Inside the mansion…… from the lobby?
"-----Could it be a burglar?"
It's not impossible.
The mansion's contents are outrageously valuable.
On top of that, with no one here now except Kohaku-san, Hisui, Akiha and myself, it's very insecure.
"……………"
I get out of bed, and slip out of the room quietly.

entries.japanese:
……もし泥棒だったら秋葉たちが危ないし、こればっかりは見過ごしておけない。
　二階からロビーの様子を眺めるだけなら、こっちにも危険はないと思う。
entries.maoEnglish:
If it was a burglar, Akiha and the others might be in danger, and I could not ignore that.
Watching the foyer from the second floor should not put me at any risk.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… If it's a burglar, Akiha and everyone will be in danger, so I can't let this one go.
I'll just look down from the second floor into the lobby; that should be safe enough.

entries.japanese:
……ロビーには異状はない。
「……………！」
　いや、誰かいる。
　玄関から入ってきて、ふらふらとおぼつかない足取りでロビーを横切っていく姿は―――
「あき……は？」
　秋葉は二階の自分の部屋にではなく、一階の西館へ歩いていく。
　その先にあるものは琥珀さんの部屋と、親父の部屋ぐらいのものだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
Nothing seemed amiss in the foyer.
“……!”
No—someone was there.
A figure had entered through the front door and was staggering unsteadily across the foyer—
“Aki—ha?”
Instead of going upstairs to her room, Akiha headed into the west wing on the ground floor.
The only rooms that way were Kohaku’s and Father’s.
entries.mirrorMoon:
There's nothing wrong there.
"……………!"
No, someone's there.
The figure that enters from the entrance and crosses the lobby with wobbling, uncertain steps, is---
"Aki…… ha?"
She's not going to her own room on the second floor, but to the first floor of the west wing.
The only things there are Kohaku-san's room and my old man's room.

entries.japanese:
「……なにしてたんだ、アイツ。
こんな夜更けに……」
　呟いてみても答えはない。
　しばらくロビーの様子を眺めてから、大人しく自分の部屋に戻ることにした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“……What was she doing out this late?”
The empty foyer offered no answer.
After watching for a while longer, I returned quietly to my room.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… What's she doing at this time of night……?"
I can murmur all I want, but there won't be any answers forthcoming.
After gazing at the lobby for a while, I decide to return to my room.

entries.japanese:
……まあ、何か用事があったのか、それとも琥珀さんに会いにいったのかもしれない。
　こっちもこっそり盗み見ていたという負い目もあるし、あれこれ詮索するのも気が引ける。
「……寝よ寝よ。
明日も学校だ」
　ベッドにもぐりこんで、目を閉じる。
―――眠りに落ちる途中。
　ロビーで見かけた、うつろな瞳をした秋葉の姿が、なにかよくない物のように、何度も何度も思い返されていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
Perhaps she had some errand, or had gone to see Kohaku.
I felt guilty enough for spying on her, so prying any further seemed wrong.
“Back to bed. I have school tomorrow.”
I crawled beneath the covers and closed my eyes.
―――As I drifted back to sleep.
The image of Akiha crossing the foyer with vacant eyes returned to me again and again, like the memory of something ominous.
entries.mirrorMoon:
……… Well, she probably had something to do, or went to see Kohaku-san.
I feel bad about sneaking around and watching her, and I don't want to just ask her about everything she does.
"…… Sleep, sleep.
There's school tomorrow."
I bury myself in bed and close my eyes.
---As I fall asleep,
my thoughts keep returning over and over to Akiha's hollow-eyed figure in the lobby, and how something seemed wrong.

entries.japanese:
……いや、秋葉との約束を守ろう。
　秋葉が行くなっていうんだから、些細な好奇心で約束を破るわけにはいかない。
「……ん」
　ゆったりとした眠気が体に浸透していく。
　今夜はこのまま、大人しく眠る事にしよう。
entries.maoEnglish:
No, I would keep my promise to Akiha.
Akiha had told me not to go, so I could not break my word over idle curiosity.
“Nn.”
A gentle drowsiness seeped through my body.
I decided to behave myself and go to sleep.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… no, I'll keep my promise with Akiha.
Akiha told me not to go there, and I can't break a promise just because of trifling curiosity.
"…… Nn."
A calm drowsiness permeates my body.
I'll keep quiet tonight and sleep.

entries.japanese: ――――喉が、カラカラに渇いて、熱い。
entries.maoEnglish: ――――My throat is parched dry and burning hot.
entries.mirrorMoon: ----My throat, dry with thirst, hot.

entries.japanese:
――――――このままでは眠れない。
　　　　　　起きて、水を飲みに行こう。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――――I can’t sleep like this.
I should get up and find some water.
entries.mirrorMoon:
------I can't sleep like this.
I'll go and get a drink of water.

entries.japanese:
夜の街に出たようだ。
　目を血走らせて誰か通りかからないか待っているのか。
entries.maoEnglish:
I seem to have gone out into the city at night.
With eyes bloodshot, am I waiting for someone to pass?
entries.mirrorMoon:
It seems I went into town at night.
It seems like I'm waiting with bloodshot eyes for someone to pass by.

entries.maoEnglish: ――――――Everything burned.
entries.mirrorMoon: ------It is hot.

entries.japanese:
ふと、窓ガラスに映った顔が見えた。
　目は血走っていて、とても正気には見えなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
My face appears suddenly in a darkened window.
Its bloodshot eyes look anything but sane.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Suddenly, I see a face reflected in the window.
The eyes are bloodshot, and the face looks quite insane.

entries.japanese: ――――――ただ、熱かった。
entries.maoEnglish: ――――――There was nothing but the heat.
entries.mirrorMoon: ------It is just so hot.

entries.japanese:
獲物を見つけたようだ。
　背後から首をしめて、それで終わり。
　見知らぬ女性はそれで死んでしまったみたいだった。
entries.maoEnglish:
A victim, found.
A chokehold from behind, and it was over.
A woman I’d never seen before seemed to die just like that.
entries.mirrorMoon:
It seems I found my prey.
Strangling her from behind, it's all over.
It seems that the unknown woman has died just from that.

entries.japanese: ―――俺は、ただ、熱かった。
entries.maoEnglish: ―――I was only burning hot.
entries.mirrorMoon: ---I am just, so hot.

entries.japanese:
死体を連れこんで、喉元に食らいついたのか。
　じゅるじゅる、という音が聞こえる。
　喉もとから、肉ごとかみ切るように血を飲んで、喉の渇きを癒している。
entries.maoEnglish:
The corpse must have been dragged somewhere, then bitten at the throat.
Wet, sucking sounds.
Blood gulped down from the neck, teeth shearing through flesh along with it, slaking that terrible thirst.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Taking the dead body, perhaps I bit into its throat.
There's a gurgling sound.
Drinking the blood flowing out of the rended neck, my thirst is quenched.

entries.japanese: ―――わからない。
entries.maoEnglish: ―――I don’t understand.
entries.mirrorMoon: ---I don't understand.

entries.japanese:
はあはあという呼吸音。
　よほど。
　よほどその行為は興奮するのか。
　死体の胸に指をつきいれた。
　肉を潰していく音、骨を崩していく音。
　心臓を素手でえぐりだす、音。
entries.maoEnglish:
Panting.
So much.
Was the act truly that exciting?
Fingers plunged into the corpse’s chest.
The sound of flesh pulping, the sound of bones breaking.
The sound of a heart being torn out with bare hands.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The sound of heavy breathing.
Does this act…
Does this act really excite me so much?
I stick my finger in the chest of the dead body.
The sound of crushing meat, the sound of breaking bones.
The sound of a heart being ripped out with my bare hand.

entries.japanese: ―――見ているだけで、頭が真っ白になる。
entries.maoEnglish: ―――The mere sight of it wipes my mind clean.
entries.mirrorMoon: ---As I watch, my head fills with pure white.

entries.japanese:
その、究極の略奪。
　頂点に位置する背徳性。
　それが、見ているものさえ熱くさせる。
　たとえそれがマイナスの快楽にしたって、熱くなるということには、かわりはないらしい。
entries.maoEnglish:
The ultimate act of plunder.
Transgression at its absolute height.
It sets even the watcher burning.
Pleasure with a minus sign before it is still pleasure enough to burn.
entries.mirrorMoon:
This, the ultimate pillage.
The height of immorality.
Just gazing at it, I feel hot.
You might say it's negative pleasure, but for making one hot, it's still the same.

entries.japanese: ―――俺には、わからない。
entries.maoEnglish: ―――I don’t understand it.
entries.mirrorMoon: ---I don't understand.

entries.japanese:
熱い血液を口からたらして、恍惚とした目で、夜空を見上げていた。
　長い髪が乱れる。
　頭上には螺旋の空。
　なんてキレイな、銀色の月。
entries.maoEnglish:
Hot blood trailed from the mouth as ecstatic eyes lifted to the night sky.
Long hair streamed wild.
Above, the heavens spiraled.
What a beautiful silver moon.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Hot blood dripping from my mouth, I gaze up at the night sky entranced.
My long hair waves around.
Above is the spiraling sky.
Such a beautiful, silver moon.

entries.japanese:
―――だから、わからない。
　　　俺は、ただ、熱かっただけなのに――――
entries.maoEnglish:
―――That’s why I don’t understand.
I was only burning hot, and yet――――
entries.mirrorMoon:
---And so, I don't understand.
I am just, only, hot----

entries.japanese:
いつもとは違う帰り道を歩く。
　見知らぬ道を通り抜けて、段々と遠野の屋敷へ近付いていく。
　まわりの風景は、知らない風景ではなかった。
　少なくとも自分は八年前───九歳まで遠野の屋敷で暮らしていたから、屋敷へ帰る道は初めてというわけでもないのだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
I followed a different road home than usual.
Unknown streets carried me steadily closer to the Tohno estate.
Yet the scenery around them was not entirely unfamiliar.
I had lived at the estate until I was nine, eight years ago, so this was not truly my first journey home.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I walk along a different path than the one I usually take.
Passing through unfamiliar streets, I slowly approach the Tohno mansion.
The surroundings are not completely unfamiliar.
After all, I had lived here until I was nine years old---eight years ago.
This is not the first time I have taken this path back to the mansion.

entries.japanese:
少しだけ気持ちは複雑だ。
　この帰り道は懐かしくて、新鮮でもある。
　さっきまで遠野の家に戻るのは気が進まなかったっていうのに、今はそれほどイヤでもなくなっている。
entries.maoEnglish:
My feelings were complicated.
The road seemed nostalgic and new at once.
Only a little while ago, I had dreaded returning to the Tohno home, but now the prospect no longer seemed so unpleasant.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… My feelings are a little complex.
The path home is nostalgic, yet fresh.
Up until just now, I had not looked forward to returning to the Tohno household.
Now, it doesn't seem so bad.

entries.japanese:
……遠野志貴が九歳まで暮らしていた家。
　そこにあるのは日本じゃ場違いな洋館で、今は妹の秋葉が残っているという話だ。
　俺を嫌っていた父親───遠野家の当主である遠野槙久は、先日他界したという。
entries.maoEnglish:
The house where Shiki Tohno had lived until the age of nine.
An absurdly out-of-place Western house stood there, and I had been told my younger sister Akiha still lived there.
My father, who had hated me───the head of the Tohno family, Makihisa Tohno───was said to have died only recently.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… The house I lived in until I was nine years old.
Right now, my sister Akiha is in that utterly un-Japanese western-style mansion.
Tohno Makihisa--My old man who hated me, and the master of the Tohno household, died a few days ago.

entries.japanese:
母親は秋葉が生まれた時に病死してしまっていたから、遠野の人間は自分と、妹である秋葉の二人きりになってしまった。
　本来なら長男である自分───遠野志貴が遠野家の跡取りになるのだろうけれど、自分にはそんな権利はない。
entries.maoEnglish:
Our mother had died of illness when Akiha was born, so my sister and I were now the only Tohnos left.
Ordinarily, as the eldest son, I───Shiki Tohno───would have inherited the family, but I no longer had that right.
entries.mirrorMoon:
My mother died from illness after Akiha was born, so the Tohnos had dwindled down to me and my sister.
Being the eldest son, you would think I would stand to become the Tohno heir… but I have no such privilege.

entries.japanese:
遠野家の跡取りになる、という事はがんじがらめの教育を受けるという事だ。
　それがイヤで自由に暮らしていて、父親から何度小言を言われたかわからない。
　そんな折、俺は事故に巻き込まれて病弱な体になってしまい、父親はこれ幸いにと俺を切り捨てた。
　父親曰く『たとえ長男であろうと、いつ死ぬかわからない者を後継者にはできん』とかなんとか。
　あいにく父親の予想を裏切って回復してしまったけれど、その頃には遠野家の跡取りは妹の秋葉に決められていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
Becoming the Tohno heir meant submitting to an education that bound you hand and foot.
I hated that and lived as freely as I could, earning more lectures from my father than I could count.
Then I was caught in the accident and left sickly, and my father seized the opportunity to cast me aside. His explanation was something like, “Eldest son or not, I cannot make an heir of someone who might die at any moment.”
Unfortunately for him, I recovered, but by then my sister Akiha had been chosen to inherit the Tohno family.
entries.mirrorMoon:
To become the Tohno heir means being bound by a strict upbringing.
I have lost count of the number of times my father scolded me over my dislike of not being able to live freely.
That was when I got involved in that accident, and my body became weakened… My father saw it as a good opportunity to get rid of me.
His reasoning was something along the lines of "someone who could die any moment can't become the heir, even if he is the eldest son".
Sadly for my father, I betrayed his expectations by making a recovery, but my sister Akiha was already deemed to be the heir to the Tohno household.

entries.japanese:
それまで遠野の娘に相応しいように、と厳格に育てられていた秋葉は、それからよけい厳しく育てられたらしい。
　昔───事故に巻き込まれるまでは一緒に屋敷の庭で遊んだ秋葉とは、あれからまったく会っていない。
entries.maoEnglish:
Akiha had already been raised under strict discipline to make her a proper daughter of the Tohno family; after that, I heard, her upbringing became harsher still.
Long ago───before the accident───we had played together in the estate gardens, but I had not seen her once in the eight years since.
entries.mirrorMoon:
And so I've heard that Akiha, who was already being raised harshly in order to become a proper daughter of the Tohno household, received an even harsher upbringing since then.
That was a long time ago--I played together with Akiha in the mansion back before the accident.
After that, I never saw her again.

entries.japanese:
……八年前に棄てた屋敷の生活。
　八年間という歳月は長くて、あの頃の記憶は大部分が薄れてしまっている。
　それでも。
　ある事柄だけは、今でも強く心に焼き付いている。
　それは―――――
entries.maoEnglish:
The life at the estate I abandoned eight years ago.
Eight years is a long time, and most of my memories from then had faded.
Even so.
One thing remained seared into my heart.
It was―――――
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… The life in the mansion I abandoned eight years ago.
Those eight years were long, and my memories of that time have largely faded.
But in spite of that, there is one thing that even now continues to burn strongly within my heart, and that is---
