entries.japanese: ―――――――ふと、目が覚めた。
entries.maoEnglish: ―――――――Then, without warning, I woke.
entries.mirrorMoon: ------Suddenly, I wake up.

entries.japanese:
広い夜。
　見渡すかぎりの草原の中で、ぼんやりと月を見ていた。
　周りには誰もいない。
　人の気配もなければ獣の息遣いも皆無だ。
　ここ数日、少しばかり無理をしたせいか。
　一人でぼんやりとしていたくて草原に寝転がっただけなのだが、そのまま沈み込むように眠ってしまったらしい。
entries.maoEnglish:
Night lay wide around me.
I was alone in an endless field, gazing vaguely at the moon.
There was no one nearby.
There was no sign of another person, not even the breathing of an animal.
Perhaps I had pushed myself too hard these last few days.
I had only stretched out in the grass because I wanted to be alone with my thoughts, but apparently I had sunk straight into sleep.
entries.mirrorMoon:
A vast night.
In the midst of a grassy field that extends as far as the eye can see, I stare blankly at the moon.
There is no one else here.
No signs of human presence; no sounds from any animals.
Maybe it's because I've pushed myself too hard these past couple of days.
I just wanted to lie down quietly and be alone, but it seems I fell asleep.

entries.japanese:
それは、明るい闇だった。
　月が近いせいだろう。
　昨夜黒い海に似ていた草原は何かのステージのように明るい。
　冴え冴えとした月光に照らし上げられた広場。
　それが、どこかの劇場のようだと思った。
　ただ、周囲に幕はない。
　世界は見渡すかぎりの草原で、カーテンのような木々もなければ、観客も団員もありはしない。
entries.maoEnglish:
It was a luminous darkness.
Perhaps it was because the moon hung so close.
The field that had looked like a black sea the night before now shone like a stage.
An open space washed in keen, cold moonlight.
A theater, I thought.
But there were no curtains.
The world was grassland as far as I could see, without so much as a line of trees to serve as drapery—and no audience, no players.
entries.mirrorMoon:
It was a bright darkness.
Probably because the moon is hanging so low.
The grassy field that looked like a black sea last night is bright, like some sort of a stage.
A clearing illuminated by sharp, sharp moonlight.
I thought it was like a theater somewhere.
Only, there are no curtains around.
This field that sweeps far and wide is devoid of any curtains of trees, nor is there an audience or stage crew.

entries.japanese:
周囲には何もない。
　あるものは月光と白い闇だけ。
　風は吹かず、草は揺れる事さえしなかった。
――――なんて、!w2000静か。
　昨日までの喧騒が何かの冗談のように思えて、軽く笑った。
　いや、冗談というのなら。
　今までの時間は幸せすぎて、振り返れば幻のようにしか思えない。
entries.maoEnglish:
There was nothing around me.
Nothing but moonlight and white darkness.
No wind blew, nor did a blade of grass stir.
――――How!w2000 quiet.
The clamor of the day before seemed like some elaborate joke, and I gave a soft laugh.
No—if anything was a joke.
All the time before this had been too happy; looking back, it could only seem like a dream.
entries.mirrorMoon:
There's nothing here.
The only things here are the moonlight and the white darkness.
The wind does not blow and the grass does not even sway.
----How quiet.
I laugh quietly as it feels like all the commotion until yesterday was just a joke.
No, if you talk about jokes,
then my life until now was so happy that, looking back at it, it seems like it was just an illusion.

entries.japanese:
さまざまな出来事があった。
　その中にはとんでもないような事もあって、自分の人生はひどく緩急のついた物だったと思う。
　当たり前のコトと、当たり前ではなかったコト。
　幻のように思えるのは、その全てだ。
　どんな些細な出来事だって、思い返してみれば偶然の上に成り立っている。
　呆れるぐらい同じ繰り返しの日々だったのに、同じ一日なんて一つもなかった。
　なら、それは。
　一つ一つがもう戻りえない、かけがえのない時間だという事ではなかったのか。
entries.maoEnglish:
So many things had happened.
Some were almost beyond belief, and my life had veered so violently between stillness and turmoil that it hardly seemed like one life at all.
Things that were ordinary, and things that had never been ordinary.
All of it felt like a dream.
Even the smallest event, when I looked back, rested upon a chain of accidents.
The days had repeated themselves with mind-numbing familiarity, yet no two had ever been the same.
If so.
Did that not mean each one had been irreplaceable—a moment that could never return?
entries.mirrorMoon:
A lot of things have happened.
There were a lot of amazing things that occurred, and my life changed pace quite often.
The expected, and the unexpected.
Everything was illusory.
Looking back, it seems that no matter how trivial things seemed, all those coincidences built on each other.
The days were only a repetition of each other, but no two days were quite the same.
Then, that means…
Perhaps each and every one of them was an irreplaceable moment I can never return to.

entries.japanese:
沢山の出来事を思い返す。
　懐かしくて笑いがこぼれる。
　この先、この思い出とは違う、また新しいコトが続いていくのかと思うと、なにやら目眩がした。
　それは嬉しいとか楽しみだとか、頭を抱えたくなるような不安とか、まあ悲喜交々。
――――――どくん、と。
　一際高く、心臓が鳴った。
entries.maoEnglish:
I remembered one thing after another.
Nostalgia drew a smile from me.
The thought that new days, different from every memory I possessed, would continue unfolding ahead left me almost dizzy.
Happiness, anticipation, anxieties that made me want to clutch my head—the usual tangle of joy and sorrow.
――――――Thump.
My heart struck once, louder than before.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I recall many things that happened.
The memories are so nostalgic, it makes me smile.
Just the thought of the new experiences awaiting me in the future, different from those of my past, makes me dizzy.
Truly a mix of emotions.
Happiness, excitement, and enough worries to give me a headache.
------Thump.
My heart beats loudly once.

entries.japanese:
その後にやってくるものは、いつもの貧血だ。
　貧血はしばらく続いて、なんとか治まってくれた。
entries.maoEnglish:
A spell of anemia followed, as it always did.
It lingered for a while, then finally subsided.
entries.mirrorMoon:
What comes after is my usual anemia.
The dizziness continues for a while, but eventually disappears.

entries.japanese:
胸の傷が癒えた所で貧血は無くならない。
　どうも、この体が不安定なのは胸の傷だけが原因、という訳ではなかったようだ。
　……まあ、もともと。
　死のカタチを視れる、というのだから、人よりは死というものに近い位置にいるという事だし。
　そんな自分が人並に長生きできる、なんて事はあんまり考えた事もなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
Healing the wound in my chest had not cured the anemia.
Apparently that injury had never been the only reason my body was so unstable.
Still, I had always known.
A person who could see the shape of death had to stand closer to death than other people did.
I had never given much thought to the possibility that someone like me might live an ordinary span.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Even though the wound on my chest healed, my anemia didn't go away.
It seems like my fragile health wasn't caused by the wound on my chest alone.
…… Well, of course.
Being able to perceive the shape of death means I stand much closer to death than others.
To be honest, I never thought about living a long life, like ordinary people.

entries.japanese:
どくん、という心音。
　柄にもなく、あとどのくらいの時間を走っていけるのかな、と考えてみる。
　結論はつまらなかった。
　何故なら、明日止まってしまおうと何十年先に止まってしまおうと、それは――――
entries.maoEnglish:
Another thump of my heart.
Uncharacteristically, I wondered how much longer I would be able to keep running.
The answer was dull and obvious.
Because whether it stopped tomorrow or decades from now, the answer would be—
entries.mirrorMoon:
Thump.
The sound of my heart beating.
It's not like me to think of this, but I wonder just how long I can keep running through time.
The conclusion is rather uninteresting.
Because, even if it stops tomorrow, or in a few decades, still----

entries.japanese:
「君。
そんな所で倒れてると危ないわよ」
――――と。
　そんな、懐かしい、声がした。
entries.maoEnglish:
“You. It’s dangerous to lie around in a place like that.”
――――Then.
I heard a voice I knew from long, long ago.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Hey you.
It's dangerous just lying around like that."
----And.
I hear a familiar voice.

entries.japanese:
「え―――――」
「え、じゃないでしょ。
こんな夜更けに草むらで寝てるなんてよっぽど暇なのね。
気をつけなさい、あやうく蹴りとばされるとこだったんだから」
　トランクを片手にもって、彼女は不機嫌そうに言った。
entries.maoEnglish:
“What―――――”
“Don’t ‘what’ me. You must have a great deal of time to waste if you’re sleeping in the grass this late at night. Be careful or I might have kicked you across the field.”
Holding a suitcase in one hand, she spoke with evident displeasure.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Eh…?"
"What do you mean, 'eh'?
You have an awful lot of free time on your hands if you can just sleep around here in the middle of the night.
I was this close to kicking you, so you better watch out."
She says this grumpily while carrying a trunk in one hand.

entries.japanese:
「――ふうん。
蹴り飛ばされるって、誰にですか」
　横になった身体をわずかに起こす。
「ばかね、そんなの決まってるじゃない。
ここにいるのは私と君だけなんだから、私以外に誰がいるっていうの？」
　腕を組んで、自信たっぷりに彼女は言った。
「は――――――」
　こみ上げてくる笑いを堪えて、月と彼女を見上げる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Oh? Kicked by whom, exactly?”
I raised myself slightly from the grass.
“Don’t be stupid. You and I are the only people here, so who else could it be?”
She folded her arms and delivered this with perfect confidence.
“Ha――――――”
Fighting down the laughter rising in me, I looked up at her and the moon.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Oh…?
Kicked?
And by who?"
I lift myself up.
"Isn't it obvious, stupid?
You and I are the only ones here, so who else could it be but me?"
She declares this confidently as she folds her arms.
"Ha-------"
Stifling the laughter spilling out of me, I gaze up at her and the moon.

entries.japanese:
「……まさかなあ。
なんとなく会える気はしてたけど、それが今日とは思ってなかった」
「奇遇ね。
私もここで会えるとは思ってなかった。
　君が来てるってコトは聞いてたけど、結局一度も会わなかったでしょう？
　だから今回は縁がないんだなって。
まあ、もっとも――――」
「顔を合わせてたら、アレですか」
「そ。
一応、私も協会側の人間だしね。
教会とは仲が悪いの」
　少しも悪びれるところがなく、彼女は笑った。
　本当に笑いを堪えるのがタイヘンだ。
　この人は、あの時からこれっぽっちも変わってなくて、嬉しくなる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I can’t believe it. I had a feeling we might meet, but I never imagined it would be tonight.”
“What a coincidence. I didn’t expect to meet you here either.
I heard you were in the area, but we never crossed paths, did we? I thought it simply wasn’t meant to happen this time. Though, of course—”
“If we had met, it would have been trouble?”
“Exactly. I’m affiliated with the Association, after all. We don’t get along with the Church.”
She laughed without the slightest remorse.
It was becoming desperately hard not to laugh myself.
She had not changed one bit since that day, and the discovery delighted me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I can't believe it… I somehow felt that I'd meet you, but I didn't think that day would be today."
"What a coincidence.
I didn't expect to see you here, either.
I heard you were here, but we never did meet up, did we?
So I was thinking that it was our fate this time not to meet.
Although…"
"If we did see each other, it would have caused trouble, right?"
"Right.
I am a member of the Association, after all.
We're not quite on good terms with The Church."
She laughs without any hint of guilt.
It really is hard holding back my laughter.
It makes me happy that this person hasn't changed one bit since that day we met.

entries.japanese:
「で、やる事もなくなったし明日にでもここを発つ予定だったんだ。
　ほら、今回の件って私の責任でもあったでしょう？
　だから最後の確認でここに寄ったみたら、危うく一般人を蹴りとばしそうになったわけ」
「……それじゃ縁があったんですよ。
白状すると、俺も少しだけ会えそうな気がしてました」
　にこりと笑う。
「そうね、こういう縁なら歓迎するわ」
　それに彼女はまったく同じ笑みを返した。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I’d finished everything I came to do and planned to leave tomorrow.
This whole affair was partly my responsibility, remember? I stopped by for one final inspection and nearly kicked an innocent civilian.”
“Then I suppose we were meant to meet. To tell the truth, I had a faint feeling I might see you too.”
I smiled.
“Yes, this is the kind of fate I’m happy to welcome.”
She answered with exactly the same smile.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"And, since I ran out of things to do, I was going to leave here tomorrow.
See, this incident was partially my fault, you know?
So, I stopped by here for a final check, and I almost ended up kicking some ordinary person."
"Then… we were fated to meet.
To be honest, I felt we would meet up again."
I smile.
"You're right.
I welcome this sort of fate."
She flashes me an identical smile in return.

entries.japanese:
「久しぶり。
大きくなったわね、志貴」
「はい。
先生もお変わりなく」
　味も素っ気もない挨拶を交わして、真剣な目で先生を見返した。
entries.maoEnglish:
“It’s been a long time. You’ve grown, Shiki.”
“Yes. You haven’t changed at all, Teacher.”
We exchanged greetings so plain they were almost curt, then I met my teacher’s eyes in earnest.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Long time no see.
You've grown up, Shiki."
"Yes.
You seem to be doing well too, Sensei."
Returning her plain greeting, I look back at Sensei with serious eyes.

entries.japanese:
草むらに座って話をした。
　あの時と同じように、なんでもない話だけをする。
　今までの事やこれからの事が話題にあがったのは、本当にわずかな時間だった。
entries.maoEnglish:
We sat in the grass and talked.
Just as we had then, we spoke only of inconsequential things.
We spent very little time on what had happened since, or what would come next.
entries.mirrorMoon:
We sit in the field of grass and talk.
We talk about senseless things, just like the old days.
It was only briefly that we talked about what had happened and what we were going to do in the future.

entries.japanese:
「そろそろ時間か。
私、ここに長居する気はないから。
夜明け前には出るから、ここでお別れね」
　言って、先生は立ち上がる。
　それに倣ってこっちも立ち上が―――ろうとして、躓いた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“It’s about time. I don’t intend to linger here. I’ll be gone before dawn, so this is where we part.”
With that, Teacher stood.
I followed her example—or tried to, and stumbled.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"It's about time.
I don't plan on staying here long.
I'm leaving before dawn, so we'll have to part here."
Saying that, Sensei stands up.
I try to stand up with her… but I collapse.

entries.japanese:
「……志貴？」
　先生の声が聞こえる。
　数回深呼吸をして立ち上がる。
「……まいったな。
昨日までの不眠不休がたたってるようです」
「みたいね。
その目眩が君の最大の欠点、か。
　見たところ怪我はないようだけど、体のほうは無事？」
「ええ、おかげさまで。
先生と違って、ちゃんと人並みの体をしてますよ」
「ふうん……君がそういうなら信じるけど」
　ちらり、と意味ありげな視線を向けて、先生はまっすぐにこちらを見た。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Shiki?”
I heard her voice.
After several deep breaths, I managed to stand.
“This is embarrassing. I suppose all those sleepless nights finally caught up with me.”
“It would seem so. That dizziness is your greatest weakness, then.
You don’t appear to be injured, but is your body all right?”
“Yes, thanks to you. Unlike yours, mine is a perfectly ordinary human body.”
“Hmm—if you say so, I’ll believe you.”
She gave me a brief, suggestive glance, then faced me squarely.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"…… Shiki?"
I can hear her voice.
I take a few deep breaths and stand back up.
"…… Dang.
It seems like no sleep or rest until last night just hit me."
"Looks like it.
That dizziness is your biggest weakness.
You don't look like you have any injuries.
Is your body alright?"
"Yeah, thanks.
Unlike you, I have a normal body."
"Hmm… If you say so."
She glances at me meaningfully, then looks directly into my eyes.

entries.japanese:
「――――志貴。
君、自分が長くないって気付いてる？」
　その、はっきりとした、言葉。
「―――――――――」
　驚きで目が点になる。
　それは先生の言葉に驚いたというワケじゃなくて、そんな言葉を言われるとは思っていなかったからだ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Shiki. You do realize you don’t have long to live, don’t you?”
The words were stark and unmistakable.
“…”
My eyes went round.
Not because the truth surprised me, but because I had never expected her to say it aloud.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----Shiki… You know you're not going to last much longer?"
Her clear words.
"---------"
I'm surprised.
It's not that I'm surprised by her words, but rather, I never thought she would say them.

entries.japanese:
「―――ええ、まあ。
なんとなく、それなりに解ってますけど」
「そう。
そのわりには落ち着いているのね。
　今だってこんな、志貴には無関係なことに顔をだして体に負担をかけてる。
　まさかとは思うけど、君は死が怖くないの？」
　じろり、と不機嫌そうに睨んでくる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Well, yes. I’ve more or less understood for some time.”
“I see. You’re remarkably calm about it.
Even now, you’re involving yourself in a matter that has nothing to do with you and putting more strain on your body.
Surely you aren’t going to tell me you don’t fear death?”
She glared at me with open irritation.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----Well, yeah… I kind of know about it already."
"Is that so?
But you seem pretty calm.
Even now, you strain your body over something that has nothing to do with you.
I would have a hard time believing it, but are you really not afraid of dying?"
She stares at me, somewhat peeved.

entries.japanese:
「それこそまさかですよ。
きっと普通の人より、俺は死が怖いと思います」
　……けど、そんなのは先のことだ。
　明日だろうが一年先だろうが、先のことは親身になって考えられない。
「先の事はあまり考えられませんよ。
それより今をどうしたいのかって、そう思う方が優先しますから」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Of course I do. I’m probably more afraid of death than most people.”
But that belonged to the future.
Whether tomorrow or a year from now, I could never care about the future with the same immediacy as the present.
“I can’t think very far ahead. What matters first is what I want to do now.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"No way.
I think I'm more afraid of death than most people."
But… that's something in the future.
It may be tomorrow or next year, but I can't think about the future too much.
"I can't think about the future too much.
I prioritize what I want to be doing now."

entries.japanese:
「そっか、君は自分の死も視えるのか。
だから人より死が怖いってわけね。
　……なるほど、私だって自分の十三階段が見えたらぞっとしない」
「いえ、別にそういうワケでもないんですけど。
明確に死期が解るわけでもないし」
entries.maoEnglish:
“I see. You can see your own death as well, which explains why you fear it more than most.
I admit, I wouldn’t relish seeing my own thirteen steps to the gallows.”
“It isn’t quite like that. I don’t know exactly when I’m going to die.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"I see, so you can see your own death as well.
That's why you're more afraid of death than others.
That makes sense… Even for me, I'd be shivering if I could see the thirteen steps to the gallows."
"No, it's not like that.
It's not like I can clearly sense when I'll die."

entries.japanese:
「似たようなものよ。
……そうね、参考までに聞かせてもらえるかな。
　君は人より不出来な体を持ってしまった。
ならそれを呪ってしまうし、これからの人生だって怖いと感じてしまうでしょう。
　ねえ志貴。
君、そんな体のまま生きていくのは辛くない？」
　……先生は色のない眼で見つめてくる。
　それは自分の知らない、魔術師としての彼女の眼だ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Close enough. For my own reference, may I ask you something?
You were born with a body more fragile than other people’s. Surely you must resent it, and surely the life ahead of you frightens you.
Tell me, Shiki. Isn’t it painful to live in a body like that?”
Her eyes had gone colorless.
They were the eyes of a mage—the side of her I had never known.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"It's almost the same thing.
Let's see… can I ask you something, for reference?
You ended up with a body weaker than those of others.
It would only be natural to curse it and fear your life.
Hey, Shiki.
Don't you find it difficult living life with such a body?"
Sensei looks at me openly, yet with unreadable eyes.
Those are the eyes of a magus, her side of which I'm not familiar with.

entries.japanese:
「―――そうでしょう？
　君はもう人並みの幸福なんて手に入らない。
その体を抱えているかぎり、君は苦しんでいくだけよ」
「―――――それは、そうだけど」
　そんなコトは、そう、苦しいコトではないだろう。
「でも、きっと幸せですよ。
　だって今までが楽しかったんです。
だからきっと、これからだって楽しいんだ」
「―――――――――――――」
　息を飲む音。
　彼女ははあ、と大きく溜息をこぼして、もとの先生に戻ってくれた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Isn’t that true? An ordinary person’s happiness is already beyond your reach. As long as you bear that body, all that awaits you is suffering.”
“That may be true, but—”
Yet it did not seem so terrible to me.
“But I’m sure I’ll be happy.
Everything until now has been wonderful. So I’m sure what comes next will be wonderful too.”
“…”
She caught her breath.
Then she released a great sigh and became my teacher again.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"---Isn't that right…?
You can no longer have 'normal' happiness like everyone else.
As long as you have that body of yours, all that awaits is suffering."
"-----That may be so… but…"
I think it's not that bad.
"But, I'm probably happy.
Because up until now was a lot of fun.
So, it'll probably be fun in the future, too."
"-------------"
The sound of her gasping.
With a large sigh, she changes back to her usual self.

entries.japanese:
「志貴」
　先生はどこか哀しげな目で、名前を呼んだ。
「ほんとのことを言うとね、私は少し後悔してる。
　あの日、私は志貴に余計な事を言ってしまったんだなって」
　まっすぐに先生の目を見た。
　……あの時とは違う。
見上げていた視線は、今では見上げられる立場になっていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Shiki.”
Teacher spoke my name with sorrow in her eyes.
“To tell you the truth, I regret something.
That day, I said something I shouldn’t have.”
I looked directly into her eyes.
Things were different now. Once I had looked up at her; now she was the one looking up at me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki."
She seems sad as she calls my name.
"To be honest, I do feel some regret.
I feel like I said something to you that I shouldn't have back then."
I look straight into her eyes.
It's different from before… Back then I had to look up to see her eyes, but now she is looking up into mine.

entries.japanese:
「かみさまは余分な力を分け与えない。
だから志貴にその力があるという事は、なにかしら意味がある事だって。
　けどね、意味を決めるのは本人だけよ。
そこに他人の、ましてかみさまなんて曖昧なモノが介入する余地はない。
　だから、君は止めてもよかった。
　その眼を否定して、何もしないままでも良かった。
　普通の……志貴は志貴に相応しい所にいても良かったんだなって、後悔してる」
「………………先生」
entries.maoEnglish:
“I told you that God gives no one a power they do not need. If you possessed that power, it had to have some meaning.
But only the person who bears a power can decide its meaning. No one else—and certainly no vague thing called God—has any place in that decision.
You could have stopped.
You could have rejected those eyes and chosen to do nothing.
You could simply have lived an ordinary life―――you could have stayed where you belonged; I regret ever telling you otherwise.”
“Teacher…”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"God doesn't give excessive power without reason.
And I told you that if you have that power, there has to be some meaning to it.
But, you know, it's up to the individual to decide what that meaning may be.
There's no room for anyone else, especially something as ambiguous as a god, to interfere.
So it would have been alright if you did nothing.
Even if you denied those eyes of yours and did nothing, it still would have been alright.
I'm regretting my words, because… you could have lead a normal life more suitable for you, as Shiki."
"……………… Sensei."

entries.japanese:
「言ったでしょう？
　君はまっすぐに生きなさいって。
志貴は本当にそうなってくれた。
　けど、それは辛いことよ。
　君の眼が君を災厄に引き寄せるのなら、君は少しぐらい曲がったほうが楽だった。
　……誰よりも卓越した殺人鬼が、誰よりも殺人を嫌っているなんて皮肉じゃない。
　志貴は普通に暮らすか、心まで逸脱してしまえれば、そんなに苦しむ事もなかったのに」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Do you remember? I told you to live an honest, unwavering life. And you truly did.
But that path is painful.
If your eyes draw disaster toward you, bending a little would have made life easier.
What bitter irony that the most gifted killer alive hates killing more than anyone.
If you had lived an ordinary life—or let your heart stray as far as your nature—you would never have suffered so much.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Didn't I tell you earlier that you should live your life with an honest heart?
You really did, Shiki.
But, that's something difficult to do.
It would have been easier for you to stray from your path a little, because your eyes draw you to disaster.
…… Isn't it ironic that a killer more skilled than anyone else also hates killing more than anyone else?
If you lived a normal life, or had your heart deviated from the true path, you wouldn't have had to go through so much pain."

entries.japanese:
「……ええ、言われてみればそうですね。
もうちょっと割れきれたり諦めたりすれば、少しは楽になれるかもしれない。
　けど、そんなの意味ありませんよ。
楽になるっていっても少しだけだし、第一苦しいなんて思ったコトないです。
　先生は勘違いしてる。
俺は単に自分がやりたい事をやってきただけだし、聖人ってわけでもない。
　単に今の自分が好きなんです。
　だから―――あの時、今のままで大人になれって言われて、嬉しかった。
　先生。
俺は後悔してないんだから、先生が後悔する理由なんてないでしょう」
entries.maoEnglish:
“Now that you say it, perhaps you’re right. If I could make cleaner breaks or give up more easily, life might be a little easier.
But that wouldn’t mean anything. It would only be a little easier, and I’ve never thought of my life as suffering in the first place.
You misunderstand me. I’ve only done the things I wanted to do, and I’m no saint.
I simply like the person I am.
That’s why I was happy when you told me to grow up without changing.
Teacher, I have no regrets. So why should you?”
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yeah… that may be true, now that you mention it.
If I gave up, it may have been a little easier.
But, that has no meaning.
It would have only made things a little easier, and to start out with, I never thought of it as particularly painful.
You have the wrong idea, Sensei.
Everything I did, I did because I wanted to.
It's not like I'm a saint or anything.
I like myself just the way I am.
That's why… I was glad that you told me back then to become an adult by living just the way I was.
Sensei.
I don't regret anything, so there's no reason for you to regret anything either."

entries.japanese:
本当に、心の底からそう思って、先生に笑いかけた。
　先生はまぶしそうに目を細めて、一度だけ目蓋を閉じた。
entries.maoEnglish:
I meant it from the bottom of my heart, and smiled at her.
She narrowed her eyes as though the sight were dazzling, then closed them once.
entries.mirrorMoon:
I really feel that from the bottom of my heart, and I smile at her.
As if dazzled by a radiant light, she narrows her eyes, then closes them briefly.

entries.japanese:
「―――――そう。
　まいったな、ほんとに君は素敵な男の子になったみたいだ」
　トランクに伸ばされる手。
entries.maoEnglish:
“I see.
Well, you’ve got me—you really have grown into a wonderful young man.”
Her hand reached for the suitcase.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-----I see……
Man, it seems you really have become a wonderful young fellow."
Her hand reaches for her trunk.

entries.japanese:
「そうね、志貴はそれでいいわ。
　……こっちの世界は捻くれたヤツばっかりだから、君みたいなのが交じってくれるとバランスがとれる。
そのぶん志貴には辛いだろうけど、本人が気にしてないんなら関係ない」
　それじゃあ、と先生は背を向けた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Yes, you’re fine exactly as you are, Shiki.
This side of the world is full of twisted people, so adding someone like you restores the balance. It may make things harder for you, but if you don’t mind, then neither do I.”
With that, Teacher turned her back.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"Yeah, you're fine just the way you are, Shiki.
…… My world is full of devious individuals, so associating with someone like you balances things out.
It might be hard on you, but if you don't mind, then I guess it's alright."
With a "see you," Sensei turns her back to me.

entries.japanese:
「―――――――――――――」
　止める事はできないし、止める理由もない。
　本当に、これが最後なんだって分かっている。
　……思い出すのは、ただ一つだけ言い忘れた事。
　あの日。
　草むらの中、消えてしまいそうだった自分に話し掛けてくれた、大切な、友達。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
I could not stop her, and I had no reason to.
I knew this truly was the last time.
I remembered the one thing I had never said.
That day.
In another field of grass, a precious friend had spoken to a child who seemed ready to vanish.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-------------"
I can't stop her, and there's no reason to.
I can feel that this really is the last time.
…… All I can remember is the one thing I forgot to say.
That day.
In an ocean of grass, an important friend who had spoken with me, who was about to disappear.

entries.japanese:
「―――――――――――――」
　風はない。
　草は揺れず、ただ背中だけが遠ざかっていく。
　あの時と同じように、唐突に、振り向く事もせず。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
There was no wind.
The grass did not stir; only her back receded.
Just as it had then—suddenly, without a backward glance.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-------------"
There's no wind.
The grass does not sway and the only thing that changes is her figure, which gets farther away.
She didn't turn around suddenly back then, and she won't now.

entries.japanese:
「――――――先生」
　呼び止めた。
　立ち止まる背中。
「なに？」
　振り向く事はなく、声だけが聞こえた。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Teacher.”
I called her back.
Her retreating figure stopped.
“What is it?”
She did not turn; only her voice returned to me.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"------Sensei."
I call out to stop her.
She halts in her tracks.
"What?"
She doesn't turn around.
Only her voice drifts to me.

entries.japanese:
「―――――――――――――」
　言うべき事は決まっている。
　もうずっと前から言いたかった言葉。
　ただ、それを口にしてしまえば、本当に二度と、この人には出会えない。
　それでも―――口にしなくちゃいけなかった。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
I knew what I had to say.
They were words I had wanted to speak for years.
Yet once I said them, I felt certain I would never see her again.
Even so, they had to be spoken.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"-------------"
I know what I must say.
The words I've always wanted to say.
It's just that… if I say these words, I really won't be able to see her ever again.
But still---I have to say them.

entries.japanese:
君は君が正しいと思う大人になればいい、と。
　過ちを素直に受けとめられて、ごめんなさいと謝れる事を、大切なのだと教えてくれた。
entries.maoEnglish:
She had told me to become the adult I believed was right.
She had taught me the importance of accepting my mistakes honestly and apologizing for them.
entries.mirrorMoon:
She told me, "All I'm saying is live true to yourself, and become a man in the manner that you think is right."
She also taught me that it is important to accept my mistakes, and to be able to apologize for them.

entries.japanese:
だから。
　ちゃんと、言わないと。
「――――ありがとう。
先生に会えて、良かった」
entries.maoEnglish:
That was why.
I had to say it properly.
“Thank you. I’m glad I met you.”
entries.mirrorMoon:
That's why.
That's why I have to say it.
"----Thank you.
I'm glad I met you, Sensei."

entries.japanese:
……それが、子供の頃。
　別れを惜しむばかりで言えなかった、遠野志貴の心だった。
entries.maoEnglish:
…Those were the feelings Shiki Tohno had been unable to voice as a child,
too consumed by the pain of parting.
entries.mirrorMoon:
…… That's what I felt as a child.
Those words were the ones from the bottom of my heart that I once could not say, because I was filled with the sadness of parting.

entries.japanese:
背中ごしに、先生が驚いているように見えた。
　彼女は立ち止まったまま俯いて、やっぱりいつも通りの顔で振り向いた。
entries.maoEnglish:
Even from behind, I thought I saw her start in surprise.
She stood with her head bowed, then turned at last, wearing the same expression she always had.
entries.mirrorMoon:
From behind, it seems Sensei is surprised.
She stands there, lowers her head, and turns toward me with her usual expression.

entries.japanese:
「――――元気でね、志貴。
縁があったらまた会いましょう」
　なんでもない事のように言って、風が吹いた。
　ざあ、という音。
　草原は揺れて、月光が途切れる。
entries.maoEnglish:
“Take care, Shiki. If fate allows it, we’ll meet again.”
She spoke as though it were nothing.
Then the wind blew.
The grassland rushed and swayed, severing the moonlight.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----Take care, Shiki… Let's meet again if we are fated to do so."
She says this as if it was nothing, and the wind suddenly gusts.
Swooosh.
It rustles through the swaying grass, and the moon's light disappears.

entries.japanese:
そのあと。
　風にさらわれたように、彼女の姿はなくなっていた。
entries.maoEnglish:
And then.
She was gone—as though the wind had carried her away.
entries.mirrorMoon:
After that,
as if abducted by the wind, she disappears.

entries.japanese:
「――――――――――――――」
　不思議と涙は流れなかった。
　悲しくもあったし、別れたくないという感情もある。
　なのに涙が流れないのは、自分があの時より大人になったという事だ。
entries.maoEnglish:
“…”
Strangely, I shed no tears.
I was sad, and I did not want to part from her.
Yet the tears would not come because I had grown since that other farewell.
entries.mirrorMoon:
"--------------"
For some strange reason, I'm not shedding any tears.
I feel sad, and I don't want to part.
But not shedding tears also means that I've grown up since then.

entries.japanese:
草原は無音に戻る。
　見上げれば、月はすでに空から消えようとしていた。
　月が消え去るのと同じように、あらゆるものは通り過ぎていく。
　それでも長い時間があれば、また、何かに出会える事もあるだろう。
　そうして、今宵の月は消えた。
entries.maoEnglish:
Silence returned to the field.
When I looked up, the moon was already slipping out of the sky.
As the moon vanished, so did all things pass away.
Yet if enough time remained, perhaps somewhere along the way I would encounter something new again.
And so the moon of that night disappeared.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The grassy field becomes silent once more.
Gazing up, it looks like the moon is about to vanish from the sky.
All things pass by, just like the moon disappearing.
And yet, after a long time, there may be the chance to meet again.
And so, tonight's moon disappears.

entries.japanese:
「――――さて」
　幕を閉じるように一度だけ目蓋を閉じた。
　空は、黎明が近い。
　あの月が落ちて消え去ったように。
　遠野志貴にとっての長い物語は、ひとまずここで幕を下ろしてくれたのだろう――――
entries.maoEnglish:
“Well, then.”
I closed my eyes once, like a curtain falling.
Dawn was near.
Just as that moon had descended and disappeared.
So the long story of Shiki Tohno had, for the moment, lowered its curtain here—
entries.mirrorMoon:
"----Well then…"
I close my eyes just once, as if lowering the curtains.
In the sky, dawn is drawing closer.
Just like the moon that has just fallen,
for the time being, the curtains are lowered on the long story for Tohno Shiki----

entries.japanese:
天は高く。
　冴え凍える夜気に包まれて天を仰ぐ。
entries.maoEnglish:
The heavens were high.
Wrapped in the keen, frozen night air, I raised my face to the sky.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The heavens soar high above.
I look up, while embraced by the clear, brisk night air.

entries.japanese:
なにもかも覚めていくユメに似て不確か。
　駆け抜けた時間は全て幻。
　カタチとなって残るコトはなく、鮮明に思い出すコトさえ儚い。
　それでも、あの月の面影だけは消える事はないと信じている。
entries.maoEnglish:
Everything was uncertain, like a dream dissolving upon waking.
All the time I had raced through was illusion.
Nothing remained in solid form, and even the clearest memory was fleeting.
Still, I believed the image of that moon would never fade.
entries.mirrorMoon:
All things are uncertain, just like a waking dream.
The past is all an illusion.
It doesn't leave behind a tangible form, and even the most vivid of memories are really just transient.
Yet, I believe that the moon's image will never fade away.

entries.japanese:
――――それも、脆く。
　いつかは終わるコトを知っていても、かまわない。
entries.maoEnglish:
――――Even if that, too, was fragile.
It did not matter that I knew it must end someday.
entries.mirrorMoon:
Even that is fragile.
Even though I know it will end one day, I don't care.

entries.japanese:
思い出は続いていく。
　その終わりでさえ、おそらくは幸福だろう。
――――月蝕は遠い。
　誰もが残された時間を、駆け抜けて、過ぎていく。
entries.maoEnglish:
The memories would continue.
Even their ending, perhaps, would be happy.
――――The eclipse is still far away.
All of us race through whatever time remains, and pass on.
entries.mirrorMoon:
The memories continue on.
I'm sure that even the end will be a happy one.
----The lunar eclipse is far away.
Everyone races through their remaining time, and passes on.
